children.translated_text:
The <s>Dhvanyāloka</s>, composed by the revered master <s>Ānandavardhana</s>.
---- First <s>Uddyota</s> (Illumination).

children.text: --- śrīsahṛdayatilakarāmaśārakakṛtayā bālapriyākhyaṭīkayodbhāsitayā gosvāmiśrīdāmodaraśāstrinirmitayā viṣamasthaladarśanyā viṣamasthaladarśinyā divyāñjanākhyaṭippanyoktayā ca śrīmadācāryābhinavaguptaviracitayā locanākhyayā vyākhyayānugataḥ /
children.translated_text: --- Accompanied by the commentary called <s>Locana</s>, composed by the revered master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>; illuminated by the sub-commentary called <s>Bālapriyā</s>, written by <s>Śrīsahṛdayatilaka Rāmaśāraka</s>; and augmented by the notes called <s>Divyāñjana</s> (Divine Collyrium), a <s>Viṣamasthaladarśinī</s> (Revealer of Difficult Passages), composed by <s>Gosvāmī Śrī Dāmodara Śāstrī</s>.
First <s>Uddyota</s> (Illumination).

children.text: --- śrīmadācāryābhinavaguptakṛtaṃ locanam śrībhāratyai namaḥ apūrvaṃ yadvastu prathayati vinā kāraṇakalāṃ- jagadbhāvaprakhyaṃ nijarasabharātsārayati ca /
children.translated_text: --- The <s>Locana</s> by the revered master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. Salutation to <s>Śrī Bhāratī</s> (Goddess of Speech). That which reveals an unprecedented entity without the art of causation, which renders the entire world's appearance, essence-ful through the fullness of its own <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment),

children.text: kramātprakhyopākhyāprasarasubhagaṃ bhāsayati ta- tsarasvatyāstattvaṃ kavisahṛdayākhyaṃ vijayate //
children.translated_text: and which, beautiful through the progression of manifestation (<s>prakhyā</s>) and narrative (<s>upākhyā</s>), illuminates [all things] — that essence of <s>Sarasvatī</s> (the Goddess of Speech), known by the name 'poet-and-connoisseur' (<s>kavisahṛdaya</s>), is triumphant.
The <s>Dhvanyāloka</s>, composed by the revered master <s>Ānandavardhana</s>.

children.text: śrīsahṛdayatilakarāmaśārakakṛtabālapriy.ā śrīgurave namaḥ śrīgurūnpūrṇavedeśaṃ saṅgameśañca mādhavam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bālapriyā</s> by <s>Śrīsahṛdayatilaka Rāmaśāraka</s>. Salutation to the revered guru. We bow repeatedly to the revered gurus, to <s>Pūrṇa</s>, <s>Vedeśa</s>, <s>Saṅgameśa</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>,
<s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śivā</s>, who are the wish-fulfilling cow for those who bow.
The <s>Kāvyāloka</s> (Light on Poetry) and the <s>Locana</s> (Eye) — these two are the 'grasped' and 'grasper' (object and subject) of the discerning;
we praise the two authors of those works — the foremost among connoisseurs of <s>rasa</s>.
Formerly, an exposition of only the first <s>uddyota</s> of the <s>Locana</s> was made;
seeing that, and having examined other texts as well,
relying upon readings well-known in <s>Kerala</s>, according to our understanding,
we compose the <s>Bālapriyā</s>, [which is] for the most part a commentary on the mature <s>Locana</s>.

children.text: atha tatrabhavantaḥ śrīmadācāryābhinavaguptapādāḥ kāvyālokavyākhyānañcikīrṣavastasya nirvighnaparisamāptaye vihitaṃ samuciteṣṭadevatānamaskārātmakammaṅgalaṃ śiṣyaśiṅkṣāyai granthatonibadhnantyapūrvamityādi /
children.translated_text: Now, the revered master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, wishing to compose a commentary on the <s>Kāvyāloka</s>, incorporates into his text an auspicious invocation in the form of salutation to the appropriate chosen deity, performed for the unobstructed completion [of the work], for the instruction of students, [beginning with] 'apūrvam' ('unprecedented') and so forth.

children.text: yatukamalamanambhasi kamaletyādikāvyātmakaṃ sarasvatītattvam, kāraṇakalāṃ vi- locanam bhaṭṭendurājacaraṇābjakṛtādhivāsa- hṛdyaśruto 'bhinavaguptapadābhidho 'ham /
children.translated_text: The essence of <s>Sarasvatī</s> in the form of poetry is [exemplified by] such verses as 'that which is a lotus not in water, a lotus...' and so forth. [The word] <s>kāraṇakalā</s> means 'the art of causation'; the <s>Locana</s> [commentary states]: 'I, named <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, whose heart is made fragrant by dwelling at the lotus-feet of the teacher <s>Bhaṭṭendurāja</s>,
however little, echoing [the original], I elucidate the <s>Kāvyāloka</s> through the application of my own <s>Locana</s> (eye/commentary) for the [benefit of] people.'

children.text:
bālapriyā nā-tattatkāryaṃ prati prasiddhaṃ yadyadupādānādikāraṇantasya kalā leśaḥ tāṃ vinā antareṇaiva apūrvaṃulokaprasiddhavastuvijātīyamadbhutañca vastunirupākhyaśaśaśṛṅgādivilakṣaṇamanambho 'dhikaraṇakakamalādikaṃ padārtham prathayati sṛṣṭvā vistārayati, kiñca yad grāvaprakhyaṃupāṣāṇatulyaṃ nisargato nīrasaṃ jagatusarvaṃ vastu nijaḥ svīyaḥ kāvyāsambandhī yo rasaḥ śṛṅgarādiḥ tasya bharādatiśayāt sārayati sāraṃ karoti vibhāvāditvayojanena rasavyañjakaṃ karotīti yāvad, vākyābhyāmābhyāṃ kāvyātmakasarasvatītattvasya viśvakartuḥ prajāpaterutkarṣarūpavyatireko vyañcitaḥ; tameva sthirīkartumāha--kramādityādi /
yajjagaditi cānuṣajyate, prakhyākaveḥ pratibhā; upākhyā vacanaṃ prathamaṃ prakhyā paścādupākhyeti tayoryaḥ kramātprasaraḥ tena subhagaṃ hṛdyaṃ sad, bhāsayati nisargeṇāramaṇīyamapi sarvaṃ vastu rasavyañjakatvasampadanena rasaṇīyaṃ satprakāśayatītyarthaḥ, cakārasyātra sambandhaḥ, atra prakhyopākhyāprasarasyāpūrvavastunirmāṇe sarasatvakaraṇe ca hetutvamārthikaṃ bodhyam, atrādyena vākyenāpūrvavastuno nirmāṇandvitīyena pūrvaṃ sato vastunassarasatvakaraṇaṃ tṛtīyena dvayorapi hṛdyatayā prakāśanañjoktamityapa vyācikṣate, tatutathāvidhamapūrvavastuprathayitṛtvādidharmaviśiṣṭam, taddharmasampattyarthamāha-kavīti /
kavisahṛdayāvityākhyā yasya tat, kavisahṛdayaśabdāvatra nirmāṇarūpakavivyāpāravicārātmakasahṛdayavyāpāraviṣayakāvyaparau, yadvā kavisahṛdayairākhyāyataucyate iti tadākhyam, atha vā kavisahṛdayayorākhyā abhīkṣṇyena khyānaṃ sphuraṇaṃ yasya tat kāvyātmakamityarthaḥ, tattvamāropitaṃ bodhyam, sarasvatyāḥuśabdaprapañcābhimāninyādevatāyāḥ, tattvaṃupāramārthikaṃ rūpam, vijayate sarvasmādupari vartate, enena tannamaskāro granthakarturgamyate; atha ca sarasvatyāstattvaṃ dhvanikāvyam, vijayate; apūrvamityādyarthaḥ pūrvavadbodhya iti pratipādyārtho 'pyāsūtrita iti dik /
athauddhatyaṃ paraharannātmano vyākhyānanaipuṇī darśayan kīrttya nuvṛttaye nāmanirdeśaṅkurvaṃśca pratijānīte-bhaṭṭetyādi /
bhaṭṭendurājasyautannāmakasya guroḥ caraṇābjayoḥupajhatulyayoḥ pādayoḥ tatsannidhāviti yāvad yo 'dhivāsastena caraṇābjaśuśrūṣayeti yāvad; hṛdyāni svahṛdayasthāni; atha ca śrotṛjanahṛdayapriyāṇi śrutāni śāstrāṇi yasya saḥ, yathā padmena surabhīkaraṇe vastuno hṛdyatvaṃ tathetyupamātra dhvanyate, yatkiñcatusvalpam, apirevārthe, yadvānuraṇannapīti yojanā, apiśabdaḥ svalpābhidhānena saha sphuṭīkaraṇasyāpātato virodhaṃ dyotayati, locanam svayamavyucchinnaparameśvaranamaskārasampatticaritārtho 'pi vyākhyātṛśrotṝṇāmavighnenābhīṣṭavyākhyāśravaṇalakṣaṇaphalasampattaye bālapriyā anuraṇanubruvan ghaṇṭā'dinādasthānīyasya mūlakṛdvacanasyānuraṇanasthānīyaṃ vyākhyānarūpaṃ svavacanamityanena prakāśyate, sveti /
lojyate dṛśyate 'neneti locanaṃ svasya locanaṃmanaḥ tasya nitarāṃ yojanayā manaḥpraṇidhānenetyarthaḥ, kāvyālokaṃ janasya sphuṭayāmi visadīkaromi, yadvā svasya locanaṃ jñānaṃ tasya niyojanayā vyākhyānarūpānuraṇanadvārā samarpaṇena sphuṭayāmi prakāśayāmi, yathā netrayojanena tathetyupamādhvaniratrāpi bodhyaḥ /
vṛttikārakṛtasya svecchetyādipadyasya tātparyārthamavatārikayā darśayati-svayamityādi /

svayamiti vṛttikārasya nirdeśaḥ, avyucchinnaḥumadhye vicchedena rahitaḥ parameśvarasyautattallīlāvigrahamavalambamānasya paramātmanaḥ; namaskāraḥ tasya sampattiḥuprakarṣaḥ tayā caritaḥulabdhaḥ arthaḥuvighnanivṛttyādirūpasākṣātprayojanaṃ yasya saḥ, tathābhūtasya maṅgalācaraṇa āpātato virodhamapiśabdo dyotayati, vyākhyātṛśrotṝṇāmiti phalasampattaya ityādinā sambandhaḥ, avighnenauvidhnadhvaṃsena, abhīṣṭeti /
children.translated_text: Then, dispelling any presumption [of pride] and displaying his own skill in commentary, and making a declaration of his name for the sake of continuing the lineage, [<s>Abhinavagupta</s>] states '<s>bhaṭṭa</s>' etc. <s>Bhaṭṭendurāja</s> means 'the teacher of that name'; <s>caraṇābjayoḥ</s> means 'at his feet, which are like lotuses, i.e., in his presence' — the meaning is 'through service at his lotus-feet.' <s>Hṛdya</s> means 'residing in his own heart'; and also 'dear to the hearts of listeners'; <s>śruta</s> means '<s>śāstras</s> (learned treatises)' — thus qualified. Just as a lotus renders an object fragrant, [producing] delightfulness — this simile is also suggested. <s>Yatkiñcit</s> means 'however little'; <s>api</s> is used in the sense of emphasis; or the construction is '<s>anuraṇan</s> (echoing) <s>api</s> (even).' The word <s>api</s> indicates the apparent contradiction between making explicit and [expressing] littleness. The <s>Locana</s> [commentary says]: though the invocation of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) is itself fulfilled [in the author's own practice], yet for the attainment of the fruit — namely, the unobstructed hearing of the desired commentary — for both commentators and listeners; the <s>Bālapriyā</s> [explains]: the echo, i.e., the commentary in the form of his own speech, standing in the place of echoing — i.e., corresponding to the original author's words, which stand in the place of a bell-sound — is thereby revealed. <s>Sva</s> means 'his own.' The <s>Locana</s> means 'that by which one sees'; <s>svasya locanam</s> means 'his own mind'; <s>tasya niyojanayā</s> means 'through its application, i.e., mental concentration.' He says: 'I elucidate the <s>Kāvyāloka</s> for people.' Alternatively, <s>svasya locanam</s> means 'his own knowledge'; <s>tasya niyojanayā</s> means 'through offering it via the commentary-form echoing'; 'I illuminate, i.e., make manifest.' The simile of vision through the application of an eye should be understood here as well.

children.text: vyākhyātṝṇāṃ vyākhyānaṃ śrotṝṇāṃ śravaṇañcabhīṣṭaṃ divyāñajanākhyā ṭippanī śrīśrīgaurakṛṣṇaḥ śaraṇam /
children.translated_text: For commentators, commentary; for listeners, hearing — [both] are desired. The <s>Divyāñjana</s> (Divine Collyrium) sub-commentary. <s>Śrī Śrī Gaura Kṛṣṇa</s> is the refuge.
Having bowed to the gurus <s>Gaura</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the <s>Locana</s> (Eye) on the <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> —
I anoint with the Divine Collyrium, in order to perceive the meaning that is hard to see.

The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [explains]: <s>kalā</s> means 'a portion or trace' of whatever well-known material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) for each respective effect; <s>vinā</s> means 'without, apart from'; <s>apūrvam</s> means 'unprecedented, of a kind different from commonly known objects, wondrous'; <s>vastu</s> means 'an entity unlike unreal things such as the horn of a hare, such as a lotus not in water'; <s>prathayati</s> means 'manifests, creates and expands'; moreover, <s>jagat</s> means 'the entire world'; <s>prakhyam</s> means 'like a stone, naturally devoid of sentiment'; <s>nijarasabharāt</s> means 'through the abundance of its own <s>rasa</s>, i.e. <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc.'; <s>sārayati</s> means 'renders essential, makes it a vehicle of <s>rasa</s> through the application of <s>vibhāva</s> etc.' — by these two statements, the distinctness of the essence of <s>Sarasvatī</s> in the form of poetry from <s>Prajāpati</s>, the creator of the universe, in the form of excellence is suggested. To further establish that, he says 'kramāt' etc. And the word <s>jagat</s> is connected [from the previous verse]. <s>Prakhyā</s> means the poet's creative intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>); <s>upākhyā</s> means verbal expression. The sequence (<s>krama</s>) of these — manifestation first, then verbal expression — by which [sequence the work is] beautiful (<s>subhaga</s>), i.e., delightful; <s>bhāsayati</s> means 'illuminates, renders attractive by bestowing the capacity to suggest <s>rasa</s> upon everything that is naturally un-delightful.' The word <s>ca</s> here has a connective function. Here, the sequence of manifestation and expression should be understood as the logical cause for the creation of unprecedented objects and the rendering [of objects] as <s>rasa</s>-ful. Here, by the first statement the creation of unprecedented objects, by the second the making-essential of existing objects, and by the third the illumination of both with delightfulness has been stated — thus he elucidates further. <s>Tat</s> means 'of such a nature, qualified by the property of manifesting unprecedented objects etc.' To explain the means of acquiring those properties, he says '<s>kavi</s>' etc. <s>Kavisahṛdayākhyam</s> means 'that whose name consists of the words kavi (poet) and sahṛdaya (connoisseur).' The words <s>kavi</s> and <s>sahṛdaya</s> here refer to the domain of poetry as the object of the creative activity of the poet and the evaluative activity of the connoisseur. Alternatively, it is 'that which is named by poets and connoisseurs,' i.e., spoken of by them. Or, <s>ākhyā</s> of poets and connoisseurs means 'that whose frequent naming/manifestation' is [expressed by them]; the meaning is: having the nature of poetry. <s>Tattva</s> should be understood as a metaphorical attribution. <s>Sarasvatyāḥ</s> means 'of the deity presiding over the manifestation of speech.' <s>Tattva</s> means 'the ultimate form.' <s>Vijayate</s> means 'is supreme over everything.' By this, the author's salutation to the Goddess is understood. And moreover, the essence of <s>Sarasvatī</s> is <s>dhvani</s>-poetry; <s>vijayate</s> means 'it triumphs.' The meaning of 'apūrvam' etc. should be understood as before — thus the subject matter too is indicated. Such is the direction.

children.text: ath.a dhvaniprasthāpakācāryaśrīmadānandavardhanaviracitaṃ dhvanyālokanibandhanaṃ vyākhyātavato bharatadarśanasūtrabhāṣyakārapradhānasyācāryyaśrīmadabhinavaguptasya locanākhye vyākhyāne viṣamasthalāni mukhyatvena viśadayitukāmasya divyāñjananāmikeyaṃ ṭippanī; prāsaṅgikī tvaparatrāpīti na pratiśrutiviroda udbhāvanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, this sub-commentary called <s>Divyāñjana</s>, intended primarily to clarify difficult passages in the commentary called <s>Locana</s> — composed by the revered master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, the foremost among the commentators on the <s>Bharatadarśana</s> (Dramaturgical Treatise) <s>sūtra</s>-<s>bhāṣya</s> — on the <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> treatise composed by the revered master <s>Ānandavardhana</s>, the propounder of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion). It also addresses incidental [difficulties elsewhere]; hence there is no contradiction with its title.

children.text: yattvatrottarapadāvyavahitapūrvatvaviśiṣṭavidyāyonyanyatarasambandhavācakardantapadoddeśyakānaṅvidhāyakānaṅṛto dvandva iti śāstreṇa vidyādvārakaikayajñārvijyasambandhena vidyāsambandhivācakahotāpotṛvadihāpi vidyādvārakaikapratipādyaviṣayakajñānānukūlavyāpāravattvasambandhena sambandhivācakayorvyākhyātṛpadaśrotṛpadayordvandve 'pi vyākhyātāśrotṝṇāmityucitamiti kaścidākṣipati tanmandam-- "ṛto vidyāyonisambandhebhyaḥ" pūrṇaitatsūtrānuvṛttita ṛtpadānuvṛttyaiva nirvāhe prakṛtasūtre punā ṛdgrahaṇamānaṅvidhyu ddeśyatāvacchedakakoṭipraviṣṭasamasyamānayāvatpadānāmṛdantatvasyāpekṣāṃ darśayad vidyayonyanyataravācitvamapi tadavacchedakakukṣau samāviveśayiṣyatīti vyākyātṛśabdasya kathaṃ cittadanyataravācitve 'pi śrītṛśabde tadvācitvaniyamādarśanād viśeṣaṇābhāvaprayuktaviśiṣṭābhāvamudrayoddeśyatāvacchedakatvānākrāntatvādānaḍo 'pravṛtteḥ sādhveva vyākhyātṛśrotṝṇāmiti /
children.translated_text: Now, regarding the compound '<s>vyākhyātṛśrotṝṇām</s>' — someone objects that [according to grammatical rules about] the <s>dvandva</s> compound involving terms denoting sciences, relationships, and <s>ṛ</s>-ending stems, and by the rule that a <s>dvandva</s> of relation-words formed through a single field of knowledge-connection (as with <s>hotāpotṛ</s>) applies, here too, since the commentator-word and listener-word are relation-terms via the connection of possessing activity favorable to the single knowledge-subject being elucidated, '<s>vyākhyātāśrotṝṇām</s>' would be appropriate — this objection is weak. Since the full <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ṛto vidyāyonisambandhebhyaḥ</s>' already carries the <s>ṛ</s>-stem suffix forward, the re-statement of <s>ṛ</s>-stem in this <s>sūtra</s> shows the need for the <s>ṛ</s>-ending status of all component words being conjoined, thereby drawing the 'one-of-the-two relation-word' criterion into the scope of the delimiting condition. Therefore, how [can the objection stand], since even if the <s>vyākhyātṛ</s>-word is a 'one-of-two' designator, the <s>śrotṛ</s>-word shows no restriction to such designation, and the distinguishing feature being absent due to the absence of the qualifier, the delimiting condition of the subject is not encompassed — hence the suffix does not apply. Therefore '<s>vyākhyātṛśrotṝṇām</s>' is perfectly correct.
Salutation to <s>Śrī Nṛhari</s> (Lord Viṣṇu as Man-Lion). The nails of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) — who are lions of their own will,
who darken the moons by their own pure radiance — may they protect you, [they who are] destroyers of the affliction of those who take refuge.

children.text:
locanam samucitāśīḥprakaṭanadvāreṇa parameśvarasāṃmukhyaṃ karoti vṛttikāraḥ--sveccheti /
madhuripornakhāḥ vo yuṣmānvyākhyātṛśrotṝṃstrāyantām, teṣāmeva sambodhanayogyatvāt; sambodhanasāro hi yuṣmadarthaḥ, trāṇaṃ cābhīṣṭalābhaṃ prati sāhāyakācaraṇaṃ, tacca tatpratidvandvivighnāpasāraṇādinā bhavatīti, iyadatra trāṇaṃ vivikṣitam, nityodyoginaśca bhagavato 'sammohādyavasāyayogitvenotsāhapratītervīraraso bālapriyā vaṇañcābhīṣṭaṃ phalaṃ tasya sampattaye niṣpattaye, tadubhayasampattau tadubhayahetukagranthapratiṣcaṭārūpaṃ phalaṃ granthakārasya ca siddhyatīti bhāvaḥ, samucitaṃugranthārambhe yogyaṃ yadāśiṣaḥ prakaṭanaṃuvacanantaddvāreṇa, parameśvarasya sāmmukhyaṃuvyākhyātṛśrotṝn pratyābimukhyaṃ trāṇecchārūpam, karoti sampādayati, tatrrāṇasya parameśvarasāmmukhyāyattatvātrrāṇāṅgabhūtaṃ tatsāmmukhyamāśīrvādena sampādayatītyarthaḥ, yadvā samucitāyā āśiṣaḥ prakaṭanaṃugranthato nibandhanaṃ taddvāreṇa, parameśvare viṣaye sāmmukhyaṃuvyākyātṛśrotṝṇāmābhimukhyamanusandhānātmakam karotyutpādayati, vṛttikāra ityanena svecchetyādikaṃ na kārikārūpasūtrādyapadyamiti darśitam, va ityasya vyākhyātṛśrotṝniti vyākhyāne hetumāha-teṣāmiti /
kuto 'tra sambodhanaprasaṅga ityata āha-sambodhaneti /
sambodhanaṃ sāraḥuprāṇo yuṣmadarthatvaprayojakoṃ'śo yasya saḥ, na hyasambodhyo yuṣmadā vyapadiśyate, trāyantāmityanenātra vivakṣitaṃ vyācaṣṭe-trāṇañceci /
abhīṣṭeti vyākhyānaśravaṇarūpetyarthaḥ, sahāyasya karma sāhāyakaṃ tatpratidvandvīta; abhīṣṭalābhapratibandhaketyarthaḥ, apasaraṇaṃunivartanam, ādipadenārthatattvamanīṣāsamunmeṣādeḥ parigrahaḥ, iyaditi /
uktarūpamityarthaḥ, atha dhvaniṃ kāvyātmānaṃ ṭippanī vṛttikāra iti /
svakṛtānāmeva mūlarūpāṇāṃ kārikāṇāṃ vyākhyā'tmakavṛtteḥ karttetyarthaḥ, ata eva viśiṣṭasyevāripsitatvena mūle maṅgalākaroṇe 'pi nācāravirodhaḥ /
ke cittu mūle 'pi "kāvyasyātme' tiprathamakārikāyāmādyapadasya kāvyetyasyānyaparatve 'pi parārthopanītodakumbhadarśanavat śravaṇamātreṇāpi; "kāvyālāpāśca ye ke cid gītakāntakhilāni ca /
śabdamūrttidharasyaite viṣṇoraṃśā mahātmana"-- ityādipramāṇato bhagavatsphorakatvena vastunirddeśarūpamaṅgalaṃ jātamevetyāpi vadanti, kārikākṛdvṛttikṛtorabhedastvagre darśayiṣyate /
sambodhanasāro hīti /
svajanyabodhāśrayatvena vaktrabhiprāyaviṣayatvāvacchinnasya locanam dhvanyate, nakhānāṃ praharaṇatvena graharaṇena ca rakṣaṇe kartavye nakhānāmavyatiriktatvena karaṇatvātsātiśayaśaktitā kartṛtvena sūcitā, dhvanitaśca parameśvarasya vyātiriktakalaṇāpekṣāvirahaḥ, madhuriporityane tasya sadaiva jagatrrāsāpasāraṇodyama uktaḥ, kīddaśasya madhuripoḥ? svecchayā kesariṇaḥ, ma tu karmapāratantryeṇa, bālapriyā pratipādayiṣyatā granthakṛtā kṛtasyāsya prathamapadyasya kāvyarūpatvādasminnapi dhvaniryojanīya iti manvāno rasādibhedena trividheṣu dhvaniṣu pradhānabhūtaṃ rasadhvanimādau yojayati-nityetyādi /
caśabdaḥ samuccaye dhvanyate ceti sambandhaḥ; na vācyārthamātramanenocyate kintu raso dhvanyate cetyarthaḥ, nityodyogina iti /
udyogo nāmaubāhyasaṃnāhātmakodyamanakriyārūpa darśitam, yathoktaṃ bharatena "uttamaprakṛtirutsāhātmako vīra iti" asaṃmohenausammoharāhityena yo 'dhyavasāyaḥ etadevaṃ kartuṃ śakyamiti vastutattvaniścayaḥ tadyogitveneti utsāhahetukathanam, asaṃmohaścadhyavasāyaśca tadyogitveneti ke cit, utsāhapratīteriti /
svecchākesariṇo madhuripoḥ prasannārticchida iti padairhiraṇyakaśipuprabhṛtinivarhaṇādiviṣayakotsāhasya vyañjanayā sahṛdayānāṃ pratīterityarthaḥ, matyādivyabhicāripratīterupalakṣaṇamidam, vastudhvaniṃ darśayati-nakhānāmityādi /
praharaṇatveneti karaṇatve hetuḥ siṃhādīnāmāyudhatvenetyarthaḥ, praharaṇatva iti pāṭhe nimitte saptamī, nanu nakhānāṃ praharaṇatve 'pi kathaṃ trāṇakriyāṃ prati karaṇatvamityatastatsambhāvanāndarśayati-praharaṇeneti /

praharaṇaṃ hi svasyānyasya vā rakṣāṃ kartumupādīyata iti bhāvaḥ, avyatiriktatvena karaṇatvāditi, avyatiriktatvamapṛthagbhūtatvamābhyantaratvamiti yāvat tadviśiṣṭakaraṇatvādityarthaḥ, karaṇaṃ dvividhaṃ bāhyamābhyantarañca, bāhyaṃ khaṅgādi; ābhyantaraṃhastādi, karaṇatvāt kartṛtveneti samabandhaḥ, karaṇatvamanuktvā kartṛtvoktyetyarthaḥ, madhuripurnakhaistrāyatāmiti vaktavyamanuktvā madhuripornakhāstrāyantāmityuktyeti yāvat, sātiśayā ṭippanī svasambodhyasya yuṣmatpadārthatayānyatra vyavasthāpitatvādityāśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For a weapon is employed to effect the protection of oneself or of another — this is the purport. 'By non-differentiation, [being] an instrument' — 'non-differentiation' means 'non-separateness,' i.e., 'internality'; being an instrument qualified by that [internality] — this is the meaning. Instruments are of two kinds: external and internal. External [instruments include] swords etc.; internal [include] hands etc. 'From being an instrument, [indicated] by agency' — this is the syntactic connection. Meaning: by stating agency without stating instrumentality — i.e., instead of saying 'May the claws of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> protect [you],' saying 'May the claws of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> protect!' — the surpassing [capacity is indicated]. The <s>ṭippanī</s> [notes]: because the entity that is to be directly addressed by the second person has been established elsewhere as the referent of the <s>yuṣmad</s> (second-person) word — this is the intention.
'Cognition of <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm)' —

children.text: vibhāvādīnāṃ mitho nāntarīyakatvena "sadbhāvaśced vibhāvāderdvayorekasya vā bhaved /
children.translated_text: Since the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. are mutually inseparable: 'If there is the existence of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. — of two or of one —
and the hint (<s>ūṭi</s>) involves the reference to another [element], then there is no fault.' //

The <s>vṛttikāra</s> (author of the commentary-prose), by means of expressing appropriate benedictions, effects the favorable attention of the Supreme Lord — [this is what is meant by] 'by [His] own will' etc. May the claws of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> protect you — that is, the listeners and expositors — since they alone are fit to be addressed; for the essence of the vocative address is the second-person meaning. And 'protection' (<s>trāṇa</s>) means rendering assistance toward the attainment of the desired [goal]; and that [assistance] operates through the removal of obstacles posed by adversaries and the like — this much is the intended meaning of 'protection' here. And since the Blessed Lord is ever active, through [His] freedom from delusion, [which manifests as His] capacity for resolve (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) — from this comes the cognition of <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), [and thus] the <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic aesthetic mood). The [term] <s>bālapriyā</s> [means] 'dear to the young' [i.e., the desired result], and <s>vaṇañca</s> is the desired fruit — for its <s>sampatti</s> (fulfillment/accomplishment). When both [results] are fulfilled, the fruit for the author of the text — in the form of the text's firm establishment caused by both — is also achieved: this is the purport. 'Appropriate' means 'suitable at the commencement of the text'; the 'expression' means 'the utterance' of benedictions — by that means [he effects] the 'favorable attention' (<s>sāmmukhya</s>) of the Supreme Lord — i.e., His disposition toward the expositors and listeners, which takes the form of a desire to protect. [The <s>vṛttikāra</s>] brings about [this disposition]; since protection depends on the Lord's favorable attention, [the vṛttikāra] brings about through the benediction that favorable attention which is subsidiary to protection — this is the meaning. Alternatively, the expression — i.e., the textual composition — of the appropriate benediction, by that means, effects — i.e., produces — the favorable attention (<s>ābhimukhya</s>), which has the nature of contemplation, of the expositors and listeners toward the Supreme Lord. By [the term] '<s>vṛttikāra</s>,' it is shown that 'by [His] own will' etc. is not a verse-form <s>sūtra</s> etc. He gives the reason for the explanation [of <s>vas</s>] as 'expositors and listeners' — 'of them' [<s>teṣām</s>]. Why is there occasion for the vocative here? — to this he says: 'the vocative' [<s>sambodhanam</s>]. That whose essence — i.e., vital core — and motivating factor for the second-person meaning is the vocative — [is so called]; for one who cannot be addressed is not designated by the second person. He explains what is intended by 'may they protect' — 'and protection' etc. 'Of the desired' means 'consisting of exposition and hearing' — this is the meaning. The action of an assistant is 'assistance' (<s>sāhāyaka</s>); 'the adversary of that' means 'that which obstructs the attainment of the desired [goal]' — this is the meaning. 'Removal' means 'turning back'; by the word 'etc.' [<s>ādi</s>], the awakening of the inquiry into the truth of meaning etc. is included. 'This much' — meaning 'of the stated form.' Now, [regarding] <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) as the soul of poetry, the <s>ṭippanī</s> [glosses]: '<s>vṛttikāra</s>' means the author of the explanatory prose commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>) on his own original verses (<s>kārikās</s>) — this is the meaning. For this very reason, since [the <s>vṛtti</s>] is desired only as something distinguished [from the <s>kārikās</s>], there is no violation of convention even when benediction is [also] performed in the root [text]. Some, however, [argue that] even in the root [text], in the first <s>kārikā</s> 'the soul of poetry (<s>kāvyasyātmā</s>)' — although the first word '<s>kāvya</s>' has reference to something else — merely by hearing it, like seeing a water-pot brought for another's purpose, [there arises auspiciousness]; and by the authority of texts such as 'Whatever poetic compositions exist, and songs, and all [the rest] — these are portions of the great-souled <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose form is sound (<s>śabdamūrti</s>)' — since it reveals the Blessed One, a factual benediction in the form of a statement about reality has already arisen — thus some say. The identity of the author of the <s>kārikās</s> and the author of the <s>vṛtti</s> will be shown later. 'The essence of the vocative' — as the locus of cognition generated by [the vocative] itself, [and] as delimited by being the object of the speaker's intention — [this is what] the <s>Locana</s> suggests. By the instrumentality of the claws as weapons — and by grasping, [i.e.,] in the task of protection — the surpassing capacity [of the claws] is indicated through their agency, since the claws are not different [from the Lord's own limbs] and thus serve as instruments. And suggested is the Lord's independence from any external implement. By 'the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>,' His perpetual endeavor to remove the terror of the world is stated. Of what sort is this enemy of <s>Madhu</s>? 'A lion by His own will' — not through the dependence of <s>karma</s>. The author of the text, intending to demonstrate [the nature of] <s>bālapriyā</s> (the suggestion dear to the young/unsophisticated), considering that since this first verse is itself in the form of poetry, <s>dhvani</s> should also be applied to it — [and so] among the three types of <s>dhvani</s> differentiated as <s>rasa</s> etc., he applies <s>rasa-dhvani</s>, which is primary, at the very beginning — [this is shown by] 'perpetually' etc. The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) functions in the sense of aggregation; the connection is: 'and it is suggested.' He is not saying merely the expressed meaning (<s>vācyārtha</s>), but [that] <s>rasa</s> is also suggested — this is the meaning. 'Perpetually active' — 'activity' (<s>udyoga</s>) means the action of exertion in the form of outward preparation of armor etc., as shown. As <s>Bharata</s> has said: 'Of excellent nature, the heroic (<s>vīra</s>) [rasa has] <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) as its soul.' 'Without delusion' — 'by the absence of delusion' — that which is 'resolve' (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), the ascertainment of the truth of the matter: 'This indeed can be done' — 'through connection with that': this is a statement of the cause of <s>utsāha</s>. Some [read]: 'and freedom from delusion, and resolve — through connection with those two.' 'Cognition of <s>utsāha</s>' — [means:] from the words 'by His own will,' 'a lion,' 'enemy of <s>Madhu</s>,' 'gracious dispeller of pain' — through the suggestion of His enthusiasm directed at the slaying of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> and others — the aesthetic apprehension [of <s>rasa</s>] by the sensitive reader (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) — this is the meaning. This is an example (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) including the cognition of <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transient emotions) such as <s>mati</s> (discernment) etc. He demonstrates <s>vastudhvani</s> (suggestion of a fact) — 'of the claws' etc. 'By [their] being weapons' — this is the reason for [their] instrumentality: meaning 'by being the armaments of lions etc.' In the reading '<s>praharaṇatva</s>' (being a weapon), the locative is in the sense of 'on the occasion of.' Now, even if the claws are weapons, how are they instruments for the act of protection? — to this he shows the basis for such a supposition: 'by a weapon' etc.

ityuktadiś.ā prakṛte sapatnamadhvādyasurālambanena yogyatayā'kṣiptānāṃ tadīyanirbhīkatvādijñānādyudīpanatadviṣayāvahelā'dyanubhāvagarvādisaṃcāriṇāṃ pānakarasanyāyena yogād utsāhaiya pratīterityarthaḥ /

bāhyakhaḍgādityarthaḥ, jagatrrāseti /

vyañjita ityarthaḥ, imamarthaṃ manasikṛtya pūrvaṃ nityodyogina ityuktamiti bodhyam, na tu karmapāratantryeṇetyādeḥ svīkṛtetyatra sambandhaḥ, ādyamicchāpadena dvitīyaṃ svapadena ca gamyamiti bodhyam, viśiṣṭeti viśiṣṭaṃudānavāntarahananāpekṣayā viśeṣavat, dānavasyauhiraṇyakaśiporhananaṃ yadvā viśiṣṭaḥusuranaratiryagādyavadhyatvarūpaviśeṣavān yo dānavastasya hananaṃ tasminnucito yastathāvidhāyāḥunaraharivigrahāvalambanaviṣayikāyā icchāyāḥ parigrahaḥ, ucitetīcchāviśeṣaṇaṃ vā tasmin yadaucityāmarthāt svasya tasmāddhetorityarthaḥ, svīkṛtasiṃharūpasyeti /
siṃharūpasya nararahapamiśratvaṃ prasiddamato noktam, ye cchindantīti /

asmin pakṣe ātiṃśabda ātiṅkāraṇaṃlakṣayati tasyāvyabhiṭacāreṇa nikhilārtikāritvañca dhvanatīti bodhyam, vināśayadbhiriti /
naśairiti śeṣaḥ, ārtirevalocchinnā bhavatīti /
tathāvidhasya hiraṇyakaśipoḥ hananamārterevocchedanaṃ na tu kasya citprāṇina iti bhagavadbuddhiriti bhāvaḥ, tasyāmapyavasthāyāṃuhananāvasthāyāmapi, uktamiti /

locanam hi mukhyātayā bhāvavṛttaya eva; svacchāyayā ca vakrahṛdyarūpayā'kṛtyā'yāsitiḥ-khedita induryaiḥ, atrārthaśaktimūlena dhvaninā bālacandratvaṃ dhvanyate, āyāsanena tatsannidhau candrasya vicchāyatvapratītirahṛdyatvapratītiśca dhvanyate, āyāsakāritvaṃ ca nakhānāṃ suprasiddham; naraharinakhānāṃ tacca lokottareṇa rūpema pratipāditam kiṃ ca tadīyāṃ svacchatāṃ kuṭilimānaṃ cāvalokya bālacandraḥ svātmani khedamanubhavati; tulye 'pi svacchakuṭilākārayoge 'mī prapannārtinivāramakuśalāḥ; na tvahamiti vyatirekālaṅkāro 'pi dhvanitaḥ, kiñcāhaṃpūrvameka evasādhāraṇavaiśadyahṛdyākārayogātsamastajanābhilaṣaṇīyatābhājanamabhavam, adya bālapriyā vakrahṛdyarūpākṛtyāyāsitatvasya bālacandra eva sambhavāttadarthasāmarthyamūlenetyarthaḥ, bālacandratvaṃ dhvanyata iti /

bālapriyā bālenduraviratamāyāsamanubhavatīvetyutprekṣāyāṃ hi pūrvoktaṃ tāneva lokobālenduṃ bahumānena paśyati na tu māmityākalanaṃ nimittaṃ tatra ca spaṣṭāpahnutiḥ; na nakhā ete kintu bālendava iti lokasya pratīteḥ; tathā cātrotprekṣā nakhaviṣayakanakhatvaniṣedhapūrvakabālendutvāroparūpalokapratītiviṣayakabālacandragatapratītinibandhanetyāto 'pahnutibalādtmānaṃ labhata ityaṅgāṅgibhāvo bodhyaḥ, nigamayatyevamityādi /
atra vīrarasadhvaniraṅgī; utsāhasya prādhānyena pratīyamānatvāditi dhyeyam, nanvatra granthakāragatabhagavadviṣayakaratervyaṅgyatvasya vaktavyatayā bhāvadhvanirevāṅgitvena vācyaḥ, rasastu tadaṅgatayeti cedatrāhuḥ-pratipannabhagavattanmayībhāvasya grandhakarturāśīḥ-kartṛtayā vāsyamidaṃ na bhāvaparaṃ bhaktasya bhedena bhajanīyadevatāviṣayakaratervyaṅgyāyāḥ khalubhāvatvam, granthakarturbhagavattanmayībhāvaśaca svayaṃ sūtrakṛdavasthāyāṃ maṅgalākaramādapūrvaprasthāvakartṛtvācca siddhaḥ, ṭippanī utprekṣāpahnutidhvanirapīti /
bālacandrakarttṛkāyāsānubhavasyotprekṣā hi nakhatvapratiṣedhapurassarabālacandratvavidhānapratyayalakṣaṇaviṣayāpahnavamātmanīnamavalambate 'to 'ṅgāṅgibhāvaḥ saṅkaro 'nayoriti bhāvaḥ /
yattvāyāsitarūpaikapadavyañjakānupraviṣṭyorenayorekavyañjakānupraveśātmā so 'treti kaścit, tanmandam-mitho 'napekṣatvarūpapṛthagvyavasthitatva eva dhvanigate yogyatāstyekavyañjakānupraveśātmanaḥ saṅkarasya, prakṛte coktadiśotprekṣāpanhutyoḥ sāpekṣataivamitho 'sti, na ca nairapekṣye saṃsṛṣṭeḥ prasaṅga iti saṅkyam? padarūpaviṣayabhedaviśiṣṭānapekṣatvasya saṃsṛṣṭau vivakṣitatvād, ekavyañjakānupraveśe ca viśeṣyasattve 'pi viśeṣaṇābhāvānna saṃsṛṣṭilakṣaṇātivyāptirityākūtam /
evaṃ vastvalaṅkāraraseti /
yadyapi sarvameva vastu tathāpīha rasālaṅkārabhinnaṃ vastupadena vivakṣitam, alaṅkāratvaṃ ca rasādipratiyogikabhedavadvyaṅgyapratiyogikabhedaviśiṣṭaśabdārthānyataraniṣṭaviṣayitāsambandhāvacchinnacamatkṛtijanakatāvacchedakatāvacchedakatvam ramaśca bhagrāvaraṇacidviśiṣṭaḥ sthāyī /
tridhā dhvaniratreti /
yadyapi prakārāntarema dhvanīnāṃbāhuvidhye 'pi dhvanyamānaviṣayabhedanibandhanadhvanivibhāgajanakatvaprakārakācāryyatātparyaviṣayībhūtadharmāṇāṃ vaividhyena dhvanitridhātvamapyaviruddhamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
In the manner stated, in the present context, by the fitness suggested through the example of the rival-liquor (<s>sapatna-madhu</s>) etc. involving the <s>asuras</s>, the experience of <s>utsāha</s> (heroic energy) arises from the combination — in the manner of the analogy of the taste of a beverage (<s>pānaka-rasa-nyāya</s>) — of the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) such as contemptuous disregard toward those [enemies], and the <s>sañcārins</s> (transitory emotions) such as pride, which are stimulated by the kindling of knowledge such as their fearlessness, all of which are suggested through fitness. This is the meaning.
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Not by another's wish' — rather, the meaning is: 'of him who assumed the lion-form' — by the very propriety of adopting that particular wish pertaining to the killing of a <s>dānava</s> (demon) of special [invulnerability]. What kind of nails? Those that cut the suffering (<s>ārti</s>) of those who have taken refuge (<s>prapanna</s>). For cutting is indeed the proper function of nails; but the capacity to be cut — which is inconceivable for suffering with respect to [ordinary] nails — is nevertheless conceivable for his nails, due to the propriety of their being fashioned by his own will. This is the purport. Alternatively: <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, the thorn of the three worlds, is the tormentor of the universe — he is, in substance, the very embodiment of suffering (<s>ārti</s>) for those who have taken refuge in the Blessed Lord alone; by those [nails] that destroy him, it is suffering itself that is severed — thus the supreme compassion of the Lord even in that [violent] state is expressed. Moreover, those nails [are characterized] by purity (<s>svaccha</s>), i.e., by the quality of clarity, by spotlessness. <s>Svaccha-mṛdu-gra</s> etc. — 'the nature of those whose power (<s>śakti</s>), i.e., capacity, is dear to children (<s>bāla-priyā</s>)' — <s>śakata</s> is also a reading. Another suggested meaning is also stated with '<s>dhvanitaś ca</s>' — the remainder is: 'by the stated suggestion.' 'By a different instrument' (<s>vyatirikta-karaṇa</s>) — the meaning is: different from an external sword. '<s>Jagat-trāsa</s>' — the meaning is: the effort directed at removing the terror that the world [experiences] from various wicked beings. 'Stated' (<s>ukta</s>) — the meaning is: suggested (<s>vyañjita</s>). Having considered this meaning, one should understand that '<s>nitya-udyoginaḥ</s>' (ever-exerting) was said earlier [for this reason], and that the connection is not with '<s>svīkṛta</s>' [in the sense] beginning with 'not by the dependence on <s>karma</s>.' One should understand that the first [meaning] is conveyed by the word '<s>icchā</s>' (wish) and the second by the word '<s>sva</s>' (own). '<s>Viśiṣṭa</s>' — distinguished, i.e., possessing the distinction of requiring consideration of the killing of a <s>dānava</s> different [from ordinary enemies]; or: the killing of a <s>dānava</s> — i.e., <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> — who is distinguished by the special characteristic of being unkillable by gods, men, or animals; the adoption of that particular wish pertaining to the assumption of the <s>Narahari</s> (man-lion) form — 'proper' (<s>ucita</s>) is either a qualifier of the wish, or it means 'from that propriety, therefore, from his own [nature].' 'Of him who assumed the lion-form' — the admixture of the lion-form with the man [i.e., <s>Narahari</s>] is well-known, hence not stated. 'Who cut' — the remainder is: 'they.' 'Cutting-capacity' — the meaning is: the agency of the action of cutting. 'Capacity to be cut' — i.e., being the object of cutting — the connection is with 'is conceivable.' 'Inconceivable' — the purport is: because suffering is formless. 'Of his' — i.e., belonging to <s>Narahari</s>. 'By his own wish' — by the wish of the Blessed Lord, the fashioning, i.e., the creation of the nails, is the cause; because of the capacity to cut even a formless entity. Or: by his own wish, i.e., by his autonomy, the propriety of nails in effecting the cutting of even the formless — this is the meaning. 'Is indeed conceivable' — is indeed determined. Conforming to worldly perspective, he says 'Or alternatively' — in this interpretation, the word <s>ārti</s> designates the cause of suffering (<s>ārti-kāraṇa</s>), and one should understand that its unexceptional [capacity for] causing all suffering is also suggested. 'By those that destroy' — the remainder is: 'by the nails.' 'Suffering itself is severed' — the purport is: the killing of such a <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> is the severing of suffering itself, not of any living being — such is the understanding of the Blessed Lord. 'Even in that state' — even in the state of killing. 'Stated' — the meaning is: suggested. [The point is:] 'He cuts suffering itself, not any living being' — such is the cognition [produced]. This is the purport. Here the qualifier 'of those who have taken refuge' etc. is both the ground for the benedictory blessing of protection and the eulogy beginning with '<s>svaccha</s>' etc. — for a deity being praised is pleased and grants the desired [boon]. There, to prevent the confusion of a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound in '<s>svaccha-svacchāya</s>,' he explains: 'by purity' etc. 'By the quality of purity' — its very elaboration is 'by spotlessness.' Abstract noun formations (<s>bhāva-vṛttayaḥ</s>) express qualities such as purity etc. The explanation of '<s>chāyayā</s>' is '<s>vakra</s>' etc. Here the suggested factual meaning (<s>vastu-dhvani</s>) is stated with '<s>artha</s>' etc.
[<s>Locana</s>:] For in the primary sense, abstract noun formations are indeed [primary]; and by its own curved, charming form — '<s>āyāsitaḥ</s>' means 'wearied' — 'the moon is wearied by those [nails].' Here, by suggestion grounded in the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktimūla</s>), the state of being a young moon (<s>bālacandra</s>) is suggested. By the wearying [of the moon], the cognition of the moon's lack of luster (<s>vicchāyatva</s>) in proximity to those [nails] and the cognition of its unloveliness (<s>ahṛdyatva</s>) are suggested. And the capacity to cause weariness is well-known for nails; but for the nails of <s>Narahari</s>, this is demonstrated in a transcendent manner. Moreover, beholding their purity and curvature, the young moon experiences distress in himself — 'though the combination of purity and curved form is equal [between us], these [nails] are skilled at removing the suffering of those who take refuge; but I am not' — thus the figure of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) is also suggested. Furthermore, 'I was formerly the sole object of everyone's desire because of my unparalleled combination of clarity and charming form; now, because of the very possibility of being a young moon — possessing a curved, charming form dear to children (<s>bāla-priyā</s>) that causes weariness — the meaning is: by the power of that meaning-capacity.' 'The state of being a young moon is suggested' — the meaning is: the youth (<s>bālatva</s>) of the moon, the referent of the word <s>indu</s>, is suggested. '<s>Āyāsita</s>' — the meaning of this is 'wearied' (<s>khedita</s>) by secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). He states its result with '<s>āyāsanena</s>' etc. 'In its proximity' — in the proximity of the nails. '<s>Vicchāyatva</s>' means loss of beauty (<s>niśśobhatva</s>). 'Is suggested' — the meaning is: arises through the operation of suggestion (<s>dhvani-vyāpāra</s>). 'Well-known' — the purport is: because [nails] are by nature instruments of striking. 'And that' — and that capacity to cause weariness. 'Transcendent' — the meaning is: by the previously stated form consisting of purity etc. 'Is demonstrated' — and thus the contrast (<s>vyatireka</s>) of <s>Narahari</s>'s nails from ordinary nails — which cause weariness through tearing etc. — is also suggested. This is the purport. With the cooperation of the qualifier 'cutter of the suffering of the refuged,' he shows another <s>vyatireka</s> and another figure with '<s>kiñca</s>' etc. 'Of those' — belonging to the nails. 'Curvature' — the connection here is with 'of those' by inversion. 'In himself' — the meaning is: unknown to others. He describes the manner of experience with 'though equal' etc. 'But I am not' — one should understand the connection of the word '<s>iti</s>' with 'experiences' and with 'the figure of <s>vyatireka</s>.' 'Suggested' — the meaning is: the manifestation of <s>vyatireka</s> for the sensitive reader through the cognition of the stated meaning. The reading is 'the figure of <s>vyatireka</s> is also suggested' — by the word '<s>api</s>' (also), the cumulation with the previously stated <s>vyatireka</s> [is indicated]. 'Of such a kind' — the meaning is: possessing clarity and charming form. 'Skilled at cutting the suffering of heat' — the purport is: for the moon, skill lies only in cutting one's own heat-suffering, not all sufferings. 'By the high regard for the young moon' — the meaning is: by the estimation 'these are not nails but young moons.' 'Weariness' — the meaning is: distress caused by ill-repute. 'As if experiences' — there is also a reading without the word '<s>iva</s>' (as if). '<s>Utprekṣā-pahnuti-dhvani</s>' — the suggestion of <s>utprekṣā-pahnuti</s> (fancy-concealment); since <s>utprekṣā</s> (fancy) and <s>pahnuti</s> (concealment) stand in the relation of principal and subordinate, this amounts to the suggestion of their combination (<s>saṅkara</s>). [<s>Ṭippanī</s>:] Here 'by the power of meaning' — the power, i.e., the capacity consisting in susceptibility to word-substitution, of the denotatum — namely, the nails of <s>Madhuri's</s> enemy [i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s>] — which is the denotatum qualified by the limiter of the mode-limiter; by such a naturally occurring operation of suggestion. 'The state of being a young moon' — the purport is: the capacity of the nails of <s>Viṣṇu</s> to cause weariness — grounded in the loveliness produced by curvature and charm — terminates, by fitness, in the moon itself. 'By the wearying' — here too, by suggestion prompted by the power of meaning pertaining to the word <s>āyāsa</s>, the factual [content] such as the moon's loss of luster is suggested as belonging to the young moon.
[<s>Locana</s>:] Moreover, such nails — ten in number, resembling young moons, skilled at cutting the suffering of heat — the world regards them with the esteem [accorded to] young moons, [thinking] 'not me' — reflecting thus, the young moon ceaselessly experiences weariness, as it were — this is the suggestion of <s>utprekṣā-pahnuti</s> (fancy-concealment). Thus, by the threefold division of factual content (<s>vastu</s>), figure (<s>alaṅkāra</s>), and <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) in this verse has been explained by our teacher in three ways. For in the <s>utprekṣā</s> 'the young moon (<s>bāla-priyā</s>) ceaselessly experiences weariness, as it were,' the previously stated 'the world regards them with the esteem of young moons, not me' — this reflection is the ground; and therein is a clear <s>pahnuti</s> (concealment): 'these are not nails but young moons' — such being the world's cognition. And thus the <s>utprekṣā</s> here, pertaining to nails, concerns the world's cognition of the attribution of young-moon-hood preceded by the negation of nail-hood — and it derives its <s>pahnuti</s> on the basis of the cognition pertaining to the young moon. Hence the relation of principal and subordinate should be understood. He concludes with 'thus' etc. Here the <s>dhvani</s> of <s>vīra-rasa</s> (heroic sentiment) is the principal; because <s>utsāha</s> (heroic energy) is cognized predominantly — this should be noted. [Objection:] But here, since the <s>rati</s> (love) of the author toward the Blessed Lord is what is suggested, <s>bhāva-dhvani</s> (suggestion of emotion) alone should be stated as the principal, and <s>rasa</s> as subordinate to it. To this they say: This statement — expressing the benediction of the author who has realized identity with the Blessed Lord — is not primarily about emotion. The <s>rati</s> toward the deity to be worshipped, which is the suggestion [here], is not properly a <s>bhāva</s> (transitory emotion) [but rather constitutive of <s>rasa</s>], since it differs from the devotee's [ordinary emotion]. And the author's identity with the Blessed Lord is established from the fact that he himself, in his capacity as the <s>sūtra</s>-composer, initiates the auspicious opening. [<s>Ṭippanī</s>:] 'The suggestion of <s>utprekṣā-pahnuti</s> also' — the <s>utprekṣā</s> of the moon's experience of weariness supports itself upon the concealment (<s>apahnavana</s>) whose subject is the cognition characterized by the attribution of young-moon-hood preceded by the negation of nail-hood; hence the relation of principal and subordinate, and hence the combination (<s>saṅkara</s>) of these two. This is the purport. As for someone's [view] that the combination here is of the type 'entry into a single suggestor' because both enter through the single suggestive word '<s>āyāsita</s>' — that is weak: for the combination of the type 'entry into a single suggestor' applies only when there is mutual independence, i.e., separate establishment — and in the present case, as explained, there is indeed mutual dependence between the <s>utprekṣā</s> and <s>pahnuti</s>. Nor should one suspect that if there is no independence, <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (conflation) would apply — for the specific independence qualified by distinctions of word, form, and subject is what is intended in <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>; and in 'entry into a single suggestor,' although the qualified entity (<s>viśeṣya</s>) is present, the absence of the qualifier [of the required type] prevents the over-extension of the definition of <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>. This is the intention. 'Thus, factual content, figure, and <s>rasa</s>' — although everything is indeed factual content [in the broadest sense], here what is intended by the word '<s>vastu</s>' is factual content distinct from <s>rasa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s>. And the nature of <s>alaṅkāra</s> is: being the limiter of the limiter of the capacity to produce aesthetic delight (<s>camatkṛti</s>) — [delight] delimited by the relation of being-the-domain-of that which is located in either word or meaning and which possesses a distinction counter-positive to the suggested [content] and counter-positive to <s>rasa</s> etc. And <s>rasa</s> is the permanent emotion (<s>sthāyin</s>) qualified by the consciousness whose obscuration has been removed. 'Threefold <s>dhvani</s> here' — although <s>dhvani</s> is manifold in other ways too, the threefoldness of <s>dhvani</s> [is asserted] because the diversity of the properties that are the intentional subject of the master's [teaching] — which generate the division of <s>dhvani</s> grounded in the distinction of the suggested content — [reduces to three]. This is the purport.

children.text: kāvyasyātmā dhvanir iti budhair yaḥ samāmnāta-pūrvas tasyābhāvaṃ jagadur apare bhāktam āhus tam anye /
children.translated_text: That which was formerly declared by the wise as "<s>dhvani</s> (resonance/suggestion) is the soul of <s>kāvya</s> (poetry)" — others have denied its existence, while some call it secondary (figurative);

children.text: kecid vācām sthitam aviṣaye tattvam ūcus tadīyaṃ tena brūmaḥ sahṛdaya-manaḥ-prītaye tat-svarūpam // DhvK_1.1 //
children.translated_text: certain [scholars] have said that its reality lies beyond the domain of words — therefore, we shall describe its true nature for the delight of the hearts of the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (connoisseurs). [DhvK 1.1]

children.text: kāvyasyātmā dhvaniriti budhairyaḥ samāmnātapūrvastasyābhāvaṃ jagadurapare bhāktamāhustamanye /
children.translated_text: That which was formerly declared by the wise as "<s>dhvani</s> (resonance/suggestion) is the soul of <s>kāvya</s> (poetry)" — others have denied its existence, while some call it secondary (figurative);

children.text: ke cidvācāṃ sthitamaviṣaye tattvamūcustadīyaṃ tena brūmaḥ sahṛdayamanaḥprītaye tatsvarūpam // 1 //
children.translated_text: certain [scholars] have said that its reality lies beyond the domain of words — therefore, we shall describe its true nature for the delight of the hearts of the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (connoisseurs). [1]

children.translated_text: But no such real entity exists from which this supposition [could arise]; rather, these are merely conceptual alternatives (<s>vikalpas</s>).

children.text: te ca tattvāvabodhavandhtatayā sphureyurapi, ata eva 'ācakṣīran' ityādayo 'tra sambhāvanāviṣayā liṅprayogā atītaparamārthe paryavasyanti /
children.translated_text: And these [alternatives] may appear as if obstructing the knowledge of the true reality; for that very reason, the optative verb-forms such as 'ācakṣīran' ('they might declare') used here in the domain of supposition resolve into the meaning of a past state of affairs.
As for instance — "If that which is inside this body were to become external,
then people, taking up sticks, would ward off dogs and crows."

<s>Locana</s> (commentary): Then, stating primarily the essential nature of the subject matter (<s>abhidheya-svarūpa</s>) and secondarily revealing through implication the purpose-of-the-purpose (<s>prayojana-prayojana</s>) and the purpose connected with it — he utters the opening statement: "<s>Kāvyasyātmā</s>" ("the soul of poetry").

Due to the proximity of the compound "<s>kāvyātma</s>" (soul-of-poetry), the word "<s>budha</s>" (wise) here is intended as meaning "one whose understanding has as its occasion the knowledge of the soul of poetry" — this intention is explained [by the <s>vṛttikāra</s>] as "by those who know the essence of poetry" (<s>kāvyatattvavidbhiḥ</s>).

[<s>Bālapriyā</s> sub-commentary:] "<s>Atha</s>" is for the purpose of commencing. "The essential nature of the subject matter" (<s>abhidheya-svarūpam</s>) means the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion). "Purpose" (<s>prayojana</s>): the purpose of the purpose — [that is,] the purpose of the knowledge of the subject matter, which has the form of <s>dhvani</s>, is delight (<s>prīti</s>); "stating" (<s>abhidadhat</s>) connects here [to both].

The character of being a sentence-meaning (<s>vākyārthatva</s>) pertains to the statement of the essential nature of the subject matter, [namely] "we shall describe its essential nature"; the character of being a word-meaning (<s>padārthatva</s>) pertains to the purpose-of-the-purpose, [namely] "for delight" — hence the primacy and non-primacy of the two statements.

"Connected with it" (<s>tatsambaddham</s>): connected with that purpose-of-the-purpose. "Purpose" has the form of knowledge of the subject matter. "Through implication" (<s>sāmarthyāt</s>): through the suggestive capacity of meaning, so to say. "Revealing" (<s>prakaṭayan</s>): making known. For the purpose of stating the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> is the knowledge of the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> among connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdayas</s>). For the purpose of that [knowledge] is the delight of the mind. Thus, since through the cause-effect relationship between the two, the delight that has the form of purpose-of-the-purpose is stated, the manifestation of the knowledge of the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> — which is the cause of that [delight] — is accomplished. This is the purport.

Now, since the word "<s>budha</s>" generally denotes any knower, [the question arises:] why was it glossed in the <s>vṛtti</s> (commentary) as "those who know the essence of poetry"? To introduce that [explanation], he says: "<s>Kāvya</s>" etc. "That whose occasion (<s>nimitta</s>), i.e., the occasion of usage, is the knowledge of the soul of poetry" — or alternatively, "<s>nimitta</s>" means the occasion of activity (<s>pravṛtti-nimitta</s>), and that is the property appearing as a qualifier in the cognition generated by that word.

[<s>Ṭippanī</s>:] "Primarily" (<s>prādhānyena</s>): principally, because it is what is intended to be established. "Subject matter" (<s>abhidheya</s>): [the subject is] of the domain of <s>dhvani</s>-essence, since it was pledged [in the words] "we shall describe."

"Purpose-of-the-purpose" (<s>prayojana-prayojana</s>): the purpose of stating the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> is the knowledge of the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s>; and the purpose of that is the delight of the connoisseur's mind — thus the delight of that kind becomes the purpose of the statement.

The inclusion of the word "<s>manas</s>" (mind) in the delimiting condition of the purpose-of-the-purpose is to reveal that in the procedural aspect, this [approach] follows predominantly the <s>Vyākaraṇa</s> (grammar) system in the manner of <s>Bharata</s>'s doctrine and the <s>dhvani</s> system — for in this doctrine, what is accepted is that the special qualities of <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) etc. are agreeable to the mind, not to the self.

"The word '<s>budha</s>' here": when general words require a specific meaning, recourse must be had to secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>); otherwise, the very possibility of being a verbal domain would not obtain.

"By the wise" (<s>budhaiḥ</s>): by those who know the essence of poetry. "The soul of poetry is <s>dhvani</s>" — that which is designated (<s>saṃjñitaḥ</s>) thus, transmitted through tradition (<s>paramparā</s>): "thoroughly" (<s>samyak</s>), meaning "completely" (<s>āsamantāt</s>), "made known" (<s>mnātaḥ</s>), i.e., "revealed" (<s>prakaṭitaḥ</s>). "Of that" — though it shines forth in the minds of connoisseurs, others [still] consider it non-existent.

<s>Locana</s>: With the word "<s>ātma</s>" (soul), [<s>Ānandavardhana</s>] explains the meaning through the word "<s>tattva</s>" (essence/reality) — showing its quality of being the essence (<s>sāratva</s>) and its capacity to distinguish [<s>kāvya</s>] from other [types of discourse].

The word "<s>iti</s>" indicates that the word "<s>dhvani</s>" here refers to the designation itself (<s>svarūpa-paratva</s>), since — because the meaning of that [word] has become a matter of dispute — there is an absence of certainty, making it impossible for it to bear the meaning [directly].

He explains this [further]: "designated" (<s>saṃjñitaḥ</s>). But in reality, it is not stated merely as a designation; rather, there indeed exists something denoted by the word "<s>dhvani</s>" — moreover, it constitutes the essence of the whole [of poetry].

For otherwise, the many wise men would not have transmitted it thus — with this intention, [<s>Abhinavagupta</s>] explains [the <s>vṛtti</s>]: "of that, in the minds of connoisseurs" etc.

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Why was it not simply said "by those who know the soul of poetry"? To that he says: "<s>Ātma</s>" etc. With the word "<s>tattva</s>" (reality/essence), which denotes un-sublated essential nature — "<s>apara</s>" (other): from other words, i.e., from what is conveyed by ordinary and Vedic words — its distinctiveness (<s>vailakṣaṇya</s>), by virtue of being praiseworthy to connoisseurs etc. — that is what it shows, i.e., suggests.

"<s>Ātma</s> as if soul" — the word "<s>ātma</s>" here is figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>); thereby, through the similarity of the <s>dhvani</s>-essence to the real soul by virtue of having un-sublated essential nature, [the word] secondarily designates it — and to indicate this, its meaning is explained by the word "<s>tattva</s>"; thereby, its quality of being the essence etc. is the suggested [meaning].

"The word <s>iti</s>": the <s>iti</s> in "<s>dhvaniḥ iti</s>" — that is the meaning. "Indicates" (<s>ācaṣṭe</s>): makes one apprehend. Since all words can refer either to the word-form itself or to the conventionally established meaning — in the use of <s>iti</s>, the reference is to the word-form; here, since <s>iti</s> is placed after the word "<s>dhvani</s>," the word "<s>dhvani</s>" serves to convey the designation-form of the word "<s>dhvani</s>" — that is the meaning.

The manifestation of the designated thing through the mode of designation occurs by suggestion etc., as in the <s>jāti-śakti</s> (universal-power) doctrine where the particular becomes manifest. Alternatively, the word "<s>dhvani</s>" through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) means "that which is designated as <s>dhvani</s>."

He states the reason for the stated meaning: "of that meaning" etc. "Of that meaning" — of what is denoted by the word "<s>dhvani</s>," qualified by the property of being suggested (<s>dhvanyamānatva</s>) — because it has become a matter of dispute, i.e., because it is the object of conflicting views as to whether <s>dhvani</s> exists or not.

"Due to the absence of certainty": in the reading "absence of certainty," the seventh case indicates cause. The meaning is: due to the absence of certainty among neutral parties regarding the entity qualified by the property of being suggested. Or alternatively, "of that meaning" connects with "due to the absence of certainty" — meaning: due to the impossibility of meaningful-ness (<s>arthavattvāsambhava</s>) of a form qualified by the property of being suggested. The word "of the word <s>dhvani</s>" carries over here. "This" means: the reference-to-word-form of the word "<s>dhvani</s>."

Now, [one might object:] if the word "<s>dhvani</s>" is thus explained as meaning "designated as <s>dhvani</s>," this contradicts the immediately following text "though it shines forth in the minds of connoisseurs" — since that statement affirms that the meaning qualified by the property of being suggested is the object of connoisseur-cognition. To resolve this doubt, he states the purport of that passage: "But in reality" etc.

"That" (<s>tat</s>) means: the word "<s>dhvani</s>." Or: the entity that is <s>dhvani</s>. "Merely as a designation": the word "merely" (<s>mātra</s>) excludes the ground-of-activity that has the form of the property of being suggested. "Denoted by the word <s>dhvani</s>": qualified by the property of being suggested. "Indeed exists" — he states the reason for this: "For otherwise" etc.

"He explains" means: he glosses the word "<s>tasya</s>" (of that) occurring in the <s>kārikā</s>. "With '<s>sahṛdaya</s>' etc." means: with the phrase "though it shines forth in the minds of connoisseurs" etc.

<s>Locana</s>: But this interpretation is more appropriate — the word "<s>iti</s>" is displaced in order and serves to recall the sentence-meaning: the meaning that is characterized by <s>dhvani</s> is what has been transmitted as "the soul of poetry" (<s>kāvyasya ātmā</s>). For if [the word "<s>dhvani</s>"] were to refer to a word-meaning, what coherence would there be in [saying] "the meaning designated as <s>dhvani</s>"? For then it would amount to saying "the word <s>dhvani</s> is the soul of poetry," like [saying] "this word '<s>go</s>' says [something]."

And the locus of disagreement is not something unreal; rather, the disagreement is based solely on the property while the property-bearer itself is real. Enough with this excessive [discussion] that is irrelevant and would vex the hearts of connoisseurs.

The [erroneous] statement of a single wise man might be due to inadvertence, but such [a designation] by many is not appropriate [to call inadvertent]. Therefore, the plural "by the wise" (<s>budhaiḥ</s>). He glosses that very [plural]: "through tradition" (<s>paramparayā</s>). By an unbroken stream, they stated this even without its being established in special texts — this is the purport.

And the many wise are not [to be met] with disregard. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] That which has been stated in the mode of designation as the entity characterized by <s>dhvani</s> being the soul of poetry — that [is described] precisely in accordance with the understanding of those whose minds are impaired by faithlessness. Since the meaning qualified by the property of being suggested is established through the cognition of connoisseurs, and in accordance with their understanding is the immediately following text — this is the purport.

Or alternatively: if the word "<s>dhvani</s>" is thus explained as meaning "designated as <s>dhvani</s>," how can there be a response to those who assert non-existence etc., since their dispute concerns the property of being suggested itself, not the designation "<s>dhvani</s>"? Therefore he says: "But in reality" etc.

"He explains" means: he speaks analytically. "With '<s>sahṛdaya</s>' etc.": by the word "etc.," the passage "though it shines forth in the minds of connoisseurs, others have declared its non-existence" etc. is included.

Noting that the <s>vṛttikāra</s>'s explanation through the construction "<s>dhvaniḥ iti</s>" is merely indicative, he says with the intention [of offering a better reading]: "But this [interpretation] is more appropriate" etc. "Or" (<s>vā</s>) completes [the sentence]: "or the explanation to be stated [is preferable]."

"More appropriate" (<s>yuktataram</s>): by the comparative suffix, it is indicated that the previous explanation also has validity. "Displaced in order" (<s>bhinnakrama</s>): since it is heard immediately [after one word], it should be construed elsewhere — meaning the construction is: "transmitted as '<s>kāvyasya ātmā</s>' (the soul of poetry)."

"Recalling the sentence-meaning" (<s>vākyārtha-parāmarśaka</s>): it conveys the character of expressing the sentence-meaning in the tradition — not that it is identical with that sentence. "Sentence" here means a collection of words.

He shows the construction: "<s>dhvani</s>" etc. The explanation of "<s>dhvaniḥ</s>" is: "the meaning characterized by <s>dhvani</s>" — meaning: qualified by the property of being suggested. And thus, it is precisely this meaning that is referred to by the word "<s>tasya</s>" (of that).

In the alternative interpretation where the word "<s>dhvani</s>" serves merely as a bare designation, he states the defect: "word" etc. "If the word '<s>dhvani</s>' were to refer merely to the designation": in that case, "what coherence" means: it would be incoherent. He states the reason: "For thus" etc.

He resolves the doubt about the incoherence of meaning-reference in the word "<s>dhvani</s>" as previously stated: "And not" etc. "The locus of disagreement": the property-bearer that is the subject of conflicting views. "Based solely on the property" etc.: just as, when the property-bearer such as sound (<s>śabda</s>) is real, the disagreement is based on properties such as permanence or impermanence — so here too, when the property-bearer designated as <s>dhvani</s> is real, the disagreement is based on properties such as being subsumed under <s>guṇa</s> (quality) or <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure), being figurative, etc. — this is the purport.

He glosses the meaning of the plural "by the wise": "of a [single] wise man" etc. "Such a statement": the statement that it is the soul of poetry. That [single person's statement] might be due to inadvertence. "Therefore" (<s>tena</s>): to indicate that such a statement is authoritative and worth accepting.

"That very" (<s>tadeva</s>): the plural itself, which has the stated purpose. The explanation of "through tradition" is "by an unbroken [stream]" etc. "This" (<s>etat</s>): the status of <s>dhvani</s> as the soul of poetry. "Special": [meaning] in special texts, "established" means "preserved through writing" — even without that, it was stated — this is the connection. The purport is: this matter is established through direct instruction.

"They declared" (<s>jaguḥ</s>): [those who assert non-existence etc.] would teach with [actual] regard for the entity. This was taught with such regard. Therefore he says: "thoroughly transmitted" (<s>samyag āmnātapūrva</s>). By the word "<s>pūrva</s>" (formerly), it is said that the novelty of this [teaching] is not to be suspected here — and he glosses: "thoroughly" (<s>samyak</s>), meaning "completely" (<s>āsamantāt</s>), "made known" (<s>mnātaḥ</s>), i.e., "revealed" (<s>prakaṭitaḥ</s>).

"Of that" (<s>tasya</s>): of that [<s>dhvani</s>] for whose apprehension one should rather strive — what suspicion of non-existence can there be? Therefore, what can we do? The foolishness of the non-existence-asserters is boundless — this is the purport.

And the conceptions of the non-existence-asserters have not been heard by us; rather, they will be hypothetically entertained and refuted. Hence the third-person reference [i.e., indirect treatment].

Nor is it proper to refute a future entity, since it has not yet arisen. [Objection:] even that [future entity], mentally projected, is refuted. [Reply:] Precisely because it is mentally projected, its future-ness is lost.

Therefore, from the perspective of past-tense manifestation, indirectness, and the absence of the apprehension of a specific locus — the past tense (<s>liṭ</s>) is employed: "<s>jaguḥ</s>" (they declared). He will reveal the refutation precisely for the purpose of explaining that [past assertion], having hypothetically entertained it.

And even this hypothetical entertainment is appropriate not for something impossible, but rather for something [already] possible — otherwise there would be no end to hypothetical entertainments. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] this is the purport.

"Through tradition" (<s>paramparayā</s>): this is the <s>vṛttikāra</s>'s intended meaning. To show the meaning of the prefix "<s>sam</s>" in "<s>samāmnātapūrva</s>" (thoroughly transmitted), he says: "And not" etc. He states the significance of the word "<s>pūrva</s>" (formerly): "<s>pūrva</s>" etc. Here: in this account. "He says" means: he suggests. "And he glosses": he glosses the stated meaning — meaning that through "<s>samyak</s>" etc., even the meaning of the word "<s>pūrva</s>" is explained.

The explanation of what is gained by stating that it was transmitted by the wise is: "though it shines forth in the minds of connoisseurs." He shows the implied meaning with "of that" etc.

He shows the derivation of the use of the past tense (<s>liṭ</s>) in "<s>jaguḥ</s>" (they declared) — and that it is in the nature of an explanation of the <s>vṛtti</s> passage "some would declare" etc. — with "And not" etc.

"By us": by the proponents of <s>dhvani</s>. "Contrary conceptions" (<s>vikalpāḥ</s>): conceptualizations of imagined meanings. If they have not been heard, then how will they be refuted? He says: "having hypothetically entertained" etc. The hypothetical entertainment is [found in passages beginning with] "some would declare" etc. And the refutation should be understood [in passages where] having cited [the opposing view] with "what has been said" etc., [the author refutes with] "that too is improper" etc.

"Therefore" (<s>ataḥ</s>): because [the views] have not been heard. He argues for the past-tense character: "And not" etc. "Precisely because of non-origination": the word "precisely" (<s>eva</s>) is repetitive, meaning: precisely because of the futurity stated earlier.

He raises a doubt: "even that" etc. "That": that future entity. "Mentally projected" (<s>buddhyāropitam</s>): made the object of cognition. He resolves: "Because of mental" etc. "Projection" (<s>āropaṇa</s>) is the instrument.

He concludes: "Therefore" etc. The use of the past tense (<s>liṭ</s>) is grounded in the impossibility of actual past-ness, manifested appearance, indirectness, and the absence of the apprehension of a specific temporal locus — this is the purport.

"Special" (<s>viśiṣṭa</s>): of the form of a particular time-specification. Having thus justified the use of the past tense, he shows the constructions of the optative (<s>liṅ</s>) in "some would declare" etc. as relevant to the present [context]: "For the explanation of that very" etc. "For the explanation of the <s>liṭ</s> (past tense) alone" — the word "alone" (<s>eva</s>) means: not independently. "For the explanation" connects with "having hypothetically entertained."

Lest one object that the explanation of "<s>jaguḥ</s>" is possible through "some would declare" etc. alone — what need for the intervening passage "others have declared its non-existence" etc.? — to forestall that, he introduces: "And even this hypothetical entertainment" etc. This is taken up for the purpose of justifying the past tense. "Of something impossible": of something not cognized in any way whatsoever. "There would be no end" (<s>aparyavasānam</s>): due to the absence of a resting-place — conceptions arise. [<s>Locana</s>:] And there would be [no end] of refutations too. Therefore, to justify the hypothetical entertainment that is about to be stated, he first says that they arise [i.e., are possible]. "Would be hypothetically entertained" — but what is being said would be merely a repetition of meaning. And the hypothetical entertainment is not of something [merely] possible but rather of something actually present — hence the statement in the present tense.

Lest one suspect that what is hypothetically entertained on the basis of an impossible entity cannot be refuted, he says: "conceptions" (<s>vikalpāḥ</s>).
