children.translated_text: Therefore, since it has been thus explained by the <s>vṛttikāra</s> (author of the commentary-prose) as being rooted in that [dhvani], even when the removal of misunderstanding is possible as the primary purpose, [the words] 'we shall describe its true nature' and 'for the delight of the hearts of the connoisseurs we shall describe its true nature' — by virtue of being the object of commentary, there would be a division of sentences — this too is the purport.
Or alternatively — in the phrase 'what is to be commented upon,' the division is: 'this commentary [is as follows].'
This commentary is the commentary of the <s>vṛttikāra</s>.
'By virtue of being a single sentence' — the meaning of this is: that which demonstrates the single-sentence unity [of the passage].

Thus. /
'But that [expression] would be an indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) of some variety of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion).' /
Thus also: /
The result of the <s>bālapriyā</s> interpretation in terms of secondary meaning (<s>bhaṅgārtha</s>) is the establishment of the ground (<s>bīja</s>) in the form of obstruction of primary meaning (<s>mukhyārtha-bādhā</s>); of the interpretation in terms of the meaning of 'serving' is the establishment of the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>); and of the interpretation in terms of the meaning of 'exceeding faith' is the establishment of the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>). This is the purport. /
By the word 'three' he shows that the ground-nature belongs to [them] only collectively — '[that which is] the ground of figurative usage (<s>upacāra-bīja</s>).' /
'<s>Upacāra</s>' (figurative usage) means <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) and <s>gauṇī</s> (metaphorical usage). /
Or: the practice through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> and <s>gauṇī</s>. /
Or: the cognition of the indicated (<s>lakṣya</s>) and the metaphorical (<s>gauṇa</s>) meaning. /
Some [say]: '<s>upacāra</s>' means the transfer of one thing to another. /
[Objection:] When what should be said is that <s>dhvani</s> does not exist as anything distinct from <s>guṇavṛtti</s> (secondary function), what is the purpose of stating [this] in co-referential terms (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>)? To this he says: 'of the co-referentiality' — /
The meaning is: of the co-referential statement in the root text '<s>taṃ bhāktam</s>' ('that is figurative') and in the <s>vṛtti</s> (gloss) with '<s>dhvani-saṃjñitam</s>' ('called <s>dhvani</s>') etc. /
In this interpretation, one should understand that the citation-marker beginning with '<s>kāvyātmānam</s>' etc. is not [relevant]. /
The co-referentiality of two words means their capacity to denote a single substrate (<s>ekadharmi</s>). /
'This is the purport' — /
What is to be refuted by the advocates of <s>dhvani</s> is the identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) of <s>dhvani</s> and <s>guṇavṛtti</s>, but not that <s>dhvani</s> is entirely untouched by figurative usage — to illuminate this meaning, this co-referential statement is for the purpose of introducing the thesis of identity which contradicts the established doctrine. This is the meaning of 'this is the purport.' /
He elaborates that very purport with 'although' etc. /
'<s>Upacāra</s>' — the meaning is: <s>guṇavṛtti</s> (secondary function). /
'Of that nature' — of the nature of figurative usage. /
'Even apart from that' — even without figurative usage. /
'Because of the existence' — because <s>dhvani</s> exists. /
'Where?' — to this he says: 'in the division beginning with <s>vivakṣitānyapara-vācya</s> (that in which the intended [meaning] is other than the expressed)' etc. /
'<s>Avivakṣita-vācya</s>' — the meaning is: in the <s>dhvani</s> [variety] called <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> (that in which the expressed meaning is not intended). /
'We shall state' — the purport is: in [examples] such as '<s>rāmo 'smi</s>' ('I am <s>Rāma</s>'). /
'He will state' — the remainder is: the root author (<s>mūlakāra</s>). In the <s>vṛtti</s>, the explanation of the word '<s>bhākta</s>' (figurative) as '<s>guṇavṛtti</s>' — with that word he elaborates in context the intended meanings with 'qualities (<s>guṇa</s>)' etc. /
'By means' — by causes (<s>nimitta</s>). /
Although by the mention of the word <s>dhvani</s>, those who formulate the definition of poetry (<s>kāvya</s>) have not brought to light any mode other than <s>guṇavṛtti</s>, nevertheless [they have shown] the practice in poetry through non-primary function. [<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Guṇas</s>' are properties such as proximity (<s>sāmīpya</s>) etc., and [qualities] such as sharpness (<s>taikṣṇya</s>) etc. /
That whose function (<s>vṛtti</s>) in another meaning is by those means — or: a word whose function is in a [transferred] domain by those means — that is called <s>guṇavṛtti</s>-word or -meaning. /
Or: functioning through the medium of <s>guṇa</s> (secondary relation) is <s>guṇavṛtti</s> — a non-primary operation of denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>). /
What has been said amounts to this: whether <s>dhvani</s> means 'that which suggests,' or 'that which is suggested,' or 'the act of suggesting' — even so, it is nothing beyond the operation of figuratively transferred word-and-meaning. /
For in [conveying] the primary meaning, denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>) alone [operates]; hence, by elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>), suggestion (<s>dhvanana</s>) is in the non-primary [domain] alone — because there is no third category (<s>tṛtīya-rāśi</s>). /
[Objection:] But who has said that <s>dhvani</s> is <s>guṇavṛtti</s>? Anticipating this doubt, he says: 'although' etc. /
'Or another' — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'In another [referent]' — in a bank (<s>tīra</s>) etc., in a young student (<s>māṇavaka</s>) etc. /
'Whose' — of the word such as '<s>Gaṅgā</s>,' '<s>siṃha</s>' (lion), etc. /
'Where' — the meaning is: in the meaning of bank etc. /
'Through the medium of <s>guṇa</s>' — through the medium of proximity, sharpness, etc. /
'Functioning' — this is an elaboration of the meaning of the word <s>vṛtti</s>. /
He states the conclusion: 'non-primary' — /
By 'non-primary,' both <s>lakṣaṇā</s> and <s>gauṇī</s> are grasped. /
'What then?' — to this he says: 'this' etc. /
'Figuratively transferred' — the meaning is: distinct from the word-meaning operations that are the subject-matter of the term <s>guṇavṛtti</s>. /
'Some such thing called <s>dhvani</s>' — some thing called <s>dhvani</s>. /
[Objection:] If, with the intent of denying <s>dhvani</s>'s existence, the non-difference of <s>dhvani</s> from <s>guṇavṛtti</s> is being established, then let the non-difference from <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) also be established! To this he says: 'in the primary meaning' — /
By the particle '<s>eva</s>' (alone), he shows that there is not even a possibility of suggestion (<s>dhvanana</s>) here. /
He states the conclusion: 'therefore' — /
'By elimination' — <s>pariśeṣa</s> is the certainty regarding what remains after [other options are] excluded; that itself is <s>pāriśeṣya</s>; from that — this is the meaning. /
'In the non-primary alone' — in <s>guṇavṛtti</s> alone. /
Here the reason is: 'the third' — /
The first category consists of the denoter, the denoted, and the denotative function (<s>abhidhā</s>); the second consists of the indicator (<s>lakṣaka</s>), the indicated (<s>lakṣya</s>), and the indicative function (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>); the third — which is what you propose — consists of the suggestor (<s>vyañjaka</s>), the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), and the suggestive function (<s>vyañjanā</s>); because of the non-existence of that [third category] — this is the meaning. /
Thus the conclusion is: <s>dhvani</s> is nothing but <s>guṇavṛtti</s>, because it is non-primary. /
'But' etc. — the word '<s>iti</s>' connects with both [clauses]. /
'Thus who has said [this]?' — anticipating the doubt, he says. /
The meaning is: having raised the objection with 'although' etc., the answer is given with 'nevertheless' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, at 'or another' — lest there be the misconception that 'another' than <s>guṇavṛtti</s> means 'primary,' he explains: '<s>guṇa</s>' etc. /
The word '<s>vā</s>' (or) is for the purpose of illustration. /
The meaning is: just as the deniers of [<s>dhvani</s>'s] existence have not said '<s>dhvani</s> is a mode of <s>guṇa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s>,' so too the advocates of the figurative view (<s>bhākta-vādins</s>) have not explicitly said '<s>dhvani</s> is <s>guṇavṛtti</s>.' /
[The author] who shows [that] the path of <s>dhvani</s> was slightly touched but not recognized — it is by constructing [the opponent's position] thus that it was said: 'Others call that figurative.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'A mode of <s>guṇa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s>' — this is the extent [of the meaning]. /
'Shows' — by <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, etc. /
<s>Bhāmaha</s> said: 'Words are denotative of meters and meanings' — to explain the difference of denotation from [mere] word, <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s> declared: 'Of words, denotation — i.e., the denotative operation — is primary, and [there is also] <s>guṇavṛtti</s> (secondary function).' /
<s>Vāmana</s> too [said]: '<s>Lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) based on similarity is <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression).' /
'Slightly touched' — by them, the <s>dhvani</s>-path was [merely] opened up; the reason for its being merely a slight touch is: as if by readers who read as written [without deeper understanding]. /
The singular number here is intended in a general sense. /
With the intention that the formulators of the definition of poetry are indeed the ones intended, he fills in: '<s>Bhaṭṭa</s>' etc. /
He shows their statements in order: '<s>Bhāmaha</s>' etc. — 'Narratives based on <s>itihāsa</s>, worldly reasoning, and the arts — these should be considered the sources of poetry.' The remaining three quarters [of the verse] are thus stated. /
'What follows from that?' — to this he says: 'of denotation' etc. /
'Here' is the remainder. /
'<s>Vāmana</s> too' — the connection is with 'declared.' /
'Based on similarity' — <s>vakrokti</s> is the figure (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) of that name. /
Thus the upshot is: by the word '<s>abhidhāna</s>' (denotation), <s>Bhāmaha</s>; by the expression '<s>guṇavṛtti</s>,' <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s>; and by the expression '<s>lakṣaṇā</s>' (indication), <s>Vāmana</s> — [all three] have shown the practice of <s>guṇavṛtti</s> in poetry. /
He explains the portion 'the path of <s>dhvani</s>, though slightly touched, was not recognized' in a manner consistent with introducing the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>): 'by them, to begin with' etc. /
The word '<s>tāvat</s>' expresses concession. /
The elaboration of 'the path of <s>dhvani</s> was slightly touched' is: '<s>dhvani</s> was [merely] opened up [through <s>guṇavṛtti</s>].' /
Because <s>guṇavṛtti</s> necessarily entails a purpose, and because that purpose has the character of being within the sole domain of the suggestive operation (<s>vyañjanā-vyāpāra</s>) — as will be explained — by those very <s>Bhāmaha</s>, <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s>, etc. who demonstrated the practice of <s>guṇavṛtti</s>, the indicator (<s>gamaka</s>) of <s>dhvani</s> was indeed displayed. This is the meaning. /
Because, although they touched the path of <s>dhvani</s>, they did not separately determine its own nature by formulating a definition — [therefore] <s>guṇavṛtti</s> alone is <s>dhvani</s>, not something distinct from it — appropriating their statement, which [merely] establishes this by implication, this school of the figurative view (<s>bhākta-vāda</s>) has proceeded. He says: 'as if by those who have read as written' etc. /
The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) means 'however.' The explanation of 'not recognized' is: the discrimination of its own nature was not made. /
Some, however — those of modest intellect in the matter of formulating definitions — have declared the reality of <s>dhvani</s> to be beyond the reach of words, knowable only by the hearts of the sensitive (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'By those whose own-nature discrimination could not be made' — the discrimination of its own nature was not made; on the contrary, [<s>dhvani</s>] is criticized, like [cracking] an unbroken coconut — merely by seizing upon those texts as heard without [proper] examination. /
Hence he says: 'having constructed [the position] thus, it was said.' /
If this is not construed thus, then the statement 'the path of <s>dhvani</s> was touched' would contradict the statement of the prior position. /
'Of modest intellect' — the meaning is: of unassertive understanding. /
And these three [groups] are successively of better understanding. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Here the reason is: 'by those unable to make the own-nature discrimination.' /
'By them' is carried forward. /
The reason for the inability is: 'as written' etc. /
The meaning is: by those who have read — i.e., retained — the exemplary texts (<s>lakṣya-bhūta</s>), i.e., the <s>dhvani</s>-bearing poetic texts, merely as written, without transgressing the letter — [and] merely by that alone. /
Or: in the simile 'as if,' 'written' means: by those who are like those who [merely] read what is written — i.e., by those who do not discriminate. This is the extent [of the meaning]. /
'Not only was the own-nature discrimination of <s>dhvani</s> not made, but the very nature worthy of discrimination was also denied' — he says: 'on the contrary' etc. /
'Is criticized' — is rejected. /
'By them' is carried forward. /
'<s>Dhvani</s>' is the remainder. /
This criticism is inferrable in the case of <s>Bhāmaha</s> etc., but directly evident in the case of the commentators on <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s>'s text etc. /
'Like an unbroken coconut' — the <s>vati</s> suffix is from the ablative-ending [stem]. /
'Seizing upon' — the connection is with this [word]. /
He shows the reason for the criticism: 'as heard' etc. /
The meaning is: merely by the seizing upon — i.e., retention — of those texts, the exemplary <s>dhvani</s>-bearing poetic texts, as heard without examination (<s>vicāra</s>). /
There is also the reading '<s>abhagna-nārikela-kalpa-yathā-śruta</s>.' /
'Hence' — the meaning is: precisely because of the stated purport. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, '<s>iti</s>' is in the sense of cause. /
The meaning of '<s>iti parikalpya</s>' etc. is: because <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s> etc. merely touched the path of <s>dhvani</s> but did not discriminate its nature, and on the contrary criticized it, therefore — constructing up to the point of their stated view that '<s>dhvani</s> is nothing but the figurative, not something distinct from it' — it was said 'Others call that figurative.' /
[Objection:] But for what purpose was the passage beginning 'the path of <s>dhvani</s>' explained in this way? Why not explain it as: 'the path of <s>dhvani</s>' — the path means that which is sought, investigated, examined; the variety characterized as <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> — 'was touched,' i.e., was known? To this he says: 'if so' etc. /
'Would be contradicted' — the meaning is: if a sub-variety of <s>dhvani</s> were known [to them], the statement '<s>dhvani</s> is nothing but <s>guṇavṛtti</s>, not something distinct from it' would be inconsistent. /
Alternatively: [Objection:] But why not explain the passage '<s>na lakṣita</s>' ('was not recognized') simply in its literal sense as 'was not seen'? To this he says: 'if so' etc. /
'The passage <s>na lakṣita</s>' is the remainder. /
'Would be contradicted' — the meaning is: the statement of [<s>dhvani</s>'s] being touched and its not being seen would be contradictory. /
He says that the order in which these types of disagreement are stated is intentional: 'these' etc. /
The three deniers of [<s>dhvani</s>'s] existence are united as 'three.' /
'Of good understanding' — of sound understanding. /
He discriminatingly shows the quality of good understanding: 'the earlier ones' etc. /
The earlier ones — the deniers of existence. /
'In every way' — by all three modes. /
'We state its nature.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] For the earlier ones are completely inverted in every way. But the middle ones, though knowing its nature, deny it through doubt. And the last ones, though not denying it, do not know how to formulate its definition. Thus, in order, the predominance of inversion, doubt, and ignorance [respectively characterizes] these [groups]. /
'Therefore' — even a single one of these disagreements, which has the form of a propositional meaning, acquires the status of a reason for the determination [of <s>dhvani</s>'s nature] — hence the singular number. /
'In such disagreements' — the seventh [case-ending] is in the sense of selection (<s>nirdhāraṇa</s>). /
Among these, even a single type of disagreement — by that very reason alone — 'we state its nature,' i.e., the nature of <s>dhvani</s> is to be explained. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The denotation-and-denotatum relation is the connection. /
'Completely inverted' — possessing inverted cognition, like the <s>Cārvākas</s> who hold the body-is-self doctrine. /
The middle ones — the advocates of the figurative view (<s>bhākta-vādins</s>). /
The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) indicates a distinction from the former; he states it: 'though knowing its nature' etc. /
The meaning is: though knowing its nature, however confusedly, that there is something beyond the expressed — [still they deny it]. /
'Through doubt' — through the doubt of whether or not there exists an operation distinct from the primary and secondary functions — they deny [it]. /
There is also the reading '<s>nihnuvate</s>.' /
'Though not denying' — the connection is with 'its nature.' /
There is also the reading '<s>anihnuvānāḥ</s>.' /
'To formulate the definition' — the remainder is: 'of <s>dhvani</s>.' /
He states the conclusion: 'therefore' — /
The obstruction-nature of inversion with respect to the inquiry into <s>dhvani</s>'s nature; but doubt's nature of being [merely] unfavorable — of these two [possessors], the latter is superior to the former. /
But the last one's [deficiency] is merely ignorance regarding the formulation of the definition — and since that is easily removable, it is superior to both. This is the purport. /
'Even a single one' — the meaning of the word '<s>api</s>' (even) is: how much more [so] three! /
'Hence the singular number' — in the word '<s>tena</s>' ('therefore'), the pronoun refers back to the meanings of the three preceding sentences. /
By the instrumental case, the reason-nature of those [disagreements] for stating <s>dhvani</s>'s nature is expressed. /
By the singular number, one should understand that each individually constitutes a reason. This is the purport. /
He elaborates the <s>vṛtti</s> in accordance with the stated meaning: 'thus' etc. /
'The seventh [case] in the sense of selection' — not the seventh in the sense of condition (<s>bhāvalakṣaṇa</s>). This is the purport. /
Making the selection manifest, he says: 'among these' etc. /
The explanation of '<s>tena</s>' in the <s>vṛtti</s> is 'thus' etc. up to 'being situated.' /
Therein, what should be supplied is 'even by a single one' — with this intention he says: 'even a single one' etc. /
'They declared its non-existence,' 'therefore we state its nature,' '[others] call it figurative' — the nature of that <s>dhvani</s> — being the inner soul of all good poetry, exceedingly beautiful, [yet] never before opened up even by the most subtle intellects of the ancient formulators of poetic definitions. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The connection (<s>sambandha</s>) of the <s>dhvani</s>-treatise is the relation of educator and educated (<s>vyutpādya-vyutpādaka</s>) between speaker and listener. The purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) is the knowledge of <s>dhvani</s>'s nature together with the removal of disagreement. The relation of purpose and treatise is that of end and means. Thus it has been stated. /
Now, to explain the portion '<s>sahṛdaya-manaḥ-prītaye</s>' ('for the delight of the sensitive mind') — which conveys the purpose of the listener's purpose — he says: 'of that indeed' — /
The meaning is: of that which has fallen into the domain of the word '<s>vimati</s>' (disagreement). /
The nature of <s>dhvani</s> — for those who would define it — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Therefore we state,' 'some have said,' 'therefore we state' — separate constructions are obtained [for each]. This is the purport. /
In the manner stated in the introduction, with 'therefore we state its nature' he has indicated the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>) etc. — which constitute the factors for the listener's engagement — and he shows this incidentally: 'the nature of <s>dhvani</s>' etc. /
'The denotation-and-denotatum relation' — the meaning is: the relation in the form of the denoter-denoted relationship. /
Here the statement is in inverted order. /
One should understand similarly for what follows above. /
The extent is: the relation of educator and educated (<s>pratipādya-pratipādaka</s>). /
'Connection' — with this there is syntactic connection. /
'Of educator and educated' — the meaning is: the relation of educator and educated. /
'Through the removal of disagreement' — the meaning is: accompanied by the removal of disagreement regarding the nature of <s>dhvani</s>. /
The purpose-nature of the removal of disagreement for the statement of <s>dhvani</s>'s nature is obtained through the expression 'therefore we state.' This is the purport. /
'Purpose' — the meaning is: the purpose of stating its nature. /
'Of end' — the meaning is: the relation of means and end. /
'Thus it has been stated' — the meaning is: thus the stated meanings have been displayed through 'therefore we state its nature.' /
'Now' etc. /
'Of the listener' — the purpose pertaining to the listener is the previously stated knowledge of <s>dhvani</s>'s nature together with the removal of disagreement; its purpose in turn — in the form of delight (<s>prīti</s>) — that which conveys it. This is the meaning. /
Because the portion beginning with '<s>lakṣayatām</s>' itself constitutes the explanation of the portion '<s>sahṛdaya</s>' etc., and the remainder is its supplement — he says 'to explain,' not 'he explains.' /
He states the contextually established meaning of the word '<s>tat</s>': '<s>vimati</s>' (disagreement). /
Showing the distant syntactic connection, he explains: 'of <s>dhvani</s>' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, '<s>ānanda</s>' is the statement of the meaning of the word '<s>prīti</s>' (delight). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Ānanda</s>' (bliss) in the mind — whose nature is <s>nirvṛti</s> (contentment), a synonym for <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder) — may attain stability (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), i.e., permanence, [a stability] that cannot be uprooted by others who are afflicted by inversion etc. — to accomplish this purpose, its nature is illuminated. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Hence what is intended here, he states: 'whose nature is <s>nirvṛti</s>' etc. /
[Objection:] But the occasion for saying 'may it attain stability' arises only if instability has been brought about by some other cause! To this he says: 'by others' etc. /
'By others' — by the deniers of existence (<s>abhāva-vādins</s>) etc. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' in 'inversion etc.,' doubt and ignorance of definition-formulation are also included. /
'By virtue of not being uprooted' — by virtue of not being destroyed. /
The meaning is: in such a way that it is not destroyed by others. /
The elaboration of the word '<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>' (stability) is: '<s>sthemāna</s>' — enduring with firmness. This is the meaning. /
The meaning conveyed by the word '<s>iti</s>' in the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'may it attain' — he brings forward: 'to accomplish the purpose' etc. /
In the <s>kārikā</s>, at '<s>prītaye</s>' — the fourth case is by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>kriyārthe</s>' etc., in the sense of 'in order to accomplish delight.' This is the purport. /
Showing the connection of '<s>dhvaneḥ svarūpam</s>' ('the nature of <s>dhvani</s>') — as the object [of '<s>lakṣayatām</s>'] and in the nominative in '<s>prakāśyate</s>' — he says: 'its nature' etc. /
'Connection' — the meaning is: relation (<s>sambandha</s>). /
Here, although the purpose-nature of the removal of disagreement for stating <s>dhvani</s>'s nature is obtained through 'therefore we state its nature,' nevertheless, that [removal of disagreement] is not the primary purpose, but rather delight (<s>prīti</s>) alone [is]. /
But that [removal of disagreement] is an auxiliary (<s>aṅga</s>) of delight — this is the purport of the fourth quarter [of the verse] beginning with '<s>tena</s>.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The connection: /
And purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) indeed has that character precisely because [there is] a non-separation of the one who employs from the entity that accomplishes it — with this intention, it should be explained as a single sentence: 'for the sake of delight we state its nature.' /
In explaining the word '<s>tat-svarūpa</s>' (its nature), he briefly indicates the extraction of the five previously stated alternatives: with '<s>sakala</s>' (all) etc. /
By the words '<s>sakala</s>' and '<s>satkavi</s>' (good poet), he negates [the view] 'in some particular aspect.' /
'Exceedingly beautiful' — he states the distinction from the figurative [view]. For there is no beauty whatsoever in [examples like] '<s>siṃho baṭuḥ</s>' ('the lad is a lion') or '<s>gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>' ('the village is on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>'). /
By the word '<s>upaniṣad-bhūta</s>' (being the inner secret), the [position of] merely giving a new name etc. is negated. /
With '<s>aṇīyasībhiḥ</s>' (by the most subtle) etc., he indicates that it is not subsumed under <s>guṇa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
With 'and moreover' etc., he displays the meaning 'falling within their system' — preceded by the etymological analysis of the word <s>prayojana</s> (purpose): 'and the purpose' etc. /
'<s>Tat</s>' — of that purpose, the entity that accomplishes it; its cognition, that is. /
The impelling nature (<s>prayoktṛtā</s>), i.e., the causative capacity — that being the life-breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) of which, by that very state — i.e., by possessing the nature of being a motivator. /
'Thus a purpose.' /
'Becomes' — there is also the reading '<s>bhāti</s>' (shines). /
'<s>Nāma</s>' — in the sense of [being] well-known. /
By this, the etymology of the word <s>prayojana</s> is shown: 'it impels (<s>prayuṅkte</s>), it motivates' — hence <s>prayojana</s>. /
'With this intention' — /
Here, the removal of disagreement does not have the capacity of being the purpose of stating <s>dhvani</s>'s nature — because, like the knowledge [of <s>dhvani</s>'s nature] that possesses it, it is itself not a [final] human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). /
Rather, delight (<s>prīti</s>) alone [is the purpose] — that alone is its primary purpose. /
The removal of disagreement is merely an auxiliary of that — with this intention. This is the meaning. /
'As a single sentence' — the meaning is: as conveying a single qualified meaning of this kind. /
'Should be explained' — the meaning is: should be explained.

saṃkṣepeṇeti /

children.translated_text: In the <s>vṛtti</s> (commentary-prose), [it says] '<s>aṇīyasībhir api</s>' (even by the most subtle).
The meaning is: 'even by the most refined and exceedingly sharp [intellects].'
The purport is: how can that which has not been previously illuminated even by such [subtle] intellects be subsumed under <s>guṇas</s> etc., which are cognizable by gross intellects?

children.text: atha ca rāmāyaṇamahābhārataprabhṛtini lakṣye sarvatra prasiddhavyavahāraṃ lakṣayatāṃ sahṛdayānāmānando manasi labhatāṃ pratiṣṭhāmiti prakāśyate // DhvA_1.1 //
children.translated_text: And moreover, let the well-known practice, [present] everywhere in the exemplary works (<s>lakṣya</s>) such as the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and others, be observed by the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (connoisseurs) who discern [it], and let delight (<s>ānanda</s>) find its abode in [their] minds — this is what is proclaimed. [DhvA 1.1]

He shows the purpose of the qualifier specifying the nature of <s>dhvani</s>, beginning with '<s>sakala</s>' (entire) etc. — by means of '<s>tatsvarūpaśabdam</s>' (the word 'its true nature') and so forth. 'In brief' — he will elaborate at length later. In brief and at length, [he presents] the refutation — thus 'he refutes.' Since by the word '<s>sakala</s>' (entire), pervasion over all domains is stated, and by the word '<s>satkavi</s>' (true poet), primacy — because [dhvani] is established by valid means of knowledge — is stated, therefore the status of being merely a minor variety, caused either by non-pervasion over the entire domain of poetry or by lack of primacy, has been refuted — this is the meaning. '<s>Vyatireka</s>' means 'distinctiveness.' '<s>Nahi</s>' — the meaning is: even though the suggested content (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) such as surpassing valor etc. exists in those two sentences, they are not supremely delightful because they lack the nature of poetry adorned by <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s> of word and meaning. '<s>Upaniṣadbhūta</s>' — the meaning is: 'of the nature of a supreme secret,' because it is difficult to know for those unacquainted with the truth of poetry. By this demonstration of supreme excellence, the refutation of [dhvani] being a mere designation is indicated — he says '<s>upaniṣad</s>' etc. 'It indicates' —

children.text:
locanam ityādinā yassāmayikatvaṃ śaṅkitaṃ tanniravakāśīkaroti /
rāmāyaṇamahābhārataśabdenādikaveḥ prabhṛti sarvaireva sūribhirasyādaraḥ kṛta iti darśayati /
lakṣayatāmityanena vācāṃ sthitamaviṣaya iti parāsyati /
lakṣyate 'neneti lakṣo lakṣaṇam /
lakṣema virūpayanti lakṣayanti, teṣāṃ lakṣaṇadvāreṇa nirūpayatāmitayarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: '<s>Sahṛdayānām</s>' (of the connoisseurs) —

children.text: yeṣāṃ kāvyānuśīlanābhyāsavaśādviśadībhūte manomukure varṇanīyatanmayībhavanayogyatā te svahṛdayasaṃvādabhājaḥ bālapriyā anenādyābhāvavādo nirākṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those whose mental mirror has become clear through the practice and repeated exercise of [appreciating] poetry, [and who possess] the capacity for becoming one with the object being described — they are called <s>sahṛdayas</s> (connoisseurs), partaking of the concord of [their own] heart. The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [notes]: by this, the first position — the denial of [dhvani's] existence — has been refuted.
'Thus [the view] is rejected' —

children.text: 'tatsvarūpaṃ brūma' ityasya lakṣaṇapradarśanena dhvanisvarūpaṃ prakāśayāma iti svalvarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning of '<s>tatsvarūpaṃ brūmaḥ</s>' (we shall describe its true nature) is: 'we shall illuminate the nature of <s>dhvani</s> through a demonstration of its definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>).'

The <s>Locana</s> [explains]: by means of [the words beginning with] '<s>atha ca</s>' etc., he renders impossible [the objection] that [dhvani] is merely conventional. By the words '<s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>' and '<s>Mahābhārata</s>' he shows that from the first poet (<s>ādikavi</s>) onward, all learned poets have shown regard for this [dhvani]. By [the word] '<s>lakṣayatām</s>' (of those who discern), [the view that dhvani] 'lies beyond the domain of words' is rejected. '<s>Lakṣyate anena</s>' means 'that by which [something] is discerned' — [hence] '<s>lakṣa</s>' means '<s>lakṣaṇa</s>' (definition/mark). '<s>Lakṣeṇa</s>' — they examine, they define (<s>lakṣayanti</s>); the meaning is: 'of those who ascertain through the means of definition.'

children.text:
tataśceha pradarśitalakṣaṇadvārā sahṛdayānāṃ dhvanernirūpaṇaṃ bhavati /
evaṃ coktanirāsaḥ sidhyatīti bhāvaḥ /

ucyanta iti śeṣaḥ /
anena rūḍhirdarsitā /
yogamapyāha-sveti /
svahṛdayameva saṃvādaḥ saṃvādakapramāṇaṃ, tadbhājaḥ vimalatareṇa hṛdayena sahavartanta ityavayavārthaḥ /
yadvā-svasmin kavihṛdayaṃ saṃvādakatvena bhajantīti tathā /
asman pakṣe samānaṃ hṛdayaṃ yeṣāmiti bahuvrīhiriti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: In our view, it is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound: 'those whose heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) is the same (<s>sama</s>)' — this is the purport.
The <s>Locana</s> [says]: '<s>sahṛdayāḥ</s>' (connoisseurs) —

children.text: yathoktam-- yo 'rtho hṛdayasaṃvādī tasya bhāvo rasodbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: As has been said: 'That meaning which accords with the heart — its emotional state (<s>bhāva</s>) is the cause of the arising of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment);
the body is pervaded by it, as dry wood [is pervaded] by fire.'

And so here, through the medium of the definition that has been demonstrated, the ascertainment of <s>dhvani</s> by the connoisseurs takes place. And thus the stated refutation [of rival views] is accomplished — this is the purport. He supports what has been said by means of an etymological analysis — '<s>lakṣyate</s>' etc. '<s>Iti lakṣo lakṣaṇam</s>' — the purport is: the word '<s>lakṣa</s>' has the suffix <s>ghañ</s> in the instrumental sense. '<s>Lakṣeṇa</s>' — from the word '<s>lakṣa</s>', by the [rule] '<s>prātipadikād dhātvarthaḥ</s>', the causal suffix <s>ṇic</s> [is applied] in the sense of ascertainment — this is the purport. Since the word '<s>sahṛdaya</s>' has an unfamiliar meaning, he explains it — '<s>yeṣām</s>' etc. '<s>Anuśīlana</s>' of poetry means 'the recitation of words and the investigation of meaning.' Its '<s>abhyāsa</s>' (practice) means 'repeated exercise'; 'by the force of that.' '<s>Viśadī</s>' etc. — 'becoming clear' is primarily the susceptibility to aesthetic experience (<s>rasāveśa</s>). By the metaphor of the mind as a mirror, it is shown that even though the mind is naturally clear, through the force of accumulated impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), there is a surpassing [clarity]. '<s>Varṇanīya</s>' — the 'describable' means the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) such as the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>) etc. The capacity for <s>tanmayībhavana</s> (becoming one with [the object]) — i.e., for assuming identity — means 'the ability, the power' — this is the meaning. The connection is: 'they are <s>sahṛdayas</s>.' The completion is: 'they are called [thus].' By this, the conventional meaning (<s>rūḍhi</s>) is shown. He also states the etymological meaning — '<s>sva</s>' etc. One's own heart itself is the <s>saṃvāda</s> (concord/validation), the validating standard (<s>pramāṇa</s>); those who partake of that — the component meaning is: they accompany [it] with a most pure heart. Or alternatively: those in whom the heart of the poet partakes of concordance — i.e., [the poet's heart] serves as the standard of validation — they are [sahṛdayas].
Thus.
'<s>Ānanda</s>' (delight) —

children.text: rasacarvaṇātmanaḥ prādhānyaṃ darsayan rasadhvanereva sarvatra mukhyabhūtamātmatvamiti darśayati /
children.translated_text: By showing the primacy of [delight] whose nature is the savoring of <s>rasa</s> (<s>rasacarvaṇā</s>), he demonstrates that the <s>ātmatva</s> (soul-nature, essential status) of <s>rasa-dhvani</s> (suggestion of aesthetic sentiment) alone is primary everywhere.

children.text: tena yaduktam--- dhanirnāmāparo yo 'pi vyāpāro vyañjanātmakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, what was stated — '<s>Dhvani</s> is merely another operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>), whose nature is suggestion (<s>vyañjana</s>);

children.text: tasya siddhe 'pi bhede syātkarvye 'śatevaṃ na rūpatā //
children.translated_text: even if its distinctness [from denotation and indication] is established, it would not have the status of being the form (<s>rūpatā</s>) [i.e., the essence] of poetry' —

children.text:

children.translated_text: There, for the poet, first of all, it is delight alone that is to be achieved, even through fame.
As it is said: 'They say that fame has heaven as its fruit' — and so forth.

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ ca vyutpattiprītī yadyapi staḥ,yathoktam-- dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu vaicakṣaṇyaṃ kalāsu ca /
children.translated_text: And for the listeners, even though both erudition (<s>vyutpatti</s>) and delight (<s>prīti</s>) exist — as has been said: 'In matters of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>, [it produces] discernment, and in the arts as well;
the devoted study of good poetry produces fame and delight.'

this [objection] has been refuted. For even though poetry has three aspects — denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>), evocation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), and the savoring of <s>rasa</s> (<s>rasacarvaṇā</s>) — the savoring of <s>rasa</s> is indeed the life-force [of poetry]. And even you do not dispute this. As you yourself have stated: 'In poetry, everyone is a taster of <s>rasa</s>, not a knower, not one bound by injunction.' The <s>Bālapriyā</s> cites the authority for what has been stated — 'as has been said' etc. '<s>Yo 'rthaḥ</s>' — that meaning which accords with one's own heart, i.e., which has the nature of concordance characterized by becoming one [with the object] — the <s>sahṛdaya</s>-praiseworthy meaning in the form of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. that is its object. '<s>Tasya bhāvaḥ</s>' — its '<s>bhāvanā</s>' (evocation), i.e., uninterrupted savoring. '<s>Rasodbhavaḥ</s>' — the cause of the manifestation of <s>rasa</s>, whose life is the savoring. '<s>Śarīram</s>' etc. — by that meaning, preceded by the pervading of the heart, even the body of the connoisseur is pervaded. Hence indeed the manifestation of <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation) etc. 'Dry wood' — not stone etc. By this illustration, even the existence of residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of <s>rati</s> (love) etc. [in the audience] is implied. By [the word] 'dry,' the clarity of mind produced by the practice of poetry [is also indicated]. He states the purpose of employing the word '<s>ānanda</s>' (delight) — '<s>rasa</s>' etc. '<s>Rasacarvaṇā</s>' (savoring of rasa) alone is the <s>ātman</s> (essence) — that <s>ānanda</s> (delight) whose [nature] is such. Its 'primacy' — primacy over <s>vastu-dhvani</s> (factual suggestion) and <s>alaṅkāra-dhvani</s> (figurative suggestion). 'He demonstrates' — the meaning is: to show that <s>rasa-dhvani</s> alone is primary among [all types of dhvani], while the other two [types] culminate in it and are therefore secondary — this is what has been stated. By demonstrating the primacy of <s>rasa-dhvani</s>, the rival position is also refuted — he says '<s>tena</s>' etc. '<s>Tena</s>' — by the demonstration of the primacy of <s>rasa-dhvani</s>. 'What was stated' — the completion is: 'by <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s>.' The connection is: 'that has been refuted.' '<s>Dhvaniḥ</s>' — by [the word] '<s>nāma</s>' (merely/nominally), showing remoteness, he indicates his own non-acceptance [of dhvani]. '<s>Aparaḥ</s>' — distinct from denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>) and evocation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). '<s>Yo 'pi</s>' — the particle '<s>api</s>' concedes the unwelcome acceptance [of dhvani's distinctness]. '<s>Tasya</s>' — even though its distinctness from denotation and evocation is established. The purport is: when truly examined, the distinctness is not established. '<s>Syāt</s>' — its status as a portion (<s>aṃśatva</s>) of poetry would be [granted]; but '<s>rūpatā</s>' — the status of being the form, i.e., the essence, [the status of being] the whole — would not be [granted]. This is the meaning. The reasoning is: <s>dhvani</s>, being a portion of poetry, is an operation of words, like denotation. By merely showing the <s>ātmatva</s> (essential status) of <s>rasa-dhvani</s>, how is this [objection] refuted? — to this he explains: '<s>tathā hi</s>' etc. '<s>Abhidhā</s>' — primary and secondary. '<s>Bhāvanā</s>' — the capacity to evoke. '<s>Rasacarvaṇā</s>' — the capacity to produce aesthetic enjoyment. This will be explained later. The construction is: 'even in [poetry having] three aspects.' 'By you' means 'by <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s>.' '<s>Kāvye</s>' — '<s>rasayitā</s>' means 'one whose nature is the savoring of <s>rasa</s>.' The completion is: '<s>sarvaḥ</s> — everyone is qualified in poetry.' '<s>Na boddhā</s>' — not [merely] a knower, as in <s>itihāsa</s> etc. 'And not one bound by injunction' — not one enjoined, as in the <s>Veda</s> etc. The <s>Locana</s> [says]: that the [essential] status [of dhvani] is merely that of a portion — with reference to <s>vastu-dhvani</s> and <s>alaṅkāra-dhvani</s> — is already established [by us]; so this is proving what is already proved. But with reference to <s>rasa-dhvani</s>, [the claim of mere portion-hood] contradicts the well-known experience of one's own accepted position and the authentication by connoisseurs.
Thus.

children.translated_text: And '<s>Ānanda</s>' (Delight) is the name of the author of the treatise.

children.text: tena sa ānandavardhanācārya etacchāstradvārema sahṛdayahṛdayeṣu pratiṣṭāṃ devatāyatanādivadanaśvarīṃ sthitiṃ gacchatviti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, may he — the master <s>Ānandavardhana</s>, through this <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) — attain an imperishable abode in the hearts of the connoisseurs, like a temple of a deity — this is the purport.
As it has been said: 'Even of those who have ascended to heaven, [if they were] composers of literary works,

children.text: āsta eva nirātaṅkaṃ kāntaṃ kāvyamayaṃ vapuḥ //
children.translated_text: their beautiful poetic body remains securely, without fear [of decay].'

Nevertheless, among those [two], delight alone is primary. Otherwise, from the <s>Vedas</s> etc. — which are like a master — and from the <s>itihāsas</s> etc. — which are like a friend — both being causes of erudition, what [distinction] of this poetic form as a cause of erudition [would there be], whose characteristic is that of a beloved wife? The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [explains]: the completion is: 'not everyone [is qualified]'; rather, 'only as a taster of <s>rasa</s>' — this is the meaning. By this statement that <s>rasacarvaṇā</s> (savoring of rasa) qualifies one for [the appreciation of] poetry, its primacy — i.e., its being the life-force [of poetry] — has already been stated — this is the purport. Some, however, [explain]: '<s>kāvye sarvaḥ</s>' — [means] 'in poetry, every operation.' '<s>Rasayitā</s>' — like a beloved wife (<s>kāntā</s>), [it is] the captivator through the savoring of <s>rasa</s>. '<s>Na boddhā</s>' — like a friend (<s>bandhu</s>), not an instructor. '<s>Na niyogabhāk</s>' — like a master (<s>prabhu</s>), not a commander — this is the meaning. Thus they explain. '<s>Tat</s>' — the meaning is: 'therefore.' Or: 'what you stated' — this is the meaning. '<s>Aṃśamātratvam</s>' — if this [claim of mere portion-hood] is intended with reference to <s>vastu-dhvani</s> and <s>alaṅkāra-dhvani</s>, then it is already established [and proves nothing new]. Since <s>rasa-dhvani</s> alone has the status of the whole, while the other two types of <s>dhvani</s> are merely portions — this being already accepted by the proponents of <s>dhvani</s> — the proving of what is [already] proved is the meaning. '<s>Rasa</s>' etc. — '<s>aṃśamātratvam</s>' carries over from the previous. '<s>Svābhyupagama</s>' etc. — the meaning is: [it] contradicts one's own doctrinal position, established examples (<s>lakṣya</s>), well-known [usage], and the experience of connoisseurs. Now, since there exist other fruits too such as fame etc., [the question arises:] why were [only] those not stated, given that '<s>sahṛdayamanaḥprītaye</s>' (for the delight of the hearts of connoisseurs) is taken as a synecdoche (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>)? — to this he says: '<s>tatra</s>' etc. The connection of '<s>tatra</s>' is: 'therein' — delight alone has been stated as primary. '<s>Tatra</s>' means 'in poetry.' '<s>Svarga</s>' etc. — [means] that whose fruit is <s>svarga</s> (heaven), i.e., unsurpassed bliss. He raises the objection — '<s>śrotṝṇām</s>' etc. [There are both] erudition [and delight]. '<s>Kāvyaniṣevaṇam</s>' — there is also the reading '<s>nibandhanam</s>.' He resolves [the objection] — '<s>tathāpi tatra</s>' etc. '<s>Tatra</s>' means 'among erudition and delight.' 'Primary' means 'the primary fruit.' He strengthens what has been stated by showing the absurdity of the opposing view — '<s>anyathā</s>' etc. '<s>Anyathā</s>' means 'in the absence of delight being the primary fruit.' What distinction does this poetic form have from the <s>Vedas</s> etc. and the <s>itihāsas</s> etc., which are [also] causes of erudition? Since erudition-causing is common to all three, there would be no distinction — this is the meaning. The mention of both [Vedas and itihāsas] is to show that erudition-causing is common to all three. The <s>Locana</s> [says]: [the] distinction — thus, delight alone has been stated as primary. And even the erudition regarding the four goals of life (<s>caturvarga</s>) — delight alone is the ultimate, primary fruit of that too.
Thus.

children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "As it is established in the mind" — such is his mind; he is indeed the emperor among connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya-cakravartī</s>) — this is the purport of [saying] "this author." As in the example: "established in battle is the supreme <s>Arjuna</s>." The self-naming is indeed an instrument for engaging the listeners — <s>Bālapriyā</s> explains that the conformity of Vāda and others to Prabhva etc. is elaborated in the <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s> and other works. "Stated" (<s>ukta</s>): meaning "stated in the <s>kārikā</s> as the fruit." But <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s statement intends that the cultivation of the four aims (<s>caturvarga</s>) and fame are fruits in a subsidiary sense, not primarily — hence he says "<s>caturvarga</s>" etc. And even of the cultivation of the four aims, the ultimate fruit is bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) alone — this is the connection. By "and also" (<s>api ca</s>), fame is included as a collective. He also explains the text "the bliss of connoisseurs" etc. alternatively — "<s>ānanda</s>" etc. The connection is with "<s>nāma ca</s>" ("and the name"). Just as <s>Bhīmasena</s> has the name <s>Bhīma</s> etc., so too — this is the purport. "By that" (<s>tena</s>): meaning "by the reason of being a name." The connection of this is with "<s>iti bhāvaḥ</s>" ("this is the purport"). "He" (<s>saḥ</s>): the original author. "This treatise" (<s>etacchāstram</s>): the <s>Dhvani</s> treatise. This has the character of a <s>śāstra</s> due to having the form of beneficial instruction. The word "<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>" (establishment) is well-known in the sense of a deity's placement in an appropriate abode — hence the example "deity" etc. "Like a deity in a deity's abode" etc.: the word "etc." (<s>ādi</s>) includes the hearts of devoted people. The explanation of "may it attain establishment" is: "may it reach imperishable stability." "Continuing through the treatise" means the continuing of the treatise itself — with this intention he reconciles <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s statement: "as stated" etc. With the intention that the stability prayed for is inevitable, he says "as" (<s>yathā</s>) etc. "As there is establishment in the mind" — in the mind of connoisseurs; "of such a kind" (<s>evaṃvidham</s>) means "of that kind." "His" (<s>asya</s>): the master's mind, or learning, or this treatise. He substantiates what was stated — "connoisseur" (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) etc. "<s>Khalu</s>" is for [indicating] well-known [fact]. "<s>Yāvat</s>" is for delimitation. The meaning is: there is no doubt regarding this prayed-for matter. By this it is shown that even for the author, the fruit in the form of delight arises through the medium of fame. He reconciles the usage when the word "<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>" has the stated meaning: "as" (<s>yathā</s>) etc. "<s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>" means stability consisting of high regard. Now, to prepare the ground for what has begun to be characterized regarding the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s>, this is stated —
That meaning which is praised by connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) and established as the soul of poetry —
(<s>DhvK</s> 1.2a)
That meaning which is praised by connoisseurs and established as the soul of poetry —
<s>Locana</s>: We shall explain at the end of the treatise, through the mode of generating the belief of approbation (<s>sambhāvanā-pratyaya</s>).

children.text: evaṃ granthakṛtaḥ kaveḥ śrotuśca mukhyaṃ prayojanamuktam // 1 //
children.translated_text: Thus the primary purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) for the author, the poet, and the listener has been stated. // 1 //

nanu 'dhvanisvarūpaṃ brūma' iti pratijñāya vācyapratīyamānākhyau dvau bhedāvarthasyeti vācyābhidhāne kā saṅgatiḥ kārakāyā ityāśaṅkya saṅgatiṃ kartumavataraṇikāṃ karoti--tatreti /
evaṃvidhe 'bhidheye prayojane ca sthita ityarthaḥ /

tatpṛṣṭe 'dhikapratīyamānāṃśolliṅganāt /

pravṛttyaṅgameveti /

sambhāvanā bahumānaḥ, pratyayaḥ taddheturāptatvabuddhiḥ, tadubhayotpādanadvāreṇetyarthaḥ /
kimetat granthakārābhipretamityatrāha-itīti /
granthānte vakṣyāmaḥ "ānandavardhana iti prathitābhidhāna" ityasya vyākhyāvasare prakāśayiṣyāmaḥ /

children.translated_text: He concludes — "thus" (<s>evam</s>).
"Of the author" (<s>granthakṛtaḥ</s>): of the author of the <s>Dhvani</s> treatise.
"The primary purpose" (<s>mukhyaṃ prayojanam</s>): having the form of delight (<s>prīti</s>).
By [the word] "primary" (<s>mukhyam</s>), subsidiary purposes such as wealth etc. are indicated — enough. // 1 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Now, [one might object:] having pledged "we shall describe the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s>," what relevance does the exposition of the expressible (<s>vācya</s>) have, since [the text says] "the two divisions of meaning are called the expressible and the suggested (<s>pratīyamāna</s>)"? Anticipating this objection, he composes an introductory passage (<s>avataraṇikā</s>) to establish the connection — "there" (<s>tatra</s>) etc. The meaning is: when the subject matter and purpose of such a kind are established. "<s>Bhūmikā</s>" (preparatory ground) is like "<s>bhūmi</s>" (ground). Just as when a novel construction is desired, the ground is first prepared, so too, when the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> — called the suggested meaning (<s>pratīyamāna</s>) — is to be examined, the exposition of the expressible, which is established without dispute, serves as the ground. [This is] because on the basis of that [expressible], the additional suggested element is indicated. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Why is the self-naming explained in this way? To that he says: "<s>sva</s>" etc. "As an instrument of engagement" (<s>pravṛttyaṅgam eva</s>): the word "<s>eva</s>" means "not for obtaining fame etc." "Through the mode of generating the belief of approbation" (<s>sambhāvanā-pratyayotpādanamukena</s>): <s>sambhāvanā</s> is high regard; <s>pratyaya</s> is the cognition of trustworthiness (<s>āptatva</s>) that causes it; through the generation of both — this is the meaning. "Is this the author's intention?" — to this he says "<s>iti</s>" etc. "We shall explain at the end of the treatise" (<s>granthānte vakṣyāmaḥ</s>): we shall make it clear on the occasion of commenting on "<s>Ānandavardhana</s> is the one whose name is well-known."

adhikasyadha
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He introduces the text beginning with "to characterize <s>dhvani</s> alone" — "<s>nanu</s>" etc. "What relevance does the exposition of the expressible have?" — the meaning is: being off-topic, that exposition is irrelevant. "<s>Tatra</s>" is a locative of characteristic (<s>bhāvalakṣaṇa-saptamī</s>), ending in the dual. By the word "<s>tat</s>," there is a reference to the previously mentioned subject matter and purpose. "Being established" (<s>sthitayoḥ</s>) is the remainder — with this intention he explains: "of such a kind" (<s>evaṃbhūta</s>) etc. There is also the reading "<s>evaṃvidha</s>" — its meaning is: of the nature of <s>dhvani</s> and of the nature of delight. Alternatively, this is merely a qualifier of the subject matter; its meaning is: "fallen within the domain of dispute." "<s>Bhūmikā</s> is like <s>bhūmi</s>" — "<s>avataraṇikā</s>" is like "<s>avataraṇa</s>" (introduction); "<s>pīṭhikā</s>" is like "<s>pīṭha</s>" (pedestal). These words end in the suffix "<s>ka</s>" [formed by the rule] "<s>iva-pratikṛtau</s>." "When a novel" (<s>yathā apūrva</s>) etc.: "<s>apūrva-nirmāṇa</s>" (novel construction) such as a palace etc., "in that" means when it is intended. "Established without dispute" (<s>nirvivāda-siddha</s>): meaning accepted by both the proponents of <s>dhvani</s> and its opponents. "Ground" (<s>bhūmi</s>): foundation, means — this is the purport. When the expressible is the ground, the exposition of that [expressible] too becomes the ground, since the expressible and suggested meanings are understood as having the relationship of foundation and founded. It is indeed relevant here to describe the expressible meaning by way of its utility for the suggested meaning — this is the purport. How does it have similarity to a ground? To that he says "<s>tat</s>" etc. "Of that" (<s>tasya</s>): of that expressible; "on the basis of" (<s>pṛṣṭhe</s>): after. Meaning: after the cognition of the expressible. "Of the additional" (<s>adhikasya</s>) —

children.text: vācya-pratīyamānākhyau tasya bhedāv ubhau smṛtau // DhvK_1.2 //
children.translated_text: The two divisions of that [meaning] are called the expressible (<s>vācya</s>) and the suggested (<s>pratīyamāna</s>). // <s>DhvK</s> 1.2 //
The two divisions of that [meaning] are called the expressible (<s>vācya</s>) and the suggested (<s>pratīyamāna</s>). // 2 //

children.translated_text:
<s>Locana</s>: The enumeration on equal footing (<s>samaśīrṣikā</s>) is to establish the undeniability of that [suggested meaning] as well. By [the word] "in tradition" (<s>smṛtau</s>), he confirms: "that which was thoroughly transmitted" (<s>yaḥ samāmnātapūrvaḥ</s>). As it has been stated that "poetry is that whose body consists of word and meaning" (<s>śabdārthaśarīraṃ kāvyam</s>), from the very use of the term "body" (<s>śarīra</s>), it must necessarily be enlivened by some soul (<s>ātman</s>). Now, word (<s>śabda</s>) occupies the position of a bodily part, since it possesses properties cognizable by all people — like [physical attributes such as] stoutness, thinness, etc. But meaning (<s>artha</s>) is not cognizable by all people.

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Not of what is distinct from the expressible (<s>vācya</s>) — [that is,] of the suggested (<s>pratīyamāna</s>), the <s>vyaṅgya</s> — because of indication (<s>ulliṅganāt</s>), i.e., inference. Some, reading "<s>tatpṛṣṭotthite</s>," [explain:] on the basis of that [expressible] as the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), by virtue of the suggested portion arising distinctly — through inference (<s>ulliṅganāt</s>), i.e., through <s>anumāna</s>. "On equal footing" (<s>samaśīrṣikayā</s>): with equal prominence. "Enumeration" (<s>gaṇanam</s>): the designation "called the expressible and the suggested" (<s>vācya-pratīyamānākhyau</s>). "Of that too" (<s>tasyāpi</s>): of the suggested too. The word "<s>api</s>" (also/even) serves the purpose of illustration. By this it is stated that the suggested exists because it is a portion of meaning, just like the expressible — thus a proof (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is also indicated. Since undeniability is established by the very statement of proof.

He explains the fruit of saying "<s>smṛtau</s>" (in tradition) when "<s>sthitau</s>" (in establishment) could have been said — "<s>smṛtau</s>" etc. That which was transmitted (<s>samāmnāta</s>) by the wise has the form of <s>smṛti</s> (tradition); just as the transmission of <s>dharma</s> etc. by <s>Manu</s> and others — and that [<s>smṛti</s>] is grounded in another means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — so too this — to confirm this, "<s>smṛtau</s>" was used. This is the purport.

Showing with reasoning the status of the meaning qualified by being-praised-by-connoisseurs as the soul of poetry — as stated by the first half of the <s>kārikā</s> "that meaning which is praised by connoisseurs and established as the soul of poetry" — he explains that half following the <s>vṛtti</s>, beginning with "<s>śabda</s>" etc. "That whose body is word and meaning" (<s>śabdārthau eva śarīram yasya tat</s>). "Stated" (<s>uktam</s>): meaning stated by the proponents of the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>). "From the very use of 'body'" (<s>tatra śarīra-grahaṇād eva</s>): from the very acceptance of word and meaning as the body of poetry. Alternatively: "<s>tatra</s>" means "when that has been stated." "<s>Śarīra</s>" etc.: meaning from the very acceptance of the body of poetry. By the word "<s>eva</s>" (alone), independence from other means of proof is indicated. "By some one" (<s>kenacit</s>): by one or the other of word and meaning. For what purpose? To that he says "<s>tat</s>" etc. "That which enlivens" (<s>anuprāṇaka</s>): that which vivifies the poetry, makes it delightful to connoisseurs — by that. "Must necessarily be" (<s>bhāvyam eva</s>) — by the word "<s>eva</s>," he shows the contingency of being a mere semblance of body otherwise. The argument is: the entity in question is a body [and therefore] must have a soul, because of being a body, like our own body etc.

"<s>Tatra</s>" etc.: there, when the soul must necessarily exist. Alternatively: by the word "<s>eva</s>" in "is indeed a bodily part" (<s>śarīrabhāga eva</s>), the fitness for occupying the soul-position is denied [to word]. "<s>Sarva</s>" etc.: "having properties cognizable by all people" — [properties such as] intensity, mildness, etc., or sweetness, harshness, etc. In the example, the properties are stoutness etc. Alternatively: the word "<s>saṃvedya</s>" is an abstract noun — meaning: because of having the property of being cognizable by all people. The argument is: the entity in question, namely word, is not the soul, because of having properties cognizable by all, like a gross body etc. Some [say] that by "<s>sarva</s>" etc., the reason shown is that of being graspable by external sense organs.

Then if meaning should be the soul, to that he says: "But meaning" (<s>arthaḥ punaḥ</s>) etc. The word "<s>punaḥ</s>" (but/however) indicates the special feature of meaning's fitness for being the soul.

"<s>Sakala</s>" etc.: since the meaning of poetry is cognizable only by connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>), and the meaning of other [ordinary] sentences is cognizable by any learned person — meaning as such, delimited merely by the property of being meaning, is not cognizable by all. This is the purport.

<s>Locana</s>: For the designation "poetry" (<s>kāvya</s>) does not arise from meaning alone, since [if it did,] ordinary and Vedic sentences would also [be called poetry], as meaning is present there too. Therefore he says: "praised by connoisseurs" (<s>sahṛdaya-ślādhyaḥ</s>). That one meaning alone is divided by those with discriminating insight (<s>vivekin</s>) through an analytical cognition into two branches (<s>dviśākhatā</s>).

For consider: when both [poetic and ordinary meaning] are equal in being meaning, why do connoisseurs praise only certain [meanings]? There must therefore be some distinguishing feature (<s>viśeṣa</s>) in that [poetic meaning]. That distinguishing feature — being the cause of distinction — is called the suggested portion (<s>pratīyamāna-bhāga</s>), and is established by the discriminating as the soul (<s>ātman</s>).

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] By this it is shown that the argument previously stated for word's not being the soul does not apply here [to the suggested meaning]. Then is the soul-hood of meaning in general [to be accepted]? No — he says "<s>na hi</s>" etc. "By meaning alone" — by the entirety of meaning that is cognizable by any learned person; with the intention that [such meaning] is a cause for usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>), hence the instrumental case indicates cause. "The designation 'poetry'" (<s>kāvya-vyapadeśaḥ</s>): the conventional usage "poetry." "In sentences" (<s>vākyeṣu</s>): meaning in the domain of sentences. "Due to its absence" (<s>tadabhāvāt</s>): due to the absence of the designation "poetry." Otherwise, those sentences too would have the designation "poetry" — this is the purport.

"Therefore he says" etc.: since neither word nor the meaning of non-poetic sentences possesses the soul-hood of poetry, he says "meaning praised by connoisseurs" (<s>arthaḥ sahṛdaya-ślādhyaḥ</s>) — to indicate the exclusion [of those]. This is the meaning.

Now, demonstrating the soul-hood of poetic meaning through showing the distinguishing feature in the form of being-praised-by-connoisseurs, he explains the purport of the second half [of the <s>kārikā</s>] — "that one" (<s>sa ekaḥ</s>) etc. "One alone" (<s>eka eva</s>): appearing as a unity. "That" (<s>saḥ</s>): that meaning praised by connoisseurs. "In two branches" (<s>dviśākhatayā</s>): as having two portions. "By the discriminating" (<s>vivekibhiḥ</s>): by those disposed to discrimination. "Through analytical cognition" (<s>vibhāga-buddhyā</s>): "<s>vibhāga</s>" means [recognizing] two portions or aspects that are contrary, i.e., distinguished from each other by mutually exclusive properties; by that cognition, i.e., by that reason.

He substantiates what was stated — "for consider" (<s>tathā hi</s>) etc. "When the nature of being meaning is equal" (<s>tulye artharūpatve</s>): meaning when the status of being meaning is equal between poetic meaning and ordinary meaning etc. Even though both are equal as meaning — this is the purport. "Why" (<s>kim iti</s>): for what reason? The purport is: for no reason other than what we intend. "Only for certain [meaning]" (<s>kasmaicid eva</s>): for poetic meaning alone. "Therefore" (<s>tat</s>): from that [it follows]. "In that" (<s>tatra</s>): in poetic meaning. "By a distinguishing feature" (<s>viśeṣeṇa</s>): by a distinguishing feature that is the cause of praise. A <s>viśeṣa</s> is a property that confers superiority. The argument: poetic meaning possesses a distinguishing feature, because of being praised by connoisseurs; what is not so is not so, like the meaning of ordinary sentences etc.

"That which" (<s>yaḥ</s>) etc. "Distinguishing feature" (<s>viśeṣaḥ</s>): that which confers distinction. "That is the suggested portion" (<s>sa pratīyamāna-bhāgaḥ</s>) — "is said to be" is the remainder. By this it is shown that the other portion is the expressible (<s>vācya</s>). "By the discriminating" etc.: "that" (<s>sa</s>) carries over. Just as the soul (<s>ātman</s>), merely by the special feature of its proximity, being distinct from inert entities like pots, causes the perception of soul-hood in the bodied aggregate through the superimposition of its own consciousness — and precisely for this reason accomplishes the praiseworthiness of that [body] — so too the suggested portion, in comparison with the meaning of other sentences, produces some special excellence (<s>atiśaya</s>) characterized by the praise of connoisseurs in poetic meaning, and therefore, due to possessing the quality of being the cause of distinction — which is the quality of the soul — it has soul-hood.

<s>Locana</s>: For the soul of poetry — [which possesses] beauty arising from the charming and fitting arrangement of the body, as it were — is of the nature of essence (<s>sāra</s>). But those whose hearts are deluded by the intermingling of the suggested with the expressible (<s>vācya-saṃvalanā</s>) dispute its separate existence — like the <s>Cārvākas</s> [disputing] the separate existence of the soul [from the body].

Precisely therefore, having begun with "meaning" (<s>artha</s>) as a unity, and having indicated the cause through the qualifier "praised by connoisseurs," in the mode of analysis (<s>apodddhāra</s>) it is said "the two divisions of that are portions" — and not that there are two souls of poetry.

He says, to explain the word "<s>kāvya</s>" occurring in the <s>kārikā</s> — "of poetry, for" (<s>kāvyasya hi</s>) etc. By the word "<s>lalita</s>" (charming), he speaks of the favor of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments). By the word "<s>ucita</s>" (fitting), showing that propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) pertains only to the domain of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), he hints at the vital nature of <s>rasa-dhvani</s>. For in its absence, with regard to what would this so-called propriety be proclaimed everywhere? This is the purport.

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "By the discriminating" (<s>vivekibhiḥ</s>): meaning it is determined through reasoning. Then why is there not such perception for everyone, and why indeed is there dispute? To that he says "<s>vācya</s>" etc. "The intermingling of the suggested with the expressible" (<s>vācya-saṃvalanā</s>): the admixture with expressible meaning; by that [intermingling], which has mounted upon the habit-energy (<s>vāsanā</s>) of deeply rooted, dense identification [with the expressible] — "deluded" (<s>vimohitam</s>): rendered incapable of discrimination; "heart" (<s>hṛdayam</s>) — by those [whose hearts are so]. "In its separate existence" (<s>tat-pṛthag-bhāve</s>): in the separate existence of the suggested from the expressible, which is the bodily [part]. He gives an example — "by the <s>Cārvākas</s>" etc. "From the body" (<s>śarīrāt</s>) is the remainder.

He puts the explained meaning into the form of the <s>kārikā</s> — "precisely therefore" (<s>ata eva</s>) etc., up to "of poetry" (<s>kāvyasya</s>). "Precisely therefore" — because the situation of the expressible and suggested follows the pattern of body and soul, and the determination of their separateness or non-separateness accords with the two perspectives of the discriminating and non-discriminating — precisely therefore. "As a unity" (<s>ekatayā</s>): meaning by the singular number. "Having begun" (<s>upakramya</s>): having commenced the statement. The unity of the expressible and suggested meanings, which was presented through an undiscriminating cognition using the analytical cognition of non-differentiation — that is designated in the introductory portion by the singular-ending "<s>arthaḥ</s>" (meaning). This is the purport. "Through the qualifier" (<s>viśeṣaṇa-dvārā</s>): through the medium of the qualifier. "The cause" (<s>hetum</s>): meaning that distinguishing feature of meaning which is the cause of connoisseur-praise and which establishes the two-part nature — the meaning is as previously stated: "there must be some distinguishing feature in that." "Having indicated" (<s>abhidhāya</s>): having shown. "In the mode of analysis" (<s>apodddhāra-daśā</s>): through analytical cognition.

The explanation of "the two divisions" (<s>bhedau</s>) is "the two portions" (<s>aṃśau</s>). The one portion that is the object of the act of praising — the expressible; and that which is the cause of that [praising] — that is the suggested portion. This is the meaning. "Not" (<s>na tu</s>) etc.: rather, the suggested alone is the soul, while the expressible is a portion, being of the nature of body. This is the purport.

Here, the first half [of the <s>kārikā</s>] designates the soul-hood of poetry for meaning in its undifferentiated, analytically-unresolved form; the second half prescribes the two-part nature in its analytically-resolved form. This is the essential meaning. There is also the <s>kārikā</s> reading: "the meaning praised by connoisseurs, which is the soul of poetry, [that] which is established" (<s>arthaḥ sahṛdaya-ślādhyaḥ kāvyātmā yo vyavasthitaḥ</s>).

"The word <s>kāvya</s>" — meaning the word "<s>kāvya</s>" in "<s>kāvyātmā</s>." He says that by the words "<s>lalita</s>" (charming) and "<s>ucita</s>" (fitting), everything related to poetry is included — "<s>lalita</s>" etc. "Speaks of the favor of <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s>" — meaning the assistance given by <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s>, i.e., the production of beauty. "Pertaining to the domain of <s>rasa</s> alone" — since plot (<s>itivṛtta</s>) and other acceptable elements are subordinate to <s>rasa</s>, what pertains to those also pertains to the domain of <s>rasa</s> alone. This is the purport. "Hints" (<s>sūcayati</s>) [at the vital nature of <s>rasa-dhvani</s>].

"Established" (<s>sthitaḥ</s>): the meaning that is praised by connoisseurs — of that, the two divisions are the expressible (<s>vācya</s>) and the suggested (<s>pratīyamāna</s>).

<s>Locana</s>: By "that meaning" (<s>yo arthaḥ</s>), while restating [what was said], he shows that even the opponent has accepted this much. "Of that" (<s>tasya</s>) etc. — he shows that the very acceptance [of the opponent] is coherent only when there are two parts. Therefore, the statement [by opponents] that "<s>dhvani</s> is not different from <s>guṇa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s>, since it is a cause of beauty" — there the reason is unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), since <s>dhvani</s> has the nature of the soul itself. For it is not the case that the soul is the cause of the beauty of the body.

But even if it were so, still — "in the expressible" [the reason would be] inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The propriety pertaining to the domain of <s>rasa</s> — the primacy of <s>rasa</s> — cannot be established without it, and when that [primacy] is established, its soul-hood is proven. This is the purport. He establishes this very point through the mode of <s>bādhaka</s> (absurdity/contradiction) in the opposing position — "in its absence" (<s>tadabhāve</s>) etc. "Of that" (<s>tasya</s>): of <s>rasa</s>, which is the vital [element]. "Would be proclaimed" (<s>uddhāpyate</s>) — "even by the deniers of [its] existence" is the remainder.

In the <s>vṛtti</s>, "<s>sanniveśa</s>" (arrangement) means the configuration of word and meaning. He states the fruit of the designation "<s>yaḥ</s>" etc.: "that meaning" (<s>yo arthaḥ</s>) etc. "When" (<s>yadā</s>): by the relative pronoun "<s>yat</s>." Meaning: by the sentence qualified by the relative pronoun. "Even by the opponent" (<s>pareṇāpi</s>): even by the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (prior-position holder). "This" (<s>etat</s>): the suggested entity. "At least" (<s>tāvat</s>): initially, or in [preliminary] agreement. "Accepted" (<s>abhyupagatam</s>): since the suggested is included within poetic meaning. This is the purport.

"That" (<s>tat</s>) etc.: "that acceptance" (<s>tadabhyupagamaḥ</s>): acceptance of the suggested. "When there are two parts, is indeed coherent" — this is the connection. Since upon accepting one part, the other part cannot be denied. This is the purport. Or: that very acceptance is coherent, not non-acceptance. Alternatively: "this" (<s>etat</s>) refers to the being-praised-by-connoisseurs of poetic meaning; "that acceptance" means acceptance of being-praised-by-connoisseurs.

And thus the inference stated by the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> is also refuted — he says "therefore" (<s>tena</s>) etc. "Therefore" (<s>tena</s>): by the stated method of establishing the soul-hood of <s>dhvani</s>. "Thus it is shown" — this is the syntactic connection. "There" (<s>tatra</s>): meaning in that inference. "Unestablished" (<s>asiddha</s>): meaning unestablished in its own form (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>).

Now, even if <s>dhvani</s> has soul-hood, why should being-a-cause-of-beauty not obtain? Therefore he states [a response] containing an example — "<s>na hi</s>" etc. The connection is: "<s>iti na bhavati hi</s>" — "this indeed does not obtain." "In the world" (<s>loke</s>) is the remainder.

Now, the suggested meaning does have being-a-cause-of-beauty through being the cause of the special excellence characterized by connoisseur-praise of the expressible meaning — so how is [the reason] unestablished? Even in the world, the soul is a cause of beauty, since even in a corpse adorned with all ornaments, beauty is not perceived — to this he says "<s>athāpi evam</s>" etc. "<s>Athāpi</s>": even if. "Thus" (<s>evam</s>): meaning the soul's being-a-cause-of-beauty. "Were" (<s>syāt</s>): upon concession. "Even so" (<s>tathāpi</s>): meaning even so there is a defect here. He states it — "in the expressible" (<s>vācye</s>) etc. "Inconclusive" (<s>anaikāntikaḥ</s>): deviating. Since the being-a-cause-of-beauty conditioned by the adjunct of intermingling with the suggested exists in the expressible meaning too, and since that [expressible meaning] is different from <s>guṇa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s> — there is deviation [of the reason] in that [case]. This is the meaning.

children.text: tatra vācyaḥ prasiddho yaḥ prakārair upamādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>), which is well-known, [has been treated] in various ways through <s>upamā</s> (simile) and other [figures];
it has been variously elaborated by others — those who establish the marks of poetry. [DhvK 1.3]
Therein, the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>), which is well-known, [has been treated] in various ways through <s>upamā</s> (simile) and other [figures];
it has been variously elaborated by others — those who establish the marks of poetry. [3]
Therefore it is not expounded here in detail. [3]
It is merely restated as occasion requires. [3]
The <s>Locana</s> [says]: the reason [for mentioning the vācya at all is this] —

children.text: na hyalaṅkārya evālaṅkāraḥ, guṇī eva guṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the <s>alaṅkārya</s> (that which is to be ornamented) is not itself the <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament); the <s>guṇin</s> (possessor of qualities) is not itself the <s>guṇa</s> (quality).
For this purpose too, the mention of the <s>vācya</s> aspect [is introduced].
For this very reason, he will say later — 'the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) is well-known.' [2]

children.text:
tatreti /

'upamādibhiḥ prakāraiḥ sa vyākṛto bahudhe'ti saṅgatiḥ /

children.translated_text: '<s>Tatra</s>' (therein) — the meaning is: 'even when the two-aspect nature is [already] established.' '<s>Prasiddha</s>' (well-known) — the meaning is: 'worldly indeed, [known from] the faces of women, gardens, the rising of the moon, etc.' The syntactic connection is: 'by the various means (<s>prakāra</s>) such as <s>upamā</s> etc., that [vācya] has been variously elaborated.' '<s>Anyaiḥ</s>' (by others) — he explains this portion of the <s>kārikā</s> by means of '<s>kāvya</s>' etc. By the specific negation in '<s>tato neha pratanyate</s>' (therefore it is not expounded here), he shows that the remainder [i.e., the pratīyamāna] is permitted — by means of '<s>kevalam</s>' etc. [3]

children.text:
bālapriyā tahyatiriktatvaṃ darśayati-na hītyādinā /
etadarthamapīti /
na kevalaṃ bhūmikārtham, anaikāntikatvapradarśanārthamapītyarthaḥ /
uttarakārikāyāṃ vācyasya prasiddhatvakathanamapyetadabhiprāyakamityāha--ata eveti /
prasiddhe hi vastuni vyabhicārodbhāvanam // .2 // // .//
children.translated_text: The <s>Bālapriyā</s> shows the distinctness — by '<s>na hi</s>' etc. '<s>Etadartham api</s>' — the meaning is: not merely for the purpose of [providing] background, but also for the purpose of demonstrating the inconclusiveness [of the opponent's reasoning]. The statement of the well-known status of the <s>vācya</s> in the following <s>kārikā</s> is also intended for this purpose — he says '<s>ata eva</s>' etc. For in the case of a well-known entity, the raising of a counter-example [to disprove the universal rule] [is possible]. [2]

children.text:
kārikāyāṃ tatreti bhāvalakṣaṇasaptamī /

apiśabdaścādhyāhārya ityāśayena vyācaṣṭe--dvyaṃśatve satyapīti /
arthasyeti śeṣaḥ /
dvayorbhedayoḥ satorapītyarthaḥ /
apiśabdenaikasyaiva bahudhā vyākaraṇe virodhaṃ darśayatānyeṣāmapāraṃ maurkhyaṃ dyotyate /
prasiddhapadaṃ vyācaṣṭe--vanitetyādi /

children.translated_text: Known.
To remove the doubt that '<s>kāvyalakṣmavidhāyibhiḥ</s>' (by those who establish the marks of poetry) belongs to the fourth quarter of the <s>kārikā</s>, he says '<s>anyaiḥ</s>' etc.
'By the specific negation' etc. —

children.text: ajñātajñāpanalakṣaṇaṃ pratipādanaṃ hi pratananaṃ, tasya viśeṣarūpasya pratiṣedhena tatpratidvandvitayā pariśiṣṭamanuvadanaṃ gamyata iti bhāvaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: For '<s>pratanana</s>' (detailed exposition) is instruction characterized by making known what is unknown; by negating that specific [detailed exposition], the remaining [activity] — namely, restatement (<s>anuvadana</s>) as its counterpart — is understood to be [what is permitted]. This is the purport. [3]

In the <s>kārikā</s>, '<s>tatra</s>' is a locative expressing the relation of inherence (<s>bhāvalakṣaṇa saptamī</s>). By the word '<s>tat</s>' (that), both the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) and the suggested (<s>pratīyamāna</s>) are referred to. [It derives] from the dual-ending form of '<s>tral</s>.' The word '<s>api</s>' (even/also) is to be supplied — with this intention he explains: 'even when the two-aspect nature is established.' The completion is: 'of meaning.' The meaning is: 'even when the two distinctions exist.' By the word '<s>api</s>' (even), in showing the contradiction in the manifold elaboration of only one [aspect], the boundless foolishness of others is indicated. He explains the word '<s>prasiddha</s>' (well-known) — '<s>vanitā</s>' etc.

children.text: pratīyamānaṃ punar anyad eva vastv asti vāṇīṣu mahā-kavīnām /
children.translated_text: The suggested meaning (<s>pratīyamāna</s>), however, is a different entity altogether [that exists] in the utterances of the great poets.
(DhvK 1.4a)
The suggested meaning (<s>pratīyamāna</s>), however, is a different entity altogether [that exists] in the utterances of the great poets.
