children.translated_text: The <s>Locana</s> [says]: '<s>anyad eva vastu</s>' (a different entity altogether) — the word '<s>punaḥ</s>' (however/again) indicates the distinction from the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>). The meaning is: 'distinct from it [the vācya] and [yet] essential.' '<s>Mahākavīnām</s>' (of the great poets) — the plural indicates [dhvani's] pervasion over all domains without exception. The purport is: the designation 'great poet' (<s>mahākavi</s>) arises solely by virtue of being endowed with a creative genius (<s>pratibhā</s>) skilled in the construction of poetry animated by the <s>pratīyamāna</s> (suggested meaning) that is to be explained [in this treatise]. 'If such [a thing] exists, it shines forth.' For the shining (<s>bhāna</s>) of what is utterly non-existent is not tenable; even silver etc. [in the shell-silver illusion] shines as something not utterly non-existent. By this [he argues]: since the shining is occasioned by existence, existence is inferred from the shining. Therefore, 'what shines, exists as such' — this has been stated. Hence, this is the form of the argument: the well-known expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) is the subject (<s>dharmin</s>). The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [explains]: by the commentary on the <s>kārikā</s> beginning with '<s>pratīyamānam</s>' etc., the <s>vṛtti</s> text from '<s>sahyārtha</s>' up to [this point] is also explained — with this intention he explains the <s>kārikā</s>: '<s>punaḥśabda</s>' etc. '<s>Vācyāt</s>' — there is also the reading '<s>vācyāṃśāt</s>' (from the vācya-aspect). He explains the word '<s>anya</s>' (other) — '<s>tat</s>' etc. — the meaning is: 'distinct from the expressed.' He explains the word '<s>vastu</s>' (entity) — '<s>sāra</s>' etc. [meaning 'essential']. '<s>Iti bahuvacanam</s>' — the plural in '<s>vāṇīṣu</s>' (in the utterances) is also a synecdoche (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) [for this]. '<s>Aśeṣaviṣayavyāpakatvam</s>' — the completion is: 'of the <s>pratīyamāna</s> (suggested meaning).' '<s>Etat</s>' — 'by the <s>pratīyamāna</s> that will be explained in this treatise.' Or '<s>etat</s>' is a qualifier of the <s>pratīyamāna</s>. '<s>Iti bhāvaḥ</s>' — the meaning is: this sense is understood from the stem-portion of [the compound] '<s>mahākavīnām</s>.' He begins to show that the <s>kārikā</s> aims at an inference establishing the existence of the <s>pratīyamāna</s> — '<s>yat</s>' etc. '<s>Yat</s>' means 'since.' '<s>Evaṃvidham</s>' — [meaning] 'distinct [from the vācya] and essential' — [such a] <s>pratīyamāna</s> exists. '<s>Tat</s>' means 'therefore.' '<s>Bhāti</s>' — this relation of reason and consequence should be understood as a factual one. By this, the supporting reasoning (<s>anukūla tarka</s>) in the form of the reason-consequence relation between existence and manifestation is also revealed. Following the <s>Naiyāyika</s> (logician's) position, he says '<s>na hi</s>' etc. '<s>Bhāna</s>' means 'cognition.' '<s>Upapanna</s>' means 'established by reasoning.' '<s>Rajatādyapi</s>' — [even] silver etc. [in illusion] does not shine as utterly non-existent; rather, silver etc., which exist [elsewhere] such as in a shop, shine in [objects like] shell — this is the purport. '<s>Anena</s>' — the meaning is: 'by [the impossibility of] the shining of the utterly non-existent.' Or: the meaning is: 'by [the words of] the <s>kārikā</s>-portion "<s>asti vibhāti</s>" (it exists, it shines).' In this interpretation, the connection is with '<s>ity uktaṃ bhavati</s>' (it has been stated). '<s>Tāvat</s>' is [used] in the sense of provisional acceptance. '<s>Yat</s>' — the meaning is: 'whatever.' '<s>Bhāti</s>' — the completion is: 'as such.' '<s>Ity uktam</s>' — the meaning is: 'thus the universal rule (<s>vyāpti</s>) has been demonstrated both in the <s>kārikā</s> and in the <s>vṛtti</s>.' '<s>Tena</s>' — the meaning is: 'by the demonstration of the invariable concomitance between shining and existence.' '<s>Ayam</s>' refers to the argument (<s>prayoga</s>) that is about to be stated — its meaning is the form of that [argument]. That is: a formal argument (<s>nyāyaprayoga</s>) in the form of an inference for the sake of another (<s>parārthānumāna</s>).

children.translated_text: Thus, to begin with, the first variety [of the suggested] is one that is far removed from the expressed [meaning] in its distinction;
for it is sometimes in the form of a prohibition when the expressed is in the form of an assertion;

children.text: yathā-- bhama dhammia vīsattho so suṇao ajja mārio deṇa /
children.translated_text: For example [in <s>Prākrit</s>]: 'O righteous lady, be brave! That <s>Suṇaka</s> has been killed today by <s>Deṇa</s>,
the resident of <s>Golāṇa-ikaccha-kuḍaṅga</s>, [known as] <s>Dariasiha</s> (Dṛṣṭasiṃha).'

But what is suggested (<s>pratīyamāna</s>) — a factual content (<s>vastu</s>) other than the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) — exists in the utterances of great poets. /
That which is well-known to the sensitive reader (<s>sahṛdaya</s>), which shines forth as distinct from the well-known, ornamented, or cognized constituent parts — like <s>lāvaṇya</s> (gracefulness) in women. /
For just as in women, <s>lāvaṇya</s>, when separately examined, is something entirely other, distinct from all the limbs — a nectar for the eyes of the sensitive, a different principle altogether — just so is that meaning [in poetry]. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] [The verse implies an inference:] It [the poetry of great poets] is like that — i.e., connected with a suggested content distinct from itself — because it appears in such a manner; like the limbs of a woman endowed with <s>lāvaṇya</s>. /
The meaning of the word '<s>prasiddha</s>' (well-known) is: being universally cognized, and being embellished. /
The pronoun-compound '<s>yat-tat</s>' (that which) — for the purpose of making manifest that its essence is aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) — shows the indescribability and the delusion of non-distinction created by mutual intertwining, in both the illustration and the illustrated. /
And this he explains with '<s>kim api</s>' (something ineffable) etc. /
For <s>lāvaṇya</s> is indeed a property distinct from the parts (<s>avayava</s>), manifested through the configuration of the parts — an altogether different quality. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] With 'well-known' etc. up to 'the substrate' (<s>dharmin</s>) — this is the statement of the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>). /
In accordance with the dictum 'having indicated the established substrate, the property to be proved is stated,' 'well-known' and 'substrate' are said — but these two do not enter the thesis-predicate. /
'Connected with a suggested [content] distinct from itself — like that' — this is the statement of the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proved). /
The meaning is: connected with a suggested [content] distinct from itself. /
To prevent the fallacy of <s>siddha-sādhana</s> (proving what is already established) in the view of those who accept that the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) itself is the suggested, the specification 'distinct from itself' is introduced — because in their view, the possession of a suggested content identical with itself would already be established. /
'Because it appears in such a manner' — this is the statement of the reason (<s>hetu</s>). /
The meaning is: because it is ascertained as possessing a suggested [content] distinct from itself. /
Here the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>): 'like the limbs of a woman.' /
Here, to show that <s>lāvaṇya</s> is to be grasped as a referent that is suggested and distinct from [the limbs] themselves, '<s>lāvaṇya-upeta</s>' (endowed with <s>lāvaṇya</s>) is said. /
'Like the limbs' — the remainder is '<s>iti</s>.' /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, at 'from the embellished or cognized [parts]' — to show that the word '<s>vā</s>' (or) has the sense of cumulation (<s>samuccaya</s>), he explains: 'of the word <s>prasiddha</s>' etc. /
The mention of the meaning in the form of 'being embellished' is for the purpose of showing the distinction of <s>lāvaṇya</s> from the beauty produced by ornaments. /
In the <s>kārikā</s>, at '<s>yat-tat</s>' — the word '<s>yat</s>' refers to the previously mentioned suggested factual content. /
The word '<s>tat</s>' has the sense of 'well-known' — with this intention it was explained in the <s>vṛtti</s> as '<s>sahṛdaya-su-prasiddham</s>' (well-known to the sensitive). He explains the meaning conveyed by both: '<s>yat-tat</s>' etc. /
'Compound' — the meaning is: the word '<s>tat</s>' together with the word '<s>yat</s>.' /
That whose essence (<s>sāra</s>), i.e., life-breath, is aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) — the nature of that. /
'For the purpose of making manifest' — for the purpose of illumination. /
'Indescribability' — the impossibility of designating [it precisely]. /
This is said with reference to the suggestion of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). /
'Mutual' — one should understand this as applying to the expressed and the suggested, and to the limbs and <s>lāvaṇya</s> [respectively]. /
'And the delusion of non-distinction' — this is the construction. /
'In both the illustration and the illustrated' etc. — the purport is that '<s>yat-tat</s>' has a connection in the illustration as well. /
He shows [this]: 'For that meaning — merely factual content prompted by the force of the expressed — and figures (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) such as <s>rasa</s> etc. — will be shown as divided into many varieties.' /
'And in all those varieties, its distinctness from the expressed [obtains].' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] And <s>lāvaṇya</s> is not merely the [proper] configuration of the parts, nor the beauty [produced] by ornaments — because even in a woman whose individually examined bodily parts are free from defects such as being one-eyed etc., and who is even adorned, [we say] 'this one is devoid of <s>lāvaṇya</s>'; and conversely, even in one not possessing such [perfection], [we say] 'this one is a moonlight of the nectar of <s>lāvaṇya</s>' — this being the usage of the sensitive. /
[Objection:] But <s>lāvaṇya</s> at least is well-known as distinct [from the parts]. The suggested (<s>pratīyamāna</s>) [in poetry] — we do not even know what it is! Far off is the establishment of its distinctness! /
And the reason 'because it appears in such a manner' is an unestablished reason (<s>asiddha hetu</s>)! — Anticipating this objection, he sets forth the nature of that [suggested content] with 'for that meaning' etc. /
And with 'and in all' etc., he will establish the [well-]knownness of the distinction. /
Therein, the suggested has two varieties: the worldly (<s>laukika</s>), and that which is within the sole domain of poetic operation (<s>kāvya-vyāpāra-eka-gocara</s>). /
The worldly one — which sometimes attains the status of being expressible by its own words — is of many kinds such as assertion, prohibition, etc., and is referred to by the word '<s>vastu</s>' (factual content). /
And that too is of two kinds: that which previously, in some sentence-meaning, was experienced in the form of a figure such as <s>upamā</s> (simile) etc., but now assumes a non-figurative form — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He indicates [this]. /
'He explains with <s>kim api</s> etc.' — one should understand that in the <s>vṛtti</s>, the connection of '<s>kim api</s>' etc. extends to the illustrated (<s>dārṣṭāntika</s>) as well. This is the purport. /
To forestall the suspicion of incompleteness in the example, he says: '<s>lāvaṇya</s> indeed' etc. /
'A different quality' — a specific property. /
He substantiates what was said: 'and not' etc. /
'Separately' — the bodily parts that are separately examined, seen, and free from defects such as being one-eyed etc. — even in one who possesses [such parts]. /
The word '<s>kāṇa</s>' refers to the state of being one-eyed. /
'Even in one not possessing such [perfection]' — the meaning is: even in one who has defects such as being one-eyed, and who is unadorned. /
'Moonlight' — this is said by way of superimposition (<s>āropa</s>). /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'separately' etc. — the meaning is: distinct from all the parts that are separately examined. /
He introduces the <s>vṛtti</s>-passage 'for that meaning' etc.: 'but' etc. /
'That' — the meaning is: what you are speaking of. /
'We do not even know' — the <s>kaimutika</s> (a fortiori) reasoning indicated by the particle '<s>eva</s>' he makes explicit: 'far off' etc. /
'Of that' is the remainder. /
Of the distinction — i.e., the difference from the expressed — the establishment (<s>prathā</s>) [is well-known]. /
Because the establishment of a property depends on the establishment of the substrate: if the suggested is not established, the difference from the expressed is also not established. This is the meaning. /
'<s>Iti</s>' is in the sense of cause. /
'In such a manner' etc. — the meaning is: the reason, in the form of 'appearing in such a manner,' is vitiated by the defect of the non-establishment of the reason. /
He substantiates what was said in the <s>vṛtti</s> with '<s>vastu-mātra</s>' (merely factual content) etc.: 'therein, of the suggested' etc. /
'Therein' — given that the suggested exists. /
'First' — to begin with. /
'Worldly' — known in ordinary life. /
'Poetic' — the operation of poetry, which consists of words and meanings; that which is within the sole domain of that operation — in the form of the suggestive function (<s>vyañjanā</s>) — and not within any other domain. /
Hence it is non-worldly. This is the purport. /
'The worldly, which' — 'it' is the remainder. /
'Sometimes' — in the state of being expressed. /
'By the word <s>vastu</s>' — the meaning is: by the term '<s>vastu-dhvani</s>' (factual-content suggestion). /
Having explained the word '<s>vastu</s>,' to facilitate the explanation of the word '<s>mātra</s>' (merely) in '<s>vastu-mātra</s>,' he first explains <s>alaṅkāra-dhvani</s> (figure-suggestion): 'and that too' etc. /
'Previously' — in the state of being expressed. /
'Now' — in the state of being suggested. /
'Elsewhere, in the expressed meaning, that which' — [<s>Locana</s>:] [is so designated] precisely because elsewhere [i.e., when expressed] the subordination [of the figure] is absent; it is designated as <s>alaṅkāra-dhvani</s> by the force of prior recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>), on the principle of 'a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [who became] an ascetic' [i.e., the prior identity persists in the name]. /
But that which is indicated by the absence of that form [of figure] is called merely factual content (<s>vastu-mātra</s>). /
For by the word '<s>mātra</s>' (merely), the other form [i.e., the figurative form] is excluded. /
But that which, even in a dream, is never expressible by its own words, does not fall within worldly usage, but rather is <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) — whose form is relishable through the operation of savoring (<s>carvaṇā</s>) consisting of the bliss of one's own self-awareness (<s>sva-saṃvid-ānanda</s>), tender with the coloring (<s>anurāga</s>) through arousal (<s>udbodha</s>) of the latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of <s>rati</s> (love) etc. that have been especially lodged in oneself since prior births, [impressions] appropriate to the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) that are beautiful through their accord with the sensitive heart and are presented by [poetic] words — that [<s>rasa</s>] is within the sole domain of poetic operation. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Because elsewhere the subordination [of the figure] is absent. /
[Objection:] But if it does not have the nature of a figure, how is there the designation '<s>alaṅkāra-dhvani</s>'? To this he says: 'prior' etc. /
The connection is with 'is designated on the principle.' /
'Ascetic' — one who has entered the <s>Jaina</s> order. /
'By the absence of that form' — by the absence of the form of a figure. /
'By the word <s>mātra</s>' — the meaning is: by the word '<s>mātra</s>' occurring in the <s>vṛtti</s> in '<s>vastu-mātra</s>.' /
'The other form' — the form of being a figure. /
'Even in a dream' — for in a dream, even what is impossible occurs. /
'Does not fall within worldly usage' — the purport is: it is not of the same form as the joy at the birth of a son, etc. /
'By words' — by the words of poetry that is beautiful with <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures). /
'Being presented' — being properly presented, i.e., in a manner appropriate for the manifestation of <s>rasa</s>; being transferred into the interior of the bud-like heart of the sensitive reader. /
By this it is shown that the factual reality of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. is not a relevant factor. /
This is well-explained in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s> etc. /
For this very reason, the status of <s>vibhāva</s> etc. is established for <s>Mālatī</s> and others just as for <s>Śakuntalā</s> and others. /
Not only is the <s>vibhāva</s>-status effected by poetic words, but also by the accord with the sensitive heart — he says: 'heart' etc. /
The <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> that are being presented by words and that are beautiful through the accord with the [sensitive] heart — appropriate to these are the latent impressions of <s>rati</s> (love) etc. that have been especially lodged [in oneself] from prior births — as stated in the dictum: 'For no sentient being exists that is devoid of mental dispositions' — through the coloring (<s>anurāga</s>) of those, i.e., through arousal. /
Tender — having attained fitness for the savoring of <s>rasa</s> — is the awareness (<s>saṃvit</s>) of the self, i.e., the mind of the savorer, the sensitive reader, which cognizes properly; the operation of savoring, which is the bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) of that [awareness]; through that — [<s>rasa</s>] whose form is relishable. /
As stated by the Sage [<s>Bharata</s>]: '<s>āsvādayanti manasā</s>' ('they savor with the mind') etc. /
Alternatively: 'tender' means eternally charming; '<s>sva-saṃvit</s>' means established through self-experience; and the operation of savoring, which consists of bliss — through that. This is the meaning. /
The remainder is: 'it is called <s>rasa-dhvani</s>' — this is stated next.

children.translated_text: 'Is far removed in its distinctions' —
That injunction and prohibition are contradictory — of this, no one has any doubt.

children.text: etadarthaṃ prathamaṃ tāvevodāharati--- 'bhrama dhārmika visrabdhaḥ sa śunako 'dya māritastena /
children.translated_text: To illustrate this, he first gives an example — 'Wander freely, O <s>Dharmika</s> (righteous one)! That dog has been killed today by him,
the proud lion dwelling in the thickets of creepers on the bank of the <s>Godavari</s> river.'

The <s>Locana</s> [says]: '<s>rasa-dhvani</s> (suggestion of aesthetic sentiment)' — and that is <s>dhvani</s> itself — and it alone is primarily the <s>atman</s> (essence). As for what was said by <s>Bhattanayaka</s> — 'It has the status of a portion, not of a form' — that objection, if [it applies] at all, would be an objection only to <s>vastu-dhvani</s> (factual suggestion) and <s>alankara-dhvani</s> (figurative suggestion); but <s>rasa-dhvani</s> has been accepted by him as the very essence, since the third aspect — the savoring of <s>rasa</s> — has been determined to transcend the two aspects of denotation (<s>abhidha</s>) and evocation (<s>bhavana</s>). That <s>vastu-dhvani</s> and <s>alankara-dhvani</s> ultimately culminate in <s>rasa-dhvani</s> — this we ourselves shall state at the appropriate places; so let that be for now. 'Implied by the power of the expressible (<s>vacyasamarthyaksipta</s>)' — pervading all three divisions. The <s>Balapriya</s> states the distinction [of <s>rasa-dhvani</s>] from <s>vastu-dhvani</s> etc. — 'and that' etc. 'Ca' is used in the sense of 'tu' (but). '<s>Dhvani</s> alone' — [meaning] the suggested alone, not the expressible: this is the force of 'eva.' 'Iti' is in the sense of 'because.' 'That alone' — <s>rasa-dhvani</s> alone. By the particle 'eva,' <s>vastu-dhvani</s> etc. are excluded. 'Primarily the <s>atman</s>' — the <s>atmatva</s> (essential status) of <s>vastu-dhvani</s> etc. is merely figurative, not primary: this is the purport. After 'iti,' the remainder is 'it is said.' 'Tat' — meaning 'that statement.' 'Yadi nama' — an expression of uncertainty within certainty. 'Upalambha' means 'objection,' i.e., the denial of <s>atmatva</s> (essential status) — this is the meaning. The remainder is 'bhavet' (would be). That statement would take the form of denying essential status only to <s>vastu-dhvani</s> and <s>alankara-dhvani</s>, not to <s>rasa-dhvani</s> — this is the meaning. 'Whence?' — to this he says 'rasa' etc. 'How is this known?' — to this he says 'rasacarvana' etc., up to 'nirnayat' (by the determination). That the denial of essential status to <s>vastu-dhvani</s> and <s>alankara-dhvani</s> is already accepted by us — so this is proving what is already proved — he says 'vastu' etc. 'Culminating in <s>rasa-dhvani</s> alone' — just as the expressible <s>vastu</s> (factual content) and <s>alankara</s> (figure) [serve <s>rasa</s>], so too the suggested <s>vastu</s> and <s>alankara</s> ultimately find their rest in <s>rasa-dhvani</s>, since they serve as <s>vibhavas</s> (determinants) etc. and function as suggestors of some <s>rasa</s>: the meaning is that they find repose in <s>rasa-dhvani</s>. For the primary <s>atmatva</s> (essential status) is constituted by being the resting-place, and that belongs to <s>rasa-dhvani</s> alone. But for <s>vastu-dhvani</s> and <s>alankara-dhvani</s>, the superiority over the expressible that is constituted by being suggested is [merely] a non-primary <s>atmatva</s>. And in relation to that, the general statement '<s>dhvani</s> is the soul of poetry' is [understood]: this is the purport. Lest there be the confusion that 'vacyasamarthyaksiptam' (implied by the power of the expressible), being in neuter singular, qualifies only 'vastumatram' (mere factual content) — to prevent that, he explains: 'vacyasamarthyaksiptam' etc. 'Of the three divisions' — when the gender and number of 'vacyasamarthyaksiptam' are adjusted [to agree with each division]. The <s>Locana</s> [says]: '<s>alankara</s>' — the general definition. For even though suggestion (<s>dhvanana</s>) is indeed an operation of words alone, nevertheless, since the cooperation of the power of meaning is never absent in any case, the quality of being implied by the power of the expressible [applies universally]. Even in suggestion that is rooted in verbal power (<s>sabdasaktimula</s>), the cognition of the suggested arises through the power of meaning alone; verbal power is merely a subsidiary cooperant — this we shall explain.

children.translated_text: '<s>Dhvanana</s>' (suggesting/resounding) —

The operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>), having the form of <s>dhvanana</s> (suggesting/resounding), is to be accepted as defined by designations that are cognate with [terms like] <s>dyotana</s> (illumination), <s>vyañjana</s> (manifestation), <s>pratyāyana</s> (making understood), and <s>avagamana</s> (comprehension). The <s>Locana</s> [says]:
As [the author] will say later: 'Abandoning the primary function [of the word], the apprehension of meaning through the secondary function (<s>guṇavṛtti</s>) —

children.text: yaduddisya phalaṃ tatra śabdo naiva skhaladgatiḥ //
children.translated_text: that toward which the word's result is directed — there the word does not stumble at all.'

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>] The syntactic connection (<s>yojanā</s>) of the two [expressions] '<s>rasādayaḥ</s>' etc. is also to be understood as before — this is the purport.

In the reading '<s>vācyasāmarthyakṣipta</s>' (implied by the capacity of the expressed meaning), [the word] '<s>artha</s>' (meaning) serves as a qualifier.

'<s>Sāmānyalakṣaṇam</s>' (general definition) — the property of being implied by the capacity of the expressed meaning (<s>vācyasāmarthyākṣiptatva</s>) is a characteristic that pervades all three subdivisions beginning with <s>vastudhvani</s> (suggestion of factual content) — this is the meaning.

[The objector] raises a doubt — 'even though (<s>yadyapi</s>)...' — since the operation of suggestion (<s>dhvananavyāpāra</s>) depends on words, just like the operations of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) etc., the definition stated for <s>vastudhvani</s> etc. would be impossible.

[The author] resolves this — 'nevertheless (<s>tathāpi</s>)...' etc.

'But if <s>dhvani</s> is rooted in the power of words (<s>śabdaśaktimūla</s>), then it is only the power of the word itself that serves as auxiliary, not anything else' — to this he says: '<s>śabda</s>...' etc.

'Then let there be no word-power' — to this he says: '<s>śabdaśakti</s>...' etc.

[The word-power serves as] a subordinate auxiliary (<s>avāntarasahakāriṇī</s>), assisting the capacity of meaning (<s>arthasāmarthyopakāriṇī</s>).

'We shall explain (<s>vakṣyāmaḥ</s>)' — the remainder is: 'in the section on the subdivision rooted in word-power (<s>śabdaśaktimūlaprabhedanirūpaṇa</s>).'

In the <s>vṛtti</s>: '<s>ādyaḥ prabhedaḥ</s>' (the first subdivision) — the meaning is: a division consisting merely of factual content (<s>vastumātra</s>) in the form of injunction, prohibition, and so forth (<s>vidhiniṣedhādirūpa</s>).

'<s>Dūraṃ vibhedavān</s>' (vastly differentiated) — the meaning is: extremely distinct (<s>atyarthaṃ bhinna</s>).

[<s>Locana</s>] Establishes the extreme differentiation — '<s>vidhi</s>...' etc.

<s>Vidhiniṣedhau</s> (injunction and prohibition) — the injunction and prohibition of one and the same action (<s>ekasyāḥ kriyāyāḥ</s>).

'<s>Viruddhau</s>' (contradictory) — contradiction (<s>virodha</s>) means the impossibility of simultaneous occurrence in a single locus (<s>yugapadekatra vṛttitvābhāva</s>), or mutual difference (<s>bhinnatva</s>).

'<s>Iti</s>' is used in the sense of 'in this manner' (<s>prakāra</s>), meaning 'in this [matter].'

'<s>Vimatī</s>' means a contrary understanding (<s>viparītā matiḥ</s>).

'For this purpose' (<s>etadarthe</s>) means: for the purpose of removing doubt (<s>avimatyartham</s>). That is to say: because there is no doubt (<s>vimatyabhāvāt</s>), this being the reason.

Alternatively — 'for this purpose' means: for the purpose of demonstrating the absolute distinction (<s>ātyantikaṃ bhedapradarśanārtham</s>).

Those very [two], namely injunction and prohibition, are [respectively] the expressed and the suggested (<s>vācyavyaṅgyabhūtau</s>).

The explanation of '<s>yathā</s>' (as for instance) — 'he gives an example (<s>udāharati</s>).'

'Drawing from elsewhere' means: he brings forth (<s>āharati</s>) the sentences that establish it, importing them into this treatise (<s>prabandham</s>).

He reads the <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit paraphrase [of the Prakrit verse]) — '<s>bhrama</s>...' etc.

There is also the reading '<s>vastabdham</s>.'

The <s>chāyā</s> is: '<s>godānadīkacchanikuñjavāsine</s>' (to the one dwelling in the thicket on the bank of the <s>Godā</s> river).

[<s>Locana</s>] There, the word '<s>godā</s>' means <s>Godāvarī</s>; the words '<s>kaccha</s>' etc. are explained as 'bank' and 'dense thicket of creepers' (<s>kūlalatāgahana</s>). This utterance is made in order to protect a certain rendezvous (<s>saṅketasthāna</s>) that constitutes the very life (<s>jīvitasarvasva</s>) [of the speaker], because of the fault of the pious man's wandering (<s>dhārmikasañcaraṇa</s>) causing obstruction [to their tryst], and because his presence strips the place of the beauty of its shoots and blossoms (<s>pallavakusumādi</s>), rendering it devoid of shade (<s>vicchāyīkaraṇa</s>).

In this case, the wandering (<s>bhramaṇa</s>), though self-established (naturally permitted), is 'restored' (<s>apodita</s>) by means of the dog-fear (<s>śvabhaya</s>) — hence the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) here is in the form of absence of prohibition (<s>niṣedhābhāvarūpa</s>), a kind of counter-exception (<s>pratiprasava</s>), and not an actual command (<s>niyoga</s>) in the form of an injunction proper (<s>praiṣādirūpa</s>). For the imperative (<s>loṭ</s>) here pertains to permission (<s>atisarga</s>) and timeliness (<s>prāptakāla</s>).

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>] Since action and its absence (<s>bhāva</s> and <s>tadabhāva</s>) are contradictory, the two cannot be simultaneously expressed (<s>yugapadvācyatā</s>). Anticipating the objection that without specifying a particular speaker, the suggested meaning would not arise, [the commentator] introduces the context — '<s>kasyāścit</s>...' etc.

The reason for protection is: '<s>jīvitasarvasvāyamānam</s>' (constituting one's very life) — the import is: because of extreme dearness (<s>atipriyātvāt</s>).

The obstruction (<s>antarāya</s>) caused by [the pious man's] wandering (<s>sañcaraṇa</s>) is an impediment (<s>vighna</s>) in the form of disruption to the opportune time for secret love-play (<s>cauryasuratasya khalpakālavicchedarūpa</s>) — this is the fault arising from that.

He states another fault also — '<s>tadava</s>...' etc.

By that pious man, the shoots and blossoms (<s>pallavakusumādi</s>) are being plucked away (<s>avalupyamāna</s>, i.e., <s>apahriyamāṇa</s>), resulting in the rendering of the place devoid of shade — from that [fault too this utterance is made].

'<s>Tatra</s>' means: that being the case (<s>tathā satī</s>).

'<s>Svataḥ</s>...' etc. — Here, in the sentence-meaning that has the form of 'wander!' (<s>bhrama</s>), the connection is: 'the injunction is in the form of absence of prohibition (<s>niṣedhābhāvarūpa</s>), not a command (<s>niyoga</s>) in the form of a directive (<s>praiṣādirūpa</s>).'

'But why should it not be [taken in] the primary sense itself?' — to this he says: '<s>pratiprasavātmaka</s>...' etc.

Here he states the reason — '<s>svataḥ</s>...' etc.

'<s>Śvabhayena</s>' — by the agent, namely [the woman's] fear of the dog.

'<s>Apoditam</s>' means: prohibited (<s>pratiṣiddham</s>).

'<s>Iti</s>' is used in the causal sense.

As stated: 'When there is a prior prohibition, the applicability of a counter-exception (<s>pratiprasava</s>) arises.'

To show the meaning of the imperative (<s>loṭ</s>) as evidence for the injunction being in the form of absence of prohibition, he says — '<s>atisarga</s>...' etc.

The meaning is this: The wandering, which was self-established, was prohibited by the fear of dogs. Now the absence of the prohibitor of that prohibited wandering is being declared. Therefore this is a counter-exception (<s>pratiprasava</s>) — for that is the cancellation of a prohibition (<s>pratiṣedhanivartana</s>). Hence, since there is now no impediment to wandering, the absence of prohibition constitutes the injunction here, not an actual command.

Indeed, she is not like a queen issuing a positive command to wander, nor [is she issuing] a prohibition of wandering like the fear of dogs. Rather, she merely states the absence of the prohibitor of wandering. Consequently, the wandering enters into the category of that which is enjoined (<s>vidhīyamānatākoṭi</s>). Therefore this imperative (<s>loṭ</s>) is used in the sense of permission for unrestricted movement (<s>kāmacārābhyanujñārūpātisarga</s>), and this imperative also conveys timeliness (<s>prāptakālārtha</s>).

Now, wishing to establish the suggestedness (<s>vyaṅgyatva</s>) of the prohibition of wandering, he refutes its expressibility etc. — with '<s>tatra</s>...' etc.

'<s>Tatra</s>' — in such a statement.

Of the two meanings in the form of injunction and prohibition — 'wander!' and 'do not wander!' —

'<s>Yugapat</s>' — simultaneously.

[<s>Locana</s>] Not sequentially, because of the impossibility of a [second] operation after cessation (<s>viramya vyāpārābhāva</s>).

The impossibility of <s>abhidhā</s>'s operating after cessation is stated on the authority of [the maxim]: '<s>viśeṣyaṃ nābhidhā gacchet</s>' (denotation does not reach the qualified particular) etc.

'But the <s>tātparyaśakti</s> (intentional force), not having reached its culmination [merely in the injunction], produces — through the force of obstruction of the primary meaning (<s>mukhyārthabādha</s>) arising from the non-connection (<s>ananvaya</s>) of the meanings of the words like '<s>dṛpta</s>' (arrogant), '<s>dhārmika</s>' (pious), etc. [with a straightforward injunction], and through a contrary <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) occasioned by contradiction (<s>virodha</s>) — the cognition of prohibition that constitutes the sentence-meaning; and it does so from the standpoint of <s>abhihitānvaya</s> (post-denotative connection). Hence this meaning is rooted in word-power alone (<s>śabdaśaktimūla</s>). For the common usage is: "he said thus" (<s>evam anena uktam</s>).'

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>] That is not so — it is not expressibility (<s>vācyatā</s>), not something denoted (<s>abhidheyatā</s>).

Here the reason is — '<s>bhāva</s>...' etc. — Just as a pot and its absence are contradictory, so too are those two [injunction and prohibition] contradictory — this is the meaning. Since, being contradictory, they cannot simultaneously enter the path of cognition (<s>yugapadbuddhipathānārohitvāt</s>).

'Not sequentially (<s>na krameṇa</s>)' — '<s>vācyatā</s>' (expressibility) is to be construed [from above].

Here he states the reason — 'because of the impossibility of operating after cessation (<s>viramya vyāpārābhāvāt</s>).'

The meaning is: because <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) cannot operate again after having ceased (<s>viramya punaḥ sambhavābhāvāt</s>). Since a single word, having made one meaning known through denotation, does not then make another meaning known through it again — therefore [sequential expression is also impossible].

Here he cites the authority — '<s>viśeṣyam</s>...' etc.

By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the [maxim] '<s>kṣīṇaśaktir viśeṣaṇe</s>' (the power is exhausted in the qualifier) is included.

<s>Abhidhā</s> — the denotation of words like '<s>go</s>' (cow) etc. The qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>) is the universal such as <s>gotva</s> (cowness) in its meaning. '<s>Kṣīṇā</s>' means: ceased (<s>viratā</s>). '<s>Śakti</s>' means: the capacity to generate cognition (<s>bodhajananasāmarthya</s>) — [denotation] being in that state. The qualified (<s>viśeṣya</s>) is the particular individual (<s>vyakti</s>) in the form of a cow etc. '<s>Na gacchet</s>' — it would not make [it] known — this is the meaning.

And therefore, only one of injunction and prohibition can be denoted — this is the import.

'If so, then let there be cognition of prohibition alone here' — [the opponent] objects: '<s>nanu</s>...' etc.

Wherever there is <s>tātparya</s> (intentional purport), that indeed is the sentence-meaning. And the object of <s>tātparya</s> here is the prohibition of wandering. Therefore that alone is the sentence-meaning — because it is intended (<s>vivakṣita</s>).

'<s>Aparyavasitā</s>' — not having reached its culmination in the injunction of wandering.

<s>Tātparyaśakti</s> — the power in the form of <s>tātparya</s>, i.e., the capacity residing in words (<s>padaniṣṭhā</s>) to generate cognition of the intended meaning (<s>vivakṣitārthapratītijananasāmarthya</s>).

It produces the cognition of the prohibition that has become the sentence-meaning.

'By what operation?' — to this he says: 'by <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication).'

He states the ground for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — '<s>virodha</s>...' etc. — meaning: through a relation in the form of contradiction (<s>virodharūpasambandhanimittayā</s>).

He demonstrates the obstruction of primary meaning as stated in '<s>vācyārthasya ca vākyārthe sambandhānupapattitaḥ</s>' (because of the impossibility of connecting the expressed meaning with the sentence-meaning) — '<s>dṛpta</s>...' etc.

If the primary meaning of '<s>bhrama</s>' (wander!) were [simply] injunction, the mention of arrogance (<s>dṛptatva</s>) etc. would be pointless (<s>vaiyarthya</s>). The non-connection (<s>ananvaya</s>) — i.e., the impossibility of syntactic connection (<s>anvayopapattyabhāva</s>) — of the primary meaning in the form of an injunction to wander with the sentence-meaning composed of the meanings of words like '<s>dṛpta</s>' (arrogant), that constitutes the obstruction of primary meaning (<s>mukhyārthabādha</s>), and by its force, i.e., with its assistance — this is the meaning.

'<s>Abhihitānvayadaśā</s>' — meaning: from the perspective of <s>abhihitānvaya</s> (the theory of post-denotative connection). That is: in accordance with the view of the <s>Abhihitānvayavādins</s>.

He states the conclusion — '<s>iti</s>...' etc.

'Rooted in word-power (<s>śabdaśaktimūla</s>)' — <s>śabdaśakti</s> is <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation); what is rooted in it [is the meaning]. The import is: because <s>tātparyaśakti</s> and <s>lakṣaṇāśakti</s> have their ground in <s>abhidhā</s>.

As will be stated: '<s>abhidhāpucchabhūtā lakṣaṇā</s>' (indication is an appendage of denotation).

'That meaning (<s>so'rthaḥ</s>)' — meaning: the prohibition of wandering.

[<s>Locana</s>] Here the authority [cited against the above view is]: 'there is another meaning beyond the expressed.' This is not correct; for three operations (<s>vyāpāra</s>) are cognized here — the operation of <s>abhidhā</s> with respect to word-meanings in their universal aspect (<s>sāmānyātman</s>); for <s>abhidhā</s> is the capacity to convey meaning in dependence upon convention (<s>samaya</s>). And convention extends only to that much [the universal], not to the particular aspect, because of [the particulars'] infinity (<s>ānantya</s>) and because a single [convention] would be deviant (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). Then, with respect to the sentence-meaning which has the form of the particular — the mutually connected [meanings] — there is <s>tātparyaśakti</s>, according to the maxim: '<s>sāmānyāny anyathāsiddher viśeṣaṃ gamayanti hi</s>' (universals, because they would otherwise be unestablished, do lead to the particular).

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>] He says — '<s>evam</s>...' etc.

'<s>Uktam iti hi vyavahāraḥ</s>' (for the usage is "he said thus") — the import is: but the usage is not '<s>vyañjitam</s>' (he suggested).

He concludes — '<s>tat na</s>...' etc.

'Beyond the expressed' (<s>vācyātiriktaḥ</s>) means: beyond what is denoted (<s>abhidheyātiriktaḥ</s>).

'The cognition of prohibition through contrary <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is not possible here, since there is no scope for it (<s>anavakāsa</s>)' — with this intent, he refutes this view — '<s>na etat</s>...' etc.

'This is not so' — meaning: this view is not correct.

'Why?' — to this he says: '<s>traya</s>...' etc.

'<s>Atra</s>' — in common usage (<s>lokavyavahāra</s>).

Three operations — <s>abhidhā</s>, <s>tātparya</s>, and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>.

'Of the word (<s>śabdasya</s>)' — this is to be supplied.

'<s>Saṃvedyante</s>' — are cognized (<s>jñāyante</s>).

He states the domain of the first operation — '<s>padārtheṣu</s>...' etc.

'<s>Sāmānyātmasu</s>' — in [meanings] whose nature is the universal, i.e., having the form of universals like <s>gotva</s> (cowness) etc.

'<s>Abhidhāvyāpāra</s>' (the operation of denotation) — the remainder is: 'of words like <s>go</s> (cow) etc.'

He states its nature — '<s>samaya</s>...' etc.

'<s>Samayāpekṣayā</s>' — with the assistance of the apprehension of convention (<s>saṅketagrahaṇasahakāreṇa</s>).

There is also the reading '<s>samayāpekṣe</s>' — meaning: that which requires (<s>apekṣate</s>) convention, i.e., the apprehension of convention.

'<s>Arthāvagamanaśakti</s>' — the capacity to make meaning known (<s>arthabodhanasāmarthya</s>).

'<s>Tāvatyeva</s>' — only in word-meanings that have the nature of universals.

He states what the restrictive particle '<s>eva</s>' excludes — '<s>na</s>...' etc.

'In the particular aspect (<s>viśeṣāṃśe</s>)' — in [the domain of] the individual (<s>vyaktyātman</s>).

'Why?' — to this he says: '<s>ānāntyāt</s>...' etc. — because of the infinity (<s>anantatva</s>) of the particular aspects — this is the meaning.

And thus, convention cannot be established for every particular. And it would be infinite — this is the import.

He states another reason — '<s>vyabhicārāt ca ekasya</s>...' etc.

Because of the deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) of each individual particular from one another — this is the meaning. The deviation is to be understood thus: the convention present in whichever particular cow-individual is cognized by the word '<s>go</s>' does not hold for other cow-individuals.

Alternatively — in '<s>samayaś ca</s>,' the word '<s>samaya</s>' means apprehension of convention (<s>saṅketagraha</s>). He states the defect if the apprehension of convention were required for usage in every particular — '<s>ānāntyāt</s>...' etc. — meaning: since the particulars are infinite, apprehension of convention in every particular is impossible.

'Then let convention-apprehension in just one particular be the basis for usage' — to this he says: '<s>vyabhicārāt ca ekasya</s>...' etc. — meaning: because even for a particular cow-individual whose convention has not been apprehended, cognition arises from the word '<s>go</s>' etc., therefore convention-apprehension is deviant there.

Now he shows the second operation along with its domain — '<s>tataḥ</s>...' etc.

'<s>Tataḥ</s>' — from the stated reason.

'<s>Parasparānvite</s>' — mutually connected through the force of syntactic expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), in the relation of principal and subordinate (<s>guṇapradhānabhāva</s>).

'Having the form of the particular (<s>viśeṣarūpe</s>)' — composed of the particulars (<s>vyakti</s>) that are implied by the word-meanings having the nature of universals.

'In the sentence-meaning (<s>vākyārthe</s>)' — in the domain.

'<s>Tātparyaśakti</s>' — the power of <s>tātparya</s>: that which is to be principally communicated is <s>para</s>; those [words] that have that as their principal object are <s>tatpara</s>; the state of being such is <s>tātparya</s>; the power of that nature — the remainder is: 'of the words.'

Raising an objection, he says — '<s>sāmānyāni</s>...' etc.

Universals (<s>sāmānyāni</s>) — the meanings of universal nature expressed by words — if particulars were otherwise not cognized, then because of the non-establishment (<s>asiddhi</s>) [of syntactic connection] with the action etc., they lead to the particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>), i.e., the individual form that is their substrate, because of their inseparability (<s>svāvinābhāva</s>) [from particulars] — they cause [it] to be known.

[<s>Locana</s>] In the reading '<s>sāmānyāny anyathā</s>' — and there, in the second level [of operation], nothing is cognized from '<s>bhrama</s>' (wander!) beyond the injunction, since only the mere syntactic connection (<s>anvayamātra</s>) is comprehended.

For it is not [the case] that, just as in '<s>gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>' (the village is on the Ganges) or '<s>siṃho baṭuḥ</s>' (the boy is a lion), the syntactic connection, even as it seeks to come into being, is obstructed due to the absence of logical fitness (<s>yogyatāviraha</s>); similarly [here]: 'your prohibitor of wandering, that dog, has been killed by a lion.'

Now then, because of the absence of any deficiency in the cause of prohibition of wandering (<s>bhramaṇaniṣedhakāra</s>), wandering is appropriate for you — [yet] there is no harm whatsoever to the syntactic connection (<s>anvaya</s>).

For this very reason, obstruction of primary meaning (<s>mukhyārthabādha</s>) is not to be suspected here — hence there is no occasion for contrary <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (<s>viparītalakṣaṇā</s>).

Let that [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] be granted. Even so, it does not enter the second level (<s>dvitīyasthānasaṅkrānta</s>) — [that is, it is not situated within the domain of <s>tātparyaśakti</s>].

For thus: <s>Lakṣaṇā</s> is occasioned when there is obstruction of primary meaning (<s>mukhyārthabādha</s>). And obstruction is nothing other than the cognition of contradiction (<s>virodhapratīti</s>). But here there is no contradiction of the word-meanings with themselves (<s>svātmani</s>).

If [you say] the contradiction is mutual (<s>parasparaṃ virodhaḥ</s>) — then this contradiction must be apprehended in the syntactic connection (<s>anvaya</s>).

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>] 'Of the words (<s>padāni</s>)' is to be supplied.

'Of the universals (<s>sāmānyānām</s>)' — of the meanings that have the form of the universals expressed by them — because of [their] inseparability (<s>avinābhāva</s>) — this is the meaning.

Having thus prepared the ground, he begins to refute <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — '<s>tatra ca</s>...' etc.

'<s>Tatra</s>' — in what constitutes the domain of <s>tātparyaśakti</s>.

'In the second level (<s>dvitīyakakṣyāyām</s>)' — in the second level relative to the domain of the operation of <s>abhidhā</s>.

From '<s>bhrama</s>...' etc. as expressed, only the injunction of wandering is cognized — nothing else in the form of prohibition — this is the meaning.

'<s>Anvayamātrasya</s>' — meaning: of merely the sentence-meaning (<s>vākyārthamātra</s>).

The particle '<s>eva</s>' serves to make clear the meaning of the word '<s>mātra</s>' (mere).

What is excluded by this — 'beyond the injunction (<s>vidhyatirikta</s>)' etc. — is to be understood from what was said earlier.

'<s>Pratipannatvāt</s>' — because it is already known (<s>jñātatvāt</s>).

He substantiates what was stated — '<s>na hi</s>...' etc.

'There is no harm to the syntactic connection' — this is the syntactic connection [of the passage].

'<s>Gaṅgāyām</s>...' etc. is an example by way of dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>).

'<s>Anvaya</s>' means: the syntactic connection of the expressed meaning with the qualified entity (<s>vācyavarmiṇoḥ anvaya</s>).

'<s>Bubhūṣan</s>' — even as it is about to come into being, even as it has begun to be.

'<s>Pratihanyate</s>' — is obstructed (<s>bādhita</s>).

'<s>Yogyatāvirahāt</s>' — because of the absence of logical fitness; meaning: because of the non-existence of a relation such as container-and-contained (<s>ādhārādheyabhāvasambandha</s>) between the qualified entity denoted by words like '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' (i.e., the river) and [something like] a village (<s>ghoṣa</s>).

'<s>Kṣati</s>' means: obstruction (<s>bādhā</s>).

He states the conclusion — '<s>ata eva</s>...' etc.

'For this very reason' — precisely because there is no harm to the syntactic connection.

Now, intending to demonstrate the operation of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) in the domain where <s>lakṣaṇā</s> serves no purpose, and refuting — even after conceding <s>lakṣaṇā</s> for argument's sake — its placement in the level maintained by the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (opponent), namely the level of <s>tātparyaśakti</s>, he says — '<s>bhavatu vā</s>...' etc.

'<s>Asau</s>' — that <s>lakṣaṇā</s>.

'<s>Dvitīyasthānasaṅkrāntā</s>' — meaning: situated within the level of <s>tātparya</s>.

'<s>Tāvat</s>' is used in the sense of provisional acceptance (<s>sampratipatti</s>), or [merely] as a sentential ornament (<s>vākyālaṅkāra</s>).

He substantiates this very point — with '<s>tathā hi</s>...' etc.

'<s>Lakṣaṇāyāḥ praklṛpti</s>' — meaning: the postulation of the apprehension of the indicated meaning (<s>lakṣyārthopasthitikalpana</s>).

'<s>Bādhā ca</s>' — meaning: and the concept of obstruction (<s>bādhāpadārtha</s>).

In some readings: '<s>sā ca</s>.'

'<s>Virodhapratītir eva</s>' — meaning: obstruction of primary meaning (<s>mukhyārthabādhā</s>) is nothing other than the cognition of the contradiction (<s>virodha</s>) of the primary meaning — this is the meaning.

With the particle '<s>eva</s>' he shows that there is no dispute on this point.

Having kept in mind the alternative — whether the contradiction of the word-meanings is with themselves or mutual — he addresses the first — '<s>na ca</s>...' etc.

'<s>Ca</s>' is used in the adversative sense (<s>tu</s>).

'<s>Atra</s>' — in this case involving <s>lakṣaṇā</s>.

The connection is: '<s>atra virodhas tu padārthānāṃ svātmani na</s>' (but here there is no contradiction of word-meanings with themselves).

'<s>Svātmani</s>' — with itself (<s>svena saha</s>).

He raises the second [alternative] as an objection — '<s>parasparam</s>...' etc.

'Of the word-meanings (<s>padārthānām</s>)' is carried over.

[<s>Locana</s>] He resolves — '<s>so'yam</s>...' etc. But the cognition of contradiction does not arise when the syntactic connection (<s>anvaya</s>) has not been apprehended. And the apprehension of syntactic connection is not through the power of <s>abhidhā</s>, since that power is exhausted (<s>upakṣīṇā</s>) in the apprehension of word-meanings and cannot operate again after cessation (<s>viramya</s>). Therefore, the apprehension of syntactic connection is through <s>tātparyaśakti</s> alone.

'But if so, [even in the case of] "a hundred elephants on the fingertip" (<s>aṅgulyagre karivaraśatam</s>)...' — however, that syntactic connection is refuted (<s>bādhita</s>) by another means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇāntara</s>) such as perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) — just as silver [appears] in a shell [that is already recognized] — and hence the statement that generates that [false] cognition lacks validity (<s>aprāmāṇya</s>).

In '<s>siṃho māṇavakaḥ</s>' (the boy is a lion), after the emergence of the obstruction of the syntactic connection delivered by the <s>tātparyaśakti</s> situated in the second level, distinct from the two powers of <s>abhidhā</s> and <s>tātparya</s> —

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>] 'Then, that [third power] is well-known as having <s>lakṣaṇā</s> as its basis (<s>lakṣaṇamūlatva</s>).'

'This contradiction that you accept' —

'In the syntactic connection (<s>anvaye</s>)' — in the mutual connection of word-meanings (<s>parasparānvaye</s>) — 'is to be apprehended (<s>pratyeya</s>),' i.e., must be known.

'<s>Na ca</s>...' etc.

'<s>Apratipanne</s>' — when [the syntactic connection] is not yet known.

The construal is: '<s>virodhapratītir na ca</s>' (there is no cognition of contradiction [when the syntactic connection is not apprehended]). The import is: when the qualified entity (<s>dharmin</s>) is not cognized, the cognition of a property (<s>dharma</s>) such as contradiction cannot occur there.

'Then let it [be cognized when the syntactic connection] is apprehended' — to this he says: '<s>pratipattiś ca</s>...' etc.

'<s>Avyāpārāt</s>' — meaning: because of the impossibility of operation (<s>vyāpārāsambhavāt</s>).

The obstruction of primary meaning (<s>mukhyārthabādhā</s>) at the locus of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, as in '<s>siṃho māṇavakaḥ</s>' (the boy is a lion) etc., is the cognition of contradiction (<s>viruddhatva</s>) in the syntactic connection — namely, the connection in the form of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) etc. appearing due to syntactic expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) and <s>tātparya</s> between the primary meaning of the word '<s>siṃha</s>' (lion) etc. and the meaning of the word '<s>māṇavaka</s>' (boy) etc.

And the contradiction in that connection is the state of being refuted (<s>bādhitatva</s>), consisting in the absence of both: the counter-positive relation with '<s>siṃha</s>' etc. and the correlate relation with '<s>māṇavaka</s>' etc.

For this very reason, some [scholars] also [explain contradiction as] the absence of the speaker's intention (<s>vaktṛvivakṣitatvābhāva</s>).

And there is the import: even when the certainty of obstruction exists, cognition generated by the sentence does arise.

Incidentally, [the opponent] raises a doubt — '<s>nanu evam</s>...' etc.

'Thus' — if [we] accept that syntactic connection, even when obstructed, is cognized from the sentence.

He resolves [the difficulty] by pointing out an undesirable consequence — '<s>kim</s>...' etc.

'<s>Kim na bhavati</s>' — it does happen indeed.

He gives an example by way of dissimilarity — '<s>daśa</s>...' etc.

'<s>Daśa dāḍimāni ṣaḍ apūpāḥ</s>' (ten pomegranates, six cakes) — meaning: as in the case cited in the <s>Mahābhāṣya</s> where [multiple unconnected sentences are juxtaposed]. There, even though cognition of the syntactic connection of each individual sentence — 'ten pomegranates' etc. — arises through supplying the verb 'exist' (<s>bhavatikriyādhyāhāra</s>), the syntactic comprehension (<s>anvayapratīti</s>) in the form of a single unified qualified meaning (<s>ekaviśiṣṭārthabodha</s>) that encompasses the mutual connection of all the sentence-meanings does not arise, because of the absence of causes such as syntactic expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>). But in the present case, since those [causes] are present, the syntactic comprehension does arise — this is the meaning.

He states the distinction — '<s>kim tu</s>...' etc.

The connection is: 'that syntactic connection, even though apprehended (<s>pratipanna</s>), is refuted by another means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇāntara</s>) such as perception — just as silver in a shell (<s>śuktikāyāṃ rajatam iva</s>).'

'<s>Iti</s>' is used in the causal sense — meaning: because the syntactic connection is refuted.

Of that [sentence] — the non-validity [follows].

'But then, even for "<s>siṃho māṇavakaḥ</s>" (the boy is a lion) etc., there would be non-validity' — to this he says: '<s>siṃha</s>...' etc.

When the syntactic connection delivered (<s>samarpita</s>) by [<s>tātparya</s>]<s>śakti</s> is cognized, the emergence (<s>ullāsa</s>) of contradiction which is the obstructor — after that —

'<s>Tadvādhaka-vidhurīkaraṇa</s>' (the neutralization of that obstructor) —

[<s>Locana</s>] Then a third power indeed (<s>tṛtīyā eva śaktiḥ</s>), skilled in neutralizing that obstructor (<s>tadvādhaka-vidhurīkaraṇa-nipuṇā</s>), called <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication), comes into play (<s>samullasati</s>).

'But if so, even in "<s>siṃho vaṭuḥ</s>" (the student is a lion), there would be the nature of poetry (<s>kāvyarūpatā</s>); because the essence called <s>dhvanana</s> (suggestion) exists there too, as will be stated immediately after.'

'But then even in a pot there would be the designation of a living being; because the self (<s>ātman</s>), being all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>), exists there too.'

'It is only in the body, which possesses a distinguished substrate (<s>viśiṣṭādhiṣṭāna</s>), that, given the reality of the self, the designation of a living being applies — not in just anything' — if [you say] this, [then similarly:] it is only in [a composition] whose body consists of word and meaning made beautiful by the propriety of <s>guṇa</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornaments), given [the presence of] the essence called <s>dhvanana</s>, that the designation of poetry applies.

And just as the self is not rendered worthless by its association with worthless [things] like pots — this is equally [applicable] [i.e., <s>dhvanana</s> is not rendered worthless by its presence in ordinary speech].

'But then <s>bhakti</s> (indication/metaphor) alone would be <s>dhvani</s>' — anticipating this, he responds: '<s>na ca evam</s>...' etc.

'<s>Evam</s>' — when <s>dhvanana</s> is present at the locus of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>.

The construal is: '<s>dhvanir na ca</s>' (it is not <s>dhvani</s>).

Here he states the reason — '<s>bhaktir hi</s>...' etc. — because the two [<s>bhakti</s> and <s>dhvani</s>] are situated in different levels (<s>bhinnakakṣyāniviṣṭatva</s>), their domains differ — therefore, this is the meaning.

For <s>bhakti</s> (indication) is the operation of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, which occupies the third level. But the operation of <s>dhvanana</s> (suggestion) [belongs to] the fourth level.

For thus: 'You yourselves state that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> operates when the three [conditions] are present' — the three being [mukhyārthabādha etc.].

'<s>Tatra</s>' — among those [three conditions].

'The obstruction of primary meaning (<s>mukhyārthabādhā</s>) is, to begin with, based on another means of valid knowledge such as perception (<s>pratyakṣādipramāṇāntaramūlā</s>).'

And the ground (<s>nimitta</s>) that is stated — proximity (<s>sāmīpya</s>) etc. — is also cognizable only through another means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇāntarāvagamyam</s>).

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>] '<s>Nipuṇā</s>' — skilled, capable (<s>samarthā</s>) in neutralizing [the obstructor].

'<s>Samullasati</s>' — comes into operation (<s>pravartate</s>).

And thus, in that [domain of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>], the indicated meaning (<s>lakṣyārtha</s>) is not obstructed — this is the import.

Anticipating an over-extension if <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is accepted — '<s>nanu evam</s>...' etc.

The connection is: 'because of the existence (<s>satva</s>) of the self [called <s>dhvanana</s>] there too.'

He responds with a counter-example — '<s>nanu ghaṭe'pi</s>...' etc.

He states the resolution — '<s>śarīrasya</s>...' etc.

'<s>Viśiṣṭa</s>' — the substrate (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), i.e., the bodily form (<s>saṃsthāna</s>), distinguished by limbs such as hands and feet — of [a body] possessing that.

He says 'the same reply [applies] to us' — '<s>guṇa</s>...' etc.

The body of [poetry] consists of word and meaning (<s>śabdārtha</s>) made beautiful (<s>sundara</s>) by the propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) of <s>guṇa</s>s and <s>alaṅkāra</s>s — of that [body], with respect to <s>rasa</s>.

'<s>Na ca</s>...' etc. — '<s>iti ca samānam</s>' (and this is equal) — just as the self is not rendered worthless (<s>asāratā</s>) by its connection with worthless things like pots, similarly, the essence called <s>dhvanana</s> is not rendered worthless by its presence in ordinary speech — this is the meaning.

Anticipating 'But then <s>bhakti</s> (indication) itself would be <s>dhvani</s>,' he responds — '<s>na ca evam</s>...' etc.

'<s>Evam</s>' — when <s>dhvanana</s> is present at the locus of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>.

The construal is: '<s>dhvanir na ca</s>' (it is not <s>dhvani</s>).

Here he states the reason — '<s>bhaktir hi</s>' — because the two belong to different levels (<s>bhinnakakṣyāniviṣṭatva</s>), their domains differ — therefore, this is the meaning.

'<s>Tritayasannidhau</s>' — meaning: when the three [conditions] — obstruction of primary meaning etc. — are present.

'You yourselves state (<s>bhavanta eva vadanti</s>)' — meaning: it is you who say this, you who assert the non-difference of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> and <s>dhvanana</s>.

There is also the reading: '<s>bhavatāṃ matam</s>' (this is your view).

Wishing to establish that the last of the three [conditions] — obstruction of primary meaning etc. — is cognizable only through the operation of <s>dhvani</s>, he first states the cognizability of the first two through other means — with '<s>tatra</s>...' etc.

'<s>Abhidhīyate</s>' — meaning: it is stated in statements such as '<s>abhidheyena sāmīpyādi</s>' (proximity to the denoted meaning, etc.).

Having thus stated that the obstruction and the ground [for <s>lakṣaṇā</s>] have their basis elsewhere, he states that the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) does not have its basis elsewhere, by describing its nature — '<s>yat tu</s>...' etc.

[<s>Locana</s>] 'But that which is the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) — the supreme purity (<s>atipavitratvā</s>), coolness (<s>śītalatva</s>), worthiness of resort (<s>sevyatva</s>), etc. of the village — which is not expressible by any other word (<s>aśabdāntaravācya</s>) and not cognizable by any other means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇāntarāpratipanna</s>) — or the exceeding valor (<s>parākramātiśayaśālitva</s>) of the student — regarding that, the word certainly does have an operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>).

For thus: The inference "[the bank] possesses the qualities of <s>Gaṅgā</s> because of proximity to <s>Gaṅgā</s>" is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) [since skulls on the bank also have proximity but not purity]. And the reason "the student is expressible by the word '<s>siṃha</s>' (lion)" is unestablished in its own form (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>) [since the student is not literally denoted by '<s>siṃha</s>'].

If [one proposes] another inference: "Wherever there is such usage of a word [by <s>lakṣaṇā</s>], there is possession of the qualities [of the denoted entity]" — even for that, a fundamental means of valid knowledge must be cited at the time of ascertaining the universal concomitance (<s>vyāptigrahaṇa</s>), and there is none.

Nor is this [cognition] a memory (<s>smṛti</s>), for memory is impossible regarding what has not been previously experienced.'

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>] The connection is: '<s>yat tu atipavitratvādikaṃ parākramātiśayaśālitvaṃ vā tatra</s>' (regarding the supreme purity etc. or the exceeding valor...).

'Of the village (<s>ghoṣasya</s>)' — and this is said with the intent that, although the purity etc. pertains to the bank, the village too conveys it, because it is the ultimate object of <s>tātparya</s>.

Alternatively — '<s>ghoṣādhikaraṇasya</s>' — meaning: of that which has the village as its locus [i.e., the bank].

'<s>Aśabdāntaravācyam</s>' — not cognizable by any word other than the figurative word (<s>lākṣaṇikaśabda</s>).

'<s>Pramāṇāntara</s>...' — meaning: by a means of valid knowledge other than the word.

'<s>Vaṭoḥ</s>...' — the three words beginning with '<s>prayojana</s>' are to be carried over.

'But then, if the word too does not produce that cognition, then why search for another operation at all?' — to this he says: '<s>tatra</s>...' etc.

'<s>Tatra</s>' — regarding the aforementioned purpose.

He reinforces the statement that the word does have an operation there — with '<s>tathā hi</s>...' etc.

'<s>Tatsāmīpyāt</s>' — the bank [has qualities] like <s>Gaṅgā</s>, having the supreme purity etc., because of proximity to <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

'Like the community of sages etc.' — this is the inference — this is the meaning.

'<s>Anaikāntikam</s>' — deviant [i.e., inconclusive] in the case of skulls etc. found on the bank of <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

'<s>Siṃha</s>...' — the student possesses the qualities of a lion because of being expressible by the word '<s>siṃha</s>' — like one acknowledged to be a [real] lion — here the reason in the form of 'expressibility by the word <s>siṃha</s>' is unestablished in its own form (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>) — this is the meaning.

He raises and refutes another inference — '<s>atha</s>...' etc.

'<s>Evam</s>' — meaning: through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>.

'<s>Iti anumānam</s>' — the inference: 'The bank possesses the qualities of the entity denoted by the word "<s>Gaṅgā</s>," because it is the object of usage of the word "<s>Gaṅgā</s>" through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>; the student possesses the qualities of the entity denoted by the word "<s>siṃha</s>," because he is the object of usage of the word "<s>siṃha</s>" through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>; whoever is the object of usage of a word through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> possesses the qualities of the entity denoted by that word' — the application of the inference in this manner should be understood.

Alternatively — '<s>iti anumānam</s>' — meaning: a reason qualified by such a universal concomitance (<s>vyāptiviśiṣṭo hetuḥ</s>).

'<s>Tasyāpi</s>...' etc. — at the time of ascertaining the concomitance in that [inference].

'<s>Maulikam</s>' — meaning: serving as the basis (<s>mūla</s>), i.e., functioning as the instrument in the ascertainment of concomitance which is a component of inference.

'<s>Pramāṇāntaram</s>' — perception etc.

'<s>Na ca asti</s>' — '<s>pramāṇāntaram</s>' (another means of valid knowledge) is to be supplied.

In cases where concomitance depends on general induction (<s>sāmānyamukhavyāptyadhīna</s>), the ascertainment of concomitance between the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and <s>hetu</s> (reason) in question, or between those of the same type, through perception etc. must be cited. And that, at the locus of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, cannot arise because of the suspicion of deviation (<s>vyabhicāraśaṅkā</s>) — this is the meaning.

'<s>Na ca</s>...' — this cognition of the purpose such as purifying power (<s>pāvanatvādi</s>) —

[<s>Locana</s>] Because of the impossibility of ascertaining the rule (<s>niyamāpratipatti</s>), the undesirable consequence would arise that there is no determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) that 'this is what the speaker intends to convey (<s>vivakṣita</s>)' — [yet] there is certainly an operation of the word here.

And the operation is not in the form of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation), because of the absence of convention (<s>samayābhāva</s>).

Nor in the form of <s>tātparya</s>, because that [power] is exhausted in the cognition of syntactic connection (<s>anvayapratīti</s>) alone.

Nor in the form of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, for the very reason stated — because of the absence of halting movement (<s>skhaladgatitvābhāva</s>) [i.e., there is no stumbling of meaning that would trigger <s>lakṣaṇā</s>].

For even if halting movement were [accepted] in that case too, then the obstruction of primary meaning would be the ground [for <s>lakṣaṇā</s>], and the purpose [would need another <s>lakṣaṇā</s>], leading to infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>).

For this very reason, whatever has been named '<s>lakṣitalakṣaṇā</s>' (indication based on the already indicated) by certain [scholars] — that is mere verbal artifice (<s>vyasanamātra</s>).

Therefore, distinct from <s>abhidhā</s>, <s>tātparya</s>, and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, [there exists] a fourth [operation] —

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>] The construal is: '<s>smṛtir na ca</s>' (nor is this a memory). Meaning: this is not something cognized through memory.

Here he states the reason — 'because of the impossibility [of memory] regarding what has not been experienced (<s>ananubhūte tadayogāt</s>).'

'But perhaps that memory can somehow be made to work' — therefore he states another reason — '<s>niyama</s>...' etc.

Because of the impossibility of apprehending any determiner (<s>niyāmaka</s>), the undesirable consequence would arise that one cannot be certain that this purpose alone is intended here — this is the meaning.

The import is: if the operation of <s>vyañjana</s> (suggestion) is accepted, the determination will be established through the specific auxiliaries [of suggestion] (<s>sahakāriviśeṣa</s>).

He concludes — '<s>iti</s>...' etc.

'<s>Iti</s>' is used in the causal sense.

'Since the purpose cannot be otherwise cognized (<s>nānyagamya</s>), therefore' — this is the meaning.

'<s>Atra</s>' — in the purpose such as purifying power etc.

Then, in order to demonstrate the establishment of the operation of <s>vyañjana</s> (suggestion) by the method of elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>), he says — '<s>vyāpāraś ca</s>...' etc.

'<s>Atra</s>' is carried over.

'<s>Samayābhāvāt</s>' — because of the absence of convention (<s>saṅketa</s>) of words like '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc. with [meanings like] purifying power etc.

'<s>Anvayapratītau</s>' — meaning: in the primary cognition of the syntactic connection of the expressed meanings (<s>prāthamikavācyārthānvayabodha</s>).

'<s>Uktāt eva</s>...' etc. — the reason stated earlier is the obstruction of primary meaning etc. (<s>mukhyārthabādhādi</s>); therefore the halting movement (<s>skhaladgatitva</s>) — the stumbling, i.e., the obstruction of the cognitive operation (<s>avabodhanavyāpāra</s>) of the word whose movement is halting — the existence of that [condition] — the meaning is: the falling away from its own meaning (<s>svārthāt bhraṃśa</s>) — the absence of that — this is the meaning.

For words like '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc., just as there is a falling away from their own meaning (the river etc.) when they are made to convey the bank etc. through the force of obstruction of primary meaning, there is no such falling away from their own meaning (the bank etc.) when the purpose — purifying power etc. — is to be conveyed. Therefore [<s>lakṣaṇā</s> does not apply] — this is the meaning.

Alternatively — '<s>uktāt eva hetoḥ</s>' — from the very reason stated earlier, namely 'because of the impossibility of ascertaining the rule (<s>niyamāpratipatti</s>)' etc.

He also states another reason — '<s>skhaladgatitvābhāvāt</s>' (because of the absence of halting movement). The meaning of this should be understood as before.

Even accepting [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] for argument's sake, he states the defect — '<s>tatrāpi</s>...' etc.

Even if halting movement [away] from the indicated meaning (<s>lakṣyārtha</s>) is accepted on the basis of [needing to convey] the purpose, there would be an infinite regress of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (<s>lakṣaṇānavasthā</s>) through the repeated postulation of the ground of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — this is the meaning.

The passage from '<s>vyāpāraś ca nābhidhātmā</s>' etc. to this point is the commentary (<s>vivaraṇa</s>) on the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> passage: '<s>nābhidhā, samayābhāvāt</s>...' etc. — this should be understood.

'By the word "<s>Gaṅgā</s>" etc., once the bank etc. has been indicated through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, the purpose — purifying power etc. — would also have to be indicated [through another <s>lakṣaṇā</s>]. For this very reason, some [scholars] have given the name "<s>lakṣitalakṣaṇā</s>" (indication based on the already indicated) to the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> [that conveys] the purpose.'

He refutes that view — '<s>ata eva</s>...' etc.

'For this very reason' — precisely because of the defect of infinite regress etc.

'<s>Nāma kṛtam</s>' — the remainder is: 'of the operation concerning the purpose.' '<s>Vyasanamātra</s>' means: mere obstinacy (<s>dhvaninirākaraṇanirbanhamātra</s>) in rejecting <s>dhvani</s> — caused by that [attachment to one's own view].

As will be stated: '<s>tenāyaṃ lakṣatalakṣaṇāyā na viṣayaḥ</s>' (therefore this is not the domain of <s>lakṣitalakṣaṇā</s>).

'<s>Tasmāt</s>...' etc. — [Therefore, there exists a fourth verbal operation, distinct from <s>abhidhā</s>, <s>tātparya</s>, and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, namely <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion).]
Thus.
