children.translated_text: Now if it is said — the apprehension of the purport (<s>tātparya</s>) [occurs] instantly, as if seen directly; what can we do about that? —
This too we do not fail to accept.
As we shall state: "Just so, for those possessed of refined minds (<s>sacetasām</s>), whose inner nature is turned away from the [mere] sentence-meaning, that meaning —"
"— flashes forth instantly in the intellect that reveals reality (<s>tattvāvabhāsinī</s>)."

Therefore: the power of comprehending the expressed meaning (<s>vācyāvagamanaśakti</s>), which depends on convention (<s>samaya</s>), is the power of denotation (<s>abhidhāśakti</s>). The power of communicating the connected meaning (<s>arthāvabodhanaśakti</s>), which is assisted by the impossibility [of making sense] otherwise than through it [i.e., denotation], is the power of purport (<s>tātparyaśakti</s>). The power of making meaning appear (<s>arthapratibhāsanaśakti</s>), which depends on auxiliary conditions such as the obstruction of the primary meaning, is the power of secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇāśakti</s>). The power of illuminating meaning (<s>arthadyotanaśakti</s>), which is assisted by the creative intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) of the perceiver — who has been purified by the continuous appearance of the denoted and other meanings, [and this power] having arisen from the very root that is the comprehension of meanings generated by the triad of [those] powers — this is the operation of suggestion (<s>dhvananavyāpāra</s>). The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [explains]: '<s>sodara</s>' (cognate) — the meaning is: synonymous terms, i.e., words that are designations, by which [this operation] is determined, i.e., ascertained. The designation '<s>dhvanana</s>' etc. is well-known. And a designation does not subsist without a designatum — hence [the operation] is to be ascertained through the impossibility [of accounting for it] otherwise than by hearing [the designation]. This is the meaning. '<s>Abhyupagantavyaḥ</s>' (is to be accepted) — the completion is: 'even by one who is unwilling.' [The Locana says:] this is concerning the purpose, not the definition — to this he cites the root-text's agreement: '<s>yad vakṣyati</s>' (as he will say). Having thus established the <s>dhvanana</s> operation with respect to its purpose, in order to clarify it as distinct from the other three operations, he shows the essential nature of the operations — by '<s>tena</s>' etc. '<s>Samayāpekṣā</s>' — the meaning is: the power called <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) is the capacity, residing in the word, to convey that meaning, with the assistance of the apprehension of the convention (<s>saṅketa</s>) for that meaning. It should be understood that 'capacity' (<s>sāmarthya</s>) is another term for '<s>śakti</s>' (power), and is a distinct category of meaning. '<s>Tadanyathā</s>' — of that <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation); '<s>anyathā</s>' means 'without itself'; '<s>anupapatti</s>' means 'impossibility'; [the power] which is assisted by [the impossibility arising from] the absence of purpose etc. Some, however, explain: the impossibility that arises for that specific connected meaning (<s>anvitārtha</s>) in the absence of <s>tātparya</s> — [that impossibility] is its assistant. '<s>Artha</s>' — the meaning is: 'the combined meaning' (<s>saṃsṛṣṭārtha</s>). '<s>Mukhya</s>' etc. — the three [conditions] such as the obstruction of the primary meaning serve as auxiliaries; [the power] depends on those — thus [it is characterized]. '<s>Tacchakti</s>' etc. — '<s>tat</s>' refers to the previously mentioned triad of powers beginning with <s>abhidhā</s>; by that [triad], the comprehension (<s>avagama</s>, i.e., cognition) of the meanings — the word-meaning, sentence-meaning, and indicated meaning — has been generated, and from that very root it has arisen; by the continuous appearance (<s>pratibhāsa</s>) of those meanings such as the denoted etc., [the perceiver] who has been purified — i.e., possessing a surplus in the form of mental impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>). The <s>Locana</s> [says]: and that [operation of suggestion], superseding the preceding three operations, is primary, being the soul of poetry — with this intention, and also because the purposive [aspect] is also a domain of negation, inasmuch as the negation comes first [in the verse's meaning], it has been stated [thus]. And this has been stated merely by way of provisional acceptance (<s>abhyupagama</s>); there is no <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) here, because of the absence of both utter suppression [of the primary meaning] and transference to another [meaning]. For the operation of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> does not apply [when the suggestive function] is grounded in the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktimūla</s>). And the distinction of powers due to the distinction of auxiliaries is perfectly clear — just as, for the very same word, when assisted by the recollection of universal concomitance etc., there is the operation of causing inference; or when assisted by the sense-organs etc., there is the operation of generating determinate cognition. The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [explains]: '<s>sampādita</s>' — the <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuition) of the perceiver who has been prepared — that serves as assistant. '<s>Arthadyotanaśakti</s>' — the capacity for manifesting meaning characterized by purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) etc. The completion is: 'this has been stated.' Even granting such [an operation] exists — how can it alone be the soul of poetry? — to this he says '<s>sa ca</s>' etc. The particle '<s>ca</s>' is for emphasis. The connection is: '<s>sa ca kāvyātmā</s>' (and that is the soul of poetry). The reason here: '<s>pradhānabhūtaḥ</s>' (being primary). The reason for that: '<s>prāgvṛttam</s>' etc. — even though [the suggestive operation] operates after the triad of <s>abhidhā</s> etc., it makes them subordinate to itself — this is the meaning. Since the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) is the soul of poetry, the suggestive function (<s>vyañjanā</s>) too should be understood as having that status. Now, by this much it follows that the negation of wandering in '<s>abhrama dhārmike</s>' ('do not wander, O virtuous one') etc. is the domain of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, while the <s>vyañjanā</s> operation pertains to the other purposive content. How, then, did the <s>vṛttikāra</s>, by saying '<s>pratiṣedharūpa</s>' ('in the form of negation'), state that the <s>vyañjanā</s> operation has the domain of negation? — to this he says '<s>ityāśayena</s>' etc. The connection is: 'with the stated intention, "that which has purpose as its domain — even that, by the prominence of negation, has been stated as having negation as its domain."' '<s>Prayojana</s>' is the domain — the purpose here being the protection of the rendezvous-place of the wanton woman, her free roaming, etc. '<s>Niṣedhapramukhatayā</s>' — by having negation as the gateway of cognition. '<s>Ityuktam</s>' — the meaning is: by the [words] '<s>kadācid āvācye vidhirūpe pratiṣedharūpaḥ</s>' (sometimes in the non-expressible, that which has the form of injunction [is expressed] in the form of prohibition), this has been indicated. The negation of wandering here is indeed the indicated meaning (<s>lakṣya</s>). The stated purpose, being the object of cognition mediated by the cognition of negation, is called 'in the form of negation' — this is the meaning. He says — in reality, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> does not apply here, and [this is stated] in conformity with the <s>vṛtti</s> text: '<s>abhyupagama</s>' etc. '<s>Abhyupagamamātreṇa</s>' — merely by way of bold assertion (<s>prauḍhivāda</s>). This is by way of contrary indication (<s>viparītalakṣaṇā</s>). '<s>Niṣedhabodhanam</s>' — the communication of negation. He gives the reason for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> not applying here: '<s>atyanta</s>' etc. For where there is utter suppression of the expressed or transference to another [meaning], there <s>lakṣaṇā</s> [operates]. But neither of these applies to the expressed meaning in the form of the injunction of wandering — therefore [lakṣaṇā does not apply]. Now, let this be <s>dhvani</s> grounded in the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktim��la</s>); even there, why not <s>lakṣaṇā</s>? — to this he says '<s>na hi</s>' etc. '<s>Arthaśaktimūla</s>' — this contains the reason. The completion is: 'in <s>dhvani</s>.' '<s>Asyāḥ</s>' — the operation of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, i.e., its applicability. Moreover, the distinction of powers due to the distinction of auxiliaries is [already] stated — he says '<s>sahakāri</s>' etc. He clarifies the stated meaning with an illustration: '<s>yathā</s>' etc. '<s>Tasyaiva</s>' — of the very same [word] that has been employed for communicating meaning. '<s>Śabdasya</s>' — of a word like '<s>gām ānaya</s>' ('bring the cow') etc. '<s>Smṛtyādi</s>' — by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the knowledge of the property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharmatājñāna</s>) is included. '<s>Anumāpakatvavyāpāraḥ</s>' — the power of causing inference. The reasoning to be understood here is: 'this speaker intends this, because of his employment of this word,' etc. 'This has been stated in the third <s>uddyota</s>.' '<s>Akṣa</s>' etc. — '<s>akṣa</s>' means the eye and other sense-organs. By the word '<s>ādi</s>', the contact [of the organ with the object] etc. is included. The <s>Locana</s> [says]: this much is undeniable even for the proponents of <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (denotation of the connected sense). Even one who, as a proponent of <s>anvitābhidhāna</s>, grasps in his heart [the principle] 'the meaning of a word is that toward which the word is directed' and wishes the operation of denotation (<s>abhidhāvyāpāra</s>) to extend ever further like an arrow — if his [denotative] operation is long, then is it one [operation] or many? As for 'one' — how [can that be]? — because the domains are different. Now if 'many' — then, due to the difference in domains and auxiliaries, it is proper that [they be] of different kinds (<s>asajātīya</s>). And in the case of a homogeneous (<s>sajātīya</s>) effect, an operation that ceases [at its own domain] has been prohibited by the experts in word-meanings, the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others. And in the case of a heterogeneous [effect], it is precisely our position [that obtains]. The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [explains]: '<s>vikalpakatvavyāpāraḥ</s>' — the power of generating determinate cognition (<s>savikalpakajñāna</s>). For a word, when assisted by the ear etc., generates its own perception. And moreover, the perceived naming-word (<s>saṃjñāśabda</s>), at the time of visual contact etc. with the named object, generates the perception of the named object qualified by itself — this is a particular doctrinal view. '<s>Iyat</s>' — the meaning is: just this much, i.e., that there exists a <s>dhvanana</s> operation beyond the triad of <s>abhidhā</s> etc. '<s>Anapahnavanīya</s>' — undeniable; the purport is: rather, it is to be accepted. '<s>Yo 'pi</s>' etc. — the particle '<s>api</s>' has the sense of '<s>tu</s>' (but/however). The connection is: 'of him who wishes, [this follows].' [According to the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> theory:] the convention for each sentence is first grasped for each respective sentence-meaning; afterward, the convention of words like '<s>go</s>' (cow) etc. in their connected meanings is grasped through the method of agreement and difference (<s>āvāpodvāpa</s>) — this and other aspects of the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> doctrine should be noted from elsewhere. '<s>Yat paraḥ</s>' — that meaning which is <s>para</s>, i.e., the primary intended meaning, the object of <s>tātparya</s>, [pertaining to] which the word [is directed] — that is the <s>śabdārtha</s> (word-meaning). '<s>Śaravat</s>' — like the operation of an arrow. '<s>Icchati</s>' — as has been said: 'This is that long, long operation, like an arrow.' Just as an arrow propelled by an archer, through a single operation called velocity, performs multiple actions such as piercing the opponent's armor, penetrating the body, etc., so too a word employed by a skilled poet, through a single operation called denotation, generates cognitions of the word-meaning, sentence-meaning, and also those [meanings] intended as both the indicated and the suggested — this is the meaning. Having presented their view thus, in order to make even them accept <s>dhvanana</s>, he presents a dilemma — is that long denotative operation one or many? — and refutes the first alternative: '<s>tasya</s>' etc. The completion is: '<s>abhimata</s>' (accepted by you). The connection is: 'if that long operation accepted [by you] —'. '<s>Tat tarhi</s>' — then. '<s>Asau ekaḥ iti kutaḥ</s>?' — the meaning is: how can it be one? It cannot be one. The reason here: '<s>bhinna</s>' etc. — because [it has] different domains, i.e., the expressed meaning, etc. When the domains differ, the difference of the operation associated with them is also inevitable — this is the purport. He concedes the second [alternative] and refutes it: '<s>atha</s>' etc. '<s>Atha</s>' means 'if.' '<s>Tat tarhi</s>.' '<s>Viṣaya</s>' — the domains, i.e., the meanings accepted as expressed, indicated, and suggested. The <s>Locana</s> [says]: now, if what is meant by 'long, long' [operation] is this — that the meaning stationed at the fourth (final) level is itself directly denoted by the sentence — then, since no convention has been established for that [final meaning], how can there be direct comprehension? [The opponent replies:] 'Convention applies to the causes [i.e., word-meanings]; but that effect-meaning is independent of convention.' [The Locana responds:] 'Behold the rhetorical skill of the <s>Śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar)!' For that meaning which partakes of the final level — [the one] that first descended into the path of cognition — the subsequent word-meaning comprehensions are The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [explains]: the auxiliaries [are] convention, obstruction of primary meaning, the special quality of the speaker, etc. From their difference [comes the difference of powers]. '<s>Asajātīya</s>' means 'of different kind.' He establishes what was stated by showing the fault in [accepting] homogeneous [operations]: '<s>sajātīya</s>' etc. The carry-over from '<s>aneko 'sau</s>' (it is many) [gives]: 'when this operation is accepted as homogeneous and many.' But it [= the operation in a homogeneous effect] does not proceed — this is the completion. He gives the reason: '<s>kārye</s>' etc. '<s>Kārye</s>' — with respect to the effect. '<s>Padārthavidbhiḥ</s>' — by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others. Now, let it be heterogeneous — to this he says: '<s>asajātīye</s>' etc. When this [operation], being heterogeneous, is accepted as many — this is the meaning. '<s>Asmannaya eva</s>' — the purport is: since the distinction of operations is established, the <s>dhvanana</s> operation is [thereby] established. Or alternatively, the meaning of '<s>asajātīya</s>' etc. is this: moreover, considering the dilemma regarding the effect of the operation — whether the cognition of multiple meanings is homogeneous or heterogeneous to the [other cognitions] — he says '<s>sajātīya</s>' etc. '<s>Sajātīye kārye</s>' — with respect to that [homogeneous] effect. '<s>Vyāpāraḥ</s>' — [meaning] <s>abhidhā</s> etc. '<s>Niṣiddha</s>' — therefore, even in accepting a different operation, our position alone [holds]. '<s>Asajātīye</s>' — '<s>kārye</s>' carries over. '<s>Asmannaya eva</s>' — the purport is: since the effect is heterogeneous, the <s>dhvanana</s> operation is established because the heterogeneity of the causal operation is inevitable when the effect is heterogeneous. Now, if 'longness' of the operation does not mean either multiplicity or homogeneity, but rather the absence of any distinction in the immediacy of conveying the intended meaning — and therefore the suggested meaning is itself the domain of denotation — he raises this objection: '<s>atha</s>' etc. '<s>Atha</s>' means 'if.' The connection is: 'if this is what is meant [by "long"].' '<s>Caturtha</s>' — meaning: 'final.' '<s>Sa eva</s>' means 'even that [meaning].' He resolves [the objection]: '<s>tarhi</s>' etc. '<s>Tatra</s>' — in the meaning stationed at the final level. '<s>Sākṣāt</s>' — the meaning is: 'by denotation.' '<s>Katham</s>' — the completion is: 'does it occur?' — the meaning is: 'it does not occur.' Now, if one accepts the cause-effect relationship between word-meanings and sentence-meanings, then by grasping the convention for the word-meanings that serve as causes, by that alone — independently of any separate convention for the final sentence-meaning — the cognition of that sentence-meaning occurs through the denotative operation — [to] this objection he raises and refutes: '<s>nimitteṣu</s>' etc. '<s>Nimitteṣu</s>' — in the word-meanings [as causes]. '<s>Asau arthaḥ</s>' — the final sentence-meaning. '<s>Paśyata</s>' etc. — this is a mocking remark. The connection is: '<s>ityuktikauśalam</s>' ('such is the rhetorical skill'). '<s>Paryantakakṣyāyāḥ bhāgī</s>' — one who partakes of the final level, i.e., one who habitually shares in it. '<s>Paścāttanāḥ</s>' — [those comprehensions] occurring after the cognition of the sentence-meaning. The <s>Locana</s> [says]: 'They become causes' — surely the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>'s great-grandson intends the causal status [of word-meanings] with respect to [the final meaning]. Now it is said — 'Previously, the comprehension of one prepared by the grasping of convention occurs in that manner with respect to that [meaning]; by this factual situation, the word-meanings serve as causes' — then, nothing at all [in the opponent's account] would be useful for tracing [that causal connection]. Nor has convention-grasping occurred with respect to individual word-meanings [in isolation], since [words are] always used in connected [sentences]. [The opponent says:] 'Through the method of agreement and difference, the situation is established' — [we reply:] if convention is accepted as pertaining to word-meanings alone, then the specific cognition [of the connected meaning] is posterior [to that].
Thus. //

children.translated_text: When, for the purpose of protecting the rendezvous, through a pretext, at some point the expressible (<s>vācya</s>) has the form of a prohibition while [the suggested has] the form of an injunction — as in: "<s>Attā</s> (the mother-in-law) sleeps here; come, look at me during the day —"

children.text: mā pahia rattiandhaa sejjāe maha ṇimajjahisi //
children.translated_text: "Do not, O traveler, blind in the darkness of night, lie down with me on the bed!"

However, although the sequential order [of word-meaning cognitions leading to the suggested meaning] is conjecturable through superior practice and repeated cultivation, it is not perceived — because there is no successive arising of homogeneous mental representations (<s>vikalpa</s>) pertaining to it; just as the sequential order of the memory of the pervading relation (<s>vyāpti</s>) and the convention (<s>samaya</s>) regarding a well-practiced subject-matter [is not perceived]. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Padārthāvagamāḥ</s>' means cognitions of word-meanings. /
'Having cognized the great-grandson' etc. — the meaning is: taking the great-grandson as the cause (<s>nimitta</s>), one's own status as the caused (<s>naimittika</s>) would be intended. /
Now, even though the cognition of word-meanings is subsequent [to the convention-grasping], because the grasping of the convention pertaining to them has occurred previously, the designation of word-meanings as causes through that [convention] is not contradicted. /
For it is observed that for a cognizer who has grasped the convention, immediately upon hearing a sentence like '<s>gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>' ('the village is on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>'), the cognition of the ultimate meaning (<s>pāryantikārtha</s>) in the form of coolness, purity, etc. arises instantaneously — raising this objection, he resolves it with 'but it is said' etc. /
'In tracing that' — what is useful for tracing, i.e., accounting by one's own theory, for that cognition of the ultimate meaning. /
Alternatively: the purport is: in tracing that, how can there be comprehension of the word-meanings' ultimate meaning, which is not conventionally established? /
Moreover, even the grasping of convention with regard to word-meanings does not hold good antecedently — he says: 'nor even' etc. /
'Of those that are syntactically connected' — of those that convey connected meaning alone. /
'Of those that have attained the status of sentences' — this is the extent. /
He raises a doubt: 'acquisition' etc. /
'Such a state' — the occurrence of convention-grasping with respect to individual word-meanings separately. /
He resolves: 'convention' etc. /
'The specific cognition is subsequent only' — the sentence-meaning cognition occurs only subsequently, not at a prior time. This is the meaning. /
And thus your established doctrine would be contradicted. This is the purport. /
'Now' etc. — the cognition of purport (<s>tātparya</s>) is the cognition of the ultimate meaning. /
'What do we do here?' — the purport is: let the causal status of convention-grasping with respect to word-meanings obtain or not! /
If so, then what we desire is established — he says: 'therefore' etc. /
He states the specific point: 'but' etc. /
'Therein' — the meaning is: in the cognition of the suggested meaning in the form of the ultimate meaning. /
'Even though conjecturable' — even though ascertainable by a means of knowledge. /
'The sequential order' — the temporal priority and posteriority of word-meaning cognitions. /
The connection is with 'is not perceived.' /
Here he states the reason: 'homogeneous' etc. /
Homogeneous — homogeneous by virtue of being auxiliaries to sentence-meaning cognition — the mental representations pertaining to word-meanings. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] And the relation of cause and caused must necessarily be resorted to; otherwise, the difference of the metaphorical (<s>gauṇa</s>) and the indicated (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>) from the primary (<s>mukhya</s>), and the procedure of 'the relative strength and weakness of the six means of knowledge beginning with <s>śruti</s> and <s>liṅga</s>' etc. would be disrupted — because this [procedure] has been established precisely through the variety of causal relations. /
And once the variety of causal relations is accepted, what further objection is there against us? /
Even those who maintain that the sentence is an undivided <s>sphoṭa</s> and its meaning [likewise undivided] — even they, who have fallen into the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (conventional reality), must follow this entire procedure. /
But in the state of transcending that — 'everything is the non-dual <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Lord' — our treatise-author was well aware of this, as he composed the <s>Tattvāloka</s> treatise. But let that rest. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Of the succession' — the meaning is: because of the non-arising, i.e., the non-tracing [of the succession]. /
For sequential order is a property pertaining to two things standing in the relation of cause and effect; for its cognition, the cognition of those two is required. This is the purport. /
He states the reason for the non-arising: 'through superior' etc. /
The meaning is: from the repeated practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) of superior cultivation (<s>anuśīlana</s>), i.e., contemplation. /
For the non-apprehension even when the sequence exists, he gives an example: 'well-practiced' etc. /
The subject-matter that has been contemplated again and again — in which [there is practice]. /
Alternatively: the meaning is: just as in the case of a well-practiced subject-matter — a probative mark (<s>hetu</s>) like smoke, or an object like a cow — the memories of the pervading relation (<s>vyāpti</s>) [with fire, etc.] and the convention (<s>samaya</s>) [of the word 'cow'] respectively, and the sequential order of the inference and the verbal cognition [that follow from them] — just like that [the sequence here too is not perceived]. /
'<s>Iti</s>' etc. — '<s>Iti</s>' is in the sense of cause. The meaning is: for this reason. /
Because the sequential order depends on the cause-effect relation, and because that [relation] has been established — this is the extent. /
He states the necessity of resorting to the cause-effect relation by way of a <s>bādhaka</s> (counter-argument) from the opposing side: 'otherwise' etc. /
The connection is: 'otherwise... disruption of the procedure.' /
'Metaphorical' etc. — for in the cognition of the metaphorical and indicated meanings, the obstruction of the primary meaning is the cause (<s>nimitta</s>); and from that, it follows that with respect to the primary meaning, there is a fundamental cause. /
Without that, neither the obstruction nor the rule distinguishing primary from non-primary would be established. This is the meaning. /
Having stated the worldly procedure, he states the Vedic one: '<s>śruti</s>' etc. /
The word-meanings of <s>śruti</s> etc. and their illustrations are elaborated in texts like the <s>Āpodevīya</s>, <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>, etc. /
'How would the stated procedure be disrupted without resorting to the cause-effect relation?' — to this he says: 'of the causal' etc. /
'By the variety of causal status' — by the difference [of types]. /
'Of this procedure.' /
'Because it has been established' — /
And this variety of causal status would not be tenable if one accepts an infinitely extended denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>). This is the purport. /
[Objection:] Well then, let the cause-effect relation be various, so that this disruption of procedure does not occur! To this he says: 'of the causal' etc. /
The meaning is: once the variety of causal status is accepted, one must also accept the difference of operations (<s>vyāpāra</s>) — so what resentment is there against what we have said? /
'Even those who' etc. — the meaning is: the <s>sphoṭa</s>-theorists, i.e., the grammarians etc. /
'That <s>avidyā</s>' — the word '<s>avidyā</s>' [here refers to] the path of conventional reality (<s>vyavahāra</s>). /
'By our treatise-author' — by the master <s>Ānandavardhana</s>. /
'Was not unaware' — was indeed aware. /
Here the reason: 'as he composed the <s>Tattvāloka</s> treatise.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Now, as for what <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s> said — 'In the use of words like <s>dṛpta-siṃha</s> (fierce lion) etc. and the use of the word <s>dhārmika</s> (righteous one), the cognition of the prohibition is produced solely by the influence of the <s>bhayānaka-rasa</s> (terrible sentiment), since without the knowledge of the natural dispositions of the [respective characters] — such as the timidity [of the <s>dhārmika</s>] and the heroism [of the <s>siṃha</s>] — there would be no certainty of the cognition of prohibition' — that is not so, because the cognition of prohibition through mere capacity of meaning (<s>artha-sāmarthya</s>) alone is the cause. /
To this it is replied: 'Who has said that the cognition of prohibition [occurs] without the apprehension of the specific characteristics of the speaker and the cognizer, and without the suggestive operation (<s>dhvanana-vyāpāra</s>) residing in words?' /
For we have stated that the cooperation of the cognizer's sensitivity (<s>pratibhā</s>) is the life-breath of the luminous [function]. /
And the influence of <s>bhayānaka-rasa</s> is not denied, since we accept only the arising of fear as such [not its role as the primary cause]. /
And for the cognizer, the experience of <s>rasa</s> is through the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> alone. /
And <s>rasa</s> is indeed suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), and even he has not accepted that <s>rasa</s> is expressible by words. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'That which' etc. — He states the manner of the statement: 'here' etc. /
Here — in [examples beginning with] '<s>bhrama</s>' (wander) etc. /
The connection is: 'the cognition of the prohibition is produced solely by the influence of <s>bhayānaka-rasa</s>.' /
'From what [evidence]?' — to this he says: '<s>dṛpta</s>' (fierce) etc. /
The two seventh-case [endings] are with respect to the meaning in the form of the cause. /
The timidity of the righteous person, established through the rule of wandering for the purpose of killing a dog, [is required]; without it, the prohibition-meaning would not be established — hence '<s>dhārmika</s>' etc. is said. /
Even by that alone, only the rule of wandering near the house would be confirmed, not the relevant prohibition — hence '<s>dṛpta-siṃha</s>' etc. also. /
The particle '<s>eva</s>' (solely) shows the predominance of the <s>bhayānaka-rasa</s> influence in generating the cognition of prohibition. /
'Let the cognition of prohibition be through the suggestive operation alone — why is it construed thus?' — to this he says: 'of their' etc. /
'Of those two' — pertaining to the <s>dhārmika</s> and the lion. /
'The natural dispositions in the form of timidity and heroism' — knowledge of the invariable concomitance (<s>niyama</s>) of their natures. /
'Without' — in the absence of. /
'Categorically' — exclusively by some other cause, to the exclusion of that invariable concomitance. /
'Through the suggestive operation alone' — this is the extent. /
'Of the prohibition' — of the prohibition of wandering. This is the meaning. /
He states the conclusion: '<s>iti</s>' etc. /
'<s>Iti tat</s>' — the meaning is: for the stated reason. /
By the word '<s>kevala</s>' (mere), he shows that even the capacity of meaning retains its role as a cooperating cause. /
The connection is: '<s>iti yat tu uktam</s>' ('as for what was said'). /
Having heard '<s>tat na kevala</s>' etc., the <s>dhvani</s>-theorist, unable to tolerate it, says: 'who' etc. /
The connection is: 'who has said this?' Alternatively: '<s>etat</s>' is a component of the compound '<s>vaktṛ-pratipattṛ-viśeṣa</s>' etc. /
The two specifics of the speaker and cognizer that pertain to this sentence — i.e., the lover eager to protect the rendezvous-place, and the timid righteous person — in the absence of their apprehension, i.e., in the absence [of knowing them]. /
By the word '<s>viśeṣa</s>' (specific), the libertine nature pertaining to the speaker and the sensitivity (<s>pratibhā</s>) pertaining to the cognizer are intended. /
[Objection:] But you yourself have said [this]! — to this he says: 'of the cognizer' etc. /
Having conceded a certain aspect of what was said, he rejects the contradictory aspect: '<s>bhayānaka</s>' etc. /
'Is not denied' — the purport is: its mere existence [is accepted], but not its being the cause with respect to the cognition of prohibition. /
'How is there the influence of <s>bhayānaka-rasa</s> upon the [character] to be understood as righteous?' — to this he says: 'of that' etc. /
'Of that <s>bhayānaka-rasa</s> influence.' /
'Through the mere arising of fear' — the third case is because it [functions] like a natural disposition (<s>prakṛti</s>) etc. /
The meaning is: 'perceive that form [of mere fear].' /
By the word '<s>mātra</s>' (mere), the status of <s>rasa</s> is excluded. /
'Through acceptance' — through the acceptance by the person to be understood [i.e., the character]. /
'But then what about the sensitive reader (<s>sahṛdaya</s>)?' — he says: 'of the cognizer' etc. /
But for the cognizer, i.e., the sensitive reader, <s>rasa</s> is manifested (<s>abhivyajyate</s>), not produced. /
And through its manifestation, there is the experience of it. This is the meaning. /
'Even for the person to be understood, let there be the arising of <s>rasa</s> like fear — what need for the supposition of its manifestation?' — to this he says: 'and <s>rasa</s>' etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] [Because <s>rasa</s> has] the very nature of being suggested. /
Even for the cognizer, the experience of <s>rasa</s> is not invariable — for that sensitive reader is not necessarily a fellow-celibate who is timid and righteous. /
If even his specific characteristic is posited as a cooperating factor, then why is the suggestive operation — animated by the sensitivity of speaker and cognizer — not tolerated? /
Moreover, one who attacks <s>vastu-dhvani</s> (factual-content suggestion) thereby establishes <s>rasa-dhvani</s> (sentiment-suggestion) as what supports it — and so this is an even more thorough demolition of <s>dhvani</s>! /
As was said: '<s>krodho 'pi devasya vareṇa tulyaḥ</s>' ('Even the anger of the god is equal to a boon'). /
[Objection:] But it was said [by the verse] that the predominance belongs to <s>rasa</s> alone, not that <s>vastu-dhvani</s> is refuted. This is the meaning. /
He resolves: 'then' — /
'Who would not accept that?' — the purport is: the subordination of <s>vastu-dhvani</s> to <s>rasa-dhvani</s> is what we desire. /
Again he raises a doubt: 'but' etc. /
He resolves: 'even so' etc. /
'Let there be two <s>dhvanis</s>' — the optative is in the sense of permissive license. /
Here the reason: 'because it is a poetic example.' /
[Objection:] But permissive license is not appropriate, because <s>rasa</s> alone delights the sensitive heart! To this he says: 'but if' etc. /
'<s>Anuvedha</s>' means experience, immersion. /
'Is satisfied' — the remainder is: 'the sensitive reader.' /
In the reading '<s>tuṣyate</s>,' the remainder is: 'by the sensitive reader.' /
'In the stated manner' — the meaning is: in the manner previously stated, that a certain woman [considers] the rendezvous-place as [precious as] her very life. /
'Erotic desire' etc. — the rendezvous-place that is the <s>uddīpana-vibhāva</s> (stimulating determinant) of the desire for union; appropriate to that very desire, and distinctive — the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) such as vocal inflection (<s>kākū</s>) etc. that are consistent with union; by the word '<s>ādi</s>,' other contemporaneous gestures are to be included. /
The <s>śṛṅgāra-rasa</s> (erotic sentiment) that is manifested from the intermingling (<s>śabalana</s>) of those — its experience (<s>anuvedha</s>). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Because <s>rasa</s> is transcendent (<s>alaukika</s>), and because it cannot be comprehended from a mere [initial] illustration, and with the intention of first demonstrating the indisputably established and clearly discriminated assertion and prohibition [as instances of <s>vastu-dhvani</s>] — this was given as an illustration of <s>vastu-dhvani</s>. /
But one who, undertaking to explain <s>dhvani</s>, has declared that <s>dhvani</s> is nothing but the power of purport (<s>tātparya-śakti</s>), or nothing but the indicative capacity of intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>) — he does not win over our hearts. /
As they say: '<s>bhinnaruciḥ hi lokaḥ</s>' ('for the world is of diverse tastes'). /
We shall refute this in due course as appropriate — but let that rest for now. /
'<s>Bhrama</s>' (wander) — 'you are released, your time for wandering has arrived.' /
'<s>Dhārmika</s>' (righteous one) — 'your wandering is proper for the purpose of [gathering] flowers and other requisites [for worship].' /
'<s>Visrabdha</s>' (fearlessly) — because of the absence of any ground for apprehension. /
'<s>Sa</s>' (he) — his non-arising again [i.e., he is dead]. /
'By him' — 'he who was previously heard by you too, through rumor, to be dwelling in the thickets of the <s>Godāvarī</s> bank.' /
For previously, he [the lion] had been made known to that one [the righteous man] for the purpose of protecting the rendezvous-place; and he now — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] This is the meaning. /
The connection is with 'occupies the mirror of the sensitive heart.' /
In the stage of analysis, <s>bhayānaka-vibhāvas</s> etc. are not perceived here; rather, those pertaining to <s>śṛṅgāra</s> alone. This is the purport. /
[Objection:] But if <s>śṛṅgāra-dhvani</s> is the principal here, then why was this <s>gāthā</s> (verse) not given as its illustration? And [why] was it given as an illustration of <s>vastu-dhvani</s>? To this he says: 'of <s>rasa</s>' etc. /
'From a mere [initial] illustration alone' — from a mere illustration alone. /
'Because of the impossibility of comprehension' — because of the impossibility of comprehension. /
The purport is: because the knowledge of the nature of <s>rasa</s> is possible only through the arguments to be stated later. /
Some [interpret] '<s>tāvanmātrāt</s>' as 'from the world alone.' /
'Indisputably' — [that which is] indisputably established and discriminated, i.e., [having] the distinction of the assertion and prohibition. /
What has been said amounts to this: <s>rasa-dhvani</s> is what is intended to be established as the soul of poetry. /
But it is not established in the world by any means of knowledge, nor yet as the subject of poetic operation. /
Therefore, one who begins to establish it must first, as a preliminary, demonstrate <s>vastu-dhvani</s> etc. as indeed other than, i.e., distinct from, the expressed — and afterward, when the general notion of <s>dhvani</s> is indisputably established, <s>rasa-dhvani</s> should be directly defined and illustrated. /
'But one who' etc. — /
'Of intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>)' — of the intended meaning. /
'Indicative capacity' — the capacity to make one infer. /
'Does not win over' — the purport is: because it lacks reasoning. /
[Objection:] But nothing apart from these two has yet descended upon the path of [our] heart! To this he says: 'we shall refute this' etc. /
What was said [in the verse] — 'you are released, your time for wandering has arrived' — in accordance with this, conforming to the optative which [has the sense of] permission at the arrived time, he explains: '<s>bhrama</s>' etc. /
'<s>Sa</s>' (he) — [this word] has the sense of one previously experienced — he says: 'he who' etc. /
The word '<s>adya</s>' (today) illuminates the meaning 'previously fate was unfavorable, but now through the greatness of your good fortune, it has become favorable' — he says: '<s>diṣṭyā</s>' (by good fortune) etc. /
He shows the suggested meaning of '<s>mārita</s>' (killed) etc. with '<s>mārita iti</s>' etc. /
The word '<s>tena</s>' (by him) also has the sense of one previously experienced — he says: 'who previously' etc. /
The connection is: 'was heard to be dwelling.' /
[Objection:] But the libertine woman herself has superimposed the existence of a lion on the <s>Godāvarī</s> bank! Then how is it stated thus? — having explained this, he substantiates: 'previously indeed' etc. /
'For the protection of that' — for the purpose of protecting the rendezvous-place. /
'He was made known to that one by her.'

children.text: locana.m dṛptatvāttato gahanānnissaratīti prasiddhagodāvarītīraparisarānusaraṇamapi tāvatkathāśeṣībhūtaṃ kā kathā tallatāgahanapraveśaśaṅkayeti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Locana</s>: Because of its boldness, its emerging from the dense forest — even the mere following of the well-known banks of the <s>Godāvarī</s> has become a residual part of the story; what then of the fear of entering the thicket of creepers? — this is the purport.
"<s>Attā</s>" means:

children.text: śvaśrūratra śete athavā nimajjati atrāhaṃ divasakaṃ pralokaya /
children.translated_text: "The mother-in-law sleeps here" — or "is immersed [in sleep]"; "here, look at me during the day."
"Do not, O traveler, blind in the night, lie upon the bed of us two!"

children.translated_text: Because of being unsuitable for union — this is the meaning.

children.text: 'diasaam' ityasya kathaṃ prathamāntatayā vyākhyānamityata āha---prakṛta iti /
children.translated_text: How is "<s>diasaam</s>" explained as being in the nominative case? To that he says: "the subject at hand" (<s>prakṛta</s>) etc.

children.text: na copekṣe kvacidvācye vidhirūpe 'nubhayarūpo yathā--- vacca maha vvia ekkei hontu ṇīsāsaroiavvāiṃ /
children.translated_text: And when, at some point, the expressible has the form of an injunction, [the suggested is] of neither form — as in: "Let there be, O my child, for just one [night], sighs and tears to be wept —"

children.text: mā tujja vi tīa viṇā dakkhiṇṇahaassa jāantu //
children.translated_text: "Let there not arise for you too, O courteous one, [sighs and tears] without her!"

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "<s>Maha</s>" is a particle with multiple meanings; here it means "of us two" (<s>āvayoḥ</s>), not "of me" (<s>mama</s>). For thus, the specific wording itself would arouse suspicion, and the covert acceptance (<s>pracchannābhyupagama</s>) would not obtain. Having seen a certain young woman (<s>taruṇī</s>) whose husband was away (<s>proṣitapatikā</s>), with the sprout of desire fully grown (<s>pravṛddha-madanāṅkura</s>), the traveler — she accepts him through the mode of prohibition (<s>niṣedha-dvārā</s>); thus the absence of [real] prohibition here. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Previously, this incident about the wayward woman (<s>svairiṇī</s>) was brought to the ears of the righteous man through a friend etc. — this is the meaning. Now, if this is so, why did she say it herself? To that he says: "and he now" (<s>sa cādhunā tu</s>) etc. "He" (<s>saḥ</s>): the lion. "Emerges from the forest" — after this, "she was overheard by him" is the remainder. So that the righteous man might not have fear — with the introductory recollection beginning with "in the Gauda [country]" — the special features of the lion's boldness etc. are to be understood. This is the purport. He states the fruit of communicating the special feature — "well-known" (<s>prasiddha</s>) etc. "This is the purport" — "is to be understood" is the remainder. And these meanings serve as auxiliaries in the suggestion of the prohibition of wandering. The same should be understood further on as well. He shows the Prakrit "<s>ṇimajjai</s>" in two Sanskrit renderings — "sleeps" (<s>śete</s>) etc. "Having multiple meanings" (<s>anekārtha-vṛtti</s>): meaning having diverse applications. "For thus the covert acceptance would not obtain" — this is the connection. Here he states the reason — "specific" (<s>viśeṣa</s>) etc. "Suspicion" (<s>śaṅkā</s>): meaning suspicion regarding the mother-in-law etc. "Covert" (<s>pracchanna</s>): the purport is that without covertness, the acceptance would not produce the <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder) in connoisseurs. "A certain [woman]" etc.: meaning having observed through her demeanor that the young woman's husband was away. The connection is with "<s>sampanna</s>" (endowed/complete). "Fully grown" (<s>pravṛddha</s>): at the moment of seeing, the sprout of desire arose —
<s>Locana</s>: "Let us at least pass the day" — this is the meaning.

children.text: pratipannamātrāyāṃ ca rātrāvandhībhūto madīyāyāṃ śayyāyāṃ māṃ śliṣaḥ, api tu nibhṛtanibhṛtamevāttābhidhānanikaṭakaṃṇṭakanidrānveṣaṇapūrvakamitīyadatra dhvanyate /
children.translated_text: "And as soon as night falls, having become blind [in darkness], embrace me on my bed" — but [rather,] very quietly, with the pretense of seeking sleep near the pronouncement of the mother-in-law's name — this is what is suggested here.
"Go — let the sighs and weeping be mine alone!"

children.text: mā tavāpi tayā vinā dākṣiṇyahatasya janiṣata //
children.translated_text: "Let them not arise for you too, O one whose gallantry is destroyed, without her!"

children.text:
atra vrajeti vidhiḥ /
na pramādādena vāyikāntarasaṃgamanaṃ tava, api tu gāḍhānurāgāt, yenānyāddaṅmukharāgaḥ gotraskhalanādi ca, kevalaṃ pūrvakṛtānupālanātmanā dākṣiṇyenaikarūpatvābhimānenaiva bālapriyā iti sambandhaḥ /
pratipannamātrāyāmitir /
iṣadarthe mātrāśabdaḥ /
andhībhūto mā śilaṣa iti /
andhībhūtatvena śleṣaṇaṃ niṣidhyate, na tu śleṣaṇamātram /
atteti /
atta ityabhidhānaṃ yasya saḥ /
'dattāvadhāne'ti pāṭhe svabhāvata eva sāvadhāna ityarthaḥ /
kaṇṭaka śvaśrūrūpaḥ /
svābhimatavirodhitvenāniṣṭakāritvātkaṇṭakatvenoktiḥ /
pūrvakamiti /
śayyaṃ prapnuhīti śeṣaḥ /
iyaditi /
uktamityarthaḥ /
vidhiriti /
vācya iti śeṣaḥ /
vyaṅgyamāha---na pramādādityādi /
tvamekarūpatābhimānena ahamekarūpa ityabhimānena /
atra madviṣaye /
'sthita iti yat tat kevalaṃ dākṣiṇyenaive'ti sambandhaḥ /
kevalaivakārābhyāmanurāgarūpahetorvyavacchedaḥ /
ata evāha-pūrveti /
pūrvakṛtena pūrvakarmaṇā addaṣṭena hetunā yadanupālanaṃ matpālanam /
yadvā-pūrvakṛtaṃ yaddākṣiṇyaṃ tasyānupālanamavicchedena pālanaṃ tadātmanā dākṣiṇyena /
phalitamāha--tadityādi /

children.translated_text: When, at some point, the expressible has the form of a prohibition, [the suggested is] of neither form — as in:
"Come, look, turn back, O you whose jeweled path is disturbed by the moonlight of your face!"

children.text: ahisāriāṇaṃ vigdhaṃ karosi aṇaṇāṇaṃ vi haāse //
children.translated_text: "You create obstacles for the <s>abhisārikās</s> (women going to meet their lovers); you cause even the unattached to despair!"

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Here "go" (<s>vraja</s>) is the injunction. Your going to another woman's company is not from carelessness, but from deep attachment, which causes infatuation directed elsewhere, slips of the name (<s>gotraskhalana</s>), etc.; merely through the gallantry (<s>dākṣiṇya</s>) consisting of maintaining what was previously established, with the pride of constancy —

children.text:
locana.m tvamatra sthitaḥ, tatsarvathā śaṭho 'sīti gāḍhamanyurūpo 'yaṃ khaṇḍitanāyikābhiprāyo 'tra pratīyate /
na cāsau vrajyābhāvarūpo niṣedhaḥ, nāpi vidhyantaramevānyaniṣedhābhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: "<s>De</s>" is a particle used in entreaty (<s>prārthanā</s>).
"<s>Ā</s>" has the meaning of "<s>tāvat</s>" (at least/for now).
Thus the meaning is: "I entreat you — at least be gracious; turn back, O you whose path dispels darkness with the moonlight of your face!"
"You create obstacles for the <s>abhisārikās</s> — you cause even others to despair!"

<s>Locana</s>: "You are standing here — therefore you are thoroughly deceitful in every way" — this deep anger is the sentiment of the wronged heroine (<s>khaṇḍita-nāyikā</s>) that is suggested here. And this is neither a prohibition in the form of an absence of going, nor is the absence of any other prohibition [itself] merely another injunction.

children.text:
atra vyavasitādgamanānnivartasveti pratīterniṣedho vācyaḥ /
gṛhāgatā nāyikā gotraskhalitādyaparādhini bālapriyā sarvatheti /
tatraivāsaktatvena, ubhayatrāpi vetyarthaḥ /
anubhayarūpatvaṃ vivṛṇoti--na cetyādi /
vrajyābhāvarūpa iti /
vrajyā gamanam /

children.translated_text: "The absence of any other prohibition" —
meaning: another absence-of-prohibition, relative to [the prohibition of] going — this is the meaning.
The connection is: another injunction that has that as its nature.
Because the suggested meaning, which has the form of an inner intention (<s>abhiprāya</s>), does not have the nature of either of those two [injunction or prohibition] — this is the purport. //

Here, the expressible (<s>vācya</s>) is a prohibition, since what is perceived is "turn back from your resolved departure." The heroine has come home. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "in every way" (<s>sarvathā</s>) — regarding the transgressor guilty of slips of the name etc.; by being attached to that very [other woman], or to both — this is the meaning. He elaborates on the "neither" nature (<s>anubhaya-rūpatva</s>) — "not" (<s>na</s>) etc.

children.text:
'prārthaya' ityādau niṣedhavācakasya nañāderaprayogādasaṅgatimāśaṅkyāha---atretyādinā /
nivartasvetyanena māgama ityarthasyoktatayā gamananiṣedho vācya iti bhāvaḥ /
vyaṅgyabodhāṅgatayā vaktrādiviśeṣaṃ darśayati---gṛhāgatetyādi /
'anyāsāmapī'tyāpiśabdārthamāha--na kevalamityādi /
locanam nāyake sata tataḥ pratigantuṃ pravṛttā, nāyakena cāṭūpakramapūrvakaṃ nivartyate /
na kevalaṃ svātmano mama ca nirvṛtividhnaṃ karoṣi, yāvadanyāsāmapi; tatastava na kadācana sukhalavalābho 'pi bhaviṣyatītyata eva hatāśāsīti vallabhābhiprāyarupaścāṭuviśeṣo vyaṅgyaḥ /
yadi vā sakhyopadiśyamānāpi tadavadhīraṇayā gacchantī sakhyocyate-na kevalamātmano vidhnaṃ karoṣi, lāghavādabahumānāspadamātmānaṃ kurvatī, ata eva hatāśā, yāvadvadanacandrikāprakāśitamārgatayānyāsāmapyabhisārikāṇāṃ vidhnaṃ karoṣīti sakhyabhiprāyarūpaścāduviśeṣo vyaṅgyaḥ /
atra tu vyākhyānadvaye 'pi vyavasitātpratīpagamanātpriyatamagṛhagamanācca nivartasveti punarapi vācya eva viśrānterguṇībhūtavyaṅgyabhedasya preyorasavadalaṅkārasyodāharaṇamidaṃ syāt, na dhvaneḥ /
tenāyamatra bhāvaḥ--kācidrabhasātpriyatamamabhisarantī tadgṛhābhimukhamāgacchatā tenaiva hṛdayavallabhenaivamupaślokyate 'pratyabhijñānacchalena, ata evātmapratyabhijñāpanārthameva narmavacanaṃ bālapriyā nirvṛtivighnamiti /
vighnapadenātra nirvṛtividhno vivakṣita iti bhāvaḥ /
phalitamāha--tata ityādi /
tataḥ sarveṣāmapi sukhavighnakaraṇāt /
ata eveti. sukhaleśasyāpyalābhādevetyartaḥ /
hateti /
hatā viṣayālābhādbhagnā āśā yasyāḥ sā /
evaṃ vācyārthaṃ vyākhyāya vyaṅgyaṃ darśayati--itītyādi /
itīti hetau /
uktena vācyarthena hetunetyarthaḥ /
vallabheti /
tvatsaddaśī nānya kācidityevaṃrūpo yo vallabhābhiprāyaḥ, tadrūpa ityarthaḥ /
prakārāntareṇa vyācaṣṭe---yadi vetyādi /
'na kevalamātmano vidhnaṃ karoṣi, yāvadanyāsāmapī'ti sambandhaḥ /
ātmano vidhnaṃ karoṣītyasya vivaraṇam---lāghavādityādi /
ata eva abahumānāspadatvakaraṇādeva /
sakhyabhiprāya iti /
sa ca pūrvavadvodhyaḥ /
pratīpagamanāditi /
svagṛhaṃ prati gamanādityarthaḥ /
viśrānteriti /
uktavyaṅgyasyeti śeṣaḥ /
preyorasavaditi /
preyaśca rasavaccānayossamāhāraḥ preyorasavattadātmakālaṅkārasyetyarthaḥ /
bhāvasya parāṅgatve preyo 'laṅkāraḥ /
rasasya tattve rasavadalaṅkāraḥ /
sakhīvacanapakṣe sakhīgatāyā nāyikāviṣayakaraterbhāvarūpāyā vyaṅgyatvāttasyāścānubhāvarūpataduktārthadvārema 'nivartasve'ti vākyārthaṃ pratyaṅgatvātpreyo 'laṅkāratvam /
nāyakoktipakṣe tūktarītyā rasavadalaṅkāratvamityarthaḥ /
na dhvaneriti /
tathā ca prakramavirodha iti bhāvaḥ /
tenāyamiti /
ayaṃ vakṣyamāṇaprakāraḥ /
upaślokyata iti /
mukhendukāntivarṇanādirūpopaślokanamātrābhiprāyakametadityarthaḥ /
nanu gūḍhābhisaraṇe nāyikāyāḥ sākṣānnāyakenopaślokanamanucitamityatrāha--apratiyabijñānacchaleneti /
apratyabhijñānaṃ kvacidvācyādvibhinnaviṣayatvena vyavasthāpito yathā--
kassa vaṇa hoi roso daṭṭhūṇa piāeṃ savvaṇaṃ aharam /
locanam hatāśa iti /
anyāsāñca vidhnaṃ karoṣi tava cepsitalābho bhaviṣyatīti kā pratyāśā /
ata eva madīyaṃ vā gṛhamāgaccha, tvadīyaṃ vā gacchāvetyubhayatrāpi tātparyādanubhayarūpo vallabhābipārāyascāṭvātmā vyaṅgya ityateyeva vyavatiṣṭate /
anye tu---'taṭasthānāṃ sahṛdayānāmabhisārikāṃ pratīyamuktiḥ' ityāhuḥ /
tatra hatāśe ityāmantraṇādi yuktamayuktaṃ veti sahṛdayā eva pramāṇam /
evaṃ vācyavyaṅgyayordhārmikapānthapriyatamābhisārikāviṣayaikye 'pi svarūpabhedādbheda iti pratipāditam /
adhunā tu viṣayabhedādapi vyaṅgyasya vācyādbheda ityāha--kvacidvācyāditi /

children.translated_text: 'Is established' —

children.text: viṣayabhedo 'pi vicitrarūpo vyavatiṣṭamānaḥ sahṛdayairvyavasthāpayituṃ śakyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the distinction of subject, being of varied form, as it persists, can be established by connoisseurs.

children.text: kasya vā na bhavati roṣo dṛṣṭvā priyāyāḥ savraṇamadharam /
children.translated_text: 'For who would not be angered upon seeing the beloved's lip, entirely wounded?
O lady accustomed to smelling [flowers] swarming with bees, now be suddenly restrained!'

[<s>Balapriya</s>:] Anticipating the objection of inconsistency arising from the non-use of the prohibitive particle 'na' etc. at the beginning of 'prarthaya' ('entreat') etc., he says 'atra' ('here') etc. Since the meaning 'do not go' has been stated by 'nivartasva' ('turn back'), the prohibition of going is the expressible meaning: this is the purport. He shows the specific features of speaker etc. as ancillary to the cognition of the suggested — 'grhagata' ('one who has come home') etc. He explains the meaning of the particle 'api' in 'anyasam api' ('of other [women] too') — 'na kevalam' ('not only') etc.
<s>Locana</s>: While the hero (<s>nayaka</s>) is present, she who has set out to return from there is dissuaded by the hero through the preamble of flattering words (<s>catu</s>). 'Not only do you obstruct your own and my delight, but even that of other [women]; therefore you will never attain even a trace of happiness — hence you are hopeless' — this particular flattering speech expressing the beloved's intention is the suggested meaning. Or alternatively: even though being instructed by her female friend, [the heroine,] disregarding that [advice,] goes forth; the friend says — 'Not only do you create an obstacle for yourself — making yourself an object of disrespect through frivolity, hence indeed hopeless — but you also obstruct other women going on romantic rendezvous, since the path is illuminated by the moonlight of your face' — this particular speech expressing the friend's intention is the suggested meaning. However, in both interpretations, since the [suggested meaning] comes to rest in the expressible itself — 'turn back' — from the going against her resolve and from the going to the beloved's house, this would be an example of the <s>preyas</s> (love-charm) and <s>rasavat</s> (rasa-bearing) sub-varieties of the <s>gunibhutavyangya</s> (subordinated suggestion) category of <s>alankara</s>, not of <s>dhvani</s>.
Therefore, the intended sense here is: a certain woman, rushing eagerly to meet her beloved, is thus addressed in verse by that very heart's darling coming toward her from the direction of his house — under the pretext of non-recognition; hence the playful speech is for the purpose of making herself known. The <s>Balapriya</s> [explains]: 'nirvrtivighnam' ('obstacle to delight') — by the word 'vighna' (obstacle), an obstacle to delight is intended: this is the purport. He states the result — 'tatah' ('therefore') etc. 'Therefore' — because of obstructing everyone's happiness. 'Hence indeed' — because of the non-attainment of even a particle of happiness: this is the meaning. 'Hata' ('destroyed') — she whose hopes have been shattered by the non-attainment of the desired [object]: this is [the meaning]. Having thus explained the expressible meaning, he shows the suggested — 'iti' etc. 'Iti' is in the causal sense. The meaning is: by the stated expressible meaning as the cause. 'Vallabha' ('beloved') — the beloved's intention of the form 'there is no other woman like you' — of that form: this is the meaning.
He explains alternatively — 'yadi va' etc. The connection is: 'not only do you create an obstacle for yourself, but for other [women] too.' The elaboration of 'you create an obstacle for yourself' is 'laghavat' ('from frivolity') etc. 'Hence indeed' — precisely because of making oneself an object of disrespect. 'The friend's intention' — and that should be understood as before. 'From going against [her resolve]' — meaning from going toward her own home. 'Comes to rest' — the remainder is: 'of the stated suggested [meaning].' 'Preyas-rasavat' — the aggregate of <s>preyas</s> (love-charm) and <s>rasavat</s> (rasa-bearing) is <s>preyorasavat</s>; of the <s>alankara</s> of that nature: this is the meaning. When a <s>bhava</s> (transient emotion) attains prominence, there is the <s>preyas</s> figure. When a <s>rasa</s> [attains prominence], there is the <s>rasavat</s> figure. In the friend's-speech interpretation, since the <s>rati</s> (love) directed toward the heroine and belonging to the friend is a suggested <s>bhava</s>, and since it functions as an <s>anubhava</s> (consequent) — being ancillary through the expressible meaning to the sentence-meaning 'turn back' — there is the <s>preyas</s> figure. In the hero's-speech interpretation, by the stated method, there is the <s>rasavat</s> figure: this is the meaning. 'Not of <s>dhvani</s>' — and thus there would be a contradiction with the present topic: this is the purport. 'Therefore this [interpretation]' — this meaning is of the kind about to be stated. 'Is addressed in verse' (<s>upaslokayate</s>) — the meaning is: the praise consisting of describing the moon-radiance of her face etc. is alone intended. Now, the hero's direct praise-verse to the heroine in the context of a secret rendezvous would be improper — to this he says 'under the pretext of non-recognition.' Non-recognition is [sometimes distinguished as having] a subject different from the expressible — as established, for example: 'For whom is there no anger upon seeing the beloved's lip, entirely wounded?'

children.text:
kasy.a veti /
anīrṣyālorapi bhavati roṣo dṛṣṭvaiva; akṛtvāpi kutaścidevāpūrvatayā bālapriyā tadviṣayakapratyabhijñānābhāvaḥ, tasya chalena tadapratyabhijñānaṃ svasminnāropyetyarthaḥ /
ata eva upaślokanarūpatvādeva /
ātmeti /
svasya bodhanāyetyarthaḥ /
priyaḍajanenaiva narmavacanasya prayoktavyatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
'hatāśa iti narmavacanam' iti sambandhaḥ /
tatpadasyoktārthānuguṇamarthamāha---anyāsāṃ cetyādi /
anyāsāṃ ca tvadgṛhagamanotsukasya mama ceti cakārārthaḥ /
vyaṅgyamāha--ata evetyādi /
ata eva yata evaṃrūpo vācyārthaḥ, tata eva /
'madīyaṃ gṛhamāgaccha tvadīyaṃ vā gṛhaṅgacchāveti cāṭavātmā vallabhābhiprāyo vyaṅgya' iti sambandhaḥ /
iyatyeveti /
uktarūpavyaṅgyaḥ vyavatiṣṭata eva, na tu paścādvācyopaskārāya dhāvatītyarthaḥ /
atra pakṣe 'nivartasve' tyasya tavādhvavasāyānnivartasveti vācyārthe bodhyaḥ /
anye tviti /
pakṣe 'smin taṭasthānāṃ nāyikāpremābāvātteṣāṃ vacanaṃ na pravartakaṃ , na vā nivartakamataḥ pūrvoktavyaṅgyasya vācyāṅgatvaṃ neti bodhyam /
āmantraṇādītyādipadena abhisārikāvighnakaraṇavacanādergrahaṇam /
nanu vṛttau 'vyavasthāpita' ityuktiḥ kathaṃ saṅgacchate vyavasthāpanasyāniṣpannatvādityato vyācaṣṭe--viṣayabhedo 'pītyādi /
vicitrarūpaḥ nānāvidhaḥ /

children.translated_text: He explains the purport of 'kasya va' — 'even for one who is not jealous' etc.

children.text: 'kasya ve'ti vākāro 'vadhāraṇārthaṅko dṛṣṭvetyuttaraṃ thojya ityāśayena vyācaṣṭe---dṛṣṭvaivetyādi /
children.translated_text: Since 'va' in 'kasya va' is a particle of emphasis, with the intention that 'drstve' ('upon seeing') should be construed as the complement, he explains — 'drstvai va' ('upon seeing alone') etc.
He explains the meaning of the particle 'eva' — 'akrtva api' ('even without having done') etc.
[<s>Prakrit</s> verse:] 'O lady accustomed to smelling [flowers full of] bees, be suddenly restrained now!'

[<s>Balapriya</s>:] The purport of 'kasya va' ('for whom') — even for one who is not jealous, anger arises upon merely seeing [the wound]. The <s>Balapriya</s> [explains]: the absence of recognition pertaining to that subject — i.e., even without actually [having committed the act], from something unprecedented; 'by the pretext of that' — attributing that non-recognition to oneself: this is the meaning. 'Hence indeed' — precisely because [it takes] the form of praise-verse. 'Atma' ('self') — the meaning is: for the purpose of making herself known. Since playful speech is to be employed by the beloved alone: this is the purport. The connection is: 'the playful speech "hopeless" is a playful remark.' He states the meaning of that word in accordance with the stated meaning — 'of other [women] too' etc. 'Of other [women] too' — and the meaning of 'ca' is: 'and of me who am eager to go to your house.' He states the suggested — 'hence indeed' etc. 'Hence indeed' — since the expressible meaning is of such a form, 'therefore.' The connection is: 'come to my house, or let us go to yours' — the flattering speech expressing the beloved's intention, which takes neither of these two forms [exclusively], is the suggested: this is what is established. 'So much alone' — the suggested of the stated form is exactly established, and does not run off to supplement the expressible afterward: this is the meaning. In this interpretation, 'nivartasva' ('turn back') should be understood in the expressible meaning as 'turn back from your determination.' Others, however, say: 'It is a speech to the heroine directed at the bystanders among the connoisseurs going on a rendezvous.' In that case, whether the address 'O hopeless one' etc. is appropriate or not — the connoisseurs themselves are the authority.
Thus, even when the subject-matter of the expressible and suggested is identical — concerning the righteous traveler and the beloved going on a rendezvous — the difference [between them] has been demonstrated through the difference in their essential nature. Now, however, he says 'kvacid vacyat' ('sometimes from the expressible') — that the suggested differs from the expressible also through difference of subject. '[Is] established' — now, this statement 'vyavasthapita' ('established') in the commentary-prose — how does it accord [with the present context], since the establishment has not [yet] been accomplished? — to this he explains: 'the distinction of subject too' etc. 'Of varied form' — meaning of many kinds.

children.text:
anye caivaṃprakārā vācyādvibhedinaḥ pratīyamānabhedāḥ pratīyamānabhedāḥ sambhavanti /
teṣāṃ diṅmātrametatpradarśitam /
dvitīyo 'pi prabhedo vācyādvibhinnaḥ saprapañcamagre darśāyiṣyate /
locanam priyāyāḥsavraṇamadharamavalokya /
sabhramarapajhāghrāmaśīle śīlaṃ hi kathañcidapi vārayituṃ na śakyam /

children.translated_text: Therefore, that is indeed a semblance of <s>srngara</s> (<s>srngara-abhasa</s>).

children.text: tadaṅgaṃ bhāvābhāsaścittavṛtteḥ praśama eva prakāntayā hṛdayamāhlādayati yato viśeṣeṇa, tata eva tatsaṅgṛhīto 'pi pṛthaggaṇito 'sau /
children.translated_text: Its limb — the semblance of <s>bhava</s> (<s>bhava-abhasa</s>) — and the subsidence (<s>prasama</s>) of the mental modification, which delights the heart especially through tranquility — for that very reason, even though included within that [rasa], it is counted separately.

children.text: yathā-- ekasmin śayane parāṅmukhatayā vītottaraṃ tāmyato- ranyonyasya hṛdi sthite 'pyanunaye saṃrakṣatorgauravam /
children.translated_text: For example — 'On one bed, turned away from each other, suffering without recourse, though the entreaty resides in the heart of each, preserving [their] dignity —

of the couple, the quarrel of pride was broken, as the glances mixed through the gradual turning of sidelong looks, together with the hasty turning-away of the embrace around the neck, accompanied by laughter.'

And other varieties of such a kind — having differences in the suggested that are distinct from the expressible — are possible.
Of those, only a mere indication has been shown here.
The second sub-type too, distinct from the expressible, will be shown in detail further on.
[Locana:] 'Upon seeing the wounded lip of the beloved —
In one habituated to smelling the blossoms visited by bees — for one's nature (sila) cannot be restrained in any way.
Upon being restrained — in the prohibition; being perverse — she who does not accept that.'
'Endure now the succession of reproaches' — this is the meaning.
Here the purport is: a certain ill-mannered woman, whose lip has been bitten by someone, when her husband is ascertained to be in the nearby vicinity — [even though] she does not look at him — is addressed thus by a certain witty friend, for the very purpose of averting the blame [falling on the husband].
'Endure now' — this is the expressible, pertaining to the ill-mannered woman.
But pertaining to the husband — 'there is no fault [of his]' — this is the suggested meaning being communicated.
And 'endure' is also suggested with reference to him.
And when the heroine is being closely pressured by her beloved, [there is] the proclamation of the heroine's extraordinary good fortune — targeting the neighboring people who are falsely suspected by him — [this is known] from the force of the word 'priya' (beloved): hence the suggested pertains to the co-wife.
'To this extent I have been humiliated among the co-wives' —
[Balapriya:] 'In reality, even though the wound is absent' — this is the meaning.
'Then how is it seen?' — to this he says: 'by someone' etc.
'By some cause, [appearing] as having a distinctive bite-mark, visibly appearing as wounded from the front' — this is the meaning.
In the reading 'having made' (krtva api) — 'having made [the mark] oneself with lac-dye etc.' — this is the meaning.
The elaboration of 'perverse' (vame) is: 'she who does not accept that.'
'Here the purport is' — the meaning is: the expressible meaning having been stated, the suggested meaning is about to be stated.
'By someone' — the meaning is: by a paramour etc.
'The blame pertaining to that' — the meaning is: the status of being the object of the husband's reproach.
Or: the blame pertaining to her.
'What is the occasion for the avoidance of blame?' — hence he said 'ascertained' etc.
'By the friend, ascertained' — this is the meaning.
'Nearby' (savidha) — the region beyond the front part.
He shows the difference of domain between the expressible and the suggested — with 'endure' etc.
'Being communicated' — the meaning is: guiltlessness.
'Endure' — the meaning is: endure the flood of anger generated by seeing the lip-wound.
'This one whose lip is thus bitten — by suspicion that it was caused by another, let me not be angry' — this is the meaning.
'Of that heroine' —
'Being reproached' — the remainder is: at the time of the beloved's arrival.
'His false [suspicion]' — the meaning is: the neighboring people who are suspected of having committed an offense (vyalika) against the husband — targeting them.
'Convincing' — making [them] know [his] guiltlessness.
'To that co-wife' — the seventh case is because of the context of stating the difference of domain; the meaning is: 'for her.'
'That' etc. — in the word 'tat' meaning the heroine.
'Good fortune' — the meaning is: the good fortune of the heroine.
'Proclamation' — the remainder is: 'is the suggested.'
'From the force of the word' — since upon hearing the word 'priya' (beloved [woman]), after the cognition of the beloved's reproach, the cognition 'she is more fortunate than I' is possible — this is the purport.
'To this extent' — the meaning is: through the clear manifestation of the ill-manners.
'Humiliated' (khalikrta) — made light of.
'On the contrary' — 'among friends' carries over.
'Esteem' — because of the complete concealment of the ill-manners: this is the purport.
The third [sub-type], however, characterized by rasa etc., is impelled by the capacity of the expressible —
[Locana:] 'It is not proper to accept lightness upon oneself; on the contrary, this is [a mark of] esteem — endure, i.e., be radiant now' — the suggested pertaining to the friend is the proclamation of good fortune.
'This one, your secretly enamored one, your heart's beloved, has thus been protected; henceforth let the mode of biting with teeth not be done openly' — this is the suggested addressed to the secret paramour.
'Thus by me this has been concealed' — the proclamation of one's own cleverness, targeting the impartial witty onlookers, is the suggested."
"That [which was stated] — this has been stated as 'vyavasthapita' (established), in accordance with the vrtti text — he says: 'that indeed' etc.
Now, if alankara-dhvani too were to be shown here just like vastu-dhvani, why is it said that it will be shown later? — to this he states the purport: 'just as' etc.
He shows the very difference — 'vastu' (content) etc.
The construction is: 'even the status of being denoted by words.'
'Are rasa etc. also like that?' — to this he says: 'rasa, bhava' etc.
By the inclusion of 'bhava etc.,' the words 'vrtti etc.' stated [in the vrtti] have been glossed.
'And yet' (atha ca) — the meaning is: 'nevertheless.'
'Therein' — the meaning is: the shining of rasa etc.
'Another device' — another operation.
'Does not exist' — here he states the reason: 'stumbling' etc.
He states the essential nature of rasa etc. — 'with propriety' etc.
He connects 'with propriety, when [the mental modification] operates' with rasa and bhava.
When the permanent (sthayin) mental modification is savored — that is rasa; when the transitory (vyabhicarin) mental modification is savored — that is bhava: this is the construction.
'With impropriety' — when the permanent mental modification operates with impropriety: this is the meaning.
'Its semblance' (tadabhasa) — rasa-abhasa (semblance of rasa).
Intending to show the difference of rasa-abhasa from hasya (humor), he states [the case] of srngara-abhasa as the primary [example] — 'of Ravana' etc.
Anticipating the objection that 'this is the very domain of hasya' and resolving it — 'even though' etc.
'Therein' — in Ravana's rati directed toward Sita.
'From srngara' — the meaning is: through the medium of srngara-abhasa.
'Subsequent' — occurring in the time after the period of becoming absorbed.
In the stage of discerning the before and after —
[Locana:] — that is the abiding; but in the stage of becoming absorbed, since it is rati itself that is being savored, srngara alone shines forth — through the determination of the sequential order — as in 'like a distant-attracting enchantment-mantra, when that name enters my hearing' etc.

children.translated_text: Because that [mental state] is not seen in another domain [outside poetry].

children.text: na hi kevalaśṛṅgarādibdamātrabhāji locanam darśayati--na ca sarvatreti /
children.translated_text: For not in what bears merely the word "<s>śṛṅgāra</s>" etc. alone — <s>Locana</s> shows — "and not everywhere" (<s>na ca sarvatra</s>) etc.

children.text: yathā bhaṭṭendurājasya--- yadviśramya vilokiteṣu bahuśo niḥsthemanī locane yadgātrāṇi daridrati pratidinaṃ lūnābjinīnālavat /
children.translated_text: As in [the verse] of <s>Bhaṭṭendurāja</s>: "When, having rested, the eyes gaze repeatedly, bereft of steadiness; when the limbs waste away day after day like the stalks of cut lotuses;"

children.text: dūrvākāṇḍaviḍambakaśca nibiḍo yatpāṇḍimā gaṇḍayoḥ kṛṣṇe yūni sayauvanāsu vanitāsveṣaiva veṣasthitiḥ //
children.translated_text: "And when a dense pallor, rivaling <s>dūrvā</s> grass blades, covers the cheeks — among youthful women in the company of a dark youth, this alone is the state of their appearance."

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Here, [what is suggested is] the subsidence (<s>praśama</s>) of the offended pride (<s>māna</s>) whose nature is jealousy and anger. And this meaning of <s>rasa</s> etc. is not [apprehended] as joy arises from [the statement] "a son is born to you." Nor [is it apprehended] through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). Rather, through the power of the connoisseur's sympathetic heart-response (<s>hṛdaya-saṃvāda</s>), upon the cognition of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] meaning through the knowledge of semblances of <s>vibhāvas</s>, by means of the ascertainment of the semblance of the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion). This is the position: the determination that <s>rati</s> (love) has the form of the comic (<s>hāsya</s>). How so? To that he says "<s>tanmayī</s>" etc. "Sequential" (<s>paurvāparya</s>): the sequence between the <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>rati</s> etc. — by the disregard, i.e., absence, of discrimination regarding that [sequence]. The syntactic connection is: "shines forth in [verses] such as '<s>ityādau</s>'." This verse will be stated in the second <s>uddyota</s>. Here, first, through identification (<s>tanmayī-bhāvana</s>), the connoisseurs savor <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s love directed at <s>Sītā</s> — so there is indeed the savoring of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>; subsequently, through knowledge that that love has an improper object (<s>anucitālambanakatva</s>), the arousal of the comic pertaining to that — so there is the savoring of <s>hāsya</s>, and the savoring of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is merely the savoring of a semblance (<s>ābhāsa</s>) — with this intention he concludes: "that" (<s>tat</s>) etc. "Its component, <s>bhāvābhāsa</s>" — meaning: the <s>bhāva</s> (transitory emotion) that is a component of the semblance of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and other <s>rasas</s> is the <s>bhāvābhāsa</s>. Since <s>bhāva-praśama</s> (subsidence of emotion) can also be grasped by the word "<s>bhāva</s>" alone, why is it mentioned separately? To that he says "of the mental state" (<s>cittavṛtteḥ</s>) etc. "That has commenced" (<s>prakrāntāyāḥ</s>): that has begun to suggest <s>rasa</s>. The syntactic connection is: "since the subsidence alone delights in a special way, therefore it is counted separately." "Though included in that" (<s>tat-saṃgṛhītaḥ api</s>): though already indicated by the word "<s>bhāva</s>." "That" (<s>asau</s>): that subsidence of <s>bhāva</s>. "On one bed" (<s>ekasmin śayane</s>): of the couple somehow brought to share one bed by a friend. "The turning away" (<s>parāṅmukhatā</s>): due to the continuation of offended pride. "With what has ceased to be subsequent" (<s>vīta-uttaram</s>): where the activity that follows lying down has departed — [the compound describes] that state. "Anguished" (<s>tāmyatoḥ</s>): tormented. "Of each other" (<s>anyonyasya</s>): of the two who, though conciliation remains in their hearts, do not make it [manifest] for fear of breaking their dignity. "From the turning of the side-glances" (<s>apāṅgayoḥ valanāt</s>): from the rolling of the eyes. "The quarrel of pride" (<s>māna-kaliḥ</s>): the quarrel born of offended anger. "With laughter" (<s>hāsena</s>): with impetuosity (<s>rabhasa</s>), with speed; where the turning away (<s>vyāvṛtta</s>) is accompanied by an embrace of the neck — that is the description. He construes — "here" (<s>ityatra</s>) etc. "Anger in the form of jealousy" (<s>īrṣyā-rūpaḥ roṣaḥ</s>) — of that nature. There is also the reading "<s>krodha</s>" (wrath). "Subsidence" (<s>praśama</s>) — "is perceived" (<s>pratīyate</s>) is the remainder. Intending to prove that <s>rasa</s> etc. are suggested through <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. — as shown by the statement "implied by the power of the expressible, it shines forth" — he first negates that it is apprehended through the <s>tātparya</s> power (purport) — "not" (<s>na ca</s>) etc., up to "thus" (<s>tathā</s>). Here, "from poetry" (<s>kāvyāt</s>) is the remainder. Just as a sentence like "a son is born to you" generates joy in the listener by conveying a pleasing content — it shines forth — but is not directly the domain of verbal operation; so too [<s>rasa</s>] is indeed different from the expressible. For the expressibility of that [<s>rasa</s>] would either be through being conveyed by its own word, or through the medium of presenting <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. In the first alternative, if <s>rasa</s> etc. are not conveyed by their own words, the consequence would be that they are not cognized at all.

<s>Locana</s>: Being savored through identification (<s>tanmayī-bhāva</s>), having its life-breath solely in the quality of being relished (<s>rasyamānatā</s>), distinct from established natural pleasures (<s>siddha-svabhāva-sukha</s>) and the like — [the meaning] flashes forth as having the nature of <s>rasa</s>. Therefore he says "it shines forth" (<s>prakāśate</s>). Hence, the operation of the word there, assisted by meaning, is suggestion (<s>dhvanana</s>) alone. Even regarding the meaning of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., since it does not generate that mental state in the manner of the joy from news of a son's birth, the operation of meaning too — distinct from generation — is called suggestion (<s>dhvanana</s>) alone.

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "By its own word" (<s>sva-śabda</s>): through the word "<s>śṛṅgāra</s>" etc. being conveyed by the denotative function alone. "Through <s>vibhāvas</s> etc." — meaning through the <s>tātparya</s> power (purport). "There" (<s>tatra</s>): meaning in the first alternative. "Positive and negative concomitance" (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>): [showing that] wherever there is cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc., it is not [dependent on own-word denotation] — this is the negative concomitance. The purport is: establishing that only suggestion operates. Alternatively: when the own-word is present, there is cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc.; when it is absent, there is absence of cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. — these are the positive and negative concomitances. "Having the essence of being relished" (<s>rasyamānatā-sāram</s>) contains the reason. And not everywhere are they conveyed by their own words. Even where that [own-word] exists, the cognition of these [<s>rasas</s>] is only through the medium of presenting specific <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. The own-word merely restates it; it does not produce it.
