children.translated_text: At that time, when the king of <s>Magadha</s> was besieging <s>Madhurā</s> —
He states the reason for the embrace — "given by him" (<s>taddatta</s>) etc.
By him, the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — <s>Locana</s>: embracing with longing a <s>vañjula</s> (Asoka) creeper growing on the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) —
That song sung by <s>Rādhā</s>, with heavy tears, voice choked and faltering in its high pitch — by which even the aquatic creatures moving beneath the water cried out with longing. //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Here, only after the cognition of <s>anubhāvas</s> and <s>vibhāvas</s>, through the method of identification (<s>tanmayī-bhavana</s>), the meaning — whose nature is <s>rasa</s>, being the domain of the savoring of the bliss of one's own consciousness (<s>sva-saṃvid-ānanda</s>) colored by the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the mental states appropriate to those <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> — flashes forth even in the absence of words like "desire" (<s>abhilāṣa</s>), "anxiety" (<s>cintā</s>), "eagerness" (<s>autsukyā</s>), "sleeplessness" (<s>nidrā</s>), "fortitude" (<s>dhṛti</s>), "languor" (<s>glāni</s>), "indolence" (<s>ālasya</s>), "fatigue" (<s>śrama</s>), "memory" (<s>smṛti</s>), "deliberation" (<s>vitarka</s>), etc. Having thus shown the absence of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), he shows the absence of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) — "even where" (<s>yatrāpi</s>) etc. "That" (<s>tat</s>): the being-conveyed-by-own-word. "Through the medium of presentation" — meaning: through the apprehension of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. occasioned by words. "Merely" (<s>kevalam</s>) etc. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He gives an example concerning the domain of <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotions) — "when" (<s>yat</s>) etc. "Having rested" (<s>viśramya</s>): pausing intermittently. "Bereft of steadiness" (<s>niḥsthemanī</s>): lacking firmness, greatly agitated. By the first quarter, the glance called "languid" (<s>alasā</s>) is described. Modesty (<s>vrīḍā</s>) and eagerness (<s>autsukyā</s>) are also suggested. "Waste away" (<s>daridrati</s>): become emaciated and dry. By the simile "like cut [lotus stalks]" etc., the faded complexion and such are suggested. "Dense" (<s>nibiḍaḥ</s>): thick, devoid of the intrusion of another color. By three quarters, the group of <s>anubhāvas</s> and <s>vyabhicārins</s> is shown. "Youth" (<s>yūni</s>): one in the flush of youth. "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>" — by this, the <s>vibhāva</s> [is indicated]. "Women" (<s>vanitāsu</s>): among the <s>gopīs</s>. "This alone" (<s>eṣā eva</s>): having exactly the form of the languid gaze etc. described above. "State of appearance" (<s>veṣa-sthitiḥ</s>): the arrangement of their appearance. "That" (<s>tat</s>): by means of the method (<s>yukti</s>) of identification (<s>tanmayī-bhavana</s>). "That" (<s>tat</s>): of those <s>rasas</s> etc., or those same <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s>; the mental states appropriate to them, having the form of <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotions) and <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotions); by the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of those, one's own consciousness (<s>sva-saṃvid</s>) is colored — the savoring that is full of bliss of that [consciousness] — its domain, i.e., its object. This is the meaning. The syntactic connection is: "the meaning having the nature of <s>rasa</s> flashes forth even in the absence of words like '<s>abhilāṣa</s>' etc." "<s>Abhilāṣa</s>" means the frustration of desire (<s>abhilāṣa-vipralambha</s>). Here it should be understood that desire is suggested by the main sentence while anxiety etc. are suggested by subordinate sentences. "Absence of positive concomitance" (<s>anvayābhāva</s>): if <s>rasa</s> etc. were cognized through their own words by <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, there would be positive concomitance — but since they are not [so cognized], there is absence of positive concomitance. This is the purport. In the <s>vṛtti</s>, the word "<s>api</s>" in "<s>yatrāpi</s>" has the sense of "<s>tu</s>" (but). "Gone" (<s>yāte</s>): by the expression "gone to <s>Dvāravatī</s>," the absence of hope for return is indicated. "<s>Madhuripu</s>" — by this, indicating preoccupation with subduing the wicked, that [hopelessness] is further reinforced.

children.translated_text: The meaning is: in what has the character of poetry according to your view.
'Not even a trace' —
'<s>Srngara</s> (erotic), <s>hasya</s> (comic), <s>karuna</s> (pathetic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>vira</s> (heroic), <s>bhayanaka</s> (terrifying),
<s>bibhatsa</s> (disgusting), and <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous) — these eight are declared to be the <s>rasas</s> in drama.'

[<s>Balapriya</s>:] Here, the <s>vibhavas</s> (determinants) and <s>anubhavas</s> (consequents) are cognized effortlessly. And <s>utkantha</s> (longing) indeed enters the domain of savoring (<s>carvana</s>). The word 'sotkantha' ('with longing') merely proves what is already proved. But the restatement that the word 'sotkantha' was employed in order to draw in the stated <s>anubhavas</s> by means of [the word] 'utkam' ('longingly') is also not purposeless — for in re-presenting the <s>anubhavas</s>, there would be either redundancy or non-identification (<s>atanmayibhava</s>); but not that it is caused by those [anubhavas] — for this he states the reason: 'visayantara' ('in a different subject-matter') etc.
'Yad visramya' — the <s>Balapriya</s> [explains]: 'datta' means 'that which was given'; '<s>jhampa</s>' is the act of leaping — a falling action preceded by striking from an elevated direction etc., occurring during the time of play; 'by that.' The word '<s>jhampa</s>' may also be masculine. 'Anatam' — in the act of giving, the bowing of the receiver is appropriate. In the reading 'sampannata,' the meaning is: endowed with the prosperity of flowers, shoots, etc. that was brought about, i.e., accomplished, by him [i.e., <s>Krsna</s>]. 'Kalindi-tata-rudha' ('grown on the bank of the <s>Kalindi</s>') — by having grown at the place of the beloved's sport, [the tree] suggests the surpassing good fortune [of the place] and the fact that it causes longing for that place. 'Tat' — of such a kind. 'Gatam' — the suffix <s>kta</s> is in the sense of <s>bhava</s> (abstract state). 'Gurvi' — in such a manner that the voice is faltering due to the throat being choked by heavy, i.e., copious, tears; and flowing, i.e., spreading; and high-pitched — and loud — [such is the song] by which, i.e., upon hearing which. 'By the creatures dwelling within the water' — by <s>sarasa</s> (cranes) etc. too, not merely by swans etc. who move on the surface of the water. 'Utkam' means 'with longing.' 'Utkujitam' means 'cooed loudly'; by the logic of identification (<s>tanmayibhavana</s>), the meaning is 'wept.' '<s>Vibhavanubhavav</s>' — the separation from the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Krsna</s>), or <s>Krsna</s> in separation, is the <s>alambana-vibhava</s> (foundational determinant); the bank of the <s>Kalindi</s> etc. are the <s>uddipana-vibhavas</s> (stimulant determinants); the embracing of creepers etc. are the <s>anubhavas</s> (consequents). There is also the reading '<s>vibhanubhavam</s>.' 'Amlanataya' — without distress, i.e., merely as expressed meaning — this is the meaning. 'Pratiyete' — there is also the reading '<s>pratiyata</s>.' 'Then what?' — to this he says: '<s>utkantha ca</s>' etc. 'Enters the domain of savoring' — the meaning is: it attains the status of being an object [of savoring]; here, no doubt based on the expectation of its own word need be entertained. 'But it is conveyed by its own word' — to this he says 'sotkantha-sabda' etc. 'Proves what is already proved' — the meaning is: makes known what is already known. Hence it is a restatement: this is the purport. By the word 'kevala' ('merely'), he shows that here [the word sotkantha] does not even serve as an auxiliary with respect to the <s>vibhavas</s> and <s>anubhavas</s>. 'Even this restatement is not purposeless,' he says: 'utkam' etc. The meaning is: it is in the conjunction of the <s>anubhavas</s> stated as 'heavy tears' etc. with the cooing of the water-creatures that identification obtains for [the cognition of] their longing; and by the word 'utkam,' the association of those <s>anubhavas</s> was intended to be conveyed. And the word 'utka' alone does not convey that, being insufficient by itself. But when the word 'sotkantha' occurs in the preceding sentence, the <s>anubhavas</s> subsumed under it are conveyed by the word 'utka,' which is synonymous with 'sotkantha' — hence the word 'sotkantha' has a purpose: this is the meaning. 'But let there again be a presentation of <s>anubhavas</s>' — to this he says 'punaḥ' etc. Not merely would there be redundancy; the identification-function of such a set of experiences would also not obtain, since the charm would be vitiated by the apprehension of impropriety — he says 'atanmayi' etc.
'Visayantara' ('in a different subject-matter') — in poetry devoid of the presentation of <s>vibhavas</s> etc., there is not even a trace of the apprehension of <s>rasa</s>. And since, without its own verbal designation, even from <s>vibhavas</s> etc. alone — when they are of a distinguished kind — the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. [arises]; and from its own verbal designation alone, there is no cognition — therefore, by the methods of agreement (<s>anvaya</s>) and difference (<s>vyatireka</s>), [the cognition of] <s>rasa</s> etc. is implied by the power of the expressible (<s>abhidheyasamarthyaksiptatva</s>), and is in no way directly expressed.
The <s>Locana</s> [says]: 'iti' etc. — 'na hi' (for it is not the case that). — the meaning is: 'that which exists even in the absence of something [else] is not caused by that [something]' — this is the purport. He confirms the very non-perception — 'na hi' etc. He clarifies the meaning of the word 'kevala' — '<s>vibhavadi</s>' etc. '<s>Kavye</s>' —

children.text:
ityatra. /
evaṃ svaśabdena saha rasādervyatirekānvayābhāvamupapatyā pradarśya tathaivopasaṃharati-yataścetyādinā kathañcidityantena /
abhidheyameva sāmarthyaṃ sahakāriśaktirūpaṃ vibhāvādikaṃ rasadhvanane śabdasya kartavye, abhidheyasya ca putrajanmaharṣabhinnayogakṣematayā jananavyatirikte divābhojanābhāvaviśiṣṭapīnatvānumitarātribhojanavilakṣaṇatayā cānumānavyatirikte dhvanane kartavye sāmarthyaṃ śaktiḥ viśiṣṭasamucito vācakasākalyamiti bālapriyā ityasya vivaraṇam yadviśramyetyādāviti /
bhāvamāha-na hīti /
'tattatkṛtaṃ na hī'ti sambandhaḥ /
nanu vibhāvādipratipādakatvābhāve kathaṃ kāvyatvaṃ, yena siddhavannirdeśa ityāśaṅkāṃ pariharan parābhimatasyaiva kāvyarūpatvaprasañjanābhiprāyeyamuktirityāha---tava mata ityādi /
svaśabdakṛtā rasādipratītiḥ na vibhāvādikṛtetyasmin mate kāvyatvenānabhimatamapi kāvyamāpadyetetyarthaḥ /
tathāvidhamevodāharaṇamāha--śṛṅgāreti /
'yataśce'tyādivṛttigranthasyānarthakyaśaṅkāmupasaṃhāratvoktyā śamayannāha--evamityādi /
vṛttāvabhidheyasāmarthyākṣiptatvamupasaṃhṛtaṃ, tattu śabdārthobhayagatadhvananavyāpāragamyatvarūpamiti vyācaṣṭe---abhidheyamevetyādi /
sāmarthyapadasya vivaraṇam--sahetyādi /
sahakāri eva śāktiḥ śaknotyanayeti śaktistadrūpam /
tatkimityatrāha--vibhāvādikamiti /
dhvanana ityākṣepapadavyākhyānam /
karmadhārayāśrayaṇena śabde yojayitvā ṣaṣṭītatpuruṣāśrayeṇārthe yojayati---abhidheyasya yetyādi /
abhidheyasyetyasya dhvanana ityanena sambandhaḥ /
bhinnayogakṣematayā bhinnasvabhāvatayā /
putrajanma khalu harṣa janayati, na tathā vibhāvādyartho rasaṃ janayatīti tadvilakṣṇatvamarthagatadhvananasya /
anumānapakṣamapi parākaroti--diveti /
sāmarthyamaityasya vyākhyānam--śaktiriti /
śaktimeva vivṛṇoti--viśiṣṭeti /
guṇālaṅkārādiviśiṣṭena samucitena rasānuguṇena ca vācakena iti tṛtīyo 'pi prabhedo vācyādbhinna eveti sthitam /
vācyena tvasya saheva pratītirityagre darśayiṣyate /
children.translated_text:
Here [in this verse]. Thus, having demonstrated through reasoning the absence of both agreement and difference between <s>rasa</s> etc. and their own verbal designation, he concludes accordingly with 'yatasca' etc., up to 'kathancit' ('in any way').
The expressible itself — the auxiliary power in the form of the <s>vibhavas</s> etc. — serves as the cooperant in the word's task of effecting <s>rasa</s>-suggestion; and of the expressible [meaning] — being distinct from the joy at the birth of a son etc. by virtue of its different essential nature (<s>bhinnayogaksemataya</s>), and from inference by being distinct like the inference of nocturnal eating from the observed corpulence of one who does not eat during the day — in effecting the distinct kind of suggestion, the power (<s>samarthya</s>) is the capacity (<s>sakti</s>), which consists of the totality of expressive words that are distinguished by and appropriate to [the rasa]. The <s>Balapriya</s> [explains]: the elaboration of 'yad visramya' etc. is at that [passage]. He states the purport — 'na hi' etc. The connection is: 'that is not caused by that.' Now, in the absence of the capacity to convey <s>vibhavas</s> etc., how can there be the status of poetry, such that [the word 'kavye'] is used as though established? — dispelling this doubt, he shows that the statement was intended to indicate the absurd consequence in the opponent's own position — 'tava mate' ('in your view') etc. The meaning is: in the view that the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. arises from its own verbal designation rather than from <s>vibhavas</s> etc., even what is not accepted as poetry would become poetry. He gives just such an example — 'srngara' etc. He allays the suspicion of purposelessness of the <s>vrtti</s> passage 'yatasca' etc. by saying it serves as the conclusion — 'evam' etc. In the <s>vrtti</s>, 'abhidheyasamarthyaksiptatvam' has been concluded; he explains that [this quality] consists of being cognizable through the suggestive operation residing in both word and meaning — 'abhidheyam eva' etc. The elaboration of the word 'samarthya' — 'saha' etc. 'Sahakari' (cooperant) itself is '<s>sakti</s>' (power) — that by which one is able: this is the form of that [power]. 'What is that?' — to this he says '<s>vibhavadikam</s>' etc. 'Dhvanana' — this is the explanation of the word introduced by way of objection. Construing [the compound] as a <s>karmadharyaya</s>, he applies it to word; then construing as a <s>tatpurusa</s> with the sixth case, he applies it to meaning — 'abhidheyasya' etc. The connection of 'abhidheyasya' with 'dhvanana' [is understood]. '<s>Bhinnayogaksemataya</s>' means 'by being of different essential nature.' The joy at a son's birth indeed generates happiness, but the meaning consisting of <s>vibhavas</s> etc. does not similarly generate <s>rasa</s> — thus the distinctness of the suggestion pertaining to meaning [is shown]. He also sets aside the inference alternative — 'diva' etc. The explanation of 'samarthyam' is '<s>sakti</s>' etc. He further elaborates '<s>sakti</s>' — '<s>visista</s>' etc. 'Distinguished by <s>gunas</s> and <s>alankaras</s> etc., and appropriate to <s>rasa</s>' — by such expressive words: thus the third variety too is distinct from the expressible — this is established.

children.text:
kāvyasyātmā sa evārthas tathā cādikaveḥ purā /
(DhvK_1.5a)
children.translated_text: That meaning alone is the soul of poetry; and thus, of the first poet (<s>adikavi</s>), formerly — (<s>DhvK</s> 1.5a)
That meaning alone is the soul of poetry; and thus, of the first poet, formerly —

children.text:
locanam dvayorapi śabdārthayordhvananaṃ vyāpāraḥ /
evaṃ dvau pakṣāvupakramyādyo dūṣitaḥ, dvitīyastu kathañciddūṣitaḥ kathañcidaṅgīkṛtaḥ, jananānumānavyāpārābhiprāyeṇa dūṣitaḥ; dhvananābhiprāyeṇāṅgīkṛtaḥ /
yastvatrāpi tātparyaśaktimeva dhvananaṃ manyate, sa na vastutattvavedī /
vibhāvānubhāvapratipādake hi vākye tātparyaśaktirbhede saṃsarge vā paryavasyet; na tu rasyamānatāsāre rase ityalaṃ bahunā /
itiśabdo hetvarthe /

children.translated_text: 'Iti' is also a causal [particle] — the connection is: 'therefore the third variety too is distinct from the expressible.'
'Together with' (<s>saha</s>) —

children.text: ivaśabdena vidyamāno 'pi kramo na saṃlakṣyata iti taddarśayati--agra iti /
children.translated_text: By the particle '<s>iva</s>' (as if/like), [it is shown that] even though the sequence exists, it is not perceivable — he shows this by 'agre' ('later') etc.
In the Second <s>Uddyota</s> (Illumination). // 4 //

<s>Locana</s>: Suggestion (<s>dhvanana</s>) is an operation of both word and meaning. Thus, having introduced two positions, the first has been refuted; the second, however, has been partly refuted and partly accepted — refuted insofar as it intends the operations of generation and inference; accepted insofar as it intends suggestion. But one who, even here, considers the power of purport (<s>tatparyasakti</s>) itself to be the suggestive operation — he does not know the true nature of things. For in a sentence that conveys <s>vibhavas</s> and <s>anubhavas</s>, the power of purport would terminate either in the distinction [of meanings] or in their combination — but not in <s>rasa</s>, whose essence is savorability. Enough of prolixity. The word 'iti' is in the causal sense.

children.text:
evaṃ 'pratīyamānaṃ punaranyadeva' itīyatā dhvanisvarūpaṃ vyākhyātam /
adhunā kāvyātmatvamitihāsavyājena ca darśayati---kāvyāsyātmeti /
sa eveti pratīyamānamātre 'pi prakrānte tṛtīya eva rasadhvaniriti mantavyaṃ, itihāsabalāt prakrāntavṛttigranthārthabalācca /
bālapriyā sākalyaṃ paripūrṇatvamityarthaḥ /
itīti hetau /
ādya iti /
'svaśabdaniveditatvena ve'ti pakṣa ityarthaḥ /
dvitīya iti /
'vibhāvādipratipādanamukhena ve'ti pakṣa ityarthaḥ /
rasādīnāmabhidheyasāmarthyākṣiptatvameveti vadato vṛttikṛtastātparyaśāktireva dhvananavyāpāro 'bhimataḥ, na tu tadvyatiriktaścaturthakakṣyāniveśī abhidheyānyathānupapattisahāyārthabodhanaśaktereva tātparyaśaktitvāditi kaścidāha, tanmatamanūdya dūṣayati--yastvityādi /
bhede saṃsarge veti /
gāmānayetyādau karmāntarebhyaḥ kriyāntarebhyaśca bhedo vākyārthaḥ, saṃsargastvārtha iti kecit /
karmaviśeṣādeḥ kriyāviśeṣeṇa sambandharūpasaṃsargo vākyārthaḥ, bhedastvārtha ityapare // .4 // // .//
children.translated_text:
Thus, by the passage 'the suggested meaning is a different entity altogether,' the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> has been explained. Now he demonstrates its status as the soul of poetry, through the medium of a legendary narrative (<s>itihasa</s>) — 'kavyasyatma' ('the soul of poetry') etc. 'Sa eva' ('that alone') — even though the suggested in general has been introduced, it should be understood that the third [variety], namely <s>rasa-dhvani</s>, is intended, on the strength of the legendary narrative and of the meaning of the commentary-prose that has been introduced.
<s>Balapriya</s>: 'Sakalyam' means 'completeness, i.e., perfection' — this is the meaning. 'Iti' is in the causal sense. 'The first [position]' — the meaning is: 'the position that [rasa etc.] are conveyed by their own verbal designation.' 'The second' — the meaning is: 'the position that [they are conveyed] through the presentation of <s>vibhavas</s> etc.' Since the author of the commentary-prose, in saying that <s>rasa</s> etc. are implied by the power of the expressible alone, accepts the power of purport (<s>tatparyasakti</s>) as the suggestive operation and not a fourth-level operation distinct from it — since the power of <s>tatparya</s> consists of the capacity for communicating meaning that is not otherwise accountable from mere denotation — someone says [this]; having cited that view, he refutes it — 'yastu' etc. '<s>Bhede samsarge va</s>' — in [sentences like] 'gam anaya' ('bring the cow'), the sentence-meaning [according to some] is the distinction of this particular action from other actions and other objects; while according to others, the combination, i.e., the relation of the specific object with the specific action, is the sentence-meaning; and according to yet others, the distinction is the sentence-meaning. // 4 //

children.text:
nanu dhvanisvarūpe vācyādbhedena samarthite, lakṣaṇanuktvā tasyātmatvapratipādikāyāḥ kārikāyāḥ kā saṅgatirityato vṛttānuvādapurassaraṃ tāṃ darśayati--evamityādinā /
vyākhyātamiti /
dhvanisvarūpaṃ tasya kāvyātmatvañceti prakṛtayordvayorādyaṃ pratipāditamityarthaḥ /
itihāsavyājeneti /
vyājaśabdena dhvanerātmatvapratipādana eva tātparyaṃ, netihāsopakṣepa iti darśitam /
prakṛtānuguṇyena vyācaṣṭe---sa evetyādi /
sa evetītyasyānantaraṃ
children.translated_text: [<s>Balapriya</s>:] Now, when the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> has been established as distinct from the expressible, what is the relevance of the <s>karika</s> that demonstrates its <s>atmatva</s> (soul-status), without having stated the definition (<s>laksana</s>)? — therefore, preceded by a restatement of the commentary-prose, he shows that [relevance] — by 'evam' etc. 'Vyakhyatam' ('has been explained') — the meaning is: of the two topics at hand — the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> and its status as the soul of poetry — the first has been established. 'Through the medium of a legendary narrative' — by the word 'vyaja' ('pretext'), it is shown that the purport lies in demonstrating the soul-status of <s>dhvani</s>, not in introducing the legendary narrative [for its own sake]. He explains in accordance with the topic at hand — 'sa eva' etc. After 'sa eva iti' —
The grief born from the separation of the <s>kraunca</s> (curlew) couple attained the form of a verse (<s>sloka</s>). // <s>DhvK</s> 1.5 //
The grief born from the separation of the <s>kraunca</s> couple attained the form of a verse. // 5 //

children.text:
locanam tena rasa eva vastuta ātmā, vastvalaṅkāradhvanī tu sarvathā rasaṃ pratiparyavasyete iti vācyādutkṛṣṭau tāvityabhiprāyeṇa 'dhvaniḥ kāvyasyātme'ti sāmānyenoktam /
śoka iti /
krauñcasya dvandvaviyogena sahacarīhananodbhūtena sāhacaryadhvaṃsanenotthito yaḥ śokaḥ sthāyibhāvo nirapekṣabhāvatvādvipralambhaśṛṅgārocitaratisthāyibhāvādanya eva, sa eva tathābhūtavibhāvatadutthākrandādyanubhāvacarvaṇayā hṛdayasaṃvādatanmayībhavanakramādāsvādyamānatāṃ bālapriyā tacchabdeneti, rasadhvanirityasyānantaraṃ parāmṛṣṭa iti ca śeṣaḥ /
mantavyamiti /
yuktyā niścetavyabhityarthaḥ /
tāmāha--itihāsetyādi /
itihāsavalāditi /
kārikāśeṣabalādityarthaḥ /
prakrānteti /
'tṛtīyastvi'tyādinā pūrvoktetyarthaḥ /
'pratīyamānasya ce'tyādi samanantaravṛttigranthasyāpyupalakṣaṇamidam /
teneti /
yasmādrasa dhvanireva sa eveti parāmarśanīyastasmādityarthaḥ /
'tena ityabhiprāyeṇa sāmānyenoktam' iti sambandhaḥ /
itiśabdaparāmṛṣṭamabhiprāyamāha--rasa evetyādi /
sarvatheti /
aṅgitve 'ṅgatve cetyarthaḥ /
itīti hetau /
anyathā pratipattinirāsāya vivakṣitaṃ vyācaṣṭe---krauñcasyetyādi /
dvandvaviyogakāṇamāha---sahacarītyādi /
dvandvaviyogenetyasya vyākyānam---sāhacaryadhvaṃsaneneti /
utthitaḥ utpannaḥ /
krauñja iti śeṣaḥ /
sāhacaryadhvaṃsotthatvena prāptaṃ śṛṅgārasthāyitvaṃ pratiṣedhati--nirapekṣetyādi /
upekṣāyāḥ saṅgamapratyāśāyāḥ niṣkrānto nirapekṣo bhāvastatvāt /
krauñcetyādikaṃ vyākhyāya śokasya ślokatāprāptiṃ vivṛṇoti---sa evetyādi /
krauñce tātasya śokasya vāsanārūpeṇādikavau sthitasya śokasya cābhedabuddhikṛtamaikyaṃ vivakṣitvā sa evetyuktam /
'sa eveti ślokarūpatāṃ prāpta' iti sambandhaḥ /
atra hetuḥ--karuṇarasarūpatāṃ pratipanna iti /
tatra cāsvādyamānatāṃ pratipanna iti /
ratyādicittavṛttirāsvādyamānā hi śṛṅgārādivyapadeśagocara iti bhāvaḥ /
āsvādyamānatāprāptau hetuḥ---hṛdayetyādi /
sahṛdayasyādau hṛdayasaṃvādaḥ, tatastanmayībhāvalābhastaduttaramāsvāda iti kramaḥ /

children.translated_text: Here too, the reason: '<s>tathābhūta</s>' (of such a nature) etc.
<s>Tathābhūta</s> means: the <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) in the form of the <s>krauñca</s>, whose companionship has been destroyed.

children.text: locanam pratipannaḥ karuṇarasarūpatāṃ laukikaśokavyatiriktāṃ svacittadgutisamāsvādyasārāṃ pratipanno rasaparipūrṇakumbhoccalanavaccittavṛttiniḥṣyandasvabhāvavāgvilāpādivacya samayānapekṣatve 'pi cittavṛttivyañjakatvāditi nayenākṛtakatayaivāveśavaśātsamucitaśabdacchandovṛttādiniyantritaślokarūpatāṃ prāptaḥ-- mā niṣāda pratiṣṭāṃ tvaṃmagamaḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Locana</s> [says]: '<s>Pratipannaḥ</s>' — having attained the form of <s>karuṇa rasa</s> (the pathetic sentiment), [which is] distinct from worldly grief, whose essence is to be savored through the emotional response (<s>dguti</s>) of one's own mind — having attained [this form], like the overflowing of a vessel filled to the brim with <s>rasa</s>, [the grief] — whose nature is the spontaneous outflow of mental dispositions [expressed as] verbal lamentations (<s>vilāpa</s>) etc. — since even without depending on convention, [such lamentations] manifest mental dispositions — by this principle, without deliberate effort, through the force of aesthetic absorption (<s>āveśa</s>), [the grief] attained the form of a verse (<s>śloka</s>) regulated by appropriate words, meter, and style: '<s>Mā niṣāda pratiṣṭhāṃ tvam agamaḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ</s> /
<s>yat krauñca-mithunād ekam avadhīḥ kāma-mohitam</s>' //

The <s>Locana</s> [says]: therefore, <s>rasa</s> alone is in reality the soul [of poetry]; <s>vastu-dhvani</s> (factual suggestion) and <s>alaṅkāra-dhvani</s> (figurative suggestion), however, culminate in <s>rasa</s> in every way — and being thus superior to the expressed meaning, they are [stated as such] — with this intention, '<s>dhvaniḥ kāvyasyātmā</s>' (dhvani is the soul of poetry) has been stated in general terms. '<s>Śoka</s>' (grief) — the grief (<s>śoka</s>) that arose in [<s>Vālmīki</s>] from the separation of the <s>krauñca</s> (curlew) pair — caused by the killing of the mate, [which constitutes] the destruction of companionship — this permanent emotion (<s>sthāyibhāva</s>) is entirely different from the permanent emotion of <s>rati</s> (love) appropriate to <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation), because of its character of being without hope (<s>nirapekṣa</s>); that very [grief], through the savoring of the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) of that nature and the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) such as the wailing that arose from them, [and] through the progressive stages of concordance of heart and becoming one [with the object], attained the state of being savored. The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [explains]: 'by that word (<s>tacchabdena</s>)' — the completion is: 'it is referred to immediately after "<s>rasa-dhvani</s>."' '<s>Mantavya</s>' (is to be understood) — the meaning is: 'is to be ascertained by reasoning.' He states that [reasoning]: '<s>itihāsa</s>' etc. '<s>Itihāsabalāt</s>' — the meaning is: 'by the force of the remainder of the <s>kārikā</s>.' '<s>Prakrānta</s>' — the meaning is: 'previously stated by [the text beginning with] "the third, however" etc.' This is also a synecdoche (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for the immediately following <s>vṛtti</s>-text beginning with '<s>pratīyamānasya ca</s>' etc. '<s>Tena</s>' — the meaning is: 'since <s>rasa-dhvani</s> alone is what is to be referred to as "that very [thing]," therefore.' The connection is: '<s>tena ityabhiprāyeṇa sāmānyenoktam</s>' (with that intention, it has been stated in general terms). He states the intention referred to by the word '<s>iti</s>': '<s>rasa eva</s>' etc. '<s>Sarvathā</s>' — the meaning is: 'both in being subordinate and in being primary.' '<s>Iti</s>' is in the sense of reason. To refute a contrary understanding, he explains what is intended: '<s>krauñcasya</s>' etc. He states the cause of the pair's separation: '<s>sahacarī</s>' etc. The explanation of '<s>dvandvaviyogena</s>' is '<s>sāhacaryadhvaṃsanena</s>' (by the destruction of companionship). '<s>Utthitaḥ</s>' means 'arose'; the completion is: 'of the <s>krauñca</s>.' He negates the status of being the permanent emotion of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> that would [otherwise] follow from arising from the destruction of companionship: '<s>nirapekṣa</s>' etc. Because the emotional state is <s>nirapekṣa</s> (without hope), i.e., devoid of the expectation of reunion (<s>saṅgamapratyāśā</s>). Having explained '<s>krauñca</s>' etc., he elucidates how the grief attained the form of a verse (<s>śloka</s>): '<s>sa eva</s>' etc. Having intended the identity — produced by the cognition of non-difference — between the grief of the father (<s>tāta</s>) regarding the <s>krauñca</s> and the grief that existed in the first poet (<s>ādikavi</s>) in the form of a residual impression (<s>vāsanā</s>), he says '<s>sa eva</s>' (that very [grief]). The connection is: '<s>sa eva</s> attained the form of a verse (<s>śloka</s>).' The reason here: 'it attained the form of <s>karuṇa rasa</s> (the pathetic sentiment).' And in that [transformation], 'it attained the state of being savored.' For a mental disposition (<s>cittavṛtti</s>) such as <s>rati</s> (love) etc., when being savored, falls within the scope of the designation <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc. — this is the purport. The reason for attaining the state of being savored: '<s>hṛdaya</s>' etc. The sequence is: first, concordance of heart for the connoisseur; then, the attainment of becoming one [with the object]; after that, the savoring.
Thus.

children.text:
na tu muneḥ śoka iti mantavyam /
evaṃ hi sati tadduḥkhena so 'pi duḥkhita iti kṛtvā rasasyātmateti niravakāśaṃ bhavet /
na ca duḥkhasantaptasyaiṣā daśeti /
evaṃ carvaṇocitaśokasthāyibhāvātmakakaruṇarasamuccalanasvabhāvatvātsa bālapriyā ākrāndanādītyādipadenāvanitalapariluṇṭhanādirgrāhyaḥ /

children.translated_text: '<s>Agama</s>' — by the Vedic augment (<s>chāndasa</s>) <s>aḍāgama</s>.
By the emphatic expression '<s>sa eva</s>' (that very [thing]) he says this: 'no other is the soul [of poetry].'

children.text: tena yadāha bhaṭṭanāyakaḥ-- śabdaprādhānyamāśritya tatra śāstraṃ pṛthagviduḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, what <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s> says — 'Relying on the primacy of words, they regard the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) as separate [from poetry];
but they call that which is conjoined with the truth of meaning an <s>ākhyāna</s> (narrative) of those two [word and meaning].'

But it should not be considered that [this is merely] the grief of the sage. For if that were the case, then — on the grounds that 'he too was pained by that [bird's] suffering' — the statement that <s>rasa</s> is the soul [of poetry] would be left without scope. Nor is this the condition of one afflicted by suffering. The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [explains]: by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.) in '<s>ākrandana</s>' (wailing) etc., rolling on the ground etc. are to be included. He states the result of the grief's attainment of the form of <s>karuṇa rasa</s>: '<s>laukika</s>' (worldly) etc. The purport is: because of the difference in the essential nature and its aggregate of conditions. To show that the other-worldly nature of <s>rasa</s> is established by the authority of one's own experience (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), he says '<s>sva</s>' etc. That which is to be savored, i.e., experienced by the mind, through the <s>dguti</s> (emotional response) of one's own mind — the mind of the one who savors — which is characterized by becoming one [with the object] and marked by <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation) etc. — whose life-force (<s>sāra</s>, <s>prāṇa</s>) that is — [this is karuṇa rasa]. To the doubt 'how can <s>rasa</s>, which is the very soul [of poetry], transform externally into the form of a verse?' — he answers with an illustration: '<s>rasa</s>' etc. Just as, when a vessel placed on the head, filled with water, overflows, the water within it flows outward — so too [the rasa overflows into verse]. To the objection of dissimilarity due to [water being] material and [rasa being] immaterial, he gives another illustration: '<s>cittavṛtti</s>' etc. Just as verbal lamentations etc. — which are transformations of mental dispositions such as grief — [overflow into speech]; by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), praises etc. are to be included. The particle '<s>ca</s>' is in the sense of alternative. Now, the soul-nature (<s>ātmatva</s>) of <s>rasa</s> in poetry should be stated only in terms of its being the object [of suggestion]. And it is not possible for a word — whose operation depends on convention — to have that [rasa] as its object — raising and addressing this objection, he shows that it has [rasa] as its object through being suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>): '<s>samayānapekṣatve 'pi</s>' (even without dependence on convention) etc. '<s>Iti nayena</s>' — the meaning is: in the world, modes of speech such as lamentation, praise, etc. manifest (<s>vyañjayanti</s>) mental dispositions in the form of grief, admiration, etc. — by this established principle. '<s>Akṛtakatayā eva</s>' — the meaning is: without the deliberate intention 'I shall express this meaning through this [utterance].' Then how [did it happen]? — to this he says: '<s>āveśavaśāt</s>' etc. '<s>Āveśa</s>' means 'self-pervadingness,' i.e., total absorption. '<s>Samucita</s>' etc. — the purport is: only appropriate words etc. manifest <s>rasa</s> etc. Having explained that 'the grief of the first poet attained the form of a verse (<s>śloka</s>),' he refutes the erroneous construction '<s>ādikaveḥ śokaḥ</s>' ('the grief of the first poet' [as a separate clause]): '<s>na tu</s>' etc. By the word '<s>muni</s>' (sage), he refutes the implication of [ordinary] suffering. He states the fault in such a construction: '<s>evam</s>' etc. '<s>Tadduḥkhena</s>' — by the known suffering of the <s>krauñca</s>. '<s>So 'pi</s>' — even the first poet (<s>ādikavi</s>). '<s>Iti kṛtvā</s>' — from this implicit reason. '<s>Iti</s>' — the meaning is: 'such a statement.' He states another fault as well: '<s>na ca</s>' etc. '<s>Eṣā daśā</s>' — the meaning is: the condition of being the utterer of a curse, or the condition of composing a verse — [is not that of one afflicted by suffering]. He summarizes: '<s>evam</s>' etc. In the manner stated, the <s>karuṇa rasa</s> — whose soul is the permanent emotion of grief that is fit for savoring — the meaning of poetry, which is the quintessential [element], adorned by the variegated charm of diverse expressed words and their meanings — that alone is the soul [of poetry]. The <s>Locana</s> [says]: that alone is the soul of poetry — the essential nature that differentiates [poetry] from other [forms of] speech. This very [point] has been stated in the <s>Hṛdayadarpaṇa</s>: 'As long as [the heart] is not filled with this, it does not pour forth that [rasa].'
When both [word and meaning] have the status of qualities [i.e., are subordinate], and the operation [of suggestion] is primary, [then] the aesthetic apprehension of poetry arises.

children.translated_text: The other variety, consisting of factual content (<s>vastu</s>) and figure (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) [is also included].

children.text: bhāvagrahaṇena vyabhicāriṇo 'pi carvyamāṇasya tāvanmātrāviśrāntāvapi sthāyicarvaṇāparyavasānocitarasapratiṣṭāmanavāpyāpi prāṇatvaṃ bhavatītyuktam /
children.translated_text: By the [synecdochic] inclusion of '<s>bhāva</s>' (emotion), it has been stated that even a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion), even when not culminating in the savoring of the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) — even without attaining the stability of <s>rasa</s> proper through the completion of <s>sthāyin</s>-savoring — has the status of being the life-breath [of poetry], through its own savoring alone, since aesthetic wonder arises from that very savoring.

children.text: yathā--- nakhaṃ nakhāgrema vighaṭṭayantī vivartayantī valayaṃ vilolam /
children.translated_text: For example: 'Scratching nail with nail-tip, twirling her loose bracelet,
with her foot, its anklet softly tinkling, gently tracing [lines] upon the ground' —

Thus that [objection] is set aside. /
For if the operation [of words] has the nature of suggesting (<s>dhvanana</s>) and the nature of relishing (<s>rasanā</s>), then nothing new has been said. /
If, however, the operation is denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>) itself, even so, it has been previously indicated that denotation does not have predominance. /
He explains the verse: 'variously' — /
'Variously' means having been made diverse in accordance with the <s>rasa</s> to be manifested by each [element]. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Welling forth' (<s>samuccalana</s>) means outward expression; the nature, i.e., the essential character, of that verse '<s>mā niṣāda</s>' etc. — its reality (<s>tattva</s>) is that [welling forth]. Therefore: /
That itself is the <s>karuṇa-rasa</s> (pathetic sentiment). /
'The soul of poetry' — /
Since the poem '<s>mā niṣāda</s>' etc. has as its essential nature the welling forth of <s>karuṇa-rasa</s>, therefore <s>rasa</s> alone is the soul of poetry. This is the purport. /
The explanation of '<s>ātmā</s>' (soul) is: 'that which is the essence-nature.' /
The substantiation of that: 'moreover' etc. /
He corroborates the statement of <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s> regarding poetry's having the nature of <s>rasa</s>-welling-forth: 'as long as' — /
'The poet' is the remainder. /
'With this <s>rasa</s>' — /
As long as [the poet] is not filled through the process of becoming one with [the <s>rasa</s>] via the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., so long he does not emit that <s>rasa</s> — does not bring it to external expression and make it relishable by others. /
Only when the poet is filled with <s>rasa</s> does he pour forth <s>rasa</s> in the form of poetry — thus poetry, whose form is the pouring forth of <s>rasa</s>, has the very form of <s>rasa</s>. This is the purport. /
Regarding the suspicion that in the passage '<s>mā niṣāda</s>' etc. written by himself [<s>Vālmīki</s>], the augment '<s>aṭ</s>' in '<s>agama</s>' might be prohibited by the rule '<s>namāṅyoga</s>' — he explains the validity: '<s>agama</s>' etc. /
'By that' — /
The meaning is: by the argumentation establishing <s>rasa</s> as the soul [of poetry]. /
The connection of this is with '<s>tad apāstam</s>' ('that is set aside'). /
'Word' — /
'Relying upon' — /
'Has proceeded' is the remainder. /
'<s>Śāstra</s>' — the <s>Vedas</s> etc. /
'By virtue of meaning-content' — by the predominance of meaning. /
'Appropriate' — <s>Itihāsa</s> etc. /
There is also the reading '<s>yukte</s>.' /
'Of these two' — of word and meaning. /
'Poetic apprehension' — poetic usage. /
The remainder is: 'in a composition possessing that.' /
'Operation' — /
In 'predominance of operation,' the meaning of the word 'operation.' /
'<s>Atha</s>' — in the sense of raising a doubt. /
'Variously — beautiful through elaboration in the expressed, the expressive, and the composition' — intending this analysis, he explains: 'of each' etc. /
'The <s>rasa</s> that is to be manifested by those various expressed [meanings] etc. — in accordance with that.' /
'Having made diverse' — /
And thus, for the first poet <s>Vālmīki</s>, the grief (<s>śoka</s>) born from the anguished cry of the <s>krauñca</s> [heron], tormented by separation from his slain companion, transformed into a <s>śloka</s> (verse). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The meaning is: that which is beautiful through elaboration in the expressed, the expressive, and the composition — endowed with excellences of word, meaning, <s>alaṅkāra</s>, and <s>guṇa</s>. /
Therefore, even though suggestion exists everywhere, the usage [of the term 'poetry'] is not applied [everywhere]. /
Even though the <s>ātman</s> (soul) exists [in all bodies], the designation '<s>jīva</s>' (living being) applies only in certain cases — this was stated earlier. /
By that, the following is rendered groundless — what was said in the <s>Hṛdayadarpaṇa</s>: 'Then poetic usage would apply everywhere.' /
'The slain companion' — the <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) is stated. /
The crying sound — the <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent). /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Of the expressed etc.' is the remainder. /
The connection of 'having made' is with 'through elaboration,' and of 'the expressed' etc. (three terms) with 'beautiful.' /
'Through elaboration' — through detailed expression. /
'Beautiful' — lovely. /
He states what is intended by this: 'word' etc. /
'By that' — the meaning is: by virtue of being poetry as described by 'variously' etc. /
'Everywhere also' — even in [expressions like] '<s>siṃho devadattaḥ</s>' ('<s>Devadatta</s> is a lion') etc. /
'Usage in that manner' — poetic usage. /
The connection is: 'therefore what was said — that is rendered groundless.' /
'<s>Vibhāva</s>' — the <s>krauñca</s> whose companionship was destroyed is the <s>ālambana-vibhāva</s> (foundational determinant); the slaying is the <s>uddīpana-vibhāva</s> (stimulating determinant). /
[Objection:] But by the text as literally heard — '<s>nihata</s>' (slain) etc. — the meaning that the sage's grief is born from that [bird's] cry seems to be directly apprehended! Then how [can grief be the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) of <s>rasa</s>]? For grief is the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> of <s>karuṇa-rasa</s>! And even though another variety of the suggested has been shown — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Born' — the remainder is: as an object of savoring (<s>carvaṇā</s>). /
[Objection:] If the <s>śloka</s> originated from the savoring of grief, then the suggested factual content would be the soul of poetry — from what [evidence can one say otherwise]? Anticipating this doubt, he says: 'for grief' etc. /
'Of <s>karuṇa</s>' — i.e., of that [<s>karuṇa-rasa</s>] whose nature is the savoring of that [grief], the <s>sthāyibhāva</s>. /
For in grief as the <s>sthāyibhāva</s>, the <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> appropriate to it, and the mental disposition that is savored — that is <s>rasa</s>. Hence, through the propriety [of the designation], the attainment of <s>rasa</s>-status by the <s>sthāyin</s> is stated. /
'Previously self-known and inferred in another [i.e., the <s>krauñca</s>]' — the mental disposition that is the <s>sthāyin</s>. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Previously the prohibition of that — hence he explains: 'as an object of savoring' etc. /
The meaning is: born from that cry and made into an object of savoring (<s>carvaṇā</s>). /
And the meaning of '<s>śoka</s>' is: the sage's grief that persists in the form of a latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>). This is the purport. /
[Objection:] But the passage 'for grief' etc. — the reiteration that grief is the <s>sthāyin</s> of <s>karuṇa-rasa</s> is here purposeless! Hence he introduces that passage: 'but' etc. /
'That' — the meaning is: 'then.' /
'The suggested factual content' — the meaning is: <s>rasa</s>. /
This is said to prevent forgetting the topic at hand. /
He explains in a manner conducive to the success of the resolution: 'of <s>karuṇa</s>' etc. /
'That savoring' — the meaning is: the savoring of grief. /
By the statement '<s>śokaḥ ślokatvam āgataḥ</s>' ('grief became a verse'), through the very statement that the <s>śloka</s> arose from the savoring of grief, the soul-status of <s>rasa</s> has been illuminated — because <s>karuṇa-rasa</s> has the nature of being the object of grief-savoring. This is the purport. /
[Objection:] But how can another [object] be the content of another's savoring? To this he substantiates: 'for in grief' etc. /
'In grief, the <s>sthāyibhāva</s>' — in the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> such as grief etc. relating to the <s>krauñca</s> etc. being described. /
The seventh case is in the sense of cause. /
'The <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> that [pertain]' — /
The meaning is: the <s>vibhāvas</s> that are the causes and the <s>anubhāvas</s> that are the effects of grief etc. /
'Appropriate to those' — appropriate to those <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> being savored. /
The extent is: homogeneous with the <s>sthāyin</s> present in each [described character]. /
'Mental disposition' — the mental disposition in the form of grief etc. that persists in the savorer as a latent impression. /
'Whose nature is being savored' — whose nature is being relished. /
'<s>Rasa</s>' — the referent of the word <s>rasa</s>. /
'Through propriety' — the meaning is: through figurative usage grounded in the relation of utility, not in the primary sense. This is the purport. /
'Attainment of <s>rasa</s>-status' — the attainment of <s>rasa</s>-hood. /
'Is stated' — is stated by formulations like '<s>sthāyibhāvo rasaḥ</s>' ('the <s>sthāyin</s> is <s>rasa</s>'). /
He shows the utility: 'previously' etc. /
The remainder is: 'by the sensitive reader.' /
'Self-known' — experienced in oneself. /
'In another' — in the <s>krauñca</s> etc. /
'Inferred' — from the crying etc. This is the implied meaning. /
'Mental disposition' — the meaning is: the <s>sthāyin</s>. /
'Impression' etc. — the meaning is: 'being such that, having deposited the impression of self-experience and the impression of self-inference, and thereby establishing the accord with the heart from both — it is, on account of that, utilized [in savoring].' /
The connection is: 'because it is utilized, therefore the propriety [of the designation applies].' /
The indication through <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s> alone is synecdochic (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>), because of their predominance. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Through the sequence of impressions, that which establishes the accord with the heart is utilized in the savoring. Because — /
[Objection:] But 'the suggested form is the soul' — therein a threefold division was taught, not <s>rasa</s> alone as the essential nature; by this narrative [of <s>Vālmīki</s>], it would be stated that only <s>rasa</s> is the soul — anticipating this, he answers by way of concession: 'and of the suggested' etc.

children.text: rasabhāvaśabdena ca tadābhāsatatpraśamāvapi saṃgṛhītāveva; avāntaravaicitrye 'pi tadekarūpatvāt /
children.translated_text: And by the term '<s>rasa-bhāva</s>,' <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>) and <s>bhāvābhāsa</s> (semblance of emotion) as well as <s>bhāvaśama</s> (tranquilization of emotion) are also included — because despite their internal diversity, they have a single essential form.
'Because of predominance' —
The meaning is: because of the culmination in <s>rasa</s>.

And since [the <s>vastu</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s> types of <s>dhvani</s>], even when not culminating in [<s>rasa</s>] alone, have the status of being the life [of poetry] through their capacity to produce distinctiveness from other words — it has been stated out of propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) [that <s>rasa</s>-<s>dhvani</s> is predominant]. This is the purport. || 5 ||
here, of <s>lajjā</s> (modesty) [the life-breath status obtains].

children.text:
bālapriy.ā pratīyamānarūpamātmeti /

vṛttau 'rase'tyādi /
rasamukhenaiva bhāvamukhenaiva cetyarthaḥ /
'upalakṣaṇam' iti /

atra bhāvagrahaṇasya phalamāha--bhāvetyādi /
'bhāvagrahaṇena ityuktam' iti sambandhaḥ /
tāvaditi /
tāvanmātre svarūpamātre /
aviśrāntiḥ viśrāntyabhāvastasyāmapītyarthaḥ /
apiśabdenāmukhyatvaṃ sūcitam /
tarhi rasapratiṣṭayā bhāvyamityata āha---sthāyītyādi /
stāyicarvaṇāyāṃ yatparyavasānaṃ tatpūrṇatākaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ tadeva ucitarasapratiṣṭā tāmaprāpyāpītyarthaḥ /
prāṇatvaṃ kāvyajīvitatvam /
bhavatīti /
taccarvaṇayaiva camatkārodayāditi bhāvaḥ /
nakhamiti /
atra valayavivartanoktyā priyatamādarśanajanitaṃ kārśyaṃ vyajyate /
atroktarnakhavighaṭṭanādibhiranubhāvairgamyena priyatamavārtāśravaṇādinā vibhāvena cābhivyajyamānāyā lajjāyāḥ śṛṅgāraniṣṭāmanavāpya carvaṇāgocarībhavantyāḥ prāṇatvamityāha--atra lajjāyā iti /
prāṇatvamityanuṣaṅgaḥ /

anyeṣāmiti śeṣaḥ /
prasaṅgādāha---tāvadityādi /

'anyaśābdavailakṣaṇyakāritvenaucityādi'ti sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'The suggested form is the soul' — /
Since by [the statement] '<s>kāvyasyātmā dhvaniḥ</s>' ('suggestion is the soul of poetry'), the soul-status of the suggested in general has been stated. This is the purport. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'in <s>rasa</s>' etc. — the meaning is: principally through <s>rasa</s> and principally through <s>bhāva</s> (emotion). /
'Is synecdochic' (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) — 'of the suggested' is connected. /
Synecdoche is: the indication of another through one that is principal, by virtue of some mutual relation — as in 'that king is going,' where the king is synecdochic for the retinue. /
Here he states the result of the inclusion of '<s>bhāva</s>': '<s>bhāva</s>' etc. /
The connection is: 'it has been stated by the inclusion of <s>bhāva</s>.' /
'<s>Tāvat</s>' — in its mere own form. /
'Non-culmination' — the absence of culmination, even in that. This is the meaning. /
By the word '<s>api</s>' (even), non-primacy is indicated. /
'Then it should attain stability through <s>rasa</s>' — to this he says: '<s>sthāyin</s>' etc. /
The culmination in the savoring of the <s>sthāyin</s> — the perfecting [of it] — that itself is the proper stability in <s>rasa</s>; even without attaining that. This is the meaning. /
'Life-breath status' — being the life of poetry. /
'Becomes so' — because aesthetic wonder arises from that very savoring. This is the purport. /
'Nail' — here, by the mention of twirling the bracelet, the emaciation born from not seeing the beloved is suggested. /
Here, of <s>lajjā</s> (modesty) being manifested by the <s>anubhāvas</s> of nail-scratching etc. and by the <s>vibhāva</s> to be inferred — hearing news of the beloved etc. — even without attaining culmination in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, becoming an object of savoring — [of this <s>lajjā</s>] the life-breath status [obtains]. He says: 'here, of <s>lajjā</s>.' /
'Life-breath status' is carried forward. /
'<s>Rasa</s>' etc. — the meaning is: by the word '<s>rasa</s>,' <s>rasābhāsa</s> is included; by the word '<s>bhāva</s>,' <s>bhāvābhāsa</s> and <s>bhāvaśama</s> are included. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, the meaning of 'because of predominance' is: because of the predominance of that <s>rasa</s>. /
He states the reason: 'because of culmination in <s>rasa</s>.' /
'Of the others' is the remainder. /
Incidentally he says: '<s>tāvat</s>' etc. /
'When not culminating in that alone' — when not culminating in the <s>vastu</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s> forms alone. /
'<s>Api ca</s>' — the particle '<s>api</s>' is in the sense of 'moreover.' /
The connection is: 'through the capacity to produce distinctiveness from other words, out of propriety.'

children.text: sarasvatī svādu tad-artha-vastu niḥṣyandamānā mahatāṃ kavīnām /
children.translated_text: The <s>Sarasvatī</s> (speech/goddess of eloquence) of great poets, flowing forth sweet content and meaning,
manifests a brilliance of <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuition) that shines forth, uncommon to the [ordinary] world. || <s>DhvK</s> 1.6 ||

children.text: sarasvatī svādu tadarthavastu niḥṣyandamānā mahatāṃ kavīnām /
children.translated_text: The <s>Sarasvatī</s> of great poets, flowing forth sweet content and meaning,
manifests a brilliance of <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuition) that shines forth, uncommon to the [ordinary] world. || 6 ||

children.text:
tat vastutattvaṃ niḥṣyandamānā mahatāṃ kavīnāṃ bhāratī alokasāmānyaṃ locanam evamitihāsamukhena pratīyamānasya kāvyatmatāṃ pradarśya svasaṃvitsiddhamapyetaditi darśayati---sarasvatīti /
vāgrūpā bhagavatītyarthaḥ /
vastuśabdenārthaśabdaṃ tatvaśabdena ca vastuśabdaṃ vyācaṣṭe--niḥṣyandamāneti /
divyamānandarasaṃ svayameva prasnuvānetyarthaḥ /
yadāha bhaṭṭanāyakaḥ-- vāgdhenurdugdha etaṃ hi rasaṃ yadbālatṛṣṇāyā /
bālapriyā athedamālocanīyaṃ sahṛdayaiḥ---śrīvālmīkinā "mā niṣāde"tyādiślokena ślokāntaraiśca sahacarasya puṃsa eva krauñcasya nihananaṃ nirdiṣṭam, atra tu 'nihate'tyādiyathāśratagranthena vṛttikṛtā, sahacarīhananodbhūtene'ti 'nihatasahacarīti vibhāva ukta' iti ca vyākhyānena locanakṛtā, 'niṣādanihatasahacarīkaṃ krauñcayuvānam' ityādivacanena kāvyamīmāṃsākāreṇa ca sahacarīhananaṃ pratipāditāmityeteṣāṃ granthakṛtāṃ rāmāyaṇavacanaviruddhārthapratipādane nimittaṃ kimiti /
atra kecit--'nihate'tyādivṛttigranthasya 'nihataḥ sahacarīvirahakātaraḥ svata eva sahacarīvirahāsahiṣṇuśca yaḥ krauñca
staduddeśyako ya ākrandastajjaniti' ityarthaḥ /
locane 'sahacarohanane'tyatra 'sahacare'ti pāṭhena bhāvyam /
'nihatasahacarīti vibhāva ukta' ityasya "nihatasahacarī"tyādigranthena vibhāvaḥ pradarśita ityarthaśceti na rāmāyaṇavacanavirodhaḥ /
kāvyamīmāṃsākṛdvacanaṃ ca yathāśrutavṛttigranthārthāvabodhamūlakamaśraddheyameveti vadanti // .5 // // .//
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "That reality of things, streaming forth — the speech of great poets, not ordinary to the world." <s>Locana</s>: Having thus demonstrated through the historical narrative (<s>itihāsa</s>) that the suggested meaning has the status of the soul of poetry, he shows that this is also established through direct self-experience (<s>svasaṃvit</s>) — "<s>Sarasvatī</s>" etc. "The divine lady in the form of speech" — this is the meaning. He glosses the word "<s>vastu</s>" (thing/fact) with "<s>artha</s>" (meaning), and the word "<s>tattva</s>" (reality) with "<s>vastu</s>" — "streaming forth" (<s>niḥṣyandamānā</s>) etc. "Spontaneously flowing with divine bliss-<s>rasa</s>" — this is the meaning. As <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s> said: "Speech is a cow; she has milked this <s>rasa</s>, for from the thirst of the young..." [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Now this should be pondered by connoisseurs — <s>Śrī Vālmīki</s> in the verse beginning "<s>mā niṣāda</s>" and in other verses indicated the slaying of the male <s>krauñca</s> bird, the companion; but here the <s>vṛtti</s> author through the text as literally read starting with "<s>nihate</s>", and the <s>Locana</s> author through the commentary "arising from the slaying of the female companion" and "the <s>vibhāva</s> is stated as the one whose female companion was slain," and the author of the <s>Kāvyamīmāṃsā</s> through the statement "the young <s>krauñca</s> whose female companion was slain by the hunter" — [all these] have presented the slaying of the female companion — what is the reason for these authors presenting a meaning contrary to the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> text? Here some [explain:] the meaning of the <s>vṛtti</s> text beginning with "<s>nihate</s>" is: "the <s>krauñca</s> who was slain, distressed by separation from his companion, himself unable to bear the separation from his companion — the cry directed at him that arises from that." In the <s>Locana</s>, in "<s>sahacare hanane</s>," the reading "<s>sahacare</s>" [masculine] should be adopted. And "the <s>vibhāva</s> is stated as <s>nihata-sahacarī</s>" means: "the <s>vibhāva</s> is shown by the text beginning with <s>nihata-sahacarī</s>" — thus there is no contradiction with the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> text. And the statement of the <s>Kāvyamīmāṃsā</s> author, being based on understanding the <s>vṛtti</s> text as literally read, is simply not to be trusted — they say. // 5 //

children.translated_text: "Speech" (<s>vāk</s>) —
Speech in the form of poetry — she herself is the cow (<s>dhenu</s>).
This divine <s>rasa</s> —

children.text: bālatṛṣṇayā locanam tena nāsya ramaḥ sa syādduhyate yogibhirhi yaḥ // .//
children.translated_text: — [milked] through the thirst of the young. <s>Locana</s>: Therefore, his is not that joy which is milked by the <s>yogins</s>. //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "Thus" (<s>evam</s>) etc. "Established through self-experience" (<s>svasaṃvit-siddham</s>): established through the direct experience of connoisseurs. "This" (<s>etat</s>): meaning the soul-hood of poetry belonging to the suggested meaning. "Shows" (<s>darśayati</s>): by the previous <s>kārikā</s>, the <s>itihāsa</s> (historical narrative) was stated as the proof for the soul-hood of the suggested; but by this [<s>kārikā</s>], to confirm that, the proof in the form of self-experience (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) is stated. For in self-experience, no one has any dispute — this is the meaning. "<s>Sarasvatī</s>" — meaning "by the popular verse beginning with '<s>Sarasvatī</s>'." He glosses the word "<s>Sarasvatī</s>" — "the divine lady in the form of speech." "<s>Tat</s>" has the meaning of "previously stated." He says that "<s>vastu-tattva</s>" is the commentary on "<s>artha-vastu</s>" — "by the word <s>vastu</s>" etc. Among meanings — factual content (<s>vastu</s>), figure (<s>alaṅkāra</s>), and <s>rasa</s> — the essential meaning-content (<s>artha-vastu</s>) is the <s>vastu</s> that is the essence. He glosses the resultant meaning of "<s>tadarthavastu</s>" as the object of the action — "streaming forth" (<s>niḥṣyandamāne</s>) etc.: "divine" (<s>divya</s>): transcendent. "Spontaneously" (<s>svayam eva</s>) indicates the ever-present orientation [of <s>Sarasvatī</s>]. "Flowing" (<s>prasnuvānā</s>): exuding. By this, the similarity of <s>Sarasvatī</s> to a cow is indicated. He cites the authority for the stated interpretation — "as he said" (<s>yad āha</s>) etc.
Without the possession by that [<s>rasa</s>], but rather by force — for that which is milked by <s>yogins</s> —

children.text: ata eva--- yaṃ sarvaśaulāḥ parikalpya vatsaṃ merau sthite dogdhari dohadakṣe /
children.translated_text: Therefore: "Treating him as the calf, with <s>Meru</s> standing as the milker, skilled in milking —"
"— all the mountain-dwellers milked the earth as instructed by <s>Pṛthu</s>, [obtaining] radiant gems and great herbs." //
