raseti /
pratibhāviśeṣaṃ parisphurantamabhivyanakti /
yenāsminnativicitrakaviparamparāvāhini saṃsāre kālidāsaprabhṛtayo dvitrāḥ pañcaṣā vā mahākavaya iti gaṇyante /
idaṃ cāparaṃ pratīyamānasyārthasya sadbhāvasādhanaṃ pramāṇam---
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] By this, the capacity of <s>Himavat</s> (the Himalayas) to be the vessel for the choicest essence-objects is stated. "Manifests the flashing forth" (<s>abhivyanakti parisphurantam</s>): that creative intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) is not something inferred by the recipients, but rather shines forth through possession by it — this is the meaning. As our teacher <s>Bhaṭṭatauta</s> stated: "The experience of the hero, the poet, and the listener is the same; therefore..." "<s>Pratibhā</s>" (creative intuition): the intelligence (<s>prajñā</s>) capable of creating novel content; its "special quality" (<s>viśeṣa</s>) is the clarity and beauty of aesthetic immersion (<s>rasāveśa</s>), i.e., the capacity for poetic creation. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "Through affection for the connoisseur-calf" — by this reason. "<s>Hi</s>" — for what is milked, i.e., flows forth; "therefore" (<s>tena tasmāt hetoḥ</s>): of this <s>rasa</s> that flows from the thirst of the young, "his joy would not be the same" (<s>ramaḥ na syāt</s>) — meaning that bliss-<s>rasa</s> which is milked by <s>yogins</s>. To clarify the dissimilarity, he states the meaning of the fourth quarter — "through possession by that" (<s>tadāveśena</s>) etc. "Possession by that" (<s>tadāveśena</s>): through immersion in <s>rasa</s>. "<s>Api</s>" has the meaning of "<s>eva</s>" (indeed). "By force" (<s>ākrāntyā</s>): through compulsion — meaning through the perfection of contemplation in the form of identification with the bliss-form lord — this is the purport. But the cow of speech, through the thirst of the young, [is milked] by the force of that immersion in <s>rasa</s> — by that very milker — this is the purport. He cites proof for the superiority of what flows spontaneously over what is extracted by force — "therefore" (<s>ata eva</s>) etc. "Therefore" — because the cow, filled with <s>rasa</s>, being subject to the possession by that [<s>rasa</s>], has agency regarding its own spontaneous flowing; precisely therefore. "Of <s>Himavat</s>" in the form of a calf — this is the purport. The connection is: "therefore, by this, the capacity of <s>Himavat</s> to be the vessel for the choicest essence is stated." Correcting the misunderstanding that "manifests" (<s>abhivyanakti</s>) means "causes to be inferred," he explains — "for the recipients" (<s>pratipattṝn</s>) etc. In "<s>abhivyanakti</s>," "for the recipients" (<s>pratipattṝn prati</s>) should be supplied. Meaning: of the recipients. "That <s>pratibhā</s>": the creative intuition belonging to the great poet. "Not inferred" (<s>na anumīyamānā</s>): meaning not the object of inference through the mark of such <s>Sarasvatī</s>. "That" (<s>tat</s>): meaning through immersion in <s>rasa</s> that is the domain of <s>pratibhā</s>. "Shining forth" (<s>bhāsamānā</s>): meaning becoming the object of direct perception. Such <s>Sarasvatī</s> of great poets manifests such a special <s>pratibhā</s> distinguished by flashing forth — through manifestation (<s>abhivyañjana</s>) consisting of removing the veil in the form of non-orientation toward <s>rasa</s>-immersion — [she] makes it an object of direct perception for the recipients. This is the meaning of the <s>kārikā</s>. This is the purport. How does the <s>rasa</s> belonging to the poet come to belong to the recipient? To that he says "as stated" (<s>yad uktam</s>) etc. "Of the hero" (<s>nāyakasya</s>): of the hero through superimposition by the poet; of the listener through the savoring of <s>rasa</s>. This is the purport. He glosses "the special quality of <s>pratibhā</s>" — "<s>pratibhā</s>" etc. "<s>Prajñā</s>": intelligence. "<s>Rasa</s>" etc. He manifests the special quality of <s>pratibhā</s> flashing forth. By which, in this world (<s>saṃsāra</s>) flowing with the stream of the most varied succession of poets, only two or three, or five or six — like <s>Kālidāsa</s> and others — are counted as great poets. And this is another proof establishing the existence of the suggested meaning —
[That suggested meaning] is not known by mere knowledge of the science of words and meanings alone;

children.text: vedyate sa tu kāvyārtha-tattvajñair eva kevalam // DhvK_1.7 //
children.translated_text: It is known only by those who truly understand the essence of poetic meaning. // <s>DhvK</s> 1.7 //
[That suggested meaning] is not known by mere knowledge of the science of words and meanings alone;
It is known only by those who truly understand the essence of poetic meaning. // 7 //

children.text:
so 'rtho yasmātkevalaṃ kāvyārthatattvajñaireva jñāyate /
yadi ca vācyarūpa locanam yadāha muniḥ---'kaverantargataṃ bhāvaṃ' iti /
yeneti /
abhivyaktena sphuratā pratibhāviśeṣeṇa nimittena mahākavitvagaṇaneti yāvat // .6 // // .//
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] That meaning, since it is known only by those who truly understand the essence of poetic meaning — and if it were of the form of the expressible — <s>Locana</s>: As the sage (<s>Bharata</s>) said: "the <s>bhāva</s> (emotion) hidden within the poet." "By which" (<s>yena</s>): by the manifested, i.e., flashing special quality of <s>pratibhā</s> as the cause — the counting as a great poet — this is the purport. // 6 //

children.text:
idaṃ ceti /
na kevalaṃ 'pratīyamānaṃ punaranyadeva' ityetatkārikāsūcitau svarūpaviṣayabhedāveva; yāvadbhinnasāmagrīvedyatvamapi vācyātiriktatve pramāṇamiti yāvat /
vedyata bālapriyā rasāveśasya kāraṇabhūtaṃ yadvaiśadyaṃ rasāveśānabhimukhatvarāhityaṃ tena yatsaundaryaṃ rasaparatvādilakṣaṇam. yadvā---rasāveśena yadvaiśadyaṃ "vivakṣātatparatvena"tyādisūcipadoṣarāhityaṃ, tena saundaryaṃ tatsūcitaguṇasāhityaṃ tadrūpaṃ kāvyanirmāṇakṣamatvamityarthaḥ /
sarasvatīpratibhāviśeṣaṃ pratipattṝṇāmabhivyanaktītyatra saṃvādamāha--yadāheti /
'yene'tyādivṛttigranthaṃ vyācaṣṭe---abhivyaktenetyādi /
abivyaktena ata eva sphuratā pratipattṝṇāṃ pratyakṣaviṣayeṇa /
'nimittene'tyantaṃ 'yene'tyasya vyākhyānam /
mahākavitvagaṇaneti /
pratipattṝṇāmādau rasasyānubhavastataḥ pratibhāyāstato mahākavitvagaṇaneti bhāvaḥ // .6 // // .//
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "And this" (<s>idaṃ ca</s>) etc. Not only the two distinctions of own-nature and domain indicated by the <s>kārikā</s> "the suggested is indeed something different" — but also the being-known-through-a-different-aggregate-of-conditions is a proof of the distinctness from the expressible — this is the purport. "Known" (<s>vedyate</s>): [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the clarity (<s>vaiśadya</s>) that is the cause of <s>rasa</s>-immersion — the absence of non-orientation toward <s>rasa</s>-immersion — by that, the beauty (<s>saundarya</s>) characterized by devotion to <s>rasa</s> etc. Alternatively: the clarity that consists of <s>rasa</s>-immersion — the absence of blemishes indicated by "with determination and devotion" etc. — by that, the beauty consisting of the companionship of the qualities indicated by those [expressions]; having that form — the capacity for poetic creation — this is the meaning. He states the corroboration of [the claim that] <s>Sarasvatī</s> manifests the special quality of <s>pratibhā</s> for the recipients — "as stated" (<s>yad āha</s>) etc. He glosses the <s>vṛtti</s> text beginning with "<s>yena</s>" — "manifested" (<s>abhivyaktena</s>) etc. "Manifested" — therefore flashing forth, i.e., being the object of direct perception for the recipients. Up to "by the cause" (<s>nimittena</s>) is the commentary on "<s>yena</s>." "The counting as a great poet" (<s>mahākavitvagaṇanā</s>): the purport is: first the experience of <s>rasa</s> for the recipients, then [the recognition of] <s>pratibhā</s>, then the counting as a great poet. // 6 //

children.text:
'na kevelam' ityādi 'vedyatvamapī'tyantaṃ 'idañcāparam' ityasya vivaraṇam /
sadbhāvetyādervācyātiriktatvena sadbhāvasyetyādyartha ityāha---vācyetyādi /
tathā ca kārikā evāsāvarthaḥ syāttadvācyavāṭacakarūpaparijñānādeva tatpratītiḥ syāt /
atha ca vācyavācakalakṣaṇamātrakṛtaśramāṇāṃ kāvyatattvārthabhāvanāvimukhānāṃ svaraśrutyādilakṣaṇamivāpragītānāṃ gāndharvalakṣaṇavidāmagocara evāsāvarthaḥ /
locanam iti /
na tu na vedyate, yena na syādasāviti bhāvaḥ /
kāvyasya tattvabhūto yo 'rthastasya bhāvanā vācyātirekeṇānavaratacarvaṇā tatra vimukhānām /
svarāḥ ṣaṅjādayaḥ sapta /
śrutirnāma śabdasya vailakṣaṇyamātrakāri yadrūpāntaraṃ tatparimāṇā svaratadantarālobhayabhedakalpitā dvāviśatividhā /
ādiśabdena jātyaṃśakagrāmarāgabhāṣāvibhāṣāntarabhāṣādeśī bālapriyā nādhikāribhedapradarśanaparā, kintu sāmagrībhedapradarśanaparā /
vācyārthabodhe 'nuśiṣṭaśabdārthajñānarūpā, nyaṅgyārthabodhe tu sahṛdayatvādirūpā ca sāmagrī pūrvottarārdhābhyāṃ darśitā ceti bhāvaḥ /
vedane siddhe tatsāmagrīcintāvakāśa ityāśyena punarapi vedyata ityuktam, tadvyācaṣṭe---na tvityādi /
yena avedanena /
asau pratīyamānārthaḥ /
vṛttau 'so 'rtha' ityādyuttarārdhasya vivaraṇaṃ 'tasmādi'ti pūrvārdhena sambandhaḥ /
tadvivaraṇaṃ 'yadici'tyādi /
'asau arthaḥ' pratīyamānārthaḥ /
'tatpratītiḥ' pratīyamānārthapratītiḥ /
iṣṭāpatti pariharati--'atha ce'tyādi /
'atha cāsāvarthaḥ kāvyatattvārthabhāvanāvimukānāṃ vācyavācakalakṣaṇamātrakṛtaśramāṇāmagocara' iti sambandhaḥ /
tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ---'apragītānāṃ gandharvalakṣaṇavidāṃ svaraśrutyādilakṣaṇamive'ti /
'agocaraḥ' agrāhyaḥ /
'gāndharvalakṣaṇavidāṃ granthapaṭhanena saṅgītalakṣaṇaṃ jānatām /
kārikāyāṃ 'sa hī'tyatra sa tviti ca pāṭhaḥ /
kāvyetyādikaṃ vyācaṣṭe---kāvyasyetyādi /
śabdasyeti /
gītādirūpaśabdasyetyarthaḥ /
vailakṣaṇyamātrakāri parasparabhedamātrakāri /
na guṇādāyakamiti bhāvaḥ /
rūpāntaraṃ rūpaviśeṣaḥ /
gītādiśabdaśravaṇe sati tasya śabdasya yadrūpāntaraṃ lavādikālāṃśaṃ nimittīkṛtya jāyate tadityarthaḥ /
taditi /
tat parimāmaṃ kālapramāṇaṃ yasyāḥ setyarthaḥ. tanmātrakāleti yāvat /
svareti /
svaraḥ tasya svarasyāntarālamubhayamarthātpārśvadvayaṃ ca teṣāṃ yo bhedastatkalpitetyarthaḥ /
śrutirnāma svarasyaivāṃśa iti yāvat /
jātītyādi /
jhātyādīnāṃ svarūpamanyato 'vadhātavyam /
apragītānāmiti bālapriyā nañsamāsaghaṭakaṃ pragītapadaṃ vyācaṣṭe---prakṛṣṭamityādi /
pakṣānramāha--kanāḍībhedavaśāt dvāviṃśatiprakāro bhavati /
ima eva bhedāḥśrutaya iti vyapadiśyante /
śravaṇārthasya dhātoḥ ktin pratyaye śrūyanta iti vyutpattyā śrūtiśabdo niṣpannaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>śruti</s>' is derived from the root '<s>śru</s>' (to hear) with the suffix '<s>ktin</s>', by the etymology: 'they are heard' (<s>śrūyante</s>).

children.text: atra nādāparaparyāyaśrutivibhāgaviṣaye bahavaḥ prakārā varttante---kecana dvāviṃśatiṃ śrutīrmanyante, apare ca ṣaṭṣaṣṭibhedabhinnāḥ śrutaya ityācakṣate, anye punarānantayaṃ kathayanti śrutīnām /
children.translated_text: Regarding this topic — the classification of <s>śruti</s>, which is another name for <s>nāda</s> (sound/tone) — there are many views: some hold there are twenty-two <s>śrutis</s>; others state that the <s>śrutis</s> are differentiated into sixty-six types; still others declare the <s>śrutis</s> to be infinite in number.

children.text: ata evoktaṃ kohalena--- dvāviṃśatiṃ kecidudāharanti śrutīḥ śrutijñānavicāradakṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hence <s>Kohala</s> has said: 'Some — those skilled in the investigation of the knowledge of <s>śrutis</s> — enumerate twenty-two <s>śrutis</s>;
some indeed [speak of] sixty-six varieties of those [śrutis]; [while others] propound their infinity.'

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The passage from '<s>na kevalam</s>' (not only) up to '<s>vedyatvam api</s>' (its knowability too) is the elaboration of '<s>idañ cāparam</s>' (and this further [point]). He states the meaning of '<s>sadbhāva</s>' etc. as 'the existence as distinct from the expressed': '<s>vācya</s>' etc. And thus, that meaning would [be present] in the <s>kārikā</s> itself; its cognition would arise from the understanding of the expressed meaning and its verbal form alone. And moreover, for those whose effort has been directed only at the definition of the expressed meaning and its verbal form, [and] who are averse to the contemplation of the essential meaning of poetry — that meaning is beyond the reach [of their comprehension], just as the definition of <s>svaras</s> (musical notes), <s>śrutis</s> (microtonal intervals), etc. is beyond the reach of those who know the definition of music (<s>gāndharva</s>) through textual study [alone] but have not actually performed music. The <s>Locana</s> [says]: 'thus' — the purport is: 'but it is not unknowable, such that it would not exist.' The contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of that meaning which is the truth of poetry — the unceasing savoring [of it] as distinct from the expressed — [is what] those who are averse [to it lack]. The <s>svaras</s> (notes) are seven: <s>ṣaḍja</s> etc. <s>Śruti</s> is the name for that particular form of sound which merely creates differentiation [between pitches]; its measure [determines the count]: twenty-two varieties are posited through the division into [intervals between] the note, the inter-note space, and both [combined]. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), <s>jāti</s>, <s>aṃśaka</s>, <s>grāma</s>, <s>rāga</s>, <s>bhāṣā</s>, <s>vibhāṣā</s>, <s>antarabhāṣā</s>, <s>deśī</s> [are included]. The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [says]: [this passage is] not aimed at showing the distinction of qualified persons, but rather at showing the distinction of the aggregate of conditions (<s>sāmagrī</s>). For the comprehension of the expressed meaning, the aggregate consists of knowledge of instructed word-meanings; but for the comprehension of the suggested meaning, the aggregate consists of the quality of being a connoisseur (<s>sahṛdayatva</s>) etc. — the two aggregates have been shown by the two halves [of the verse]. This is the purport. Once the knowability [of the suggested meaning] is established, there is scope for investigating its aggregate of conditions — with this intention, 'it is indeed known' has been stated; he explains that: '<s>na tu</s>' etc. '<s>Yena</s>' — by non-cognition. '<s>Asau</s>' — the suggested meaning. The elaboration of the second half of the <s>vṛtti</s> text '<s>so 'rthaḥ</s>' etc. is connected with the first half by '<s>tasmāt</s>' etc. Its elaboration is '<s>yadi</s>' etc. '<s>Asau arthaḥ</s>' — the suggested meaning. '<s>Tatpratītiḥ</s>' — the cognition of the suggested meaning. He removes the welcome consequence (<s>iṣṭāpatti</s>): '<s>atha ca</s>' etc. The connection is: 'and moreover, that meaning is beyond the reach of those who are averse to the contemplation of the essential meaning of poetry, whose effort has been limited to the mere definition of the expressed and its verbal form.' The illustration there: 'like the definition of <s>svaras</s>, <s>śrutis</s>, etc. for those who know the definition of <s>gāndhaarva</s> (music) through book-reading [alone] but have not actually performed music.' '<s>Agocara</s>' — ungraspable. '<s>Gāndharvalakṣaṇavidām</s>' — of those who know the definition of music through textual study. In the <s>kārikā</s>, '<s>sa hi</s>' — there is also the reading '<s>sa tu</s>.' He explains '<s>kāvya</s>' etc.: '<s>kāvyasya</s>' etc. '<s>Śabdasya</s>' — meaning 'of sound in the form of song etc.' '<s>Vailakṣaṇyamātrakāri</s>' — merely creating mutual differentiation; the purport is: not conferring qualities. '<s>Rūpāntara</s>' — a particular form; when a sound in the form of song etc. is heard, that particular form which arises based on the temporal fraction (<s>lavādikālāṃśa</s>) of that sound. '<s>Tat</s>' — its measure (<s>parimāṇa</s>), i.e., the temporal extent, is [the basis for counting]. '<s>Svara</s>' etc. — the interval between the note, the inter-note space, and both sides — from whose differentiation [the śrutis] are posited: this is the meaning. <s>Śruti</s> is indeed a portion of the <s>svara</s> — this is the meaning. '<s>Jāti</s>' etc. — the essential nature of <s>jātis</s> etc. should be ascertained from elsewhere. '<s>Apragītānām</s>' — The <s>Bālapriyā</s> explains the word '<s>pragīta</s>' in the compound with the negative: '<s>prakṛṣṭam</s>' etc. He states the [alternative] interpretations — by the differentiation of the vocal channel (<s>kanāḍī</s>), [the sound] becomes of twenty-two varieties. These very differentiations are designated as <s>śrutis</s>.
Thus.

children.text:
tatra dvāviṃśatipakṣa eva prakṛte granthakārābhimataḥ /
etāsāṃ śrutīnāṃ mitho bhedaḥ--viṇādaṇḍe pūrvottarabāvena dvāviṃśatiṃ tantrīḥ parikalpya prathamāpekṣayā dvitīyāditantrīṣu kiñcitkiñcidddaḍhīkaraṇapūrvakaṃ vādyamānāsu tāsu pratyakṣato 'vagantuṃ śakyaḥ /
ābhyaśca śrutibhyaḥ ṣaṅjarṣabhagāndhāramadyamapañcamadhaivataniṣādākhyāḥ sapta svarā bhavanti /
svataḥ sahakārikāraṇanirapekṣaṃ rañjayati śrotṛcittamanuraktaṃ karotīti svaraḥ, iti tadvyutpattiḥ /
saptānāmapyamīṣāṃ svarāṇāṃ vyastānāṃ satāṃ dṛṣṭāddaṣṭaphalaupayikatvaṃ na bhavatīti tatsiddhaye grāmasyāvaśyakatā jāyate /
grāmo nāma svarasamūhaḥ /
etāvattyucyamāne laukikavaidikavākyeṣvapi svarasamūhasya sambhavāttatrātivyāptissyāditi tahyāvṛttaye mūrcchanākramatāvavarṇālaṅkārajātyādyāśrayatve sati svarasamūhatvaṃ grāmatvamiti lakṣaṇaṃ vaktavyam /
mūrcachanādīnāṃ svarūpavibhāgādayaḥ saṅgītaratnākarasya svarādhyāyato 'vaseyāḥ /
sa cāyaṃ grāmo dvividhaḥ--ṣaṅjagrāmaḥ, madhyamagrāmaśceti /
tatraikasman vīṇādaṇḍe dvāviṃśatiṃ tantrīḥ parikalpaya āditasturīyāyāṃ tantryāṃ ṣaṅjasvaraḥ, saptamyāṃ ṛṣabhaḥ, navamyāṃ gāndhāraḥ, trayodaśyāṃ madhyamaḥ, saptadaśyāṃ pañcamaḥ, viṃśyāṃ dhaivataḥ, dvāviṃśyāṃ niṣādaśceti svareṣu vinyasteṣu ṣaṅjagrāmo bhavati /
ayameva śuddhāśrayaḥ ṣaṅjagrāma iti vyavahliyate /
evamaparasmin vīṇādaṇḍe āditasturīyāyāṃ tantryāṃ madhyamaḥ, saptamyāṃ pañcamaḥ, ekādaśyāṃ dhaivataḥ, trayodaśyāṃ niṣādaḥ, saptadaśyāṃ ṣaṅjaḥ, viṃśyāmṛṣabhaḥ, dvāviśyāṃ gāndhāraśceti vinyasteṣu svareṣu madhyamagrāmo bhavati /
ayameva vikṛtāśrayo madhyamagrāma iti vyapadiśyate /
evañca ṣaṅjagrāme---ṣaṅjamadhyamapañcamāḥ catasṛbhyaḥ śrutibhya utpannāḥ, ṛṣabhadhaivatau tisṛbhya utpannau, gāndhāraniṣādau dvābhyāmutpannau; madhyamagrāme ca madhyamadhaivataṣaṅjāḥ catasṛbhya utpannāḥ, pañcamarṣabhau tisṛbhya utpannau, niṣādagandhārau dvābhyāmutpannāvita dvaigrāmikyo dvāviṃśyaḥ śrutayaḥ svaratadantarālobhayabhedakalpitāḥ siddhāḥ /
tatra ṣaṅjagrāmamadhyamagrāmayormilitvā santyaṣṭādaśa jātayaḥ--ṣāṅjī, ārṣabhī, gāndharī, madhyamā, patrvamī, dhaivatī, naiṣādī, paṅjakaiśikī, ṣaṅjodīcyavā, ṣaṅjagātuṃ veti /
children.translated_text: Among these, combining the <s>ṣaḍja-grāma</s> and the <s>madhyama-grāma</s>, there are eighteen <s>jātis</s> (melody-types): <s>ṣāḍjī</s>, <s>ārṣabhī</s>, <s>gāndhārī</s>, <s>madhyamā</s>, <s>pañcamī</s>, <s>dhaivatī</s>, <s>naiṣādī</s>, <s>pañcakaiśikī</s>, <s>ṣaḍjodīcyavā</s>, <s>ṣaḍjagātum</s> etc.

children.text: evaṃ vācyavyatirekiṇo vyaṅgyasya sadbhāvaṃ pratipādya prādhānyaṃ tasyaiveti darśayati--- locanam mārgā gṛhyante /
children.translated_text: Having thus established the existence of the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) as distinct from the expressed (<s>vācya</s>), he shows that the primacy belongs to that [suggested meaning] alone — The <s>Locana</s> [says]: 'the paths are grasped.'

children.text: prakṛṣṭaṃ gītaṃ gānaṃ yeṣāṃ te pragītāḥ, gātuṃ vā prārabdhā ityādikarmaṇiktaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Pragīta</s>' — those whose singing (<s>gīta</s>) is accomplished (<s>prakṛṣṭa</s>), i.e., who have [actually] performed music; or [formed] from the desiderative root meaning 'who have begun to sing' — with the past passive participial suffix in the agent-sense.
And by [the mention of] 'beginning,' the completion up to the fruition [of the musical performance] is implied. [7]

Among these, the position of twenty-two [śrutis] is the one accepted by the author of the present treatise. The mutual differentiation of these <s>śrutis</s> — by arranging twenty-two strings on a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) neck in ascending order and, starting from the first, tightening each successive string slightly more before playing — can be directly perceived. And from these <s>śrutis</s>, the seven <s>svaras</s> (notes) named <s>ṣaḍja</s>, <s>ṛṣabha</s>, <s>gāndhāra</s>, <s>madhyama</s>, <s>pañcama</s>, <s>dhaivata</s>, and <s>niṣāda</s> arise. The etymology of '<s>svara</s>' is: 'that which delights (<s>rañjayati</s>) the listener's mind spontaneously, without dependence on auxiliary causes — [that is, makes it] enraptured (<s>anurakta</s>).' Even though these seven <s>svaras</s> exist separately, they do not produce the fruit that is both seen and unseen — hence the necessity of a <s>grāma</s> (scale) for their realization. A <s>grāma</s> is a collection of <s>svaras</s>. If merely stated thus, over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) to collections of svaras in worldly and Vedic sentences would arise; to prevent that, the definition should be stated as: <s>grāma</s>-hood is being a collection of svaras that depends on <s>mūrchanā</s> (melodic progression), <s>krama</s> (sequence), <s>tāna</s> (melodic elaboration), <s>varṇa</s> (melodic movements), <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornaments), <s>jāti</s> (melody-types), etc. The essential natures and divisions of <s>mūrchanā</s> etc. should be learned from the <s>Svara</s> chapter of the <s>Saṅgītaratnākara</s>. And this <s>grāma</s> is of two types: the <s>ṣaḍja-grāma</s> and the <s>madhyama-grāma</s>. Among these, on one <s>vīṇā</s> neck, arranging twenty-two strings — the <s>ṣaḍja</s> note on the fourth string from the beginning, <s>ṛṣabha</s> on the seventh, <s>gāndhāra</s> on the ninth, <s>madhyama</s> on the thirteenth, <s>pañcama</s> on the seventeenth, <s>dhaivata</s> on the twentieth, and <s>niṣāda</s> on the twenty-second — when the notes are thus arranged, the <s>ṣaḍja-grāma</s> results. This very [arrangement] is called the <s>ṣaḍja-grāma</s> with pure foundation (<s>śuddhāśraya</s>). Similarly, on another <s>vīṇā</s> neck — <s>madhyama</s> on the fourth string from the beginning, <s>pañcama</s> on the seventh, <s>dhaivata</s> on the eleventh, <s>niṣāda</s> on the thirteenth, <s>ṣaḍja</s> on the seventeenth, <s>ṛṣabha</s> on the twentieth, and <s>gāndhāra</s> on the twenty-second — when the notes are thus arranged, the <s>madhyama-grāma</s> results. This very [arrangement] is designated as the <s>madhyama-grāma</s> with modified foundation (<s>vikṛtāśraya</s>). And thus, in the <s>ṣaḍja-grāma</s>: <s>ṣaḍja</s>, <s>madhyama</s>, and <s>pañcama</s> arise from four <s>śrutis</s>; <s>ṛṣabha</s> and <s>dhaivata</s> from three; <s>gāndhāra</s> and <s>niṣāda</s> from two. In the <s>madhyama-grāma</s>: <s>madhyama</s>, <s>dhaivata</s>, and <s>ṣaḍja</s> arise from four; <s>pañcama</s> and <s>ṛṣabha</s> from three; <s>niṣāda</s> and <s>gāndhāra</s> from two — thus the twenty-two <s>śrutis</s> belonging to the two <s>grāmas</s>, posited through the division of note, inter-note space, and both, are established.
'[They are] to be recognized.' The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [says]: '<s>ādikarmaṇi</s>' etc.
The meaning is: 'having the sense of inception.'
'<s>Phala</s>' (fruit) —
The fruit here is the direct realization of <s>svaras</s> etc. [7]
'<s>Evam</s>' (thus) — the meaning is: through the difference in essential nature, and through being knowable by different aggregates of conditions.
'<s>Evam</s>' (thus) — lest there be a mistake of referring merely to what is proximate, he explains: '<s>svarūpabhedena</s>' (through difference of essential nature) etc.
That meaning, and a certain word endowed with the capacity to manifest it —

children.text: yatnataḥ pratyabhijñeyau tau śabdārthau mahākaveḥ // DhvK_1.8 //
children.translated_text: those two — the word and meaning of the great poet — are to be recognized with effort. [DhvK 1.8]
That meaning, and a certain word endowed with the capacity to manifest it —
those two — the word and meaning of the great poet — are to be recognized with effort. [8]

children.text:
vyaṅgyo 'rthastadvyaktisāmarthyayogī śabdaśca kaścana, na śabdamātram /
tāveva śabdārthau mahākaveḥ pratyabhijñeyau /
vyahgyavyañjakābhyāmeva suprayuktābhyāṃ locanam tyarhārthe kṛtyaḥ, sarvo hi tathā yatate itīyatā prādhānye lokasiddhatvaṃ pramāṇamuktam /
niyogārthena ca kṛtyena śikṣākrama uktaḥ /

bālapriyā 'svarūpaviṣayabhedene'ti ca pāṭhaḥ /
kathaṃ prādhānyaṃ darśitamityato vyācaṣṭe---arhārtha ityādi /

ko 'sāvityatrāha--pratibhāvata iti /
svayaṃ svayameva /

children.translated_text: The attainment of the status of great poet (<s>mahākavitva</s>) [comes] through [the recognition] of great poets — not merely through the composition of expressed words and meanings.

children.text: locanam yathoktamasmatparamagurubhiḥ śrīmadutpalapādaiḥ-- taistairapyupayācitairupanatastanvyāḥ sthito 'pyantike kānto lokasamāna evamaparijñāto na rantuṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Locana</s> [says]: as has been said by our supreme guru, the illustrious <s>Utpaladeva</s>: 'Even though the beloved stands nearby — wooed with various [entreaties] and approaching — the lover, like an ordinary man, not having recognized [her], is unable to enjoy [her];

children.text: lokasyaiṣa tathānavekṣitaguṇaḥ svātmāpi viśveśvaro naivālaṃ nijavaibhavāya tadiyaṃ tatpratyabhijñoditā ḥ
children.translated_text: just so, the Lord of the universe (<s>Viśveśvara</s>), whose qualities are thus unexamined by the world — even [His own] Self is not sufficient for [the manifestation of] His own glory; hence this <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition) has been taught.'
Thus.

The suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) and a certain word endowed with the capacity to manifest it — not just any word. Those very word and meaning of the great poet are to be recognized. Only when both the suggested and the suggestor are well-employed — The <s>Locana</s> [says]: the <s>kṛtya</s> suffix [in '<s>pratyabhijñeyau</s>'] is in the sense of worthiness (<s>arha</s>); for everyone thus strives [to recognize them] — by this much, the well-known [practice] among people is cited as the authority for [dhvani's] primacy. And by the <s>kṛtya</s> suffix in the sense of injunction (<s>niyoga</s>), the sequence of instruction [for the poet] is stated. By the word '<s>pratyabhijñeya</s>' (to be recognized), he says this: 'Although, by the principle that poetry arises spontaneously in one endowed with <s>pratibhā</s> (creative genius), this [dhvani] manifests of its own accord [in the poet], nevertheless, when it is specifically analyzed as "this is of this nature," it branches out a thousandfold.' The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [says]: there is also the reading '<s>svarūpaviṣayabhedena</s>.' [The question:] 'How has the primacy been shown?' — to this he explains: '<s>arhārtha</s>' etc. '<s>Kṛtyaḥ</s>' — the <s>kṛtya</s> suffix. '<s>Sarvaḥ</s>' — every connoisseur. The connection is: '<s>tathā hi</s>' (for indeed). The meaning is: 'by [their being] worthy [of recognition].' '<s>Yatate</s>' — [everyone] exerts [themselves] out of desire to know such [types of] word and meaning. He states the conclusion: '<s>iti</s>' etc. '<s>Iyatā</s>' — by this much, i.e., by the statement that [these are] to be recognized by connoisseurs. '<s>Prādhānye</s>' — concerning the primacy of the suggested. '<s>Loka</s>' etc. — the meaning is: 'the practice of connoisseurs.' The connection is: 'By connoisseurs, that meaning and such a word — those are the word and meaning of the great poet that are to be recognized with effort.' '<s>Tau</s>' (those two) indicates the form of recognition: 'these [before us] are those word and meaning of such a kind belonging to the great poet' — meaning they are worthy of the connoisseur's recognition of the form 'these are [indeed] those.' And an alternative meaning is also to be accepted — he says '<s>niyoga</s>' etc. In this interpretation, '<s>tau</s>' means 'those previously stated.' And the first half [of the verse] constitutes a separate sentence. '<s>Śikṣākrama</s>' — the method of poetic instruction. He states the purpose of the recognition of word and meaning: '<s>pratyabhijñeya</s>' etc. '<s>Kāvyam</s>' etc. The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) indicates the distinction from <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) etc. '<s>Jātu</s>' — only sometimes. '<s>Kasyacit</s>' — not of everyone. 'Who is that?' — to this he says: '<s>pratibhāvataḥ</s>' (of one endowed with creative genius). '<s>Svayam</s>' — of its own accord. '<s>Asya</s>' — of this poet. '<s>Etat</s>' — this poetry. '<s>Idam</s>' — 'this should be done in this way' — this is the mode of analytical examination. '<s>Nirūpyamāṇam</s>' — the meaning is: 'when being analyzed and practiced.' '<s>Tat</s>' carries over. '<s>Sahasra</s>' etc. — the meaning is: 'it becomes thousandfold.' The purport is: because the varieties of <s>vicchitti</s> (artistic variation) are infinite. He supports the necessity of specific analysis with an illustration by contrast: '<s>yathoktam</s>' (as has been said) etc. The completion is: 'at the end of the <s>Pratyabhijñā-śāstra</s>.'

tena jñātasyāpi viśeṣato nirūpaṇamanusandhānātmakamatra pratyabhijñānaṃ, na tu tadevadamityetāvanmātram /

yo mahākavirahaṃ bhūyāsamityāśāste /
evaṃ vyaṅgyasyārthasya vyañjakasya śabdasya ca prādhānyaṃ vadatā vyaṅkyavyañjakabhāvasyāpi bālapriyā taistairiti /
sāmānyato 'vagatasyāpīśvarasya viśeṣato 'vagamamantareṇa na phalaparyantībhāvalābha ityartapradarśanaparo 'yaṃ ślokaḥ /
taistairupayācitaiḥ dūtīsampreṣaṇātmavṛttāntanivedanādibhirupacārapūrvakayācanaiḥ /
'upanato 'pī'ti yojanā /
na kevalamupanataḥ, tanvyā antike sthito 'pi /

ata eva lokasamānaḥ janasādhāraṇatvaṃ prāptaḥ /

yathā rantuṃ ramayituṃ tanvīmānandayitumiti yāvat /
na prabhavatīti śeṣaḥ /
evaṃ dṛṣṭāntaṃ pradarśya prakṛtamāha---lokasyetyādi /
'lokasyātme'ti sambandhaḥ /
anavekṣiteti /
lokena viśeṣato 'jñātetyarthaḥ /
yasmātsāmānyato jñāte 'pi viśeṣājñānasambhavaḥ, tasmāt svataḥ sphuritayorapi śabdārthayoḥ mahākavinā yuktameva pratyabhijñānakaraṇamiti bhāvaḥ /
tarhi ko 'tra pratyabhijñāpadārtha ityata uktaphalatayā tatsvrūpamāha---tenetyādi /
mahākavitvarvṛttau śikṣānarhatvānniyogāyogamāśaṅkya vyācaṣṭe--yo mahetyādi /
mahākavirityasya mahākavitvaprakārakāśasāviṣaya ityartha iti bhāvaḥ /
vṛttau 'mahākavestau śabdārthau sahṛdayaiḥ pratyabhijñeyāvi'viti 'tāveva śabdārthau mahākaveḥ pratyabhijñeyāvi'ti ca yojanā bodhyā /
mahākavinā pratyabhijñeyāvi'viti 'tāveva śabdārthau mahākaveḥ pratyabhijñetyāvi'ti ca yojanā bodhyā /
mahākavinā pratyabhijñeyāvityaseyopapādakam--'vyaṅgye'tyādi /
'suprayuktābhyāṃ' viśeṣato nirūpya prayuktābhyām /
'mahākavīnām' ityasya ukto 'rthaḥ /
vṛttigranthena vyañajakasyāpi pradhānyaṃ darśitamata āha--evamityādi /
upapannamiti /
dhvaniriti idānīṃ vyaṅgyavyañjakayoḥ prādhānye 'pi yadvācyavācakāveva prathamamupādadate kavayastadapi yuktamevetyāha--
children.translated_text:
[<s>Balapriya</s>:] Therefore, the recognition (<s>pratyabhijna</s>) here is a specific examination in the form of investigation, even of what is [already] known — not merely [the recognition] 'this is that very thing.' 'Of a great poet (<s>mahakavi</s>)' — [meaning] one who aspires 'may I become a great poet.' Thus, in stating the primacy of both the suggested meaning and the suggestive word, [the author shows that] the relation of suggested-and-suggestor itself [is also primary].
<s>Balapriya</s>: 'By those various [means]' — this verse aims to show that even when the Lord (<s>Isvara</s>) has been known in general, without knowing [Him] specifically, the attainment of the fruit is not achieved. 'By those various entreaties' — by courteous solicitations such as sending messengers, conveying one's story, etc. The construction is: 'even though having approached.' Not only having approached, but even standing near the slender lady. 'Thus unrecognized' — he who was heard by me as distinguished by superhuman beauty and other qualities, and for that very reason was sought after with extreme passion — that this is that very beloved, [remains] specifically unknown. Hence 'equal to ordinary people' — having attained the status of being common. 'The beloved' — the man who is the object of the slender lady's desire. 'So as to enjoy, to delight, to bring bliss to the slender lady' — this is the meaning. The remainder is: 'is not able [to do so].' Having thus shown the illustration, he states the subject at hand — 'of the world' etc. The connection is: 'the self of the world.' 'Unexamined' — the meaning is: not specifically known by people. Since even when something is known in general, specific ignorance is possible, therefore, even for word and meaning that are self-evident, it is perfectly appropriate for the great poet to effect recognition: this is the purport.
'Then what is the referent of the word "recognition" here?' — to this, he states its nature as having the stated fruit: 'tena' ('by that') etc. Anticipating the objection that since greatness in poetry does not warrant instruction, the injunction would be inappropriate, he explains — 'yo maha' etc. The meaning of '<s>mahakavi</s>' — its intended meaning is 'that which has as its object the manifestation of great-poet-hood' — this is the purport. In the commentary-prose, the constructions 'the word and meaning of the great poet are to be recognized by the connoisseurs' and 'those very word and meaning of the great poet are to be recognized' should both be understood. The justification for 'to be recognized by the great poet' — [begins with] '<s>vyangye</s>' etc. '<s>Suprayuktabhyam</s>' — by [word and meaning] that have been specifically examined and employed. The stated meaning of '<s>mahakavinam</s>' [is as given]. Since the commentary-prose text shows the primacy of the suggestor as well, he says — 'evam' etc. 'It is established' — that <s>dhvani</s>...
Now, even though both the suggested and the suggestor are primary, poets first take up the expressible and the expressive [word] — this too is perfectly appropriate, he says —
Just as a person desiring light makes effort with respect to the flame of a lamp,

children.text: tad-upāyatayā tadvad arthe vācye tad-ādṛtaḥ // DhvK_1.9 //
children.translated_text: since that [flame] is the means to [light] — so too, devoted to [light/suggestion], he is attentive to the expressible meaning. // <s>DhvK</s> 1.9 //
Just as a person desiring light makes effort with respect to the flame of a lamp,
since that [flame] is the means to [light] — so too, devoted to [suggestion], he is attentive to the expressible meaning. // 9 //

children.text:
yathā hyālokārthī sannapi dīpaśikhāyāṃ yatnavāñjano bhavati tadupāyatayā /
na hi dīpaśikāmantareṇālokaḥ sambhaviti /
tadvadyvaṅgyamarthaṃ pratyāddato jano vācye 'rthe yatnavān bhavati /
locanam prādhānyamuktamiti dhvanati dhvanyate dhvananamiti tritayamapyupapannamityuktam // .8 // // .//
children.translated_text:
For just as a person desiring light makes effort with respect to the flame of a lamp, since that is the means to [light] — for light is not possible without the flame of a lamp — so too, a person devoted to the suggested meaning is attentive to the expressible meaning.
<s>Locana</s>: Since primacy has been stated, '<s>dhvani</s> suggests, is suggested, suggestion' — this triad too is established, thus it has been stated. // 8 //

children.text: nanu prathamopādīyamānatvādvācyavācakatadbhāvasyaiva prādhānyamityāśaṅkyopāyānāmeva prathamamupādānaṃ bhavatītyabhiprāyema viruddho 'yaṃ prādhānye sādhye heturiti darśayati--idānīmityādinā /
children.translated_text: [<s>Balapriya</s>:] Now, anticipating the objection that since the expressible-and-expressive relationship is taken up first, it is that which has primacy — he shows that the taking up of means first [does not imply their primacy], and that this reason is contradictory to the thesis to be proved — by 'idanim' ('now') etc.
'<s>Alokana</s>' (illumination/seeing) is '<s>aloka</s>' (light); the meaning is: the seeing of the faces, lotuses, etc. of women.
And therein the means is the flame of the lamp. // 9 //
<s>Balapriya</s>: The meaning is: what is about to be stated is established. // 8 //

children.text:
vyaṅgyavyañjakaprādhānyānuvādena vācyavācakayoḥ prathamopādānayuktatvavacanaṃ vṛttāvayuktaṃ, prādhānyānuvādasyānupayogādityataḥ śaṅkottaratvena ghaṭayati---nanvityādi /
vācyetyādi /
dvandvaikavadbhāvaḥ /
prathamopādīyamānatvahetoḥ ko doṣa ityataḥ so 'pi darśita ityāha---upāyānāmevetyādi /
viruddha iti /
sādhyābhāvenāpārādānyena vyāpta ityarthaḥ /
aprayojaka ityartho vā /
ālokaśabdasya prakāśarūpārthe prasiddheḥ prakṛte tadarsamāha--ālokanamiti /

children.translated_text: The meaning is: visual cognition.
The elaboration of '<s>alokanam</s>' itself is 'vanita' ('of women') etc.
In the commentary-prose, '<s>pratipadakasya</s>' ('of the conveyor') —
The meaning is: 'of the speaker.' // 9 //

[<s>Balapriya</s>:] The statement in the commentary-prose about the appropriateness of taking up the expressible and the expressive first, by way of restating the primacy of the suggested and the suggestor, is [apparently] inappropriate — since the restatement of primacy serves no purpose. Therefore, he resolves this as being the answer to an objection — 'nanu' ('but') etc. 'Vacya' etc. — the <s>dvandva</s> compound has the singular-like form. 'What is the fault of the reason "being taken up first"?' — to this he shows that the fault has been demonstrated — 'upayanam eva' ('of the means alone') etc. 'Contradictory' — the meaning is: pervaded by the absence of the <s>sadhya</s> (property to be proved), or by something else [contrary]. Or the meaning is: 'non-probative.' Since the word '<s>aloka</s>' is well-known in the sense of 'illumination,' he states its meaning in the present context — '<s>alokanam</s>' etc.

children.text:
anena pratipādakasya kavervyaṅgyamarthaṃ prati vyāpāro darśitaḥ /
pratipādyasyāpi taṃ darśayitumāha----
children.translated_text: By this, the operation of the conveyor, i.e., the poet, with respect to the suggested meaning has been shown. To show [the operation] of the recipient as well, he says —
Just as the sentence-meaning is comprehended through the medium of word-meanings,
so too, the apprehension of the [suggested] entity is preceded by the expressible meaning. // <s>DhvK</s> 1.10 //
Just as the sentence-meaning is comprehended through the medium of word-meanings,
so too, the apprehension of the [suggested] entity is preceded by the expressible meaning. // 10 //

children.text:
yathā hi padārthadvāreṇa vākyārthāvagamastathā vācyārthapratītipūrvikā vyaṅgyasyārthasya pratipattiḥ /
locanam pratipaditi bhāve kvip /
'tasya vastuna' iti vyaṅgyarūpasya sārasyetyarthaḥ /
anena ślokenātyantasahṛdayo yo na bhavati tasyaiṣa sphuṭasaṃvedya eva kramaḥ /
yathātyantaśabdavṛttajño yo na bhavati tasya padārthavākyārthakramaḥ /
kāṣṭāprāptasahṛdayabhāvasta tu vākyavṛttakuśalasyeva sannapi kramo 'bhyastānumānāvinābhāvasmṛtyādivadasaṃvedya iti darśitam // .10 // // .//
children.translated_text:
For just as the comprehension of sentence-meaning [occurs] through the medium of word-meanings, so too the apprehension of the suggested meaning is preceded by the cognition of the expressible meaning.
<s>Locana</s>: '<s>Pratipad</s>' — the suffix <s>kvip</s> is in the sense of <s>bhava</s> (abstract state). 'Of that entity' — the meaning is: of the essence that has the form of the suggested. By this verse, for one who is not an extremely refined connoisseur, this sequence is clearly perceivable — just as for one who is not extremely learned in verbal usage, the sequence of word-meaning and sentence-meaning [is perceivable]. But for one who has reached the pinnacle of connoisseurship, even though the sequence exists — just as for one skilled in sentence-structure — the sequence, though present, is imperceptible, like the inseparable memory of invariable concomitance etc. in practiced inference — this has been shown. // 10 //

children.text:
bālapriyā vṛttau 'pratipādyasye'ti /
vācyārthasyetyarthaḥ /
'tam' iti /
vyaṅgyamarthaṃ prati vyāpāramityarthaḥ /
sa ca svapratītyutpādanarūpaḥ /
kārikāyāṃ 'pratipattasye'tyatrānyathāpratipattinirāsāyāha--pratipadityādi /
pratipattiriti tadartha iti bhāvaḥ /
kārikāyāṃ 'padārthe'tyasya 'vācyārthe'tyasya ca jñāyamānatattadarthetyarthaḥ /

'sampratīyata' iti /

'anena ślokena iti darśitam' iti sambandhaḥ /
yaḥ yaḥ pratipattā /
tasya tathāvidhasya pratipattuḥ /
eṣaḥ vācyavyaṅgyaniṣṭaḥ /
atra dṛṣṭāntamāha---yathetyādi /
śabdavṛtteti /
vākyavṛttetyarthaḥ /
padārthetyādi /
sphuṭasaṃvedya ityanuṣaṅgaḥ /
kāṣṭāprāpteti /
utkarṣaprāptetyarthaḥ /
vākyavṛttakuśālasyeti /
vākyasphoṭādikaṃ jānata ityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: An illustration for the imperceptibility of a sequence that nevertheless exists — '<s>abhyasta</s>' ('practiced') etc.

children.text: abhyaste viṣaye anumānamanumitiḥ avinābhāvasmṛtiḥ vyāptismṛtiḥ tayoḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Abhyasta</s>' (practiced) — in a practiced domain; '<s>anumana</s>' means inferential cognition; '<s>avinabhavasmrtih</s>' means the memory of invariable concomitance; 'of those two' —
By the word '<s>adi</s>' (etc.), the memory of convention and the comprehension of meaning are included.
The meaning is: like the sequence pertaining to those. // 10 //

<s>Balapriya</s>: In the commentary-prose, '<s>pratipadyasya</s>' — the meaning is: 'of the expressible meaning.' '<s>Tam</s>' — the meaning is: 'the operation with respect to the suggested meaning.' And that [operation] has the form of producing its own cognition. In the <s>karika</s>, to prevent a misunderstanding of '<s>pratipattasya</s>' ('of the apprehended'), he says '<s>pratipad</s>' etc. '<s>Pratipatti</s>' — its meaning is 'apprehension': this is the purport. In the <s>karika</s>, '<s>padarthah</s>' and '<s>vacyarthah</s>' — the meaning is 'that respective knowledge being known.' Or: 'that respective knowledge.' '<s>Sampratiyata</s>' — the meaning is: 'is known by the recipients.' Here, another fruit of stating the similarity of the expressible-suggested cognitions to the word-meaning-sentence-meaning cognitions — he says '<s>anena</s>' etc. The connection is: 'by this verse, it has been shown.' '<s>Yah</s>' — whichever recipient. 'Of him' — of such a recipient. '<s>Esah</s>' — pertaining to the expressible and suggested. Here he gives an illustration — '<s>yatha</s>' etc. '<s>Sabdavrtta</s>' — the meaning is: 'sentence-structure.' '<s>Padarthah</s>' etc. — the carry-over is '<s>sphutasamvedya</s>' (clearly perceivable). '<s>Kasthapraptah</s>' — the meaning is: having reached the pinnacle, i.e., the summit. '<s>Vakyavrttakusalasya</s>' — the meaning is: of one who knows sentence-structure (<s>sphota</s>) etc.

children.text: idānīṃ vācyārthapratītipūrvakatve 'pi tatpratītervyaṅgyasyārthasya prādhānyaṃ yathā na vyālupyate tathā darśayati---
children.translated_text: Now he shows how, even when the cognition of the suggested meaning is preceded by the cognition of the expressible, the primacy of the suggested is not compromised —
Just as, by its own power alone, while conveying the sentence-meaning,

children.text: yathā vyāpāra-niṣpattau padārtho na vibhāvyate // DhvK_1.11 //
children.translated_text: the word-meaning is not perceived [separately] at the completion of [its] operation — // <s>DhvK</s> 1.11 //
Just as, by its own power alone, while conveying the sentence-meaning,
the word-meaning is not perceived [separately] at the completion of [its] operation — // 11 //

children.text:
locanam na vyālupyata iti /
prādhānyādeva tatparyantānusaraṇaraṇaraṇakatvaritā madhye viśrānti na kurvata iti kramasya sāto 'pyalakṣaṇaṃ prādhānye hetuḥ /
svamāmarthyamākāṅkṣāyogyatāsannidhayaḥ /
vibhāvyata iti /
viśabdena vibhaktatoktā; vibhaktatayā bālapriyā 'svasāmarthyai'tyādikārikādvayamavatārayati vṛttau--'idānīm' ityādi /
'tatpratīteḥ' vyaṅgyapratīteḥ /
'na vyālupyate' nāpagacchati pratyuta sidhyati /
nanu kārikāyāṃ sato 'pi kramasyālakṣaṇaṃ darśitaṃ, tasya kathaṃ prādhānyopapādakatvamityata āha--prādhānyādevetyādi /
prādhānyādeva vyaṅgyasyetyarthāt /
taditi /
tatparyantaṃ prayojanabhūtapratīyamānārthaparyantaṃ yadanusaraṇaṃ budhyānudhāvanaṃ, 'tattātparye'ti pāṭhe pratīyamānarūpatātparyārthaṃ prati yadanusaraṇamityarthaḥ /
tatra raṇaraṇakena autsukyena tvaritāḥ santa ityarthaḥ /
sahṛdayā iti śeṣaḥ /
madhye vācyāṃśacarvaṇāyām /
viśrāntiṃ na kurvata iti /
tathā ca kā kathā kramaparyālocanāyāmiti bhāvaḥ /
heturiti /
jñāpakamityarthaḥ /
'svasāmarthye'tyasya svasya padārthasya yat sāmarthyaṃ sahakārītyarthābhiprāyeṇa vivṛṇoti--ākāṅkṣetyādi /
kārikāyāṃ 'vyāpāraniṣpattā'viti svavyāpārasya vākyārthapratipādanarūpasya niṣpattau satyāṃ vākyārthabuddhāvityarthaḥ /
vṛttau 'vibhaktataye'ti kārikopaskāra iti bhramaṃ nudati-viśabdeneti /
bhāvyate pratipattṛbhirjñāyate /
aneneti /
vibhāvanamātraniṣedhena yathā svasāmarthyavaśenaiva vākyārthaṃ prakāśayannapi padārtho vyāpāraniṣpattau na bhāvyate vibhaktatayā /
children.translated_text:
<s>Locana</s>: 'Is not compromised' — precisely because of its primacy, [the sensitive readers,] hastened by the eagerness of pursuing [the meaning] to its ultimate terminus, do not rest midway — thus, even though the sequence exists, its imperceptibility is the indicator of primacy.
'Its own power' — expectancy (<s>akanksa</s>), fitness (<s>yogyata</s>), and contiguity (<s>sannidhi</s>).
'Is not perceived' — by the particle '<s>vi</s>,' separateness is stated; 'perceived separately,' i.e., [not perceived] as distinct.
<s>Balapriya</s>: He introduces the pair of <s>karikas</s> beginning with '<s>svasamarthya</s>' from the commentary-prose — 'idanim' etc. 'Of that cognition' — of the cognition of the suggested. 'Is not compromised' — does not depart; rather, is indeed established.
'But the <s>karika</s> shows the imperceptibility of an existing sequence — how does that serve to establish primacy?' — to this he says: 'pradhanyad eva' ('precisely because of primacy') etc. 'Precisely because of the primacy' — the meaning is: of the suggested. 'Tat' — pursuing to the terminus, i.e., to the purpose-serving suggested meaning; '<s>anusarana</s>' means the mind's pursuit of that; in the reading '<s>tattatparye</s>', the meaning is: the pursuit toward the purport that has the form of the suggested. 'Therein, by eagerness (<s>ranaranaka</s>),' being hastened — this is the meaning. The remainder is: 'the connoisseurs.' 'Midway' — in the savoring of the expressible portion.
'Do not rest' — and thus, what need is there to speak of deliberation about the sequence: this is the purport. 'Indicator' — the meaning is: 'sign.' He explains '<s>svasamarthya</s>' ('its own power') with the intention that the word's own power is the cooperant capacity — '<s>akanksa</s>' etc.
In the <s>karika</s>, '<s>vyaparaniṣpattau</s>' — when its own operation, which has the form of conveying the sentence-meaning, is completed, i.e., at the time of the cognition of the sentence-meaning — this is the meaning.
In the commentary-prose, lest '<s>vibhaktataye</s>' ('separately') be mistaken as a gloss on the <s>karika</s>, he dispels [this confusion] — 'by the particle <s>vi</s>' etc. '<s>Bhavyate</s>' — the meaning is: is cognized by the recipients. 'By this' — just as the word-meaning, while illuminating the sentence-meaning by its own power alone, is not perceived separately at the completion of its operation —
— so too, for those possessed of refined minds, that meaning, belonging to those whose inner nature is turned away from the [mere] expressible meaning,
flashes forth instantly in the intellect that reveals reality. // <s>DhvK</s> 1.12 //
So too, for those possessed of refined minds, that meaning, belonging to those whose inner nature is turned away from the expressible meaning,
flashes forth instantly in the intellect that reveals reality. // 12 //

children.text:
locanam na bhāvyata ityarthaḥ /
anena vidyamāna eva kramo na saṃvedyata ityuktam /
tena yatsphoṭābhiprāyeṇāsanneva krama iti vyācakṣate tatpratyuta viruddhameva /
vācye 'rthe vimukho viśrāntinibandhanaṃ paritoṣamalabhamāna ātmā hṛdayaṃ yeṣāmityanena sacetasāmityasyaivārtho 'bhivyaktaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whose inner nature (<s>atman</s>), i.e., heart, is turned away from the expressible meaning, finding no satisfaction — [i.e.,] not obtaining contentment — that is the ground of repose' — by this, the very meaning of '<s>sacetasam</s>' ('of those possessed of refined minds') has been expressed.

children.text: sahṛdayānāmeva tarhyayaṃ mahimāstu, na tu kāvyasyāsau kaścidatiśaya ityāśaṅkyāha-avabhāsata iti /
children.translated_text: 'Then let this greatness belong to the connoisseurs alone, and let it not be any special excellence of poetry itself' — anticipating this objection, he says: '<s>avabhasate</s>' ('flashes forth').

children.text: tenātra vibhaktatayā na bhāsate, na tu vācyasya sarvathaivānavabhāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, here it does not shine forth separately — but it is not the case that the expressible does not shine forth at all.

children.text: ata eva tṛtīyoddyote ghaṭapradīpaddaṣṭāntabalādvyaṅgyapratītikāle 'pi vācyapratītirna vighaṭata iti yadvakṣyati tena sahāsya granthasya na virodhaḥ // 11//
children.translated_text: For this very reason, what will be stated in the Third <s>Uddyota</s> — that by the force of the pot-and-lamp illustration, even at the time of the cognition of the suggested, the cognition of the expressible is not disrupted — there is no contradiction between that and the present text. // 11 //

<s>Locana</s>: The meaning is: '[the word-meaning] is not perceived [separately].' By this it has been stated that the sequence, though existing, is not perceivable. Therefore, those who explain — with reference to the <s>sphota</s> theory — that 'there is simply no sequence' — that [position] is rather contradictory.

avabhāsata itīti /
kāvyaśravaṇasamayasamanantarasamāsādyamānajanmanastadarśavabhāsasya kāryasya parisphuṭopalabdhasya kāvyavyāpāraikanibandhanatvaniścayātkāvyasyaivāyamatiśaya iti bhāvaḥ /

vibhaktatā vyaṅgyārthāpekṣayā pṛthakatvam /

sarvathaiveti /
svarūpeṇāpīti yāvat /

ata eveti /
uktavyākyānādevetyarthaḥ /
vācyasya svarūpato 'vabhāsāṅgīkaraṇādvibhāgamātrasyānavabhāsāṅgīkārācceti yāvat /
evaṃ vācyavyatirekiṇo vyaṅgyasyārthasya sadbhāvaṃ pratipādya prakṛta upayojayannāha---
children.translated_text:
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The meaning is: because of the acknowledgment of the existence of the [suggested] entity (<s>vastu-sattā</s>). /
'By that' — the meaning is: by the demonstration of the [sequential] order that exists but is not apprehended. /
The connection of this is with 'is contradictory indeed.' /
'With the intent of the <s>sphoṭa</s> [theory]' — the meaning is: with the intent that the sentence and its meaning are an undivided <s>sphoṭa</s>-form. /
In the <s>kārikā</s>, '<s>so 'rthaḥ</s>' — the expressed meaning in the form of the sentence-meaning. /
'<s>Tattvārthe</s>' — the meaning is: in the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgyārtha</s>). /
At '<s>vācyārtha-vimukhātmanām</s>' (of those whose nature is turned away from the expressed meaning), taking the contextually derived meaning of the word '<s>vimukha</s>' (turned away), he explains: 'expressed' etc. /
[It describes] that for which repose (<s>viśrānti</s>) alone is the ground, the cause. /
The purport is: not entirely turned away from the expressed. /
He states the result of this qualifier: 'by this' etc. /
'Manifested' — demonstrated. /
'Of the sensitive readers alone' etc. — if this instantaneous flashing [of the suggested meaning] is conditioned by the intellect of the sensitive reader of the stated definition, then by the methods of agreement and difference (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), since that very intellect would be its cause, this would be a transcendent quality of the sensitive readers alone, not of poetry. This is the meaning. /
'Appears, <s>iti</s>' — because of the certainty that this effect — whose birth is obtained immediately and simultaneously at the time of hearing the poetry, and which clearly appears as such — has the poetic operation alone as its sole ground; therefore this excellence belongs to poetry itself. This is the purport. /
'By that' etc. — by that stated manner of explaining the two <s>kārikās</s>. /
'Here, in the expressed meaning.' /
'Distinctness' — separateness with respect to the suggested meaning. /
'Does not appear' — the meaning is: merely the non-appearance of distinctness. /
'In every way' — the extent is: even in its own form. /
But some, reading '<s>vibhaktataye</s>' [say]: 'here' means 'in the cognition.' /
'In the mode of distinctness' — from the expressed, by implication. /
'Does not appear' — the remainder is: the suggested meaning; by which the sequential order might be observed — thus they explain. /
'For this very reason' — the meaning is: precisely from the stated explanation. /
The extent is: because of the acceptance that the expressed appears in its own form, and the acceptance that mere distinction [of the suggested from it] does not appear. /
Having thus established the existence of the suggested meaning as distinct from the expressed, he applies it to the topic at hand, saying —

children.text: yatrārthaḥ śabdo vā tam artham upasarjanīkṛta-svārthau /
children.translated_text: Where meaning or word, having subordinated their own [expressed] meaning, suggest that [other] meaning —

children.text: vyaṅktaḥ kāvya-viśeṣaḥ sa dhvanir iti sūribhiḥ kathitaḥ // DhvK_1.13 //
children.translated_text: that particular kind of poetry is called <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) by the wise. || <s>DhvK</s> 1.13 ||
Where meaning or word, having subordinated their own meaning, suggest that meaning —

children.text: vyaṅktaḥ kāvyaviśeṣaḥ sa dhvaniriti sūribhiḥ kathitaḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: that particular kind of poetry is called <s>dhvani</s> by the wise. || 13 ||

children.text:
locanam sadbhāvamiti /
sattāṃ sādhubhāvaṃ prādhānyaṃ cetyarthaḥ /
dvayaṃ hi pratipipādayiṣitam /
prakṛta iti lakṣaṇe /
upayojayan upayogaṃ gamayan /
tamarthamiti cāyamupayogaḥ /
svaśabda ātmavācī /
svaścārthaśca tau svārthau; tau guṇīkṛttau yābhyām; yathāsaṃkhyena tenārtho guṇīkṛtātmā,śabdo guṇīkṛtābhidheyaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Sva</s>' (self) and '<s>artha</s>' (meaning/purpose) — these two are '<s>svārthau</s>' (own meanings); those two having been subordinated by which [word and meaning respectively]; by the principle of respective correlation (<s>yathāsaṃkhya</s>): meaning [subordinates] its own self, and word [subordinates] its own denotation.
'That meaning' —

children.text: 'sarasvatī svādu tadarthavastu' bālapriyā na virodha iti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] [With the earlier verse] '<s>Sarasvatī svādu tad-artha-vastu</s>' — there is no contradiction.
This [expression] is synecdochic (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>); one should understand that there is no disparity in the illustration either. || 12 ||

[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Existence' — the meaning is: both reality (<s>sattā</s>) and excellence (<s>sādhubhāva</s>), i.e., predominance. /
For two things were intended to be established. /
'In the topic at hand' — in [formulating] the definition. /
'Applying' — causing the application. /
'That meaning' — and this is the application. /
The word '<s>sva</s>' (own) means 'self-referring.'

children.translated_text: "What is other than that is merely <s>citra</s> (ornamental/pictorial)" — we shall show this later.

children.text: yadapyuktam---'kāmanīyakamanativartamānasya tasyoktālaṅkārādiprakāreṣvantarbhāvaḥ' iti, tadapyasamīcīnam; vācyavācakamātrāśrayiṇi prasthāne vyaṅgyavyañjakasamāśrayema vyavasthitasya dhvaneḥ kathamantarbhāvaḥ, vācyavācakacārutvahetavo hi tasyāṅgabhūtāḥ, sa tvaṅgirūpa eveti pratipādayiṣyamāṇatvāt /
children.translated_text: And what was said — "since its beauty (<s>kāmanīyaka</s>) does not go beyond [the known], it can be subsumed under the stated categories of <s>alaṅkāra</s> etc." — that too is improper; for how can <s>dhvani</s>, which is established as depending on the suggested and the suggestive function, be subsumed in a system that depends merely on the expressible and the signifier? For the causes of the beauty of the expressible and signifier are its subsidiaries, while <s>dhvani</s> itself has the nature of the principal (<s>aṅgin</s>) — since this will be demonstrated.
And the corroborative verse here is: "Since <s>dhvani</s> is grounded in the relationship of the suggested and the suggestive function,"
"How can it be subsumed under the causes of the beauty of the expressible and the signifier?"

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The commentary on "<s>sādhubhāvam</s>" (excellence/goodness) is "primacy" (<s>prādhānyam</s>). "This is the meaning" (<s>ityarthaḥ</s>): as stated — "the word <s>sat</s> is used in the senses of 'existence' (<s>sadbhāva</s>) and 'excellence' (<s>sādhubhāva</s>)." The two [senses] are the two stated meanings. "Definition" (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>): meaning the definition of the <s>dhvani</s> under discussion. "Utility" (<s>upayoga</s>): of the existence of meaning-suggested [content]. "In what aspect is there application?" — to that he says "<s>tam</s>" (that) etc. When the existence of the suggested is established, precisely that [already] established meaning — the reference through the word "<s>tat</s>" is appropriate. This is the purport. He explains the meaning of "<s>artha</s>" as meaning — "and its own" (<s>svaś ca</s>) etc. The elaboration of "made subordinate" (<s>upasarjanīkṛtau</s>) is "made secondary" (<s>guṇīkṛtau</s>). He states the resultant meaning — "therefore" (<s>tena</s>) etc. Meaning: such a meaning and such a word. Where the meaning — a particular expressible — or the word — a particular signifier — suggests that meaning, that special kind of poetry is <s>dhvani</s>. By this, [it is distinguished] from the causes of the beauty of the expressible and the signifier — from <s>upamā</s> (simile) etc. and from <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) etc. — <s>Locana</s>: thus it has been stated. "Suggest" (<s>vyaṅktaḥ</s>): they illuminate. By the dual number in "<s>vyaṅktaḥ</s>" (the two suggest), he says this: although in the case of unintended-expressible (<s>avivakṣita-vācya</s>), word alone is the suggestor, still the cooperation of meaning is not severed — otherwise even a word whose meaning is unknown would be a suggestor. And in the case of intended-other-primary-expressible (<s>vivakṣitānya-para-vācya</s>), the cooperation of word also obtains, since without being the denotatum of a specific word, that meaning would not be a suggestor — thus everywhere the operation of both word and meaning is suggestion (<s>dhvanana</s>). Therefore, <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s>'s criticism of the dual number is merely elephant-eye-closing [willful blindness]. The disjunction "meaning or word" (<s>arthaḥ śabdo vā</s>) is intended in terms of primacy. "Poetry" and "a special kind thereof" — or "a special kind of poetry." From the inclusion of the word "<s>kāvya</s>" (poetry), the definition of <s>dhvani</s> falls on the back of [i.e., presupposes] word and meaning adorned by <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s> — as stated by [the word] "soul" (<s>ātmā</s>).

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Now, since in each individual case only one of word and meaning serves as the suggestor, the dual "<s>vyaṅktaḥ</s>" is unjustified — to that he says "by the dual" (<s>dvivacanena</s>) etc. The connection is: "the operation of both is suggestion — this is what is said by the dual." "Of a specific word" (<s>viśiṣṭa-śabda</s>): because the phonemes differ according to <s>rasa</s>. This is the purport. "Therefore" (<s>tena</s>): meaning by the reasoning that justifies the dual. "Elephant-eye-closing" (<s>gaja-nimīlikā</s>): just as an elephant's closing of the eyes is not deliberate but natural — so the word "<s>gaja-nimīlikā</s>" designates [willful] non-reflection.

Now, if it is a conjunction, then the reading should be "meaning and word" (<s>artha-śabdau</s>) — to that he says "meaning" (<s>arthaḥ</s>) etc. "Primacy" (<s>prādhānya</s>): meaning primacy in the suggestive function. The purport is this: the particle "<s>vā</s>" (or) here does not indicate a disjunction regarding the agenthood of word and meaning in the suggestive act — in which case there would be a singular as in "whether the head, the dog, or the youngest son touches [the food]" — but rather it indicates a disjunction regarding the primacy of word and meaning as agents in the suggestive act. And thus the sentence-meaning is: word and meaning, whose primacy in suggestion is [alternately] predicated, suggest [the vyaṅgya] — this is the meaning.

He explains the word "<s>viśeṣa</s>" (special/particular) with the intention of its meaning "qualified" — "poetry" (<s>kāvya</s>) etc. He states an alternative — "of poetry, or" (<s>kāvyasya vā</s>) etc. "<s>Kāvya</s>" etc.: the connection is: "the soul that is characterized as <s>dhvani</s> — it falls on the back of word and meaning adorned by <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s> — this is said by the inclusion of the word 'poetry.' " Its falling on the back of word and meaning is because of being their subsidiary. <s>Locana</s>: Therefore, this leaves no scope — even in <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (presumption from what is heard), there would be the usage "<s>dhvani</s>." And what was said — "the perception of beauty would then be the soul of poetry" — that we accept indeed. For the dispute is merely about the name. And what was said — "if the perception of beauty is the soul of poetry, it would also arise from direct perception and other means of knowledge" — in that context, in the discussion about designating the soul of poetry as consisting of word and meaning, what relevance has this objection? So this amounts to nothing.

"That" (<s>sa</s>): meaning or word, or [their] operation. Even meaning — whether expressible or suggestive — "sounds" (<s>dhvanati</s>); likewise word. Or the suggested "resounds" (<s>dhvanyate</s>); or the operation [of suggestion]. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "Therefore" (<s>tena</s>): since the usage of <s>dhvani</s> applies to word and meaning adorned by <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s> that fall on its back — this is the meaning. "Would be" (<s>syāt</s>): as in "the plump <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day" — since eating at night etc. is inferable. This is the purport.

"Then the perception of beauty" etc.: if the soul of poetry is something other than the well-known causes such as <s>guṇas</s> etc. by virtue of being a cause of beauty, then let the perception of beauty itself be that soul, since it is directly observed and there is no need to postulate an unseen additional entity — thus <s>dhvani</s> beyond those [<s>guṇas</s> etc.] does not exist — this is the objection. Whence the acceptance? To that he says "about the name" (<s>nāmni</s>) etc. "<s>Khalu</s>" is for emphasis. "Perception of beauty" means: [the question of] what is the object or cause of the perception of beauty that is something other than <s>guṇas</s> etc. — the dispute is about the name "<s>dhvani</s>." This is the meaning.

"The perception of the beautiful" (<s>cāruṇaḥ pratītiḥ</s>): meaning the perception of a beautiful thing. The perception of beauty qualified by the thing [perceived]. This is the purport. "That" (<s>sā</s>): meaning the perception of the beautiful thing — likewise, the domain of the usage "<s>dhvani</s>." That <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> is ignorant of the context — therefore dismissing [the objection], he responds — "there" (<s>tatra</s>) etc. "There" — in the domain of direct perception etc. The connection is: "what relevance has this [objection]?" Now, since it is said that poetry consists of word and meaning — to that he says "meaning or" (<s>artho vā</s>) etc. How does each become denotable by the word "<s>dhvani</s>"? To that he says "even meaning" (<s>artho 'pi</s>) etc. Everywhere, the word "<s>iti</s>" connects with "has been established as <s>dhvani</s>." "Thus" (<s>evam</s>): meaning in the manner of "sounding" (<s>dhvanati</s>). Word, expressible, suggested, and suggestion — all four are, by [appropriate] connection, denotable by the word "<s>dhvani</s>." This is the meaning. "By primacy" (<s>prādhānyena</s>): reason for the primary status; because the aggregate is primary relative to its components. The domain of <s>dhvani</s> has been shown to be distinct.

And what was said — "since <s>dhvani</s> transgresses the well-known systems, it would lose the status of poetry, therefore <s>dhvani</s> does not exist" — that too is improper. For it is merely not well-known to the definition-makers (<s>lakṣaṇa-kṛt</s>); but when the defined object (<s>lakṣya</s>) is examined, that alone is the essence of poetry that delights the hearts of connoisseurs. <s>Locana</s>: The suggestion of word and meaning. But by the <s>kārikā</s>, it is established that primarily the aggregate itself, in its poetic form, is <s>dhvani</s> in the primary sense. "Distinct" (<s>vibhakta</s>): because <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s> have their life-breath in the expressible-signifier relationship. The meaning of the word "domain" (<s>viṣaya</s>). Thus, "what is this <s>dhvani</s> that is different from those?" — this has been refuted.

"Of the definition-makers alone" (<s>lakṣaṇa-kṛtām eva</s>): the reason [offered by the opponent] — non-recognition by definition-makers — is contradicted; for precisely from that [novelty] arises the need for careful definition. But non-recognition in the defined object (<s>lakṣya</s>) is an unestablished reason. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "Primarily" (<s>mukhyatayā</s>): while for the others, non-primarily. This is the purport. "<s>Dhvani</s>" etc.: meaning stated as the denotatum of the word "<s>dhvani</s>" by convention (<s>rūḍhi</s>). And thus, that special kind of poetry — having the aggregate-nature of word, expressible, suggested, and suggestive function — is called <s>dhvani</s>; called as the denotatum of the word "<s>dhvani</s>" by convention — this is the meaning of the <s>kārikā</s>. Being a special kind of such poetry is the definition; being denotable by the word "<s>dhvani</s>" by convention is the delimitor of the defined. And it should be understood that only the definition composed of the special-kind-of-poetry is relevant in the present context, hence it was stated.

In the <s>vṛtti</s>, "by this" (<s>anena</s>): meaning by this statement of the definition. "From <s>upamā</s> etc." — meaning from [the entities that are] their domain. "Distinct" (<s>vibhakta</s>): different. How does <s>dhvani</s> have a domain distinct from <s>upamā</s> etc.? To that he says "<s>guṇa</s>" etc. Because they depend on the expressible-signifier, they subsist on that relationship. To substantiate the stated meaning, intending the etymology "<s>viṣaya</s> — that which binds (<s>sinoti</s>) its own related entity by the special quality (<s>viśeṣeṇa</s>)" — he states the meaning of the word "domain" — "non-existence elsewhere" (<s>ananyatra bhāvaḥ</s>): meaning the absence of existence elsewhere. The meaning of the word "domain" is to be understood as conveyed by the qualifying mode. The purport is: "the domain of <s>dhvani</s>" means that beyond which the usage "<s>dhvani</s>" has no existence.

With the intention that by the statement of the definition alone, the view of the first non-existence-asserter has been refuted, and that the <s>vṛtti</s> author's refutation of the second non-existence-asserter's view through "and what was said" etc. [follows] — he shows this: "thus" (<s>evam</s>) etc. "Thus" means: since by the method of stating the definition, the existence of <s>dhvani</s> has been established. "<s>Iti</s>" means: this has been said in conclusion. <s>Dhvani</s> as a type of poetry is not denotable by the word "<s>kāvya</s>" because it transgresses the well-known systems — intending the doubt whether this [argument of the opponent] means non-recognition by definition-makers or non-recognition in the defined object, the refutation is stated through "since" (<s>yataḥ</s>) etc. — he explains: "of the definition-makers" (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) etc. He establishes the contradictory nature: "precisely therefore" (<s>tata eva</s>). Precisely because of non-recognition by definition-makers — since the reason [of non-recognition] operates even among poetry-types denotable by the word "<s>kāvya</s>" through conformity with the definition of <s>dhvani</s>, the reason is contradicted. This is the meaning.

citramiti /

children.translated_text: Or <s>citra</s> because it imitates poetry; or because it is merely a sketch; or because it is merely a craft.
"Later" (<s>agre</s>) —
Through the [relation of] principal and subordinate (<s>pradhāna-guṇa-bhāva</s>), the suggested being thus established,
poetry is twofold; what is other than that is called <s>citra</s> (ornamental/pictorial). //

<s>Locana</s>: And what is comparable to dance, song, etc. — that is nothing of poetry. "<s>Citra</s>" (ornamental): causing wonder through plot (<s>vṛtta</s>) etc., but not consisting of the pulsation of <s>rasa</s> that is the essence of the <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder) desired by connoisseurs — this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: '<s>Madhyakakṣā</s>' (middle level) —
[The suggested meaning] exists in <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) and other [figures].

children.text: samāsoktau tāvat---- upoḍharāgema vilolatārakaṃ tathā gṛhītaṃ śaśinā niśāmukham /
children.translated_text: In <s>samāsokti</s>, for instance — 'With heightened passion and trembling gaze, thus was the face of Night seized by the Moon;

children.text: yathā samastaṃ timiśaṃśukaṃ tayā puro 'pi rāgādgalitaṃ na lakṣitam //
children.translated_text: just as her entire dark garment had slipped away from passion in his presence, [yet] was not noticed [by her].'

[This] will be stated in the Third <s>Uddyota</s>. '<s>Parikara</s>' (ancillary verse) — a verse that serves to provide additional content to the meaning of the <s>kārikā</s> is a '<s>parikaraśloka</s>.' The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [says]: what was stated — that the [suggested meaning] distinct from <s>guṇas</s> etc. is merely of the nature of dance etc. — that too he refutes: '<s>yat ca</s>' etc. '<s>Kāvyasya</s>' — the meaning is: 'of that which is characterized by the definition of <s>dhvani</s>.' '<s>Na kiñcit</s>' — the meaning is: 'it brings upon [itself only] ridicule.' In the commentary-prose, '<s>sahṛdayahṛdayāhlādakārī</s>' (that which produces delight in the hearts of connoisseurs) — with the intention that this captures both <s>dhvani</s> and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion), he explains the word '<s>citra</s>' (marvelous) in '<s>tato 'nyac citram eva</s>' (anything else is merely marvelous): '<s>vismayakṛt</s>' etc. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' in '<s>vṛttādi</s>' (styles etc.), <s>yamaka</s> (word-play), <s>upamā</s> (simile), etc. are included. He states the intended exclusion: '<s>na tu</s>' etc. Or, the usage of the word '<s>citra</s>' for poetry [without dhvani] is in a secondary sense — he says: '<s>kāvya</s>' etc. '<s>Kāvya</s>' — the meaning is: '<s>dhvani</s>-poetry.' The well-known [forms of] '<s>citra</s>' (painting/picture) in the world have the qualities of imitating <s>Viṣṇu</s> etc., of being mere depictions, and of being artistic forms — through association with these, the word '<s>citra</s>' is applied to poetry [that is merely ornamental]. The particle '<s>va</s>' is in the sense of aggregation. In the commentary-prose, '<s>prasthāna</s>' (system/path) — the meaning is: 'in <s>alaṅkāra</s> etc.' '<s>Vācye</s>' etc. — the meaning is: '<s>alaṅkāras</s> etc.' '<s>Tasya</s>' — of <s>dhvani</s>. '<s>Saḥ</s>' — <s>dhvani</s>. '<s>Pratipādayiṣyamāṇatvāt</s>' — because it is about to be stated. Since the ancillary verse requires [something further], he answers the question 'ancillary to what?' — '<s>kārikārthasya</s>' etc. The explanation of '<s>parikārartham</s>' is '<s>adhikāvāpaṃ kartum</s>' (to provide additional content). Now, where the suggested meaning does not shine forth clearly — let that not be the domain of <s>dhvani</s>. But where there is cognition [of the suggested], as in [the figures of] <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), <s>ākṣepa</s> (indirect reference), <s>anukta</s> (the unstated), <s>nimittaviśeṣokti</s> (specific expression of a cause), <s>paryāyokti</s> (circumlocution), <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment), and other figures involving <s>saṅkara</s> (combination) — there, [one might argue,] the subsumption of <s>dhvani</s> [under these figures] would follow. To refute this, it has been said: '<s>upasarjanīkṛtasvārthau</s>' (having subordinated their own meaning). Where word or meaning, having subordinated its own referent — i.e., having made its denotation secondary — suggests another meaning, that is <s>dhvani</s>. How then can it be subsumed under those [figures]? For <s>dhvani</s> [requires] the primacy of the suggested. And this [condition] is not [met in those cases]. The <s>Locana</s> [says]: '<s>yatra</s>' — by the [figures called] <s>alaṅkāras</s>; '<s>vaiśadyena</s>' — the meaning is: 'with charm and clarity.' '<s>Abhihitam</s>' — the use of the past tense [is because the explanation] of '<s>vyañjakta</s>' (suggests) has been [already] stated at the beginning. '<s>Guṇīkṛtātmā</s>' — by the word '<s>ātmā</s>' (self), the meaning of '<s>sva</s>' (own) is explained. '<s>Na ca etat</s>' — the primacy of the suggested. And even though that primacy does not shine forth in [the moment of] cognition — since by the principle of '<s>buddhau tattvāvabhāsinyām</s>' (in the intellect that reveals reality), there is rest in the undivided savoring — nevertheless, when discerning critics undertake the search for the life-force [of poetry], when the suggested meaning is [found to] re-enter the level of the expressible, animating the expressible alone, then — because of its being an instrument for the expressible — it has the status of an <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament). Therefore, the aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) is obtained from the expressible itself as adorned by that [suggestion]. Even though <s>rasa-dhvani</s> exists at the ultimate level, that suggested meaning [in the intermediate cases] is stationed at the middle level. The <s>Bālapriyā</s> [explains]: in the <s>kārikā</s>, '<s>āvāpa</s>' of the additional, required meaning that is not stated [in the kārikā] — i.e., adding it — this is the meaning. '<s>Alaṅkāra</s>' — the meaning is: in <s>upamā</s>, <s>svābhāvokti</s>, and other [figures]. He gives the reason for saying '<s>abhihitam</s>' (stated) rather than '<s>āha</s>' (says): '<s>abhihitam</s>' etc. He recalls what was previously stated: '<s>ātmā</s>' etc. Since both <s>dhvani</s> and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> are equal in the absence of the cognition of primacy at the stage of cognition, [one might] suspect that primacy is the same [for both] — he removes [this doubt] by revealing the intention: '<s>prādhānyam ca</s>' etc. '<s>Prādhānya</s>' — the primacy of the suggested. '<s>Akhaṇḍa</s>' — '<s>khaṇḍa</s>' is differentiation characterized by the primacy of qualities etc.; free from that is '<s>akhaṇḍa</s>' (undivided); the rest (<s>viśrānti</s>) of the minds of connoisseurs in the savoring of such undivided <s>rasa</s> etc., which has become the sentence-meaning. '<s>Vivecakaiḥ</s>' — by the connoisseurs. Implicitly: after the undivided savoring. '<s>Jīvitānveṣaṇe kriyamāṇe</s>' — this applies to both [dhvani and guṇībhūtavyaṅgya]. '<s>Yat</s>' etc. — that which previously transcended the expressible, and because of its suggestedness entered a higher level, yet again, [being] prior, re-enters the level of the expressible and animates the expressible alone — when it persists [in that state]: this is the meaning. The connection is: 'then it has the status of an <s>alaṅkāra</s>.' The completion is: 'it is determined [as such].' '<s>Tadupakaraṇatvāt</s>' — because it is an instrument, i.e., a subordinate part, of the expressible. The purport is: because without the suggested, the charm of the expressible would not be established. '<s>Eva</s>' — the meaning is: 'not otherwise.' '<s>Tasya</s>' — of the suggested. 'Granted this is so — what of it?' — to this he says: '<s>tataḥ</s>' etc. '<s>Tataḥ</s>' — because of its status as an <s>alaṅkāra</s>. '<s>Tadupaskṛtāt</s>' — from [the expressible] adorned by the suggested. '<s>Camatkāralābhaḥ</s>' — and when conversely the suggested meaning, adorned by the expressible, persists animating the poetry — then the aesthetic wonder is obtained from that [suggested meaning]: this is implicitly established by the other [case]. [The objection:] 'Since the subordinate exists in the superordinate, why does [the subordinate] culminate in another subordinate [element]?' — anticipating this, he resolves it: '<s>yadyapi</s>' etc.

children.text: ityāda.u vyaṅgyenānugataṃ vācyameva prādhānyena pratīyate locanam na rasonmukhībhavati; svātantryeṇāpi tu vācyamevārtha saṃskartuṃ dhāvatīti guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatokta /
children.translated_text: In such [verses] and others, the expressible meaning, accompanied by the suggested, is cognized primarily. The <s>Locana</s> [says]: [the mind] does not become oriented toward <s>rasa</s>; rather, even independently, [the suggested meaning] runs to adorn the expressible meaning alone — hence it is called <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion).
'In <s>samāsokti</s>' —
Where, through qualifiers identical [to those of the expressed subject], another meaning is understood from what is stated —
that is called <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) by the wise, because of its conciseness of meaning.
