children.translated_text: In the interpretation: the actions of the heroine toward the hero are superimposed upon Night; and the actions of the hero toward the heroine are superimposed upon the Moon — in this explanation, there is no [problem of] <s>ekasesa</s> (single-remainder compound).
'<s>Aksepa</s>' (implied objection) —
A prohibition, as it were, of the desired, made with the intention of specifying a particular [quality] —
concerning a subject either about to be stated or already stated — that is considered <s>aksepa</s>, and it is of two kinds.

[<s>Balapriya</s>:] Here, the essential nature of the definition of <s>samasokti</s> (condensed expression), the reason (<s>hetu</s>) [for calling it so], and its etymological analysis — these have been stated in sequence by the four quarter-verses.
'Upodharagah' — the redness of twilight bearing passion (<s>raga</s>). 'Vilolatarakah' — the stars that are sparkling, i.e., the eyes with trembling in their third portion; where these [are present] — thus. 'Jhatiti' — immediately and with the eagerness of love. 'Grasped, illuminated, kissed, and mounted' — [describes the actions]. 'The face of Night' — the onset [of night], or the face-lotus [of the heroine].
'Just as' — immediately, with grasping and with the eagerness of love. '<s>Timiransuka</s>' — the darkness and the garments; a fine-rayed darkness-garment — the veil of darkness dappled with rays; the darkness-garment is a dark blue net — appropriate for a newly-wed, demure bride.
Due to redness arising from twilight-born passion, and from love-passion as well.
<s>Balapriya</s>: The first level is the expressible, the second is <s>vastu-dhvani</s> (factual suggestion), and the third is <s>rasa-dhvani</s> (suggestion of aesthetic sentiment) — this is the established [hierarchy].
'Independently' — the expressible [includes] 'the definition' etc. 'The essential nature of the definition' — the meaning is: 'the definition and its essential nature.' There is also the reading 'the definition, the essential nature.'
Here, the <s>samasokti</s> is elaborated: since the narrative of Night and Moon belongs to the topic at hand, it is expressible; the narrative of the hero and heroine, being not directly topical, is suggested — with this intention, he explains the shared qualifier — 'upodhah' etc. The flickering of the stars [is understood] through suggestion. '<s>Netratribhagah</s>' — the meaning is: 'glances from the third portion [i.e., corner] of the eyes.' 'Thus grasped' — he explains in accordance with the present topic — 'jhatiti' ('immediately') etc. 'Mounted' — because kissing in that very manner conveys <s>rasa</s>. As stated: 'Love is indeed perverse.' He explains the word 'yatha' ('just as') for the purpose of showing uniformity — 'jhatiti' etc.
In '<s>timiransukam</s>,' dispelling the confusion of a <s>rupaka</s> (metaphor), he says 'timiram ca' ('darkness and') etc. With the intention that the suffix '-ka' denotes smallness, he explains the word '<s>ansuka</s>' — 'fine-rayed' etc. The meaning is: of the moon. '<s>Timiransukam</s>' is a <s>dvandva</s> compound with singular-like form. He states the result — '<s>rasmi</s>' etc. '<s>Savala</s>' means 'variegated.' '<s>Nilajalika</s>' — a well-known name in <s>Kamasastra</s> (the science of love) for a blue-colored silk garment. He states its appropriateness here — '<s>navodha</s>' etc.
Since in the present context the falling of the darkness-garment is not caused by passion, he supplements — 'anantaram' ('afterward') etc.
The explanation of '<s>purah</s>' ('before/in front') is '<s>purvasyam</s>' ('in the eastern direction') etc.
<s>Locana</s>: '<s>Hetoh</s>' (of the reason). '<s>Purah</s>' also [means] 'in the eastern direction' and 'in front.' '<s>Galitam</s>' — subsided, or fallen. 'By Night, which serves as the instrument' — mixed with it; or by way of synecdoche (<s>upalaksana</s>).
'Not perceived' — meaning 'not known as the onset of that [Night]'; for when the darkness is mixed with rays, people recognize it as 'the face of Night,' but not in clear light.
In the interpretation pertaining to the heroine, '<s>taya</s>' is the agent-word [meaning 'by her']. In the interpretation pertaining to Night, the particle '<s>api</s>' follows '<s>laksitam</s>' ('perceived').
And here, the falling of the blue garment in front [happens] at the commencement of kissing by the hero who is behind [her]. Or alternatively, the construction is: 'the face [was] grasped in front by the hero thus.'
Therefore, here, even though the suggested is cognized, it does not have primacy. For the hero's actions, by making Night and Moon into <s>srngara</s>-<s>vibhavas</s> (erotic determinants), assume the status of a figure (<s>alankara</s>); and from that — from the expressible that has become a <s>vibhava</s> — there flows the distillation of <s>rasa</s>.
But one who explains: '<s>taya</s> — by Night — is the agent-word, and since agency is not tenable for an insentient [entity], the hero's actions are raised by the very word [i.e., are directly denoted], not suggested — hence [this is] <s>samasokti</s>' — he abandons the very meaning of the text, which is accompanied by the suggested. And if so conceived, there would be <s>rupaka</s> (metaphor) of the <s>ekadesa-vivarti</s> (partial-transformation) type — as in '<s>rajahamsair avijyanta sarad eva saronrpah</s>' ('the lake-kings were fanned by royal swans — Autumn herself') — and not <s>samasokti</s>; because there would be no shared qualifier.
<s>Balapriya</s>: Since the mixing of darkness and fine rays cannot be instrumentally caused by Night, '<s>taya</s>' is in the instrumental of instrument — he says '<s>karanabhutaya</s>' etc. Since Night can serve as an indicator (<s>jnapaka</s>) with respect to that mixing, '<s>taya</s>' may be in the instrumental of synecdoche — he says '<s>upalaksanatvena va</s>' etc. The connection is: 'mixed with it, by her synecdochic [role].'
He explains by showing the form of 'not perceived' — '<s>ratri</s>' etc. '<s>Na jnatam</s>' — the remainder is 'by people.' '<s>Galitam</s>' — the suffix <s>kta</s> is in the sense of abstract state. '<s>Galitam</s>' — this is a separate sentence up to this point.
'Hence indeed, not perceived' — to show the causal connection, he says '<s>timira</s>' etc. 'In the interpretation of Night' — by this, the connection elsewhere is shown as 'puro 'pi' ('in front too').
'Afterward' — and thus the particle '<s>api</s>' cumulates [the meanings of] falling and non-perception: this is the meaning.
'How [does] the falling of the blue garment precede [the kissing]?' — to this he justifies — 'atra ca' etc. He says, following the propriety of kissing — 'yadi va' etc. The purport is: the construction of '<s>purah</s>' is with the non-adjacent word '<s>grhitam</s>' ('grasped').
'By that' — the meaning is: by the dual meaning stated. 'In the suggested' — meaning: in the suggested content consisting of the hero's actions.
'Assumes the status of a figure' — here the qualifying statement contains the reason — '<s>nisa</s>' etc. '<s>Samskurvanah</s>' — embellishing through superimposition. Having thus shown the subordination of the suggested, he shows that there is also <s>dhvani</s>-status with respect to <s>rasa</s> — '<s>tatah</s>' etc. '<s>Tatah</s>' — from that which has been embellished. '<s>Vibhavibhutat</s>' — having not experienced <s>vibhava</s>-status before, [it is that which has] now attained <s>vibhava</s>-status through the embellishment: this is the meaning.
'By the word' — the meaning is: by the words 'Night' and 'Moon.' '<s>Unnitah</s>' — inferred, or imagined. 'The expressible alone' — because there is no operation beyond denotation: this is the purport.
'<s>Samasokti</s>' — and by the force of the technical name [alone], the certainty of expressible-status [is established] — he says '<s>ata eva</s>' etc.
He refutes — '<s>sah</s>' etc. The connection is: 'iti granthartha' ('thus the textual meaning'). He states another defect — '<s>ekadesa</s>' etc. '<s>Ittham</s>' — the meaning is: if the hero's actions are taken as expressible. '<s>Itivat</s>' — just as here the <s>saronrpah</s> (lake-kings) [illustrates the point], since only the superimposed narrative of heroine and hero constitutes the sentence-meaning of Night and Moon.
Even in [cases of] <s>aksepa</s> (implied objection), it is the charm of the expressible alone that is [cognized as] primary, being cognized as the sentence-meaning through the very force of the <s>aksepa</s> expression — this is known.
For there, the prohibition that is verbally mounted [i.e., directly expressed], through the intention to specify a particular [quality] — <s>Locana</s> — is understood: and by this, through the exclusion of the denotative operation — enough of these subsidiary [discussions].

children.text: tatrādya.u yathā--- ahaṃ tvāṃ yadi nekṣeya kṣaṇamapyutsukā tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Of these, the first [kind] is as follows: 'If I were not to see you even for a moment, I would be anxious —
let this much suffice; what is the use of saying anything else that is displeasing to you?'

children.text:
bālapriyā ityuktyanuguṇatayā rājahaṃsānāṃ cāmaratvaṃ śaradaścāmaragrāhiṇītvaṃ cārthāt sidhyati, tathā prakṛte timirāṃśukapadānuguṇatayā niśādernāyikātvādikamata ekadeśavivartirūpakaṃ syādityarthaḥ /
na tu samāsoktirityatra hetumāha-tulyeti /
uktamuktipadānuguṇyaṃ nirākaroti--gamyata ityādi /
aneneti /
lakṣaṇavacanenetyarthaḥ /
uktiriti tu prakṛtaviṣayatayaivopapadyate yatroktityādyārambhāditi bhāvaḥ /
nāyikāyā ityādi /
nāyikāyā vyavahāre nīlāmbaragalanānavalokanādirūpo vyāpāraḥ, nāyakasya tu vadanacumbanārambhādilakṣaṇaḥ /
iti vyākhyāna iti /
evamarthasya vivakṣitasya vyākhyāne satītyarthaḥ /
naikaśeṣaprasaṅga iti /
nāyikānāyaketyatra "pumāṃsstriye"tyekaśeṣaprasaṅgo netyarthaḥ /
evaṃ samāsoktau vyaṅgyopaskṛtaṃ vācyameva pradhānamatastatra dhvanilakṣaṇasya nātivyāptiriti pradarśyākṣepe 'pi sa eva prakāra ityāha vṛtto-'ākṣepe 'pī' tyādi /
ākṣepe 'pi 'vācyasyaiva cārutvaṃ, prādhānyena jñāyata' iti sambandhaḥ /
atra hetuḥ 'vākyārtha' ityādi /
vākyārthe viṣaye yā ākṣepoktiḥ, tasyāḥ sāmarthyādityarthaḥ /
kathaṃ tatrākṣepoktirityata uktam--'vyagye'ti /
vyaṅgayo yo viśeṣastadākṣepiṇastadākarṣitvādityarthaḥ /
'śabdopārūḍha' iti /
śabdavācya ityarthaḥ /
locane bhāmahokte tallakṣaṇādyodāharaṇe darśayati--pratiṣedha iti /
viśeṣābidhitsayā vyaṅgyabhūtaviśeṣapratipipādayiṣayā /
yaḥ iṣṭasya vaktumiṣṭasya /
pratiṣedha iva locanam iti vakṣyamāṇamaraṇaviṣayo niṣedhātmākṣepaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Prohibition, as it were' — <s>Locana</s>: this is the <s>aksepa</s> that has the nature of a prohibition, whose subject is about to be stated — namely, about dying.

Therein, 'let this much suffice' — this very [expression], which implies '<s>mriye</s>' ('I die'), is the ground of charm by means of the objected [content]; and [the verse,] ornamented by the objected [content] through the objector, is a fine [example], with [the expressible as] primary.

children.text: uktaviṣayastu yathā mamaiva--- bho bhoḥ kiṃ kimakāṇḍa eva patitastvaṃ pāntha kānyā gatiḥ tattāddaktṛṣitasya me khalamatiḥ so 'yaṃ jalaṃ gūhate /
children.translated_text: And [the <s>aksepa</s>] whose subject has been stated is as follows — by me myself: 'O traveler, what indeed has happened? You have fallen down without cause! What is [your] destination? That wicked-minded one — he it is — hides the water from me who am thirsty and scorched!

children.text: asthānopanatāmakālasulabhāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ prati krudhya bhoḥ trailokyaprathitaprabhāvamihimā mārgaḥ punarmāravaḥ //
children.translated_text: Be angry, sir, at the craving that has come at the wrong place and been obtained at the wrong time! The road — of world-renowned power — is again a desert mirage.'

<s>Balapriya</s>: In accordance with the stated [interpretation], the fanning-function of the royal swans and the fan-holding function of Autumn are understood from the context — so too in the present case, the heroine-status of Night etc. is understood in accordance with the words '<s>timiransuka</s>' etc.; hence this would be a <s>rupaka</s> of the partial-transformation type: this is the meaning.
'And not <s>samasokti</s>' — for this he states the reason — '<s>tulya</s>' etc. He rejects the consistency of the stated expression — '<s>gamyate</s>' etc. 'By this' — the meaning is: 'by the statement of the definition.' But the word '<s>ukti</s>' (expression) is justified only as pertaining to the present topic, since [the text] begins with 'where there is <s>ukti</s>' etc.: this is the purport.
'Of the heroine' etc. — the actions (<s>vyapara</s>) of the heroine consist of the falling of the blue garment, the non-perception, etc.; while those of the hero consist of the commencement of kissing the face, etc.
'In this interpretation' — the meaning is: when the meaning of such a kind has been intended in the explanation. 'The [problem of] <s>ekasesa</s>' — the meaning is: the <s>ekasesa</s> rule '<s>pumanstriye</s>' [would not apply] in the expression '<s>nayikanayaka</s>' (heroine-hero).
Thus, having shown that in <s>samasokti</s>, the expressible alone — embellished by the suggested — is primary, and hence the definition of <s>dhvani</s> does not over-extend to it, [the commentary says] that the same procedure [applies] in <s>aksepa</s> (implied objection) as well — [quoting] the <s>vrtti</s>: '<s>aksepe 'pi</s>' etc.
In <s>aksepa</s> too, the connection is: 'the charm of the expressible alone is [cognized as primary], and is known as primary.' Here the reason — '<s>vakyartha</s>' etc. 'In the sentence-meaning as the domain, the <s>aksepa</s>-expression — by the force of that': this is the meaning. 'How is there an <s>aksepa</s>-expression there?' — to this it has been said: '<s>vyangye</s>' etc. The meaning is: [the expression] that attracts a particular quality belonging to the suggested, i.e., that draws it in.
'Verbally mounted (<s>sabdoparudha</s>)' — the meaning is: directly expressed by the word. [The <s>Locana</s>] shows in the <s>Bhamaha</s>-cited definition and example: '<s>pratisedha</s>' etc. 'With the intention of specifying a particular quality' — with the desire to convey a particular quality that is the suggested.

children.translated_text: That <s>ākṣepa</s> which has this form — which projects a specific suggested meaning — is the primary body of poetry,
for the intent to assign primacy to the expressed or the suggested is grounded in the superiority of beauty.
For example: 'The twilight is full of passion (<s>anurāga</s>); the day goes before her (<s>tat-purassaraḥ</s>).'

children.text: locanam kiṃ vā komalakāntibhiḥ kisalayaiḥ satyeva tatrādhare hī dhātuḥ punaruktavasturacanārambheṣvapūrvā grahaḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] 'Or what use are [those] tender shoots with their delicate lustre, when that lip truly exists? Alas! In the creation of things whose description is redundant, [the Creator's] disposition is unprecedented!'

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The semblance of a prohibition (<s>pratiṣedhābhāsa</s>) — precisely because of its being desirable [as a poetic device]. /
That is <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection/rejection). /
He states its twofold nature: 'to be stated' etc. /
Here, with respect to what is about to be stated, the prohibition pertains to the statement itself; but with respect to what has been stated, sometimes [it pertains] to the entity itself, sometimes to the statement of the entity. This should be understood. /
'I' — the utterance of a certain woman, full of longing, addressed to her beloved who is about to depart. /
'I am eager — if I cannot bear to part from you even for a moment, then let there be just this much — speech lasting only this long!' /
Hence 'by anything else that is displeasing to you' — this contains the implied reason. /
'By the stated speech.' /
The meaning is: 'What will I not say?' /
Here he applies the definition: '<s>iti</s>' etc. /
'Having the form of a prohibition' — the meaning is: having the form of a semblance of prohibition of the statement, i.e., 'what use is there in saying [more]?' /
He shows that here too the expressed alone has primacy: 'there' etc. /
'<s>Iti etad eva</s>' means: the expressed meaning alone. /
'Projects' (<s>ākṣipat</s>) — suggests. /
'By the projected' — by the suggested meaning in the form of the resolution to die. /
'The projecting [expression]' is stated as '<s>iyad evāstu</s>' (let there be just this much) etc. /
'Ho ho' — there are also the readings '<s>khala-sṛtiḥ seyam</s>' ('this is the path of the rogue') and '<s>khala-matisso 'yam</s>' ('this one is the rogue-minded'). /
Here the expressed meaning pertains to a traveler in a desert-path. /
But the suggested meaning pertains to the present topic of servitude to a wicked master and its futility. /
By the repetition '<s>bho bho</s>' (hey, hey!), the excess of care toward the one to be awakened is indicated. /
'<s>Akāṇḍe</s>' — at an entirely wrong place. /
'What? What? [You have] fallen!' — the meaning is: by coming here, by serving this [master], the desired fruit is not attained. /
By the word '<s>pāntha</s>' (traveler), inexperience in servitude is indicated. /
When some long-serving [retainer] speaks thus, the traveler, somewhat angered, says: '<s>kā</s>' etc., up to '<s>khala</s>' (rogue). /
O rogue! /
'The thirst of one so extremely thirsty' — <s>tṛṣā</s> means both thirst for water and desire for wealth. /
'What other refuge do I have?' — the meaning is: 'I have none.' /
'Having come here because no other path was available; having resorted to this master because no other refuge was available' — this is the meaning. /
Hearing that, another says: '<s>sṛtiḥ</s>' etc. — 'That which you have resorted to — this path, this master — conceals water and wealth within a pitcher.' /
'Whence would it distribute?' — the purport is: it is inconceivable. /
In the reading '<s>khala-matisso 'yam</s>,' '<s>so 'yam</s>' — the statement is directed at both the desert-path and the master. /
Some [say] the speech up to '<s>gūhata</s>' (conceals) belongs to the traveler alone. /
The other speaker, laughing at the anger revealed by the word '<s>khala</s>' (rogue), says: '<s>asthāne</s>' (in the wrong place) etc. /
'Untimely availability' — when the object is easily available, thirst does not arise; when it is unavailable, it does. /
The purport is: 'Direct your craving toward your own craving, not against me!' /
'How is its arising in the wrong place?' — to this he says: '<s>trailokya</s>' etc. /
The magnificence of his power — extreme harmfulness, extreme greed, etc. /
'<s>Māravaḥ</s>' — a desert-related path; and also a wicked master. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Here a certain servant, having arrived [at the master's court], his heart being pierced by the hope 'what should I not obtain from this one?' — is awakened by someone through this <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection). /
Therein, by the <s>ākṣepa</s>, i.e., by the expressed meaning in the form of a prohibition — the very [expressed content about] servitude to a wicked person, its futility, and the distress caused by it — in its capacity as the <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) of <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness), the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) of <s>śānta-rasa</s> (the tranquil sentiment) — has the power to produce aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkṛti</s>). /
But <s>Vāmana</s>'s definition of <s>ākṣepa</s> is: 'the rejection of the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>).' /
The rejection of the standard of comparison such as the moon etc.: 'when this [face etc.] exists, what need is there of you [moon]?' /
For example: 'Her face is so gentle and lovely — what use is the moon of the full-moon night? If her eyes are the abode of beauty, what then of those blue lotuses?' /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] With the stated suggested meaning in mind, he says: 'here' etc. /
The connection is: 'a certain servant is awakened by someone.' /
'Having arrived' etc. — the two [expressions] are qualifiers of the servant. /
'Having arrived' — having reached the master to be served. /
'What is to be obtained' — wealth etc. /
'From this' — from the master. /
'Why?' — for what reason? /
'Does not obtain' — whose heart is being pierced by the hope that arises moment after moment, the hope born immediately after each speculation — this being the reason for awakening [him]. /
'By someone' — by some long-serving person, some agent. /
'By this <s>ākṣepa</s>' — made with the desire to convey the specific suggested meaning in the form of the futility of serving a wicked person etc.; in the form of a prohibition, i.e., 'what? What? Have you fallen in the wrong place?' /
'Is awakened' — the meaning is: the nature of the master — his extreme greediness etc. — was already known previously; out of compassion he is awakened [to it]. /
He shows that here too the suggested is subordinate to the expressed: 'there' etc. /
'There' — in the example. /
'In the form of a prohibition' — the meaning is: in the form of a prohibition of the fruit of falling, i.e., 'what? What?' /
'By the <s>ākṣepa</s>' — the meaning of the instrumental case is specificity; it qualifies the expressed, i.e., 'the expressed together with that.' /
'Of the expressed alone' — the meaning is: with respect to the expressed meaning pertaining to the traveler, desert-path, etc. /
The connection is with 'the power to produce aesthetic wonder.' /
'Of what?' — to this he says: 'wicked person' etc. /
'Wicked person' — a bad master. /
Of the suggested — by implication. /
He states the reason for this suggested meaning's effecting the aesthetic wonder of the expressed: '<s>śānta</s>' etc. /
The futility of serving a wicked person is the <s>vibhāva</s>; the distress caused by it is the <s>anubhāva</s>. /
'What? What? Have you fallen in the wrong place?' — in the <s>ākṣepa</s> in the form of prohibiting the desired fruit of falling, the <s>ākṣepya</s> (object of rejection), namely the futility of serving a wicked person etc. — by which the <s>ākṣepaka</s> (the rejecting [expressed]) is ornamented — that very expressed [meaning] is primary. This is the purport. /
As in '<s>prāṇā yena samarpitāḥ</s>' ('by whom lives were offered') etc., here too <s>aprastuta-praśaṃsā</s> (indirect praise through irrelevant description) is present — hence one should understand that this <s>ākṣepa</s> is mixed with that [figure]. /
The connection is with '<s>Vāmana</s>'s definition.' /
He shows the meaning of the word <s>ākṣepa</s>: 'in this' etc. /
'In this' — in the face etc. that is regarded as the object of comparison (<s>upameya</s>). /
'By you' — by the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), the moon etc. [applied to] the face etc. /
'Use' (<s>kṛtya</s>) — purpose, fruit. /
'Of her' — '<s>tat</s>' has the sense of one previously experienced; with '<s>dṛśau</s>' (eyes) also the construction should be understood by inversion. /
'Gentle' (<s>saumya</s>) — of sweet appearance; and therefore 'lovely' (<s>subhaga</s>). /
'What? What purpose?' /
'The eyes' — the remainder is: 'exist.' /
'<s>Yadi</s>' (if) — in the sense of restating what is established. /
'By those' — by the well-known [lotuses]. /
'There, in that [face].' /
'<s>Hī</s>' — the meaning is: 'alas, what a pity!'

children.text: kiṃ tena kṛtyamiti tvapahastanārūpa ākṣepo vācya eva camatkārakāraṇam /
children.translated_text: 'What use is that?' — the <s>ākṣepa</s> in the form of dismissal is the cause of aesthetic wonder in the expressed meaning alone.
Or the rejection of the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) means, by [semantic] capacity, the attraction [of something implied].
For example: 'She, bearing upon her pale cloud-like [breast] the appearance of nail-scratches like <s>Indra</s>'s rainbow,
propitiating the moon though it bears a stain, intensified the heat of the sun.'
Here the suggested meaning — the sense of comparison (<s>upamā</s>) — also embellishes the expressed alone.

children.text:
ityatrerṣyākaluṣitanāyakāntaramupamānamākṣiptamap.i vācyarthamevālaṅkarotītyeṣā tu samāsoktireva /
tadāha---cārutvotkarṣeti /
atraiva prasiddaṃ dṛṣṭāntamāha---anurāgavatīti /
tenopaprameyasamarthanamevāparisamāptamiti mantavyam /
tatrodāharamatvena bālapriyā punariti /
punaruktānāmanupādeyānāṃ niṣphalānāṃ vastūnāṃ pārvaṇacandrādīnāṃ racanāyāṃ sṛṣṭau viṣaye ye ārambhā vyāpārāḥ teṣu /
apūrvaḥ anyatrāddaṣṭaḥ /
grahaḥ abhisandhiviśeṣaḥ /
atrāpi vyaṅgayasya guṇībhāvaṃ darsayati---atretyādi /
upamārthaḥ candrādisāddaśyarūpārthaḥ /
vācyasyaivopaskurute vāyyārthamevālaṅkareti /
atra hetumāha---kimityādi /
'iti vācya ākṣepa eva camatkārakāraṇam' iti sambandhaḥ /
apahastanārūpaḥ nirasanarūpaḥ /
"upamānākṣepa" iti sūtramanyathā vyācaṣṭe---yadi vetyādi /
sāmarthyādarthasāmarthyāt /
ākarṣaṇaṃ vyañjanam /
aindramiti /
payodharo medhaḥ stanasca /
prasādayantītyādi /
śaratkāle hi candrasya prasādātiśayo ravitāpādhikyaṃ ca /
atra lakṣamaṃ yojayati---atretyādir /
irṣyetir /
irṣyayā ākṣāntyā kaluṣitaṃ yannāyakāntaraṃ tadrūpamupamānamityarthaḥ /
ākṣiptamiti /
vyañjitamityarthaḥ /
nāyikāvyañjanasyāpyupalakṣaṇamidam /
nāyikāpakṣe nakhakṣatasthatayā śrutamapyupamānatvamaindre dhanuṣiyojanīyamindracāpābhaṃ nakakṣataṃ dadhānetyarthaḥ /
eṣetyādi /
vāmanamate ākṣepodāharaṇatvenoktaṃ idaṃ bhāmahamate samāsoktyudāharaṇamevetyarthaḥ /
tadāheti /
vācyasyaiva prādhānyaṃ na vyaṅgyasyetyasminnuktārthe hetumāhetyarthaḥ /
atraiveti /
cārutvotkarṣakṛtaṃ prādhānyamityasminnartha evetyarthaḥ /
evakāro 'laṅkārodāharaṇatvaśaṅkāśamanārthaḥ /
anurāgavatīti /
anurāgau raktimā premaviśeṣaśca /
tatpurassaraḥ tasyāḥsa purassaraḥ pūrvakāle sammukhaṃ ca saranniti dvayorarthayoradhyavasāyenaikyaṃ bodhyamata evāho ityādeparupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Tat-purassaraḥ</s>' — he goes before her; '<s>purassara</s>' means both 'in the earlier time' and 'in front of' — one should understand that by <s>adhyavasāya</s> (figurative identification), the two meanings [of the day going before the twilight, and the lover going before the beloved] are unified. Hence the appropriateness of '<s>aho</s>' (ah!) etc. [expressing wonder].
In the interpretation with respect to the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero), the meaning is: standing in front [of her].
'By that' —

children.text: ddaṣṭāntoktitayā aho daivagatiḥ kīddaktathāpi na samāgamaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the form of a speech through illustration (<s>dṛṣṭānta-ukti</s>): 'Ah, [such is] the course of fate! [It is] of such a kind — and yet there is no meeting!'

Here, the rival lover (<s>nāyakāntara</s>) soiled by jealousy, though projected as the standard of comparison, ornaments the expressed meaning alone — this is in fact nothing but <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression). /
Therefore he says: 'the superiority of beauty' etc. /
For this very [point], he cites a well-known example: '<s>anurāgavatī</s>' etc. /
By that, one should consider that the substantiation through the illustration is itself not yet complete. /
As an example therein — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Again' — in the creation, i.e., in the fashioning of things that are redundant, i.e., not to be accepted, i.e., fruitless — things like the full-moon, etc. — the activities, i.e., efforts [of the Creator] with respect to those. /
'Unprecedented' — not seen elsewhere. /
'Disposition' (<s>graha</s>) — a particular design. /
He shows the subordination of the suggested here too: 'here' etc. /
'The sense of comparison' — the meaning in the form of resemblance to the moon etc. /
'Embellishes the expressed alone' — ornaments the expressed meaning alone. /
Here he states the reason: 'what [use]' etc. /
The connection is: 'thus the <s>ākṣepa</s> in the form of the expressed alone is the cause of aesthetic wonder.' /
'In the form of dismissal' — in the form of rejection. /
He explains the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>upamāna-ākṣepaḥ</s>' (rejection of the standard of comparison) differently: 'or' etc. /
'By capacity' — by the capacity of meaning. /
'Attraction' — suggestion. /
'<s>Aindra</s>' (of <s>Indra</s>) — '<s>payodhara</s>' means both 'cloud' and 'breast.' /
'Propitiating' etc. — for in autumn, the moon's clarity is especially great, and the sun's heat is excessive. /
Here he applies the definition: 'here' etc. /
'Jealousy' — soiled by jealousy, i.e., by intolerance — the rival lover (<s>nāyakāntara</s>) that has that form is the standard of comparison. This is the meaning. /
'Projected' — the meaning is: suggested. /
This is also synecdochic for the suggestion of the <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine). /
In the interpretation with respect to the <s>nāyikā</s>, the nail-scratch, though heard as such, should be construed as belonging to the rainbow of <s>Indra</s> in its capacity as the standard of comparison — the meaning is: 'bearing a nail-scratch that resembles <s>Indra</s>'s bow.' /
'This' etc. — what was given in <s>Vāmana</s>'s view as an example of <s>ākṣepa</s>, in <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s view is simply an example of <s>samāsokti</s>. This is the meaning. /
'Therefore he says' — the meaning is: he states the reason for the point that it is the expressed meaning alone, not the suggested, that has primacy. /
'For this very [point]' — the meaning is: for this very thesis that primacy is produced by the superiority of beauty. /
The particle '<s>eva</s>' is for dispelling the suspicion that it might be an example of a figure (<s>alaṅkāra</s>). /
'<s>Anurāgavatī</s>' — '<s>anurāga</s>' means both reddishness and a special kind of love.

children.text:
atra satyāmapi vyaṅgyapratītau vācyasyaiva cārutvamutkarṣavaditi tasyaiva prādhānyavivakṣā /
yathā ca dīpakāpahnutyādau vyaṅgyatvenopamāyāḥ pratītāvapi prādhānyenāvivikṣitatvānna tayā vyapadeśastadvadatrāpi draṣṭavyam /
locanam samāsoktiślokaḥ paṭhitaḥ /
aho daivagatiriti /
gurupāratantryādinimitto 'samāgama ityarthaḥ /
tasyaiveti /
vācyasyaiveti yāvat /
vāmanābhiprāyemāyamākṣepaḥ, bhāmahābhiprāyeṇa tu samāsoktirityamumāśayaṃ hṛdaye gṛhītvā samāsoktyakṣepayoḥ yuktyedamekamevodāharaṇaṃ vyataradgranthakṛt /
eṣāpi samāsoktirvāstu ākṣepo vā, kimanenāsmākame /
sarvathālaṅkāreṣu vyaṅgyaṃ vācye guṇībhavatīti naḥ sādhyamityatrāśayo 'tra granthe 'smadgurubhirnirūpitaḥ /
evaṃ prādhānyavivakṣāyāṃ dṛṣṭāntamuktvā vyapadeśo 'pi prādhānyakṛta eva bhavatītyatra dṛṣṭāntaṃ svaparaprasiddhamāha---yathā ceti /
upamāyā iti /
upamānopameyabhāva syetyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'By that' — by <s>upamā</s> (comparison).

children.text: dīpake hi 'ādimadhyāntaviṣayaṃ tridhā dīpakamiṣyate' iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: For in <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), the definition is: '<s>Dīpaka</s> is regarded as threefold, pertaining to the beginning, middle, and end.'

children.text: maṇiḥ śāṇollīḍhaḥ samaravijayī hetidalitaḥ kalāśeṣaścandra suratamṛditā bālalanā /
children.translated_text: A gem polished on a whetstone, a battle-victorious [warrior] struck by weapons, the moon reduced to a sliver, a young woman crushed in lovemaking,

children.text: madakṣīṇo nāgaḥ śaradi saridāśyānapulinā tanimnā śobhante galitavibhavāścārthiṣu janāḥ //
children.translated_text: an elephant weakened by rut, a river in autumn with its sandbanks exposed — these, diminished in their splendor, shine forth [all the more] among those who seek [them]. ||

Here, even though the cognition of the suggested meaning obtains, the beauty of the expressed alone is superior — hence the intent to assign primacy to that [expressed] alone. /
And just as in <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), <s>apahnuti</s> (concealment), etc., even though the cognition of <s>upamā</s> (comparison) in its suggested form obtains, because it is not principally intended, there is no designation by it — so too should it be viewed here. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The <s>samāsokti</s> verse has been cited. /
'Ah, the course of fate!' — the meaning is: the non-meeting is caused by dependence on an elder (<s>guru</s>) etc. /
'Of that alone' — the extent is: of the expressed alone. /
In <s>Vāmana</s>'s view, this is an <s>ākṣepa</s>; in <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s view, it is a <s>samāsokti</s> — grasping this intention in [his] heart, the author of the treatise presented this single example as serving for both <s>samāsokti</s> and <s>ākṣepa</s> by reasoning. /
Let this be <s>samāsokti</s> or <s>ākṣepa</s> — what does it matter to us? /
In all cases, in [all] figures, the suggested is subordinate to the expressed — this is our thesis. This intention has been determined in this treatise by our teacher. /
Having thus cited an example for primacy-assignment, he states that the designation too is made solely by reason of primacy — and gives a well-known example accepted by both [parties]: 'just as' etc. /
'Of <s>upamā</s>' — the meaning is: the relation of standard of comparison and object of comparison.

children.text:
bālapriy.ā alaṅkārodāharaṇatvābhāvenetyarthaḥ /
aparisamāptameveti yojanā /
tatreti /
ākṣepasamarthana ityarthaḥ /
nāyakayorasamāgame gamyaṃ hetuṃ darśayati---gurvityādi /
'anurāge'tyādyudāharaṇapradarśanābiprāyamāha---vāmanetyādi /
vāmanābhiprāyema upamānapratyāyanapakṣarūpeṇa /
idamiti /
anurāgetyādikamityarthaḥ /
atra grantha iti /
cārutvetyādiprādhānyavivakṣetyantagrantha ityarthaḥ /
dīpake hīti /
'ityatra dīpanakṛtameva cārutvam' ityanvayaḥ /
dīpake hītyasya sthāne 'tathāhī'ti ca pāṭhaḥ /
bhāmahoktalakṣaṇamanyattadudāharaṇañca darśayati---ādītyādi /
atrādyādayaśśabdā vākyaviṣayāḥ /
tatrāntyadīpakamudāharati---maṇiriti /
locanam ityatra dīpanakṛtameva cārutvam /

children.translated_text: "<s>Apahnuti</s> (denial) is a somewhat concealed simile of the desired [object]" —
There, the beauty is produced by the <s>apahnuti</s> (denial) alone.

children.text: yathā--- neyaṃ virauti bhṛṅgālī madena mukharā muhuḥ /
children.translated_text: As in: "This is not the swarm of bees buzzing repeatedly, intoxicated and vociferous —"
"This is the sound of <s>Kandarpa</s>'s (Cupid's) bow being drawn!"

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Meaning: because it does not serve as an illustration of an <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure). The construal is: "it remains incomplete." "There" (<s>tatra</s>): meaning justification of the objection. He shows the inferable reason for the non-meeting of the two protagonists — "because of the weighty" (<s>guru</s>) etc. He states the intention of presenting the illustration beginning with "in love" (<s>anurāge</s>) — "<s>Vāmana</s>" etc. With <s>Vāmana</s>'s intention, in the form of the position that [the beauty is] conveyed by the vehicle of comparison (<s>upamāna-pratyāyana</s>). "This" (<s>idam</s>): meaning that which begins with "in love" etc. "Here the text" (<s>atra grantha</s>): meaning the text up to the statement of primacy beginning with "in beauty" etc. "For in <s>dīpaka</s>" (<s>dīpake hi</s>): the syntactic connection is: "here the beauty is produced by <s>dīpana</s> (illumination/intensification) alone." In place of "for in <s>dīpaka</s>" there is also the reading "for thus" (<s>tathā hi</s>). He shows the definition stated by <s>Bhāmaha</s> and another example — "beginning with" (<s>ādi</s>) etc. Here words like "beginning" (<s>ādi</s>) refer to sentences. There he cites a final <s>dīpaka</s> — "jewel" (<s>maṇi</s>) etc. <s>Locana</s>: Here the beauty is produced by <s>dīpana</s> alone.
Thus. //
Having thus considered the objection, he states another proposition in the order of the enumeration — "in [the figure] whose cause is unstated" (<s>anukta-nimittāyām</s>) etc.
"When one part is absent, the praise of another quality —"
"— for the purpose of proclaiming a distinction, that is called <s>viśeṣokti</s> (special statement)."

children.text: yathā--- sa ekastrīṇi jayati jaganti kusumāyudhaḥ /
children.translated_text: As in: "He alone, the flower-weaponed one (<s>Kusumāyudha</s>, Cupid), conquers the three worlds —"

children.text: haratāpi tanuṃ yasya śambhunā na hṛtaṃ balam //
children.translated_text: "— whose power is not taken away even by <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), who destroyed his body!"
And this [figure] has an inconceivable cause (<s>acintya-nimitta</s>); therefore in this [figure] there is no existence of a suggested meaning.

children.text: uktanimittāyāmapi vastusvabhāvamātratve paryavasānamiti tatrāpi na vyaṅgyasadbhāvaśaṅkā /
children.translated_text: Even in [the variant] with a stated cause, the conclusion rests in the mere nature of factual content (<s>vastu-svabhāva</s>); therefore there too, no suspicion of the existence of suggested meaning.

children.text: yathā--- karpūra iva dagdho 'pi śaktimānyo jane jane /
children.translated_text: As in: "Like camphor, even though burned, he is powerful in every person —"
"Salutations to him, the flower-bowed one (<s>Kusumadhanvan</s>, Cupid), whose valor is irresistible!"

children.text:
bālapriy.ā śloko 'rtha kuvalayānande 'pyudāhṛtaḥ /
dīpanakṛtameveti /
dīpanaṃ nāmānekatraikadharmānvayaḥ /
evakāreṇa vyaṅgyāyā upamāyā vyavacchedaḥ /

atrāpahnutipadasyāvṛttirbodhyā /
abhīṣṭasya varṇyatvenābhimatasya /
kiñjidantargatā vyaṅgyā upamā yasyāssā /
apahnutiḥ niṣedhaḥ /
apahnutiḥ tannāmālaṅkāraḥ /
apahnutyeti /
apahnaveneti ca pāṭhaḥ /
śobhācārutvam /
neyamiti /
muhurvirautītyanvayaḥ /
'madena mukharā ākṛṣyamāṇasye'ti ca bimbapratibimbatayoktiḥ /
'anuktanimittāyām' ityādigranyasya pūrvagranthena sambandhaṃ darśayannavatārayati--evamityādi /
uddeśeti /
samāsoktyākṣepetyādipūrvoktetyarthaḥ /
'anuktanimittāyā'miti kathanasya phalaṃ vaktumupakramamāṃṇa āha---eketyādi /
eketyādilakṣaṇaṃ bhāmahīyam /
ekadesasya tanumattvādeḥ kāraṇasya /
guṇāntarasya balavatvādirūpakāryasya /
saṃstutiḥ kathanam /
viśeṣaprathanāya kasyacidatiśayasya khyāpanāya /
sa iti /
saḥ prasiddhaḥ /
apiśabdaḥ sambhunetyatrāpi yojyaḥ /
balasya tanvāśrayatvāttanuvigame balavigamo nyāyyaḥ /
iha tu tanuvigame 'pi balasadbhāva uktaḥ /
tatra ca yatkiñcinnimittaṃ bhavet, parantu tadacintyamityāha---iyañceti /
vastusvabhāvamātratve paryavasānamiti /
vārthāntaravyañjakatvamityarthaḥ /
karpūra iti /

children.translated_text: "Irresistible" (<s>avārya</s>) etc. — this is the statement of the cause.
"Therefore" (<s>tena</s>) —

children.text: yasmādukte prakāradvaye vyaṅyasadbhāvo anuktanimittāyāmapi viśeṣoktau---- āhūto 'pi sahāyaiḥ omityuktvā vimuktanidro 'pi /
children.translated_text: Since in the two stated types there is no existence of suggested meaning, even in the <s>viśeṣokti</s> whose cause is unstated — [as in:] "Even though called by his companions, even though having said '<s>om</s>' and awoken from sleep,"

children.text: gantumanā api pathikaḥ saṅkocaṃ naiva śithilayati //
children.translated_text: "Even though intending to go, the traveler does not at all loosen his contraction (embrace)."

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] This verse is cited also in the <s>Kuvalayānanda</s>. "Produced by <s>dīpana</s> alone" (<s>dīpanakṛtam eva</s>): <s>dīpana</s> means the application of one property to many [subjects simultaneously]. By the word "<s>eva</s>" (alone), the suggested simile (<s>vyaṅgyā upamā</s>) is excluded. He shows the definition and example of <s>apahnuti</s> from <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s work — "<s>apahnuti</s>" etc. Here the repetition of the word "<s>apahnuti</s>" should be noted. "Of the desired" (<s>abhīṣṭasya</s>): of what is intended as the subject of description. "Somewhat concealed" (<s>kiñcid antargatā</s>): a suggested simile. "<s>Apahnuti</s>" means denial; <s>apahnuti</s> is the name of the <s>alaṅkāra</s>. "By <s>apahnuti</s>" (<s>apahnutyā</s>): there is also the reading "<s>apahnava</s>" (by denial). "Beauty" (<s>śobhā</s>): charm. "This is not" (<s>na iyam</s>): the syntactic connection is "buzzes repeatedly" (<s>muhur virauti</s>). "Intoxicated, vociferous, of the one being drawn" — this is stated as reflection and image (<s>bimba-pratibimba</s>). Introducing the connection of the text beginning with "in [the figure] whose cause is unstated" with the preceding text, he provides a transition — "thus" (<s>evam</s>) etc. "In the order of the enumeration" (<s>uddeśe</s>): meaning as previously stated in the order of concise statement (<s>samāsokti</s>), objection (<s>ākṣepa</s>), etc. Beginning to state the purpose of saying "in [the figure] whose cause is unstated" — he says "one part" (<s>eka</s>) etc. The definition beginning with "one part" is from <s>Bhāmaha</s>. "Of one part" (<s>ekadeśasya</s>): of a cause such as thinness of body. "Of another quality" (<s>guṇāntarasya</s>): of an effect in the form of power etc. "Praise" (<s>saṃstutiḥ</s>): narration. "For the purpose of proclaiming a distinction" (<s>viśeṣa-prathanāya</s>): for making known some special excellence. "He" (<s>saḥ</s>): that well-known [Cupid]. The word "<s>api</s>" (even) should also be construed with "<s>Śambhu</s>." Since power resides in the body, when the body perishes, power should also perish; but here, even when the body is destroyed, the existence of power is stated. And whatever the cause of that might be, it is inconceivable — he says "and this" (<s>iyaṃ ca</s>) etc. "Rests in mere factual content" (<s>vastu-svabhāva-mātratve paryavasānam</s>): meaning it does not suggest any additional meaning. "Like camphor" (<s>karpūra</s>) etc.

ityāda.u vyaṅgyasya prakaraṇasāmarthyātpratītimātram /
na tu tatpratītinimittā locanam tena prakāradvayamavadhīrya tṛtīyaṃ prakāramāśaṅkate--anuktanimittāyāmapīti /
vyahgyasyeti /
śītakṛtā khalvārtiratra nimittamiti bhaṭṭodbhaṭaḥ, tadabhiprāyeṇāha-na tvatra kāciccārutvaniṣpattiriti /
yattu rasikairapi nimittaṃ kalpitam-'kāntāsamāgame gamanādapi laghutaramupāyaṃ svapnaṃ manyamāno nidrāgamabuddhyā saṅkocaṃ nātyajat' iti tadapi nimittaṃ cārutvahetutayā nālaṅkāravidbhiḥ kalpitam, api tu viśeṣoktibhāga eva na śithilayatītyevambhūto 'bhivyajyamānanimittopaskṛtaścārutvahetuḥ /
anyathā tu viśeṣoktireveyaṃ na bhavet /
evamabhiprāyadvayamapi sādhāraṇoktyā granthakṛnnyarūpayanna tvaudbhaṭenaivābhiprāyeṇa grantho vyavasthita iti mantavyam /
children.translated_text: Thus, the author of the treatise formulated both intentions through a general statement — and it should not be thought that the text is established only with <s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s intention.
"Even in <s>paryāyokta</s> (periphrasis)" —
"<s>Paryāyokta</s> (periphrasis) is that which is expressed in another manner —"
"— devoid of the functions of the expressible and the signifier, having the nature of [indirect] comprehension."

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In [verses] beginning with this, there is merely the cognition of the suggested through the power of context (<s>prakaraṇa-sāmarthya</s>), but the cognition of that [suggested meaning] is not the cause [of the beauty]. <s>Locana</s>: Therefore, disregarding the two [previous] types, he raises an objection regarding the third type — "in [the figure] whose cause is unstated" (<s>anukta-nimittāyām api</s>) etc. "Of the suggested" (<s>vyaṅgyasya</s>): <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s> [says that] the suffering caused by cold is the cause here — with that intention he says: "but here there is no production of beauty." As for the cause imagined even by connoisseurs (<s>rasika</s>) — "thinking sleep to be a means lighter than even going for meeting the beloved, he did not abandon his contraction out of the intention of falling asleep" — that too was not imagined as a cause of beauty by the <s>alaṅkāra</s> theorists, but rather: the <s>viśeṣokti</s> element itself — "does not loosen" — is the cause of beauty, adorned by a suggested cause of this nature. Otherwise, this would not even be a <s>viśeṣokti</s> at all.
This is the definition.
As in: "Of the sage who was a wanderer from the [right] path, who had a firm desire for the destruction of enemies —"
"By this bow of <s>Rāma</s>, the teaching of <s>dharma</s> was taught!"
Thus. //

children.translated_text: <s>Mada</s> (intoxication) is joy born from the enjoyment of distinguished objects.
<s>Priti</s> (affection) is attachment to objects.
<s>Mana</s> (pride) is the elevation of the mind; its breaking — this is a qualifier of <s>Ananga</s> (the god of love).

children.text: locanam sa priyāsaṅgamotkaṇṭhāṃ sāsahyāṃ manasaḥ śucam //
children.translated_text: <s>Locana</s>: 'That unbearable grief of the mind, [arising from] the longing for union with the beloved —'

<s>Bālapriyā</s>: [There is] no [<s>Bālapriyā</s> commentary on this passage]; 'therefore' — this is the meaning. /
'Here, the cause (<s>nimitta</s>)' — the meaning is: the cause that is to be inferred from the contraction and relaxation [of the eyelids]. /
'More subtle' — the purport is: because the onset of sleep is obtainable only through the non-abandonment of contraction. /
'That too is a cause' — the meaning is: the cause in the form of the cognition of the onset of sleep, as imagined by connoisseurs. /
'But rather' etc. — the construction is: 'the <s>viśeṣokti</s> (specific expression) portion is of the nature: it does not relax.' /
'The cause being manifested' — the meaning is: the aforementioned cause. /
'But otherwise' — the meaning is: because of the absence of the specific form of embellishment by the manifested cause. /
'The two views' — the meaning is: the two views of <s>Udbhaṭa</s> and the connoisseurs. /
By the general statement 'of the suggested' etc. /
He states the definition given by <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s>: '<s>paryāyoktam</s>' (circumlocution) etc. /
'<s>Tat</s>' (that) is to be supplied. /
He shows the meaning of the word '<s>paryāya</s>': 'by another' etc. /
He clarifies that very [point]: 'the expressible' etc. /
'The destruction of the enemy' — since the existence of enemies is not fitting for a sage, the desire for their destruction is even more unfitting, and the firmness of that [desire] is utterly unfitting; hence he says '<s>utpata</s>' etc. /
'Of <s>Rāma</s>' — of <s>Bhārgava Rāma</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>). /
'By this <s>Bhīṣma</s>' — as the agent; 'by means of the bow' — as the instrument. /
'Taught' — performed. /
'<s>Dharmadeśanā</s>' — religious instruction. /
Here too, he shows that the expressible alone is primary: 'here' etc. /
'A certain accomplishment of beauty' — [this means] there is no primacy [of the suggested]. /
Even in <s>paryāyokti</s>, if the suggested has primacy, then let that be the subsumption of that [<s>paryāyokti</s>] within <s>dhvani</s>. /
But not the subsumption of <s>dhvani</s> within that [<s>paryāyokti</s>]. /
Because [<s>dhvani</s>] is about to be demonstrated as having a vast scope and as being the principal (<s>aṅgin</s>). /
<s>Locana</s>: Here, although it is suggested that <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s power overwhelms the power of <s>Bhārgava</s>, nevertheless, the poetic meaning is adorned by the expressible alone — 'the religious instruction was taught' — aided by that [suggestion]. /
Therefore, '<s>paryāyokta</s>' means: that which is stated by circumlocution — i.e., by an alternative mode of cognition through the suggested — that which is expressed as 'being stated' is said to be '<s>paryāyokta</s>' — this is the definition-statement; '<s>paryāyoktam</s>' is the defined-term; and being a figure of meaning (<s>arthālaṅkāra</s>) is the general characteristic — all this is consistent. /
But if one forcefully explains '<s>abhidhīyate</s>' (is stated) as '<s>abhidhīyate pratīyate pradhānatayā</s>' (is stated, i.e., is cognized with primacy), and the example is '<s>bhama dhammia</s>' etc. — then its status as a figure would be far removed, since [the discussion] terminates in its own essential nature [as <s>dhvani</s>]. /
In that case, it should not be counted among the figures. /
And its further sub-varieties would need to be stated. /
Therefore he says: 'if with primacy' etc. /
'In <s>dhvani</s>' — the meaning is: it would be the self [of <s>dhvani</s>] itself and not a figure, since it would be subsumed in its own self. /
'There' — <s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'is suggested' — the meaning is: is manifested. /
'Aided by that' — the meaning is: embellished by that suggested meaning. /
'By the expressible alone' — by the expressible meaning alone. /
'The poetic meaning' — the <s>vīra-rasa</s> (heroic sentiment). /
'Therefore' — the connection is: 'therefore all is consistent.' /
The purport is: if the suggested had primacy, all this would be untenable, therefore the primacy of the expressible must be accepted. /
'<s>Paryāyoktaṃ yadanyena prakāreṇābhidhīyate</s>' (circumlocution is that which is stated by another mode) — this much alone is the definition stated by <s>Bhāmaha</s>; therein, the explanation of 'by another mode' is [the passage] from '<s>paryāyeṇa</s>' up to '<s>upalakṣitam</s>.' /
The word '<s>paryāya</s>' means precisely 'by another mode' — to indicate this, '<s>paryāyeṇa</s>' was used here. /
Therefore its explanation is: 'by an alternative mode.' /
What is that mode? To this he says: 'of the nature of cognition' etc. /
The elaboration of this very [point] is: 'by the suggested.' /
He states the meaning of the instrumental case: '<s>upalakṣitam</s>' (characterized). /
The connection is: 'that which is stated, being stated, is called <s>paryāyokta</s>.' /
The explanation of '<s>abhidhīyamānam</s>' (being stated) is: 'being stated indeed' (<s>uktam eva sat</s>). /
'This is the definition-statement' — the meaning is: [the passage ending in] '<s>iti</s>' is the definitional sentence. /
By this very definition-sentence, the primacy of the expressible accompanied by the suggested is understood: this is the purport. /
'This is the defined-term' — by this fitting name too, what was previously stated is understood: this is the purport. /
'Being a figure of meaning is the general characteristic' — [this means:] if the suggested had primacy, the attainment of being the embellished [entity] would breach its status as a figure: this is the purport. /
'General characteristic' means: common property. /
He raises the alternative view: 'but if' etc. /
'Forcefully' — the meaning is: by straining the words. /
'Is cognized with primacy' — '<s>abhi</s>' in the sense of 'facing toward.' /
And that [primacy] is what necessitates it: this is the purport. /
In this alternative, he states what would be undesirable: 'that' etc. /
Now, 'let it not be a figure' — to this he says: 'that' etc. /
Not only would there be abandonment of its well-known nature, but even unfamiliar sub-varieties would have to be imagined: he says 'varieties' etc. /
Moreover, in the <s>paryāyokta</s> of the type exemplified by <s>Bhāmaha</s>, the primacy does not belong to the suggested. /
Because the expressible is not subordinated there, and hence not intended [as secondary]. /
Regarding <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment) and <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), however — <s>Locana</s>: in such as are intended as figures, <s>dhvani</s> is not subsumed; [and] such [cases] are not what we call <s>dhvani</s>. /
For <s>dhvani</s> has a vast scope, pervading <s>bhāva</s> etc. everywhere, and because of being the ground of all [poetic elements], it is the principal. /
And a figure is not all-pervading like another figure. /
Nor is it the principal, because it depends on the embellished [entity]. /
Now, if its all-pervasiveness and principal status were accepted, and its status as a figure abandoned — then it would be relying on our very system; merely out of jealousy it would be called '<s>paryāyokta</s>': this is the purport. /
'And this much' — the meaning is: even this much, i.e., the primacy of the suggested. /
He shows [this] with 'not again' etc. — the meaning is: the meaning shown by the passage beginning with 'not again.' /
That which is <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s preferred form, as shown by his example — there too the suggested has no primacy, because it is not the cause of beauty. /
Therefore, following his lead, whatever other example of the same type is imagined — there too the suggested has no primacy: this is the connection. /
But if, not accepting that example, one cites '<s>bhama dhammia</s>' etc. as the example — that is mere discipleship to us [i.e., our school]. /
Only [such a one], without relying on the [proper] system, through mere hearsay — thus self-aggrandizes: an ignoble act. As the historians say: 'Through disrespect and concealment, one who listens goes to hell.' /
For <s>Bhāmaha</s> cited [as example]: 'Whether in homes or on roads, we do not eat the food that learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> do not eat.' /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'because of the many types' — this is the purport. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, only the subsumption within <s>dhvani</s> was stated; he states the consequence of that as terminating in its non-status as a figure: 'in its own self' etc. /
'Of such kind' — the meaning is: having a subordinated suggested meaning. /
He states the reason for non-subsumption: 'not' etc. /
'Of all' — the meaning is: of <s>guṇas</s> etc. /
'Like another figure' — the meaning is: like the well-known bracelet etc. [i.e., in the world, one ornament does not pervade all others]. /
'Now' etc. — if <s>paryāyokta</s> is accepted as all-pervading and as the principal, that is: this is the meaning. /
'Then' — the construction is: merely from jealousy, it relies on our very system [but] is called '<s>paryāyokta</s>.' /
'Even this much' — the meaning is: even the primacy of the suggested. /
'Shows' — the meaning is: shows the meaning stated by the passage beginning with 'not again.' /
'There too' — the meaning is: even in <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s example. /
He raises the alternative and refutes it: 'but if' etc. /
'Only but without relying on the system, through mere hearsay' — the meaning is: without studying the <s>śāstra</s> properly through approaching a teacher as prescribed, [but only] through a semblance of learning. /
'Through disrespect' — toward learning and teacher — this is to be supplied. /
'Through concealment' — having made self-concealment, [i.e.,] having hidden one's identity. /
'Goes' — reaches. /
What is that example of <s>Bhāmaha</s>? To this he says: 'by <s>Bhāmaha</s>' etc. /
'In homes' — the construction is: 'We do not eat that food which learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> do not eat, whether in homes or on roads.' /
The primacy of the expressible and the subordination of the suggested are well-known [in this example]. /
Even in the <s>saṅkara</s> (combination) figure, when one figure supports the shadow of another figure — <s>Locana</s>: for this speech of Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s> prohibits the offering of food (<s>rasadāna</s>) by circumlocution. /
As he himself says: 'and that, for the prevention of the offering of food.' /
And this prohibition of the food-offering, [being] the suggested, has no beauty whatsoever by which primacy might be suspected. /
Rather, that suggested [meaning], corroborated by the suggestion — the non-eating without the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s eating — that very thing, in the stated manner, being <s>paryāyokta</s>, adorns the contextual meaning of eating. /
For his intention is not 'let my food be non-poisoned' — [hence] this is a figure (<s>paryāyokta</s>) indeed. /
'Of concealment and illumination' — this has been previously determined. /
Therefore he says: 'well-known' etc. /
'Well-known' — perceived, established, and authoritative: this is the meaning. /
And previously this was designated as belonging to <s>upamā</s> etc.; he shows that it is not so [now] by '<s>pūrvam</s>' etc. /
With the shadow of another, by that shadow — 'having been shown as an example for the purpose of filling the topical order, and also said again as "there is no <s>dhvani</s> because of the absence of primacy of the suggested"' — this is the connection. /
'With another shadow, the reality is one and the same' — [it is] only of the nature of <s>upamā</s>, the suspicion of <s>dhvani</s>-status arising from its suggested character. /
But what the <s>Vivaraṇa</s> author [says] — that there is no universal concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of <s>dīpaka</s> with <s>upamā</s>, elaborating with many examples — that is useless, insubstantial, and easily refuted. /
'Intoxication produces delight, and love produces the breaking of pride' — <s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'we eat' — this is the construction. /
'Statement' — 'toward <s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>)' is to be supplied. /
'By circumlocution' — the meaning is: by an alternative mode of cognition. /
'Prohibits the offering of food' — the meaning is: conveys the cessation of the offering of poison. /
The intention of <s>Caidya</s>-contrived poison-offering — 'let it not happen to me' — or 'let the food be non-poisoned' — this is the suggested purport of the Lord for the connoisseurs: this is the meaning. /
'Has no beauty' — the connection is [with the previous statement]. /
The purport is: the beauty belongs to the expressible alone. /
'Corroborated by that suggestion' — the meaning is: by the stated suggestion. /
'That very expressible' — that very [expressible meaning]. /
'In the stated manner' — the meaning is: being characterized by the suggested through the mode of cognition. /
'The contextual food-meaning' — the meaning is: the meaning of 'we eat,' which is contextually established as food that has been offered by the learned and eaten [by them]: such a meaning. /
'The suggested [content] is not intended [as primary]' — and therefore the lack of primacy [of the suggested] — he says: 'not indeed of this' etc. /
'Of this' — of <s>Vāsudeva</s>. /
'Not intended' — not conveyed to <s>Caidya</s>, not informed [to him]. /
He concludes: 'thus' etc. /
He explains '<s>prasiddha</s>' (well-known) in three ways: 'perceived' etc. /
'In <s>dīpaka</s>, <s>apahṇuti</s>, etc.' — when what was previously stated gives rise to the suspicion of repetition, he says [that] despite identity of essence, there is no repetition because of difference of mode: '<s>pūrvam</s>' etc. /
'By that shadow, this mode' — the meaning is: in this manner. /
'The absence of primacy of the suggested — not being <s>dhvani</s> — is said again' — this is the connection. /
'The reality is one' — the meaning is: the reality of the absence of primacy of the suggested in <s>upamā</s>. /
The suspicion of <s>dhvani</s>-status [arises] because of the suggested character of <s>upamā</s> alone — the meaning [is clear]. /
The demonstration of the concomitance of <s>upamā</s> through examples — he says — '<s>mada</s>' etc.

Here too, even though there is the relation of being successively generated, [there is simile] because the relation of <s>upamana</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) is easily conceivable.
For it is not the case that sequentially related things cannot have the relation of standard and object of comparison.

children.text: tathā hi--- rāma iva daśaratho 'bhūddaśaratha iva radhurajo 'pi radhusaddaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: For example: '<s>Dasaratha</s> was like <s>Rama</s>, and <s>Raghu</s> too was like <s>Dasaratha</s> — resembling <s>Raghu</s>,
<s>Aja</s> [was] like [him] — and [thus] the dynasty of <s>Dilipa</s>! Wondrous is this fame of <s>Rama</s>!'
Thus.

children.text: tasmātkramikatvaṃ samaṃ vā prākaraṇikatvamupamāṃ niruṃṇaddhīti ko 'yaṃ trāsa itlaṃ gardabhīdohānuvartanena /
children.translated_text: Therefore, [the objection that] sequentiality or topicality prevents simile — what is this fear? Enough of following the milking of a she-donkey [i.e., a futile pursuit].
'Even in the <s>sankara</s> (combination) figure' —
'When there is the outline of contradictory ornamentations, simultaneously, and the impossibility of [both] functioning [together],

children.text: ekasya ca grahe nyāyadoṣābhāve ca saṅkaraḥ //
children.translated_text: and when one is grasped [over the other], and there is no logical defect — that is <s>sankara</s> (combination).'
Thus — it is not that [it] does not occur.
Thus, from the definition, [this is] one type.
For example, by me myself: 'Moon-faced, with dark-lotus eyes, with a row of teeth [white as] white jasmine — she
has been fashioned by the Creator with delightful forms born of sky, water, and earth.'

it.i /
atra śaśī vadanamasyāḥ tadvadvā vadanamasyā iti rūpakopamollekhādyugapaddvayāsambhavādekatarapakṣatyāgagrahaṇe pramāṇābhāvātsaṅkara iti vyaṅgyavācyatāyā evaniścayātkā dhvanisambhāvanā /

children.translated_text:
'Which is suggested, which is expressible?' — since there is no determination, [there is] no possibility of <s>dhvani</s> constituted by the primacy of the suggested.
<s>Locana</s>: Here itself [there is also] <s>yamaka</s> (paronomasia) and <s>upama</s> (simile).

children.text: tṛtīyaḥ prakāraḥ-- yatraikatra vākyāṃśe 'neko 'rthālaṅkārastatrāpi dvayoḥ sāmyātkasya vyaṅgyatā /
children.translated_text: The third type [is]: where, in a single portion of a sentence, there are multiple figures of meaning — there too, due to the equality of two [figures], whose has the status of being suggested?
For example: 'Since [the Day] has the same rising and setting [as the Sun], when the Sun has gone toward its setting,
the Day, exhausted, enters the cave of darkness, as if for rest.'

Thus. Here, [the question arises:] 'the moon is her face' or 'her face is like the moon' — since the simultaneous occurrence of <s>rupaka</s> (metaphor) and <s>upama</s> (simile) in outline is impossible, and since there is no valid ground for abandoning one alternative and accepting the other, there is <s>sankara</s> — and since there is precisely no determination of [which is] suggested and [which is] expressible, what possibility is there of <s>dhvani</s>?
As for the second type — the co-presence of figures of sound and meaning in a single [passage] — there too, what doubt [can there be] about the suggested?
For example: '<s>Smara</s> (Love), you delight [her] beloved like <s>Smara</s> (yourself), [causing him] to remember — through [his] embrace' etc.
<s>Balapriya</s>: '<s>Uttara</s>' — the meaning is: even though each successive [emotion] is generated by the preceding one. By this, sequentiality is stated. '<s>Upamana</s>' — the meaning is: because the similarity among them, in terms of being generators of mental modifications, is easily conceivable. He shows that sequentially related things can have the relation of standard and object of comparison — '<s>Rama iva</s>' etc. Here, similarity should be understood as consisting in possessing a particular quality.
'Does not not occur' — the meaning is: it does occur indeed. He concludes with ridicule — 'therefore' etc.
The four types of <s>sankara</s> (combination) — based on the distinction of doubt-combination etc. — he presents their definitions following the view of <s>Bhattodbhata</s>: '<s>viruddha</s>' etc. 'Of contradictory ornamentations' — when there is the outline, i.e., the manifestation, of two [contradictory figures]; 'simultaneously'; '<s>tadvrttyasambhave</s>' — the meaning is: the impossibility of both functioning [together]. 'When one is grasped' — when one of the two is grasped by abandoning the other. '<s>Nyaya</s>' means a supporting cognition; '<s>dosa</s>' means an opposing [cognition].
'<s>Sasi</s>' — the three qualifiers '<s>sasivadana</s>' etc. in sequence support '<s>gagana</s>' etc. [i.e., sky, water, earth]. '<s>Eka</s>' — the meaning is: in the abandoning and accepting of one of the two alternatives. '<s>Iti</s>' is in the causal sense. '<s>Vyangya</s>' etc. —
And <s>utpreksa</s> (poetic fancy) is indicated by the particle '<s>iva</s>' ('as if').
Thus these two varieties have been stated.
'Figures of sound, meaning, and usage, occurring together in a single sentence,
or entering a single portion of a sentence — that is called <s>sankara</s> (combination).'

Thus. For here, [the verse] depicts a dutiful son of noble family who is zealous in undertaking vows appropriate to the misfortune of [his] master — [this] is the <s>ekadesa-vivarti rupaka</s> (partial-transformation metaphor).
Thus.
The fourth type, however, [is] where figures stand in the relation of beneficiary and benefactor (<s>anugrahya-anugrahaka</s>).
For example: 'Like a wind-blown blue lotus — the unsteady glance of the large-eyed one;

children.text: tayā gṛhītaṃ nu mṛgāṅganābhyastato gahītaṃ nu mṛgāṅganābhiḥ //
children.translated_text: was it taken from the female deer by her? Or was it taken from her by the female deer?'

children.text: atra mṛgāṅganāvalokanena tadavalokanasyopamā yadyapi vyaṅgyā, tathāpi vāyyasya sā sandehālaṅkārasyābhyutthānakārimītvenānugrahakatvādguṇībhūtā, anugrāhyatvena hi sandehe paryavasānam /
children.translated_text: Here, although the simile — [comparing] her glance to the glance of female deer — is suggested, nevertheless it is subordinated, since it serves as a supporter of the expressible <s>sandeha</s> (doubt) figure by way of providing its occasion for arising; for it culminates in doubt, by virtue of being the beneficiary.
As stated: 'Where ornamentations stand related through mutual assistance,
and do not independently attain their own realization — that too is <s>sankara</s> (combination).'

children.translated_text: The purport is: because both are in a state of oscillation [between expressible and suggested].

children.text: nanu yatra vyaṅgyameva prādhānyena bhāti tatra kiṃ kartavyam /
children.translated_text: Now, where the suggested alone shines forth with primacy — what is to be done in that case?

children.text: yathā--- hīi ṇa guṇāṇurāo khalāṇaṃ ṇavaraṃ pasiddhisaraṇāṇam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Prakrit</s>:] 'Ah, the wicked have no appreciation for qualities — they are merely devoted to [their own] fame!

children.text: kira pahiṇusai sasimaṇaṃ cande piāmuhe diṭṭhe //
children.translated_text: It is said that the moon-gem exudes [moisture] upon seeing the moon, not upon seeing the beloved's face!'

<s>Balapriya</s>: 'What [is the meaning]?' Having shown <s>sankara</s> consisting of co-occurrence in a single sentence, he shows <s>sankara</s> consisting of entrance into a single portion of a sentence — '<s>yatra</s>' etc. 'Due to equality' — the meaning is: due to similarity in being expressible.
'<s>Svami</s>' — when there is the misfortune of the master, the appropriate undertaking of vows — zealous in that — a son of noble family; the depiction of such [a figure] has the Day as its subject. '<s>Tamoguham</s>' — this is a partial-transformation metaphor (<s>ekadesa-vivarti rupaka</s>). That the Sun's mastership, the going as misfortune, dwelling in a cave as vow-taking, and the entrance therein as the purposive action — [all this] is understood through the verbal metaphor '<s>tamoguham</s>': this is the purport.
'<s>Utpreksa</s>' (fancy) has been indicated by the word '<s>iva</s>.' He states the consensus regarding the stated two varieties — '<s>tad idam</s>' etc. By this <s>karika</s>, the definition of the stated two varieties has been presented.
Following the commentary-prose, he illustrates the <s>sankara</s> in which the expressible and suggested stand in the relation of beneficiary and benefactor — '<s>pravata</s>' etc. '<s>Taya</s>' — the meaning is: by <s>Sri Parvati</s>.
'But even granting the benefactor-status [of the simile], whence its subordination?' — to this he says: '<s>anugrahyatvena</s>' ('by virtue of being the beneficiary') etc. [What] 'of doubt' — this is to be supplied. 'Culminates' — of the suggested simile that is the benefactor: this is to be supplied. Then the suggested is not intended as primary — hence it does not fall within the domain of <s>dhvani</s>.
When, however, [there is] the possibility of two figures, the expressible and the suggested have equal primacy. Or, when the suggested resides there through the subordination of the expressible — then...
<s>Locana</s>: Then he says '<s>yad alankara</s>' etc. Thus, in the fourth type too, <s>dhvani</s>-status has been refuted. As for the second and third types, it was stated that there is not even a possibility of suggestion.
In the first type — illustrated by '<s>sasivadana</s>' etc. — [it might seem that] there is somehow a possibility; anticipating this objection, he refutes it — '<s>alankara-dvaya</s>' etc. '<s>Samam</s>' —
