atrārthāntaranyāsastāvadvācyatvenābhāt.i, vyatirekāpahnutī tu vyaṅgyatvena pradhānatayetyabhiprāyeṇāśaṅkate---atheti /
tatrottaram--tadā so 'pīti /
saṅkarālaṅkāra bālapriyā asmiṃścaturthe bhede dhvanyabhāvaparatayā vṛttigranthamavatārayati---tadāheti /
āndolyamānatvāditi /
vācyatvavyaṅgyatvābhyāṃ sandihyamānatvādityarthaḥ /
nanvityādi /
yatreti /

children.translated_text: The meaning is: in whatever [type of] <s>sankara-alankara</s> (combination-figure).

children.text: bhavati na guṇānurāgaḥ khalānāṃ kevalaṃ prasiddhiśaraṇānām /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit shadow-translation:] 'The wicked, who are merely devoted to [their own] fame, have no appreciation for qualities.

children.text: kila prasnaiti śaśimaṇiḥ candre na priyāmukhe dṛṣṭe //
children.translated_text: It is said that the moon-gem exudes [moisture] upon seeing the moon, not upon seeing the beloved's face.'

[<s>Balapriya</s>:] Here, <s>arthantaranyasa</s> (corroboration through another matter) at least shines forth as expressible, while <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) and <s>apahnuti</s> (concealment) [shine forth] as suggested and as primary — with this intention, he raises an objection: '<s>atha</s>' etc. The answer to that — 'then that too [is <s>dhvani</s>]' etc. '<s>Sankara-alankara</s>' — the <s>Balapriya</s> introduces the commentary-prose passage directed at the non-existence of <s>dhvani</s> in this fourth variety — 'then he says' etc. 'Due to oscillation' — the meaning is: due to being in doubt between expressible-status and suggested-status.
'<s>Nanu</s>' ('but') etc. '<s>Yatra</s>' —

children.text:
iti cchāyā /
guṇānurāgaḥ parairvarṇyamāneṣvapi keṣāñcidguṇeṣu prītiḥ /
na bhavatītyatra hetumāha--prasiddhīti /
vastutatvāvamarśarahitānāmiti bhāvaḥ /
uktaṃ sāmānyaṃ viśeṣeṇa samarthayate---kiletyādi /
'śaśimaṇiḥ candre dṛṣṭe prasnauti kila; priyāmukhe dṛṣṭe na prasnautī'tyānvayaḥ /
yadi śasimaṇergumānurāgassyāttadā priyāmukhadarśane kathaṃ na niḥṣyandeteti bhāvaḥ /
vyatireketi /
candraḥ priyāmukhameva candra ityarthasya khyāpanādapahnutiśceti bhāvaḥ /
vyaṅgyatvenetyādi /
vyaṅgyatvena pradhānatayā ca bhāta ityarthaḥ /
saṅkaroktereva dhvanitvabuddhinivartakatvaṃ vṛttāvuktaṃ, so 'pi dhvaniviṣayo 'stu, na tu sa eva dhvaniriti vaktuṃ śakyam /
paryāyoktanirdiṣṭanyāyāt /
api ca saṅkarālaṅkāre 'pi ca kvacit saṅkaroktireva locanam evāyaṃ na bhavati, api tvalaṅkāradhvanināmāyaṃ dhvanerdvitīyo bhedaḥ /
yacca paryāyokte nirūpataṃ tatsarvamatrāpyanusaraṇīyam /
atha sarveṣu saṅkaraprabhedeṣu vyaṅgyasambhāvanānirāsaprakāraṃ sādhāraṇamāha---api ceti /

children.translated_text: The connection is: 'even in a <s>sankara-alankara</s> somewhere' — meaning: different from all [the four] varieties.

children.text: saṅkīrmatā hi miśratvaṃ lolībhāvaḥ, tatra kathamekasya prādhānyaṃ kṣīrajalavat /
children.translated_text: For <s>sankirtana</s> (being mixed) is mixing, i.e., fluctuation — and therein, how can there be the primacy of one, [when they are mixed] like milk and water?
'The praise of a thing that has departed from the subject at hand, [being the praise] of another entity —
that is <s>aprastuta-prasamsa</s> (praise of the non-topical), and it is declared to be of three kinds.'

Thus the <s>chaya</s> (Sanskrit rendering). '<s>Gunanuraga</s>' (appreciation of qualities) — affection for qualities that are being praised even by others. 'Does not exist' — for this he states the reason: '<s>prasiddhi</s>' etc. The purport is: of those who are devoid of reflection on the truth of things. He substantiates the general [statement] with a particular [example] — '<s>kila</s>' etc. The construction is: 'The moon-gem exudes [moisture] upon seeing the moon, it is said; it does not exude upon seeing the beloved's face.' The purport is: if the moon-gem had an appreciation for qualities, then why would it not exude upon seeing the beloved's face?
'<s>Vyatireka</s>' (contrast) — and since the moon is declared to be 'the beloved's face is itself the [true] moon,' there is <s>apahnuti</s> (concealment) as well: this is the purport. '<s>Vyangya</s>' etc. — the meaning is: [they] shine forth as suggested and as primary.
The <s>vrtti</s> states that the very utterance of <s>sankara</s> prevents the cognition of <s>dhvani</s>-status — 'that too may be a domain of <s>dhvani</s>, but it cannot be said that that itself is <s>dhvani</s>' — by the principle expounded in <s>paryayokta</s> (circumlocution). Moreover, even in the <s>sankara-alankara</s>, somewhere the <s>sankara</s>-utterance itself...
<s>Locana</s>: This indeed does not occur [as simple <s>sankara</s>]; rather, this is the second variety of <s>dhvani</s>, called <s>alankara-dhvani</s> (suggestion of a figure). And whatever was analyzed in <s>paryayokta</s>, all of that is to be followed here too. Then, stating the general method of refuting the possibility of suggestion in all the varieties of <s>sankara</s>, he says '<s>api ca</s>' etc.

children.text:
aprastutasya varṇanaṃ prastutākṣepima ityarthaḥ /
sa cākṣepastrividho bhavati---sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvāt, nimittanimittibhāvāt sārūpyācca /
tatra prathame prakāradvaye prastutāprastutayostulyameva prādhānyamiti pratijñāṃ karoti-aprastutetyādinā prādhānyamityantena /
children.translated_text: Therein, for the first two varieties, he makes the claim that the topical and non-topical have equal primacy — by '<s>aprastuta</s>' etc., up to '<s>pradhanyam</s>' ('primacy').

children.text: tatra sāmānyaviśeṣabhāve 'pi dvayī gatiḥ--sāmānyamaprākaraṇikaṃ śabdenocyate, gamyate tu prākaraṇiko viśeṣaḥ sa ekaḥ prakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, in [the case of] the general-particular relation too, there are two possibilities: the general, being non-topical, is expressed by words, while the particular, being topical, is understood — that is one variety.
For example: 'Ah, the cruelty of <s>samsara</s>! Ah, the wickedness of misfortunes!
Ah, the interminable ways of Fate, which is crooked by nature!'

The description of the non-topical [entails] the implication (<s>aksepa</s>) of the topical — this is the meaning. And that implication is of three kinds: by the relation of general and particular (<s>samanya-visesa</s>), by the relation of cause and effect (<s>nimitta-nimitti</s>), and by resemblance (<s>sarupya</s>).

children.text:
atra hi daivaprādhānyaṃ sarvatra sāmānyarūpamaprastutaṃ varṇitaṃ satprakṛte vastuni kvāpi vinaṣṭe viśeṣātmani paryavasyati /
tatrāpi viśeṣāṃśasya sāmānyena vyāptatvādyvaṅgyaviśeṣavadvācyasāmānyasyāpi prādhānyam, na hi sāmānyaviśeṣayoryugapatprādhānyaṃ virudhyate /
yadā tu viseṣo 'prākaramikaḥ prākaraṇikaṃ sāmānyamākṣipati tadā dvitīyaḥ bālapriyā tatkathamityatrāha--saṅkīrṇateti /
'mikṣatvam' ityasya vivaraṇam---lolībhāva iti /
ātyantikassaṃśleṣa ityarthaḥ /
adhikārāditi bhāmahīyamidam /
adhikāraḥ prastutatvam /
sārārthaṃ vyācaṣṭe-aprastutasya varṇanamiti /
stutiśabdārthakathanaṃ varṇanamiti /
dvayī gatiriti /
prakāradvayamityarthaḥ /
sa iti /
sāmānyādviśeṣapratītirūpa ityarthaḥ /
daivaprādhānyamiti /
'daivasvātantryam' iti ca pāṭhaḥ /
sarvatra sāmānyarūpamiti /
saṃsāranairghṛṇyādāvanugatamityarthaḥ /
sarvasya tadāyattasthititvāditi bhāvaḥ /
kvāpīti /
preyasīputrādirūpa ityarthaḥ /
atra vyaṅgyavācyayossamaprādhānyaṃ darśayati--tatrāpītyādi /
nanu vyaṅgyasya viśeṣasyāstu prādhānyaṃ, vācyasya sāmānyasya tatkathaṃ syādityatrāha--viśeṣāṃśasyeti /
prādhānyamiti /
dhvanisambhāvanāṃ nirākaroti /
aprastutapraśaṃsāyāmapi yadā sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvānnimittanimittibhāvādvā abhidhīyamānasyāprastutsaya pratīyamānena prastutenābhisambandhaḥ tadābhidhīyamānapratīyamānayoḥ samameva prādhānyam /
yadā tāvatsāmānyasyāprastutasyābhidhīyamānasya prākaraṇikena viśeṣeṇa pratīyamānena sambandhastadā viśeṣapratītau satyāmapi prādhānyena tatsāmānyenāvinābhāvātsāmānyasyāpi prādhānyam /
yadāpi viśeṣasya sāmānyaniṣṭhatvaṃ tadāpi sāmānyasya prādhānye sāmanye sarvaviśeṣāṇāmantarbhāvādviśeṣasyāpi prādhānyam /
children.translated_text: Even when the particular has its foundation in the general, still, when the general has primacy — since all particulars are included within the general — the particular too has primacy.
[Locana] A [second] variety:

children.text: yathā--- etattasya mukhātkiyattakamalinīpattre kaṇaṃ pārthaso yanmuktāmaṇirityamaṃsta sa jaḍaḥ śṛṇvanyadasmādapi /
children.translated_text: For example — "Hear from me too what this much [amounts to] from his mouth: the son of <s>Pṛthā</s> supposed that a drop on a lotus leaf was a pearl — that fool!

children.text: aṅgulyagralaghukriyāpravilayinyādīyamāne śanai. statroṅḍīya gato hahetyanudinaṃ nidrāti nāntaḥ śucā //
children.translated_text: When it was slowly being taken up, dissolving at the light touch of a fingertip, it flew up from there — and with a cry of "Alas!" he sleeps not day after day, consumed by inner grief."

[Locana] Here, the predominance of fate (<s>daivaprādhānya</s>), which is a <s>sāmānya</s> (general) form present everywhere, is described as <s>aprastuta</s> (the irrelevant), and when some real thing of a particular nature is destroyed, it culminates in the <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular). Even there, because the particular aspect is pervaded by the general, just as the suggested particular has primacy, so too does the expressed general — for the simultaneous primacy of the general and particular is not contradictory. But when a non-contextual particular draws in the contextual general, then it is the second [type]. [Bālapriyā] To the question "how is that?" he says — "<s>saṅkīrṇatā</s>" (intermixture). The explanation of "<s>mikṣatva</s>" (blending) is "<s>lolībhāva</s>" (fluctuation) — meaning absolute fusion. "By reason of the topic" (<s>adhikārāt</s>) — this is from <s>Bhāmaha</s>. "Topic" (<s>adhikāra</s>) means relevance to the subject at hand. He explains the essential meaning — "description of the irrelevant" (<s>aprastutasya varṇanam</s>). The meaning of the word "praise" (<s>stuti</s>) is "description" (<s>varṇana</s>). "Twofold course" (<s>dvayī gati</s>) — meaning two varieties. "That" (<s>sa</s>) — meaning of the form where the particular is cognized from the general. "Predominance of fate" (<s>daivaprādhānya</s>) — there is also the reading "independence of fate" (<s>daivasvātantrya</s>). "Of general form everywhere" — meaning pervading the cruelty of <s>saṃsāra</s> and so forth. The sense is: because the existence of everything depends on that. "Somewhere" (<s>kvāpi</s>) — meaning in the form of a beloved, a son, and so forth. Here he shows the equal primacy of the suggested and expressed — "even there" (<s>tatrāpi</s>) and so on. Now, let the suggested particular have primacy — but how could the expressed general have it? To this he replies — "of the particular aspect" (<s>viśeṣāṃśasya</s>). "Primacy" — he refutes the supposition of <s>dhvani</s>. Even in <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant), when through the relation of general-to-particular or cause-to-effect there is a connection between the irrelevant being expressed and the relevant being suggested, then there is equal primacy of the expressed and the suggested. When the general, which is irrelevant and being expressed, is connected with the contextual particular that is being suggested, then even though the particular is cognized, because of its inseparability from that general, the general too has primacy.

children.text:
atrāsthān.e mahattvasambhavanaṃ sāmānyaṃ prastutam, prastutaṃ tu jalabindau maṇitvasambhāvanaṃ viśeṣarūpaṃ vācyam /
tatrrāpi sāmānyaviśeṣayoryugapatprādhānye na virodha ityuktam /
evamekaḥ prakāro dvibhedo 'pi vicāritaḥ, yadā tāvadityādinā viśeṣasyāpi prādhānyamityantena /
etameva nyāyaṃ nimittanaimittikabhāve 'tidiśaṃstasyāpi dviprakāratāṃ bālapriyā viśeṣaprādhānyanāntarīyakatvaṃ sāmānyaprādhānyasyeti bhāvaḥ /
na hi virudhyata iti /
yathā 'raktaṃ paṭaṃ vaye'tyādau dvayostrayāṇaṃ vā vidhirit bhāvaḥ /
etaditi /
mukhāditi /
ārambhata ityarthaḥ /
prathamatassambhūtamiti yāvat /
'etadvakṣyamāṇaṃ śṛṇvi'ti sambandhaḥ /
muktāmaṇirityamasta yat etattasya jaḍasya kiyat vakṣyamāṇāpekṣayā atyalpamevetyarthaḥ /
sāddaśyanimittakastadbhramasya sambhavājjalakaṇe muktāmaṇibhramo bhavediti bhāvaḥ /
śṛṇviti /
asmāt pūrvoktāt /
anyadapi tvaṃ śṛṇu; kiṃ tadityatrāha---aṅgulīti /
sa jaḍa ityatrāpyanuṣajyate /
jātamuktāmaṇibhramo jaḍa ityarthaḥ /
tatreti /
tasmiñjalakaṇa ityarthaḥ /
'kutroḍḍīye'ti pāṭhe tu tasminniti śeṣo bodhyaḥ /
śanaiḥ muktāmaṇibudhyā mandam /
ādīyamāne aṅgulyagrasya laghukriyayā alpacācalanena pravlayini aṅguloveva lagra ityarthastathā sati /
uḍḍīyeti /
ayamiti śeṣaḥ /
tasyādarśinānmamāyaṃ muktāmaṇiḥ khamutpatya gata iti matvā antaḥśucā na nidrātītyarthaḥ /
nimittanimittibhāve cāyameva nyāyaḥ /

children.translated_text: [Locana] But when through mere resemblance (<s>sārūpya</s>) alone, in <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>, [the connection obtains between] the irrelevant and the relevant — he shows with "cause" (<s>nimitta</s>):
Sometimes the cause (<s>nimitta</s>), being the irrelevant that is expressed, draws in the effect (<s>naimitttika</s>), which is the relevant.

children.text: yathā----- ye yāntyabhyudaye prītiṃ nojjhanti vyasaneṣu ca /
children.translated_text: For example — "Those who rejoice in prosperity and do not abandon [one] in adversity,
they are kinsmen, they are true friends — the rest of the world is self-serving."

[Locana] Here, the attribution of greatness to what is unworthy is the <s>sāmānya</s> (general) that is relevant (<s>prastuta</s>), while the particular expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) is the supposition that a water drop is a pearl. Even there, the simultaneous primacy of general and particular is not contradictory, as stated. Thus one variety, though itself twofold, has been examined — from "when" (<s>yadā tāvat</s>) up to "the particular too has primacy." [Bālapriyā] Extending this same principle to the cause-effect relation (<s>nimittanaimittikabhāva</s>), he shows its twofold nature as well — the inseparability of the primacy of the general from the primacy of the particular is the purport. "Is not contradictory" — just as in "weave a red cloth" and similar cases, where there is an injunction of two or three [things simultaneously], that is the sense. "This" (<s>etat</s>) — "from his mouth" — meaning "from the beginning," i.e. "first produced." The connection is: "hear this that is about to be told." "He supposed it was a pearl" — "this" refers to how small it is from the perspective of what follows — meaning it is very little indeed. The sense is: because confusion as a pearl is possible for a water drop on account of resemblance. "Hear" — from what was said before, hear yet another thing too; what is it? To this he says — "the fingertip" (<s>aṅgulī</s>). "That fool" (<s>sa jaḍaḥ</s>) is to be connected here as well — meaning the fool who mistook it for a pearl. "There" (<s>tatra</s>) — meaning in that water drop. With the reading "where did it fly," "from that" is to be understood as the remainder. "Slowly" — gently, due to the belief that it was a pearl. "Being taken up" — dissolving through the light action of the fingertip, the slight movement — "the tip of the finger" is the meaning; that being the case, "it flew up" — "this" is to be supplied; not seeing it, thinking "my pearl has flown up into the sky," he does not sleep due to inner grief — that is the meaning. In the cause-effect relation too, this same principle [applies].

children.text:
atrāprastuta.ṃ suhṛdbāndhavarūpatvaṃ nimitt sajjanāsaktyā varṇayati naimittikīṃ śraddheyavacanatāṃ prastutāmātmano 'bhivyaṅktum; yatra naimittikapratītāvapi nimittapratītireva pradhānībhavatyanuprāṇākatveneti vyaṅgyavyañjakayoḥ prādhānyam /
kadācittu nemititakamaprastutaṃ varṇyamānaṃ satprastutaṃ nimittaṃ vyanakti /

children.translated_text: As in the <s>Setubandha</s> —
"<s>saggaṃ apārijāaṃ kotthuhalacchirahiaṃ mahumahassa uram</s>" (Prākrit:)
"<s>sumarābhi mahaṇapurao amuddhaandaṃ ca harajaḍāpabbhāram</s>" (Prākrit:)

[Locana] Here, the irrelevant — the quality of being a true friend and kinsman, which is the cause (<s>nimitta</s>) — is described through attachment to good people, in order to suggest the relevant effect (<s>naimitttika</s>): the trustworthiness of one's words. Where, even when the effect is cognized, the cognition of the cause itself becomes predominant as the animating force — hence there is primacy of both the suggested and its suggestor. But sometimes the irrelevant effect that is being described suggests the relevant cause.

children.text: tatra nimittapratītāvapi nemittikaṃ vācyabhūtam; pratyuta tannimittānuprāṇitatvenoddhurakandharīkarotyātmānamiti samapradhānataiva vācyavyaṅgyayoḥ /
children.translated_text: There, even when the cause is cognized, the effect remains what is expressed; rather, by being animated by that cause, it holds its head high — thus there is equal primacy of expressed and suggested.

Of this too there are two sub-varieties: sometimes the wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) arises from the expressed irrelevant, while the suggested merely looks on through its face (<s>tanmukhaprekṣa</s>, i.e. is subordinate).

children.text: yathāsmadupādhyāyabhaṭṭendurājasya---- prāṇā yena samarpitāstava balādyena tvamutthāpitaḥ skandhe yasya ciraṃ sthito 'si vidadhe yaste saparyāmapi /
children.translated_text: As [in this verse] of our teacher <s>Bhaṭṭa Indurāja</s> — "He by whom your life-breaths were offered, he by whom you were forcibly raised up, he on whose shoulder you long stood, and he who performed worship of you too —

children.text: tasyāsya smitamātrakeṇa janayan prāṇāpahārakriyāṃ bhrātaḥ pratyupakāriṇāṃ dhuri paraṃ vetāla līlāyate //
children.translated_text: of this very one, by a mere smile you bring about the act of taking life — O brother, O <s>Vetāla</s>, among repayers of kindness you sport supreme!"

[Locana] Here <s>Jāmbavān</s>, by describing the irrelevant effect (<s>naimitttika</s>) — the remembrance of <s>Hari</s>'s chest bereft of the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem and <s>Lakṣmī</s> — aims to suggest the relevant cause (<s>nimitta</s>): that one who is worthy of being heeded in counsel, whose worth is established through service to elders, longevity, and worldly skill.

children.text:
bālapriyā atrāsthāna iti /
jaḍānāmiti śeṣaḥ /
ye iti /
aparaḥ uktaviparītavṛttiḥ /
nimittaṃ śraddheyavacanatānimittam /
sajjanāsaktyeti /
sajjanabahumatyetyarthaḥ /
naimittaketi /
śraddheyavacanatetyarthaḥ /
nimittapratītireveti /
na hi vaktustathāvidhabāndhavatvādipratītiṃ vinā śraddheyavacanatvaṃ pratītipathamavatarediti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: For without the cognition of the speaker's qualities of being such a kinsman and so forth, the trustworthiness of his words would not enter the path of cognition — that is the sense.
"<s>Saggam</s>" (Prākrit) —
[Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] "Heaven without the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree, the chest of the slayer of <s>Madhu</s> bereft of the <s>Kaustubha</s> and <s>Lakṣmī</s>,
I remember, [standing] before [him at] the churning — and the mass of <s>Hara</s>'s matted locks without the undeluded moon."

[Bālapriyā] "Here, in what is unworthy" — the remainder is "of fools." "Those who" (<s>ye</s>) — "the other" (<s>apara</s>) means one whose conduct is the opposite of what was described. "Cause" — meaning the cause of trustworthiness of speech. "Through attachment to good people" (<s>sajjanāsaktyā</s>) — meaning through the esteem of good people. "The effect" (<s>naimitttika</s>) — meaning the trustworthiness of speech. "The cognition of the cause itself" —

children.text:
iti chāyā /
vṛddhetyāditrayaṃ prastutamityasya viśeṣaṇama /
uddhurakandharīkarotīti /
pradhānīkarotītyarthaḥ /
tanmukhaprekṣamiti /
tathā ca apradhānamiti bhāvaḥ /
prāṇā iti /
locanam atra yadyapi sārūpyavaśena kṛtadhnaḥ kaścidanyaḥ prastuta ākṣipyate, tathāpyaprastutasyaiva vetālavṛttāntasya camatkārakāritvam /
na hyacetanopālambhavadasambhāvyamāno 'yamartho na ca na hṛdya iti vācyasyātra pradhānatā /
children.translated_text: For this meaning, like the reproach of an insentient being, is not entirely inconceivable, nor is it not delightful — hence the primacy of the expressed here.

children.text: yadi punaracetanādinātyantāsambhāvyamānatadarthaviśeṣaṇenāprastutena varṇitena prastutamākṣipyamāṇaṃ camatkārakāri tadā vastudhvanirasau /
children.translated_text: But if the irrelevant, described with qualifications of its meaning that are entirely inconceivable for an insentient being and the like, draws in the relevant and produces wonder, then this is <s>vastudhvani</s> (suggestion of a matter of fact).

children.text: yathā mamaiva---- bhāvavrāta haṭhājjanasya hṛdayānyākramya yannartayan bhaṅgībhirvividhābhirātmahṛdayaṃ pracchādya saṃkrīḍase /
children.translated_text: As [in this verse] of my own — "O host of emotions (<s>bhāvavrāta</s>)! You who by force invade people's hearts and make them dance, who sport by concealing your own heart through manifold gestures —

children.text: sa tvāmāha jaḍaṃ tataḥ sahṛdayammanyatvaduḥśikṣito manye 'muṣya jaḍātmatā stutipadaṃ tvatsāmyasambhāvanāt //
children.translated_text: that person, poorly trained by the conceit of being a <s>sahṛdaya</s> (connoisseur), calls you 'dull' (<s>jaḍa</s>) — but I think that his being called 'dull' is actually a term of praise, because of the supposition of equality with you."

[Bālapriyā] Thus the <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit rendering). The three items beginning with "of elders" (<s>vṛddha</s>) are qualifications of "the relevant" (<s>prastuta</s>). "Holds its head high" (<s>uddhurakandharīkaroti</s>) — meaning "makes predominant." "Looks on through its face" (<s>tanmukhaprekṣa</s>) — and thus "is not predominant" is the sense. "The life-breaths" (<s>prāṇā</s>) — [Locana] Here, although through resemblance a certain ingrate is the relevant [meaning] being drawn in, nevertheless it is the irrelevant story of the <s>Vetāla</s> itself that produces wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>).

children.translated_text: the connection is: "I think it is a term of praise for him."
The connection of "by whom" (<s>yena</s>) is with "concealing" (<s>pracchādayan</s>) and so forth.
As it has been said — "To one who has known the truth, this world is like the dull, the mad, and the possessed;
and the knower of truth too [appears] to the world like the dull, the mad, and the possessed."

[Bālapriyā] A certain great person (<s>mahāpuruṣa</s>), though free from passion, acting as if passionate — by this principle — though the darkness has been dispelled by the light of his deep discrimination, yet concealing himself in the midst of the world, making the world talkative while himself acknowledging only non-manifestation — when that very world dismisses him as "this one is a fool," then his extraordinary conduct is the relevant [meaning]. There are also the readings "you were produced" (<s>tvamutpādita</s>) and "worship formerly" (<s>saparyāṃ pura</s>). "Through resemblance" — meaning by the force of resemblance in the form of the ingrate's nature toward one who offered life-breaths and so forth. "Of the irrelevant itself" — the remainder is "of the expressed." Here he states the reason — "for" (<s>na hi</s>) and so on. "Nor is it not delightful" — meaning it is indeed delightful. "But if" (<s>yadi</s>) and so on — the construction is: "drawn in by an insentient being and the like." The qualifications of "of the insentient and the like" are "entirely" and so forth — the qualifications of the meaning of the irrelevant that are entirely inconceivable — where [described] by such [qualifications]. "This is <s>vastudhvani</s>" — the sense is: this is not the figure <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>. "Emotion" (<s>bhāva</s>) — "host" (<s>vrāta</s>) means group, of entities such as moonrise, gardens, etc.; O host of emotions! The connection is: you sport in such a way that. "Therefore" (<s>tataḥ</s>) — because of sporting in this way. "Poorly trained by the conceit of being a connoisseur" — badly brought up through the pride "I am a <s>sahṛdaya</s>." "That" (<s>saḥ</s>) — that person. He calls you dull. But of this person who speaks thus, his being called dull — that being told "you are dull" — that, because of the supposition of equality with you, because of the appearance of resemblance to you,

children.translated_text: Here then is the summary: — [<s>Locana</s>:] For that [purpose], to give a response common to all [cases], he begins: 'here then is this' etc.
The purport is: how much [more] should be written for each word!

children.text: tatra vyājastutiryathā--- kiṃ vṛttāntaiḥ paragṛhagataiḥ kintu nāhaṃ samartha- stūṇīṃ sthātuṃ prakṛtimukharo dākṣiṇātyasvabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, <s>vyāja-stuti</s> (ironic praise) is exemplified: 'What use are the reports that have gone to other houses? But I am not able to remain silent — being garrulous by nature, of southern temperament —

children.text: gehe gehe vipaṇiṣu tathā catvare pānagoṣṭhyā- munmatteva bhramati bhavato vallabhā hanta kīrtiḥ //
children.translated_text: in every house, in the markets, likewise in the square, at the drinking-party — your beloved Fame wanders about like a madwoman, alas!'

'Profound' — that which is discrimination (<s>viveka</s>) itself, i.e., illumination (<s>āloka</s>) — by which the expanse of darkness, i.e., the mass of the darkness of delusion, is vanquished. /
'Making garrulous' — the meaning is: causing many utterances pregnant with self-deprecation. /
'In oneself' — in one's own self. /
'<s>Apratibhāsa</s>' — the understanding attributed by people [i.e., the failure of recognition]. /
Now, the connection: even then, when something irrelevant (<s>aprastuta</s>) but similar in form is being described, when it is not principally intended — it falls within <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) [not mere figure]. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] It is illuminated principally as the suggested. /
For the world disdains the state of nature (<s>bhāva</s>) — [such as] the arising of the moon over the garden, etc. — [thinking] 'this is inert.' But that very [nature], on the contrary, makes the mind of some lover tormented by longing and anxiety, and makes another overwhelmed by excessive joy — and thus, by sheer force, it makes the world dance at its pleasure through the causes of emotional transformation. /
And not even a hint of its heart is known — what kind it is. Rather, it is profoundly deep, supremely clever, completely free of pride, and exceptionally skillful in play. If it is called 'inert' by the world, then for that very reason — which is rather the ground for attributing cleverness — it is esteemed. And the self (<s>ātman</s>) [= the speaker], who for that very reason is conversely suspected of inertness, is for that very reason esteemed as a connoisseur (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). Therefore, if it is said to this world 'you are inert,' then the inertness of this kind of mass of natural states — i.e., of the unclever [world] — is well-known. Thus that [statement] is, on the contrary, a praise. /
It is suggested: 'This world is even worse than the inert.' /
Therefore he says: 'when, however' etc. /
'Otherwise, however' — /
Otherwise indeed, it is merely another figure, a particular figure — the suggested [meaning] has no primacy whatsoever. This is the purport. /
In the enumeration, the inclusion of '<s>yadā</s>' etc. was made; in [the compound] '<s>samāsokti</s>' etc., [which is] a <s>dvandva</s> — by that, the group of figures beginning with <s>vyāja-stuti</s> (ironic praise) is also conceived as potentially admitting a suggested dimension. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He shows the expressed meaning: '<s>jaḍo 'yam</s>' etc. up to '<s>stuti</s>' (praise). /
The connection is: 'is disdained thus.' /
'By the world' — the agent. /
'And that' — both the garden etc. and the natural state. /
'On the contrary' — not merely 'not inert,' but rather: 'even possessing a clever nature.' This is the meaning. /
'Of another' — the meaning is: of one who has met with the beloved. /
'By forcefully seizing' — the explanation thereof is: 'at its pleasure, through the causes of transformation.' /
'Of transformations' — through the instigation of eagerness, joy, etc. /
'Concealing its own heart' — the explanation thereof is: 'not [known]' etc. /
The elaboration of 'on the contrary' is: 'profoundly deep' etc. /
The connection of 'that' (<s>sa</s>) is here too. /
He explains the second half: 'that, if' etc. /
'That' — the mass of natural states endowed with the stated qualities. /
The construction of '<s>jaḍa iti</s>' is with '<s>sambhāvitaḥ</s>' (esteemed). /
The explanation of '<s>tataḥ</s>' is: 'for that very reason.' /
The meaning is: from [the reason] in the form of the stated kind of playful activity. /
The qualifier of 'from the reason' is: 'rather, on the ground of attributing cleverness' etc. /
The explanation of '<s>sahṛdaya</s>' etc. is: '<s>ātmā ca</s>' etc. /
'<s>Tat</s>' — the meaning is: 'then.' /
The connection is: 'that is the praise of this world.' /
The meaning is: what kind of praise is this? /
'From what [evidence]?' — to this he says: '<s>tat</s>' etc. /
'Then' — at the time of that utterance. /
'The inertness of this kind' etc. — the meaning is this: the statement addressed to people, attributing inertness, depends on the established inertness of one who is [actually] not inert. /
This being the case, because of the equal applicability [of the argument], since non-inertness is possible for the people too, the statement 'you are inert' directed at the people would culminate in actual praise. /
Having thus explained the expressed meaning of the irrelevant [description], he shows the ultimate suggested meaning: 'even worse than the inert' etc. /
'Therefore he says' — the meaning is: what was said [by the author] about the status of <s>dhvani</s> when the suggested meaning cognized through similarity has primacy — he says that. /
He shows that the particle '<s>eva</s>' is in displaced position: 'otherwise indeed' etc. /
The meaning stated by the word '<s>tu</s>' (however) is: 'otherwise, it is merely another figure.'
Here the suggested meaning, which has the form of a praise, embellishes the expressed alone by that.

children.text: yattūdāhṛtaṃ kenacit---- āsīnnātha pitāmahī tava mahī jātā tato 'nantaraṃ mātā samprati sāmburāśiraśanā jāyā kulodbhūtaye /
children.translated_text: But what was cited by someone: 'Your grandmother was the Earth, O lord; then, immediately after, your mother was born — she who now wears the ocean as her girdle — [she became your] wife, for the perpetuation of the lineage;

children.text: pūrṇe varṣaśate bhaviṣyati punaḥ saivānavadyā snuṣā yuktaṃ nāma samagranītividuṣāṃ kiṃ bhūpatīnāṃ kule //
children.translated_text: and when a full hundred years are completed, that same blameless one will again be your daughter-in-law. Is this indeed fitting in the families of kings who are learned in all statecraft?'
— this appears to us as crude (<s>grāmya</s>), because it causes the recollection of what is extremely indecent.

children.text: kā cānena stutiḥ kṛtā? tvaṃ vaṃśakrameṇa rājeti hi kiyadidam? ityevaṃprāyā vyājastutiḥ sahṛdagoṣṭhīṣu ninditetyupekṣyaiva /
children.translated_text: 'And what praise has been made by this? That you are a king by hereditary succession — how insignificant is this?' — such <s>vyāja-stuti</s> (ironic praise), censured in the assemblies of connoisseurs, should simply be disregarded.
That whose transformation, arising unimpeded, [is expressed] by a cause which
conveys that intention (<s>abhiprāya</s>) and its impediment — that is called <s>bhāva</s> (emotion-figure).

children.translated_text: Pertaining to a specific mental disposition (<s>citta-vṛtti-viśeṣa</s>), such as love (<s>anurāga</s>) etc. — produced [from it].
The explanation of '<s>apratibandha</s>' (unimpeded) is: 'certain' (<s>niyata</s>).
Where the suggested has no primacy, [and is] merely following the expressed —
<s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) and the like are there clearly instances of 'expressed-ornamented' (<s>vācyālaṅkṛtayaḥ</s>).

Thus. /
Here too, when the expressed has primacy, the figure-status as <s>bhāva-alaṅkāra</s> (emotion-figure) [obtains]. /
Of a specific mental disposition (<s>citta-vṛtti-viśeṣa</s>), a transformation such as speech-activity etc. that is related [to it and] unimpeded, i.e., certain — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Again' — /
'Being another figure' — lest there be a misunderstanding here, he clarifies: 'being a specific figure.' /
'This is the purport' — in the domain of irrelevant description (<s>aprastuta-varṇana</s>), where the expressed meaning — the irrelevant content — has the power to produce aesthetic wonder, and the relevant [content] is suggested as subordinate to it, there is the figure of <s>aprastuta-praśaṃsā</s> (indirect eulogy). But where the suggested relevant [content] has primacy, there it is <s>vastu-dhvani</s> alone, not a figure — this is the intent of the treatise-author. This is the meaning. /
'Having the form of praise' — the meaning is: the praising of the quality in the form of being of supreme renown — '<s>bhavataḥ kīrtiḥ</s>' (your Fame) pervades the universe. /
'There was' etc. — '<s>snuṣā</s>' means daughter-in-law. /
'Extremely indecent' — since even when grandmother-hood and motherhood are stated, the seed of indecent recollection sprouts; and by the description of [the Earth's] being wife and daughter-in-law, it is all the more manifested — with this intention, 'extremely indecent' is said. /
Having stated the defect in the expressed meaning, he states it in the suggested too: 'and what' etc. /
'How insignificant is this' — the purport is: because there is no perception of any special superiority over other kings. /
He presents the <s>bhāva-alaṅkāra</s> (emotion-figure) stated by <s>Rudraṭa</s>, [included] through the word '<s>prabhṛti</s>' (beginning with) in the earlier '<s>vyāja-stuti-prabhṛti</s>': '<s>yasya</s>' etc. /
The construction: 'The transformation of a [specific mental disposition], unimpeded, arising through a cause (<s>hetu</s>) which conveys that intention and its impediment — that is <s>bhāva</s> [as a figure].' /
With the intention that here too there is a twofold nature, he says: 'here too' etc. /
He explains the definitional statement: '<s>yasya</s>' etc.
Where the suggested [has] merely a flash [of cognition], or merely follows the expressed meaning —

children.text: na dhvaniryatra vā tasya prādhānyaṃ na pratīyate //
children.translated_text: [that is] not <s>dhvani</s>; or where its primacy is not perceived —

children.text: locanam prabhavaṃstaṃ cittavṛttiviśeṣarūpamabhiprāyaṃ yena hetunā gamayati sa heturyatheṣṭopabhogyatvādilakṣaṇo 'rtho bhāvālaṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] 'Arising' — the intention (<s>abhiprāya</s>) in the form of a specific mental disposition — the cause (<s>hetu</s>) by which [a transformation] conveys it — that cause, which is a meaning characterized by being enjoyable at will etc. — is the <s>bhāva-alaṅkāra</s> (emotion-figure).

children.text: yathā--- ekākinī yadabalā taruṇī tathāhamasmingṛhe gṛhapatiśca gato videśam /
children.translated_text: For example: 'I am alone, a young woman, without protector, in this house — and the master of the house has gone abroad.

children.text: kaṃ yācase tadiha vāsamiyaṃ varākī śvaśrūrmamāndhabadhirā nanu mūḍha pāntha //
children.translated_text: Whom do you beseech? Come, stay here then — this wretched mother-in-law of mine is blind and deaf — don't be foolish, O traveler!'

children.translated_text: 'Cognition of meaning' — cognition of the suggested meaning.
To avoid redundancy with '<s>vācyamātrānuyāyinaḥ</s>' (merely following the expressed), he explains: 'by the expressed' etc.

children.text: 'na pratīyata' tatparāveva śabdārthau yatra vyaṅgyaṃ prīta sthitau /
children.translated_text: 'Is not perceived' — where word and meaning are devoted solely to that [expressed] and the suggested stands arrested —

children.text: dhvaneḥ sa eva viṣayo mantavyaḥ saṅkarojjhitaḥ //
children.translated_text: that alone should be considered the domain of <s>dhvani</s>, free from confusion. ||

Here the suggested meaning, embellishing each individual word-meaning, is subordinate — hence the expressed is primary. /
But when the suggested has primacy, there is no figure-status whatsoever — this has been determined. Enough of prolixity. /
'Where' — in poetry. /
'Ornamented' — and the subordination to the expressed is precisely because of the ornament-status. /
'Merely a flash' — where in <s>upamā</s> (simile) etc. there is an indistinct cognition of [the suggested] meaning. /
'Following the expressed meaning' — the meaning is: following along with the expressed meaning, i.e., equal primacy, as in <s>aprastuta-praśaṃsā</s> (indirect eulogy). /
'Is not perceived' — clearly. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'By a cause' — the remainder is: 'by what is conveyed by the sentence.' /
In the reading '<s>yena pratibaddhena</s>' (by which, being connected), the meaning of '<s>pratibaddhena</s>' is as stated. /
'That cause' — the meaning is: the <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent), i.e., the activity etc., of someone's specific mental disposition — through the medium of the suggested cause — is the indicator of that specific mental disposition. That is the cause (<s>hetu</s>). /
With the intention of the forthcoming example, he shows that cause: 'enjoyable at will' etc. /
The meaning is: the heroine's inner thought etc. [conveyed by] 'I am to be enjoyed by you at will, there is no impediment whatsoever.' /
'Alone' — '<s>tathā</s>' in the sense of cumulation. /
'<s>Tat</s>' — the meaning is: 'since I am of this nature and the master of the house has gone — therefore.' /
'But surely you have your mother-in-law — beseech her!' — to this she says: 'this one' etc. /
'Here the suggested' — the meaning is: that which is suggested by each word such as 'alone' etc. — [namely] the absence of another lover, her own desirability to be enjoyed, etc. /
And by the sentence as a whole, her self-invitation, i.e., being enjoyable at will, is indicated. /
[Objection:] But this suggested meaning is primary here! — therefore he states in general: 'when the suggested has primacy' etc. /
The examples of '<s>tat-pratibandhaṃ ca gamayati</s>' etc. should be understood from <s>Rudraṭa</s>'s text. /
'<s>Vyaṅgyasya</s>' etc. — these three are ancillary verses. /
He explains the word '<s>yatra</s>' in '<s>yatrāprādhānyam</s>': 'in poetry.' /
The reason for non-primacy is: being merely a follower of the expressed; the reason for that is: being an embellisher of the expressed meaning; and that is shown by the word '<s>alaṅkṛti</s>' — he says: 'precisely because of ornament-status.' /
He explains '<s>vyaṅgyasya pratibhāmātre</s>' with example: 'where' etc. /
'<s>Mliṣṭā</s>' — indistinct.

children.translated_text: The final sounds (<s>śabda</s>) — having arrived at the auricle (<s>śrotra-śaṣkulī</s>) through a continuous stream — are heard; thus in the [grammatical] system, "sounds born of sounds" (<s>śabdajāḥ śabdāḥ</s>) are said to be "heard" (<s>śrūyamāṇāḥ</s>).

children.text: teṣāṃ ghaṇṭānuraṇanarūpatvaṃ tāvadasti; te ca dhvaniśabdenoktāḥ /
children.translated_text: These at least have the nature of reverberation (<s>anuraṇana</s>) of a bell; and they are designated by the word "<s>dhvani</s>."

children.text: yathāha bhagavān bhartṛhariḥ--- yaḥ saṃyogaviyogābhyāṃ karaṇairupajanyate /
children.translated_text: As the venerable <s>Bhartṛhari</s> said: "That which is produced by the conjunction and disjunction of the organs of articulation —"
"— that is the <s>sphoṭa</s>; the sounds born of sounds are called <s>dhvanis</s> by others."

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Therefore <s>dhvani</s> cannot be subsumed elsewhere. And for this further reason there is no subsumption: because <s>dhvani</s> has been declared to be the principal (<s>aṅgin</s>), a special kind of poetry. Its subsidiaries (<s>aṅga</s>) — <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures), <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), and <s>vṛttis</s> (styles) — will be demonstrated. And a part (<s>avayava</s>) that has become separate is not recognized as the whole (<s>avayavin</s>).

<s>Locana</s>: The primacy does not shine forth clearly; rather, it is forced through interpretation — and even so, it does not enter the heart. As in the commentaries by others on "<s>deā pasiaṇiātāsu</s>" [the previously cited <s>Prākrit</s> verse]. Therefore, in four types [of cases], there is no usage of "<s>dhvani</s>" — even when the suggested exists: [1] when the suggested is not primary, [2] when its cognition is strained (<s>mliṣṭa-pratīti</s>), [3] when it has equal primacy with the expressible, and [4] when its primacy is unclear (<s>asphuṭa</s>). Where then [does the usage apply]? He says — "only those focused on that" (<s>tatparau eva</s>) etc. "Abandoned" (<s>ujjhita</s>) means: abandoned through the suspicion of the intrusion of <s>alaṅkāras</s> due to mixture (<s>saṅkara</s>). [The reading] "by the <s>saṅkara-alaṅkāra</s>" is incorrect, for if it were taken as indicating other <s>alaṅkāras</s>, it would be strained.

"And for this [further reason]" (<s>itaś ca</s>): not only is there no identity of <s>alaṅkāras</s> and <s>dhvani</s> because they depend on mutually opposed relationships — expressible-signifier on the one hand and suggested-suggestive on the other — but also because of the opposition between the principal (<s>aṅgin</s>) form and the subsidiary (<s>aṅga</s>) form, as between a master and his servant. This is the meaning.

"Part" (<s>avayava</s>): meaning each individual one. Therefore he says "having become separate" (<s>pṛthag-bhūtaḥ</s>). Now, lest one object — "let the separately existing [part] not be [the whole], but let the one that has fallen within the aggregate be the whole" — anticipating this, he says "but in non-separateness" (<s>apṛthag-bhāve tu</s>) etc. The commentary on "even then it is not that" [in the <s>Bālapriyā</s>] is: "it does not shine forth clearly" (<s>sphuṭatayā na cakāsti</s>). "Is forced through interpretation" (<s>balāt kalpyate</s>): and that is an extraction during the stage of examination through reasoning. "Does not enter the heart" (<s>na anupraviśati</s>): because it dissolves when the investigation of reasoning is absent. This is the purport. He gives an example — "as" (<s>yathā</s>) etc. "<s>Deā</s>" etc.: the <s>gāthā</s> (verse) previously cited as "I entreat you, be gracious" etc. The elaboration of "there is no <s>dhvani</s>" is: "there is no usage of <s>dhvani</s>." "Even when it exists" (<s>sadbhāve api</s>): "of <s>dhvani</s>" is the remainder.

The elaboration of "in four types" is: "when the suggested is not primary" etc. The commentary on "<s>saṅkara</s>" (mixture) is: "intrusion of <s>alaṅkāras</s>" etc. — meaning through the previously mentioned suspicion of the intrusion of <s>samāsokti</s> etc. He rejects the literal meaning — "by the <s>saṅkara-alaṅkāra</s>" etc. In the <s>vṛtti</s>, "and for this [reason]" (<s>itaś ca</s>) — keeping in mind that "<s>itaḥ</s>" means "from the reason about to be stated," he explains: "not only" (<s>na kevalam</s>) etc. "No identity" (<s>na tādātmyam</s>): meaning absence of oneness. "Principal" (<s>aṅgī</s>) etc.: meaning of the principal-ness and subsidiary-ness [respectively].

Now, since the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) beyond the parts is not apprehended, the denial that "a part is not the whole" is unjustified — showing that the singular is intended, he resolves: "each individual" (<s>ekaika</s>) etc. "Therefore he says" (<s>tad āha</s>) — this merely restates what was said — "having become separate" etc. "Now [if] the separately existing" — "part" (<s>avayava</s>) is the remainder. "Thus" — [let it be] the whole. "Having fallen within the aggregate" — having assumed the form of the aggregate. "Let it be the whole, then."

In the <s>vṛtti</s>: "its subsidiary status" — meaning the status of being the suggested of the whole. "But in non-separateness, its subsidiary status" — but not its identity. "And even where there is identity, because <s>dhvani</s> has a vast domain, it does not rest solely on that [<s>alaṅkāra</s>]." "Declared by the learned" (<s>sūribhiḥ kathitaḥ</s>): an expression that requires cognoscenti to understand — it is established that [this usage] is not arbitrarily applied. For the first among the learned are the grammarians, since grammar is the foundation of all sciences.

<s>Locana</s>: There is only one aggregate; for other constituents too exist within it. And among those constituents, the suggested (<s>pratīyamāna</s>) too exists, and it does not have the form of <s>alaṅkāra</s> — precisely because of its primacy. But that which has the form of <s>alaṅkāra</s> is not <s>dhvani</s>, because of its non-primacy. Therefore he says: "but not its identity." Now, lest one object — "you have merely anointed some particular <s>alaṅkāra</s> with the coronation of primacy and called it <s>dhvani</s>, the soul" — anticipating this, he says: "and even where" (<s>yatrāpi vā</s>) etc. For we have not made it to be any one among <s>samāsokti</s> and other [figures]; even in its distinction from that, because of its existence [independently]; because even when the essential nature of all <s>alaṅkāras</s> like <s>samāsokti</s> etc. is absent, it has been shown — as in "<s>attā ettha</s>" and "<s>kassa vā ṇa</s>" etc. Therefore he says: "it does not rest solely on that."

"Cognoscenti-originated" (<s>vidvad-upajña</s>): a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound — "an expression whose first origin (<s>upajñā</s>) or first commencement is from the learned." Therefore, the neuter gender based on the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> "<s>upajñā-upakramam</s>" [is also possible]. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "Of that" (<s>tasya</s>): of the part. "Identity" (<s>tattvam</s>): meaning the status of being the whole. He states the purport in the <s>Locana</s> — "even then" (<s>tadāpi</s>) etc. "Even then" — even in the stage of falling within the aggregate. "That" (<s>saḥ</s>) — the part in the form of the aggregate-[constituent]. "Is only one" — is not the [entire] aggregate, not the whole in the form of the aggregate. Here he states the reason — "of others too" etc. "Because of existing there" — meaning because of being present in the aggregate.

children.translated_text: "By impressions" (<s>pratyayaiḥ</s>) —
"Indescribable" (<s>anupākhyeyaiḥ</s>): that cannot be explained as "this is thus."
"Conducive to apprehension" (<s>grahaṇānuguṇaiḥ</s>): favorable to the apprehension of the <s>sphoṭa</s> in its manifest form.
<s>Locana</s>: In the word illuminated by <s>dhvani</s>, the essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) is ascertained. //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Thus. In this way, the suggested meaning too — characterized by reverberation (<s>anuraṇana</s>), corresponding to the pleasant ring of a bell etc. — is designated by the term "<s>dhvani</s>." Similarly, the heard phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) — denoted by the word "<s>nāda</s>," which are the manifestors of the <s>sphoṭa</s> grasped by the final cognition — are designated by the word "<s>dhvani</s>." As that same venerable [<s>Bhartṛhari</s>] said: "Through impressions (<s>pratyaya</s>) that are indescribable, conducive to apprehension..." [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Now, intending to establish that the four — suggested meaning, word, [expressible] meaning, and the suggestive function — are all denoted by the word "<s>dhvani</s>" by the authority of scholarly convention, he first explains [the denotability of] the suggested meaning in a manner conducive to establishing its denotation by the word "<s>dhvani</s>" — "the auricle" (<s>śrotra</s>) etc. "The auricle" (<s>śrotra-śaṣkulī</s>): the space delimited by the ear-region resembling the auricle. "Through a continuous stream" (<s>santānena</s>): meaning by the wave-succession principle (<s>vīcī-santāna-nyāya</s>). "In the system" (<s>prakriyāyām</s>): meaning in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and other systems. "Sounds born of sounds" (<s>śabdajāḥ śabdāḥ</s>): the purport is "the final [sounds]." "Of these" (<s>teṣām</s>): of the heard, final sounds born of [previous] sounds. "Bell" (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>): the purport is the similarity in being produced by prior sounds. "That which" (<s>yaḥ</s>): this verse is for making manifest the distinction between <s>sphoṭa</s> and <s>dhvani</s> in the origination theory. "By conjunction and disjunction" (<s>saṃyoga-viyogābhyām</s>): by the conjunction with and disjunction from the articulatory points of the organs. "By the organs" (<s>karaṇaiḥ</s>): the instrumental has agentive sense; meaning by the tongue-tip etc. This is clear in the <s>Prātiśākhya</s>. "That is the <s>sphoṭa</s>" — meaning the first-produced sound is called <s>sphoṭa</s>. "Sounds born of sounds" — the purport is "the heard [ones]." "By others" (<s>anyaiḥ</s>): meaning by the proponents of the origination theory. As stated by the <s>vṛtti</s> author: "In the impermanence view, the sound that is first produced through the contact with articulatory points and organs is called <s>sphoṭa</s>" etc.

"Bell etc." (<s>ghaṇṭādi</s>): the pleasant ring (<s>nirhnāda</s>) of a bell etc. is the reverberation (<s>anuraṇana</s>); corresponding to that, resembling that — this is the reason for the designation of the suggested by the word "<s>dhvani</s>." Now, if only a specific type of suggested meaning is designated by "<s>dhvani</s>," and not <s>rasa</s> etc. — since <s>rasa</s> lacks the nature of reverberation — to that he says "reverberation" (<s>anuraṇana</s>) etc. The purport is: this is merely indicative (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). Now, establishing that the signifier (<s>vācaka</s>) word and the signified (<s>vācya</s>) meaning are also designatable by "<s>dhvani</s>" — "similarly" (<s>tathā</s>) etc. "Denoted by the word <s>nāda</s>" — meaning: designated by grammarians with the word "<s>nāda</s>." "Final" (<s>antya</s>): apprehended by the final cognition of phonemes, which is produced with the cooperation of the impressions generated by the experience of each preceding phoneme; "grasped" (<s>nirgrāhya</s>): i.e., apprehended with fully manifest form; that which manifests the <s>sphoṭa</s>. "These" (<s>te</s>): meaning those phonemes.
Therefore, the suggestive word and meaning too are here designated by the word "<s>dhvani</s>."
Moreover, even when the phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) exist in only their basic measure (<s>tāvan-mātra-parimāṇa</s>) —
As stated: "Even with the slightest effort, when a word is uttered, the intellect —"

children.text: yadi vā naiva gṛhṇāti varṇaṃ vā sakalaṃ sphuṭam //
children.translated_text: "— either does not grasp [it] at all, or [grasps] the phoneme completely and distinctly."
Thus.
Thus.

children.text: teṣu tāvatsveva śrūyamāṇeṣu vakturyo 'nyo drutāvilambitādivṛttibhedātmā prasiddāduccāraṇavyāpārādabhyadhikaḥ sa dhvaniruktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when those very [phonemes] are being heard, the speaker's [particular quality] that is something additional beyond the well-known act of pronunciation — consisting of the distinctions of style (<s>vṛtti</s>) such as rapid, slow, etc. — that is called <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: yadāha sa eva--- śabdasyordhvamabhivyaktervṛttibhede tu vaikṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: As that same [<s>Bhartṛhari</s>] said: "After the manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) of the word, in the difference of style (<s>vṛtti-bheda</s>), the modified [sounds] —"
"— the <s>dhvanis</s> accumulate; the <s>sphoṭa</s>-nature is not differentiated by them."

children.translated_text: 'Its own self' (<s>svātmā</s>) —
is said [to be] twofold in general.
Of the first, the example is: 'Three [kinds of] men gather the golden-blossomed earth:
the heroic, the learned, and he who knows how to serve.'

Thus. /
It has been stated that <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) is an operation distinct from the well-known word-operations — even those that are dissimilar — i.e., distinct from the operations in the form of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation), <s>tātparya</s> (purport), and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication). /
Thus the fourfold [entity] too is <s>dhvani</s>. /
And by virtue of its connection with that, the entire body of poetry too [is <s>dhvani</s>]. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'In the word that is illuminated by <s>dhvani</s>' — in the object [i.e., <s>sphoṭa</s>]; by the cognitions that arise as intermediaries — i.e., by the indistinct cognitions pertaining to <s>sphoṭa</s>. /
'The own form' — the form of <s>sphoṭa</s> — 'is ascertained,' i.e., clearly known. /
As stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [of <s>Patañjali</s>]: 'For the many cognitions — of indescribable form, conforming to the grasping of the manifest form, serving as means — which arise when the word (<s>śabda</s>) is being illuminated by the sound-elements (<s>dhvani</s>), become the causes of grasping the word's own form.' /
'By that' — the meaning is: because the suggestors (<s>vyañjaka</s>) are designated by the word '<s>dhvani</s>,' having been used [thus] by them [the grammarians]. /
Hence, to establish that the operation of suggestion (<s>vyañjanā</s>) too is designatable by the word '<s>dhvani</s>,' he says: 'moreover' etc. /
'Of just that measure' — the meaning is: possessing the specific measure by which they are grasped by the auditory sense-faculty. /
The word '<s>api</s>' is in the sense of cumulation; its connection is with 'being heard.' /
'In the phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>), which exist in their own form as possessing specific measure, and which in that very form have entered the domain of the auditory sense-faculty in an undivided manner' — this is the meaning. /
The connection of this [passage], which contains a corroborating verse, is with the passage beginning 'that which is other than the speaker's [intention]' etc. /
'By the slightest' — a word uttered even with the slightest effort. /
'The intellect does not grasp [only] a portion.' /
Alternatively: it grasps the entire phoneme clearly; but partial grasping and non-grasping are not possible, because the phoneme is partless. This is the purport. /
By this, the statement 'when being heard in just that measure' has been substantiated. /
'That' — the meaning is: such a type of operation. /
'Of the word (<s>śabda</s>)' — this verse is explained thus in the <s>Mañjūṣā</s>: the remainder is: 'after the manifestation of the word, i.e., <s>sphoṭa</s>, modified <s>dhvanis</s> (sounds) arise.' /
'Those, however, in the difference of delivery (<s>vṛtti</s>)' — in the difference of delivery such as rapid etc. /
'Contribute' — they become a cause therein. /
'But the <s>sphoṭa</s> is not differentiated by them.' This is the meaning. /
And the modified nature of these [sounds] is because of being produced by laziness etc. /
In the reading '<s>vṛtti-bhedam</s>,' the meaning of '<s>samupohante</s>' is: 'they generate.' /
'The fourfold' — the meaning is: the tetrad [consisting of] the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) etc. /
'<s>Dhvani</s>' — designatable by the word <s>dhvani</s>. /
'The entire body of poetry too' — poetry too, which consists of the aggregate of the suggested, the expressed, the expressive, and the operation. /
'By that' — since poetry whose soul is word [and meaning] is called '<s>dhvani</s>' because of the commonality of the suggestive function — thus it has been said. /
And the illumination of such a <s>dhvani</s> — which has a vast domain through the compilation of the forthcoming varieties and their sub-varieties — is not [accomplished] by the mere presentation of some unfamiliar particular figure (<s>alaṅkāra</s>). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] <s>Dhvani</s>. /
Hence the designation as both distinct and non-distinct [from poetry] is also not inappropriate — 'mixed with the expressed and the expressive.' /
'Mixed with the expressed and the expressive' — combined with the expressed and the expressive. This is a compound with middle-term elision (<s>madhyamapadalopī samāsa</s>). /
'Like <s>gām evaṃ puruṣaṃ paśum</s>' — the cumulation here is even without the particle '<s>ca</s>.' /
Hence: the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) too is <s>dhvani</s>, the expressive word (<s>vācaka</s>) too is <s>dhvani</s> — because both suggest (<s>dhvanati</s>), i.e., by the reason that both have the suggestive function. /
'Is mixed' — through the intermingling of <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> — hence the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) too is <s>dhvani</s>, because it is suggested (<s>dhvanyate</s>). /
'Wording' (<s>śabdana</s>) is word (<s>śabda</s>), i.e., the word-operation — and that is not in the form of <s>abhidhā</s> etc., but rather is essential (<s>ātmabhūta</s>) — that too is <s>dhvanana</s> (suggesting), hence <s>dhvani</s>. /
And the meaning that is designated as 'poetry' — that too is <s>dhvani</s>, because it consists of the stated fourfold <s>dhvani</s>. /
Hence he states the common reason: 'because of the commonality of suggestiveness' — /
The relation of suggested and suggestor is common, i.e., the same, in all the cases. This is the meaning. /
Now, as for what was said — 'because of the infinity of verbal constructs' etc. — he resolves that: 'of such a [<s>dhvani</s>]' etc. /
The forthcoming varieties — for example, the two main forms. /
Their sub-varieties — for example: '<s>arthāntara-saṃkramita-vācya</s>' (expressed meaning transferred to another meaning) and '<s>atyanta-tiraskṛta-vācya</s>' (expressed meaning completely concealed) for <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> (unintended expressed); '<s>asaṃlakṣya-krama-vyaṅgya</s>' (suggested with imperceptible sequence) and '<s>saṃlakṣya-krama-vyaṅgya</s>' (suggested with perceptible sequence) for <s>vivakṣitānyapara-vācya</s> (where another meaning beyond the expressed is intended). /
And within those too there are sub-sub-varieties. /
'Of vast domain' — the meaning is: pervading all instances of literary [expression]. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The meaning is: because of the reason that poetry attains the status of <s>dhvani</s> by virtue of being constituted by the aggregate of the entities designated by the word <s>dhvani</s>. /
'Distinct and non-distinct' etc. — the meaning is: the designation of distinction [is seen] in '<s>kāvyasyātmā dhvaniḥ</s>' ('<s>dhvani</s> is the soul of poetry') and '<s>kāvya-viśeṣaḥ sa dhvaniḥ</s>' ('that <s>dhvani</s> is a particular kind of poetry'), and the designation of non-distinction [is also made]. /
'Not inappropriate' — the meaning is: is indeed appropriate. /
To explain the word '<s>vācya-vācaka</s>' etc. in accordance with the stated fivefold designability by '<s>dhvani</s>,' he explains: 'expressed and expressive' etc. /
'A compound with middle-term elision' — thus the meaning is: 'the expressed and the mixed.' This is the purport. /
'Even without [<s>ca</s>]' — thus the meaning is: 'and the one designated as poetry whose soul is word.' This is the purport. /
He states the result of the stated explanation: 'hence' etc. /
'Because it suggests' — the meaning is: the reason being 'it causes to manifest.' /
'<s>Dhvani</s>' — the suffix is in the agentive sense (<s>kartari pratyaya</s>). This is the purport. /
He says that by the word '<s>saṃmiśra</s>' (mixed), the suggested meaning is intended: 'is mixed' etc. /
'<s>Vibhāva</s>' etc. — the meaning is: through the connection of <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> in intermingling. /
'Because it is suggested' — the suffix is in the objective sense (<s>karmaṇi pratyaya</s>). This is the purport. /
He explains the word '<s>śabdātmā</s>': '<s>śabdana</s>' etc. /
'Suggesting (<s>dhvanana</s>) is <s>dhvani</s>' — here the suffix is in the abstract sense (<s>bhāve pratyaya</s>). This is the purport. /
'For this very reason' — because the <s>dhvani</s>-status of the five secondary referents is what is intended to be expressed in this treatise, therefore a common reason is stated. This is the meaning. /
To gain commonality for the reason, with the intention that the word '<s>vyañjakatva</s>' (suggestiveness) refers to the relation of suggested and suggestor, he explains: '<s>vyaṅgya</s>' etc. /
'Equal' — the agitation of those whose minds have been imbued with that [<s>dhvani</s>] is indeed appropriate. /
And toward them, one should not at all display an attitude soiled by jealousy. /
Thus, to this extent, the deniers of <s>dhvani</s>'s existence have been answered. <s>Dhvani</s> exists. /
And it is of two kinds: <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> (unintended expressed) and <s>vivakṣitānyapara-vācya</s> (where another meaning beyond the intended expressed is primary). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] By the word '<s>viśeṣa</s>' (particular), he states the non-pervasiveness [of <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status]. /
By the word '<s>mātra</s>' (mere), the absence of principal status (<s>aṅgitva</s>). /
Therein: those whose minds are cultivated, i.e., directed, toward the nature of <s>dhvani</s>; or: whose minds are imbued, i.e., pervaded, with that — in the form of aesthetic wonder — and hence are the cause of [bodily] transformations such as half-closing the eyes etc. /
'The deniers of existence' — though divided into three sub-types. This is the meaning. /
He states the result of their refutation: 'it exists' etc. /
With the intent that when examples are presented, the figurative view (<s>bhāktatva</s>) is easily doubted and also easily resolved — for the purpose of providing occasion for examples, even though the figurative view — [which is] the first to be eligible for resolution — has not been resolved first, the author of the <s>vṛtti</s> himself, following the structure of the forthcoming <s>Uddyotas</s>, undertakes the determination of the varieties: 'and it' etc. /
For all five referents of the word '<s>dhvani</s>,' the co-referential usage such as '<s>avivakṣita-vācyo dhvaniḥ</s>' is to be appropriately constructed through the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> meanings — '<s>yena</s>' (by which), '<s>yatra</s>' (in which), '<s>yataḥ</s>' (from which), '<s>yasmai</s>' (for which purpose), '<s>yasya</s>' (of which [relation]). /
In the case where the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) is the referent of <s>dhvani</s>, he states the specific point: 'in the expressed meaning' etc.

children.text:
locana.m yadi vā karmadhārayeṇārthapakṣe avivakṣitaścāsau vācyaśceti /
vivakṣitānyaparaścāsau vācyaśceti /
tatrārthaḥ kadācidanupapadyamānatvādinā nimittenāvivakṣito bhavati /
kadācidupapadyamāna iti kṛtvā vivakṣita eva, vyaṅgyaparyantāṃ tu pratītiṃ svasaubhāgyamahimnā karoti /
ata evārtho 'tra prādhānyena vyañjakaḥ, pūrvatra śabdaḥ /
nanu ca vivakṣā cānyaparatvaṃ ceti viruddham /
anyaparatvenaiva vivakṣaṇātko virodhaḥ? sāmānyeneti /
vastvalaṅkārarasātmanā hi tribhedo 'pi dhvanirubhābhyāmevābhyāṃ saṅgṛhīta iti bhāvaḥ /
nanu tannāmapṛṣṭe etannāmaniveśanasya kiṃ phalam? ucyate--
anena hi nāmadvayena dhvananātmani vyāpāre pūrvaprasiddhābhidhātātparyalakṣaṇātmakavyāpāratritayāvagatārthapratīteḥ pratipattṛgatāyāḥ prayoktrabhiprāyarūpāyāśca vivikṣāyā) sahakāritvamuktamiti dhvanisvarūpameva nāmabhyāmeva projjīvitam /
suvarmapuṣpāmiti /
suvarṇāni puṣpyatīti suvarṇapuṣpā, etacca vākyamevāsambhavatsvārthamiti kṛtvāvivakṣitavācyam /
bālapriyā śeṣaḥ /
avivakṣitapadasya yathāśrutārthābhiprāyeṇāha-yadi vetyādi /
vācyasyāvivakṣitatvādikamupapādayati---tatrārtha ityādi /
ādipadenānupayogitvaṃ gṛhyate /
upapadyamāna iti /
artha ityanuṣajyate /
vyaṅgyaparyantāṃ vyaṅgyapratītiparyantām /
pratītiṃsvagocarāṃ pratītim /
śaṅkate---nanvita /
viruddhamiti. vivakṣitatve anyaparatvasambhavāditi bhāvaḥ /
uttaramāha---anyetyādi /
ko virodha iti /
pradhānatayā vivakṣitatvasyaivānyaparatvopamardakatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
pṛcchati--nanviti /
tannāmapṛṣṭe tasya dhvanināmnaḥ pṛṣṭe paścāt /
etannāmeti /
avivakṣitavācyādināmetyarthaḥ /
asti dhvaniḥ sa cetyādiśca nirdeśaḥ kimartha ityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: To this he replies — "it is said" (<s>ucyate</s>) etc.
This is the meaning: the connection with the operation of suggestion (<s>dhvanana-vyāpāra</s>) is indeed the basis for the denotability of the five [entities] by the word "<s>dhvani</s>."

children.text: tatra ca vyāpāre dvitīyasyāpi--- śikhariṇi kva nu nāma kiyacciraṃ kimabhidhānamasāvakarottapaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in that [suggestive] operation, [here is an example] of the second [type, i.e., <s>vivakṣitānya-para-vācya</s>] too: "On which mountain peak, pray, for how long, and by what name, did he perform austerities —"

children.text: taruṇi yena tavādharapāṭalaṃ daśati bimbaphalaṃ śukaśāvakaḥ //
children.translated_text: "O young woman, by which [merit] a baby parrot bites the <s>bimba</s> fruit that is [like] the coral-redness of your lip!"

<s>Locana</s>: Or, by a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound, in the meaning-alternative: "that is unintended (<s>avivakṣita</s>) and it is the expressible (<s>vācya</s>)" [= <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s>]; and "that is intended-with-another-as-primary (<s>vivakṣitānya-para</s>) and it is the expressible" [= <s>vivakṣitānya-para-vācya</s>]. There, the meaning (<s>artha</s>) sometimes becomes unintended through a reason such as impossibility. Sometimes, being taken as possible, it is indeed intended, but by the majesty of its own excellence, it produces a cognition extending to the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). Therefore, meaning is here primarily the suggestor, whereas previously [in the first type], word [was the suggestor].

Now, "intention" (<s>vivakṣā</s>) and "having another as primary" (<s>anyaparatva</s>) are contradictory! What contradiction, since the intending is precisely as having another as primary? "In general" (<s>sāmānyena</s>): the purport is that <s>dhvani</s>, even though threefold as factual (<s>vastu</s>), figurative (<s>alaṅkāra</s>), and <s>rasa</s>-natured, is comprehended by these two [types] alone.

Now, after the name [<s>dhvani</s>] has been stated, what purpose is served by introducing these [sub-]names? It is replied — by these two names, the cooperative role of the recipient's cognition — produced through the three previously known operations of denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>), purport (<s>tātparya</s>), and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — and of the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>) in the operation whose nature is suggestion (<s>dhvanana</s>) has been stated; thus the very essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> has been vivified by these names alone.

"<s>Suvarṇapuṣpā</s>" (she who blossoms with gold): "she blossoms with gold" (<s>suvarṇāni puṣpyati</s>) — and this sentence, since its literal meaning is impossible, is [an instance of] <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s>.

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The remainder. He states the meaning of the word "<s>avivakṣita</s>" with the intention of the as-heard meaning — "or" (<s>yadi vā</s>) etc. He substantiates the unintendedness etc. of the expressible — "there, the meaning" (<s>tatra arthaḥ</s>) etc. By the word "etc." (<s>ādi</s>), inapplicability is also included. "Being possible" (<s>upapadyamāna</s>): "meaning" (<s>artha</s>) carries over. "Extending to the suggested" (<s>vyaṅgya-paryantām</s>): extending to the cognition of the suggested. "Cognition" (<s>pratītim</s>): cognition within its own domain. He objects — "now" (<s>nanu</s>) etc. "Contradictory" (<s>viruddham</s>): because in [the state of] being intended, being-other-directed is impossible. This is the purport. He replies — "by other" (<s>anya</s>) etc. "What contradiction?" — because intention as primary itself overrides being-other-directed. This is the purport. He asks — "now" (<s>nanu</s>) etc. "After that name has been stated" (<s>tannāma-pṛṣṭe</s>): after the name "<s>dhvani</s>" [has been introduced]. "This name" (<s>etannāma</s>): meaning the names "<s>avivakṣita-vācya</s>" etc. The meaning is: what purpose does the designation "there exists <s>dhvani</s>, and it is [of such types]" etc. serve?

children.translated_text: It has been stated that the cognition of the suggested arises from the beauty of the sentence-meaning itself; merely to a slight extent (<s>leśena</s>) is there also the utility of the operation of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>.
But in [the type called] <s>asaṃlakṣyakrama-vyaṅgya</s> (suggestion whose sequence is imperceptible), there is not even the slightest glimmer of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>.
Because the sequence itself is imperceptible — this we shall explain [later].

children.text: tena dvitīye 'pi bhede catvāra eva vyāpārāḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in the second division [<s>vivakṣitānya-para-vācya</s>], there are only four operations. // 13 //

<s>Locana</s>: Therefore, having denoted the word-meanings and having comprehended the syntactic connection through the <s>tātparya</s> power itself, under the force of a sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka</s>), [the mind] sets aside that [literal connection] and, through similarity (<s>sādṛśya</s>), apprehends through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> the state of being the recipient of easily obtained abundant riches. The purpose of that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — the excellence [of the woman], concealed as something not denotable by words, like the pair of pitcher-breasts of the heroine — reaches great value through suggestion. Here the word is primarily the suggestor; meaning cooperates with it — thus there are four operations.

"<s>Śikhariṇī</s>" (on a mountain peak): for even the most eminent perfected places such as <s>Śrīparvata</s> etc. would not grant this perfection without obstacles. And a limited time such as a thousand divine <s>kalpas</s> etc. is [mentioned] here. And no austerity performed at even the foremost [sacred sites] has been heard of as producing such supreme fruit.

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The cooperative role of both the recipient's cognition of meaning — produced by the three [operations] of denotation etc. performed by both word and meaning — and the speaker's intention exists; therefore, to demonstrate that too, this pair of names was devised, not merely to demonstrate the sub-divisions. There, since <s>avivakṣita-vācya dhvani</s> is rooted in <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, by that name the cooperation of the recipient's cognition is shown; by the name <s>vivakṣitānya-para-vācya</s>, the cooperation of intention is shown — thus the very essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> has been vivified by these names.

"Under the force of sublation, setting aside that [literal meaning]" — meaning that syntactic connection. "Setting aside" (<s>upahanana</s>) means sublation. "Through similarity" (<s>sādṛśyāt</s>): this is the statement of the ground [for <s>lakṣaṇā</s>]. "Apprehends through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>" — meaning: conveys "<s>suvarṇa-puṣpām</s>" through secondary signification. The connection is: "the purpose of that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — the excellence — is suggested." "Great value" (<s>māhārghatā</s>): beauty. "Reaches" (<s>upayat</s>): attains.

"Here" (<s>atra</s>): meaning in the <s>avivakṣita-vācya dhvani</s>. "Four" (<s>catvāraḥ</s>): meaning four [operations] beginning with denotation. The commentary on the "<s>suvarṇa</s>" verse should be seen in our commentary on the <s>Kuvalayānanda</s>.

"<s>Śikhariṇī</s>" (mountain peak): here he states the suggested meaning of "<s>nāma</s>" (pray), "<s>kiyaccchiram</s>" (for how long), and "<s>kim abhidhānam</s>" (by what name) in sequence — beginning with "<s>na hi</s>" etc. "This" (<s>imām</s>): meaning the perfection of the nature of having a baby parrot bite the <s>bimba</s>-fruit-like lip of the young woman. "Here" (<s>atra</s>): meaning in the attainment of such a perfection. "Of such a kind" (<s>evaṃvidha</s>): meaning of the nature of the <s>bimba</s>-fruit biting as described.

Without indicating [the addressee] as "your lip" through [the formula] "the coral of your lip, O lotus-eyed one," he states the reason for the indication through "your lip" etc. — "<s>tava</s>" etc. "Separate" (<s>bhinnam</s>): distinct. <s>Locana</s>: "<s>tava</s>" (your) is a separate word. Through a compound, [that meaning] would be apprehended as dissolved [into the compound]; with the intention of "your — he bites," [it is kept separate]. Therefore what they say — "it was not made '<s>tvadadhara-pāṭalam</s>' due to metrical constraints" — that is quite wrong. "He bites" (<s>daśati</s>) means he savors — with unbroken continuity, not consuming everything like a glutton; rather, as a connoisseur of <s>rasa</s>, his attainment of that [fruit] is itself like the connoisseurship of <s>rasa</s>; and even the timely acquisition of the <s>bimba</s>-fruit and its savoring is of austerity alone.

And the suggested meaning is: the stimulation (<s>uddīpana</s>) of the <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) — i.e., the characteristic of the young woman who is the object of love (<s>ratyālambana</s>) — consisting of a flattering composition (<s>cāṭu-viracana</s>) made with skill (<s>vaidagdhya</s>) and without abandoning propriety (<s>aucitya</s>), for the purpose of making known the hidden personal intention whose nature is the desire to taste the lip.

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "Performed" (<s>kṛtam</s>). "How so?" — to that he says "in a compound" (<s>samāsa</s>) etc. "Through being dissolved [in the compound], it would [or would not] be perceived" — thus is the reading in some manuscripts. "In a compound" — when the second-person word is compounded with the word "lip." "The meaning of 'your'" is the remainder. "Through dissolution" (<s>vigalitatayā</s>): through separateness — it would not be perceived. This is the meaning. Now, for primary perception, expression in separated form is necessary — this is what follows. For what purpose? To that he says "<s>tava</s>" etc. The meaning is: with the intention that "your" has syntactic connection with the act of biting too. The connection is with "separate" (<s>bhinnam</s>).

The purport is this: just as in the Vedic sentence "by the red-brown [cow], O tawny-eyed one" etc., the redness etc. connected with the cow [is syntactically connected] with the purchase through the relation of being-to-be-accomplished; or just as in the worldly sentence "the wealthy one is happy" etc., the wealth connected with the possessive suffix is syntactically connected with happiness through the relation of being-an-instrument — so here too, "yours" connected with the lip is syntactically connected even with the biting of the <s>bimba</s>-fruit through the relation of being-an-instrument. Because this baby parrot bites the <s>bimba</s>-fruit, rendered beautiful by its acquisition of your lip's redness, precisely as connected with you — the meaning intended is: "he bites precisely targeting you primarily." Therefore "<s>tava</s>" was expressed in separated form.

"With unbroken" etc.: the connection is with "he savors" (<s>āsvādayati</s>). If there were complete consumption, there would be severance of the continuity — but it is not so. This is the meaning. "Like a glutton" (<s>audārika-vat</s>): for he, being ignorant of the art of <s>rasa</s>-savoring, consumes the food-substance entirely. "Here" (<s>atra</s>): meaning in the act of <s>rasa</s>-savoring. "Like the attainment of that" — like the attainment of such a <s>bimba</s>-fruit. "Timely" — the acquisition at the proper time of the <s>bimba</s>-fruit and its savoring is of austerity alone. And the connection of "<s>iti</s>" too is: "this too is the suggested meaning."

"Hidden" (<s>pracchanna</s>): <s>Locana</s>: And here there are only three operations — denotation, purport, and suggestion — because of the absence of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, the third [operation], in this middle level, since the sublation of primary meaning etc. is absent. Or, if because of the impossibility of the meaning of a suddenly specific question, there is sublation of primary meaning and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> through similarity in between — let the purpose of that [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] be precisely what is suggested; that occupies the fourth level. Only in the former case, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> alone is primary, being a cooperant in the operation of suggestion. Here, however, [the primary cooperants are] the powers of denotation and purport.

children.translated_text: "<s>Asaṃlakṣya</s>" (imperceptible) —
"Because of the very imperceptibility" (<s>asaṃlakṣyatvād eva</s>) —
Because when the sequence is imperceptible, the flashing forth of sublation of primary meaning etc. — which is the cause of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — is impossible. This is the purport.
He concludes the proposition under discussion with "or" (<s>yadi vā</s>) — "therefore" (<s>tena</s>) etc. // 13 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The hidden personal intention whose nature is the desire to taste the lip — for the purpose of making that known, the flattering composition made with skill and without abandoning propriety, having the described form — through that medium, the stimulation (<s>uddīpana</s>) of the <s>vibhāva</s>, i.e., the characteristic of the young woman who is the object of love (<s>ratyālambana</s>), meaning the production of desire in conformity with one's own intention. "Suggested" (<s>vyaṅgyam</s>): meaning primarily suggested in this verse. "Or" (<s>yadi vā</s>): alternatively. "Suddenly" (<s>ākasmika</s>): unexpected — this is the ground for impossibility. "Specific" (<s>viśiṣṭa</s>): the impossibility of the question-meaning characterized by a parrot performing austerities at a specific place etc. This is the meaning. "Through similarity, <s>lakṣaṇā</s>" — "this baby parrot" denotes some young lover; "bites the <s>bimba</s>-fruit of the lip's redness" denotes lip-tasting etc. through similarity. This is the purport. "Is precisely the suggested" (<s>dhvanyamānam eva tat</s>): "that" means what was previously stated beginning with "hidden" etc. He states the distinction of the two [types] — "only" (<s>kevalam</s>) etc. "In the former" — in the example beginning with "<s>suvarṇa</s>" etc. By "primary" (<s>pradhānam</s>), it is shown that the other two have slight cooperative role. "Here" (<s>iha</s>): meaning in the [verse beginning with] "<s>śikhariṇī</s>" etc. "Powers" (<s>śaktī</s>): the connection is with "primary," by inversion. Here he states the reason — "from the beauty of the sentence-meaning" (<s>vākyārtha</s>) etc. To show that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is not entirely functionless, he says — "to a slight extent" (<s>leśena</s>) etc. "It has been stated" (<s>ity uktam</s>): meaning stated by the text beginning with "or" (<s>yadi vā</s>) etc. Now, in this manner, is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> present everywhere in <s>vivakṣitānya-para-vācya</s>? No — he says:
