children.translated_text:
This <s>dhvani</s>, of the stated variety, bears non-unity by <s>bhakti</s> (metaphorical extension), because of the difference in forms. /
Where the meaning distinct from the expressible is illuminated by the expressible and the signifier with purposive intent (<s>tātparya</s>), and there is primacy of the suggested — that is <s>dhvani</s>. /
But <s>bhakti</s> (metaphorical extension) is merely <s>upacāra</s> (secondary usage). /
<s>Locana</s>: He refutes the first position: '<s>bhaktyā bibharti</s>' etc. /
'Of the stated variety' — this should be applied to the five referents: word, meaning, operation, suggested, and aggregate. /
To show the difference of form, he first states the form of <s>dhvani</s>: 'the expressible' etc. /
'With purposive intent' — as being the ground of repose (<s>viśrānti</s>), i.e., as serving the function: this is the extent. /
'Illumination' — the meaning is: making manifest (<s>dyotana</s>). /
'Merely <s>upacāra</s>' — <s>upacāra</s> is secondary function (<s>guṇavṛtti</s>), i.e., <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication). /
'<s>Upacaraṇa</s>' — the meaning is: an extended, i.e., heightened, usage. /
By the word '<s>mātra</s>' (merely), he says this: where, from the operation of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — the third [function] — a fourth operation, consisting of illuminating a purpose, which though actually possible by the nature of things, is as good as non-existent because it is not employed and hence disregarded. /
'Regarding which meaning' — <s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'like synonyms' — the meaning is: like the referent denoted by synonymous words such as '<s>Indra</s>' and '<s>Śakra</s>.' /
'Identity in form' — oneness. /
'Like <s>pṛthivītva</s> (earth-ness)' etc. — just as <s>pṛthivītva</s> (earth-ness) is a definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of earth in the form of a property that differentiates [it] from water etc., so is <s>bhakti</s> a definition of <s>dhvani</s>? — this is the meaning. /
'Or' etc. — just as in 'the crow marks <s>Devadatta</s>'s house,' the crow, merely from its occasional presence, is an indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) of <s>Devadatta</s>'s house — so is <s>bhakti</s> an indicator of <s>dhvani</s>? — this is the meaning. /
The construction of the <s>kārikā</s> is: 'this <s>dhvani</s> does not bear oneness, i.e., unity, by <s>bhakti</s>.' /
The five locative-ending words beginning with 'word' are connected with 'in the referents.' /
He explains '<s>tātparyeṇa</s>' (with purposive intent): '<s>viśrānti</s>' etc. /
How does the word '<s>upacāra</s>' apply in the secondary function (<s>guṇavṛtti</s>) and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication)? To this he says: '<s>upacaraṇa</s>' etc. /
The well-known usage of a certain word for a certain meaning — transcending that and applying the usage of that word to another meaning connected with it — is a heightened usage. /
He states the purpose of the word '<s>mātra</s>' in '<s>upacāramātram</s>': 'by the word <s>mātra</s>' etc. /
'Where' — the meaning is: in the examples beginning with '<s>parimlānam</s>' (wilted) etc. /
'Purpose' etc. — for there, the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of '<s>vadati</s>' (speaks) is in the sense of 'makes known through the cause of resemblance'; the purpose of that [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] is the vivid cognition of the torment — thus the operation of <s>dhvanana</s> (suggestion), though actually possible by the nature of things through the abandonment of primary denotation and the otherwise-unexplainability [that characterizes <s>lakṣaṇā</s>]: this is the meaning. /
'Because it is not employed' etc. — the purport is: because there is no special beauty of that purpose [attained through suggestion]. /
Now, since it is necessarily attended to precisely because it is in the domain of purpose, how can it be as good as non-existent? — to this doubt, in order to show that the domain of that operation does not have primary purposiveness because it does not accord with the definition of purpose (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — but rather [the purpose] is primary itself — he states the definition of primary purpose given by the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> author: '<s>yam</s>' etc. /
The <s>sūtra</s> is: 'That meaning regarding which [the usage] proceeds — that is its purpose.' /
'Lest this be so — that <s>bhakti</s> is the definition of <s>dhvani</s>' — he says:

children.text: ativyāpter athāvyāpter na cāsau lakṣyate tayā // DhvK_1.14 //
children.translated_text: Because of over-extension, or because of under-extension, [<s>dhvani</s>] is not defined (<s>lakṣyate</s>) by that [<s>bhakti</s>]. // <s>DhvK</s> 1.14 //
Because of over-extension, or because of under-extension, [<s>dhvani</s>] is not defined by that [<s>bhakti</s>]. // 14 //

children.translated_text: In '<s>prasiddhyanurodhe</s>' (conformity to convention): '<s>prasiddhi</s>' means excellent establishment — 'establishment' (<s>siddhi</s>) means the ascending of usage onto the path of practice; and its excellence is its being handed down through unbroken tradition — with this intention, he explains the meaning of the word '<s>prasiddhi</s>': 'through tradition' etc.
Poets are seen [to do this].

<s>Dhvani</s> is not at all defined by <s>bhakti</s> (metaphorical extension). /
How so? Because of over-extension and under-extension. /
Therein, the over-extension [is] because <s>bhakti</s> is possible even in the domain other than <s>dhvani</s>. /
For where there is no great beauty produced by the suggested, even there, with word-usage operating through indicated (secondary) denotation, usages motivated by conformity to convention [are found]. /
<s>Locana</s>: For [this is] the definition of purpose. /
Even there, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) exists — so how could <s>dhvanana</s> (suggestion) and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> be one and the same thing? /
He refutes the second position: 'because of over-extension' etc. /
'That' (<s>asau</s>) — <s>dhvani</s>. /
'By that' (<s>tayā</s>) — by <s>bhakti</s>. /
Now, since <s>dhvanana</s> (suggestion) is necessarily present, how is there a domain separate from it? — to this he says: 'great beauty' etc. /
Therefore, precisely because the purpose is to be disregarded, there is no function whatsoever of being a suggestor: this is the purport. /
By the word 'great' (<s>mahat</s>), [it is indicated that] that [suggestion] becomes merely a <s>guṇa</s> (quality). /
As it has been said — '<s>samādhi</s> (placing upon) is the superimposition of the property of another, somewhere, as intended' — he shows [this]. /
Now, in the absence of purpose, how is there such usage? — to this he says: 'in conformity to convention' etc. /
Because of continuous traditional practice in just that manner. /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'Even there' — the meaning is: even in such examples. /
'<s>Lakṣaṇā</s> exists' — the purport is this: if <s>bhakti</s> and <s>dhvani</s> were one and the same thing, then in the cited domain, either the existence of <s>dhvani</s> or the absence of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> would follow. /
But neither of these [obtains]. /
Therefore, since the essential nature of <s>bhakti</s>, which has the nature of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, is ascertained as distinct from <s>dhvani</s>, there is no scope for the suspicion of unity — to show this meaning, the word '<s>mātra</s>' was used. /
'The second position' — the meaning is: the position that '<s>bhakti</s> is the definition of <s>dhvani</s>.' /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, from 'lest this be' etc.: 'let <s>bhakti</s> and <s>dhvani</s> be one and the same thing' — let this not be so. 'Let <s>bhakti</s> be the definition of <s>dhvani</s>' — in response to this doubt, he says: this is the meaning. /
He introduces the passage beginning with 'for where' etc.: 'now' etc. /
'<s>Dhvanana</s> is necessarily present' — '<s>lakṣaṇā</s>' is to be supplied. /
He states the purport: 'therefore' etc. /
Therefore — precisely because of the absence of great beauty. /
'By the function of being a suggestor' — by the operation of suggestion. /
'There is no function whatsoever' — the mere existence of suggestion does not motivate the usage of '<s>dhvani</s>'; rather, only the possession of surpassing beauty [does]. /
And that is not present here — hence there is no being in the domain of <s>dhvani</s>-usage: this is the purport. /
'Merely a <s>guṇa</s>' — the meaning is: merely some quality of the composition. /
'That' — the meaning is: the suggestive function. /
The construction is: 'becomes' [with] 'shows.' /
The purport is: through the word 'great,' the demonstration of some [slight] beauty produced by the suggested [is given]. /
'<s>Samādhi</s>' — <s>samādhi</s> is a <s>guṇa</s> (quality) of that name. /
'Of another' — of an irrelevant thing; 'the property of that.' /
'Somewhere' — upon the relevant thing. /
Examples of this are '<s>kumudāni nimīlantī</s>' (the water-lilies are closing their eyes) etc. /
Likewise — "She is kissed a hundred times, embraced a thousand times,

children.text: viramia puṇo ramijjai pio jaṇo ṇatthi punaruttam //
children.translated_text: resting and making love again — there is no repetition with the beloved."
(She is kissed a hundred times, embraced a thousand times,

children.text: viramya punā ramyate priyo jano nāsti punaruktam //
children.translated_text: resting and making love again — there is no repetition with the beloved.
Thus the <s>chāyā</s> [Sanskrit rendering].) Likewise —
"Angry, then appeased, with downcast faces, then laughing —

children.translated_text: however they are embraced, wanton women steal the heart."

children.text: ajjāeṃ pahāro ṇavaladāe diṇṇo pieṇa thaṇavaṭṭe /
children.translated_text: "The blow given by the noble lady to the young creeper, [planted] by the beloved upon [her] breast,

<s>Locana</s>: But we say — '<s>prasiddhi</s>' (convention) means the non-concealment of the purpose: this is the meaning. /
Even in its manifest form, that purpose, though shining forth, requires concealment like a treasure: this is the purport. /
In '<s>vadati</s>' (speaks) — in this secondary usage, the vivid cognition is the purpose. /
If the unconcealed [meaning] were stated with its own proper word, would there be any lack of beauty? [Yes, there would.] Or, would the charm increase through description in a concealed manner? /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: He undertakes to explain the word '<s>prasiddhi</s>' in the ultimate manner: 'but we' etc. /
'<s>Prasiddhi</s>' (convention) — the establishment (<s>siddhi</s>), i.e., the cognition (<s>pratīti</s>), of the purpose with heightened manifestness; [meaning] the conspicuous appearance [of that purpose] as possessing the fitness to be the domain of an operation beyond suggestion — this is the extent. /
'In conformity with that' — in conformity with the opposite, i.e., the unfitness to be the domain of the operation of suggestion, [and] in conformity with that very [unfitness]. /
He explains 'usage motivated by which': '<s>prasiddhi</s> means' etc. /
'The non-concealment of the purpose' — the manifestness: this is the meaning of the word '<s>prasiddhi</s>' here; but not the previously stated [meaning]: this is the purport. /
Now, since in the domain of <s>dhvani</s> too the purpose appears manifestly and hence non-concealment is the same — to this doubt he states the distinction: 'even in its manifest form' etc. /
'That purpose' — the purpose belonging to the domain of <s>dhvani</s>. /
'In its manifest form' — appearing manifestly. /
The construction is: 'even [though] shining forth with [manifest] form.' /
The meaning is: even though appearing [manifestly]. /
'Concealment' — the state of not appearing in the condition of fully manifest usage — [i.e.,] the beauty-producing state of being hidden: this is the meaning. /
'Like a treasure' — like a buried treasure: requires, i.e., expects [concealment]. /
In '<s>vadati</s>' etc. — and that it is not so [in the present case] — he says: '<s>vadati</s>' etc. /
'Vivid' etc. — 'if that form of purpose, being unconcealed, were stated with its own word' — this is the construction. /
'If it were expressed as: it clearly conveys her torment' etc. — this is the meaning. /
'Through description in a concealed manner' —
(The blow given by the noble lady to the young creeper, [planted] by the beloved upon [her] breast,

children.translated_text: "<s>Avarundhijjai</s>" means "is embraced."
"<s>Punaruktam</s>" (repetition) — [here] undesirability is indicated, since the repetition of a stated meaning is impossible [in this context].
"Angry [then] appeased, with tearful faces [then] laughing —

children.text: yathā gṛhītāstathā hṛdayaṃ haranti svairiṇyo mahilāḥ // .//
children.translated_text: however they are embraced, wanton women steal the heart."
Thus the <s>chāyā</s> [Sanskrit rendering].) <s>Locana</s>: Has additional beauty arisen? With this very intention he will say: "because what cannot [be expressed] by another expression" etc.

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā] That too, as before, is not praiseworthy.
[Bālapriyā] 'Appropriate' (<s>ucita</s>) —

children.text: tathā---- parārthe yaḥ pīḍābhanubhavati bhaṅge 'pi madhuro yadīyaḥ sarvoṣāmiha khalu vikāro 'pyabhimataḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise — 'He who endures suffering for the sake of others, whose [nature] is sweet even when broken, whose every transformation here is indeed welcomed —

children.text: na samprāpto vṛddhiṃ yadi sa bhṛśamakṣetrapatitaḥ kimikṣordeṣo 'sau na punaraguṇāyā marubhuvaḥ //
children.translated_text: If he has not attained growth, it is because he has fallen on barren ground; is the fault that of the sugarcane (<s>ikṣu</s>)? It is rather [the fault] of the worthless desert land.' //

[Bālapriyā] Here, by 'grasping' (<s>grahaṇa</s>), desirability (<s>upādeyatā</s>) is indicated through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification).
By 'carrying away' (<s>haraṇa</s>), the state of being subject to another's control (<s>paratantratā</s>) is arrived at.
Likewise — '<s>ajja</s>' means: on the breast of the youngest wife, by the beloved, through the familiar sport (<s>ucita-krīḍā-yoga</s>), with a fresh vine-like [gesture], even a gentle blow was given — [this], indicating good fortune (<s>saubhāgya</s>) to the co-wives who have not obtained a share in such amorous play, pierces their hearts — thus '<s>Bālapriyā</s> says' and so forth is the description. This is the meaning.
'Why' (<s>kim</s>) — regarding the prohibition in both cases:
Mere description through concealment (<s>gūḍhatā</s>) is not the cause of <s>dhvani</s> usage; rather, it is precisely that concealed description which produces a charm (<s>cārutva</s>) distinct from the state expressible by one's own words, as in '<s>suvarṇapuṣpām</s>' and so forth.
But in 'she says' and similar cases, since no particular charm is found whether described covertly or openly, the opposite [conclusion follows] — this is the purport.
He corroborates the stated meaning with the forthcoming verse — 'by this very' (<s>anenaiva</s>).
'Withered' (<s>parimlāna</s>) — this is the speech of the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>) in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>.
'On both sides' (<s>ubhayataḥ</s>) — on two portions; tossings at the edges of the bed, turnings, and rollings about.
The reason stated as 'full' (<s>pīna</s>) etc. is expressed through inference by observing effects such as wilting.
Here, since the bed (<s>śayana</s>), being insentient, cannot be construed as the agent of action in the primary sense, through the obstruction of the primary meaning, indication (<s>jñāpana</s>) is understood via resemblance (<s>sādṛśya</s>); and making clear what is not understood is stated as the purpose.
'Is kissed' (<s>cumbyate</s>) — 'by the heroine' (<s>nāyikayā</s>) is to be supplied.
The syntactic connection is: 'the beloved person is kissed a hundred times' and so forth.
'There is no repetition' (<s>nāsti punaruktam</s>) — the meaning is that there is no repetition of kissing and so forth.
Here, since the primary meaning in the form of repeated statement regarding kissing etc. is obstructed, it is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — thus he says 'repetition' and so forth.
'Of the stated meaning' (<s>uktārthasya</s>) — means: of the meaning in the form of statement.
Here the purpose is in the form of possessing additional fruit, and that too, as before, is not worthy of esteem — this should be understood.
'Angered' (<s>kupitā</s>) — in 'seized' (<s>gṛhītā</s>), 'by the man' (<s>puruṣeṇa</s>) is to be supplied.
Here, since the primary meanings of 'seized' and 'carrying away,' namely taking possession and removing, are impossible, he says 'by grasping' (<s>grahaṇena</s>) and so forth.
Here, making one's own (<s>ātmasātkaraṇa</s>) and utter helplessness (<s>vaivalya</s>) are successively the purposes of the two <s>lakṣaṇās</s>.

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā] Although with reference to the noble person being discussed (<s>prastuta-mahāpuruṣa</s>), the word 'experiences' (<s>anubhavati</s>) is indeed primary [in meaning], nevertheless, when sugarcane (<s>ikṣu</s>) — the non-subject — is being praised, since the experience (<s>anubhavana</s>) of suffering is impossible [for sugarcane], the state of having suffering (<s>pīḍāvattva</s>) is indicated through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>; and that culminates in the state of being crushed (<s>pīḍyamānatva</s>).

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā] Anticipating the objection 'But there is a purpose here, so why is it not <s>dhvani</s>?', he says 'And such [usage] is never' (<s>na ca evaṃvidha</s>) // 14 //

[Locana] Here, in the sugarcane aspect (<s>ikṣu-pakṣa</s>), the word 'experiences' (<s>anubhavati</s>) [is used figuratively].
And such [usage] is never the domain of <s>dhvani</s>.
[Locana] 'Unbearable' (<s>duḥsaha</s>) has become so precisely because of softness (<s>mṛdukatva</s>).
The blow given to one becomes the death of another.
And that which is both unbearable and yet gentle — this is the wonder (<s>citra</s>).

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā] — means: is the domain of <s>dhvani</s> usage.
[Bālapriyā] In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'such' (<s>evaṃvidha</s>) means —
[Bālapriyā] a purpose of such a kind, which is not worthy of esteem — this is the meaning.
[Bālapriyā] 'The domain of <s>dhvani</s>' means: the domain of <s>dhvani</s> usage. // 14 //

[Bālapriyā] 'Appropriate sport' (<s>ucita-krīḍā-yoga</s>) means either the sport that is customary, i.e., the occasion of amorous play, or alternatively, the conjunction that would arise in appropriate play — by that reason.
'Given' (<s>datta</s>) is the syntactic connection.
In 'it became unbearable to the co-wives' (<s>sapatnīnāṃ duḥsaho jāta</s>), he shows the implied reason through a qualifier — with '<s>saubhāgya</s>' etc. up to 'who have not obtained.'
He shows the reason for its indicating good fortune — 'because of its softness' (<s>mṛdukatvāt</s>). He clarifies the contradiction indicated by the particle 'even' (<s>api</s>) in 'even though gentle' (<s>mṛduko 'pi</s>) — with 'of one' (<s>anyasya</s>) etc.
Given to one, it becomes [pain] for another — this is one [contradiction]; though gentle and thus bearable, yet it is unbearable — this is another contradiction. This is the meaning.
Here, since 'giving' (<s>dāna</s>) in its primary sense is obstructed, in 'a blow was given,' by 'giving,' the fruitfulness achievable through giving is indicated through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — thus he says 'by giving' (<s>dānena</s>) and so forth.
'Fruitfulness' (<s>phalavatva</s>) — means the fulfillment (<s>caritārthatva</s>) of the youngest wife.
And the purpose is the enjoyability (<s>sukhopabhogyatva</s>) of the blow.
That too is not worthy of esteem.
'For the sake of others' (<s>parārtha</s>) — sugarcane is crushed for the sake of others.
And a great person endures suffering for the sake of others.
Sugarcane, even when broken, possesses sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>).
The person too, even when treated harshly, remains of a favourable disposition.
Transformation (<s>vikāra</s>) refers to jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>) etc. and anger (<s>kopa</s>) etc.
Growth (<s>vṛddhi</s>) means nourishment and prosperity.
'Barren ground' (<s>akṣetra</s>) means alkaline soil (<s>ūṣara-bhūmi</s>) and an unsuitable place.
Here, he establishes the figurative nature stated in the <s>vṛtti</s> as 'the word "experiences" in the sugarcane aspect' — with 'although' (<s>yadyapi</s>) and so forth.
'Because of the impossibility of experiencing' (<s>anubhavanena asambhavatā</s>) — for experience (<s>anubhavana</s>), which is cognition (<s>jñāna</s>) in its primary sense, is impossible for sugarcane since it is insentient. This is the meaning.
And that state of having suffering (<s>pīḍāvattva</s>)
culminating in 'being crushed' (<s>pīḍyamānatva</s>) — means 'being ground' (<s>mardyamānatva</s>). This is the meaning.
And the purpose is the state of being in a wretched condition — that too is not worthy of esteem.
'But' (<s>nanv</s>) etc.
'Is suggested' (<s>dhvanyate</s>) —
Because —
That charm (<s>cārutva</s>) which cannot be [expressed] by any other mode of expression (<s>ukti-antara</s>), revealing [it],

tathāvidhe ca viṣaye kvacitsambhavannapi locanam yata uktyantareṇeti /
uktyantareṇa dhvanyatiriktena sphuṭena śabdārthavyāpāraviśeṣeṇetyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā] 'Word' (<s>śabda</s>) — should be construed in five senses.
[Bālapriyā] 'Becomes the domain of <s>dhvani</s>-expression' — means: is designated by the word '<s>dhvani</s>.'
[Bālapriyā] 'Illustrated' (<s>udāhṛta</s>) —
[Bālapriyā] in 'she says' (<s>vadati</s>) and so forth. // 15 //

[Locana] And in those [cases] there is figurative usage (<s>upacarita-śabda-vṛtti</s>).
And in such a domain, even when [<s>dhvani</s>] is possible in some cases —
[Locana] 'Because by another mode of expression' (<s>yata ukty-antareṇa</s>) —
'By another mode of expression' means: by a clear operation of word and meaning that is distinct from <s>dhvani</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text:
evaṃ yatra prayojanaṃ sadapi nādarāspadaṃ tatra ko dhvananavyāpāra ityuktvā yatra mūlata eva prayojanaṃ nāsti, bhavati copacārastatrāpi ko dhvananavyāpāra ityāha---kiñceti /
lāvaṇyādyā ye śabdāḥ svaviṣayāllavaṇarasayuktatvādeḥ svārthādanyatra hṛdyatvādau rūḍhā; bālapriyā 'uktvantareṇe'tyatra uktiśabdo vyāpāravāco, antaraśabdaśca dhvanyapekṣayānyavācītyāha---dhvanyatiriktenetyādi /
sphuṭena vyavahārabhūmiṣu prasiddhena /

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā] He states the meaning of the word '<s>śabda</s>' in '<s>śabdo vyañjakatām</s>' — 'in five [senses]' (<s>pañcasu</s>) —

children.text: śabdyate abhidhīyata iti vācyaḥ, śabdyate 'neneti vācakaḥ, śabdyate vyajyata iti vyaṅgyaḥ, śabdanamiti vyāpāraḥ /
children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā] That which is sounded, i.e., denoted, is the expressible (<s>vācya</s>); that by which it is sounded is the expressor (<s>vācaka</s>); that which is sounded forth, i.e., suggested, is the suggestible (<s>vyaṅgya</s>); and the act of sounding is the operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>).
[Bālapriyā] And since it is the aggregate of the aforementioned four, the aggregate (<s>samudāya</s>) is also the meaning of the word '<s>śabda</s>' here. This is the meaning.
[Bālapriyā] The explanation of 'in the illustrated domain' (<s>udāhṛte viṣaye</s>) is — 'in "she says" and so forth' (<s>vadati ityādau</s>). // 15 //

[Bālapriyā] Having thus said that where even though a purpose exists it is not worthy of esteem, there is no operation of suggestion (<s>dhvanana-vyāpāra</s>), he now says that where there is fundamentally no purpose at all and yet there is figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>), there too there is no operation of suggestion — with 'moreover' (<s>kiñca</s>).
'<s>Lāvaṇya</s> and the like' — words which are established (<s>rūḍha</s>) in a domain other than their own, [namely other than] their own meaning of 'possessing salt-flavor' (<s>lavaṇa-rasa-yukata</s>), in the sense of 'charm' (<s>hṛdyatva</s>) etc.
[Bālapriyā] In 'by another expression' (<s>ukty-antareṇa</s>), the word 'expression' (<s>ukti</s>) denotes operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>), and the word 'other' (<s>antara</s>) means 'different' with reference to <s>dhvani</s> — thus he says 'distinct from <s>dhvani</s>' and so forth.
'Clear' (<s>sphuṭa</s>) means well-known in the domains of [ordinary] usage.

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā] He explains the <s>vṛtti</s> passage from 'such' (<s>tathāvidha</s>) up to 'through the medium' (<s>mukhena</s>) through objection and resolution — with 'but' (<s>nanv</s>) etc.

children.text: pustake dṛśyamānāyā 'devaḍi'tyādigāthāyā granteṣu tatra tatrākṣarabhedā dṛśyante /
children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā] In the manuscripts, the verse beginning with '<s>devaḍi</s>' etc. shows variant readings (<s>akṣara-bheda</s>) here and there in the texts.

children.text: ataścāsyāḥ svarūpaṃ chāyāṃ ca niścetuṃ na śaknomi /
children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā] Therefore I am unable to ascertain its exact form (<s>svarūpa</s>) and its paraphrase (<s>chāyā</s>).
[Bālapriyā] Let the learned connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) determine [it]. //

[Bālapriyā] 'Fundamentally' (<s>mūlata eva</s>) etc.
For <s>dhvani</s>, two things are required: a purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) and that purpose being worthy of esteem (<s>ādarāspadatva</s>); of these two, the fundamental one, namely the purpose itself, does not exist — this is the meaning.
By the word 'own domain' (<s>sva-viṣaya</s>), one's own primary meaning is intended — thus he says '<s>lavaṇa</s>' etc.
The statement of being established (<s>rūḍhatva</s>) is for the purpose of making evident the absence of purpose — thus he says 'because of being established' (<s>rūḍhatvāt</s>) etc.
For establishment (<s>rūḍhatva</s>) is the capacity to convey one's own meaning without intermediary; here, the fact of being devoid of the intermediary consisting of the expectation of the triad — obstruction of primary meaning, connection with that, and purpose — is shown by the word 'established' (<s>rūḍha</s>), and thus the absence of purpose is firmly established. This is the meaning.
<s>Dhvani</s> usage operates through another means,
not through the medium of such words.
[Locana] 'Because of being established, devoid of the intermediary of expecting the triad' —
As he said: 'Some <s>lakṣaṇās</s> (secondary significations) that are well-established (<s>nirūḍhā</s>) function like primary denotation (<s>abhidhāna</s>) by virtue of [conventional] capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>).'
Those [words], even when employed in a domain other than their own, do not become the locus of <s>dhvani</s>; there is no <s>dhvani</s> usage there.
'Figurative' (<s>upacaritā</s>) — the <s>gauṇī</s> function of the word is meant; figurative [usages] are understood.
'Smoothing' (<s>anuloma</s>) means rubbing in the direction of the hair.
'Against the bank' (<s>pratikūla</s>) means the current standing in opposition to the bank.
'Of equal weight' (<s>tulya-guru</s>) means a fellow student (<s>sabrahmacārī</s>) — this is the primary domain.
The other [usage] is indeed figurative (<s>upacarita</s>).
And here, since <s>lakṣaṇā</s> does not operate with any purpose in view, <s>dhvani</s> usage does not pertain to that domain.
[Bālapriyā] 'Well-established' (<s>nirūḍhā</s>) means —
certain <s>lakṣaṇās</s>;
by capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>), that is, by the force of [conventional] usage (<s>prayoga-sāmarthya</s>), they function like primary denotation.
He glosses the verse portion 'employed' (<s>prayuktāḥ</s>) etc. by continuing the syntax — 'those, in that [domain]' (<s>te tasmin</s>) etc.
He glosses the prose passage 'and in those there is figurative word-usage' (<s>teṣu ca upacarita-śabda-vṛttiḥ</s>) — with 'figurative' (<s>upacaritā</s>) etc.
He states the meaning of the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>) in '<s>lāvaṇyādyāḥ</s>' — with '<s>ādi</s>' etc.
'Another' (<s>anya</s>) means —
one who goes along with (<s>anurodhī</s>), one who opposes (<s>virodhī</s>), one who is equal (<s>tulya</s>) — these are the commonly known meanings. This is the meaning.
[Bālapriyā] '<s>priyatamā-mukhasya iva</s>' and '<s>priyatamasya iva</s>' are [variant] readings.
[Bālapriyā] 'By the power of suggestion alone' (<s>vyañjakatvena eva</s>) —
[Bālapriyā] means: by the suggestive operation residing in the meaning (<s>artha-gata-vyañjana-vyāpāra</s>) alone. This is the meaning.
[Bālapriyā] He glosses the passage 'not in such [a domain]' (<s>na tathāvidhe</s>) etc. — 'not figurative' (<s>na tu upacarita</s>) // 16 //

[Bālapriyā] Intending to introduce the passage beginning with 'moreover' (<s>api ca</s>), he restates what was said — with 'thus' (<s>evam</s>) etc.
'By that' (<s>tena</s>) — means: by the absence of the stated scope (<s>ukta-vyāpti-abhāvena</s>).
Moreover —
Abandoning the primary function (<s>mukhyā vṛtti</s>), the apprehension of meaning through a secondary function (<s>guṇa-vṛtti</s>),

children.text: yad uddiśya phalaṃ tatra śabdo naiva skhalad-gatiḥ // DhvK_1.17 //
children.translated_text: When directed toward a purpose (<s>phala</s>), the word (<s>śabda</s>) therein does not proceed with halting gait (<s>skhalad-gati</s>). // <s>DhvK</s> 1.17 //
Abandoning the primary function, the apprehension of meaning through a secondary function,

children.translated_text: 'Is not the domain' —
Rather, another [operation] entirely has that as its domain. This is the purport.

children.text: yathā---"ā hanta kimidaṃ tanvi netrayoḥ śrāvaṇastava /
children.translated_text: For example: 'Ah, alas! What is this, O slender one? In your eyes, the rainy season (<s>śrāvaṇa</s>);
on your cheeks, autumn; on your body, summer; on your lotus-face, winter.'

[<s>Locana</s>:] Then there would be the over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) that wherever there is figurative usage (<s>bhakti</s>), the designation '<s>dhvani</s>' would apply everywhere. /
Even accepting [your position], we say: let it be that wherever there is figurative usage, there is <s>dhvani</s>. /
Even so, the domain of the operation of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) is not the domain of the operation of <s>dhvanana</s> (suggesting). /
And there is no property-substrate relation between two [operations] that have different domains. /
And it is the property itself that is called <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. /
Now, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is an operation whose domain is the non-primary meaning. /
But <s>dhvanana</s> has as its domain the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>). /
And a second operation of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> pertaining to that [purpose] domain is not reasonable, because the ensemble of conditions for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is absent — with this intention he says: 'moreover' etc. /
Having abandoned, i.e., completed, the primary function — the operation of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) — the presentation, i.e., conveyance, of a non-primary meaning through <s>guṇavṛtti</s> (secondary function) in the form of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — that [presentation] is performed aiming at a purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) which is the object in the form of a result. In that [domain] — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'This is the over-extension' — the meaning is: such is the form of the undesirable consequence (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>). /
'Stated' is the remainder. /
The meaning is: because the absence of <s>dhvani</s> has been demonstrated even when figurative usage exists, in [examples like] '<s>vadati</s>' (speaks) etc. and in words like '<s>lāvaṇya</s>' (gracefulness). /
'What is accepted and what is asserted?' — to both [questions] he answers in order: 'let it be' etc. /
He substantiates the different-domain-ness: 'therein' etc. /
'Non-primary' — the non-primary meaning of a word like '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' is the bank etc. /
'Purpose' — the meaning is: the coolness, purity, etc. belonging to the <s>Gaṅgā</s> etc. /
'Pertaining to that domain too' — the meaning is: pertaining to the domain of purpose too. /
'The ensemble of conditions for <s>lakṣaṇā</s>' — the meaning is: the obstruction [of primary meaning] etc. /
[Objection:] But since the function of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is impossible without <s>abhidhā</s> [first operating], how can there be 'abandoning' of it? — hence he explains the word '<s>parityajya</s>' (abandoning) in a manner suited to the context: '<s>parisamāpya</s>' (having completed). /
The 'abandoning' here is not the disregarding of it, but rather: having first accepted the meaning within its domain, the running-beyond (<s>atilaṅghana</s>) in the form of surpassing it, through its medium, for the purpose of conveying another meaning. This is the meaning. /
For 'result' he states the meaning in the accusative: 'object' (<s>karma</s>). /
He states the referent of the word 'result': 'in the form of purpose.' /
'Is performed' — this is a supplementary completion. /
For therein, when the purpose — characterized as the illumination of a meaning distinguished by the superiority of beauty — is to be effected: if — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] There is indeed a second operation for the purpose. /
But that is not <s>lakṣaṇā</s> itself; because <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is the operation of a word whose movement, i.e., power of conveying [meaning], stumbles and is impeded by the operation of an obstructing [factor]. /
But for a word that conveys the purpose, there is no conjunction with an obstructing [factor]. /
In the absence of such [obstruction], even there [i.e., in the purpose-domain], since one would need to search for yet another cause and yet another purpose, there would be infinite regress. /
Hence the purport is: this [purpose-meaning] is not the domain of the definition of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. /
'Presentation' (<s>darśanam</s>) — the statement is in the causative form (<s>ṇyanta</s>). /
'To be effected' — the meaning is: to be made known. /
'As non-primary' — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The explanation of '<s>tatra</s>' is: 'purpose.' /
'<s>Tāvat</s>' — in the sense of concession. /
'Second' — the meaning is: other than the operation pertaining to the non-primary meaning domain. /
'Operation' — the remainder is: must necessarily be accepted. /
'Then let the operation of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> pertaining to that domain too be accepted!' — to this he says: 'but not' etc. /
'That' — the meaning is: the second operation. /
As the reason for '<s>na ca lakṣaṇaiva</s>' ('but that is not <s>lakṣaṇā</s> itself'), he cites the last quarter of the <s>kārikā</s>: 'because' etc. /
Thus by '<s>naiva skhaladgatiḥ</s>' ('not at all stumbling in movement'), the absence of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is established. This is the purport. /
'By the obstructing [factor]' — the meaning is: by the operation of an obstructing means of knowledge. /
'Impeded' — rendered hesitant. /
'Power of conveying' — the meaning is: the power of conveying its own meaning. /
'Of that' — the meaning is: belonging to such a word. /
'Let it be so — what follows from that?' — to this he says: 'but not' etc. /
'That conveys' — the purport is: at the time of conveying. /
'Of the word' — the meaning is: of a word like '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc. that has the function [of denoting] the bank etc. /
'Conjunction with an obstructing [factor]' — the meaning is: having an obstructed meaning, in the form of the unfitness of its meaning for syntactic connection with the meaning of another word like '<s>ghoṣa</s>' (village) etc. /
'Even accepting' — he says: 'in such a case' etc. /
'In such a case' — when there is conjunction with an obstructing [factor]. /
'Even there' — even in the purpose to be conveyed. /
'A cause' — a cause in the form of a relation. /
'Because of infinite regress through searching' — the connection of this is with 'but not the conjunction with an obstructing [factor].' /
Some [say]: by the indicated [meaning] — the bank etc. — the meaning in the form of the purpose is conveyed through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. He rejects that view: 'hence' etc. /
'Hence' — because <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is the operation of a word whose movement stumbles — for that reason. /
The connection of '<s>abhidhā-puccha-bhūtā eva lakṣaṇā</s>' ('<s>lakṣaṇā</s> is nothing but a tail-end of <s>abhidhā</s>') is with this.

children.translated_text:
Thus. /
Here, by the word '<s>śrāvaṇa</s>' etc., the rainy season etc. is indicated (<s>lakṣya</s>); by that, the flowing of tears etc. [is suggested]. /
Hence the purpose here is the excess of longing (<s>utkaṇṭhā</s>) — [conveyed] through <s>lakṣita-lakṣaṇā</s> (indication of what is indicated). /
Therein, by the word '<s>śrāvaṇa</s>' etc., the flowing of tears etc. itself is indicated — hence, because of the absence of <s>lakṣita-lakṣaṇā</s>, this is not its domain. This is the meaning — according to some. /
He substantiates the explanation 'presentation means conveyance': '<s>darśanam</s>' etc. /
'To be made known' — this is the meaning. /
'In the purpose characterized as the illumination of a meaning distinguished by the superiority of beauty' — the non-primary status of the word [would imply that] then its usage would be faulty indeed. /
But it is not so. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Impeded by the obstructing [factor]' — this is the meaning. /
'Of that' — of the word. /
'Would be faulty indeed' — for that word is used in that non-primary meaning for the easy attainment of the cognition of the purpose. /
If, however, in [the example] '<s>siṃho vaṭuḥ</s>' ('the lad is a lion'), even when the excess of heroism is to be conveyed, there is stumbling movement of the word, then it would not at all produce the cognition of that [heroism] — so what is the point of its usage? /
'It will do so through figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>)' — if so, then even there another purpose must be sought; and in that too figurative usage [would apply] — and so there is infinite regress. /
But if there is no stumbling movement there [in the purpose-domain], then in the purpose to be conveyed, there is no operation called <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, because of the absence of its ensemble of conditions. /
And it is not the case that there is no operation [at all]. /
And it is not <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) either, because of the absence of a convention (<s>samaya</s>) pertaining to it. /
That other operation, distinct from <s>abhidhā</s> and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, is the operation of <s>dhvanana</s> (suggesting). /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] This has been explained with the intention of the reading '<s>na</s>.' /
In the reading '<s>cārutva-atiśaya-viśiṣṭa-artha-prakāśana-lakṣaṇa</s>,' the meaning of '<s>kartavya</s>' is: 'to be produced.' /
Since the stumbling movement is negated when the purpose is the content to be conveyed, what is intended by the word 'non-primary' is precisely that — he says: 'by the obstructing [factor]' etc. /
[Objection:] But how does the acceptance of non-primary status in the stated form lead to faultiness? For faultiness consists in the absence of grammatical refinement etc. — to this doubt, [the answer is:] because of the failure to produce the cognition of the intended meaning, i.e., purposelessness. That is what is intended here — he says: 'of the purpose' etc. /
'Of the cognition of the purpose' — of the knowledge of the excess of heroism etc. /
'For easy attainment' — for easy production. /
'That word' — a word like '<s>siṃha</s>' (lion) etc. that is an indicator (<s>lakṣaka</s>). /
'In that non-primary meaning' — the meaning is: in the meaning such as the lad etc. /
'What follows from that?' — to this he says: 'but if' etc. /
'Of heroism' — the meaning is: in the excess of heroism too, as in the lad. /
'The cognition of that' — the cognition of the excess of heroism. 'What is the point?' — the meaning is: the appearance of purposelessness of that usage. /
Now, intending to establish the operation of <s>dhvanana</s> for the purpose, he displays the stated meaning through objection and resolution: 'through figurative usage' etc. /
'It will produce' — the carry-over is: 'the cognition of that, the usage of that.' /
'Even there' — the meaning is: even when the excess of heroism is the indicated [meaning]. /
'Another purpose must be sought' — the meaning is: since <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is invariably purposive, some other purpose must be desired. /
'In that too' — in that purpose too, if figurative usage is to be accepted as before, then in that too something else, and in that too something else — thus there would be an infinite regress that destroys the root. This is the meaning. /
Hence the acceptance of stumbling movement is not reasonable. This is the purport. /
[Objection:] Let there be no stumbling movement — but even so, from what [evidence] does the absence of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> [follow]? To this he says: 'but if' etc. /
To arrive at <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion) by elimination, he says: 'and not' etc. /
'Of the convention' — the meaning is: of the conventional assignment (<s>saṅketa</s>). /
Intending to substantiate the forthcoming [verse] that <s>guṇavṛtti</s> (secondary function) is based solely on the expressiveness (<s>vācakatva</s>), he first establishes the tail-end status of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> with respect to <s>abhidhā</s>: 'hence' etc. /
'Hence' — since <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is the operation of a word whose movement stumbles, for that reason. /
The connection of '<s>abhidhā-puccha-bhūtā eva lakṣaṇā</s>' ('<s>lakṣaṇā</s> is merely a tail-end of <s>abhidhā</s>') is with this. /
Therefore —
<s>Guṇavṛtti</s> (secondary function) is established solely on the basis of expressiveness (<s>vācakatva</s>);

children.text: vyañjakatvaika-mūlasya dhvaneḥ syāl lakṣaṇaṃ katham // DhvK_1.18 //
children.translated_text: how could there be a definition of <s>dhvani</s>, which has suggestiveness (<s>vyañjakatva</s>) alone as its foundation? || <s>DhvK</s> 1.18 ||
<s>Guṇavṛtti</s> is established solely on the basis of expressiveness;
how could there be a definition of <s>dhvani</s>, which has suggestiveness alone as its foundation? || 18 ||

children.text:
tasmādanyo dhvaniranyā ca guṇavṛttiḥ /
avyāptirapyasya lakṣaṇasya /
locanam caivamiti /
na ca prayoge duṣṭatā kācit prayojanasyābidhnenaiva pratīteḥ /
children.translated_text: And there is no faultiness in the usage [of such words], since the purpose is cognized through <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) alone.

children.text: tenābhidhaiva mukhye 'rthe bādhakena pravivitsurnirudhyamānā satī acaritārthatvādanyatra prasarati /
children.translated_text: Hence <s>abhidhā</s> itself, operating in the primary meaning, when obstructed by an opposing [factor] while seeking to proceed, since its purpose remains unfulfilled, extends to another [meaning].
For this very reason, the usage 'this is a non-primary meaning of this [word]' [arises].
And in precisely that way, the grasping of the convention too exists there in a non-primary manner — hence <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is nothing but a tail-end of <s>abhidhā</s>. || 17 ||

Therefore <s>dhvani</s> is one thing and <s>guṇavṛtti</s> is another. /
This definition also has the defect of under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] And thus —

asya guṇavṛttirūpasyetyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Convention' (<s>sanketa</s>) —

children.text: na he śabdasya yaḥ kaścidevāṃmukhyo 'rthaḥ kintvayamartho 'sya śabdasyāmukhya iti niyata evetyatastathāvidhopadeśarūpasya /
children.translated_text: For it is not the case that some particular [meaning] alone is the non-primary meaning of a word; rather, 'this meaning is the non-primary [meaning] of this word' — this is invariably fixed; therefore [one needs] an instruction (<s>upadesa</s>) of such a kind, or

children.text: ayamartho 'smācchabdādboddhavya iti icchārūpasya vā saṅketasya grahamamapītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'this meaning is to be understood from this word' — [one needs] the apprehension of a convention (<s>sanketa</s>) in the form of a desire — this too [is required]: this is the meaning.
This has been elaborated in the <s>Kavyaprakasa</s>, in [the section on] convention. // 17 //

[Balapriya:] He concludes — 'therefore' (<s>tasmad</s>) etc.
Since <s>laksana</s> (indication) is merely an appendage (<s>puccha</s>) of <s>abhidha</s> (denotation), therefore 'signifier-ness' (<s>vacakatva</s>) depends on the operation of <s>abhidha</s>; because [indication] arises through the obstruction of that [denotation], and because it is an appendage of that [denotation], [it has] secondary function (<s>gunavrtti</s>) — the meaning is: 'the figurative and indicative usage' (<s>gauna-laksanika-kara</s>).
How could that [secondary function] be the definition of <s>dhvani</s>, which has the nature of <s>vyanjana</s> (suggestion)? Because they have different domains — thus.
He concludes — 'therefore' etc.
Since over-extension has been stated, and in connection with that, the difference of domain [has been shown], therefore 'it does not [define it]' — this is the meaning.
Thus, having explained the over-extension mentioned in the <s>karika</s> 'because of over-extension, or because of under-extension, it is not defined by that,' he explains the under-extension — 'there is under-extension too of this' etc.
'Of this' — meaning: of this [bhakti] which has the form of secondary function (<s>gunavrtti</s>).
<s>Balapriya</s>: Regarding 'how?' — '<s>abhidha</s> itself' etc.
The syntactic connection is: '<s>abhidha</s> itself extends elsewhere.'
<s>Abhidha</s> (denotation) is the denotative capacity residing in words like '<s>Ganga</s>' etc., or the word '<s>Ganga</s>' etc. possessing that [capacity].
'Elsewhere' — in something other than the primary meaning such as the stream etc., [i.e.,] in the bank etc.
The reason for extending elsewhere is: 'because of non-fulfillment of purpose' (<s>acaritarthatvat</s>).
The meaning is: because of not producing its own effect in the form of the cognition of a completed, qualified meaning.
Here too he states the reason — 'in the primary meaning' etc.
The syntactic connection is: 'when the primary meaning, being desired to be entered [by the word], is obstructed by an invalidator.'
After '<s>badhakena</s>' (by an invalidator), there is also the reading '<s>vidhuri-krta</s>' (made desolate) in some texts.
'For this very reason' — from the reason already stated.
'Non-primary of this' (<s>amukhyo 'sya</s>) — just as there is the usage 'this is the primary meaning' with reference to the stream etc. for the word '<s>Ganga</s>' etc., so too there is the usage 'this is the non-primary meaning' with reference to the bank etc. — this is the meaning.
And thus, the status of being a meaning is equal for both; the difference is produced only by primary-ness and non-primary-ness — this is the purport.
He says that the apprehension of convention (<s>sanketa</s>) too is the same — 'just so' etc.
Just as [there is] apprehension of convention with respect to the primary meaning, just so —

children.translated_text: 'Even there' — even in the figurative domain.
'That alone' — indication alone.
"By connection with the denotatum, by proximity, by association,
by contrariety, and by connection with action — <s>laksana</s> (indication) is declared to be fivefold."

[Balapriya:] He concludes — 'therefore' etc.
'Therefore, he concludes' — this is also a [variant] reading.
Showing the connection of 'therefore' (<s>tasmad</s>) with the <s>karika</s>, he explains that word: 'since' (<s>yatah</s>) etc.
He shows that dependence on signifier-status takes the form of being grounded in that [denotation] — 'that' (<s>tad</s>) etc.
The explanation of 'secondary function' (<s>gunavrtti</s>) is: 'figurative' (<s>gauna</s>) etc.
For the variety of <s>dhvani</s> intended [here] has the definition of 'intended-other-beyond-the-expressible' (<s>vivaksitanyaparavacya</s>).
And many other varieties too are covered by <s>bhakti</s> (metaphorical extension); therefore <s>bhakti</s> is not a [valid] definition.
<s>Locana</s>: Wherever <s>dhvani</s> exists, if <s>bhakti</s> were [also] to exist there, there would be no under-extension.
But this is not the case; in [the type called] <s>avivaksita-vacya</s> (unintended expressible), there is <s>bhakti</s> — [as in] '<s>suvarnapuspam</s>' (golden-blossomed) etc.
But in '<s>sikharini</s>' etc., how [could there be bhakti]?
Now, <s>laksana</s> (indication) at least extends even to the figurative (<s>gauna</s>) [usage].
However, the word merely indicates (<s>laksayitva</s>) that meaning and then enters into co-referentiality (<s>samanadhikaranya</s>) with that very [meaning] — as in '<s>simho vatuh</s>' ('the boy is a lion').
Or, the meaning indicates another meaning, and its own signifier makes the signifier of that [other meaning] co-referential.
Or, the word and meaning together indicate that [other meaning] and become mixed with another pair of word and meaning — thus is the difference of the figurative (<s>gauna</s>) from the indicative (<s>laksanika</s>).
As stated: 'In the figurative, there is word-usage; not in indication' — even there, indication indeed exists; therefore that alone [i.e., indication] pervades everywhere.
<s>Balapriya</s>: In the <s>vrtti</s>, the syntactic connection is: 'they are not covered by' — 'indeed.'
He elaborates the purport — 'wherever' etc.
'In <s>sikharini</s> etc.' — the remainder is: '[which is an example of] <s>vivaksitanyaparavacya</s> (intended-other-beyond-the-expressible).'
'How [could there be]?' — the meaning is: <s>bhakti</s> does not exist.
And thus there is under-extension — this is the purport.
Now, granting that <s>bhakti</s> extends in the figurative domain too, in the example '<s>sikharini</s>' etc. shown as [an instance of] <s>vivaksitanyaparavacya</s>, it [bhakti] operates indeed — so the statement of its absence there is inconsistent — accepting this objection and in accordance with it too, intending to explain the passage beginning with '<s>vivaksitanyaparavacya</s>' etc. for the purpose of instructing the student, he introduces that objection — 'now' (<s>nanu</s>) etc.
'Even the figurative' — even the domain of '<s>simho vatur</s>' etc.
'Extends' — the purport is: because the requisites of <s>laksana</s> (indication) are present.
Now, if so, whence the difference of the figurative from the indicative? — to this he says: 'however' (<s>kevalam</s>) etc., up to 'difference.'
'The word' — the word '<s>simha</s>' (lion) etc.
'That meaning' — the meaning [which is] the boy (<s>vatu</s>) etc.
'With that very [word]' — with the very word '<s>vatu</s>' etc. that signifies the boy etc.
'Enters into co-referentiality' — becomes co-referential.
Co-referentiality of words means: conveying one and the same referent through different forms.
This is the distinguishing feature of the figurative from the indicative — this is the purport.
The same should be understood in what follows too.
'Or, the meaning' — the meaning is: the meaning of the word '<s>simha</s>' etc.
'Another meaning' — consisting of the boy (<s>vatu</s>) etc.
'Its own signifier' — the word '<s>simha</s>' etc.
'The signifier of that' — the word '<s>vatu</s>' etc.
'Or, the word and meaning' — the word '<s>simha</s>' etc. and its meaning.
'That' — the meaning [which is] the boy etc.
'By another pair' — by the word '<s>vatu</s>' etc. and its meaning.
In the reading '<s>tabhyam</s>' too, this is the meaning.
'Become mixed' — mixing means: of the two words, conveying one and the same property-bearer; of the two meanings, being connected in the manner of non-difference.
He states a supporting [citation] for the stated meaning — 'figurative' (<s>gauna</s>) etc.
'In the figurative' — in the figurative domain.
'Word-usage' — the usage of the word that denotes the indicated meaning.
As the <s>Locana</s> states: And that [<s>laksana</s>] is fivefold.
Namely — [1] by connection with the denotatum: for the word '<s>dvirepha</s>' (two-lettered), the denotatum is the word '<s>bhramara</s>' (bee), [derived] as 'that which has two <s>rephas</s>'; by the connection with that word '<s>bhramara</s>,' the meaning [which is] the six-footed [creature] is indicated by the word '<s>dvirepha</s>,' having made the connection with the denotatum — [which is] in the form of being an explanator — as the ground.
[2] By proximity — '<s>Gangayam ghosah</s>' ('the village is on the Ganga').
[3] By association (<s>samavaya</s>) — meaning by [inherent] relation — as in '<s>yastih pravesaya</s>' ('make the sticks enter').
[4] By contrariety — as when someone says to an enemy: '<s>kim iva upakrtam na tena mama</s>' ('what favor has not been done to me by him?').
[5] By connection with action — meaning by the relation of cause and effect — as in the usage regarding a food-thief: '<s>pranaan ayam harati</s>' ('he steals [my] life-breaths').
Thus, by this fivefold <s>laksana</s> (indication), the entire [domain] is pervaded.
For instance — in '<s>sikharini</s>' — <s>Balapriya</s>: In '<s>simho vatur</s>' etc., there is the usage of the word denoting the boy (<s>vatu</s>) etc.
'Not in indication' — the meaning is: in the domain of indication, there is no usage of the word denoting the indicated meaning.
For example, in '<s>Gangayam ghosah</s>' etc., there is no usage of the word denoting the bank etc.
He states the result — 'therefore, even there' etc.
'Therefore' (<s>iti</s>) — this also connects with what precedes.

children.translated_text: "Utility" (<s>upayogaḥ</s>): meaning it certainly exists.
The maxim of "<s>upādāya</s>" etc. demonstrates the reasoning that [something] whose cognition has been accomplished has no [further] utility.
"Those that are to be abandoned even after being adopted — those they call means (<s>upāya</s>);"
"For the restriction regarding means does not necessarily persist."

He explains the statement in parts: 'by the denotatum' etc. /
Here, by the word '<s>saṃyoga</s>' (conjunction), the relation in the form of the signified-signifier relationship is intended; by the word '<s>samavāya</s>' (inherence), the other [relation] — in the form of container-contained, resemblance, etc. — is intended. /
There is also the reading: 'through proximity to the denotatum, resemblance, etc.' /
That very [point] — 'he states the figurative [usage]' — was shown previously. /
'By that' — the meaning is: by that which is the denotatum of the word '<s>dvirepha</s>' (bee/two-<s>repha</s>). /
The construction is: 'of which meaning.' /
The explanation of '<s>saṃyoga</s>' is: 'relation' — the meaning is: a relation consisting of the signified-signifier relationship. /
The connection is: 'having made [it] a cause, [it] is indicated.' /
'From the relation' — the meaning is: from the relation in the form of container-contained. /
'What has been benefited, as it were' — the purport is: here, harm is indicated. /
As in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>: 'benefited by many' etc. /
'<s>Prāṇān</s>' (vital breaths) — the purport is: by the word '<s>prāṇa</s>,' food is indicated. /
'Everything indeed' — the meaning is: everything that has fallen within the domain of secondary usage. /
'For thus' — the meaning is: 'and so.' /
By the passage from 'now' up to '<s>lakṣaṇā</s> exists,' the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) has been stated with acceptance. /
<s>Locana</s>: here, in the incidental question and other [cases] — in the entry of obstructors — because of resemblance, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) indeed exists. /
Now, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> has been accepted here in the middle [of the discussion] — how then was it said [that this is] '<s>vivakṣitānyapara</s>' (where another meaning beyond the intended is primary)? The sub-type intended here is the primary one — '<s>asaṃlakṣyakrama</s>' (with imperceptible sequence). /
And by the word '<s>tadbheda</s>' (its sub-type), the sub-types of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, their semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>), their quiescence (<s>praśama</s>), and their further sub-varieties [are meant]; and in these, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is not tenable. /
For thus: in poetry that conveys <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), since in the primary meaning there is not even the conceivability of the entry of an obstructor — what scope is there for <s>lakṣaṇā</s>? /
Now, what need for obstruction? This alone is the essential nature of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>: 'The cognition inseparable from the denotatum is called <s>lakṣaṇā</s>' [quoting the <s>Bhaṭṭavārtika</s>]. /
And here, <s>rasa</s> etc. are indicated as inseparable from the denotata — <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, etc. — because <s>vibhāva</s> and <s>anubhāva</s> have the nature of cause and effect [respectively with regard to <s>rasa</s>], and because the <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) are their auxiliaries — [one might argue thus]. /
Not so; for if by the word 'smoke,' when smoke is cognized, the subsequent recollection of fire too were to be effected by <s>lakṣaṇā</s> alone, then from fire, the recollection of removal of cold — and so on — the meaning of the word would be unresolved [endlessly]. /
If [you say]: because the word 'smoke' rests in its own meaning, there is no operation extending that far — then it has been conceded that the obstruction of the primary meaning is the life-breath of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>; for when that [obstruction] obtains, there is absence of resting in one's own meaning. /
And there is no obstructor whatsoever in the conveying of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: He resolves [this]: 'now, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> has been accepted here' etc. /
The meaning is: the acceptance of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> in '<s>śakharinī</s>' etc. was previously shown. /
He asks: 'how then' etc. /
The meaning is: how is what was said in the <s>vṛtti</s> — '<s>vivakṣitānyapara</s>' — consistent? /
The purport is: because when <s>lakṣaṇā</s> obtains, the intended-ness (<s>vivakṣitatva</s>) of the expressible is impossible. /
He answers: 'its sub-type' etc. /
The meaning is: by the word '<s>vivakṣitānyapara-vācya</s>' in the <s>vṛtti</s>, the sub-type — the primary one, <s>asaṃlakṣyakrama</s> (with imperceptible sequence) — is intended. /
'By the word <s>tadbheda</s>' — the meaning is: by the word '<s>tadbheda</s>' in the <s>vṛtti</s> passage '<s>tadbheda-prakārāḥ</s>' (the modes of its sub-types). /
'And their further sub-varieties' — the meaning is: <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, <s>hāsya</s>, etc. /
'Here too, why should <s>lakṣaṇā</s> not obtain?' — to this he says: 'not' etc. /
He elaborates the non-tenability: 'for thus' etc. /
'The entry of an obstructor too' — the word '<s>api</s>' (also) cumulates [this with] the purpose. /
He raises the objection: 'now' etc. /
'What need for obstruction' — whether it exists or not, what result follows from considering the obstruction of the primary meaning? — this is the meaning. /
'This alone' — what is about to be stated: this is the meaning. /
'<s>Abhi</s>' — [in '<s>abhidheya</s>'] — through some relation connected with the denotatum; the cognition of that which is inseparable — i.e., knowledge — or that which causes [such knowledge]. /
'Thus' — this is what is stated in the <s>Bhaṭṭavārtika</s>: this is the meaning. /
He applies [this] to the present case: 'here' etc. /
Here — in <s>dhvani</s> with imperceptible sequence. /
The connection is: '<s>rasa</s> etc. are indicated by the cause of the inseparable.' /
He substantiates the inseparability: '<s>vibhāva</s>' etc. /
'Cause' etc. — '<s>rasa</s>' is to be supplied. /
He resolves [this]: 'not so' etc. /
Intending to show that the obstruction of the primary meaning is indeed the seed of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, he first states the over-extension: 'by the word smoke' etc. /
'Fire' etc. — because fire is inseparable from smoke: this is the purport. /
'The meaning of the word' — the meaning of the word 'smoke': this is the meaning. /
The <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> resolves the stated over-extension: 'of the word smoke' etc. /
'In its own meaning' — in smoke, or in what is qualified by it. /
'Because of resting' — because of having completed the operation of producing cognition. /
'That far' — in the meaning of fire etc. /
'Then it has been conceded' — the <s>siddhāntin</s> (proponent) says: 'it has been conceded' etc. /
'The life-breath' — the meaning is: the seed. /
<s>Locana</s>: Now, [one might argue:] just as after cognizing smoke, the recollection of fire [occurs] — similarly, after cognizing <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., the cognition of mental dispositions such as <s>rati</s> (love) etc. [occurs] — and there is no word-operation here at all. /
Now, this knower of the nature of cognition — the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> — should be asked this: Is your intended '<s>rasa</s>-cognition' here [in poetry] merely the cognition of another's mental disposition? One should not err thus; for in that case, since it would be merely the inference of worldly mental dispositions, what <s>rasa</s>-ness would there be? /
But the extra-worldly (<s>alaukika</s>) aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) that is the savoring of <s>rasa</s>, whose life-breath is the relishing of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. present in poetry — that should not be reduced to the level of stale [experience] by equating it with recollection, inference, etc. /
Rather, one whose heart has been cultivated by worldly cause-and-effect inference etc., while cognizing the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. [in poetry], does not cognize them with detachment; rather, /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'seed' — this is the meaning. /
'Seed — the life-breath' — this is also a reading. /
'From what [evidence]?' — to this he says: 'when that obtains' etc. /
'That' — the meaning is: the obstruction of the primary meaning. /
Even when the capacity to denote its own meaning is the same, the word 'smoke' rests in its own meaning. /
'On the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the hamlet' — here the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' does not [denote <s>Gaṅgā</s> itself] — here the obstruction of the primary meaning alone is the cause; of that alone is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> the seed: this is the meaning. /
'Then here too there would be obstruction of the primary meaning and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>' — that this is not so, he says: 'and not' etc. /
He raises the undesired consequence by way of incidental discussion: 'now, thus' etc. /
The cognition of mental dispositions such as <s>rati</s> etc., which follows upon the cognition of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., is just like the recollection of fire etc. produced by the cognition of smoke etc. — hence it is not produced by word-operation; far removed is its being produced by suggestion (<s>vyañjanā</s>): this is the meaning. /
The formulation: 'The cognition in question — of <s>rati</s> etc. — is not verbal (<s>śābdī</s>), because it is produced by cognition of word-generated meaning — like the recollection of fire etc. produced by the cognition generated by the word smoke.' /
What is it that you wish to establish here — that the cognition of another's mental disposition such as <s>rati</s> is not produced by word-operation? Or that <s>rasa</s>-cognition [is not]? In the first case, [the argument] proves what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>); in the second, there is the defect of absence of an example, since <s>rasa</s>-cognition is distinct from other cognitions — with this intention, he asks mockingly: 'this' etc. /
He elaborates the question: 'what' etc. /
'Here' — the meaning is: in poetry. /
'One should not' — the meaning is: one should not err thus. /
'From what [evidence]?' — to this he says: 'for thus' etc. /
'Thus' — if the <s>rasa</s>-status is accepted as merely the cognition of worldly mental dispositions. /
'Merely' — the remainder after this is: '<s>rasa</s>-cognition.' /
'What <s>rasa</s>-ness?' — for the usage of the word '<s>rasa</s>' is motivated by the quality of being relishable (<s>rasanīyatā</s>). /
And the cognition that has the nature of inference does not possess relishability — because it is not observed in the inference of fire etc.: this is the meaning. /
'What then is <s>rasa</s>-cognition?' — to this he says: 'but that which' etc. /
'Extra-worldly (<s>alaukika</s>)' — by this, worldly pleasant experience is excluded. /
Showing the reason for its extra-worldly nature, he states its cause: 'of poetry' etc. /
'That' (<s>asau</s>) — that savoring of <s>rasa</s>. /
'By equating with recollection and inference' — the construction of this is with 'reduced to staleness.' /
'Worldly' — the meaning is: occurring in the world. /
'Cause' etc. — 'cause' is [things like] fire and smoke, <s>rati</s> etc. being [known through] sidelong glances etc. /
'Cause' is fire etc.; 'effect' is smoke etc., of mental dispositions such as <s>rati</s> — sidelong glances etc. /
And the inference of the cause through the effect — by '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), inclusion of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). /
'By that' — 'the heart has been cultivated' — by this, it is shown that the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the cognizer too is useful in <s>rasa</s>-cognition. /
'<s>Vibhāvas</s> etc.' — the meaning is: <s>pramadā</s> (beautiful women) etc. /
'While cognizing' — the remainder is: from poetry or drama. /
'With detachment' — the meaning is: as belonging to another. /
'Does not cognize' — the connection of '<s>vibhāvas</s> etc.' applies here too. /
'How then does that cognition [arise]?' — to this he says: 'rather' etc. /
'Of the heart' — <s>Locana</s>: through the arising of savoring, beautiful with the impressions of mental dispositions appropriate to <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions) and <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) — becoming complete in the about-to-be-fulfilled savoring of <s>rasa</s> — as a sprout-like emergence — without ascending the path of inference, recollection, etc., through the appropriateness of becoming absorbed in identification (<s>tanmayībhavana</s>) — whose life-breath is relishing. /
And that relishing is not produced from any other means of knowledge previously; otherwise there would be recollection now. /
Nor is it produced now from any other means of knowledge — because in the extra-worldly [domain], perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) etc. have no operation. /
For this very reason, the usage of '<s>vibhāva</s>' etc. [as technical terms] is itself extra-worldly. /
As it is said: '<s>Vibhāva</s> is for the purpose of special cognition — in the world, only "cause" is spoken of, not "<s>vibhāva</s>." /
<s>Anubhāva</s> (consequent) too is extra-worldly. /
"Because this <s>anubhāva</s> — the enactment performed through speech, body, and temperament — causes [one] to experience [the <s>sthāyins</s>], therefore [it is called] <s>anubhāva</s>." /
For that experiencing-as-absorption in the corresponding mental dispositions is indeed the experiencing [meant here]. /
But the world says only "effect," not "<s>anubhāva</s>." /
For this very reason, and with the intention that another's mental disposition is not cognized [in <s>rasa</s>-experience], the word '<s>sthāyin</s>' (permanent emotion) was not included in the <s>sūtra</s>: "<s>rasa-niṣpatti</s> (the arising of <s>rasa</s>) [results] from the combination of <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, and <s>vyabhicārin</s>." /
That [inclusion of <s>sthāyin</s>] would rather become a thorn [in the argument]. /
The <s>rasa</s>-status of the <s>sthāyin</s>, however, is spoken of due to propriety.' /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'of the heart — accord' — accord means agreement; that whose alternate name is <s>sahṛdayatva</s> (connoisseurship) — being compelled by that: this is the meaning. /
'About to be fulfilled' — the savoring of <s>rasa</s> that is about to become complete — of that wish-fulfilling tree that will bear the fruit of cultivation in the four aims of life (<s>caturvarga</s>) — by the sprout-like emergence, as cause: this is the meaning. /
'Inference' etc. — the meaning is: without resorting to the means of inference, recollection, etc. — i.e., without relying on the knowledge of invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) etc. /
'Becoming absorbed' — the identification of connoisseurs with the respective mental dispositions — the arousal of one's own similar mental dispositions through the contemplation of each mental disposition — that is the experiencing: this is the meaning. /
'Universally' — this is the extent. /
The connection is: 'cognizes <s>vibhāvas</s> etc.' /
When <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. are cognized universally — then alone is there <s>rasa</s>-relishing: this is clear from elsewhere. /
He refutes [the objection that <s>rasa</s>-cognition] has the nature of recollection etc.: 'and not' etc. /
'For this very reason' — because <s>rasa</s>-cognition is extra-worldly, the usage of '<s>vibhāva</s>' etc. for its causes is [itself] extra-worldly: this is the meaning. /
'As it is said' — 'by the sage [<s>Bharata</s>]' is to be supplied. /
'<s>Vibhāva</s> is for the purpose of special cognition' — '<s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) are so called because' the <s>sthāyins</s> and <s>vyabhicārins</s> 'are specially known through them.' /
Indeed, cognition does not arise from <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) alone, since <s>anubhāvas</s> such as tears can have multiple causes — [hence the need for <s>vibhāvas</s>]: this is the meaning. /
'In the world' etc. — the usage for causes of mental dispositions in the world is only 'cause,' not '<s>vibhāva</s>': this is the meaning. /
'That which this one' — the construction is: 'this is the <s>anubhāva</s>.' /
'Causes to experience' — the remainder is: the <s>sthāyins</s> and <s>vyabhicārins</s>. /
'<s>Anubhāva</s>' — the remainder after this is: 'is said to be.' /
The experiencing [meant here is] the experiencing of connoisseurs (<s>sāmājika-sahṛdaya</s>) through the identification with the respective mental dispositions brought about by the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. — and [as discussed] in the <s>Rasagaṅgādhara</s> etc. /
Here, he says that the experiencing is distinct from worldly experiencing: 'that mental disposition' etc. /
Not merely the cognition of another's mental disposition — that is the experiencing here; rather, the identification of one's own [mental disposition] with those mental dispositions — the arousal of one's own mental disposition of the same kind through the contemplation of <s>sthāyins</s> etc. — that is the experiencing: this is the meaning. /
He cites the authority for the stated meaning: 'for this very reason' etc. /
For this very reason — because experiencing is of the stated nature and not merely the cognition of another's mental disposition — therefore, from this reason: this is the meaning. /
'Not another's' etc. — rather, one's own mental disposition alone is experienced by the audience members: this is the meaning. /
'Was not included' — to this the question: 'of which?' — to satisfy [this], '[in] the <s>sūtra</s>.' /
The connection of '<s>sthāyin</s>' is: '<s>Locana</s>: through the arising of savoring, beautiful with the impressions of mental dispositions appropriate to <s>bhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s>, and from the cognition of the <s>sthāyin</s> — <s>rati</s> etc. — [ascertained] through gardens, thrilling of the hair, etc. /
For the accord of the heart is the foundation of <s>rasa</s>-relishing, and the basis of the accord of the heart is knowledge of worldly mental dispositions — because without that, the accord of the heart does not arise. /
And in that state, through causes such as beautiful women etc., through effects such as thrilling of the hair etc. — which are ascertained again and again as pervaded by their own causes — the cognition of the permanent [emotion] such as <s>rati</s> etc. arises; and from that [as well]: this is the meaning. /
Now, since the <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) too has the nature of mental disposition, [one might argue that] it too, like the <s>sthāyin</s>, does not deserve inclusion in the <s>sūtra</s> — to this he says: 'the <s>vyabhicārin</s>' etc. /
The <s>vyabhicārins</s>, being subordinate to the <s>sthāyin</s>-mental-disposition as <s>guṇas</s> (accessories) — and being like <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. in their proximity — were enumerated among them: this is the meaning. /
By way of incidental discussion, he elaborates the <s>rasa-niṣpatti</s> (arising of <s>rasa</s>) stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'for this very reason' etc. /
'The arising of <s>rasa</s>-ness — this alone is the arising' — this is the arising stated in the <s>sūtra</s>. /
The arising of <s>rasa</s>-ness: this is the meaning. /
As stated in the <s>Abhinavabhāratī</s>: 'How then [is the word] arising [used] in the <s>sūtra</s>? This is not the arising of <s>rasa</s> [itself], but rather of <s>rasa</s>-relishing pertaining to it; if the arising of <s>rasa</s> — whose life depends solely on that [relishing] — is [thereby] spoken of, then there is no defect here.' /
'What indeed is this <s>rasa</s>-relishing?' — therefore he states its essential nature: 'that which' etc. /
'By the narrative' — by the narrative [of poetry] come forth causes such as the meeting of kinsmen etc.; the worldly mental disposition such as joy etc. that arises from those — by the subordination, i.e., suppression, i.e., exclusion, of that: this is the extent. /
He states the essential nature of relishing: 'therefore' etc. /
Therefore — because of being extra-worldly due to distinction from worldly mental dispositions. /
Here, 'relishing' is the relishing pertaining to <s>rasa</s>. /
He shows what is excluded by the particle '<s>eva</s>': 'but not' etc. /
Just as the operation of the sense-faculties etc. is cognition-production (<s>jñāpana</s>), or just as the operation of the staff, the potter's wheel, etc. is production (<s>utpādana</s>) — similarly, <s>Locana</s>: now, if this is neither cognition-production nor production, then what is it? This is not extra-worldly — <s>rasa</s> [is not]. /
Now, is <s>vibhāva</s> etc. here a cognition-producer (<s>jñāpaka</s>), a cause (<s>hetu</s>), or a producer (<s>kāraka</s>)? It is not a cognition-producer, not a producer; rather, it is useful for relishing. /
Now, where else has this been seen? Precisely because it has not been seen — that is why it has been called extra-worldly. /
Now, thus <s>rasa</s> would not be a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>)! Let it be so — what of it? Because the attainment of delight and cultivation is accomplished through that very relishing — what else need be demonstrated? /
Now, this is without valid basis (<s>apramāṇaka</s>)! Not so — because it is established through self-cognition (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>). /
Because a specific type of knowledge itself has the nature of relishing — enough of prolixity. /
And therefore this <s>rasa</s> is extra-worldly. /
By which [reasoning] even the graceful and harsh <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), though useless for conveying meaning, has suggestive power with respect to <s>rasa</s>; what suspicion could there even be of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> there? The relishing of <s>rasa</s> is seen through the very pressing of the poetic word. /
For that very poetry, again and again — <s>Bālapriyā</s>: the operation of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. is neither cognition-production nor production: this is the meaning. /
He raises the objection: 'now' etc. /
By the previously stated [reasoning], this <s>rasa</s>-relishing is not of the nature of cognition-production, nor of the nature of production — this has been established; then of what nature [is it]?: this is the meaning. /
'This' — the meaning is: of the nature of <s>rasa</s>-relishing. /
He answers: 'now, this' etc. /
The purport is: the unfitness for cognition-production and production, due to the extra-worldly nature of <s>rasa</s>, becomes an ornament [i.e., a virtue, not a defect]. /
Now, in the absence of cognition-producer or producer status, the inclusion of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. for the sake of <s>rasa</s>-cognition is pointless; and if that [status] were present, the extra-worldly nature of <s>rasa</s> would be lost — he objects: 'now' etc. /
For the rule that a cause (<s>hetu</s>) must be either a producer or a cognition-producer is worldly; but <s>vibhāva</s> etc., even in the absence of that [rule], is useful for relishing — hence not purposeless: with this intention, he resolves: 'not a cognition-producer' etc. /
He objects further upon that: 'now' etc. /
He resolves: 'precisely because' etc. /
He objects again: 'now' etc. /
'Thus' — the meaning is: given the extra-worldly nature of <s>rasa</s>. /
'<s>Rasa</s> would not be a means of valid knowledge' — and if not a valid means of knowledge, it would not produce knowledge of the means to attain the good and avoid the bad: this is the purport. /
Even when invalidity seems to follow, there is causal efficacy — he says: 'let it be so' etc. /
'Of delight and cultivation' — delight and cultivation; of those — or: cultivation preceded by delight; of that accomplishment: this is the meaning. /
Now, given the extra-worldly nature of <s>rasa</s>, there is no means of valid knowledge to establish it — he objects: 'now' etc. /
He resolves: 'not so' etc. /
Now, given the acceptance that <s>rasa</s> has the nature of specific relishing, how can there be establishment through self-cognition? — to this apprehension he says: 'of a specific knowledge' etc. /
As stated in the <s>Abhinavabhāratī</s>: 'And relishing is indeed of the nature of cognition (<s>bodha</s>); but it is distinct from other cognitions — because of the extra-worldly distinctness of its means, the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc.' /
He establishes once more the extra-worldly nature of <s>rasa</s>: 'and therefore' etc. /
For if <s>rasa</s> were cognizable only through the signifying word, its worldliness like that of the expressed meaning could somehow be suspected; but suggestiveness (<s>vyaṅgyatva</s>) belongs even to <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) etc., which are devoid of signifying capacity. /
And the suggested object of <s>anuprāsa</s> is not seen in the world — therefore, from this too, the extra-worldly nature of <s>rasa</s> is established: this is the meaning. /
Having thus established the extra-worldly nature of <s>rasa</s>, he connects [this] to the topic at hand: 'what' etc. /
'There' — the meaning is: when <s>rasa</s> is suggested even by <s>anuprāsa</s>. /
'What [suspicion of] <s>lakṣaṇā</s>' — in the absence of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) itself, there is simply no occasion for <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, which depends on the back of that: this is the meaning. /
He cites the experience as evidence for the suggestive power of the word's own form, independent of the denotative operation: 'of the poetic word' etc. /
'The poetic word' — [a word] distinguished by <s>anuprāsa</s> etc.; its pressing, i.e., repetition, is 'of that.' /
'That relishing' — <s>rasa</s>-relishing. /
He elaborates on what was stated: 'is seen' etc. /
The very poetry that was read and relished — that itself is read and relished again and again: this is the meaning. /
'But not' — of the poetry whose cognition-function has been completed — of the poetic word; there, in <s>rasa</s>-relishing, /
uselessness — but not [otherwise].
