children.translated_text: Precisely therefore, the author of the treatise has stated in general the absence of <s>bhakti</s> (portion) in the <s>vivakṣitānya-para-vācya</s> type of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: asmābhistu durdurūṭaṃ pratyāyayitumuktam--bhavatvatra lakṣaṇā, alakṣyakrame tu kupito 'pi kiṃ kariṣyasīti /
children.translated_text: But we have explained, to make the difficult understandable: "let there be <s>lakṣaṇā</s> here; but in [the type whose] sequence is imperceptible — even if angry, what will you do?"

children.text: yadi tu na kupyate 'suvarṇapuṣpāṃ' ityādāvavivakṣitavācye 'pi mukhyārthabādhādilakṣaṇāsāmagrīmanapekṣyaiva vyaṅgyārthaviśrāntirityalaṃ bahunā /
children.translated_text: But if one does not object — even in the <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> [type], as in "<s>suvarṇapuṣpām</s>" etc., without depending on the aggregate of conditions for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> such as sublation of primary meaning etc., the repose in the suggested meaning —
He concludes — "therefore <s>bhakti</s>" etc. // 18 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Meaning: according to this maxim. The purport is: this very maxim does not apply here. He states the resultant meaning — "<s>iti</s>" etc. He says that the imperceptibility of sequence in the suggested, which was stated, also conduces to the stated meaning — "precisely therefore" (<s>ata eva</s>) etc. "Precisely therefore": because the word by its very own form, without depending on the denotation of meaning, has the suggestive capacity. The purport is: if the word's suggestive capacity were dependent only on the intervening cognition of meaning, then the sequence would necessarily be perceptible.

"There would be a division of the sentence" (<s>vākyabhedaḥ syāt</s>): the purport is because poetry produces the cognition of two meanings — the expressible and the suggested. He substantiates what was stated as "due to unfamiliarity with that" — "<s>śāstra</s>" (treatise) etc. "<s>Śāstra</s>": a sentence other than poetry. "Convention" (<s>samaya</s>): by the force of the convention (<s>saṅketa</s>) of each word for each meaning, meaning with the cooperation of grasping each respective convention. "Conveying the meaning" — this contains the reason. "Simultaneously" (<s>yugapat</s>): at one time. "Contradictory" (<s>viruddha</s>): contradictory by pertaining to contradictory meanings. Alternatively: the impossibility arises because the recollections of the conventions of two contradictory meanings cannot be simultaneous. The purport is: where the context etc. pertains to one meaning, the recollection of the convention for the other meaning is blocked.

"Two meanings" (<s>arthadvayam</s>): a pair of contradictory meanings. "How would it convey" — meaning: it would not produce cognition. "Non-contradictoriness" (<s>aviruddhatva</s>): meaning when there is mutual relationship through directly being connected with one action. "Of the two meanings" — the connection is by inversion. An example of this should be understood: "the white one runs; <s>Mādhava</s> who gives everything, drink" etc.

"Of such extent" (<s>tāvān</s>): meaning of just that extent which is cognized. "The sentence-meaning would be one" — the purport is that division in the sentence-meaning is not accepted. "In sequence" (<s>krameṇa</s>): the connection is: how would a treatise convey two meanings? Here he states another reason — "having paused" (<s>viramya</s>) etc. "Having paused" — since the operation of the word that has paused has no connection; therefore — this is the meaning. "That very" (<s>sa eva</s>): that sentence-meaning which was cognized — this is the meaning. The word "<s>eva</s>" is repetitive. Here he states the reason — "due to convention, context, etc." (<s>samaya-prakaraṇādeḥ</s>).

<s>Locana</s>: "Absence of restriction" (<s>niyamābhāva</s>) — therefore, [the maxim is like] "one who desires heaven should perform the <s>agnihotra</s>" —

children.text:
nanu mā bhūddhvaniriti bhaktiriti caikaṃ rūpam /
mā ca bhūdbhaktirdhvanerlakṣaṇam /
upalakṣaṇaṃ tu bhaviṣyati; yatra dhvanirbhavati, tatra bhaktirapyastīti bhaktyupalakṣito dhvaniḥ /
na tāvadetatsarvatrāsti, iyatā ca kiṃ parasya siddhaṃ? kiṃ vā naḥ truṭitaṃ? iti tadāha---kasyacidityādi /

saṃvedayanta iti /
jānantītyarthaḥ /
ata evādau tathā vyākhyātamiti bhāvaḥ /
atra granthakṛdvacanaṃ saṃvādayati---ata evetyādi /

nāstikamayavāggrastamityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: "Has been stated" (<s>ity uktam</s>) — this is the connection.

children.text: nanu kasya nāma kopastattvaṃ kathyatāmityatrāha---yadi tviti /
children.translated_text: Now, whose anger is it? Let the truth be told! — To this he says "but if" (<s>yadi tu</s>) etc.
"Repose in the suggested meaning" (<s>vyaṅgyārtha-viśrāntiḥ</s>) —
The purport is that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is not capable [of operating] even in the desired domain. // 18 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Now, let it not be that "<s>dhvani</s>" and "<s>bhakti</s>" are one and the same form. And let <s>bhakti</s> not be the definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of <s>dhvani</s>. But it will be an indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>): wherever there is <s>dhvani</s>, there <s>bhakti</s> also exists — thus <s>dhvani</s> is indicated by <s>bhakti</s>. Now, this is not the case everywhere; and with just this much, what has the opponent established? Or what of ours has been broken? — Therefore he says "of a certain [kind]" (<s>kasyacit</s>) etc. Now, <s>bhakti</s> has been discussed by the etymologists (<s>nairukta</s>); and through the indication by <s>bhakti</s>, <s>dhvani</s> too — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the excellence of the kind described, not shared by anything else, is from that alone — this is the meaning. "They perceive" (<s>saṃvedayante</s>): meaning they know. Therefore it was so explained at the beginning — this is the purport.

children.text:

children.translated_text:
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Now, to reject even the <s>upalakṣaṇa</s> (indicator) position, he raises the doubt — preceded by a restatement of the <s>vṛtti</s> — with "now" (<s>nanu</s>) etc., up to "<s>dhvani</s> indicated by <s>bhakti</s>." To [the question] "how will it be an indicator?" he says "where" (<s>yatra</s>) etc. Just as a crow etc. [perched on] a house is neither the essential nature [of the house] nor its definition, but merely from its occasional presence serves as a cause for the cognition of distinction — so too <s>bhakti</s>. This is the meaning.

He introduces the <s>kārikā</s> as a response to this — "now, to begin with" (<s>na tāvat</s>) etc. "<s>Tāvat</s>" is for [indicating] agreement. "This" (<s>etat</s>): meaning the <s>upalakṣaṇa</s>. The meaning is: it is agreed that the indicator-entity does not exist everywhere. "With just this much" (<s>iyatā ca</s>) etc. —

children.text: lakṣaṇe 'nyaiḥ kṛte cāsya pakṣa-saṃsiddhir eva naḥ // DhvK_1.19a //
children.translated_text: "And when a definition has been made by others, the establishment of our position is assured." // <s>DhvK</s> 1.19a //
"And when a definition has been made by others, the establishment of our position is assured." // 19 //

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā:] "Of all" —
meaning: of both the worldly and the learned.
"Through hyperbole" (<s>atiśayokti</s>) —

children.text: yathā 'tānyakṣarāṇi hṛdaye kimapi sphuranti' itivadatiśayoktyānākhyeyatoktā sārarūpatāṃ pratipādayitumiti darśitamiti śivam // 19 //
children.translated_text: Just as inexpressibility is stated through hyperbole such as "those syllables somehow flash in the heart," [the purpose is] to establish [<s>dhvani</s>'s] essential nature — thus it has been shown. <s>Śivam</s> (auspiciousness). // 19 //

[Locana:] Even if the definition of <s>dhvani</s> has already been formulated by others, our position is still established; for "<s>dhvani</s> exists" is not [merely] a thesis — it has already been established, and thus we have accomplished our desired aim effortlessly.
Those who have declared the nature of <s>dhvani</s> to be merely something experienced in the hearts of the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (connoisseurs), something inexpressible — they too are not opponents who have examined [the matter carefully].
[Locana:] They will comprehend and come to know its complete classification.
Anticipating the objection "what is the use of that definition," he says — "if indeed" (<s>yadi ca</s>).
For the relation of expression and expressed meaning pervades all the <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech); and so, once the function of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) has been examined by grammarians and <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, where then is any scope for the work of <s>alaṅkārikas</s> (rhetoricians)?
Likewise, once the logicians have stated that effects arise through the force of causes, what new task would remain for <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) and other agents or knowers — thus everyone would be without enterprise.
Therefore he says — "there would follow the futility of definition and formulation."
Or even if it is not a new unveiling, but rather what was previously unveiled has been properly examined by us — even so, what fault is there? With this intention he says — "moreover" (<s>kiṃ ca</s>) etc.
"Previously" (<s>prāge</s>) — the remainder is: "through our effort."
Thus, in refuting the three-fold denial doctrine and the view of subsumption under <s>bhakti</s> (figurative usage), the view of indefinability has also been refuted as one among them.
Therefore no root verse (<s>mūlakārikā</s>) is heard that directly refutes it.
[Bālapriyā:] But the author of the <s>vṛtti</s> (prose commentary), even though it has been refuted, explicitly restates it for the sake of completeness of the subject matter. Regarding the function of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) —
"Of the <s>alaṅkārikas</s>" — meaning: of the authors of treatises on <s>alaṅkāra</s> (poetic ornamentation).
"Where then is their scope" — since the relation of expression and expressed meaning pervades all <s>alaṅkāras</s>, and since that [relation] depends on the function of <s>abhidhā</s>, once that has been examined, the examination of <s>alaṅkāras</s> by their authors would indeed be fruitless — this is the meaning.
He reveals yet another undesirable consequence — "likewise" (<s>tathā</s>) etc.
The connection is: "what new [task] would there be?"
"Thus" (<s>iti</s>) — in the sense of reason.
"Everyone would be without enterprise" — "everyone" means the class of agents and knowers beginning with <s>Īśvara</s>.
He connects the explained meaning with the text — "therefore he says" (<s>tadāha</s>).
"The futility of definition and formulation" — <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (definition) and <s>karaṇa</s> (formulation) together are <s>lakṣaṇakaraṇa</s>; the implication of futility of both, i.e., of their examination — this is the meaning.
He introduces the text beginning with "moreover" — "let it not be" (<s>mā</s>) etc.
The syntactical connection is: "let there be no new unveiling."
Addressing the doubt — why did the author of the <s>kārikās</s> not explicitly reject the view of indefinability, as he did the other positions? — he introduces the passage beginning with "those who also" (<s>ye 'pi</s>).
"Has indeed been refuted" — for the refutation of other positions has been accomplished here through the demonstration of <s>dhvani</s>; and since that [demonstration] is not possible if [<s>dhvani</s>] is indefinable, the indefinability position too has been refuted as a necessary consequence — this is the meaning.
Then why did the author of the <s>vṛtti</s> cite and refute that position? To this he says — "the <s>vṛttikṛt</s>" (the commentator).
"The arrangement of the subject matter" (<s>prameyaśayyā</s>) — the particular arrangement of the subject matter: even though the general and specific definitions of <s>dhvani</s> have been established by the method stated and to be stated, if its inexpressibility were accepted, that would apply to all things whatsoever.
But if the <s>dhvani</s>, through the hyperbolic expression (<s>atiśayokti</s>), surpasses other kinds of poetry — [Locana:] having cited their position, he refutes it with "those who also" (<s>ye 'pi</s>) etc.
By the method stated, the general definition "where the meaning or the word" has been established.
By the method to be stated, the specific definition will be given through "transferred to another meaning" (<s>arthāntare saṅkramitam</s>) etc.
There, in the first <s>uddyota</s> (illumination), only the general definition of <s>dhvani</s> has been formulated by the author of the <s>kārikās</s>.
In the second <s>uddyota</s>, the author of the <s>kārikās</s>, presenting the sub-classification and the specific definition, states through repetition the primary division: "it is twofold" (<s>dvividhaḥ</s>).

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā:] With the intention that everything is of the nature of <s>Paramaśiva</s> (the Supreme <s>Śiva</s>), he concludes — "<s>Śivam</s>" (auspiciousness).
By the word "thus" (<s>iti</s>), there is a reference back to his own commentary.
Moreover, "<s>Śivam</s>" — being in the form of a reference to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), it is the supreme benediction.
[Vṛtti:] Their essential nature is being described — those too are indeed proper speakers.

[Bālapriyā:] "Of that" (<s>tasyāḥ</s>) — for the completion [of the subject]. If the indefinability position were not itself refuted, that completion would not occur — this is the implication.
Regarding "by the method stated" etc., indicating that the connection is according to enumeration, he explains — "where the meaning" (<s>yatrārtha</s>) etc.
"Specific definition" — meaning: the statement of the specific definition.
The statement of the specific definition in the <s>vṛtti</s> beginning with "and it is twofold" (<s>sa ca dvividhaḥ</s>) is in accordance with the intent of the author of the <s>kārikās</s> — thus he says: "there, in the first <s>uddyota</s>" etc.
"There" — among the general and specific definitions.
The syntactical connection is: "he stated the primary division" (<s>mūlavibhāgam avocad</s>).
Now, if what has been stated is that the inexpressibility of <s>dhvani</s> is not due to its non-existence nor due to its being defective, but rather due to its surpassing excellence — then it is entirely proper to express it. With this [thought] the <s>vṛtti</s> says — "but if" (<s>yadi punar</s>) etc.
"Surpassing other poetry" (<s>kāvyāntarātiśāyi</s>) — meaning: surpassing <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (poetry where suggestion is subordinate) and <s>citra</s> (pictorial poetry).
"Essential nature" (<s>svarūpam</s>) — meaning: its nature as the essence.
"By them" (<s>taiḥ</s>) — meaning: by the <s>pūrvapakṣins</s> (objectors).
"That" (<s>tad</s>) — meaning: "then" (<s>tarhi</s>).
"Those also" (<s>te 'pi</s>) etc. — meaning: their statement is proper since it accords with our own view.
Here, it should be understood that through the word "also" (<s>api</s>) in "those also" (<s>te 'pi</s>), the author of the text indicates his own appropriateness of expression everywhere.
About to comment on the word "through hyperbole" (<s>atiśayoktyā</s>) found in the <s>vṛtti</s>, he first gives an example of <s>atiśayokti</s> — "just as those" (<s>yathā tāni</s>) etc.
"Drowsy-eyed from sleep, languid with intoxication, those [syllables] of hers, neither meaningful nor meaningless, even now, O deer-eyed one, [flash] sweetly" — [this is] the first three quarters [of the verse].
The commentary on "through this hyperbole" is: "through hyperbole, the statement of inexpressibility."
He completes [the sense] — "in order to establish the essential nature."
By this, it is shown that the meaning of the word <s>rūpa</s> in "surpassing other poetry in nature" is "being the essence."
After "in order to establish," the remainder is: "by the method stated."

children.text: locana.m kiṃ locanaṃ vināloko bhāti candrikayāpi hi /
children.translated_text: [Locana:] What — does <s>āloka</s> (light) shine even with moonlight, without the <s>Locana</s> (eye)?
Therefore <s>Abhinavagupta</s> has here performed the opening of the <s>Locana</s> (eye).
By whose very power of opening, the universe opens forth in an instant —
I venerate that <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuition), auspicious, resting in the abode of the Self.

Thus [ends] the first <s>uddyota</s> (illumination) in the <s>Sahṛdayālokalocana</s> (the Eye of the Connoisseur's Light), unveiled by the venerable great <s>Māheśvara</s> master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, in the investigation of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text:

ālokaḥ kāvyālokagranthaḥ /
candrikayā anyakṛtayā candrikākhyavyākhyayā /
api kiṃ bhāti na bhātītyarthaḥ /
hīti prasiddhe 'vadhāraṇe vā /
atha ca locanaṃ netraṃ vinā /
lokaḥ bhūvanam /
candrikayā jyotsnayā, api kiṃ bhāti kiṃ sphurati na pratyakṣaviṣayo bhavatītyaprastutārthaḥ tatsāmyaṃ cātra dhvanyate /
teneti /
tasmāddhetorityarthaḥ /
athodyotānte 'pyanuṣṭhitaṃ maṅgalaṃ nibadhnāti---yaditi /
yasyāḥ śakteḥ unmīlanayuktyā spandanayogainaiva /
viśvaṃ sarvaṃ vastu /

pratibhāṃ jñānātmikām /

children.translated_text: <s>Śivā</s> (auspicious) — named <s>Śiva</s>.
That power (<s>śakti</s>) — I venerate.

children.text: atha ca yasyāḥ pratibhāyāḥ unmīlanayuktyā prakāśayogena /
children.translated_text: And also: by whose <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuition), through the means of opening, through the connection of manifestation,

children.text: viśvam kṣaṇādunmīlati navanavatayā bhāti svātmanyevāyatane viśrāntāṃ vāsanārūpeṇāvasthitām, śivāṃ rasāveśavaiśadyasubhagām, tāṃ pratibhāṃ kavīnāṃ prajñām, vande ityādyartho 'pi bodhya iti sarvaṃ śivam // 19 //
children.translated_text: the universe opens forth in an instant, shining with ever-new freshness; resting in the Self itself as the abode, established in the form of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>); auspicious (<s>śivā</s>), beautiful with the clarity of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic savoring) and immersion; that <s>pratibhā</s> — the creative wisdom of poets — I venerate. This alternative meaning too should be understood. Thus, all is auspicious (<s>śivam</s>). // 19 //

[Bālapriyā:] In his own commentary, for the purpose of engaging the audience, he says — "what" (<s>kim</s>) etc.
<s>Locana</s> — this commentary named <s>Locana</s>.
<s>Āloka</s> — the text <s>Kāvyāloka</s> (Light of Poetry).
"With moonlight" (<s>candrikayā</s>) — with a commentary called <s>Candrikā</s> composed by another.
"Does it shine?" — the meaning is: does it not shine? It does not.
"Indeed" (<s>hi</s>) — in the sense of well-known [fact] or emphasis.
And also: "<s>Locana</s>" [means] the eye, without which — "<s>loka</s>" [means] the world — "with moonlight" (<s>candrikayā</s>), with the light of the moon — "does it shine?" — does it become visible, does it become an object of direct perception? — this is the implied meaning, and the similarity between the two is suggested here.
"Therefore" (<s>tena</s>) — meaning: for that reason.
Then, at the end of the <s>uddyota</s> too, having performed the established benediction, he composes — "that which" (<s>yad</s>).
By whose power (<s>śakti</s>), through the means of opening, through the connection of vibration (<s>spandana</s>) alone,
the universe — all things — opens forth, becomes manifest, in an instant.
"In an instant" — by this, independence [from other causes] is indicated.
"In the Self" (<s>svātmani</s>) — in one's own essential nature.
Or alternatively: resting in <s>Brahman</s>-consciousness itself as the abode, the locus.
<s>Pratibhā</s> — of the nature of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>).

children.text: prauḍhaṃ kva locanaṃ mandaḥ kvāhaṃ tena mayā kṛtā /
children.translated_text: Where is the profound <s>Locana</s>, and where am I, a dullard? Yet by me has been composed
this annotation (<s>ṭippaṇī</s>) following earlier commentaries — let the wise correct it.
Thus [ends] the first <s>uddyota</s> in the annotation on the <s>Locana</s>, composed by the connoisseur's ornament, king of scholars, the illustrious <s>Rāmaśāraka</s>.

children.text:
dvitīya uddyotaḥ
/ śrīrastu /
dvitīya uddyotaḥ evamavivakṣitavācyavivakṣitānyaparavācyatvena dhvanirdviprakāraḥ prakāśitaḥ /
tatrāvivakṣitavācyasya prabhedapratipādanāyedamucyate--
children.translated_text:
Second <s>Uddyota</s> (Illumination).
May there be prosperity.
Second <s>Uddyota</s>. [Vṛtti:] Thus <s>dhvani</s> has been shown to be of two kinds, by way of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (unintended literal meaning) and <s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s> (intended other-than-literal primary meaning).
Of these, for the purpose of establishing the sub-divisions of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s>, the following is stated —
[That whose literal meaning has been] transferred to another meaning, or completely obscured —

children.text: avivakṣita-vācyasya dhvaner vācyaṃ dvidhā matam // DhvK_2.1 //
children.translated_text: the literal meaning of <s>dhvani</s> whose expressed sense is unintended is regarded as twofold. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.1 //
[That whose literal meaning has been] transferred to another meaning, or completely obscured —
the literal meaning of <s>dhvani</s> whose expressed sense is unintended is regarded as twofold. // 1 //

children.text: locanam dvitīya uddyotaḥ yā smaryamāṇā śreyāṃsi sūte dhvaṃsayate rujaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Locana:] Second <s>Uddyota</s>. She who, when remembered, produces blessings and destroys afflictions —
that auspicious <s>kalpavallī</s> (wish-fulfilling creeper), bountiful with desired fruits — I praise.

children.text:
vṛttikāraḥ saṅgatimuddyetasya kurvaṇa upakramate--
evamityādi /
prakāśita iti /
mayā vṛttikāreṇa sateti bhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: And this was not stated by me as my own aphorism, but rather in accordance with the intent of the author of the <s>kārikās</s> — thus he says —
"of these" (<s>tatra</s>) —

children.text: tatra dviprakāraprakāśane vṛttikārakṛte yannimittaṃ bījabhūtamiti bālapriyā dvitīya uddyotaḥ locanasyottarasyāto na vyākhyā prapyate 'tra tat /
children.translated_text:
[Bālapriyā:] Second <s>Uddyota</s>. "Of these" — in the showing of the two kinds done by the <s>vṛttikāra</s>, what served as the seminal basis — the commentary on the subsequent <s>Locana</s> is not available here.
Therefore,
I shall comment briefly according to my understanding — may the learned be gracious to me herein.

[Locana:] The author of the <s>vṛtti</s>, establishing the connection (<s>saṅgati</s>) of the <s>uddyota</s>, begins —
"thus" (<s>evam</s>) etc.
"Has been shown" (<s>prakāśitaḥ</s>) — the sense is: by me, the <s>vṛttikāra</s> (commentator).

children.translated_text: The elaboration of '<s>sikarinah</s>' (bearing fine spray) is —
'fine' (<s>suksma</s>) etc.
'Thus' (<s>iti</s>) —

children.text: kāmaṃ santu dṛḍhaṃ kaṭhorahṛdayo rāmo 'smi sarve sahe vaidehī tu kathaṃ bhaviṣyati hahā hā devi dhīrā bhava //
children.translated_text: 'Let it be — I am firmly hard-hearted <s>Rama</s>, I endure all; but how will <s>Vaidehi</s> fare? Alas, alas, O goddess, be steadfast!'

[Balapriya:] '<s>Ya</s>' (which) — which is auspicious (<s>siva</s>).
'Being remembered by people' — while being remembered, she produces (<s>sute</s>), i.e., generates, their well-being (<s>sreyamsi</s>).
'<s>Rujah</s>' — calamities.
'<s>Abhista</s>' — a generous bestower of desired fruits.
Or alternatively — that in which there are desired fruits, which is great (<s>udara</s>) — [she is like] a <s>kalpavalli</s> (wish-fulfilling creeper) — 'her' — this is a <s>rupaka</s> (metaphor).
As <s>Amara</s> [i.e., the <s>Amarakosa</s>] states: '<s>udara</s> [means] a giver and [one who is] great.'
'The connection of the <s>Uddyota</s>' — the meaning is: the connection of the Second <s>Uddyota</s> with the First <s>Uddyota</s>.
'Of the stated with the forthcoming' — the meaning is: the connection of what has been said with what is about to be said.
And that connection here should be understood as having the nature of an occasion (<s>prasanga</s>).
'Effecting' (<s>kurvana</s>) — accomplishing.
'Commences' (<s>upakramate</s>) — begins to state.
Because it was not illuminated by the <s>sutrakara</s> (author of the aphorisms), he says — 'by me myself' etc.
He introduces the passage beginning with 'therein' — with 'and not' (<s>na ca</s>) etc.
'This' (<s>etad</s>) — the meaning is: the twofold nature.
'Beyond the <s>sutra</s>' (<s>utsutram</s>) — transgressing the <s>sutra</s>; meaning: not intended by the <s>sutrakara</s>.
The word 'therein' (<s>tatra</s>) — intending [to ask] whether it is a reference to the action of illuminating the stated two varieties, he explains — 'the illumination of the two varieties' etc.
'The cause' (<s>nimittam</s>) — either [means] the statement of the 'therein'-meaning, or it is filled in [as implied].
The elaboration of this very [point] is — 'being the seed' (<s>bijabhutam</s>).
Its syntactic connection is with '[it] is stated' (<s>ucyate</s>).
'Thus the connection' — the meaning is: thus is the connection of the preceding and the following.
He explains otherwise — 'or alternatively' (<s>yadi va</s>) etc.
'Sequel of the preceding' (<s>purvasesha</s>) — connected with the preceding.
At the end of the First <s>Uddyota</s>, by the <s>vrttikara</s> — <s>Locana</s> — the connection.
Or alternatively — 'therein' is a sequel of the preceding.
'Therein' — in the First <s>Uddyota</s>, by the <s>vrttikara</s>, the sub-variety (<s>avantara-prakara</s>) of <s>avivaksita-vacya</s> (unintended expressible) that was illuminated — for the elucidation of that, this is stated.
And through the very medium of elucidating those sub-varieties, and through the medium of restatement (<s>anuvada</s>), the distinctness of the variety of <s>avivaksita-vacya dhvani</s> from <s>vivaksitanyaparavacya</s> (intended-other-beyond-expressible) — for the elucidation of that, this is stated.
Fundamentally, the twofold division is approved even by the <s>karikakara</s> (author of the verses) — this is the purport.
'Transferred' (<s>sankramitam</s>) — by the causative suffix (<s>nic</s>), [it is indicated that] the group of auxiliaries (<s>sahakarivarga</s>) in the operation of suggestion (<s>vyanjana-vyapara</s>) — this is their power, as stated; and by the word 'concealed' (<s>tiraskrta</s>) [likewise].
The syntactic connection is: 'the expressible (<s>vacya</s>) by which, being unintended (<s>avivaksita</s>), the <s>dhvani</s> is designated as <s>avivaksita-vacya</s> — that expressible is twofold.'
That meaning which, even though it fits (<s>upapadyamana</s>), due to being of no use merely to that extent, having gone as it were to otherness (<s>anyata</s>) through association with another property (<s>dharmantara-samvalana</s>), being indicated (<s>laksyamana</s>), possessing a continuous underlying property-bearer (<s>anugata-dharmin</s>), abides by the principle of a thread (<s>sutra-nyaya</s>) — that is called 'transformed into another form' (<s>rupantara-parinata</s>).
<s>Balapriya</s>: Since it was said 'thus ends the First <s>Uddyota</s>,' in this interpretation, the word 'therein' (<s>tatra</s>) refers back to that — he says: 'the First <s>Uddyota</s>' etc.
To show its syntactic connection with what precedes, he says: 'by the <s>vrttikara</s>, illuminated' etc.
In this interpretation, the remainder 'therefore' (<s>atah</s>) should be understood.
He explains the passage beginning with '<s>avivaksite</s>' etc. — '<s>avivaksitavacyasya</s>' etc.
'Sub-variety' (<s>avantara-prakara</s>) — sub-property (<s>avantara-dharma</s>).
'This' (<s>idam</s>) — the meaning is: the <s>sutra</s> from '<s>arthantara</s>' (another meaning) up to '<s>matam</s>' (approved).
To establish the connection with what will be stated in '<s>athasamlaksyakramoddyota</s>' etc. as well, he also explains otherwise — '<s>tadavantara</s>' etc.
The elucidation of the sub-varieties beginning with '<s>arthantare sankramitam</s>' — through that very medium, preceded by that very [elucidation].
The restatement (<s>anuvada</s>) of <s>avivaksita-vacya dhvani</s> — through that medium.
The syntactic connection of this is with 'is stated' (<s>ucyate</s>).
'Of <s>avivaksita-vacya</s>' — the meaning is: that which pertains to it (<s>tadanuyogika</s>).
Keeping in mind what will be stated, he said '<s>vivaksitanyaparavacyat</s>.'
'Distinctness' (<s>prabhinnatva</s>) — mutual absence (<s>anyonyabhava</s>).
'For the elucidation of that' — for making that known.
'This' — the meaning is: [the concept of] <s>avivaksita-vacya</s>.
He states the result — 'fundamentally' (<s>bhavati</s>) etc.
'Fundamental twofold nature' — the original duality.
The syntactic connection of 'by the causative' (<s>nica</s>) is with 'stated' (<s>ukta</s>).
'Which' (<s>yah</s>) — the meaning is: <s>laksana</s> (indication), the speaker's intention (<s>vaktrvivaksa</s>), etc.
'This' (<s>ayam</s>) — transference (<s>sankramana</s>).
'Its power' (<s>tasya prabhavah</s>) — produced by it.
He himself is the instigating agent (<s>prayojaka-karta</s>) — this is the purport.
'Stated' — let it be understood.
And by the word 'concealed' (<s>tiraskrta</s>) — its syntactic connection is with 'stated' (<s>uktam</s>).
He elaborates on '<s>avivaksite</s>' etc. — 'by which' (<s>yena</s>) etc.
'By the expressible' (<s>vacyena</s>) — the meaning is: by the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) qualified by the universal (<s>jati</s>) etc. denoted by the respective words.
He elaborates '<s>arthantare sankramitam</s>' etc. — 'that meaning which' (<s>yo 'rthah</s>) etc.
'That meaning' — the meaning such as tranquility (<s>sama</s>) etc. in [the verse] 'I am <s>Rama</s>' etc.
'Even though it fits' — even though it is capable of syntactic connection through the mode of the universal etc. [denoted by] the expressible.
'Due to being of no use' — due to absence of utility by reason of not contributing any distinguishing feature, or by reason of redundancy.
'Through association with another property' — by virtue of being the content of a cognition whose mode is a property other than the expressible property.
'Being indicated' — being cognized through <s>laksana</s> (indication).
Hence indeed, 'having gone as it were to otherness.'
Or alternatively — 'through association with another property,' by virtue of the reason that it is the content of a cognition whose mode is a property other than the expressible property, 'having gone as it were to otherness,' 'being indicated' — being cognized.
'Possessing a continuous underlying property-bearer' — even though the indicated properties differ in each case, the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) in the form of the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) is continuous — this is the purport.
'By the principle of a thread' (<s>sutra-nyaya</s>) — just as a single thread is strung through flowers etc., so too — this is the meaning.
And by those two of such a kind — of the suggested alone there is a distinction.
Therein, [the type called] <s>arthantara-sankramita-vacya</s> (expressible transferred to another meaning) is as follows —
'With a greasy dark-blue radiance coating the sky, with swelling, stirring herons, dense clouds, winds bearing fine spray, the delightful peacock-calls of the friends of rain-clouds —'
<s>Locana</s>: 'That which, even though not fitting, merely through the medium of expediency, [causes] the cognition of another meaning — runs away as it were — that is the concealed [type]' — thus.
Now, when the division of the suggested (<s>vyangya</s>) is being determined, the statement of division as 'the expressible is twofold' is not consistent — anticipating this objection, he says: 'of such a kind' (<s>tathavidhabhyam ca</s>) etc.
The word '<s>ca</s>' is in the sense of 'because.'
For it is proper that from the diversity of the suggestor there should be diversity of the suggested — this is the purport.
However, if the word '<s>dhvani</s>' refers to the meaning [i.e., the suggested], then there is no defect — this is the purport.
With the intention that the very name indicating the division establishes the definition as well, he states only the example — '<s>arthantara-sankramita-vacya</s>, as follows' etc.
In this verse, the word '<s>Rama</s>' — this is the connection.
'Greasy' (<s>snigdha</s>) — succulent from contact with water. 'Dark-blue' (<s>syamala</s>) — of the dark color befitting a <s>Dravida</s> woman. With the radiance (<s>kanti</s>), i.e., the luster, that is 'greasy and dark-blue,' the sky (<s>viyat</s>) is coated, i.e., smeared — by which [clouds]. 'Stirring' (<s>vellantya</s>) — expanding; or moving due to being driven by the wind and due to joy.
<s>Balapriya</s>: '<s>Rupantara-parinata</s>' (transformed into another form) — this is itself the elaboration of '<s>arthantare sankramitam</s>' (transferred to another meaning).
'That which' (<s>yah tu</s>) — the meaning is: the meaning of words such as '<s>andha</s>' (blind) etc. in [the verse] '<s>nisvasandha</s>' (blinded by sighs) etc.
'Not fitting' (<s>anupapadyamanah</s>) — not capable of syntactic connection.
'Merely through the medium of expediency' — because the connection with the primary meaning serves as the ground of <s>laksana</s> (indication): this is the purport.
'Concealed' (<s>tiraskrta</s>) — 'stated' (<s>ukta</s>) is to be supplied.
'Now' (<s>nanu</s>) — of the suggested <s>dhvani</s>, i.e., of the referent of the word '<s>dhvani</s>' which is the suggested.
'If' (<s>yada</s>) — [means] 'when.'
The syntactic connection is: 'the statement of division of the expressible.'
In the <s>vrtti</s>, '<s>tathavidhabhyam</s>' — the meaning is: by the two [types] <s>arthantara-sankramita</s> and <s>atyanta-tiraskrta</s>.
'By those two' (<s>tabhyam</s>) — by the two [types of] expressible.
'Distinction' (<s>visesa</s>) — difference.
After '<s>visesa</s>,' some texts have the reading: 'thus, this variety belongs to <s>dhvani</s> alone, which is directed toward illuminating the suggested.'
In the <s>Locana</s>, he states the purport — 'however, if the meaning [is intended by <s>dhvani</s>]' etc.
'The meaning of the word <s>dhvani</s> is the suggestor' — if so: this is the meaning.
'That' (<s>sa ca</s>) — that meaning is either a meaning or a word.
Therein, in the first alternative, the meaning of '<s>avivaksitavacyasya</s>' should be understood as stated at the beginning of the First <s>Uddyota</s>: 'that whose expressible, i.e., own form (<s>svatma</s>), is unintended, i.e., not made primary.'
'Defect' (<s>dosa</s>) — the meaning is: the defect stated in the introduction.
'Luster' (<s>cakacakya</s>) — the meaning is: sparkling radiance.
'Expanding' (<s>vijrmbhamanah</s>) — meaning: full of vigor.
'Due to being driven by the wind' — because of the dark color of the clouds and the white color of the herons: this is the purport.
'Due to joy' — due to the joy born from the attainment of association with clouds: this is the meaning.
The elaboration of 'dense' (<s>ghana</s>) is — 'clouds' (<s>megha</s>).
By '<s>ghana</s>,' density is also conveyed.
By '<s>velladbalaka</s>' (stirring herons), the power to evoke the memory of union (<s>sambhoga</s>) [is also conveyed].
Hence he says — 'thus the sky' (<s>evam nabhah</s>) etc.

children.translated_text: A confection prepared with jaggery is a <s>guḍamodaka</s> (jaggery-sweet); [the experience] that is like the savoring of that — the variegated, distinctive aesthetic savoring (<s>carvaṇā</s>), which enters into each and every quality as belonging to <s>Rāma</s> — [this] is the ground for that. And as in my own [verse] on the sport of the uneven-arrowed one (<s>Viṣamabāṇa</s>, i.e., <s>Kāma</s>) —

children.text: tālā jāanti guṇā jālā de sahiaehiṃ gheppānti /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] Qualities arise when they are grasped by the sensitive-hearted (<s>sahṛdayas</s>).
Nurtured by the sun's rays, lotuses become [truly] lotuses!

[<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Sita</s>-birds' — a particular species of white birds in which [they appear]. Thus the sky remains difficult to perceive for that long. /
The directions too are unbearable. /
Because 'the winds that emit fine water droplets' — their gentle-gentleness and their coming from no fixed direction are indicated by the plural number. /
'Then let one enter and sit in the caves somewhere' — to this he says: /
Those who are the friends of the clouds, and among them, the peacocks who have beautiful hearts — their joyful, harmonious, sweet <s>kekā</s>-calls (distinctive cries) — all these remind one of the unbearable story of the clouds; and they themselves are unbearable — this is the purport. /
Thus, [the hero] whose <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) has been aroused by the <s>uddīpana-vibhāvas</s> (excitant causes), considering the commonality of the <s>vibhāvas</s> with [himself and] his beloved due to the mutuality of <s>rati</s> (love), from this point onward, having placed his beloved in his heart, first narrates his own circumstances — /
'<s>Kāmaṃ santv</s>' (let them be as they wish) — thus. /
'<s>Dṛḍham</s>' (firmly) — in the sense of intensity. /
'<s>Kaṭhorahṛdaya</s>' (hard-hearted) — thus. /
The word '<s>kaṭhorahṛdaya</s>' is used to provide scope for the suggestion of particular meanings of the word '<s>Rāma</s>.' /
Just as when '<s>tadgeham</s>' (that house) is said, [additionally] '<s>natabhitti</s>' (with bowed walls) [is specified]. /
Otherwise, how would the word '<s>Rāma</s>' not suggest the meaning colored by other qualities such as being born in <s>Daśaratha</s>'s lineage, being the object of <s>Kausalyā</s>'s affection, childhood exploits, winning <s>Jānakī</s>, etc.? /
'<s>Asmi</s>' (I am) — thus. /
'<s>Bālapriyā</s>': '<s>śīkarim</s>' — by the reason of indicating the connection with water-spray — this is the meaning. /
The word '<s>mandamandatvam</s>' (gentle-gentleness) has its connection with '<s>sūcitam</s>' (indicated). /
He shows what is suggested by the plural — '<s>eṣām</s>' (of these) — thus. /
'<s>Suhṛda</s>' (friend) — the meaning is: kinsman. /
He states another meaning — '<s>teṣu</s>' (among them) — thus. /
'<s>Śobhanahṛdayā</s>' (beautiful-hearted) — precisely therefore '<s>ānanda</s>' (joy) — this is the purport. /
Showing that because the melodiousness is caused by joy, the <s>kekā</s>-calls qualified by it are also caused by joy, he says — 'by joy, the melodious [calls]' — thus. /
'<s>Evam</s>' (thus) etc. — /
By the previously mentioned <s>uddīpana-vibhāvas</s> (excitant causes), his <s>vipralambha</s> (separation) has been aroused — [he is one] whose <s>rati</s> (love) is delimited by the time of separation. /
'<s>Paraspara</s>' (mutual) etc. — /
Because <s>rati</s> (love), which is of the nature of regarding each other as one's entire life, belongs mutually [to both] man and woman — this is the meaning. /
Of the <s>vibhāvas</s> — the rain-clouds filled with water, etc. /
'Commonality' — commonality with the beloved. /
'<s>Abhimanyamāna</s>' (considering) — the meaning is: examining. /
'<s>Ita</s>' (from here) — the meaning is: from '<s>kāmam</s>' onwards. /
'<s>Tāvad</s>' (first) — the meaning is: at first. /
'<s>Kāmaṃ santv</s>' — the meaning is: let them be as they wish. /
'<s>Rāmaśabdārtha</s>' etc. — the meaning is: the word '<s>Rāma</s>' serves as an auxiliary in the suggestion of particular meanings. /
'<s>Tadgeham</s>' (that house) — this verse will be cited in the Third <s>Uddyota</s>. /
'<s>Anyathā</s>' (otherwise) — the meaning is: in the absence of '<s>kaṭhorahṛdaya</s>.' /
'Childhood exploits' — the meaning is: such as the practice of learning, the slaying of <s>Tāṭakā</s>, etc. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the conquest of <s>Paraśurāma</s> and such [events] are included. /
'Winning' etc. — whatever other qualities [there are], colored by them — having as its object a cognition of that form. /
'How would it not suggest' — thus. /
And thus the word '<s>kaṭhorahṛdaya</s>' is indicated as having been specified as an auxiliary for the suggestion by the word '<s>Rāma</s>' of only those qualities that are consonant with that meaning — this is the purport. /
'I bear everything' — whatever suffering befalls, I bear all of it — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Vaidehī</s>' — here is the word '<s>Rāma</s>.' /
For by this, the referent colored by other suggested qualities is conveyed, not merely the referent. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The meaning is: 'I shall be just this.' /
'Will be' — is a general verb-form. /
Thereby the meaning is: what will [he/she] do? /
And yet — her very existence is inconceivable — thus. /
Having placed in his heart the beloved in the manner described, through a succession of memory, words, and mental deliberation, [she has been] made present before him, and being on the verge of his heart bursting, he says with agitation — '<s>hahā ha</s>' — thus. /
'<s>Devī</s>' — the meaning is: your fortitude is fitting. /
By this — by the word '<s>Rāma</s>' whose meaning is not [directly] applicable — this is the purport. /
The suggested content, in the form of purpose, is the immeasurable exile from the kingdom, etc. /
And that, being innumerable, cannot be conveyed through the operation of denotation. /
Even when conveyed sequentially, because it cannot become the object of a single cognition, it is not the ground of variegated aesthetic savoring, and thus does not produce supreme charm. /
But when suggested, that innumerable [content], precisely through the non-emergence of distinctness, bears — what form does it not bear? — and becomes the ground of variegated aesthetic savoring like the flavors of beverages, sweetmeats, jaggery-sweets, and confections. /
As stated: 'What cannot be expressed by any other utterance' — thus. /
'<s>Bālapriyā</s>' — and by this, the incapacity to endure suffering is suggested. /
'General verb-form' — the remainder is: it makes known. /
Even in the primary meaning, the intention [is present] — he says: 'and yet' etc. /
He introduces the fourth quarter-verse — 'as stated' etc. /
'Memory' — the recollection of the rain-cloud etc. as <s>uddīpaka</s> (excitant) belonging commonly [to both]. /
'Word' — the word '<s>Vaidehī</s>,' the cognition born from it — this is the extent. /
'Mental deliberation' — the speculation 'how will [she] survive?' /
Through a succession of these — this is the meaning. /
He explains the passage beginning with '<s>vyaṅgya</s>' (suggested) etc. — '<s>vyaṅgyam</s>' etc. /
'Purpose' — the meaning is: the purpose of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary meaning). /
'Then what?' — to this he says: 'of the kingdom' etc. /
'Of the kingdom' — the meaning is: from the loss of the kingdom. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), all suffering such as forest-exile, separation from father and wife, etc. is included. /
Intending to establish its suggestedness, he says: 'and that' etc. /
'That' — that purpose. /
'Denotation' etc. — the meaning is: incapable of being denoted all at once. /
'Sequentially' — 'that' and 'through the operation of denotation' are to be supplied. /
'Of a single cognition' — the meaning is: because of the absence of being the object of a single cognition. /
'When suggested' — the meaning is: when manifested. /
The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) indicates distinction. /
'That innumerable' — the meaning is: the purpose qualified by innumerability. /
'Non-emergence of distinctness' — non-emergence means indistinctness; distinctness means mutual difference, i.e., separation — the meaning is: precisely through being qualified by that. /
Just as in savoring the flavor of beverages etc., the portions of camphor etc. are not experienced separately, but only through their mutual intermingling — similarly, in the cognition of purpose, the qualities such as exile from the kingdom etc. — this is the meaning. /
'What form' — the meaning is: it bears manifold forms. /
Through the varied nature of the recipient's imagination etc., it appears in manifold ways — this is the extent. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — in the sense of reason. /
'Variegated' etc. — 'variegated' is the qualifier of the three [items] — beverages, etc. — meaning 'of various flavors.'
(<s>Chāyā</s>:) Then qualities arise when they are grasped by the sensitive-hearted (<s>sahṛdayas</s>).
Nurtured by the sun's rays, lotuses become [truly] lotuses!

children.translated_text: For the meaning obstructed by irrelevance is the domain of this <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion); <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary meaning) is indeed its basis.

children.text: yattu hṛdayadarpaṇa uktam---'hahā heti saṃrambhārtho 'yaṃ camatkāraḥ' iti /
children.translated_text: However, what was stated in the <s>Hṛdayadarpaṇa</s>: 'The exclamation "<s>hahā ha</s>" expresses agitation (<s>saṃrambha</s>), [and] this is aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>)' — thus.

Even in that [interpretation], <s>saṃrambha</s> (agitation) is <s>āvega</s> (impetuosity), a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) of <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) — therefore <s>rasa-dhvani</s> (suggestion of <s>rasa</s>) is at least accepted.
And without the assistance of the meaning manifested by the word '<s>Rāma</s>,' there is no delight in agitation (<s>saṃrambha</s>) either.

(Thus the <s>chāyā</s>.) /
Here the second word '<s>kamala</s>' (lotus) — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] This very [principle] should be understood everywhere as the cause of excellence through the suggestedness of purpose. /
By the word '<s>mātra</s>' (merely), [he indicates that] the referent is not disparaged here — he says: 'as also' etc. /
'<s>Tālā</s>' — then (<s>tadā</s>). /
'<s>Jālā</s>' — when (<s>yadā</s>). /
'<s>Dheppanti</s>' — are grasped (<s>gṛhyante</s>). /
He states the corroboration through another meaning — 'by the sun's rays' etc. /
'The word <s>kamala</s>' — the meaning is: [the word] conveys the referent colored by hundreds of other qualities such as being the receptacle of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, etc. /
Therefore, in the pure primary meaning, the obstruction-cause is [present]; in that meaning, the co-presence of those qualities [exists]. /
By that cause, the word '<s>Rāma</s>' [conveys] a meaning colored by other qualities — '<s>Bālapriyā</s>' — this is the meaning. /
The statement that the totality of purposes cannot be denoted — he provides support for that — 'as stated' etc. /
'This very [principle]' — the meaning is: precisely [its being] the ground of variegated aesthetic savoring. /
'Of purpose' — accompanied by excellence. /
'By the word <s>mātra</s>' — the meaning is: by the word '<s>mātra</s>' occurring in the <s>vṛtti</s> passage 'not merely the referent.' /
'He says' — the <s>vṛtti</s>-author makes known — this is the meaning. /
Here the supporting [evidence] for the word '<s>Rāma</s>' as <s>lakṣya</s> (denoting through secondary meaning) — the delimiting condition of <s>Rāma</s> being the <s>lakṣya</s> of the word '<s>Rāma</s>' is either [its] being the denotatum of the word '<s>Rāma</s>' in general, or [its] being the object of suffering — this should be understood. /
'That' — the remainder is: 'the word-meanings.' /
'Then' — being endowed with qualities, those word-meanings having qualities — existing thus — /
'Arise' — come into being. /
'When?' — to this he says — 'when' etc. /
'Those' — those qualified word-meanings. /
'Are grasped' — are appreciated. /
With the intention that the latter half supports [the former] through corroboration, he says — 'he states corroboration' etc. /
'By the sun' — nurtured by the sun's rays, touched by [his] hand-rays, and moreover cherished — lotuses, the water-flowers. /
'<s>Kamalāni</s>' (lotuses) — become known as lotuses — this is the meaning. /
Here he shows the suggested content — '<s>Lakṣmī</s>' etc. /
'Being the receptacle of <s>Lakṣmī</s>' — being the abode of beauty. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), being possessed of bloom, fragrance-endowment, etc. are included. /
'Being the receptacle of <s>Lakṣmī</s>' etc. — whatever hundreds of other qualities [there are] — the variegated nature of those, qualified by that variegated nature — 'that' is the extent. /
'Colored by that' — this is the meaning. /
The referent — the lotus. /
'Conveys' — suggests. /
Some [say] that here the word '<s>Rāma</s>' suggests <s>arvedas</s> (absence of bliss) etc. through secondary meaning by [the quality of] being possessed of exile-from-kingdom etc. /
Similarly in the word '<s>kamala</s>' too it should be understood — they say. To refute that view, he presents — 'therefore' etc. /
'Therefore' — the meaning is: by the reason to be stated. /
Its connection is with '<s>aprātītikam</s>' (not based on apprehension). /
'In the pure primary meaning' — the meaning is: in the mere primary meaning of the word '<s>Rāma</s>.' /
'Obstruction' — the meaning is: obstruction in the form of inapplicability to the present context. /
'In that meaning' — the meaning is: in the referent as the substrate of the word '<s>Rāma</s>' in its primary sense. /
'Co-presence of those qualities' — the meaning is: the connection with the qualities such as exile-from-kingdom etc. that are intended. /
By this, the connection in the form of container-content between the primary meaning has been demonstrated. /
'In both' — the remainder is: it exists. /
'Colored by other qualities' — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] denotes through secondary meaning (<s>lakṣayati</s>). /
The suggested contents, uncommon, not denotable by words — are other qualities. /
Similarly the word '<s>kamala</s>.' /
But the word '<s>guṇa</s>' (quality) conveys merely the referent — thus. /
Therein, what has been forcibly imposed by some — that is not based on apprehension (<s>aprātītikam</s>).

kamalapade ca kaḥ saṃrambha ityāstāṃ tāvat /
anupayogātmikā ca mukhyārthabādhātrāstīti lakṣaṇāmūlatvādavivakṣitavācyabhedatāsyopapannaiva śuddhārthasyāvivakṣaṇāt /

mukhyārthasya padārthāntarānvayānupapattijñānamiva prakṛtānuṣayuktatvajñānamapi lakṣaṇābījamato 'nupayuktatvajñānarūpo 'pi mukhyārthabādhāpadārtha ityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Of the meaning in the form of a particular (<s>vyakti</s>) qualified by class (<s>jāti</s>) etc., as expressed [by the word]' — this is the meaning. /
'Of that too' — /

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] The <s>atyanta-tiraskṛta-vācya</s> (completely concealed expressed meaning) [is exemplified] as in the case of the first poet <s>Vālmīki</s>: 'The moon, whose beauty has passed to the sun, whose orb is veiled by frost,
does not shine, like a mirror blinded by breath.'

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'I endure' — '<s>tasyāḥ kiṃ vartate</s>' ('what is the matter with her?') — such indeed is the nature of the agitation (<s>saṃrambha</s>). /
'And in the case of <s>kamala</s> (lotus), what agitation [is there]?' — let that be set aside for now. /
'And the sublation of the primary meaning in the form of inapplicability exists' — therefore, since it is rooted in <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication), its status as a variety of <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> (unintended expressed) is indeed established, because the pure meaning is not intended to be expressed. /
'The meaning in the form of a particular (<s>vyakti</s>) qualified by properties such as exile from the kingdom etc., as denoted by the word <s>Rāma</s>' — this is the meaning. /
'Then what is suggested?' — to this he says: '<s>vyaṅgyāni</s>' etc. /
'Inexpressible by words' — incapable of being denoted by words. /
'Other properties' — other properties such as despondency (<s>nirveda</s>), languor (<s>glāni</s>), delusion (<s>moha</s>), etc. /
'Likewise with the word <s>kamala</s> (lotus)' — /
The second word <s>kamala</s> indicates a meaning transformed into [the quality of] being a receptacle for <s>Lakṣmī</s> etc.; but the suggested [meaning] is charm (<s>manoharatva</s>) etc. — this is the meaning. /
'Qualities are born' — here the word <s>guṇa</s> does not recur [in a second sense]; the second word <s>guṇa</s> [does not] indicate a meaning transformed into other properties such as excellence etc. — to remove such a doubt he says: 'the word <s>guṇa</s>' etc. /
'Merely a proper name' — /
'Merely the primary meaning' — this is the meaning. /
'Not a meaning transformed into other properties' — this is the meaning of the word '<s>mātra</s>' (merely). /
'Therein' — /
'In the two examples stated earlier' — this is the meaning. /
'By force' — by the power of the intellect. /
'Superimposed' — /
'Stated through superimposition' — this is the meaning. /
'That' — /
'That which was stated' — this is the meaning. /
'Not established by apprehension' — /
'Not established by the apprehension of connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>)' — this is the meaning. /
Here he states the reason: '<s>anupayoga</s>' etc. /
'Sublated by inapplicability' — dependent on sublation in the form of inapplicability. /
'<s>Hi</s>' — in the sense of reason. /
'The meaning' — the meaning stated by you, [namely] the meaning of exile from the kingdom etc. /
'Is the domain of this <s>dhvani</s>' — /
'Is the domain of the <s>dhvani</s>-operation pertaining to the <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> level' — this is the meaning. /
'But not the domain of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>' — this is the purport. /
'For through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, the apprehension of meaning is only through one type of property, not through many types of properties.' /
However, here <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is an auxiliary — he says: '<s>lakṣaṇā</s>' etc. /
'<s>Yat tu</s>' etc. /
'<s>Haha</s>' etc. /
'By this [exclamation] <s>hahā he</s>, the meaning — [i.e.] the effect — of the agitation toward the cows' — this is the meaning. /
'Even therein' — is a restatement; 'even though it has the stated meaning' — this is the meaning. /
The gloss of '<s>saṃrambha</s>' (agitation) is: '<s>āvega</s>' (impetuous rush). /
'<s>Rasa-dhvani</s>' etc. /
'The <s>rasa-dhvani</s> that is not approved by you is accepted first' — this is the meaning. /
And thus the acceptance of the <s>artha-dhvani</s> (content-suggestion) stated earlier /
has also followed as a consequence — he says: '<s>na ca</s>' etc. /
'The meaning manifested by the word <s>Rāma</s>' — /
'The meaning of exile from the kingdom etc.' — this is the meaning. /
He states the reason for the stated meaning: '<s>ahaṃ sahe</s>' etc. /
'"I endure everything" — the meaning manifested by the word <s>Rāma</s> is a reinforcement of this meaning' — this is the purport. /
In the two stated examples, he himself elucidates the sublation of primary meaning and thereby establishes the status as a variety of <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s>: '<s>anupayogātmikā ca</s>' etc. /
'The cognition of unfitness for connection with another word-meaning, just like the cognition of the impossibility of syntactic connection of the primary meaning, is also a seed of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>; therefore the entity [called] sublation of primary meaning is also in the form of cognition of unfitness' — this is the meaning. /
'Here' — /
'In the two stated examples' — this is the meaning. /
'Of the pure meaning' — /

children.translated_text: 'Like a mirror' — this is the meaning. /
He states the reason for 'not appropriate' with a humorous [allusion]: '<s>Jaiminīya</s>' etc. /

children.text: gaaṇaṃ ca mattamehaṃ dhārāluliajjuṇāiṃ a vaṇāiṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prākrit verse:] The sky with intoxicated clouds, the forests with <s>Arjuna</s> trees tossed by rain-showers,
and the nights, dark yet with a humble moon — they captivate.

Thus. /
Here the word '<s>andha</s>' (blind) — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Not concealment in the form of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), since even that much [concealment] is carried over [to other examples]. /
And for this very reason, the expression '<s>ādikavi</s>' (first poet) is used as indicating the transformed expressed meaning. /
He states that <s>dhvani</s> is well-known as an object of indication: '<s>ravi</s>' etc. /
This is a description of winter at <s>Pañcavaṭī</s>, spoken by <s>Rāma</s>. /
'Blind' — one whose sight is impaired. /
'Even of one born blind' — because the impairment of sight [occurs] in the womb. /
'"This one is blind, he does not see even what is in front"' — here the concealment of the meaning of '<s>andha</s>' is not complete. /
But here, even the blindness being superimposed upon a mirror cannot be accepted — /
The word '<s>andha</s>' here, taking as its ground (<s>nimitta</s>) the inability to make clear the reflected image which belongs to one who has lost sight, indicates the mirror through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication). /
It suggests innumerable purposes — the entire mass of properties such as extraordinary dimness, inapplicability, etc. /
<s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s>, however, said: 'Even here the <s>iva</s>-word ("like") brings about figuration (<s>gauṇatā</s>), not in any [special] way' — but that [statement] is made without considering the meaning of the verse. /
For the <s>iva</s>-word indicates the similarity between the mirror and the moon. /
And '<s>niḥśvāsāndha</s>' (blinded by breath) is a qualifier of the mirror. /
If the <s>iva</s>-word were to be construed with the meaning of '<s>andha</s>' (blind), then the example would be 'the mirror is the moon.' /
And such a construal of the <s>iva</s>-word is forced. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Of the meaning in the form of a particular too' — this is the meaning. /
'Because of that much carrying-over' — because of its entrance into both the indicated and the suggested meanings — this is the meaning. /
'Blind' — /
'The primary meaning of the word <s>andha</s>' — this is the meaning. /
'Now, impairment arises after birth from some cause or another; and that being so, how is the usage of "blind" [applicable] to one born blind?' — to this he says: 'even of one born blind' etc. /
Intending to make clear the complete concealment of the expressed meaning of the word '<s>andha</s>' in the given example, he shows its absence elsewhere: '<s>andha</s>' etc. /
'And "blind" — the statement of impairment of sight is a figurative usage through superimposition.' /
Here the reason is: 'even what is in front' etc. /
'Of the meaning of <s>andha</s>' — /
'Of the primary meaning of the word <s>andha</s>' — this is the meaning. /
'But here' — /
'In the given example' — this is the meaning. /
'Cannot be accepted' — because the mirror has no sight at all — this is the purport. /
'Reflected image' etc. — /
'The similarity [which is] the nature of the word's meaning' — this is the meaning. /
This alone is the delimiting condition of the indicated [meaning] here. /
'One who has lost sight' — /
'One whose sight is impaired' — this is the meaning. /
'Indicates the mirror' — the meaning is: makes known the mirror through the form of inability to make clear the reflected image. /
'If construed with the meaning of <s>andha</s>' — /
'If construed as <s>niḥśvāsāndha iva</s> [= "as if blinded by breath"]' — this is the meaning. /
'Then the example would be' — the meaning is: then it should be so construed. /
'But it is so!' — to this he says: 'and such a construal' etc. /
'<s>Niḥśvāsāndha iva</s> — a mirror — that [moon] resembles such a moon' — this is the construal — and this is the meaning. /
'Forced' — because the meaning is strained — this is the purport. /
Dispelling the doubt that the <s>iva</s>-word might be connected with both: he says '<s>na ca</s>' etc. /
'Like that' — /

children.text: locanam na ca niḥśvāsenāndha ivādarśaḥ sa iva candra iti kalpanā yuktā /

children.translated_text: 'For in the <s>Jaiminīya</s>-sūtra such [construals] are applied, not in poetry as well!' — enough of this. /
'<s>Gamaṇam</s>' — /

children.text: gaganaṃ ca mattameghaṃ dhārālulitārjunāni ca vanāni /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit shadow:] The sky with intoxicated clouds, and the forests with <s>Arjuna</s> trees tossed by rain-showers,
the nights, dark yet with a humble moon — they captivate.
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'And the fancy that [the moon is] like a mirror blinded by breath, and that [mirror] in turn like the moon — is not appropriate.'

children.text:
iti cchāyā /
caśabdo 'piśabdārthe /
gaganaṃ mattamedhamapi na kevalaṃ tārakitam /
dārālulitārjunavṛkṣāṇyapi vanāni na kevalaṃ malayamārutāndolitasahakārāṇi /
nirahaṅkāramṛgāṅkā nīlā apiniśā na kevalaṃ sitakarakaradhavalitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The nights, dark, with a humble (<s>nirahaṅkāra</s>) moon' — not merely whitened by the rays of the white-rayed [moon]. /
'Captivate' — the meaning is: they make one eager. /

By the word '<s>matta</s>' (intoxicated), whose primary meaning as 'drunk with liquor' is sublated by its total impossibility here, indicating the cloud through similarity [with an intoxicated person], there are suggested thousands of properties — unruliness, irresistibility, etc. /

By the word '<s>nirahaṅkāra</s>' (without ego/pride) too, indicating the moon, [are suggested] its dependence, dimness, the abandonment of the desire to rise in the form of ambition to excel, and so forth. // 1 //

Thus is the <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit rendering). /
The particle '<s>ca</s>' is in the sense of '<s>api</s>' (even). /
'The sky with intoxicated clouds' — not merely studded with stars. /
'Forests with <s>Arjuna</s> trees tossed by rain-showers' — not merely swaying with <s>sahakāra</s> trees stirred by the Malaya breeze. /

children.text:
avivakṣitavācyasya prabhinnatvamiti yaduktaṃ tatkutaḥ? na hi svarūpādeva bhedo bhavatītyāṅkya vivaṅkṣitavācyādevāsya bhedo bhavati, vivakṣā tadabhāvayorvirodhādityabhiprāyeṇāha---asaṃlakṣyeti /
bālapriyā gaganaṃ ceti varṣāvarṇanam. ca śabda iti /

evamuparyapi bodhyam /
vācyasyātyantatiraskṛtatvamupapādayati----mattaśabdenetyādi /
bādhiteti /
anvayānupapattirūpabādhāviśiṣṭetyarthaḥ /
sādṛśyāditi /
sādṛśyātmakamukhyārthasambandhānnimittādityarthaḥ /
sādṛśyaṃ maryādollaṅghanādinā /
asabhañjaseti /
anucitetyarthaḥ /
nirahaṅkāraśabdenāpīti /
pratiṣedhasya prasaktipūrvakatvānnarahaṅkāraśabdo hyahaṅkārasvarūpayogye cetanaviśeṣe eva svarasataḥ prayujyata ityato 'tra mukhyārthasyānvayānupapattirūpabādhā bodhyā /
lakṣayateti /
sādṛśyādityanuṣajyate /

children.translated_text: 'And that [similarity is] through dimness etc.' /
'That' etc. — /
'By the word <s>tat</s> there is reference to <s>nirahaṅkāra</s>; [the properties] such as dependence etc. belonging to that' — this is the meaning. /

children.text: ujjigamiṣā unnatīcchā, tadrūpā yā jīgīṣā utkarṣecchā tattyāgaprabhṛtirityarthaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Ujjigamiṣā</s>' — the desire to rise; of that nature is the competitive desire (<s>jigīṣā</s>), [i.e.,] the desire for superiority; the abandonment of that and so forth' — this is the meaning. // 1 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Now, the distinctness of the <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> (unintended expressed) — as was stated — from what [does it derive]? For a difference does not arise from one's own nature alone — thus reflecting, [we say:] its difference is from the <s>vivakṣita-vācya</s> (intended expressed) alone, because intendedness and its absence are mutually contradictory — with this intention he says: '<s>asaṃlakṣya</s>' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Gaganaṃ ca</s>' etc. — is a description of the rainy season. 'The particle <s>ca</s>' — /
The particle <s>ca</s> in both '<s>gaganaṃ ca</s>' and '<s>arjunāni ca</s>' — this is the meaning. /
The sky with intoxicated clouds, even — he states the meaning conveyed by the particle '<s>api</s>': '<s>na</s>' etc. /
The same should be understood in what follows above. /
He establishes the complete concealment of the expressed meaning: 'by the word <s>matta</s>' etc. /
'Sublated' — /
'Qualified by sublation in the form of impossibility of syntactic connection' — this is the meaning. /
'Through similarity' — through the relation [which is] the ground, in the form of similarity with the primary meaning — this is the meaning. /
'The similarity' — by transgression of boundaries etc. /
'Unruliness' — /
'Unfitness' — this is the meaning. /
'By the word <s>nirahaṅkāra</s> too' — /
'Since negation presupposes applicability, the word <s>nirahaṅkāra</s> is naturally used only with reference to a conscious being who is fit to possess ego-sense; therefore here the sublation of primary meaning in the form of impossibility of syntactic connection should be understood.' /
'Indicates' — '<s>sādṛśyāt</s>' (through similarity) carries over. /

children.text:
sūtravṛttikṛtoraikyamabhipretyāvatārayati---avivakṣitavācyasyetyādi /
uktamiti /
'prabhedapratipādanāye'ti pūrvagranthenoktamityarthaḥ /
taditi /
prabhinnatvamityarthaḥ /
kata iti /
kasmātpratiyogina ityarthaḥ /
na hi svarūpādeva bhedo bhavatīti /
svasmādeva bhedo na bhavatītyarthaḥ /
asyeti /
avivakṣitavācyasyetyarthaḥ /
vivakṣetyādi /
vivakṣitatvovivakṣitasvayorekatrāsambhavādityarthaḥ /
nanu vivakṣitānyaparābhidheyasyeti atra mattanirahaṅkāraśabdau /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Intending the unity of the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>vṛtti</s> authors, he introduces: '<s>avivakṣita-vācyasya</s>' etc. /
'Stated' — /
'Stated by the earlier text "<s>prabhedapratipādanāya</s>"' — this is the meaning. /
'That' — /
'Distinctness' — this is the meaning. /
'From what' — /
'From what counter-correlate' — this is the meaning. /
'For a difference does not arise from one's own nature alone' — /
'It does not differ from itself' — this is the meaning. /
'Of this' — /
'Of the <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s>' — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Vivakṣā</s>' etc. — /
'Because intendedness and non-intendedness cannot co-exist in one [entity]' — this is the meaning. /
Now, in '<s>vivakṣitānyaparābhidheyasya</s>' here [the words] <s>matta</s> and <s>nirahaṅkāra</s> — /
[<s>Kārikā</s>:] That whose illumination has imperceptible sequence, and the other which is illuminated in sequence —

children.text: vivakṣitābhidheyasya dhvaner ātmā dvidhā mataḥ // DhvK_2.2 //
children.translated_text: the self of <s>dhvani</s> whose expressible is intended is considered to be twofold. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.2 //
[Repeated <s>kārikā</s>:] That whose illumination has imperceptible sequence, and the other which is illuminated in sequence —
the self of <s>dhvani</s> whose expressible is intended is considered to be twofold. // 2 //

children.text:
mukhyatayā prakāśamāno vyaṅgyo 'rtho dhvanerātmā /
sa ca vācyārthāpekṣayā kaścidalakṣyakramatayā prakāśate, kaścitkrameṇeti dvidhā mataḥ /
locanam samyaṅ na lakṣayituṃ śakyaḥ kramo yasya tādṛśa uddyota uddyotanavyāpāro 'syeti bahuvrīhiḥ /
dhvaniśabdasāṃnadhyādvivakṣitābhidheyatvenānyaparatvamatrākṣiptamiti bahuvrīhiḥ /
dhvaniśabdasāṃnidhyādvivakṣitābhidheyatvenānyaparatvamatrākṣiptamiti svakaṇṭhena noktam /
dhvaneriti /
vyaṅgyasyetyarthaḥ /
ātmeti /

children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] By the previous verse, the distinction of the suggested was stated in terms of the expressed meaning. /

children.text: idānīṃ tu dyotanavyāpāramukhena dyotyasya khātmaniṣṭa evetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, however, the distinction through the mode of the illuminating operation is stated — [pertaining to] the self residing in the suggested itself — this is the meaning. /

children.text: vyaṅgyasya dhvanerdyetane svātnani kaḥ krama ityāśaṅkyāha----vācyārthāpekṣayeti /
children.translated_text: 'What sequence [exists] in the illumination — in the self — of the suggested <s>dhvani</s>?' — anticipating this question, he says: 'in relation to the expressed meaning' etc. /
The expressed meaning is the <s>vibhāva</s> (stimulus) etc. // 2 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] The suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya artha</s>), shining forth as primary, is the self of <s>dhvani</s>. /
And it is considered twofold: some [suggested meaning] shines forth with imperceptible sequence in relation to the expressed meaning, and some with [perceptible] sequence. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'That whose illumination — whose operation of illuminating — has a sequence (<s>krama</s>) that cannot be properly discerned: such is the <s>uddyota</s>' — this is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. /
'Because of the proximity of the word <s>dhvani</s>, the status of being <s>anyapara</s> (directed toward another [meaning]) with the expressed meaning being intended is implied here' — therefore it was not stated in his own words. /
'Of <s>dhvani</s>' — /
'Of the suggested' — this is the meaning. /
'Self' (<s>ātmā</s>) — /

children.text:
tatreti /
tayormadhyādityarthaḥ /
yo rasādirarthaḥ sa evākramo dhvanerātmā na tvakrama eva saḥ /
kramatvamapi hi tasya kadācidbhavati /
tadā cārthaśaktyudbhavānusvānarūpabhedateti vakṣyate /
ātmaśabdaḥ svabhāvavacanaḥ prakāramāha /

asaṃlakṣyakrama iti yāvat /
nanu kiṃ sarvadaiva rasādirartho dhvaneḥ prakāraḥ? netyāha; kiṃ tu yadāṅgitvena pradhānatvenāvabhāsamānaḥ /
etacca sāmānyalakṣaṇe 'guṇīkṛtasvārthāvi'tyatra bālapriyā kuto noktamityata āha---dhvaniśabdetyādi /
vivakṣitābhidhetveneti /
bivakṣitābhidheyatvoktyetyarthaḥ /
atreti /
abhidheye ityarthaḥ /
ākṣiptamiti /
darśitamityarthaḥ /
viśeṣamāha---pūrvaślokenetyādi /
idānīmiti /
asmin śloke ityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Residing in its own self alone' —
The continuation is with [the phrase] 'the sub-type has been stated.'
The elaboration of '<s>dhvaner ātmā</s>' (the essence of <s>dhvani</s>) in the <s>vṛtti</s> is: 'for the principal status' etc.
He introduces the passage beginning with 'of the expressible meaning' etc.: 'of the suggested' etc. // 2 //

'There' — the meaning is: from among those two. /
The meaning that is <s>rasa</s> etc. — that itself is the <s>akrama</s> (imperceptible-sequence) essence of <s>dhvani</s>; but it is not the case that it is exclusively <s>akrama</s>. /
For <s>krama</s> (perceptible sequence) also sometimes obtains for it. /
Then it will be stated [that it falls under] the category 'born from the power of meaning, of the nature of reverberation.' /
The word '<s>ātman</s>' (essence) denotes essential nature; he states the mode. /
Therefore, the meaning that is <s>rasa</s> etc. — that is the sub-type of <s>dhvani</s> [called] <s>akrama</s> (imperceptible-sequence). /
'<s>Asaṃlakṣyakrama</s>' — this is the extent. /
Now, is the meaning of <s>rasa</s> etc. always a mode of <s>dhvani</s>? No, he says; rather, [only] when it shines forth as the principal (<s>aṅgin</s>), with primacy. /
And this [qualifier] 'having subordinated their own meaning' was [already stated] in the general definition — so why was it not stated [there]? To this he says: 'by the word <s>dhvani</s>' etc. /
'As having intended expressible-status' — the meaning is: by the statement of intended expressible-status. /
'Here' — the meaning is: in the [category of] the expressible. /
'Has been indicated' — the meaning is: has been shown. /
He states the specific point: 'by the previous verse' etc. /
'Now' — the meaning is: in this verse.

children.text:
rasetyādikārikāyāmaṅgibhāvena bhāsamāno rasabhāvādiḥ akramo ghnanerātmā vyavasthita ityanvayo vaktavyaḥ /
tathā ca tathāvidharasabhāvādisāmānyamasaṃlakṣyakrama ityarthaḥ sidhyati /
sa cārtho bādhitaḥ, kvacidbhāvādeḥ saṃlakṣyakramatvasyāpyaṅgīkṛtatvādato vivakṣitamarthaṃ vyācaṣṭe---yo rasādirityādi /
akramaḥ asaṃlakṣyakramaḥ /
na tvakrama eva sa iti /
rasabhāvādirakrama eva bhavatīti tu naivetyarthaḥ /
kuta ityatrāha---krameti /
saṃlakṣyakramatvamapītyartaḥ /
'kramavattvam' iti ci pāṭhaḥ /
tasya bhāvādeḥ /
vakṣyata iti /
"evaṃvādini devarṣāvi"tyādyudāharaṇapūrvakaṃ vakṣyata ityarthaḥ /
aṅgibhāvena bhāsamāna ityasya vivaraṇam--aṅgitvenetyādi etadukteḥ paunaruktyamāśaṅkate--rataccetyādi /
tatra
children.translated_text:
In the <s>kārikā</s> beginning with '<s>rasa</s>' etc., the syntactic connection should be stated as: '<s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc., shining forth as the principal (<s>aṅgin</s>), is the <s>akrama</s> (imperceptible-sequence) essence of <s>dhvani</s> — [this] is established.' /
And thus the meaning that the generality of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc. of such a kind constitutes <s>asaṃlakṣyakrama</s> (imperceptible sequence) is established. /
But that meaning is contradicted, since the <s>saṃlakṣyakrama</s> (perceptible sequence) nature of <s>bhāva</s> etc. has also been accepted in some cases — therefore he explains the intended meaning: 'that which is <s>rasa</s> etc.' etc. /
'<s>Akrama</s>' — <s>asaṃlakṣyakrama</s> (imperceptible sequence). /
'But it is not exclusively <s>akrama</s>' — the meaning is: that <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc. is exclusively <s>akrama</s> — this is not so indeed. /
'From what evidence?' — to this he says: '<s>krama</s>' etc. /
The meaning is: <s>saṃlakṣyakrama</s> (perceptible sequence) also [obtains]. /
'<s>Kramavattvam</s>' is also a reading. /
'Of that' — of <s>bhāva</s> etc. /
'Will be stated' — the meaning is: will be stated with examples beginning with 'when the divine sage spoke thus' etc. /
The elaboration of 'shining forth as the principal' is: 'with principal status' etc. He raises the suspicion of repetition from this statement: 'and this' etc. /
Therein
<s>Rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), their semblances (<s>tadābhāsa</s>), their quiescence (<s>tatpraśānti</s>), etc. — the <s>akrama</s> (imperceptible-sequence [type]),
the essence of <s>dhvani</s> — shining forth as the principal (<s>aṅgin</s>) — is established. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.3 //
<s>Rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, their semblances, their quiescence, etc. — the <s>akrama</s> (imperceptible-sequence [type]),
the essence of <s>dhvani</s> — shining forth as the principal — is established. // 3 //

children.text:
locanam yadyapi nirūpitam, tathāpi rasavadādyalaṅkāraprakāśanāvakāśadānāyānūditam /
sa ca rasādirdhvanirvyavasthita eva; na hi tacchūnyaṃ kāvyaṃ kiñcidasti /
yadyapi ca rasenaiva sarvaṃ jīvati kāvyam tathāpi tasya rasasyaikadhanacamatkārātmano 'pi kutaścidaṃśātprayojakībhūtādadhiko 'sau camatkāro bhavati /
children.translated_text: And although all poetry lives by <s>rasa</s> alone, nevertheless, from a certain aspect of that <s>rasa</s> — even though [<s>rasa</s>] has the nature of a single-mass aesthetic wonder (<s>ekadhana-camatkāra</s>) — [when] that aspect becomes the motivating cause, there is a greater aesthetic wonder than that.

children.text: tatra yadā kaścidudriktāvasthāṃ pratipanno vyabhicārī camatkārātiśayaprayojako bhavati, tadā bhāvadhvaniḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, when a certain <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion), having attained a state of heightened prominence, becomes the cause of an excess of aesthetic wonder — then [it is called] <s>bhāva-dhvani</s> (suggestion of emotion).

children.text: yathā---- tiṣṭetkopavaśātprabhāvapihitā dīrghaṃ na sā kupyati svargāyotpatitā bhavenmayi punarbhāvārdramasyā manaḥ /
children.translated_text:
For example: 'Let her remain hidden by [her] power due to anger — but she does not stay angry for long; /
having flown up to heaven, her mind would again become tender with love toward me;

children.text: tāṃ hartuṃ vibudhadviṣo 'pi na ca me śaktāḥ purovavartinīṃ sā cātyantamagocaraṃ nayanayoryāteti ko 'yaṃ vidhiḥ //
children.translated_text:
even the enemies of the gods are not able to seize her who stands before me; /
yet she has gone utterly beyond the range of [my] eyes — what is this fate?'

<s>Locana</s>: Although [this] has been determined [already], nevertheless it is reiterated to provide occasion for illuminating the <s>alaṅkāras</s> such as <s>rasavat</s> etc. /
And that <s>dhvani</s> of <s>rasa</s> etc. is indeed established; for there is no poetry whatsoever that is devoid of it.

children.text:
atra hi vipralambharasasadbhāve 'pīyati vitarkākhyavyabhicāricamatkriyāprayukta āsvādātiśayaḥ /

yathā-- yote gotraviparyaye śrutipathaṃ śayyāmanuprāptayā nirdhyātaṃ parivartanaṃ punarapi prārabdhumaṅgīkṛtam /
