vyavasthita iti padaṃ vyācaṣṭe----sa cetyādi /
vyavasthita iti /
sarvatra kāvye sthita ityarthaḥ /
bhāvetyādinā nirdiṣṭa bhāvādidhvaniṃ śaṅkāpūrvakaṃ vyavasthāpayati---yadyapītyādi /
tasyeti /
kāvyajīnitasyetyarthaḥ /
'rasasya aṃśādi'ti sambandhaḥ /
rasāṅgabhūtādityarthaḥ /
tiṣṭediti /
vikramorvaśīye purūravaso vacanam /
sā urvaśī /
kopavasāddhetoḥ /
prabhāveṇāntardhānakaraṇavidyayā pihitā antarhitā /
tiṣṭhediti sambhāvanāyāṃ liṅ /
'etanna yuktaṃ yata' iti śeṣo 'tra bodhyaḥ /
evamuttaratrāpi /
svargāya svargaṃ gantum /
vibudhadviṣaḥ asurāḥ agocaram aviṣayatvam /
vidhiḥ prakāraḥ yadāheti /
vividhamityanena triprakāratvamapi darśitamiti bhāvaḥ /
udayāvasthāprayukta iti /
udayaunmukhyaprayukta ityarthaḥ /
yāta iti /
śayyāmanuprāptayā priyeṇa saha śayānayā tanvaṅgyā /
gotrasya nāmno viparyaye vanitāntaranāmnītyarthaḥ /
śrutipathaṃ yāte śrute sati /
parivartanaṃ nirdhyātaṃ cintitam /

children.translated_text: 'To perform' —
the continuation is with [the word] 'turning away.'
Or [it is] the distant reference of 'that.'

children.text: locanam bhūyastatprakṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ ca śithilakṣiptaikadorlekhayā tanvaṅgyā na tu pāritaḥ stanabharaḥ kraṣṭuṃ priyasyorasaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Locana</s>: 'Again, that turning away was intended and also performed — with a single languid casting of one arm — by the slender-limbed woman; but the weight of her breasts was not drawn away from her beloved's chest.'

Here, even though the <s>rasa</s> of <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) exists, the excess of savoring is produced by the aesthetic relishing of the <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) called <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation). /
The <s>vyabhicārins</s> have three properties: arising (<s>udaya</s>), persistence (<s>sthiti</s>), and subsidence (<s>apāya</s>). /
As it is said: 'They are called <s>vyabhicārins</s> because they move about diversely, facing [the <s>sthāyin</s>].' /
Therein, [the aesthetic wonder] is sometimes produced by the state of arising. /
For example: 'When the change of name was heard by her who had come to the bed, [the thought of] turning away was contemplated, and then undertaken to be performed again. /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: He resolves: 'nevertheless' etc. /
'<s>Rasavat</s> etc.' — the purport is: because when [the suggested] shines forth as a subsidiary (<s>aṅga</s>), the question arises: what is the mode? /
He explains the word '<s>vyavasthita</s>' (established): 'and that' etc. /
'Established' — the meaning is: situated in all poetry. /
With the passage beginning with '<s>bhāva</s>' etc., he establishes, preceded by an objection, the <s>bhāva-dhvani</s> etc. that was indicated: 'although' etc. /
'Of that' — the meaning is: of [<s>rasa</s>] that is the life of poetry. /
The connection is: '<s>rasa</s>'s aspect.' /
The meaning is: of the subsidiary of <s>rasa</s>. /
'Let her remain' — the speech of <s>Purūravas</s> in the <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s>. /
'She' — <s>Urvaśī</s>. /
'Due to anger' — as the cause. /
'Hidden by power' — concealed by the art of making oneself invisible. /
'Let her remain' — the optative is in the sense of supposition. /
'The remainder to be understood here is: this is not fitting because...' /
Likewise in what follows. /
'To heaven' — to go to heaven. /
'Enemies of the gods' — the <s>Asuras</s>. 'Beyond the range' — beyond the domain. /
'Fate' — mode, manner. /
As he says — 'diversely' — by this, the threefold nature too is shown: this is the purport. /
'Produced by the state of arising' — the meaning is: produced by the state of being about to arise. /
'Goes' (<s>yāta</s>) — when the slender-limbed woman, lying in bed with her beloved, heard the change of name — the name of another woman being [spoken]: this is the meaning. /
'Heard on the path of hearing' — when it was heard. /
'Turning away was contemplated' — thought about. /

children.text:
atra hi praṇayakopasyojjigamiṣayaiva yadavasthānaṃ na tu pārita ityudayāvakāśanirākaraṇāttadevāsvādajīvitam /
sthitiḥ punarudāhṛtā---'tiṣṭetkopavaśāt' ityādinā /
kvacittu vyabhicāriṇaḥ praśamāvasthayā prayuktaścamatkāraḥ /
yathodāhṛtaṃ prāk 'ekasmin śayane parāṅmukhatayā' iti /
ayaṃ tatpraśama ityuktaḥ /
atra cerṣyāvipralambhasya rasasyāpi praśama iti śakyaṃ yojayitum /
children.translated_text: And here, 'the quiescence of the <s>rasa</s> of jealous love-in-separation' — this too can be construed.
But sometimes, the juncture (<s>sandhi</s>) of the <s>vyabhicārin</s> itself is the ground of relishing.

children.text: yathā--- osuru sumṭhi āhaṃ muhu cumbau jeṇa /
children.translated_text: For example: '<s>Osuru</s> — truly, I am overcome! Again and again [he] kissed — by whom?'
'The satiation of draughts of nectar-<s>rasa</s> was recognized — by him!'

Here, the <s>praṇayakopa</s> (love-quarrel anger) — through its very wish to rise up, its remaining [in that state] rather than departing — by the removal of the occasion for its arising, that very [residual state] is the life of the aesthetic savoring. /
Persistence, on the other hand, was exemplified: 'Let her remain hidden by [her] power due to anger' etc. /
But sometimes the aesthetic wonder is produced by the subsidence-state of the <s>vyabhicārin</s>. /
As was previously exemplified: 'On one bed, with faces turned away' etc. /
This was called 'quiescence of that (<s>tatpraśama</s>).'

children.translated_text: He states his own view: 'and here' etc.
'<s>Osuru</s>' —
'By whom the face, beautified by tears of jealousy, was kissed —'
'By him, the satiation of the draughts of nectar-<s>rasa</s> was recognized.'

Here, in the verse heard [as <s>Prākrit</s>], the anger — the face, made faltering and indistinct by the bitterness of anger, gently weeping — whose face was kissed by the one [i.e., the beloved] — by him, the satiation of the series of restings-after-swallowing of nectar-<s>rasa</s> was known — thus the juncture of anger and appeasement is the ground of aesthetic wonder. /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'Or the distant reference' — 'again, but' — 'to perform' was intended. /
'Again, that turning away.' /
'Intended' — made the object of effort. /
'And also performed' — and also accomplished. /
The continuation of these two is with 'again, that.' /
'With a single languid casting of one arm' — first languid, i.e., made slack; afterward cast elsewhere — a single arm-gesture; by her having such [a gesture]. /
'Again, that turning away' — 'and also performed.' /
The sequence demonstrated here is: knows, desires, endeavors, acts. /
'But' — the word '<s>tu</s>' is for specification. /
The connection is: 'the weight of breasts was not drawn away from her beloved's chest.' /
This verse was explained by <s>Pratīhārendurāja</s> in his commentary on the <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasaṅgraha</s>. /
'By its very wish to rise up' — by the state of being about to arise. /
He elaborates the meaning of '<s>eva</s>' (only): 'but not' etc. /
'Thus it was called' — the remainder is: 'by the predecessors.'

What will the blameless ones say? Whence this mind? Even in a dream she is unattainable. /
O heart, attain composure! What fortunate youth will indeed place [his lips] on [her] lower lip?'

Thus the <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit rendering) appears [to be]. /
'Of draughts' — of eatings; the sixth case is in the sense of the instrumental of manner. /
As in '<s>nāgniḥ tṛpyati kāṣṭhānām</s>' ('fire is not satiated of logs') etc. /
Here, 'in the verse heard' — the word '<s>irṣyā</s>' (jealousy) [is understood] though expressed [only implicitly]; the place of repose belongs to it. /
Or alternatively: draughts that are preceded by repose in the nectar-<s>rasa</s> — i.e., draughts [made] by resting and resting again. /
'Recognized' — up to this, the narration of the expressed meaning. /

children.translated_text: <s>Rasa-dhvani</s> (suggestion of <s>rasa</s>), however, is that very [suggestion] where the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion), aroused here primarily through the combination of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions), [produces in] the percipient (<s>pratipattu</s>) an excellence of aesthetic relish occasioned precisely by the savoring of the <s>sthāyin</s>-component.

For here, speculation (<s>vitarka</s>) and eagerness (<s>autsukya</s>), resolve (<s>mati</s>) and memory (<s>smaraṇa</s>), apprehension (<s>śaṅkā</s>) and despondency (<s>dainya</s>), fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>) and anxiety (<s>cintā</s>) — arising in pairs through mutual opposition of the obstructed and the obstructor — and at the end, granting predominance to anxiety alone, [they] become the locus of supreme aesthetic relish. /
Thus other [examples] too may be imagined. /
And these — the variegation through the juncture of impetus (<s>udaya-sandhi</s>), etc. — are included by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.) in the <s>kārikā</s>. /
But if this is so — since greater aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) is seen through the medium of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) as well, then <s>vibhāva-dhvani</s> (suggestion of determinants) and <s>anubhāva-dhvani</s> (suggestion of consequents) should also be stated. /
Not so; for <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> are expressible by their own words themselves. /
Their aesthetic savoring too ultimately resolves into mental states (<s>cittavṛttis</s>) — therefore nothing beyond <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> is to be savored. /
But when <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> too become suggested, then why should <s>vastu-dhvani</s> (suggestion of factual content) not be accepted? /
But when from a semblance of a <s>vibhāva</s> (<s>vibhāvābhāsa</s>) there arises a semblance of <s>rati</s> (love) — then [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Kvākāryam</s>' (where is the impropriety?) — thus. /
This is the utterance of <s>Yayāti</s> who desires <s>Devayānī</s>. /
The impropriety is in the form of attachment to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> girl. /
By the word '<s>kva</s>' twice, the apprehension of the impossibility of the two being together [is conveyed]. /
Thereby extreme impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>) is suggested. /
Here is speculation (<s>vitarka</s>). /

'What will [they] say?' /
Here is apprehension (<s>śaṅkā</s>). /
'Even in a dream' — even in [a situation] where unprecedented and unheard-of [events] can occur — she is unattainable. /
Here is despondency (<s>dainya</s>) caused by non-attainment of the desired. /
'<s>Ceta</s>' (O heart!) etc. — /
Here is fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>). /
'<s>Ka</s>' (who?) etc. — /
'Fortunate' — not ill-fated like me. /
'Will nurture, will enjoy' — /
Here anxiety (<s>cintā</s>) is also suggested. /
Therefore he says — 'here indeed' etc. /
'Speculation and eagerness' etc. — /
By the sentences contained in each quarter-verse of '<s>kvākāryam</s>' etc., [the emotions] are sequentially suggested — this is the purport. /
'Mutually obstructed' — the meaning is: speculation etc. is obstructed by eagerness etc. /
'<s>Bhavantī</s>' and '<s>dadatī</s>' — the dual number [is used because they arise in pairs]. /
'Of anxiety' — of that which is suggested by the final sentence — this is the purport. /
In passing, he raises a doubt — 'but if so' etc. /
He resolves it — 'not so' etc. /
'Expressible by their own words' — capable of being denoted by their own words. /
'Ultimately resolves into mental states' — the meaning is: it resolves into the savoring of mental states such as <s>rati</s> (love) etc. /
'Is not accepted' — the purport is: it is indeed accepted. /
He explains the '<s>ābhāsa</s>' (semblance) that was indicated by 'then [there is] semblance' — 'but when' etc. /
'<s>Vibhāva</s> and <s>anubhāva</s>' — this has been elaborated in the <s>Rasagaṅgādhara</s> and other [works]. /
'From a semblance of <s>vibhāva</s>' — when the <s>vibhāva</s> is a semblance, the <s>anubhāva</s> too becomes a semblance. /
He raises a doubt — 'even though' etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] From a semblance of <s>vibhāva</s>, a semblance of aesthetic savoring — this is the domain of <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>). /
Just as the semblance of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) [arises] when hearing the poetry of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>. /
Although the sage [<s>Bharata</s>] has defined: 'that which is an imitation of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is <s>hāsya</s> (the comic),' nevertheless the <s>hāsya-rasa</s> (comic sentiment) there arises subsequently. /
'Like a spell of attraction and delusion, when that name reaches my ears, my heart cannot remain steady even for a moment without her' — /
Here, however, there is no occasion for the savoring of <s>hāsya</s> (the comic). /
But is there not <s>rati</s> (love) as the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) here? /
Since there is no mutual bond of stability — who has said that this is <s>rati</s>? /
For that is a semblance of <s>rati</s> (<s>ratyābhāsa</s>). /
And its semblance-status [is due to the fact] that the apprehension 'is <s>Sītā</s> indifferent toward me or hostile?' does not touch his heart at all. /
For if that apprehension were to touch [his heart], his desire too would dissolve. /
And 'this one is enamored of me' — even this certainty has not been achieved, [prevented] by the delusion born of desire. /
Precisely therefore, its semblance-status is established in reality, like the semblance of silver in mother-of-pearl. /
Thus the word '<s>śṛṅgārānukṛti</s>' (imitation of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>) — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] [this] has been defined by the sage — thus. /
And therefore the <s>hāsya-rasa</s> (comic sentiment) is proper to state there — this is the purport. /
'Subsequently' — the meaning is: arising after the savoring of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
After that savoring, through the awakening of laughter among the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (sensitive readers) — grounded in the desire and such [emotions] of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who desires one who is not enamored of him — this is the purport. /
'Like a spell' etc. — /
'May whatever happiness of attaining her be achieved — through these limbs, afflicted by love, of one who has been bewildered, whose desire for other objects has been destroyed' — this is the latter half. /
'<s>Prakurute</s>' — here the reading '<s>prasahate</s>' also [exists]. /
'Distance-attracting' and 'delusion' — a spell that does these — like that, in that [name] — [this is a] simile. /
By that [simile], the unfailingness of the power of distant attraction etc. is indicated. /
'That name' — the name of <s>Sītā</s>. /
'<s>Anaṅgāturaiḥ</s>' — by these limbs afflicted by love. /
'<s>Ākulitasya</s>' — of one who has been bewildered; '<s>vikṣatā</s>' — destroyed; '<s>ratiḥ</s>' — interest in other objects — of one who has become averse. /
'Of one who has become averse' — this is the extent. /
'<s>Me</s>' (of me) — carries over. /
'Not the comic' — the remainder is: at first. /
Rather, the savoring of the semblance of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> alone — this is the purport. /
'Who [has said]?' — the syntactic construction is: who has said that this is <s>rati</s>? /
Here, the <s>rati</s> (love) that is apprehended is merely a mental state (<s>cittavṛtti</s>) in the form of desire (<s>abhilāṣa</s>), not a <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) — this is the purport. /
'For that is a semblance of <s>rati</s>' — 'that' refers to the mental state in the form of desire belonging to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>. /
A semblance of <s>rati</s> — appearing as if it were <s>rati</s> in the form of a <s>sthāyibhāva</s>. /
'And therefore' — by the reason to be stated — this is the meaning. /
'Of this <s>Rāvaṇa</s>' — toward me, as his object. /
'<s>Upekṣikā</s>' — possessed of indifference. /
'<s>Dviṣṭā</s>' — possessed of hatred. /
'At that touch' — at the touch of such an apprehension. /
'His' — of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>. /
'And not' — '<s>kṛtam</s>' is a particle expressing negation. /
'This one is enamored of me' — the absence of even this certainty — this is the meaning. /
And that certainty [does not] exist — this is the extent. /
Here he states the reason — '<s>kāma</s>' etc. /
The reading '<s>niścayena kṛtya</s>' also [exists]. /
In that reading, the construction is '<s>na ca kṛtyam</s>' — 'and there is no purpose in [that] certainty' — this is the meaning. /
For that certainty is useless in the generation of desire — this is the purport. /
In the other reading, the connection of '<s>kāmakṛtān mohāt</s>' (from the delusion born of desire) is with '<s>na spṛśaty eva</s>' (does not touch at all) — this should be understood. /
'Precisely therefore' — from the very reason stated. /
'Its semblance-status' — its status as a semblance of <s>rati</s>. /
'There' — in the mental state in the form of desire belonging to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>. /
'Is established' — the remainder is: by the percipients. /
'Using the word <s>śṛṅgārānukṛti</s>' — the meaning is: using it in the statement '<s>śṛṅgārānukṛtir yā tu sa hāsyaḥ</s>' (that which is an imitation of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is <s>hāsya</s>). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The sage too, in using [this word], has indicated [this]. /
For '<s>anukṛti</s>' (imitation) means inauthenticity, semblance — this is one and the same meaning. /
Precisely therefore, even though desire is lodged in one party alone, the usage of the word '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' there should be understood as [referring to it] in its semblance form. /
By '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>,' the semblance-form of <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and other [<s>rasas</s>] too is indicated. /
Thus these — <s>bhāva-dhvani</s> (suggestion of emotional states) and the rest — are outflows of <s>rasa-dhvani</s> alone. When [the element] predominant in aesthetic relish is thus analyzed and separately established —

children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Here, indeed, the meaning of "<s>Bālapriyā</s>" is this — for <s>Vatsarāja</s>, upon viewing the painting-panel sanctified by his own portrait depicting the heroine's form. The words <s>anukṛti</s> etc. are synonyms — this is the meaning. "By <s>śṛṅgāra</s>" — the meaning is: by the word <s>śṛṅgāra</s> occurring in the sage's statement "imitation of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>." "Of <s>vīra</s> etc." — for when they have a senior etc. as their object, they become semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>). He concludes with "thus" etc. To the question "how then is there separate classification?" he replies with "relishing" (<s>āsvāda</s>). The syntactic connection is: "the principal motivating portion is thus divided." "Is separately established" — separately, in the distinct forms of <s>rasa-dhvani</s>, <s>bhāva-dhvani</s>, etc. Here he gives an example with "just as." "Fragrance-preparation" (<s>gandhayukti</s>) means the combining of aromatic substances. "One" — even in that one relishing which is the enjoyment of the pervading fragrance that has fused together. <s>Māṃsī</s> is a particular aromatic substance. "Thus" connects with "is separately established." "<s>Vibhāva</s>" — that in which the apprehension of the <s>sthāyin</s> (dominant emotion) has arisen through the conjunction of the three — <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, and <s>vyabhicārin</s> — and through their savoring. "With difficulty" — this is the speech of the king to the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>. "Of her" connects with the fifth-case forms beginning with "thigh-pair" (<s>ūruyugam</s>). "The three folds are like waves" — either the three folds resemble waves, or the wave resembles the three folds — hence uneven, with hollows and elevations. "As if thirsty" — as though due to thirst. "Water-drops" (<s>jalalavāḥ</s>) means tear-drops. "Exuding those" — it should be understood as written thus. Here, from the thigh-pair and hips the excessive breadth, of the waist the slenderness, and of the breasts the greatness are understood — thus the extraordinary beauty is suggested; and by "water-drops" etc. the intensity of the heroine's separation-grief is also suggested. And here there is an allusion to a certain narrative of forest-wandering. "Heroine" — by the heroine's form, i.e., by means of the painted portrait of the heroine, the jester is being described in great detail, and [the panel is] sanctified by his own portrait, i.e., the painted portrait of the hero. Alternatively — the meaning of <s>rasa</s> etc. manifests simultaneously with the expressible meaning through the heroine's form. And that, not manifesting as the principal element (<s>aṅgin</s>), is the soul of <s>dhvani</s>. Now it is demonstrated that the domain of <s>dhvani</s> consisting of <s>alakṣyakrama-dyotana</s> (imperceptible-sequence illumination) is distinct from the <s>rasavat</s> and other <s>alaṅkāras</s> —
Of the various causes of beauty in the expressible (<s>vācya</s>) and the expressive (<s>vācaka</s>),

children.translated_text: "Simultaneously" (<s>saheva</s>) —
By the word "as if" (<s>iva</s>), the imperceptibility is explained despite the actual existence of the sequence.
"With the expressible" (<s>vācyena</s>) —
That is, with the <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, etc. // 3 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] The <s>rati</s> (love) <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (dominant emotion), having the form of mutual dependence, having mounted the stage of savoring (<s>carvaṇā</s>) through the conjunction of <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> — thus. Enough of prolixity. This is established — the meaning of <s>rasa</s> etc., manifesting as the principal element (<s>aṅgin</s>), is a variety of <s>dhvani</s> whose suggested content has an imperceptible sequence (<s>asaṃlakṣyakrama-vyaṅgya</s>).

children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] And the <s>Bālapriyā</s> [author explains]: "being described" (<s>anuvarṇyamānā</s>) means being viewed; the reading "<s>nirvarṇyamāne</s>" (being examined) is most correct. The meaning is: from the viewing of that painting-panel which was sanctified by his own portrait (<s>svātmapratikṛti</s>).
"Awakened" (<s>prabuddha</s>) — this is to be supplied.
"Having mounted the stage of savoring" (<s>carvaṇārūḍha</s>) —
The meaning is: having become the object of the connoisseurs' savoring (<s>sahṛdaya-carvaṇā</s>). // 3 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Now, it is said "manifesting as the principal element" (<s>aṅgitva</s>); but does this subsidiary status (<s>aṅgatva</s>) also exist for <s>rasa</s> etc.? — with this intent, that this qualifying term is used to negate that [subsidiary status], he begins with "now" etc. The subsidiary status of <s>rasa</s> etc. exists in the form of the <s>rasavat</s>, <s>preyas</s>, <s>ūrjasvin</s>, and <s>samāhita</s> <s>alaṅkāras</s> — this is the purport. And by this indirect method he indicates that <s>rasa-dhvani</s> etc. are not subsumed within the <s>rasavat</s> and other <s>alaṅkāras</s>. Previously it was shown that <s>vastu-dhvani</s> is not subsumed within <s>samāsokti</s> and other figures. "Causes of beauty in the expressible and the expressive" — this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound: the expressible, the expressive, and the causes of their beauty. In the <s>vṛtti</s> also: "words and figures-of-speech and meanings and figures-of-meaning" — this is a <s>dvandva</s>. "Is considered" (<s>mata</s>) — the meaning is: this has already been stated previously. Now, <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s> has objected: "When <s>rasa</s> is apprehended as belonging to another, then there would be mere indifference (<s>tāṭasthya</s>).

utpattipakṣe ca karuṇasyotpādādduḥkhitve karuṇaprekṣāsu punarapravṛttiḥ syāt /
'tanna utpattirapi, nāpyabhivyaktiḥ, śaktirūpasya hi śṛṅgārasyabhivyaktau viṣayārjanatāratamyapravṛttiḥ syāt tatrāpi kiṃ khagato 'bhivyajyate rasaḥ paragato veti pūrvavadeva doṣaḥ /
tena na pratīyate notpadyate nābhivyajyate kāvyena rasaḥ /
kiṃ tvanyaśabdavailakṣaṇyaṃ kāvyātmanaḥ śabdasya tryaṃśatāprasādāt /
tatrābhidāyakatvaṃ vācyaviṣayam, bhāvakatvaṃ rasādiviṣayam, bhogakṛtvaṃ sahṛdayaviṣayamiti trayoṃ'śabhūtā vyāpārāḥ /
tatrābhidhābhāgo yadi śuddhaḥ syāttattantrādibhyaḥ śāstranyāyebhyaḥ śleṣādyalaṅkāraṇāṃ ko bhedaḥ? vṛttibhedavaicitryaṃ cākiñcitkaram /
śrutiduṣṭādivarjanaṃ ca kimartham? bālapriyā pratipattāviveti sambandhaḥ dūṣaṇāntaramāha---utpattipakṣe ityādi /
sahṛdayānāmiti śeṣaḥ /
karuṇaprekṣāsu karuṇarasapradhānanāṭyeṣu /
taditi /
tasmādityarthaḥ /
nāpyabhiviyaktiriti /
rasasyeti śeṣaḥ /
tasya prāgasiddhatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
pūrvasiddhameva hi ghaṭādikaṃ pradīpādinābhivyajyate /
nanu ratyādirūpo rasaḥ sūkṣmarūpema sahṛdayānāmātmani vartata ityataḥ siddha evetyatrāha---śaktītyādi /
śaktirūpasya vāsanātatmakasūkṣmarūpeṇa sthitasya /
śṛṅgārasya rateḥ /
śṛṅgārapadaṃ vīrāderupalakṣakam /
abhivyaktau sahṛdayahṛdaye 'bhivyaktyaṅgīkāre /
viṣayeti /
viṣayo ratyādiviṣayaḥ kāntādiḥ abhivyaktyupāya iti yāvat /
tasya arjane sampādane tāratamyapravṛttiḥ taratamabhāvena pravṛttiḥ syāditi /
yathā andhakārasthaghaṭāderadhikādhikābhivyaktaye tadupāyabhūtālokasyādhikādhikasyārjane janānāṃ pravṛttistathā vāsanātmatayā antaḥ sthitasya ratyāderadhikādhikābhivyaktaye tadupāyabhūtasya vibhāvāderadhikādhikasyānubhavarūpārjane sahṛdayānāṃ pravṛttiḥ prasajyetetyarthaḥ /
adhikādhikaviṣayānubhave vāsanāyā jhaṭityabhivyaraktisambhavāditi bhāvaḥ /
dūṣaṇāntaramāha---tatrāpītyādi /
tatrāpa abhivyaktipakṣe 'pi /
upasaṃharati---tenetyādi /
na pratīyata ityādi /
sahṛdayātmanīti śeṣaḥ /
svamatamāha---kintvityādi /
anyaśabdeti /
śāstrīyādiśabdetyarthaḥ /
śateti /
trayoṃ'sā yasya tasya bhāvastattā, tasyāḥ prasādātsambandhādityarthaḥ /
tryaṃśatāṃ darśayati---tatretyādi /
vācyeti. vācyo 'rtho viṣayo yasya tat, vācyārthasambandhītyarthaḥ /
rasādīti /
raso ratyādiḥ, ādipadena vibhāvadergrahaṇam /
bhāvakatvabhogakṛtvayoḥ svarūpaṃ darśayistadaṅgīkāre yuktiṃ tāvadāha-tatretyādi /
abhidhābhāgaḥ abhidhāyakatvāṃśaḥ /
śuddhaḥ itataravyāpārānāliṅgitaḥ tat tarhi /
tantrādibhya iti /
tantraṃ nāmānekārthabodhecchayā padasyaikasya sakṛduccāraṇam /
ko bheda iti /
śāstrai locanam tena rasabhāvanākhyo divatīyo vyāpāraḥ; yadvaśadabhidhā vilakṣaṇaiva /
taccaitadbhāvakatvaṃ nāma rasān prati yatkāvyasya tadvibhāvādīnāṃ sādhāraṇatvāpādanaṃ nāma /
bhāvite ca rase tasya bhogaḥ yo 'nubhavasmaraṇapratipattibhyo vilakṣaṇa eva drutivistaravikāsātmā rajastamovaicitryānuviddhasattvamayanijacitsvabhāvanirvṛtiviśrāntilakṣaṇaḥ parabrahmāsvādasavidhaḥ /
sa eva ca pradhānabhūtoṃ'śaḥ siddharūpa iti /
vyutpattirnāmāpradhānameve'ti /
bālapriyā "halantyami"ti paṇinīyasūtrādāviva "sarvado mādhava" ityādiśleṣasthale 'pi tantrādinānekārthabodhasambhavādubhayorbhedo na syādityarthaḥ /
vṛttīti /
vṛttibhedāḥ upanāgarikādyāḥ teṣāṃ vaicitryaṃ ca akiñcitkaramiti /
kāvye abhidhāmātrasvīkāre vyarthamityarthaḥ /
kimarthamiti. niṣphalamityarthaḥ /
teneti /
uktahetunetyarthaḥ /
rasabhāvaneti /
ratyādibhāvanetyarthaḥ /
dvitīya iti /
abhidhānantarabhāvītyarthaḥ /
yadvaśāditi /
bhāvakatvavyāpārarūpaprayojakādityarthaḥ /
vilakṣaṇaiveti /
śāstrīyādiśabdagatābhidhāto vicātīyaivetyarthaḥ /
taccetyādi /
rasān prati etadbhāvakatvaṃ nāma taditi sambandhaḥ /
kāvyasyeti. nāṭyasyāpyupalakṣaṇam /
tadvibhāvādīnāmiti /
tasya ratyādirūparasasya vibhāvāditrayāṇāṃ cetyarthaḥ /
sādhāramatvāpādanamiti /
sādhāraṇīkaraṇamityarthaḥ /
sāmānyenopasthāpakatvamiti yāvat /
bhāvite uktabhāvanāviṣayīkṛte /
rase rāmādigatatyādau /
tasyeti /
bhāvitasya ratyāderityarthaḥ /
bhoga iti /
sākṣātkāraviśeṣa ityarthaḥ /
sahṛdayānāṃ bhavatīti śeṣaḥ /
tathāca bhāvanopanīto rāmādigataratyādiḥ sthāyī sahṛdayairbhujyamāno rasaḥ ratyādeḥ sādhāraṇyena pratītyā ca na tāṭasthyādidoṣa iti bhāvaḥ /
bhogasvarūpamāha---ya ityādi /
anubhaveti /
anubhavasmaraṇarūpāḥ yāḥ pratīpattayo laukikyaḥ pratītayastābhya ityarthaḥ /
'drutivistāravikāsātme'tyatra hetumāha----raja ityādi /
vaicitryānuviddheti pāṭhaḥ /
"rajastamonuvedyavaicitryabalādi"tyabhinavabhāratyāmukteḥ /
rajastamasorvaicitryeṇa viśeṣeṇa anuviddhaṃ yatsatvaṃ tanmayī /
prācuryārthe mayaṭ /
nijacitsvabhāvā svātmacaitanyarūpā ca yā nivṛtiḥ lokottarānandaḥ, tasyāṃ viśrāntiḥ vigalitavedyāntaratayā sthitiḥ tallakṣaṇa ityarthaḥ /
atra rajaso guṇasyānuvedhena drutiḥ tamaso vistāraḥ satvasya vikāsa iti vivekaḥ /
uktaṃ hi kāvyaprakāśasaṅkete---"yadāhi rajaso guṇasya drutiḥ tamaso vistāraḥ satvasya vikāsaḥ tadā bhogaḥ svarūpaṃ lamata" iti /
uktarītyā bhogasyātmānandaviṣayakatvādāha---pareti /
sa eveti /
uktavidhabhoga evetyarthaḥ /
siddharūpa iti /
cidānandarūpasyātmanaḥ siddharūpatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
vyutpattiriti /
pratipattṝṇāṃ locanam atrocyate---rasasvarūpa eva tāvadvipratipattayaḥ prativādinām /
tathāhi-pūrvāvasthāyāṃ yaḥ sthāyī sa eva vyabhicārisampātādinā prāptaparipoṣo 'nukāryagata eva rasaḥ /
nāṭye tu prayujyamānatvānnāṭyarasa iti kecit /
pravāhadharmiṇyāṃ cittavṛttau cittavṛtteḥ cittavṛttyantareṇa kaḥ paripoṣārthaḥ? vismayaśokakrodhādeśca krameṇa tāvanna paripoṣa iti nānukārye rasaḥ /
anukartari catadbhāve layādyananusaraṇaṃ syāt /
rāmajikagate vā bālapriyā caturvargopāyavyutpattirityarthaḥ /
itīti /
iti bhaṭṭanāyakoktamiti sambandhaḥ /
rasasvarūpa eveti /
rasapadārtha evetyarthaḥ /
vibhinnāḥ pratipattayo vipratipattayaḥ vibhinnāni matāni /
tathāhīti /
nāṭyasthale vipratipattīrādau vivṛṇuma ityarthaḥ /
tatra lalanādibhirālambanavibhāvaiḥ sthāyī ratyādiko janitaḥ, udyānādibhirvyabhicāribhiḥ paripoṣito rāmādāvanukārye rasaḥ, naṭe tu rāmādirūpatānusandhānavaśādāropyamāṇassāmājikānāṃ camatkārakārīti bhaṭṭalollaṭādimatamādau darśayati---pūrvetyādi /
pūrvāvastāyāmiti /
aprāptaparipoṣāvasthāyāmityarthaḥ /
yaḥ sthāyīti /
sthāyitvena vyapadiśyamāno yo ratyādirityarthaḥ /
'sa eva prāptaparipoṣo rasa' itisambandhaḥ /
rasaḥ rasapadārthaḥ /
sa cānukāryagata eveti /
anukāryarāmādāvevotpadyamāno vartata ityarthaḥ /
anenānukartari tadāropa iti darśitam /
tasmānnāṭyarasā iti bharatoktanāṭyarasaśabdārthamāha----nāṭya ityādi /
nāṭyasya nāṭyasambandhī vā raso nāṭyarasa iti vyutpattiriti bhāvaḥ /
matamidaṃ dūṣayitvā prakārāntareṇa vadatāṃ śrīśaṅkukādīnāṃ mataṃ darśayati----pravāhetyādi /
cittavṛttau ratyādicittavṛttau /
pravāhadharmiṇyāṃ tattatkāraṇavaśena punaḥ punarutpadyamānāyāṃ naśyantyāṃ ca satyāmiti hetugarbham /
cittavṛtteḥ ratyādisyāyicittavṛtteḥ /
cittavṛtyantareṇa utkaṇṭhādivyabhicāriṇī paripoṣārthaḥ ka iti /
paripoṣarūpaṃ phalaṃ na bhavatītyarthaḥ /
ato vyabhicāribhiḥ paripoṣasya kathanamanupapannamiti bhāvaḥ /
viṣaryayaścāstītyāha---vismayetyādi /
krameṇa kālakrameṇa /
na paripoṣa iti /
kintvapacaya eveti bhāvaḥ /
yathoktaṃ kāvyaprakāśasaṅkete---"iṣṭaviyogajo mahān śokaḥ kramema śāmyati, na tu dṛḍhībhavati krodhotsāharatayaśca nijanijakāraṇodbhūtā api kālavasādamarṣasthairyasavāviparyaye 'pacīyanta" iti /
itīti hetau /
nānukārye rasa iti /
anukāryarāmādigato rasa ityuktapakṣo na yukta ityarthaḥ /
tarhi anukartṛgato 'stvityatrāha---anukartarītyādi /
anukartari naṭe /
tadbhāve rasasatve sati /
layādīti /
layo nāma nṛttagītavādyānāmekatānatārūpaṃ sāmyaṃ rasasya naṭe siddhatvena tadupayogilayādyanusaraṇaṃ na syādityarthaḥ /
tarhi sāmājikato 'stvityatrāhasāmājiketyādi /
locanam kaścamatkāraḥ? pratyuta karuṇādau duḥkhaprāptiḥ /
tasmānnāyaṃ pakṣaḥ /
kastarhi? ihānantyānniyatasyānukāro na śakyaḥ, niṣprayojanaśca viśiṣṭatāpratītau tāṭasthyena vyutpattyabhāvāt /
tasmādaniyatāvasthātmakaṃ sthāyinamuddiśya vibhāvānubhāvyabhicāribhiḥ saṃyujyamānairayaṃ rāmaḥ sukhīti smṛtivilakṣaṇā sthāyini pratītigocaratayāsvādarūpā pratipattiranu kartrālambanā nāṭyaikagāminī rasaḥ /
sa ca na vyatiriktamādhāramapekṣate /
kiṃ tvanukāryābhinnābhimate nartake āsvādayitā sāmājika ityetāvanmātramadaḥ /
tena nāṭya eva bālapriyā tadbhāve ityanuṣajyate /
kaścamatkāra iti /
rāmāderiva sāmājikasyāpi ratyādirūparasotpattau camatkāro na jāyeteti bhāvaḥ /
duḥkhaprāptiriti /
syāditi śeṣaḥ /
nāyaṃ pakṣa iti /
uktaḥ pakṣo na yukta ityarthaḥ /
kastarhīti /
pakṣa ityanuṣajyate /
praśrasyottaraṃ vaktumupakramamāṇa āha---ihetyādi /
ānantyāditi /
tattadgatasya ratyādibhāvasya mandatamamandataramandamadhyamatvādibhedenāsaṃkhvatvādityarthaḥ /
niyatasyeti /
niścitaikāvasthāviśiṣṭasyetyarthaḥ /
sthāyina iti śeṣaḥ /
anukāro na śakya iti /
sthāyina ānantyānniyataikāvasthatvena jñātumaśakyatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
kathañcittatsambhave 'pyāha---niṣprayejanaścetyādi /
anukāra ityanuṣajyate /
niṣprayojanatve hetumāha---viśiṣṭatetyādi /
sthāyino rāmādivyaktiviśeṣavṛttitvavaiśiṣṭyamavabudhya naṭena tadanukāre kriyamāṇe tathaiva sāmājikānāṃ pratītyā tasya taṭasthatvena caturvargopāyavyutpatteranudayādityarthaḥ /
anena sthāyyanukāro rasa iti pakṣo 'pyayukta iti darśitam /
khamatamāha---tasmādityādi /
'sthāyinamuddiśya saṃyujyamānai'riti sambandhaḥ /
'sthāyipratītimuddiśya saṃyujyamānai'riti sambandhaḥ /
sthāyipratītimuddiśya naṭena prayujyamānairityarthaḥ /
vibhāveti /
tairliṅgairityarthaḥ /
pratipattirityanenāsya sambandhaḥ /
ayaṃ rāmaḥ sukhīti /
rāmo 'yaṃ sītāviṣayakaratimānityarthaḥ /
sāmājikānāṃ citraturaganyāyena naṭe rāmādibuddharjāyate /
itītyasya pratipattirityanena sambandhaḥ /
sthāyini pratītigocaratayeti /
sthāyinaḥ pratītiviṣayatvena hetunetyarthaḥ /
vastusaundaryāditi bhāvaḥ /
āsvādarūpeti /
camatkāricarvaṇārūpetyarthaḥ /
pratipattiriti /
sāmājikānāmanumitirityarthaḥ /
anukartrālambaneti /
ayamityanena naṭasya viṣayīkaraṇādanukartṛviṣayiketyarthaḥ /
sa ceti /
tathāvidhasthāyipratītirūpo rasaścetyarthaḥ /
vyatiriktamiti /
vakṣyamāṇādanyamityarthaḥ /
anukāryābhinnābhimate anukāryarāmādyabhedena gṛhīte /
nartaka iti /
astīti śeṣaḥ /
tathāvidhapratītirūparasasya nartakaviśeṣyakatvānnartake viśeṣyatāsambandhena satvātsa evāśraya ityarthaḥ /
āsvādayitā āsvādarūpapratīteḥ samavāyenāśrayaḥ /
nāṭya eveti /
locanam rasaḥ, nānukāryādiṣviti kecit /
anye tu---anukartari yaḥ sthāyyavabhāso 'bhinayādisāmagpyādikṛto bhittāvivaharitālādinā aśvāvabhāsaḥ, sa eva lokātītatayāsvādāparasaṃjñayā pratītyā rasyamāno rasa iti nāṭyādrasā nāṭyarasāḥ /
apare punarvibhāvānubhāvamātrameva viśiṣṭasāmagapyā samarpyamāṇaṃ tadvibhāvanīyānubhāvanīyasthāyirūpacittavṛttyucitavāsanānuṣaktaṃ svanirvṛticarvaṇāviśiṣṭameva rasaḥ /
tannāṭyameva rasāḥ /
anye tu śuddhaṃ vibhāvam, apare śuddhamanu bhāvam, kecittu sthāyimātram, itare vyabhicāriṇam, anye tatsaṃyogam, eke 'nukāryam, kecana sakalameva samudāyaṃ rasamāhurityalaṃ bahunā /
kāvye 'pi ca lokanāṭyadharmisthānīyena svabhāvoktivakroktiprakāradvayenālaukikaprasannamadhuraujasviśabdasamarpyamāṇavibhāvādiyogādi yameva rasavārtā /
astu vātra nāṭyādvicitrarūpā rasapratītiḥ; upāyavailakṣaṇyādiyameva tāvadatra saraṇiḥ /
evaṃ sthite prathamapakṣa bālapriyā nāṭye iti chedaḥ /
rasasyoktarītyā naṭāśrayakatvena nāṭyāśrayakatvamityarthaḥ /
rāmādigatasthāyino 'nukāre naṭe sthāyyavabhāso mithyājñānarūpaḥ sāmājikānāṃ jāyate, sa eva camatkārakārī rasa iti kecittanmatamāha----anya ityādi /
'aśvāvabhāsa ive'tyanvayaḥ /
sa eveti /
avabhāsamānaḥ sthāyyevetyarthaḥ /
rasyamāna iti /
viṣayīkriyamāṇa ityarthaḥ /
nāṭyādrasā iti /
sthāyyavabhāsasya nāṭyahetukatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
matāntaramāha---apara ityādi /
vibhāvānubhāvamātrameveti /
rasa ityanenāsya sambandhaḥ /
kathamityatrāha---viśiṣṭetyādi /
viśiṣṭasāmagrayā bhāvakatvaviśiṣṭayā nāṭyādisāmagrayā /
samarpyamāṇamiti /
sāmājikeṣpiti śeṣaḥ /
taditi /
tābhyāṃ vibhavānubhavābhyāṃ kramādvibhāvaniyā anubhāvanīyā ca yā ratyādisthāyirūpacittavṛtyucitā vāsanā sāmājikagatā tadanuṣaktaṃ tatsambaddham /
sveti /
svasya sāmājikasya nirvṛtirūpā yā carvaṇā tadviśiṣṭaṃ tadviṣayabhūtam /
nāṭyameveti /
vibhavānubhavayornaṇṭanayogyatvarūpanāṭyatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
'śuddhaṃ vibhāvam' ityādau sarvatra rasamāhurityasya sambandho bodhyaḥ /
loketyādi /
"svabhāvābhinayopetaṃ na nāstrīpuruṣāśrayaṃ nāṭyaṃ lokadharmi" "svarālaṅkārasaṃyuktamasvasthapuruṣāśrayaṃ nāṭyaṃ nāṭyadharmi" tatsthānīyena tattulyena /
svabhāveti /
vakroktiśabdārthaḥ pūrvamuktaḥ /
dvayeneti tṛtīyārtho vaiśiṣṭyaṃ śabde 'nveti /
dvayenetyalaukikatve heturvā /
alaukiketi /
alaukiko laukikaśabdavyatiriktaḥ prasanno madhura ojasvī ca yaḥ śabdaḥ, tena samarpyamāṇānāṃ vibhāvādīnāṃ yogādityarthaḥ /
iyameveti /
uktaprakāraivetyarthaḥ /
rasavārtā rasapadārthaḥ tatpratītirvā /
astu vātreti /
atra kāvye /
vicitrarūpā vijātīyā /
atra hetumāha---upāyeti /
iyamiti /
vakṣyamāṇarūpetyarthaḥ /
locanam evaitāni dūṣaṇāni, pratīteḥ svaparagatatvādivikalpanena /
sarvapakṣeṣu ca pratītiraparihāryā rasasya /
apratītaṃ hi piśācavadavyavahārya syāt /
kiṃ tu yathā pratītimātratvenāviśiṣṭatve 'pi prātyakṣikī ānumānikī āgamotthā pratibhānakṛtā yogipratyakṣajā ca pratītirupāyavailakṣṇyādanyaiva, tadvadiyamapi pratītiścarvaṇāsvādanabhogāparanāmā bhavatu /
tannidānabhūtāyā hṛdayasaṃvādādyupakṛtāyā vibhāvādisāmagpyā lokottararūpatvāt /
rasāḥ pratīyanta iti odanaṃ pacatītivadyvavahāraḥ pratīyamāna eva hi rasaḥ /
pratītireva viśiṣṭā rasanā /
sā ca nāṭye laukikānumānapratītervilakṣaṇā; tāṃ ca pramukhe upāyatayā sandadhānā /
evaṃ kāvye anyaśābdapratītervilakṣaṇā, tāṃ ca pramukhe upāyatayāpekṣamāṇā /
tasmādanutthānopahataḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ /
rāmādicaritaṃ tu na sarvasya hṛdayasaṃvādīti mahatsāhasam /
citravāsanāviśiṣṭatvāccetasaḥ /

children.translated_text: Therein, manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) occurs either as primary or otherwise.
When primary, it is <s>dhvani</s>; otherwise, <s>rasa</s> and other <s>alaṅkāras</s> — thus he says: 'the primary meaning' etc.
'Established' — thus.
Because it has been established through division by the previously stated reasoning — this is the purport. // 4 //

[Balapriya:] In the karika beginning with 'the expressible' etc. and in the vrtti beginning with 'figures of sound' etc., lest there be confusion with another meaning, he explains the intended meaning — 'the expressible' etc.
Incidentally, intending to establish the nature of rasa, he first presents other positions as prima facie views — 'but it was said' etc.
The word 'but' (nanu) indicates an objection, and conveys the prima facie status of the views stated by <s>Bhatta Nayaka</s> and others.
Regarding 'how was it said?' — he explains with '<s>rasa</s>' etc. up to 'bestowal alone.'
'<s>Rasa</s>' — the meaning is: <s>srngara</s> (erotic sentiment) and other rasas, which have the form of <s>rati</s> (love) and other [permanent emotions].
'<s>Yad</s>' — in the sense of 'if.'
'<s>Para</s>' — the meaning is: other than the connoisseur (<s>sahrdaya</s>).
'Impartial' (<s>tatastha</s>) — the meaning is: having no relation to the connoisseur.
When there is impartiality, the capacity for being savored would not exist — this is the purport.
'And not' etc. — the syntactic connection is: 'that [rasa] is not cognized as belonging to oneself'; because there is no means to produce that [cognition] — this is the purport.
He states an invalidator for the acceptance of cognition as belonging to oneself — 'in one's own self' etc.
<s>Locana</s>: As belonging to oneself — that [rasa] is cognized from poetry consisting of the deeds of <s>Rama</s> and others.
And if cognized as belonging to one's own self, then the arising of <s>rasa</s> in one's own self would have to be accepted.
But that is unreasonable for <s>Sita</s> — because she is not a <s>vibhava</s> (determinant) for the spectator.
If [one argues that] 'beloved-ness' (<s>kantatva</s>) is universal and serves as an impelling factor for vibhava-status that causes the blossoming of latent impressions (<s>vasana</s>) — then how [would that work] in the case of deities, warriors (<s>varman</s>), etc.?
Nor is the remembrance of one's own beloved perceived [to occur] in between [the aesthetic experience].
And for <s>Rama</s> and others, who are not universally known, how could their <s>vibhavas</s> such as building the bridge over the ocean attain universality?
Nor is <s>Rama</s> remembered as possessing enthusiasm (<s>utsaha</s>) etc., because [such things] have not been experienced [by the spectator].
Even from verbal [testimony], upon cognizing that, there is no arising of <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Balapriya</s>: 'As belonging to one's own self' — as belonging to the self of the connoisseur (<s>sahrdaya</s>).
'In one's own self' etc. — the cognition of the apprehender takes the form of direct perception of one's own mental modification alone; and thus the arising of that mental modification is necessarily [implied].
Because direct perception is impossible without an object — this is the purport.
'Now, let the rasa arise!' — to this he says: 'but that' etc. 'But that' — and that arising of <s>rasa</s> in one's own self.
Since <s>Rama</s> etc. were mentioned earlier, '<s>Sita</s>' was said [as representative].
The meaning is: <s>Sita</s> and others [like her].
'The spectator' (<s>samajika</s>) — the meaning is: the connoisseur.
He raises an objection — 'beloved-ness' etc.
'Universal' (<s>sadharana</s>) — non-exclusive.
'<s>Vasana</s>' — the <s>vasana</s> (latent impression) of <s>rati</s> (love) etc. residing in the connoisseur; the <s>vibhava</s> (determinant) that is the cause of the blossoming, i.e., awakening, of that [vasana]; the status of that [vibhava], i.e., the vibhava-status that has the nature of being the cause of the blossoming of latent impressions — this is the meaning.
In the reading '<s>hetu</s>' — the construction is: 'being a cause.'
'Impelling factor' (<s>prayojaka</s>) — and thus, because of <s>Sita</s>'s human-ness, the connoisseurs experience the cognition of beloved-ness regarding <s>Sita</s> and others — this is the purport.
He responds — 'in the case of deities' etc.
'That too' — that cognition of beloved-ness too.
'How?' — the meaning is: when the heroine is described as a deity or warrior etc., the cognition of desirability in the form of beloved-ness does not arise regarding deities etc. because of the obstruction due to the knowledge of their being objects of worship — this is the meaning.
Now, when knowledge of <s>Sita</s> etc. arises from poetry, the connoisseurs' remembrance of their own beloved arises, and through that there is the awakening of those latent impressions — to this he says: 'nor' etc.
'Is not perceived' — is not experienced by the connoisseurs.
Regarding the heroic <s>rasa</s> (<s>vira</s>) too, he says — 'of those not universally known' etc.
'Not universally known' — different from what is commonly known.
'<s>Vibhavas</s>' — vibhavas of enthusiasm residing in the connoisseur.
'Universality' — universal applicability.
'How could they attain?' — the building of a bridge over the ocean etc. is a cause of enthusiasm; the cognition of one's own capacity to accomplish [such deeds], or the sympathy of the heart — [none of these] would arise in the connoisseurs: this is the purport.
The knowledge of the permanent emotion of enthusiasm etc. residing in <s>Rama</s> and others is also a cause of the awakening of <s>rasa</s> in the connoisseurs — that too is difficult [to establish] — he says: 'nor' etc.
Now, from poetry there arises a cognition in the form of experience — to this he says: 'even from verbal [testimony]' etc.
'Upon that cognition' — upon the cognition of the enthusiasm etc. residing in <s>Rama</s> etc.
'Even [granting it]' — this is the construction.
'No arising of <s>rasa</s>' — no arising of <s>rasa</s> for the connoisseurs.
Here he states an illustration — 'as from direct perception' etc.
<s>Locana</s>: As from direct perception — upon cognizing the couple consisting of the hero and heroine.
And in the origination view (<s>utpatti-paksa</s>), since the <s>karuna</s> (compassion) would be produced [as a real emotion], the unpleasantness thereof would cause non-engagement in further witnessing of compassion-themed [performances].
'Not that: neither origination, nor manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>); for if <s>srngara</s>, which has the nature of a latent capacity (<s>sakti</s>), were to be manifested, there would be a graduated striving for the acquisition of the object [of desire]; and even there [one faces] the same defect as before — does the <s>rasa</s> get manifested as belonging to oneself or as belonging to another?
Therefore, <s>rasa</s> is neither cognized, nor produced, nor manifested by poetry.
Rather, the distinctiveness of poetic language from other language [lies in] the three-fold capacity (<s>tryamsata</s>) of the word that is the essence of poetry.
Therein, the denotative capacity (<s>abhidhayakatva</s>) pertains to the expressible domain; the power of realization (<s>bhavakatva</s>) pertains to the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc.; and the power of producing relish (<s>bhogakrtva</s>) pertains to the domain of the connoisseur — thus three component operations.
Therein, if the denotative component were taken as pure [i.e., as the only operation], what difference would there be from scientific texts (<s>tantra</s>) and other treatises, [and from] figures like <s>slesa</s> (paronomasia)? And the variety of styles (<s>vrtti</s>) would be of no consequence.
And what would be the purpose of avoiding faults such as cacophony (<s>srutidusta</s>)?'
<s>Balapriya</s>: 'As from the cognizer' — the syntactic connection is 'as from direct perception.'
He states another objection — 'in the origination view' etc.
'Of the connoisseurs' — this is the remainder.
'In the witnessing of compassion' — in dramas dominated by the <s>karuna rasa</s> (compassionate sentiment).
'That' — the meaning is: therefore.
'Nor manifestation' — 'of <s>rasa</s>' is the remainder.
Because it is not previously established — this is the purport.
For only what is previously established — like a pot etc. — is manifested by a lamp etc.
Now, <s>rasa</s> in the form of <s>rati</s> (love) etc. exists in a subtle form as latent impressions (<s>vasana</s>) in the self of the connoisseurs, and hence is already established — to this he says: 'of what has the nature of a capacity' etc.
'Having the nature of a capacity' — abiding in a subtle form as latent impressions.
'Of <s>srngara</s>' — of <s>rati</s> (love).
The word '<s>srngara</s>' is an indicator (<s>upalaksaka</s>) for the heroic (<s>vira</s>) etc.
'In manifestation' — upon accepting manifestation in the heart of the connoisseur.
'Object' (<s>visaya</s>) — the object of <s>rati</s> etc. is the beloved etc.; meaning: the means of manifestation.
'Graduated striving' — striving in a more-and-more fashion for its acquisition, i.e., attainment.
Just as for a pot etc. situated in darkness, people strive for more and more acquisition of light, the means of its manifestation, for its progressively greater manifestation — so too for <s>rati</s> etc. abiding within as latent impressions, the connoisseurs' striving for progressively greater experiential acquisition of the <s>vibhavas</s> etc. that are the means of its manifestation would follow — this is the meaning.
Because with progressively greater experience of the object, the sudden manifestation of the latent impression is possible — this is the purport.
He states another objection — 'even there' etc.
'Even there' — even in the manifestation view.
He concludes — 'therefore' etc.
'Is not cognized' etc. — 'in the self of the connoisseur' is the remainder.
He states his own view — 'rather' (<s>kintu</s>) etc.
'Other language' — scientific language etc.: this is the meaning.
'Of the word' (<s>sabda</s>) — the three-fold capacity (<s>tryamsata</s>); from its relation (<s>prasada</s>): this is the meaning.
He shows the three-fold capacity — 'therein' etc.
'The expressible' — the expressible meaning is its domain — that [operation pertains to] the expressible-meaning domain: this is the meaning.
'<s>Rasa</s> etc.' — <s>rasa</s> is <s>rati</s> (love) etc.; by the word 'etc.' (<s>adi</s>), <s>vibhava</s> etc. are included.
He states the nature of <s>bhavakatva</s> and <s>bhogakrtva</s>, and then states the reasoning upon their acceptance — 'therein' etc.
'The denotative component' — the aspect of denotativeness.
'Pure' — untouched by the other operations; then indeed.
'From <s>tantras</s>' etc. — '<s>tantra</s>' is the single utterance of a word with the intention of conveying multiple meanings.
'What difference?' — the meaning is: there would be no difference between the two [i.e., poetry and scientific texts].
'Styles' (<s>vrtti</s>) — the varieties of style are <s>upanagarika</s> and others; their variety would be of no consequence.
The meaning is: if only denotation were accepted in poetry, it would be pointless.
'What purpose?' — the meaning is: it would be fruitless.
'Therefore' — the meaning is: by the stated reasoning.
'Realization of <s>rasa</s>' (<s>rasabhavana</s>) — the meaning is: the realization of <s>rati</s> (love) etc.
'Second' — the meaning is: occurring after denotation.
'By virtue of which' (<s>yadvasa</s>) — the meaning is: by the prompting agent that is the <s>bhavakatva</s> operation.
'Is entirely different' — the meaning is: is of a category entirely different from denotation belonging to scientific and other language.

But the <s>bhavakatva</s> of both [word and meaning together] has been stated by us alone.
'Where meaning or word suggests that meaning' — in that [passage].
Therefore, through the operation called suggestiveness (<s>vyanjakatva</s>), with the requirement (<s>itikartavyata</s>) of <s>gunas</s>, <s>alankaras</s>, and propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) etc. as instrumental causes, poetry realizes <s>rasas</s> — it produces them. Thus, even in the three-part realization (<s>bhavana</s>), the operation of <s>dhvanana</s> (suggesting) is supreme in the instrumental component.
And this relish-producing [function] — since <s>rasa</s>-savoring is non-different from aesthetic wonder — is established as naturally attained when the <s>dhvanana</s> operation is established.
And the variety of <s>sattva</s> etc. [in their] principal-subsidiary relations being infinite, the enumeration of savoring as effusion (<s>druti</s>) etc. is not appropriate.
And let this <s>rasa</s>-savoring have the nature of fellow-studentship with the savoring of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
And the education (<s>vyutpatti</s>) is distinct from those produced by instruction and demonstration [i.e., by the treatise and the epic/narrative tradition].
'Just as <s>Rama</s>, so am I' — who shall we blame for producing an education in the form of the spontaneous flowering of one's own poetic capacity, which transcends the standard of comparison?
Therefore this stands established: <s>rasas</s> are manifested, and it is through cognition alone that they are savored.
<s>Balapriya</s>: 'By you yourself [the origination view] has been revived' — this is the syntactic connection.
Here the reason is: 'because of realization' — because of accepting poetry's capacity to produce <s>rasa</s>: this is the meaning.
'By different words' — by ordinary language: this is the meaning.
The word-and-meaning complex that is poetry generates the <s>rasa</s>-savoring of the connoisseurs through its possession of appropriate <s>gunas</s> and <s>alankaras</s> — he says: 'therefore, through the operation called suggestiveness' etc.
Ritual sacrifice (<s>yaga</s>) and other <s>dharmas</s> are enjoined upon a person for the purpose of heaven etc. by Vedic sentences such as '<s>yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice).
As follows: in '<s>yajeta</s>,' there are two components — the verbal root '<s>yaji</s>' and the suffix.
In the suffix too, there are two components — the denotative component and the optative component.
By both components, <s>bhavana</s> (realization) alone is denoted.
<s>Bhavana</s> is the operation conducive to the coming-into-being of what is to come into being.
And it is twofold: objective (<s>arthi</s>) and verbal (<s>sabdi</s>).
The objective [bhavana] — having the form of an operation pertaining to an action generated by the desire for a purpose — is denoted by the denotative component.
It requires three components: the goal to be achieved (<s>sadhya</s>), the means (<s>sadhana</s>), and the procedure (<s>itikartavyata</s>).
'What is to be realized, by what, and how?'
Therein, when the goal is sought — heaven etc. as the desired goal.
When the means is sought — the verbal root's meaning, sacrifice etc., as the instrument. When the procedure is sought — the subsidiary rites such as <s>prayaja</s> etc. as the procedure — these apply to that <s>bhavana</s>: thus say the <s>Mimamsakas</s>.
And thus, just as the Vedic sentence '<s>yajeta</s>' etc. is productive (<s>bhavaka</s>) in the sense of enjoining upon a person for the purpose of heaven, realizing heaven through sacrifice as the instrument and through the procedure of subsidiary rites for one who desires heaven — so too poetry is productive (<s>bhavaka</s>), realizing <s>rasa</s> for the connoisseur through the instrument of the operation of suggestiveness and through the procedure consisting of propriety of <s>gunas</s> and <s>alankaras</s>: this is the meaning.
The word '<s>iti</s>' denotes manner; '<s>kartavyata</s>' means action.
The manner of the action — the procedure (<s>itikartavyata</s>) — means the auxiliary: this should be understood.
'Three-part' — possessing the three components of goal etc.: this is the meaning.
'In the realization' — in the realization of <s>rasa</s>: this is the meaning.
'In the instrumental component' — in the means-component.
'Causal component' — this is also a reading.
'Relish too' etc. — the syntactic connection is: 'is not produced.'
The negation (<s>nan</s>) is emphatic (<s>kaku</s>).
The meaning is: it is indeed produced. Or the reading is '<s>nanu kriyata</s>' — he states the distinction: 'rather' (<s>api tu</s>) etc.
The syntactic connection is: 'rather, in the relish to be produced, the transcendent operation of <s>dhvanana</s> alone is supreme.'
'Dense' (<s>ghana</s>) — the constriction (<s>sankatata</s>), i.e., the concealment of the bliss-portion, by the dense darkness in the form of ignorance in the form of clouds — through its removal, i.e., breaking, and thereby: this is the meaning.
'Transcendent' — different from the experience of ordinary pleasure.
'Relish' (<s>bhoga</s>) — direct realization of one's own consciousness (<s>atma-caitanya</s>) as delimited by the permanent emotion of <s>rati</s> etc. infused with the states (<s>bhava</s>) of <s>vibhava</s> etc. — with the breaking of the veil of the bliss-portion: this is the meaning.
'To be produced' — to be generated.
The poetry that is defined by following the principal meaning — the realization of <s>rasa</s>, its semblances (<s>abhasa</s>), and its subsidence (<s>prasama</s>) — in which the figures of sound, meaning, and <s>gunas</s> (qualities) exist in mutually distinct forms through their dependence on <s>dhvani</s> — in that poetry, the designation '<s>dhvani</s>' [applies].
<s>Locana</s>: Because relish, being savored, is non-different from the arising of aesthetic wonder — hence.
And because the variety of the principal-subsidiary relation of <s>sattva</s> etc. is infinite, the enumeration of savoring as effusion (<s>druti</s>) etc. is not appropriate.
And let this <s>rasa</s>-savoring have the nature of fellow-studentship (<s>sabrahmacari</s>) with the savoring of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
And the education is different from that produced by instruction (<s>sasana</s>) and demonstration (<s>pratipada</s>), i.e., by the treatise and the epic narrative.
'Just as <s>Rama</s>, so am I' — who shall we blame for producing an education in the form of the spontaneous flowering of one's own poetic capacity, which transcends the standard of comparison?
Therefore this stands established: <s>rasas</s> are manifested, and through cognition alone they are savored.

children.translated_text: The meaning is: <s>rasa</s>-experience is itself of the nature of cognition (<s>pratīti</s>).
'Therein, manifestation occurs as primary or otherwise' — thus.
'Otherwise' — as non-primary.
'Or as non-primary' — this is also a variant reading. // 4 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Mūrdhābhiṣikta</s>' (supreme) is the primary cause. /
<s>Kāvya</s> (poetry), by virtue of being its substratum, is a cooperating cause — this is the purport. /
'That is this' — /
'What you have said' — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Rasya</s>' — /
The <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder) that arises through the reason of being relished, that wonder-natured direct experience — because of its non-difference from that, because of its identity — this is the meaning. /
Keeping in mind what was previously stated beginning with '<s>druti</s>-<s>vistāra</s>' etc., he says: 'of <s>sattva</s> etc.' and so on. /
'<s>Aṅgāṅgibhāva</s>' (principal-subordinate relation) — /
The meaning is: lesser and greater degree. /
'Due to infinitude' — /
The meaning is: due to being innumerable. /
'In the form of <s>druti</s> etc.' — /
The meaning is: in the nature of <s>druti</s> etc. /
'Not proper' — /
Because of the infinitude of the causes, the infinitude of the past mental states is also impossible — this is the purport. /
Accepting a certain portion of what <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s> stated — 'the other [view]' etc. /
Keeping in mind that statement that <s>vyutpatti</s> (training) is indeed secondary, he says: '<s>vyutpādana</s> (instruction) etc.' /
'Of <s>kāvya</s> (poetry)' — this is the remainder. /
'<s>Śāsana</s> (teaching)' — /
Teaching by means of <s>śāstra</s> (treatise), instruction through <s>itihāsa</s> (history) — different from both of these — this is the meaning. /
Showing the difference, he says: 'as' etc. /
After 'I,' the remainder is 'should conduct myself.' /
The meaning is: I should act just as <s>Rāma</s> did. /
'Thus' etc. — /
The comparison (<s>upamiti</s>), the cognition of similarity, that is produced by <s>śāstra</s> and <s>itihāsa</s> — [poetry produces something] beyond that — this is the meaning. /
Not merely the stated comparison, but something more than that — this is the extent. /
'<s>Rasa</s>' — /
The creative intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) that serves as the means for the relishing of <s>rasa</s>, belonging to the perceiver himself — its blossoming, its expansion — of that nature — this is the meaning. /
'Produces' — /
'Poetry' — this is the remainder. /
For through repeated engagement with poetry, the blossoming of one's own creative intuition that serves as the means for <s>rasa</s>-relishing occurs. /
At the end, by the word 'produces,' it is indicated that [poetry] also produces the <s>vyutpatti</s> in the form of the comparison stated at the beginning. /
He concludes: 'therefore' etc. /
'This is established' — this is the connection. /
'<s>Rasas</s> are manifested' — /
The meaning is: the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotions) qualified by being the objects of manifestation are the referents of the word '<s>rasa</s>.' /
'Manifestation is according to the analogy of pot and lamp' — this will be stated. /
'<s>Pratīti</s>' etc. —
Where the sentence-meaning is predominantly something else, and where <s>rasa</s> and others are subsidiary —

children.translated_text: By the word '<s>rasavat</s>' and the word '<s>preyas</s>,' all the <s>rasavat</s> and other <s>alaṅkāras</s> are synecdochically indicated — this is what he says: '<s>rasa</s> and others are seen as subsidiary' — 'in the stated domain' is the remainder.
'<s>Bālapriyā</s>' — thus it has been stated.
"<s>Preyas</s> — <s>Vidura</s> spoke to <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> who had come to the house, as follows:

children.text: adya yā mama govinda jātā tvayi gṛhāgate //
children.translated_text: Today, O <s>Govinda</s>, the joy that has arisen in me upon your arrival at the house —

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Although the domain of the <s>rasavat</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure possessing <s>rasa</s>) has been demonstrated by others, nevertheless, in whatever poetry another meaning that has become the sentence-meaning is primary, and those <s>rasa</s> etc. that are subsidiary to it — they are the domain of the <s>alaṅkāra</s> called '<s>rasa</s>-etc.' — this is my position. /
For example, in <s>cāṭu</s>-poems (flattery verses), even when the <s>preyas</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure of endearment) has sentence-meaning status, <s>rasa</s> and others are seen as subsidiary. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Elsewhere' — /
In the essential nature of <s>rasa</s>, in mere content, or in the suitability for <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status. /
'My view' — keeping the opposing position in mind as refutable, he first presents his own position because it is desired — 'nevertheless' etc. /
For the domain demonstrated by others is as follows: [it is not established] in the manner to come — this is the purport. /
'In whatever poetry' — this apparently incongruent sentence should be construed thus: in whatever poetry the previously mentioned <s>rasa</s> etc. are subsidiary, and another meaning has become the sentence-meaning — the word '<s>ca</s>' has the sense of '<s>tu</s>' (but); those <s>rasa</s> etc. that are subsidiary, belonging to that poetry, are the domain of the <s>alaṅkāra</s>-designation '<s>rasavat</s>' etc.; that alone which is subsidiary is denoted by the word '<s>alaṅkāra</s>,' not anything else — this is the extent. /
He gives an example of this — 'for example' etc. /
'That' refers to subsidiarity. /
'As in this cited example, so elsewhere too' — this is the meaning. /
With the intention of <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s view, '[even when] in <s>cāṭu</s>-poems the <s>preyas</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s> has sentence-meaning status, <s>rasa</s> and others are seen as subsidiary' — this is one sentence. /
For <s>Bhāmaha</s> stated that the description of affection — devotion, parental love, etc. — directed toward teachers, gods, and princes is the <s>preyas</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] In the <s>Bālapriyā</s>-<s>kārikā</s>, 'elsewhere' means 'in something other than <s>rasa</s> etc.' — this is the meaning. /
Such sentence-meaning is of three kinds, he says: 'the essential nature of <s>rasa</s>' etc. /
'Suitable for <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status' — /
The meaning is: in <s>upamā</s> (simile) etc. /
Since <s>upamā</s> etc. are not <s>alaṅkāras</s> when they are primarily suggested, the word 'suitable' is used. /
'My view' — /
The meaning is: by this [phrase] 'my view.' /
'The opposing position' — /
The meaning is: the alternative position to be stated. /
'Nevertheless' — /
This is a word-commentary [on the root text]. /
He states the purport: 'for' etc. /
'Incongruent' — /
Because in 'and those that are subsidiary to it,' the word 'that' refers only to the poetry itself, and since it is impossible for the meaning thus literally construed — the subsidiarity determined in relation to that [poetry] — to apply to <s>rasa</s> etc., the passage has incongruent meaning — this is the meaning. /
'Those' etc. — /
The purport is that 'those <s>rasa</s> etc. that are subsidiary' connects with the preceding sentence as well. /
The explanation of 'those' is: 'previously mentioned.' /
The meaning is: those indicated in the <s>kārikā</s> beginning with '<s>rasabhāva</s>' etc. /
'Another' — other than <s>rasa</s> etc. /
'The word <s>ca</s>' — /
The meaning is: the word '<s>ca</s>' in 'and of that.' /
The explanation of 'of that' is: 'of the poetry.' /
'Belonging to' — this states the meaning of the genitive case. /
And thus, since the genitive-ending meaning of 'of that' has its connection with <s>rasa</s> etc. through the relation to poetry, there is no incongruity of meaning — this is the purport. /
'Subsidiary' — /
The meaning is: subsidiary to the other [element] that is the sentence-meaning. /
The elaboration of '<s>rasa</s>-etc.' is: '<s>rasavat</s> etc.' /
He states the result: 'that alone' etc. /
He begins to explain the passage 'in <s>cāṭu</s>-poems' etc.: '<s>Bhāmaha</s>' etc. /
'In <s>cāṭu</s>-poems' etc. up to 'are seen' is one sentence — this is also a variant reading. /
He elaborates: '<s>Bhāmaha</s>' etc. /
'<s>Guru</s>' etc. — /
The affection directed toward teachers etc. — devotion, parental love, etc. — expressed either by its own designating word or through <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) — this is the meaning. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Therein, where the <s>preyas</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s> resides — that <s>preyas</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s> is here called the embellishment-object (<s>alaṅkaraṇīya</s>). /
But it is not proper that the <s>alaṅkāra</s> itself should have sentence-meaning status. /
Or alternatively, 'sentence-meaning status' means 'predominance' — /
To the extent that it produces <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder) — this is the extent. /
But those who follow <s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s view explain differently: 'in <s>cāṭu</s>-poems' — in the domain of flattery-verses; 'when the sentence-meaning status,' i.e., when the <s>cāṭus</s> have sentence-meaning status; 'of the <s>preyas</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s> also' — its connection is with the preceding [word] 'domain.' /
For in <s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s view, <s>preyas</s> is stated as a <s>bhāva</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s> (emotional figure), love being a synecdoche for [all] <s>bhāvas</s>. /
The word '<s>api</s>' (also) means 'not only is this the domain of the <s>rasavat</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s>, but also of <s>preyas</s> and others' — he states the meaning of '<s>api</s>': 'not only' etc.
in time, this same joy would arise again only from your coming." //

children.translated_text: 'By love' — by love in the form of <s>rati</s> (pleasure/attachment), which constitutes the meaning of the word '<s>preyas</s>.'
'By synecdoche' — thus.
As stated by <s>Udbhaṭa</s>: 'That poetry which is composed by the wise through the indication of <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) etc.
of <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions) such as <s>rati</s> (love) and others — that is called <s>preyas</s>.' //

[This] has been demonstrated by the passage — this is the meaning. /
Therein, when that speech occurs: /
In the domain of <s>cāṭu</s> (flattery), in [verses] such as 'why with laughter' etc., the described prowess of the king etc. alone has sentence-meaning status, not the <s>preyas</s>-type <s>alaṅkāra</s> — therefore, he explains the word 'that' through resort to the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> construction: '<s>preyas</s>' etc. /
'Here' — /
The meaning is: in the sentence 'in <s>cāṭu</s>-poems' etc. /
'Sentence-meaning status' means being primarily conveyed by the sentence. /
With the intention of the literal meaning '<s>preyas</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s> is the <s>preyas</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s>,' he says: 'or alternatively' etc. /
He elaborates 'predominance': '<s>camatkāra</s>' etc. /
Ah, the prowess of the king by which the enemy-women experience such misfortune — the affection directed toward that prowess, being concerned with the affairs of enemy-women, has the nature of <s>camatkāra</s> (wonder) — this should be understood. /
'Differently' — /
The meaning is: breaking the sentence apart. /
He shows the interpretation: 'in <s>cāṭu</s>-poems' etc. /
'When the sentence-meaning status' — when being conveyed by the sentence. /
He states the result: 'of the <s>cāṭus</s>, the sentence-meaning status' etc. /
<s>Cāṭu</s> means the praiseworthy content, the described prowess of the king etc. /
The word '<s>api</s>' is in displaced order — he says: 'of the <s>preyas</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s> also' etc. /
The meaning is: of the <s>preyas</s>-type <s>alaṅkāra</s> also. /
'Where does it connect?' — to this he says: 'domain' etc. /
The meaning is: it connects with the word 'domain' that follows in singular form. /
'<s>Cāṭu</s>' is the remainder — the meaning is: the <s>cāṭu</s>-poem. /
'<s>Preyas</s> has been stated' — /
The meaning is: stated as the <s>preyas</s>-<s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
'<s>Preyas</s> has been stated' — this is also a variant reading. /
Here he states the reason: 'by love' etc.

children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] In the lover's case, "disregarded"; in the other [the fire-weapon's case], "shaken off."

children.text: avadhūta iti na pratīpsitaḥ bālapriyā kṣipta ityādyamarukastham /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "Rejected" (<s>avadhūta</s>) means not desired. "Cast aside" etc. is from <s>Amaruka</s>'s [<s>Amaruśataka</s>].
"He" (<s>saḥ</s>) — belonging to the time of the burning of <s>Tripura</s>; "<s>Śāmbhava</s>" means related to <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>).

children.text: āliṅganyo 'vadhūtastripurayuvatibhiḥ sāśrunetrotpalābhiḥ kāmīvārdrāparādhaḥ sa dahatu duritaṃ śāmbhavo vaḥ śarāgniḥ //
children.translated_text: "Worthy of embrace yet rejected by the <s>Tripura</s> maidens with tear-filled lotus-eyes, like a lover whose offense is fresh — may that <s>Śāmbhava</s> arrow-fire of yours burn away sin!"

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Here, the subsidiary status (<s>aṅgabhāva</s>) of the pure <s>karuṇa rasa</s> (compassionate sentiment) clearly constitutes the <s>rasavat alaṅkāra</s>. Thus, in such a domain, the subsidiary status of other <s>rasas</s> is equally evident. [<s>Locana</s>:] "Pure" means not mixed with another <s>rasa</s> serving as a subsidiary or with another <s>alaṅkāra</s>; but when mixed, it is "combined" (<s>saṅkīrṇa</s>). Because a dream resembles actual experience, the beloved is seen in the dream laughing. "You shall not leave me again" — now, knowing your deceitful nature, I shall not release you from my arm-embrace. Hence "with empty bangles." And reproach of one's own person is fitting — thus he says "who is this heartless one." "By whom were you" — even when a slip of the name occurs, I have never caused you distress. "In dreams" — in dream-experiences, in sleep-ramblings, "many" because of repeated occurrence. "Your kinsman, the enemy-women-folk" — thus he says. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "By the word <s>preyas</s>" — the meaning is: with the word <s>preyas</s> accompanied by the particle "also" (<s>api</s>). "<s>Rasa</s> etc. <s>alaṅkāras</s>" — the reading "<s>rasavat</s> etc. <s>alaṅkāras</s>" also exists. "That very" — the meaning is: from the very stated purport. He completes: "of the stated domain" — meaning in the context of flattery (<s>cāṭu</s>). The depiction of affection toward elders etc. is itself the <s>preyas alaṅkāra</s>; in the context of flattery, even when that is not principal, <s>rasas</s> etc. are subsidiaries either because of that affection or because of the king's glory as its object — this is the meaning of the line following <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s view. The depiction of <s>rati</s> (love), <s>hāsa</s> (laughter), and such specific emotional states is the <s>bhāva alaṅkāra</s>; that itself is the <s>preyas alaṅkāra</s>. In the flattery-context of "what use is laughter" etc., the flattery is the sentence-meaning, and therein both the <s>rasavat alaṅkāra</s> and <s>bhāva alaṅkāra</s> exist — this is the essential meaning following <s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s view. In the <s>vṛtti</s>: "that" etc. — the construction is "that <s>rasa</s> etc. is an <s>alaṅkāra</s>." The particle "ca" is for sentence-ornamentation. "Or" — the word "or" (<s>vā</s>) is used in the sense of aggregation. The reading "he illustrates with 'what' (<s>kim</s>)" is absent in some [manuscripts]. He addresses the beloved seen in a dream — "what" etc. The meaning is: there is nothing to be accomplished by laughter now. He explains the appropriateness of seeing [the beloved] laughing — "of the dream" etc. "You shall not" etc. — the meaning is: you shall not go away from me henceforth. He states the import of this — "now" etc. Him whose deceitful nature has been discovered. "The deceitful one who secretly causes displeasure" — thus in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s>. He states the indicator of the stated meaning — "hence" etc. "Of one's own person" — meaning of one's own people; the genitive is in the objective sense. The connection is "this travel-loving [woman], who." "Who" — meaning: how improper! He states the import of "by whom" etc. — "slip of the name" etc. [<s>Locana</s>:] The beloved, clinging specifically in his embrace, whose throat-grip is such — being in just that state, upon awakening, with arm-embrace rendered empty-bangled, weeps aloud. Here, through the <s>śoka</s> (grief) <s>sthāyibhāva</s> kindled by the dream-vision, through the <s>karuṇa rasa</s> being savored, the king's glory shines forth beautified — thus <s>karuṇa</s> is purely an <s>alaṅkāra</s>. For this sentence-meaning is not as it would be unadorned ("it is not that enemies were slain by you"), but rather the sentence-meaning is made more beautiful here, and the beauty is produced by <s>karuṇa rasa</s> alone. Just as by a concrete thing like the moon, another thing like a face is ornamented — because it appears beautiful through being compared to it — similarly, when a thing or another <s>rasa</s> is embellished by a <s>rasa</s>, it shines beautifully. So what objection is there to <s>rasa</s> also being an ornament, just like a concrete thing? Objection: by <s>rasa</s> doing what is the main subject ornamented? Response: then by <s>upamā</s> (simile) too, doing what would it ornament? Objection: by it the main subject is compared. Response: by <s>rasa</s> too, then, that subject is made savorous — this is self-evident. Therefore, what some have objected — "here, among the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., what is ornamented by <s>rasa</s>?" — that is refuted by non-acceptance; because the main subject (<s>prastutārtha</s>) has been designated as the thing to be ornamented. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "In many" — this explains the plural number. "Your" (<s>vaḥ</s>) is explained as "your kinsman." He elaborates what was stated in the <s>vṛtti</s> — "here the subsidiary status of pure <s>karuṇa rasa</s>" — with "here" etc. The connection is: "here the king's glory shines beautified by such <s>karuṇa rasa</s>." "Being savored" means being an object of the connoisseurs' savoring. "<s>Alaṅkāra</s>" — meaning it is an <s>alaṅkāra</s> because it embellishes the sentence-meaning in the form of the king's glory being described. He substantiates what was said — with "for not" etc. The construction is: "this sentence-meaning is not as it is unornamented, this is not such — for." "And of the beauty" — meaning: and the beauty of the sentence-meaning. He substantiates with an example what was said "produced by <s>karuṇa rasa</s> alone" — with "by the moon" etc. up to "what objection." "Is ornamented" — the rest is: in poetry such as "her whose face is beautiful as the moon." He raises an objection — "but" (<s>nanu</s>). He responds — "then" (<s>tarhi</s>). He replies — "but." He gives the same reply — "by <s>rasa</s> too." "Is made savorous" means is made to possess <s>rasa</s>. "Self-evident" means established through the connoisseurs' own experience. "Therefore" — meaning: for the reason to be stated. "That" means the objection. "By non-acceptance" — meaning: refuted by the reason of non-acceptance of the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. as things to be ornamented. Then who is to be ornamented? — to this he says "of the main subject" etc. The main subject is the intended, the topic at hand. In "what use is laughter" etc., through the narrated incident of the enemy-women, the king's glory is conveyed through the suggestion of the beloved's destruction as its cause — that itself is the main subject. This should be noted in other cases too. "By designation" — meaning: by the <s>vṛttikāra</s>'s demonstration. An example of the combined (<s>saṅkīrṇa</s>) type where <s>rasa</s> etc. is subsidiary: "Cast aside, clinging to [her] hand, forcibly struck yet seizing the garment-edge, grasping [her] hair yet pushed away, falling at [her] feet yet not looked at with agitation." [<s>Locana</s>:] He shows the real state — with "thus." Where the proclamation of a king's etc. glory is of such a nature — that is the meaning. "Cast aside" —

children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The verse beginning with "in <s>rasa</s>" etc. is an ancillary verse (<s>parikara-śloka</s>).

children.text: tatra sarvāsāmalaṅkṛtīnāmityasya yatra hi rasasya vākyārthībhāvastatra kathamalaṅkāratvam? alaṅkāro hi cārutvahetuḥ prasiddhaḥ; na tvasāvātmaivātmanaścārutvahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] Regarding the statement "of all embellishments" — where <s>rasa</s> has the status of being the sentence-meaning, how can it have the status of an <s>alaṅkāra</s>? For an <s>alaṅkāra</s> is well-known as a cause of beauty; but it cannot be itself the cause of its own beauty.
And thus, here is the summary: The establishment of the ornament-status of all embellishments depends on the placement [of <s>rasas</s> etc.] based on the purport of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc.
This is the proof of the ornament-status of all embellishments. //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Here, the extraordinary glory of the enemy of <s>Tripura</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) is the sentence-meaning, while the jealous love-in-separation (<s>īrṣyā-vipralambha</s>) accompanied by <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) is subsidiary — thus, this alone is the proper domain of the <s>rasavat</s> and other <s>alaṅkāras</s>. And precisely because of the establishment of both <s>īrṣyā-vipralambha</s> and <s>karuṇa</s> in subsidiary status, their co-presence is not a fault. [<s>Locana</s>:] By the reciprocal embrace; in the other case [the fire-weapon], made to blaze by the shaking of all limbs. The tearfulness is due to jealousy in one case, and due to hopelessness in the other. By the simile "like a lover" (<s>kāmīva</s>), the jealous love-in-separation that is evoked, favored by <s>śleṣa</s> — the subsidiary status belongs to that [<s>vipralambha</s>] together with <s>śleṣa</s> and <s>upamā</s>, not to it alone. Although the <s>karuṇa rasa</s> also genuinely exists here, nevertheless, since it does not function for the apprehension of the beauty of <s>vipralambha</s> — with this intent he said only "accompanied by <s>śleṣa</s>" and not also "accompanied by <s>karuṇa</s>." To confirm this point, which he conceived as novel, he says "of precisely this type." "Hence" — since here <s>vipralambha</s> has the status of <s>alaṅkāra</s> and not of the sentence-meaning, for that reason — this is the meaning. "Not a fault" — for if one of the two <s>rasas</s> had been principal, the second <s>rasa</s> could not have co-existed. But <s>vipralambha</s>, having <s>rati</s> as its <s>sthāyibhāva</s>, is of a dependent nature, and it is indeed contradictory to <s>karuṇa</s>, which, having <s>śoka</s> as its <s>sthāyibhāva</s>, is of an independent nature. Thus, having established their co-presence through the occasion of the term <s>alaṅkāra</s> — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The connection is "may the arrow-fire burn your sin." Who is he? He whose offense is fresh, i.e., just occurred at that time. "Like a lover" — while clinging to [her] hand. "Whose lotus-eyes are tear-filled" — by such women. "By the <s>Tripura</s> maidens, cast aside" — thus the syntactic connection. There he explains the meaning of "cast aside" — "lover" etc. "In the other case" — meaning in the arrow-fire interpretation. He himself demonstrates the subsidiary status stated in the <s>vṛtti</s> — "like a lover" etc. "Evoked" means clearly suggested. "Of that" — of that jealous love-in-separation. This explains "accompanied by <s>śleṣa</s>" — "<s>śleṣa</s>" etc. "Subsidiary status" — meaning subsidiary status with respect to the sentence-meaning in the form of the extraordinary glory of <s>Tripura</s>'s enemy. "Not of it alone" — this connects with "its subsidiary status." "<s>Karuṇa rasa</s> also exists" — and accordingly one should also say "accompanied by that." This is the purport. "That" (<s>sa</s>) means <s>karuṇa</s>. "For the apprehension of its beauty" — for the apprehension of the beauty of <s>vipralambha</s>. "Does not function" — the purport is that <s>karuṇa</s> does not here have subsidiary status to <s>vipralambha</s>. He glosses "hence" — with "since" etc. "Sentence-meaning status" — meaning principal status as the thing to be ornamented. "Of one of the two <s>rasas</s>" — meaning of one among <s>vipralambha</s> and <s>karuṇa</s>. "Principal" means equally principal. "Second" means the other of the two. "Could not co-exist" — the rest is: in a single poem. Here he states the reason — "<s>rati</s>" etc. This topic will be discussed in the Third <s>Udyota</s>.
