children.translated_text: When <s>bhāva</s> (emotion) has subsidiary status (<s>aparāṅgatva</s>), it is the <s>bhāva-alaṅkāra</s> (emotion-figure); that same is also called <s>preyas</s> (the endearing) — and also <s>preyān</s>.
When <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>) and <s>bhāvābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>bhāva</s>) have subsidiary status — [that is] <s>ūrjasvin</s> (the vigorous).

children.text: locanam tatra bhāvālaṅktārasya śuddhasyodāharaṇaṃ yathā--- tava śatapatrapatramṛdutāmratalaścaramaścalakalahaṃsanūpurakaladhvaninā mukharaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Locana</s>: Therein, an example of the pure <s>bhāva-alaṅkāra</s> is as follows: 'Your foot — soft as a lotus-petal, with a coppery sole, /
resounding with the tinkling sound of the anklets like playful young swans —

children.text: mahiṣamahāsurasya śirasi prasabhaṃ nihitaḥ kanakamahāmahīdhragurutāṃ kathamamba gataḥ //
children.translated_text:
placed forcefully upon the head of the great demon <s>Mahiṣa</s> — /
how, O Mother, did it attain the weight of the great golden mountain [<s>Sumeru</s>]?'

<s>Locana</s>: What was stated as 'of this very kind' — he explains the intention of the particle '<s>eva</s>' (only/precisely) therein: 'for where' etc. /
Of all [figures] — <s>upamā</s> etc. /
Now, the purport is this: whatever reason [there is] for the <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status of <s>upamā</s> etc., just such is the reason for [the <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status] of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
Therefore, there must necessarily be some other embellished entity (<s>alaṅkārya</s>). /
And although that [embellished entity] may be even a mere thing (<s>vastu</s>), nevertheless, since that [thing] again ultimately culminates in the form of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., there is purposive intent (<s>tātparya</s>) toward <s>rasa</s> etc. alone — hence everywhere the essence-status (<s>ātmabhāva</s>) belongs to <s>rasa-dhvani</s> alone. /
As was stated: 'the purposive intent is toward <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc.' /
'Of that' — of the principal, which has become the essence. /
What has been stated amounts to this: although the expressible meaning is embellished by <s>upamā</s> (simile), nevertheless, that very embellishment of it consists in the endowment of the capacity to manifest the suggested meaning — hence, in reality, the embellished entity is of the nature of <s>dhvani</s> itself. /
For even by bracelets (<s>kaṭaka</s>), armlets (<s>keyūra</s>), etc., which inhere in the body, it is the conscious self (<s>ātman</s>) alone that is embellished — by virtue of being indicative of the appropriateness of the specific mental dispositions belonging to that [self]. /
For thus: an insentient — <s>Bālapriyā</s>: lest there be the confusion of meaning that 'the embellished entities are those of the <s>rasavat</s> and other <s>alaṅkāras</s>,' he explains: 'of <s>upamā</s> etc.' etc. /
'Of <s>upamā</s> etc.' — the meaning is: of <s>upamā</s> etc. and of <s>rasavat</s> etc. /
Intending to introduce the passage beginning with '<s>rasabhāve</s>' etc., he says: 'now, the purport' etc. /
'Whatever reason' — the meaning is: whatever cause. /
And that is: being embellished by another. /
'Therefore' — the meaning is: the embellished entity. /
'A mere thing' — as in the passage beginning with 'what use is laughter,' where [it is] the power of the king etc. /
'Of that' — the meaning is: of the thing. /
'Of <s>rasa-dhvani</s>' — the meaning is: of <s>rasa</s>-<s>bhāva</s> etc. <s>dhvani</s>. /
In 'what use is laughter' etc., the <s>rati-bhāva</s> (emotion of love) directed toward the king being described, made manifest by his power — that is the principal. /
'By <s>upamā</s>' — the meaning is: by <s>upamā</s> etc. /
'Of that' — the meaning is: of the expressible meaning. /
'Of the suggested meaning' — the meaning is: of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
The expressible meanings being described — endowed with surplus [beauty] by the <s>alaṅkāras</s> such as <s>upamā</s> etc. — clearly suggest the specific mental disposition residing in the poet, the hero-character, or some other [person], and sometimes also another meaning — thus the endowment of the capacity to manifest the suggested meaning, effected by <s>upamā</s> etc. upon the expressible meaning, is the embellishment: this is the meaning. /
'Of the nature of <s>dhvani</s>' — the meaning is: the essence (<s>ātman</s>) has the form of <s>dhvani</s>. /
He gives a worldly illustration for the stated meaning: 'bracelet' etc. /
'The self alone' — not the body. /
'How is the self embellished?' — to this he says: 'the various' etc. /
The various specific mental dispositions such as being amorous (<s>rāgitva</s>) etc. that belong to the self — the appropriateness of those [dispositions] — by virtue of indicating that, i.e., by the nature of being suggestive of that, the various ornaments suggest: 'this person's mental disposition is appropriate to this [ornament].' Just as ornaments such as necklace, bracelet, earrings etc. adorning the body of a young person indicate the appropriateness of amorousness for that [person]; and staff, ochre garment, etc. adorning the body of an ascetic indicate the appropriateness of detachment — by being indicative of those [dispositions]: this is the meaning. /
He substantiates what was stated: 'for thus' etc. /
Therefore, where <s>rasa</s> etc. have become the sentence-meaning, all of that is not the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc. as <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) — it is a variety of <s>dhvani</s>; <s>upamā</s> etc. are its <s>alaṅkāras</s>. /
But where, with the sentence-meaning status of another thing as primary, the production of beauty is effected by <s>rasa</s> etc. — that is the domain of the <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
Thus, the distinct domains of <s>dhvani</s>, <s>upamā</s> etc., and the <s>rasavat</s> <s>alaṅkāra</s> are [established]. /
But if it is said that where insentient [things] have sentence-meaning status — that is the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc. as <s>alaṅkāra</s> — <s>Locana</s>: a corpse adorned with earrings etc. does not shine, because of the absence of an embellished entity. /
An ascetic's body equipped with bracelets etc. becomes laughable, because of the inappropriateness [of the ornaments] to the embellished entity. /
For the body itself has no inappropriateness — in reality, it is the self alone that is the embellished entity, because of the self-awareness 'I am adorned.' /
'Of the <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status of <s>rasa</s> etc.' — the sixth cases are of different substrates (<s>vyadhikaraṇa</s>): 'the <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status that belongs to <s>rasa</s> etc. — that [poetry] is its very domain.' /
Following this, the earlier passage too should be construed: 'the domain of the act of embellishment performed by <s>rasa</s> etc.' /
'Thus' — the meaning is: by the domain-division stated by us. /
'Of <s>upamā</s> etc.' — where <s>rasa</s>'s embellished-entity status [obtains] and there is no other <s>rasa</s> as subsidiary — there, <s>upamā</s> etc. are pure [figures]; hence, by [the possibility of] combination [with <s>rasavat</s>], there is no encroachment upon the domain of <s>upamā</s> etc.: this is the purport. /
'And of the <s>rasavat</s> <s>alaṅkāra</s>' — by this, the <s>bhāva</s>-<s>alaṅkāras</s> too — <s>preyas</s>, <s>ūrjasvin</s>, <s>samāhita</s> — are included. /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'because of the absence of an embellished entity' — because of the insentience of the corpse: this is the purport. /
By this, the statement 'the sentient alone is embellished' has been substantiated. /
'Of an ascetic's body' etc. — for bracelets etc. indicate the appropriateness of amorousness. /
And amorousness is inappropriate for an ascetic's self — hence bracelets etc. adorning the ascetic's body are laughable: this is the meaning. /
The appropriateness of specific mental dispositions belonging to the various sentient selves for those selves — that [appropriateness] is [what makes] those [ornaments] embellishing; otherwise they are laughable: this is the purport. /
He states experiential evidence too: 'I' etc. /
'Of different substrates' — the purport is: the two words are not co-referential. /
He explains: 'of <s>rasa</s> etc.' etc. /
'The <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status residing in <s>rasa</s> etc.' — the agency of <s>rasa</s> etc. in the act of embellishment — that is, the embellishment performed by <s>rasa</s> etc.: this is the extent. /
'That alone is its domain' — this is the connection. /
'That' — the pronoun refers back to what was stated in the <s>vṛtti</s>; the correlate of 'where' — that poetry: this is the meaning. /
'Domain' — substrate. /
'Earlier' — the meaning is: in the sentence 'all of that is not the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc. as <s>alaṅkāra</s>.' /
He states the construal: '<s>rasa</s> etc.' etc. /
In this sentence too, 'that' is the correlate of 'where.' /
He shows the distinct domains of <s>upamā</s> etc. and <s>rasavat</s> etc.: 'where' etc. /
'By combination' — the meaning is: by combination with <s>rasavat</s> etc. /
The elaboration of '<s>bhāva</s> etc. <s>alaṅkāras</s>' is: '<s>preyas</s>, <s>ūrjasvin</s>, <s>samāhita</s>.' /
'<s>Samāhita</s> etc.' — this is also a reading.

Here, in this hymn to the <s>Devī</s>, [the fact that] the <s>bhāva</s> (emotion) of <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation), <s>vismaya</s> (wonder), etc., having become the sentence-meaning, is the cause of beauty —
because of its subsidiary status, it is the domain of the <s>bhāva-alaṅkāra</s> (emotion-figure).

children.text: rasābhāsasyālaṅkāratā yathā mamaiva stotre--- samastaguṇasampadaḥ samamalaṅkriyāṇāṃ gaṇair-- bhavanti yadi bhūṣaṇaṃ tava tathāpi no śobhase /
children.translated_text: The <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status of <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>) is as follows — in my own hymn: 'Even if the hosts — equal in their aggregate of all qualities — become your ornaments,

children.text: śivaṃ hṛdayavallabhaṃ yadi yathā tathā rañjayeḥ tadeva nanu vāṇi te bhavati sarvalalokottaram //
children.translated_text:
still you do not shine. If you would delight <s>Śiva</s>, [your] heart's beloved, in whatever way — /
that alone, O <s>Vāṇī</s> (Goddess of Speech), becomes for you what transcends all worlds.'

children.translated_text: that would be to declare the <s>rasa</s>-lessness of great poetic compositions (<s>kāvya-prabandha</s>) that are repositories of <s>rasa</s>.
For example — <s>Locana</s>: because it is also stated that '[<s>śṛṅgāra</s> has] the nature of a noble youth, with a brilliant appearance.'

children.text: bhāvābhāsāṅgatā yathā--- sa pātu vo yasya hatāvaśeṣāstattulyavarṇāñjanarañjiteṣu /
children.translated_text: The subsidiary status of <s>bhāvābhāsa</s> (semblance of emotion) is as follows: 'May He protect you — He whose [enemies], slain until only a remnant remained — [yet] in [the eyes of] their own wives,
though endowed with loveliness, though the pupils were tinged with collyrium of the same hue as those [slain demons] — the <s>Daityas</s> tremble [even at their wives' eyes].'

Here, the mere praise of the Supreme Lord is the supremely valuable [content] of speech — this is the sentence-meaning; and the <s>śṛṅgārābhāsa</s> (semblance of the erotic), accompanied by <s>śleṣa</s> (pun), is the cause of beauty. /
For this is not a full <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, since the heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>) lacks qualities and lacks ornamentation. /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: the distinction is that when the quiescence of <s>bhāva</s> (<s>bhāvaśānti</s>) has subsidiary status, [it is] <s>samāhita</s> (the composed). /
'Pure' — the meaning is: not combined with another <s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
'Your' — O Mother, your [foot]. /
'<s>Śata</s>' etc. — '<s>śatapatra</s>' is a lotus; its petal — soft like that and coppery — is the sole (<s>tala</s>), the lower part, of which: [describing] that [foot]. /
'A tinkling sound of playful young swan-like anklets' — [the foot is] 'resounding' with that sound. /
The foot [is placed] upon the head of the great demon named <s>Mahiṣa</s>. /
'Forcefully' — upon the head, having been placed. /
'The great golden mountain' — the mountain (<s>parvata</s>) which is made of gold, [i.e.,] <s>Sumeru</s>. /
By the statement of being made of gold, the excess of heaviness is indicated. /
The connection is: 'how did it attain heaviness?' /
The attainment of heaviness is ascertained through the crushing of <s>Mahiṣa</s>'s head: this is the purport. /
'In the hymn to the <s>Devī</s>' — the meaning is: when the power of the <s>Devī</s> is being praised, or in the <s>rati-bhāva</s> (emotion of love) directed toward that. /
'Deliberation' — the deliberation etc. is understood from the word 'how.' /
Although here the purity of <s>vitarka</s> etc. is difficult [to maintain] because of combination with the <s>upamā</s> stated in '<s>śatapatra</s>' etc., nevertheless, since <s>vitarka</s> etc. can arise even from the mere statement '<s>mṛdu-tāmra-tala</s>' (soft and coppery-soled), and since the <s>upamā</s> is not a subsidiary of that [<s>vitarka</s>], the purity consisting in its non-contamination [by other figures] is easily [established]. /
'Of all' etc. — superimposing heroine-status [upon the goddess <s>Vāṇī</s>], this is a reply to one's own speech. /
O <s>Vāṇī</s>! The excellences (<s>sampad</s>) of all qualities — <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) etc. and also beauty etc. /
Of ornamentations — <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), <s>upamā</s>, etc. and also bracelets etc. /
Together with hosts. /
If they become your ornament, although [that is so], still you do not shine. /
Then how does beauty arise? — to this he says: '<s>Śiva</s>' etc. /
You [would delight] <s>Śiva</s>, the heart's beloved of all, i.e., dear as the self. /
'<s>Śiva</s>' also [means] the Supreme Lord and also the auspicious-formed, dearest [beloved]. /
'In whatever way' — by whatever means. /
With or without the accompaniment of <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s>: this is the meaning. /
'Would delight' — would please through the exposition of qualities, and also would charm [romantically]. /
If so, then that very [act of delighting], that very charming — /
becomes for you an ornament that transcends all worlds: this is the meaning. /
Here, he elaborates the semblance-nature of the suggested <s>śṛṅgāra</s>: 'not indeed' etc. /
'For' (<s>hi</s>) — since. /
When the heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>) lacks qualities and lacks ornamentation, the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is not full — hence this [is a semblance].

He refutes this: 'then' etc.
The meaning is: 'from that statement, i.e., from that reason.' //

Here, the terror of those whose nature is fierce (<s>raudra</s>) — being inappropriate [for them] — is caused by the power of the Lord: thus it is a <s>bhāvābhāsa</s> (semblance of emotion). /
Likewise, the subsidiary status of <s>tatpraśama</s> (quiescence of that) should be illustrated.

'For us' — /

children.translated_text: [Our] view is: [the verse beginning with] 'With waves as frowning brows, with a girdle of agitated rows of birds, dragging foam like a garment loosened by impetuosity,

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'But description of the inanimate has been stated as the domain' — anticipating this objection, he states the reason: '<s>yasmāt</s>' (because) etc. /
'In some way or another' — in the form of <s>vibhāva</s> (stimulus) etc. /
'In that' — /
'In the construal as a narrative about a sentient being.' /
'Lack of <s>rasa</s>' — /
Now, where there is <s>rasa</s> [as the principal], there necessarily also exists the <s>rasavat-alaṅkāra</s> (figure of <s>rasa</s>) — this is the view of others. /
Therefore, if there is no <s>rasavat-alaṅkāra</s>, then surely there is no <s>rasa</s> there — the 'lack of <s>rasa</s>' is stated in accordance with the view of others. /
But for us, the absence of <s>rasavat-alaṅkāra</s> does not [entail] the absence of <s>rasa</s>. /
Rather, [it is] the absence of <s>rasa</s> that constitutes the soul of <s>dhvani</s>; and such <s>rasa</s> does indeed exist here. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Complete' — the meaning is: not [complete]. /
Rather, [it is] a semblance (<s>ābhāsa</s>) — this is the purport. /
'Of whom' — the sixth case is in the sense of the agent's remainder. /

'Equal to the description of the Lord' — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Sva</s>' etc. — /
'Being seen' is the remainder. /
'Thus a semblance of <s>bhāva</s>' — /
Therein, when the <s>rasa</s> is subordinated (<s>guṇībhāva</s>) because the <s>rati</s> (love) is stimulated by the divine majesty (<s>bhagavatprabhāva</s>), there is a semblance of <s>bhāva</s> — the <s>ūrjasvin-alaṅkāra</s> (figure of vigorous emotion) — this is the meaning. /
With the passage '<s>yadi tu</s>' etc., he states the meaning to be understood: '<s>parasya</s>' etc. /
'Its description' — /

'That' — /

'Distinct' — /
'Description of the inanimate' — this is the meaning. /
'That alone' — this is the construal. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, he raises a doubt: '<s>atha</s>' etc. /
'In that' — /
'In the construal as a narrative about a sentient being' — this is the meaning. /
'This one' — /
'<s>Yatra</s>' — this is the back-reference. /
'Of that, a great one' — /
'<s>Tat</s>' — then; '<s>mahataḥ</s>' — of the greater [portion]. /
The statement of 'lack of <s>rasa</s>' is not in accordance with one's own view, but rather in accordance with the view of others — he says in the <s>Locana</s>: '<s>yatra hi</s>' etc. /
'<s>Rasa</s>' — /
'The principal sentence-meaning' is the remainder. /
'Of others' — /

children.translated_text: 'Whose blossoming has ceased due to the absence of her own season — this one is empty of ornaments, as it were.' /
He establishes the heroine's casting off of ornaments: '<s>viyoga</s>' etc. /
'Due to the emaciation caused by separation and also due to remorse' — this is the meaning. /

children.text: cintā maunamivāśritā madhukṛtāṃ śabdairvinā lakṣyate caṇḍī māmavadhūya pādapatitaṃ jātānutāpeva sa //
children.translated_text: [Verse continued:] 'Contemplation has assumed the guise of silence; she is perceived without the sounds of bees; she is wrathful, having rejected me who fell at her feet — [yet] she seems to have become remorseful.'

Or [consider]: 'Slender, with lips washed by tears, as if [she were] a shoot moistened by cloud-water; empty of ornaments, as it were; her blossoming ceased due to the absence of her own season —' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'With waves as brows' — /
The waves themselves are the frowning brows of hers; 'dragging' — pulling along, forcibly drawing; /
'Garment' — cloth. /
The purport is: as if to prevent the beloved from holding on [to her]. /
'Repeatedly' — whatever stumbles, i.e., whatever offenses — aiming at those, i.e., collecting them in her heart — the impatient woman (<s>māninī</s>) — this is the meaning. /
And furthermore: overcome by remorse after my separation, [and yet] patient [enough] to seek the cooling of her grief, she has assumed the state of a river — [thus]. /
'Slender' — /
Emaciated by separation, and yet remorseful, she casts off her ornaments. /
'Her own season' — mostly the spring and summer. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '[Our view] is the remainder.' /
'Of such a kind' — /
'That which constitutes the soul of <s>dhvani</s>' — this is the meaning. /
'Here' — /
'In the examples to be stated' — this is the meaning. /
'With waves as brows' — /
'<s>Asahanā</s>' (impatient) — this is <s>Urvaśī</s>. /
'In the form of a river' — '<s>nadībhāvena</s>' (by the state of being a river) is also a reading. /
'Has become — undoubtedly' — this is an <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy). /
'This is not a river, but rather she' — I imagine — this is the meaning. /
He substantiates what was said: 'with waves as brows' etc. /
In [the attributions] 'waves as brows' etc., there is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) through the superimposition of brow-ness etc. /
'Like a garment' — this is <s>upamā</s> (simile). /
'Loosened by impetuosity' — loosened in its binding due to the rush of anger. /
'<s>Yathā</s>' — /
'<s>Yataḥ</s>' (since) — this is the meaning; '<s>tataḥ</s>' (therefore) is the remainder. /
'<s>Āviddham</s>' (crookedly) — crookedly. /
Alternatively, '<s>yathāviddham</s>' is a single word — meaning: not transgressing crookedness. /
'Aiming at stumbles' — in the case of the river, 'having encountered stumbling on rocks etc.' — this is the meaning. /
In the <s>Locana</s>: 'waves as brows' etc. — /
Likewise, 'agitated rows of birds are the girdle' — this should be understood. /
'Offenses' — /
'Mine' is the remainder. /
'Impatient woman' — /
'An angry one' — this is the meaning. /
'Patient' — /
'Because of impatience, as it were' — this is the meaning. /
'Slender' — /
Before this, 'this one' is understood — /
'This one' — a creeper. /
'<s>Caṇḍī</s>' — exceedingly wrathful. /
For this very reason, she remained having rejected, i.e., scorned, me who had fallen at her feet. /
For this very reason, she has become remorseful. /
'She' — appears to be <s>Urvaśī</s>. /
The three <s>utprekṣās</s> (poetic fancies) belonging to this [description] are stated with '<s>tanvī</s>' etc. /
'<s>Tanvī</s>' — common to both [the creeper and the woman]. /
'This one' — a creeper. /
'Whose shoots are moist from cloud-showers' — the state of having such [shoots]; by that, i.e., because of that — 'whose lower lip is washed by tears, as it were' — /

children.text: yathā vā---- teṣāṃ gopavadhūvilāsasuhṛdāṃ rādhārahaḥsākṣiṇāṃ kṣemaṃ bhadra kalindaśailatanayātīre latāveśmanām /
children.translated_text: Or [consider]: 'Is it well with those bower-houses on the bank of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> mountain — those which were friends to the dalliances of the cowherd-women, witnesses to the secret loves of <s>Rādhā</s> —

children.translated_text: whose leaves of tender love-bed fashioning have had their use severed? Now, I imagine, those shoots are becoming withered, their dark lustre fading.'

children.translated_text:
[<s>Locana</s>:] The silence is for the purpose of considering a means [of union]; 'Why did I reject my beloved even when he fell at my feet?' — and the silence is from this thought. /
'<s>Caṇḍī</s>' — an angry woman. /
These two verses are primarily about the description of rivers and creepers, and in their purport are utterances of <s>Purūravas</s> who is seized by madness. /
'Of those' — /
O good one! 'Of those' — those who are established in my very heart. /
Of the <s>gopavadhūs</s> (cowherd women), the <s>gopīs</s>, who are companions in amorous sport, confidants in jesting. /
For those who are secretly in love, there is no other confidant in jesting. /
And to indicate that <s>Rādhā</s> is the supreme object of love, he says — those who are direct witnesses of <s>Rādhā's</s> pleasures; <s>Kalindaśailatanayā</s> is <s>Yamunā</s>; the question about the welfare and well-being of the bower-houses on her banks is asked with an undertone of longing. /
Thus, having questioned him, the Lord <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who has come from <s>Dvārakā</s>, whose impressions are awakened by seeing the cowherds, whose <s>rati</s> (love) emotion is aroused by the <s>ālambana</s> (foundational) and <s>uddīpana</s> (stimulating) <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), speaks [a verse] expressing inner eagerness — the purpose of the <s>smaratalpasya</s> (love-couch) of <s>Madana</s> (Cupid's bed) is the soft, delicate cutting and breaking; that itself is the use, the fruitfulness. /
Alternatively: in the love-couch, whose arrangement (<s>kḷpti</s>) is soft, delicate, and excellent — the result of cutting, when it is cut — /
'In my absence, who would arrange the love-couch?' — this is the purport. /
Therefore, carrying the certainty of mutual love, he says — 'those, know' etc. /
The sentence-meaning here has the status of object [of the verb]. /
Now [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'of the bees' — of the humming ones — 'without sounds' — by the absence of sounds. /
This thought has taken refuge in silence — thus [the meaning]. /
Here, the heroine's silence is explained in two ways — 'for the purpose of a means' etc. /
The means is the means of union. /
'Of those' — /
'Of those' — to explain what was experienced, he says — 'who' etc. /
'By seeing the cowherds' — awakened, aroused impressions — impressions born from experiences such as bower-houses — one whose [impressions are] such. /
'Awakened' etc. — the triad [of words] qualifies the verb 'says.' /
'<s>Prabuddharatibhāva</s>' is also a reading. /
The <s>rati</s> emotion is directed toward the <s>gopīs</s>. /
'For the purpose of fashioning' — /
The meaning is: for the purpose of construction. /
'Having made soft' — /
The meaning is: because of softness as the cause. /
He states an alternative meaning — 'alternatively' etc. /
'Love-couch' — /
The purport is: made from an upper garment etc. /
'<s>Kḷpti</s>' — /
The meaning is: scattering. /
'Delicate' — this is the elaboration of that very [word] — 'excellent' etc. /
He establishes the state of being cut — 'in my [absence]' etc. /
Therefore, precisely because of the severance of the stated use — /
'Mutual' — /
Of oneself and of the <s>gopīs</s> — in the subject matter beginning with 'who' etc., even when there is the status of sentence-meaning for inanimate things, the construal with the circumstances of sentient beings is indeed [present]. /
Now, where there is construal with the circumstances of sentient beings, there <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) etc. is the <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure). /
This being so, <s>upamā</s> (simile) and other [figures] would be without subject matter, or with very sparse subject matter, /
because there is no such inanimate subject matter where there is no construal with the circumstances of sentient beings, even minimally as <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'They grow old' — /
But in my presence, because of the uninterrupted stated use, these [sprouts] would never attain the staleness of decay from old age — this is the purport. /
'Their fading blue luster' — by this, even though he has been away only for some time, the intensity of longing is suggested. /
Thus this is either a speech to oneself, or alternatively a deliberative address directed to the cowherd. /
'With many examples, of a great, extensive composition' — what was stated is thus indicated. /
'Now' etc. — /
The remainder is: with the intention that there should be no absence of <s>rasa</s> here. /
Now, anticipating the objection that 'where there is absolutely no entry of sentient circumstances, that will be the domain of <s>upamā</s> etc.,' he says — 'because' etc. /
'Even minimally' — /
Even inanimate things like <s>stambha</s> (paralysis) and <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation), when being described, by virtue of being <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), necessarily imply something sentient — so what needs to be said here? /
Even an extremely inert thing like a moonlit garden etc., even when it rests in itself, when being described, necessarily — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] having abandoned the status of <s>cittavṛtti</s>-<s>vibhāva</s> (determinant of mental states) — the mutual love resting upon each other is indeed pregnant with the certainty of that [love] — this is the meaning. /
In the absence of that certainty, what will be stated [later] would be unfounded, since for the <s>gopīs</s> taking pleasure in another man, the possibility of that use [of the love-couch] would exist — this is the purport. /
'Those' — the meaning is: those connected with the bower-house. /
'They grow old, they become worn' — through this, what is implied he says — 'in my [absence]' etc. /
'Uninterrupted' — /
The uninterrupted stated use, the previously mentioned use — because of its application. /
'These' — /
These sprouts. /
'Decay' — /
The staleness (<s>khilīkāra</s>) in the form of discoloration etc. caused by decay from old age — that. /
'Fading' — through the present participle, what is implied he says — 'for some time' etc. /
'Of one who has been away' — /
The remainder is: of the Lord. /
'Longing' — /
Longing means eagerness or desire to see. /
He states the purpose of showing three examples — 'with many' etc. /
'With many' — with three. /
'With examples' — its connection is with 'that is indicated.' /
'Of a great' — this is a paraphrase of what is in the <s>vṛtti</s>. /
Its explanation — 'of extensive.' /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'now' means 'if.' /
There, the construal is: 'if <s>rasa</s> etc. is the <s>alaṅkāra</s>.' /
Here, the intention is shown by supplying [the implicit thought] — 'absence of <s>rasa</s>' etc. /
He introduces the passage beginning with 'because' — 'now' etc. /
'Where there is no construal with inanimate subject matter even minimally as <s>vibhāva</s>, that inanimate subject matter does not exist' — this is the construal of the <s>vṛtti</s>. /
'Even minimally as <s>vibhāva</s>, the construal' — what is said in the <s>vṛtti</s>, its intended meaning he states — '<s>stambha</s>' etc. /
Even inanimate things like <s>stambha</s> (paralysis) and <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation), when being described — this is the construal. /
It necessarily implies the sentient, by being an indicator of sentient [states] through being indicative of particular mental states. /
'So much' — in the sense of acceptance. /
'What needs to be said here' — /
Since the indicative nature of <s>anubhāva</s> for <s>bhāva</s> is well established, nothing needs to be said here — this is the meaning. /
He elaborates the construal as <s>vibhāva</s> — 'even extremely inert' etc. /
'A moonlit garden etc., even resting in itself, when being described' — this is the connection. /
'Resting in itself' — concluded in itself through the apprehension of the expressed meaning. /
'<s>Citta</s>' — /
Of the particular mental state, and therefore by virtue of being subsidiary to that, the <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
But what is the principal element (<s>aṅgī</s>) — <s>rasa</s> or <s>bhāva</s> — that which is in every way the <s>alaṅkārya</s> (object to be adorned), that is the soul of <s>dhvani</s> — /
Furthermore —

children.text: tam artham avalambante ye 'ṅginaṃ te guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those that depend upon that principal meaning are known as <s>guṇas</s> (qualities);

children.text: aṅgāśritās tv alaṅkārā mantavyāḥ kaṭakādivat // DhvK_2.6 //
children.translated_text: but those that reside in the subsidiary parts are to be regarded as <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments), like bracelets and such. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.6 //
Those that depend upon that principal meaning are known as <s>guṇas</s> (qualities);
but those that reside in the subsidiary parts are to be regarded as <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments), like bracelets and such. // 6 //

children.text:
yetamarthaṃ rasādilakṣaṇamaṅginaṃ santamavalambante te gumāḥ śauryādivat /
vācyavācakalakṣaṇānyaṅgāni ye punastadāśritāste 'laṅkārā mantavyāḥ kaṭakādivat /
locanam kāvye 'nākhyeya eva syāt; śāstretihāsayorapi vā /
evaṃ paramataṃ dūṣayitvā svamatameva pratyāmnāyenopasaṃharati--tasmāditi /
yataḥ parokto viṣayavibhāgo na yukta ityarthaḥ /
bhāvo veti vāgrahaṇāttadābhāsatatpraśamādayaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'In every way' — this qualifies the verb.
Therefore the meaning is: in every manner.
'The <s>alaṅkārya</s> (object to be adorned)' —
precisely for this reason it is not an <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament) — this is the purport. // 5 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Those that depend upon that meaning, which is principal — characterized by <s>rasa</s> etc. — they are <s>guṇas</s>, like valor etc. /
The subsidiary parts (<s>aṅgas</s>), characterized as the expressible and the expressive — those that depend upon them are <s>alaṅkāras</s>, to be regarded like bracelets and such. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] In poetry, it would simply be inexpressible; or even in <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) and <s>itihāsa</s> (epic). /
Thus, having refuted the opposing view, he concludes his own position by restatement — 'therefore' etc. /
Since the division of subject matter described above is not proper — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Bhāva</s> or' — by the word 'or' (<s>vā</s>), <s>bhāvābhāsa</s> (semblance of emotion), <s>bhāvapraśama</s> (quiescence of emotion), and the like [are included].

children.text:
alaṅkāryavyatiriktaścālaṅkāro 'bhyupagantavyaḥ, loke tathā siddhatvāt, yathā guṇivyatirikto guṇaḥ /
guṇālaṅkāravyavahāraśca guṇinyalaṅkārye ca sati yuktaḥ /
sa cārasmatpakṣa evopapanna ityabhiprāyadvayenāha---kiñcetyādi /

children.translated_text: Not only this much reasoning [supports] the subsidiary status of <s>rasa</s>, but also something else — this is the meaning of the cumulative [conjunction].
The <s>kārikā</s> too should be construed with the twofold intention alone.

children.text: kevalaṃ prathamābhiprāye prathamaṃ kārikārdhaṃ dṛṣṭāntābhiprāyeṇa vyākhyeyam /
children.translated_text: Only in the first intention should the first half of the <s>kārikā</s> be explained with the purport of the illustration.
Thus the <s>vṛtti</s> passage too should be construed. // 6 //

And the <s>alaṅkāra</s> must be acknowledged as distinct from the <s>alaṅkārya</s>, since it is so established in common usage, just as a <s>guṇa</s> (quality) is distinct from the <s>guṇin</s> (quality-possessor). /
And the usage of [the terms] <s>guṇa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s> is appropriate only when there exists a <s>guṇin</s> (quality-possessor) and an <s>alaṅkārya</s> (object to be adorned). /
That [distinction] is established only in our position — with this twofold intention he says — 'furthermore' etc.

children.text:
bālapriyā uddīpanavibhāvatāmityarthaḥ /
śāstreti /
anākhyeya ityanuṣajyate /
na hi tadasti vastu yanna kiñjiccittavṛttiviśeṣamudbodhayatīti bhāvaḥ /
pratyāmnāyena uktasyaiva punaḥ kathanena /

children.translated_text: By the word '<s>āmnāya</s>' (tradition), the authoritativeness [of the teaching], like that of the <s>Veda</s>, is indicated.
'By the word <s>vā</s>' —
'Are included' — this is the remainder.
'<s>Alaṅkārya</s>' — through the expression, what is implied he says — 'precisely for this reason' etc. // 5 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The meaning is: the status of being <s>uddīpana</s>-<s>vibhāva</s> (stimulating determinant). /
'In <s>śāstra</s>' — '<s>anākhyeya</s>' (inexpressible) is to be carried over. /
For there is no object whatsoever that does not arouse some particular mental state — this is the purport. /
'By restatement' (<s>pratyāmnāyena</s>) — by saying again what was already said.

children.text:
'kiñce'tyādigranthamavatārayati----alaṅkāryetyādi /
abhiprāyāntaraṃ cāha---guṇeti /
sa ceti /
guṇālaṅkāravyavahāraścetyarthaḥ /
kiñcetyasyārthamāha---netyādi /
yuktijātaṃ yuktisamūhaḥ /
abhiprāyadvayeneti /
ukteneti bhāvaḥ /
yojanāṃ darśayati---kevalamityādi /
prathamābhiprāyaiti /
alaṅkāryavyatiriktaścālaṅkāro 'bhyupagantavya ityabhiprāya ityarthaḥ /
prathamaṃ kārikārdhamiti /
tamarthamityādyardhamityarthaḥ /
dṛṣṭānteti /
yatā guṇivyatirikto guṇa iti dṛṣṭāntetyarthaḥ /
dvitīyābhiprāyastu pūrvottarārdhābhyāṃ gamya iti bhāvaḥ /
vṛttau tamarthamityasya vivaṇaṃ---'rasādilakṣaṇam' iti /

children.translated_text: 'Being principal' — this is its qualifier, meaning: having become the principal element.
'Like valor etc.' — the illustration is to be understood.
'Depending upon those' —
the meaning is: depending upon the subsidiary parts. // 6 //

He introduces the passage beginning with 'furthermore' — '<s>alaṅkārya</s>' etc. /
And he states the other intention — '<s>guṇa</s>' etc. /
'And that' — the meaning is: and the usage of <s>guṇa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
He states the meaning of 'furthermore' — 'not' etc. /
'Group of reasoning' — a collection of arguments. /
'With the twofold intention' — the purport is: with the [two intentions] already stated. /
He shows the construal — 'only' etc. /
'In the first intention' — /
The meaning is: the intention that '<s>alaṅkāra</s> must be acknowledged as distinct from the <s>alaṅkārya</s>.' /
'The first half of the <s>kārikā</s>' — the meaning is: the half beginning with 'those that depend upon that meaning.' /
'With the purport of the illustration' — the meaning is: with the illustration 'just as a <s>guṇa</s> is distinct from the <s>guṇin</s>.' /
But the second intention is to be understood from both halves — this is the purport. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, the elaboration of 'those that depend upon that meaning' is — 'characterized by <s>rasa</s> etc.'
And thus —

children.text: śṛṅgāra eva madhuraḥ paraḥ prahlādano rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) alone is the sweet, supremely delightful <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment);

children.text: tan-mayaṃ kāvyam āśritya mādhuryaṃ pratitiṣṭhati // DhvK_2.7 //
children.translated_text: it is through poetry pervaded by it that <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) becomes established. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.7 //

children.text: śṛṅgāra eva madhuraḥ paraḥ prahlādano rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) alone is the sweet, supremely delightful <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment);
it is through poetry pervaded by it that <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) becomes established. // 7 //

children.translated_text:
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'But <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) etc. are the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) of word and meaning; then how is it said that the <s>guṇas</s> depend on <s>rasa</s> etc. as the principal element?' — anticipating this objection, he says: '<s>tathā ca</s>' etc. /
'By that forthcoming method of resolution, this too is justified' — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> alone' — /
He states the reason for [<s>śṛṅgāra</s> being called] '<s>madhura</s>' (sweet): '<s>paraḥ prahlādanaḥ</s>' (supremely delightful). /
For in <s>rati</s> (love), across all species — gods, animals, humans, etc. — the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) is utterly unbroken; therefore there is no one in that [domain of love] who is not full of heart-resonance (<s>hṛdaya-saṃvāda</s>) — for even in an ascetic, that aesthetic wonder indeed exists. /
For this very reason it is called '<s>madhura</s>.' /
For the sweet <s>rasa</s> of sugar etc., whether for a discerning person or an undiscerning one, whether healthy or sick, the moment it falls upon the tongue, is immediately desirable. /
'<s>Tanmayam</s>' (pervaded by that) — /
That <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, being the soul, is the subject of [the poem] where [it shines] as the suggested. /
'Poetry' — /
'Word and meaning' — this is the meaning. /
'Is established' — /
'Attains establishment' — this is the extent. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He introduces the passage '<s>tathā ca</s>' etc.: '<s>nanu</s>' etc. /
'Of word and meaning' etc. — /
'Because it was so stated by the ancients' — this is the purport. /
He explains '<s>tathā ca</s>' in accordance with the topic at hand: '<s>tena</s>' etc. /
He explains the <s>kārikā</s>: '<s>madhura</s>' etc. /
'<s>Madhura</s>' — qualified by the quality called <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). /
'Reason' — /
'Indicator' — this is the meaning. /
He substantiates the supreme-delight-ness: '<s>ratau</s>' etc. /
'In <s>rati</s>' — the remainder is: 'when it arises.' /
'Latent impression' — /
'A subtle state, synonymous with <s>saṃskāra</s> (impression)' — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — in the sense of reason. /
'<s>Na</s>' etc. — /
'There' — in <s>rati</s>. /
'Full of heart-resonance' — abundantly rich in heart-resonance. /
'There is no such one who is not full of heart-resonance in that [domain of love]' — this is the syntactic connection. /
'Everyone has heart-resonance in <s>rati</s>' — this is the meaning. /
'That aesthetic wonder' — /
'Heart-resonance in <s>rati</s>' — this is the meaning. /
He connects what was said in the introduction: '<s>ataḥ</s>' etc. /
He clarifies what was said with an illustration: '<s>madhuro hi</s>' etc. /
The purport is: this meaning too is intended in the <s>kārikā</s> by '<s>madhura</s>' etc. in the manner of an illustration. /
'Discerning or undiscerning' — /
'Of everyone' — this is the meaning. /
'Desirable indeed' — /
'Delightful indeed' — this is the purport. /
He explains '<s>tanmayam</s>' by the rule '<s>tatprakṛtavacane mayaṭ</s>': '<s>sa</s>' etc. /
The substantiation of 'as the soul' is: 'as the suggested.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] What this amounts to saying is: in reality, <s>mādhurya</s> is a <s>guṇa</s> (quality) of <s>rasa</s> itself, [specifically] of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc. /
That [<s>mādhurya</s>], belonging to the sweet <s>rasa</s>, when transferred to word and meaning that manifest it — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He states the purport of the <s>kārikā</s>: '<s>etad uktam</s>' etc. /
By the word '<s>śṛṅgārādi</s>' etc., <s>karuṇa</s> is included. /
'That' — /
'<s>Mādhurya</s>' — this is the meaning. /
'Transferred' — superimposed through direct association. /
He states the result: '<s>madhura</s>' etc. /
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> alone, in comparison to other <s>rasas</s>, is sweet because of being the cause of delight. /
Because word and meaning are devoted to manifesting it, the <s>guṇa</s> characterized as <s>mādhurya</s> [belongs to] poetry. /
But auditory pleasantness (<s>śravyatva</s>) is common even to <s>ojas</s> (vigor). /
[<s>Kārikā</s>:] In <s>śṛṅgāra</s> of the type called <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation), and in <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic), with special intensity,

children.text: mādhuryam ārdratāṃ yāti yatas tatrādhikaṃ manaḥ // DhvK_2.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) attains tenderness (<s>ārdratā</s>), because therein the mind [becomes] more [deeply affected]. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.8 //
[Repeated <s>kārikā</s>:] In <s>śṛṅgāra</s> of the type called <s>vipralambha</s>, and in <s>karuṇa</s>, with special intensity,
<s>mādhurya</s> attains tenderness, because therein the mind [becomes] more [deeply affected]. // 8 //

children.text:
locanam vyañjakayoḥ śabdārthayorupacaritaṃ madhuraśṛṅgārarasābhivyaktisamarthatā śabdārthayormādhuryamiti hi lakṣaṇam /
tasmādyuktamuktaṃ 'tamartham' ityādi /
kārikārthaṃ vṛttyāha--śṛṅgāra iti /
nanu 'śravyaṃ nātisamastārthaśabdaṃ madhuramiṣyate'iti mādhuryasya lakṣaṇam /

children.translated_text: He says 'No': '<s>śravyatvam</s>' etc. /
The entire definition is [merely] an indicator (<s>upalakṣita</s>). /
'Even of <s>ojas</s>' — /

children.text: 'yo yaḥ śastraṃ' ityatra hi śravyatvamasamastatvaṃ cāstyeveti bhāvaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: For in '<s>yo yaḥ śastram</s>' ('whoever [wields] a weapon') etc., pleasantness to hear and non-compoundedness indeed exist — this is the purport. // 7 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] Of the two suggestors — word and meaning — [<s>mādhurya</s>] is transferred: the capacity of word and meaning to manifest the sweet <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> — this indeed is the definition of <s>mādhurya</s>. /
Therefore it is rightly said: '<s>tam artham</s>' etc. /
He states the meaning of the <s>kārikā</s> through the <s>vṛtti</s>: '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' etc. /
Now, [the objection:] 'That which is pleasant to hear, not excessively compounded in meaning and word, is accepted as <s>madhura</s> (sweet)' — this is the definition of <s>mādhurya</s>. /

children.text:
sambhoga śṛṅgārānmadurataro vipralambhaḥ, tato 'pi madhuratamaḥ karuma iti tadabhivyañjanakauśalaṃ śabdārthayorbhadhurataratvaṃ madhuratamatvaṃ cetyabhiprāyeṇāha--śṛṅgāra ityādi /
karuṇeceti caśabdaḥ kramamāha /
prakarṣavaditi /
uttarottaraṃ taratamayogeneti bhāvaḥ /
ārdratāmiti /
sahṛdayasya cetaḥ svābhāvikamanāviṣṭatvātmakaṃ kāṭhinyaṃ krodhādidoptarūpatvaṃ bālapriyā śṛṅgāreti /
śṛṅgārādītyarthaḥ /
lakṣaṇamiti /
svarūpamityarthaḥ /
anena 'tatprakāśane'tyādi vṛtyartho darśitaḥ /
vṛttau 'rasāntarāpekṣayā prahlādahetutvādi'ti sambandhaḥ /
locane--nanvityādi /
nātisamastārthaśabdaṃ madhuramiti /
kāvyamiti śeṣaḥ /
itīti /
iti bhāmahoktamityarthaḥ /
lakṣaṇamiti /
śravyatvādighaṭitalakṣaṇamityarthaḥ /
etadantaḥ śaṅkāgranthaḥ /
netyāheti /
uktamativyāptyā lakṣaṇaṃ na bhavatītyāhetyarthaḥ /
sarvamiti /
śravyamityādinoktaṃ sarvamityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Of <s>ojas</s>' — /
'Of vigorous poetry' — this is the meaning. /
He cites that [example] to show the over-extension: '<s>yo yaḥ</s>' etc. /
This verse will be cited in the <s>vṛtti</s>. // 7 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] <s>Vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) is sweeter than <s>sambhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-union); even sweeter than that is <s>karuṇa</s> — thus the skill in manifesting them [constitutes] the greater and greatest sweetness of word and meaning — with this intention he says: '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' etc. /
'<s>Karuṇe ca</s>' — the particle '<s>ca</s>' indicates sequence. /
'With special intensity' — /
'Progressively, in ascending degree' — this is the purport. /
'Tenderness' — the natural hardness of the connoisseur's mind — its uninvaded character — the fierceness born of anger etc. — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Śṛṅgāra</s>' etc. — /
'<s>Śṛṅgārādi</s>' — this is the meaning. /
'Definition' — /
'Essential nature' — this is the meaning. /
By this, the meaning of the <s>vṛtti</s> passage '<s>tatprakāśana</s>' etc. has been shown. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>: 'in comparison to other <s>rasas</s>, because of being the cause of delight' — this is the syntactic connection. /
In the <s>Locana</s>: '<s>nanu</s>' etc. /
'<s>Nātisamastārthaśabdaṃ madhuram</s>' — /
'Poetry' is the remainder. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — /
'Thus stated by <s>Bhāmaha</s>' — this is the meaning. /
'Definition' — /
'The definition constructed from pleasantness etc.' — this is the meaning. /
Up to this is the passage of the objection. /
'He says no' — /
'He says that the stated definition, being over-extended, is not [valid]' — this is the meaning. /
'All' — /
'All that was stated beginning with "pleasant to hear"' — this is the meaning. /

children.text:
avatārayati--sambhogetyādi /
itīti hetau /
tadabhītyādi /
tatpadena madhuratarasya madhuratamasya ca rasasya parāmarśaḥ /
kramamāheti /
tathā ca kramema prakarṣavadityarthaḥ /
tamevāha---uttarottaramiti /
ārdratāmetītyetadvyācaṣṭe---sahṛdayasyetyādi /
'cetastyajatī'ti sambandhaḥ /
svābhāvikaṃ kāṭhinyamiti /
yathoktaṃ bhaktirasāyane---"cittadravyaṃ tu kaṭhinaṃ svabhāvādi'ti /
krodhādīti /
krodhādyāhitaṃ dīptatvamityarthaḥ /
vipralambhaśṛṅgārakarumayostu māduryameva prakarṣavat /
sahṛdayahṛdayāvarjanātiśayanimittvāditi /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He introduces: '<s>sambhoga</s>' etc. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — in the sense of reason. /
'<s>Tad abhī</s>' etc. — /
By the word '<s>tat</s>' there is reference to the sweeter and the sweetest <s>rasa</s>. /
'He indicates sequence' — /
'And thus, in sequence, with special intensity' — this is the meaning. /
He states precisely that: '<s>uttarottaram</s>' (progressively). /
He explains '<s>ārdratām</s>' (tenderness): '<s>sahṛdayasya</s>' etc. /
'Of the connoisseur's mind' — the natural hardness — the uninvaded character constituting rigidity — the fierceness born of anger etc. — /
The <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>karuṇa</s>, however, possess <s>mādhurya</s> with special intensity — /
because of being the cause of surpassing captivation of the connoisseurs' hearts — /
[<s>Kārikā</s>:] The <s>raudra</s> (furious) and other <s>rasas</s> are characterized in poetry by <s>dīpti</s> (blazing brilliance);
<s>ojas</s> (vigor) is established as depending on the word and meaning that are the causes of their manifestation. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.9 //
[Repeated <s>kārikā</s>:] The <s>raudra</s> and other <s>rasas</s> are characterized in poetry by <s>dīpti</s> (blazing brilliance);
<s>ojas</s> is established as depending on the word and meaning that are the causes of their manifestation. // 9 //

children.text:
raudrādayo hi rasāḥ parāṃ dīptimujjavalatāṃ janayantīti lakṣaṇayā ta locanam vismayahāsādirāgitvaṃ ca tyajatītyarthaḥ /
adhikamiti /
krameṇetyāśayaḥ tena karuṇe 'pi sarvathaiva cittaṃ dravatītyuktaṃ bhavati /
nanu karuṇe 'pi yadi madhurimāsti, tarhi pūrvakārikāyāṃ śṛṅgāra evetyevakāraḥ kimarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: He responds: /

children.text: nānena rasāntaraṃ vyavacchidyate; api tvātmabhūtasya rasasyaiva paramārthato guṇā mādhuryādayaḥ, upacāreṇa tu śabdārthayorityevakāreṇa dyotyate /
children.translated_text: 'By this [particle <s>eva</s>], another <s>rasa</s> is not excluded; rather, [it indicates that] <s>mādhurya</s> etc. are in reality <s>guṇas</s> of the <s>rasa</s> itself that is the soul [of poetry], and only figuratively [<s>guṇas</s>] of word and meaning — this is what is indicated by the particle <s>eva</s>.' /
He states the meaning of the <s>vṛtti</s>: '<s>vipralambha</s>' etc. // 8 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] For the <s>raudra</s> and other <s>rasas</s> generate supreme <s>dīpti</s> (blazing brilliance), i.e., intense effulgence — therefore, through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication), they — [<s>Locana</s>:] the abandoning of the coloring by wonder, laughter, etc. and the relinquishing [of softness]' — this is the meaning. /
'More' — /
'In sequence' — this is the intent. Thus, [the implication is:] in <s>karuṇa</s> too, the mind melts completely — this is what is stated. /
'Now, if sweetness exists even in <s>karuṇa</s>, then in the earlier <s>kārikā</s>, what is the purpose of the restrictive particle <s>eva</s> in "<s>śṛṅgāra</s> alone"?' /

children.text:
raudretyāgadi /
ādiśabdaḥ prakāre /
tena vīrādbhutayorapi grahaṇam /
dīptiḥ pratipatturhṛdaye vikāsavistāraprajvalanasvabhāvā /
sā ca mukhyatayā ojaśśabdavācyā /
bālapriyā vismayeti /
rāgitvaṃ rūṣitatvaṃ vismayahāsādyāhitaṃ vikṣepamityarthaḥ /
tyajatīti /
tathā cārdratā nā cittasya śṛṅgārādicarvaṇājanyaḥ kāṭhinyādiparityāgaḥ, tena drutyākhyo vṛttiviśeṣo veti bhāvaḥ /
spaṣṭamidaṃ kāvyapradīpodyote /
krameṇeti /
ārdratāyāḥ krameṇādhikyamiti bhāvaḥ /
sarvathaiva atyadhikameva /
kimartha iti /
kiṃśabdaḥ praśne /
kaḥ artho yasya saḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Because the meaning in the form of exclusion from all other connections would be contradicted' — this is the purport. /
He responds: '<s>ucyate</s>' etc. /
'The particle <s>eva</s> is devoted to excluding word and their meanings [as the true substrate of guṇas]' — this is the purport. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, the construal is: '<s>prakarṣavat eva</s>' (with intensity alone). // 8 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Raudra</s>' etc. — /
The word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.) is in the sense of similarity. /
Thereby <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous) are also included. /
'<s>Dīpti</s>' (blazing brilliance) — a quality whose nature in the apprehender's heart is expansion, effusion, and flaming forth. /
And that [quality] is primarily denoted by the word '<s>ojas</s>' (vigor). /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Vismaya</s>' — /
'<s>Rāgitva</s>' (coloring) — the disturbance (<s>vikṣepa</s>) effected by wonder, laughter, etc. — this is the meaning. /
'Relinquishing' — /
And thus, '<s>ārdratā</s>' (tenderness) is the abandonment of hardness etc. — the specific emotional modification of the mind produced by the savoring of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc.; therefore it is a particular mode of emotional flow (<s>druti</s>) — this is the purport. /
This is made clear in the <s>Kāvyapradīpodyota</s>. /
'In sequence' — /
'In sequence of increasing tenderness' — this is the purport. /
'Completely' — /
'Exceedingly' [— this is the meaning]. /
'What is the purpose?' — /
The word '<s>kim</s>' is interrogative; '<s>kimarthaḥ</s>' [means] 'of what purpose is it?' /

children.text:
prakāra iti /
sādṛśya ityarthaḥ, na tu prāthamye /
raudrānantaraṃ virādereva pāṭha ityatrāniyamāditi bhāvaḥ /
vīrādbhutayoriti /

children.translated_text: '<s>Lakṣita-lakṣaṇā</s>' — [according to] others: the indirect relation of that which can be denoted. /

children.translated_text: The passage '<s>dīrgha</s>' etc. is itself the elaboration of '<s>tat-prakāśana-paraḥ śabdaḥ</s>' (the word devoted to manifesting it) — to make this clear, he says: '<s>dīrgha</s>' etc. /

children.text: dīptirityucyata iti yathā---- cañcadbhujabhramitacaṇḍagadābhidhāta-- sañcūrṇitoruyugalasya suyodhanasya /
children.translated_text: '<s>Dīpti</s> it is called' — as for example: 'Of <s>Suyodhana</s> whose thigh-pair was crushed to powder by the blow of the fierce mace whirled by the swinging arm,
<s>Bhīma</s>, with hands sticky, clotted with rich blood, shall adorn your tresses, O queen!'

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Prakāra</s>' (type) — /
'Similarity' — this is the meaning; not in the sense of primacy. /
Because there is no fixed rule that <s>vīra</s> must be listed immediately after <s>raudra</s> — this is the purport. /
'Of <s>vīra</s> and <s>adbhuta</s>' — /
If <s>adbhuta</s> is taken here by the word '<s>ādi</s>,' then since generating blazing brilliance [applies to it], and since in the earlier passage '<s>krodhādi-dīpta-rūpatvam vismaya-hāsādi</s>,' wonder was already included by the word '<s>krodhādi</s>' etc., the repeated mention of '<s>vismaya</s>' would be inconsistent; therefore here the reading should be '<s>vīra-bībhatsa</s>' (heroic and disgusting). /
Further on, in '<s>hāsya-bhayānaka-bībhatsa-śānteṣu</s>' and '<s>bībhatse 'py evam</s>,' the word '<s>adbhuta</s>' should be read in place of '<s>bībhatsa</s>'; that being the case, concordance with the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> etc. is also achieved. /
Therein, the mention of <s>mādhurya</s> alone for <s>śānta</s> should be construed as following another's view — this appears [to be the case]. /
'Expansion' — /
'<s>Dīpti</s> is a [quality] whose nature is exactly the flaming-forth that is [simultaneously] expansion' — the statement amounts to this: what is called <s>dīpti</s> is precisely of this nature. /
The word and sentence devoted to manifesting it — with long-compound construction and ornamental style. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Constituted by the savoring of <s>raudra</s> etc., by that <s>dīpti</s> — [which is] a particular mode of savoring, an effect — they [the <s>raudra</s> etc. <s>rasas</s>] are characterized, i.e., known as distinct from other <s>rasas</s>. /
Therefore, by the figurative transfer of effect to cause, <s>raudra</s> etc. itself is denoted by the word '<s>ojas</s>.' /
Thence, through <s>lakṣita-lakṣaṇā</s> (indication of the indicated), the word and sentence devoted to manifesting them — having the form of long-compound construction — is also called '<s>dīpti</s>.' /
Just as — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'A certain emotional modification of the mind' — this is the meaning. /
'And that' etc. — /
'"<s>Ojas</s>" means "blazing"' — thus [says] <s>Amara</s> [in his lexicon]. /
'Constituted by savoring' — /
'Generating the emotional modification in the form of blazing brilliance' — this is the meaning. /
'A particular mode of savoring' — /
'In the form of a particular emotional modification of the mind' — this is the meaning. /
'An effect' — /
'Born from the savoring of <s>raudra</s> etc. <s>rasas</s>' — this is the meaning. /
'Are characterized' — /
'Are known' — this is the meaning. /
He completes: '<s>rasa</s>' etc. /
'As distinct' — as different. /
'The figurative transfer of effect to cause [entails that] <s>raudra</s> etc. itself is denoted by the word "<s>ojas</s>"' — this is the construal. /
The particle '<s>eva</s>' has the sense of emphasis, or — /
The word '<s>ojas</s>' in usages like '<s>ojasvi-kāvyam</s>' (vigorous poetry) etc. means <s>raudra</s> etc. through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — this is the meaning. /
By this, the <s>vṛtti</s> passage '<s>raudrādayaḥ</s>' etc. has been elucidated. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, the construal is: '<s>lakṣaṇayā eva</s>' (through indication alone). /
The word '<s>dīpti</s>' in '<s>dīptir ity ucyante</s>' is an indicator of the word '<s>ojas</s>.' /
'Devoted to manifesting' — /
'Devoted to manifesting <s>raudra</s> etc.' — this is the meaning. This is the <s>vṛtti</s> passage explaining the second half of the <s>kārikā</s> — he elucidates it: '<s>tataḥ</s>' etc. /
Keeping in mind the connection of the words '<s>lakṣaṇayā dīptir ity ucyate</s>,' he says: '<s>lakṣita-lakṣaṇayā</s>' etc. /
'<s>Lakṣita-lakṣaṇā</s>' — [i.e.,] <s>lakṣaṇā</s> through the indicated meaning — [according to] some. /

children.translated_text: "Of unbroken momentum" etc. —
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] The meaning that is devoted to revealing that [<s>ojas</s>], not requiring the composition of long compounds, expressed through clear words —

children.text: yathā---- yo yaḥ śastraṃ bibhirti svabhujagurumadaḥ pāṇḍavīnāṃ camunāṃ yo yaḥ pāñcālagotre śiśuradhikavayā garbhaśayyāṃ gato vā /
children.translated_text: As in: "Whoever among the armies of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> women bears a weapon, proud of the might of his own arms; whoever in the <s>Pāñcāla</s> clan, whether child or one of greater age, or one who has gone to the bed of the womb —

children.text: yo yastatkarmasākṣī carati mayi raṇe yaśca yaśca pratīpaḥ krodhāndhastasya tasya svayamapi jagatāmantakasyāntako 'ham //
children.translated_text: Whoever wanders as witness to that deed, and whoever stands opposed to me in battle — blind with rage, of each and every one of them, I myself am the death of Death, the ender of the world!"

[<s>Locana</s>:] "Whirling" (<s>cañcat</s>) etc. And the meaning that is devoted to revealing that [vigor], when expressed through clear, indicative words (<s>vācakas</s>), is called <s>dīpti</s> (brilliance) even without requiring compounding. As in "whoever" etc. "Whirling" — by the two arms whirling with speed, the fierce mace that was spun — by its blow delivered all around to the thighs, the thigh-pair was simultaneously and thoroughly crushed, rendered incapable of rising again — him, <s>Suyodhana</s>, disregarding [him], the blood that was congealed — i.e., viscous and not dried over time — clinging to the hands without dripping, exceedingly dense in its innermost nature and not merely fluid — with that blood his palms were reddened. Hence he, <s>Bhīma</s>, is terror-inspiring to cowards. "Your" — of her to whom various kinds of insult were done; he will make a head-ornament of [her] braid (<s>veṇī</s>), even though it was an indignity unfit for a queen, removing the braid-form and adorning it with pieces of blood fallen from his hand as if with a garland of red flowers — this is an <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy). By the word "queen" (<s>devī</s>), which evokes the memory of the dishonoring of the family consort, the function of stimulating anger (<s>krodha</s>) as an excitant (<s>uddīpana-vibhāva</s>) is achieved — hence no suspicion of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> should arise here. And the disregarding of <s>Suyodhana</s> means not making any effort for a second mace-blow etc. — and that is because the thighs were already crushed. By the mention of "congealed" (<s>styāna</s>), <s>Bhīma</s>'s haste in washing away the anger toward <s>Draupadī</s> is indicated. And the compounding, because of its nature of carrying unbroken momentum — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The word <s>dīpti</s> indicates (<s>upalakṣaka</s>) the word <s>ojas</s> (vigor). The explanation of "clear" (<s>prasanna</s>) is "indicative" (<s>gamaka</s>) — meaning: immediately conveying the sense. "Of <s>Suyodhana</s>" — using the genitive in the sense of disregard ("the sixth case-ending denotes disregard"), he says "disregarding <s>Suyodhana</s>." The elaboration of "congealed" — "viscous": meaning dense. "Not" etc. — the meaning is: it is not the case that it was clinging due to drying over time. The explanation of "clinging" — "by the hands" etc. "Exceedingly" etc. — the meaning of "dense" here is exceedingly internal. "Terror-inspiring to cowards" — a coward is one who is afraid. The construction is: the insult-series, though unfit for a queen. "Unfit for a queen" means unfit for one who has been consecrated. "Making a head-ornament" — <s>uttaṃsa</s> means crest-ornament. "From the hand" — pieces of blood that dripped, i.e., fell, from the hand. "Red flower" — meaning red blossom. "<s>Utprekṣā</s>" is drawn from "indicated." "Family" — the dishonor is the hair-dragging etc. done by <s>Duḥśāsana</s> at <s>Suyodhana</s>'s instigation. "Haste" — meaning <s>Bhīmasena</s>'s haste. "Indicated" — the purport is: from the effort to make a head-ornament while the blood is still in the congealed state. He shows that the compounding here suggests <s>ojas</s> — "by the compounding" etc. By the compounding beginning with "whirling" (<s>cañjat</s>).

children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] In the above, the quality of <s>ojas</s> (vigor) belongs to both [word and meaning]. [<s>Locana</s>:] In precisely that much [text], the cognition — which, not finding rest in the middle, extends in a single continuous flow up to the point of disregarding <s>Suyodhana</s> with crushed thighs — being unitary, is the supreme nourisher of the fierceness (<s>auddhatya</s>). Others, however, explain: the blood that is congealed, dense, and clinging, belonging to <s>Suyodhana</s> — with that, his palms are reddened. "Whoever" — he whose pride is great in his own two arms; among the armies, meaning <s>Arjuna</s> etc. Due to the killing of <s>Droṇa</s> by the <s>Pāñcāla</s> prince <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, <s>Aśvatthāman</s> has excessive fury toward that clan. "Witness to that deed" — beginning with <s>Karṇa</s> etc. "In battle" — in the great war; whoever stands opposed, i.e., acts contrary — if such a one becomes the destroyer of the entire world, even of him I am the destroyer; how much more so of any other human or divine being! [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "Rapidly" — because it is uttered swiftly and in continuous form, it possesses unbroken momentum — this is the meaning. "In precisely that much" — the qualifier of cognition is "with momentum only" — this is the meaning. "Crushed" etc. — meaning that the range of content extends from the mace-whirling up to the disregarding of him. "Cognition" — meaning the connoisseurs' cognition. "Being unitary" — meaning it is a single [cognition]. The reading is also: "appears as a single mass." "Of the fierceness" — meaning of the bold-heroic temperament (<s>dhīroddhatatva</s>) belonging to the speaker; that is, of the anger belonging to <s>Bhīma</s>. But some say the genitive "of <s>Suyodhana</s>" is at the end, and its connection is with "blood" — he states their view with "others, however." He glosses "wanders" — taking the verb in the present tense — "acts," meaning "does." He glosses "whatever" — taking it as a seventh-case participle — "in whatever." He explains the meaning of "also" — "how much more" etc. In the <s>vṛtti</s>: "the meaning not requiring the composition of long compounds, expressed through clear words, and devoted to revealing that" —

children.text: samarpakatvaṃ kāvyasya yat tu sarva-rasān prati /

children.text: sa prasādo guṇo jñeyaḥ sarva-sādhāraṇa-kriyaḥ // DhvK_2.10 //

The capacity of poetry to deliver [its content] with respect to all <s>rasas</s> —
That should be known as the <s>guṇa</s> of <s>prasāda</s>, whose function is common to all. // 10 //

locanam vā /
atra pṛthagbhūtaireva kramādvimṛśyamānairarthaiḥ padātpadaṃ krodhaḥ parāṃ dhārāmāśrita ityasamastataiva dīptinibandhanam /
evaṃ mādhuryadīptī parasparapratidvandvitayā sthite śṛṅgārādiraudrādigate iti pradarśayatā tatsamāveśavaicitryaṃ hāsyabhayānakabībhatsaśānteṣu darśitam /
hāsyasya śṛṅgārāṅgatayā mādhuryaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ vikāsadharmatayā caujo 'pi prakṛṣṭamiti sāmyaṃ dvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Of <s>hāsya</s> (comic), because of its subsidiary relation to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, <s>mādhurya</s> is predominant; and because of its nature of blossoming expansion, <s>ojas</s> is also predominant — thus both are equal.

children.text: bhayānakasya magnacittavṛttisvabhāvatve 'pi vibhāvasya dīptatayā ojaḥ prakṛṣṭaṃ māghuryamalpam /
children.translated_text: Of <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible), even though the mental state is by nature submerged, because the <s>vibhāva</s> (cause) is brilliant, <s>ojas</s> is predominant and <s>mādhurya</s> is slight.
The same applies to <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting).

children.text: śānte tu vibhāvavaicitryātkadācidojaḥ prakṛṣṭaṃ kadācinmādhuryamiti vibhāgaḥ //9//
children.translated_text: But in <s>śānta</s> (tranquil), due to the variety of <s>vibhāvas</s>, sometimes <s>ojas</s> is predominant and sometimes <s>mādhurya</s> — this is the distinction. // 9 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] Or — here, through meanings that are distinct and examined sequentially, step by step, word by word, the anger reaches its highest pitch — thus, the absence of compounding itself is the basis for <s>dīpti</s> (brilliance). Thus, having shown that <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) and <s>dīpti</s> (brilliance/vigor) are mutually opposed, residing respectively in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc. and <s>raudra</s> etc., he demonstrates the variety of their co-presence in <s>hāsya</s>, <s>bhayānaka</s>, <s>bībhatsa</s>, and <s>śānta</s>.

children.translated_text: The meaning is: the co-presence of <s>mādhurya</s> and <s>ojas</s>.
He substantiates what was stated — with "of <s>hāsya</s>" etc.
"As subsidiary to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>" —

This is an indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) of [<s>hāsya</s>'s] arising from the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, and "nature of blossoming expansion" of its arising from <s>vīra</s> etc. // 9 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] "Capacity to deliver" (<s>samarpakatva</s>) means the capacity to properly deliver — i.e., the agency of functioning through self-immersion (<s>svātmāveśa</s>) toward the recipients (<s>pratipattṛ</s>), in accord with the heart, instantly, by the analogy of fire [catching] dry wood, and the purity thereof, like clear water — lucidity (<s>prasannatva</s>). [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] This is the construction. He applies this to the example — with "here" etc. "Distinct" — meaning cognizable through separate, different words. "Sequentially" — meaning in order, pausing at intervals. "Through meanings being examined" — meaning through meanings being considered by the speaker in such and such a manner. "Anger" — meaning the anger belonging to the speaker. "Pitch" — meaning peak. In the reading "<s>dīpti</s>," the meaning is "manifestation." "Reaches" — the rest is: shines forth for the connoisseurs. "Absence of compounding" — meaning the absence of compounds among the words, or their few compounds. "Basis for <s>dīpti</s>" — meaning that which suggests <s>ojas</s>. He says incidentally — "thus" etc. "<s>Mādhurya</s> and <s>dīpti</s>" — meaning <s>mādhurya</s> and <s>ojas</s>. "Mutually" — meaning in mutual opposition. "<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> etc." — should be understood in serial correspondence. "The variety of their co-presence" —

pratipattṝniti /
taddhṛdayānītyarthaḥ /
svātmeti /
svasvarūpetyarthaḥ /

atra dṛṣṭantamāha---śuṣketyādi /
yathā śuṣkakāṣṭhamagriḥ, yathā vā akaluṣaṃ svacchaṃ vastrādi udakaṃ jhaṭiti vyāpnoti tathetyarthaḥ /
tadakāluṣyamiti /
jhaṭiti svātmāveśena vyāpakatvarūpaṃ svacchatvamityarthaḥ /

sa ca sarvarasasādhāraṇo guṇaḥ sarvaracanāsādhāraṇaśca vyaṅgyārthāpekṣayaiva mukhyatayā vyavasthito mantavyaḥ /

nanu rasagato gumastatkathaṃ śabdārthayoḥ svacchatetyāśaṅkyāha---sa ceti /
caśabdo 'vadhāraṇe /
sarvarasasādhāraṇa eva guṇaḥ /
sa eva ca guṇa evaṃvidhaḥ /
sarvāyeyaṃ racanā śabdagatā cārthagatā ca samastā cāsamastā ca tatra sādhāramaḥ /

children.translated_text: The capacity of meaning to deliver exists, first of all, only with respect to the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), not otherwise.

children.text: śabdasyāpi svavācyārpaktvaṃ nāma kiyadalaukikaṃ yena gumaḥ syāditi bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: And even of words, the mere capacity to deliver one's own expressible meaning is hardly extraordinary enough to constitute a <s>guṇa</s> — this is the purport.

children.text: evaṃ mādhuryaujaḥprasādā eva trayo guṇā upapannā bhāmahābhiprāyeṇa /
children.translated_text: Thus, only three <s>guṇas</s> are established — <s>mādhurya</s>, <s>ojas</s>, and <s>prasāda</s> — in accordance with <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s view.

children.text: te ca pratipattrāsvādamayā mukhyatayā tata āsvādye upacaritā rase tatastadvyañjakayoḥ śabdārthayoriti tātparyam // 10 //
children.translated_text: And they pertain primarily to the savoring by the recipients; from there they are extended (<s>upacarita</s>) to <s>rasa</s> as the object of savoring; and from there to word and meaning as that which suggests it — this is the purport. // 10 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] "Capacity to deliver" (<s>samarpakatva</s>) etc. Of poetry, with respect to all <s>rasas</s>, i.e., of all <s>rasas</s> — the capacity to deliver, which is the agency of instantly pervading, i.e., functioning in the form of immersion, through the accordance of the heart, toward the recipients — of [that poetry] whose activity is common to all. "<s>Prasāda</s> is the <s>guṇa</s> to be known" — this is the meaning of the verse. He elaborates this meaning — with "capacity to deliver" etc. "Through the accordance of the heart" — this is the cause of the immersion. "The recipients" — meaning their hearts. "Self" (<s>svātman</s>) — meaning one's own nature. "Of all <s>rasas</s>" — this should be drawn here. The connection is: "instantly pervading." Here he gives an example — "dry" etc. Just as fire [pervades] dry wood, or just as clear, limpid water instantly pervades cloth etc. — thus is the meaning. "Its purity" — meaning the clarity that takes the form of pervading through self-immersion instantly. <s>Prasāda</s> (lucidity) is the clarity of word and meaning. And it should be considered that this <s>guṇa</s>, common to all <s>rasas</s> and common to all compositional modes, is primarily established only with reference to the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgyārtha</s>). [<s>Locana</s>:] Indeed, [<s>prasāda</s>] is a <s>guṇa</s> of all <s>rasas</s>. But by extension, the capacity of word and meaning to deliver with respect to such a type of suggested meaning is also <s>prasāda</s>. He explains that — "<s>prasāda</s>" etc. Objection: if the <s>guṇa</s> pertains to <s>rasa</s>, how then is it the clarity of word and meaning? — anticipating this, he says "and that" etc. The particle "ca" is for emphasis. It is a <s>guṇa</s> common to all <s>rasas</s> alone. And that very <s>guṇa</s> of this kind — all this composition, whether pertaining to word or to meaning, whether compounded or uncompounded — is common to it. "Primarily" —
