śabdārthayostattadarpakatvaṃ na guṇaḥ, kintu rasasyaiva svātmāveśena jhaṭiti sahṛdayahṛdayavyāpakatvamato mukhyatayā rasaniṣṭha eva prasādākhyo guṇaḥ, upacārāttu saśabdārthayorapīti bhāvārthaḥ /
upasaṃharati---evamityadi /
bhāmaheti /
"mādhuryamabhivāñchanta" ityādibhāsahavacanānurodhenetyarthaḥ /
te cetyādi /
te mādhuryaujaḥprasādā guṇāḥ /
pratipattrāsvādamayā iti /
pratipatturye drutidīptiprasādātmakacittavṛttiviśeṣarūpāsvādāḥ mukhyatayā tatsvarūpā ityarthaḥ /
te ca cittasthā iti bhāvaḥ /
tata ityādi /
tattadāsvādāḥ tattadrasacarvaṇājanyā ityāsvādyetattadrase te upacaritā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The various relishings, produced by the savoring of the various <s>rasas</s> — hence, being [said to be] in the various <s>rasas</s> that are the objects of relishing, they are secondary-usage [attributions]: this is the meaning.
'From that' etc. —
The continuation is with [the word] 'secondary-usage [attribution].'
The purport is: because word and meaning are not the direct causes of the savoring of the various <s>rasas</s>. // 10 //

<s>Bālapriyā</s>: Now, if <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity) is thus a <s>guṇa</s> (quality), how was it stated as residing in poetry? — to this he says: 'by secondary usage (<s>upacāra</s>)' etc. /
In such a <s>rasa</s>-natured — /
'The suggested meaning' — the meaning is: pertaining to that. /
'The power to convey' — the power to convey instantaneously. /
'That' — the meaning is: the power to convey <s>rasa</s> etc. as the suggested, instantaneously. /
'Also' — in the sense of cumulation. /
'Quality' — the meaning is: <s>prasāda</s>. /
'How' — the meaning is: how does the lucidity of word and meaning become <s>prasāda</s>? /
That [<s>prasāda</s>] is indeed a quality common to all <s>rasas</s>; that very [quality] alone is the quality common to all <s>rasas</s> — the twofold determination is merely [a matter of emphasis] — he says: 'all' etc. /
Here, by the first particle '<s>eva</s>' (alone), the exclusion of being common to word and meaning [is made]; by the second, the exclusion of <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) and <s>ojas</s> (vigor). /
'A quality of this kind' — the meaning is: a quality common to all <s>rasas</s>. /
He explains 'of all <s>rasas</s>' etc.: 'all' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'of the suggested meaning' etc. /
'That' (<s>sa</s>) is a continuation. /
He substantiates this: 'of the meaning' etc. /
'Of the meaning' — of the expressible meaning. /
'To begin with' etc. — the purport is: the capacity to convey the suggested that resides in the expressible meaning — how remarkable is that, really [i.e., it is nothing extraordinary]! /
The purport is: the capacity of word and meaning to convey this or that is not a <s>guṇa</s>; rather, it is <s>rasa</s> itself — by its self-absorption [in the connoisseur] — that instantaneously pervades the hearts of the connoisseurs — hence, primarily, the <s>guṇa</s> called <s>prasāda</s> resides in <s>rasa</s> alone; it is only by secondary usage that it is [said to reside] in word and meaning as well: this is the essential purport. /
He concludes: 'thus' etc. /
'<s>Bhāmaha</s>' — the meaning is: in accordance with the statements of <s>Bhāmaha</s> beginning with 'those who desire <s>mādhurya</s>' etc. /
'Those' etc. — those <s>guṇas</s>: <s>mādhurya</s>, <s>ojas</s>, and <s>prasāda</s>. /
'Consisting of the relishing of the cognizer' — the meaning is: the specific mental dispositions of the cognizer in the form of fluidity (<s>druti</s>), brilliance (<s>dīpti</s>), and lucidity (<s>prasāda</s>) — the relishings that have those as their primary nature: this is the meaning. /
And those reside in the mind: this is the purport. /
'From that' etc. —

children.text: śruti-duṣṭādayo doṣā anityā ye ca darśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The faults (<s>doṣas</s>) beginning with '<s>śrutiduṣṭa</s>' (offensive to the ear), and those that have been shown to be non-permanent (<s>anitya</s>) —

children.text: dhvany-ātmany eva śṛṅgāre te heyā ity udāhṛtāḥ // DhvK_2.11 //
children.translated_text: in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic <s>rasa</s>) that has <s>dhvani</s> as its soul — those are to be avoided: thus it has been illustrated. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.11 //

children.text: śrutiduṣṭādayo doṣā anityā ye ca darśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The faults beginning with '<s>śrutiduṣṭa</s>,' and those that have been shown to be non-permanent —
in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> that has <s>dhvani</s> as its soul — those are to be avoided: thus it has been illustrated. // 11 //

children.text:
anityā doṣāśca ye śrutiduṣṭādayaḥ sūcitāste 'pi na vātye arthamātre, na ca vyaṅgye śṛṅgāvyatirekiṇi śṛṅgāre vā dhvaneranātmamūte /
kiṃ tarhi? dhvanyātmanyeva śṛṅgāre 'ṅgitayā vyaṅgye te heyā ityudāhṛtāḥ /
anyathā hi teṣāmanityadoṣataiva na syāt /
evamayamasaṃlakṣyakramadṛyoto dhvanerātmā pradarśitaḥ sāmānyena /
locanam evamasmatpakṣa eva guṇālaṅkāravyavahāro vibhāgenopapadyata iti pradarśya nityānityadoṣavibhāgo 'pyasmatpakṣa eva saṅgacchata iti darśayitumāha---śrutiduṣṭādaya ityādi /
vāntādayo 'sabhyasmṛtihetavaḥ /
śrutiduṣṭā arthaduṣṭā vākyārthabalādaślīlārthapratipattikāriṇaḥ /
yathā---'chandrānveṣī mihāṃstabdho ghātāyaivopasarpati' iti /
kalpanāduṣṭāstu dvayoḥ padayoḥ kalpanayā /
yathā 'kuru rucim' ityatra kramavyatyase /
śrutikaṣṭastu adhākṣīt akṣotsīt tṛṇeḍhi ityādi /
śṛṅgāra ityucitarasopalakṣaṇārtham /

children.translated_text: Because those [faults] are to be avoided in <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>śānta</s> (quiescent), <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous), etc. as well.
'Have been indicated' —

children.text: na tveṣāṃ viṣayavibhāgapradarśanenānityatvaṃ bālapriyā "śrutiduṣṭārthaduṣṭe ca kalpanāduṣṭamityapi /
children.translated_text:
But the non-permanence of these has not [been established merely] by showing the division of their domains. /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: '<s>Śrutiduṣṭa</s> (offensive to the ear) and <s>arthaduṣṭa</s> (offensive in meaning), and also that called <s>kalpanāduṣṭa</s> (faulty in construction),
and likewise <s>śrutikaṣṭa</s> (harsh to the ear) — thus they declare the fourfold fault of speech.'

And the non-permanent faults (<s>doṣas</s>), [those] beginning with '<s>śrutiduṣṭa</s>' (offensive to the ear) that have been indicated — they are not [to be avoided] in mere expressible meaning alone, nor in the suggested when it is other than <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, nor in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> that does not have <s>dhvani</s> as its essence. /
What then? They are to be avoided in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> that has <s>dhvani</s> as its very soul — [that is,] where [<s>śṛṅgāra</s> is] suggested with principal status: thus it has been illustrated. /
For otherwise, their non-permanent fault-status itself would not obtain. /
Thus, this essence of <s>dhvani</s> — the <s>asaṃlakṣyakrama-dyota</s> (illumination with imperceptible sequence) — has been demonstrated in general. /
<s>Locana</s>: Having thus demonstrated that on our position alone the usage of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures) is coherently established through proper division, he shows that the division of permanent and non-permanent faults too is consistent only on our position — he says: '<s>śrutiduṣṭa</s> etc.' etc. /
'<s>Vānta</s>' (vomit) etc. — [these are words] causing the recollection of indecent things. /
'<s>Śrutiduṣṭa</s>' (offensive to the ear) [and] '<s>arthaduṣṭa</s>' (offensive in meaning) — [those are] words that, by the force of the sentence-meaning, produce the cognition of an indecent meaning. /
For example: '<s>chandrānveṣī</s> (moon-seeker) — the fog, standing firm, approaches as if to strike' — [here an indecent double meaning arises]. /
'<s>Kalpanāduṣṭa</s>' (faults of construction) — [arise] from the construction of two words. /
For example, in '<s>kuru rucim</s>' (make [it] pleasing), through the transposition of sequence [yielding an indecent compound]. /
'<s>Śrutikaṣṭa</s>' (harsh to the ear) — as in '<s>adhākṣīt</s>', '<s>akṣotsīt</s>', '<s>tṛṇeḍhi</s>', etc. /
'<s>Śṛṅgāra</s>' — [this word in the <s>kārikā</s>] is intended as an indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for the appropriate <s>rasa</s>.

children.text:
ityādinā bhāmahoktan śṛtidudhṭādidoṣān sodāharaṇān darśayati---vāntādayāsabhyetyādi /
'śrutiduṣṭāḥ asabhyasmṛtihetavo vāntādaya' iti sambandhaḥ /
śrutiduṣṭāḥ śrutiduṣṭatvarūpadoṣavantaḥ /
evamuttaratrāpi bodhyam /
kāriṇa iti /
śabdā iti śeṣaḥ /
chidreti rājavarṇanam /
parasya chidrānveṣī /
stabdhaḥ acañcalaḥ /
ghātāya pareṣāṃ vināśanāya /
atra puruṣaśepharūpāślīlārthasya pratītirbhavati /
kalpanayeti /
bhavantīti śeṣaḥ /
kramavyatyāsa iti /
ruciṅkuru iti parivartana ityarthaḥ /
ciṅkurnāma yonyantarvartyaṅkuraḥ /
adhākṣīdityādi /
tiḍantam /
śṛṅgāra itīti /
dhvanyātmanyeva śṛṅgāra ityatratyaṃ, śṛṅgārapadamityarthaḥ /
bhāvaṃ vivṛṇoti---na tvityādi /
bhinnavṛttādidoṣebhyaḥ viviktaṃ vyatyastam anityatvam /
eṣāṃ śrutiduṣṭādīnām /
viṣayavibhāgapradarśanena viṣayavibhāgaṃ pradarśya, na tu pradarśitamiti
children.translated_text:
With the passage beginning with '<s>vānta</s> etc., indecent' etc., he shows, with examples, the <s>śrutiduṣṭa</s> and other faults stated by <s>Bhāmaha</s>. /
The connection is: '<s>vānta</s> etc. are <s>śrutiduṣṭa</s> — [those] causing the recollection of indecent things.' /
'<s>Śrutiduṣṭa</s>' — possessing the fault in the form of being offensive to the ear. /
Likewise in what follows. /
'Causing' — the remainder is: 'words.' /
'<s>Chidra</s>' — a description of a king. /
'One who seeks out the weakness of the other.' /
'Firm' — unmoving. /
'For the strike' — for the destruction of others. /
Here, the cognition of an indecent meaning in the form of the male organ arises. /
'By the construction' — the remainder is: 'they arise.' /
'Transposition of sequence' — '<s>ruciṅkuru</s>' means transposition: this is the meaning. /
'<s>Ciṅkur</s>' is a sprout existing in another womb [i.e., an indecent compound formed by transposition]. /
'<s>Adhākṣīt</s>' etc. — these are finite verb forms. /
'<s>Śṛṅgāra</s>' etc. — the meaning is: the word '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' in the <s>kārikā</s> passage '<s>dhvanyātmany eva śṛṅgāre</s>.' /
He elaborates the purport: 'but not' etc. /
Distinguished from faults like broken meter (<s>bhinnavṛtta</s>) etc. — the non-permanence is the opposite [i.e., sometimes faults, sometimes not]. /
'Of these' — of <s>śrutiduṣṭa</s> etc. /
'By showing the domain-division' — having shown the domain-division, but not: '[what was] shown [is merely that]' —

children.text: tasyāṅgānāṃ prabhedā ye prabhedāḥ svagatāś ca ye /
children.translated_text: The sub-varieties of its subsidiaries (<s>aṅgas</s>), and the sub-varieties that are internal to it —
in the mutual combination of those, [there is] infinity. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.12 //

children.text: tasyāṅgānāṃ prabhedā ye prabhedāḥ svagatāśca ye /
children.translated_text: The sub-varieties of its subsidiaries, and the sub-varieties that are internal to it —
in the mutual combination of those, [there is] infinity. // 12 //

children.text: aṅgitā vyaṅgyo rasādirvivakṣitānyaparavācyasya dhvanereka ātmā ya uktastasyāṅganāṃ vācyavācakānupātināmalaṅkārāṇāṃ ye prabhedā niravadhayo ye ca svagatāstasyāṅgino 'rthasya rasabhāvatadābhāsatatpraśamalakṣaṇā vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāripratipādanasahitā anantāḥ svāśrayāpekṣayā niḥ--- locanam bhinnavṛttādidoṣebhyo viviktaṃ pradarśitam /
children.translated_text:
The principal (<s>aṅgin</s>) [element] — the suggested <s>rasa</s> etc. — is one essence of <s>dhvani</s> whose expressible has the intention of [conveying] another [meaning], as was stated. Of its subsidiaries (<s>aṅgas</s>) — the <s>alaṅkāras</s> that follow the expressible and the expressive — the sub-varieties are unlimited. And the internal [sub-varieties] of the principal meaning — characterized by <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, their semblances, and their quiescence — accompanied by the presentation of <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> — are infinite, relative to their own substrate. /
<s>Locana</s>: Distinguished from faults such as broken meter etc. — [the non-permanence] has been demonstrated.
Nor [has] the distinction from <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) [been shown by them].

children.text: bībhatsahāsyalaudrādau tveṣāmasmābhirupagamāt śṛṅgārādau ca varjanādanityatvaṃ ca doṣatvaṃ ca samarthitameveti /
children.translated_text: But since these [faults] are accepted by us in <s>bībhatsa</s> (the disgusting), <s>hāsya</s> (the comic), <s>raudra</s> (the furious), etc., and avoided in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc. — both their non-permanence and their fault-status have been established.
This is the purport. // 12 //

aṅgānāmityalaṅkārāṇām /
svagatā iti /
ātmagatāḥ sambhogavipralambhādyā ātmīyagatā vibhāvādigatāsteṣāṃ loṣṭaprastāreṇāṅgāṅgibhāve kā gaṇaneti bhāvaḥ /

bālapriyā sambandhaḥ /

nāpi guṇebhyo vyatiriktatvamiti /
eṣamaguṇatvamapi noktamityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Has been established' —
the meaning is: has been demonstrated by the passage beginning with '<s>dhvanyātmany eva</s>' etc.
In the <s>vṛtti</s> passage beginning with '<s>śṛṅgāre vā</s>' etc., the continuation is with '<s>na ca</s>' (and not).

children.text: 'heyā ityudāhṛtā' ityasya 'te 'pi na vācye 'rthamātre' ityādivākyatrayeṇāpi sambandhaśca bodhyaḥ // 11 //
children.translated_text: And the connection of '<s>heyā ity udāhṛtāḥ</s>' (to be avoided, as illustrated) with the three sentences beginning with '<s>te 'pi na vācye 'rthamātre</s>' should be understood. // 11 //

'Of the subsidiaries' — of the <s>alaṅkāras</s>. /
'Internal' — 'self-referent' (<s>ātmagata</s>) [means] belonging to the self; [sub-types such as] <s>sambhoga</s> (union), <s>vipralambha</s> (separation), etc. 'Belonging to one's own [components]' — [those] belonging to <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. Of those, by the <s>loṣṭaprastāra</s> (clod-expansion) method in the principal-subsidiary relationship — what count [is possible]?: this is the purport. /
'Own substrate' — the nature of the woman, man, and their appropriateness etc. /
'Mutual seeing with love' — this is synecdochic (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>), [including] also conversation etc. /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: The connection [is as follows]. /
Just as faults of broken meter etc. have been stated by <s>Bhāmaha</s> and others, so too have the <s>śrutiduṣṭa</s> and other faults been stated; but the non-permanence of these has not been stated: this is the meaning. /
'Nor the distinction from <s>guṇas</s>' — the meaning is: their non-<s>guṇa</s> status also has not been stated [by them].

children.translated_text: The substrate [is something like] the <s>Malaya</s> [mountain range] etc. — what is said regarding the <s>vibhāvas</s> such as the wind etc. — that is already covered by the word 'place' (<s>deśa</s>).
Therefore, 'substrate' [here means] 'cause' (<s>kāraṇa</s>).

children.text: yathā mamaiva--- dayitayā grathitā sragiyaṃ mayā hṛdayadhāmani nityaniyojitā /
children.translated_text:
For example, by me myself: 'This garland, strung by [my] beloved, /
is forever fastened by me upon the abode of [my] heart.'
[The garland] drips the nectar of <s>sudhā</s>, even though dry, which removes the burning fever of separation.

'Of the <s>alaṅkāras</s>' — the subsidiary status of <s>alaṅkāras</s> with respect to <s>rasa</s> etc. was thus substantiated. In the <s>Kāvyapradīpodyota</s> [it is stated]: 'Even pleasing meanings, when expressed by a mean word, do not produce the same aesthetic relish — hence <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) etc., through the medium of word, are auxiliaries to <s>rasa</s> etc.; and <s>upamā</s> (simile) etc., through the medium of enhancing the <s>vibhāva</s> etc. that manifest the suggested <s>rasa</s> etc., are embellishers of <s>rasa</s> etc. And [expressions] endowed with the surplus [beauty] produced by <s>alaṅkāras</s> generate a surplus of relishing. /
For a certain surplus is experienced in the ornamented [expression] compared to the unornamented. /
For <s>alaṅkāras</s>, enhancing the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., serve in many ways as <s>uddīpana</s> (stimulants); and sometimes [they serve] even as <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) — as when a description of the heroine etc. is composed by the hero etc. — thus some say.' /
In [the expression] '<s>svagatā</s>' (internal), the word '<s>sva</s>' (own/self) refers to the self, the other, what belongs to oneself, and what belongs to another — he explains: '<s>ātmagatā</s>' (belonging to the self) etc. /
The elaboration of '<s>ātmagatā</s>' is: '<s>sambhoga</s>' (union) etc. /
Of '<s>ātmīyagatā</s>' (belonging to one's own [components]) — '<s>vibhāvas</s> etc.' /
'Of those' — the meaning is: of the sub-types. /
'By the <s>loṣṭaprastāra</s> (clod-expansion)' — '<s>prastāra</s>' is a type of procedure (<s>prakriyābheda</s>) that reveals the essential nature of meters. /
It is defined in the <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s> by [the rule] '<s>pāde sarvagurāv</s>' etc.; by that method, the counting of the sub-types is impossible: this is the meaning. /
In '<s>svāśrayāpekṣayā</s>' (relative to their own substrate), he explains the word '<s>svāśraya</s>': '<s>strī</s>' etc. /
The meaning is: the natures of woman and man, and their appropriateness, etc. /
He explains 'mutual love-sight': 'mutually' etc. /
The limits, i.e., specific distinctions, of those — when the mutual combination of those is being devised, even the modes of any one <s>rasa</s> cannot be enumerated — how much less those of all [<s>rasas</s>]. /
For thus: the two primary divisions of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> as the principal are: <s>sambhoga</s> (union) and <s>vipralambha</s> (separation). /
And the modes of <s>sambhoga</s> are characterized by: mutual love-sight, lovemaking, pleasure-excursions, etc. /
<s>Locana</s>: Lovemaking comprises the sixty-four [arts] — embracing etc. /
Pleasure-excursion is going to gardens. /
By '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), water-sports, drinking-parties, moonrise-games, etc. [are included]. /
The <s>abhilāṣa-vipralambha</s> (separation due to longing) should be understood as [occurring] when, even though the <s>rati</s> (love) — consisting of mutual regard of each other as the all-in-all of one's life — has arisen in both, the meeting is not obtained due to some cause. /
As in [the passage beginning] 'what does it mean to say "makes happy"?' etc. between <s>Vatsarāja</s> and the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> — but not before [that exchange] for <s>Ratnāvalī</s>; for at that time — /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: He elaborates the passage beginning with 'of <s>vipralambha</s> too' etc.: '<s>abhilāṣa-vipralambha</s>' etc. /
'What does it mean to say "makes happy"' — this is the speech of <s>Vatsarāja</s> to the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> in the drama <s>Ratnāvalī</s>. /
'But not before for <s>Ratnāvalī</s>' — the continuation is with 'therefore.' /
Before this speech, there is no <s>abhilāṣa-vipralambha</s> for <s>Ratnāvalī</s> at all: this is the meaning. /
Because only upon hearing this speech does <s>Ratnāvalī</s> become certain of the king's love for her: this is the purport. /
Showing this very reason, he says: 'at that time' etc. /
'At that time' — at the earlier time. /
'Of <s>vipralambha</s> too' — <s>abhilāṣa</s> (longing), <s>irṣyā</s> (jealousy), <s>viraha</s> (separation), <s>pravāsa</s> (sojourn abroad) — these are [the sub-types] of <s>vipralambha</s>. /
And of each of those, the division by <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, and <s>vyabhicārin</s>. /
And of those, the division by substrate-conditions such as place, time, etc. — thus, relative to its own internal sub-types, the immeasurability of even that one [<s>rasa</s>]; how much more when the devising of subsidiary sub-types [is added]! /
For those subsidiary sub-types, when the mutual combination with each principal sub-type is being devised — they attain infinity indeed. /
<s>Locana</s>: In the absence of <s>rati</s> (love), a mere state of desire — that [is a further sub-type]. /
<s>Irṣyā-vipralambha</s> (jealousy-separation) — [occurs] with the <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (wronged heroine) through the breaking of love-pledges etc. /
<s>Viraha-vipralambha</s> (separation-by-absence) — should be understood [as occurring] with the <s>khaṇḍitā</s> who, even when being appeased, does not accept appeasement, and who thereafter, pervaded by the heat of remorse, becomes <s>virahot-kaṇṭhitā</s> (longing-in-separation). /
<s>Pravāsa-vipralambha</s> (separation-by-sojourn) — [occurs] with the <s>proṣitabhartṛkā</s> (whose husband has gone abroad): this is the division. /
By '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), [vipralambha] caused by a curse etc. — and [that which is only] as-if-<s>vipralambha</s> through deception. /
For in deception, the desired object is not obtained — just so here. /
'And of those' — in one case, of <s>sambhoga</s> etc.; in the other, of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc.

children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] "Of that" — of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. The varieties of the principal <s>rasas</s> etc. [arise from] the construction of their relationships — this is the meaning. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "Due to the absence of <s>rati</s>" — the seventh case-ending is in the sense of cause. The meaning is: because of the absence of <s>rati</s> (love) as the reason. For <s>rati</s>, the <s>sthāyin</s> of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, requires certainty of mutual abode. The state of mere desire is that — the <s>rati</s> in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> is in the form of longing (<s>abhilāṣa</s>) only. "Affection" (<s>praṇaya</s>) — <s>praṇaya</s> means love or entreaty. "With the <s>khaṇḍitā</s>" — the connection is "with the <s>khaṇḍitā</s> [heroine]." "Being appeased" etc. is a qualifier of the <s>khaṇḍitā</s>. He justifies the use of the term <s>vipralambha</s> (deception) for the stated [states] of longing etc. — "as if <s>vipralambha</s>." The purport is that the word <s>vipralambha</s> is secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>). He states the similarity of the two — "in deception" etc. "Thus here" — meaning: likewise in longing etc. In the <s>vṛtti</s>, both occurrences of "of those" in "and of each of those" and "and of those in place" are explained in sequence — with "in one" etc. Regarding the word "substrate" (<s>āśraya</s>) in "difference of place, time, substrate, and state" — he says that the explanation of some is not correct — with "substrate" etc. "That" etc. — the meaning is: if that were the meaning, there would be redundancy. "By the beloved" — the reading "even more dry" also exists. The dryness is due to the intensity of heart-burning. "Drips the nectar" — causes to flow — this is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). Here, as an excitant (<s>uddīpaka</s>) —
Only a direction is indicated, by which the understanding of the learned and sensitive ones,
Having obtained illumination, will apply everywhere. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.13 //
Only a direction is indicated, by which the understanding of the learned and sensitive ones,
Having obtained illumination, will apply everywhere. // 13 //

children.text:
diṅmātrakathanena hi vyutpannānāṃ sahṛdayānāmekatrāpi rasabhede sahālaṅkārairaṅgāṅgibhāvaparijñānādāsāditālokā buddhiḥ sarvatraiva bhaviṣyati /
tatra-----
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] For by indicating merely a direction, the understanding of the learned connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdayas</s>), having obtained illumination through the knowledge of the subsidiary-principal relationship (<s>aṅga-aṅgi-bhāva</s>) together with <s>alaṅkāras</s> even in a single variety of <s>rasa</s>, will apply everywhere. Regarding that —
Of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> as the principal [<s>rasa</s>], <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) bound with deliberate uniformity of pattern

children.text: sarveṣv eva prabhedeṣu nānuprāsaḥ prakāśakaḥ // DhvK_2.14 //
children.translated_text: Is not expressive in any of the varieties. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.14 //
Of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> as the principal [<s>rasa</s>], <s>anuprāsa</s> bound with deliberate uniformity of pattern
Is not expressive in any of the varieties. // 14 //

children.text:
aṅgino hi śṛṅgārasya ye uktaḥ /
prabhedāsteṣu sarveṣvekaprakārānubandhi tayā prabandhena pravṛtto 'nuprāso na vyañjakaḥ /
aṅgina ityanenāṅgabhūtasya śṛṅgārasyaikarūpānubandhanuprāsanibandhane kāmacāramāha /
dhvanyātmabhūte śṛṅgāre yamakādinibandhanam /
locanam yeneti /
diṅmātroktenetyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: "Of the sensitive ones" —
The purport is: of those who aspire to great poetic skill and connoisseurship.
"Everywhere" —
The connection is: "whose understanding has obtained illumination, i.e., thorough cultivation (<s>vyutpatti</s>), regarding all <s>rasas</s> etc." // 13 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] For of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> as the principal [<s>rasa</s>], the stated varieties — in all of them, <s>anuprāsa</s> employed in a continuous composition maintaining a single pattern is not suggestive. By saying "of the principal" he allows freedom for <s>anuprāsa</s> of uniform pattern when <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is subsidiary. The composition of <s>yamaka</s> etc. in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> that has <s>dhvani</s> as its soul — [<s>Locana</s>:] "By which" — meaning: by what has been stated as merely a direction.
The meaning is: when the direction to be stated [is present].
"With effort" (<s>yatnāt</s>) —
The intended meaning is causal: because it is done deliberately.

children.text: ekarūpaṃ tvanubandhaṃ tyaktvā vicitro 'nuprāso nibadhyamāno na doṣāyetyekarūpagrahaṇam // 14 //
children.translated_text: But abandoning uniform pattern and composing varied <s>anuprāsa</s> is not a fault — hence the qualification "uniform." // 14 //
"Regarding that" —
"<s>Yamaka</s> etc." — the word "etc." (<s>ādi</s>) denotes varieties.
"Difficult" (<s>duṣkara</s>) [refers to] <s>muraja</s>-patterns, <s>cakrabandha</s>, etc.

dhvanerātmabhūtaḥ śṛṅgārastātparyeṇa vācyavācakābhyāṃ prakāśyamānastasminyamakādīnāṃ yamakaprakārāṇāṃ nibandhanaṃ duṣkaraśabdabhaṅgaśleṣādīnāṃ śaktāvapi pramāditvam /
'pramāditvā'mityanenaitaddṛśyate---kākatālīyena kadācitkasyacidekasya yamakāderniṣpattāvapi bhūmnālaṅkārāntaravadrasāṅgatvena nibandho na kartavya iti /

atra yuktirabhidhīyate-----
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> that has <s>dhvani</s> as its essence — when it is being manifested by the expressible and the expressive in their fullness — therein, the composition of <s>yamakas</s>, i.e., varieties of <s>yamaka</s>, and the composition of difficult word-breaking, <s>śleṣa</s>, etc. [amounts to] negligence even when one has the capacity. By the word "negligence" (<s>pramāditva</s>) this is indicated: even if by coincidence (<s>kākatālīya</s>) some single <s>yamaka</s> etc. is accomplished, one should not, in abundance, compose [them] as subsidiaries to <s>rasa</s> as one would other <s>alaṅkāras</s>. By "especially in <s>vipralambha</s>" — in <s>vipralambha</s>, the predominance of delicacy (<s>saukumārya</s>) is indicated. When that is to be illuminated, the composition of <s>yamaka</s> etc. as subsidiary should decidedly not be done. Here the rationale is stated —
That <s>alaṅkāra</s> whose composition can be accomplished as drawn forth by <s>rasa</s>,
Achievable without separate effort — that is considered [appropriate as] an <s>alaṅkāra</s> in <s>dhvani</s>. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.16 //

The meaning is: word-breaking in the word <s>aśoka</s> etc. is not faulty.

children.translated_text: The word <s>aśoka</s> conventionally denotes a particular tree, but through word-breaking, by the etymological analysis "one in whom there is no grief" (<s>nāsti śoko yasya</s>), it also conveys "free from grief" — this is the purport. In the <s>vṛtti</s>: "negligence even when one has the capacity" —

children.text: " avyutpattikṛto doṣaḥ śaktyā saṃvriyate kave"riti vakṣyamāṇatvena doṣatirodhāyakaśaktau satyāmapi kaveḥ pramāditvajñāpakatvenākartavyatvātkadācitkasyacidekasya yamakāderniṣpattirna doṣāvaheti bhāvaḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: Since it will be stated [later] that "a fault arising from lack of cultivation is concealed by the poet's power," even though such poetic power exists as capable of concealing faults, because [the composition of <s>yamaka</s> etc.] causes awareness of negligence and hence should not be done — the occasional accomplishment of a single <s>yamaka</s> etc. does not constitute a fault — this is the purport. // 15 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "Rationale" — meaning: a principle applicable to all [cases]. "By <s>rasa</s>" — through the conjunction with <s>rasa</s>, i.e., through the arrangement of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. alone. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The explanation of "of <s>yamakas</s> etc." in the <s>vṛtti</s> is "of varieties of <s>yamaka</s>." He gives the justification for this — "the word 'etc.'" etc. The elaboration of "varieties of <s>yamaka</s>" — "difficult" etc. He glosses that — "difficult" etc. He states the implication when word-breaking and <s>śleṣa</s> are mentioned — "meaning-<s>śleṣa</s>" etc. The meaning is: non-breaking <s>śleṣa</s>, i.e., <s>śleṣa</s> without word-breaking. It is clear in the <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s> etc. that non-breaking <s>śleṣa</s> and meaning-<s>śleṣa</s> are one and the same according to the ancients. "You are passionate/red" — here, in the word <s>raktaśilīmukha</s> etc., there is meaning-<s>śleṣa</s>.

children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] That [<s>alaṅkāra</s>] may be so [appropriate] in this <s>dhvani</s> of imperceptible-sequence suggestion.
The meaning is: its subsidiary status to <s>rasa</s> alone is primary.

children.text: yathā---- kapole pattrālī karatalanirodhena mṛditā nipīto niḥśvāsairayamamṛtahṛdyo 'dhararasaḥ /
children.translated_text: As in: "The leaf-pattern on [her] cheek is crushed by the restraint of [his] palm; this nectar-hearted lip-<s>rasa</s> is drunk by [her] sighs;

children.text: muhuḥ kaṇṭhe lagnastaralayati bāṣpastanataṭīṃ priyo manyurjātastava niranurodhe na tu vayam //
children.translated_text: Tears clinging repeatedly to the throat make the bosom tremble; beloved, anger has arisen — it is at your indifference, not at us. //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He glosses the word "rationale" (<s>yukti</s>) by understanding the term as it literally sounds — "all" etc. Showing the purport of the general statements "in <s>rasa</s>" and "in <s>dhvani</s>," he glosses the verse — "by <s>rasa</s>" etc. The elaboration in substance of "as drawn forth by <s>rasa</s>" etc. — "through the conjunction with <s>rasa</s>" etc. "As necessarily entailed by that" — by the word "that" the arrangement of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. is referred to; the meaning is: as being accomplished by the very effort that produces that [arrangement]. "Which" — even if an <s>alaṅkāra</s> is marvelous in its accomplishment, that <s>alaṅkāra</s> whose composition can be accomplished solely as drawn forth by <s>rasa</s> — [<s>Locana</s>:] performing [it] as necessarily entailed — the one who attains that — that alone is an <s>alaṅkāra</s> here in the path of <s>rasa</s>, not any other. Therefore, even in <s>vīra</s>, <s>adbhuta</s>, and other <s>rasas</s>, <s>yamaka</s> etc. is an obstruction to <s>rasa</s> for both the poet and the recipient — everywhere. With the intention of winning over those people who, bereft of ascending the chariot of connoisseurship, have lost their discrimination through the flood of sheep-like following — I have said "especially in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>vipralambha</s>" — this is the purport. And thus he will state generally: "therefore, subsidiary status of these does not exist in <s>rasa</s>." "In accomplishment" — meaning: when it comes about spontaneously through the grace of creative intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>), without requiring deliberate production. "Marvelous" — i.e., a source of wonder: "how was this composed!" [Example:] "With leaf-patterns on her cheek, her face turned aside by the restraint of [his] palm, her sighs exhausting her lower lip, her throat choked by the oncoming flood of tears, her breast heaving with unbroken weeping — while she refuses to abandon anger, as far as she is appeased by flattering speech" — thus, for the speaker whose mind is absorbed in savoring the <s>anubhāvas</s> pertaining to jealous love-in-separation, <s>śleṣa</s>, <s>rūpaka</s>, <s>vyatireka</s>, and other [figures] arise effortlessly, without causing any obstruction to the <s>rasa</s>-savoring of the one who savors too. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The meaning is: the <s>yamaka alaṅkāra</s>. The connection is: "that alone is an <s>alaṅkāra</s> here in the path of <s>rasa</s>." The elaboration of "in <s>dhvani</s>" — "here, in the path of <s>rasa</s>." Meaning: in [the <s>dhvani</s> of] <s>rasa</s> in general with imperceptible sequence. "Therefore" — meaning: by the general statement "in <s>dhvani</s>." "<s>Vīra</s>" etc. — meaning: when they alone [are principal]. The construction is: "<s>yamaka</s> etc. is an obstruction to <s>rasa</s>." "Everywhere" connects with "<s>vīra</s>" etc. Objection: this contradicts what was previously stated — to this he says "sheep-following" (<s>gaḍḍurikā</s>). <s>Gaḍḍurikā</s> means a flock of sheep that follows a ram — by analogy, unthinking imitation. Those people whose discrimination has been destroyed by the flood of such [imitation], and who are bereft of ascending the chariot of connoisseurship — with the intention of winning them over — this is the meaning. "By me" — meaning by the original author (<s>mūlakṛt</s>). "Purport" means the original author's intention. He cites support for what was stated — "and thus" etc. "In accomplishment" means in arising. The elaboration of "spontaneously" — "without requiring" etc. Meaning: when there is no dependence on any other effort favorable to its production. He shows the <s>alaṅkāras</s> by elaborating the essential meaning of "cheek" (<s>kapola</s>) etc. — with "hand" etc. "Sighs" — she whose lower lip is exhausted, i.e., wilted, by sighs. "Unbroken" — the reading "broken-and-unbroken" also exists. "Is appeased" — the rest is: the heroine in a state of amorous anger, by the hero as speaker. "Jealousy" etc. — <s>anubhāva</s> means sighing etc.; its savoring means repeated contemplation. "Of the speaker" — this statement applies to both the hero composed by the poet and the poet himself. The connection is with "arisen effortlessly." "<s>Śleṣa</s>" etc. — in "the nectar-hearted lip-<s>rasa</s>" (<s>adhararasa</s>), because the word <s>rasa</s> has double meaning — as flavor being tasted and as sweetness — there is <s>śleṣa</s>. Or, in this verse there is meaning-<s>śleṣa</s>. Because: "anger is the lover" is a <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor); the meaning of "cheek" etc. substantiates that; the agency of causing actions like pressing by the palm-restraint is common to both anger and the lover. "Drunk" (<s>nipīta</s>) has a causative sense implied. "Tears" (<s>bāṣpa</s>) — anger in the form of tears is also an alternative meaning. "We are not lovers" is the <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). By the first word, <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) is captured. "Of the one who savors" — meaning: of the connoisseur. The connection is: does not cause [obstruction]. A definition is that property which pervades the differentia of the definiendum and is co-extensive with the genuine instances.

children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] And subsidiarity to <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>) is also not contradicted [for <s>yamaka</s> etc.]. /

children.text: aṅgitayā tu vyaṅgye rase nāṅgatvaṃ pṛthakprayatnanirvartyatvādyamakādeḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] But as principal, [<s>yamaka</s> etc.] cannot have subsidiarity when the suggested <s>rasa</s> is the principal element, because <s>yamaka</s> etc. require a separate effort. /

children.text: asyaivārthasya saṅgrahaślokāḥ---- rasavanti hi vastūni sālaṅkārāṇi kānicit /
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Summary verses for this very meaning — Indeed, some compositions endowed with <s>rasa</s> and adorned with <s>alaṅkāras</s>,
are accomplished by the great poet (<s>mahākavi</s>) through a single effort alone. //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] And the defining mark of being a subsidiary of <s>rasa</s> (<s>rasāṅgatva</s>) is being accomplished without a separate effort (<s>apṛthagyatnanirvartyatva</s>). Thus, whatever <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure of speech) is produced by a poet who has resolved upon <s>rasa</s> as the primary aim — that is a subsidiary of <s>rasa</s>; but one produced by a poet who has abandoned that disposition and resorted to a different effort — that is not a subsidiary of <s>rasa</s>. / And in <s>yamaka</s> (paronomasia) composed in a continuous series, deliberately, a resort to a different effort inevitably occurs, in the form of searching for particular words. / If one objects that the same applies to other <s>alaṅkāras</s> — not so; for other <s>alaṅkāras</s>, even when they involve difficult constructions upon examination, are the mark of a mind absorbed in <s>rasa</s>. / [<s>Locana</s>:] 'Mark' — the meaning is 'indicator' (<s>vyāpaka</s>). / The syntactic connection is with 'composed in a continuous series.' / Therefore, because deliberateness is inevitable, the word <s>buddhipūrvaka</s> (deliberate) is employed. / A different effort (<s>yatnāntara</s>) means an effort other than absorption in <s>rasa</s>. / 'Difficult constructions upon examination' (<s>nirūpyamāṇadurghaṭana</s>) — the meaning is: things that, even when deliberately intended, are impossible to accomplish. / Alternatively: 'difficult constructions upon examination' means they inspire wonder — 'How were these composed?' / [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In the present context, he says that by the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>) only 'indicator' is intended — 'the meaning is vyāpaka.' / Some hold that the reading should be 'the meaning is jñāpaka (sign).' / The sense is that non-accomplishment-by-separate-effort is the indicator of an <s>alaṅkāra</s>'s subsidiarity to <s>rasa</s> — this is the meaning of the <s>vṛtti</s> passage beginning with '<s>rasāṅgatva</s>.' / To establish the stated meaning, [<s>Ānandavardhana</s>] shows the negative case (<s>vyatireka</s>) in the <s>vṛtti</s> with 'whoever [intends] <s>rasa</s>' etc. / The construal is: 'whatever <s>alaṅkāra</s> is produced.' / '<s>Tāṃ vāsanām</s>' — the meaning is: the disposition of resolve upon <s>rasa</s>-composition. / '<s>Atyūhya</s>' — having transgressed, having abandoned. / '<s>Āsthitasya</s>' — of one who has resorted to; its syntactic connection is with 'of the poet' (<s>kaveḥ</s>). / '<s>Sa na rasāṅgam</s>' — the meaning is: in that <s>alaṅkāra</s>, subsidiarity to <s>rasa</s> does not exist. / He states that in the composition of <s>yamaka</s> etc. a different effort is necessary — '<s>yamaka</s>' etc. / '<s>Prabandhena</s>' — without interruption. / Lest there be a misconstrual of this with '<s>buddhipūrvakam</s>' (deliberately), [<s>Abhinavagupta</s>] shows the construal in the <s>Locana</s> — 'composed' (<s>kriyamāṇe</s>). / In the phrase 'resort to a different effort' (<s>yatnāntaraparigraha</s>), he glosses the word <s>yatnāntara</s> — '<s>rasa</s>' etc.: a different effort from the one that produces <s>rasa</s>. / He explains '<s>nirūpyamāṇadurghaṭana</s>' in two ways according to context — '<s>nirūpyamāṇāni</s>' etc.: the meaning is 'impossible to accomplish'; and alternatively, those that inspire wonder, 'How were these composed?' / Where it says 'impossible to accomplish,' [such figures] come spontaneously (<s>ahampūrvikayā</s>) to the gifted poet; as in the <s>Kādambarī</s> at the occasion of <s>Kādambarī</s>'s appearance, / and as on the bridge when <s>Sītā Devī</s> was overwhelmed by the sight of <s>Māyā-Rāma</s>'s head. / And this is fitting, since <s>rasas</s> are to be evoked only through particular expressible contents (<s>vācyaviśeṣa</s>). / And the words that convey those [contents] — the particular expressibles that illuminate them, namely <s>rūpaka</s> and other <s>alaṅkāras</s> — / therefore their externality to the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> does not obtain. / But in the difficult paths of <s>yamaka</s>, that [externality] remains as it is. / As for the fact that some <s>yamakas</s> etc. are seen to contain <s>rasa</s>, there the <s>rasas</s> etc. have subsidiarity, while the <s>yamakas</s> etc. have principality alone. /
But in the composition of <s>yamaka</s> etc., a separate effort arises for him.
Therefore, even for one who is capable, subsidiarity to <s>rasa</s> does not exist for these [<s>yamaka</s> etc.]. //
But the state of being subsidiary to <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>) is not precluded for <s>yamaka</s> etc.
However, when <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic <s>rasa</s>) has <s>dhvani</s> as its essence, subsidiarity [of <s>yamaka</s>] is not tenable. //

children.text:
locanam ahampūrvaḥ agmya ityarthaḥ /
ahamādāhamādau pravarta ityarthaḥ /
ahampūrva ityasya bhāvo 'hampūrvikā /
ahamiti nipāto vibhaktipratirūpako 'smadarthavṛttiḥ /
etaditi /
ahaṃpūrvikayā parāpatanamityarthaḥ /
kānicaditi /
kālidāsādikṛtānītyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] The syntactic connection is: 'even of one who is capable, a separate effort arises.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Eṣām</s>' — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] means 'of <s>yamaka</s> and others.' /

children.text: 'dhvanyātmabhūte śṛṅgāre iti yaduktaṃ tat prādhānyanārdhaślokena saṅgṛhīte dhvanyātmabhūta iti // 16 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] What was stated as '<s>dhvanyātmabhūte śṛṅgāre</s>' (when <s>śṛṅgāra</s> has <s>dhvani</s> as its essence) is summarized in the half-verse on principality — '<s>dhvanyātmabhūta</s>' etc. // 16 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Ahampūrvaḥ</s>' — the meaning is 'having come spontaneously.' / The meaning is: 'I [come] first, I act first.' / The abstract noun (<s>bhāva</s>) of '<s>ahampūrva</s>' is '<s>ahampūrvikā</s>' (spontaneous self-presentation). / '<s>Aham</s>' is an indeclinable particle functioning as a substitute for a case-ending, operating in the sense of the first person. / '<s>Etat</s>' — / the meaning is: 'a spontaneous arriving' (<s>ahampūrvikayā parāpatanam</s>). / '<s>Kānicid</s>' — the meaning is: those composed by <s>Kālidāsa</s> and others. /

children.text:
bālapriyā kaveriti, vismayāvahānītyatra sahṛdayasyeti ca śeṣaḥ /
ahampūrvikayetyetadvyācaṣṭe---ahamityādi /
pūrva ityasya vyākhyā agṣa iti /
paryavasitamāha--ahamādāvityādi /
vṛttau 'tatpratipādakaiśca śabdai'riti /
ākṣeptavyā ityanenāsya sambandhaḥ /
'tatprakāśina' iti /
atra tatpadena śabdasya parāmarśaḥ /
'teṣām' iti /
rūpakādīnāmityarthaḥ /
'tadi'ti /
bahiraṅgatvamityarthaḥ /
'rasābhāse cāṅgatva'miti /

children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>yamakādīnām</s>' (of <s>yamaka</s> etc.) should be supplied. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The author of the <s>vṛtti</s> summarizes the stated meanings in verses — '<s>rasavantī</s>' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The construal is: 'such compositions are accomplished by the great poet through a single effort alone.' /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In the <s>Locana</s>, [<s>Abhinavagupta</s>] shows the construal — '<s>śaktasyāpi</s>' (even of one who is capable). // 16 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In '<s>kaveḥ</s>' (of the poet), and in '<s>vismayāvahāni</s>' (inspiring wonder), '<s>sahṛdayasya</s>' (of the sensitive reader) should be supplied. / She explains '<s>ahampūrvikayā</s>' — '<s>aham</s>' etc. / The gloss of '<s>pūrva</s>' is '<s>agra</s>' (foremost). / She states the final meaning — '<s>ahamādau</s>' etc. / In the <s>vṛtti</s>, '<s>tatpratipādakaiś ca śabdaiḥ</s>' (and by the words that convey those [contents]) — / its syntactic connection is with '<s>ākṣeptavyāḥ</s>' (are to be evoked). / '<s>Tatprakāśinaḥ</s>' (those that illuminate that) — / here by the word '<s>tat</s>' there is reference to the word [rather than the meaning]. / '<s>Teṣām</s>' — / the meaning is: of <s>rūpaka</s> and other [<s>alaṅkāras</s>]. / '<s>Tat</s>' — / the meaning is: externality (<s>bahiraṅgatva</s>). / '<s>Rasābhāse ca aṅgatvam</s>' (and subsidiarity to <s>rasābhāsa</s>) — /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Now the class of <s>alaṅkāras</s> that serves as the suggestive vehicle (<s>vyañjaka</s>) of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> whose essence is <s>dhvani</s> is described —
[<s>Kārikā</s>:] In <s>śṛṅgāra</s> whose essence is <s>dhvani</s>, [the class of <s>alaṅkāras</s>] placed with discernment,
the group of <s>alaṅkāras</s> beginning with <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), attains its true designation. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.17 //
[Repeated <s>kārikā</s>:] In <s>śṛṅgāra</s> whose essence is <s>dhvani</s>, placed with discernment,
the group of <s>alaṅkāras</s> beginning with <s>rūpaka</s> attains its true designation. // 17 //

children.text:
alaṅkāro he bāhyālaṅkārasāmyādaṅginaścārutvaheturucyate /
vācyālaṅkāravargaśca rūpakādiryāvānukto vakṣyate ca kaiścit, alaṅkārāmāmanantatvāt /
sa sarvo 'pi yadi samīkṣya viniveśyate tadalakṣyakramavyaṅgyasya dhvaneraṅginaḥ sarvasyaiva cārutvaheturniṣpadyate /
eṣā cāsya viniveśane samīkṣā---
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] An <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament) is so called because, by analogy with external ornament, it is the cause of beauty (<s>cārutva</s>) in the principal element (<s>aṅgin</s>). / And the class of expressible <s>alaṅkāras</s> (<s>vācyālaṅkāravarga</s>), namely <s>rūpaka</s> and others — as many as have been stated and will be stated by various [authorities], since <s>alaṅkāras</s> are infinite — / if all of these are placed with discernment (<s>samīkṣya</s>), then they become the cause of beauty for the entire principal element, which is <s>dhvani</s> with imperceptible sequence of suggestion (<s>alakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s>). / And this is the discernment (<s>samīkṣā</s>) in their placement —
[<s>Kārikā</s>:] The intention should be with devotion to that [<s>rasa</s>], never with principality [of the <s>alaṅkāra</s>];
and at the right moment, adoption and abandonment [of <s>alaṅkāras</s>], not desiring excessive elaboration. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.18 //
And even when fully developed, in the state of subsidiarity, careful examination through effort.
[Repeated <s>kārikā</s>:] The intention should be with devotion to that [<s>rasa</s>], never with principality [of the <s>alaṅkāra</s>];
and at the right moment, adoption and abandonment, not desiring excessive elaboration. // 18 //
And even when fully developed, in the state of subsidiarity, careful examination through effort.

children.text:
locanam itānīmiti /
heyavarga uktaḥ, upādeyavargastu vaktavya iti bhāvaḥ /
vyañjaka iti /
yaśca yathā cetyadhyāhāhaḥ /
yathārthatāmiti /
cārutvahetutāmityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Ukta</s>' (stated) — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] by <s>Bhāmaha</s> and other definers of <s>alaṅkāras</s>. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] For the reason stated in '<s>vakṣyate ca</s>' (and will be stated), he gives the cause — 'because <s>alaṅkāras</s> are infinite.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Because creative insight (<s>pratibhā</s>) is infinite, '<s>kaiścid</s>' means 'by some future [authors] as well' — this is the meaning. // 17 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Idānīm</s>' (now) — / the sense is that the class to be rejected (<s>heyavarga</s>) has been stated, and the class to be adopted (<s>upādeyavarga</s>) is yet to be stated. / '<s>Vyañjaka</s>' (suggestive) — / '<s>yaś ca yathā ca</s>' (which and how) should be supplied. / '<s>Yathārthatām</s>' (its true designation) — / the meaning is: the state of being a cause of beauty (<s>cārutvahetutā</s>). /

children.text:
samīkṣyeti /
samīkṣyetyanena śabdena kārikāyāmukteti bhāvaḥ /
ślokapādeṣu caturṣu ślokārdhe cāṅgatvasādhanamidam; rūpakādiriti pratyekaṃ sambandhaḥ /
yamalaṅkāraṃ tadaṅgatayā vivakṣati nāṅgitvena, yamavasare gṛhṇāti, yamavasare tyajati, yaṃ nātyantaṃ nirveḍhumicchati, yaṃ yatnādaṅgatvena pratyavekṣate, sa evamupanibadhyamāno rasābhivyaktiheturbhavatīti vitataṃ mahāvākyam /
tanmahāvākyamadhye codāharamāvakāśamudāhalaraṇasvarūpaṃ tadyojanaṃ tatsamarthanaṃ ca nirūpayituṃ granthāntaramati vṛtigranthasya sambandhaḥ /

children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Yaś ca</s>' (and which) — /

children.text: yo 'laṅkāro yathā vyañjakaḥ, tathā ākhyāyata ityarthaṃ iti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The sense is: whichever <s>alaṅkāra</s>, in whatever manner it is suggestive (<s>vyañjaka</s>), is thus described — this is the meaning. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She shows that the meaning of '<s>yathārthatām</s>' is '<s>anvarthatām</s>' (true to its name) — '<s>cārutva</s>' (beauty) etc. /

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The elaboration of '<s>alaṅkārāṇām anantatvāt kaiścid</s>' (by some, because <s>alaṅkāras</s> are infinite) — '<s>pratibhānantyāt anyaiḥ</s>' (because creative insight is infinite, by others) etc. // 17 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Samīkṣya</s>' (with discernment) — / the sense is that this is stated through the word '<s>samīkṣya</s>' in the <s>kārikā</s>. / In the four quarter-verses and [the additional] half-verse, this is the demonstration of subsidiarity (<s>aṅgatvasādhana</s>); the connection is with each [<s>alaṅkāra</s>] beginning with <s>rūpaka</s>. / Whichever <s>alaṅkāra</s> one intends as subsidiary, not as principal; whichever one adopts at the right occasion and abandons at the right occasion; whichever one does not wish to elaborate excessively; whichever one examines with care as subsidiary — that one, when composed in this manner, becomes the cause of the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> — this is the extended great statement (<s>mahāvākya</s>). / Within that great statement, to set forth the scope of illustration, the nature of the illustrations, their application, and their justification, the connection of another section of text with the <s>vṛtti</s> text [is established]. /

children.text:
'eṣā samīkṣe'ti vṛttāvuktaṃ, samīkṣāyāḥ ko 'tra prastāva ityata āha locane---samīkṣyetyādi /
samīkṣyetyaneneti /
'samīkṣya viniveśita' ityatra samīkṣyaśabdenetyarthaḥ /
kārikādvayasārārthakathanapūrvakaṃ pūrvāparagranthasambandhaṃ darśayati---yamalaṅkāramityādi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In the <s>vṛtti</s> it was said '<s>eṣā samīkṣā</s>' (this is the discernment); as to what occasion there is for [mentioning] discernment, [<s>Abhinavagupta</s>] says in the <s>Locana</s> — '<s>samīkṣya</s>' etc. / '<s>Samīkṣya</s> by this [word]' — the meaning is: by the word '<s>samīkṣya</s>' in '<s>samīkṣya viniveśitaḥ</s>' (placed with discernment). / Having stated the essential meaning of the two <s>kārikās</s>, he shows the connection with the preceding and following text — '<s>yam alaṅkāram</s>' (whichever <s>alaṅkāra</s>) etc. /
[<s>Kārikā</s>:] [This is] the demonstration of subsidiarity (<s>aṅgatvasādhana</s>) of the group of <s>alaṅkāras</s> beginning with <s>rūpaka</s>. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.19 //
[Repeated <s>kārikā</s>:] The demonstration of subsidiarity of the group of <s>alaṅkāras</s> beginning with <s>rūpaka</s>. // 19 //
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] A poet whose mind is highly devoted to <s>rasa</s>-composition intends whichever <s>alaṅkāra</s> as subsidiary to that [<s>rasa</s>]. /

children.text: yathā---- calāpāṅgāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ spṛśasi bahuśo vepathumatīṃ rahasyākhyāyīva svanasi mṛdu karṇāntikacaraḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] For example — You touch again and again with your gaze her whose sidelong glances are restless and trembling; moving near her ear, you hum softly as if whispering a secret;

children.text: karau vyādhunvatyāḥ pibasi ratisarvasvamadharaṃ vayaṃ tattvānveṣānmadhukara hastāstvaṃ khalu kṛtī //
children.translated_text: and from her who shakes her hands [to ward you off], you drink the nectar of her lower lip, the very treasure of love — O bee, we are defeated in our quest for truth, but you are truly accomplished! //

children.text:
atra hi bhramarasvabhāvoktiralaṅkāro rasānuguṇaḥ /
locanam calāpāṅgāmiti /
he madhukara, vayamevaṃvidhābhilāṣacāṭupravaṇā api tattvānveṣamādvastuvṛtte 'nviṣyamāṇe hatā āyāsamātrapātrībhūtā jātāḥ /
tvaṃ khalviti nipātenāyatnasiddhaṃ tataiva caritārthatvamiti śakuntalāṃ pratyabhilāṣiṇo duṣyantasyeyamuktiḥ /
tathāhikathametadīyakaṭākṣagocarā bhūyāsma, kathameṣāsmadabhiprāyavyañjakaṃ rahovacanamākarṇyāt, kathaṃ nu haṭhādanicchantatyā api paricumbanaṃ vidheyāsmeti yadasmākaṃ manorājyapadavīmadhiśete tattavāyatnasiddham /
bhramaro hi nīlotpaladhiyā tadāśaṅkākarīṃ dṛṣṭiṃ punaḥpunaḥ spṛśati /
śravaṇāvakāśaparyantatvācca netrayorutpalaśaṅkānapagamāttatraiva dandhvanyamāna āste /
sahajasaukumāryatrāsakātarāyāśca ratinidhānabhūtaṃ vikasitāravindakuvalayāmodamadhuramadharaṃ pibatīti bhramarasvabhāvoktiralaṅkāro 'ṅgatāmeva prakṛtarasasyopagataḥ /
anye tu bhramarasvabhāve bālapriyā calāpāṅgāmiti /
śloko 'yamasmābhiḥ śākuntalavyākhyāyāṃ savistaraṃ vyākhyātaḥ /
vayamityanena gamyamarthamāha--evamityādi /
evaṃvidhāḥ vakṣyamāṇāḥ abhilāṣā yeṣāṃ te /
cāṭau cāṭuvacane pravaṇāstatparāśca /
ayatnetyādi vyaṅgyārthakathanam /
'katham' ityādi 'siddham' ityantaṃ duṣyantavacanarūpema nirdiṣṭam /
bhramaro hītyādivyākhyāturvacanam /
tatraiva śravaṇāvakāśe eva /
dandhvanyamāna iti /
atiśayena dhvaniṃ kurvannityarthaḥ /
'bhramarasvabhāvoktiri'tyādigranthamarthato vyacaṣṭe---iti bhramarasvabhāvoktirityādi /
samāsoktivyatirekayoḥ satve 'pyatra svabhāvokteḥ purasphūrtikatvāttanmātramuktam /
prakṛtarasasyeti /
vipralambhasyetyarathaḥ /
aṅgatāmevopagata iti /

children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Na aṅgitvena</s>' — not as principal. /

children.text: kadācidrasāditātparyeṇa vivakṣito 'pi hmalaṅkāraḥ kaścidaṅgitvena vivakṣito dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] Sometimes an <s>alaṅkāra</s>, even when intended with the purport of <s>rasa</s> etc., is seen to be intended as principal by someone. /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] For example: 'He who, by the mere peremptory command of the discus-blow, rendered the love-festival of <s>Rāhu</s>'s wives
barren of the dalliance whose chief delight was the embrace, leaving only kissing as its remainder.'

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Here indeed, the <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) of the bee's nature is an <s>alaṅkāra</s> consonant with <s>rasa</s>. / [<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Calāpāṅgām</s>' (she whose sidelong glances are restless) etc. — / O bee! We, though inclined toward such desires and flattering words, are defeated (<s>hatāḥ</s>) in our quest for truth — when the reality is investigated, we have become mere vessels of exertion. / By the particle '<s>khalu</s>' in '<s>tvaṃ khalu</s>' (you indeed), effortless accomplishment from that very [activity] is [indicated] — and the fulfillment of purpose is [suggested]. This is the utterance of <s>Duṣyanta</s> who is desirous toward <s>Śakuntalā</s>. / For thus [is the meaning]: 'How may we come within the range of her sidelong glances? How may she hear our secret words that express our intention? How indeed may we accomplish a kiss even of one who resists?' — that which occupies the path of our daydreams is effortlessly accomplished for you. / For the bee, thinking the [eye to be] a blue lotus, touches again and again the glance that arouses suspicion [of being a flower]. / And because the range of hearing extends to the vicinity of the ears, when the suspicion of [the eye being] a lotus is not dispelled, [the bee] stays right there humming. / And of her who is frightened by natural delicacy, [the bee] drinks the lower lip — sweet with the fragrance of blossoming lotus and water-lily, the repository of love's pleasure — thus the <s>alaṅkāra</s> of <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) of the bee's behavior has assumed subsidiarity to the <s>rasa</s> at hand. / Others, however, [take it as] the bee's natural behavior. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Calāpāṅgām</s>' etc. — / This verse has been explained by us in detail in the commentary on the <s>Śākuntala</s>. / She states the meaning conveyed by '<s>vayam</s>' (we) — '<s>evam</s>' etc.: / '<s>evaṃvidhāḥ</s>' means 'of the kind to be described'; '<s>abhilāṣāḥ</s>' (desires) are those whose; '<s>cāṭu</s>' means flattering speech, '<s>pravaṇāḥ</s>' means devoted to that. / '<s>Ayatna</s>' etc. — this is the statement of the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgyārtha</s>). / From '<s>katham</s>' to '<s>siddham</s>' is presented in the form of <s>Duṣyanta</s>'s speech. / '<s>Bhramaro hi</s>' etc. is the commentator's [explanatory] statement. / '<s>Tatraiva</s>' — in the vicinity of the ear itself. / '<s>Dandhvanyamānaḥ</s>' — the meaning is: making sound (<s>dhvani</s>) excessively. / She explains the purport of the passage beginning '<s>bhramarasvabhāvoktiḥ</s>' — '<s>iti bhramarasvabhāvoktiḥ</s>' etc. / Although <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) and <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) are also present here, because <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) is what first springs forth, only that is mentioned. / '<s>Prakṛtarasasya</s>' — the meaning is: of <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation). / '<s>Aṅgatām eva upagataḥ</s>' (has assumed subsidiarity alone) — /

children.translated_text: extending its own languor through incessant exhalations of breeze — this amorous one, seeing her now as if another woman surely,

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] For here the intention is the principal status (<s>aṅgitva</s>) of <s>paryāyokta</s> (indirect expression), even when <s>rasa</s> etc. is the purport. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Whose utterance is such' — they say: 'Here there is <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) of the bee, [and also] <s>rūpaka-vyatireka</s> (metaphor-contrast).' /
The blow of the discus (<s>cakra</s>) itself is the peremptory command (<s>prasabhājñā</s>) — the inviolable injunction; by that [injunction], he who rendered the love-festival of <s>Rāhu</s>'s beloved women such that only kissing remained. /
Because the embrace — the chief, i.e., principal element — in those dalliances was [rendered] barren, i.e., empty — such was the love-festival. /
Here someone says: '<s>Paryāyokta</s> alone is what the poet primarily intended here, not <s>rasa</s> etc.' /
'Then how is it said "even when <s>rasa</s> etc. is the purport"?' /
Not so; for the glory of <s>Vāsudeva</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) is what is intended here. /
And it [<s>vīra-rasa</s>] does not shine here as the cause of beauty; rather, <s>paryāyokta</s> alone [serves that function]. /
Although in this poem there is no suspicion of any fault, nevertheless this serves as an illustration — [showing] that even when it is subsidiary, a figure (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) can obscure the essential nature of the principal subject (<s>prakṛta</s>) that is to be nourished. /
And from that, inappropriateness (<s>anaucitya</s>) sometimes arises — this is the treatise-author's intent. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Because such behavior of the bee is an exciter of passion' — this is the purport. /
'<s>Rūpaka</s>' — /
'<s>Rūpaka-vyatireka</s>' — a <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) combined with <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor); in the bee, there is <s>rūpaka</s> through the superimposition of hero-status; and in the fourth quarter, <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). /
In reality, it is not <s>rūpaka</s> here but <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) — with the intent of signaling awkwardness [in the rival interpretation], [he says] 'some.' /
The gloss of the <s>vṛtti</s>'s '<s>aṅgitva</s>' (principal status) is: '<s>prādhānya</s>' (predominance). /
'<s>Kadācit</s>' — /
'In some poem' — this is the meaning. /
In the <s>Locana</s>: '<s>cakra</s>' etc. — /
'<s>Cakrābhighāta</s>' — the striking all around by the discus — that itself [is the peremptory command]. /
'Not <s>rasa</s> etc.' — /
The continuation is with '<s>prādhānyena vivakṣitam</s>' (primarily intended). /
'<s>Rasādi-tātparye saty api</s>' — this is a restatement of the <s>vṛtti</s>. /
He responds: '<s>maivam</s>' etc. /
'Intended' — /
'Primarily' is the remainder. /
And thus the purport is: the purport of <s>vīra-rasa</s> exists here. /
He states the specific point: '<s>sa ca</s>' etc. /
'Rather, <s>paryāyokta</s> alone' — /
The continuation is with '<s>cārutva-hetutayā cakāsti</s>' (shines as the cause of beauty). /
He raises a doubt: '<s>yadyapi</s>' etc. /
'No suspicion of fault whatsoever' — /
'Nothing that would obstruct aesthetic wonder is to be suspected' — this is the meaning. /
And thus the purport is: even when <s>paryāyokta</s> has predominance, no harm [results]. /
He resolves: '<s>tathāpi</s>' etc. /
'Like an illustration' — /
'Equivalent to an illustration' — this is the meaning. /
'This' — /
'The example beginning with "<s>cakra</s>"' — this is the meaning. /
He elaborates the purport: '<s>yat</s>' etc. /
'If, even being subsidiary, a figure obscures the essential nature of the principal subject that is to be nourished' — this is the syntactic connection. /
'In some cases' is the remainder. /
Therein the illustration is the present verse — this is the purport. /
'What follows from that?' — to this he says: '<s>tataś ca</s>' etc. /
'Inappropriateness sometimes [arises]' — /
The example of this — '<s>srastaḥ sragdāmaśobhā</s>' etc. — was cited at the beginning of the <s>Kāvyānuśāsana</s>. /

Here, the <s>upamā-śleṣa</s> (simile-punning), through its role as a path-clearer for the impending <s>īrṣyā-vipralambha</s> (jealous love-in-separation) of the <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), stands promoting the orientation toward savoring it — [being] grasped at the occasion, at the threshold of the <s>rasa</s>'s coming to prominence as a precursor. /

'<s>Uddāma</s>' — /
This is from the play <s>Ratnāvalī</s>. /
This is the speech of <s>Vatsarāja</s> to his jester-companion, upon discovering that his own <s>Navamālikā</s> creeper had blossomed through a special longing (<s>dohada</s>). /
'Today, seeing this garden-creeper as if another woman, I shall make the face of the queen blaze with the radiance of anger' — this is the syntactic connection. /
'When I am looking at my own creeper blossoming [as if it were] another woman, the face of <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, who is jealous because of the absence of blossoming of her own <s>Mādhavī</s> creeper, will become reddened with anger — I shall make it so' — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Dhruvam</s>' (surely) — in the sense of certainty. /
Considering the second half to be clear in meaning, he explains the first half: '<s>uddāmā</s>' etc. /

'<s>Īrṣyā</s>' — /
'Of jealousy arising from <s>Vāsavadattā</s>' — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Bhāvinaḥ</s>' — /
'That which is about to be elaborated at the end of the second act' — this is the meaning. /

He instructs regarding acting: '<s>abhinaya</s>' etc. /

children.translated_text: 'Of another form' (anyarupa) — by this, the dissimilarity (vaidharmya) of the radiance has been shown; what is said by 'no kalpa' etc. is stated [to establish that].
'With relentless force' (adayaraya) — with vigorous velocity; that which shatters mountains (ksmadharah).

children.text: vāyoriti kartari ṣaṣṭī gāḍhamudgīrṇā gāḍhodgīrṇojjvalaśrīrahani na rahitā no tamaḥkajjalena /
children.translated_text: 'Of the wind' (vayoh) — the sixth case is in the agentive sense. 'Intensely blazing splendor' (gadham udgirna ujjvala srih) — not devoid (na rahita) of that even during the day (ahani); 'not [even by] the soot of darkness (tamah-kajjalena).'

children.text: prāptotpattiḥ pataṅgānna punarupagatā moṣamuṣṇātviṣo vo vartiḥ saivānyarūpā sukhayatu nikhiladvīpadīpasya dīptiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Having attained the origination of moths (patanga), but not having obtained destruction (mosa) by the hot-rayed one (usnatvisa, the Sun) — may that very wick (varti), of another form, the radiance of the lamp of all islands (nikhila-dvipa-dipa) — give you happiness!'

[Locana:] But through sentence-meaning acting (vakyartha-abhinaya) by means of subsidiary gestures (upanga) etc.
Not that there is no acting at all — without some means [it would be impossible].
And the word 'dhruva' (fixed/constant) refers to the provision of occasion for the emotion of jealousy (irsya) that is about to arise.
'Rakta' (colored/red) — crimson.
'I too am rakta (colored/impassioned)' — with awakened love.
And therein, the awakener as vibhava (determinant) should be understood as the redness of her sallava (the asoka's blossom).
Thus, in each quarter-verse, the primary meaning should be explained as a vibhava (determinant).
Hence this is a hetu-slesa (causal paronomasia).
For in the case of sahokti (co-expression), upama (simile), and hetu (cause) figures, there is predominantly the support of slesa (paronomasia).
With this very intention —
[Balapriya:] 'By subsidiary gestures etc.' — 'acting' (abhinaya) carries over.
'With awakened love' — 'I am enamored by the qualities of my beloved, with awakened love' — the meaning through the principle of tantra (single utterance for multiple meanings): this is the purport.
'What is the awakener?' — here the commentator says: 'therein' etc.
'Vibhava' — the meaning is: excitant vibhava (uddipana-vibhava).
'Its' (tadiya) — the meaning is: belonging to the asoka tree.
'In each quarter-verse' — the meaning is: in the second and third quarter-verses.
'As vibhava' — the meaning is: as excitant vibhava.
'Should be explained' — since bees (silimukha, lit. 'sharp-faced') released from the bow of Smara (Kama, the god of love), i.e., arrows discharged from Kama's bow, come to you, therefore to me too, similarly, arrows (silimukha) released from the bow of Smara, i.e., discharged from Kama's bow, come.
'Kante' (O beloved) etc. — although here the strike of the beloved's foot-sole serves for your delight, i.e., for the blossoming of flowers, in the same way the strike of the beloved's foot-sole — a particular mode of lovemaking (ratabandha-visesa) — serves for my delight, i.e., for my satisfaction — this is the literal meaning; nevertheless, since when the asoka blooms through the strike of his own beloved's foot-sole, the hero's satisfaction arises — 'for your delight' means 'for my delight too' — this should be explained as a causal relationship: this is the purport.
For here, even though the slesa (paronomasia) extends through the composition, when it is abandoned with the intent of expressing vyatireka (contrast), it nourishes a particular rasa.
There is no convergence of two figures here — rather, it is itself another figure, characterized by the combination of slesa and vyatireka, like Narasimha (man-lion) — if so objected: no; because that [sankara] is established in a different manner.
For where, in the very word that is the domain of slesa, the cognition of vyatireka arises through another mode — that is the domain of that [sankara].
For example — 'He is Hari by name, a god; he is sahari (accompanied by horses), with a host of excellent steeds' etc.
[Locana:] Bhamaha formulated — 'that [slesa], being of three kinds, through the specification of sahokti, upama, and hetu' — by this statement, not with the intention of denying its support of other figures.
'A particular rasa' — vipralambha (love-in-separation).
'By the word sasoka (with grief/with asoka)' — by the one who brings in vyatireka (contrast), the occasion has been given for the transitory emotions (vyabhicarin) such as despondency (nirveda), anxiety (cinta), etc. that are co-present with grief (soka) and that nourish vipralambha.
'What then?' — this is a single sankara-alankara (combination figure); therein, what is abandoned and what is grasped? — this is the opponent's intention.
'Of that' — of the sankara.
For in one domain, the flash of the cognition of two figures is sankara (combination).
The word 'sahari' is one domain.
'Sa harih' — he is Hari; or 'saha haribhih' — together with horses, hence 'sahari.'
[Balapriya:] 'Hetu-slesa' — a slesa (paronomasia) combined with the hetu (cause) figure: this is the meaning.
He substantiates what was stated — 'sahokti' etc.
'With this very [intention]' — with the very intention of the predominantly supporting nature of slesa: this is the meaning.
'By this statement, he formulated' — this is the syntactic connection.
'Tat-sahokti' — 'tat' [means] the paronomastic utterance (slista-vacah).
'By this eva-particle' — he states what is excluded — 'not, however' etc.
The abandonment of a previously grasped figure through the intent of expressing another figure conducive to the rasa at hand is a limb (anga) of the rasa at hand — with this [intention], he elaborates the nourishing capacity of vyatireka for vipralambha in the present context — 'by the word sasoka' etc.
'Bringing in vyatireka' — the meaning is: showing the speaker's contrast with the asoka tree.
'Occasion has been given' — the meaning is: the abiding [of those transitory emotions] has been shown.
In the vrtti, 'slesa' — the meaning is: slesa-upama (paronomastic simile).
'There is not' etc. up to 'if so objected' — this is the objection passage.
Therein, he states the purport of 'what then?' — 'sankara' etc.
'Sankara' — the meaning is: sankara of the single-sentence-entry type (ekavakyaanupravesa-sankara).
In the vrtti, he resolves — 'no' etc.
He shows precisely the establishment through another mode — 'where' etc.
He states the purport — 'in one [domain]' etc.
'Of the figures' — the meaning is: the flash (ullasa), i.e., arising, of the cognition of two figures.
'Sankara' — sankara of the single-sentence-entry type.
'Sa harih' — description of a king.
'Although of incomparable deeds, nevertheless Acyuta does not attain your equal' — this is the first half.
Here he shows the single-domain-ness — 'sa hari' etc.
'Domain' — the remainder is: of slesa and vyatireka.
'Sahari by name' — therein, 'sa hari' is two words — he says: 'sah harih.'
'Sah' — Acyuta.
'By name, hari' — named Hari: this is the meaning.
Since the word 'hari' meaning 'horse' is compounded with 'saha' — with this intention, he explains the second word 'sahari' — 'or alternatively' etc.
'Or alternatively' — 'and moreover': this is the meaning, since particles have multiple senses.
Or — 'yadi va' is a variant reading.
'With horses' (haribhih) — with horses.
'With a host' (nivahena) — the instrumental is either causal or in the sense of identity.
In the last quarter-verse, here indeed one word is the domain of slesa and another of vyatireka.
And if in such a domain, the fabrication of being another figure [were proposed], that would amount to the theft of the domain of samsrsti (conjunction of figures).
'The attainment of vyatireka's own nature is through the very medium of slesa — hence this is not a domain of samsrsti' — if so objected: no; because vyatireka is seen in other modes too.
For example — [the verse beginning with] 'no kalpa' etc.
[Locana:] 'Here indeed' (atra hi) — the word 'hi' is in the sense of 'tu' (but); the meaning is: 'but you are rakta (red/impassioned)' etc.
'Another' — 'rakta' etc.
'And another' — 'asoka-sasoka' etc.
'Now, taking the sentence-form domain as single, let there be sankara because of single-domain-ness!' — anticipating this objection, he says: 'if' etc.
'Of such a sentence-characterized domain' — the word 'domain' should be understood as intending singleness.
'If singleness of domain is stated with reference to a single sentence, then nowhere would there be samsrsti (conjunction), because it would be pervaded by sankara (combination).'
'Now, vyatireka is pregnant with upama; and the upama comes through the very medium of slesa — hence slesa here is the supporter of vyatireka, and so this is a domain of sankara alone.'
'But where the relation of supporter and supported does not exist, even when [the figures] enter a single sentence, it is precisely samsrsti (conjunction)' — thus he says: 'slesa' etc.
'Through upama brought about by the power of slesa' — this is the meaning.
He refutes this — 'no' etc.
This is the purport: does vyatireka arise in all cases when upama is expressed by its own word [i.e., an explicit simile-word], or [also] when it is implied?
He refutes the first alternative — 'in another mode' etc.
'Without the expression of upama' — this is the meaning.
'Samya' — means 'capable of quenching': this is the meaning.
A lamp-wick, however, can be quenched by mere wind.
[Balapriya:] 'You' is the remainder.
'Deva' — this is a qualifier for both [the lamp and the king/sun].
Although here two [words] 'saharih' and 'saharih' have been taken up, nevertheless since they form a single sequence (ekanupurvinkatva), they constitute a single domain: this is the purport.
He explains the words in the vrtti from another quarter-verse — 'rakta' etc.
'Of sentence-characterized' — of sentence-form.
Showing the result of intending singleness, he elaborates the vrtti-meaning of 'tad' etc. — 'of a single sentence' etc.
'This is a domain of sankara alone' — of sankara in the sense of supporter-supported relation.
'There is no theft of samsrsti's domain' — he says: 'but where' etc.
'Thus he says' — the meaning is: he shows this very objection.
'No' etc. — he shows the purport of the refutation passage — 'this [is the purport]' etc.
'What?' (kim) — interrogative.
'When implied' — when suggested (vyangya).
'Without the expression of upama' — without a word denoting simile.
'No kalpa' etc. — this is from the Suryasataka.
'Of usnatvisah' — of the Sun itself.
'The radiance (dipti) of the lamp of all islands (nikhila-dvipa-dipa) is of another form (anyarupa)' — that well-known wick (varti) — may it give you happiness: this is the syntactic connection.
