children.translated_text: The perception of beauty from mere <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) exists — therefore, since <s>śleṣa</s> is intended only as a subordinate element of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), its independent <s>alaṅkāra</s> status also should not be denied.

children.text: yata evaṃvide viṣaye sāmyamātrādapi supratipāditāccārutvaṃ dṛśyata eva /
children.translated_text: Because in such a subject, beauty is seen even from mere <s>sāmya</s> (similarity) that has been well demonstrated.

As for example: 'My cries [are equal] to your thunderings, the tears of [my] eyes to [your] ceaseless rain-showers, and the fires of grief born of separation from him [are equal] to the flashes of your lightning —

children.text: antarme dayitāmukhaṃ tava śaśī vṛttiḥ samaivāvayo- statkiṃ māmaniśaṃ sakhe jaladhara tvaṃ dagdhamevodyataḥ //
children.translated_text: within me is the face of my beloved, and for you [there is] the moon; the course of our two [lives] is exactly the same — then why, O friend cloud, are you determined to burn me ceaselessly?'

Here indeed, <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) has been shown without the elaboration of the demonstration of <s>sāmya</s> (similarity). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Not here' — darkness is itself collyrium; by that — /
not 'devoid of,' but rather 'devoid indeed.' /
But the lamp-wick is associated even with darkness. /
Because [collyrium] is extremely imperceptible, 'we would apply collyrium' — /
[the moth comes] from the sun (<s>pataṅga</s>). /
But the lamp-wick is destroyed by the moth, not produced [by it]. /
'Similarity' etc. — /
The meaning is: even without the demonstration (<s>pratipādana</s>) of <s>sāmya</s> (similarity, i.e., <s>upamā</s>) through elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>), i.e., through extended description, by its own word [i.e., without explicitly naming it]. /
The purport of this is: the merely suggested <s>upamā</s> (simile) alone is the supporter of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), and does not require expression in its own words. /
Therefore, the <s>śleṣopamā</s> (simile-through-pun) has not been employed as a supporter of <s>vyatireka</s>. /
Objection: even if elsewhere this is not so, nevertheless here it has been employed precisely because of the predominance of that [śleṣa]; without that predominance, since there would be no basis for beauty on its own — therefore, <s>śleṣopamā</s> does not attain the status of a separate <s>alaṅkāra</s> at all. /
To this he says — 'not here' etc. /
Holding in his heart [the thought] 'this is unestablished, because it is contradicted by direct experience,' the <s>Bālapriyā</s> was brought forth, denying [the objector's] direct experience — she whose radiance is brilliant. /
He shows the dissimilarity of the wick with respect to what is to be understood — 'lamp-wick' etc. /
'Darkness and collyrium are darkness-collyrium' — with the intention of [treating them as] a compound, he says: 'even with darkness' etc. /
The construction is: 'we would apply collyrium, and [the wick] is associated [with darkness].' /
The indication of being associated with both [darkness and collyrium]. /
'Because of extreme imperceptibility' etc. /
The birth obtained from the moth (<s>pataṅga</s>) — the wick does not undergo destruction from the moth but is not produced [by it] — here he states the dissimilarity residing in the wick — 'from the moth' etc. /
'<s>Pataṅga</s> [means] sun and moth' — [says] <s>Amara</s>. /
Thus it should also be understood that the lamp-wick is dim in radiance during the day. /
'Demonstration by its own word' — this is the connection. /
He states the purport — 'the purport of this' etc. /
'Supporter' — /
The purport is: because <s>vyatireka</s> has <s>upamā</s> as its core. /
'In its own words' — by its own expression. /
'Employed' — expressed in its own words. /
'Objection' etc. /
'Elsewhere' — the meaning is: in [passages like] 'not when imagination ceases' etc. /
'Here' — the meaning is: in [the verse beginning] 'you are tinged' etc. /
'Predominance of that' — meaning predominance toward <s>vyatireka</s>, i.e., supportiveness of <s>vyatireka</s>. /
'Of that itself' — the meaning is: of itself. /
'<s>Iti</s>' in the causal sense. /
'Here' — in [the verse] 'you are tinged' etc. /
'Separate' etc. — /
The construction is: does not attain the status of a separate <s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
But rather, together with <s>vyatireka</s>, it attains the relation of supporter and supported — this is the purport. /
'To this he says' — /
By the passage beginning with 'not here,' he presents that objection — this is the meaning. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>: 'here, since <s>śleṣa</s>'s being intended only as a subordinate element of <s>vyatireka</s>, the perception of beauty from <s>śleṣa</s> alone does not exist — therefore its independent <s>alaṅkāra</s> status also should not be asserted' — this is the construction. /
The connection of 'of <s>śleṣa</s>' is also with 'not independent <s>alaṅkāra</s> status.' /
'Independently' means 'separately.' /
In the <s>Locana</s>: 'this' etc. — /
This — what was objected. /
'Direct experience' — meaning one's own experience. /
The opponent — the former objector. /
The connection is with 'silences.' /

children.text:
ityādau /
locanam paraṃ śleṣaṃ vinopamāmātrema cārutvasampannamudāharaṇāntaraṃ darśayanniruttarīkaroti--yata ityādinā /
udāharaṇaśloke tṛtīyāntapadeṣu tulyaśabdo 'bhisambandhanīyaḥ /
anyatsarvaṃ 'raktastvaṃ' itivadyojyam /
bālapriyā kathamityatrāha--śleṣamityādi /
śleṣaṃ vinā upamāmātreṇeti /
mātrapadārthavivaraṇaṃ śleṣaṃ vineti /
śleṣarahitopramāgarbhavyatirekemeti yāvat /
vṛttau--'evam' ityādi /
'evaṃvide viṣaye' vyatirekaviṣaye /
'sāmyamātrādi'ti /
mātraśabdena śleṣavyavacchedaḥ sāmyaśabdasyopamāgarbhavyatireko 'rthaḥ /
'ākrandā' ityādisthale śleṣaṃ vinā upamāgarbhavyatirekeṇaiva cārutvasya darśanā'draktastva'mityādāvapi śleṣasya vyatirekānugrāhakatvaṃ vinā pṛthagalaṅkāratvaṃ bhavatyeveti parihāragranthābhiprāyaḥ /
anena prabandhapravṛtto 'pītyādi pūrvoktaṃ nirvyūḍham /
tulyaśabda it /
me ākrandāḥ tava stanitaitaistulyā ityādi sambandhanīyamityarthaḥ /
śrotṛjanamanaḥkṣobhakāritvādinā tulyatvam /
tasyāvicchedo virahaḥ tasmādbhavantīti tathā /
śokā eva śikhino 'gnayaḥ /
'antari'tyādi /
atra mukhaśaśinostulyatvaṃ gamyam /
'vṛttiri'tyādi /
uktaprakāreṇāvayordharmau tulyāvevetyarthaḥ /
'tadi'ti /
asmaddharmayostulyatvenāvayostulyatvādityarthaḥ /
ata evāha---'sakhe' iti /
anena dahanamanucitamanukūlācaraṇameva yuktamiti, 'jaladhare'tyanena santāpaharaṇasāmarthyaṃ ca dyotyate /
aniśaṃ dagdhuṃ pīḍayitumeva, na tu kadācitsukhayitumapi /
'kiṃ' kutaḥ /
'udyataḥ' ayamudyamo na yuktaḥ, ahantu naivaṃvidha iti bhāvaḥ /
atra bandhujanapīḍākāritvena jaladharasya svasmādvyatireka uktaḥ, sāmyaṃ cādāvuktam /
śleṣaśca nāstīti bodhyam /
yojayamiti /
stanitādikamākrandanādihetutayāpi yojanīyamityarthaḥ /
vṛttau---'ākṣiptam' iti /
uktamityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'For the nourishment of <s>rasa</s>' — and it has been resolved — this is the construction.
[The heart] whose sole purpose is the sustaining of <s>rasa</s> — that [<s>alaṅkāra</s>] which it does not wish to fully develop (<s>nirvāhayitum</s>) —

children.text: yathā--- kopātkomalalobāhulatikāpāśena baddhvā dṛḍhaṃ nītvā vāsaniketanaṃ dayitayā sāyaṃ sakhīnāṃ puraḥ /
children.translated_text: As for example: 'Having bound [him] firmly with the creeper-noose of [her] tender, soft arms out of anger, having led [him] to the bedroom, in the evening, before [her] friends, the beloved —

children.text: bhūyo naivamiti skhalatkalagirā saṃsūcya duśceṣṭitaṃ dhanyo hanyata eva ninhutiparaḥ preyānrudatyā hasan //
children.translated_text: declaring the misdeed with faltering, sweet words: "never again like this!" — the blessed lover, intent on denial, is beaten indeed by [his] weeping [beloved] as he laughs.'

[<s>Locana</s>:] In this and similar [passages]. /
Showing another example, replete with beauty through mere <s>upamā</s> (simile) without <s>śleṣa</s> (pun), he silences the opponent — with 'because' etc. /
In the example verse, the word '<s>tulya</s>' (equal) should be connected with the words ending in the instrumental case. /
Everything else should be construed as in 'you are tinged' etc. /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: To the question 'how?', he says — '<s>śleṣam</s>' etc. — /
'Through mere <s>upamā</s> without <s>śleṣa</s>' — /
'Mere' is explained by 'without <s>śleṣa</s>.' /
The meaning is: through <s>upamā</s>-cored <s>vyatireka</s> devoid of <s>śleṣa</s>. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>: 'thus' etc. — /
'In such a subject' — in the subject of <s>vyatireka</s>. /
'From mere <s>sāmya</s>' etc. — /
By the word 'mere' (<s>mātra</s>), the exclusion of <s>śleṣa</s>; the meaning of the word '<s>sāmya</s>' (similarity) is <s>upamā</s>-cored <s>vyatireka</s>. /
In the passage 'cries' etc., since beauty is seen through <s>vyatireka</s> with <s>upamā</s>-core without <s>śleṣa</s>, even in 'you are tinged' etc. the resolution is that <s>śleṣa</s> does not have independent <s>alaṅkāra</s> status apart from its supportiveness of <s>vyatireka</s> — this is the purport of the resolution passage. /
By this, what was previously stated with 'even proceeding through extended [description]' etc. has been resolved. /
'The word <s>tulya</s>' etc. — /
The meaning is: 'my cries are equal to your thunderings' etc. should be connected. /
'Of listeners, producing agitation of the mind' etc. — the equality [is thus]. /
The uninterrupted continuation of that is separation (<s>virahas</s>); [the fires of grief] arise from that — thus so described. /
The fires of grief are indeed fires (<s>śikhin</s>). /
'Within' etc. — /
Here the equality of the face and the moon is to be understood. /
'The course' etc. — /
The meaning is: the attributes of both of us are exactly equal, in the manner described. /
'Therefore' — /
The meaning is: since the attributes of both of us are equal, [we are] of equal nature. /
For this very reason he says 'friend' (<s>sakhe</s>). /
By this, the burning is shown as inappropriate, and friendly conduct alone as fitting. By '<s>jaladhara</s>' (cloud, lit. water-bearer), the capacity for removing heat is also suggested. /
'Ceaselessly to burn' — to torment; but never even to gladden. /
'Why' — from what cause? /
'Determined' — this determination is not fitting; I am not of such a nature — this is the purport. /
Here, the <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) of the cloud from oneself has been stated through its causing suffering to loved ones; and the similarity was stated at the beginning. /
And <s>śleṣa</s> is absent — this should be understood.

children.text:
atra he rūpakamākṣiptamanirvyūḍhaṃ ca paraṃ rasapuṣṭaye /
nirvoḍhumiṣṭamapi yaṃ yatnādaṅgatvena pratyavekṣate yathā--- śyāmāsvaṅgaṃ cakitahariṇīprekṣaṇe dṛṣṭipātaṃ locanam evaṃ grahaṇatyāgau samarthya 'nātinirvahaṇaiṣitā' iti bhāgaṃ vyācaṣṭe--raseti /
cakāraḥ samīkṣāprakārasamuccārthaḥ /
bāhulatikāyāḥ bandhanīyapāśatvena rūpaṇaṃ yadi nirvāhayet, dayitā vyādhavadhūḥ vāsagṛhaṃ kārāgārapañjarādīti paramanaucityaṃ syāt /
sakhīnāṃ pura iti /
bhavatyo 'navarataṃ bruvate nāyamevaṃ karotīti tatpaśyantvidānīmiti bhāvaḥ /
skhalantī kopāveśena kalā madhurā ca gīryasyāḥ sā /
kāsau gīrityāha--bhūyo naivamityevaṃrūpā /
evamiti yaduktaṃ tatkimityāha--duśceṣṭitaṃ nakhapadāda saṃsūcya aṅgulyādinirdeśena /
inyata eveti /
na tu sakhyādikṛto 'nunayo 'nurudhyate /
yato 'sau hasanaṃ nimittīkṛtya nihnutiparaḥ priyatamaśca tadīyaṃ vyalīlaṃ kā soḍhuṃ samartheti /
nirvoḍhumiti /
niḥśeṣeṇa parisamāpayitumityarthaḥ /
śyāmāsu sugandhipriyaṅgulatāsu bālapriyā etadvivṛṇoti locane---bāhvityādi /
iti nirvāhayedyadīti sambandhaḥ /
dayitādīnāṃ vyādhavadhūtvādirūpaṇasya kathanena bāhulatikāyāḥ pāśatvarūpaṇaṃ kavirnirvāhayedyadītyarthaḥ /
tadeti śeṣaḥ /
paramanaucityaṃ syāditi /
tathā ca rasabhaṅgaḥ syāditi bhāvaḥ /
na karotīti bruvata ityanena sambandhaḥ /
iti bhāva iti /
sakhīnāṃ puronayane nāyikābhiprāya ityarthaḥ /
sakhīnāṃ puro nītvetyanenoktābhiprāyo gamyata ityarthaḥ /
duśceṣṭitamityasya vyākhyānam---nakhapadādīti /
'nirdeśena saṃsūcye'tyanvayaḥ /
evakārārthamāha---na tvityādi /
nihnutītyādikamuktārthe hetugarbhamityāśayena vyācaṣṭe---yata ityādi /
bhāvārthamāha---tadīyamityādi tadīyaṃ prayatamasambandhi /
ato hanyata eveti bhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: This verse is from the <s>Amaruśataka</s>.
The verse beginning with '<s>śyāmā</s>' etc. is from the <s>Meghasandeśa</s>.

children.text: śyāmānāṃ viśiṣyoktau bījabhūtamaṅgasāthadharmyaṃ gaṇḍacchāyāṃ śaśini śikhināṃ barhabhāreṣu keśān /
children.translated_text: [I see] the likeness of [your] cheek's glow in the moon, [your] hair in the plume-burdens of peacocks, the special quality of [your] form in dark-complexioned [<s>priyangu</s> creepers],

children.text: atpaśyāmi pratanuṣu nadīvīciṣu bhrūvilāsān hantaikasthaṃ kvacidapi na te bhīru sādṛśyamasti //
children.translated_text: [your] brow-play in the slender waves of rivers — alas, O timid one, nowhere does your complete likeness exist in any single [object]!

Here, oh! — <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) has been suggested but not fully developed, and it is for the nourishment of <s>rasa</s>. /
That [<s>alaṅkāra</s>] which one wishes to develop, yet carefully regards as merely subsidiary — as in: '[seeing] a form in dark-complexioned women, a glance in the gaze of a startled doe —' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Thus, weighing acceptance and rejection, he explains the passage 'not excessively wishing to develop' — '<s>rasa</s>' etc. /
The word '<s>ca</s>' is for the cumulation of modes of consideration. /
The <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) of the arm-creeper as a noose for binding — if one were to fully develop it, [then] the beloved [would become] a huntress, the bedroom a cage-prison — and there would be extreme impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>). /
'Before the friends' — /
The purport is: 'you constantly say he does not do this — now see for yourselves!' /
She whose speech is faltering due to the intensity of anger, and [yet] sweet — she is [described thus]. /
'What sort of speech?' — to this he says: 'never again like this' — of this form. /
'Like this' — what is referred to [by this word]? To this he says: 'the misdeed' — nail-marks etc. — 'declaring by pointing with finger' etc. /
'Is beaten indeed' — /
And the appeasement by friends etc. is not heeded. /
Because he, taking [her] laughter as pretext, is intent on denial, and [she is] his dearest one — who is capable of enduring her dissembling? /
'To develop' — the meaning is: to fully bring to completion. /
'[Seeing] in dark-complexioned women' — [seeing] in fragrant <s>priyangu</s> creepers. /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: He elaborates this in the <s>Locana</s> — 'arm' etc. /
The connection is: 'if one were to develop that [metaphor], then...' /
By the statement of the beloved etc. being [metaphorically] a huntress etc., [the implication is that] the rūpaṇa of the arm-creeper as a noose could be developed by the poet if he wished — this is the meaning. /
'That' is the remainder. /
'There would be extreme impropriety' — /
The purport is: and thus there would be the destruction of <s>rasa</s>. /
'Does not do this' — the connection is: as the friends say. /
'This is the purport' — /
The meaning is: the intention of the heroine in bringing [him] before the friends. /
'Having been led before the friends' — the intention understood from this [action] is as stated — this is the meaning. /
The explanation of '<s>duśceṣṭita</s>' (misdeed) — 'nail-marks' etc. /
'By pointing, declaring' — the construction. /
The meaning of the '<s>eva</s>' particle he states — 'not' etc. /
'Denial' etc. — what is in the form of an [objector's] statement is explained with an implied reason — 'because' etc. /
He states the purport — 'his' etc. — 'his' meaning belonging to the beloved. /
Therefore 'is beaten indeed' — this is the purport.

children.text:
ityādau /
sa evamupanibadhyamāno 'laṅkāro rasābhivyaktihetuḥ kaverbhavati /
uktaprakārātikrame tu niyamenaiva rasabhaṅgahetuḥ sampadyate /
lakṣyaṃ ca tathāvidhaṃ mahākaviprabandheṣvapi dṛśyate bahuśaḥ /
tattu sūktitasahasradyotitātmānāṃ mahātmanāṃ doṣoddhoṣaṇamātmana eva dūṣaṇaṃ bhavatīti na vibhajya darśitam /
kiṃ tu rūpakāderalaṅkāravargasya yeyaṃ vyañjakatve rasādiviṣaye lakṣaṇadigdarśitā tāmanusaran svayaṃ cānyallakṣaṇamutprekṣamāṇo yadyalakṣyakramapratibhamanantaroktamenaṃ locanam pāṇḍamnā tanimnā kaṇṭakitatvena ca yogāt /
śaśinīti pāṇḍuratvāt /
utpaśyāmīti yatnenotprekṣe /
jīvitasandhāraṇāyetyarthaḥ /
hanteti kaṣṭam, ekasthasādṛśyābhāve ha dolāyamāno 'haṃ sarvatra sthito na kutracidekasya dhṛtiṃ labha iti bhāva /
bhīrviti /
yo hi kātarahṛdayo bhavatināsau sarvasvamekasthaṃ dhārayatītyarthaḥ /
atra hyutprekṣāyāstadbhāvādhyāroparūpāyā anuprāṇakaṃ sādṛśyaṃ yathopakrāntaṃ, tathā nirvāhitamapi vipralambharasapoṣakameva jātam /
tattu lakṣyaṃ na darśitamiti sambandhaḥ /
pratyudāharaṇe hyadarśite 'pyudāharaṇānuśīlanadiśā kṛtakṛtyateti darśayati--kiṃ tviti /
anyallakṣaṇamiti /
parīkṣāprakāramityarthaḥ /
tadyathāvasare tyaktasyāpi punargrahaṇamityādi /
yathā mamaiva--śītāṃśoramṛtacchaṭā yada karāḥ kasmānmano me mṛśaṃ bālapriyā gamyaṃ darśayati---pāṇḍimnetyādi /
kaṇṭakitvaṃ tīkṣṇāgrāvayavaviśeṣavatvaṃ romaharṣavatvaṃ ca /
hanteti /
viṣādārthakamityāha--kaṣṭamekasthetyādi /
'bhīru' iti sambudhyā dyotyamarthamāha---yo hītyādi /
na dhārayati nāvakthāpayata anyāpaharaṇaśaṅkayeti bhāvaḥ /
tadbhāveti /
atasmiṃstattādātmyāhāryasambhāvanārūpāyā ityarthaḥ /
atra ca śyāmādāvaṅgāditādātmyasambhāvanā bodhyā /
anuprāṇakamiti /
aṅgamityarthaḥ /
sādṛśyamiti /
gamyamiti śeṣaḥ /
tatheti /
aṅgasādṛśyasya upakrāntasya upasaṃhārāditi bhāvaḥ /
nirvāhitamiti /
utprekṣānirvahaṇadvārā nirvāhitamityarthaḥ /
vṛttāvupasaṃharati---'sa eva' mityādi /
'tathāvidham' iti /
uktaprakārātikrāntamityarthaḥ /
śītāṃśoriti /
virahiṇa uktiḥ /
'śītāṃśoḥ karāḥ' kiraṇāḥ amṛtacchaṭāḥ, yadīti siddhānuvāde /
yathā--"sragiyaṃ yadi jīvitāpahe"tyādau /
'kasmāt' kutaḥ /
me manaḥ dhvanerātmānamupanibadhnāti sukaviḥ samāhitacetāstādā tasyātmalābho bhavati mahīyāniti /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] etc. /
That figure, when composed in this manner, becomes for the poet a cause of the manifestation of <s>rasa</s>. /
But when the stated method is transgressed, it invariably becomes a cause of the destruction of <s>rasa</s>. /
And such instances are seen abundantly even in the works of great poets. /
But since proclaiming faults of great souls — whose selves are illuminated by thousands of fine verses — is a blemish upon oneself, that [evidence] has not been analyzed and displayed. /
Rather, following this direction of definition that has been shown for the group of <s>alaṅkāras</s> beginning with <s>rūpaka</s> regarding their suggestive capacity in the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc., and also conjecturing other criteria of one's own — if, through imperceptible-sequence intuition, the immediately stated — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'Because of the pallor, slenderness, and bristling' — /
'<s>Śaśinī</s>' — because of the pallor. /
'I imagine' — I fancy with effort. /
'For the sustaining of life' — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Hanta</s>' — alas; 'In the absence of resemblance to a single [entity], I, swaying [in doubt], stationed everywhere, nowhere attain steadiness regarding a single [identification]' — this is the purport. /
'<s>Bhīru</s>' (O timid one) — /
'For one who is timid of heart does not deposit his entire wealth in a single place' — this is the meaning. /
For here, of the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) — which has the form of superimposing identity where none exists — the subsidiary resemblance, as it was begun, so too when carried through, became a nourisher of <s>vipralambha-rasa</s> (love-in-separation). /
But that instance [of faults] has not been displayed — this is the connection. /
For even without showing counter-examples, the direction of studying [positive] examples suffices for [achieving] the goal — he shows this: '<s>kiṃ tu</s>' etc. /
'Another criterion' — /
'A method of examination' — this is the meaning. /
'Such as: the re-adoption of what was abandoned at the [right] occasion' — and so forth. /
'As in my own [verse]: "<s>Śītāṃśu's</s> (the moon's) nectar-rays, if [they are] hands, why do they grope my mind?"' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He shows the meaning to be understood: '<s>pāṇḍimna</s>' etc. /
'Bristling' — having sharp-tipped parts, [and also] having horripilation. /
'<s>Hanta</s>' — /
It expresses distress — he says: 'Alas!' — 'In the absence of resemblance to a single entity' etc. /
By the vocative '<s>bhīru</s>' (O timid one), he states the meaning conveyed: '<s>yo hi</s>' etc. /
'Does not deposit' — does not entrust — because of the apprehension that someone else might steal it — this is the purport. /
'Identity-where-none-exists' — /
'The superimposition of identity between things not actually identical — a probable fancy of that nature' — this is the meaning. /
And here the fancy of identity of limbs etc. with dark things etc. should be understood. /
'Subsidiary' — /
'A limb' — this is the meaning. /
'Resemblance' — /
'Discernible' is the remainder. /
'As carried through' — because the subsidiary resemblance that was begun was also concluded — this is the purport. /
'Carried through' — /
'Carried through by means of the completion of the <s>utprekṣā</s>' — this is the meaning. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, he concludes: '<s>sa evam</s>' etc. /
'Of such a kind' — /
'Transgressing the stated method' — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Śītāṃśu's</s>' — the speech of a person in separation. /
'<s>Śītāṃśu's</s> hands' — rays; 'nectar-rays' — if [they are nectar-rays]. '<s>Yadi</s>' is in the sense of a settled fact. /
As in: '<s>srag iyaṃ yadi jīvitāpahe</s>' ('if this garland [is sent] to the life-destroyer') etc. /
'<s>Kasmāt</s>' — why? /
'My mind' — the good poet, binding the self of <s>dhvani</s>, with concentrated mind — then his attainment of self becomes a great [thing]. /
[<s>Kārikā</s>:] That self of it which, resembling a reverberation (<s>anusvāna</s>), shines forth in sequence —
because it is rooted in the power of word and meaning, it too is established as twofold. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.20 //
[Repeated <s>kārikā</s>:] That self of it which, resembling a reverberation, shines forth in sequence —
because it is rooted in the power of word and meaning, it too is established as twofold. // 20 //
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'They scorch — or, being contaminated by contact with the mass of <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison),

children.text: kiṃ prāṇānna harantyuta priyatamāsañjalpamantrākṣarai- rakṣyante kimu mohamemi hahahā no vejhi keyaṃ gatiḥ //
children.translated_text: do they not take away [my] life-breaths? Or are they protected by the spell-syllables of the beloved's sweet talk? Or am I falling into a swoon? — Ha, ha, ha! — No, I don't know; what is this condition?'
Here indeed, <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>sandeha</s> (doubt), and <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration) are abandoned and then readopted for the nourishment of <s>rasa</s>. Enough of this. // 18 //

children.text:
evaṃ vivakṣitānyaparavācyadhvaneḥ prathamaṃ bhedamalakṣyakramaṃ vicāryaṃ dvitīyaṃ bhedaṃ vibhaktumāha---krameṇetyādi /
bālapriyā bhṛśaṃ sampluṣyantisantāpayanti /
amṛtacchaṭātmakatvena sampaloṣakatvāyogāditi bhāvaḥ /
asyopapattiṃ sandihāna āha--athetyādi /
atheti vikalpe /
karā ityanuṣajyate /
kālakūṭānāṃ paṭalyā samūhena yaḥ saṃvāsaḥ dvayorekotpannatvātsahavāsaḥ saṃsargaṃ iti yāvat, tena sandūṣitāḥ santāpakatvādisvīyadoṣaviśiṣṭāḥ kṛtāḥ /
tarhi te kiṃ kutaḥ prāṇānna haranti? prāṇāpahārakatvasyāpi tatsvabhāvatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
prāṇaharaṇābhāve hetumāśaṅkamāna āha--utetyādi /
uteti vikalpe /
priyatamāyāḥ sañjalpeṣu yāni mantrākṣarāṇi viṣāpahārīṇi taiḥ /
rakṣyante prāṇā iti vipariṇāmenānuṣaṅgaḥ /
atrāpyanupapattiṃ manyamāna āha--kiṃ tvityādi /
kimu kutaḥ /
rūpaketi /
karā amṛtacchaṭā iti rūpakaṃ, kālakūṭetyādau sandehaḥ, priyatamāsañjalpeṣu mantrākṣarāropānnidarśanā /
tyāgaḥ /
athetyādinā punarupādānaṃ, tathā sandūṣitatvasandehasya 'kiṃ prāṇāni'tyādinā tyāgaḥ /
utetyādinā punarupādanamevaṃ priyatametyādi nidarśanāyāḥ, mohaṃ mūrcchāmemi prāpnomītyanena tyāgaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'This condition' — this state, this natural course of things. /

children.text: kā no vejhi na jānāmītyanena punarupādānaṃ ca pratyāyyata iti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What [is this]? I do not know' — by this, the readoption too is made understood — this is the purport. /

children.text: yadvā sampluṣyantītyantena rūpakasyāharantītyantena sandehasya, emītyantena nidarśanāyāśca tyāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively: by [the portion] ending in '<s>sampluṣyanti</s>' (they scorch), the abandonment of <s>rūpaka</s>; by [the portion] ending in '<s>āharanti</s>' (they take away), [the abandonment] of <s>sandeha</s>; by [the portion] ending in '<s>emi</s>' (I go/fall), [the abandonment] of <s>nidarśanā</s>. /
By '<s>no vedmi</s>' (I don't know) etc., the readoption of those — this should be understood. // 18 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Having thus examined the first variety of <s>vivakṣitānyapara-vācya-dhvani</s> — the one with imperceptible sequence — he now proceeds to classify the second variety: '<s>krameṇa</s>' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'They scorch intensely — they cause burning.' /
'Because being nectar-rays, the capacity to scorch is unfitting' — this is the purport. /
Doubting whether this is justified, he says: '<s>atha</s>' etc. /
'<s>Atha</s>' — in the sense of alternative. /
'Hands' (<s>karāḥ</s>) carries over. /
'By the mass, i.e., the aggregate, of <s>kālakūṭas</s> — the cohabitation, i.e., being born together, constituting association — contaminated by that, i.e., made to possess one's own defects such as the capacity to burn.' /
'Then why do they not take away the life-breaths?' — because the capacity to kill is also their nature — this is the purport. /
Doubting the reason for the absence of killing, he says: '<s>uta</s>' etc. /
'<s>Uta</s>' — in the sense of alternative. /
'By the spell-syllables in the sweet talks of the beloved' — which are antidotes to poison. /
'The life-breaths are protected' — by inversion, carries over. /
Considering even this unjustified, he says: '<s>kiṃ tu</s>' etc. /
'<s>Kimu</s>' — from what [cause]? /
'<s>Rūpaka</s>' — /
'The hands are nectar-rays' — this is <s>rūpaka</s>; in '<s>kālakūṭa</s>' etc., <s>sandeha</s> (doubt); through the superimposition of spell-syllables on the beloved's sweet talk, <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration). /
Abandonment — /
By '<s>atha</s>' etc., readoption; likewise, the abandonment of the doubt about contamination by '<s>kiṃ prāṇān</s>' etc. /
By '<s>uta</s>' etc., readoption; likewise, the abandonment of <s>nidarśanā</s> by '<s>mohaṃ emi</s>' ('I fall into a swoon'). /

children.text:
hetutvenopātta iti /
yataḥ krameṇa bhāti, ato 'nusvānasannibha ityartha iti bhāvaḥ /
asya vivakṣitānyaparavācyasya dhvaneḥ saṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgyatvādanuraṇana- prakhyo ya ātmā so 'pi śūbdaśaktimūlo 'rthaśaktimūlaśceti dviprakāraḥ /
nanu śabdaśaktyā yatrārthāntaraṃ prakāśate sa yadi dhvaneḥ prakāra ucyate tadidānīṃ śleṣasya viṣaya evāpahṛtaḥ syāt, nāpahṛta ityāha---
children.translated_text:
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Adopted as a cause' — /
Since it shines forth in sequence, therefore it is like a reverberation — this is the meaning — this is the purport. /
Of this <s>dhvani</s> whose expressible is intended as being directed to another — because the suggested has perceptible sequence — that self which is like a reverberation, it too is of two kinds: rooted in the power of word and rooted in the power of meaning. /
'Now, if another meaning is manifested by the power of word, and if that is called a variety of <s>dhvani</s>, then the domain of <s>śleṣa</s> (double-entendre) would simply be usurped!' — to which he replies: 'Not usurped' — he says: /
[<s>Kārikā</s>:] A figure that is merely implied (<s>ākṣipta</s>) shines forth through the power of word;

children.text: yasminn anuktaḥ śabdena śabda-śakty-udbhavo hi saḥ // DhvK_2.21 //
children.translated_text: that [<s>dhvani</s>] in which [the suggested] is not [directly] expressed by the word — that is born from the power of word. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.21 //
[Repeated <s>kārikā</s>:] A figure that is merely implied shines forth through the power of word;
that in which [the suggested] is not expressed by the word — that is born from the power of word. // 21 //

children.text:
yasmādalaṅkāro na vastumātraṃ yasmin kāvye śabdaśaktyā prakāśate sa śabdaśaktyudabhavo dhvaniratyasmākaṃ vivakṣitam /
vastudvaye ca śabdaśaktyā prakāśamāne śleṣaḥ /
yathā--- yena dhvastamanobhavena balijitkāyaḥ purāstrīkṛto yaścedvṛttabhujaṅgahāravalayo gaṅgāṃ ca yo 'dhārayat /
locanam prathamapādo 'nuvādabhāgo hetutvenopāttaḥ /
ghaṇṭāyā anuraṇanamabhighātajaśabdāpekṣayā kramemaiva bhāti /

children.translated_text: 'It too' — /
Not only is <s>dhvani</s> twofold from its root. /
Nor is only <s>vivakṣitānyapara-vācya</s> twofold. /
This one too is twofold — this is the meaning of the word '<s>api</s>.' // 20 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Since the figure — not a mere content (<s>vastu</s>) — which in a certain poem shines forth through the power of word, that is the <s>dhvani</s> born from the power of word — this is our intention. /
And when two contents shine forth through the power of word, that is <s>śleṣa</s> (double-entendre). /
For example: 'He by whom, having destroyed <s>Manobhava</s> (Cupid/the mind-born), <s>Balijit's</s> (<s>Indra's</s>/<s>Viṣṇu's</s>) body was formerly turned into a woman; and he whose coiling-serpent-destroying bracelets [resound] — and who bore the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The first quarter is the resumptive portion, adopted as a cause. /
The reverberation of a bell shines forth in sequence, only in dependence on the [initial] stroke. /

children.text:
kārikāgataṃ hiśabdaṃ vyācaṣṭe--yasmāditi /
alaṅkāraśabdasya vyavacchedyaṃ darśayati--na vastumātramiti /
vastudvaye ceti /
caśabdastuśabdasyārthe /
yeneti /
yena dhvastaṃ bālakrīḍāyāmanaḥ śakaṭam /
abhavenājena satā /
balino dānavānyo jayati tādṛgyena kāyo vapuḥ purāmṛtaharaṇakāle strītvaṃ prāpitaḥ /
yaścedvṛttaṃ samadaṃ kāliyākhyaṃ bhujaṅgaṃ hatavān /
rave śabde layo yasya /
'akāro viṣṇuḥ' ityukteḥ /
yaścāgaṃ govardhanaparvataṃ gāṃ ca bhūmiṃ pātālagatāmadhārayat /
children.translated_text: 'And who bore <s>Govardana</s> mountain [= the go-vardana] and also the earth (<s>gā</s>) [= <s>bhūmi</s>] when it had gone to the netherworld.' /

children.text: yasya ca nāma stutyamṛṣaya āhuḥ kiṃ tat? śaśinaṃ mathnātīti kvip rāhuḥ, tasya śiroharo bālapriyā anusvānapadārthaṃvivṛṇvaṃstadbhānasya kramikatvaṃ darśayanti---ghaṇṭāyā ityādi /
children.translated_text: 'And whose name the sages call praiseworthy — what is that? "He who grinds the moon" — by <s>kvip</s> suffix — <s>Rāhu</s>; the cutter of his head' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Elucidating the meaning of '<s>anusvāna</s>' (reverberation), they show the sequential nature of its manifestation: 'of a bell' etc. /

children.text: vivakṣitānyaparavācya ityasya sthāne 'avivakṣitavācya' iti ca pāṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In place of <s>vivakṣitānyapara-vācya</s>, the reading <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> also exists.' /
The meaning of the word '<s>api</s>' is to be understood from '<s>so 'pi</s>' as well. // 20 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He glosses the word '<s>hi</s>' in the <s>kārikā</s>: '<s>yasmāt</s>' etc. /
He shows what is excluded by the word '<s>alaṅkāra</s>': '<s>na vastumātram</s>' (not mere content) etc. /
'And two contents' — the word '<s>ca</s>' is in the sense of '<s>tu</s>' (but). /
'By whom' — by whom the mind-born (<s>Manobhava</s>) [= <s>Kāma</s>] was destroyed, [and alternatively:] by whom, being non-born (<s>ajena</s>), i.e., unborn — /
Of <s>Bali's</s> conqueror, i.e., the <s>Dānavas</s>' conqueror — the body was made into a woman at the time of the stealing of the nectar. /
And whose coiled (<s>vṛtta</s>), i.e., round, serpent (<s>bhujaṅga</s>) he struck (<s>hata</s>) — /
'In sound' (<s>rave</s>) — 'whose sound has dissolution' (<s>laya</s>). /
'<s>Akāra</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — as stated [in the lexicons]. /

children.text:
'na vastumātra'miti kārikāsthaivakāravyavacchedyamiti bhramaḥ syādato vyācaṣṭe---alaṅkāraśabdasyeti /
evakāravyavacchedyamupari vakṣyati /
yenetyatrādau viṣṇupakṣe vyācaṣṭe---bālakrīḍāyāmityādi /
'tādṛkkāyo yena strītvaṃ prāpita' ityādyanvayaḥ /
laya iti /

children.translated_text: 'Identity' — this is the meaning. /
'Of the nature of sound' — this is the extent. /
He states the authority for that: '<s>akāra</s>' etc. /

children.text: yasyāhuḥ śaśimacchiro hara iti stutyaṃ ca nāmāmarāḥ pāyātsa svayamandhakakṣayakarastvāṃ sarvadomādhavaḥ //
children.translated_text: [Verse:] 'Whose name the immortals call praiseworthy: "Cut off the head of the moon-grinder (<s>Rāhu</s>)!" — may that <s>Mādhava</s>, self-born destroyer of <s>Andhaka</s>, protect you from all [evil]!'

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Lest there be the error that the <s>eva</s>-particle in the <s>kārikā</s> excludes [only] <s>vastu</s>' — therefore he glosses: 'of the word <s>alaṅkāra</s>' etc. /
'The object to be excluded by the <s>eva</s>-particle will be stated later.' /
In '<s>yena</s>' (by whom), he first explains in terms of the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-interpretation: '<s>bālakrīḍāyām</s>' etc. /
'By such a body, which was made into a woman' — this is the syntactic connection. /
'<s>Laya</s>' — /

children.text: nanvalaṅkārāntarapratibhāyāmapi śleṣavyapadeśo bhavatīti darśitaṃ bhaṭṭodbhaṭena, tatpunarapi śabdaśaktimūlo dhvanirniravakāśa ityāśaṅkyedamuktaṃ 'ākṣiptaḥ' iti /
tadayamarthaḥ--yatra śabdaśaktyā sākṣādalaṅkārāntaraṃ vācyaṃ satpratibhāsate sa sarvaḥ śleṣaviṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] This is the meaning: where through the power of word, another figure that is directly expressed (<s>vācya</s>) flashes — all that is the domain of <s>śleṣa</s>. /

children.text: yatra tu śabdaśaktyā sāmarthyākṣiptaṃ vācyavyatiriktaṃ vyaṅgyamevālaṅkārāntaraṃ prakāśate sa dhvanerviṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: But where through the power of word, a suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) figure, distinct from the expressed and merely implied by the capacity [of word], shines forth — that is the domain of <s>dhvani</s>. /

children.text: śabdaśaktyā sākṣādalaṅkārāntarapratibhā yathā--- tasyā vināpi hāreṇa nisargādeva hāriṇau /
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] An instance of another figure flashing directly through the power of word: 'Of her, even without a necklace (<s>hāra</s>), being naturally captivating (<s>hāriṇau</s>),
did the two breasts not produce wonder in everyone?'

[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Now, <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s> has shown that even when another figure flashes, the designation <s>śleṣa</s> [still] applies' — if so, then <s>dhvani</s> rooted in the power of word would have no scope [left] — anticipating this doubt, this has been said: '<s>ākṣiptaḥ</s>' (merely implied). /

children.text:
atra śṛṅgāravyabhicārī vismayākhyo bhāvaḥ sākṣādvirodhālaṅkāraśca pratibhāsata iti virodhacchāyānugrāhiṇaḥ śleṣasyāyaṃ viṣayaḥ, na tvanusvānopamavyaṅgyasya dhveneḥ /
locanam mūdhāpahāraka iti /
sa tvāṃ mādhavo viṣṇuḥ sarvadaḥ pāyāt /
kīdṛk? andhakanāmnāṃ janānāṃ yena kṣayo nivāso dvārakāyāṃ kṛtaḥ /
yadi vā mausale iṣīkābhisteṣāṃ kṣayovināśo yena kṛtaḥ /
dvitīyo 'rthaḥ--yena dhvastakāmena satā balijito vidhṇoḥ sambandhī kāyaḥ purā tripuranirdahanāvasare 'strīkṛtaḥ śaratvaṃ nītaḥ /
udvṛttā bhujaṅgā eva hārā valayāśca yasya, mandākinīṃ ca yo 'dhārayat, yasya ca ṝṣayaḥ śaśimaccandrayuktaṃ śira āhuḥ, hara iti ca yasya nāma stutyamāhuḥ, sa bhagavānsvayamevāndhakāsurasya vināśakārī tvāṃ sarvadā kalvakālamumāyā dhavo vallabhaḥ pāyādati /
atra vastumātraṃ dvitīyaṃ pratītaṃ nālaṅkāra iti śleṣasyaiva viṣayaḥ /
ākṣiptaśabdasya kārikāgatasya vyavacchedyaṃ darśayituṃ codyonopakramate---nanvalaṅkāretyādinā /
tasyā vināpīti /
apiśabdo 'yaṃ virodhamācakṣāṇo 'rthadvaye 'pyabhidhāśaktiṃ bālapriyā śeṣaṃ spaṣṭam /
vastumātramityādi /
mādhavasyomādhavasya ca stotavyatvena prakṛtatvāttayoḥ sāmyaṃ na vivakṣitamiti bhāvaḥ /
vṛttau 'sākṣādalaṅkārāntaraṃ vācya'miti /
alaṅkārāntaramalaṅkāraviśeṣaḥ /
vācyamabhidheyamiti tadarthaḥ /
apiśabdo 'yamiti /
hārema vināpītyapiśabda ityarthaḥ /
virodhaṃ hāratadabhāvayorekatra vṛttitvarūpam /
ācakṣāṇaḥ bodhayan /
arthadvaye vakṣyamāṇe /

children.translated_text: "Expressive power" — the power of the word <s>hārin</s> (charming/necklace-bearing) that is of the nature of denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>).

children.text: alakṣyakramavyaṅgyasya tu dhvanervācyena śleṣeṇa virodhena vā vyañjitasya viṣaya eva /
children.translated_text: But this is indeed the domain of <s>dhvani</s> of imperceptible-sequence suggestion — [<s>dhvani</s>] suggested through the expressible <s>śleṣa</s> or contradiction.

children.text: yathā mamaiva-- ślādhyāśeṣatanuṃ sudarśanakaraḥ sarvāṅgalīlājata- trailokyāṃ caramāravindalalitenākrāntaloko hariḥ /
children.translated_text: As in this [verse] of mine: "<s>Hari</s>, whose hand bears <s>Sudarśana</s> (the discus), whose body praiseworthy in every part gives rise to grace in all limbs, who pervades the worlds with the play of his ultimate lotus-[feet],

children.text: bibhrāmāṃ mukhabhindurūpamakhilaṃ candrātmacakṣurdadha- tsthāne yāṃ svatanorapaśyadadhikāṃ sā rukmiṇī vo 'vatāt //
children.translated_text: Bearing the full moon-form beauty of [her] face, placing the eye that is the moon itself — she whom he saw in his own body's stead as surpassing [it] — may that <s>Rukmiṇī</s> protect you!"

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Here, the emotion called wonder (<s>vismaya</s>), which is a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, and the figure of contradiction (<s>virodha-alaṅkāra</s>) directly appear — hence this is the domain of <s>śleṣa</s> that supports the semblance of contradiction, not of <s>dhvani</s> whose suggested content is like the reverberation of a bell. [<s>Locana</s>:] "Stealer of minds" — may that <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) always protect you. Of what kind? He by whom the destruction of people called <s>Andhakas</s> was accomplished, [or] their dwelling was established in <s>Dvārakā</s>. Or: He by whom their destruction was accomplished in the [battle of the] mace (<s>musala</s>) through reeds. The second meaning: He who, being one who destroyed <s>Kāma</s>, [Śiva,] the kinsman of <s>Viṣṇu</s> who conquered <s>Bali</s> — his body was formerly made into an arrow on the occasion of burning <s>Tripura</s>. He whose necklaces and bangles are none other than rearing serpents, who bore the <s>Mandākinī</s> (Ganges), whose head the sages call "moon-bearing," and whose name they praise as "<s>Hara</s>" — may that Lord himself, the destroyer of the <s>Andhaka</s> demon, always [protect you], He who is <s>Umā</s>'s beloved (<s>dhava</s>). Here, what is apprehended as the second meaning is mere content (<s>vastu</s>), not a figure — hence this is the domain of <s>śleṣa</s> alone. To show what is excluded by the word "drawn forth" (<s>ākṣipta</s>) occurring in the verse, he initiates an objection — with "but the <s>alaṅkāra</s>" etc. "Even without her" — this word "even" (<s>api</s>), conveying contradiction, [indicates] the expressive power (<s>abhidhā-śakti</s>) in both meanings. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The rest is clear. "Mere content" etc. — since both <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) and <s>Umā</s>'s husband (<s>Śiva</s>) are contextually relevant as objects of praise, their similarity is not intended — this is the purport. In the <s>vṛtti</s>: "a different <s>alaṅkāra</s> is directly expressible." "A different <s>alaṅkāra</s>" means a particular figure. "Expressible" means denoted — that is the meaning. "This word 'even'" — the meaning is: the word <s>api</s> in "even without necklaces." "Contradiction" — in the form of the co-existence of necklaces and their absence in one [entity]. "Conveying" means making known. "In both meanings" — in the two meanings to be stated.
Here, <s>śleṣa</s> that supports the semblance of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) is apprehended precisely as the expressible.

children.text: yathā ca--- bhramimaratimalasahṛdayatāṃ pralayaṃ mūrchāṃ tamaḥ śarīrasādam /
children.translated_text: And as in: "Bewilderment, distraction, impurity, loss of consciousness, <s>pralaya</s> (dissolution), fainting, darkness, bodily decay,

children.text: maraṇaṃ ca jaladabhujagajaṃ prasahyaṃ kurute viṣaṃ viyoginīnām //
children.translated_text: And death — the poison born of cloud-serpents forcibly inflicts [all these] upon women in separation."

children.text:
locanam niyacchati harato hṛdayamavaśyamiti hāriṇau /
hāro vidyate yayostau hāriṇāviti /
ata eva vismayaśabdo 'syaivārthasyopodbalakaḥ /
apiśabdābhāve tu na tata evārthadvayasyābhidhā syāt, svasaundaryādeva stanayorvismayahetutvopapatteḥ /
vismayākhyo bhāva iti dṛṣṭantābhiprāyeṇopāttam /
yathā vismayaḥ śabdena pratibhāti vismaya ityanena śabdena tathā virodho 'pi pratibhātyapītyanena śabdena /
nanu kiṃ sarvathātra dhanirnāstītyāśaṅkyāha--alakṣyeti /
virodhena veti /
vāgrahaṇena śleṣavirodhasaṅkarālaṅkāro 'yamiti darśayati, anugrahayogādekataratyāgagrahaṇanimittābhāvo he vāśabdena sūcyate /
sudarśanaṃ cakraṃ kare yasya /
vyatirekapakṣe sudarśanau ślādhyau karāveva yasya /
caraṇaravindasya lalitaṃ tribhuvanākramaṇakrījanam /
candrarūpaṃ cakṣurdhārayan /
vācyatayaiveti /
svatanoradhikāmiti śabdena vyatirekasyoktatvāt /
bālapriyā arthadvayamāha-harata ityādi /
'ityārthadvaye' iti sambandhaḥ /
ata eva apiśabdaprayogādeva /
vismayaśabdaḥ dvitīyāntavismayaśabdaḥ /
upodbalakaḥ bodhe sahakārī /
ekatra viruddhārthabodhe hi vismayaḥ /
uktamupapādayati--apiśabdābhāve tviti /
tata evārthadvayasyābhidhā na syādityanvayaḥ /
tata eva vismayaśabdādeva /
abhidhā abhidhānam /
kuta ityatrāha---sveti /
vṛttau---'vismayākhyo bhāvaḥ pratibhāsata' iti kimarthamuktamityatrāha--dṛṣṭānteti /
śabdena pratibhātītyuktasyaiva vivaraṇam--vismaya ityādi /
pratibhātītyasyānuṣaṅgaḥ /
darśayatītyatra hetumāha--anugrahayogāditi /
virodhaśleṣayoranugrāhyanugrāhakabhāvādityarthaḥ /
eketi /
ekatarasya tyāge grahaṇe vā yannimittaṃ tadabhāva ityarthaḥ /
vācyatayaivetyasya vyatireka ityanenāpi sambandho vivakṣita ityāha---svatanoradhikāmitīti yathā vā---
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He states that the connection of "precisely as the expressible" is also intended with "<s>vyatireka</s>" through "surpassing his own body" — as in, or as in:
[Prakrit:] <s>camahiamāṇasakañcaṇapaṅkaaṇimmahiaparimalā jasya</s> /
<s>akhaṇḍiadāṇapasārā bāhuppalihā vvia gaindā</s> //

[<s>Locana</s>:] "Captivating" (<s>hāriṇau</s>) — they inevitably steal (<s>harati</s>) the heart — hence they are <s>hāriṇau</s>. Or: those which possess necklaces (<s>hāra</s>) are <s>hāriṇau</s>. Hence the word "wonder" (<s>vismaya</s>) is a corroborator of this very meaning. But in the absence of the word "even" (<s>api</s>), the denotation of both meanings would not follow from that alone, since the wonder-worthiness of the breasts can be justified by their own beauty alone. "The emotion called wonder" — this is stated with the intent of the example. Just as wonder appears through the word "wonder," so too contradiction appears through the word "even" (<s>api</s>). "But surely there is no <s>dhvani</s> here at all?" — anticipating this doubt, he says "of imperceptible [sequence]" etc. "Or by contradiction" — by the word "or" (<s>vā</s>) he shows that this is a combined figure of <s>śleṣa</s>-and-<s>virodha</s>; the word "or" indicates the absence of grounds for abandoning or adopting either one, since both support [the effect]. "<s>Sudarśana</s>" — the discus (<s>cakra</s>) in whose hand. In the <s>vyatireka</s> interpretation: he whose two hands alone are praiseworthy and beautiful (<s>sudarśana</s>). "The play of the ultimate lotus" — the sport of the lotus-foot's striding over the three worlds. "Bearing a moon-form eye" — holding [it]. "Precisely as the expressible" — because the <s>vyatireka</s> is stated by the words "surpassing his own body." [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He states the two meanings — "steals" etc. The connection is with "in both meanings." "Hence" — precisely because of the use of the word "even" (<s>api</s>). "The word 'wonder'" — the word <s>vismaya</s> in the accusative case. "Corroborator" — an auxiliary in cognition. For wonder arises from the cognition of contradictory meanings in one [entity]. He substantiates what was said — "but in the absence of the word 'even'" etc. The construction is: the denotation of both meanings would not follow from that alone. "From that alone" — from the word <s>vismaya</s> alone. "Denotation" means expression. "Why?" — to this he says "by their own" etc. In the <s>vṛtti</s>: "the emotion called wonder appears" — why was this said? — to this he says "with the intent of the example" etc. The elaboration of "appears through the word" — "wonder" etc. The connection is with "appears." He states the reason for "shows" — "from the relation of support" etc. Meaning: because of the supporter-supported relationship between <s>virodha</s> and <s>śleṣa</s>. "One" — meaning: the absence of any ground for abandoning or adopting one of the two.
(Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:) Whose [arms have] fragrance churned from crushed golden lotuses,
Whose arm-girths are like lordly elephants with unbroken flow of rut-fluid //

The authors of the <s>Kuvalayānanda</s> call this very <s>vakrokti</s> "<s>vivṛtokti</s>" (explicit speech).

children.text: ekastvaṃ viṣameṣu khinnamanasāṃ sarvābalānāṃ gatir- gopyaivaṃ gaditaḥ saleśamavatādgoṣṭhe harirvaściram //
children.translated_text: 'You alone are the refuge of all weak women whose minds are distressed in difficult [paths] — ' Thus addressed by the cowherd woman (<s>gopi</s>), may <s>Hari</s> protect you in the cow-pen (<s>gostha</s>) for a long time, with a trace [of suggestion]!

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Here, <s>śleṣa</s> that supports the semblance of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) appears precisely as the expressible. And the drawn-forth (<s>ākṣipta</s>) <s>alaṅkāra</s> — where, however, its nature is expressed by another word, not — [<s>Locana</s>:] By the force of contemplating the meaning of the word "serpent" (<s>bhujaga</s>), the word "poison" (<s>viṣa</s>), even while denoting water, cannot refrain [from denoting poison], but rather expresses the second meaning characterized as <s>hālāhala</s> (cosmic poison). Because without that denotation, the denotative function itself would remain incomplete. But of the [terms] from "bewilderment" (<s>bhrami</s>) through "death" (<s>maraṇa</s>), the meaning is entirely common [to both interpretations]. "Crushed" (<s>nirāśīkṛta</s>) — the minds/hearts that have been rendered hopeless, i.e., the hearts of enemies that have been shattered — those themselves are the golden lotuses. Because of being agitated by those as causes. "Churned fragrance" — owing to the word "lordly elephant" (<s>gajendra</s>), the words <s>camahima</s> (treading), <s>parimala</s> (fragrance), and <s>dāna</s> (charity/rut-fluid), even while conveying the meanings of trampling, aroma, and generosity respectively, do not have their denotative function completed — and thus they denote the second meaning as well, of the stated form. Thus, having shown what is excluded by the word "drawn forth" (<s>ākṣipta</s>), in order to show what is excluded by the word "only" (<s>eva</s>), he says "and that" etc. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She substantiates the <s>śleṣa</s>, [showing] the reason for restricting denotation to one of the two meanings when words capable of conveying both meanings are used — with "serpent" etc. The connection of "by force alone" is with "cannot refrain, but rather expresses." "Why?" — to this he says "without that" etc. "Entirely common" — and thus in that portion there is meaning-<s>śleṣa</s> — this is the purport. "Rendered hopeless" — here "hope" (<s>āśā</s>) should be understood as pertaining to victory. He shows the reason to be inferred for the golden-lotus characterization — "because of being agitated" etc. As in the <s>Kumārasambhava</s>: "surely a body fashioned from golden lotuses" etc. The elaboration of the intended meaning by "churned fragrance" — "whose glory of prowess is spread" etc. Whose glory of prowess, i.e., the extent of valor, is spread across the directions — such [elephants/arms] whose arm-girths are like lordly elephants — this is the connection. He applies qualifiers to the lordly elephant — "elephant" etc. "And the word" — the rest is: in sequence. "Of the stated form" — meaning: as previously described. "Denotes indeed" — because that meaning too is contextually relevant — this is the purport. In the <s>vṛtti</s>: "here in the <s>rūpaka</s>" — the meaning of "here" is: in the meaning of the stated verses. He shows the purport of the forthcoming and preceding text for ease of understanding — with "of both meanings" etc., up to "this is the purport." When a word capable of conveying both meanings is used — "one" — the restriction, i.e., the constraining, of denotation to one of the two objects — the <s>dhvani</s>-usage in the form of suggestion born from the resonance of word-power — therein, there is only the usage of expressible figures like <s>vakrokti</s> etc. As in — [<s>Locana</s>:] There is not, as in "he by whom <s>Kāma</s> was destroyed" etc. Or where, on the contrary, there exists evidence for the presence of a second denotative function, as in "even without her" etc. — there, in all [those cases], certainly, up to the end of "<s>camahia</s>" — that meaning is simply expressible — this is clear. Where, even though a reason for restricting denotation to one [meaning] such as context exists, [and] thereby denotation does not transfer to the second meaning — there that second meaning is called "drawn forth" (<s>ākṣipta</s>). And even there, if there exists such a word by which that restricting factor (context etc.) is rendered powerless — hence that denotative power, even though obstructed, is as if reborn (<s>pratiprasūta</s>) — even there, this is not the domain of <s>dhvani</s> — this is the purport. The particle "ca" has the meaning of "even" (<s>api</s>), [placed] in a different position. "Even though drawn forth" — meaning: even though it has begun to be immediately entertained as drawn forth. It is not [merely] drawn forth, but rather, through another word causing the rebirth of denotation, its nature has been fully expressed. By the word "again" (<s>punar</s>) he indicates that the explained [concept is] the "rebirth" (<s>pratiprasava</s>). Thus the word "only" (<s>eva</s>) negates [the status of the] "drawn-forth semblance" — this is the meaning. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The connection of this is with that; its cause is conjunction etc. "Thus" (<s>iti</s>) means "in 'thus' etc." The connection is with "where." "Second denotation" — meaning: denotation of the second meaning. "From 'even without her' etc. up to '<s>camahia</s>' etc." — meaning: the four examples [from] "even without her" etc. "There" — meaning: in the four [examples] from "by whom" etc. to "of her" etc. "Indeed" (<s>tāvat</s>) — in equal acceptance. "That meaning" — meaning: the second meaning. "Even there" etc. — "such" is a back-reference to "by whom." "By which" — meaning: by which word. "Rendered powerless" — having its constraining capacity defeated. "The denotative power" — the power of denoting the second meaning; "even though obstructed" — even though made unfavorable to cognition; "reborn" — again made favorable to cognition. "Only" (<s>eva</s>) — the reading "as if" (<s>iva</s>) also exists. "The particle 'ca'" — meaning: the particle "ca" in "and that" (<s>sa ca</s>). "In a different position" — meaning: it should be construed after the word "drawn forth" (<s>ākṣipta</s>). The elaboration of "even though drawn forth" — "as drawn forth" etc. He states the meaning conveyed by the concessive particle <s>api</s> — "not, however" etc. In the <s>vṛtti</s>: "that <s>alaṅkāra</s>" — the meaning is: the <s>śleṣa</s>. "The second meaning" — this much. The elaboration of "by another word" etc. — "by a word" etc. "By another word" — by a particular word. "But surely the denotation of <s>śleṣa</s> by another word such as '<s>saleśa</s>' is impossible?" — to this he says "of denotation" etc. "Of denotation" — of the denotation of the second meaning. "By the word 'again'" — meaning: by the word <s>punar</s> in "where again." "Explained" — meaning: as previously stated. He states the result — "therefore" etc.

children.translated_text: But where [a meaning] impelled by contextual capacity (<s>samarthya-aksipta</s>), together with another figure, shines forth through word-power (<s>sabda-sakti</s>) — all of that is the domain of <s>dhvani</s>.
For example — 'In the interval, the great <s>Kala</s> (Time/Death), called Summer, having withdrawn the pair of flower-seasons, expanded with a laugh of dazzling white blooming jasmine.'
And likewise — 'Elevated, with a swelling necklace, smeared with dark aloe-wood,
the weight of her bosom — of the slender woman — whom did it not make desirous?'

[Locana:] 'O <s>Kesava</s>, with my sight stolen by the dust of the cows, I saw nothing; by that reason I stumbled on the path.
Why indeed — for what reason — do you not support me, who have fallen, with your hand?
Since you alone are exceedingly strong on uneven [ground], and are the refuge, i.e., the means of support, for all weak women — children, the elderly, women, etc. — whose minds are distressed and who are unable to walk.' In a meaning of such a kind, although these words have their denotative power restricted by the context, nevertheless in the second meaning about to be explained, the denotative power, being obstructed, is revived by the [expression] '<s>salesa</s>' ('with a trace').
Here, '<s>salesa</s>' means 'with a hint' (<s>sasucana</s>), for diminishing is itself hinting.
'O <s>Kesava</s>! O cowherd (<s>gopa</s>)! O lord (<s>svamin</s>)! With my gaze stolen by passion (<s>raga</s>)' — or the syntactic connection is: 'with my gaze stolen by the eclipse (<s>uparaga</s>) of <s>Kesava</s>-[love].'
'I stumbled' — I became a woman of broken virtue.
'Me who have fallen' (<s>patitam</s>) — [expressing] the attitude of a husband toward me.
'One' (<s>eka</s>) — you alone, possessing extraordinary good fortune.
'Since you are the refuge of all weak women whose minds are tormented by love, being served by them with the removal of the turbidity of jealousy — the means of protecting [their] life': this is the meaning.
Thus, of the <s>slesa-alankara</s> (paronomasia figure) —
[Balapriya:] The explanation of the word '<s>paraga</s>' is: 'dust' (<s>dhuli</s>).
The syntactic connection is: 'I stumbled on the path.'
With the intention that the word '<s>eka</s>' has its primary meaning, he says: 'exceedingly strong.'
The explanation of '<s>visamasu</s>' is: 'on uneven [ground].'
The elaboration of the abstract meaning of '<s>khinnamanasam</s>' is: 'unable to walk' etc.
The syntactic connection is: 'these words.'
The meaning is: the words '<s>Kesava</s>,' '<s>goparaga</s>,' etc.
The syntactic connection of '<s>prakaranena</s>' (by the context) is with '<s>niyantrita</s>' (restricted) and '<s>niruddha</s>' (obstructed).
'The denotative power' — 'of these' is the remainder.
'Revived' (<s>pratyujjivita</s>) — re-enlivened.
He elaborates the reviving — 'here' etc.
The meaning of '<s>salesam</s>' is: 'with a hint' (<s>sasucana</s>).
'How is this obtained?' — to this he says: '<s>alpi</s>' (diminishing) etc.
He explains the second meaning — 'O <s>Kesava</s>!' etc.
'<s>Kesava</s>, <s>Gopa</s>' — the purport is that there are two vocatives.
'O lord' (<s>svaminn</s>) — this is the elaboration of '<s>nathe</s>.''
He states alternatively — 'by the <s>Kesava</s>-love (<s>Kesavaga</s>)' etc.
'By the <s>Kesava</s>-love' — by the passion (<s>anuraga</s>) directed toward <s>Kesava</s>, i.e., by the eclipse (<s>uparaga</s>) [of reason].
'The attitude of a husband' — [she who has] fallen: he says '<s>bhartr-bhava</s>' etc.
'The passage "herein between" etc. is found in the second chapter of the <s>Harsacarita</s>.'
'A pair of months' — the meaning is: a pair of months consisting of <s>Caitra</s> and <s>Vaisakha</s>.
'White' (<s>dhavala</s>) means dazzlingly [white]; the peals of laughter (<s>atta-hasa</s>) — the blossomed (<s>phulla</s>), i.e., blooming, jasmine flowers (<s>mallika</s>) — [the compound] '<s>phulla-mallika-dhavala-atta-hasa</s>' is a <s>vyadhikarana-bahuvrihi</s> [compound where the qualifier and qualified are in different grammatical relations] — he explains: '<s>dhavalani</s>' etc.
Let every such [example] indeed be entirely the domain of <s>vacya-slesa</s> (expressible paronomasia).

children.translated_text: '<s>Sva</s>' (dog) [comes] from here; '<s>sveta</s>' means white.
'In question-and-answer etc.' —
"When the learned make the splitting of an inquiry,
or in a witty assembly through sentences — that is known as question-and-answer."

[Locana:] Having established the domain [of vacya-slesa], he speaks of <s>dhvani</s> — 'but where' etc.
'Having withdrawn the pair that is the flower-season' — the pair of months.
'White' (<s>dhavala</s>) — delightful; the peals (<s>atta</s>) are shops/terraces; [he] who has such — the laugh (<s>hasa</s>), i.e., the blossoming, i.e., the whiteness, of the blooming jasmine flowers — in which [that whiteness exists].
But in the interpretation '[the great Kala] whose dazzling laugh is the blooming jasmine itself' — this would be equivalent to [the problematic reading] '<s>jalada-bhujaga-jam</s>' etc.
'Great' (<s>mahan</s>) and 'Time/season' (<s>kala</s>) — because of the conjunction of the length of days and unbearable [heat].
Here, the denotative powers [of the words] are restricted by the context of season-description; hence, overriding the maxim 'the establishment of the aggregate is stronger than the establishment of the parts,' the words '<s>Mahakala</s>' etc. have accomplished their purpose by denoting just this [literal] meaning.
Thereafter, the apprehension of the [other] meaning is through the operation of <s>dhvanana</s> (suggestion) alone, which is grounded in word-power.
Here some think —
[Balapriya:] The explanation of '<s>hasa</s>' is: 'blossoming' (<s>vikasa</s>).
The elaboration of that very [word] is: 'whiteness' (<s>sitima</s>).
'Whiteness' (<s>sitima</s>) — the state of being white.
He states the seed for abandoning the literal meaning — '<s>phulla</s>' etc.
'This would be equivalent to that' — and thus it would not be the intended example of <s>dhvani</s>: this is the purport.
Substantiating the 'greatness' [of Kala] — 'the length of days' etc.
'The length of days and unbearableness — because of the conjunction of these two': this is the meaning.
'Impelled by capacity' (<s>samarthya-aksipta</s>) — being suggested by the capacity of meaning that serves as an auxiliary.
'Another figure' (<s>alankara-antara</s>) — a particular figure.
'Shines forth through word-power' — shines forth primarily through word-power: he substantiates what was stated in the <s>vrtti</s> — 'here' etc.
'The context that is the season-description, or the context of season-description' — restricted by that, i.e., confined to their respective meanings — those whose denotative powers [are thus restricted] — those [words].
'Hence, from context alone' —
'This maxim' — as stated: 'conventional usage (<s>rudhi</s>) is stronger than compositional derivation (<s>yoga</s>).'
'This very meaning' — the meaning previously stated: this is the meaning.
'Thereafter, the apprehension of meaning' — the cognition of a meaning such as '<s>Mahakala</s> (the great [deity] of time/destruction), withdrawing the era, making the terrible white-toothed laugh of a terrifying deity' etc.: this is the meaning.
Here he shows the difference of opinion — 'here some' etc.
'Of these' — of '<s>Mahakala</s>' etc.: this is the meaning.
[Locana:] '[The words,] whose denotative power for meaning in another domain was previously known to the apprehender, having been restricted [by context] — from these, the apprehension [of the other meaning] is through the operation of <s>dhvanana</s> alone, which is grounded in word-power; hence the grounding in word-power and the suggested nature — these are not contradictory.' Thus [say some].
Others however [say] — 'In the explanation of the second alternative, through the capacity of meaning, the second denotation itself is re-enlivened; from that, the second meaning is denoted, not suggested. But thereafter, the configuration (<s>rupana</s>) of that second meaning, once apprehended, with the first meaning that is contextual — that indeed shines forth, and it does not [come] from elsewhere, i.e., from word [alone] — hence it is through the operation of <s>dhvanana</s>.
Therein, no denotative power whatsoever need be suspected [of operating].
And in that [configuration], the second word-power is the ground.
Because without it, the configuration would not arise.
Hence it is appropriate that this is figure-<s>dhvani</s> (<s>alankara-dhvani</s>).'

children.translated_text: And it will be stated: 'Let [the objection of] conveying unconnected meaning not be pressed' etc.
But in the earlier [verse], by the very word '<s>salesa</s>' (with a trace), the unconnectedness has been refuted.

children.text: bālapriyā yathā---"kāhamasmi guhā vakti praśne 'muṣmin kimuttaram /
children.translated_text: [Balapriya:] For example — 'Who am I? A cave (guha) speaks; in this question, what is the answer?
How is it that you do not know what was said? You are treating [me] with contempt, O friend!'

Thus the definition.
[Locana:] 'A word is brought in; therein, even by the force of another word, that other meaning — being apprehended, being cognized — because of being grounded [in word-power], it is appropriate that it is cognized [as suggested].' Thus [say some].
Another however [says] — 'In the explanation of the second alternative, through that capacity of meaning, the second denotation itself is re-enlivened; from that, the second meaning is denoted, not suggested. But thereafter, the configuration of that second meaning, once apprehended, with the first contextual meaning — that indeed shines forth, and not from elsewhere, i.e., from word — hence it is through the operation of <s>dhvanana</s>.
Therein, no denotative power whatsoever need be suspected.
And in that [configuration], the second word-power is the ground.
Because without it, the configuration would not arise.
Hence it is appropriate that this is figure-<s>dhvani</s>.'

children.translated_text: In the earlier [passage], '[with a] glance at <s>Keśava</s>' etc.
'Refuted' —

children.text: tatra hi dvitīyārtha eva prādhānyena vivakṣitaḥ, prathamārthastu yathā vā--- dattānandāḥ prajānāṃ samucitasamayākṛṣṭasṛṣṭeḥ payobhiḥ pūrvāhṇe viprakīrṇā diśi diśi viramatyahni saṃhārabhājaḥ /
children.translated_text: For there, the second meaning alone is primarily intended; but the first meaning — as for example: 'Having given delight to the people with waters drawn forth and released at the appropriate season, scattered about in the forenoon, in every direction, ceasing when the day ends, partaking of dissolution —

[the rays/cows] of the blazing-rayed [sun], boats for crossing the ocean of the fear of existence arising from long suffering, of those most purifying — may they generate for you the highest limitless joy!'

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Thus. /
Here, 'you mistreat' — this is expressed by the syllables '<s>ka</s>' and '<s>tha</s>'; 'you show' is the reply. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), [the passages] beginning with '<s>yena dhvaste</s>' (by whom destroyed) etc. are included. /
'<s>Vācya</s>' (expressible) — the meaning is: a <s>vācya-alaṅkāra</s> (expressible figure) such as <s>śleṣa</s> etc. /
The purport is: because both meanings are contextually relevant. /
'Where' — the meaning is: in [the verse beginning with] '<s>kusumasamayam</s>' (the season of flowers) etc. /
'From the operation of suggestion alone' — the meaning is: from the suggestive power alone, since <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) is restricted to the contextually relevant meaning. /
'By the force of another word' — the meaning is: by the denotative power of another word. /
'<s>Pratipannam api</s>' (even when apprehended) — the construction is: '[it] is apprehended.' /
'<s>Pratīya</s>' — the meaning is: [the word] whose root is the word apprehended through suggestion, i.e., understood through the operation of <s>dhvani</s>. /
That is to say: because it is rooted in the operation of <s>dhvani</s>. /
'<s>Pratīyamānam eva</s>' — means 'the suggested alone.' /
In the explanation of the second position — /
The meaning is: the explanation stated [beginning with] '<s>anye tu</s>' (others, however) etc. /
'By that' — the meaning is: by the concomitance of meanings. /
'Second denotation' — the meaning is: denotation of the second meaning. /
The connection is: 'of that which has been apprehended, of that second meaning.' /
'<s>Rūpaṇā</s>' (figuration) — the meaning is: superimposition of non-difference. /
That is to say: the non-difference being superimposed. /
This is an <s>upalakṣaṇa</s> (synecdoche) for <s>upamā</s> etc. /
'That, to begin with' — that <s>rūpaṇā</s> (figuration). /
'And not' etc. — /
'Shines' carries over. /
The meaning is: does not shine from anything other than the word. /
But the purport is: [it shines] from the word alone. /
'There' — the meaning is: in the <s>rūpaṇā</s>. /
'Of that' — the meaning is: of the <s>rūpaṇā</s>. /
'Because of the non-arising' — the purport is: because of the non-apprehension of the second meaning that serves as the correlate. /
For precisely this reason — because of the suggestedness of the mere <s>rūpaṇā</s> (figuration) etc. alone. /
'<s>Alaṅkāra</s>' — the meaning is: <s>rūpaka</s> etc. /
'<s>Iti yuktam</s>' (thus it is fitting) — the meaning is: thus the statement is justified. /
Otherwise, there would also be the usage of <s>vastu-dhvani</s> (factual suggestion) due to the suggestedness of the second meaning — this is the purport. /
'Will be stated' — the remainder is: 'in the <s>vṛtti</s>.' /
There, 'the relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> (standard and object of comparison)' — /
Because the statement 'is to be imagined' indicates the suggestedness of precisely that aspect — this is the purport. /
The passage '<s>śabdaśaktyā prakāśamāne</s>' (when manifested by the power of the word) is also favorable to this position; incidentally, he says — 'in the earlier [passage]' etc.
