children.translated_text: As, for example, in the same [work by <s>Bāṇa</s>]: 'like a <s>sayavāya</s> (a particular [combination]) of contradictory substances —
For thus: "even though the youthful darkness is present, [she has] a radiant form" — in passages like these.

children.text: yathā vā mamaiva--- sarvaikaśaraṇamakṣayamadhīśamīśaṃ dhiyāṃ hariṃ kṛṣṇam /
children.translated_text: Or as in [the verse] by myself: '<s>Sarva</s>-<s>eka-śaraṇam</s> (the sole refuge of all / having arrows [as] the sole shelter), <s>akṣayam</s> (imperishable / not declining), <s>adhīśam</s> (supreme lord), <s>īśam dhiyām</s> (lord of thoughts / master of the wise), <s>Harim</s> (<s>Hari</s> / tawny one), <s>Kṛṣṇam</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> / dark one) —

<s>caturātmānam</s> (of fourfold nature / whose self is clever), <s>niṣkriyam</s> (without action / devoid of deeds), <s>arimardanam</s> (destroyer of enemies) — bow to the bearer of the discus (<s>cakradhara</s>)!'

In these examples, when the non-contextual secondary meaning is manifested by the power of the word, lest the sentence be charged with expressing an unconnected meaning — the relation of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) between the non-contextual and contextual meanings is to be imagined through textual capacity — thus this <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), implied by the meaning, is not word-based, and is entirely distinct from <s>anusvāna</s>-type (echo/reverberant) <s>dhvani</s> of the suggested <s>upamā</s> figure. /
Others too — [<s>Locana</s>:] the disconnection has been refuted by the word alone. /
In '<s>yena dhvaste</s>' (by whom destroyed), the disconnection does not appear at all. /
In '<s>tasyā vināpi</s>' (even without her) by the word '<s>api</s>' (even), in '<s>ślāghyā</s>' (praiseworthy) by the additional word, and in '<s>bhramiṃ</s>' etc. by <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) — the disconnection has been refuted: this is the purport. /
'<s>Payobhiḥ</s>' — means by waters and by milk. /
'<s>Saṃhāra</s>' — means destruction, and also gathering into one place. /
'<s>Gāvaḥ</s>' — means rays and cows. /
'Expressing an unconnected meaning' — the meaning is: [a meaning] that is simply not perceived. /
'The relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the purport is: for the purpose of concealing that [disconnection]. /
By this, it has also been conveyed that there is no <s>rūpaṇā</s> (figuration) etc. there. /
'Does not appear' — the purport is: because both [meanings] are contextually relevant as objects of praise. /
'<s>Tātparyam</s>' — up to this [word] is the view stated with '<s>itare tu</s>' (the others, however). /
This view is followed by the authors of the <s>Kuvalayānanda</s> etc. /
'<s>Annata</s>' — /
The <s>prollasad-hāra</s> (gleaming necklace) is where [the necklace gleams], and the <s>prollasantī dhārā</s> (gushing stream) is where [the stream gushes] — and he [is such]. /
'<s>Kālāgarūṇā</s>' — like dark aloe-wood, and dark — <s>payodhara</s> means breast and cloud. /
'Of her' — of the woman; 'and the rainy season' — whom? — a young man and a traveler. /
'<s>Dattānandāḥ</s>' — this is from the <s>Sūryaśataka</s>. /
Drawn forth at the appropriate season earlier, and released afterwards — by those. Of the blazing-rayed [sun], purifying in the highest degree, existing [thus]. /
In the <s>Locana</s>, he glosses the words requiring explanation — '<s>payobhiḥ</s>' etc. /
In the ray-interpretation, 'by waters'; in the cow-interpretation, 'by milk.' /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, '<s>asambaddhārthābhidhāyitvam</s>' — /
The meaning is: the expression of a meaning unconnected with the contextual meaning. /
'<s>Mā prasāṅkṣīt</s>' (lest it be charged) — /
The meaning is: let there be no occasion for that charge. /
Here, to ward off the undesired consequence, he states the purport — '<s>asaṃvedyamānam eva</s>' etc. /
The meaning is: simply not perceived by the connoisseurs — that is 'expressing an unconnected meaning.' /
And [such] <s>alaṅkāras</s> are indeed possible in <s>dhvani</s> that is of the <s>anusvāna</s>-form (echo/reverberant) and rooted in the power of the word. /
For thus, <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) too is seen in the <s>anusvāna</s>-form rooted in the power of the word. /
As, for example, in <s>Bhaṭṭa Bāṇa</s>'s description of the country called <s>Sthāṇvīśvara</s>: 'Where the women walk like elephants and are virtuous, the fair ones are devoted to wealth, the dark ones are attached to jewels, with white-toothed pure faces and breath fragrant with wine.' /
Here indeed, whether the expressible <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) or <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) supporting it — it cannot be said [which is the figure]. /
Because the <s>virodha-alaṅkāra</s> (figure of contradiction) has not been directly manifested by the word. /
For where the <s>virodha-alaṅkāra</s> is directly conveyed by the word, there — in [<s>Locana</s>:] in that <s>śliṣṭokti</s> (punning expression) which is a form of poetry, the <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) or <s>śleṣa</s> (pun) — their <s>saṅkara</s> (combination) — that becomes the domain. /
That domain obtains — this is the meaning. /
Of what? Of the <s>vācya-alaṅkāra</s> (expressible figure), i.e., of the status of being an expressible figure — this is the meaning. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The purport is: the meaning. /
'By that' — the meaning is: because of the statement of imagining the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship as having the nature of <s>upamā</s>, and because that [statement] is synecdochic. /
'<s>Upamā-rūpaṇā</s>' etc. — /
In the locus of <s>dhvani</s> involving <s>upamā</s>, <s>rūpaka</s>, etc., the cognitive act of comparison, figuration, etc. alone [operates] — this is the meaning. /
'Walking like an elephant' — the meaning is: walking like an elephant. /
'And the <s>Śabaras</s>' — the meaning is: and the <s>Caṇḍālas</s>. /
'Thus the contradiction' — the meaning is: the contradiction of going to <s>Caṇḍālas</s> with virtuous conduct. /
And by the first meaning, the resolution of that [contradiction]. /
Thus should be understood in what follows as well. /
'<s>Gaurī</s>' — fair-complexioned, and [consorts of] <s>Pārvatī</s>. /
'<s>Śyāmā</s>' — dark-complexioned, and youthful. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>: 'because not directly manifested by the word' — /
The purport is: because the conjunctive particles '<s>ca</s>' in '<s>śīlavatyaś ca</s>' etc. have a cumulative sense. /
'Or <s>śleṣa</s> — the <s>saṅkara</s>' — the '<s>vā</s>' (or) there between <s>virodha</s> and <s>śleṣa</s> indicates their <s>saṅkara</s> (combination) — this is the meaning. /
'That becomes the domain' — this is an elaboration of that very [point] — 'that' etc. /
The connection of 'of <s>vācya-alaṅkāra</s>' with 'the domain' is shown expectancy-wise — 'of what?' etc. /
He states the literal meaning of 'of <s>vācya-alaṅkāra</s>' — 'of <s>vācya-alaṅkṛti</s>' (of the expressible ornamentation). /
He states the intended meaning — 'of the status of being <s>vācya-alaṅkṛti</s>.' /
Or the domain of <s>śleṣa</s>.

children.text:
atra hi śabdaśaktimūlānusvānarūpo virodhaḥ sphuṭameva pratīyate /
evaṃvido vyatireko 'pi dṛśyate /
yathā mamaiva--- khaṃ ye 'tyujjvalayanti lūnatamaso ye vā nakhodbhāsino locanam tatraiva virodhe śleṣe vā vācyālaṅkāratvaṃ suvacamiti yāvat /
vāleṣu keśeṣvandhakāraḥ kārṣṇyaṃ, bālaḥ pratyagraścāndhakārastamaḥ /
nanu mātaṅgetyādāvapi dharmadvaye yaścakāraḥ sa virodhadyotaka eva /
anyathā pratadharmaṃ sarvadharmānte vā na kvacidvā cakāraḥ syāt yadi samuccayārthaḥ syādityabhiprāyeṇodāharaṇāntaramāha---yatheti /
śaraṇaṃ gṛhamakṣayarūpamagṛhaṃ katham /
yo na dhīśaḥ sa kathaṃ dhiyāmīśaḥ /
yo hariḥ kapilaḥ sa kathaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ /
caturaḥ parākramayukto yasyātmā sa kathaṃ niṣkriyaḥ /
arīṇāmarayuktānāṃ yo nāśayitā sa kathaṃ cakraṃ vahumānena dhārayati /
virodha iti /
virodhanamityarthaḥ /
pratiyata iti /
sphuṭaṃ nocyate kenaciditi bhāvaḥ /
bālapriyā tathā ca virodhaśleṣasaṅkarasya vācyālaṅkṛtitvanirūpitaṃ viṣayatvamiti vākyārthaḥ /
viṣayatvamatrāśrayatvaṃ bodhyam /
phalitamāha---tatraivetyādi /
bhāsvanmūrtiḥ prakāśamānatanuḥ sūryamūrtiśca /
sarvetyādyudāharaṇāntarabhavatārayati---nanvityādi /
dharmadvaye yaścakāra iti /
mātaṅgagāminyaśśīlavatyaśca gauryo vibhavaratāścetyādau dharmadvayavācakānte yaścakāra ityarthaḥ /
evakāreṇa samuccayadyotakatvavyavacchedaḥ /
uktārthe hetumāha---anyathetyādi /
anyathā virodhadyotakatvābhāve tadeti śeṣaḥ /
anyathā cakāro yadi samuccayārthassyāttadā pratidharmaṃ sarvadharmānte vā syāt, kvacidvā na syādityanvayaḥ /
sarvadharmānta ityatra sarvaśabdānta iti ca pāṭhaḥ /
cakārasyātra samuccayārthakatve "ghaṭañca paṭhañca pustakañcānaya, ghaṭaṃ paṭaṃ pustakañcānaya, ghaṭaṃ paṭaṃ pustakamānaya itipatprayogassyādityarthaḥ /
gṛhamagṛhamityādi virūddhārthakathanam /
śaraṇaṃ rakṣitāram /
akṣayaṃ nāśarahitamityādyaviruddhārthā bodhyāḥ virodhanamiti /
virodhanakriyetyarthaḥ /
sphuṭamiti /

children.translated_text: The meaning is: without doubt.

children.text: pratīyata ityasya dhvanyata ityartha ityāha--nocyate kenaciditi /
children.translated_text: The meaning of '<s>pratīyate</s>' (is apprehended) as '<s>dhvanyate</s>' (is suggested) — he says: 'not stated by anyone' etc.
Those who nourish the beauty of lotuses, and those who are cast-lotus-radiant (i.e., whose radiance surpasses lotuses);

children.text: ye mūrdhasvavabhāsinaḥ kṣitibhṛtāṃ ye cāmarāṇāṃ śirāṃ- syākrāmantyubhaye 'pi te dinapateḥ pādāḥ śriye santu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: those who are self-luminous on the peaks of mountains, and those who invade the heads of the immortals — may those feet (<s>pādāḥ</s>, also: rays) of the Lord of the Day (<s>Dinapati</s>, the Sun), both kinds, be for your prosperity!

Here indeed, the <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) of the <s>anusvāna</s>-form (reverberant type) rooted in the power of the word is clearly apprehended. /
A <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) of such a kind is also seen. /
As in [a verse] by myself: 'Those who make the sky exceedingly brilliant, those who shine with clipped darkness, those who —' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] In that very [domain of] <s>virodha</s> or <s>śleṣa</s>, the status of <s>vācya-alaṅkāra</s> (expressible figure) is easy to state — this is the purport. /
'In the locks' — in the hair — darkness [means] blackness, and 'young' means fresh; and darkness [means] the dark. /
Now, in '<s>mātaṅga</s>' etc. too, whatever conjunctive particle ('<s>ca</s>') occurs with two properties — that itself is an indicator of <s>virodha</s> (contradiction). /
Otherwise, that '<s>ca</s>' particle would occur either with each property, or at the end of all properties, or not at all — if it were cumulative in sense — thus, with the intention [of showing this], he cites another example — 'as in' etc. /
'<s>Śaraṇam</s>' — means 'house'; '<s>akṣayam</s>' — means 'imperishable' — [how then can it be] 'houseless'? /
He who is not '<s>dhīśa</s>' (lord of thought) — how can he be '<s>īśa</s> of <s>dhīs</s>' (lord of the wise)? /
He who is <s>Hari</s> (tawny) — how can he be <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (dark)? /
He whose self (<s>ātman</s>) is clever (<s>catura</s>) — how can he be without action (<s>niṣkriya</s>)? /
He who is the destroyer of enemies — how does he hold the discus (<s>cakra</s>) with reverence? /
'<s>Virodha</s>' — the meaning is: contradiction. /
'Is apprehended' — /
The purport is: it is clearly [apprehended], i.e., it is not stated by anyone [explicitly]. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] And thus the purport of the sentence is: the domain of <s>vācya-alaṅkṛti</s> (expressible ornamentation) status has been determined [to belong] to the <s>saṅkara</s> (combination) of <s>virodha</s> and <s>śleṣa</s>. /
The word 'domain' here should be understood as 'locus' (<s>āśrayatva</s>). /
He states the result — 'in that very' etc. /
'<s>Bhāsvanmūrti</s>' — means a radiant body, and also the form of the Sun. /
Citing another example, <s>Abhinavagupta</s> establishes [the point] — 'now' etc. /
'With two properties' — the meaning is: at the juncture of two words denoting two properties in '<s>mātaṅgagāminyaḥ śīlavatyaś ca gauryo vibhavaratāś ca</s>' etc. /
The '<s>eva</s>'-particle excludes the sense of cumulation. /
He states the reason for what was said — 'otherwise' etc. /
Otherwise — in the absence of being an indicator of <s>virodha</s>; 'that' is the remainder. /
Otherwise, if the '<s>ca</s>' particle were cumulative in sense, then it would occur with each property, or at the end of all properties, or not at all — this is the construction. /
'<s>Sarvaśabdānta</s>' is also a variant reading for '<s>sarvadharmānta</s>.' /
If the '<s>ca</s>' particle here were cumulative, [one would expect] usages like 'bring the pot and the cloth and the book,' 'bring the pot, the cloth, and the book,' or 'bring the pot, the cloth, the book' — this is the meaning. /
'House — houseless' etc. — this is the statement of contradictory meanings. /
'<s>Śaraṇam</s>' — means 'protector.' /
'<s>Akṣayam</s>' — 'free from destruction' etc. — the non-contradictory meanings should be understood. /
'Contradiction' — /
The meaning is: the act of contradicting. /
'Clearly' —

children.text:
evamanye 'pi śabdaśaktimūlānusvānarūpavyaṅgyadhvaniprakārāḥ santi te sahṛdayaiḥ svayamanusartavyāḥ /
iha tu granthavistarabhayānna tatprapañcaḥ kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, there are other varieties of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) in the form of <s>anusvāna</s> (resonance) based on the power of words (<s>śabdaśaktimūla</s>) as <s>vyaṅgya</s> (the suggested); these should be traced out by the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (sensitive readers) on their own. Here, however, out of fear of expanding the treatise, their elaboration has not been undertaken.

children.text: arthaśaktyudbhavas tv anyo yatrārthaḥ sa prakāśate /
children.translated_text: But the other, born of the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktyudbhava</s>), is that where the meaning itself shines forth —

children.text: yas tātparyeṇa vastv anyad vyanakty uktiṃ vinā svataḥ // DhvK_2.22 //
children.translated_text: which, by its own purport (<s>tātparya</s>), suggests another object without [explicit] verbal expression. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.22 //
But the other, born of the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktyudbhava</s>), is that where the meaning itself shines forth —
which, by its own purport, suggests another object without [explicit] verbal expression. // 22 //

children.text: locanam nakhairudbhāsante ye 'vaśyaṃ khe gagane na udbhāsanta /
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] Those that shine forth with nails do not necessarily shine forth in the sky, in the heavens —
both are of the nature of rays, and have the form of parts such as fingers, heels, etc. — this is the meaning. // 21 //

children.translated_text: they step upon, that is, touch at the time of obeisance, the heads of the immortals (<s>amarāṇām</s>), the gods (<s>devānām</s>), and do not shine forth upon them.
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Fingers' etc. —
The meaning is: 'feet' (<s>caraṇāḥ</s>).

children.text: a6 lūnatamastvādidharmaiḥ kiraṇatulyānāṃ dinapateścaraṇānāṃ gaganānudbhāsitvādibhiḥ kiraṇebhyo vyatireko dhvanita iti bodhyam // 2.1 //
children.translated_text: It should be understood that the distinction (<s>vyatireka</s>) of the feet of the Lord of the Day (<s>dinapati</s>), which are equal to rays by their properties of destroying darkness etc., from [actual] rays is suggested through their not shining forth in the sky etc. // 2.1 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Having set aside <s>dhvani</s> born of word-power (<s>śabdaśaktyudbhava</s>), he now shows <s>dhvani</s> born of meaning-power (<s>arthaśaktyudbhava</s>) — with '<s>artha</s>' etc. 'Another' means: different from that born of word-power. The phrase 'by itself, by purport' (<s>svatas tātparyeṇa</s>) — this expression is aimed at excluding the operation of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) and states the operation of suggestion (<s>dhvanana</s>), not the <s>tātparya</s> power [itself]; for it has been said earlier that that [<s>tātparya</s> power] is exhausted in the apprehension of the expressed meaning (<s>vācyārtha</s>) alone. With this very intent, [<s>Bālapriyā</s> explains:] '<s>kha</s>' means the sky (<s>ākāśa</s>). Those rays (<s>kiraṇāḥ</s>) that have destroyed (<s>lūna</s>, <s>vināśita</s>) darkness, great sin — those [are meant]. 'And those' — those are the feet (<s>caraṇāḥ</s>). He states both the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) and the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) meaning of 'shining with nails' (<s>nakhodbhāsina</s>) — with 'with nails' etc. Those rays that nourish the beauty (<s>śrī</s>, <s>kānti</s>) of lotuses (<s>saroruhāṇām</s>, <s>pajhānām</s>) — those are the feet. 'Cast down' (<s>kṣipta</s>) — those rays whose lotus-lustre is cast down, whose lotus-beauty is destroyed, and those feet [that rest] upon the peaks and summits of mountains (<s>kṣitibhṛtām</s>, <s>parvatānām</s>) —

children.text:
'arthe'tyādi kārikāyāṃ 'anyaḥ arthaśaktyudbhavastu tatra bhavati, yatra sa arthaḥ prakāśate, ya uktiṃ vinā svatastātparyeṇa anyadvastu vyanaktī'tyanvayaḥ /
kasmādanya ityatrāha locane---śabdeti /

itīdamiti sambandhaḥ /
idaṃ padamiti ca pāṭhaḥ /
seti /
tātparyaśaktirityarthaḥ /
anenetyādi /
svatastātparyeṇetyasya vivaraṇaṃ vṛttau--'svasāmarthyādi'titi bhāvaḥ /
'śabdavyāpāra'miti /
abhidhāmityarthaḥ /
vṛttau'līle'tyādi /
idamadhomukhatvasyāpyupalakṣaṇam /
'prakāśayatī'ti /
anubhāvavatvādvyañjayatītyarthaḥ /
yadi lajjātmakavyabhicāripratītistarhyayamalakṣyakramavyaṅgyasyaiva dhvanerviṣayo na tu vastudhvaneriti śaṅkate--'na ce'tyādi /

children.translated_text: He resolves it — with '<s>yataḥ</s>' etc.

children.text: nanvatra vyabhicāriṇo vācyatvarūpasākṣācchabdaniveditatvasya kathanamasaṅgataṃ, yatrārthaḥ svasāmarthyādarthāntaramabhivyanākti śabdavyāpāraṃ vinaiva so 'rthaśakyudbhavo nāmānusvānopamavyaṅgyo dhvaniḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the statement here of the <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) being directly communicated by words, i.e., their being <s>vācya</s> (expressed), is inconsistent [with the earlier position]. Where a meaning by its own capacity suggests another meaning without the operation of words — that is the <s>dhvani</s> called <s>arthaśaktyudbhava</s> (born of meaning-power), in the form of <s>vyaṅgya</s> (the suggested), comparable to <s>anusvāna</s> (resonance).
For example: 'When the divine sage (<s>devarṣi</s>) spoke thus, at her father's side, with face downcast,
<s>Pārvatī</s> began counting the petals of the <s>līlākamalapatra</s> (play-lotus).'

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In the <s>kārikā</s> beginning with '<s>arthe</s>' etc., the syntactic connection (<s>anvaya</s>) is: 'Another, born of the power of meaning, is that which arises where that meaning shines forth, which by itself through purport suggests another object without [explicit] statement.' To the question 'why another?', the <s>Locana</s> answers — with '<s>śabda</s>' etc. He explains '<s>svatas tātparyeṇa</s>' — with '<s>svataḥ</s>' etc. The connection is: 'thus this.' 'This expression' (<s>idaṃ padam</s>) is also a reading. '<s>Sā</s>' — the meaning is: the <s>tātparya</s> power. 'By this' etc. — the explanation in the <s>vṛtti</s> of '<s>svatas tātparyeṇa</s>' is 'by its own capacity' (<s>svasāmarthya</s>) etc. — this is the purport. '<s>Śabdavyāpāram</s>' — the meaning is: <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation). In the <s>vṛtti</s>, '<s>līlā</s>' etc. — this is also an <s>upalakṣaṇa</s> (indication) of the downward-gazing [mentioned earlier]. '<s>Prakāśayati</s>' — the meaning is: 'suggests' (<s>vyañjayati</s>), because it possesses the nature of an <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent). If the cognition of <s>lajjā</s> (modesty) as a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) [is intended], then this would be a case of <s>dhvani</s> of the <s>alakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s> (imperceptible-sequence suggestion) type alone, not of <s>vastudhvani</s> (factual suggestion) — he raises this doubt with '<s>na ca</s>' etc.

children.text:
atra hi līlākamalapatrragaṇanamupasarjanīkṛtasvarūpaṃ śabdavyāpāraṃ vinaivārthāntaraṃ vyabhicāribhāvalakṣaṇaṃ prakāśayati /
na cāyamalakṣyakramavyaṅgyasyaiva dhvanerviṣayaḥ /
yato yatra sākṣācchabdaniveditebhyo vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāribhyo rasādīnāṃ pratītiḥ, sa tasya kevalasya mārgaḥ /
yathā kumārasambhave madhuprasaṅge vasantapuṣpābharaṇaṃ vahantyā devyā āgamanādivarṇanaṃ manobhavaśarasandhānaparyantaṃ śambhośca parivṛttadhairyasya ceṣṭāviśeṣavarṇanādi sākṣācchabdaniveditam /
locanam vṛttau vyācaṣṭe---yatrārthaḥ svasāmarthyāditi /
svata iti śabdaḥ svaśabdena vyākhyātaḥ /
uktiṃ vineti vyācaṣṭe---śabdavyāpāraṃ vinaiveti /
udāharati---yathā evamiti /
arthāntaramiti lajjātmakam /
sākṣāditi /
vyabhicāraṇāṃ yatrālakṣyakramatayā vyavadhivandhyaiva pratipattiḥ svavibhāvādabalāttatra sākṣācchabdaniveditatvaṃ vivakṣitamiti na pūrvāparavirodhaḥ /
pūrvaṃ hyuktaṃ vyabhicāriṇāmapi bhāvatvānna svaśabdataḥ pratipattirityādi vistarataḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati--yadyapi rasabhāvādirartho dhvanyamāna eva bhavati na vācyaḥ kadācidapi, tathāpi na sarvo 'lakṣyakramasya viṣayaḥ /
yatra hi vibhāvānubhāvebhyaḥ sthāyigatebhyo vyabhicārigatebhyaśca pūrṇobhyo jhaṭityeva bālapriyā tasya tadabhāvasya pūrvamuktatvādityatassākṣācchabdaniveditatvaṃ vivṛṇoti locane---vyabhicāriṇāmityādi /
'yatra vyabhicāriṇāṃ svasvavibhāvādibalādalakṣyakramatayā vyavadhivandhyaiva pratipattiri'tyanvayaḥ /
vyavadhivandhyā avyavadhānā /
pūrvoktaṃ smārayati---pūrvamityādi /
ityādi vistarataḥ pūrvamuktaṃ hīti sambandhaḥ /
'tasmādayamanyo dhvaneḥ prakāra' ityantavṛttigranthasya sārārthamāha---etaduktamityādi /
sarvaḥ alakṣyakramasya iticchedaḥ /
sthāyigatebhyaḥ sthāyisambandhibhyaḥ /
'nirvāṇe'tyādi kumārasambhavatṛtīyasargastham /
ityādāvityādipadena 'āvarjitā kiñcidive'tyādeḥ iha tu sāmarthyākṣiptavyabhicārimukhena rasapratītiḥ tasmādayamanyo dhvaneḥ prakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: In '<s>ityādau</s>' etc. — by the word '<s>ādi</s>', [the passage] '<s>āvarjitā kiñcid iva</s>' etc. [is included]. Here, however, the cognition of <s>rasa</s> is through the medium of <s>vyabhicārins</s> implied by [the meaning's own] capacity (<s>sāmarthyākṣipta</s>); therefore this is another variety of <s>dhvani</s>.
[<s>Locana</s>:] The manifestation of <s>rasa</s> therein, however, belongs to the <s>alakṣyakrama</s> (imperceptible-sequence) type.
For example: 'Then, as if rekindling his valor, which had become mostly extinguished, through [her] bodily excellence,
the princess of the immovable [Himālaya], followed by the forest deities, was seen [by <s>Śiva</s>].'

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Here, the counting of the play-lotus petals, whose own nature has been subordinated, reveals another meaning — namely, the <s>vyabhicāribhāva</s> (transitory emotion) [of modesty] — without any operation of words. And this is not a case of <s>dhvani</s> of the <s>alakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s> type alone, because where the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. arises from <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) that are directly communicated by words — that is the exclusive domain of that [<s>alakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s> type]. As in the <s>Kumārasambhava</s>, in the episode of <s>Madhu</s> (Spring/Love), the description of the Goddess's arrival wearing the ornaments of spring flowers, up to the fitting of <s>Manobhava</s>'s (Cupid's) arrow, and the description of the particular gestures of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) whose composure has been overturned — all this is directly communicated by words. [<s>Locana</s>:] He explains the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'where the meaning by its own capacity' etc. The word '<s>svataḥ</s>' is glossed by the word '<s>sva</s>' (one's own). He explains 'without statement' — 'without the operation of words.' He gives the example — 'as, thus' etc. 'Another meaning' means that which is of the nature of <s>lajjā</s> (modesty). 'Directly' — where the apprehension of <s>vyabhicārins</s> is in the <s>alakṣyakrama</s> (imperceptible-sequence) mode, being entirely dependent on their own <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. without any intermediary, there the 'being directly communicated by words' is what is intended — thus there is no contradiction between the earlier and later [statements]. For earlier it was said in detail that even <s>vyabhicārins</s>, being of the nature of <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions), are not apprehended from their own words etc. This amounts to saying: although <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc. as suggested meanings are always only suggested (<s>dhvanyamāna</s>) and never expressed (<s>vācya</s>), still, not all [cases] fall within the domain of <s>alakṣyakrama</s>. For where from <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> pertaining to the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) and from those pertaining to the <s>vyabhicārins</s>, all being complete, instantly — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] since the absence of that [distinction] has been previously stated, therefore he explains the 'being directly communicated by words' in the <s>Locana</s> — with '<s>vyabhicāriṇām</s>' etc. The syntactic construction is: 'where the apprehension of the <s>vyabhicārins</s>, being in the <s>alakṣyakrama</s> mode by the force of their respective <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., is entirely without intermediary (<s>vyavadhivandhyā</s>).' '<s>Vyavadhivandhyā</s>' means 'without intervening [steps]' (<s>avyavadhānā</s>). He recalls what was said before — with '<s>pūrvam</s>' etc. The connection is: 'it was said before in detail, for...' He states the essential meaning of the <s>vṛtti</s> passage ending with 'therefore this is another variety of <s>dhvani</s>' — with '<s>etad uktam</s>' etc. The word-division is: '<s>sarvaḥ alakṣyakramasya</s>.' '<s>Sthāyigatebhyaḥ</s>' means: 'from those pertaining to the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion).' '<s>Nirvāṇe</s>' etc. is from the third canto of the <s>Kumārasambhava</s>.

children.text: saṃmohanaṃ nāma ca puṣpadhanvā dhanuṣyamoghaṃ samadhatta bāṇam /
children.translated_text: 'And <s>Puṣpadhanvā</s> (the Flower-armed [Cupid]) placed upon his bow an unerring arrow called <s>Saṃmohana</s> (Bewilderment).'
By this, the employment of the <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) function has been stated.
'And <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), his composure somewhat overturned, like the ocean at the commencement of moonrise,
cast his eyes upon the face of <s>Umā</s>, whose lower lip [was like] a <s>bimbaphala</s> (bimba fruit).'

In this and similar [passages], the description of the naturally fitting character constitutes the complete <s>ālambana</s> (foundational) and <s>uddīpana</s> (stimulant) <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant). 'And the three-eyed one (<s>Trilocana</s>) began to accept [her], out of love for the one dear [to him] (<s>praṇayipriya</s>) —'

children.translated_text: 'Of the reader' (<s>pratipattṛ</s>) is the remainder.

children.text: yatra ca śabdavyāpārasahāyo 'rthontarasya vyañjakatvenopādīyate sa nāsya dhvanerviṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And where [a meaning] is employed as a suggestor of another meaning with the assistance of the operation of words — that is not within the scope of this [type of] <s>dhvani</s>.
For example: 'By the clever woman, knowing the <s>viṭa</s> (libertine) to be absent-minded at the time of the rendezvous,
the play-lotus, in which her intention was placed through laughing glances, was closed.'

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Here, because the Goddess was already inclined toward him (<s>Śiva</s>) from the very beginning, and because he had now become favorably disposed toward her, and because of the deepening of the partiality indicated through loving affection (<s>praṇayipriyatā</s>), the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) in the form of <s>rati</s> (love) and the <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) such as eagerness (<s>autsukyā</s>), impetuosity (<s>āvega</s>), fickleness (<s>cāpalya</s>), joy (<s>harṣa</s>), and longing (<s>ādeśa</s>) — for all these, the group of <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) has become universalized (<s>sādhāraṇībhūta</s>) and is thereby manifested. Thus the savoring (<s>carvaṇā</s>) of the <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> culminates in the savoring of the <s>vyabhicārins</s>. Due to the dependence (<s>pāratantrya</s>) of the <s>vyabhicārins</s>, the savoring of the <s>sthāyin</s>, which is like a thread (<s>sūtra</s>) [stringing together] garlands (<s>srak</s>), has the character of <s>alakṣyakrama</s> (imperceptible sequence). Here, however [in the '<s>evaṃvādini</s>' verse], the counting of lotus petals and the downcast gaze — since these are possible for maidens even for other reasons — the heart [of the reader] does not immediately come to rest in <s>lajjā</s> (modesty); rather, [it arrives there] through the recollection of the previously narrated events such as the penance etc. [of the Goddess]. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Sampūrṇa</s>' etc. — '<s>sampūrṇa</s>' qualifies the description. The <s>ālambana</s> (foundational determinant) here is the Goddess; the <s>uddīpana</s> (stimulant determinant) is beauty, spring flowers, ornaments, etc. '<s>Vibhāvatopayoga</s>' — the meaning is: the employment of the <s>vibhāva</s> function. 'Stated' — the meaning is: shown by '<s>pratigrahītum</s>' etc. and '<s>saṃmohanam</s>' etc. The connection of 'here indeed' is with '<s>anubhāvavargaḥ prakāśitaḥ</s>' (the group of <s>anubhāvas</s> has been manifested). '<s>Tatpravaṇatvāt</s>' — the meaning is: because of [her] attachment to <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). '<s>Tasya</s>' — the meaning is: of <s>Hara</s>. '<s>Tadunmukhī</s>' — the meaning is: favorably disposed toward the Goddess. '<s>Praṇayipriyatayā</s>' — the meaning is: through the undertaking of the acceptance of the garland etc. occasioned by that [love]. The connection is with '<s>sūcitasya</s>' (of what is indicated). The indicated partiality (<s>pakṣapāta</s>), which is in the form of the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) characterized by <s>rasa</s> deepening, and the <s>vyabhicārins</s> — the connection is: the group of <s>anubhāvas</s> of those. The <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) takes the form of the overturning of composure, the employment of the eyes, etc. '<s>Iti</s>' is in the sense of cause (<s>hetu</s>). 'By the savoring of <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> alone' — by the particle '<s>eva</s>', all other causes are excluded. '<s>Pāratantrya</s>' — the meaning is: because of dependence on the <s>sthāyin</s>. '<s>Srak</s>' — the <s>vyabhicārins</s> are like garlands; the <s>sthāyin</s> is like the thread. 'Here, however' — the meaning is: in the [verse beginning] '<s>evaṃ vādini</s>' etc. '<s>Anyathāpi</s>' — the meaning is: even for a reason other than <s>lajjā</s>. '<s>Hṛdayam</s>' — the remainder is: 'of the reader' (<s>pratipattṛ</s>). 'There' — the meaning is: in [the emotion of] <s>lajjā</s>. '<s>Kramavyaṅgyataiva</s>' — the remainder is: 'of <s>lajjā</s>.' '<s>Prāk</s>' — the meaning is: through the recollection of the previously occurring narrative of the Goddess's penance etc.; through that medium. '<s>Smāraṇena</s>' is also a reading. 'There, in <s>lajjā</s>' — [the heart] creates, produces [the cognition].

children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Here, the suggestive capacity of the closing of the playful lotus has been communicated through the utterance itself. [<s>Locana</s>:] There it produces apprehension — hence it is precisely suggestion with perceptible sequence (<s>kramavyaṅgya</s>). But <s>rasa</s> here too shines forth only from a distance, when the transitory emotion (<s>vyabhicārin</s>) in its own nature is contemplated — hence, relative to that, it is precisely of imperceptible sequence. However, relative to <s>lajjā</s> (modesty), there is perceptible sequence. The word "only" (<s>eva</s>) and the word "mere" (<s>kevala</s>) indicate precisely this point. To show what is excluded by the statement "without the utterance," he begins — "where, and" etc. The particle "ca" has the meaning of "but" (<s>tu</s>). "Of this" — the purport is: even there, imperceptible-sequence [suggestion] would indeed exist. He gives an example — "at the tryst" etc. "Suggestive capacity" — the rest is: with respect to the twilight hour. "Through the utterance itself" — meaning: through the first three quarters. And even though here, when another word is present, no word has the denotative power with respect to the meaning of "twilight," the suggestive capacity is not disrupted — nevertheless, this meaning has been stated by the words themselves, and this meaning is the suggestor of another meaning. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "Precisely of perceptible-sequence suggestion" — the meaning is: the suggestion of <s>lajjā</s> is precisely of perceptible sequence. "<s>Rasa</s>" — meaning <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. "Here too" — in "thus speaking" etc. as well. "Only from a distance" — only after a delay. The connection is with "when contemplated." The apprehension of the transitory emotion of <s>lajjā</s> comes only after a delay, and when that apprehension occurs, the <s>rasa</s>-apprehension comes instantly — this is the meaning. "Relative to that" — relative to <s>rasa</s>. "Precisely of imperceptible sequence" — by the word "precisely" (<s>eva</s>), perceptible-sequence status is excluded. Then how is perceptible-sequence status stated here? — to this he says "relative to <s>lajjā</s>" etc. "The word 'only' and the word 'mere'" — meaning: the word <s>eva</s> in "of imperceptible-sequence suggestion only" and the word <s>kevala</s> in "of that alone." In the <s>vṛtti</s>, "of this <s>dhvani</s>" means "of perceptible-sequence <s>dhvani</s>." He states the result of that statement — "but of imperceptible sequence" etc. "At the tryst" — him whose mind, at the time of the tryst, [was set on] the gallant (<s>viṭa</s>), and who wished to know about that; hence, through the two laughing eyes, whose intention, i.e., the desire to know the tryst-time, was communicated — him. The connection is with "having known." [In the <s>Locana</s>:] "No word has the denotative power with respect to the meaning of twilight" — the meaning is: the meaning in the form of twilight is not conveyed by any word through denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>). "Hence" (<s>iti</s>) — in the sense of reason. "Is not disrupted" — and therefore the domain of <s>dhvani</s> is indeed appropriate here — this is the purport. "Through the words" — the construction is: that this meaning is a suggestor of another meaning has been stated through the words themselves. The suggestive capacity of the lotus-closing with respect to the twilight hour has been demonstrated through the words constituting the first three quarters — this is the meaning. And hence, the connection is: that is set aside. "Concealing" — meaning: whose essence is the beauty that arises from being concealed. "And thus, the life-breath [of poetry]" —
Where the suggested meaning, though drawn forth by the power of word, meaning,
Is again revealed by the poet through his own utterance — that is a different <s>alaṅkāra</s> of <s>dhvani</s>. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.23 //
Where the suggested meaning, though drawn forth by the power of word, meaning,
Is again revealed by the poet through his own utterance — that is a different <s>alaṅkāra</s> of <s>dhvani</s>. // 23 //

śabdaśaktyārthaśaktyā śabdārthaśaktyā vākṣipto 'pi vyaṅgyo 'rthaḥ kavinā punaryatra svoktyā prakāśīkriyate so 'smādanusvānopamavyaṅgyāddhvaneranya evālaṅkāraḥ /
alakṣyakramavyaṅgyasya vā dhvaneḥ sati sambhave sa tādṛganyo 'laṅkāraḥ /

yathā kaścidāha--'gambhīro 'haṃ na me kṛtyaṃ ko 'pi veda na sūcitam /
children.translated_text: As when someone says: "I am profound; no one knows my purpose; nothing has been hinted at;
I speak a little."
Thereby, the meaning intended to indicate profundity (<s>gāmbhīrya</s>) is, on the contrary, made manifest.
Hence he says: "suggestive capacity" and "through the utterance itself." // 2.2 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] The suggested meaning, though drawn forth by the power of word, the power of meaning, or the power of both word and meaning, where it is again made manifest by the poet through his own utterance — that is a different <s>alaṅkāra</s> from this <s>dhvani</s> of reverberation-like suggestion. Or: given the possibility of <s>dhvani</s> of imperceptible-sequence suggestion, that is a different <s>alaṅkāra</s> of such a kind. [<s>Locana</s>:] And hence, what constitutes the life-breath of <s>dhvani</s> — the beauty born of being concealed — that is set aside.

children.translated_text: "Intended to indicate profundity" —
The meaning is: the meaning in the form of absence of facial change etc. that indicates profundity.
"Made manifest" — revealed.

children.text: uktābhiprāyeṇaiva vṛttau 'vyañjakatvamuktyaiva nivedita' mityuktaṃ, na tu vyaṅgyārthaḥ śabdāntareṇa pradarśita itītyāha--ata eveti // 2.2 //
children.translated_text: With the very stated intent, it was said in the <s>vṛtti</s> "the suggestive capacity has been communicated through the utterance itself" — not that the suggested meaning was demonstrated by another word — thus he says "hence" etc. // 2.2 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] The <s>vṛttikāra</s> introduces a transitional passage that serves the dual purpose of concluding the two previously discussed types and indicating the third type, with the thought "I shall accomplish both with a single effort" — with "and thus" etc. Therefore, by the two stated types, this third type too should be understood — this is the meaning. "Word and meaning" — "word" and "meaning" are reduced to "word-meaning" by <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (single-remainder compound). "A different [<s>alaṅkāra</s>]" — meaning: that is not <s>dhvani</s>, but rather a figure such as <s>śleṣa</s> etc. Or alternatively, by the word "<s>dhvani</s>" [is meant] the imperceptible-sequence [<s>dhvani</s>]; of that principal <s>alaṅkārya</s> (<s>aṅgin</s>) — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the life-breath. He gives an example — with "as" etc. "Profound" — a profound person does not speak his purpose in words, but sometimes hints at it — with this worldly convention in mind, this is someone's utterance. I am not profound. Hence, my purpose, when hinted, no one knows, i.e., perceives. Hence I speak a little — this is the construction. "Thereby" — meaning: by the stated sentence.

children.translated_text: "That" (<s>sa</s>) — meaning: the suggested meaning.

children.translated_text: The half-verse beginning with "different" is explained in two ways in the <s>vṛtti</s>; following that, he explains the first meaning in the <s>Locana</s> — "not <s>dhvani</s>" etc.

children.text: tatra śabdaśaktyā yathā--- vatse mā gā viṣādaṃ śvasanamurujavaṃ santyajordhvapravṛttaṃ kampaḥ ko vā guruste bhavatu balabhidā jṛmbhitenātra yāhi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] There, through word-power, as in: "Dear child, do not go to despair; abandon the heavy, swift breath rising upward; what trembling is this — or is your guru great? Go here, where <s>Balabhit</s> (<s>Indra</s>) has stretched forth —

children.text: pratyākhyānaṃ surāṇāmiti bhayaśamanacchajhanā kārayitvā yasmai lakṣmīmadvādvaḥ sa dahatu duritaṃ manthamūḍhāṃ payodhiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'The rejection of the gods' — having caused her, through the pretext of allaying fear, [to understand that] he to whom <s>Lakṣmī</s> was given — may that ocean, in which the churning-bewildered [<s>Lakṣmī</s> was confused], burn away sin!"

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Since the literal meaning of "and thus" lacks coherence, he explains by providing a transitional interpretation — "the two previously discussed types" etc. "The two previously discussed types" — meaning: the two types of <s>dhvani</s> rooted in word-power and meaning-power. "The third type" — meaning: the type of <s>dhvani</s> rooted in the power of both word and meaning. "By <s>ekaśeṣa</s>" — "word" and "meaning" [combine as] "word-meaning," and "word-meaning" and "word-meaning" [combine as] "word-meanings," of those the power — thus all three divisions are captured — this is the purport. In the verse, the reading is "<s>kṣipto 'pi</s>." The word-division is: <s>ākṣiptaḥ</s>. "That" (<s>sa</s>) is a back-reference to "where" (<s>yatra</s>). Meaning: that poem. Or alternatively, the rest is "there."

children.translated_text: "Here" —
The meaning is: with respect to <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s>, who is distinguished by extraordinary qualities.

children.text: arthaśaktyā yathā---- ambā śete 'tra vṛddhā pariṇatavayasāmagraṇaritra tāto niḥśeṣāgārakarmaśramaśithilatanuḥ kumbhadāsī tathātra /
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Through meaning-power, as in: "Mother sleeps here, aged; and father, the chief vessel of those advanced in years, his body weakened by the exhaustion of all household work; and the pot-maidservant likewise here;

children.text: asmin pāpāhamekā katipayadivasaproṣitaprāṇanāthā pānthāyetthaṃ taruṇyā kathitamavasaravyāhṛtivyājapūrvam //
children.translated_text: In this [house] I alone, a sinner, whose lord of life has been away for a few days" — thus was spoken by the young woman to the traveler, with the pretext of narrating the evening situation. //

[<s>Locana</s>:] "That suggested meaning" — the meaning is: it is a second, extraordinary <s>alaṅkāra</s> different from the merely expressible figure. He will explain in the <s>vṛtti</s> in two ways in just this manner. "Despair" (<s>viṣāda</s>) — <s>viṣa</s> (poison) plus <s>ada</s> (eating), i.e., <s>Śiva</s> [the poison-consumer]. "Rising upward" — here the second meaning "fire" should be understood. "Trembling" (<s>kampa</s>) — the lord of waters; or: is <s>Ka</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) your guru? "By <s>Balabhit</s> (<s>Indra</s>) stretching forth" — meaning: intoxicated with the pride of sovereignty. And "stretching forth" (<s>jṛmbhita</s>) — it breaks (<s>bhinatti</s>) strength (<s>bala</s>) because it involves bodily contortion and causes fatigue. "The rejection" — by the very words (<s>vacas</s>), the second meaning is denoted here — this has been communicated. "Having caused" — for she, <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), having placed the lotus-eyed one (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) in her heart, arose [from the ocean] and herself rejected the other gods. But due to her natural delicacy, she was bewildered by the wave-breaking of the ocean agitated by <s>Mandara</s> — and he, while awakening her, accomplished what was appropriate to that [situation] — by revealing faults elsewhere [in other gods like <s>Śiva</s>] through words like "despair" etc., and here [to <s>Viṣṇu</s>] through a particular gesture of "go here" that showed regard for all [his] virtues. Hence he says "bewildered by the churning." [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] "That suggested meaning." She explains the second [interpretation] — "or alternatively" etc. In the first interpretation, "of <s>dhvani</s>" is an ablative referring to perceptible-sequence <s>dhvani</s>; in this [second] interpretation, it is a genitive referring to imperceptible-sequence <s>dhvani</s> — thus she says "by the word <s>dhvani</s>" etc. "Stated" is to be supplied. "Different of such a kind" — she glosses the word "different" following the <s>vṛtti</s> — "merely expressible" etc. The elaboration of "of such a kind" — "extraordinary." "Dear child" — O child, do not go to grief. Abandon the heavy, swift breath — the deep sighing — rising upward. And the reading "cover up" (<s>saṃvṛṇu</s>) [also exists]. Since the literal meaning of "great guru" etc. is clear, he explains the other meaning — "poison" etc. "Despair" (<s>viṣāda</s>) — meaning: <s>Śiva</s>. The elaboration of "rising upward" — "fire." "And the second meaning should be understood" — the meaning is: the aggregation "breath and [that which is] rising upward" should be known. "Guru" — father. He states the literal meaning of "by <s>Balabhit</s>'s stretching forth" incidentally — "stretching forth" etc. He shows the revelation of the second meaning through the poet's own utterance — with "rejection" etc. "Through words themselves" — the connection is with "communicated." "The second meaning" — meaning: the meaning in the form of abandoning <s>Śiva</s> and other gods. "Having caused" — the causative sense here takes the form of performing what is appropriate to that [situation], not of impelling the inactive to act, since that would be incongruent with <s>rasa</s> — thus he says "for she" etc. The connection is: "due to delicacy, bewildered." "Her" is to be supplied. The construction is: he, the ocean, while awakening, accomplished what was appropriate. "He" — the ocean. "Elsewhere" — meaning: with respect to the gods <s>Śiva</s> etc. "By revealing faults" — meaning: by manifesting faults such as poison-eating through the words "despair" etc.

ambā tāta ityābhyāṃ pitrornaisargikavātsalyaśālitvena tau mama sarvatrāpyanukūlāveveti /
tadviseṣaṇābhyāṃ nidrāparavaśatvaṃ parasāhāyyaṃ vināśayanādutthānāśaktatvamityādi, niśśeṣetyādinā dāsyā gāḍhanidritatvam, uktairhetubhisteṣāmanāśaṅkanīyatvaṃ, dāsītyanena svajñāvartitvaṃ, pāpetyanenādyāvādhesarasasambhogānubhavarāhityam, eketyanena puruṣāntarānubhogābhāvaḥ, ata eva sambhogautsukyaṃ, katipayetyādinā patyuracirātpratyāgamanamanāśaṅkyamiti prāṇanāthaityanena pativiṣayakānurāgābhāva iti ca dyotyata ityūhyamiti bhāvaḥ /
itīti hetau /
svakaṇṭhena noktamiti /
svayaṃ vyākhyānena na pradarśitamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Through both powers [of word and meaning], as in: 'By a glance stolen by the eclipse of <s>Keśava</s>' etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Thus, in the stated manner — under the pretext of warding off fear, rejecting the gods, having caused <s>Lakṣmī</s> to be churned from the ocean — the ocean gave her to him; may he burn away your sin — this is the syntactic connection. /
'<s>Amba</s>' (Mother) — /
Here, the suggestive capacity of each individual word is easily imaginable by connoisseurs — hence it was not stated in the commentator's own words. /
The word '<s>vyāja</s>' (pretext) here is a self-expression [by the poet]. /
Thus, under the guise of concluding, having examined the two types with examples, he states the third type: '<s>ubhaya</s>' etc. /
The word-power, for its part, [operates] through the word-<s>śleṣa</s> involving '<s>goparāga</s>' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Sakala</s>' — /
'Showing the esteem, i.e., one's own high regard, for all the qualities related to the Lord' — this is the meaning. /
'For that very reason' — /
'Because the causative meaning [implies] the capacity to accomplish' — this is the meaning. /
'Churned from the ocean' — /
'An indicator of that' — this is the purport. /
He explains the second half: '<s>iti</s>' etc. /
'Having caused <s>Lakṣmī</s> to be produced' — /
The object-designation [is obtained] by the rule '<s>hṛ-kror anyatarasyām</s>.' /
A certain <s>svairiṇī</s> (wanton woman), her passion inflamed upon seeing a handsome traveler, says to him: '<s>Amba</s>' (Mother!) — /
'Sleeps' — this carries over to what follows as well. /
'Of those who have reached advanced age' — of the old. /
'Whose body is weakened by the exhaustion from all the household tasks that she herself performed' — such is she. /
'On the occasion' — /
The utterance of the occasion — of the pretext in the form of the mother's sleeping etc. at that place — is the pretext; that which has that as its prior [portion] — such is [the verse]. /
'Here the two of us can sport at will, no one would know — tormented by desire from seeing you, gratify me with love' — thus the speaker is indicating [her intention]; this is suggested to the connoisseurs who know the distinguishing features of the speaker etc. /
But the suggested meaning — preceded by the pretext of the statement about the occasion — was disclosed by the poet through the word '<s>vyāja</s>' (pretext). /
'Easily imaginable' — /
By '<s>ambā</s>' and '<s>tāta</s>' (Mother, Father): 'Being endowed with natural parental affection, those two are always favorable to me everywhere' — /
By the qualifiers of those two [parents]: the being overpowered by sleep, the inability to rise from bed without another's help — and so forth; by '<s>niśśeṣa</s>' etc.: the deep sleep of the maid; by the stated reasons: that they are not to be suspected; by '<s>dāsī</s>': her being under one's own command; by '<s>pāpa</s>': the absence of experience of the pleasure of union from the time of her youth; by '<s>ekā</s>': the absence of enjoyment with any other man; and for that very reason, the eagerness for union; by '<s>katipaya</s>' etc.: that the husband's return is not to be feared shortly — '<s>prāṇanātha</s>' (lord of life) — and the absence of love toward the husband — thus it is to be surmised — this is the purport. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — in the sense of reason. /
'Not stated in his own words' — /
'Not displayed through his own commentary' — this is the meaning. /
[<s>Kārikā</s>:] That whose body is produced solely through bold expression (<s>prauḍhokti</s>), and that which is naturally possible (<s>svataḥ sambhavī</s>) —

children.text: artho 'pi dvividho jñeyo vastuno 'nyasya dīpakaḥ // DhvK_2.24 //
children.translated_text: the meaning too should be known as twofold: an illuminator (<s>dīpaka</s>) of a content other [than itself]. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.24 //
[Repeated <s>kārikā</s>:] That whose body is produced solely through bold expression, and that which is naturally possible —
the meaning too should be known as twofold: an illuminator of a content other [than itself]. // 24 //

children.text: arthaśaktyudbhavānuraṇanarūpavyaṅgye dhvanau yo vyañjako 'rtha uktastasyāpi dvau prakārau---kaveḥ kavinibaddhasya vā vaktuḥ prauḍhoktimātraniṣpannaśarīra ekaḥ, svatassambhavī ca dvitīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Of the <s>dhvani</s> whose suggested content has the form of a reverberation and arises from the power of meaning — the meaning which is the suggestor has two kinds: one whose body is produced solely through the bold expression of the poet or of a speaker created by the poet, and the second which is naturally possible (<s>svataḥ sambhavī</s>). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The meaning-power, for its part, [operates] through the context. /

children.text: yāvadatra rādhāramaṇasyākhilataruṇījanacchannānurāgagarimāspadatvaṃ na viditaṃ tāvadarthāntarasyāpratīteḥ, saleśamiti cātra svoktiḥ // 2.3 //
children.translated_text: As long as the status of <s>Rādhā</s>'s lover [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] as one whose depth lies in secret passion for all young women is not known, so long the apprehension of another meaning [is absent]; and '<s>sa-leśam</s>' (with a trace) — here too is a self-expression [by the poet]. // 23 //

children.text:
evamarthaśaktyudbhavasya sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ kṛtam. śleṣādyalaṅkarebhyaścāsya vibhakto viṣaya uktaḥ /
adhunāsya prabhedanirūpaṇaṃ karoti---prauḍhoktītyādinā /
yo 'rthāntarasya dīpako vyañjako 'rtha uktaḥ so 'pi dvividhaḥ /
na kevalamanusvānopamo dvividhaḥ, yāvattadbhedo yo dvitīyaḥ so 'pa vyañjakārthadvaividhyadvāreṇa dvividha ityapiśabdasyārthaḥ /
prauḍhokterapyavāntarabhedamāha---kaveriti /

children.translated_text: Therefore these are three sub-types. /

children.text: prakarṣema ūḍaḥ sampādayitavyena vastunā prāptastatkuśalaḥ prauḍhaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Prauḍha</s>' — one who has attained mastery (<s>ūḍha</s>) to the highest degree (<s>prakarṣeṇa</s>) with respect to the matter to be accomplished; [i.e.,] one skilled in that. /
'<s>Ukti</s>' (expression) too — one suited to the presentation of the matter to be conveyed — is called '<s>prauḍhā</s>' (bold). /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He simply elaborates what was said — 'The meaning-power [operates] through the context': '<s>yāvat</s>' etc. // 23 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Thus the general definition of what arises from the power of meaning has been given, and its domain has been demarcated from the <s>alaṅkāras</s> such as <s>śleṣa</s> etc. /
Now he undertakes the classification of its sub-types: with '<s>prauḍhokti</s>' etc. /
'The meaning which is an illuminator of another content, and which has been stated [as the suggestor]' — that too is twofold. /
Not only is the reverberation-like [<s>dhvani</s>] twofold; even its sub-type, the second, is also twofold through the twofold nature of the suggestive meaning — this is the meaning of the word '<s>api</s>.' /
He states the internal sub-division of <s>prauḍhokti</s>: '<s>kavi</s>' etc. /

kaviprauḍhoktimātrasiddhaḥ, kavinibaddhavaktṛpraurḍhektimātrasiddhaḥ, svatassambhavī ceti trayo bhedā ityarthaḥ /
prauḍhapadavyutpattimāha--prakarṣeṇetyādi /

prauḍha iti /
prauḍha ityucyata ityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: An instance of [<s>dhvani</s>] whose body is produced solely through the poet's bold expression: /

children.text: sajjehi surahimāso ṇa dāva appei juaijaṇalakkhamuhe /
children.translated_text: [Prākrit verse:] The fragrant month [of spring] prepares — but does not yet dispatch — at the faces of the young women as targets,
the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless Love-god), [tipped] with fresh mango buds, with new leaf-blades as feathers.

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He states the meaning of the word '<s>api</s>' in '<s>artho 'pi</s>': '<s>na kevalam</s>' etc. /
He introduces '<s>kavi</s>' etc.: '<s>prauḍhokti</s>' etc. /
'These are three sub-types' — /
'[1] Produced solely through the bold expression of the poet, [2] produced solely through the bold expression of the speaker created by the poet, and [3] naturally possible — these are three sub-types' — this is the meaning. /
He states the etymology of '<s>prauḍha</s>': '<s>prakarṣeṇa</s>' etc. /
'<s>Ūḍha</s>' — the explanation thereof is: '<s>sampādayitavya</s>' etc. /
'<s>Tat</s>' — /
'Therefore' — this is the meaning. /
'Skilled by virtue of having attained the matter to be accomplished' — this is the extent. /
'<s>Prauḍha</s>' — /
'Is called <s>prauḍha</s>' — this is the meaning. /
Since '<s>prauḍha</s>' is established, by the rule '<s>prāt ūhoḍhe</s>' etc., <s>vṛddhi</s> [augment applies]. /
'Suited to conveying' — /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] An instance [of <s>dhvani</s>] whose body is produced solely through the bold expression of a speaker created by the poet — as already exemplified: '<s>śikhariṇī</s>' etc. /

children.text: locanam sajjayati surabhimāso na tāvadarpayati yuvatijanalakṣyamukhān /
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] [Sanskrit rendering:] The fragrant month prepares — but does not yet dispatch — at the faces of the young women as targets,
the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s>, with fresh mango buds [as tips], with new leaf-blades as feathers.

children.translated_text: Or alternatively, as follows: /
[Prākrit verse:] By your breasts, which are swelling upward,

children.text: abbhuṭṭhāṇaṃ via mammahasya diṇṇaṃ tuha thaṇohim //
children.translated_text: it is as if an arising has been given to the god of love, with the support of youth respectfully offered.

[<s>Locana</s>:] Here, spring — [imagined as] a conscious being, the friend of <s>Anaṅga</s> — prepares but does not yet dispatch — through this kind of bold expression, suited to presenting the matter to be conveyed, the spring season with its bursting mango blossoms is described; and from that, what is suggested manifests in sequence the onset of passion's agitation (<s>manmathonmāthana</s>), which will become more and more intense. /
Otherwise, [the statement] 'In spring, mangoes bud along with sprouts' would be mere content, not a suggestor. /
And this [bold] expression belongs to the poet alone. /
'<s>Śikhariṇī</s>' — /
Here, 'a parrot bites the red <s>bimba</s> fruit' — there is no suggestive capacity whatsoever [in the mere content]. /
But when there is a bold expression of this sort by a young, desirous speaker created by the poet, then there is suggestive capacity. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Suited to being offered to the hearts of connoisseurs' — this is the meaning. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>: 'and the second which is naturally possible' — this is a reading found in some [manuscripts]. /
'Prepares' — /
'The fragrant month' — the month associated with spring — at the faces of the young women as targets; /
In the reading '<s>lakṣa-sahān</s>': 'those that endure them — [the arrows are] to be used on them alone' — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Nava</s>' — /
'Fresh leaves and blades that receive' — those. /
'<s>Abhi</s>' — /
'Fresh mango blossoms etc.' — this is the meaning. /
Those same [are] the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s>. /
'Prepares but does not yet dispatch' — this is the syntactic connection. /
To justify the syntactic connection with 'preparing' etc., he says in the <s>Locana</s>: 'Spring as conscious' etc. /
'Spring is superimposed as a conscious being' — this is the purport. /
'Bursting of mango' — the manifestation, i.e., the emergence of the mango — such is [the season] — this is the meaning. /
The word '<s>sahakāra</s>' (mango) is an indicator for other blossoms as well. /
'Described' — /
'Stated' — this is the meaning. /
'By expression — described' — this is the connection. /
'From that, the suggested' etc. — /
By 'prepares the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s>, but does not yet dispatch' — the onset of passion's agitation [is suggested]; by 'does not yet dispatch' — through the medium of suggesting the future dispatching, the impending intensification of passion's agitation is indicated — this is the meaning. /
'Otherwise' — /
'In a manner other than the stated method' — this is the meaning. /
He states that method: '<s>vasante</s>' etc. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — /
'The meaning conveyed by this statement' — this is the meaning. /
'Would not be' etc. — /
'Would not be a suggestor of the stated meaning' — this is the meaning. /
'Here' etc. — /
In place of '<s>śuka</s>' (parrot), the reading '<s>ayaṃ śukapotaka</s>' (this little parrot) also exists. /
'<s>Iti</s>' etc. — /
'There is no suggestive capacity of what is conveyed by the statement as such' — this is the meaning. /
'In this manner' — /
'In the form of [the verse] "<s>śikhariṇī</s>" etc.' — this is the meaning. /

children.text:
svataḥ sambhavī ya aucatyena bahirapi sambhāvyamānasadbhāvo na kevalaṃ bhaṇitivaśenaivābhiniṣpannaśariraḥ /
yathodāhṛtam 'evaṃvādini' ityādi /

children.translated_text: Or as follows: /
[Prākrit verse:] With peacock-feather ear-ornaments, the hunter's wife walks about proudly
among her co-wives who are adorned with ornaments made of pearl-fruits.

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] The 'naturally possible' (<s>svataḥ sambhavī</s>) is that whose real existence is conceivable through propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) even externally [to the poem] — not one whose body is produced by the power of expression alone. /
As already exemplified: '<s>evaṃvādini</s>' (when he was speaking thus) etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] [Sanskrit rendering:] By your breasts, which are swelling upward, with the support of youth respectfully bestowed,
it is as if an arising has been given to <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love).

children.text:
stanau tāvadiha pradhānabhūtau tato 'pi gauravitaḥ kāmastābhyāmabhyutthānenoparcyate /
yauvanaṃ cānayoḥ paricārakabhāvena sthitamityevaṃvidhenoktivaicitryeṇa tvadīyastanāvaloka napravṛddhamanmathāvasthaḥ ko na bhavatīti bhaṅgyā svābhiprāyadhvananaṃ kṛtam /
tava tāruṇyenonnatau stanāviti hi vacanena vyañjakatā /

children.translated_text: 'Not only' — /
'The ingenuity of expression is useful in every way' — this is the purport. /
[Sanskrit rendering:] With peacock-feather ear-ornaments, the hunter's wife walks about proudly
among her co-wives who are adorned with ornaments of pearls.

[<s>Locana</s>:] Here the breasts are the principal element; more weighty even than those, <s>Kāma</s> is honored by the offering of their rising. /
And youth stands in the role of an attendant to them — by such ingenuity of expression, 'who would not be in a state of heightened passion from beholding your breasts?' — thus by indirection, the suggestion of one's own desire has been made. /
'Your breasts, swollen with youth' — by such a statement alone, there would be suggestive capacity. /

śikhimātramāraṇameva tadāsaktasya kṛtyam /
anyāsu tvāsakto hastino 'pyamārayaditi hi vacanenoktamuttamasaubhāgyam /

children.translated_text:
[<s>Locana</s>:] The killing of peacocks alone — that is the proper occupation of one devoted to that. /
But [the verse implies:] 'Not attached to other women; and even elephants he does not kill' — by such a statement, the supreme good fortune [of the hunter's wife] is expressed. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Suggestive capacity' — /
'The suggested meanings were demonstrated in the First <s>Uddyota</s>.' /
'<s>Sādara</s>' — /
'Having done [so]' — in the reading [with <s>kṛtvā</s>], it is completed [thus]. /
'Respectfully bestowed by youth — whose support of [his] hand is from youth — such as that.' /
'By your two breasts, which are swelling upward, an arising, as it were, has been given to <s>Manmatha</s>' — this is the syntactic connection. /
Here, with the intent that the superimposition of the narrative of attendants etc. upon youth etc. constitutes <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) that is subsidiary to <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), he elucidates: 'the breasts' etc. /
'Thus indeed' etc. — /
'By such a statement, the suggestive capacity of what is conveyed [would exist] — but not [with the same force]' — this is the meaning. /
'Not only' — this is a reference to the key-word [of the passage]. /
'<s>Svataḥ sambhavī</s>' (naturally possible) — intending that [the word conveys:] 'conceivable in the world too,' in the <s>vṛtti</s> with '<s>yaḥ</s>' etc. it was elucidated; therein, by '<s>na kevalam</s>' etc., he shows the meaning to be understood: 'the ingenuity of expression' etc. /
'Useful' — /
'In poetry' is the remainder. /
'In the absence of ingenuity of expression, the conceivability would not hold' — this is the purport. /
'<s>Śikhi</s>' (peacock) — /
This <s>gāthā</s> (verse) will be cited by the <s>vṛtti</s>-author in the Third <s>Uddyota</s> and commented upon there. /
'<s>Jāyā</s>' — /
'Newly married' — this is the meaning. /
'Ornament' — adornment. /
'Of co-wives' — /
'Of those married earlier' — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Śikhi</s>' — because of proximity to peacocks — /
[<s>Kārikā</s>:] Where through the power of meaning, another figure too is apprehended — /
Suggested like the reverberation of a bell — that is the other variety of <s>dhvani</s>. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.25 //
Where, through the power of meaning, yet another <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) is apprehended —
suggested like the reverberation of a bell — that is the other variety of <s>dhvani</s>. // 25 //
Anticipating the objection that its domain is extremely rare, the following is stated —

children.text: locanam racitāni vividhabhaṅgībhiḥ prasādhanānīta tāsāṃ sambhogavyagrimābhāvāttadviracanaśilpakauśalameva paramiti daurbhāgyātiśaya idānīmiti prakāśitam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] 'Ornaments fashioned with various artistic bends — since the absence of [her] being the foremost in lovemaking [means that] the craftsmanship of their fashioning alone is supreme — the excess of ill-fortune is now [thus] made manifest.'

children.text: garvaśca bālyāvivekādināpi bhavatīti nātra svoktisadbhāvaḥ śaṅkyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And pride arises even from childish lack of discernment etc. — hence the genuineness of her own statement should not be doubted here.

children.text: eṣa cārtho yathā yathā varṇyate āstāṃ vā varṇnā, bahirapi yadi pratyakṣādināvalokyate tathā tathā saubhāgyātiśayaṃ vyādhavadhvā dyotayati // 2.4 //
children.translated_text: And this meaning, the more it is described — or let the description be set aside — even if one observes externally through direct perception etc., the more [one sees that] the huntress's wife is revealing the excess of [her] good fortune. // 2.4 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Where another <s>alaṅkāra</s>, distinct from the expressible <s>alaṅkāra</s>, shines forth as being apprehended through the capacity of the meaning — that is the other <s>dhvani</s>, called 'born from the power of meaning' (<s>arthaśaktyudbhava</s>), whose suggested content is of the <s>anusvāna</s>-form (reverberant type).

children.text: evamarthaśaktyudbhavo dvibhedo vastumātrasya vyañjanīyatve vastudhvanirūpatayā nirūpitaḥ /

children.translated_text: Now, [to show that] of that very [meaning-power-born <s>dhvani</s>], when the object of suggestion has the form of an <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure), there is also <s>alaṅkāra-dhvani</s> (figure-suggestion) status — he says: 'of meaning' etc.

children.text: na kevalaṃ śabdaśakteralaṅkāraḥ pratīyate pūrvoktanītyā yāvadarthaśakterapi /
children.translated_text: Not only is an <s>alaṅkāra</s> apprehended through the power of the word, as was previously stated, but also through the power of meaning.

children.text: yadi vā na kevalaṃ yatra vastumātraṃ pratīyate yāvalaṅkāro 'pītyapiśabdārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, not only where mere content (<s>vastu</s>) is apprehended [as suggested], but where an <s>alaṅkāra</s> too [is suggested] — this is the meaning of the word '<s>api</s>' (also/too).
He glosses the word '<s>anya</s>' (other) — '<s>vācya</s>' (expressible) etc. // 2.5 //

Thus, the <s>arthaśaktyudbhava</s> (meaning-power-born [<s>dhvani</s>]), having two divisions, has been determined in its form as <s>vastu-dhvani</s> (factual suggestion) when mere content (<s>vastu</s>) is the object of suggestion.

'Childishness-born lack of discernment' — lack of discernment caused by childishness is '<s>bālyāviveka</s>.'
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), other possible causes are included.

children.text: svataḥsasbhavī ya aucityena bahirapi sambhāvyamānetyādyuktaṃ yojayati---eṣa cārtha ityādi //24//
children.translated_text: What was stated with 'arising naturally, if observed externally too through propriety' etc. — he construes — 'and this meaning' etc. // 24 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Anticipating' etc. — /
'Through the power of the word, a <s>śleṣa</s>-type <s>alaṅkāra</s> shines forth' — this is the apprehension. /
'Through the power of meaning' — this is the purport. /
'Of one attached to her' — the meaning is: of the hunter who is excessively attached to his wife. /
'Duty' — the purport is: because of inability to bear separation from her. /
'In the others' — the meaning is: in the co-wives. /
'Even an elephant' — the purport is: even one far away. /
Thus by this utterance — the meaning is: by the stated sentence-meaning. /
'Stated' — suggested. /
'The supreme good fortune' — the remainder is: of the wife. /
He shows the suggested [meaning] of 'pearl' etc. — 'fashioned' etc. /
'Now' — the meaning is: at the time just after the new marriage.
'Of that very' — of the very <s>arthaśaktyudbhava</s> (meaning-power-born [<s>dhvani</s>]).
Its connection is with '<s>alaṅkāra-dhvanitva</s>' (figure-suggestion status).
'<s>Vyañjanīye</s>' — when the suggested object is of the nature of the meaning.

children.text: yatrāpītyapiśabdasya arthaśakterapīti alaṅkāro 'pīti yojanāṃ vikalpena darśayannāha---na kevalamityādi // 2.5 //
children.translated_text: Showing alternatively the construal of the word '<s>api</s>' in '<s>yatrāpi</s>' as '<s>arthaśakter api</s>' (through the power of meaning also) and '<s>alaṅkāro 'pi</s>' (an <s>alaṅkāra</s> also) — he says: 'not only' etc. // 2.5 //
He introduces the <s>kārikā</s> beginning with '<s>arthe</s>' (of meaning) — 'thus' etc.

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He shows the seed of the apprehension — 'through the power of the word' etc. /
'By the word' — the meaning is: by the word in the <s>kārikā</s>.
The group of <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures) beginning with <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) that has attained expressible status —

children.text: sa sarvo gamyamānatvaṃ bibhrad bhūmnā pradarśitaḥ // DhvK_2.26 //
children.translated_text: all of that, bearing the status of being apprehended [as suggested], has been extensively demonstrated. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.26 //
The group of <s>alaṅkāras</s> beginning with <s>rūpaka</s> that has attained expressible status —
all of that, bearing the status of being apprehended [as suggested], has been extensively demonstrated. // 26 //

children.text:
anyatra vācyatvena prasiddho yo rūpakādiralaṅkāraḥ so 'nyatra pratīyamānatayā bāhulyena pradarśitastatrabhavadbhirbhaṭṭodbhaṭādibhiḥ /
tathā ca sasandehādiṣūpamārūpakātiśayoktīnāṃ prakāśamānatvaṃ pradarśitāmityalaṅkārāntarasyālaṅkārāntare vyaṅgyatvaṃ na yatnapratipādyam /

children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] But the seed of the apprehension [is this]: 'Which <s>alaṅkāra</s> shines forth [as suggested]?'

children.text: sarva iti pradarśita iti ca padenāsambhāvanātra mithyaivetyāha /
children.translated_text: By the words '<s>sarva</s>' (all) and '<s>pradarśita</s>' (demonstrated), [he indicates that] this is merely an impossibility-claim, and that it is false — he says [so].

children.text: upamānena tattvaṃ ca bhedaṃ ca vadataḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: [As <s>Udbhaṭa</s> stated:] 'Of one who again states both the identity and the difference by means of the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) —
the speech involving doubt (<s>sasandeha</s>) for the purpose of praise [is understood] by the wise as involving real doubt' —

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] The group of <s>alaṅkāras</s> beginning with <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), well known elsewhere as expressible, has been extensively demonstrated in its apprehended (suggested) form by the revered masters — <s>Bhaṭṭa Udbhaṭa</s> and others. /
And thus, in <s>sasandeha</s> (doubt) and other [figures], the manifestation of <s>upamā</s> (simile), <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), and <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) has been demonstrated — therefore, the suggestedness of one <s>alaṅkāra</s> within another <s>alaṅkāra</s> does not require laborious proof.

children.translated_text:
thus. /
In [the verse] 'Is this her hand, or this tendril-fingered sprout swaying in the wind?' etc. — <s>upamā</s> (simile) or <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) is suggested. /
And <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is almost universally suggested in all <s>alaṅkāras</s>. /
'Of another <s>alaṅkāra</s>' — the passage 'where an <s>alaṅkāra</s> also suggests another <s>alaṅkāra</s>' — since in that case a figure is suggested by mere content, how remarkable is that? — with this purport, the word '<s>alaṅkārāntara</s>' (another <s>alaṅkāra</s>) was used by the <s>vṛtti</s>-author, but it is not relevant to the present context. For the present subject is not 'a figure is suggested by a figure,' but rather 'in the meaning-power-born <s>dhvani</s>, an <s>alaṅkāra</s> too is among the suggested contents' — this alone being the relevant topic. /
And in the conclusion passage — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] she explains the <s>vṛtti</s> passage 'and thus in <s>sasandeha</s> etc.' — 'by the standard of comparison' etc. /
The definition quoted is from <s>Udbhaṭa</s>. /
'Identity' — the meaning is: non-difference. /
'Difference' — the remainder is: 'of the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison).' /
'Of one who states' — of the poet who describes. /
'Thus' — /
'By the <s>kārikā</s> beginning with <s>alaṅkārāntaracchāyā</s> (the semblance of another figure)' etc. — what was formulated even without the basis of difference-non-ascertainment has been noted [as] his synecdochic [statement]. /
'Of her' — /
Since the complete verse is not known [to us], it is explained as it appears — the construal is: 'Is this her hand, or [is it] a sprout?' /
'<s>Nu</s>' — in the sense of doubt. /
Common to both [hands and sprouts] — 'wind' etc. /
'Whose fingers are like leaves swaying in the wind' — such [a sprout]. /
The mobility of the fingers follows logically. /
'Of <s>upamā</s>, <s>rūpaka</s>, and <s>atiśayokti</s>' — the mutual combination here is not intended — with this intent he says: '<s>upamā</s> or <s>rūpaka</s>' etc. /
'And of <s>atiśayokti</s>' — this will be stated in the Third <s>Uddyota</s>. /
The passage '<s>ity alaṅkārāntarasya</s>' etc. is incongruent as literally read with the present topic — hence he states its purport — 'where' etc. /
'In that poetry' — or alternatively: 'because of that, in that poetry.' /
Or alternatively: the construction is 'from that, thus.' /
'How remarkable is that' etc. — /
'Not to be doubted' — this is the meaning. /
The word '<s>alaṅkārāntara</s>' [means] the word '<s>alaṅkārāntara</s>' in the locative case. /
'Not relevant to the present context' — here he states the reason — 'for' etc. /
Then what is the point of saying this much again? —
Even in the apprehension of another <s>alaṅkāra</s>, where [it] shines forth —

children.text: tat-paratvaṃ na vācyasya nāsau mārgo dhvaner mataḥ // DhvK_2.27 //
children.translated_text: the predominance of that [figure-apprehension] does not [make it] expressible — that is not considered a path of <s>dhvani</s>. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.27 //
Even in the apprehension of another <s>alaṅkāra</s>, where [it] shines forth —

children.text: tatparatvaṃ na vācyasya nāsau mārgo dhvanermataḥ // 27 //
children.translated_text: the predominance of that [figure-apprehension] does not [make it] expressible — that is not considered a path of <s>dhvani</s>. // 27 //

alaṅkārāntareṣu tvanuraṇanarūpālaṅkārapratītau satyāmapi yatra vācyasya vyaṅgyapratipādanaunmukhyena cārutvaṃ na prakāśate nāsau dhvanermārgaḥ /
tathā ca dīpakādāvalaṅkāre upamāyā gamyamānatve 'pi tatparatvena cārutvasyāvyavasthānānna dhvanivyapadeśaḥ /
yathā-----
candamaūehi ṇisā ṇalini kamalehi kusumagucchehi laā /
locanam 'te 'laṅkārāḥ parāṃ chāyāṃ yānti dhvanyaṅgatāṃ gatāḥ' ityatra śleke vṛttikṛt 'dhvanyaṅgatā cobhobhyāṃ prākarābhyāṃ' ityupakramya 'tatreha prakāraṇādvyaṅgyatvenetyavagantavyam' iti vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] In the verse 'those <s>alaṅkāras</s> attain the highest beauty when they have become subsidiary to <s>dhvani</s>' — the <s>vṛtti</s>-author, having begun with 'and the <s>dhvani</s>-subsidiarity is through both modes,' will say 'therein, from the present context, [it is to be understood] as suggestedness' etc.

children.text: antaraśabdo vobhayatrāpi viśeṣaparyāyaḥ; vaiṣayikī saptamī, na tu prāgvyākhyāyāmiva nimittasaptamī /
children.translated_text: And the word '<s>antara</s>' (other) in both places is a synonym for 'particular/specific'; the locative is of the domain-type, not a causal locative as in the previous interpretation.

This, then, is the meaning: that a particular suggested <s>alaṅkāra</s> shines forth in the domain of a particular expressible <s>alaṅkāra</s> — this is what has been stated by <s>Udbhaṭa</s> and others — hence 'an <s>alaṅkāra</s> is suggested through the power of meaning' has already been accepted by them.
Only, they state it in terms of the domain of a particular expressible <s>alaṅkāra</s>, because they are definers of <s>alaṅkāras</s> — this is the purport. // 2.6 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] However, in the reverberant-form <s>alaṅkāra</s>-apprehension of another <s>alaṅkāra</s>, even when it exists, where the beauty of the expressible does not appear through the orientation toward conveying the suggested — that is not a path of <s>dhvani</s>. /
And thus, in the figure of <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) etc., even though the apprehension of <s>upamā</s> (simile) as suggested is present, since beauty is not stably established through orientation toward that [upamā] — there is no <s>dhvani</s> designation. /
As for example: 'The night [is adorned] by moon-rays, the lotus-pond by lotuses, the flower-cluster by creepers —

children.translated_text: The meaning is: in a domain that is a particular expressible <s>alaṅkāra</s>.
That is to say: in a poem possessing a particular expressible <s>alaṅkāra</s>.
'Shines forth' —
as when <s>upamā</s> (simile) etc. [appears] in <s>sasandeha</s> (doubt) etc. // 2.6 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Anticipating the objection 'if this has already been stated by the predecessors, what is the point of your effort?' — he says: 'this much' etc. /
'By us' — this is the completion of the sentence. /
The word '<s>punar</s>' (again) indicates the distinction from what was stated. /
'Moon-rays' etc. — /
The moon-rays of the night etc. have no attainment of superiority whatsoever without the night etc. /
Even for good people, without poetic discourse — what sort of [excellence]? /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Of the relevant context' — this is what he says — 'of meaning' etc. /
Here he states the supporting [evidence] — 'and thus' etc. /
'From the context, as suggestedness' — /
Its connection is with '<s>dhvanyaṅgatā</s>' (subsidiarity to <s>dhvani</s>). /
'By another <s>alaṅkāra</s>, the suggestedness of another <s>alaṅkāra</s>' — its meaning 'the suggestedness of one <s>alaṅkāra</s> caused by another <s>alaṅkāra</s>' was explained with the intended sense in view. /
But with the intention of another meaning, he explains — 'the word <s>antara</s>' etc. /
'A synonym for particular/specific' — a word meaning 'particular.' /
'Domain-type' — expressing domain-related meaning. /
'Locative' — the meaning is: the locative in '<s>alaṅkārāntare</s>' (in another <s>alaṅkāra</s>). /
He states the result — 'this then' etc. /
'Expressible' —

children.text: atra gurvīkriyata ityasya candramayūkhairniśetyādibhiḥ pañcabhiḥ pratyekaṃ sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the meaning of 'is made weighty' (<s>gurvīkriyate</s>) has a connection with each of the five — 'moon-rays,' 'night,' etc.

children.text: atra niśayā candramayūkhāḥ guravaḥ kriyante ityādivipariṇāmena padānāṃ sambandhādarthasāmarthyādvā pratīyamānamarthāntaraṃ darśayati---candretyādi /
children.translated_text: Here, [the meaning] 'the night makes the moon-rays weighty' etc. — by the transposition (<s>vipariṇāma</s>) of the words, or through the capacity of meaning, he shows the suggested secondary meaning — 'moon-rays' etc.
'Of what kind?' —

children.text: haṃsehi sarasohā kavvakahā sajjanehi karai garuri //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] By swans the autumnal beauty, by poetic discourse [the delight of] good people — is made weighty. //
'Moon-rays' etc. —
(Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:) The night [is adorned] by moon-rays, the lotus-pond by lotuses, the flower-cluster by creepers,
the autumnal beauty by swans, poetic discourse by good people — is made weighty. //
