children.translated_text: He shows that what was presented by 'where' etc. becomes threefold through alternatives — 'and therein' etc.
The word 'sometimes' (kadacit) also connects with the two following sentences.

children.text: yathā--- prāptaśrīreṣa kasmātpunarapi mayi taṃ manthakhedaṃ vidadhyā- nnidrāmapyasya pūrvāmanalasamanaso naiva sambhāvayāmi /
children.translated_text: For example — 'This one has obtained prosperity — why would he inflict upon me again that suffering of churning? I do not even suspect that this one, whose mind is like fire, [would ever have] prior sleep.

children.text: setuṃ badhnāti bhūyaḥ kimiti ca sakaladvīpanāthānuyāta- stvayyāyāte vitarkāniti dadhata ivābhāti kampaḥ payodheḥ //
children.translated_text: Why does he build a bridge again?' — and having been followed by the lords of all islands, 'when you arrive' — as if holding [these] speculations — the trembling of the ocean shines forth!'

Thus the chaya [Sanskrit rendering].) In [verses] such as these, even though simile is embedded [within them], the charm is established through the medium of the expressible figure alone, not through the purport of the suggested figure.
Therefore, in those [cases], it is proper that the designation 'poetry' is applied through the medium of the expressible figure alone.
But where the expressible is established precisely through its being directed toward the suggested — there, the designation through the medium of the suggested is appropriate.
[Locana:] Good people (sadhujana) —
And what the moon-rays do to the night — making it weighty through brilliance, desirability, etc.; what lotuses do to the lake — [providing] beauty, fragrance, splendor, etc.; what clusters of flowers do to the creeper — accessibility, charm, etc.; what swans do to autumnal beauty — pleasing to the ear, charm, etc. — all this, to the tale of poetry, by good people — just this much meaning is 'made weighty' — this shines forth through the force of the dipaka (illumination) figure.
The word 'tale' (katha) says this: let certain subtle distinctions of poetry — such as dhvani-status — be set aside; without good people, even the very word 'poetry' is destroyed.
But when they [good people] are present, even a mere verbal composition that is fortunate enough to receive the designation of the word 'poetry' abides [beautifully]; thus, by them it is made such that it attains worthiness of respect — through the very force of what is to be excluded by the dipaka, the meaning that is intended — where its predominance [is established] — that is the path of dhvani: he explains it in this form — 'but where' etc.
And therein, sometimes through the expressible figure, the suggested is another figure; or alternatively, the mere existence of the expressible figure, not its suggestive capacity, [is what is in play]; the absence of the expressible figure —
[Balapriya:] 'Does not occur' — this is the meaning.
He elaborates 'making weighty' — 'and by the moon-rays' etc.
'What is done' — 'that' is the remainder.
In sentences such as 'by lotuses' etc. too, 'what is done' carries over.
'All that' — the meaning is: the previously stated desirability, charm, etc. that is fit for syntactic connection with 'the tale of poetry.'
'By good people' — 'is done' carries over.
'Shines forth' — the meaning is: is cognized as expressible.
He states the result of having said 'tale of poetry' (kavyakatha) rather than just 'poetry' (kavita) — 'the word tale' etc.
The meaning of 'tale of poetry' is: poetry that is being narrated.
Therein, the word 'tale' illuminates what will be stated: this is the meaning.
'Subtle distinctions' — dhvani-status etc.
'In those' — the meaning is: in good people.
The syntactic connection is: 'even a mere verbal composition that is fortunate in receiving the designation of the word poetry abides beautifully.'
'Why?' — to this he says: 'thus' etc.
By 'thus the force of the dipaka' etc., the vrtti passage beginning with 'the expressible' etc. has been elaborated.
'Not of the simile' — the meaning is: the simile that is implied between the swans etc. and the tale of poetry, and between the night etc. and [poetry], does not have primacy, among the good people.
'By the force of what is to be excluded' — the meaning is: by the power of reasoning such as 'where it shines, its predominance does not [belong to the expressible]' etc.
'Intended' — desired to be expressed.

children.translated_text: <s>Upama</s>-<s>dhvani</s> (simile-suggestion) is as follows —

children.text: vīrāṇaṃ ramai ghusiṇaruṇammi ṇa tadā piāthaṇucchaṅge /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'The beauty of heroic men, in the reddened [twilight of battle], not then the swelling of the beloved's breast —
the gaze [fixed] on the surface of the elephant's frontal globe, like [one fixed on] dense vermilion!'

[Locana:] 'Or' (<s>eva va</s>) — the alternative is threefold.
And this should be applied to the examples as appropriate.
He illustrates — 'having obtained prosperity' etc.
When a certain king, possessing an infinite army, dwells near the ocean — because of the rising of the full moon and the immersion [therein] of his forces — the trembling of the ocean has arisen for that reason.
That [trembling] is imagined through this doubt — hence, from the combination (sankara) of doubt (sandeha) and poetic fancy (utpreksa), the combination-figure (sankara-alankara) is the expressible.
And through that, the status of being [an avatar of] Vasudeva —
[Balapriya:] The examples of these [three types] will become clear.
'Having obtained prosperity' — this king, who has obtained prosperity (sri) and [the goddess] Rama — 'by whom.'
Therefore, 'upon me again — that previously experienced —
churning-suffering (mantha-kheda)' — suffering caused by churning — 'why' (kasmat), 'for what reason,' 'would he inflict' (vidadhyat), 'would he do?'
Here, first 'again' etc. is the doubt; afterward, through the cognition that the fruit of churning is the obtaining of Laksmi, 'why' is the curiosity about another fruit.
The same should be understood in what follows above.
'Whose mind is like fire' (analasamanasa) — whose mind is devoid of laziness: this is implicit as a reason.
'Of this king, I do not even suspect prior sleep.'
'A bridge' (setu) — 'stone-made' (esamayi) carries over.
'Since this one is followed by the lords of all islands, why (kim iti) does he build a bridge upon me again?'
'When you arrive' — when [the king] arrives in [the ocean's] own vicinity — these speculations (vitarka), implied by the preceding sentences — [such as] 'should he churn [me]?' — these doubts.
'As if holding [them]' (dadhata iva) — as if bearing those — 'of the ocean' (payodheh) — the trembling (kampa), the agitation of water and also the quaking — 'shines forth' (abhati): this is the syntactic connection.
Here he elaborates the expressible and the suggested figure — 'when a certain' etc.
'That' (sa) — the meaning is: the trembling (kampa).
Here, the non-difference of the water's agitation and the quaking should be understood as a metaphorical superimposition.
'Through this doubt' — the meaning is: by the doubt '[would] he churn [me]?' indicated by the sentence 'holding speculations' — through that as the reason.
'Is imagined' (utpreksyate) — through the trembling as the effect, the stated doubt-form as the reason is poetically fancied in the ocean.
Or alternatively — the trembling in the form of water-agitation is poetically fancied as a quaking caused by the stated doubt: this is the purport.
'From the combination' (sankarad) — the meaning is: from the combination of the single-sentence-entry type.
In such a domain, the designation of <s>rupaka</s>-<s>dhvani</s> (metaphor-suggestion) is proper, because the charm of poetry is established through reliance on the <s>rupaka</s> (metaphor) in the form of reverberation (anuranana).

children.translated_text: Therefore, 'by that very designation' — this is the connection.
Because the <s>upamā-dhvani</s> (simile-suggestion) example has an identical construction, the definition has not been formulated in the author's own words.

children.text: vīrāṇāṃ ramate ghusṛṇāruṇe na tathā priyāstanotsaṅge /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] The gaze of heroes delights not so much in the saffron-reddened swelling of the beloved's breast —
as it does in the surface of the enemy elephant's frontal globe, thick with vermilion. //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Some read this as an example here, but that is wrong; because by the force of the word '<s>bhavat</s>' (you/your lordship), the meaning 'you are <s>Vāsudeva</s>' is made explicit. /
<s>Lāvaṇya</s> (grace) means form and charm; <s>kānti</s> (radiance) means lustre — by these two, the directions have been filled, distributed, made delightful, and perfected. /
Now, immediately after the turbidity of anger, with a disposition toward graciousness — /
'<s>Smera</s>' means having a slightly smiling nature; '<s>taralāyate</s>' means trembling — the eyes, beautiful with the swaying and blossoming of graciousness, of her — [this is] an address to her. /
Alternatively, 'now she does not go' — but when a moment has passed, [the ocean] became agitated. /
'Your face, reddened by the flush of anger and smiling, is like the full moon-disc tinged with twilight red' — thus should it be imagined by the sensitive reader (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) through the agitation of his wavering mind. /
'And it does not go' — that is quite clear; in the sense of correspondence, this body of water is a collection of inertness. /
Words like '<s>jala</s>' (water) etc. are primarily expressive of emotional states; '<s>bālapriyā</s>' however is a corrupt reading — he says: 'as stated' etc. /
He states the reason for 'that is wrong' — 'by <s>bhavat</s>' etc. /
'Because it is made explicit' — /
Since through the statement of the described king being the agent of killing, his non-difference from <s>Vāsudeva</s> is made explicit — this is the meaning. /
And thus, here the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) has become subordinate (<s>guṇībhūta</s>) — this is the purport. /
To avoid redundancy, he explains the intended meaning of the word '<s>lāvaṇya</s>' — '<s>saṃsthāna</s>' etc. /
The meaning is: beauty of form. /
The elaboration of '<s>saṃvibhaktāni</s>' is '<s>hṛdyāni</s>' etc. /
'<s>Diṅmukhāni</s>' — /
The meaning is: the starting points of the directions. /
The places where the face has a connection through one's own vision are '<s>diṅmukhāni</s>' — this is the purport. /
He explains the connection of '<s>adhunā</s>' (now) with '<s>smere</s>' (smiling) — 'by anger' etc. /
'By graciousness' — /
Beautiful through the swaying and blossoming of graciousness — this is the meaning. /
He states an alternative meaning following the suggested sense — 'alternatively' etc. /
The purport is that '<s>adhunā</s>' also connects with '<s>na eti</s>' (does not go). /
He shows the alternative meaning conveyed by '<s>adhunā na eti</s>' — 'but when passed' etc. /
'<s>Vṛtte</s>' means gone, passed. /
'<s>Kṣaṇāntare</s>' means at a particular moment — that is, at the time of moonrise. /
'Became agitated' — /
'The ocean' is the remainder. /
The purport is: the agitation of the ocean was observed. /
He shows the <s>rūpaka-dhvani</s> (metaphor-suggestion) — 'by anger' etc. /
'<s>Iti</s>' is in the causal sense. /
The meaning is: because such a face is non-different from such a moon-disc. /
That is to say: from seeing it. /
'Should be imagined' etc. — /
The meaning is: it should be imagined by the sensitive reader through agitation in the form of mental wavering caused by the passion of love (<s>madana-vikāra</s>). /
As for the ocean, the agitation is of the nature of water-surge. /
Here the non-differentiation of the two types of agitation is intended. /
If the word '<s>kṣobha</s>' (agitation) merely means mental wavering, then only the excess of the face's beauty is suggested, not the non-difference from the moon — /
therefore, the meaning of agitation as water-surge caused by moonrise is also intended. /
'And it does not go' — /
'The ocean [does not attain] agitation' is the remainder. /
'That' — /
The meaning is: because agitation was not attained. /
Previously it was said: 'inertness — the eye.' /
And here, the agitation, which is of the nature of love's passion (<s>madana-vikāra</s>), arises in the sensitive reader through beholding your face — since [the verse] rests in just this much of denotation, the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) is indeed suggested through reverberation (<s>anuranana</s>). /
The expressible figure (<s>vācya-alaṅkāra</s>) here is <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), and it is not a suggestor. /
The reverberant-form <s>rūpaka</s> that is suggested through the power of meaning — it is through reliance on that [rūpaka] that the charm of the poetry here is established. /

children.translated_text: Or, for example — from my own [work], in the <s>Viṣamabāṇalīlā</s> (The Play of Crooked Arrows), the valor against the <s>Asuras</s> by <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the god of love) —
[Prakrit:] Their heart, single-mindedly [devoted] to seizing the jewels [that are] brothers of <s>Śrī</s> —
was placed by the flower-arrowed [<s>Kāmadeva</s>] upon the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips of their beloveds. //

[<s>Locana</s>:] Even though the gaze wavers — due to being devoted to reassuring the adorned beloved and simultaneously having a mind eager for the rush of battle — nevertheless there is an excess of haste in battle: this is the <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) as the expressible figure. /
And in that, the <s>upamā</s> (simile) that is suggested is [this]: by the beloved's breast-mounds, even the fearsome enemies — who cause terror to all people — while eager to crush [them], the elephant's frontal-globe surfaces — '<s>bālapriyā</s>' [means:] this is the statement of non-difference between the container and the contained through superimposition. /
The connection is with '<s>manye</s>' (I think). /
'<s>Niścinomi</s>' (I ascertain) is its meaning. /
Because such a face is manifest, due to the non-attainment of agitation, the great inertness attributed by people to the ocean — I ascertain — this is the meaning. /
Here too, the superimposed identity of the meaning of the word '<s>jāḍya</s>' (inertness/ignorance) with water should be understood. /
'Primarily expressive of emotional states' — /
The meaning is: primarily denoting meanings such as inertness. /
Refuting the status of the suggested as being subsidiary to the expressible, he establishes <s>dhvani</s> — 'and here' etc. /
'Through beholding your face' — /
The reading with the seventh case-ending (locative) also [exists]. /
'<s>Iyati</s>' (this much) — /
The meaning is: in just this much meaning — that because such agitation was not attained, the ocean is a mass of inertness — I ascertain. /
'<s>Rūpaka</s>' — /
The meaning is: the non-difference of the heroine's face from the full moon. /
'<s>Śleṣa</s>' — /
The meaning is: the <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) residing in the word '<s>jaḍa</s>' (inert). /
'Not a suggestor' — because it is not useful for the stated <s>rūpaka-dhvani</s> — this is the purport. /
He elaborates '<s>anuraṇana-rūpa-rūpaka</s>' etc. — 'the reverberant-form <s>rūpaka</s>' etc. /
Now, in the <s>vṛtti</s>, the definition of the <s>upamā-dhvani</s> example was not formulated in the author's own words — why? To this he says — 'because of identical construction' etc. /
'In his own words' means: in his own statement. /
'Of heroes' — /
The gaze of heroes delights in the surface of the enemy elephant's frontal globe thick with vermilion, just as it does not [delight] in the saffron-reddened swelling of the beloved's breast — this is the construal. /
'<s>Ghusṛṇa</s>' means saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>). /
He elaborates — 'adorned' etc. /
'Adorned' means decorated. /
'<s>Samāśvāsana</s>' means delighting through enjoyment. /
'Immediately preceding' — the meaning is: proximate. /
'Wavering' means unsteady. /
'This is <s>vyatireka</s> as the expressible figure' — /
Because it demonstrates the excess of delight in the enemy elephant's frontal globe compared to the delight in the beloved's breast, the excess of haste in battle compared to the haste for enjoyment is conveyed — since that is being expressed, it has the status of an expressible figure. /
Alternatively, the meaning of 'this is <s>vyatireka</s>' is: '<s>iti</s>' means 'that which suggests the meaning' — the <s>vyatireka</s> [is such]. /
And that is as previously stated. /
Here he elaborates the <s>upamā-dhvani</s> — 'in that' etc. /
'In that verse' — /
'Which <s>upamā</s>' etc. — the connection of 'on the elephant's frontal-globe surfaces' is with '<s>upamā</s>' (simile). /
The meaning is: the suggested <s>upamā</s>, which has the elephant's frontal-globe surfaces as its correlate and the beloved's breast-mounds as its counter-correlate. /
He elaborates its predominance — 'all' etc. /
These are qualifications of the frontal-globe surfaces, concerned with stating the actual state of affairs. /
(Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:) Their heart, single-mindedly [devoted] to seizing the jewels [that are] brothers of <s>Śrī</s> —
was placed by the flower-arrowed [<s>Kāmadeva</s>] upon the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips of their beloveds. //

children.text: iti chāyā ) ākṣepadhvaniryathā---- sa vaktumakhilān śakto hayagrīvāśritān guṇān /
children.translated_text: (Thus the <s>chāyā</s>.) An example of <s>ākṣepa-dhvani</s> (suggestion through denial) is as follows — 'He is capable of describing all the virtues residing in <s>Hayagrīva</s>,
who is capable of knowing the measure of the great ocean by means of water-pots.' //

atrātiśayoktyā hayagrīvaguṇānāmavarṇanīyatāpratipādanarūpasyāsādhāraṇatadviśeṣaprakāśanaparasyākṣepasya prakāśanam /
arthāntaranyāsadhvaniḥ śabdaśaktimūlānuraṇanarūpavyaṅgyo 'rthaktimūlānuraṇanarūpavyaṅgyaśca sambhavati /

children.translated_text: Of these, the example of the first [type] —

children.text: devvāettammi phale kiṃ kīrai ettiaṃ puṇā bhaṇimo /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Having been granted the fruit by the gods, what then — we shall tell this much again:"
the <s>Kiṅkilla</s> [tree's] sprouts are not equal to the sprouts of other [trees]!' //

[<s>Locana</s>:] The eye — of those who through its power receive delight as if with esteem — that very [gaze] produces the wonder of the excess of heroic valor: thus the predominance of the <s>upamā</s> (simile). /
'Valor against the <s>Asuras</s>' — /
For therein, the conquest of the three worlds by him [<s>Kāmadeva</s>] is described. /
Of those <s>Asuras</s> dwelling in the netherworld — by whom, again and again, the plundering of <s>Indra</s>'s city and such [deeds] — what was not done? — that heart, meaning: [the heart] that belonged to those who [performed] such [feats] — which was of unshakeable resolve even against the most difficult [foes] — and that [heart] — /
Of those who are brothers of <s>Śrī</s> — therefore of inexpressible excellence — this is the meaning. /
Of those jewels, the complete seizure — [with a heart] single-mindedly devoted to that — that heart, by the flower-arrowed one, by one whose arsenal of instruments is of the most delicate kind, was placed upon the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips of the beloveds — made to be such that [the heroes'] sense of accomplishment was satisfied by merely beholding, fondly gazing at, and kissing [those lips] — [this was] done by <s>Kāmadeva</s>. /
Their heart, which had been extremely blazing with the desire for conquest — this is what is meant. /
Here, <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is the expressible figure. /
'<s>Bālapriyā</s>' — among the enemies, meaning: among those who are enemies, or among those related to enemies. /
The word '<s>api</s>' (even) indicates the contradiction in the arising of delight and esteem. /
The connection of 'on the elephant's frontal-globe surfaces' is with '<s>rati</s>' (delight) and with '<s>bahumāna</s>' (esteem). /
'Through its power' — through the power of the simile. /
'<s>Rati</s>' means affection. /
'Bearing' means possessing. /
'<s>Iva</s>' indicates apprehension. /
'Esteem' — /
The meaning is: of the heroes who bear affection toward the elephant's frontal-globe surfaces through the similarity to the beloved's breast-mounds — their high regard for those [surfaces] is as if [they were lovers]. /
Or alternatively: '<s>ratim ādadānām</s>' means 'of those who are enamored' — '<s>iva</s>' [indicates] 'as if' — this is also a [valid] meaning. /
'<s>Iti</s>' is in the causal sense. /
'That very' — that very aforementioned simile. /
'Heroic' — /
The meaning is: the wonder-producing quality (<s>camatkāra-kāritva</s>) of the warriors' excess of valor — that is what is meant. /
'Produces' means accomplishes. /
'<s>Iti</s>' is in the causal sense. /
The meaning is: by serving as an aid to <s>vīra-rasa</s> (the heroic sentiment). /
'Therein, of his' — the meaning is: in the <s>Viṣamabāṇalīlā</s>, of <s>Kāmadeva</s>. /
The elaboration of '<s>teṣām</s>' (of those) is: 'by whom' etc. /
The explanation of '<s>tat</s>' (that) is: 'which [heart] that belonged to those' etc. /
'Unshakeable' — the meaning is: immovable. /
The statement of the implied meaning — 'of inexpressible [excellence]' etc. /
And 'of the most delicate kind' etc. /
He states the intended meaning of '<s>bimbādhare niveśitam</s>' (placed upon the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips) — 'that' etc. /
The statement of the sense of the first half by 'their heart, which' etc. — '<s>tat</s>' is the remainder. /
The connection is: that [heart], by <s>Kāmadeva</s>, was made to bear the sense of accomplishment satisfied by merely beholding, fondly gazing at, and kissing [those lips]. /
'Here <s>atiśayokti</s>' — /
Here, through <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), the manifestation of the <s>ākṣepa</s> (denial) — whose form is the demonstration of the indescribability of <s>Hayagrīva</s>'s virtues, and which is oriented toward revealing his unique distinction — [is achieved]. /
The <s>arthāntaranyāsa-dhvani</s> (suggestion through corroborative instance) — the suggested through word-power-based reverberation and the suggested through meaning-power-based reverberation — both are possible. /

children.text:
locanam pratīyamānā copamā /
sakalaratnasāratulyo bimbādhara iti hi teṣāṃ bahumāno vāstava eva /
ata eva na rūpakadhvaniḥ /
rūpakasyāropyamāṇatvenāvāstavatvāt /
teṣāmasurāṇāṃ vastuvṛttyaiva sādṛśyaṃ sphurati /
tadeva ca sādṛśyaṃ camatkārahetuḥ prādhānyena /
atiśayoktyeti /
vācyālaṅkārarūpayetyarthaḥ /
avarṇanīyatāpratipādanamevākṣepasya rūpamiṣṭapratiṣedhātmakatvāt /

children.translated_text: He states its predominance by means of the qualifier — 'unique' etc.
By [saying] 'is possible,' he indicates that incidentally, the word-power-based [type] is also examined here.
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] On account of the cause, the speech that transcends ordinary experience —
where non-difference is bound upon what is different, and multiplicity [is bound] upon what is other — //

[<s>Locana</s>:] The <s>upamā</s> (simile) that is apprehended is [as follows]: /
The <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip is equal to the essence of all jewels — thus their esteem is indeed real. /
Therefore, this is not <s>rūpaka-dhvani</s> (metaphor-suggestion). /
Because <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), being of the nature of superimposition, is unreal. /
Of those <s>Asuras</s>, the similarity shines forth through the actual state of affairs itself. /
And that very similarity is the cause of wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>), predominantly. /
'Through <s>atiśayokti</s>' — the meaning is: in the form of an expressible figure. /
'Demonstration of indescribability' is indeed the form of <s>ākṣepa</s> (denial), because [<s>ākṣepa</s>] has the nature of negating what is desired. /

children.text:
tathā sambhāvyamānārthanibandhe 'tiśayoktigīḥ /
ityādinā tallakṣaṇamuktamudbhaṭādibhiḥ /

niveśanāsambandhe 'pi tatsambandhakathanāt sambandhātiśayoktirvā /
pratīyamāneti /
dhvanyamānetyarthaḥ /
uktaṃ vivṛṇoti---sakaletyādi /
samupādeyatvāditā ratnāsāratulyatvam /
ata eva vakṣyamāṇādeva /
rūpakasyāropyamāṇatveneti /
ratnasārarūpopamānābhedasya kalpitatvenetyarthaḥ /

sādṛśyamiti /
bimbādhare ratnasārasādṛśyamityarthaḥ /
vṛttau 'anatiśayoktye'tyuktaṃ tadvivṛṇoti---vācyetyādi /

'yo 'mbukumbhairi'tyādinā sambhāvyamānārthanibandhanāditi bhāvaḥ /
avarṇanīyatāpratipādanamevetyatra hetumāha---iṣṭeti /
iṣṭamatra varṇanīyatvapratipādanamiti bhāvaḥ /
'asādhāraṇe'tyādikathanasya phalaṃ darśayati--tasyetyādiviśeṣaṇadvāreṇa tasya prādhānyamāhetyanvayaḥ /
atra 'yo 'mbukumbhairi'tyādyatiśayoktyā hayagrīvaguṇānāmavaṇanīyatvapratipādanarūpākṣepo dhvanyate, tena tadguṇānāmasādhāraṇo viśeṣaśceti bhāvaḥ /
vṛttau 'śabdaśaktī'tyādyuktau kā saṅgatirityata āha---sambhavatītyādi /
atreti /
padaprakāśaścāyaṃ dhvaniriti vākyasyārthāntaratātparye 'pi sati na virodhaḥ /

children.translated_text: The example of the second [type] is as follows —
[Prakrit:] 'Me, whose anger is placed in the heart, whose face is not showing displeasure — [yet] you seek to appease me —

children.text: avaraddhasya vi ṇa hu de pahujāṇaa rosiuṃ sakkam //
children.translated_text: O man of much knowledge, it is indeed not possible for you to be angry even with one who has offended!' //

[Bālapriyā:] 'Thus, in a composition whose subject-matter is conjectured, the speech of atiśayokti (hyperbole)' — by this and other [definitions], its definition was stated by Udbhaṭa and others. / The heart that was single-minded in seizing the jewels — that being placed upon the bimba-fruit lip — since in reality the identity of two distinct hearts, which are particular mental states, is demonstrated here — the meaning is: this is atiśayokti (hyperbole) in the form of non-difference upon what is different. / Or alternatively, since the connection [of placing] is stated even though there is no actual relation of placing — it is sambandhātiśayokti (hyperbole of relation). / 'Apprehended' — / The meaning is: suggested. / He elaborates what was stated — 'all' etc. / The equality with the essence of jewels is [established] through desirability etc. / Therefore, from what will be stated itself — / 'Because rūpaka has the nature of superimposition' — / The meaning is: because the non-difference [posited] between the bimba-fruit lip and the jewel-essence, which is an upamāna (standard of comparison), is fabricated. / The reading 'rūpakasyopacāratvena' (because rūpaka has the nature of figurative usage) also [exists]. / 'Similarity' — / The meaning is: the similarity of the bimba-fruit lip to the jewel-essence. / He elaborates what was said in the vṛtti as 'atiśayokti' — 'expressible' etc. / 'In the form of an expressible figure' — / The purport is: because it is grounded in a conjectured subject-matter through 'who [can know the measure] by water-pots' etc. / He states the reason for 'demonstration of indescribability is indeed [the form]' — 'desired' etc. / The purport is: the desired [objective] here is the demonstration of describability [of the virtues]. / He shows the result of the statement 'unique' etc. — 'its' etc. — the construal is: he states its predominance by means of the qualifier. / Here, through the atiśayokti beginning with 'who [can know] by water-pots,' the ākṣepa (denial) in the form of demonstrating the indescribability of Hayagrīva's virtues is suggested — thereby the unique distinction of those virtues [is conveyed] — this is the purport. / As to what coherence there is in the vṛtti's statement 'word-power' etc. — he says: 'is possible' etc. / 'Here' — / And this dhvani being a word-illuminator — [even though] the sentence's purport is in a different meaning — there is no contradiction. /
(Sanskrit chāyā:) 'Me, with anger placed in the heart, with face not showing displeasure — [yet] you seek to appease me —

children.translated_text: The example of the second [type] is as follows —

children.text: jāejja vaṇuddese khujja vvia pāavo gaḍiavatto /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Would that I were born in a forest-region, as a hunchbacked tree with fallen leaves —

children.text: mā māṇusammi loe tāekvaraso dariddo a //
children.translated_text: rather than in the human world, single-minded in giving, yet destitute!' //

[Bālapriyā:] The Aśoka tree has no fruit like the mango etc. — what can be done? — the sprouts, however, are extremely delightful — just this much is the denotative meaning, complete in itself. / Here, through the power of the word 'phala' (fruit), the corroborating content (samarthaka) of this matter is apprehended even before [the rest]. / For [the corroborating content is] of the general form: 'Even for one engaged in means for transcendent conquest, the fruit in the form of success depends on fate and might sometimes not occur.' / Now, the aprastutapraśaṃsā (praise of the irrelevant) is predominantly suggested in this entire sentence — then how can arthāntaranyāsa (corroborative instance) be suggested? Since the simultaneous predominance of both in one [passage] is impossible — anticipating this objection, he says: 'word-illuminator' etc. / For all the elaboration of dhvani will be [classified as] word-illuminator and sentence-illuminator. / Therein, [Bālapriyā:] the meaning is: in the examination of meaning-power-based [dhvani]. / The elaboration of [the passage ending with] 'what can be done?' — 'Aśoka's' etc. / The elaboration of the second half — 'sprouts' etc. / 'This much' — / The meaning is: by just the stated meaning alone. / He elaborates the dhvani — 'here' etc. / The construal of 'here' is: of this general-form corroborating content of this matter, [apprehended] through the power of the word 'phala' — it is apprehended even before [the rest]. / For in 'when the fruit depends on fate, what can be done?' — the word 'phala' by the force of context denotes the meaning of the form of fruit (of a tree) through denotation, and from that the contextual meaning 'the Aśoka has no fruit' is obtained; and further, the word 'phala' through meaning-power-based dhvani conveys the meaning of the form of result/purpose — and from that, the general meaning 'the successes of all depend on fate and might not occur' is obtained as corroborating the previously stated contextual meaning — this is the meaning. / 'Is apprehended even before' — the meaning of this is: it is apprehended at the very time of hearing 'when the fruit depends on fate.' / He introduces the passage 'word-illuminator' etc. — 'now' etc. / 'Aprastutapraśaṃsā' — / The meaning is: the contextual meaning in the form of praise of some king etc. who did not attain the fruit of success despite being engaged in means — [that is the] aprastutapraśaṃsā. / 'Predominantly suggested' — / The contextual meaning residing in the aprastutapraśaṃsā is suggested, and it is sometimes predominant — this was stated in the First Uddyota. / 'The suggestedness of arthāntaranyāsa' — / 'Predominantly' carries over. / As to 'why?' — he says: 'of both' etc. / He states the intended meaning — 'for all' etc. / 'But in the sentence, aprastutapraśaṃsā' — / 'Predominantly suggested' is the remainder. / Now, if this is so, how is the designation [arthāntaranyāsa-dhvani] applied here? For here, [the dhvani] illuminated by the particular word [phala] — with the corroborating general meaning conjoined with an alternative purport through the expressible particular 'even for a bahujña (man of much knowledge) who has offended, anger cannot be produced' — shines forth [predominantly]. / [Locana:] In the word 'phala' (fruit), the arthāntaranyāsa-dhvani (suggestion through corroborative instance) is predominant. / But in the sentence, it is aprastutapraśaṃsā (praise of the irrelevant). / Therein too, the predominance of the corroborating nature conveyed by the word 'phala' shines forth — therefore this is indeed arthāntaranyāsa-dhvani — this is the purport. / [Of her] whose anger is placed in the heart — not manifested outwardly. / Therefore, 'me, whose face does not show displeasure — yet you who are appeasing me — O bahujña (man of much knowledge), it is indeed not possible even for you who have offended to produce anger [in me].' / Here, 'bahujña' in the sense of address rests in a particular [meaning]. / But then, from the subsequent reflection on its meaning, the general-form corroborative [meaning] that is apprehended — that alone is what produces wonder (camatkāra). / For she, being a khaṇḍitā (woman offended by her lover's infidelity), having been appeased through [his] cleverness — showing her resentment toward him — speaks thus: / 'Any clever rogue (bahujña) thus, even when at fault, conceals the occasion of his own fault through various words — so you should not hold false pride in yourself' — this is [what she means]. / 'Conjoined' — / The purport is: because the general is connected to the particular. / [Bālapriyā:] He says — 'therein too' etc. / 'Phala' — / The meaning is: the predominance of the relation between the two meanings — corroborating power and corroborated content — conveyed by the word 'phala.' / 'Shines forth' — shines forth to the sensitive readers. / 'Arthāntara' etc. — / By the principle 'designations follow predominance,' the designation arthāntaranyāsa-dhvani alone [applies] here — this is the purport. / The reply of a certain woman who has concealed her anger within, whose signs of anger are not manifest, who is being appeased by the offending lover — [is] 'in the heart' etc. / He elaborates — 'whose anger is placed in the heart' etc. / 'Appeasing' ends in the vocative. / Or alternatively — 'you are' is the remainder. / 'It is not possible to produce anger' — / 'By me' is the remainder. / O bahujña! Since you are one who appeases me, therefore even toward you who have offended, I cannot produce anger — this is the meaning. / 'Of a bahujña' — / The meaning is: toward a bahujña. / 'Not possible' — / The meaning is: not possible by anyone. / The purport is: because of his concealment of his own fault through his cleverness. / 'Thus' — / The meaning is: of such a form. / The qualifier of 'samarthaka (corroborating) [and] samāna (general)' is 'anvitam anyat' (conjoined, other) etc. / 'Shines forth through purport' — / The meaning is: is suggested. / He elaborates the meaning stated in the vṛtti — 'here' etc. / 'Rests in a particular' — / The meaning is: 'I am not at fault,' 'I do not think of another woman,' 'be gracious to me who am solely devoted to you' etc. — as one knowledgeable of the particular meaning [conveyed by] the vocative 'bahujña' — this is the meaning. / He shows the dhvani — 'subsequently' etc. / 'The general-form corroborative' — / But that — [it is] what will be stated by 'whoever' etc. — 'she' — / The meaning is: the heroine in question. / 'Khaṇḍitā' — / 'When the lover is known to have gone to another, the khaṇḍitā is afflicted with jealousy' — this is its definition. / 'Appeased through cleverness' — pacified through his own cleverness; 'by the hero' is the remainder. / As to how she speaks — he says: 'whoever' etc. / 'You should not hold false self-regard' — because clever rogues, even when at fault, conceal the occasion of their own fault through various words — this is the meaning. / He shows by 'anvitam' that the relation intended is that of general-particular — 'of the particular' etc. / He elaborates 'prevails' etc. — 'his own' etc. / The vyatireka-dhvani (contrast-suggestion) is also possible in both forms. / Of these, the example of the first [type] was already shown earlier. /
(Sanskrit chāyā:) 'Would that I were born in a forest-region, as a hunchbacked tree with fallen leaves —
rather than in the human world, single-minded in giving (tyāga), yet destitute!' //

children.text: ita chāyā) atra hi tyāgaikarasasya daridrasya janmānabhinandanaṃ truṭitapatrrakubjapā dapajanmābhinandanaṃ ca sākṣācchabdavācyam /
children.translated_text: (Thus the chāyā.) For here, the non-celebration of the birth of one who is single-minded in giving yet destitute, and the celebration of the birth of a leafless hunchbacked tree — are directly stated by the words.

children.text: tathāvidhādapi pādapāttādṛśasya puṃsa upamānopameyatvapratītipūrvakaṃ śocyatāyāmādhikyaṃ tātparyeṇa prakāśayati /
children.translated_text: It illuminates through purport (tātparya) the excess of pitiableness of such a man compared to even such a tree — preceded by the apprehension of the upamāna-upameya (standard-of-comparison and object-of-comparison) relation.

this Malaya breeze causes travelers to swoon in spring.' //

[<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Vyatireka-dhvani</s> (contrast-suggestion) also' — by the word '<s>api</s>' (also) he states that, just like <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroborative instance), it too is of two kinds. /
'Previously' — thus. /
'Those who brilliantly illuminate the sky' — thus. /
'You are reddened by new sprouts' — thus. /
'May I be born' — in a forest region alone, in a secluded, dense part of the forest where, due to the abundance of clearly visible numerous trees, no one even looks. /
'Hunchbacked' — hence useless for the fashioning of forms [i.e., sculptures]. /
'With fallen leaves' — the purport is: it does not even provide shade; of what use would its bearing flowers and fruits be? /
Even such [a tree] might sometimes be useful to a charcoal-maker, or for the dwelling of owls and such — this is the implied meaning. /
'In the human' — the purport is: where supplicants are easily available. /
'World' — where one is seen by supplicants — through that, the supplicants [are implied]; and nothing can be done [for them] — that is a great misfortune — this is the purport. /
Here [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The reading 'those who brilliantly illuminate the sky' followed immediately by 'you are reddened by new sprouts' is seen in some [manuscripts]; that is erroneous. /
Or the reading '<s>na tu raktastvam</s>' etc. /
'<s>Kubja</s> (hunchbacked) alone' — this is the <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit rendering). /
He says that the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone) connects with '<s>vanoddeśa</s>' (forest region) — 'of the forest' etc. /
The elaboration of '<s>vanoddeśa</s>' — 'of the forest' etc. /
He states the implied meaning — 'where' etc. /
Thus in what follows above too it should be understood. /
'Fashioning of forms' — the meaning is: the manufacture of sculptures and such works. /
'With fallen leaves' — the reading '<s>truṭitatra</s>' (broken there) also [exists]. /
'Of a charcoal-maker' — the meaning is: of one who makes a living by charcoal. /
'I, a hunchbacked, leaf-fallen tree, may I be born as if in a forest region. /
With the sole delight of giving, and being poor — in the human world, may I not be born' — this is the syntactic construction. /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] The syntactic connection of '<s>śabdavācyam</s>' (expressible by word) is with '<s>prakāśayati</s>' (illuminates). /
For here, in spring, the <s>Malaya</s> breeze's capacity to cause the fainting of travelers is precisely through its being the arouser of the passion of love (<s>manmatha</s>). /
But that [capacity] is poetically fancied (<s>utprekṣita</s>) as being caused by the breath-wind of serpents clinging to sandalwood [trees] — thus the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), even though not directly stated, is perceived in reverberant form through the capacity of the sentence-meaning. /
And in such a subject-matter, it cannot be said that without the use of words like '<s>iva</s>' (like) etc., there is mere incoherence. /
Because of its indicative power, elsewhere too — [<s>Locana</s>:] there is no expressible figure (<s>vācyālaṅkāra</s>). /
By [saying] '<s>upamāna</s>' (standard of comparison), he establishes the purity of the path of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). /
'Superiority' — the meaning is: <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). /
'Poetically fancied' — for [the wind] intensified by poison-wind, [i.e.,] augmented, increased, causes delusion. /
And one who has fainted, among travelers, causes the loss of fortitude in others too, thereby producing [further] fainting — thus the poetic fancy (<s>utprekṣā</s>) is twofold. /
But here the qualifier functions only as being contained within the cause. /
So what? For the causal relationship is not real. /
Nevertheless, the causal relationship is poetically fancied — this amounts to something. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Establishes the purity of the path' — the purport is: the apprehension of the <s>upameya</s>-status (object-of-comparison status) through some degree of similarity, which is a component of <s>upamā</s> (simile), is a subsidiary element of the apprehension of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). /
In the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'in sandalwood' etc. — the meaning is: in the sandalwood trees on Mount <s>Malaya</s>. /
'In spring' — in the <s>vasanta</s> season. /
'Of the traveler' etc. — the meaning is: its capacity to produce the delusion of those separated [from their beloveds]. /
'In the passion of love' — the meaning is: as the stimulant of desire — through the real cause. /
'But that' — the meaning is: that capacity to cause the fainting of travelers. /
'In sandalwood' etc. — the meaning is: poetically fancied as caused by the breath-wind of serpents clinging to sandalwood. /
He elaborates this — 'by poison-wind' etc. /
'By poison-wind' — by wind mixed with poison. /
In the present context, the purport is: the connection of the breath-wind with poison is understood through its association with serpents. /
'<s>Mūrcchā</s>-<s>moha</s>-<s>samucchrāya</s>' — thus the <s>dhātupāṭha</s> (verbal root list). /
Therein, mostly in the sense of <s>samucchrāya</s> (increase) — he explains: '<s>bṛṃhita</s>' (augmented); the elaboration of that very [word] is '<s>upacita</s>' (increased). /
'Causes delusion' — the meaning is: it produces the state of delusion in another through its own contact. /
With the intention of elaborating in the sense of a group, he explains — 'and one who has fainted' etc. /
Here, the wind, which is the single referent of the word, should be understood as the traveler being imagined [as the wind]. /
'Loss of fortitude' — the meaning is: through that [fainting of others]. /
'Fainting' — the meaning is: delusion. /
'The poetic fancy is twofold' — the fancying of being intensified by poison-wind, and the attainment of the state of delusion — thus of both, the causal relationship to the <s>Malaya</s> breeze's causing the fainting of travelers is poetically fancied — this is the meaning. /
He shows, through doubt and resolution, that the <s>vṛtti</s> passage '<s>mūrchitatvenotprekṣitam</s>' (fancied as being caused by the intensified state) pertains to the stated causal poetic fancy — 'but here' etc. /
The qualifier — the qualifier [beginning with] 'in sandalwood' etc. /
'Only as being contained within the cause' — the meaning is: only as containing the cause. /
He resolves — 'so what?' etc. /
'So what?' — even if there is containment of the cause, what of it? /
'Why?' — to this he says — 'for' etc. /
The meaning is: the real causal relationship of that qualifier to the <s>Malaya</s> breeze's capacity to cause the fainting of travelers does not exist. /
'Nevertheless' — the meaning is: but. /
'The causal relationship is poetically fancied' — the meaning is: the causality of both [factors] is poetically fancied. /
'And the causal relationship is also [fancied]' — this reading also [exists]. /
In that reading, the word '<s>api</s>' effects the conjunction of the poetic fancy of the two [items] regarding the <s>Malaya</s> breeze. /
[The qualifier stating that] it is connected with the breath-wind of serpents clinging to sandalwood — [this] merely describes its actual nature; hence the completion of the expressible meaning should be understood. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'even though not directly stated' — the meaning is: even though not indicated by words like '<s>iva</s>' (like) etc. /
In the absence of their use, even then the apprehension of that meaning [occurs] — because of its being observed — he says: 'elsewhere too' etc. /
The passage beginning with '<s>tadaprayoga</s>' (without its use) he elaborates — 'of that very [word]' etc.
(<s>Chāyā</s>:) Even of your face clouded by jealousy, surely this full-moon,

(Thus the <s>chāyā</s>.) [<s>Locana</s>:] 'That' — even without the use of '<s>iva</s>' (like) and such [words], [there is] the apprehension of that meaning, i.e., the <s>utprekṣā</s>-form [of suggestion] — because of its being observed. /
He illustrates this very [point] — 'for example' etc. /
'Clouded by jealousy' — having a slightly reddish hue. /
But if the face, being serene, always bore resemblance [to the moon] — or what would [the moon] do? — that your face should become [like the moon] — this is beyond even the range of wishes — this is the purport of the word '<s>api</s>' (even). /
'In [its own] body' — in its own person — 'does not shine' — rather fills the ten directions — because [of this]. /
'Today' — the meaning is: only for this limited extent of time, for one day alone. /
Here, the filling of the directions by the full moon is a matter naturally established; it is poetically fancied thus [as being caused by attaining resemblance to her face]. /
[Anticipating the objection:] 'But the word <s>nanu</s> (surely), by expressing speculative poetic fancy, removes the incoherence' — considering this, [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>anuraṇana-rūpā</s>' (reverberant in form) — [meaning:] of the <s>saṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s> (gradually-perceived suggestion) type. /
'Is perceived' — is known. /
He raises a doubt — 'and not' etc. — 'in such a subject-matter' — the meaning is: in the context of 'clinging to sandalwood' etc. /
'Incoherence' — the meaning is: the incoherence of the <s>utprekṣā</s> with the sentence. /
That is to say: the non-expressibility by the sentence. /
He resolves — 'because of its indicative power' etc. /
The meaning is: because the qualifier 'clinging to sandalwood' etc., with the assistance of the recipient's imagination etc., has indicative power. /
Here he states the authority — 'elsewhere too' etc. /
He elaborates the passage '<s>tadaprayoga</s>' etc. — 'of that very' etc. /
'Jealousy' — this is an utterance to appease the angry heroine. The explanation of '<s>irṣyākaluṣasya</s>' (clouded by jealousy) — '<s>iṣat</s>' (slightly) etc. /
He states what is implied by the word '<s>api</s>' — 'but if' etc. /
'Would bear' and 'would do' — 'the moon' is the remainder in both. /
'Today' — he states the implication of this — 'always' etc. /
'That, then, what would it do?' — /
Due to the excess of satisfaction, 'whatever it would do, I do not know' — this is the meaning. /
'This becomes [that]' — the meaning is: becomes the moon. /
'In [its own] body alone' — this is the <s>chāyā</s>. /
The connection of '<s>eva</s>' (alone) is with '<s>na māti</s>' (does not shine) — he says: 'does not' etc. /
Here he states the implied reason — 'it fills the ten directions, because.' /
He elaborates the word '<s>adya</s>' (today) — 'for this extent' etc. /
He shows the <s>dhvani</s> — 'here' etc. /
'The filling of the directions' — the meaning is: the filling of the directions by its own radiance, which is obtained through 'it shines in its body alone.' /
'Naturally established' — not unnatural [i.e., a real phenomenon]. /
'Is poetically fancied thus' — the meaning is: the attainment of resemblance to your face is poetically fancied as the cause of the filling of the directions. /
He introduces another example — 'but' etc. /
By the word '<s>nanu</s>' (surely) — the meaning is: by the word '<s>nanu</s>' occurring in the <s>gāthā</s> (verse). /
The construal is: 'having attained resemblance — surely' — this is the purport. /
He explains the verse beginning with '<s>trāse</s>' (in fear) — 'everywhere' etc.
And in the usage of word and meaning, established convention (<s>prasiddhi</s>) alone is the authority.

utkṛṣṭamityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Is perceived' — is known.
'Valabhya' — the apprehension through śleṣa (double meaning), even though not [directly] in the word, operates as primary through the capacity of the meaning.

children.text: yathāsaṅkhyadhvaniryathā--- aṅkuritaḥ pallavitaḥ korakitaḥ puṣpitaśca sahakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: The yathāsaṅkhya-dhvani (suggestion through enumeration) is as follows — 'The sahakāra (mango) tree has sprouted, put forth leaves, formed buds, and blossomed;

children.text: aṅkuritaḥ pallavitaḥ korakitaḥ puṣpitaśca hṛdi madanaḥ //
children.translated_text: in the heart, <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) has sprouted, put forth leaves, formed buds, and blossomed.' //

[Bālapriyā:] Here, immediately after the apprehension of the sentence-meaning 'the brides together with the balconies attend [upon him],' as if [they were] brides — [Locana:] he cites another example — 'as for instance' etc. /
From all sides, leaping over dwellings, not alighting, even though not pursued by any bowmen, that deer did not stand still anywhere, due to the natural restlessness born of fear. /
And there, utprekṣā (poetic fancy) is suggested — by the women, struck by the arrows of their glances drawn to the ears, the beauty of whose eyes is their entire wealth, therefore he did not stand still. /
Anticipating the objection 'let this too be incoherent,' he says — 'of word and meaning' etc. /
'Patākā' — having attained the status of banner-cloths. /
'Beautiful' — because of this reason. /
'Patākās' — having attained fame. /
Of what appearance — of such appearance as 'beautiful'; 'secluded' — because of the absence of crowding with people, and for this reason, increasing rāga (desire for enjoyment). /
Others, however, [take] rāga as 'colorful beauty.' /
Also, increasing rāga (passionate attachment). /
Because they are secluded — the laṭabhās (beautiful women) whose limbs are well-proportioned. /
Whose balcony-edges have folds that bend. /
The creepers whose triple folds (trivalī) are bending. /
'Together' — the meaning is: 'along with.' /
But from the word 'sama' the meaning 'equal/similar' is also understood. /
[Bālapriyā:] He follows [the interpretation]; regarding 'did not stand still,' the actual reason — being agitated by fear — is shown by this, he says: 'by fear' etc. /
'Drawn to the ears' — extending to the edges of the ears, and also drawn to the ear; the eye-arrows — the eyes themselves being arrows — by those; therefore he did not stand still. /
The meaning is: he did not remain, precisely because of the stated reason. /
And thus here the suggestion is hetūtprekṣā-dhvani (suggestion of poetic fancy regarding cause) — this is the purport. /
Here too, the praise of the women's glance — the description of their nature beginning with 'drawn to the ear' etc. — the derivation of the sentence-meaning should be understood [accordingly]. /
'This too' — the meaning is: the cited example too. /
'Incoherent' — the meaning is: not conveying the meaning in the form of utprekṣā. /
In the vṛtti, 'of the word' — /
The meaning is: thus the usage 'such is the meaning of this word.' /
'Fame itself' — the apprehension of the cognizers itself. /
And thus, even in the stated context, even without a word like 'iva' (as if), the claim that the apprehension of the meaning in the form of utprekṣā by the sensitive reader is incoherent is not justified — this is the purport. /
He explains — 'patākā' etc. /
Here the first meaning applies to the balconies, and the second to the brides. /
He states an alternative interpretation — 'others' etc. /
'Laṭabhā' — the meaning is: beautiful women. /
'But' etc. — /
'From the word sama' — /
[Locana:] True; that too, through the force of śleṣa (double meaning) —

children.text:
atra hi yathoddeśamanūddeśe yacacārutvamanuraṇanarūpaṃ madanāviśeṣaṇabhūtāṅkuritādiśabdagataṃ tanmadanasahakārayostulyayogitāsamuccayalakṣaṇādvācyādatiricyamānamālakṣyate /
evamanye 'pyalaṅkārā yathoyogaṃ locanam tārkikamīmāṃsakayorna dhvaniprasaṅga ityalaṃ bahunā /
tadāha--aśabdāpīti /

children.translated_text: 'Thus others too' —
the suggestedness of all arthālaṅkāras (figures of meaning) is observed.

children.text: yathā ca dīpakadhvaniḥ-- mā bhavantamanalaḥ pavano vā vāraṇo madavalaḥ paraśurvā /
children.translated_text: And the dīpaka-dhvani (suggestion through the illumination figure) is as follows — 'May neither fire, nor wind, nor a mighty elephant in rut, nor an axe,

children.text: vajramindrakaraviprasṛtaṃ vā svasti te 'stu latayā saha vṛkṣa //
children.translated_text: nor the thunderbolt released from <s>Indra's</s> hand [harm you] — may you be well, O tree, together with the creeper!' //

For here, the charm that belongs to the words 'aṅkurita' (sprouted) etc. — which qualify <s>Madana</s> and are in the form of reverberation (anuraṇana), [proceeding] item by item as enumerated — being perceived as exceeding the expressible, which is characterized by tulyayogitā (common predication) and samuccaya (aggregation) of <s>Madana</s> and the sahakāra tree, that [charm] is perceived [as suggested]. /
Thus other alaṅkāras too, as appropriate —
The aprastutapraśaṃsā-dhvani (suggestion through praise of the irrelevant) is also [illustrated] —
[Prakrit:] 'Searching, you will die [among] the thorn-covered ketakī groves;
O bee, wandering about, you will not find [anything] resembling the mālatī flower!' //

Here, from the concealed dīpaka (illumination) figure in the word 'bādhiṣṭa' (would obstruct), the charm arises through the apprehension that [the tree and creeper] are objects of the most intense affection.

children.text:
priyatamena sākamudyāne viharantī kācinnāyikā bhramaramevamāheti bhṛṅgasyābhidhāyāṃ bālapriyā 'aṅkurite' iti saptamyantapāṭho 'pi pūrvārdhe dṛśyate /
locane--yathāceti /
tathā ca iti ca pāṭhaḥ /
ityatretyasya dīpakadhvanirityanenāpi sambandhaḥ /

bādhiṣṭheti dīpakāditi /
māṅarthānvitaluṅantabādhatyartharūpādanalādyanekānvayi dharmādityarthaḥ /
atyanteti /

cārutvaniṣpattiriti /
yatastato dīpakadhvaniriti sambandhaḥ /
atra "yaśca nimbaṃ paraśune"tyādāviva mā bhavantamanala ityatra dhākṣīdityasya, pavano vetyādau bhāṅkṣīrityasya, paraśurvetyādau bhaitsīdityasya cādhyāhāreṇa vācyārthaniṣpattirbodhyā /
aprastutapraśaṃsādhvanirapīti /

children.translated_text: The meaning is: the aprastutapraśaṃsā-dhvani (suggestion through praise of the irrelevant) caused by similarity is also [illustrated].
'Ḍuṇḍhu' etc. —
[Sanskrit chāyā:] Searching, you will die [among] the thorn-covered ketakī groves;
O bee, wandering about, you will not attain [anything] resembling the mālatī flower! //

A certain heroine, sporting in a garden with her beloved, addresses a bee thus — in the designation of the bee. [Bālapriyā:] The reading with the locative ending 'aṅkurite' is also seen in the first half. /
In the Locana — 'and as' etc. /
'And thus' is also a reading. /
Thus —

children.translated_text: 'He who' (<s>yaḥ</s>) — [this refers to the subject of the verse]. /

children.text: yaḥ gaurāṅgīkucakumbha iva bhūriḥ subhagaścābhogo yasya tasmin /
children.translated_text: He who — in [that which has] an expanse (<s>abhoga</s>) as abundantly beautiful as the breast-mound of a fair-limbed woman (<s>gaurāṅgī</s>) — in that [moon]. /

children.text: sudhādhāmani candre kālāgaruṇā yā patrabhaṅgaracanā racitaḥ patrabhaṅga iti yāvat, tadrūpeṇa yo vāsaḥ, yadvā---racanāyā āvāsaḥ āspadatvaṃ tena ekena sārāyate /
children.translated_text: In the moon (<s>sudhā-dhāman</s>, the abode of nectar) — the leaf-pattern design (<s>patra-bhaṅga-racanā</s>) made of dark <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood), [or alternatively:] the dwelling (<s>āvāsa</s>) for such design, i.e., being its locus — by that single [attribute] he is reduced to mere essence (<s>sārāyate</s>). /

children.text: he natāṅgi sundari ! locanam vicchedānaladīpitotkavanitācetodhivāsodbhavaṃ santāpaṃ vininīṣureṣa vitatairaṅgairnatāṅgi smaraḥ //
children.translated_text: O one of graceful form (<s>natāṅgi</s>), O beautiful one! [<s>Locana</s>:] Wishing to remove the burning pain (<s>santāpa</s>) that arises from dwelling in the hearts of women who are distressed by separation, [hearts] kindled by the fire of separation — <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), with outstretched limbs, O graceful one — //

Thus the <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit rendering). /
He elaborates — 'by the beloved' etc. /
'<s>Bhramara</s>' (bee) — the meaning is: a lotus-born bee moving toward the <s>ketakī</s> (screw-pine). /
'She says' — the meaning is: because she speaks, for that reason. /
'Of the bee' — the meaning is: of the story of the bee. /
When denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>) has its [proper] referent — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] It is precisely relevance [to the topic at hand]. /
Nor is there a cognition of irrelevance from the vocative address [to the bee], for on the contrary, the vocative is a manifestation of her naïveté (<s>maugdhya</s>) — therefore, through denotation at least, <s>aprastuta-praśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) is not completed. /
When denotation is completed, then by the force of the denoted meaning, the referral to another subject (<s>anyāpadeśatā</s>) is suggested. /
That is: a young wife, full of pride in her own good fortune, resembling a delicate-fragrant <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) blossom, out of guileless loving devotion, reproaches her beloved who is wandering about [among courtesans] — [those places] that have gained excessive fame through artificial sophistication, that are pervaded by <s>śambhalī</s>-thorns [i.e., procuresses], that are like groves of <s>ketakī</s> (screw-pine) whose fragrance spreads far — [he who is] frequenting the quarters of courtesans. /
The <s>apahnava-dhvani</s> (denial-suggestion) is as in [the verse] by our teacher <s>Bhaṭṭa Indurāja</s> — 'He who, in the moon — the abode of nectar — [which is] as abundantly beautiful as the breast-mound of a fair-limbed woman, is reduced to being the sole essence of the dwelling-design of leaf-patterns made of dark <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood)' — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Precisely relevance' — by the word '<s>eva</s>' (precisely), irrelevance is excluded. /
One might object — 'nor' etc. /
'From the vocative' — '<s>bhṛṅgasya</s>' (of the bee) carries over syntactically. /
The meaning is: from the vocative addressed to the bee, which is not a proper object of address. /
'Cognition of irrelevance' — knowledge of irrelevance. /
'Nor' — this is the syntactic connection. /
Asking 'why?' — he says: 'on the contrary' etc. /
Of that <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine), the <s>maugdhya</s> (naïveté), i.e., the state of being a <s>mugdhā</s> — as defined in '<s>mugdhā</s> is one who is new to the passion of youth' — its manifestation, i.e., caused by naïveté — this is the extent [of the meaning]. /
'<s>Iti</s>' is in the causal sense. /
'Through denotation at least' etc. — if the bee's story were irrelevant [to the topic], then the meaning in the form of reproaching the beloved would be the resting-place of the sentence, and through denotation its completability would follow; but since in the present case the bee's story too has the possibility of being relevant, it is primarily intended; the meaning in the form of reproaching the beloved is not completed through denotation — this is the meaning. /
'When completed' etc. — the meaning is: when, by the force of the context, the cognition of the denoted meaning pertaining to the bee and its [story] has been produced. /
'By the force of the denoted meaning' — the meaning is: by the force of similarity with the denoted meaning. /
'Referral to another subject' — the meaning is: another matter [is indicated]. /
Thus he says — 'that' etc. /
'<s>Sukumāra</s>' means beautiful; there is also the reading '<s>mugdha-kulavadhūr</s>' (naive young wife). /
'Of love' — the meaning is: of love directed toward the beloved. /
The connection is: out of devotion, she reproaches. /
'Artificial' — that which has gained excessive fame through artificial sophistication. /
'<s>Śambhalī</s>' — the meaning is: pervaded by procuresses who are like thorns. /
There is also the reading '<s>ḍāmbhika-kaṇṭaka</s>' (deceitful thorns). /
'Far-reaching' — the meaning is: whose fragrance spreads far — such <s>ketakī</s> groves — those [courtesans' quarters] are like them. /
'Frequenting' — the meaning is: repeatedly going there for the purpose of enjoying [them]. /
