'tvatkucasadṛśaścandraścandraścandrasamastvakuvābhogaḥ' ityarthapratiterupameyopamādhvanirapi /

children.translated_text: In this way, other varieties too can be imagined here.
Because the speech of a great poet is like a <s>kāmadhenu</s> (wish-fulfilling cow) in this respect.

children.text: yataḥ--- helāpi kasyacidacintyaphalaprasūtyai kasyāpi nālamaṇave 'pi phalāya yatnaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since — mere play (<s>helā</s>) of one [person] yields inconceivable fruit,

children.text: digdantiromacalanaṃ dharaṇīṃ dhunoti khātsampatannapi latāṃ calayenna bhṛṅgaḥ //
children.translated_text: The movement of a hair on an elephant of the quarters shakes the earth, but a bee, even falling upon [a creeper], does not make a vine tremble. //

Here, the marks (<s>lakṣmaṇa</s>) situated in the middle of the lunar disc — being of dark hue smeared with the scorching-stain [born from] the fire of separation that has arisen in the hearts of lovesick women — are suggested as having the form of the god of love (<s>Manmatha</s>) through <s>apahnava</s> (poetic denial). /
In the same [verse] there is also <s>sasandeha-dhvani</s> (doubt-suggestion) — since the name of that [figure] in the moon has not been taken [explicitly]. /
Rather, in the moon — which stands in the place of the breast-expanse of a fair-limbed woman — [the mark] which excels as the sole essence by being the locus for the leaf-pattern design of dark <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) — we do not know what this entity is — thus <s>sasandeha</s> (doubt) too is suggested. /
A [heroine], having previously not accepted [her beloved's] advances and now repentant, distressed by the longing of separation, having become a <s>vāsakasajjā</s> (one adorned and prepared for the beloved's arrival) through the performance of adornment etc. in expectation of the beloved's coming — at the occasion of the rise of the full moon, the beloved, brought through a female messenger, making a flattering speech — 'This leaf-pattern design of dark <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) placed on your breast-mounds acts as a stimulant of love' — and [saying] 'this [dark mark] on the moon, with a lustre dark as a <s>kuvalaya</s>-petal, does the very same thing' — thus <s>prativastūpamā-dhvani</s> (counter-image simile suggestion) is also [present]. /
The word '<s>sudhā-dhāman</s>' (abode of nectar), adopted as a synonym for the moon, also [functions as expressing] the cause [of cooling] in the phrase 'wishing to remove the burning pain' — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Eṣa</s>' (this) — '<s>yaḥ</s>' (who) in the verse serves as the reference — the meaning is '<s>saḥ</s>' (he/that). /
'Separation' — separation from the beloved is itself the fire; by that [fire], kindled — the hearts of women who are <s>utkā</s> (distressed/longing) — from dwelling in them, that which arises — that [burning pain]. /
'Wishing to remove the burning pain' — wishing to lead away, to quench — this contains an implicit reason. /
'With outstretched' — the meaning is: with spread-out [limbs]. /
<s>Smara</s> (the god of love), characterized by [his] limbs, manifests — this is the syntactic connection. /
He demonstrates the <s>dhvani</s> — by 'here' etc. /
'<s>Apahnava</s>' (denial) — the meaning is: 'this is not the [moon's] mark, but rather the god of love of such-and-such a form' — this is the denial. /
The passage 'since' etc. up to 'excels' is the commentator's statement. /
'Of that' — the meaning is: of the mark (<s>lakṣmaṇa</s>). /
'Has not been taken' — the meaning is: has not been specifically stated. /
'Rather' carries over syntactically. /
'Rather' — the connection is with 'has been taken.' /
'Thus stated' — this is the meaning. /
The expanse-possessing breast of a fair-limbed woman — equal to that — this is the meaning. /
The elaboration of '<s>racanā-āvāsa</s>' (dwelling for design) is — 'by being the locus for the design' etc. /
'Excels' — the meaning is: attains [that status]. /
This is a statement of the resultant meaning. /
'<s>Sāra</s>' (essence) — the analysis is either: 'excels as if excellent' or 'becomes the essence.' /
'That' — the meaning is: because of such a description. /
'We do not know' etc. — this is the expression of the form of doubt. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — the meaning is: from the cognition of the speaker-hero's doubt in the form of non-determination as stated above. /
'<s>Sasandeha</s>' — the figure of <s>sasandeha</s> (doubt). /
'<s>Api</s>' (also) — in the sense of conjunction. /
'Previously' etc. — '<s>praṇaya</s>' means the beloved's solicitation. /
'Repentant' — the meaning is: possessing subsequent regret. /
'Having become' — '<s>nāyikā</s>' (heroine) is the remainder. /
The connection with 'making a flattering speech' belongs to this [clause]. /
'Your' etc. — this is the flattering speech. /
'Does the very same thing' — the meaning is: acts as a stimulant of love. /
'Thus <s>prativastūpamā-dhvani</s>' — the meaning is: by the cognition of the meaning of the speaker-hero's flattering speech — 'the leaf-pattern design of dark <s>aguru</s> placed on your breast-mounds acts as a stimulant of love; this [mark] on the moon, with a lustre dark as a <s>kuvalaya</s>-petal, does the very same thing' — thereby there is a <s>dhvani</s> of <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-image simile). /
'The cause' — the rest is: of the purpose expressed by the potential mood [in the verb]. /
There is also the reading: 'kindles along with beauties' [instead of 'removes the burning']. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] He reveals — thus there is also a <s>hetu-alaṅkāra-dhvani</s> (suggestion of the figure of causation). /
'The beauty of your breasts and the beauty of the moon together kindle love' — thus there is also a <s>sahokti-dhvani</s> (suggestion of the figure of co-statement). /
'The moon is like your breasts; your breast-expanse is like the moon' — from the cognition of such meaning, there is also an <s>upameyopamā-dhvani</s> (suggestion of the figure of mutual comparison). /

children.text: eṣāṃ tu bhedānāṃ saṃsṛṣṭitva saṅkaratvaṃ ca yathāyogaṃ cintyam /
children.translated_text: But the intermingling (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>) and combination (<s>saṅkara</s>) of these varieties should be considered as appropriate.

children.text: atiśayoktidhvaniryathā mamaiva--- kelīkandalitasya vibhramamadhordhuryaṃ vapuste dṛśau bhaṅgībhaṅgarakāmakārbhukamidaṃ bhrūnarmakarmakramaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Atiśayokti-dhvani</s> (hyperbole-suggestion) is as follows, from my own [work] — 'Your body is the foremost champion of the charm that blossoms in sport (<s>kelī</s>); your two eyes are the playful, curving bow of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) with its sequence of graceful movements;

children.text: āpāte 'pi vikārakāraṇamaho vaktrāmbujanmāsavaḥ satyaṃ sundari vedhasastrijagatīsārastvamekākṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: even at first glance, the nectars born from your lotus-face are the cause of emotional transformation — truly, O beautiful one, you are the single form that is the essence of <s>Brahmā</s>'s three worlds!' //

children.text:
atra hi madhu māsamadanāsavānāṃ trailokye subhagatānyonyaṃ paripoṣakatvena /
te tu bālapriyā heleti /
helā līlā /
yatnaḥ buddhipūrvako vyāpāraḥ /
vākyadvaye bhavatīti śeṣaḥ /
uktaṃ sāmānyaṃ viśeṣeṇa samarthayati---digdantītyādi /
digdantino 'ṅgacalanamiti ca pāṭhaḥ /
eṣāṃ tvityādi /
apahnavena sahetareṣāṃ saṃsṛṣṭiḥ, sasandehaprativastūpamopameyopamānāmekavākyānupraveśasaṅkara ityādikaṃ cintyamityarthaḥ /
kelīti /
he sundari ! te tava dṛśau kelīvilāsijanasya krīḍā tasyāḥ kandalaṃ navāṅkuraḥ riṣadāvirbhāva iti yāvat /
tadasya sañjātamiti kelīkandalitaḥ, tasya acirāvirbhūtasyetyarthaḥ /
vibhramaḥ strīṇāṃ śṛhgāraceṣṭā tatkārī vibhramaḥ śobhā, tacchālī vā yo madhurvasantaḥ tasya dhuraṃ kāmoddīpanādibhāraṃ vahatīti dhuryam /
vapuḥ sta iti śeṣaḥ /
tvadīyaṃ netradvitayamacirāvirbhūtasya vasantasya kāmoddīpanādikāryakāri śarīraṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
tathā te idamityādyekaṃ padam /
ayamanubhavaikagocaro bhruvornarmakarmaṇaḥ līlāyāḥ kramaḥ kramikalīlāviśiṣṭabhrūyugmamityarthaḥ /
bhaṅkī racanāviśeṣaḥ, tayā hetunā bhaṅguraṃ vakraṃ, yadvā---bhaṅgīyuktaṃ vakraṃ ca yat kāmasya kārbhukaṃ kramikakarmaviśiṣṭaṃ dhanuḥ tadbhavati /
yadvā---idamiti bhinnaṃ padaṃ karmukaviśeṣaṇaṃ, kramikakarmaviśiṣṭamiti tadarthaḥ /
tathā te vaktrāmbujanmani mukhapajhe ya āsavaḥ madyaviśeṣaḥ /
atrāsavatvenādhararasasyādhyavasāyaḥ /
āpāte 'pi kiñjidāsvāde 'pi /
kikārāṇāṃ sammohānandādirūpacittavikārāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bhavati /
aho idamadbhutam /
ataḥ tvamekā vedhasaḥ kṛtiḥ sṛṣṭiḥ trijagatīsāraḥ trailokyasārabhūtā bhavati /
satyaṃ niścitam /
atra hītyasya dhvanyata ityādibhiḥ sambandhaḥ /
poṣakatvenetyantaṃ hetuvacanam /
te ityādivyaṅgyakathanam /
yojanīyāḥ /
evamalaṅkāradhvanimārgaṃ vyutpādya tasya prayojanavattāṃ khyāpayitumidamucyate--
children.translated_text:
For here, <s>madhu</s> (honey/spring), the month of <s>Māsa</s>, and the intoxicating liquor of love (<s>madanāsava</s>) — in the three worlds, their mutual quality of being enhancers of each other's beauty — /
But [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Helā</s>' etc. — '<s>helā</s>' means play (<s>līlā</s>). /
'<s>Yatna</s>' (effort) means a purposeful action. /
'Occurs' is the remainder for both sentences. /
He supports the general [statement] with a specific [example] — 'of the elephant of the quarters' etc. /
There is also the reading '<s>digdantino 'ṅga-calanam</s>' (the bodily movement of the elephant of the quarters). /
'Of these, but' etc. — /
The intermingling (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>) with denial [and other figures], the combination (<s>saṅkara</s>) — where doubt, counter-image simile, and mutual comparison [figures] enter a single sentence — such and similar [combinations] should be considered — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Kelī</s>' etc. — /
O beautiful one! Your two eyes — of sport (<s>kelī</s>), i.e., of amorous play — the fresh sprout (<s>kandala</s>), i.e., the newly appeared [form] — of that [sport] which has just arisen — that is the meaning. /
The charm (<s>vibhrama</s>) — the erotic gestures of women — that which produces them is <s>vibhrama</s>, i.e., beauty, or [the body] endowed with it — of the sweet springtime (<s>madhura-vasanta</s>) — [your body] bears its yoke (<s>dhurya</s>), i.e., carries the burden of love's arousal etc. /
'<s>Vapuḥ</s>' (body) — '<s>asti</s>' (is) is the remainder. /
The meaning is: your pair of eyes is the body that produces the effects of love's arousal etc. of the newly arisen spring. /
Likewise, '<s>te idam</s>' etc. is a single word. /
This sequence of sport-actions of the eyebrows — [namely,] the pair of eyebrows distinguished by sequential playful action — that is apprehensible only through direct experience — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Bhaṅgī</s>' is a particular mode of arrangement; by that as cause, it is curved (<s>bhaṅgura</s>), i.e., crooked; or alternatively: that which is endowed with <s>bhaṅgī</s> (grace) and is crooked — that is <s>Kāma</s>'s bow, distinguished by sequential action — it becomes [that bow]. /
Or alternatively: '<s>idam</s>' is a separate word qualifying the bow, and its meaning is 'distinguished by sequential action.' /
Likewise, the <s>āsavas</s> (intoxicating nectars) born in your lotus-face (<s>vaktrāmbuja</s>). /
Here, the lip-juice is metaphorically identified as <s>āsava</s> (liquor). /
'Even at first glance' — even upon the slightest taste. /
It becomes the cause of emotional transformations (<s>vikāras</s>) — in the form of bewilderment, bliss, etc. /
How wonderful! /
Therefore, you alone are <s>Brahmā</s>'s creation (<s>kṛti</s>), his fashioning — the essence of the three worlds, i.e., you are the quintessence of the three worlds. /
'<s>Satyam</s>' (truly) — certainly. /
The connection of 'for here' is with 'is suggested' etc. /
The passage ending with 'being enhancers' is the statement of the reason. /
'<s>Te</s>' (those) etc. is the statement of what is suggested. /
[These] should be connected [syntactically]. /
Having thus expounded the path of <s>alaṅkāra-dhvani</s> (figure-suggestion), in order to proclaim its purposefulness, this is stated —
Those [figures] whose embodiment (<s>śarīrīkaraṇa</s>) is not established in [the domain of] the expressible —

children.text: te 'laṅkārāḥ parāṃ chāyāṃ yānti dhvanyaṅgatāṃ gataḥ // DhvK_2.28 //
children.translated_text: those <s>alaṅkāras</s> attain the highest beauty when they have become subsidiary to <s>dhvani</s>. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.28 //
Those [figures] whose embodiment is not established in [the domain of] the expressible —

children.text: te 'laṅkārāḥ parāṃ chāyāṃ yānti dhvanyaṅgatāṃ gataḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: those <s>alaṅkāras</s> attain the highest beauty when they have become subsidiary to <s>dhvani</s>. // 28 //

children.text:
dhvanyaṅgatā cobhābhyāṃ prakārābhyāṃ vyañjakatvena vyaṅgyatvena ca /
tatreha prakaraṇādyvaṅgyatvenetyavagantavyam /
vyaṅgyatve 'pyalaṅkārāṇāṃ pradhānyavivakṣāyāmeva locanam tvayi lokottareṇa vapuṣā sambhūya sthitā ityatiśayoktirdhvanyate /
āpāte 'pi vikārakāraṇamityāsvādaparamparākriyayāpi vinā vikārātmanaḥ phalasya sampattiriti vibhāvanādhvanirapi /
vibhramamadhordhuryamiti tulyayogitādhvanirapi /

children.translated_text: Thus it should be understood that all <s>alaṅkāras</s> have the capacity to be suggested.
But not in the manner that some have restricted to a fixed domain.
'As appropriate' — thus.
The meaning to be construed is: sometimes an <s>alaṅkāra</s> and sometimes content (<s>vastu</s>) is the suggestor. // 2.7 //

And subsidiarity to <s>dhvani</s> (<s>dhvanyaṅgatā</s>) is of both kinds — through being the suggestor (<s>vyañjakatva</s>) and through being the suggested (<s>vyaṅgyatva</s>). /
Herein, from the context, it should be understood as suggestedness. /
Even when the suggestedness of <s>alaṅkāras</s> is intended as predominant — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'In you, with a body that is extraordinary in the world, having come together and remained' — the <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is suggested. /
'Even at first encounter, it causes transformation' — even without the successive process of relishing, the attainment of the fruit in the form of transformation [occurs] — thus the <s>vibhāvanā-dhvani</s> (suggestion through impossibility) also [is present]. /
'The foremost in coquettish charm' — the <s>tulyayogitā-dhvani</s> (suggestion through equal applicability) also [is present].

children.text:
nanuktāstāvaccirantanairalaṅkārāsteṣāṃ tu bhavatā yadi vyaṅgyatvaṃ pradarśitaṃ kimiyatetyāśaṅkyāha--evamityādi /
yeṣāmalaṅkārāṇāṃ vācyatvena śarīrīkaraṇaṃ śarīrabhūtātprastutādarthāntarabhūtatayā aśarīrāṇāṃ kaṭakādisthānīyānāṃ śarīratāpādanaṃ vyavasthitaṃ bālapriyā te madhumadanāsavāḥ /
lokāttareṇa vapuṣeti /
netrarūpeṇa bhrūrūpeṇādhararasarūpeṇa ca śarīreṇetyarthaḥ /
madanadhanuṣo bhrūrūpeṇa sthityā madanasya sthitiḥ sidhyatīti bodhyam /
itīti /
itivaktṛkāmukavākyārthapratītyetyarthaḥ /
atiśayoktiriti /
netrādau /
vasantādyabhedapratītyā bhede abhedarūpātiśayoktirityarthaḥ /
tulyayogiteti /
dṛgdvayasya madhośca sāmyavivakṣayā dṛśau vibhramamadhordhuryaṃ vapurityuktyā "nyūnasyāpi viśiṣṭene"tyādinā bhāmahādilakṣitā tulyayogitetyarthaḥ /
'evamanye 'pyalaṅkārā' iti bahuvacanalabdhamarthamāha---evamityādi /
gamyaṃ vyavacchedyamāha---na tvityādi /
na tviti /

children.translated_text: 'Thus' — is the remainder.
'Fixed' — thus.

children.text: niyataḥ niyamitaḥ viṣayaḥ alaṅkāraviśeṣarūpāśrayo yasya tatkṛtamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Fixed' means restricted; the meaning is: one whose domain — the particular <s>alaṅkāra</s>-form substrate — has been limited by that [restriction].
'Being suggested' (<s>dhvanyamānatva</s>) carries over. // 2.7 //

Anticipating the objection 'the <s>alaṅkāras</s> stated by the ancients are just these many; if their suggestedness has been demonstrated by you, what is the point of this much [discussion]?' — he says: 'thus' etc. /
Of those <s>alaṅkāras</s> whose embodiment (<s>śarīrīkaraṇa</s>) through expressibility is established — the conferring of bodily status upon those that are bodiless, standing in the position of bracelets etc., as other than the present body-constituted [content] — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Those are the intoxicating liquors of love.' /
'With a body extraordinary in the world' — /
The meaning is: by a body in the form of the eyes, the eyebrows, and the essence of the lips. /
It should be understood that by the remaining of the bow of <s>Madana</s> (Kāmadeva) in the form of the eyebrows, the abiding of <s>Madana</s> himself is established. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — /
The meaning is: through the cognition of the sentence-meaning spoken by the speaker-lover. /
'<s>Atiśayokti</s>' — /
In the eyes etc. — /
The meaning is: the <s>atiśayokti</s> in the form of non-difference upon what is different, through the cognition of non-difference with spring etc. /
'<s>Tulyayogitā</s>' — /
With the intention of stating the equality of the two eyes and [the god of] love, by the statement 'the eyes are the foremost in coquettish charm' — the <s>tulyayogitā</s> defined by <s>Bhāmaha</s> and others as 'even of the inferior with the superior' etc. — this is the meaning. /
He states the meaning obtained by the plural in 'thus other <s>alaṅkāras</s> also': 'thus' etc. /
He states what is to be excluded from the implication: 'but not' etc. /
'But not' —

children.text:
kimiyateti /
alaṅkārāṇāṃ vyaṅgyatvapradarśanena kiṃ phalamityarthaḥ /
āheti /
śarīrītyādinā tatphalaṃ darśayatītyarthaḥ /
kārikāṃ vyācaṣṭe--yeṣāmityādi /
vācyatveneti hetau tṛtīyā /
cvipratyayārthaṃ darśayan vyācaṣṭe---śarīrabhūtādityādi /
śarīratāpādanamiti /
śarīratvasampādanamityarthaḥ /
vyavasthitatve gamyaṃ hetumāha---sukavināmayatnasampādyatayā /
satyāṃ dhvanāvantaḥpātaḥ /
itarathā tu guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatvaṃ pratipādayiṣyate /
āṅgitvena vyaṅgyatāyāmapi /
alaṅkārāṇāṃ dvayī gatiḥ--kadācidvastumātreṇa vyajyante, kadācidalaṅkāreṇa /
tatra--- vyajyante vastumātreṇa yadālaṅkṛtayastayā /
dhruvaṃ dhvanyaṅgatā tāsāṃ
children.translated_text:
'What is the point of this much' — /
The meaning is: what is the result of demonstrating the suggestedness of <s>alaṅkāras</s>? /
'He says' — /
The meaning is: he shows that result by means of 'embodiment' etc. /
He explains the <s>kārikā</s>: 'of those' etc. /
'Through expressibility' — the instrumental is in the causal sense. /
Showing the meaning of the <s>cvi</s>-suffix, he explains: 'from the body-constituted' etc. /
'The conferring of bodily status' — /
The meaning is: the accomplishment of bodily status. /
He states the implied reason for 'established': because it is accomplished through the effort of skilled poets. /
When <s>dhvani</s> is present, [there is] entry into the inner [nature of poetry]. /
Otherwise, however, the status of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggested meaning) will be demonstrated. /
Even when suggestedness takes the form of the principal — /
The twofold course of <s>alaṅkāras</s> [is this]: sometimes they are suggested by mere content, sometimes by [another] <s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
In that regard — when figures are suggested by mere content, they are adorned through that;  /
assuredly their subsidiarity to <s>dhvani</s> [is established] —
... the poetic mode (<s>kāvya-vṛtti</s>) is dependent on that. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.29 //
Here is the reason —
Here is the reason — the poetic mode is dependent on that. // 29 //

children.text:
locanam yadi vā vācyatve sati yeṣāṃ śarīratāpādanamapi na vyavasthitaṃ durghaṭamiti yāvat /
te 'laṅkārā dhvanervyāpārasya kāvyasya vāṅgatāṃ vyaṅgyarūpatayā gatāḥ santaḥ parāṃ durlabhāṃ chāyāṃ kāntimātmarūpatāṃ yānti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati---sukavirvidagdhapurandhīvadbhūṣaṇaṃ yadyapi śliṣṭaṃ yojayati, tathāpi śarīratāpattirevāsya kaṣṭasampādyā kuṅkumapītikāyā iva /
children.translated_text: This is what is said: just as a skilled poet — like a sophisticated lady — though [she] applies ornament in a fitting manner, nevertheless the attainment of bodily status for it is extremely difficult to accomplish — like that of a saffron paste.
But as for self-identity (<s>ātmatā</s>) — what possibility is there even [of that]?

children.text: evambhūtā ceyaṃ vyaṅgyatā yā apradhānabhūtāpi vācyamātrālaṅkārebhya utkarṣamalaṅkārāṇāṃ vitarati /
children.translated_text: Such is this suggestedness, which, even while being non-predominant, bestows upon the <s>alaṅkāras</s> an excellence beyond that of merely expressible <s>alaṅkāras</s>.
Like kingship even in a child's game — keeping this meaning in mind, he says: 'otherwise, however' etc. // 2.8 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] Or alternatively, even when expressibility is present, of those [<s>alaṅkāras</s>] for whom even the conferring of bodily status is not established — is difficult to achieve, that is — those <s>alaṅkāras</s>, having attained subsidiarity to <s>dhvani</s>, to the poetic function, in the form of suggestedness, attain a supreme, rare splendor (<s>chāyā</s>), a radiance, an identity with the self.

tatreti /

children.translated_text: 'Of what kind?' — to this he says: 'which' etc.
'Like kingship' — thus.
'Of the royal child compared to other children' —
is the remainder. // 2.8 //

'Therein' — /
When the twofold course exists. /
'Here is the reason' — this is the <s>vṛtti</s> passage. /
'Of poetry, of the poet's activity' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'of skilled poets' etc. /
'When expressibility is present' — this is a locative absolute. /
'Not' is a separate word — thus he explains alternatively: 'or alternatively' etc. /
He explains the word '<s>dhvani</s>' in '<s>dhvanyaṅgatām</s>' (subsidiarity to <s>dhvani</s>) in two ways: 'of the [poetic] activity' etc. /
'How is there subsidiarity?' — to this he says: 'in the form of suggestedness' etc. /
With the intention of the alternative explanation, he states the purport: 'this is what is said' etc. /
'Ornament' — /
The meaning is: <s>upamā</s> and other [figures], as well as saffron and such [cosmetics]. /
'In a fitting manner' — /
The meaning is: closely attached. /
'Very closely attached' is also a variant reading. /
'Attainment of bodily status' means accomplishment of bodily status. /
'Of it' — /
The meaning is: of ornament such as <s>upamā</s> etc. /
'Saffron' — /
A particular unguent containing saffron is the saffron paste; the meaning is: like that [paste]. /
'Of self-identity' — /
The meaning is: of the accomplishment of self-identity. /
'Of it' carries over. /
'What possibility even' — /
The meaning is: the accomplishment of self-identity is extremely difficult to achieve. /
He introduces the passage 'otherwise, however' etc.: 'such' etc. /
The construal is: this suggestedness is such.

children.translated_text:
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] For this has been stated: 'The determination of predominance between the expressible and the suggested is based on the excellence of beauty.' /
And when suggestedness is of mere content, the domain [of <s>dhvani</s>] should be inferred from the examples just shown. /
Thus, whether by mere content or by content in the form of a particular <s>alaṅkāra</s> — [<s>Locana</s>:] The poetic mode is dependent on the <s>alaṅkāra</s>, being inclined toward <s>alaṅkāra</s>, because — /
'Otherwise' — /
The meaning is: if there is no orientation toward that [<s>alaṅkāra</s>]. /
Therefore, therein, <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatā</s> (subordinated suggested meaning) is not even to be suspected — /
this is the purport. /
'Of those same adorned [figures]' — this is a supplement to the <s>kārikā</s> about to be recited. /
'Again' — this is a supplement within the middle of the <s>kārikā</s>. /
'Subsidiarity to <s>dhvani</s>' — /
The meaning is: being a variety of <s>dhvani</s>. /
'Predominance of the suggested' — /
Here is the reason: 'from the excellence of beauty.' /
'If' — /
But when that [suggested element] is not predominant, the expressible <s>alaṅkāra</s> alone is predominant — thus it is <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> — this is the purport. /
Anticipating the objection 'an <s>alaṅkāra</s> is suggested by content and also by another <s>alaṅkāra</s> — why then have examples of this not been shown?' — he says: 'content' etc. /
He summarizes this in brief: 'thus' etc. /
Of the suggested — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] she explains with the intention of the <s>kārikā</s> reading: 'of poetry' etc. /
'Of the poet's activity' — /
The meaning is: of [the activity] that has the form of word and meaning. /
'Mode' (<s>vṛtti</s>) — /
The meaning is: standing, abiding. /
With the intention that 'that <s>alaṅkāra</s> is the substrate on which it depends,' she explains: '<s>alaṅkāra</s>' etc. /
'If there is no orientation toward that' — /
The meaning is: if there is no orientation toward the suggested <s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'it would be merely a verbal statement' — /
'That' refers to what is considered to be poetry. /
'Merely a verbal statement' — the meaning is: not constituting poetry. /
Therefore one must accept the orientation toward that, and thus it is indeed subsidiarity to <s>dhvani</s> — this is the purport. /
He shows the purport of this in the <s>Locana</s>: 'therefore' etc. /
The connection of 'of those same' is also with 'when the suggested status of being another <s>alaṅkāra</s> [is present].' /
With the intention that the meaning of 'of those same' is 'of the adorned ones,' he says it was stated in the <s>vṛtti</s> as 'of those same adorned ones': 'of those same' etc. /
'About to be recited' etc. — /
The meaning is: by attaining connection with the forthcoming <s>kārikā</s> too, [this phrase] serves as a remover of the expectation 'of which ones?' /
He explains in accordance with the present context: 'being a variety of <s>dhvani</s>' etc. /
The meaning is: being a sub-variety of <s>dhvani</s>. /
'The expressible <s>alaṅkāra</s> alone' — /
The meaning is: <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) etc. alone. /
The meaning of '<s>alaṅkārāntaravyaṅgyabhāve</s>' in the <s>kārikā</s> is: 'when there is suggestedness by another <s>alaṅkāra</s>.' /
He states the essential meaning of the passage beginning with 'thus': 'of the suggested' etc. /
Or [alternatively,] when illumination [occurs], when the excellence of beauty is established as the basis, when there is predominance — the suggested <s>dhvani</s> arising from the power of meaning, in the reverberant form, should be understood. /
Having thus demonstrated the varieties of <s>dhvani</s>, in order to make the discrimination of <s>dhvani</s>-semblance (<s>dhvanābhāsa</s>), it is stated —
Where the cognized meaning appears as obscured (<s>pramliṣṭa</s>) —

children.text: vācyasyāṅgatayā vāpi nāsyāsau gocaro dhvaneḥ // DhvK_2.31 //
children.translated_text: or as subsidiary to the expressible — that is not the domain of this <s>dhvani</s>. // <s>DhvK</s> 2.31 //
Where the cognized meaning appears as obscured —
or as subsidiary to the expressible — that is not the domain of this <s>dhvani</s>. // 31 //

children.text: kamalāarā ṇaṃ maliā haṃsā uḍḍāviā ṇa a piucchā /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] The lotuses have been split, the jasmine flowers [scattered], the swans have flown away, and the tails of peacocks [have drooped] —

children.text: locanam vyañjakasya ca pratyekaṃ vastvalaṅkārarūpatayā dviprakāratvāccaturvidho 'yamathaśaktyudbhava iti tātparyam //29//
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] And because the suggestor individually has a twofold nature — of content and of <s>alaṅkāra</s>-form — this meaning-power-born [<s>dhvani</s>] is fourfold — this is the purport. // 29 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] The cognized [meaning] is also twofold: clear (<s>sphuṭa</s>) and unclear (<s>asphuṭa</s>). /
Of these, that which manifests clearly through the power of word or the power of meaning alone is the path of <s>dhvani</s>, not the other. /
Even that which is clear but which is cognized as appearing subsidiary to the expressible — that is not the domain of this <s>dhvani</s> in the reverberant-form suggested.

children.translated_text: This is the elaboration of the first half [of the verse] beginning with 'where' etc.
[The vṛtti states:] 'Though twofold also' etc.
The construal is: the apprehended [meaning], being clear and unclear, is also twofold.

children.text: keṇa vi gāmataḍāe abbhaṃ uttāṇaaṃ phaliham //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] By someone, a cloud has been laid face-up in the village pond! //

[Bālapriyā:] 'Thus' — / The two root divisions are: avivakṣitavācya (where the literal meaning is not intended) and vivakṣitānyaparavācya (where the literal meaning is intended but another meaning is paramount). / The first has two subdivisions: atyantatiraskṛtavācya (where the literal meaning is completely suppressed) and arthāntarasaṃkramitavācya (where the literal meaning is transferred to another meaning). / The second has two subdivisions: alakṣyakrama (imperceptible sequence) and anuraṇanarūpa (reverberant form). / The first [alakṣyakrama] has infinite subdivisions. / The second is twofold: śabdaśaktimūla (rooted in word-power) and arthaśaktimūla (rooted in meaning-power). / The latter [arthaśaktimūla] is threefold: kaviprauḍhoktikṛtaśarīra (embodied through the poet's bold expression), kavinibaddhavaktṛprauḍhoktikṛtaśarīra (embodied through the bold expression of a speaker created by the poet), and svatassambhavī (naturally arising). / And each of these, through the stated method of dividing the suggested and the suggestor, becomes fourfold — thus the arthaśaktimūla is of twelve kinds. / The first four subdivisions [make] sixteen principal varieties. / And these will be stated as each being twofold through being illuminated by word or by sentence. / But the alakṣyakrama [type] has thirty-five subdivisions through being illuminated by phoneme, word, sentence, composition, and extended narrative. / The distinction from their semblances — from the semblances of dhvani — is the classification. / [Bālapriyā:] For easy comprehension, she compiles the stated and forthcoming subdivisions of dhvani — by the passage from 'avivakṣitavācya' to 'thirty-five subdivisions.' / 'Through the stated method of dividing' — / The meaning is: through the division into vastu (content) and alaṅkāra (figure). / 'The first four' — / The meaning is: the four [types] are atyantatiraskṛtavācya, arthāntarasaṅkramitavācya, alakṣyakramavyaṅgya, and śabdaśaktimūlānuraṇanarūpa. / 'Will be stated as twofold' — / And thus the meaning is: thirty-two. / 'Phoneme' etc. — / Since the division through word and sentence illumination has already been stated, by this [additional criterion] only the three [further] divisions through phoneme, composition, and narrative illumination are intended — and thus there are thirty-five subdivisions. / 'From their semblances' etc. — / The connection of 'of dhvani' should be understood here as well. /

children.text:
atra hi pratiyamānasya mugdhavadhvā jaladharapratibimbadarśanasya vācyāṅgatvameva /
evaṃvidhe viṣaye 'nyatrāpi yatra vyaṅgyāpekṣayā vācyasya cārutvotkarṣapratītyā prādhānyamavasīyate, tatra vyaṅgyāpekṣayā vācyasya cārutvotkarṣapratītyā prādhānyamavasīyate, tatra vyaṅgyasyāṅgatvena pratīterdhvaneraviṣayatvam /

children.translated_text: For example —
[Prakrit:] Of [the young wife] hearing the clamor of birds flying up from a thicket of cane,
though engaged in household work — her limbs grow languid! //

[Vṛtti:] For here, the apprehended [meaning] — the naive young woman's seeing the reflection of a cloud — has the status of being merely subsidiary to the expressible. / In this type of subject matter, and elsewhere too, where the predominance of the expressible over the suggested is determined through the apprehension of the expressible's superior charm — there, because the suggested is apprehended as merely subsidiary, it is not within the domain of dhvani.

children.text: evaṃvidho hi viṣayaḥ prāyeṇa guṇībhūtavyaṅgyasyodāharaṇatvena nirdakṣyate /
locanam asyetyātmabhūtasya dhvanerasau kāvyaviśeṣo na gocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: [Locana:] 'Of this' — that variety of poetry whose essential nature is dhvani — that [poetry] is not its domain.

children.text: kamalākarā na malitā haṃsā uḍḍāyitā na ca sahasā /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] The lotus-pools are not muddied, the swans have not suddenly flown up —
The meaning is: [it is] not [within its] domain.
[Sanskrit chāyā:] By someone, a cloud has been placed face-up in the village pond! //
[Vṛtti:] For this type of subject matter will mostly be pointed out as an example of guṇībhūtavyaṅgya (subordinate suggestion).

children.text:
iti cchāyā /
anye tu pi ucchā pitṛṣvasaḥ itthamāmantryate /
kenāpi atinipuṇena /
vācyāṅgatvameveti /
vācyenaiva hi vismayavibhāvarūpeṇa mugdhimātiśayaḥ pratīyata iti vācyādeva cārutvasampat /
children.translated_text: [Locana:] For through the expressible alone — in the form of an excitant (vibhāva) of wonder — the excess of naivety (mugdhimā) is apprehended; thus from the expressible alone comes the wealth of charm.
[Locana:] But the expressible, for the sake of establishing itself, suggests another meaning out of a desire for its own benefit.
[Sanskrit chāyā:] Of [the young wife] hearing the clamor of birds flying up from a dense thicket of cane-reeds,
though engaged in household work — her limbs grow languid. //

Thus the chāyā. / Others [read]: 'pi ucchā' — [meaning] the paternal aunt is addressed in this manner. / 'By someone' — by someone extremely skillful. / 'Has the status of being merely subsidiary to the expressible' — /

children.translated_text: For example —

children.text: ucciṇasu paḍia kusumaṃ mā dhuṇa sehāliaṃ haliasuhṇe /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Pick up the fallen flower, do not shake the śephālikā [tree], O daughter-in-law of the farmer —

children.text: aha de visamavirāvo samureṇa suo valaasaddo //
children.translated_text: else your father-in-law will hear the sound of [your] bangles, and the consequence for you will be harsh!' //

Thus the chāyā. / [Bālapriyā:] 'Api' is in the sense of inclusion (samuccaya). / 'Clear' — / The meaning is: distinct from the unclear. / 'Unclear' — this is the elaboration of '[that which] shines forth in a blurred manner.' / The elaboration of the second half beginning with 'expressible' etc. — 'clear also' etc. / [Bālapriyā:] She states in the Locana the meaning of the fourth quarter 'not of this,' which was not illuminated by the vṛtti passage — 'of this' etc. / The speech of a certain naive young woman who, seeing a cloud reflected in a pond, was astonished — [addressed] to her companions or to her paternal aunt — beginning with 'lotuses' etc. / 'By someone, in the village pond, a cloud — a mass of cloud — having been laid face-up, being made supine (since otherwise the viewing below the water would not be as [it is] above) — has been thrown, however.' / 'The lotus-pools are not muddied' — have not become soiled, or alternatively: the chāyā is 'have become soiled.' / 'The swans have suddenly flown up' — have gone upward. / 'And not' — the purport is: this is not wonderful. / Some read the chāyā as 'paternal aunt' instead of 'suddenly' — he says: 'others' etc. / The elaboration of 'by someone' — 'by someone extremely skillful.' / He elaborates 'has the status of being subsidiary to the expressible' — 'for by the expressible alone' etc. / 'For establishing itself' — for the resting-place of its own cognition. / 'Another meaning' — / The meaning is: the suggested [meaning], namely the naive young woman's seeing the cloud-reflection. / 'Out of a desire for its own benefit' — desiring its own benefit, acting as if [it desires]. / 'Vetasa' — / This verse is also cited in the Kāvyaprakāśa. / She elaborates the guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatva (status of subordinate suggestion) here — 'here' etc. / But where, through the apprehension by context etc., the expressible meaning whose entire nature has been ascertained — [and which is] again stated by its own word — since its own cognition has been previously accomplished, it does not rest in just that much [meaning alone]. /

children.translated_text: [Vṛtti:] For here, [a woman] making love with her undisciplined husband — [and] her friend [signals her] through the sound of bangles heard outside — [Locana:] And [the fact that] the apprehended [meaning] of such a kind has the status of subsidiary — 'that is the domain of this dhvani' — by this statement, which clearly states that the suggested meaning's predominance is the foundation [of dhvani], it follows that in guṇībhūtavyaṅgya (subordinate suggestion) the foundation is precisely the opposite of this.

children.text: uccinu patitaṃ kusumaṃ mā dhunīhi śephālikāṃ hālakasnuṣe /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Pick up the fallen flower, do not shake the śephālikā [tree], O daughter-in-law of the farmer —

children.text: eṣa te viṣamavipākaḥ śvaśureṇa śruto valayaśabdaḥ //
children.translated_text: your father-in-law will hear the sound of [your] bangles, and the consequence for you will be harsh!' //

[Locana:] Here, the arrival at a place suitable for secret lovemaking with the paramour who has been given a signal is suggested — and it supports the expressible [meaning] itself. / For thus: 'engaged in household work' — even though occupied with other [matters]; 'of the young wife' — even though bound by the constraint of excessive modesty; 'limbs' — not even a single limb was such that through the concealment of composure (gāmbhīrya) it could be restrained; 'grow languid' — let alone accomplishing household work, they are unable even to sustain their own selves. / '[The limbs] are thus clearly observed during [her] engagement in household work' — / From this very expressible [meaning comes] the wealth of charm — through the apprehension of the excess of subjugation to passion (<s>madana</s>). / 'But where' — / Context etc. is that which has 'context' (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) as its first [member]; from the competence of the proximity of other words, and from inferential signs and the like — from the ascertainment through these alone — where the meaning, whose entire nature has been ascertained — / 'Again expressible' — again stated by its own word; therefore, since the cognition of its own self has been previously accomplished, it does not rest in just that much [meaning alone]. / [Bālapriyā:] '[Having been] given a signal' — / The arrival of the paramour — the secret lover — at a suitable place for lovemaking, namely the dense thicket of cane-reeds — [is what is] suggested. / 'Suggested' — the meaning is: manifested through the mention of the bird-clamor. / 'Other' etc. — / And 'excessive' etc. — these are statements of the implied meaning. / By these two, the existence of an obstacle to the arising of languidness in all the limbs is shown. / 'Through composure' — through the concealment that is the disguising of one's expression, through [its] power. / 'Are unable' — / This is a continuation of 'limbs.' / He states the meaning implied by 'engaged in household work' — 'in household work' etc. / 'Thus' — / The meaning is: as possessing an excess of languidness. / The connection is: '[the limbs] are thus clearly not observed during engagement in household work.' / Therefore, hearing the clamor alone is what generates the excess of languidness — this is the purport. / With the reading 'and in engagement' — the break is at 'not observed.' / 'From this very expressible' — / The meaning is: from the expressible meaning alone — in the form of the languidness of all limbs, distinguished by being extended at the very time of hearing the clamor, of such a [young wife as described]. / The words 'prakaraṇādi' etc. — with the intent of including what was indicated by 'conjunction and separation' etc. as delimiting denotation, he explains: 'that which has prakaraṇa as its first [member]' etc. / 'Of other words' etc. — / The meaning is: of the aggregate formed by those. / 'From the ascertainment through these alone' — / The meaning is: from the very ignorance of those. / Showing the connection of 'where' — he explains the passage beginning with 'the meaning whose [nature has been] ascertained' — 'where the meaning' etc. / 'Ascertained' — / The ascertainment here — generated by the sentence and residing in the audience to be informed — is to be understood. / Since the knowledge of context etc. is the cause precisely for sentence-generated cognition, this is an indication [covering] also the ascertainment not generated by inference. / In [the verse beginning with] 'pick up' etc. — 'the shaking of the śephālikā should not be done, because it produces undesirable [consequences] like the father-in-law's anger' — the ascertainment generated by the sentence, residing in the heroine etc. to be informed, is to be understood. / 'Whose entire nature' — this is the elaboration of the word 'particular.' /

children.translated_text: Thus the chāyā. / Because the father-in-law, carefully tending the śephālikā creeper, becomes angry at its being pulled and shaken — / therefore here, the harsh consequence is to be understood. / Otherwise, it would be an ākṣepa (denial) of the suggested by one's own statement. / And here, the explanation should be made following the [verse] 'whose anger would not arise?' / This suggested [meaning] is to be considered necessary for the apprehension — the obtaining — of the expressible meaning. / Otherwise, the expressible meaning would not be obtained. / Since it is self-evident, that meaning would be simply not worth stating — this is what is meant. / Now, if so, the supportive function of the suggested has been stated in reverse — [Bālapriyā:] the elaboration of 'precisely' — 'of its own' etc. / 'Just that much' — / The meaning is: just the expressible meaning. / The elaboration of 'through the status of the apprehended as subsidiary' etc. — 'of the apprehended' etc. / 'That' — / The meaning is: that poetry. / He states the intended meaning — 'by this' etc. / 'Pick up' — / 'Śephālikā' — / The Amarakośa [states]: 'śophālikā is also [called] suvahe.' / Hālika means a ploughman (farmer); his snuṣā is [his] daughter-in-law (son's wife). / He states the reason for the prohibition of shaking — 'this' etc. / 'This' — being heard by me. / 'Your bangle-sound' — / Having been heard by the father-in-law, would have a harsh consequence — a consequence whose ripening is harsh, producing undesirable [results]. / 'Would be' is the remainder. / He removes the suspicion that the expression 'harsh consequence' might function as an ākṣepa (denial) of the suggested — by 'because' etc. / 'The explanation should be made' — / The purport is: the suggested [meaning] should be determined variously according to the difference in subject matter. / Here, even when some suggested [meaning] is subsidiary to the expressible, by taking up another suggested [meaning], the status of dhvani [is maintained] — he shows this in the vṛtti: by 'here' etc. / 'With the undisciplined husband' — with the paramour (lover). / 'The friend' — / The meaning is: the heroine. / He elaborates the passage 'this is to be considered necessary for the apprehension of the expressible meaning' — 'of the expressible meaning' etc. / 'Of the expressible meaning' — of the expressible meaning of the verse beginning with 'pick up.' / 'For the obtaining' — / For the completion of expectation-free cognition. / Or the meaning is: for fruitful cognition. / The elaboration of 'this' — 'this suggested' etc. / The meaning is: the suggested [meaning] in the form of the friend's alerting the heroine. / 'Is to be considered necessary' — / The meaning is: is to be considered necessary as an auxiliary. / The cognition of the heroine to be alerted — 'the friend alerts me' — and for the sensitive readers, 'the friend alerts the heroine who is making love' — the cognition being cognized, or that suggested [meaning], is an auxiliary toward the obtaining of the expressible meaning — this is what is meant. / He establishes what was stated — 'otherwise' etc. / 'Otherwise' — in the absence of dependence on the suggested. / 'Would not be obtained' — / As to 'why?' — he says: 'since self-evident' etc. / 'Since self-evident' — since known on its own by the heroine etc. / 'Simply not worth stating' — / The purport is: since it would be purposeless. / 'That meaning' — / The meaning is: the meaning of 'do not shake the śephālikā' etc. / 'Of the suggested' — the meaning is: of the stated suggested. / 'Again expressible' — the passage is to be explained as already explained — thus it is intimated by the friend. / This suggested [meaning] is to be considered necessary for the apprehension of the expressible meaning. / And when the expressible meaning has been apprehended — since it is being stated with the purport of concealing the impropriety — it is again merely subsidiary to the suggested; thus it is included within the reverberant-form suggested dhvani. / Thus, when the discrimination of dhvani-semblance in the case of vivakṣitavācya (intended literal meaning) dhvani is under discussion, he states [the same discrimination] also for avivakṣitavācya (unintended literal meaning) —

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā:] The concealment of impropriety — of the secret lovemaking — is the non-disclosure by the bangle-sound etc.
The meaning is: with that purport.
'Subsidiary status of the suggested' —
The meaning is: the subsidiary status of the suggested [meaning] 'do not make the bangle-sound' etc. // 31 //

[Bālapriyā:] 'In the discrimination of dhvani-semblance' — the seventh [case] is in the causal sense. / The meaning is: on the occasion characterized by the discrimination of dhvani-semblance. / As to 'whose dhvani-semblance?' — expecting this, he says: 'of the vivakṣitavācya (intended literal meaning).' / But in the clear explanation, 'under discussion' would be incongruent. / For the discrimination of dhvani-semblance of the vivakṣitābhidheya (intended denotation) [type] is at the completion [of the discussion], / not now under discussion, / nor does it follow subsequently. / 'One who stumbles in expression' — / The meaning is: of figurative (gauṇa) or secondary (lākṣaṇika) words. / 'Lack of learning' (avyutpatti) is the tendency of composition toward alliteration (anuprāsa) etc. / For example: 'In the intimate acquaintance abundant with the bond of love that sways — of mature married women — / in the sky-space of the mind, he who constantly sports — he is the abode of good fortune.' / Here, through the allure of alliteration, 'preṅkhat' (swaying) is used as a secondary (lākṣaṇika) [expression], 'cittākāśa' (mind-sky) as a figurative (gauṇa) usage — even though employed by the poet, [these] do not culminate in the beautiful purpose of the suggested form. / 'Lack of ability' (aśakti) is the inability to fulfill the meter etc. / [Bālapriyā:] She explains 'apprehended' — 'stated by the word.' / In the vṛtti, 'of it' — / The meaning is: of the expressible meaning. / 'Of impropriety' etc. —

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā:] 'Dhvani-semblance' — / The meaning is: discrimination of dhvani-semblance. / 'But in the clear explanation' etc. — / The meaning is: with the explanation of 'under discussion' (prastute) as 'begun' or 'being under consideration,' that word would be incongruent. / As to 'why?' — she says: 'for at the completion' etc. / She shows that the word avyutpatti (lack of learning) intends its effect — 'alliteration etc.' / The meaning is: the tendency of composition through alliteration etc. as its purpose, which constitutes poetic activity. / 'Swaying' — / Of that which is swaying, i.e. unsteady — as stated: 'the love of women, being restless with eagerness for ever-increasing clusters of qualities.' / The meaning of 'bond of love' (premaprabandha) is: the firm binding, the stabilization, of love; in [an acquaintance] abundant with that. / 'Secondary' — / The remainder is: in the sense of 'unsteady.' / 'Figurative' — / The purport is: because the mind is called 'sky' due to imperceptibility etc. / She explains the word 'lack of ability' — 'of the meter' etc. / The composition of one who stumbles, who employs figurative words — whether from lack of learning or lack of ability — that too is not the domain of dhvani. / Because —

children.translated_text: 'Is defined' — 'is known by this' — following this derivation, she says: 'pramāṇa (means of valid knowledge).'
The word 'lakṣaṇa' (definition) does not naturally mean 'pramāṇa' (means of knowledge) — with the intent that this word means 'distinguishing characteristic,' she says: 'or alternatively' etc.

Since definition (lakṣaṇa) and knowledge (jñāna) have the relation of thing-to-be-determined and its determiner, their identity is attributed here in the statement — she says: 'the cognition itself' etc.
And that [cognition] is precisely of the kind exemplified. //

[Locana:] Here, the first word ending in 'chief' is used figuratively for the moon. / In the sense of 'vessel' and 'trembling' — 'made of walls.' / Here, this does not foster any beauty whatsoever, apart from filling the meter. / 'And that' — / In the First Uddyota, where it was said 'poets whose usage is governed by conformity to established [convention]' — there the example 'he speaks of sleeping on lotus-leaves' etc. was stated as bhākta (secondary). / That [secondary usage] is not merely not the domain of dhvani — rather, this other [type] too [is not] — this is the meaning of the word 'ca' (and). / The kārikā-author restates the very nature of dhvani already established, as the cause for discriminating dhvani-semblance — with this intent, the vṛtti-author provides the supplement: 'because' etc. / 'Manifestation' — / By the principle 'the action of bringing denotes bringing the object,' the manifesting suggested [meaning is intended]. / 'Definition of dhvani' — the nature of dhvani is complete; or alternatively, the manifestation, i.e. the cognition, is the definition (pramāṇa) of dhvani, and that is complete — because it conveys the nature of complete dhvani. / Or alternatively, the cognition itself — [Bālapriyā:] 'Crooked' — / 'Crooked' means of odd number; of him whose arrows are such — of Kāmadeva — the assemblage of family [members] — O chief [of that assemblage], meaning: O Moon! / 'By you who fall into the ocean — by you who have fallen.' / In the reading 'kuraṅga' — by the deer [of the moon]; in 'latākuraṅgeṇa' — by the deer; 'the vessel whose middle portion is tossed' — 'in that' modifies 'in oneself.' / In the reading 'taraṅga' — it modifies the ocean. / 'Made of walls' — unmoving. / 'In oneself' — in one's own body. / 'Trembling' — / The meaning is: and it trembles. / 'Has been made' — has been produced. / The connection of 'figuratively used' extends to the next two sentences as well. / 'And that' — the word 'ca' (and) is the conjunctive stated in the First Uddyota — she says: 'in the First Uddyota' etc. / 'That' etc. — / Not merely that much is not the domain of dhvani — this is the meaning. / 'Another too' — / The meaning is: of the type stated by 'from lack of learning' etc. / She explains the passage beginning with 'manifestation' — 'of the action' etc. / By the word 'manifestation,' the manifesting suggested [meaning] is denoted — this is the purport. / The connection is: 'complete nature.' / Now, 'of the suggested that has become predominant' — the construal of this is difficult — therefore she says: 'manifestation' etc. / 'That' — the clear cognition.
Thus ends the Second Uddyota in the Dhvanyāloka composed by the revered master Ānandavardhana. //
[Locana:] The definition of dhvani — because a definition is to be determined by cognition.

children.text: vṛttāvevakāreṇa tato 'nyasya cābhāsarūpatvameveti sūcayatā tadābhāsavivekahetubhāvoyaḥ prakrantaḥ sa eva nirvāhita iti śivam //
children.translated_text: [Locana:] By the word 'eva' (only/precisely) in the vṛtti, [he indicates that] anything other than that has merely the status of semblance — thus, the demonstration of the cause for discriminating dhvani-semblance that was undertaken has been accomplished — may all be auspicious! //
I, Abhinavagupta, pay homage to her [Parā Devī / Supreme Goddess] who manifests this world —
as the Paśyantī (the Seer) — an abundance of mere shining forth, threaded through with [apparent] difference. //

children.translated_text: Thus ends the Second Uddyota in the Locana — the light of the sensitive reader — composed by the revered great Śaiva master Abhinavagupta, in the compendium on Dhvani. //

[Bālapriyā:] 'Because it is to be determined by cognition' — / The meaning is: because it is to be ascertained through cognition of the defined [entity]. / For the definition of cow etc. is determined through cognition of cow etc. / 'By the word eva' — / The meaning is: by the word 'eva' in 'of the exemplified kind precisely.' / 'Abundant' — / By the supreme Goddess (Parameśvarī) who is of the nature of Māyā — this 'abundant,' i.e. copious, world — with the first-case ending. / Is drawn forth. / 'Prollāsa' (shining forth) — the apprehension; merely that — existing, but not as a real entity — this is the purport. / 'With difference' — with difference from Brahman. / Or alternatively, 'sadbhedena' is a single word — the meaning is: with difference from Brahman (Sat, the Real). /
Third Uddyota

somehow I shall comment upon it; may the learned ones be gracious to me herein. //

children.translated_text:
'I remember' — /
'<s>Smara</s>' means <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love); his destruction (<s>saṃhāra</s>) itself is a sport (<s>līlā</s>); the skill (<s>pāṭava</s>), the capacity, in that — one who possesses that. /
By 'forcibly taking away half the body of <s>Śambhu</s>' — the skill of <s>Parameśvarī</s> (the Supreme Goddess) that exceeds even that of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) of that kind is indicated. /
'<s>Uddyota</s>' — /
Another <s>Uddyota</s>, the other <s>Uddyota</s>, is the Third <s>Uddyota</s>; its connection (<s>saṅgati</s>) — the connecting link in the form of association with the Second <s>Uddyota</s> — this is the meaning. /
'To establish' means to accomplish. /
By the statement 'demonstrated through the medium of the suggested,' the non-demonstration through the medium of the suggestor is implied — raising the objection that this is untenable, and showing the intention of that statement, he introduces [the discussion]: 'therein' etc. /
'Although' etc. should be construed at the beginning. /
'Therein' — in <s>dhvani</s>. /
'Through the medium of the expressible' etc. — /
The meaning is: the varieties such as <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> etc. of <s>dhvani</s> are possible only by depending on the expressible qualified by unintendedness etc. as the differentiator. /
'From that, what [follows]?' — he says: 'and the expressible' etc. /
'As was stated' — /
The meaning is: it has been stated that the expressible has suggestive capacity. /
'Even with this much, what is achieved?' — to this he says: 'and from that' etc. /
'That' — /
The meaning is: the suggestor. /
'Suppressed by the suggested' — /
The purport is: by the statement that the expressible is unintended, its being made non-predominant by the suggested is established. /
'Inclined toward the suggested meaning' — dependent on the suggested. /
He concludes: 'thus' etc. /
'Of the two root divisions' — /
The meaning is: of the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> and the <s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s>. /
'Through the medium of the suggested' etc. — /
The meaning is: through the dependence on the suggested alone. /
'Therefore' — precisely because of the stated intention. /
'Moreover' — /
Through the medium of the suggested,
of the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (unintended literal meaning), the illumination by word and by sentence;
and of the other one [<s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s>], whose suggested meaning has the reverberant form — of that <s>dhvani</s> — // <s>DhvK</s> 3.1 //
Of the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s>, the illumination by word and by sentence;
and of the other one, whose suggested meaning has the reverberant form — of that <s>dhvani</s> — // 1 //

children.translated_text: That whose form (<s>rūpa</s>) is [characterized by] reverberation (<s>anuraṇana</s>) — that is, having a resemblance to portrayal — such is the suggested meaning of that [<s>dhvani</s>] — this is the meaning.

children.text: maharṣerityanena tadanusandhatte yatprāguktam, atha ca rāmāyaṇamahābhārata prabhṛtini lakṣye dṛśyata iti /
children.translated_text: 'Of the great sage' — by this, he connects what was stated earlier, and also [indicates that] it is seen as the model in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Mahābhārata</s>, and other works.

children.text: dhṛtiḥ kṣamā dayā śaucaṃ kāruṇyaṃ vāganiṣṭhurā /
children.translated_text: Steadfastness, forbearance, compassion, purity, kindness, non-harshness of speech,
and non-treachery toward friends — these seven are the kindling-sticks of prosperity. //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Of the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> — in the variety where the literal meaning is completely suppressed (<s>atyantatiraskṛtavācya</s>) — the illumination by word: as in the case of the great sage <s>Vyāsa</s>'s [verse]: 'These seven are the kindling-sticks of prosperity'; or as in <s>Kālidāsa</s>'s: 'Who, when you are girded [for departure], would disregard a wife distressed by separation?'; or as in: 'What indeed is not an ornament for those of sweet forms?' — in these examples, the words '<s>samidhaḥ</s>' (kindling-sticks), '<s>sannaddhe</s>' (girded), and '<s>madhurāṇām</s>' (of the sweet ones) have been employed with the intention of suggestive capacity. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] That meaning attains differentiation only through the resort of being viewed through the medium of the suggested. /
Therefore he says: 'through the medium of the suggested.' /
Moreover, although meaning is the suggestor, nevertheless it is also capable of being suggested; but the word (<s>śabda</s>) is never suggested — rather, it is always only a suggestor. /
This is what he states: 'through the medium of the suggestor.' /
And it is not the case that the variety of the expressible — in the form of unintendedness etc. — has in every way not been illuminated; rather, though illuminated [earlier], it is now [illuminated] again through the pure suggestor medium. /
For thus: without being viewed through the medium of the suggested, the word (<s>pada</s>), the sentence (<s>vākya</s>), the phonemes (<s>varṇāḥ</s>), the word-portion (<s>padabhāga</s>), the composition (<s>saṅghaṭanā</s>), and the extended passage (<s>mahāvākya</s>) — [these] varieties of suggestors exist by their very nature; and since their suggestedness can never arise like that of meaning, the variety that is illuminated through the medium of the purely suggestor-restricted essential nature — this is the purport. /
But one who explains: 'through the medium of the suggested content, figure, and <s>rasa</s>' — he should be questioned thus: this threefold division was not made by the <s>kārikā</s>-author; /
it was shown by the <s>vṛtti</s>-author. /
Now, the <s>vṛtti</s>-author does not make the display of variety — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the meaning is: there is also another intention in the statement 'demonstrated.' /
This is what he says: 'although' etc. /
'Meaning' means the expressible. /
'Suggested' etc. — /
The meaning is: it is sometimes also capable of being suggested. /
'This is what he states' — /
The meaning is: he states it from that intention. /
Anticipating the objection 'if so, then in "again, through the medium of the suggestor," the word "again" is untenable,' he elaborates the purport: 'and it is not the case' etc. /
'Therein' — /
The meaning is: the expressible qualified by unintendedness etc. /
'Not by suggestive capacity' — this is the construal. /
In the reading '<s>vyañjakamukhatvam</s>' — the variety of <s>dhvani</s>, the sub-variety, that has as its cause the form of unintendedness etc. belonging to the expressible — /
therein, the <s>dhvani</s>-variety — this is the meaning. /
'And it is not the case that it does not exist' — he elaborates the meaning already stated: 'through the medium of the suggestor also' etc. /
And thus he states the resultant meaning of 'through the medium of the suggestor': 'purely' etc. /
The meaning is: through the medium of the pure suggestor alone. /
'Of these' — /
The meaning is: of the word etc. /
'Is possible' — /
'Is conceivable' is also a variant reading. /
'<s>Iti</s>' is in the causal sense. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Then if this was done [before] and this is [now] being done, what is the connection between different agents? Nor is the coherence with the entire previous treatise thereby established — /
since the modes of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> etc. have also been demonstrated — enough of quarreling with [those who share] the lineage of one's own revered teachers! /
The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) in the <s>kārikā</s> is for the purpose of dispelling the doubt of enumeration-correspondence. /
Thus the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s>, though having two sub-varieties, is individually twofold — as word-illuminated and sentence-illuminated. /
The variety belonging to the other — the <s>vivakṣitābhidheya</s> (intended denotation) — called <s>kramadyotya</s> (sequentially illuminated), together with its own sub-varieties, is also individually twofold in each case.

children.translated_text: Or for example —

children.text: emea jaṇo tissā deu kavolopamāi sasibimbam /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Just so, people give the moon-disc as a comparison for her cheek;

children.text: paramatthaviāre uṇa cando cando via varāo //

The meaning of the word '<s>samit</s>' (sacrificial fuel) is here entirely set aside, due to impossibility. /
And the suggested meaning conveyed by the word '<s>samit</s>' — the capacity to kindle <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) without dependence on anything else — is what <s>Vakra</s> (i.e. <s>Bhaṭṭa Tota</s>) intended as suggested for the seven [fires]. /
Although this meaning is observed even from examples like 'the mirror blinded as if by breath' etc., nevertheless, incidentally, additional examples are given to show the pervasiveness across many observable [instances]. /
And here the complete setting aside of the expressible — following what was stated earlier — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'its own form' — /
The meaning is: the own form of the word etc. /
'Thus, when the agents differ, what is the coherence?' — /
The meaning is: when the agents differ, coherence is not possible. /
'When the suggested is demonstrated through the medium of the suggested, and then this is illuminated through the medium of the suggester' — by this, the single-agent-hood of demonstrating and illuminating is naturally understood; that would be incoherent — this is the extent [of the objection]. /
'What is the coherence — thus it should be asked' — this is the connection. /
He states another fault — 'nor' etc. /
'The conjunction <s>ca</s>' etc. — /
In the absence of the conjunction <s>ca</s>, the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (where the expressible is not intended) would be illuminated by the word, and the other [type] would be illuminated by the sentence — thus there would be confusion of meaning through enumeration — this is the purport. /
'By that' — /
The meaning is: by the conjunction <s>ca</s> having the sense of aggregation. /
'Of the other' — explaining with the intention that this is a predicate in a different substrate — 'of the intended' etc. /
The elaboration of 'in reverberation' etc. — 'in sequence' etc. /
The elaboration of 'form' — 'fashioning' etc. /
He states the result — 'similarity' etc. /
'Thus' — /
The connection is: what was stated earlier. /
Of the meaning of the word '<s>samit</s>' — qualified by the property of being fuel. /
'By the word <s>samit</s>' — /
The remainder is: the stimulating capacity is indicated. /
The word '<s>samit</s>' here indicates through the mode of stimulating capacity that pervades both the expressible and the indicated. /
Thus in 'readiness is indicated' etc., the meaning to be understood is: it indicates through the mode of properties such as readiness that pervade both [meanings]. /
After 'and by the word' — of that same [type] in the <s>arthāntarasaṅkramitavācya</s> (where the expressible is transferred to another meaning), as follows — 'by <s>Rāma</s>, for whom [<s>Sītā</s>] is dearer than life, what has been done — [<s>Locana</s>:] should be construed — what more to say of what is repeated? /
And here, by the word '<s>sannaddha</s>' (armed), which indicates readiness through its primary meaning being impossible [in context], the intentions of <s>Vakra</s> — mercilessness, irremediability, unprecedented action, etc. — are suggested. /
Likewise, by the word '<s>madhura</s>' (sweet), which indicates the capacity to delight all subjects and to satisfy — the fact that [she] is an object of supreme desire is not surprising here — this is what <s>Vakra</s> intended as suggested. /
'Of that same' — /
The meaning is: of the second variety of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s>. /
'The anger of rejection — what was done was fitting — by the cruel <s>Rākṣasa</s>; and that too was so endured by you, O woman of noble family, that she holds her head high. /
Now it is useless for you who bear this bow, which is the witness of your calamity' — thus. /
He who is cruel by the very nature of a <s>Rākṣasa</s>, who being intolerably haughty due to the unassailability of his command, and being blinded by rage when forcibly rejected — for him, this much is an action befitting his own mental disposition, namely the severing of the head; even though venerable — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the reading 'the suggested meaning' is seen; if that [reading] is accepted, the meaning of 'suggested' is 'made known.' /
'With its primary meaning being impossible' — /
The primary meaning is 'armored.' /
'<s>Sannaddha</s> means armored' — thus the <s>Amarakośa</s>. /
'Are suggested' — /
The remainder is: of <s>Megha</s> (the cloud), [which is] the referent of 'you.' /
'By the word <s>madhura</s>' — /
The purport is: by the word denoting the quality of sweetness (<s>mādhurya-rasa</s>). /
'Of all' — /
The meaning is: one property among the capacity to delight all objects, to satisfy, etc. /
'Here' — /
The meaning is: in the [poetic] forms. /
In 'the anger of rejection' — this is the speech of Lord <s>Śrī Rāmacandra</s> addressed to Goddess <s>Sītā</s>. /
He elaborates — 'a <s>Rākṣasa</s>' etc. /
'Who' — <s>Rāvaṇa</s>. /
The elaboration of 'the anger of rejection' — 'whose command is unassailable' etc., up to 'blinded by rage.' /
'Unassailable command' — whose command cannot be transgressed; by the haughtiness born of that — the conceit 'I am one whose command cannot be transgressed' — by that, is the reason for being blinded by rage. /
'Being rejected' — rejected by you [<s>Sītā</s>]. /
'This action is befitting his own mental disposition' — this is the connection. /
'This' — he elaborates this — 'namely the severing of the head.' /
'Of love, for the beloved, this is not fitting.' /
Here, the word '<s>Rāmeṇa</s>' (by <s>Rāma</s>) is the suggester, whose expressible has been transferred [to other meanings] due to being of the sole <s>rasa</s> of heroic daring etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Someone will transgress my command' — thus [he thought]. /
'By her' — the meaning is: even such a one [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>], endowed with unsurpassed sovereignty etc., was disregarded by her — this is 'your' [<s>Sītā's</s>]. /
'That too' — even the severing of the head. /
'In the same way' — with equanimity, with a perception of it as a festive occasion — endured, as observed through the widening of eyes, the serenity of face, etc. /
'In such a way that a woman of noble family' — whoever, even if mostly low-born, is denoted by the word '<s>kulavadhū</s>' (woman of noble family). /
'Holds her head high' — 'we are indeed such women of noble family' — with this pride, she holds her head erect — this is the meaning. /
Alternatively he explains — 'moreover' etc. /
'That' is elaborated — 'at the occasion of head-severing' etc. /
The explanation of 'so endured' — 'in such a way that she holds her head high' etc. /
'Holds her head high' — the meaning is: when some lover, blinded by the rage of rejection, is ready to sever [her] head, she holds her head erect [to offer it] — through the rejection of the prayer. /
'Not having engaged' — this is the elaboration of the past tense [usage]. /
About to explain the second half, he says — 'thus' etc. /
'Again' — this is the elaboration of the word '<s>tu</s>.' /
The explanation of 'useless' etc. — 'exile from the kingdom' etc. /
'Of [the one] for whom [she] is dearer than life' — 'surely then' etc. /
And — /
'Of this' — the meaning is: of the bearing of the bow. /
'This' — the meaning is: that the bearing of the bow has the purpose of protecting one's own life. /
He explains the <s>vṛtti</s> passage beginning with 'by <s>Rāma</s>' — 'by <s>Rāma</s>' etc. /
The elaboration of 'of the sole <s>rasa</s> of heroic daring' — 'unequaled' etc. /
The statement of the referents of the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.) — 'truthfulness' etc. /
Here, the delimiters of the indicated meaning of the word '<s>Rāma</s>' are: cowardice, according to the <s>Pradīpakāra</s>; deceitful affection, according to <s>Cakravartī</s>; aversion to manly effort, according to <s>Bhaṭṭa Gopāla</s>.
Here the second word '<s>candra</s>' (moon) is one whose expressible meaning has been transferred to another meaning (<s>arthāntarasaṅkramitavācya</s>).

children.text: avivakṣitavācyasyātyantatiraskṛtavācye prabhede vākyaprakāśatā yathā---- yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī /
children.translated_text: In the variety of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (non-intended expressible) called <s>atyantatiraskṛtavācya</s> (completely set aside expressible), the illumination at the level of the sentence is as follows — 'What is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one is awake;

children.text: yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ //
children.translated_text: that in which beings are awake is night for the seeing sage.' //

children.translated_text: For by this sentence, neither the meaning of 'night' nor any meaning of 'wakefulness' is intended;

children.text: kiṃ tarhi? tattvajñānāvahitatvamatattvaparāṅmukhatvaṃ ca muneḥ pratipādyata iti tiraskṛtavācyasyāsya vyañjakatvam /
children.translated_text: what then? The sage's devotion to the knowledge of truth and his turning away from what is not truth are being taught — thus the suggestive capacity of this [verse] whose expressible is [completely] set aside.

[<s>Locana</s>:] Through the combination of <s>ālambana</s> (foundational) and <s>uddīpana</s> (stimulating) <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) relating to grief, the <s>karuṇa rasa</s> (pathetic sentiment) of <s>Rāma</s> is made manifest — thus. /
'Just so' — /
Just so, people give the moon-disc as a comparison for her cheek. /
But in ultimate analysis, the moon is a poor wretch, merely like a moon. (Thus the <s>chāyā</s> [Sanskrit rendering].) /
'Just so' — blindly, through their own lack of discernment. /
'People' — those who merely follow popular convention. /
'Of her' — of one whose body possesses the great wealth of an assemblage of incomparable qualities. /
'As a comparison for the cheek' — the cheek-surface, which is the principal [feature], situated in the middle of the face that is the very essence of artless charm — as a comparison for that; rather, what should be [placed as] superior to that — the moon-disc, which is far inferior to [the cheek], is tainted by the pretext of its spot [<s>kalaṅka</s>]. /
Thus, even though the world has fallen into the current of [this conventional] comparison, nevertheless, if discerning critics examine [it], then the pitiable one — 'who is known as the moon, is merely a moon' — the meaning is: [the word '<s>candra</s>'] has been transferred to other properties such as waning, lack of brilliance, and impurity. /
And here, just as the transference to other suggested properties — what was stated earlier should be recalled. /
Likewise in what follows. /
Thus, having illustrated both varieties of the first type [of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s>] as illuminated by the word, he illustrates [them] as illuminated by the sentence — 'what is night' etc. /
'Intended' — /
For by that which was stated [literally], no instruction to any person being instructed is accomplished. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Grief' etc. — /
The <s>ālambana-vibhāva</s> (foundational determinant) is the apprehended death of the beloved. /
The <s>uddīpana-vibhāva</s> (stimulating determinant) is the recollection of actions etc. connected with the beloved that are not shared [with others]. /
He explains the purport of 'just so' etc. — 'blindly' etc. /
'Superior to the cheek' — the meaning is: more excellent than the cheek. /
The syntactic connection is: 'should be presented as a comparison.' /
The meaning is: should be stated as an <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison). /
'Than that' — the meaning is: than the cheek. /
The elaboration of the word '<s>śaśin</s>' (moon) — 'by the spot' etc. /
'Tainted by the pretext of the spot' — the hare (<s>śaśa</s>) which serves as the pretext for the spot, by that it is made crooked, made impure. /
'<s>Via</s>' — with the intention that it has a restrictive sense, he says — 'is merely a moon' etc. /
The <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) of the second word '<s>candra</s>' should be understood here as either in the form of being denoted by the word '<s>candra</s>' or in the form of being devoid of [the moon's] qualities. /
He states the suggested properties — 'waning' etc. /
'The meaning that has been transferred' — /
The meaning is: the meaning of the word '<s>candra</s>.' /
'Here' — the meaning is: in the two examples cited. /
'What was stated earlier' — the meaning is: what was stated at the beginning of the Second <s>Uddyota</s>. /
'For by that which was stated' — /
The meaning is: by the meaning of 'night' etc., [namely] the meaning of 'night' as [literal] night etc.
(For some [time] is made poisonous; for some it passes as the creator of nectar;
for some it is made of both poison and nectar; for some it is neither poison nor nectar — [such is] <s>Kāla</s> (time). //
