children.translated_text: The statement of the implied meaning — 'that which cannot be [questioned]' etc. /
The purport is: because fate is invisible. /

children.text: 'asmi na sṛṣṭa' prātuṃ dhanairarthijanasya vāñchāṃ daivena sṛṣṭo yadi nāma nāsmi /
children.translated_text: 'I have not been created' — to fulfill the desire of a person who desires wealth, if I have not been created by fate —

children.text: pathi prasannāmbudharastaḍāgaḥ kūpo 'thavā kiṃ na jaḍaḥ kṛto 'ham // 1 //
children.translated_text: then [why] am I [made to be] an inert pond of clear water on the road, or a well? Why was I not [simply] made [into something useful]? // 1 //

Thus the <s>chāyā</s>.) [<s>Locana</s>:] One must be awake during the night; at other times, one should remain as if it were [ordinary] night — what is achieved by [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] having said this? /
Therefore, this sentence, whose literal meaning has been obstructed, suggests: through the extraordinary reason indicated by <s>tattva-dṛṣṭi</s> (vision of truth), the <s>saṃyamin</s> (self-controlled one) gives attention [to the night of all beings], and turns away from <s>mithyā-dṛṣṭi</s> (false vision). /
And because the meaning of the word '<s>sarva</s>' (all) is also justified by its relative [rather than absolute] sense — the meaning should not be thought of as forced merely through the impossibility of construing the word '<s>sarva</s>' otherwise. /
That which is the night of all fourteen [classes of] beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to immovable entities — [that night being] the <s>tattva-dṛṣṭi</s> (vision of truth) that generates delusion — in that [night], the <s>saṃyamin</s> (self-controlled one) is awake — how is this [state] to be attained? /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'No [instruction]' — the syntactic connection is: no instruction is accomplished [merely by the literal sense]. /
The purport is: the necessary purpose of this instruction found in the <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> must be [established]. /
Asking 'why is it not accomplished?' — he says: 'during the night' etc. /
'At other times, as if it were night' — the meaning is: during the day, as if it were night. /
'Obstructed' — the meaning is: obstructed by uselessness. /
'Sentence' — the meaning is: the aggregate of words [such as] 'night, is awake' etc. /
The implied meanings of each word will be demonstrated. /
'Extraordinary' etc. — the meaning is: by the reason of being extraordinary. /
But [one might object:] here, when the meaning of the word '<s>niśā</s>' (night) [is construed] as the time for sleep, and the connection with all beings is [accepted], then because of the compatibility with the meaning of the word '<s>sarva</s>' (all), the <s>saṃyamin</s> too would have that connection [with sleep]; and since he [the <s>saṃyamin</s>] is inconsistent with the connection to the meaning of '<s>jāgarti</s>' (is awake), therefore, because the suggested [meaning] has been made explicit by [the literal meaning], there is no <s>dhvani</s> status — he dispels this doubt: 'of the meaning of the word <s>sarva</s>' etc. /
'By its relative [sense]' — since the word '<s>sarva</s>' here denotes [all beings] delimited by the exclusion of the <s>saṃyamin</s> — therefore, [it is established] by relative [meaning] — this is the meaning. /
'The meaning of the word <s>sarva</s>' — the meaning is: the connection with the meaning of the word '<s>sarva</s>.' /
'This meaning' — the previously stated suggested meaning. /
'Forced' — made explicit. /
He explains the verse — 'of all' etc. /
'Of fourteen [classes of] beings' — the meaning is: of beings of fourteen types — [namely:] the divine, which is of eight types through the divisions of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, <s>Aindra</s>, <s>Paitrya</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Yākṣa</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and <s>Paiśāca</s>; the human, which is of one type; and the animal, which is of five types through the divisions of cattle, birds, serpents, insects, and immovable entities — thus of beings of fourteen types as well, meaning: of embodied beings. /
As stated in the <s>Sāṅkhyakārikā</s>: 'The divine is of eight types' etc. /
'Generating delusion' — this is the statement of the implied meaning of the word '<s>niśā</s>' (night). /
'That' — to this he says: '<s>tattva-dṛṣṭi</s>' (vision of truth). /
He states the implied meaning of the word '<s>jāgarti</s>' (is awake) — 'how' etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Not merely by the avoidance of sense-objects is one a <s>saṃyamin</s> — this is the extent [of the meaning]. /
Or alternatively: in the night of all beings — that which generates delusion — [the <s>saṃyamin</s>] is awake; how is this [delusion-generating night] to be rejected? /
That in which all beings are awake — that <s>mithyā-dṛṣṭi</s> (false vision) — is abundantly awakened [in them], i.e., they are of extremely alert form — that is his night, the domain of non-awakening. /
For in the activity of that [false vision], he is not awakened. /
Exactly thus does one established in extraordinary conduct perceive and think. /
Of that one alone are the activities of the inner and outer faculties fully accomplished. /
But another does not perceive and does not think — [this is the meaning]. /
The purport is: one must abide with <s>tattva-dṛṣṭi</s> (vision of truth) as the orientation. /
And thus, '<s>paśyataḥ</s>' (of the one who sees) — even this [word] of the sage [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] — and likewise [the rest] — is not merely bewildered in its own [literal] meaning, /
but rather rests in the suggested meaning alone. /
And the words '<s>yat</s>' (which) and '<s>tat</s>' (that) do not have independent meaning — thus this entire group of words, accompanied by the verb, is oriented toward the suggested [meaning]. /
Thus he says — 'for by this sentence' etc. /
'Is conveyed' — the meaning is: is suggested. /
'Made poisonous' — having attained the state of being poisonous. /
For some who are of evil deeds, or for some who are exceedingly discriminating — [time passes]. /
For some who are of good deeds, or for some who are completely non-discriminating — [time] passes as the creator of nectar. /
For some of mixed actions, or for some who possess both discrimination and non-discrimination — [time is] made of both poison and nectar. /
For some who are mostly deluded, or for some who have ascended to the stage of <s>yoga</s> attained through practice — [time is] neither poison nor nectar — time passes [thus] — this is the syntactic connection. /
And the words '<s>viṣa</s>' (poison) and '<s>amṛta</s>' (nectar), as established secondary meaning (<s>nirūḍha-lakṣaṇā</s>) — like the words '<s>lāvaṇya</s>' (grace) etc. — function [here] with reference to the means of suffering and happiness, as in: '<s>viṣa</s>' (poison) = neem [tree], '<s>amṛta</s>' (nectar) = wood-apple. /
And here [these words] do not rest merely in the means of happiness and suffering, but rather terminate in the happiness and suffering that are to be accomplished by oneself. /
Nor are those means in all respects — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She, with the thought 'how is this to be attained?' pursues the means for its attainment — this is the meaning. /
He states the purport — 'not merely' etc. /
'<s>Saṃyamin</s>' — one denoted by the word '<s>saṃyamin</s>.' /
Since the delusion-generating nature of <s>tattva-dṛṣṭi</s> is not well known — therefore he explains otherwise: 'or alternatively' etc. /
'Generating delusion' — the meaning is: in <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). /
'<s>Mithyā-dṛṣṭi</s>' — the meaning is: in <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), or in the dualistic phenomenal world that is its effect. /
'Of that one' — the meaning is: of the <s>saṃyamin</s>. /
'The domain of non-awakening' — the elaboration of this very [phrase]: 'for in the activity of that [false vision]' etc. /
'He' — the meaning is: the <s>saṃyamin</s>. /
'Established in extraordinary conduct' — this is the statement of the implied meaning of the word '<s>saṃyamin</s>' itself. /
The elaboration of '<s>paśyato muneḥ</s>' (of the seeing sage) — 'perceives and thinks.' /
Here, 'perceives' is stated as a characterization of the activity of the external faculties whose purpose is accomplished, and 'thinks' as that of the internal faculties — he says: 'of that one alone' etc. /
By this, he states the implied meaning — 'another' etc. /
He states the resultant suggested meaning — '<s>tattva</s>' etc. /
'Rests in the suggested meaning alone' — the meaning is: in the primary suggested meaning as previously stated. /
Thus he says — 'by this sentence.' /
The meaning is: he says [so] from the stated purport. /
The elaboration of '<s>keṣām api</s>' (for some) — 'for some of evil deeds' etc. /
'Passes' — 'crosses over' — this is [the meaning of the verb]. /
With the intention of the <s>gāthā</s> reading '<s>amia-ṇimmāo</s>,' he gives the <s>chāyā</s>: '<s>amṛta-nirmāṇa</s>' (creator of nectar). /
The meaning is: that whose creation is like nectar. /
Intending to establish the transferred denotation of the words '<s>viṣa</s>' and '<s>amṛta</s>' to [the senses of] suffering and happiness as stated in the <s>vṛtti</s>, he says: 'the words <s>viṣa</s> and <s>amṛta</s>' etc. /
'Happiness and suffering' — the statement is in reverse order; the meaning is: of the means of suffering and happiness. /
Or alternatively, thus is the [correct] reading. /
The same should be understood for what follows. /
Here he cites an example — 'as in' etc. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — here [the meaning is]: 'in [such usages as] these.' /
He states a special feature of the present example — 'and here' etc. /
'Here' — the meaning is: in the present example. /
'Merely in [the means of happiness and suffering]' — the meaning is: in just the means of happiness and suffering. /
In 'merely resting in that' — here, indeed, in the sentence, by the words '<s>viṣa</s>' and '<s>amṛta</s>' — which are transferred denotators of happiness and suffering — the conventional usage [holds] — thus the transferred-denotation status of [the meaning] transferred to another sense [is demonstrated] — its suggestive capacity [is shown]. /
Of the intended denotative meaning (<s>vivakṣitābhidheya</s>), the reverberant-form suggested — [when arising from] word-power-born [<s>dhvani</s>] — the illumination by a word [is as follows] — [<s>Locana</s>:] not the intended [meaning]. /
Because of the absence of means for those two — he says: 'by transferred denotators' etc. /
'For some' — and of this [word], the transference is to a particular [class]. /
And of '<s>atikrāmati</s>' (passes), the transference is to the action alone. /
And of '<s>kāla</s>' (time), the transference is to all conventional usage. /
But the <s>vṛtti</s>-author explained the grasping of just '<s>viṣa</s>' and '<s>amṛta</s>' as merely illustrative of the transference. /
Thus he says — 'sentence' etc. /
Having thus illustrated the four types indicated by the first half of the <s>kārikā</s>, he illustrates in order the six other types accepted in the second half of the <s>kārikā</s> — beginning with '<s>vivakṣitābhidheya</s>' etc. /
'To fulfill' — to complete. /
'With wealth' — the plural is for indicating: 'whoever desires whatever [wealth].' /
Hence the word '<s>artha</s>' (wealth/purpose) [is used]. /
'Of a person' — for generally the world desires wealth, not benefits through virtues. /
'By fate' — the meaning is: that which cannot be questioned. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'And' — this is the syntactic connection. /
'Not the intended [meaning]' is to be extracted. /
'To be accomplished by oneself' — the meaning is: to be accomplished by one's own [efforts]. /
The word '<s>sva</s>' (own) pertains to the means. /
'Nor' — 'not the intended,' 'the intended indeed' [are the alternatives]. /
Asking 'why?' — he says: 'because of the absence of means' etc. /
Thus he says — the meaning is: by the stated purport, he states the transferred-denotation status of happiness and suffering. /
'<s>Viṣam</s> (poison) = neem, <s>amṛtam</s> (nectar) = wood-apple' — etc. — in these [usages], through established secondary meaning, what is intended is: neem is a means of suffering, wood-apple is a means of happiness — in the present [verse], however, '<s>kāla</s>' (time) passes for some as full of suffering and for some as full of happiness — since this meaning is intended, the secondary meaning of the word '<s>viṣa</s>' as 'some-means-related suffering' and of the word '<s>amṛta</s>' as 'some-means-related happiness' is a secondary meaning [that applies]; the specific [nature of] the suffering and happiness is suggested; because [the words] '<s>viṣa</s>' and '<s>amṛta</s>' appear as means [of suffering and happiness], the transferred-denotation status [is established] — this is the purport. /
'For some' — and of this [word], the transference is to a particular [class] — the meaning is: of the word '<s>keṣām api</s>' (for some), which denotes [beings] delimited by unknown specific properties, the transference is to the particular [classes] stated as 'of evil-doers' etc. /
That of evil-doers etc. — the unknown nature etc. — is suggested. /
'To the action alone' — [time] occurs in the sense of existence. /
'To all conventional usage' — the meaning is: to the class of things within the domain of conventional usage. /
'Second' — the meaning is: those accepted by the second half of the <s>kārikā</s>, those stated thereby. /
'To fulfill' — '<s>asmi</s>' is an indeclinable [meaning] 'I.' /
'With wealth' — [the construction is:] if it is the case that I have not been created by fate to fulfill the desire of a person who desires wealth — /
'Then' is the remainder. /
'Inert am I' — [either] a pond of clear water on the road, or a well — why? For what reason? /
'Not made' — not created by fate. /
Because a pond is superior to a well, it is mentioned first. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Whoever desires whatever [wealth]' — the meaning is: whatever person, among [items like] cattle, gold, etc., desires whatever wealth. /
'Hence' — the meaning is: because of the stated purport. /

tasyaiva vākyaprakāśatā yatā harṣacarite siṃhanādavākyeṣu--'vṛtte 'sminmahāpralaye dharaṇīdhāraṇāyādhunā tvaṃ śeṣaḥ' /

ata eva jaḍaḥ śītalo nirvedasantāparahitaḥ /
tathā jaḍaḥ śītajalayogitayā paropakārasamarthaḥ /
anena tṛtīyārthenāyaṃ jaḍaśabdastaṭākārthena punaruktārthasambandha ityabhiprāyeṇāha--kūpasamānādhikaraṇatāmiti /

itīyatā pūrṇe vākyārthe kalpāvasāne bhūpīṭhabhārodvahanakṣam eko bālapriyā ityanena gamyamarthamāha--anyo hītyādi /

tamarthamāha--kiṅkartavyatāmūḍha iti /

atrārthāntarañcāha---ata evetyādi /
ata eva vivekābhāvādeva /

laḍayorabhedājjaḍapadaṃ jalamayārthakañcetyāha---tathetyādi /

asminnityasya vivaraṇam---śoketyādi /
vṛtte jāte /

children.translated_text: Of this same [type] — in the variety of meaning-power-born [<s>dhvani</s>] whose body is produced solely through the poet's bold expression (<s>kaviprauḍhokti</s>) — the word-illumination, as in the <s>Harivijaya</s>:
[Prakrit:] Wearing mango-sprouts as ear-ornaments, having for a brief moment a greatly costly, captivating, divine fragrance —
though not offered, the face of the spring-beauty was seized by the flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāmadeva</s>). //

[Vṛtti:] For here, the word '<s>jaḍa</s>' (inert/dull), employed by one who is disgusted in co-referentiality with oneself, attains co-referentiality with a well through its own [word-]power, in the reverberant form. /
The sentence-illumination of the same [type] is as in the lion-roar passages of the <s>Harṣacarita</s>: 'When this great dissolution has occurred, you are now the <s>Śeṣa</s> (remainder) for upholding the earth.' /
For this sentence clearly illuminates, through word-power, another meaning in the reverberant form. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'I am' — /
For certainly someone else has been created, not I — this is the despair. /
'It holds clear, world-benefiting water' — /
'Or a well' — /
The meaning is: unnoticed even by people. /
'In co-referentiality with oneself' — /
'<s>Jaḍa</s>' means bewildered about what to do — this is the meaning; and also: the well is '<s>jaḍa</s>' — 'who is there to ask?' and 'of what kind?' — having discrimination that is impossible [to exercise] — thus. /
Therefore also: '<s>jaḍa</s>' means cold — free from the heat of despair. /
Likewise: '<s>jaḍa</s>' means capable of benefiting others through the possession of cool water. /
With the intention that by this third meaning, this word '<s>jaḍa</s>' has a connection of repeated meaning with the meaning 'reservoir,' he says: 'co-referentiality with a well.' /
'Through its own power' — he construes this as arising from word-power. /
'Great dissolution' — /
Where there is a complete dissolution of a great festival — in such [a situation] that has become the cause of grief, when it has occurred — 'for the upholding of the earth,' for the consolation of the burden of kingship — 'you are the <s>Śeṣa</s>' (the remainder/the serpent), the one who remains. /
In this much completed sentence-meaning, [the further meaning:] 'at the end of the cosmic age, the one [serpent] capable of bearing the burden of the earth's surface' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] she states the implied meaning through this: 'for certainly another' etc. /
'World-benefiting' — /
'By people' etc. — /
This too is an elaboration of the implied meaning. /
The quoting of '<s>ātmasamānādhikaraṇatā</s>' as a lemma — is for the purpose of indicating that the meaning of the word '<s>jaḍa</s>' connected with the first-person meaning will be explained [first]. /
He states that meaning: 'bewildered about what to do.' /
He states the suggested meaning connected with 'well': 'and also' etc. /
Here he states yet another meaning: 'therefore also' etc. /
'Therefore' — precisely because of the absence of discrimination. /
'Cold' — /
'<s>Śiśira</s> [means] <s>jaḍa</s>' — [says] the <s>Amarakośa</s>. /
By this he states the implied meaning: 'free from despair' etc. /
Since there is no difference between <s>la</s> and <s>ḍa</s>, the word '<s>jaḍa</s>' also has the meaning 'made of water' — he says: 'likewise' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, by 'attains co-referentiality with a well,' only the co-referentiality of the word '<s>jaḍa</s>' with the word 'well' is stated, not also co-referentiality with the word 'reservoir' — whence [is that]? — removing this doubt, he introduces that passage: 'by this' etc. /
'By this third meaning' — /
The meaning is: by the third [meaning] stated among those said to be connected with 'well' — namely the meaning 'through the bearing of cool water' etc. — as the reason. /
'With the meaning reservoir' — /
The meaning is: together with that. /
'Repeated meaning' — /
The meaning is: the repetition of meaning would occur through the mere statement of the qualifier 'holding clear water.' /
'Through its own power' — to remove misunderstanding here, he says: 'word' etc. /
He states the expressible meaning: 'of the great' etc. /
The elaboration of 'in this' — 'the cause of grief' etc. /
'Occurred' — having arisen. /
He shows the suggested other meaning: 'at the cosmic age' etc.

children.text:
atra hyasamarpitamapi kusumaśareṇa madhumāsalakṣmyā mukhaṃ gṛhītamityasamarpitamapītyetadavasthābhidhāyipadamarthaśaktyā kusumaśarasya balātkāraṃ prakāśayati /
atraiva prabhede vākyaprakāśatā yathodāhṛtaṃ prāk 'sajjehi surahimāso' ityādi /
atra sajjayati surabhimāso na tāvadarpayatyanaṅgāya śarānityayaṃ vākyārthaḥ kaviprauḍhoktimātraniṣpannaśarīro manmathonmāthakadanāvasthāṃ vasantasamayasya sūcayati /
locanam nāgarāja eva digdantiprabhṛtiṣvapi pralīneṣvityarthāntaram /
cūtāṅkurāvataṃsaṃ kṣaṇaprasaramahārghamanoharasurāmodam /
mahārghaṇa utsavaprasareṇa manoharasurasya manmathadevasya āmodaścamatkāro yatra tat /
children.translated_text: '<s>Mahārgha</s>' — whose delight (<s>āmoda</s>), that is the <s>camatkāra</s> (wonder), of the divine one (<s>sura</s>), meaning the god of love (<s>Manmatha</s>), is captivating through the surge of festival — that [is the meaning].
Here the word '<s>mahārgha</s>' (greatly costly) is placed later [in the compound], due to the absence of [strict word-order] rules in Prakrit.
'<s>Chaṇa</s>' means festival.
'Though not offered, the face of the spring-beauty was seized by the flower-arrowed one.' //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] For here, 'though not offered, the face of the spring-beauty was seized by the flower-arrowed one' — the word '<s>asamarpitam api</s>' (though not offered), which describes a [particular] state, illuminates through the power of meaning the forceful appropriation by <s>Kusumaśara</s> (the flower-arrowed <s>Kāmadeva</s>). /
In this same variety, the sentence-illumination is as previously illustrated: '<s>sajjehi surahimāso</s>' (prepare! the spring month) etc. /
Here, 'the spring month prepares, it does not yet supply <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love) with arrows' — this sentence-meaning, whose body is produced solely through the poet's bold expression, indicates the state of torment caused by <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) during the spring season. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Nāgarāja</s>' alone — even when <s>Digdantī</s> (the cosmic elephants of the directions) and others have dissolved — this is the other meaning. /
'Wearing mango-sprout ear-ornaments, having for a brief moment a greatly costly, captivating, divine delight' —

children.text:
mukhaṃ prārambho vakkraṃ ca /
tacca surāmodayuktaṃ bhavati /
madhvārambhe kāmaścittamākṣipatītyetāvānayamarthaḥ kaviprauḍhoktyārthāntaravyañjakaḥ sampāditaḥ /

children.translated_text: In this [type] — in the variety of meaning-power-born [<s>dhvani</s>] whose body consists of the bold expression of a speaker created by the poet (<s>kavinibaddhavaktṛprauḍhokti</s>) — two examples of word-illumination and sentence-illumination have not been given.

children.text: 'prauḍhoktimātraniṣpannaśarīraḥ sambhavī svataḥ' iti prācyakārikāyā iyataivodāhṛtatvaṃ bhavedityabhiprāyeṇa /
children.translated_text: With the intention that the [earlier <s>kārikā</s>] '<s>prauḍhoktimātraniṣpannaśarīraḥ sambhavī svataḥ</s>' would be illustrated by just this much.

children.text: tatra padaprakāśatā yathā--- satyaṃ manoramāḥ kāmāḥ satyaṃ ramyā vibhūtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, the word-illumination is as follows: 'Truly, pleasures are delightful; truly, riches are charming —
but life is [as fickle as] the sidelong glance of an intoxicated woman, trembling and unsteady!' //

'Face' (<s>mukha</s>) means beginning, and also surface. /
And that [face/beginning] is endowed with divine delight. /
'At the onset of spring, <s>Kāma</s> seizes the mind' — just this much is the meaning; [the poet] has accomplished it through bold expression as suggestive of another meaning.

children.text:
bālapriyā 'mahāpralaya' ityasya kalpāvasāna iti, 'dharaṇīdhāraṇāye'tyasya bhūbhāretyādi, śeṣa' ityasya nāgarāja iti ca vivaraṇam /
digdantītyādi /
bhāvārthakathanam /
atropamā vyaṅgyā bodhyā /
madhumāsalakṣmyā nāyikātvapratītyā tadanuguṇamarthamāha---vaktrañceti /
surā madyam /
arthāntaravyañjaka iti /
arthāntaraṃ vṛttāvuktam /
atretyādi /
ityabhiprāyeṇa na dattamiti sambandhaḥ /
satyamiti /
kāvyaprakāśe 'pyudāhṛto 'yaṃ ślokaḥ /

children.translated_text: In the variety of meaning-power-born [<s>dhvani</s>] whose body arises naturally (<s>svataḥsambhavī</s>) — the word-illumination is as follows:

children.text: vāṇiaa hattidantā kutto ahyāṇa bādhakittī a /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'O merchant! Whence [come] elephant-tusks for us, and tiger-skins?
So long as the daughter-in-law with disheveled hair and face [beaming] moves about coquettishly in the house, embracing [her husband]!' //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The elaboration of '<s>mahāpralaya</s>' is 'at the end of the cosmic age'; of '<s>dharaṇīdhāraṇāya</s>' is 'the burden of the earth' etc.; and of '<s>Śeṣa</s>' is '<s>Nāgarāja</s>' (the king of serpents). /
'<s>Digdantī</s>' etc. — /
This is a statement of the implied meaning. /
Here the suggested <s>upamā</s> (simile) should be understood. /
By the cognition of '<s>madhumāsalakṣmī</s>' (the beauty of the spring month) as a heroine, he states the meaning accordingly: 'the face' etc. /
'<s>Surā</s>' means liquor. /
'Suggestive of another meaning' — /
The 'other meaning' was stated in the <s>vṛtti</s>. /
'Herein' etc. — /
The connection is: 'with this intention, [examples] have not been given.' /
'Truly' — /
This verse is also cited in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>.

children.text: atra lulitālakamukhītyetatpadaṃ vyādhavadhvāḥ svataḥsambhāvitaśarīrārthaśaktyā suratakrīḍāsaktiṃ sūcayaṃstadīyasya bhartuḥ satatasambhogakṣāmatāṃ prakāśayati /

locanam ityatra kavinā yo virāgī vaktā nibaddhastatprauḍhoktyā jīvitaśabdo 'rthaśaktimūlatayedaṃ dhvanayati---sarva evāmī kāmā vibhūtayaśca svajīvitamātropayoginaḥ, tadabhāve hi sadbhirapi tairasadrūpatāpyate, tadeva ca jīvitaṃ prāṇadhāraṇarūpatvātprāṇavṛtteśca cāñcalyādanāsthāpadamiti viṣayeṣu varākeṣu kiṃ doṣoddhoṣaṇadaurjanyena nijameva jīvitamupālabhyam, tadapi ca nisargacañcalamiti na sāparādhamityetāvatā gāḍhaṃ vairāgyamiti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] 'Thus' — here, the speaker composed by the poet is a renunciant; through his bold expression, the word '<s>jīvita</s>' (life) suggests the following through meaning-power: all these pleasures and riches are useful only to one's own life; in their absence, even good people are not afflicted by them [i.e., by their loss]; and that very life, being of the nature of sustaining the vital breath — and because of the fickleness of the vital function — is an object of indifference. Thus, what is the use of finding fault with these pitiable sense-objects? Rather, one should reproach one's own life itself; and even that is fickle by nature — hence it is not blameworthy — by just this much, deep dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) [is suggested].
The sentence-illumination is as in [the verse beginning with] '<s>śikhariṇī</s>' etc.
(Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:) 'O merchant! Whence [come] elephant-tusks for us, and tiger-skins?
So long as the daughter-in-law with disheveled locks and face moves about coquettishly in the house, embracing [her husband]!' //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Here, the word '<s>lulitālakamukhī</s>' (she whose face has disheveled locks), through the naturally arising power of meaning regarding the hunter's wife, indicates [her] attachment to amorous play, and thereby illuminates her husband's capacity for constant lovemaking.

luliteti /

snuṣā putrabhāryā /
pariṣvakkata iti /

children.translated_text: The sentence-illumination of that same [type] is as follows:
[Prakrit:] 'The bride, wearing peacock-feather ear-ornaments, moves about proudly with the gait of [her] husband,
amidst [things that serve as] ornaments made of strung pearls!' //

Thus the <s>chāyā</s>. / 'Moves about coquettishly' (<s>savibhramaṃ caṅkramyate</s>). /
Here, '<s>lulita</s>' etc. — [being] merely a description of [her] natural form, [and] through [her] pride — the non-acquisition of elephant-tusks etc. is conceivable — therefore, in just this much sentence-meaning there is no incongruity whatsoever. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Pleasures' — the desired [objects] such as women etc.; 'in their absence' — in the absence of life. /
'Life is an object of indifference' — this is the connection. /
Here the reason — 'of the vital breath' etc. /
'<s>Iti</s>' is in the causal sense. /
'Fickle by nature' — /
The meaning is: because of the reason of being naturally fickle. /
The purport is: because one's nature is impossible to remove. /
'O merchant' — /
The meaning is: whence are [these things] in our house? They are not [present] — this is the meaning. /
Here, showing occupation with another task as the reason, he says: 'so long as' etc. /
'So long as' means 'since.' /
'<s>Lulita</s>' — /
'<s>Lulitāḥ</s>' means locks scattered here and there; she whose face is such — thus. /
'Daughter-in-law' — the son's wife. /
'Embraces' — /
Therefore, we are occupied with her care — this is the purport. /
'Naturally' etc. — /
A body that is naturally conceivable — conceivable even in the world through propriety — through the power, the capacity, of such a meaning — this is the meaning. /
In the <s>Locana</s>, the explanation of '<s>pariṣvakkate</s>' (embraces) is: 'moves about coquettishly.' /
He removes the doubt that the suggested is merely subsidiary to establishing the expressible: 'here' etc. /
'<s>Lulita</s> etc.' — /
The meaning is: and so forth. /
'Merely of [her] form' etc. — /
The meaning is: merely a description of form. /
'Through pride' — /
The meaning is: through the conceit of being wealthy etc. /
The word '<s>ca</s>' conjoins another conceivable reason. /
'Elephant' etc. —

anenāpi vākyena vyādhavadhvā śikhipicchakarṇapūrāyā navapariṇītāyāḥ kasyāścitsaubhāgyātiśayaḥ prakāśyate /

children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā:] 'Dhvani-designation' — the designation 'word-illuminated dhvani.'
[Bālapriyā:] She introduces the passage 'of the undesirable' etc. in the Locana: 'now' etc.
Up to 'are merely reminders' — [the kārikā reads:] 'Just as the hearing of the undesirable produces the fault [of cacophony],
so in those [compositions] that are faulty to the ear, clearly the recall of the desirable [produces] the quality [of euphony]. //

[Locana:] By this sentence too, the excess of good fortune of a certain newly-wed bride of a hunter — one who wears peacock-feather ear-ornaments — is revealed. / Because it illuminates the meaning that her husband, solely devoted to her enjoyment, is capable of killing only a peacock — thereby the excess of misfortune of other women, long married, whose ornaments are fashioned of pearls, is proclaimed — / because it illuminates the meaning that during the time of their enjoyment, that very same hunter was capable of slaying the mightiest elephant. / Now, it was stated that dhvani is a variety of poetry — how then can it be word-illuminated? / For a variety of poetry is a particular arrangement of words that is the cause of the apprehension of qualified meaning. / And this status [as a variety of poetry] is not consistent with being word-illuminated. / Because individual words, being merely reminders (smāraka), are not denoters. / The reply is: 'This may be a fault' — [Locana:] 'Peacock-feather' — / The verse was already construed above. / 'Now' — / This objection applies in the view where dhvani is only the aggregate. / 'Its status' — / The meaning is: the status of being a variety of poetry. / What was stated as 'because of non-denotation' — that is an inefficacious reason — he first shows this through quibble (chala): 'this may be a fault' etc. / Having thus parried through quibble — [Bālapriyā:] 'The non-fetching of elephant-tusks' — the reading 'non-fetching of tusks etc.' also [exists]. / 'Of the daughter-in-law's husband' is the remainder. / 'Aggregate' — / The meaning is: the aggregate of denoter, denoted, suggested, etc. / 'In this view' — / The purport is: since the objection is valid only in the view where in the kārikā beginning with 'avivakṣitavācya' the word dhvani refers to the aggregate alone. / In the vṛtti, 'now' etc. / 'It was stated' — / The purport is: [referring to] 'where the meaning or the word' etc. / 'Therefore' (tat) — / He substantiates the objection: 'For a variety of poetry' etc. / 'Qualified' — / The meaning is: the qualified meaning that is twofold as expressible and suggested — the cause for the apprehension of that. / 'A particular arrangement of words' etc. — / The meaning is: a particular [arrangement] of composed words. / That is to say: a qualified meaning, and a particular sentence-arrangement that conveys it. / 'Then what follows from that?' — he says: 'and its status' etc. / 'When it is word-illuminated' — when it is to be illuminated by words. / 'Is not consistent' — does not cohere. / The meaning is: its status [as a variety of poetry] is contradicted by being word-illuminated. / As to 'why?' — he says: 'of individual words' etc. / 'Because of non-denotation' — because of the absence of capacity to produce awareness. / By those [individual words], their respective meanings are merely recalled; but those recalled [meanings], assisted by syntactic expectancy etc., produce awareness of the sentence-meaning — in this view, word-illumination in the form of words being mere reminders pertains only to their respective meanings. / And therein, there is no dhvani-status in the form of being a variety of poetry — therefore dhvani cannot be word-illuminated, but can only be sentence-illuminated: this is the purport. / With the passage 'because of non-denotation etc.' — understanding that the intended meaning 'individual words do not illuminate dhvani, because of their non-denotative status' has emerged — he introduces the refutation passage 'this may be a fault' in the Locana: 'because of non-denotation' etc. / 'Inefficacious' — / If denotative capacity were the operative factor in dhvani-designation. / But that is not so; because [dhvani] is established through its suggestive capacity. / Moreover, even the apprehension of beauty in poetry, though achieved by an aggregate delimited by particular configurations (like bodies), is attributed through positive and negative concomitance to the parts — therefore the dhvani-designation for individual words too, through the medium of suggestive capacity, is not contradictory. / [Locana:] He also refutes by means of the real state of affairs: 'moreover' etc. / If the opponent were to say: 'I did not adduce non-denotation as a reason for the absence of dhvani, but rather I said: poetry is dhvani; / and poetry is a sentence that produces expectation-free comprehension, not an individual word' — to this he replies: 'granted; / nevertheless, we have not said that individual words are dhvani; / rather, only the aggregate [is dhvani]; and thus, "word-illuminated dhvani" — by the word "illumination" (prakāśa) this is stated. Now, from where [comes] the individual word's such capacity — since the apprehension-sequence is unfragmented?' — anticipating this, he says: 'of poetry' etc. / For it was said earlier, at the time of discrimination, that 'the instruction of division [is made].' / Now, [if asked:] how can that beauty-apprehension be attributed to the parts, i.e. to individual words? For those are merely reminders. / 'Then what follows from that?' — because the beauty-apprehension is grounded precisely in [their] being reminders of delightful suggested meanings — by what [argument is this] — [Bālapriyā:] the meaning is: [it is] inefficacious. / 'Through quibble' — through a stratagem, namely by not disclosing the forthcoming intended meaning — this is what is meant. / 'First' — at the outset. / 'By means of the real state of affairs also' — / The meaning is: also by disclosing the truly intended meaning. / Now, what is the purpose of the refutation by the real state of affairs? — therefore, in order to introduce the passage 'of poetry' etc., he sets the stage: 'if the opponent' etc. / 'In the absence of dhvani' — in the absence of being a dhvani-illuminator. / 'Of individual words' is the remainder. / 'Adduced as a reason' — stated as a reason. / 'But rather' etc. — / The meaning is: a variety of poetry is dhvani; and poetry of such a kind is a sentence — thus a sentence alone is dhvani; but an individual word is not dhvani. / And thus, when dhvani is absent in individual words, non-sentence-status is the reason: this is the purport. / 'The opponent would say' — this is the connection. / 'He replies' — / 'The proponent' is the remainder. / 'Nevertheless' — up to this point is the concession. / The connection is: 'not said.' / 'Only the aggregate' — / 'Is dhvani — this is what was said' carries over. / Here he states the supporting [argument]: 'and thus' etc. / 'Therein' — / The meaning is: in the sentence. / 'Of such a kind' — favorable to the illumination of dhvani. / 'Thus from where' — how is this possible. / Here is the reason: 'unfragmented' etc. / He states the supporting [argument] for 'is attributed to the parts': 'it was said, for' etc. / The connection of 'of poetry' in the vṛtti is with 'in beauty.' / 'Configurations' — / The meaning is: the aggregate that is distinguished — i.e. qualified — by particular configurations, i.e. particular word-arrangements, and by particular conjunctions of parts such as the face etc. — though to be accomplished by that [aggregate] — this is the meaning. / And thus, the apprehended beauty pertains to the aggregate: this is the purport. / 'In the parts' — in the individual words, and in [body parts such as] the face etc. / 'Is attributed' — / The purport is: by predominance. / 'Iti' is in the causal sense. / 'Through the medium of suggestive capacity' — through the predominance of suggestive capacity. /
Even when individual words are merely reminders, [and the dhvani is] manifested by mere words —
therefore, in all the varieties of that dhvani, beauty exists. //
As a beautiful woman [shines forth] with a single ornament radiant with charm (vicchitti),
so the speech (bhāratī) of a skilled poet shines forth as dhvani, illuminated by a [single] word.' //
These are the ancillary verses (parikaraślokas).
But the dhvani whose suggested [meaning] is of the imperceptible-sequence (alakṣyakrama) type — [manifested] in phonemes, words, etc.,

children.text: vākye saṅghaṭanāyāṃ ca sa prabandhe 'pi dīpyate // DhvK_3.2 //
children.translated_text: in sentences and in compositions — that shines forth even in extended narratives. // DhvK 3.2 //
But the dhvani whose suggested [meaning] is of the imperceptible-sequence type — [manifested] in phonemes, words, etc.,

children.text: vākye saṅghaṭanāyāṃ ca sa prabandhe 'pi dīpyate // 2 //
children.translated_text: in sentences and in compositions — that shines forth even in extended narratives. // 2 //

children.text:
locanam vāryate /
yathā śrutiduṣṭānāṃ pelavādipadānāmasabhyapelādyarthaṃ prati na vācakatvam /
api tu smārakatvam /
tadvaśācca cārusvarūpaṃ kāvyaṃ śrutiduṣṭam /
tacca śrutiduṣṭatvamanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ bhāgeṣu vyavasthāpyate tathā prakṛte 'pīti tadāha--aniṣṭasyeti /
aniṣṭārthasmārakasyetyarthaḥ /
duṣṭatāmityacārutvam /
guṇamiti cārutvam /
evaṃ dṛṣṭāntamabhidhāya pādatrayeṇa turyeṇa dārṣṭāntikārtha uktaḥ /

children.translated_text: [Locana:] Now he concludes: 'of individual words' etc.

children.text: yata eva miṣṭasmṛtiścārutvamāvaiti tena hetunā sarveṣu prakāreṣu nirūpitasya padamātrāvabhāsino 'pi padaprakāśasyāpi dhvane ramyatāsti smārakatve 'pi padānāmiti samanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Locana:] Since the recall of the delightful achieves beauty — for that very reason, in all the modes of dhvani that has been established as manifested by mere words too, as word-illuminated, beauty exists, even when words are merely reminders: this is the construal.
The word 'api' (even) connects with both [clauses] by the crow's-eye principle (kākākṣinyāya).
[Locana:] Now he demonstrates the positive and negative concomitance of the individual word in the apprehension of beauty: 'with charm' etc. // 1 //

[Locana:] [The objection] is answered. / Just as words that are harsh to the ear — such as 'pelava' etc. — are not denoters with respect to their vulgar meanings like 'pela' etc., / but rather are merely reminders — / and through that [reminder-capacity], beautiful poetry becomes cacophonous, / and that cacophony is established through positive and negative concomitance in the parts — so too in the present case: thus he says: 'of the undesirable' etc. / The meaning of 'of the undesirable' is: of that which reminds of undesirable meaning. / 'Fault' (duṣṭatā) means lack of beauty. / 'Quality' (guṇa) means beauty. / Having thus stated the illustrative example through three quarters [of the verse], the illustrated meaning is stated by the fourth [quarter]. /

children.text:
evaṃ kārikāṃ vyākhyāya tadasaṅgṛhītamalakṣyakramavyaṅgyaṃ prapañcayitumāha--yastviti /
tuśabdaḥ pūrvabhedebhyo 'sya viśeṣadyotakaḥ /
varṇasamudāyaśca padam /
tatsamudāyo vākyam /
saṅghaṭanā padagatā vākyagatā ca /
saṅghaṭitavākyasamudāyaḥ prabandhaḥ bālapriyā śaṅkāgranthaḥ /
tataḥ kimitmādirvakṣyamāṇārthakaḥ parihāragranthaḥ /
pelavādipadānāmiti /
'atipelavamatiparimitavarṇaṃ laghutaramudāharati śaṭha' ityādau pelavādiśabdānāmityarthaḥ /
asabhyeti /
asabhyo yaḥ pelādyarthaḥ pelādiśabdārthastaṃ pratītyarthaḥ /
pelaśabdo hi lāṭabhāṣāyāṃ vṛṣaṇavācakaḥ /
navācakatvamiti /
tadarthasya tadvākyārthaghaṭakatvābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: The connection is: 'having stated through three quarters [of the verse].'
The elaboration of 'for that very reason' (tena) — 'since' etc.
'Of the established' — this is supplied.
The word 'api' — [refers to] the word 'api' in 'even when merely reminders.' // 2 //

[Bālapriyā:] Having thus explained the kārikā, in order to elaborate the alakṣyakramavyaṅgya (imperceptible-sequence suggestion) that was not included therein, he says: 'but that which' etc. / The word 'tu' (but) indicates the distinction of this [type] from the previous varieties. / An aggregate of phonemes is a word. / An aggregate of those is a sentence. / Composition (saṅghaṭanā) pertains to words and to sentences. / An aggregate of composed sentences is an extended narrative (prabandha). / [Bālapriyā:] The objection-passage. / 'Then what follows from that?' etc. — this refers to the forthcoming meaning; the refutation-passage. / 'Of words like pelava etc.' — / In [the verse] 'he utters an extremely soft, exceedingly limited-in-syllables, very light [word], O rogue' etc. — the meaning is: of words such as 'pelava' etc. / 'Vulgar' — / The meaning is: toward that which is vulgar — that pelā-meaning, i.e. the meaning of the word 'pelā.' / For the word 'pela' in the Lāṭa dialect denotes the testicles. / 'Not denotation' — / The purport is: because its meaning does not contribute to the meaning of that sentence. /
Anticipating the doubt that phonemes (varṇas), being meaningless, cannot have suggestive capacity — this is stated:
The sibilants (śa and ṣa), conjuncts with 'r' (repha), and also the aspirate ḍha — predominantly

children.text: virodhinaḥ syuḥ śṛṅgāre te na varṇā rasa-cyutaḥ // DhvK_3.3 //
children.translated_text: would be antagonistic in śṛṅgāra (erotic sentiment) — therefore, phonemes can cause the loss of rasa. // DhvK 3.3 //

children.text: ta eva tu niveśyante bībhatsādau rase yadā /
children.translated_text: But when those very [phonemes] are deployed in bībhatsa (the disgusting) and other rasas,

children.text: tadā taṃ dīpayanty eva te na varṇā rasa-cyutaḥ // DhvK_3.4 //
children.translated_text: then they indeed illuminate that [rasa] — therefore, phonemes can cause the loss of rasa. // DhvK 3.4 //
The sibilants (śa and ṣa), conjuncts with 'r,' and also the aspirate ḍha — predominantly

children.text: virodhinaḥ syuḥ śṛṅgāre tena varṇā rasacyutaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: would be antagonistic in śṛṅgāra — therefore, phonemes can cause the loss of rasa. // 3 //

children.text: ta eva tu niveśyante bībhatsādau rase yadā /
children.translated_text: But when those very [phonemes] are deployed in bībhatsa and other rasas,

children.text: tadā taṃ dīpayantyeva tena varṇā rasacyutaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: then they indeed illuminate that [rasa] — therefore, phonemes can cause the loss of rasa. // 4 //
[Locana:] With this intention, the successive treatment of phonemes etc. [is undertaken].
[Locana:] By the word 'ādi' (etc.), the inclusion of word-portions, word-pairs, etc. is [indicated].
[Locana:] By the locative case, the instrumental-cause relationship is stated.
[Locana:] 'Shines forth' (dīpyate) means 'manifests' (avabhāsate) — in the capacity of illuminating poetry in its entirety — thus its status as a variety of poetry is established as before. // 2 //
[Vṛtti:] Through the pair of verses, the suggestive capacity of phonemes has been demonstrated through positive and negative concomitance.

paruṣā vṛttivirodhinī śṛṅgārasya /
yataste varṇā bhūyasā prayujyamānā na rasāṃścyotanti sravanti /
yadi vā tena śṛṅgāravirodhitvena hetunāvarṇāḥ śaṣādayo rasācchṛṅgārāccyavante taṃ na vyañjayantīti vyatireka uktaḥ /
anvayamāha--ta evatviti /
śādayaḥ /
tamiti bībhatsādikaṃ rasam /
dīpayanti dyotayanti /
kārikādvayaṃ tātparyeṇa vyācaṣṭe---ślokadvayeneti /
yathāsaṃkhyaprasaṅgaparahārārthaṃ bālapriyā ādiśabdeneti /
'padādiṣvi'tyādipadenetyarthaḥ /
saptamyeti /
padādiṣvityādisthayā saptamyetyarthaḥ /
nimittatvamuktamiti /
na tvadhikaraṇatvamiti bhāvaḥ /
dīpyata ityasya vivaraṇam---sakalakāvyāvabhāsakatayāvabhāsata iti /

children.translated_text: The <s>alakṣyakrama</s> (imperceptible-sequence) <s>dhvani</s>, however, is a particular kind of poetry that has a composite nature (<s>samudāyātmaka</s>).
That is illuminated by phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) etc. as its causes — from this statement, this meaning is established — this is the purport.
'The status of being a particular kind of poetry' —
the remainder is: 'of <s>dhvani</s>.' // 2 //

'<s>Bhūyasā</s>' (predominantly) connects with each one individually. /
Therefore '<s>śa</s>-sound,' '<s>bhūyasā</s>' (predominantly) etc. should be explained. /
The conjunct with <s>repha</s> as predominant — '<s>karhi</s>,' '<s>ardra</s>' etc. /
'<s>Virodhinaḥ</s>' (opposing) — the <s>paruṣā vṛtti</s> (harsh style) is opposed to <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment). /
Those phonemes, when predominantly employed, do not cause <s>rasas</s> to flow, [i.e.,] they do not express them. /
Alternatively, by that reason of being opposed to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, the phonemes — <s>śa</s>, <s>ṣa</s>, etc. — fall away from <s>rasa</s>, i.e., from <s>śṛṅgāra</s>; they do not suggest it — thus the <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) is stated. /
He states the <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) — '<s>ta eva tu</s>' (those very ones, however) etc. /
'<s>Śa</s>-sound etc.' /
'That' — the <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting) and other <s>rasas</s>. /
'<s>Dīpayanti</s>' — they illuminate, they reveal. /
He explains the two <s>kārikā</s>-verses in their essential purport — 'by two verses' etc. /
For the purpose of removing the assumption of enumeration-correspondence (<s>yathāsaṃkhya</s>) — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'by the word <s>ādi</s>' etc. /
'In word-beginnings etc.' — the meaning is: by the word '<s>ādi</s>' [in the expression '<s>padādiṣu</s>']. /
'Seventh [case]' — the meaning is: by the locative case in '<s>padādiṣu</s>' etc. /
'The causal relation has been stated' — the purport is: but not the substrate relation (<s>adhikaraṇatva</s>). /
The elaboration of '<s>dīpyate</s>' (shines forth) is: 'it shines forth as the illuminator of all poetry.'

children.text: te iti tiṣṭhetyuktaṃ kimiva na tayā yatsamutsṛjya bāṣpaṃ mathyāsaktaścakitahariṇīhārinetratribhāgaḥ //
children.translated_text: '<s>Te</s>' means 'stay!' — [the verse says:] 'What is it that she has not [done] — having cast aside her tears, absorbed in churning, the trembling three-quarter-portion of her eyes resembling those of a startled doe!' //

[Locana:] 'By the two verses' — this is not done [correctly]. /
For by the first verse, <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) was stated, and by the second, <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance). /
In this subject matter — in that which is characterized by <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) — the use of harsh sounds (<s>śaṣādi</s>) should not be employed by one who desires good poetic craftsmanship — since the instruction has this as its fruit, the <s>vyatireka</s> was stated first, in the manner of a prohibition. /
Nor is it the case that [harsh sounds] should never be used at all; rather, in <s>bībhatsa</s> (the disgusting sentiment) and others, they must indeed be used — thus afterward comes the <s>anvaya</s>. /
But the <s>vṛtti</s>-author, following the convention that <s>vyatireka</s> is preceded by <s>anvaya</s>, has taken up the <s>anvaya</s> first. /
What is stated [thereby] is this — although indeed the full realization of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) is the sole basis of <s>rasa</s>-experience, /
nevertheless, those <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. become such [effective rasa-producers] when presented through words endowed with distinguished phonetic capacity — this is established by one's own experience. /
Therefore, of the phonemes too — whose nature, discerned through the convention of hearing, requires consideration — there is a quality perceivable solely by the ear, consisting of softness and harshness. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In the reading '<s>tena</s>' (by that), it is one word; but in the reading '<s>rasacyuta</s>' (fallen from <s>rasa</s>), one should understand that '<s>te na</s>' forms two [separate words]. /
'According to enumeration' etc. — /
In the designation 'by the two verses' (<s>ślokābhyām</s>), through the apprehension of the meaning 'those <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> that were demonstrated by the two verses — by those [respectively],' the possibility of <s>yathāsaṅkhya</s> (sequential correlation) with the <s>anvaya</s> arises; but in the designation 'by the pair of verses' (<s>ślokadvayena</s>), through the apprehension of the meaning 'those <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> that were demonstrated by the composite whole constituted of two verse-members,' the possibility of that [sequential correlation] does not arise — this is the purport. /
But let there be <s>yathāsaṅkhya</s> here — to this he says: 'by the first' etc. /
He states the reason for showing <s>vyatireka</s> first in the <s>kārikā</s> — 'in this' etc. /
Then what is the reason for stating it differently in the <s>vṛtti</s>? — to this he says: 'the <s>vṛtti</s>-author' etc. /
Since only the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. are the suggesters of <s>rasa</s>, how then can the phonemes etc. [matter]? — showing this doubt, he resolves it — 'what is stated' etc. /
'Distinguished' — /
Distinguished [means] endowed with the distinguished manner of the refined (<s>upanāgaraka</s>) etc.; pertaining to that [subject matter] — this is the extent [of the meaning]. /
By '<s>śruti</s>' (hearing) — presented by words that are apprehended through hearing — this is the meaning. /
'Such' — /
The meaning is: serving as the basis of <s>rasa</s>-experience. /
'Of the phonemes too' — /
This connects with 'nature' [stated earlier]. /
'<s>Śruti</s>' (hearing) — /
For here, the word '<s>te</s>' (those/they) clearly manifests as <s>rasa</s>-laden to the sensitive readers. /
The illumination by a constituent of a word —

children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] In the <s>kārikā</s>, [the locative] is not merely a causal seventh [case], but also [expresses] a meaning that pertains to a domain that exists nowhere else — thus.
'Pure' — unmixed with any <s>arthālaṅkāra</s> (meaning-figure).

children.text: kṛtakakupitaibāṣpāmbhobhiḥ sadainyavilokitair- vanamapi gatā yasya prītyā dhṛtāpi tathāmbayā /
children.translated_text: 'With feigned anger, with tears as [their] water, with glances full of despondency — even though she went to the forest, [she was] held back thus by her mother out of love for him.

children.text: navajaladharaśyāmāḥ paśyandiśo bhavatīṃ vinā kaṭhinahṛdayo jīvatyeva priye sa tava priyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Seeing the directions dark as fresh rain-clouds, without you — hard-hearted [as he is], your beloved lives on, O dear one!' //

Here, the word '<s>tribhāga</s>' (one-third). /
And the sentence-form <s>alakṣyakramavyaṅgya-dhvani</s> (imperceptible-sequence suggestion) is considered twofold: pure (<s>śuddha</s>) and mixed with <s>alaṅkāra</s> (<s>alaṅkāra-saṅkīrṇa</s>). /
Of these, an example of the pure [type] — as in the <s>Rāmābhyudaya</s>: 'with feigned anger' etc. [<s>Locana</s>:] 'The word <s>tribhāga</s>' — thus. /
Even though she departed, defying her elders, nevertheless she looked at me with longing, anger, despondency, pride, and languid emotion — thus, through such recollection, the stimulation of <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) caused by mutual dependence as the very life [of each other] and by the journey — shines forth clearly in the proximity of the word '<s>tribhāga</s>' — thus. /
'And sentence-form' — the purport of the non-differential statement using the nominative case is this: /
Even though the <s>alakṣyakrama</s> (imperceptible-sequence) suggested [meaning], while shining forth when phonemes, words, their portions, etc. are present, nevertheless shines forth as pervading the entire poetry alone, because its vital essence lies in the combination of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. /
Therefore, phonemes etc. have merely causal status; but the sentence assists the <s>alakṣyakrama-dhvani</s> not merely as a cause like phonemes etc., but rather, because it is engaged in the comprehensive apprehension of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., it shines forth as itself constituted by <s>rasa</s> etc. — thus the word '<s>vākya</s>' (sentence) in the <s>kārikā</s> — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the purport is that the word [<s>vākya</s>] alone has primacy here. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, the additional example beginning with '<s>jhaṭiti kanake</s>' (suddenly in gold) has been interpolated, and therefore was not elaborated in the <s>Locana</s>. /
A certain person himself reflects upon the manner in which the beloved, who had seen him prepared for travel in the presence of elders, looked at him; or alternatively, he narrates [this] to an intimate friend — 'by the conjunction of modesty' etc. /
'Of elders' — of the father and such [relatives]. /
The trembling that was bound, i.e., produced, in the pitcher-like breasts — him who had that. /
'Anger' — the anger born from his effort [to travel], even despite the attempt to restrain [his] departure. /
'Was "you stay" not said to me?' — as if [it was]; indeed it was said. /
'Since' — by her, having shed tears, [with a glance] like a frightened deer, or charming like the eye of a frightened doe; or alternatively — the eye that is charming like a frightened doe's — one-third of that, i.e., the third portion. /
Or '<s>cakitahariṇīhāri</s>' is a separate word, serving as a qualifier of the action of casting [the glance]. /
The syntactic construction is: 'fixed upon me, cast upon me.' /
He elaborates the suggestive capacity of the word '<s>tribhāga</s>' — 'the elders' etc. /
'With longing' — the purport is: emotions such as longing etc. were manifested in the eye. /
'Through recollection' — accessible through recollection alone. /
'Mutual dependence as the cause' — the meaning is: being the cause of the mutual bond of stable affection. /
'Nominative' — the meaning is: by the nominative-case statement 'sentence-form <s>dhvani</s>.' /
'Of the non-differential statement' — of the cognition of non-difference. /
This will be stated by 'this is sentence-form' etc. /
The connection is: 'even though shining forth when [phonemes etc.] are present.' /
Even though the shining forth is not produced by phonemes, words, etc., nevertheless — this is the meaning. /
'Therefore' — because of shining forth through having the combination of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. as its vital essence — this is the meaning. /
'Like phonemes etc.' — the example is by contrast. /
'Comprehensive' — the meaning is: because of being the conveyor of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. in their entirety. /
'That' — the sentence. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — in the causal sense. /
'<s>Vākya</s>' etc. — the meaning is: the word '<s>vākya</s>' occurring in the <s>kārikā</s>. /
With the verse. /
For this sentence, displaying the mutual affection that has attained full maturity, illuminates from every quarter the supreme essence of <s>rasa</s>. /
[An example of one] mixed with another <s>alaṅkāra</s> is as follows — the verse beginning with '<s>smaranavanadīpūreṇoḍhāḥ</s>' (swept away by the flood of the river of passion).

children.translated_text: 'The essence of <s>rasa</s>' —
the essence that is <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment in separation).
'Swept away by the flood of the river of passion (<s>smara</s>), and again held back by the bridges of the elders — even though they stand with unfulfilled desires from afar,

children.text: tadapi likhitaprakhyairaṅgaiḥ parasparamunmukhā nayananalinīnālānītaṃ pibanti rasaṃ priyāḥ //
children.translated_text: nevertheless, with limbs that resemble paintings, facing each other, the lovers drink the <s>rasa</s> (nectar) brought through the lotus-stalks of their eyes.' //

Here, 'thus held back by her mother in those various ways' — yet, out of being overpowered by love, even the transgression of the elders' words was done by you — this [is suggested]. /
'O dear one, dear one' — by these [words], the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) of <s>rati</s> (love) — whose nature is the mutual regard of each other as one's entire life — is stated. /
'Fresh rain-cloud' etc. — the viewing of rain-season clouds never before endured is stated as an <s>uddīpana-vibhāva</s> (stimulating determinant) of <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation). /
'Lives on indeed' — the conditional nature [of this statement] is indicated by the word '<s>eva</s>' (indeed), for the purpose of removing the scope for <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos). /
'From every quarter' — the meaning is: here, no single word has a greater degree of causality for the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> than any other.

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Not' etc. — the meaning of the seventh [case] there is not merely causal — this is the extent. /
'Existing nowhere else' — the non-existence elsewhere, i.e., the impossibility of existing elsewhere — [the locative] has a meaning whose domain is of that form. /
'<s>Vākya</s>' (sentence) — the seventh-case meaning is also 'domain' — this is the meaning. /
'With feigned [anger]' — the syntactic connection of the instrumental-ending [words] is with '<s>dhṛtā</s>' (held back). /
'Out of love for him' — out of love for me. /
'Held back' — restrained. /
He explains — 'here' etc. /
'Was done' — the remainder is: is suggested. /
'O dear one, dear one' — the meaning is: by these two [words]. /
'Stated' — suggested. /
'Fresh rain-cloud' — the meaning is: by this. /
'Lives on indeed' — the conditional nature is stated by the word '<s>eva</s>' — this is the syntactic connection. /
'Passion' etc. — the reading '<s>vidhṛtās tiṣṭhanty ārād apūrṇa</s>' also [exists]. /
'<s>Prāvṛṣeṇya</s>' — belonging to the rainy season. /
He states the implied similarity in the superimposition of the nature of a flood — '<s>sarabhasa</s>' (impetuous) etc. /
By '<s>ūḍhāḥ</s>' (swept away), what is intended here — he says: 'mutual' etc. /
The elaboration of '<s>punaḥ</s>' (again) is '<s>anantaram</s>' (immediately afterward); and by the word '<s>guru</s>' (elder), there is also an alternative meaning — for here, the <s>rasa</s>, adorned by the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) that follows the character of a suggestor as stated, is manifested all the more. /
Having said 'the <s>alakṣyakramavyaṅgya-dhvani</s> shines forth in the composition (<s>saṅghaṭanā</s>),' the very nature of <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> is now being determined —
[<s>Kārikā</s>:] Without compounds, adorned with moderate compounds,
and with long compounds — thus composition (<s>saṅghaṭanā</s>) is stated as threefold. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.5 //
Without compounds, adorned with moderate compounds,

children.translated_text: For those swans etc. are appropriate for the sport of drinking water brought through a single lotus-stalk — anticipating this [objection], he says: 'with the character of a suggestor as stated' etc.

For it was stated earlier — in the passage beginning with '<s>vivakṣātatparatvena</s>' (through the orientation of intention) — '<s>nātinirvahaṇaiṣitā</s>' (the desire for excessive sustaining [of the metaphor] is not [required]).
'Adorned' —
the meaning is: through the medium of the adornment of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., the <s>rasa</s> too has been adorned. // 3–

By some. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'By <s>rūpaka</s>' — <s>Smara</s> (passion) itself is a river-flood of the rainy season — impetuously, precisely because of its great intensity — by that [flood] they are swept away, brought unwittingly into mutual face-to-face encounter. /
Immediately afterward, the elders — the mother-in-law and such — are themselves the bridges, because they obstruct the advance of desire. /
And since the elders are not to be transgressed, [they are like] bridges; held back by those — [the lovers are] those whose desires have been thwarted. /
Precisely therefore, they stand with unfulfilled desires. /
Nevertheless, through the mutual face-to-face orientation that constitutes their mutual identification with each other — with limbs that are almost like paintings due to the restraint of all activity in their own bodies — the eyes alone are the lotus-stalks; by those [stalks], the <s>rasa</s> (nectar) that is brought — characterized by mutual longing — they savor; through the device of mingling the rays of glances that are constituted by mutual longing, they even pass the time — thus. /
But here the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) is not fully sustained, since the couple of lovers has not been superimposed in the form of swans, <s>cakravāka</s> birds, etc.

'In the composition' — the suffix is in the abstract sense (<s>bhāve pratyaya</s>); and the seventh [case] is merely in the causal sense, like [the locative] with phonemes etc. /
'Stated' — in the <s>kārikā</s>. /

'<s>Rasa</s>' etc. — the meaning is: the water that is in the form of mutual longing. /
He states the purport — 'mutual' etc. /
The meaning is: through the device, the arrangement, of the mingling of the rays of glances that are constituted by mutual longing, that manifest mutual longing. /
In '<s>priyāḥ</s>' (lovers), as also in '<s>haṃsa-cakravāka</s>,' the single-remainder compound should be understood.

children.translated_text: For thus: even in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment), long compounds are seen; and in <s>raudra</s> (fury) and other [<s>rasas</s>], the absence of compounds [is seen].
Therein, the long compound in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is as follows: '<s>mandārakusumareṇupiñjaritālakā</s>' (she whose locks are yellowed by the pollen of <s>mandāra</s> flowers) etc.
Or as follows: 'Your face, O helpless one, resting on [your] palm, its painted-leaf ornament effaced by the incessant falling of drops of eye-water —
this [face of yours] — whom does it not torment?' //

'Abiding in dependence upon the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), it manifests <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) etc. — /
the <s>rasas</s> —' That <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> (composition/arrangement) manifests <s>rasas</s> etc. while abiding in dependence upon the <s>guṇas</s> — thus. /
And here, what is to be considered through alternatives is: the identity or the difference of the <s>guṇas</s> and the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>. /
Even in the case of difference, there are two possibilities: /
Either the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> has the <s>guṇas</s> as its substrate, or the <s>guṇas</s> have the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> as their substrate. /
In the identity-position and in the position where the <s>guṇas</s> are the substrate of the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> — [the meaning is:] the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> abides in dependence upon the <s>guṇas</s>, which are either identical with itself or which serve as its receptacle — [<s>Locana</s>:] The first word of the second half of the <s>kārikā</s>. '<s>Rasas</s> — the criterion for their regulation is propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) with respect to speaker and subject' — this is the half-<s>kārikā</s>. /
He shows that the first meaning is included by the plural: '<s>rasas</s> etc.' /
'And here' — /
In this very half-<s>kārikā</s>. /
This range of meanings can be arranged, i.e., explained, through alternatives — 'what is that?' he says: 'of the <s>guṇas</s>' etc. /
The three positions that are conceivable can be explained. /
'How?' he says: 'in the identity-position' etc. /
'Identical with itself' — /
For the purpose of demonstrating the nature of a thing through conceptual division, the statement of the substrate as being one's own — even of a division that has been shown — is seen, as in: 'the tree-ness residing in the <s>śiṃśapā</s> (rosewood tree).' /
'Serving as its receptacle' — /
<s>Bhaṭṭa Udbhaṭa</s> and others [hold that] the <s>guṇas</s> are properties of the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>, and properties reside in their possessors — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Where is this stated?' — to this she says: 'in the <s>kārikā</s>' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, at the point where [it says] '<s>saṅghaṭanā</s> manifests,' she supplies the subject-word: 'by some.' /
'That' etc. — is the introductory passage. /
She shows in the <s>Locana</s> that the <s>kārikā</s> reading is up to '<s>rasān</s>': '<s>rasas</s>' etc. /
The meaning is: <s>rasas</s> etc. /
'How is it derived?' — to this she says: 'by the plural' etc. /
'By the plural' — by the plural in '<s>rasān</s>.' /
The explanation of 'here' is: 'in this very' etc. /
'To be considered through alternatives' — she explains this in accordance with the context: 'through alternatives' etc. /
'This' — what is to be stated. /
'Can be [arranged]' — /
The purport is that the analysis of '<s>vikalpya</s>' (to be considered through alternatives) is '<s>vikalpena kalpya</s>' (to be arranged through alternatives). /
She states the purport: 'the three' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>: 'or the difference' — /
The meaning is: or the distinction. /
'Two possibilities' — /
The meaning is: twofoldness. /
'How the twofoldness?' — to this she says: 'the <s>guṇas</s> as substrate' etc. /
The meaning of the two locative-ending words ['position'] is connected with this. /
'Identical with itself' — /
The meaning is: non-different from itself. /
'Serving as its receptacle' — /
The meaning is: residing in itself. /
'This is the meaning' — /
'Of the <s>kārikā</s>' is the remainder. /
In the identity-position of <s>guṇa</s> and <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>, she shows in the <s>Locana</s> the justification of the expression 'abiding in dependence upon the <s>guṇas</s>' as a substrate-content relation: 'of the nature of a thing' etc. /
'Of the nature of a thing' — to demonstrate the nature of a thing. /
'Through conceptual division' — [of a thing] in which the division has been shown through conceptualization. /
The meaning is: even of a thing that is non-different from itself, by conceptually positing a division. /
'As its own substrate' — the meaning is: the statement as having itself as substrate. /
In accordance with the view that universal and individual are identical, she gives an example: '<s>śiṃśapā</s>' etc. /
'Thus' — the meaning is: and so forth. /
'This is the meaning' — /
But when in the difference-position, [it is] the position where the <s>guṇas</s> are the substrate of the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> — then 'abiding in dependence upon the <s>guṇas</s>' means: having a nature dependent on the <s>guṇas</s>, but not being of the very form of the <s>guṇas</s> — this is the meaning. /
But then, what is the purpose of this analysis through alternatives? It is stated: /
If the <s>guṇas</s> and the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> are one entity, or if the <s>guṇas</s> have the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> as substrate, then the consequence would be that the <s>guṇas</s>, like the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>, would have an unrestricted domain. /
For the excellence of <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) and <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity) among the <s>guṇas</s> pertains exclusively to <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos) and <s>vipralambhaśṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation). /
<s>Ojas</s> (vigor) pertains to <s>raudra</s> (fury), <s>adbhuta</s> (wonder), and other [<s>rasas</s>]. /
<s>Mādhurya</s> and <s>prasāda</s> pertain exclusively to <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and their semblances — the restriction of domain [<s>Locana</s>:] is a well-known path. /
'Dependent on the <s>guṇas</s>' — /
Here, the meaning of 'substrate' is not that of the container-content relation; /
for the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> does not reside in the <s>guṇas</s>. /
Therefore, just as in 'the body of subjects depends on the king' — where the meaning is 'the ministers and other subjects are [dependent] through the propriety of depending on the king' — similarly, the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> [is] of a nature dependent on the <s>guṇas</s>, governed by them, looking toward them — this is the meaning obtained. /
'Like the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>' — /
In the first position, because of the identical fate through identity; in the other [position], because of [the <s>guṇas</s>'] being properties [of the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>] — this is the purport. /
'Let there be an unrestricted domain' — anticipating this acceptance, he says: 'for the <s>guṇas</s>' etc. /
The word '<s>hi</s>' (for) is in the sense of '<s>tu</s>' (but): /
This is not tenable, but it follows through the force of reasoning — this is the meaning. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She shows in 'dṛśyate' (is seen) the connection; in the identity of tree-ness and <s>śiṃśapā</s>, even though they are identical, by conceptually positing a division, the statement of <s>śiṃśapā</s> as having tree-ness as substrate — just as [that is possible], so too in the present case — this is the purport. /
She states the supporting evidence for 'serving as its receptacle': '<s>saṅghaṭanā</s>' etc. /
She states the basis for the explanation 'having a nature dependent on the <s>guṇas</s>': 'here' etc. /
'The meaning of substrate' — the meaning of the word 'substrate.' /
'Not [that]' — to this she states the reason: 'for' etc. /
'Therefore' — /
The meaning is: through the obstruction of the primary meaning of the word 'substrate.' /
'Is obtained' — this is its connection. /
'Through the propriety of depending on the king' — the meaning is: for the suitability of the connection with the meaning of the word 'depending on the king.' /
The instrumental in the causal-result [sense]. /
After this, '<s>rājaparatantrā amātyādiprakṛtayaḥ</s>' (the ministers and other subjects are dependent on the king) should be read; if the reading '<s>rājaparatantrāḥ</s>' is absent, that word must be supplied. /
'Similarly' — /
The meaning is: likewise. The elaboration of 'dependent on the <s>guṇas</s>' etc. is: 'governed by them' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'what [is the purpose]?' etc. is the objection. /
'It is stated' etc. is the answer. /
'One entity' — /
The meaning is: one reality. /
She states the purport of the passage 'like the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>' in the <s>Locana</s>: 'in the first position' etc. /
'In the first position' — in the position that the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> are one entity. /
'Of the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>' is the remainder. /
'Of identical fate' — of identical nature. /
'In the other [position]' — in the position that the <s>guṇas</s> have the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> as substrate. /
'Because of being properties' — because of being properties of the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>. /
'Of identical fate' carries over. /
She elaborates 'the consequence of unrestricted domain': 'this is not tenable' etc. /
'Thus' — /
The meaning is: having an unrestricted domain. /
'Is not tenable' — /
Because of the established restricted domain of the <s>guṇas</s> — this is the purport. /
'Follows' — is entailed. /
'Anticipating this acceptance,' he says — /
The meaning is: he wards off this undesired consequence. /
The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) is in the restrictive sense. /
'Established' — and the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>'s [unrestricted domain] is violated.

children.translated_text: 'Of [two] entities' — is the remainder.
'Of <s>guṇa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s>' — this is the extent.
Those which support that principal meaning are known as <s>guṇas</s> (qualities);
but those dependent on the subsidiary [elements] should be regarded as <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments), like bracelets and such. //

And so forth. /
Likewise, even in <s>raudra</s> and other [<s>rasas</s>], the absence of compounds is seen — /
as in: 'whoever bears a weapon, arrogant in the strength of his own arm' etc. /
Therefore the <s>guṇas</s> are not of the very nature of <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>, nor do they have the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> as their substrate. /
But if the <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> is not the substrate of the <s>guṇas</s>, then on what basis should these be conceptualized? /
It is stated: their basis has already been established. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Thus' — /
This restriction that was stated regarding the <s>guṇas</s> — that is relevant here. /
Assuming this to be so, he presents empirical observation as the evidence: 'for thus' etc. /
'Is seen' — having stated [this], he introduces the example as the locus of observation: 'therein' etc. /
Anticipating the doubt 'there is no <s>śṛṅgāra</s> here,' he presents a second example: 'or as follows' etc. /
For this [verse] is uttered by the hero for the purpose of appeasing the heroine who is angered by the offense of love. /
'Therefore' — /
This much [is meant]: neither of these two interpretations is suitable for the <s>kārikā</s>. /
'On what basis' — /
For if their basis were word and meaning, then what distinction would there be from the <s>alaṅkāras</s>? — thus the ancients have stated — this is the purport. /
'Already established' — /
The meaning is: by the author of our root text. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She explains the 'that' word in 'that is violated': 'this' etc. /
'The restriction stated' — /
The purport is: the restriction that in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc. only the absence-of-compound type of <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> [prevails], and in <s>raudra</s> etc. only the long-compound type — such a restriction. /
'Is violated' — the meaning of this is: is contradicted. /
'Assuming this to be so' — the meaning is: the violation of the restriction. /
She introduces the example: 'is seen.' /
She introduces another example: 'there is no' etc. /
The purport is: because of the absence of cognition of <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) etc. /
'Incessant' — /
The 'falling of drops of eye-water' that is incessant — by that, the painted-leaf ornament is effaced, removed — that [face]. /
'Your' — of you. /
'This face' — this is the syntactic connection. /
She states the purport: 'neither of these' etc. /
She states the intent of the objection 'on what basis': 'word' etc. /
'Of the <s>guṇas</s>' is the remainder. /
'What distinction' — /
The meaning is: there would be no distinction. /
'Of the root text' — /
The meaning is: of the <s>kārikā</s>. /
She elaborates the purport of the passage 'nor is there identity of these two': 'for' etc. /
'Identity' —
