children.translated_text: But the fault that is caused by lack of [poetic] power —
that is perceived immediately. /
And a verse by another [author] on this point — 'The fault caused by a poet's lack of learning is concealed by [his] power;
but that [fault] which is caused by lack of power — that is perceived immediately.' //

Thus. /
Or alternatively, let the <s>guṇas</s> (poetic qualities) be properties of words alone — even so, they are not equivalent to <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) and such [figures]. /
Because <s>anuprāsa</s> and the like have been demonstrated to be properties of words that do not require meaning. /
But the <s>guṇas</s> are properties of words that are capable of conveying the expressible [meaning] that reveals a particular suggested [meaning]. /
And the word-property-status of these [<s>guṇas</s>], even when they reside in another locus [i.e., in <s>rasa</s>], is like the body-property-status of valor etc. [which belong to the soul but are attributed to the body]. /
But [one might object:] if the <s>guṇas</s> are properties of words, then it follows that they are either identical with the arrangement [of words] or that [the arrangement] is their locus. /
For unarranged words, being incapable of denoting the <s>guṇas</s> that reside in <s>rasa</s> etc. — which are conveyed through particular meanings — cannot serve as their locus. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Or alternatively' — for identity does not [follow] merely from having a single locus, since that would absurdly entail the identity of color and conjunction. /
If [you say] that in conjunction, a second [entity] is required — here too, the dependence on the expressible that assists the suggested [meaning] is present — so the [situation] is the same. /
Nor is this the position that I maintain; rather, let it be that even according to the view of these non-discriminating [thinkers], the word-property-status [of the <s>guṇas</s>] is like the body-property-status of valor etc. /
For a non-discriminating person is incapable of distinguishing the division between the figurative and the primary [usage]. /
Nevertheless, there is no fault — thus, with this ultimate [intention], this was stated — he says: 'the word-property-status' etc. /
'Even when residing in another locus' — the meaning is: even when residing in the self [i.e., <s>rasa</s>]. /
'Properties of words' — if the <s>guṇas</s> are [attributed] to words through figurative usage, then this is the purport: the capacity of words to convey the expressible that manifests <s>rasas</s> beginning with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> as the suggested — that alone is the <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) of words. /
And that, being located in words, is obtained precisely through a particular arrangement. /
Now, is not the arrangement something non-different [from the words themselves]? Rather, the arranged [words] themselves — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the absurd consequence of identity — /
The purport is: because of residing in a single substance such as a pot. /
He dispels the absurd consequence of identity — 'conjunction' etc. /
'A second [entity] is required' — the meaning is: since conjunction as an effect arises from two [entities], the dependence of conjunction on that [second entity] with respect to which the conjunction arises — this is the meaning. /
But color, arising in just one [substance], does not require a second — this is the purport. /
The mode of resolution is the same — he says: 'here' etc. /
'Here too, even in the <s>guṇas</s>' — /
'Suggested' — by this, the <s>vṛtti</s> text 'but the <s>guṇas</s> [are properties] that [reveal] the suggested' etc. is elaborated. /
He introduces the passage 'and the word-property-status' etc. — 'nor' etc. /
The construction is: 'this is not my maintained position.' /
'Of these' — the meaning is: of the <s>guṇas</s>. /
The connection is: 'let the word-property-status be.' /
'The division between the figurative' — the meaning is: the distinction of the figurative from the primary [usage]. /
'Incapable of knowing.' /
'This was stated' — what was stated by 'or alternatively' etc. /
'Thus' — the meaning is: what was stated [is this]. /
'Even when residing in the self' — by the word '<s>ātman</s>' (self), <s>rasa</s> and the individual soul should be understood. /
She states the purport of the passage from 'if the <s>guṇas</s> are properties of words' to 'it follows indeed' — 'through figurative usage' etc. /
The elaboration of the passage ending with '<s>guṇas</s>' — 'through figurative usage' etc. /
'This' — what follows immediately is not so; because the suggested-status of <s>rasas</s> etc. through phonemes and words has been demonstrated. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] words — that which resides in them, that capacity — is dependent on the arrangement — thus the purport of what has been stated. /
But [objection:] let the word-property-status [of <s>guṇas</s>], or the word-identity [with <s>guṇas</s>], be [accepted] to that extent [at least] — why this introduction of arrangement in between? — anticipating this, the previous-position advocate himself says: 'for' etc. /
Through particular meanings — not through the general [meanings] denoted by individual words in isolation, but through [meanings] that are conveyed by the aggregate of mutually expectant words, namely the forms of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. — the <s>rasas</s>, <s>bhāvas</s>, their semblances, and their subsidence — of the <s>guṇas</s> that reside in these primarily, unarranged words cannot be the locus even figuratively — this is the purport. /
Here the reason is — 'because of being incapable of denoting.' /
The meaning is: for unarranged [words] do not bring about, do not make manifest, the expressible that is useful for the suggested in the form free from expectancy. /
He dispels this — 'not so.' /
For insofar as the phoneme-suggested <s>rasa</s> has been stated [as existing], to that extent, even of a word that is incapable of denoting its own meaning [in isolation], through merely being heard, by its own felicity, just like a phoneme — its being a cause of the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> is clearly perceived — therefore that alone is <s>mādhurya</s> etc. — what need of arrangement? Likewise, insofar as the word-suggested <s>dhvani</s> has been stated, to that extent, even of an isolated word — through its capacity to evoke the awareness of a meaning suitable for manifesting <s>rasa</s>, even by merely reminding [one] of its own meaning — that alone is <s>mādhurya</s> etc. — even there, what use is arrangement? /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the meaning is: what is about to be stated. /
'And that, located in words' — the meaning is: the capacity of the stated form, being located in words. /
'Particular' — the meaning is: obtained precisely through a particular arrangement with other words — this is the meaning. /
'Then what?' — to this he says: 'now' etc. /
'Now' — and further. /
'Not different' — not distinct from the words. /
'Residing in them' — residing in the arranged words. /
'That' — the previously stated [capacity]. /
'Thus' — in the causal sense. /
'And residing in the arrangement' — the arrangement-form-status should also be understood in the stated manner. /
'But [objection]' — the rest is: 'of the <s>guṇas</s>.' /
'To that extent' — the meaning is: through figurative usage. /
That very [previous-position advocate] says — by this, the passage 'and that, located in words, obtained precisely through a particular arrangement' — this meaning is demonstrated by himself — is revealed. /
Through particular meanings — the meaning is: [meanings] that are conveyed by the aggregate of mutually expectant words — meaning the forms of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. /
By this, what is excluded is stated — 'not through' etc. /
General [meanings] — general-form meanings are expressible by words — this was stated before. /
'Because of being incapable of denoting' — intending the meaning 'because of being incapable of manifesting' — he explains: 'for' etc. /
'Words' is the remainder. /
'The expressible — they bring about' — they make manifest the sentence-meaning. /
He elaborates the purport of the passage beginning with '<s>varṇa</s>' (phoneme) — 'for the phoneme-suggested <s>rasa</s>' etc. /
'Insofar as' — since. /
'Has been stated' — demonstrated by '<s>yastvalakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s>' (that which has imperceptible-sequence suggestion) etc. /
'To that extent' — from that. /
'Even of a word that is incapable of denoting' — even of one that merely reminds of its own meaning. /
Of a word, which is of the form of an aggregate of phonemes — /
Just like a phoneme — /
Clearly perceived — the purport is: by the principle of <s>kaimutyanyāya</s> (a fortiori reasoning). /
'And likewise' — the meaning is: and when the word-suggested <s>dhvani</s>-status of <s>rasas</s> etc. has been established. /
'Even of an isolated' — the meaning is: even of an unarranged [word]. /
Or alternatively, even when sentence-suggested [<s>dhvani</s>]-status is accepted for <s>rasas</s> etc. — no particular fixed arrangement of those [words] is accepted as the locus of the <s>guṇas</s> — [<s>Locana</s>:] words alone, [words] whose [status is] characterized by the presence of a particular suggested [meaning] — are the locus [of the <s>guṇas</s>]. /
'But [objection]' — /
If with the intention of sentence-suggested <s>dhvani</s>, this should be considered [an objection] — [say] some. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'But' etc. /
'With arrangement' — with a particular arrangement. /
'Its own' — the meaning is: the beauty of the sentence. /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] 'Of them' — the meaning is: of the <s>guṇas</s>. /
'Characterized by the presence of a particular suggested [meaning]' — the meaning is: revealing a particular suggested [meaning]. /
She states in the <s>Locana</s> the purport of the passage beginning with 'or alternatively, even when accepted' — 'this' etc. /
'Of <s>mādhurya</s>' — the meaning is: of <s>mādhurya</s> etc. /
'A particular fixed arrangement is not the locus or the essential nature of <s>mādhurya</s>' — this is the syntactic connection. /
Here he states the reason — 'without that' etc. /
'Because of the existence of <s>mādhurya</s> etc.' — the meaning is: because <s>mādhurya</s> etc. exist [even without a fixed arrangement]. /
'Because of existence' — by this, the deviation [from the rule] is demonstrated. /
Therefore he says — 'sentence' etc. /
'Of <s>rasa</s> etc.' carries over. /
'Even setting aside the arrangement' — even without the cooperation of the arrangement. /
'Because of the capacity to suggest that <s>rasa</s>' — because of the possibility of suggesting that particular <s>rasa</s>. /
'Not productive' — not useful. /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] 'But' etc. /
'Thus' — the meaning is: the word-property-status through non-fixed-arrangement. /
'Let that be stated' — let it be said so. /
'Further' — in the particular [case]. /
'Here too we do not not say' — the meaning is: even to this objection, we certainly give an answer. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'In the sentence-suggested' etc. /
'This' — the meaning is: the objection. /
'Should be considered' — the purport is: because the arrangement is possible only in the sentence. /
And there is a charm perceptible to the hearts of the sensitive readers (<s>sahṛdayas</s>). /
Therefore, in the word-property-status through non-fixed-arrangement of the <s>guṇas</s>, there is no loss whatsoever. /
But of those [<s>guṇas</s>], like the sense-faculties of the eye etc., the nature restricted to its respective domain never deviates. /
Therefore, the <s>guṇas</s> are one thing and the arrangement is another. /
Nor do the <s>guṇas</s> reside in the arrangement — this is one view. /
Or alternatively, the <s>guṇas</s> are of the very form of the arrangement. /
But what was said — 'Like the arrangement, the non-fixed-domain-status of the <s>guṇas</s> too would follow, /
because deviation is observed in the [poetic] examples' — /
to that too, this is said: /
Wherever in the example the deviation is with respect to an imagined domain, let that be so in its own nature. /
How does the absence of charm in such a domain not appear to the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (sensitive readers)? — if [asked] so: because it is concealed by the poet's power. /
For there is a twofold fault — one caused by the poet's lack of learning, and one caused by lack of [poetic] power. /
Therein, the fault caused by lack of learning, being concealed by [poetic] power, is sometimes not perceived. /

[Locana:] But we say — even when <s>ojas</s> (energy), which is of the nature of <s>raudra</s> (furious) etc., is suggested by phonemes and words, the inherent beauty of the individual phonemes and words does not unfold to that degree so long as they are not marked by [appropriate] combination — thus, in a general sense, this is the prima facie view. /
'Manifesting' — the present participle is in the sense of 'being the mark and cause.' /
The purport is: <s>ojas</s> is inferred through the manifestation of <s>raudra</s> etc. /
'Nor' — /
The word '<s>ca</s>' is in the sense of reason. /
Since in [verses like] 'whoever bears a weapon' etc., no absence of charm is perceived — therefore, this is the meaning. /
'Of those' — of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). /
'Each in its own way' — /
And by [the statement] '<s>śṛṅgāra</s> alone is the supreme, mind-delighting <s>rasa</s>' etc., the restriction to domains has already been stated. /
'Or alternatively' — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Of phonemes' etc. — /
The meaning is: even when <s>ojas</s> is suggested by phonemes and words. /
'Of the nature of <s>raudra</s> etc.' — having the properties of <s>raudra</s> and other <s>rasas</s>. /
'To that degree' — surpassingly. /
'Does not unfold so long' — this is the connection. /
'Those' — /
The meaning is: phonemes and words. /
'Marked by combination' — /
The meaning is: qualified by combination. /
'In a general sense only' — /
The meaning is: with the general intention of <s>dhvani</s> suggested by phonemes, words, and sentences. /
'<s>Raudra</s> etc.' — /
The meaning is: inferred, ascertained through the manifestation of <s>raudra</s> etc. /
'No absence of charm' — /
The syntactic connection is: absence of charm is not perceived. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'of those' — /
The meaning is: of the <s>guṇas</s>. /
This connects with 'of the nature.' /
For thus — even the impropriety of the well-known depiction of the erotic union (<s>saṃbhoga-śṛṅgāra</s>) concerning supreme deities by great poets does not appear as vulgarity, because it is eclipsed by [poetic] power. /
As in the <s>Kumārasambhava</s>, the description of the union of the Goddess [<s>Pārvatī</s> with <s>Śiva</s>]. /
In such and similar subject matters, the non-abandonment of propriety — thus [<s>Locana</s>:] the purport is: the very capacity of words for <s>rasa</s>-manifestation is their combining in such and such a way. /
'<s>Śakti</s>' (power) — creative intuition, the quality of freshness in depicting the subject matter to be described. /
'<s>Vyutpatti</s>' (learning) — the skill in comprehensively reviewing, in proper sequence, all matters useful to that [description]. /
'Of that' — of the poet. /
'Impropriety' — /
The non-obstruction of the wonder experienced by the <s>rasika</s>-connoisseurs — that alone is the essence of <s>rasa</s>, since [<s>rasa</s>] depends on relishing. /
And in the contemplation of the erotic union of supreme deities, there would be some room for obstruction of wonder through shame, embarrassment, etc., as in [contemplating] one's parents' union — this is the meaning. /
'Because it is eclipsed by power' — /
For that union too was described by a poet possessing such creative intuition that the heart, resting in that [description] alone, does not allow [the reader] to make sequential reflections — just as when a man of effortless prowess fights even in an inappropriate situation, at that very moment applause is offered by the spectators, but not upon sequential reflection. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'In the domain' — /
The objects of the senses like sight are forms etc., but the objects of the <s>guṇas</s> are the <s>rasas</s>. /
'View' — /
The meaning is: opinion. /
He states the purport of the passage beginning with 'or alternatively' — in the <s>Locana</s>: '<s>rasa</s>' etc. /
'In such and such a way' — /
The meaning is: in conformity with each particular <s>rasa</s>. /
'This is the purport' — /
The <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) etc. residing in words is nothing but the capacity for manifesting each particular <s>rasa</s> — <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc. — and that [capacity] is [dependent on] combination in such and such a way. /
Therefore, the <s>guṇas</s> are nothing but the forms of combination — this is the meaning of the purport. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'but what' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: 'but what was said' — thus. /
'In which observable [instance]' — /
The meaning is: in [verses like] 'unceasing' etc. and 'whoever bears a weapon' etc. /
'Contrived' — /
The meaning is: the deviation from the domain stated in 'without compounding' etc. /
He elaborates the terms '<s>śakti</s>' and '<s>vyutpatti</s>' in the <s>Locana</s> — '<s>śakti</s>' etc. /
'Useful to that' — /
The meaning is: the skill, the capacity, in reviewing in proper sequence all matters that are useful to that subject to be described. /
He elaborates the impropriety of the depiction of <s>saṃbhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> concerning supreme deities — 'which' etc. /
'Non-obstruction of wonder' — the absence of anything that obstructs wonder. /
'Parents' union' — /
The meaning is: the contemplation of the union of mother and father. /
He elaborates the passage beginning with 'because eclipsed by power' — 'the union too' etc. /
'That' — the meaning is: concerning supreme deities. /
'In that alone' — in the described union itself. /
'The heart' is the agent. /
'Does not give' — [does not give] itself, of the sensitive reader — this is the remainder. /
Alternatively — 'it' is the remainder. /
The meaning is: the described union. /
'The heart' is the object. /
'Even in an inappropriate situation' — /
The meaning is: even in the domain of children, elders, etc. /
'At that moment' — at the time of battle. /
'Is offered' — is given by the spectators. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'non-abandonment of propriety' — /
'In whatever manner' — in the manner of description. /
'Non-abandonment of propriety' — the absence of impropriety. /
'Has been shown' — /
The meaning is: has been demonstrated by the body of passages beginning with '<s>vibhāva-bhāva</s>' etc. /
'Hereafter' — further on. /
But wouldn't it be proper to say 'will be shown' rather than 'has been shown'? — to this he says in the <s>Locana</s>: 'has indeed been shown hereafter.' /
And the eclipsing by power is ascertained through positive and negative concomitance. /
For thus — when <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is composed in such a subject matter by a poet lacking [poetic] power, it clearly appears as a fault. /
But in this position, what is the absence of charm in 'whoever bears a weapon' etc.? We would be imposing something that is not actually perceived. /
Therefore, for the restriction upon combination — whether it is distinct from <s>guṇa</s> or identical with <s>guṇa</s> — some other determining cause must be stated — thus it is said.
. . . . the cause of that restriction is <s>aucitya</s> (propriety) of the speaker and the subject matter. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.6b //
The cause of that restriction is <s>aucitya</s> (propriety) of the speaker and the subject matter. // 6 //

children.translated_text: The meaning is: the introduction of <s>ojas</s> (energy) in place of [<s>mādhurya</s> in] <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc., and of <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) in <s>raudra</s> (the furious) etc.
'External to hearing' —
the meaning is: unheard.
He states the purport of the passage from 'therefore' to 'not contradictory' — by 'if the <s>guṇas</s>' etc. // 5-6 //

[Locana:] Therein, the speaker is either the poet or one created by the poet; and one created by the poet is either devoid of rasa-emotion or endowed with rasa-emotion; the rasa too is either based on the protagonist of the story or based on his adversary; and the protagonist is differentiated into types such as dhīrodātta (noble-heroic) etc., being either the primary [character] or the one next to him — these are the alternatives. / And the expressible is an element (aṅga) of rasa that is the essence of dhvani — [Locana:] the purport is: here too [the same applies]. / 'Has been demonstrated precisely' — / 'By the kārikā-author' — [the past tense is used] because [the statement] has been completed. / For it will be stated: 'There is no other cause for the destruction of rasa than impropriety (anaucitya)' etc. / 'Not apprehended even' — / The meaning is: even by those who are skilled in discriminating through consideration of what precedes and follows. / 'Being distinct from guṇas' — / For in the view that [guṇas and saṅghaṭanā] are distinct, there simply is no determinant-cause for composition (saṅghaṭanā); and in the view of their identity too, another [reason] must be stated — [namely] that rasa is not the determinant-cause. / 'Its regulation' — this is the remainder of the kārikā. / 'Protagonist of the story' (kathānāyaka) means one who leads the story to the state of being a component of one's own purpose — [that is,] one who is the recipient of the fruit at the denouement. / 'Dhīrodātta etc.' — / The dhīrodātta has dharma, war-valor as primary; the dhīroddhata has heroism and ferocity as primary; / the dhīralalita has heroism and the erotic as primary; / the dhīrapraśānta has generosity, dharma, heroism, and tranquility as primary — thus the four heroes correspond respectively to the sāttvatī, ārabhaṭī, kaiśikī, and bhāratī vṛttis (dramatic styles) as primary. / The primary [hero] is the protagonist; the one next to him is the sub-hero (upanāyaka). / 'Alternatives' — / The meaning is: varieties of the speaker. / 'The expressible' — / [Bālapriyā:] 'by the kārikā-author' — / The purport is: since the statement of the kārikā has been completed, the past-tense reference is appropriate. / 'For it will be stated' — / 'And by the vṛtti-author' is the remainder. / In the vṛtti, 'now' etc. / 'In this view' — / The meaning is: in the view where guṇas are identical with composition (saṅghaṭanā). / 'What is the lack of beauty?' — this is the objection. / The reply to that — 'not apprehended' etc. / 'Lack of beauty' carries over. / As to 'by whom is it not apprehended?' — he says in the Locana: 'those who [consider] what precedes and follows' etc. / He elaborates: 'in the view of distinction, for' etc. / 'Does not exist' — / The meaning is: only the domain-restriction of guṇas has been stated; no determinant-cause for composition has been stated. / 'Rasa is not the determinant-cause' — / The purport is: because of deviation in the examples. / In the vṛtti, 'it is said' — / The meaning is: the determinant-cause is shown for this reason. / 'Remainder of the kārikā' — / The purport is: not filled in by the vṛtti-author. / He explains the word 'kathānāyaka' (protagonist) — 'the story' etc. / 'Of one's own purpose' — / The meaning is: of what is to be accomplished by oneself. / The word 'sva' (own) refers to the recipient of the fruit. / 'Dharma' — / The meaning is: dharma-valor and war-valor as primary. / Though the dhīroddhata etc. have ferocity, the erotic, and tranquility respectively as primary, since heroic enthusiasm (utsāha) also necessarily exists in them, he says: 'heroism' etc. / 'Sātvatī' etc. — / The definitions of the sāttvatī and other vṛttis should be consulted elsewhere. / She explains the word 'alternatives' in accordance with the context: 'varieties of the speaker' etc. / The meaning of 'of the speaker and the expressible' — the internal sub-varieties of the stated speaker [and expressible]. / She explains 'the expressible is that which has a performable meaning (abhineyārtha)': 'performable' etc. / 'By speech, gesture, temperament, and spectacle' — the meaning is: by four [modes]. / The elaboration of 'of the nature of the suggested' — 'of the nature of dhvani.' / The meaning is: of the nature of dhvani. / He substantiates what was stated: 'that very one' etc. / 'That very one' — the suggested alone. / 'Connection with performance' — the status of being performable. / 'By speech, gesture' — up to 'bhāvayanti' (they bring into being) — this is the etymological derivation of the word bhāva. / 'Etc.' — the connection is: 'thus the sage states in various places.' / Since 'kāvyārtha' (the meaning of poetry) is etymologically derived as 'that which is to be extracted from poetry,' the word denotes the suggested rasa etc. — this is the purport. / Now, is there then no performance of the expressible meaning? — to this he says: 'as inseparable from rasa-performance' etc. / He concludes the explanation: 'therefore' etc. / 'Therefore' is in the causal sense. / The construal is: therefore this statement of expressible-arrangement alone is more appropriate. / The meaning is: the explanation as already stated is more fitting. / 'But not' etc. — / If the expressible itself is what is to be performed, then in 'the expressible has a performable meaning,' the compound analysis is 'that whose meaning is performable' — since the referent of the word 'vācya' and the referent of the word 'artha' are identical, the sixth case (genitive) [in the compound] would be explained as involving an appearance of difference as in 'Rāhu's head' — thus it is explained by others — this is the remainder. / Having shown the meaning of 'the speaker created by the poet is devoid of rasa-emotion' and anticipating an objection therein, he resolves it: 'devoid of rasa-emotion' etc. / The elaboration of 'devoid of rasa-emotion' — 'not possessed.' / The meaning is: devoid of possession by rasa etc. / 'Who is such?' — to this he says: 'an ascetic etc.' / 'Api' is in the conjunctive sense. / 'Follows the primary rasa precisely' — / And thus, he acts freely according to the particular mental states. / Even when the speaker created by the poet is devoid of rasa-emotion, that is [just] the same; but when the poet or the poet-created speaker is the speaker endowed with rasa-emotion, and the rasa — being based on the primary [character] — is of the essence of dhvani, then the composition must necessarily be in a medium-compound or non-compound style. / In karuṇa (pathetic) and vipralambha-śṛṅgāra (love-in-separation), however, only a non-compound composition [is appropriate]. / If asked 'how?' — the reply is: / When rasa is to be conveyed predominantly, all that obstructs or opposes its apprehension must be entirely avoided. / And thus, since long-compound compositions, with the possibility of multiple types [of construction], sometimes obstruct the apprehension of rasa — there should be no excessive attachment to them. / [Locana:] The two causatives. / 'Especially in [poetry with] performable meaning' — / For with an interrupted (unbroken) suggested [meaning], the performance of meanings requiring compounds cannot be accomplished. / Vocal inflections (kāku) and other [devices], and songs and such in between for the sake of lucidity — / in those [compositions with long compounds], they are difficult to employ, and the apprehension would involve much doubt — it would not be appropriate for drama. / Because that [dramatic apprehension] is of the nature of direct perception — this is the purport. / 'Elsewhere too' — / Even in [poetry] without performable meaning. / 'Becomes sluggish' — / The meaning is: the aesthetic relish is obstructed, i.e. impeded. / Of that long-compound composition, whatever expressible that, by virtue of requiring it — i.e. being inseparable from it — serves as suggestor of rasa (rasa-appropriate and to be employed for rasa-suggestion) — its need for long-compound composition is the cause of non-deficiency [in that case]. / The explanation that 'the hero's ākṣepa means activity' does not fit well — enough! / 'Is pervasive' — / Whatever composition it may be, it should be crafted so that apprehension of the expressible occurs instantly — this is what is meant. / 'It has been stated' — / By the [passage] 'the quality of poetry that is surrender' etc. / 'Does not suggest' — / [Bālapriyā:] The construal is: 'does not look good.' / To remove the curiosity 'whence comes this [principle]?' — she states the purport: 'with uninterrupted [suggestion]' etc. / 'Therein' should be supplied in each sentence — the meaning is: when there is long-compound composition. / 'With uninterrupted suggested [meaning] it cannot be accomplished' — but rather, it would have to be accomplished only by breaking up the suggested meaning — this is the purport. / She states additional defects: 'vocal inflections' etc. / 'In between' — in the middle, songs etc. for the sake of lucidity. / 'Difficult to employ' — employed with difficulty. / 'Therein, the apprehension involving much doubt' — and it would not be appropriate for drama: this is the construal. / She states the reason: 'of the nature of direct perception' etc. / The meaning is: because it is of the nature of direct realization (sākṣātkāra), free from obstructions such as doubt. / 'Of that' — / The meaning is: of dramatic apprehension. / Drama (nāṭya) is defined as apprehension whose essence is the relish of rasa — as stated in the Abhinavabhāratī. / In the vṛtti, 'therein, and elsewhere' — / The carryover of 'of that' should be understood here too. / In the Locana, she states the intended meaning: 'the aesthetic relish' etc. / In the vṛtti, 'in another rasa' etc. — / The connection is: when another rasa such as raudra (furious) etc. is to be conveyed, medium-compound composition is not defective; sometimes even long-compound composition is not defective. / The cause of non-deficiency of long-compound [style] — 'its ākṣepa' etc. / She explains this passage: 'of that' etc. / 'Of the composition' — the sixth case (genitive) in the sense of the object. / 'Ākṣepa' means the drawing-in, the employment, of words belonging to its own domain within a compound. / 'Inseparable from that' — this qualifies the expressible, she says: 'by that' etc. / For that [prasāda quality] is common to all rasas and common to all compositions — thus it is stated. / For even non-compound composition, if it transgresses lucidity (prasāda), does not suggest karuṇa or vipralambha-śṛṅgāra. / And when lucidity is not abandoned, even medium-compound [style] does illuminate [them]. / Therefore, lucidity (prasāda) must be observed everywhere. / And for this very reason, in [the verse] 'whoever bears a weapon' etc. — if the presence of ojas (vigor) is to be accepted — that is precisely the quality called prasāda, not mādhurya (sweetness). / Nor is there lack of beauty — because the intended rasa is illuminated. / Therefore, whether guṇas are non-different from composition or different from it, composition has domain-restriction as stated, based on propriety — thus it too has the capacity to suggest rasa. / And that [composition], being a cause of rasa-manifestation, has the stated determinant-cause as the very restricted domain of guṇas — thus establishment through the medium of guṇas is also non-contradictory. / [Locana:] The purport is: because the suggestor does not convey its own expressible [meaning]. / 'That' — / Since non-abandonment of lucidity is desired, the positive and negative concomitance are stated here in the author's own words regarding this meaning. / 'Not mādhurya' — / For the mutual-absence-nature of ojas and mādhurya was previously established; hence their mixture is entirely contrary to [literary] tradition — this is the purport. / 'Intended' — / The meaning is: by lucidity alone that rasa is illuminated, not not-illuminated. / 'Therefore' — / If guṇas are of one nature with composition, then the restriction of guṇas is itself the restriction of composition. / Even in the view that composition depends on guṇas, it is the same. / Even in the view that guṇas depend on composition — [Bālapriyā:] the connection is: the expressible that is not a suggestor of the suggested. / The purport is: only when the respective denoting words are marked with long-compound composition do the expressible meanings become suggestors. / The construal of 'by the requirement' is with 'is not defective' — she says: 'that' etc. / Having shown an alternative explanation of 'its ākṣepa,' she refutes it: 'of the hero' etc. / 'Does not fit' — / The purport is: because it does not accord with the construal. / She elaborates what was stated as 'the quality called prasāda is pervasive': 'whatever' etc. / 'Whatever composition it may be' — / The meaning is: composition in the form of long-compound etc. / 'Because it is desired' — / The meaning is: because the observance of lucidity is intended. / Its connection is with 'stated.' / 'In this meaning' — / The meaning is: in the [principle] that lucidity must be observed everywhere. / 'In the author's own words' etc. — / The construal is with 'when not abandoned, [it] does illuminate' — and the vyatireka is also stated by 'when lucidity is transgressed' etc. — this is the meaning. / She states the purport: 'of ojas and mādhurya' etc. / 'Mutual' — / The meaning is: the nature of ojas is the absence of mādhurya, and the nature of mādhurya is the absence of that [ojas]. / 'Mixture' — /

children.text: viṣayāśrayam apy anyad aucityaṃ tāṃ niyacchati /
children.translated_text: Yet another <s>aucitya</s> (propriety), based on the subject domain, regulates that [combination];

children.text: kāvya-prabhedāśrayataḥ sthitā bhedavatī hi sā // DhvK_3.7 //
children.translated_text: for it [the combination] abides as possessed of varieties, depending on the subdivisions of poetry. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.7 //
Yet another <s>aucitya</s> (propriety), based on the subject domain, regulates that [combination];
for it [the combination] abides as possessed of varieties, depending on the subdivisions of poetry. // 7 //
For the subdivisions of poetry are: the <s>muktaka</s> (standalone verse), composed in Sanskrit, Prakrit, or <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>;
the <s>sandānitaka</s> (linked pair), <s>viśeṣaka</s> (distinguishing set), <s>kalāpaka</s> (cluster), and <s>kulaka</s> (family [of verses]);

children.text: paryāyabandhaḥ parikathā khaṇḍakathā sakalakathe sargabandho 'bhineyārthamākhyāyikākathe ityevamādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>paryāyabandha</s> (cycle composition), the <s>parikathā</s> (narrative), the <s>khaṇḍakathā</s> (fragmentary tale), the <s>sakalakathā</s> (complete tale), the <s>sargabandha</s> (canto composition), the <s>abhineyārtha</s> (dramatic composition), the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> and <s>kathā</s> — and so forth.

children.text: tadāśrayeṇāpi locanam hetutvenoktaṃ tadguṇānāmapi niyamaheturiti pakṣatraye 'pi na kaścidvaplava iti tātparyam // 5//
children.translated_text: Based on those [subdivisions] also — [<s>Locana</s>:] What has been stated as a cause [of restriction] is also the cause of restriction for the <s>guṇas</s> of those [subdivisions] — in all three positions, there is no wavering — this is the purport. // 5 //
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Even when <s>aucitya</s> of speaker and subject matter is present, another <s>aucitya</s>, based on the domain, regulates the combination.

children.translated_text: In the <s>sargabandha</s> — [<s>Locana</s>:] But how is the combination of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. [possible] in a <s>muktaka</s>, such that <s>rasa</s> would depend on it? — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'in <s>muktakas</s>' etc.
Of <s>Amaruka</s> —

children.text: kathamapi kṛtapratyāpattau priye skhalitottare virahakṛśayā kṛtvā vyājaprakalpitamaśrutam /
children.translated_text: 'When the beloved, with whom a reconciliation had somehow been effected, stumbled in her reply — by the one emaciated by separation, having contrived a pretended [moment of] not-hearing,

children.text: ahanasakhīśrotraprāptiṃ viśaṅkya samambhramaṃ vivalitadṛśā śūnye gehe samucchvasitaṃ tataḥ //
children.translated_text: fearing that it might reach the ears of her companion, with flurried haste, in the empty house, with rolling eyes, a sigh was heaved' //

He says there is yet another regulator — 'based on the domain' etc. /
By the word 'domain' (<s>viṣaya</s>), a particular type of aggregate is meant. /
For just as a man who has entered an aggregate in the form of an army etc., even if he is timid, conducts himself in conformity with the propriety of that [aggregate], so too a poetic sentence, when situated within a particular aggregate-form such as the <s>sandānitaka</s> etc., operates according to the propriety of that [form]. /
But as for the <s>muktaka</s> — what is stated by the word 'domain' [refers to] its independence, due to the absence of an aggregate, just as space is self-established — to show this much alone [the <s>muktaka</s> is mentioned]. /
By the word 'also' (<s>api</s>), he says this: even when the <s>aucitya</s> of speaker and subject matter is present, the <s>aucitya</s> of domain merely extends to differences of degree, but the <s>aucitya</s> of domain does not override the <s>aucitya</s> of speaker and subject matter. /
'<s>Muktaka</s>' — released (<s>mukta</s>), i.e. not embraced by another; the suffix <s>kan</s> is in the sense of a technical name. /
Therefore, even though [a verse] that is situated within a longer composition may have a self-contained meaning requiring no further expectancy, it is not called a <s>muktaka</s>. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He elaborates the <s>muktaka</s> itself with an illustration — 'just as' etc. /
'Army' — an aggregate whose nature is an army etc.; one who has entered into it, who is situated [therein]. /
'Even if timid' — /
The meaning is: even if naturally timid. /
'<s>Kātarādi</s>' (timid etc.) is also a reading. /
'In conformity with that' — the meaning is: in conformity with the army etc. /
That is to say: as if not timid. /
'Poetic sentence' — the meaning is: a sentence that constitutes poetry. /
But would this not mean that since the <s>muktaka</s>, being a single verse, lacks the nature of an aggregate, the <s>vṛtti</s>'s statement of it as a subdivision of poetry is pointless? — to this he says: 'but as for the <s>muktaka</s>' etc. /
'That' — that statement. /
'Due to the absence of an aggregate' — due to the absence of the nature of an aggregate. /
'Independence' — /
The meaning is: since the <s>muktaka</s> too overflows with <s>rasa</s>, it has independence with respect to the regulation of combination — merely this much is to be shown, and therefore the <s>muktaka</s> too is stated as a subdivision of poetry. /
Here he gives an illustration — 'self-established' etc. /
When it is said that the four [elements] — earth etc. — are established in space, and the question arises 'where then is space established?', the answer is: 'space is established in itself, in space' — just as <s>Brahman</s> [is established] in <s>Brahman</s>, space is established in space alone, not elsewhere — this is the meaning. /
Just as that statement merely shows the independence of space — similarly, this is the meaning. /
'Even when present' — /
The meaning is: even when [the <s>aucitya</s> of speaker and subject matter] indeed [exists]. /
'Of degree' — /
The meaning is: causing only differences of degree. /
'Not embraced by another' — /
The meaning is: not dependent on any other [verse] for the completion of understanding without expectancy. /
'In the sense of a technical name' — /
By this [it follows that] the combination possesses varieties. /
Therein, in the <s>muktakas</s>, for a poet who is devoted to the weaving of <s>rasa</s>, the <s>aucitya</s> based on that [<s>rasa</s>] applies. /
And that has already been demonstrated. /
Otherwise, there is freedom [of choice]. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The qualifier is 'in Sanskrit' etc. /
Since they arise in sequence, they are enumerated in that very order. /
When the action is completed in two [verses], it is a <s>sandānitaka</s>. /
In three, a <s>viśeṣaka</s>. /
In four, a <s>kalāpaka</s>. /
In five or more, a <s>kulaka</s>. /
Thus [these are] varieties distinguished by the completion of action — and are enumerated as a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound). /
Even at the completion of a subsidiary action, a <s>paryāyabandha</s> is one that is composed with the purpose of describing something worthy of attention, such as the description of spring. /
A <s>parikathā</s> is one that, aiming at a single human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) such as <s>dharma</s>, narrates various events in diverse modes. /
A <s>khaṇḍakathā</s> is the description of a portion [of a story]. /
A <s>sakalakathā</s> is the description of the events up to the complete fruition. /
Since both are well known in Prakrit, they are enumerated as a <s>dvandva</s>. /
But for the earlier [types] — <s>muktaka</s> etc. — there is no restriction to [any one] language. /
A <s>sargabandha</s>, which has the form of a <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem) and has a <s>puruṣārtha</s> as its fruit, being a composition describing all subject matters — is in Sanskrit only. /
The <s>abhineyārtha</s> (dramatic composition), comprising the ten dramatic forms (<s>daśarūpaka</s>) along with subsidiary elaborations like <s>nāṭikā</s>, <s>troṭaka</s>, <s>rāsaka</s>, <s>prakaraṇikā</s>, etc. — is of a mixed-language form. /
An <s>ākhyāyikā</s> is one equipped with <s>ucchvāsas</s> (chapters) and meters such as <s>vaktra</s> and <s>aparavaktra</s>. /
A <s>kathā</s> is one without those [features]. /
Since both are of the nature of prose composition, they are enumerated as a <s>dvandva</s>. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the <s>campū</s> [is included]. /
As <s>Daṇḍin</s> said: 'A <s>campū</s> is composed of both prose and verse.' /
'Otherwise' — when there is no devotion to the weaving of <s>rasa</s>. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The convention (<s>rūḍhi</s>) has been demonstrated. /
'By that' — the meaning is: even though the convention exists. /
'Is not called a <s>muktaka</s>' — the purport is: because the convention is accepted only when [a verse is] outside a longer composition. /
Since 'composed in Sanskrit, Prakrit, or <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>' is stated with a singular ending, he says — 'of the <s>muktaka</s> alone' etc. /
'A qualifier' — the remainder is: because it is stated with a singular ending. /
But with '<s>sandānitaka</s>' etc., the term should be construed conversely — this is the purport. /
By this, there is no inconsistency with what will be stated: 'but for the earlier [types] — <s>muktaka</s> etc. — there is no restriction to [any one] language.' /
<s>Hemacandra</s> too has said thus: 'these [can] exist in all languages.' /
The definitions of Sanskrit etc. are stated in the <s>Kāvyādarśa</s> and other [works]. /
'Since they arise in sequence' — /
The purport is: since Prakrit arose from Sanskrit, and <s>Apabhraṃśa</s> from that [Prakrit]. /
'In that very [order]' — in the order of Sanskrit etc. /
In 'in three' etc. — the meaning is: since the varieties are distinguished by the completion of action, they have equal importance, and hence [are enumerated] as a <s>dvandva</s>. /
'As a <s>dvandva</s>' — by the [compound beginning with] '<s>sandānitaka</s>' etc. /
'Composed' — bound together. /
'A single [<s>puruṣārtha</s>] such as <s>dharma</s>' — the meaning is: one among the <s>puruṣārthas</s> — <s>dharma</s> etc. /
'Of a portion' — the meaning is: a portion of the well-known events. /
'Having the form of a <s>mahākāvya</s>' — the definitions of <s>mahākāvya</s> etc. are stated in the <s>Kāvyādarśa</s> and other [works]. /
'As a <s>dvandva</s>' — by the <s>dvandva</s> '<s>ākhyāyikā-kathā</s>' etc. /
'By some means accomplished' etc. — the meaning is: having feigned not hearing, through a stratagem. /
'Empty' — empty of companions. /
This verse has been elaborated in the commentary on the <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasaṅgraha</s>. /
'In <s>muktakas</s> with medium or long compounds, poets are seen to be devoted to the weaving of <s>rasa</s>, just as in longer compositions. /
For the <s>muktakas</s> of the poet <s>Amaruka</s>, overflowing with <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> and approaching the nature of a longer composition, are indeed well known. /
But in <s>sandānitakas</s> etc., due to the propriety of elaborate binding, the composition should be in medium or long compounds only. /
In compositions based on longer works, the propriety of the stated type of composition itself must be followed. /
But in the <s>paryāyabandha</s>, the combination should be in uncompounded or medium-compound [style] only. /
Sometimes, based on the propriety of the meaning, even in a combination with long compounds, harsh and vulgar style should be avoided. /
In the <s>parikathā</s>, there is freedom, because in that [genre], since only events are presented, there is no great devotion to the weaving of <s>rasa</s>. /
But in the <s>khaṇḍakathā</s> and <s>sakalakathā</s>, which are well known in Prakrit, since the binding in <s>kulakas</s> etc. predominates, there is no contradiction even in combinations with long compounds. /
But the propriety of style should be followed according to the <s>rasa</s>.

children.translated_text:
For in this verse, the apprehension of the fullness of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. is indeed evident. /
'Elaborate' — /
For in an uncompounded combination, the apprehension, being slow in form, being accompanied by expectancy, pursuing the verb-word that is far off, and resting merely in the apprehension of the expressible — would not be fit for the savoring of the essence of <s>rasa</s> — this is the purport. /
'In those based on longer compositions' — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He substantiates what was said as 'only' — 'in an uncompounded [combination]' etc. /
'In the combination' — the remainder is: when [such a combination] exists. /
'Slow in form' — the meaning is: becoming sluggish. /
'With expectancy' — the meaning is: accompanied by expectancy for the verb etc. /
'Resting in the apprehension of the expressible alone' — the purport is: since the apprehension of the expressible itself arises only after a long time. /
'Would not be' — and thus, to avoid the sluggishness of the apprehension of the expressible, the combination should be in medium or long compounds — this is the purport. /
'In those based on longer compositions' — here, the continuation is from '<s>sandānitaka</s> etc.' only, not from '<s>muktakas</s>' as well — for the <s>muktaka</s> as defined earlier, when its purport is <s>rasa</s>, the propriety according to <s>rasa</s> applies; otherwise there is freedom — since poets following both paths [are seen to compose] in the <s>sargabandha</s> mode, devotion to <s>rasa</s> is preferable. /
But in dramatic compositions, devotion to the weaving of <s>rasa</s> must be maintained in all cases. /
But in the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> and <s>kathā</s>, since prose composition predominates and since prose follows a different path from metrical composition — here the cause of regulation, even if unprecedented, is a matter worthy of consideration.

children.text: etad yathoktam aucityam eva tasyā niyāmakam /
children.translated_text: This very <s>aucitya</s> (propriety), as stated, is the regulator of that [combination]
everywhere, even in prose composition that is free from the constraint of meter. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.8 //

children.translated_text: When the purport is narrative, a <s>sargabandha</s> (canto composition), like <s>Bhaṭṭa Jayantaka's</s> <s>Kādambarīkathāsāra</s>.
The orientation toward <s>rasa</s> is as in the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> etc.
But others explain: 'of both' refers to both Sanskrit and Prakrit.

children.text: tatra tu rasatātparyaṃ sādhīya iti yaduktaṃ tatkimapekṣayeti neyārthaṃ syāt // 7 //
children.translated_text: But therein, the statement that 'the orientation toward <s>rasa</s> is stronger' — with reference to what? — this would be a matter requiring interpretation. // 7 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] This <s>aucitya</s> pertaining to the speaker and subject matter, which has been stated as the regulator of combination — this very [<s>aucitya</s>] is the cause of regulation even in prose, which is free from the constraint of meter, with reference to the domain. /
For thus, here too, when the speaker is a poet or one whose speech is composed by a poet, and is devoid of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s> — then there is freedom [of choice]. /
But when the speaker is endowed with <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>, what was stated earlier must be followed. /
And even there, the <s>aucitya</s> of the domain [applies]. /
In the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> — [<s>Locana</s>:] In <s>sandānitakas</s> etc. up to <s>kulakas</s>. /
Or alternatively, let the <s>muktaka</s> exist even within a longer composition; for that which enables the savoring of <s>rasa</s> even without reference to what precedes and follows — that alone is a <s>muktaka</s>. /
As for example — the verse beginning with 'having depicted you angry from love' etc. /
'Sometimes' — in the domain of <s>raudra</s> (the furious) etc. /
'Not greatly' — since the devotion to the weaving of <s>rasa</s> is not extreme — this is the connection. /
'Propriety of style' — the propriety of styles — <s>paruṣa</s> (harsh), <s>upanāgarika</s> (refined), <s>grāmya</s> (vulgar) — according to the [type of] composition and according to the <s>rasa</s>. /
'Otherwise' — when the purport is merely the narrative, even regarding styles there is freedom. /
'In both' — this is a locative.

children.text:
bālapriyā prabandheṣvasambhavādityāha---sandānitakādiṣvityādi /
pakṣāntaramāha---yadi vetyādi /
nanu tarhi kiṃ muktakalakṣaṇamityata āha--pūrvetyādi /
nātyantamityādyekaṃ padam /
rasabandhe 'bhiniveśo rasabandhābhiniveśaḥ atyantaṃ rasabandhābhiniveśo yastasyābhāvaḥ /
nātyantaṃrasabandhābhiniveśastasmādityartha ityabhiprāyeṇa vyācaṣṭe---rasabandha ityādi /
atyantaṃ rasabandhānabhiniveśāditi ca vṛttau pāṭhaḥ /
dvayorapi mārgayoriti saptamyante /

children.translated_text: 'Of the orientation' — is the remainder.
The meaning is 'of the orientation toward narrative' and 'of the orientation toward <s>rasa</s>' — she says: 'of both' etc.
She states another interpretation of 'of both paths': 'others' etc.
She refutes that: 'therein' etc. // 7 //

[Bālapriyā:] Since [this] is impossible in extended compositions — he says: 'in <s>sandānitaka</s> (linked compositions) etc.' /
He states an alternative position: 'or alternatively' etc. /
'But then what is the definition of <s>muktaka</s> (standalone verse)?' — to this he says: 'the former' etc. /
'Not excessively' etc. is one compound word. /
'Devotion to <s>rasa</s>-composition' — excessive devotion to <s>rasa</s>-composition — the absence of that. /
'Not excessive devotion to <s>rasa</s>-composition, therefore' — with this intention she explains: '<s>rasabandha</s>' etc. /
'From the absence of excessive devotion to <s>rasa</s>-composition' — this is also a reading in the <s>vṛtti</s>. /
'Of both paths' — in the locative case.

children.text:
tu bhūmnā madhyamasamāsādīrghasamāse eva saṅghaṭane /
gadyasya vikaṭabandhāśrayeṇa chāyāvattvāt /
tatra ca tasya prakṛṣyamāṇatvāt /
kathāyāṃ tu vikaṭabandhaprācurye 'pi gadyasya rasabandhoktamaucityamanusartavyam /
children.translated_text:
[Vṛtti:] But predominantly, [the composition involves] the moderate-compound to long-compound type of arrangement. /
Because prose has the nature of <s>chāyā</s> (shadow/rendering) through its resort to the <s>vikaṭabandha</s> (elaborate/intricate composition). /
And therein, because of its being especially prominent. /
But in narrative, even though the <s>vikaṭabandha</s> is abundant in prose, the propriety stated for <s>rasa</s>-composition should be followed.
The propriety stated in <s>rasa</s>-composition shines everywhere; the composition that has taken resort [to that propriety] —

children.text: racanā viṣayāpekṣaṃ tat tu kiṃcid vibhedavat // DhvK_3.9 //
children.translated_text: that, however, admits of some variation with respect to the subject-matter. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.9 //
The propriety stated in <s>rasa</s>-composition shines everywhere; the composition that has taken resort [to that propriety] —
that, however, admits of some variation with respect to the subject-matter. // 9 //

children.text: athavā padyavadgadyabandhe 'pi rasabandhoktamaucityaṃ sarvatra saṃśritā racanā locanam viṣayāpekṣamiti /
children.translated_text: [Vṛtti:] Or alternatively, even in prose composition as in verse, the composition that has everywhere taken resort to the propriety stated for <s>rasa</s>-composition — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'with respect to the subject-matter' — thus.
The varieties of prose composition themselves should be accepted as the domain. // 8 //
He shows the established position: 'the propriety stated in <s>rasa</s>-composition' etc.
And in the <s>vṛtti</s>, the word '<s>vā</s>' (or/alternatively) is an indicator of the established status of precisely this position.
For example: 'Women, kings, fire, and poison — when resorted to with prudence —
are either for one's own benefit, or else solely for the accumulation of suffering.' //
Thus.
'<s>Racanā</s>' means <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> (composition).

children.text: tarhi viṣayaucityaṃ sarvathaiva tyaktaṃ netyāha---tadena rasaucityaṃ viṣayaṃ sahakāritayāpekṣya kiñjidvibhedo 'vantaravaicitryaṃ vidyate yasya sampādyatvena tādṛśaṃ bālapriyā viṣayatveneti /
children.translated_text: 'Then has the propriety with respect to subject-matter been entirely abandoned?' — 'No,' he says. 'That very <s>rasa</s>-propriety, in dependence on the subject-matter as a cooperating factor, admits of some variation — inner diversity — that exists as something to be accomplished — of such a kind.' [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'As subject-matter' —
The meaning is: in the capacity of being the meaning of the word 'subject-matter.' // 8 //

children.text:
'rasabandhe'ti kārikāyāṃ racanā sarvatra rasabandhoktamaucityaṃ saṃśritā bhātītyanvayaḥ /
vṛttau 'athave'ti na vikalpārthaka ityāha---vṛttau ca vāśabda iti /
cakāro vākyālaṅkāre /
vāśabda iti /
athavetyatra vāśabda ityarthaḥ /
asyeti /

sthitidyotaka iti /
niścitatvarūpasthitatvadyotaka ityarthaḥ /
sammatatvadyotaka iti yāvat /
athavetyādinā pakṣāntarakathane khalu śāstrakārāṇāṃ nirbharaḥ /
uktārthe mahākaviprayogamupaṣṭambhakatayā darśayati - striya iti /
yuktyā niṣevitaṃ stryādicatuṣṭayaṃ svārthasya svaprayojanāya bhavata /
itthaṃ prasiddhyanurodhenoktvā svamatamāha---yadi vetyādi /
yuktyānyathā vā niṣevitaṃ taccatuṣṭayaṃ kevalaṃ duḥkhasambhārāya duḥkhātiśayāyaiva bhavati /
atra yadiveti duḥkhasambhārāyaiveti sathitapakṣadyotakam /
"viṣapyamṛtaṃ kvacidbhavedabhṛtaṃ vā viṣamīśvarecchaye"ti raghuvaṃśaślokavyākhyāne "vāśabdo vākyārthasya sthitapakṣatāṃ dyotayatī"tyaruṇācalanāthāḥ /
kārikāṃ vyacaṣṭe--racanetyādi /
tarhīti /

rasabandhoktaucityamityarthaḥ /

bhavati /
tattu viṣayāpekṣaṃ kiñjidvaśeṣavadbhavati, na tu sarvākāram /
tathā hi gadyavandhe 'pyatidīrghasamāsā racanā na vipralambhaśṛṅgārakaruṇayorākhyāyikāyāmapi śobhate /
nāṭakādāvapyasamāsaiva na raudravīrādivarṇane /
viṣayāpekṣaṃ tvaucityaṃ pramāṇato 'pakṛṣyate prakṛṣyate ca /
tathā hyākhyāyikāyāṃ nātyantamasamāsā svaviṣaye 'pi nāṭakādau nātidīrghasamāsā ceti saṅghaṭanāyā diganusartavyā /
idānīmalakṣyakramavyaṅgyo dhvaniḥ prabandhātmā rāmāyaṇamahābhāratādau locanam bhavati /
etadvyācaṣṭe - tattviti /
sarvākāramiti kriyāviśeṣaṇam /
asamāsaiveti /
sarvatraiveti śeṣaḥ /
tathā hi vākyābhinayalakṣaṇe 'cūrṇapādaiḥ prasannaiḥ' ityādi munirabhyadhāt /
children.translated_text: For thus, in the [rules concerning] sentence-acting (<s>vākyābhinaya</s>), the sage (<s>Bharata</s>) declared: 'with clear, uncompounded phrases' etc.
Here he states the exception: 'not' etc.
'In a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc.' — thus.
'Even in its own domain' — is the connection. // 9 //

In the <s>kārikā</s> '<s>rasabandhe</s>' (in <s>rasa</s>-composition), the construal is: the composition (<s>racanā</s>) that has everywhere taken resort to the propriety stated in <s>rasa</s>-composition shines. /
The word '<s>vā</s>' (or) in the <s>vṛtti</s> with '<s>athavā</s>' (or alternatively) is not in the sense of an alternative — she says: 'in the <s>vṛtti</s>, the word <s>vā</s>' etc. /
The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) is a sentential <s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
'The word <s>vā</s>' — /
The meaning is: the word '<s>vā</s>' in '<s>athavā</s>.' /
'Of this' — /
The meaning is: of [the position] that will be stated beginning with '<s>padyavat</s>' (as in verse). /
'Indicator of established status' — /
The meaning is: an indicator of established status in the form of certainty. /
The meaning is: an indicator of being accepted. /
The treatise-authors' practice in stating alternative positions through '<s>athavā</s>' etc. is indeed well known. /
He shows the usage of a great poet to corroborate the stated meaning: '<s>striyaḥ</s>' (women) etc. /
'Resorted to with prudence' — the quartet of women etc. serves one's own purpose, one's own benefit. /
Having thus stated [the view] in accordance with common understanding, he states his own view: 'or alternatively' etc. /
'Resorted to with prudence or otherwise' — that quartet solely for the accumulation of suffering, for the excess of suffering. /
Here, '<s>yadi vā</s>' (or alternatively) and '<s>duḥkhasambhārāyaiva</s>' (solely for the accumulation of suffering) are indicators of the established position. /
'<s>Viṣam apy amṛtaṃ kvacid bhaved amṛtaṃ vā viṣam īśvarecchayā</s>' (Poison may sometimes become nectar, or nectar become poison, by the will of the Lord) — in the commentary on this <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> verse, <s>Aruṇācalanātha</s> [states]: 'the word <s>vā</s> indicates the established position of the sentence-meaning.' /
She explains the <s>kārikā</s>: '<s>racanā</s>' etc. /
'Then' — /
The meaning is: when the composition's resorting to the propriety stated in <s>rasa</s>-composition in every case is accepted. /
'Abandoned' — /
'Has it been entirely abandoned?' — this is the objection. /
'No, he says' — /
The meaning is: he replies 'not abandoned.' /
The explanation of 'that' is: 'that very' etc. /
He states the referent of 'that': '<s>rasa</s>-propriety' etc. /
The meaning is: the propriety stated in <s>rasa</s>-composition. /
The elaboration of 'with respect to the subject-matter' — 'the subject-matter' etc. /
So it is. /
'That, however, admits of some variation with respect to the subject-matter' — it is not in every way [so]. /
For thus: even in prose composition, an excessively long-compound arrangement does not look good in <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation) and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos), even in an <s>ākhyāyikā</s> (novel/romance). /
Even in a <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) etc., complete absence of compounds is not [appropriate] in the depiction of <s>raudra</s> (fury), <s>vīra</s> (heroism), and such [<s>rasas</s>]. /
But propriety with respect to subject-matter is diminished or augmented in relation to the standard. /
For thus: in an <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, even in its own domain, not excessively without compounds; in a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc., not with excessively long compounds — this is the direction to be followed regarding <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>. /
Now, the <s>alakṣyakramavyaṅgya-dhvani</s> (imperceptible-sequence suggestion) in the form of an extended composition shines in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Mahābhārata</s>, and other works. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] He explains 'that': '<s>tat</s>' etc. /
'In every way' is a qualification of the verb. /
'Without compounds' — /
'In every case' is the remainder.

children.translated_text: 'In a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc.' — thus.
'Even in its own domain' — is the continuation.
The meaning is: the arrangement with excessively long compounds does not look good. // 9 //

children.text: "itīkāvyārthe"tyādiślekaḥ kvacidgranthe na dṛśyate, ata eva na vyākhyātaḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: The verse '<s>iti kāvyārthe</s>' etc. is not seen in some manuscripts; therefore it was not commented upon. // 9 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] She introduces [the passage]: 'thus' etc. /
'The procedure' — the meaning is: the manner. /
'Is worthy of examination' — worthy of analysis. /
She shows the referent of '<s>tat</s>' in the connection 'now that is being demonstrated': 'now' etc. /
'First, to begin with' — this is a quotation of the lemma. /
She shows the basis for the order of exposition — '<s>vibhāva</s>' etc.: 'of the composition' etc. /
'The bringing to the conclusion of the fruit' — /
Of the narrative — it is well known and manifest. /
But how it is illuminated — that is being demonstrated.

children.text:
locane 'vatārayati---evamityādi /
yetikartavyateti /
yaḥ prakāra ityarthaḥ /
nirūpyā nirūpaṇārhā /

prathamantāvaditīti pratīkadhāraṇam /

kathāyā iti prakāśamānaḥ prasiddha eva /
tasya tu yathā prakāśanaṃ tatpratipādyate---
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Locana</s>, she introduces: 'thus' etc. /
'The procedure' — the meaning is: what manner. /
'Worthy of examination' — worthy of analysis. /
She shows the referent of '<s>tat</s>' in the connection 'now that is being demonstrated': 'now' etc. /
'First, to begin with' — this is a quotation of the lemma. /
She shows the basis for the order of exposition beginning with '<s>vibhāva</s>' etc.: 'of the composition' etc. /
'The bringing to the conclusion of the fruit' — /
Of the narrative — it is well known and manifest. /
But how it is illuminated — that is being demonstrated.
The method of beautifying through propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and <s>sañcārins</s> (transitory states) —
is the rule for the narrative body, whether based on historical events or on poetic imagination. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.10 //
Abandoning the succession that comes from adherence to historical events when it is incongruent —
one should, through imagination, interweave a narrative elevation suited to the desired <s>rasa</s>. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.11 //
The construction of junctures (<s>sandhi</s>) and juncture-components (<s>sandhyaṅga</s>) should be in consideration of <s>rasa</s>-manifestation,
not merely through the desire to fulfill the prescribed rules of the treatise. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.12 //
The stimulation and subsidence, as occasion demands, in between —
is the tracking of the principal <s>rasa</s> whose repose has begun. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.13 //
The fitting employment of <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures), even when they are capable [of being used] —
is the basis for the composition's suggestive capacity regarding <s>rasas</s> and others. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.14 //
The method of beautifying through propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>bhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>sañcārins</s> —
is the rule for the narrative body, whether based on historical events or on poetic imagination. // 10 //
Abandoning the succession that comes from adherence to historical events when it is incongruent —
one should, through imagination, interweave a narrative elevation suited to the desired <s>rasa</s>. // 11 //
The construction of junctures and juncture-components should be in consideration of <s>rasa</s>-manifestation,
not merely through the desire to fulfill the prescribed rules of the treatise. // 12 //
The stimulation and subsidence, as occasion demands, in between —
is the tracking of the principal <s>rasa</s> whose repose has begun. // 13 //
The fitting employment of <s>alaṅkāras</s>, even when they are capable [of being used] —
is the basis for the composition's suggestive capacity regarding <s>rasas</s> and others. // 14 //

children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] And even more so when the narrative body (<s>kathāśarīra</s>) is invented by the poet himself from [mere] tradition (<s>vṛtta</s>), one must be especially diligent.
For therein, when the poet stumbles through inattention, the suspicion of lack of learning (<s>avyutpatti</s>) becomes very great.
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] And the supporting verse (<s>parikara-śloka</s>) here [is]: 'Having created the narrative body (<s>kathāśarīra</s>), the subject-matter should be fashioned in such a way
that everything shines forth as entirely pervaded by <s>rasa</s>.' //

It has been said that the extended composition (<s>prabandha</s>) too is a suggestor of <s>rasas</s> etc. — the basis for its suggestive capacity [is as follows]. /
Firstly, the construction of the story-body (<s>kathā-śarīra</s>) with its charm of propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) regarding <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and <s>sañcārins</s> (transitory emotions) — as appropriate to the <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc. intended to be conveyed — whichever <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, or <s>sañcārin</s> is suitable, the construction of the story-body with the charm of their propriety — this is the first basis for suggestive capacity. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Alertness toward <s>rasa</s>, and in the description of the appropriate <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., the propriety of <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures). /
He explains the fivefold [basis] in that order — by 'of <s>vibhāvas</s>' etc. /
'Their propriety' — one who wishes to describe <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic <s>rasa</s>) must resort to such a story in which [there appear] <s>vibhāvas</s> such as the spring season, garlands, etc., and <s>anubhāvas</s> such as amorous play (<s>līlā</s>) etc. — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the remainder [is to be supplied]. /
'The fivefold' — the first four are stated in order by four verses; but the fifth is [stated] by a half-verse — this should be understood. /
He elaborates 'the construction of the story-body with the charm of the propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc.' with reference to a particular <s>rasa</s> — 'in the description of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, kissing' etc. /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] '<s>Prakṛti</s>' (nature) etc. — '<s>prakṛti</s>' means inherent nature. /
'Divine' etc. — divine, human, divine-human, subterranean, etc. — the meaning is: of many kinds. /
Therein, the divine nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) is the state of being exclusively of immortal form, as in the case of Lord <s>Maheśvara</s> etc. /
The human is the state of being exclusively of mortal form, as in the case of <s>Mādhava</s> etc. /
The divine-human should be understood [as in the case] of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> etc. /
'That' — the meaning is: the nature (<s>prakṛti</s>). /
'Unmixed' — unmixed with another <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion). /
There is also the reading '<s>aucityabhāga</s>' (the portion of propriety). /
In some texts, after 'occurs,' there is also the reading 'not otherwise.' /
'Otherwise' etc. — 'otherwise' means by transgressing the stated manner. /
The construction is: when the enthusiasm etc. of a divine [character] is composed with an exclusively human locus, or when the enthusiasm etc. of an exclusively human [character] is composed with an exclusively divine locus. /
'And thus' — the meaning is: 'for thus.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Its domain' — the meaning is: pertaining to the domain of activity. /
'This' — the meaning is: the word 'activity.' /
Asking 'why?' — he says: 'the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion)' etc. /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] There is also the reading '<s>bhānti</s>' or '<s>bhavanti</s>.' /
And therefore in <s>Bharata</s>'s [<s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s>], the requirement that a <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) must have a well-known subject-matter and a well-known, noble hero has been presented as mandatory. /
For thereby, the poet does not become confused regarding the propriety or impropriety of the hero's [character]. /
But one who would compose a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc. with an invented subject-matter — for him there would be a great risk of error in describing the nature of an unfamiliar, improper hero. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] What is said amounts to this: that which is to be described should be of such a kind that the conviction of the audience is not shattered. /
For when, in the case of an exclusively human [character], the leaping across seven oceans in a single step is depicted as impossible and therefore false — this, flashing in the heart, instills in the mind a sense of falsity even in the instruction on the four aims of life (<s>caturvarga</s>) that is [also] to be imparted. /
But in the case of <s>Rāma</s> etc., even such exploits, being mounted upon the accumulated trust of a succession of prior traditions, do not flash forth as false. /
And therefore, even when extraordinary power is poetically fancied in [<s>Rāma</s>'s] case, it is of just that kind [i.e., credible]. /
But one should not describe [a character] that falls into the domain of the inconceivable. /
'For thereby' — because of having a well-known, noble hero as the subject-matter. /
'Becomes confused' — [wondering] 'what should I describe?' /
'But one who' — the poet. /
'A great risk of error' — therefore, one should not compose a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc. with an invented subject — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] she raises an objection — 'but' etc. /
'In the serpent-world' — there is also the reading '<s>nākaloka</s>' (the celestial world). /
'Therefore' — the meaning is: for that reason. /
The connection of '<s>kṣamābhujām</s>' (of the earth-bearing kings) is with 'in the description.' /
'<s>Kim</s>' (what/why) — in the sense of a question or a prohibition. /
He resolves — 'this is not' etc. /
'This is not the case' — this objection does not hold. /
Asking 'why?' — he says: 'not' etc. /
The connection is: we do not say that both types of description of the excess of kings' prowess are improper. /
He states the essential meaning of the passage 'but that which is distinct' etc. — in the <s>Locana</s>: 'what is said' etc. /
'Wherever' — the meaning is: in whatever character is being described. /
'Shattering of conviction' — the non-establishment of conviction. /
'Of an exclusively human [character]' — 'being described' is the remainder. /
'The leaping across seven oceans' — the subject [of the verb]; 'instills' — this is the syntactic connection. /
'As untrue' — the meaning is: as false. /
He states a distinction — 'but of <s>Rāma</s> etc.' /
'Of such a kind' — the meaning is: of the form of ocean-leaping etc. /
'Prior traditions' — ancient, prior — the succession of traditions — the trust accumulated by them — mounted upon that — this contains an implicit reason. /
'Even of him' — even of <s>Rāma</s> etc. /
'Is poetically fancied' — is described with imaginative invention. /
'Of just that kind' — would indeed flash forth as false. /
He states the ultimate purport — 'but one should not' etc. /
'Falling into the domain of the inconceivable' — the meaning is: that which becomes the object of the cognition of inconceivability. /
He states the form of the confusion — 'what' etc. /
Since the sage [<s>Bharata</s>] has not stipulated that the subject-matter of a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc. must be invented — with the literal reading 'a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc. with invented subject-matter' being incongruous — [understanding:] one who would compose [a work] that, being of invented subject-matter, [is nonetheless called] a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc. — for him there would be a great risk of error — keeping this construction in mind, she elaborates the purport: 'thereby' etc. /
'Thereby' — by the occasion, i.e., the reason, of the great risk of error for the poet. /
By the sage, a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc. — but if some kind of examination of propriety regarding divine, human, etc. [natures] is made in the description of emotions such as enthusiasm, let it be made — but what purpose does it serve for <s>rati</s> (love) etc.? For <s>rati</s> is conducted with the conventions of <s>Bhārata-varṣa</s> (the Indian subcontinent) alone, even in the description of divine [characters] — this is the established [view]. /
Not so; for there, through transgression of propriety, a fault would arise for the divine [characters]. /
For thus, when the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> of a character of noble nature (<s>uttama-prakṛti</s>) is composed with the propriety of a character of base nature (<s>adhama-prakṛti</s>) — what would not be laughable? /
The threefold propriety of nature exists even in <s>Bhārata-varṣa</s> with regard to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
But the divine propriety is irrelevant there — if [you say] so: we do not speak of any other divine propriety specific to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
Rather, what [we mean is:] just as in the domain of <s>Bhārata-varṣa</s>, the composition of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> with noble heroes such as kings is [done appropriately], so too [such composition] with a divine locus is beautiful. /
And the composition of well-known vulgar <s>śṛṅgāra</s> associated with well-known [characters] such as kings is not well-known in <s>nāṭakas</s> etc.; in the same way, it should be avoided for divine [characters]. /
Because a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc. has a definite meaning [to convey], and because the enactment of <s>sambhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-union) is indecent — the avoidance there [is justified] — if [you say] so: no; for if the enactment of such a subject is indecent, then by what [reasoning] is the indecency of such a subject in poetry to be prevented? Therefore, whether in poetry intended for enactment or not intended for enactment, the description of vulgar union between a hero of noble nature such as a king and heroines of noble nature — that is supremely indecent, like the description of the union of one's own parents. /
Likewise with respect to noble deities etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'By the sage has been stipulated' — the purport is: it should not be done. /
The word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.) is in the sense of 'similar type,' for the inclusion of well-known divine characters beginning with <s>Hima</s> (?). /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The syntactic connection is: '[a work] being of invented subject-matter has not been stipulated [by the sage].' /
'<s>Iti</s>' is in the causal sense. /
'Should not be done' — the meaning is: a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc. should not be composed by the poet as having invented subject-matter. /
She elaborates the word '<s>ādi</s>' in '<s>nāṭakādi</s>' — 'in the sense of similar type' etc. /
'In the sense of similar type' — in the sense of similarity; and that should be understood as similarity with respect to having well-known subject-matter. /
The connection with the word '<s>ḍimādi</s>' etc. should be grasped. /
'The <s>nāṭaka</s> has well-known subject-matter and a well-known, noble hero' — this is the definition of the <s>ḍima</s> [type of drama]. /
'The <s>vyāyoga</s> should be composed by those who know the rules, with a well-known hero as its body' etc. — this is the definition of the <s>vyāyoga</s> [type of drama], stated in the <s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s> etc. /
Someone says: since in '<s>nāṭakādi</s>,' the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound (with the derivation '<s>nāṭakam ādiḥ yasya</s>') is a <s>tadguṇasaṃvijñāna-bahuvrīhi</s> (attributive compound signifying the [qualities of the] first [member]), the word '<s>nāṭakādi</s>' is intended to denote the genre [beginning with <s>nāṭaka</s>] — therefore there is no impossibility of the literal meaning — he states that view: 'another [says]' etc. /
Nor is vulgar lovemaking the only mode of <s>sambhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-union) — for there are also other varieties such as the mutual display of love etc. — why should these not be described in the context of a hero of noble nature? Therefore, as with enthusiasm, propriety of nature must be followed even with respect to <s>rati</s> (love). /
Likewise with wonder etc. /
But the fact that even in the works of great poets, lack of due consideration in such subject-matter is observed in the [poetic] examples — that is indeed a fault. /
But it is not perceived in their case because it is concealed by [their poetic] power — this has already been stated. /
And the propriety of <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) is well known from <s>Bharata</s> etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Another [says]' — [who maintains:] 'the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> as stated is merely synecdochic' — he says [this] pertaining only to the genre. /
There is also the reading '<s>nāṭikādi</s>' (beginning with <s>nāṭikā</s>). /
Therein, the word '<s>ādi</s>' indicates the genre; thereby, in the definition of <s>nāṭikā</s> as stipulated by the sage — 'the subject-matter is to be invented from the conventions of <s>prakaraṇa</s> and <s>nāṭaka</s>, the hero is a king' — here, through the principle of respective correspondence, the well-known, noble, kingly hero should be understood — this is the purport. /
Asking 'how then should <s>sambhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-union) be composed by the poet?' — he says: 'nor' etc. /
'Likewise' — by the sage too, in place after place, the propriety of nature with regard to <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, etc. has been extensively taken as authoritative — as stated in 'with steadfastness for the noble, middling, and base [characters]; with agitation for the lowly' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'The <s>bahuvrīhi</s> as stated is synecdochic' — the meaning is: the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> '<s>nāṭakādi</s>' is one that [indirectly] designates another [genre]. /
'<s>Iti</s>' is in the causal sense. /
He states [it] in another manner — '<s>nāṭikādi</s>' etc. /
'Indicating the genre' — conveying similarity. /
Similarity should be understood as [referring to similarity] with respect to having invented subject-matter; and <s>prakaraṇa</s> etc. should be grasped by the word '<s>ādi</s>' — this is the purport. /
'Thereby' — the meaning is: by the statement that the <s>nāṭikā</s> etc. has invented subject-matter. /
That is to say: only the subject-matter is invented. /
'Should be understood' — the purport is: the invention does not apply to the hero. /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] 'But' etc. /
'Divine' — divine and human, and the propriety that begins with that (<s>aucitya</s>) — its examination. /
The connection is: 'if it is done.' /
'That' — then. /
'By that' — by the examination of propriety regarding divine, human, etc. /
'There' — the meaning is: with regard to <s>rati</s> etc. /
He raises the objection again — 'but that which' etc. /
He resolves — 'not' etc. /
'Even with divine locus' — '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>-composition' carries over. /
'Nor' — 'in <s>nāṭakas</s> etc., among kings etc., it is not well-known' — this is the syntactic connection. /
'Well-known' — the meaning is: well-known as belonging to base characters. /
'That' — the meaning is: the composition of vulgar <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
He raises an objection — 'because a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc.' /
'There' — the meaning is: in a <s>nāṭaka</s> etc. /
'Indecency of such a subject' — the meaning is: the indecency of the subject of <s>sambhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-union). /
'That [indecency]' — the meaning is: the indecency. /
She introduces the passage 'nor is [vulgar lovemaking] the only [mode of <s>sambhoga-śṛṅgāra</s>]' etc. — in the <s>Locana</s>: 'how then' etc. /
For [the passage] 'likewise with wonder etc.' she cites the authority — 'by the sage too' etc. /
'With steadfastness' etc. — only this much is said: by a poet who follows the established [practice] laid down by <s>Bharata</s> and others, who reflects upon the compositions of the great poets, and who follows his own creative intuition — being of composed mind — the utmost effort must be made to avoid the violation of propriety regarding <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. /
The adoption of the story-body — whether taken from tradition or imagined — that possesses propriety is the suggestor — by this, this [principle] is conveyed: among the various stories rich in <s>rasa</s> found in the <s>itihāsas</s> etc., that story-body which possesses propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. alone is to be adopted, not the other.

locanam ityattviti /
lakṣṇajñatvaṃ lakṣyapariśīlanamadṛṣṭaprasādoditasvapratibhāśālitvaṃ cānusartavyamiti saṃkṣepaḥ /
