children.translated_text: For without propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc., what sort of <s>rasavatva</s> (possession of <s>rasa</s>) [could there be]?
'Of the poet' —
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] [The following is found in <s>Bharata</s>:] 'In women and persons of low nature, grief born from misfortune [is expressed through] lamentation;
in persons of the highest and middle [rank], through fortitude; and in those of low [rank], through weeping.' //

[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Thus indeed' — /
In summary: knowledge of definitions (<s>lakṣaṇajñatva</s>), practice with exemplary works (<s>lakṣyapariśīlana</s>), and the possession of one's own creative genius (<s>svapratibhā</s>) arising from the grace of the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) — these are to be cultivated. /
'Among those possessed of <s>rasa</s>' — the seventh [case] is in the sense of disregard (<s>anādara</s>). /
And the status of being possessed of <s>rasa</s> (<s>rasavatva</s>) should be understood according to the notion held by undiscriminating people.

children.translated_text: the savoring alone is the aim; and the means for that [is] the proper following of propriety in <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc.
And that has already been demonstrated.

children.text: kiñca---- santi siddharasaprakhyā ye ca rāmāyaṇādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover: 'There exist [works] such as the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> and others, which are renowned for their established <s>rasa</s>,
which are based on narrative — one's own fancy (<s>svecchā</s>) that is opposed to <s>rasa</s> should not be conjoined with those.' //

Thus the reading in the <s>Bhāvādhyāya</s> (Chapter on Emotions). /
Here, the word '<s>abhineya</s>' (to be enacted) is to be understood as carrying over. /
He states the meaning obtained from the three instrumental-ending words in '<s>Bharata</s> and others' composition, established practice, and the one who follows' — 'knowledge of definitions' etc. /
'The unseen' — <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is merit (<s>sukṛta</s>); '<s>prasāda</s>' (grace) is the grace of deities etc.; '<s>svapratibhā</s>' (one's own creative genius) that has arisen from both of these — the possession of that — this is the meaning. /
'In the sense of disregard' — even though there exist various narratives possessed of <s>rasa</s> among the <s>Itihāsas</s> and other [sources], disregarding those narratives, from among them, only that narrative body which possesses propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) should be adopted by the poet — not another [narrative body] that is devoid of propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc.; even if possessed of <s>rasa</s>, [such a] narrative body should not be adopted — this is the meaning of the <s>vṛtti</s> — this is the purport. /
But if there is an absence of propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., how can there be <s>rasavatva</s> (possession of <s>rasa</s>)? — to this he says: 'And <s>rasavatva</s>' etc. /
'Undiscriminating' etc. — the meaning is: according to the opinion of undiscriminating people, i.e., their notion of <s>rasavatva</s> — this should be understood in that sense. /
Here he states the reason — 'propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s>' etc. /
He elaborates on what was said — 'the suspicion of lack of learning becomes very great' — 'for not' etc. /
'Therein' — the meaning is: in a narrative body invented by oneself. /
'An evasive answer' (<s>jātyuttara</s>) — the meaning is: an improper answer. /
The connection of 'therein' is: even an evasive answer is not possible. /
He elaborates on 'there exist' etc. — 'established' etc. /
'Savoring' —

children.text: prārambhādīnāmmukhādisandhīnāṃ locanam tasyānupūrvyā virjñayāḥ pañcāvasthāḥ prayoktṛbhiḥ //
children.translated_text: [Vṛtti:] The five stages of the junctures beginning with prārambha (commencement) — corresponding to mukha (opening) etc. — [Locana:] by the practitioners are to be known through that sequence. //

[Locana:] For in those story-bases, first of all, one's own fancy (svecchā) should not be applied. / As has been stated: 'In the path of a story, not even the slightest deviation [is permissible].' / Even if one's own fancy is to be applied, it should not be applied in a manner opposed to rasa. / This is another foundation for the suggestive capacity of extended narratives (prabandha) with respect to rasa: / having abandoned a situation that comes about through the course of events and is somehow unconducive to rasa, one should, even by imagining anew, arrange the elevation of a story suitable to the desired rasa in between — as in Kālidāsa's extended compositions. / And as in [the work] composed by Sarvasena — [Locana:] For therein, a generic reply (jātyuttara) is also possible: 'it was not bound by me according to the force of the itihāsa alone.' / 'And therein' — / In accomplishing the pervasion by rasa. / 'Established' — / Those in which the rasa is established, i.e., whose only remainder is the savoring — not [a rasa that] needs to be produced [through description]. / The substrates (āśrayas) of stories are the itihāsas (epics/histories); with those itihāsa-meanings, with them, one's own fancy should not be combined. / And the meaning of 'with' (saha) here is the relation of object and perceiver — he explains: by the locative 'in those.' / One's own fancy should not be applied in those; or if somehow it is applied, it should not be applied in a manner opposed to the rasa well-known [in connection with those stories]. / For example, if someone were to make Rāma the hero of a nāṭikā by attributing to him the dhīralalita (gallant-graceful) type — that would be entirely inappropriate. / 'As has been stated' — / In the Rāmābhyudaya by Yaśovarman: 'Established as if on a couch.' / 'Kālidāsa' — / In the Raghuvaṃśa, the description of marriages etc. of kings such as Aja and others is not established in the itihāsas. / In the Harivijaya, the Pārijāta-seizure and such [episodes] have been depicted as ancillary to pleasing the beloved — even though not seen in the itihāsas. / Similarly, in the Arjunacarita, Arjuna's conquest of the netherworld etc. — [Bālapriyā:] that whose remaining portion is the savoring by the sensitive reader alone. / She states what is to be excluded by the word 'mātra' (only): 'not, however' etc. / 'To be produced' — to be accomplished through description. / Those which have established rasa and which are famous — the siddharasaprakhyā — which serve as story-bases, such as the Rāmāyaṇa etc. — this is the connection. / Therein, she explains the word 'kathāśraya' (story-base): 'of stories' etc. / She explains 'taiḥ' (with those): 'with the itihāsa-meanings.' / With the intent that 'na taiḥ' (not with those) culminates in two sentences — [the vṛtti is] explained as 'in those' etc.; there, 'taiḥ' (by those) means 'teṣu' (in those). / 'How is this derived?' — she introduces that passage: 'taiḥ' etc. / 'Teṣu' is a locative. / The purport is: this locative expresses a domain-substrate relation. / 'Svecchā' — / The meaning is: meanings fabricated by one's own fancy. / 'In those' — / The meaning is: in the story-bases that are famous for established rasa. / 'As [in the case of] Rāma' — / The purport is: for his rasa as well-known from the Rāmāyaṇa is the heroic (vīra). / In the vṛtti, 'not even the slightest deviation' — / The meaning is: not even the slightest deviation should be made. / 'In the narrated events' etc. — / 'Somehow unconducive to rasa' — by some means; in the Harivijaya. / 'And as in my own Arjunacarita, the mahākāvya.' / The poet, while composing a kāvya, must be entirely subservient to rasa. / Therein, in the narrated events, if he sees a situation unconducive to rasa, he should, even by breaking that, independently generate another story-development that is conducive to rasa. / For the poet has no purpose in merely carrying out the narrative of events, since that is already accomplished by the itihāsa itself. / This is another principal foundation for the suggestive capacity of extended narrative with respect to rasa — namely, the arrangement of the junctures (sandhis) — those called mukha (opening), pratimukha (progression), garbha (development), avamarśa (pause), and nirvahaṇa (denouement) — and of their components such as upakṣepa (suggestion) etc. — [Locana:] what is described but not well-known in the itihāsa. / He says that this alone is appropriate: 'the poet' etc. / 'Of the junctures' — / Here, from those śāstras that are like a master — the Śrutis, Smṛtis, etc. — whose sole purpose is the injunction 'this must be done' — those who have not gained learning [from these]; nor also from those śāstras that are like a friend — the itihāsa-śāstras — which reveal the connection of action and fruit based on reasoning, as in 'this person did this deed, and this fruit arose from it' — those who have gained learning [from these]; but who must nevertheless be instructed — those who are endowed with competence for accomplishing the welfare of the subjects, like princes — for them, learning about the means of the four aims of life (caturvarga) is to be imparted through entering their hearts. / And entering the heart is entirely in the form of rasa-savoring. / And that rasa is obtained through the grace of the conjunction of vibhāvas (determinants) etc. that are appropriate to the four aims, which are inseparable [from the rasa] — thus, in the composition of vibhāvas etc. appropriate to rasa, the compelling force of rasa-savoring alone is the motivating factor for the naturally arising learning — thus delight (prīti) alone is the motivating factor for learning. / And rasa is of the nature of delight — that alone is drama, drama alone is the Veda — [says] our teacher. / And these two — delight and learning — are not of different form, because both have a single object. / The propriety of vibhāvas etc. alone — [Bālapriyā:] 'devoid of conformity to rasa.' / 'Utprekṣya' — having considered. / 'Antarā' — in between. / 'Of the desired' — / The meaning is: the arrangement, the construction, of a story suitable to the desired rasa. / She clearly elaborates the meaning already stated: 'the poet' etc. / The readings 'prabandham' and 'kāvyam' both [exist]. / In the Locana, she elaborates the meaning of the passage 'of the junctures' etc.: 'here, from those like a master' etc. / 'This must be done' — this is an indication, including 'this must not be done.' / 'From the śāstras' — the fifth [case] is in the causal sense. / 'Nor also' — / The connection is with 'those who have gained learning.' / 'Of this one' — a designation for a particular hero. / 'This deed' — / The meaning is: this fruit arose. / 'Śāstrī' — the śāstras that are constituted by itihāsa — from those itihāsa-śāstras. / 'But who must nevertheless be instructed' — she states the reason: 'those who are endowed with the competence for accomplishing the welfare of the subjects' etc. / 'The competence' — the competence in the form of birth in a royal family etc. — 'endowed with that' means: having taken refuge in that — this is the meaning. / 'The four aims' — / The conjunction of vibhāvas etc. — the learning about the means of the four aims is an inseparable, consequential fruit of which — such is the conjunction — obtained through its grace, i.e., produced by it — this is the meaning. / 'Thus' — / The meaning is: in the stated manner. / 'Delight alone' — / The meaning is: the bliss of rasa-savoring alone. / 'Of different form' — / The meaning is: having different objects. / [Locana:] Since delight is truly the cause — we have stated this repeatedly. / The cognition of vibhāvas etc. appropriate to that rasa, in their proper form, as having culminated in the fruit — is called learning (vyutpatti). / And the fruit is that which arises from the unseen (adṛṣṭa), from the grace of the deity, or from elsewhere. / And that cannot be taught — because there can be no learning about the means for it. / Therefore, through the sequence of means, the success of one who proceeds [correctly] and the failure of one who proceeds without means — thus, through the hero and antagonist [respectively], learning about the means of benefit and harm is to be accomplished. / And the means, being taken up by the agent, undergoes five stages. / Namely: its own nature, a slight advancement from its own nature, competence for accomplishing the purpose, the state of being doubtful due to the onset of an obstacle, and [after] the removal of the opposing factor, the firmly-established culmination in the fruit through the overcoming of the obstruction. / Thus, for those who endure hardship, who are apprehensive of failure, who act after deliberation — their adoption of causes is exactly thus. / Those five stages of exactly this kind, pertaining to the causes — the sage has stated: 'In the conjunction of the fruit to be accomplished, the operation of the cause is [of five kinds]' — [Bālapriyā:] 'As having culminated in the fruit' — / The connection is with 'the cognition of their proper form.' / 'That' — / The meaning is: the fruit born of the unseen etc. / 'Therefore' — through the teaching of such fruit. / 'Because there can be no learning about the means' — / The meaning is: because learning about the means for such fruit cannot arise. / 'Therefore' — / The meaning is: for the stated reason. / 'Success' — / The meaning is: success in attaining the fruit. / 'Without means' — / By the word 'without means,' both absence of means and undesirable means are intended. / 'Failure' — / The meaning is: non-attainment of the fruit and attainment of the undesirable. / 'Through the hero and antagonist' — / The connection is with 'of benefit and harm.' / The meaning is: learning about the means of benefit and harm, which pertain respectively to the hero and antagonist in order — is to be accomplished. / 'Is to be accomplished' — / The meaning is: is to be produced by the poet. / 'By the agent' — / The meaning is: by the hero etc. / The connection of the accusative-ending [words] 'its own nature' etc. is with the earlier word 'five stages.' / 'Its own nature' — / The meaning is: the own nature of the means being undertaken. / 'A slight advancement' — / The meaning is: some growth. / Such is the competence for accomplishing the purpose — this is the second stage. / 'Onset of an obstacle' etc. — / The meaning is: the state of the purpose-accomplishment being doubted due to the onset of an obstacle. / 'When the opposing factor has been removed' — / The meaning is: when the obstacle has been removed. / That is to say: the state of the purpose being ascertained through the removal of the obstacle. / But in the Pratāparudrīya commentary, [it is stated:] 'The first stage is a slight advancement from the own nature; the second is competence for accomplishing the purpose; the third is the state of the purpose being doubted due to the onset of an obstacle; the fourth is the ascertainment of the purpose through the removal of the obstacle; the fifth is the firm culmination in the fruit through the overcoming of the obstruction' — in accordance with that, the construal of 'from its own nature, a slight advancement' should be understood as connecting with 'its own nature.' / 'Those who endure hardship' — / The meaning is: those who endure labor. / As stated: 'though thwarted again and again by obstacles' etc. / 'Apprehensive of failure' — / The meaning is: apprehensive of non-accomplishment of the purpose. /
[Kārikā:] Commencement (prārambha), effort (prayatna), and the possibility of attainment (prāpteḥ sambhavaḥ),
and the certainty of obtaining the fruit (niyatā phalaprāptiḥ), and the conjunction with the fruit (phalayogaḥ) — [these are] the fifth. //

children.translated_text: The intent of one who uses the word '<s>kevala</s>' (merely) and the word '<s>icchā</s>' (desire) is this: the sage <s>Bharata</s> has stated that the purpose of the <s>sandhyaṅgas</s> (juncture-limbs) is precisely the production of the narrative's ability to suggest <s>rasa</s>, [that narrative] being a component of <s>rasa</s>.
But not the achievement of invisible merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) like the limbs of the preliminary rites (<s>pūrvaraṅga</s>), nor the warding off of obstacles.
As stated: 'The composition of the desired subject-matter, the non-diminishment of the narrative,
the attainment of charm (<s>rāga</s>) in the performance, and the concealment of secrets,

Thus — the stages of the cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>), and the accomplished narrative (<s>itivṛtta</s>) of the agent that brings them about, is divided fivefold. /
Those very [five divisions] — named <s>mukha</s> (opening), <s>pratimukha</s> (progression), <s>garbha</s> (development), <s>avamarśa</s> (pause), and <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion) — with names corresponding to their meanings — are the five <s>sandhis</s> (junctures), i.e., portions of the narrative. [<s>Locana</s>:] Because they are joined together (<s>sandhīyante</s>). /
And those <s>sandhis</s> too, in relation to their respective accomplishments, are sub-divided into narrative portions through the observation of such sequential stages — [these are] the <s>sandhyaṅgas</s> (limbs of the junctures) — '<s>upakṣepa</s>' (introduction), '<s>parikara</s>' (preparation), '<s>parinyāsa</s>' (placement), '<s>vilobhana</s>' (enticement) etc. /
The <s>arthaprakṛtis</s> (elements of the plot) are included within these very [junctures]. /
Thus: for the hero whose success depends on himself — <s>bīja</s> (seed), <s>bindu</s> (drop), and <s>kārya</s> (objective) — these three. /
Through the seed, all activities [are initiated]; through the drop, reconnection [is achieved]; through the objective, accomplishment [is reached]. For these three — having the form of observation (<s>sandarśana</s>), entreaty (<s>prārthanā</s>), and resolve (<s>vyavasāya</s>) — are the agent's dispositions (<s>prakṛtis</s>), particular aspects of his nature, in accomplishing the purpose. /
But when the success depends on a minister, [it is expressed] by the terms '<s>prakīrṇa</s>' (miscellaneous) and '<s>patākā</s>' (banner), through the minister's engagement for the master's purpose alone, or for his own purpose alone, or for his own purpose as well — thus has been stated. /
Thus, the five-juncture structure of the principal narrative that ends with the accomplishment of the intended fruit, along with the completeness of the juncture-limbs, is to be composed [in a manner] that bestows learning upon all people. /
But in an incidental narrative, this rule does not apply — as the sage [<s>Bharata</s>] stated: 'In an incidental [narrative], because it serves another's purpose, this rule does not apply.' /
This being so, in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> — because there is no impropriety in the hero, who is of the <s>dhīralalita</s> (gentle-sportive) type, engaging in enjoyment that is not opposed to <s>dharma</s>; rather, because it is praiseworthy [since he] 'would not be without happiness' — with the purpose of obtaining the princess, which is subsidiary to the greater fruit of sovereignty over the earth — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The definitions of those limbs — <s>upakṣepa</s> etc. — are to be seen in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s> and other [works]. /
'Its own accomplishment' — the meaning is: the fruit [that is] its own accomplishment. /
'The <s>arthaprakṛtis</s> are included within these very [junctures]' — they are to be understood as defined: '<s>bīja</s>, <s>bindu</s>, <s>patākā</s>, <s>prakarī</s>, and <s>kārya</s>.' /
'For the hero whose success depends on himself' — the hero is threefold: one whose success depends on himself, one whose success depends on a minister, and one whose success depends on both. /
'Through the seed, all activities' — the remainder is: are intended. /
Thus in the following two sentences also it should be understood. /
'Reconnection' — the meaning is: when the main purpose has been interrupted by subsidiary objectives, the re-joining of it. /
'Observation' etc. — having placed each respective purpose in mind, having entreated for its accomplishment, the resolve for that purpose arises — thus, because they are generated by observation etc., the seed etc. are of that nature — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Artha</s>-' etc. — by this, the component meaning of '<s>arthaprakṛtayaḥ</s>' has been shown. /
Now, intending to show the meaning of the words '<s>prakarī</s>' and '<s>patākā</s>,' he says: 'minister' etc. /
'For the master's purpose' — for the hero's purpose. /
The reason for the designation by the words '<s>prakarī</s>' and '<s>patākā</s>' is, in order: the qualities of being miscellaneous and of being well known. /
'By the sage' — the connection is: 'has been stated.' /
The meaning of '<s>iti</s>' is: 'thus saying.' /
He shows the example — 'this being so' etc. /
The syntactic construction is: 'this being so, in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, [they] have been demonstrated.' /
'Because praiseworthy' — the meaning is: because laudable. /
By the word '<s>iti</s>': the engagement in enjoyment not opposed to <s>dharma</s> [is praised] with a view to the manifestation of <s>rasa</s>, as in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>; not merely out of the desire to establish conformity with treatise-rules. /
As in the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>, the composition of the juncture-limb called <s>vilāsa</s> (sport) belonging to <s>pratimukha</s> (progression) in the second act — though not in accord with the dominant <s>rasa</s> — merely out of the desire to follow <s>Bharata</s>'s doctrine. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] At the commencement of the prologue (<s>prastāvanā</s>), all five <s>sandhis</s>, accompanied by the five stages, complete with appropriate <s>sandhyaṅgas</s>, and endowed with <s>arthaprakṛtis</s>, have indeed been demonstrated. /
From the very seed, beginning with 'at this beginning, which is the cause of the master's prosperity,' through the statements 'one whose tale of war has ceased' and 'the kingdom [for one who has] conquered the enemy' — from the <s>upakṣepa</s> (introduction) of 'this is the occasion for the enjoyment of pleasures' onwards, [everything] has been determined. /
But the detailed presentation of the nature of all <s>sandhyaṅgas</s>, shown on the pages of that text [<s>Ratnāvalī</s>], would bring excessive prolixity to this treatise. /
Whereas, when presented individually, because of the fruitlessness of connecting the previous and subsequent [contexts], it would merely produce confusion — therefore it has not been expanded. /
Because the meaning of this [topic] is desirable as worthy of effort — the <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) stated in his own words by 'not merely' — for that, he provides an example — 'not merely' etc.
the wonderful narration, and the illumination of what is to be made known —
this sixfold purpose of the limbs [of juncture] has been observed in the treatise.' //

children.translated_text: For <s>rasa</s>, when pressed intensely and without respite, would quickly wilt — like a delicate <s>mālatī</s> blossom.
And especially <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment).
As the sage [<s>Bharata</s>] stated: 'That which involves the coy resistance of the woman, and from which [the lover] is turned away,

children.text: durlabhatvaṃ yato nāryā kāminaḥ sā parā ratiḥ //
children.translated_text: and through which the woman becomes unattainable — for the lover, that is the supreme <s>rati</s> (love).' //

Thus — and therefore: 'The effort aimed at the enjoyment of love is called <s>vilāsa</s> (sport).' /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The meaning is: because laudable. /
'Shown on the pages of that text' — the meaning is: shown by citing all the relevant sentences from the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>. /
'Individually' — the meaning is: merely as examples, without the preceding and following sentences. /
'Not expanded' — the meaning is: not stated in detail with examples in the <s>vṛtti</s>. /
'Of this meaning' — the meaning is: of the meaning stated [above], namely that the composition of <s>sandhis</s> and <s>sandhyaṅgas</s> should be done with a view to the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
The connection is: 'thus the <s>vyatireka</s> [is shown by].' /
'Not merely' — the meaning is: by the passage beginning with 'not merely.' /
Of the one who uses [these words] — the remainder is: of the <s>kārikā</s>-author. /
'This' — the meaning is: what will be stated by the passage ending with 'not attained by the unlearned.' /
He connects '<s>sandhyaṅgas</s>' with 'purpose' — 'of the desired [subject-matter]' — the teaching of composition. /
'Attainment of charm for the performance' — the enrichment of the acting with charm (<s>rāga</s>). /
The meaning is: the enrichment of the audience's delight through witnessing the performance. /
'Wonderful' — the meaning is: producing aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>). /
'And therefore' — the meaning is: for the stated reason. /
Its connection is with '<s>prayukta</s>' (employed). /
'Effort' etc. — this too is another cause for the narrative's suggestive capacity for <s>rasa</s> — namely, the stimulation and quelling [of emotions] at appropriate intervals — [<s>Locana</s>:] thus [referring to] the definition of the <s>vilāsa</s> (sport) <s>sandhyaṅga</s> belonging to <s>pratimukha</s>. /
The word '<s>ratibhoga</s>' (enjoyment of love) is used in the sense of indicating the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. that serve as subordinate suggestors of the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) of the dominant <s>rasa</s> — as in 'not attained by the unlearned' etc. — for the dominant <s>rasa</s> here is <s>vīra</s> (heroic). /
'Stimulation' — stimulation by completing the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. /
For example: '<s>ayaṃ sa rājā Udayanaḥ</s>' (This is king <s>Udayana</s>) etc. — for <s>Sāgarikā</s>. /
'Quelling' — in the flight from <s>Vāsavadattā</s>. /
'Renewed stimulation' — in the painting on the canvas. /
'Quelling' — at the entrance of <s>Susaṅgatā</s> — and so forth.

children.translated_text: She corroborates what was stated: 'in the conclusion' etc.
'Recovered' —

children.text: dṛṣṭāyūyaṃ nirjitā vidviṣaśca prāptā devī bhūtadhātrī ca bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You have been seen, enemies have been conquered, the queen has been recovered, and the mother of beings [too] —

children.text: sambandho 'bhūddarśakenāpi sārdhaṃ kiṃ te duḥkhaṃ yattataśśāntamadya //
children.translated_text: the relationship with the seer was [also renewed]. What grief of yours remains that has not been pacified today?' //

Thus. /
Even in <s>vīra-rasa</s> (heroic sentiment) and others, if without stimulation and subsidence as occasion demands, with the desired result arising suddenly like magic, the relation of means and end that [the poet] desired to make manifest would simply not be shown. /
'Again' — /
The desire [to resume the rasa], mostly apprehended as threatened [with interruption] due to the force of historical events — [Bālapriyā:] '<s>samīhā</s>' means desire. /
'For the purpose of <s>rati</s>-enjoyment' — /
The meaning is: pertaining to the experience of lovemaking. /
Or alternatively: the enjoyment of <s>rati</s>, i.e., the object (<s>viṣaya</s>) of the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) named <s>rati</s> — a woman etc. — that which is for the purpose of that, i.e., for the purpose of union with that — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Ādhikārika</s>' (principal) — /
The meaning is: that which is the principal <s>rasa</s> being depicted, the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) of that [rasa], and the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. that are its sub-suggestors — these serve as their indicators, i.e., have the status of marking them. /
The purport is: not merely oriented toward the previously stated expressible meaning. /
'Employed' — /
The remainder is: by the sage (<s>Bharata</s>). /
'As [properly] understood' — /
One whose meaning (<s>artha</s>) has been properly understood, i.e., cognized, in accordance with the sage's intention — is 'not thus'; rather, only the literal meaning has been grasped — this is the purport. /
The remainder is: by the author of the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>. /
The connection of '<s>iti</s>' is with '<s>āśaya</s>' (intention). /
But what is the principal <s>rasa</s> in the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>? — to this he says: 'the present [one]' etc. /
The purport is: not <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
He shows the fault if otherwise: 'deeply' etc. /
'Continuously relished' — savored without interruption. /
'<s>Mālatī</s>' — the meaning is: <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) [that is] continuously pressed. /
'Which' — /
The disposition of contrariness in a woman is the desire for contrary conduct. /
And since and because the lovemaking of the woman is obstructed — is the remainder. /
Since and because she [obstructs] — this triad — the lovemaking of a woman whose desire has been thwarted is the supreme cause of delight — this is the meaning. /
Not only in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> but also in other <s>rasas</s> is the stated [principle] to be accepted — he says: '<s>vīra</s>' etc. /
'With a magical result' — /
The meaning is: with a result demonstrated by illusion (<s>indrajāla</s>) etc. /
'Desired to make manifest' — desired by the poet to make visible. /
'Means' — /
The meaning is: the relation of cause and effect between the respective activities of the hero etc. and the fourfold aims of life (<s>caturvarga</s>). The construal is: 'would not [be shown].' /
By the word 'begun' he states what is intended in the present context: 'mostly apprehended as threatened' etc. /
'Has arisen' — has occurred. /
He states the meaning of 'repose': 'interruption' etc. /
And thus: wherever the interruption of the principal <s>rasa</s> would occur — there, [the tracking] of the <s>rasa</s>, as in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> itself. /
And of the principal <s>rasa</s> whose repose has begun — the tracking [is maintained]. /
As in the <s>Tāpasavatsarāja</s> (<s>Svapnavāsavadattā</s>). /
And of the particular type of extended composition — the <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) etc. — this further thing should be understood as a cause of <s>rasa</s>-manifestation: the fitting employment of <s>alaṅkāras</s> even when they are capable [of being used]. /
For a capable poet, sometimes engrossed in the construction of <s>alaṅkāras</s> alone, commences an extended composition without regard for <s>rasa</s>-composition, [being drawn] by the pull of those [alaṅkāras] — for the purpose of instructing [against] that, this is stated. /
And poets are seen who are exclusively devoted to the construction of <s>alaṅkāras</s>, disregarding <s>rasa</s>, in their extended compositions. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] But not [the case where] the repose [is] the occurrence [of anything] at every point, [i.e.,] the interruption of which is such. /
'Of the <s>rasa</s>' — /
The extent is: of anything that is a component of <s>rasa</s>. /
For in the <s>Tāpasavatsarāja</s> (<s>Svapnavāsavadattā</s>), the bond of love directed toward <s>Vāsavadattā</s> — whose nature is the conviction that she is one's entire life — pervading the entire plot, grasping the stages of <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos), <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation), etc. through the propriety of its <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. — extends throughout the narrative. /
For through the recovery of the kingdom — by means of the grandeur of the minister's policy — and through the obtaining of <s>Padmāvatī</s> that is subsidiary to that — sustained in a form brought back to life — the discovery of <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, having attained the supreme most desirable state, is itself the fruit therein. /
For in the conclusion: 'The queen has been recovered, and the mother of beings [too]; and the relationship with the seer [was renewed]' — thus the primacy of recovering the queen has been brought to completion. /
And in this much variegated narrative-canvas, the bond of love for <s>Vāsavadattā</s> — standing as the background wall — [is maintained] from the first act onward, through the very activity of that [bond], even during the marriage with <s>Padmāvatī</s> etc. /
Therefore, that very bond of love directed toward <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, though its interruption is apprehended from the force of the narrative, is [nevertheless] tracked — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the meaning is: therein, that tracking must be accomplished. /
By the word '<s>rasa</s>' in 'of the principal <s>rasa</s>' — she states what is intended: 'of a component of <s>rasa</s>' etc. /
'Of anything' — the meaning is: of a <s>vibhāva</s> etc. /
She elaborates what was stated as 'as in the <s>Tāpasavatsarāja</s>': 'for in the <s>Tāpasavatsarāja</s>' etc. /
'Bond of love' — /
The remainder is: residing in <s>Vatsarāja</s>. /
'Entire' — /
The connection of this is with 'pervading the plot.' /
'<s>Karuṇa</s>' — /
The sequence here should be understood. /
She corroborates what was said: 'by the kingdom' etc. /
The reason for 'recovered' — 'by the recovery of the kingdom' — sustained in a form brought back to life. /
The two qualifications of the recovery of the kingdom: 'by the minister's' etc.

'Your gaze is nectar-showering — is it not indeed nectar-showering?' — this is the meaning. /

children.translated_text: Absence of <s>rasa</s> is in the sport of <s>Viṣamabāṇa</s> (the Uneven-arrowed one, i.e. <s>Kāmadeva</s>).
And as in the dialogue of the vulture and the jackal etc. in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>.
[<s>Locana</s>:] [Prakrit:] 'By play, with the tip of his tusk, having lifted up the entire disc of the earth — today,
how is even a lotus-stalk ornament heavy upon your body?' //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Of this <s>dhvani</s> whose expressible is intended but whose primary [purport] is something else (<s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s>) — the variety that has been illustrated as having suggestion in the form of reverberation, being of two kinds — that too manifests in certain longer compositions. /
For example, in the <s>Madhumathana-vijaya</s>, in the utterances of <s>Pāñcajanya</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> conch]. /
Or, as in my own [work], in the encounter with the companion of <s>Kāmadeva</s> — [<s>Locana</s>:] He undertakes [this section] to show that not only is [<s>dhvani</s>] directly suggested by a composition, but also indirectly — 'furthermore' etc. /
'<s>Anusvāna</s> (reverberation) and <s>upamā</s> (simile)' — rooted in the power of word and rooted in the power of meaning; the variety that has been illustrated of <s>dhvani</s> — that [variety], when certain compositions serve as the suggestive occasions, being established in the state of being suggested — /
'Of this' — the remainder is: as the suggestor of the <s>rasa</s>-etc.-<s>dhvani</s> that is the present topic, it shines forth. /
The <s>vṛtti</s> passage too should be construed in just this way. /
Alternatively — the variety illustrated as '<s>anusvāna</s> and <s>upamā</s>' that shines forth in compositions — for this too, the connection with the next verse '<s>dyotyo 'lakṣyakramaḥ kvacit</s>' (the imperceptibly-sequenced [<s>dhvani</s>] is illuminated sometimes) provides the coherence of the <s>kārikā</s> and <s>vṛtti</s>. /
What is stated [thereby] is this: sometimes the <s>dhvani</s> whose suggestion is in the form of reverberation is directly suggested by a composition — but it ultimately culminates in <s>rasa</s>-etc.-<s>dhvani</s>. /
But if this were explained in a straightforward manner, then this passage would be incoherent with the preceding and following passages whose subject is the imperceptibly-sequenced [<s>dhvani</s>], and the utterances of <s>Pāñcajanya</s> etc. would have been said to be devoid of <s>rasa</s> — enough [of this alternative]. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] With the intention of the meaning he himself will explain, he introduces the passage 'furthermore' etc. — 'not only' etc. /
'Indirectly too' — the meaning is: through the medium of another suggested [meaning]. /
He explains the <s>kārikā</s> — '<s>anusvāna</s>' etc. /
'Of <s>dhvani</s>' —
That [intention], once manifested, culminates in the very nature of the <s>rasa</s> at hand.
The companions are spring, youth, the <s>Malaya</s> breeze, etc.; in the encounter with them —
[Prakrit:] 'I become one whose [boundary] lines are swept away, without a goad, and devoid of discrimination;

'Enough of standing in this cremation ground, swarming with vultures and jackals,
terrible with abundance of skeletons, frightening to all living beings!' //
Such and similar utterances of Youth suggest each one's own characteristic nature; and that characteristic nature culminates in the <s>rasa</s> at hand.
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'By play' —
'By play, with the tip of his tusk, having lifted up the entire disc of the earth — today,
how is even the carrying of a lotus-stalk heavy upon your body?' //

[Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'Of him who playfully, with the tip of his tusk, lifted up the entire disc of the earth — today,
how is even a lotus-stalk ornament heavy upon your body?' //

In '<s>vibhajya</s>' (dividing), there is also the reading '<s>nirbhajya</s>' (breaking apart). /
As [in the verse] of the great sage <s>Vyāsa</s> — 'The times of happiness have passed; terrible [times] have arrived.

[<s>Locana</s>:] What is being said amounts to this: <s>rasa</s> is manifested by phonemes and other [elements] up to the extended composition — either directly, through the medium of conveying <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc., or through the medium of suggesting <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. successively — therein, the successive suggestive capacity of the composition was stated first, incidentally. /
But now, [the suggestive capacity] of phonemes, words, etc. is being stated. /
Therefore, even in the <s>vṛtti</s>, [the passage] 'is seen being manifested' — the sentence-complement to be supplied at 'the suggestive capacity is seen' etc. is of the following form: 'through the medium of suggesting <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., successively.' /
'My enemies' — 'that I should have enemies is improper' — the plural [in '<s>arayaḥ</s>'] suggests the <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) of anger in the form of the impropriety of the relation. /
'In whom austerity is found' — through the possessive suffix (<s>taddhita</s> with the sense of '<s>matvarthīya</s>'), the devoid-of-valor nature [of the sage] is expressed. /
Therein, by the particle-group '<s>api</s>' (even), the utter inconceivability [is conveyed]. /
'If [the killing] is done by me' — even if there is the purchase of life [i.e., the killing serves survival], still the act of killing is improper. /
And that he [a mere ascetic] should be the agent of that [killing] — by the word '<s>api</s>' (even), [the sense is:] a mere human being. /
'In this very [place]' — 'presided over by me' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] she states the purport: 'what is said' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: <s>rasa</s> is manifested either directly through the medium of conveying <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., or successively through the medium of suggesting <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. /
'At first' — the meaning is: in the previous <s>kārikā</s>. /
She construes the <s>vṛtti</s> text in accordance with the explained meaning — 'therefore' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: 'the sentence-complement [to be supplied] is of such a form.' /
'Through the medium of suggesting' — the purport is: the meaning is that <s>rasa</s> etc., through the particular [elements] beginning with phonemes, is manifested successively through the medium of suggesting <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. — such is the meaning of 'is seen being manifested' etc. /
'Humiliation' — this is the self-deprecatory speech of the angry <s>Rāvaṇa</s> when <s>Śrī Rāma</s> is destroying the <s>Rākṣasa</s> clan. /
The syntactic connection is: 'my enemies exist, this itself is a humiliation' etc. /
'One who has awakened' — this should be understood as the possessive suffix added to the form derived from the causative. /
'<s>Svarga</s> (heaven) indeed' — '<s>grāmaṭikā</s>' means a small village. /
This verse is also cited in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. /
She elaborates the suggestive capacity stated in the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'my' etc. /
'With numerousness' — 'that I, being mighty, should have enemies is improper' — the plural in '<s>arayaḥ</s>' (enemies) suggests the <s>vibhāva</s> of anger in the form of the impropriety of the relation — this is the meaning of 'the plural.' /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, '<s>sambandha</s>' means: the relation expressed by the genitive case. /
'Is expressed' — of the meaning of the word '<s>tapaḥ</s>' etc. — the remainder [is to be supplied]. /
'Utter inconceivability' — the meaning is: the utter inconceivability of enmity directed toward an ascetic is expressed. /
The connection of the word 'is expressed' should be understood, as appropriate, with what follows as well. /
'The act of killing' — the remainder is: 'even by any agent whatsoever.' /
'He' — that ascetic — 'a mere human being' — a despicable mere mortal. /
The elaboration of the prefix '<s>ni-</s>' — 'completely' etc. /
Just as here, in this verse, the suggestive capacity of all these [elements] is clearly perceived in abundance. /
Therein, by '<s>me yad arayaḥ</s>' (that I should have enemies) — the suggestive capacity of <s>sup</s>-endings (nominal case-endings) and relation-expressing [forms]. /
In '<s>tatrāpy asau tāpasa</s>' (there too, that ascetic) — [the suggestive capacity] of the demonstrative pronoun and particles. /
In '<s>so 'py atraiva nihanti rākṣasa-kulaṃ jīvaty aho rāvaṇaḥ</s>' (he too, right here, slays the <s>Rākṣasa</s> clan — alas, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> lives!) — [the suggestive capacity] of verbal endings (<s>tiṅ</s>) and case-powers (<s>kāraka</s>). /
In the half-verse beginning with '<s>dhig dhik chakra-jitam</s>' (fie, fie on the conqueror of <s>Indra</s>) — [the suggestive capacity] of <s>kṛt</s>-suffixes, <s>taddhita</s>-suffixes, compounds, and prefixes. /
And when such abundance of suggestive [elements] is present, the all-surpassing beauty of composition (<s>bandha-chāyā</s>) blossoms forth. /
For where even a single word that reveals the suggested [meaning] appears, even there some beauty of composition exists in the poetry — how much more so where there is a confluence of many such [words]! /
As in the verse cited just above. /
For here, in the word '<s>Rāvaṇa</s>' — even though the verse is adorned through the variety of <s>dhvani</s> called <s>arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācya</s> (meaning transferred to another sense) — there is yet another outshining of the aforementioned types of suggestive [capacity]. /
And such modes of composition are mostly seen in abundance in the works of great poets. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The place — the locus — the <s>Rākṣasa</s> army being completely destroyed [is] the object [of the action] — this, being unimaginable, having presented itself — the non-attainment of [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s own] heroic effort is suggested by the words that convey verbal endings and case-powers. /
The <s>arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācya</s> status of '<s>Rāvaṇa</s>' was explained previously. /
'Fie, fie' — the suggestive capacity of the particle, [the compound] 'one who conquered <s>Indra</s>' — [understood as] 'this is a legend,' and of the compound '<s>svarga</s>' etc. in conjunction with a subordinate compound — toward the recollection of one's own prowess. /
'<s>Grāmaṭikā</s>' — through the use of the diminutive <s>taddhita</s>-suffix together with the feminine suffix — toward [conveying] the object of disrespect; in the word '<s>viluṇṭhana</s>' (plundering), of the prefix '<s>vi-</s>' — toward [conveying] merciless assault — the suggestive capacity [is thus]. /
Of the word '<s>vṛthā</s>' (in vain), the particle — the suggestive capacity toward self-deprecation of one's own prowess. /
'With arms' — by the plural, rather, [the sense] 'this is merely a burden' is suggested. /
Therefore, even when this verse is divided particle by particle, every single portion shines forth as suggestive — what more [need be said]? /
He shows the fruit of demonstrating this purpose — 'thus' etc. /
He illustrates what was said about 'a single word' — 'as here' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The meaning is: the name of the <s>Rākṣasa</s> clan too will be destroyed, in that manner. /
'<s>Rākṣasa</s> army' — there is also the reading '<s>rākṣasa-kula</s>' (the <s>Rākṣasa</s> clan). /
She demonstrates the sentence-level suggested meaning of '<s>so 'pi</s>' etc. — 'this very [thing]' etc. /
'Non-attainment of heroic effort' — the meaning is: the absence of the excellence of one's own prowess. /
The syntactic connection is: it is suggested by the words that convey verbal endings and case-powers. /
'Verbal endings, and the words that convey case-powers' — and by those. /
Verbal endings — '<s>nihanti</s>' (slays) — the case-powers are: the nature of being the locus (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>), and the object (<s>karman</s>). /
'Was explained previously' — the purport is: the prowess of conquering the city of <s>Mahendra</s> etc. is suggested by the word '<s>Rāvaṇa</s>.' /
'Of the particle' — the remainder is: 'the suggestive capacity.' /
'A legend' — the meaning is: speech whose meaning is fabricated. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — the meaning is: toward [the cognition] that it is such. /
'In conjunction with' — this is a qualifying genitive of 'of the particle.' /

children.text:
atra hi kṛttaddhitavacanairalakṣyakramavyaṅgyaḥ, 'pṛthivī gatayauvanā' locanam atikrāntaṃ na tu kadācana vartamānatāmavalambamānaṃ sukhaṃ yeṣu te kālā iti, sarva eva na tu sukhaṃ prati vartamānaḥ sa ko 'pi kālaleśa ityarthaḥ /
pratīpānyupasthitāni vṛttāni pratyāvartamānāni tathā dūrabhāvīnyapi pratyupasthitāni nikaṭatayā vartamānāni bhavanti dāruṇāni duḥkhāni yeṣu te /
duḥkhaṃ bahuprakārameva prativartamānāḥ sarve kālāṃśā ityanena kālasya tāvannirvedamabhivyañjayataḥ śāntarasavyañjakatvam /
deśasyāpyāha--pṛthivī śvaḥ śvaḥ prātaḥ prātardināddinaṃ pāpīyadivasāḥ pāpānāṃ sambandhinaḥ pāpiṣṭhajanasvāmikā divasā yasyāṃ sā tathoktā /
svābhāvata eva tāvatkālo duḥkhamayaḥ tatrāpi pāpiṣṭhajanasvāmikapṛthivīlakṣayauvanā vṛddhastrīvadasaṃbhāvyamānasaṃbhogā gatayauvanatayā hi yo yo divasa āgacchati bālapriyā atra vyaṅgayatvenoktānāmarthānāṃ rāvaṇagatakrodhanirvedātiśayavyañjakatvaṃ bodhyam /
ślokaṃ vyākhyāti--atikrāntamityādi /
bhūtārthakaktapratyayena gamyamarthamāha---na tvityādi /
kālā iti bahuvacanārthavivaraṇam--sarva eveti /
tena gamyamāha---na tvityādi /
pratītyasya vivaraṇam--pratīpānīti /
pratikūlānīntyarthaḥ /
vṛttāni pratyāvartamānānyupasthitānīti sambandhaḥ /
gatānyapi pratyāvartamānatvena jñāyamānānītyarthaḥ /
anyathāpi vyācaṣṭe---tathetyādi /
uktamevārthaṃ sphuṭamāha---duḥkhamityādi /
ityanenetyādi /
nirvedābhivyañjanadvārā prakṛtaśāntarasavyañjakatvamityarthaḥ /
pāpīyeti chapratyayāntamityāśayena vyācaṣṭe---pāpānāmityādi /
pāpānāṃ sambandhina ityasyaiva vivaraṇam---pāpiṣṭhetyādi /
bhūmārthakājantaḥ pāpaśabdo 'trātiśayitatapāpaviśiṣṭārthaka iti bhāvaḥ /
pāpatrayatātparyamāha---svabhāvata ityādi /
pāpiṣṭheti /
pāpiṣṭhajanasvāmikaḥ pṛthivīlakṣaṇo yo deśastasya daurātmyādityarthaḥ /
śvaḥ śva ityasya gatayauvanetyanenāpi sambandha ityāha---śvaḥśva ityādi /
gatayauvanetyasya mukhyārthaṃ tasya prakṛte bādhallakṣaṇānimittaṃ tatsārūpyaṃ ca darśayati--vṛddhetyādi /
sambhogasmukhānubhavaḥ /
gatayauvanāpadenātra sukhānādhāyiketyartho lakṣyate, sukhānubhavasya sambhāvanāpi nāstītyartho vyaṅgyaśceti bhāvaḥ /
gatayauvaneti pāpīyānityatra hetugarbhaṃ pāpīyapadamarthāntaraparaṃ cetyanyathā vyācaṣṭe---gatetyādi /
yadi vetyādau yojyam /

children.translated_text: '<s>Gata</s>' (having gone/lost) — /
and by this, the <s>dhvani</s> of the type <s>atyanta-tiraskṛta-vācya</s> (where the literal meaning is completely suppressed) is demonstrated. /

children.text: eṣāṃ ca subādīnāmekaikaśaḥ samuditānāṃ ca vyañjakatvaṃ mahākavīnāṃ prabandheṣu prāyeṇa dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: And the suggestive capacity of these <s>sup</s>-endings (nominal endings) etc. — both individually and collectively — is mostly seen in the compositions of great poets. /

children.text: subantasya vyañjakatvaṃ yathā--- tālaiḥ śiñjadvayasubhagaiḥ kāntayā nartito me yāmadhyāste divasavigame nīlakaṇṭhaḥ suhṛdvaḥ //
children.translated_text: The suggestive capacity of a <s>subanta</s> (nominal form) is as follows: 'By cymbals whose chiming pairs are beautiful, by my beloved — for me the blue-throated peacock, your friend, is made to dance at the end of the day.' //

For here, through the <s>kṛt</s>-suffixes and <s>taddhita</s>-suffixes and case-forms, there is <s>alakṣyakrama-vyaṅgya</s> (suggestion through imperceptible sequence); '<s>pṛthivī gatayauvanā</s>' (the earth has lost her youth) — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'The times in which happiness has been transcended' — not [merely passed,] but never assuming a present state — such times — that is, entirely [so] — not even a single fragment of time presents itself to happiness — this is the meaning. /
'Terrible [things] have approached' — that which has occurred, having reversed itself; and also, things that are in the far future, having become proximate, have presented themselves — [those] that are terrible, i.e., [full of] suffering. /
Suffering of many kinds — all portions of time that keep recurring — by this, [the verse], while manifesting <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness) with respect to time, [also] has the suggestive capacity for <s>śānta-rasa</s> (the <s>rasa</s> of tranquility). /
He states [the same] for place too — 'the earth, day after day, each morning, from day to day — whose days are <s>pāpīya</s> (more wicked)' — associated with the wicked, having the most sinful people as its masters — whose days are such — thus described. /
By its very nature, time is full of suffering; and on top of that, the earth characterized by having the most sinful people as its masters — [this earth] that has lost its youth — like an old woman whose enjoyment is inconceivable — through having lost its youth, whatever day arrives — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] here, the suggestive capacity of the stated meanings toward suggesting the excess of anger and world-weariness belonging to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> should be understood. /
She explains the verse — 'the times in which [happiness] has been transcended' etc. /
She states the implied meaning through the past-tense suffix (<s>kta</s>-pratyaya) — 'not [merely passed] but' etc. /
The elaboration of '<s>kālāḥ</s>' in the plural — 'entirely' etc. /
From that, she states the implication — 'not even' etc. /
The elaboration of '<s>pratī</s>' (prefix) — 'opposing' etc. /
'Opposing' — the meaning is: contrary. /
The connection is: those that have occurred, being perceived as recurring, have approached. /
The meaning is: those that are past, being perceived as coming back. /
She also explains otherwise — 'likewise' etc. /
She states the stated meaning clearly — 'suffering' etc. /
'By this' etc. — the meaning is: through the medium of suggesting <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness), [there is] the suggestive capacity for the <s>śānta-rasa</s> at hand. /
She explains '<s>pāpīya</s>' as having the comparative suffix (<s>cha</s>-pratyaya) — 'of the wicked' etc. /
'Associated with the wicked' — this is the elaboration of the same. /
'<s>Pāpiṣṭha</s>' etc. — the purport is that the word '<s>pāpa</s>' here, ending in a suffix denoting excess, has the meaning of one distinguished by greatly intensified wickedness. /
She states the purport of the threefold [use of] '<s>pāpa</s>' — 'by its very nature' etc. /
'<s>Pāpiṣṭha</s>' — the meaning is: because of the wickedness of the place characterized by the earth having the most sinful people as its masters. /
She states that '<s>śvaḥ śvaḥ</s>' (day after day) also has a syntactic connection with '<s>gatayauvanā</s>' (having lost her youth) — '<s>śvaḥ śvaḥ</s>' etc. /
She shows the primary meaning of '<s>gatayauvanā</s>,' the obstacle to [that primary meaning] in the present context, and the basis for the similarity [justifying secondary meaning] — 'like an old woman' etc. /
'Enjoyment' — the direct experience of pleasure. /
By the word '<s>gatayauvanā</s>' (having lost her youth), here the secondary meaning 'not conducive to happiness' is indicated; the suggested meaning is that there is no possibility even of the experience of happiness — this is the purport. /
'<s>Gatayauvanā</s>' (having lost her youth) — she explains '<s>pāpīyān</s>' as containing an implicit reason and as oriented toward another meaning — '<s>gata</s>' etc. /
'If alternatively' etc. should be connected at the beginning. /
The suggestive capacity of a <s>tiṅanta</s> (verbal form) is as follows —

children.text: avasara rouṃ cia ṇimmiāiṃ mā puṃsa me haacchīiṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Go away! [My eyes] were created only for weeping — do not destroy my eyes that are [already] lost [to sorrow].

children.text: daṃsaṃṇamettumbhattehiṃ jahi hiaaṃ tuha ṇa ṇāam //
children.translated_text: Strike the heart that, by the mere sight of you, has not known yours [i.e., your heart]!' //

children.text:
locanam sa sa pūrvapūrvāpekṣayā pāpīyān nikṛṣṭatvāt /
yadiveyasunanto 'yaṃ śabdo muninaivaṃ prayukto ṇijanto vā /
atyanteti /
so 'pi prakāro 'syaivāṅgatāmetīti bhāvaḥ /
subantasyeti /
samuditatve tūdāharaṇaṃ dattaṃ vyastatve cojyata iti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: But as for the combined [suggestive capacity], an example has been given; as for the separate [capacity], it is stated [now] — this is the purport. /
'By cymbals' — the plural suggests the manifold skill [of the beloved], hinting at the stimulation of <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation). /

children.text: apasara roditumeva nirmite mā puṃsaya hate akṣiṇī me /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:) 'Go away! [My eyes] were created only for weeping — do not destroy my eyes that are [already] lost. /

children.text: darśanamātronmattābhyāṃ yābhyāṃ tava hṛdayamevaṃrūpaṃ na jñātam //
children.translated_text: By [the sight of] you, [my eyes] that are maddened by a mere glance — by which [eyes] your heart of such a nature was not known [to be so cruel]!' //

[<s>Locana</s>:] That — each preceding [day] compared to its predecessor is more wicked, because of its inferior quality. /
Or, if this word [<s>pāpīyas</s>] was used by the sage [<s>Vyāsa</s>] in the <s>ṇijanta</s> (causative) form — /
'Completely' etc. — the purport is: that mode too attains subsidiary status to this very [main topic]. /
'Of a <s>subanta</s>' — /

children.text:
anmatto hi na kiñcijjānātīti na kasyāpyatrāparādhaḥ daivenetthameva nirmāṇaṃ bālapriyā pṛthivyā iti śeṣaḥ /
nanu pāpīyānityuktārthaḥ kathaṃ labhyata ityatrāha---itasunanta iti /
nanvasmin pakṣe pāpīyo divaseti bhāvyamityata āha--muninetyādi /
ārṣo 'yaṃ prayoga ityarthaḥ. a6 pakṣāntaramāha---ṇijanto veti /
muninā prayukta ityanuṣajyate ṇijanteyasunanto munināprayukto vetyarthaḥ /
lokān pāpīyasaḥ karotītyarthe pāpīyaśśabdāṇṇaci kartaryavi ṭerṇicaśca lopādakārānto 'yaṃ pāpīyaśabda iti bhāvaḥ /
anusvānetyādikārikā yathā vyākhyātā, tathā prakṛte yojayata---so 'pītyādi /
so 'pi prakāraḥ atyantatiraskṛvācyo dhvaniḥ /
rasasyeti /
prakṛtasya śāntasyetyarthaḥ /
dattamiti /
nyakkāra ityādiślokena darśitamityarthaḥ /
'tālai, rityādyuttarameghasandeśastham /
vaidagdhyamiti nartanaviṣayakaṃ vaidagadhyamityarthaḥ /
apasaretyādivirahiṇyāśśaṭhaṃ pratyuktiḥ /
me hatākṣiṇī it chāyā /
tvamapasara apehi /
kuta ityatrāha--roditumityādi /
rīditumeva nirmite sṛṣṭe me hatākṣiṇī kutsite nayane /
mā puṃsaya mā abhivardhaya, mā tvadabhimukhaṃ vikāsayeti /
yāvat /
puṃsa abhivardhana iti curādī /
hṛdayaṃ tava na jñātamita chāyā /
tadyvākhyānam---tavetyādi /
evaṃrūpamiti /
mathi anāsaktaṃ bhāvītyarthaḥ /
bhāvārthamāha---unmatto hītyādi /

children.translated_text: An example of <s>tiṅanta</s> (verbal ending as suggestor): as in '<s>apasara</s>' (go away), or alternatively —

children.text: mā panthaṃ rundhīo avehi bālaa ahosi ahirīo /
children.translated_text: Do not block the path! Go away, boy — you are shameless!
We are not free agents; our empty house must be guarded.

<s>Bālapriyā</s>: For a madman does not know anything, so there is no fault of anyone here — fate has fashioned things thus. 'Of the earth' is to be supplied. Now, as to how the meaning stated as '<s>pāpīyān</s>' (more sinful) is obtained, he says — '<s>itasunanta</s>' etc. Since in this interpretation it would have to be '<s>pāpīyo divasa</s>', he says — '<s>muninā</s>' etc. The meaning is: this is an archaic usage (<s>ārṣa prayoga</s>). He states an alternative interpretation — '<s>ṇijanto va</s>' etc. 'Employed by the sage' is to be connected: the meaning is 'either a <s>ṇijanta</s> (causative ending) or an <s>itasunanta</s> employed by the sage.' The word <s>pāpīya</s> in the sense of 'makes people more sinful,' with the <s>ṇac</s> suffix in the active sense, the elision of <s>ṭi</s>, and the <s>ṇic</s> (causative) — this word <s>pāpīya</s> ends in the vowel <s>a</s>: such is the purport. The verse beginning with '<s>anusvāna</s>' etc., as it has been explained, should be applied to the present topic — '<s>so 'pi</s>' etc. That mode too is <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) where the expressible meaning is completely concealed. '<s>Rasasya</s>' means: of the <s>śānta</s> (quiescent) <s>rasa</s> under discussion. '<s>Dattam</s>' means: it has been demonstrated by the verse beginning '<s>nyakkāra</s>' etc. '<s>Tālai</s>' etc. is found in the <s>Uttara-Meghasandeśa</s> (latter part of the Cloud Messenger). '<s>Vaidagdhya</s>' means: skill pertaining to dance. '<s>Apasara</s>' etc. is the retort of a woman in separation (<s>virahiṇī</s>) to a deceitful man (<s>śaṭha</s>). The <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit gloss) is: '<s>me hatākṣiṇī</s>' (my wretched eyes). 'You, go away (<s>apasara</s>), depart (<s>apehi</s>)!' To the question 'why?', he says — '<s>roditum</s>' etc. 'My wretched eyes were created solely for weeping; do not nourish them (<s>mā puṃsaya</s>), do not cause them to flourish, do not cause them to open toward you' — this is the import. <s>Puṃsa</s> (nourishing) is of the <s>curādi</s> (tenth conjugation) class. The <s>chāyā</s> is: 'your heart is not known.' The explanation of that is — '<s>tava</s>' etc. '<s>Evaṃrūpam</s>' means: of such a nature. '<s>Mathi</s>' means: the feeling (<s>bhāva</s>) is one of non-attachment. He states the implied meaning — '<s>unmatto hi</s>' etc.
An example of <s>sambandha</s> (genitive relationship as suggestor), as follows —

children.text: aṇaṇatta vacca bālaa hṇā arnti kiṃ maṃ puloesieam /
children.translated_text: Go elsewhere, boy! I am bathing — why do you stare at me so?
O sir, for those who fear their wives, there is no riverbank at all!
<s>Locana</s>: '<s>Kṛtam</s>' (it is done) —

children.text: apasara mā vṛthā prayāsaṃ kārṣīḥ daivasya viparivartayitumaśakyatvāditi tiṅanto vyañjakaḥ tadanugṛhītāni padāntarāṇyapīti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Go away, do not make a futile effort, for the course of fate cannot be reversed' — here the <s>tiṅanta</s> (verbal ending) is the suggestor (<s>vyañjaka</s>), and the other words that follow it are also supported by it: such is the purport.

children.text: mā panthānaṃ rudhaḥ apehi bālaka aprauḍha aho asi ahnīkaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit rendering): 'Do not block the path; go away, boy — you are immature; alas, you are shameless!'

children.text: vayaṃ paratantrā yataḥ śūnyagṛhaṃ māmakaṃ rakṣaṇīyaṃ vartate //
children.translated_text: 'We are dependent on others, since our empty house needs to be guarded.'

children.text:

vyañjaka iti /
rirṣyādivyañjaka ityarthaḥ /

ṇirichāo ityasya chāyāvivaraṇam /
vayaṃ paratantrā iti /

prakāśayasīti /

children.translated_text: 'the desire for union (<s>sambhoga</s>)' is to be supplied.

children.text: atra śloke śṛṅgāraḥ sambhogo vyaṅya pūrvaślorake tu vipralambha iti bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: In this verse, <s>śṛṅgāra</s> in the mode of union (<s>sambhoga</s>) is the suggested meaning, whereas in the previous verse it was <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) — this is the difference.

children.text: vṛttau--'aṇṇatte'ti anyatra vraja bālakasnāntīṃ kiṃ mā pralokayasyetat /
children.translated_text: In the <s>vṛtti</s> (prose commentary): '<s>aṇṇatte</s>' means 'go elsewhere, boy — why do you stare at me so intently while I am bathing?'
'O sir, for those who fear their wives, there is no riverbank at all!'

Here, the <s>tiṅanta</s> form '<s>apehi</s>' (go away) suggests the following: 'You are indeed immature, since you display it thus in public. But there is an assignation place — the empty house — you should come there instead.' '<s>Anyatra vraja bālaka</s>' (go elsewhere, boy) — 'O you of immature understanding, why do you gaze at me so intently while I am bathing?' '<s>Bho</s>' is an insolent form of address. 'For those who fear their wives, there is no riverbank as a meeting-place at all.' Here, the meaning is that this place belongs to those who fear their wives — so the <s>sambandha</s> (genitive relation) is far-removed (from its apparent meaning). <s>Bālapriyā</s>: '<s>Tiṅantaśabda</s>' means: the verbal ending. '<s>Vyañjaka</s>' means: a suggestor of jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) and the like. '<s>Bālaka</s>' is glossed as '<s>aprauḍha</s>' (immature). '<s>Ṇiricchāo</s>' — its <s>chāyā</s> (gloss) is explained. '<s>Vayaṃ paratantrāḥ</s>' — the <s>chāyā</s> is: 'the empty house is not to be guarded' (i.e., it is unguarded — implying an invitation). The explanation of this is — '<s>yataḥ</s>' etc. '<s>Prakāśayasi</s>' means:

children.translated_text: The suffix <s>ka</s> indicates an excess of contempt (<s>avajñātiśaya</s>).
And compound words (<s>samāsa</s>) too, when employed with propriety of usage (<s>vṛttyaucitya</s>), serve as suggestors.

children.text: nipātānāṃ vyañjakatvaṃ yathā--- ayamekapade tayā viyogaḥ priyayā copanataḥ suduḥsaho me /
children.translated_text: The suggestive power of particles (<s>nipāta</s>) is illustrated as follows — 'This separation from my beloved, occurring all at once, is utterly unbearable to me;
and the days must be endured that are made lovely by the absence of sunshine, with the rising of fresh rain-clouds.'

Thus. The letter <s>yā</s>. This is the speech of a woman who desires a certain householder who is gazing at her with passion as she bathes in a lake. In place of '<s>taḍam</s>' (bank), the reading '<s>tittham</s>' is also seen; its <s>chāyā</s> is '<s>tīrtham</s>' (bathing-ghat). In the <s>Locana</s>: '<s>sambandhi</s>' indicates the meaning of the genitive case. The construction is: 'this bank does not at all belong to (<s>sambandhi</s>) those who fear their wives.' What follows is a gloss of the same statement — '<s>jāyātaḥ</s>' etc. The meaning is: the connection — namely, the presence of such people at this place — is far-removed. '<s>Ataḥ vraja</s>' (therefore, go away). '<s>Anena sambandhena</s>' means: by the genitive relationship. '<s>Īrṣyā</s>' (jealousy) — in artful usages (<s>kṛtaka-prayoga</s>) of Prakrit, the suggestive power (<s>vyañjakatva</s>) in the domain of <s>taddhita</s> suffixes is indeed conveyed.
Here, the particle '<s>ca</s>' (and) is the suggestor.
Or, as in another example — 'Her face, with lower lip covered by her finger, charmingly faltering with syllables of prohibition,

children.text: mukhamaṃsavivarti pakṣmalākṣyāḥ kathamapyunnamitaṃ na cumbitaṃ tu //
children.translated_text: with eyes flickering sideways, that face of the one with beautiful lashes — somehow it was raised up, but it was not kissed.'
Here, the particle '<s>tu</s>' (but) is the suggestor.
Though the illuminative function (<s>dyotakatva</s>) of particles is well-established, here it is spoken of with reference to <s>rasa</s> — this should be understood.

children.text: upasargāṇāṃ vyañcakatvaṃ yathā--- nīvārāḥ śukagarbhakoṭaramukhabhraṣṭāstaruṇāmadhaḥ prasnigdhāḥ kvacidiṅgudīphalabhidaḥ sūcyanta evopalāḥ /
children.translated_text: The suggestive power of prefixes (<s>upasarga</s>) is illustrated as follows — 'The wild rice grains, fallen from the hollows that serve as nests for parrots in the trees, lie below; in places, the smooth stones that crack open <s>iṅgudī</s> fruits are pointed out;

children.text: viśvāsopagabhādabhinnagatayaḥ śabdaṃ sahante mṛgā- stoyādhārapathāśca valkalaśikhāniṣyandalekhāṅkitāḥ //
children.translated_text: the deer, whose gait is unbroken due to the confidence born of trust, endure sounds without fleeing — and the water-channels are marked with streaks of moisture dripping from the tips of bark garments.'

prasiddhamapīti /

kagrahaṇaṃ taddhitopalakṣaṇārthamiti /

premetyatra kāmeti ca pāṭhaḥ /

'ayam' ityādivikramorvaśīyastham /

'upanataśca 'bhavitavyañje'ti caśabdāvityarthaḥ /

yathā--'prabhraśyatyuttarīyatviṣi samāsi samudvīkṣya vītāvṛtīndrāgjantūn' ityādau /

prakarṣeṇa snigdhā iti praśabdaḥ prakarṣaṃ dyotayanniṅgudīphalānāṃ sarasatvamācakṣāṇa āśramasya saundaryātiśayandhvanati /
'tāpasasya phalaviseṣaviṣayo 'bhilāṣātireko dhvanyate' iti tvasat ; abhijñānaśākuntale hi rājña iyamuktirna tāpasasyetyalam /

children.translated_text: By saying '<s>dvitrāṇām</s>' (two or three), he rules out a greater number.
'Having been fully, loftily, and particularly beheld' — an excess of the Lord's compassion is expressed.
'Him who moves about in human fashion, those of ordinary understanding, making inferences based on their own limited intellect —
O Lord, incomprehensible even to the masters of <s>yoga</s>, the ignorant seek to know You by their own reasoning.'

<s>Locana</s>: By the word '<s>sambandha</s>' (genitive relation), an excess of jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) is expressed by the woman with concealed desire. The mention of '<s>ka</s>' in '<s>kṛtaka</s>' is meant to indicate <s>taddhita</s> suffixes by extension (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). '<s>Kṛtaka</s>' means: poetic expressions in which the <s>ka</s>-suffix is used, as in '<s>jāyābhīrukāṇām</s>' (of those who fear their wives). For those who are ignorant of <s>rasa</s>, who are slavishly devoted to their lawful wives — who else in the world is more contemptible? Thus the <s>ka</s>-suffix suggests an excess of contempt. '<s>Samāsānāṃ ca</s>' (and of compounds) — the connection is: the suggestive power of compounds alone is being indicated. '<s>Caśabda</s>' (the word <s>ca</s>) — the singular is used in a generic sense. The two occurrences of '<s>ca</s>' say this: by the logic of the crow-and-the-palm-fruit (<s>kākatālīya-nyāya</s>) — as when a boil appears on the cheek — both the separation and the rainy season have arrived simultaneously; this alone suffices to take one's life. Hence, by the word '<s>ramya</s>' (lovely), the function of an excitant (<s>uddīpana-vibhāva</s>) is all the more expressed. '<s>Tuśabda</s>' (the word <s>tu</s>) — it suggests subsequent remorse (<s>paścāttāpa</s>): that even if only that much — a mere kiss — had been attained, one would have been fulfilled: such is the purport. '<s>Prasiddham api</s>' (though well-known) — <s>Bālapriyā</s>: the meaning is jealousy caused by attachment to one's wife. 'The mention of <s>ka</s> is meant to indicate <s>taddhita</s> by extension' means: in '<s>kṛtakaprayogeṣu</s>,' the mention of the <s>ka</s>-suffix is a marker for <s>taddhita</s> suffixes beginning with <s>ka</s>. He glosses — '<s>kṛta</s>' etc. The gloss of '<s>ka</s>' is — '<s>kapratyaya</s>' etc. He explains '<s>avajñātiśaye kaḥ</s>' (the suffix <s>ka</s> in the sense of excessive contempt) — '<s>ye</s>' etc. In '<s>prema</s>' (love), the reading '<s>kāma</s>' (desire) also exists. '<s>Kevalānām eva</s>' is supplied. '<s>Ayam</s>' etc. is from the <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s>. '<s>Dvau caśabdau</s>' (the two <s>ca</s>-words) — the meaning is: the <s>ca</s>-words in '<s>upanataśca</s>' and '<s>bhavitavyañca</s>.' And so, the usage of two or three prefixes together in a single word is also directed toward the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> alone. As in '<s>prabhraśyati uttarīyam</s>' etc. and '<s>samudvīkṣya vītāvṛtīn</s>' etc. Or as in '<s>manuṣyavṛttyā samupācarantam</s>' etc. <s>Locana</s>: For in the treatises of grammarians and others, because particles (<s>nipāta</s>) lack prior independent usage, because of the non-occurrence of case-endings like the genitive, and because of the absence of gender and number — on account of their difference from denotative words (<s>vācaka</s>) — it is proclaimed that particles are illuminators (<s>dyotaka</s>): such is the purport. The prefix '<s>pra</s>' in '<s>prasnigdhāḥ</s>' (very smooth), by illuminating intensity, while denoting the succulence of <s>iṅgudī</s> fruits, suggests the surpassing beauty of the hermitage. The interpretation 'the sage's excessive desire for a particular fruit is suggested' is incorrect; for in the <s>Abhijñānaśākuntala</s>, this is the speech of the king, not of the sage. Enough of this.

samyagbhūtamupāṃśukṛtvā ā samantāccarantamityanena lokānujighṛkṣātiśayastattadācarataḥ parameśvarasya dhvanitaḥ /
bālapriyā samayaścetyanantaraṃ dvayamiti śeṣaḥ /

ṣaṣṭhyādyaśravaṇāditi /
yathā candrasya candreṇa vā sadṛśaṃ mukhamityādau ṣaṣṭhyādikaṃ śrūyate, tathā candra ivetyādau ṣaṣṭhyādikaṃ na śrūyate yatastasmādityarthaḥ /
liṅgeti /
nipātārthasyeti śeṣaḥ /
samudvīkṣye' tyetadvyācaṣṭe--samyagityādi /
bhagavataḥ sūryasya /
manuṣyeti /
kṛtābhimānī iti'ca pāṭhaḥ /
samupācarantamityetadvivṛṇoti---samyagityādi /
'ye jīvantī'ti /
ūrjite guṇini dṛṣṭe sata, ye jīvanti sma utkṛṣṭajīvitā abhūvan /
ye prītyā vapuṣi na mānti sma, ye prasyandipramadāśravaḥ pulakitāḥ santaḥ pranṛtyanti smetyādyanvayaḥ /
'sādhuddhiṣa' asajjanān /
sādhudviṣāmiti pāṭhe karmaṇaśśeṣatvavivakṣayā ṣaṣṭhī /
'puṣyatā' poṣayatā /
ye svavapuṣīti pāṭhe tu jīvantītyādau nipātānāmapi tathaiva /
children.translated_text: In the reading '<s>ye svavapuṣi</s>,' particles too function in the same way in '<s>jīvanti</s>' etc.
As in: '<s>aho batāsi spṛhaṇīyavīryaḥ</s>' (Alas! You are one whose valor is to be envied) and so forth.

children.text: yathā vā--- ye jīvanti na mānti ye sma vapuṣi prītyā pranṛtyanti ca prasyandipramadāśravaḥ pulakitā dṛṣṭe guṇinyūrjite /
children.translated_text: Or as in — 'Those who truly lived, who took no pride in their own bodies, who with joy danced with hair standing on end, tears of delight streaming forth, when one endowed with excellent qualities was seen —

children.text: hā dhikkaṣṭamaho kva yāmi śaraṇaṃ teṣāṃ janānāṃ kṛte nītānāṃ pralayaṃ śaṭhena vidhinā sādhudviṣaḥ puṣyatā //
children.translated_text: Alas! Woe! What misery! Where shall I find refuge? For the sake of those people who have been brought to destruction by deceitful fate, which nourishes the enemies of the good!'

By '<s>samyag-bhūtam upāṃśu-kṛtvā ā samantāc carantam</s>' (having become fully present, moving secretly and everywhere) — the supreme Lord's exceeding desire to show compassion to all beings, as He follows various modes of conduct, is suggested. <s>Bālapriyā</s>: After '<s>samayaśca</s>' (and the season), '<s>dvayam</s>' (both) is to be supplied. The two verses beginning with '<s>muhuḥ</s>' are from the <s>Śākuntala</s> and have been explained at length in our commentary on the <s>Śākuntala</s>. He explains the 'well-known' nature — '<s>vaiyākaraṇādi</s>' etc. '<s>Gṛheṣu</s>' (in the treatises) is connected with '<s>uddhoṣyate</s>' (is proclaimed). He states the fourfold reason for the difference from denotative words — '<s>prāk</s>' etc. '<s>Prākprayogasvātantryaprayogābhāvāt</s>' — the preferable reading, analyzed separately, is: '<s>prākprayogāt</s>' (because of prior position) and '<s>svātantryeṇa prayogābhāvāt</s>' (because of the absence of independent usage). The meaning is: because particles designated as <s>upasarga</s> (prefixes), such as '<s>pra</s>' in '<s>prasākṣāt</s>' etc., are used only before the verb-root, and because such particles cannot be used independently without a correlative denotative word. '<s>Ṣaṣṭhyādyaśravaṇāt</s>' (because of the non-occurrence of case-endings) means: just as in '<s>candrasya</s>' or '<s>candreṇa vā sadṛśaṃ mukham</s>' (a face resembling the moon) case-endings like the genitive are heard, so in '<s>candra iva</s>' (like the moon) etc. they are not heard — therefore. '<s>Liṅga</s>' (gender) — '<s>nipātārthasya</s>' (of the meaning of the particle) is to be supplied. He glosses '<s>samudvīkṣya</s>' — '<s>samyak</s>' etc. '<s>Bhagavataḥ</s>' means: of the Lord <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun). '<s>Manuṣya</s>' etc. — the reading '<s>kṛtābhimānī</s>' also exists. He explains '<s>samupācarantam</s>' — '<s>samyak</s>' etc. '<s>Ye jīvanti</s>' — when one endowed with excellent qualities is seen, those who lived truly (<s>utkṛṣṭajīvitāḥ</s>) were those who did not pride themselves on their appearance, who, with tears of joy flowing, stood with hair standing on end and danced with delight — such is the construction. '<s>Sādhudviṣa</s>' means: of the wicked. In the reading '<s>sādhudviṣām</s>,' the genitive is used with the intention of treating the object as a remainder (<s>karmaṇaḥ śeṣatva</s>). '<s>Puṣyatā</s>' means: nourishing, sustaining.
And so forth.
And the repetition of words (<s>padapaunaruktya</s>) too, when employed with a view to suggestive power (<s>vyañjakatva</s>), sometimes produces beauty (<s>śobhā</s>).

children.text: yathā--- yadvañjanāhitamatirbahucāṭugarbhaṃ kāryonmukhaḥ khalajanaḥ kṛtakaṃ bravīti /
children.translated_text: As in — 'Whatever a wicked person, intent on his purpose, speaks — full of abundant flattery, with meaning contrived through suggestion —

children.text: tatsādhavo nana vidanta vidanti kintu kartu vṛthāprāṇayamasya na pārayanti //
children.translated_text: that, the virtuous indeed do understand, they understand it well; but they are unable to render futile the effort of such a person.

children.translated_text: The suggestive capacity of tense (<s>kāla</s>) is as follows —
[Prakrit:] Without distinction of even and uneven, in all directions with gentle-gentle movement,

children.text: airā hohinti pahā maṇorahāṇaṃ pi dullaṅghā //
children.translated_text: soon the roads will become impassable even for wishes! //

etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Just so' — the meaning is: the instruction that even two or three [words] should be employed for their suggestive capacity regarding <s>rasa</s>. /
Excess of praise and excess of world-weariness (<s>nirveda</s>) are suggested by '<s>aho bata</s>' (ah, alas!) and '<s>hā dhik</s>' (alas, fie!) respectively. /
In passing, he states that another kind of repetition too is a suggestor — 'word-repetition' etc. /
The use of '<s>pada</s>' (word) is an indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) that applies also to sentence-repetition etc. as appropriate. /
'They know' — for they indeed know everything supremely — this is what is suggested. /
Sentence-repetition is as follows: after the statement '<s>paśya dvīpād anyasmād api</s>' (look, from another island too), [the repetition] '<s>kaḥ saṃdehaḥ dvīpād anyasmād api</s>' (what doubt, from another island too) — by this, the unobstructed attainment of the desired [object] is suggested. /
'<s>Kiṃ kim? Svasthā bhavanti mayi jīvati</s>' (What? What? Are they well while I am alive?) — by this, the excess of indignation (<s>amarṣa</s>) [is suggested]. /
'<s>Sarvakṣitibhṛtāṃ nātha, dṛṣṭā sarvāṅgasundarī</s>' (O lord of all kings, [she has been] seen — beautiful in every limb) — [this suggests] the excess of madness (<s>unmāda</s>). /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] It should be understood that the past tense (<s>laḍ</s>) is used for proximity to the present. /
In the <s>Locana</s> — 'is suggested' — here, enumeration-correspondence should be understood. /
'[That which is] suggestive' — this is also cited in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. /
'From an island' etc. — this is from the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>. /
'Are well' — this is from the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>. /
'Excess of indignation' — the remainder is: of the speaker, <s>Bhīmasena</s>. /
'Of all kings' etc. — this is from the <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s>. /
'Excess of madness' — the remainder is: of the speaker, <s>Purūravas</s>.
(<s>Chāyā</s>:) Without distinction of even and uneven, in all directions with gentle-gentle movement,
soon the roads will become impassable even for wishes! //

children.text: iti chāyā) atra hyacirādbhaviṣyanti panthāna ityatra bhaviṣyantītyasmin pade pratyayaḥ kālaviśeṣābhidhāyī rasaparipoṣahetuḥ prakāśate /
ayaṃ hi gāthārthaḥ pravāsavipralambhaśṛṅgāravibhāvatayā vibhāvyamāno rasavān /
children.translated_text: For this meaning of the <s>gāthā</s> (verse), when apprehended as a <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) of <s>pravāsa-vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment in separation due to travel), is possessed of <s>rasa</s>.
Just as here the suffix-portion (<s>pratyayāṃśa</s>) is the suggestor, so elsewhere the root-portion (<s>prakṛtyaṃśa</s>) too is observed [as suggestive].

children.text: yathā---tadgehaṃ natamiti mandiramidaṃ labdhāvagāhaṃ divaḥ sā dhenurjaratī caranti kariṇāmetā dhanābhā dhaṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: For example: 'That house — bowed! This mansion — has gained access to the sky! That cow — aged! These elephants roam about! These are pots resembling wealth!

children.text: sa kṣudo musaladhvaniḥ kalamidaṃ saṅgītakaṃ yoṣitā- māścaryaṃ divasaurdvijo 'yamiyatīṃ bhūmiṃ samāropitaḥ //
children.translated_text: That [sound] of the mortar is hunger! This is the music of women! Wonder — this Brahmin of the daytime has been raised to this much land!' //

(Thus the <s>chāyā</s>.) For here, in '<s>acirād bhaviṣyanti panthānaḥ</s>' (soon the roads will become) — in the word '<s>bhaviṣyanti</s>' (will become), the suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>) that denotes a particular tense (<s>kāla</s>) shines forth as the cause of the maturation of <s>rasa</s>.
