children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] But for those [words] whose beauty rests on denotative capacity (<s>vācakatva</s>) — [<s>Locana</s>:] by seeing [them], there is the capacity to convey the meaning that has been rendered beautiful by their habitation, as it were, by a beautiful woman.

children.text: tathāhi-'taṭī tāraṃ tāmyati' ityatra taṭaśabdasya puṇṭaśabdasya puṃstvanapuṃsakatve anādṛtya strītvamevāśritaṃ sahṛdayaiḥ 'strīti nāmāpi madhuraṃ' iti kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: For example — in '<s>taṭī tāraṃ tāmyati</s>' (the bank languishes loudly), the feminine gender alone was adopted by sensitive readers for the word '<s>taṭa</s>' (bank), disregarding the masculine and neuter genders of the word '<s>puṇṭa</s>' — reasoning that 'even the mere name "woman" is sweet.'

children.text: yathā vāsmadupādhyāyasya vidvatkavisahṛdayacakravartino bhaṭṭendurājasya--- indīvaradyuti yadā bibhṛyānna lakṣma syurvismayaikasuhṛdo 'sya yadā vilāsāḥ /
children.translated_text:
As in the [verse] of our teacher, <s>Bhaṭṭa Indurāja</s>, the emperor among learned poets and sensitive readers — /
'When it would not bear the lustre of a blue lotus, when its graces would be the sole friends of wonder,
let it be so by the force of the ripening of merit — yet how could the moon have the tender beauty of [her] cheek?' //

[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Of tense' (<s>kāla</s>) — /
Even of the mass of meaning that has entered into a <s>tiṅanta</s> (finite verbal) word, whose form consists of <s>kāraka</s> (case-relation), tense, number, and <s>upagraha</s> (voice), the suggestive capacity belonging to a [particular] portion should be investigated by one of subtle vision through positive and negative concomitance — this is the purport. /
'Maturation of <s>rasa</s>' — /
The rainy season being imagined [as future] causes trembling — how much more so when it is actually present — thus is suggested. /
Because of the incidental connection of parts and wholes, he says — 'just as here' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The connection is with 'is suggested.' /
He states the purport — '<s>tiṅanta</s>' etc. /
'Entered into a <s>tiṅanta</s> word' — the meaning is: cognizable through the <s>tiṅanta</s> word. /
'<s>Kāraka</s>' etc. — /
The meaning is: whose form consists of the four [factors] beginning with <s>kāraka</s>. /
'<s>Upagraha</s>' — <s>ātmanepada</s> and <s>parasmaipada</s> (middle and active voice) are what is meant by that; the result of the action as intended by the agent, etc. — this much [is the import]. /
'Belonging to a portion' — /
The meaning is: belonging to the tense, which is one component of the four [factors] beginning with <s>kāraka</s>. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>, 'even and uneven' — /
'<s>Samaviṣamāḥ samāḥ</s>' — even; '<s>viṣamāś ca deśāḥ</s>' — and uneven places are without distinction, [i.e.,] of one form due to being submerged by the flow of water — those in which [they are such]. /
'Even for wishes' — /
The word '<s>api</s>' means 'how much more so for people.' /
He explains what was stated as 'the cause of the maturation of <s>rasa</s> shines forth' — 'being imagined' etc. /
'Being imagined' — being inferred as about to come into being shortly. /
'Causes trembling' — /
The remainder is: of people in separation (<s>virahin</s>s). /
'That house' — /
This verse is also cited in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. /
'This much land' — /
The meaning is: the limit of prosperity. /
'<s>Bhūti</s>' is also a reading. /
In this verse, in the word '<s>divasaiḥ</s>' (by days), the root-portion (<s>prakṛtyaṃśa</s>) too is a revealer (<s>dyotaka</s>). /
And the suggestive capacity of pronouns (<s>sarvanāman</s>) is as in the verse stated immediately after. /
And here, having established in the mind precisely the suggestive capacity of the pronouns, the poet did not employ words like '<s>kva</s>' (where) etc. /
In this direction, [the <s>Locana</s> says]: 'In the sense of day' — for here, the <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) is of the absolute impossibility of this meaning [viz. prosperity]. /
'And of pronouns' — /
The meaning is: 'and of the root-portion.' /
Thus, by means of the root-portion, the combined suggestiveness of the pronoun is observed — thus it is stated, and so there is no redundancy. /
For the word '<s>tat</s>' (that) in [the verse] 'That house' — aided by the root-portion of '<s>natabhitti</s>' (bowed walls) — suggests the state of being a repository of all inauspiciousness, [namely] being infested with mice etc., of the house. /
For if '<s>tat</s>' (that) alone were uttered, even an excess of excellence could be envisaged. /
Nor are these specific features — indicators of being an abode of misfortune — stated by the word '<s>natabhitti</s>' (bowed walls) alone either. /
Similarly, in '<s>sā dhenuḥ</s>' (that cow) etc. too, the same should be construed. /
And in such a context, the capacity of the word '<s>tat</s>' (that) to evoke the appearance of remembrance [is operative] — /
but not as connected with the word '<s>yat</s>' (which) — as was stated previously. /
Therefore here, through the words '<s>tat</s>' (that) and '<s>idam</s>' (this) etc., by indicating the utterly contradictory domains of remembrance and present experience, the sense of wonder as a <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) is brought about. /
But in the absence of the words '<s>tat</s>-<s>idam</s>' etc., everything would be incoherent — thus the vitality should be construed as belonging precisely to the '<s>tat</s>' and '<s>idam</s>' portions. /
And this [principle that] the suggestive capacity of two together [or] of three together is to be understood as illustrative (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). /
Thus, by the method of arranging clods [in all possible combinations], infinite variety is indicated. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He explains what was said beginning with '<s>divasaiḥ</s>' — 'the meaning of day' etc. /
'The meaning of day' — the meaning of the root-form '<s>divasa</s>' (day). /
'Of this meaning' — the meaning is: of the meaning that has the form of attainment of prosperity. /
Now, since it was already stated that the root-portion is a revealer, the suggestive capacity of pronouns is already obtained — so saying it again is redundant — to this he says: 'and of the root-portion' etc. /
By the word '<s>ca</s>' (and) in 'and of the pronouns,' the previously stated meaning is obtained — this is the purport. /
He states what is obtained through this explanation — 'thus' etc. /
'The word <s>tat</s>' — /
The meaning is: the word '<s>tat</s>' in '<s>tadgeham</s>' (that house). /
'Suggests' — /
The remainder is: 'of the house.' /
He substantiates the stated combined suggestiveness of the two — '<s>tat</s>' etc. /
'Could be envisaged' — /
The remainder is: as something to be suggested. /
'By the word <s>natabhitti</s> alone' — /
The connection by inversion is: 'by [it] alone.' /
'These specific features' — /
The meaning is: specific features in the form of being infested with mice etc. /
The connection is: 'nor are they stated.' /
The remainder is: 'they would [not] be.' /
The meaning is: the suggestive capacity of the two separately stated meanings would not exist. /
Regarding the [<s>Locana</s> passage] 'in such a context,' he recalls what was stated earlier — 'in such a context' etc. /
'Therefore' — /
The meaning is: precisely because the word '<s>tat</s>' has the capacity to evoke the appearance of remembrance. /
'Of remembrance and experience' — /
The meaning is: of the remembrance cognized through the word '<s>tat</s>' and of the experience cognized through the word '<s>idam</s>' (this). /
'Utterly' — /
The meaning is: by indicating the state of having utterly contradictory domains — [this is the construction]. /
Here it should be understood that 'remembrance' refers to the type of attributes such as having bowed walls and being infested with mice etc., [while] 'experience' refers to the type of attributes stated as 'the day having gained opportunity' etc. /
The construction is: 'brought about by the words <s>tat-idam</s> etc.' /
'Of the <s>tat</s> and <s>idam</s> portions precisely' — /
The meaning is: of '<s>tat</s>' etc. and precisely of '<s>idam</s>' etc. /
'Vitality' — /
The meaning is: the capacity to produce aesthetic delight (<s>camatkāra</s>). /
'And this' etc. — /
The meaning is: the suggestive capacity of two together and of three together is illustrative (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). /
'Indicated' — /
The meaning is: demonstrated. /
Other suggestive particularities too should be independently discerned by sensitive readers (<s>sahṛdaya</s>s). /
And all this, though already conveyed by the very statement that word, sentence, and composition are revealers (<s>dyotaka</s>s), is stated again with variety for the sake of generating understanding (<s>vyutpatti</s>). /
Now, it was said that <s>rasa</s> etc. are evoked by the force of meaning — and so the discussion of the variety of suggestive capacity of <s>sup</s>-endings etc. is incoherent. /
[This was] stated here, on the occasion of stating the suggestive capacity of words. /
Moreover, even though <s>rasa</s> etc. are evoked by particular meanings, because those particular meanings are inseparable from the suggestive words, the examination of the nature of the suggestors, as demonstrated, is useful precisely through analysis. /
And the beauty of particular words as shown elsewhere through classification should be understood as established precisely through their suggestive capacity.

children.text:
atra hīndīvaralakṣmavismayasuhṛdvilāsanāmapariṇāmakomalādayaḥ śabdāḥ śṛṅgārābhivyañjanadṛṣṭaśaktayo 'tra paraṃ saundaryamāvahanti /
avaśyaṃ caitadabhyupagantavyamityāha---ko 'nyatheti /
asaṃvedyastāvadasau na yukta ityāśayenāha--sahṛdayeti /
punariti /
bālapriyā tadānīmiti /
prakṛtaprayogakāla ityarthaḥ /
śṛṅgārātiriktavarṇanasthala iti yāvat /
puṃstvanapuṃsakatve iti /
'taṭaṃ triṣvi' tyanuśāsanaprāpte te ityarthaḥ /
indīvareti /
puṇyapariṇāmavaśādinduḥ indīvaradyuti lakṣya na bimṛyādyadā, asya vilāsāḥ vismayaikasuhṛdaḥ syuḥ yadā, tathāpi kapolatalakomalakāntiḥ kiṃ kiṃ syānnāmeti sambandhaḥ /
yadeti yadītyarthe /
kapoleti /
sundarīkapolatala iva komalakāntirityarthaḥ /
kerīkapoleti pāṭhe kerīśabdaḥ strīviśeṣavācī bodhyaḥ /
kiṃ kiṃ syānnāmeti /
naiva syādityarthaḥ /
atreti /
candraṃ vilokya madhyasthasya kasyacidrasikasya vacana ityarthaḥ /
'anya' ityādiśaṅkāgranthamavatārayati--asaṃvedya ityādi /
asāviti prasāda evārthāpekṣāyāṃ teṣāṃ viśeṣaḥ /
arthānapekṣāyāṃ tvanuprāsādireva /
evaṃ rasādīnāṃ vyañjakasvarūpamabhidhāya teṣāmeva virodhirūpaṃ lakṣayitumidamupakramyate---
children.translated_text:
For here, the words '<s>indīvara</s>' (blue lotus), '<s>lakṣman</s>' (mark/lustre), '<s>vismaya</s>' (wonder), '<s>suhṛd</s>' (friend), '<s>vilāsa</s>' (grace), '<s>nāman</s>' (name/surely), '<s>pariṇāma</s>' (ripening), '<s>komala</s>' (tender), and others — [these] words whose power has been observed in suggesting <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) — bring supreme beauty here. /
And this must necessarily be accepted — he says 'what otherwise' etc. /
That it is not imperceptible — with this intention he says 'by sensitive readers' etc. /
'Again' — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'At that time' — /
The meaning is: at the time of the usage in question; that is, in a context of description other than <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
'Disregarding the masculine and neuter genders' — /
The meaning is: those [genders] obtained by the grammatical rule '<s>taṭaṃ triṣu</s>' (the word <s>taṭa</s> is [used] in all three [genders]). /
'<s>Indīvara</s>' — /
The construction is: the moon (<s>indu</s>), by the force of the ripening of merit, would not bear the lustre of a blue lotus; when its graces would be the sole friends of wonder; even so, how could it have the tender beauty of [her] cheek? /
'<s>Yadā</s>' is in the sense of '<s>yadi</s>' (if). /
'Cheek' — /
The meaning is: tender beauty like [that of] a beautiful woman's cheek-surface. /
In the reading '<s>kerīkapola</s>' — the word '<s>kerī</s>' should be understood as denoting a particular [kind of] woman. /
'How could it be' — /
The meaning is: it could never be. /
'Here' — /
The meaning is: this is the utterance of some dispassionate connoisseur upon beholding the moon. /
He introduces the objection-passage beginning with 'other' — 'imperceptible' etc. /
'That' — the distinction of those [words], when there is regard for meaning, is precisely <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity). /
But when there is no regard for meaning, it is nothing but <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) etc. /
Having thus described the nature of <s>rasa</s> etc. as suggestors, this [section] is commenced in order to define their conflict-form —

children.text: prabandhe muktake vāpi rasādīn bandhum icchatā /
children.translated_text: Whether in a continuous composition (<s>prabandha</s>) or in a standalone verse (<s>muktaka</s>), by one who desires to bind <s>rasas</s> etc.,

children.text: yatnaḥ kāryaḥ sumatinā parihāre virodhinām // DhvK_3.17 //
children.translated_text: effort should be made by the wise-minded one in the avoidance of contradictory elements. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.17 //
Whether in a continuous composition (<s>prabandha</s>) or in a standalone verse (<s>muktaka</s>), by one who desires to bind <s>rasas</s> etc.,
effort should be made by the wise-minded one in the avoidance of contradictory elements. // 17 //

children.text:
prabandhe muktake vāpi rasabhāvanibandhanaṃ pratyādṛtamanāḥ kavirvirodhipahihāre paraṃ yatnamādadhīta /
anyathā tvasya rasamayaḥ śloka eko 'pi samyaṅna samapdyate /
locanam aniyantrītapuruṣecchāyatto hi samayaḥ kathaṃ niyataḥ syāt /
mukhyaṃ cārutvamiti /
viśeṣa iti pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ /
arthāpekṣāyāmiti /
vācyāpekṣāyāmityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: '<s>Anuprāsa</s> etc.' — this is stated. /

children.text: śabdāntareṇa saha yā racanā tadapekṣo 'sau viśeṣa ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the composition (<s>racanā</s>) which is with another word — the particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>) that depends on that. /
By the inclusion [signified by] '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the inclusion of the <s>śabdaguṇālaṅkāras</s> (sound-based ornamental qualities) is [intended]. /

children.text: ata eva racanayā prasādena cārutvena copabṛṃhitā eva śabdāḥ kāvye yojyā iti tātparyam // 15//
children.translated_text: Therefore, the purport is: only words that are enriched by composition (<s>racanā</s>), lucidity (<s>prasāda</s>), and charm (<s>cārutva</s>) should be employed in poetry. // 15 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Whether in a continuous composition or in a standalone verse, the poet whose mind is devoted to the establishment of <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> should make the utmost effort in the avoidance of contradictory elements. /
Otherwise, not even a single verse pervaded by <s>rasa</s> will properly succeed for him. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Unrestrained' — since convention depends on the uncontrolled will of individuals, how can it be fixed? /
'Principal charm' — this is the meaning. /
'Particular' — the connection is with the preceding [statement]. /
'With regard to the requirement of meaning' — /
The meaning is: with regard to the requirement of the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>). /

children.text: rasādīnāṃ yadvyañjakaṃ varṇapadādiprabandhāntaṃ tasya svarūpamabhidhāyeti sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The connection is: having described the nature of the suggestor (<s>vyañjaka</s>) of <s>rasas</s> etc. — extending from phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) and words (<s>pada</s>) up to the composition (<s>prabandha</s>) —
'It is commenced' — this [is stated]. /

children.text: virodhināmapi lakṣaṇakaraṇe prayojanamucyate śakyahānatvaṃ nāma anayā kārikayā /
children.translated_text: The purpose of defining the contradictory elements is stated — namely, 'the possibility of avoidance' — by this <s>kārikā</s>. /
The definition, however, will come [later] beginning with 'that which is related to a contradictory <s>rasa</s>' etc. — this is the meaning. // 17 //

children.text:
nanu 'vibhāvabhāvānubhāvasañcāryaucityacāruṇaḥ' iti yaduktaṃ tata eva vyatirekamukhenaitadapyavagaṃsyate /
maivam ;vyatirekeṇa hi tadabhāvamātraṃ pratīyate na tu tadviruddham /
tadabhāvamātraṃ ca na tathā dūṣakaṃ yathā tadviruddham /
pathyānupayogo hi na tathā vyādhiṃ bālapriyā śabdagato viśeṣa ityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: By [the passage beginning with] 'unrestrained' etc., the purport of the passage beginning with 'again' etc. is stated. /
He explains the meaning of the word '<s>anuprāsa</s>' — 'with another word' etc. /
He states the implication — 'therefore, by composition' etc. /
'Enriched' [means] distinguished, endowed with special qualities. // 15 //

Objection: from what was stated as 'charming with the propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>bhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>sañcārins</s>,' this too would be understood through the method of exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>). /
Not so; for through exclusion, only the mere absence of that is understood, not what is contradictory to it. /
And the mere absence of that is not as damaging as what is contradictory to it. /
For the non-use of a remedy does not [aggravate] the disease as much as — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the meaning is: the particular pertaining to words. /
He states the purport — 'of the contradictory elements also' etc. /

children.text: śakyahānatvaṃ nāma prayojanamanayā kārakayā ucyata iti sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The connection is: the purpose — namely, 'the possibility of avoidance' — is stated by this <s>kārikā</s>. /

children.text: virodhināṃ lakṣaṇe jñāte teṣāṃ parihāraḥ śakya iti tadeva prayojanamityarthaḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: when the definition of the contradictory elements is known, their avoidance becomes possible — that itself is the purpose. // 17 //

children.text:
etadapīti /
virodhināṃ pariharaṇamapītyarthaḥ /
tadabhāvamātramiti /
vibhāvādyaucityaśālinaḥ kathāśarīrasya vidhirityādinā tadaucityavirahiṇo vidhirna kārya ityādyathamātramityarthaḥ /
yatnata itīti /
yatnata ityādinetyarthaḥ /
vṛttau 'śāntā'dīti kāni punastāni virodhīni yāni yatnataḥ kaveḥ parihartavyānītyucyate--
children.translated_text:
'This too' — /
The meaning is: the avoidance of contradictory elements too. /
'Mere absence of that' — /
The meaning is: through the rule of the body of the story possessing propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., [we understand] only the mere negation that a rule lacking such propriety should not be made. /
'With effort' — /
The meaning is: by [the passage beginning with] 'with effort' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, [beginning with] '<s>Śānta</s>' etc. — what then are those contradictory elements that are to be carefully avoided by the poet? — it is stated —
The inclusion of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. that are related to a contradictory <s>rasa</s>, /
the description of another subject matter even when one is elaborately connected [with the current rasa], // <s>DhvK</s> 3.18-19 //

children.text: akāṇḍa eva vicchittir akāṇḍe ca prakāśanam /
children.translated_text: an abrupt interruption, and a sudden bringing to light [of the rasa], /
the repeated illumination even of [a rasa] that has attained full development, /

children.text: rasasya syād virodhāya vṛtty-anaucityam eva ca // DhvK_3.19 //
children.translated_text: and impropriety of literary style (<s>vṛtti</s>) — [all] these would be detrimental to <s>rasa</s>. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.19 //
The inclusion of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. that are related to a contradictory <s>rasa</s>, /
the description of another subject matter even when one is elaborately connected [with the current rasa], // 18 //
an abrupt interruption, and a sudden bringing to light [of the rasa], /
the repeated illumination even of [a rasa] that has attained full development, /
and impropriety of literary style (<s>vṛtti</s>) — [all] these would be detrimental to <s>rasa</s>. // 19 //

children.text:
prastutarasāpekṣayā virodhī yo rasastasya sambandhināṃ vibhāvabhāvānubhāvānāṃ parigraho rasavirodhahetukaḥ sambhavanīyaḥ /
tatra virodhirasavibhāvaparigraho yathā śāntarasavibhāveṣu tadvibhāvatayaiva nirūpiteṣvanantarameva śṛṅgārādivibhāvavarṇane /
virodhirasabhāvaparigraho yathā priyaṃ prati praṇayakalahakupitāsu kāminīṣu vairāgyakathābhiranunaye /
virodhirasānubhāvaparigraho yathā praṇayakupitāyāṃ priyāyāmaprasīdantyāṃ nāyakasya kopāveśavivaśasya raudrānubhāvavarṇane /
locanam janayati yadvadapathyopayogaḥ tadāha---yatnata iti /
'vibhāve'tyādinā ślokena yaduktaṃ tadviruddhaṃ virodhītyādinārdhaślokenāha /
'itavṛtte'tyādinā ślokadvayena yaduktaṃ tadviruddhaṃ vistareṇetyardhaślokenāha /
'uddīpane'tyardhaślokoktasya viruddhaṃ akāeḍa ityardhaślokena /
'rasasye'tyardhaślokoktasya viruddhaṃ paripoṣaṃ gatasyetyardhaślokena /
'alaṅkṛtīnām' ityanena yaduktaṃ tadviruddhamanyadapi ca viruddhaṃ vṛtyanaucityamityanena /
etatkrameṇa vyācaṣṭe---prastutarasāpekṣayetyādinā /
hāsyaśṛṅgārayorvīrādbhutayo raudrakaruṇayorbhayānakabībhatsayorna vibhāvavirodha ityabhiprāyeṇa śāntaśṛṅgārāvupanyastau, praśamarāgayorvirodhāt /
virodhinī rasasya yo bhāvo vyabhicārī tasya parigrahaḥ, virodhinastu yaḥ sthāyī sthāyitayā bālapriyā 'śṛṅgārādī'ci ca nirdeśe bījamāha---hāsyaśṛṅgārayārityādi /
bhayānakabībhatsayorityasyānantaraṃ "śāntabībhatsayo"riti ca kvacit granthe pāṭhaḥ /
śāntaśṛṅgārayorvirodhe hetumāha---praśameti /
virodhāditi /
sahānavasthānādatyarthaḥ /
pratipattaryekasmin śame udbuddhe tadavyavadhānena rāgodbodhāsambhavāditi bhāvaḥ /
ataḥ śāntavibhāve varṇite tadanantarameva śṛṅgārādivibhāvavarṇanaṃ na kāyam /
virodhirasasyetyādigranthaṃ ayaṃ cānyo rasabhaṅgaheturyatprastutarasāpekṣayā vastuno 'nyasya kathañcidanvitasyāpi vistareṇa kathanam /
yathā vipralambhaśṛṅgāre nāyakasya kasyacadvarṇayitumupakrānte kaveryamakādyalaṅkāranibandhanarasikatayā mahatā prabandhena parvatādivarṇane /
ayaṃ cāparo rasabhaṅgaheturavagantavyo yadakāṇḍa locanam tatparigraho 'sambhavanīya eva tadanutthānaprasaṅgāt /
vyabhicāritayā tu paragraho bhavatyeva /
ata eva sāmānyena bhāvagrahaṇam /
vairāgyakathāmirita vairāgyaśabdena nirvedaḥ śāntasya yaḥ sthāyī sa uktaḥ /
yathā---'prasāde vartasva prakaṭaya mudaṃ santyaja ruṣam' ityādyupakramyārthāntaranyāso 'na mugdhe pratyetuṃ prabhavati gataḥ kālahariṇaḥ' iti /
manāgapa nirvedānupraveśe sati ratervicchedaḥ /
jñātaviṣayasatattvo hi jīvitasarvasvābhimānaṃ kathaṃ bhajeta /
na hi jñātaśuktikārajatatattvastadupādeyadhiyaṃ bhajate ṛte saṃvṛtimātrāt /
kathābhiriti bahuvacanaṃ śāntarasasya vyabhicāriṇo dhṛtiṃ matiprabhṛtīn saṅgṛhṇāta /
nanvanyadanunmattaḥ kathaṃ varṇayet, kimuta vistarata ityāha---kathañjidanvitasyeti bālapriyā vivṛṇoti---virodhina ityādi /
tadanutthānaprasaṅgāditi /
tasya sthāyitvenotthāne prasaṅgasyābhāvādityarthaḥ /
tadutthāne prakṛtasthāyino vicchedaḥ syāditi bhāvaḥ /
sāmānyenetyādi /
svata eva vyabhicāriṇaḥ vyabhicāratvena sthāyinaśca bodhanāya bhāva iti sāmānyata uktamityathaḥ /
prasāda iti /
kāvyaprakāśe 'pyudāhṛto 'yaṃ ślokaḥ /
'priye śuṣyantyaṅgānyabhṛtamiva te siñcitu vacaḥ /
nidhānaṃ saukhyānāṃ kṣaṇamabhimukhaṃ sthāpaya mukham' iti dvitīyatṛtīyapādau /
he mugdhe vivekarahite, gataḥ kāla eva hariṇaḥ asthiratvāt pratyetuṃ pratyāgantum na prabhavati sa punarnāgacchatītyarthaḥ /
atra śāntasya vibhāvaḥ kālānityatvalakṣaṇo nibandhaḥ tatprakāśito nirvedo vyabhicārī cetyato 'tra virodhirasavibhāvabhāvayoḥ parigrahaḥ sa ca prakṛtarasapratikūla ityāha---manāgapītyādi /
nirvedānuvedhe iti ca pāṭhaḥ /
vicchada iti /
bhavediti śeṣaḥ /
atra hetumāha---jñātetyādi /
jñātaṃ viṣayāṇāṃ satatvaṃ duḥkhamiśritatvapariṇāmavirasatvādinā heyatvarūpaṃ tattvaṃ yena saḥ /
jīvitasarvasvābhimānamiti /
vanitādau viṣaya iti śeṣaḥ /
bhajetetyatra karotviti ca pāṭhaḥ /
dṛṣṭāntamāha--na hītyādi /
śuktau bhāsamānaṃ rajataṃ śuktikārajatamityucyate, jñātaṃ śuktikārajatatatvaṃ yena saḥ /
taditi /
tadviśeṣyakopādeyatvabuddhimityarthaḥ /
saṃvṛtimātrādṛta iti /
saṃvṛttyaiva tatropādeyatvabuddhiṃ bhajata iti bhāvaḥ /
saṃvṛtiravidyā bhramarūpā tadvṛttirvā vṛttau 'kathañcidanvitasye'ti /
yayā kayāpi vidhayā prakṛtena sambaddhasyetyarthaḥ /
etadgranthamavatārayati---nanvityādi /
api tāvaditi śabdābhyāmiti /
eva vicchittiḥ rasasyākāṇḍa eva ca prakāśanam /
tatrānavasare virāmo rasasya yathā nāyakasya kasyacitspṛhaṇīyasamāgamayā nāyikayā kayācitparāṃ paripoṣapadarvī prāpte śṛṅgāre vidite ca paramparānurāge samāgamopāyacintocitaṃ vyavahāramutsṛjya svatantratayā vyāpārāntaravarṇane /
anavasare ca prakāśanaṃ rasasya yathā pravṛtte pravṛttavividhavīrasaṅkṣaye kalpasaṅkṣayakalpe saṅgrame rāmadevaprāyasyāpi tāvannāyakasyānupakrāntavipralambhaśṛṅgārasya nimittamucitamantareṇaiva śṛṅgārakathāyāmavatāravarṇane /
na caivaṃvidhe viṣaye daivavyāmohitatvaṃ kathāpuruṣasya parihāro yato rasabandha eva kaveḥ prādhānyena pravṛttinibandhanaṃ yuktam /
itivṛttavarṇanaṃ tadupāya evetyuktaṃ prāk 'ālokārthī yathā dīpaśikhāyāṃ yatnavāñjanaḥ' ityādinā /
ata eva cetivṛttamātravarṇanaprādhānye 'ṅgāṅgibhāvarahitarasabhāvanibandhena ca kavīnāmevaṃvidhāni skhalitāni bhavantīti rasādirūpavyaṅgyatātparyamevaiṣāṃ locanam vyāpārāntareti /
yathāvatsarājacarite caturthe 'ṅke--ratnāvalīnāmadheyamapyagṛṅṇato vijayavarmavṛttāntavarṇane /
api tāvaditi śabdābhyāṃ duryodhanādestadvarṇanaṃ dūrāpāstamiti veṇīsaṃhāre dvitīyāṅkamevodāharaṇatvena dhvanati /
ata eva vakṣyati--'daivavyāmohitatvam' iti /
pūrvaṃ tu sandhyaṅgābhiprāyeṇa pratyudāharaṇamuktam /
kathāpuruṣasyeti pratināyakasyeti yāvat /
ata eva ceti /
yato rasabandha eva mukhyaḥ kavivyāpāraviṣayaḥ itivṛttamātravarṇanaprādhānye bālapriyā rāmadevaprāyasyāpi tāvadityatratyābhyāṃ tāmyāmityarthaḥ /
dhvanatītyanenāsya sambandhaḥ /
tadvarṇanamiti /
saṅgrāme pravṛtte nimittamucitamantareṇaiva śṛṅgāravarṇanamityarthaḥ /
ata eveti /
dvitīyāṅkasya udāharaṇatvena dhvananādevetyarthaḥ /
daivavyāmohitatvamiti /
daivena vyāmohitaḥ kṛtyākṛtyavivekarāhityaṃ prāpitastatvamityarthaḥ /
veṇīsaṃhāre duryodhanasya tadgamyata iti bhāvaḥ /
yathā veṇīsaṃhāre iti pūrvamuktamanyābhiprāyeṇeti smārayati--pūrvamityādi /
kathāpuruṣasyetyanena vivakṣitamāha--pratināyakasyeti /
na tu pradhānanāyakasyetyarthaḥ /
tasya tathātvenaucityāpātāditi bhāvaḥ /
vṛttau 'rasabandha' iti prathamāntaṃ rasānukūlaśabdārthanibandha ityarthaḥ /
pravṛttinibandhanamiti /
pravṛttiviṣaya ityarthaḥ /
yadvā rasabandhe iti saptamyantam /
'pravṛttinibandhanaṃ' pravṛtteḥ sambandho viṣayatetyarthaḥ /
'ata eve'tyasyārabdha ityanena sambandhaḥ /
locane vyācaṣṭe---yata ityādi /
vṛttau prādhānye sati yadibandhanaṃ tasminniti sambandhaḥ /
yuktamiti yatno 'smābhirārabdho na dhvanipratipādanamātrābhiniveśena /
punaścāyamanyo rasabhaṅgaheturavadhāraṇīyo yatparipoṣaṃ gatasyāpi rasasya paunaḥ--punyena dīpanam /
ubhayukto hi rasaḥ svasāmagrīlabdhaparipoṣaḥ punaḥ punaḥ parāmṛśyamāṇaḥ parimlānakusumakalpaḥ kalpate /
tathā vṛttervyavahārasya yadanaucityaṃ tadapi rasabhaṅgahetureva /
yathā nāyakaṃ prati nāyikāyāḥ kasyāściducitāṃ bhaṅgimantareṇa svayaṃ sambhogābhilāṣakathane /
yadi vā vṛttīnāṃ bharataprasiddhānāṃ kaiśikyādīnāṃ kāvyālaṅkārāntaraprasiddhānāmupanāgarikādyānāṃ vā yadanaucityamaviṣaye nibandhanaṃ tadapi rasabhaṅgahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, the impropriety of styles — whether those well known from <s>Bharata</s> such as <s>kaiśikī</s> etc., or those known from other <s>kāvyālaṅkāra</s> texts such as <s>upanāgarika</s> (refined) etc. — their inappropriate application is also a cause of <s>rasa</s>-disruption.

children.text: evameṣāṃ rasavirodhināmanyeṣāṃ cānayā diśā svayamutprekṣitānāṃ parihāre satkavibhiravahitairbhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: Thus, good poets should be careful in avoiding these things that are antagonistic to <s>rasa</s>, as well as others that may be conceived by oneself in this direction.
And the attendant verses here are: '<s>Rasa</s> etc. are the primary domains of activity for good poets;
in their composition, they should always be attentive and vigilant.' //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] The inclusion of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions), and <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) belonging to a <s>rasa</s> that is antagonistic with respect to the <s>rasa</s> at hand — that should be understood as a cause of <s>rasa</s>-conflict. /
Therein, the inclusion of a <s>vibhāva</s> of an antagonistic <s>rasa</s> is as follows: when the <s>vibhāvas</s> of <s>śānta rasa</s> (quiescent sentiment) have just been described in their capacity as <s>vibhāvas</s>, immediately afterward describing the <s>vibhāvas</s> of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) etc. /
The inclusion of a <s>bhāva</s> of an antagonistic <s>rasa</s> is as follows: when heroines are angry with the hero due to a lovers' quarrel, [attempting] reconciliation through talk of world-weariness (<s>vairāgya</s>). /
The inclusion of an <s>anubhāva</s> of an antagonistic <s>rasa</s> is as follows: when the beloved heroine, angry from love, does not relent, describing the <s>anubhāvas</s> of <s>raudra</s> (the furious) of the hero who is overcome by an onset of anger. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Just as the consumption of unwholesome food [causes harm] — he says this — 'with effort' etc. /
What was stated by the verse beginning with '<s>vibhāve</s>' — the contradictory [of that] is stated by the half-verse beginning with '<s>virodhī</s>.' /
What was stated by the two verses beginning with '<s>itavṛtte</s>' — the contradictory [of that] is stated by the half-verse beginning with '<s>vistareṇa</s>.' /
What was stated in the half-verse beginning with '<s>uddīpane</s>' — the contradictory [of that is stated] by the half-verse beginning with '<s>akāṇḍa</s>.' /
What was stated in the half-verse beginning with '<s>rasasya</s>' — the contradictory [of that is stated] by the half-verse beginning with '<s>paripoṣaṃ gatasya</s>.' /
What was stated by '<s>alaṅkṛtīnām</s>' — the contradictory [of that], and other contradictories too, [are stated] by '<s>vṛtty-anaucitya</s>' (impropriety of style). /
He explains these in order — beginning with 'with respect to the <s>rasa</s> at hand' etc. /
<s>Hāsya</s> (comic) and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous), <s>raudra</s> (furious) and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible) and <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting) — among these there is no <s>vibhāva</s>-conflict — with this intention, <s>śānta</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> are presented [as examples], because of the conflict between tranquility (<s>praśama</s>) and passion (<s>rāga</s>). /
The inclusion of a <s>bhāva</s> (transitory emotion) of a <s>rasa</s> that is antagonistic — the <s>bhāva</s> here is the <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion); but a <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) that is antagonistic — [its inclusion] in its capacity as a <s>sthāyin</s> — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He states the basis for the designation '<s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc.' — '<s>hāsya</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s>' etc. /
After '<s>bhayānaka</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s>' the reading '<s>śānta</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s>' is also found in some texts. /
He states the reason for the conflict between <s>śānta</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> — '<s>praśama</s>' etc. /
'Because of conflict' — the meaning is: because they cannot coexist. /
When tranquility has been aroused in the cognizer, the arousal of passion immediately thereafter without interruption is impossible — this is the purport. /
Therefore, after describing the <s>vibhāvas</s> of <s>śānta</s>, the description of <s>vibhāvas</s> of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc. immediately afterward should not be done. /
He introduces the passage beginning with 'of the antagonistic <s>rasa</s>' — and this is another cause of <s>rasa</s>-disruption: with respect to the <s>rasa</s> at hand, the detailed narration of some other matter that is somehow connected. /
For example, in <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment in separation), when the poet has begun to describe a certain hero, through delight in composing <s>alaṅkāras</s> like <s>yamaka</s> (paronomasia) etc., [he engages in] a lengthy description of mountains etc. /
And this is yet another cause of <s>rasa</s>-disruption that should be understood: that untimely — [<s>Locana</s>:] that inclusion [of the <s>sthāyin</s>] is simply impossible, because there would then be the consequence of that [<s>rasa</s>] not arising [as such]. /
But its inclusion as a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) can indeed occur. /
Precisely for this reason, the general term '<s>bhāva</s>' is used. /
'Talk of world-weariness' — by the word '<s>vairāgya</s>' (world-weariness), <s>nirveda</s> (disillusionment), which is the <s>sthāyin</s> of <s>śānta</s>, is meant. /
As for example — beginning with '<s>prasāde vartasva prakaṭaya mudaṃ santyaja ruṣam</s>' (Dwell in serenity, show your joy, abandon your anger) and then presenting an <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) — '<s>na mugdhe pratyetuṃ prabhavati gataḥ kālahariṇaḥ</s>' (O naive one, the deer of time that has gone cannot return). /
Even a slight entry of <s>nirveda</s> causes the disruption of <s>rati</s> (romantic love). /
For how would one who has known the true nature of sense-objects cherish the conceit that [those objects are] the very essence of life? /
For one who has known the true nature of nacre-silver does not cherish the notion that it is worth acquiring — except through mere conventional appearance. /
The plural 'by talks' includes <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), <s>mati</s> (deliberation), and other <s>vyabhicārins</s> of <s>śānta rasa</s>. /
But how would anyone who is not mad describe [such matters], let alone in detail? — to this he says: 'somehow connected' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] He elaborates — 'of the antagonistic' etc. /
'Because there would then be the consequence of that not arising' — the meaning is: because there is no occasion for its arising as a <s>sthāyin</s>. /
The purport is: if it arose [as a <s>sthāyin</s>], there would be a disruption of the <s>sthāyin</s> at hand. /
'In general' etc. — /
The meaning is: the term '<s>bhāva</s>' is used generally in order to convey both the <s>vyabhicārin</s> by its own nature and the <s>sthāyin</s> [functioning] as a <s>vyabhicārin</s>. /
'Serenity' — this verse has also been cited in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. /
The second and third <s>pādas</s> are: '<s>priye śuṣyanty aṅgāny abhṛtam iva te siñcatu vacaḥ / nidhānaṃ saukhyānāṃ kṣaṇam abhimukhaṃ sthāpaya mukham</s>' (Beloved, your limbs are withering — let my words water [them] like an unwatered [plant]; O treasury of happiness, turn your face toward [me] for a moment). /
O naive one, devoid of discrimination — the deer of time that has gone cannot return, it does not come back again — this is the meaning. /
Here, the foundation characterized by the impermanence of time is a <s>vibhāva</s> of <s>śānta</s>; <s>nirveda</s>, which is thereby manifested, is a <s>vyabhicārin</s> — therefore here is the inclusion of both <s>vibhāva</s> and <s>bhāva</s> of the antagonistic <s>rasa</s>; and that is adverse to the <s>rasa</s> at hand — he says: 'even slightly' etc. /
'<s>Nirvedānuvedhe</s>' (penetration of <s>nirveda</s>) is also a reading. /
'Disruption' — the remainder is: 'would occur.' /
Here he states the reason — 'one who has known' etc. /
'One who has known the true nature of sense-objects' — one by whom the true nature (<s>tattva</s>) of sense-objects — characterized by being to be abandoned because of being mixed with suffering, becoming insipid through transformation, etc. — has been known. /
'The conceit that [they are] the very essence of life' — the remainder is: toward women etc. as sense-objects. /
'Would cherish' — 'would do' is also a reading. /
He gives an illustration — 'for' etc. /
'Nacre-silver' — silver appearing in nacre is called nacre-silver; one by whom the true nature of nacre-silver has been known. /
'That' — the meaning is: the notion that it is worth acquiring with reference to that [nacre-silver]. /
'Except through mere conventional appearance' — the purport is: only through <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional reality) does one cherish that notion of worthiness. /
'<s>Saṃvṛti</s>' means <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), the form of error, or its operation. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'somehow connected' — /
The meaning is: connected with the matter at hand by some means or other. /
He introduces this passage — 'but' etc. /
'By the two words <s>api tāvat</s> (even so far)' — /
'<s>Eva</s>' signifies the interruption of <s>rasa</s>, and '<s>akāṇḍa</s>' signifies the untimely disclosure. /
Therein, the cessation of <s>rasa</s> at an inappropriate moment — as when, after <s>śṛṅgāra</s> has reached its full maturation through the hero's [coming together with] a certain heroine whose union is eagerly desired, and when the mutual love is known, [the poet], abandoning the conduct appropriate to contemplating the means of union, independently describes other activities. /
And the disclosure of <s>rasa</s> at an inappropriate moment — as when, in a battle that has commenced, resembling the destruction at the end of an age, with the destruction of various heroes underway, for a hero like <s>Rāmadeva</s>, [the poet] describes his entering into a narration of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> without an appropriate occasion, even though the <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment in separation) has not been initiated. /
Nor in such a case is the defense that the character in the story is deluded by fate [valid], because it is proper that the poet's primary motivation should be the weaving of <s>rasa</s>. /
The narration of events is merely the means to that — this was stated earlier by '<s>ālokārthī yathā dīpaśikhāyāṃ yatnavāñjanaḥ</s>' (as one who desires light takes care of the lamp-flame) etc. /
Precisely for this reason, when the narration of mere events predominates, and through the composition of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s> devoid of the principal-subsidiary relationship, such lapses occur for poets — [this shows that] the purport should be the suggested [meaning] in the form of <s>rasa</s> etc. — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'Other activities' — /
As in the <s>Vatsarājacarita</s>, in the fourth act — the narration of the affairs of <s>Vijayavarman</s> without even mentioning the name <s>Ratnāvalī</s>. /
'By the two words <s>api tāvat</s>' — the description of that [untimely śṛṅgāra] by <s>Duryodhana</s> etc. having been completely rejected — this suggests the second act of the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> itself as the illustration. /
Precisely for this reason, he will say: 'delusion by fate' etc. /
But previously, the counter-example was stated with the intention [of illustrating] the elements of dramatic juncture (<s>sandhyaṅga</s>). /
'The character in the story' — that is to say, the antagonist. /
Precisely for this reason — since the weaving of <s>rasa</s> alone is the primary domain of the poet's activity — when the narration of mere events predominates — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'like <s>Rāmadeva</s>, even so much' — by the two [words 'api tāvat'] here, the meaning is 'even so.' /
'Suggests' — this connects with [the preceding]. /
'That description' — the meaning is: the description of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> in the midst of battle without appropriate occasion. /
'Precisely for this reason' — the meaning is: precisely because the second act suggests [this]. /
'Delusion by fate' — the meaning is: deluded by fate, having attained the state of lacking discrimination between what should and should not be done. /
In the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>, this is understood of <s>Duryodhana</s> — this is the purport. /
What was previously stated in the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> with a different intention — he reminds [us of this] — 'previously' etc. /
'The character in the story' — he states what is intended by this — 'the antagonist.' /
Not the principal hero — this is the meaning. /
Because for him, such [behavior] would not be fitting — this is the purport. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, '<s>rasabandha</s>' — in the nominative, meaning: the weaving of words and meanings favorable to <s>rasa</s>. /
'The basis of activity' — the meaning is: the domain of activity. /
Alternatively, '<s>rasabandhe</s>' is in the locative. /
'The basis of activity' — the meaning is: the connection of activity is its domain. /
The connection of 'precisely for this reason' is with 'has been begun.' /
In the <s>Locana</s>, he explains — 'because' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, when predominance exists, in that basis — this is the connection. /
'Proper' means: the effort begun by us is not [merely] out of attachment to the exposition of <s>dhvani</s> alone. /
And moreover, this is yet another cause of <s>rasa</s>-disruption that should be noted: the repeated illumination of a <s>rasa</s> that has already attained its full maturation. /
For a <s>rasa</s> [treated] in both ways — having attained maturation through its own complete ensemble [of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc.] — when reviewed again and again, becomes like a wilted flower. /
Likewise, the impropriety of style or conduct — that too is indeed a cause of <s>rasa</s>-disruption. /
As when a certain heroine, without the appropriate coquettish behavior toward the hero, declares her own desire for union by herself.

children.text: nīrasastu prabandho yaḥ so 'paśabdo mahān kaveḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A composition devoid of <s>rasa</s> is a great blemish for the poet;
by that [fault], he would be a non-poet; by other [faults], merely one who has not observed the rules.' //

children.text:
locanam sati yadaṅgāṅgibhāvarahitānāmavicāritaguṇapradhānabhāvānāṃ rasabhāvānāṃ nibandhanaṃ tannimittāni skhalitāni sarve doṣā ityarthaḥ /
na dhvanipratipādanamātreti /
vyaṅgyo 'rtho bhavatu mā vā bhūt kastatrābhiniveśaḥ? kākadantaparīkṣāprāyameva tatsyāditi bhāvaḥ /
vṛttyanaucityameva cetibahudā vyācaṣṭe tadapītyanena caśabdaṃ kārikāgataṃ vyācaṣṭe /
rasabhaṅgahetureva ityanenaivakārasya kārikāgatasya bhinnakramatvamuktam /
rasasya virodhāyaivetyarthaḥ /
nāyakaṃ pratīti /
nāyakasya hi dhīrodāttādibhedabhinnasya sarvathā vīrarasānuvedhena bhavitavyamiti taṃ prati kātarapuruṣocitamadhairyayojanaṃ duṣṭameva /
teṣāmiti rasādīnām /
tairiti sukavibhiḥ /
so 'paśabda iti duryaśa ityarthaḥ /
nanu kālidāsaḥ bālapriyā cakārau vākyālaṅkāre ityāśayena vyācaṣṭe---itivṛttetyādi /
bahudhā vyācaṣṭa iti /
vṛttervyavahārasyetyādinā rasabhaṅgaheturityantagranthena tredhā vyācaṣṭa ityarthaḥ /
tadapītyaneneti /
tatpadottarāpiśabdenetyarthaḥ /
nāyakaṃ prati nāyakayā svayaṃ sambhogābhilāṣasya kathane nibaddhe nāyakasyādhairyayojanamāpatati, tacca duṣṭamiti bhāvaṃ vivṛṇoti---nāyakasyetyādi /
bhāvitavyamiti /

children.translated_text: '<s>Kātarapuruṣa</s>' (timid man) —
The meaning is: a man who lacks boldness (<s>adhīra</s>).

children.text: vṛttau 'ucitāṃ bhaṅgimantareṇe' pūrve viśṛṅkhalagiraḥ kavayaḥ prāptakīrtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>vṛtti</s>, [the passage] 'without a fitting turn of expression' (<s>ucitāṃ bhaṅgim antareṇa</s>) — 'The earlier poets, whose speech was unrestrained, attained fame;
relying on them, this policy should not be abandoned by the wise.' //

[Locana:] When there is no principal-subordinate relation (<s>aṅgāṅgibhāva</s>), the compositions of <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> that have unconsidered quality-principal relations — the stumbling-blocks occasioned by them are all faults — this is the meaning. /
'Not merely the exposition of <s>dhvani</s>' — /
Let there be a suggested meaning or let there not be — what obsession is there with that? That would amount to examining the teeth of a crow — this is the purport. /
He explains 'the impropriety of the <s>vṛtti</s> (style) itself' in many ways — by 'that too,' he explains the word '<s>ca</s>' occurring in the <s>kārikā</s>. /
'Is itself the cause of <s>rasa</s>-disruption' — by this, the different ordering of the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone) occurring in the <s>kārikā</s> is stated. /
The meaning is: for the very opposition to <s>rasa</s>. /
'Toward the hero' — /
For the hero, who is distinguished by types such as <s>dhīrodātta</s> (calm and exalted) etc., must in every way be permeated by <s>vīra-rasa</s> (the heroic sentiment); therefore, the attribution of cowardice appropriate to a timid man toward him is indeed a fault. /
'Of those' means: of <s>rasas</s> etc. /
'By them' means: by good poets. /
'That ill-repute' (<s>apaśabda</s>) means: bad reputation — this is the meaning. /
Now, <s>Kālidāsa</s> — [Bālapriyā:] with the intention that both [uses of] '<s>ca</s>' are sentence-ornaments (<s>vākyālaṅkāra</s>), she explains — 'of the <s>vṛtti</s>' etc. /
'Explains in many ways' — /
The meaning is: by the passage from 'of the <s>vṛtti</s>, of usage' up to 'is itself the cause of <s>rasa</s>-disruption,' [the commentator] explains in three ways. /
'By that too' — /
The meaning is: by the word '<s>api</s>' following the word '<s>tat</s>.' /
Toward the hero — when the heroine herself composes the narration of her desire for union, [if] cowardice is attributed to the hero, that is faulty — he elucidates this purport: 'of the hero' etc. /
'Must be so' — /
The purport is: because all [heroes] are conventionally referred to by the word '<s>vīra</s>' (heroic).
'And the foremost lord-poets, headed by <s>Vālmīki</s> and <s>Vyāsa</s>, who are renowned —
this principle shown by us is not contrary to their intention.' //
Thus. /
When the intended <s>rasa</s> has been well-established, the statement of those that are opposed [to it] —

children.text: bādhyānām aṅga-bhāvaṃ vā prāptānām uktir acchalā // DhvK_3.20 //
children.translated_text: those that are suppressible, or those that have attained subordinate status — is without fault. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.20 //
When the intended <s>rasa</s> has been well-established, the statement of those that are opposed [to it] —
those that are suppressible, or those that have attained subordinate status — is without fault. // 20 //

children.text:
svasāmagnyā labdhaparipoṣe tu vivakṣite rase virodhināṃ virodhirasāṅgānāṃ bādhyānāmaṅgabhāvaṃ vā prāptanāṃ satāmuktiradoṣā /
bādhyatvaṃ hi virodhināṃ śakyābhibhavatve sati nānyathā /
tathāca teṣāmuktiḥ prastutarasaparipoṣāyaiva sampadyate /
aṅgabhāvaṃ prāptānāṃ ca teṣāṃ virodhitvameva nivartate /
aṅgabhāvaprāptirhi teṣāṃ svābhāvikī samāropakṛtā vā /
tatra yeṣāṃ naisargikī teṣāṃ tāvaduktāvavirodha eva /
yathā vipralambhaśṛṅgāre tadaṅgānāṃ locanam paripoṣaṃ gatasyāpi karuṇasya rativilāseṣu paunaḥpunyena dīpanamakārṣīt, tatko 'yaṃ rasavirodhināṃ parihāranirbandha ityāśaṅkyāha--pūrva iti /
children.translated_text: Just as in <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation), of its constituent elements — [Locana:] Even though <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos) has attained fullness, [the poet] made it repeatedly kindle the amorous sports (<s>rati-vilāsa</s>) — then what is this insistence on avoiding those that conflict with <s>rasa</s>? — anticipating this objection, he says: 'the earlier' etc.

children.text: na hi vasiṣṭhādibhiḥ kathañcidyadi smṛtimārgastyaktastadvayamapi tathā tyajāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: For if [the path of] <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) has been abandoned somehow by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and others, we do not thereby abandon both [paths] in that manner.
Because the conduct of those above is of inconceivable causation — this is the purport.
By the word '<s>iti</s>' he indicates the completion of the ancillary verses (<s>parikara-śloka</s>). // 19 //

[Vṛtti:] When the intended <s>rasa</s>, having attained fullness through its own capacities, has been well-established — the statement of those that are opposed, [namely] the constituent elements (<s>aṅgas</s>) of opposing <s>rasas</s>, [of those] that are suppressible, or that have attained subordinate status — is without fault. /
For the suppressibility of those that are opposed [obtains] only when they can be overpowered — not otherwise. /
And thus, the statement of those [opposing elements] conduces precisely to the fullness of the principal <s>rasa</s>. /
And of those that have attained subordinate status, the very opposition ceases. /
For the attainment of subordinate status by those [elements] is either natural or superimposed. /
Therein, for those whose [subordination] is innate, there is indeed no conflict even in their statement.

children.text:
evaṃ virodhināṃ parihāre sāmānyenokte pratiprasavaṃ viyataviṣayamāha---vivakṣita itī /
bādhyānāmiti /
bādhyatvābhiprāyeṇāṅgatvābhiprāyeṇa vetyarthaḥ /
acchalā nirdeṣetyarthaḥ /
bādhyatvābhiprāyaṃ vyācaṣṭe--bādhyatvaṃ hīti /
āṅgabhāvābhiprāyamubhayathā vyācaṣṭe, bālapriyā tyenena bhaṅgyā tatkathanaṃ duṣyantādernāyakasyeva nāyikāyā api na doṣa iti darśitam /
bhāvārthamāha--na hītyādi /

children.translated_text: 'For we do not abandon' — this is the syntactic connection.
Even if <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and others abandon that, it is not a fault — he says: 'of inconceivable' etc.
'<s>Uparacaritānām</s>' (of those whose conduct is above) is also a reading.
The meaning of '<s>uparicaritānām</s>' is: of those whose conduct is exalted. // 19 //

Thus, having stated the avoidance of conflicting [rasas] in general, he states the exception and its domain — 'when the intended' etc. /
'Of those that are suppressible' — /
The meaning is: with the intention of suppressibility, or with the intention of subordination. /
'Without fault' means: without defect — this is the meaning. /
He explains the intention of suppressibility — 'for the suppressibility' etc. /
He explains the intention of subordination in two ways — [Bālapriyā:] by this turn of expression, that narration [when applied] to not only the hero (<s>dūṣyanta</s>) etc. but also to the heroine is not a fault — this is shown. /
She states the purport — 'for' etc.

children.translated_text: Therein, in such a context —
Of this, [namely] of death —

children.text: kāvyānuśāsane 'pyevamuktam--"śṛṅgāre tu maraṇādhyavasāyo tatra labdhapratiṣṭhe tu vivakṣite rase virodhirasāṅgānāṃ bādhyatvenoktāvadoṣo yathā--- kvākāryaṃ śaśalakṣmaṇaḥ kva ca kulaṃ bhūyo 'pi dṛśyeta sā doṣāṇāṃ praśamāya me śrutamaho kope 'pi kāntaṃ mukham /
children.translated_text: It has been stated thus even in the <s>Kāvyānuśāsana</s> — 'In <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, the determination of death — when the intended <s>rasa</s> has been well-established, the statement of the constituent elements of conflicting <s>rasas</s>, when they are suppressible, is without fault — as for example: "What business has the moon here? Where is [my noble] family? Would that she might be seen again! For the pacification of [my] faults, I have heard — ah, even in anger the face of the beloved [is beautiful]!

children.text: kiṃ vakṣyantyapakalmaṣāḥ kṛtadhiyaḥ svapne 'pi sā durlabhā cetaḥ svāsthyamupaihi kaḥ khalu yuvā dhanyo 'dharaṃ pāsyati //
children.translated_text: What will those of purified intellect, those free from sin, say? Even in a dream she is unattainable — O heart, compose yourself! Who indeed is the fortunate youth who will drink [her] lip?" //

She explains the <s>kārikā</s>-portion 'of those that are suppressible' etc. — 'with the intention of suppressibility' etc. /
The syntactic connection of this is with 'statement' (<s>ukti</s>). /
'Explains in two ways' — /
The meaning is: [the commentator] has explained in two ways by the passage beginning with 'the attainment of subordinate status.' /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'of its constituent elements, namely diseases etc.' — /
The carryover from 'there is no conflict even in their statement.' /
In the sentence above, the carryover is of 'in their statement' alone. /
By the word '<s>tat</s>' here, [there is] reference to <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation). /
Of diseases etc. — of those diseases etc. that are its (<s>karuṇa</s>'s) constituent elements — the absence of fault belongs only to those, not to those that are not its constituent elements. /
And when there is possibility of constituent-status, even the introduction of death is not excessive. /
[This is] because when the substratum is destroyed, the complete cessation of the <s>rasa</s> would follow. /
But <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos) in such a context will attain fullness — if so, no; because of its irrelevance, and because of the cessation of what is contextually relevant. /
Where <s>karuṇa-rasa</s> itself is the subject of the poem, there is no conflict. /
Or, in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, when death does not involve long-term irreversibility, its introduction occasionally is not absolutely contradictory. /
But when there is long-term irreversibility, its intervening [presence causes] a break in the flow — thus, composition-practice by a poet whose chief concern is <s>rasa</s>-binding — [Locana:] therein, first he establishes the natural mode — 'of its constituent elements' etc. /
Of those that, through their independence, even though conflicting with <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> which is dependent [on union], are seen in every way as constituents of <s>karuṇa</s> — of those diseases etc. — this is the meaning. /
For they occur in <s>karuṇa</s> necessarily, and it is precisely they that occur [there]; /
but in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, they occur [only sometimes], and not necessarily those same [elements]. /
Of those that are not its constituent elements — the meaning is: such as sloth, fierceness, disgust. /
And when there is possibility of constituent-status — /
The purport is: 'all [transitory emotions] are <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>' — since this has been stated. /
When the substratum — one or the other of the man and woman who constitute the basis — perishes, <s>rati</s> (love) itself would be destroyed, because it has the nature of life-and-all for both substrata. /
'Of what is contextually relevant' — the meaning is: of <s>vipralambha</s>. /
'The subject of the poem' means: contextually relevant — this is the meaning. /
Now, if all <s>vyabhicārins</s> [are possible in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>], then this [rule] would be contradicted — anticipating this objection, he says: 'in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>' etc. /
'Not of long duration' — where the rest-point of death is such that conceptual certainty does not arise at all, there the <s>vyabhicārin</s>-status [of death applies]. /
'Occasionally' — if a skilled poet has the ability to construct such a turn. /
As for example — 'At the <s>tīrtha</s> where the waters of the daughter of <s>Jahnu</s> and the <s>Sarayū</s> mingle, by the abandonment of his body, having instantly attained a place in the register of the immortals — /
[Bālapriyā:] She shows the natural subordinate-status and the contextually-relevant <s>rasa</s>'s subordinate-status — 'through their independence' etc. /
'For they' — /
The meaning is: diseases etc. /
'In <s>karuṇa</s>' etc. — /
The meaning is: they necessarily occur in <s>karuṇa</s>, and it is precisely they [and no others] that occur — a twofold restriction. /
'Not necessarily those same [elements]' — the meaning is: there is no restriction that only those occur. /
She states the grounds for death's being possible as a constituent of <s>vipralambha</s> — 'all' etc. /
The meaning is: since '<s>ālasya</s> (sloth), <s>augnya</s> (fierceness), <s>jugupsā</s> (disgust) excepted, all are <s>vyabhicārins</s>' has been stated by the sage. /
She explains the passage 'when the substratum is destroyed' etc. — 'of the substratum' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>' etc. /
'Of death' — the meaning is: the death of one of the two, the hero or heroine. /
The syntactic connection of 'this' (<s>asya</s>) is with 'introduction' (<s>upanibandha</s>). /
'Not of long duration' — /
The meaning is: when the time after death is not long, [and] by that [brief time] or [through] the return — the reunion of the hero and heroine — when there is possibility of that. /
In the <s>Locana</s>, she states the purport — 'where' etc. /
'Rest-point of certainty' — the establishment of the rest-point of conceptual certainty. /

children.text: locanam pūrvākārādhikacaturayā saṅgataḥ kāntayāsau līlāgāreṣvaramata punarnandanābhyantareṣu //
children.translated_text: [Locana:] 'United with his beloved, whose beauty exceeded her former appearance, by a fourfold skill — he sported in the pleasure-houses and again in the inner groves of <s>Nandana</s>.' //

children.translated_text: 'Of that' — of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>.

children.text: yathā vā puṇḍarīkasya mahāśvetāṃ prati pravṛttanirbharānurāgasya dvitīyamunikumāropadeśavarṇane /
children.translated_text: Just as, alternatively, in the description of the second sage-youth's instruction regarding <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>'s fully manifested intense love toward <s>Mahāśvetā</s> —

children.text: svābhāvikyāmaṅgabhāvaprāptāvadoṣo yathā--- bhramimaratimalasahṛdayatāṃ pralayaṃ mūrcchāṃ tamaḥ śarīrasādam /
children.translated_text: When there is a natural attainment of subsidiary status (<s>aṅgabhāva</s>), there is no fault — as in: 'Dizziness, death, torpor, compassion, dissolution [of activity], swooning, darkness, bodily exhaustion,

children.text: maraṇaṃ ca jaladabhujagajaṃ prasahya kurute viṣaṃ viyoginīnām //
children.translated_text: and death — the poison born from the cloud-serpent forcefully inflicts [all these] upon women in separation.' //

Here the constituent-status of death with respect to <s>rati</s> (love) is evident. /
Therefore, the skilled poet did not compose a mere word-binding at the point of death, because it is introduced only as something being narrated in passing. /
But if a word-binding were placed [at the point of death], in every case there would be only an upsurge of grief — even when the return occurs after an extremely brief time — then, from the perspective of far-seeing sensitive audience-members, death is called a constituent [only] when irreversibility is not of long duration — alas, even in the <s>Tāpasa-Vatsarāja</s>, because the minds of those [audience-members], prepared through hearing <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>'s political stratagems, never believe in <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s death at all, there would not be even the name of <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos) — enough with much digression! /
Therefore, 'long duration' here [means] attaining a word-binding — this should be understood. /
Thus the natural constituent-status has been explained. /
As for the superimposed [constituent-status], the opposite of that — since the meaning is obtained [by implication], it was not explained in his own words. /
Having thus explained the three modes, he illustrates them in order — with 'therein' etc. /
'What business has the moon' — /
[Bālapriyā:] 'And the poet should compose either the reunion quickly after death, or death itself should be narrated [only in passing]' — /
'At the <s>tīrtha</s>' — this is from the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s>. /
'By the abandonment of the body' (<s>dehatyāga</s>) is also a reading. /
'With his beloved' — with <s>Indumatī</s>. /
'He' — <s>Aja</s>. /
'Constituent-status of <s>rati</s>' — /
The meaning is: constituent-status of love (<s>ramaṇa</s>). /
'Of death' — the meaning is: of the death shown by the [passage] 'by the abandonment of the body' etc. /
Because the previous verse describes the hope of reunion, here the constituent-status of death with respect to <s>vipralambha</s> is evident — this is the purport. /
'Word-binding' means: the establishment of the rest-point of conceptual certainty. /
'Because it is introduced only as something being narrated in passing' — this is the purport. /
'Extremely' — /
The meaning is: even when the return, the reunion, occurs after an extremely brief time. /
'An upsurge of grief alone' — the syntactic connection of this is with 'would be.' /
'Of the sensitive audience-members' — the savoring of grief alone would occur — this is the meaning. /
Some explain the passage 'not of long duration' etc. differently — narrating this, she says: 'then' etc. /
'Then' means: alternatively. /
She responds — 'alas' etc. /
'Improper narration' — the reason-indicating word is: because of the possibility of the <s>gopīs</s>' enjoying another man and thus of that purpose being fulfilled [by another] — /
this is the purport. /
The meaning of '<s>te</s>' (those) is: connected with the bower-houses. /
'Become old' means become decrepit — through this implication, he says: 'when I' etc. /
'Unceasing' — /
Because of the connection with the unceasing stated purpose, the previously mentioned purpose. /
'These' — /
These sprouts. /
She establishes the state of being severed: 'when I' etc. /
'Therefore' — precisely because of the stated severing of purpose. /
'Long duration' here — she concludes her own view: 'therefore' etc. /
'Long duration' — the meaning of the word 'long duration' in this context is: the attainment of a word-binding. /
'Superimposed' — the remainder is: constituent-status. /
'The opposite of that' — the meaning is: because actual constituent-status is absent, while natural constituent-status is its opposite. /
'Explained' — the meaning is: demonstrated. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'of that' — of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>.

ityādau /

yathā vā---'kopātkomalalolabāhulatikāpāśena' ityādau /
iyaṃ locanam vitarka autsukyena matiḥ smṛtyā śaṅkā dainyena dhṛtiścintayā ca bādhyate /

children.translated_text: 'When superimposed' — /
'the attainment of subsidiary status' is the remainder. /

children.text: pāṇḍukṣāmaṃ vaktraṃ hadayaṃ sarasaṃ tavālasaṃ ca vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Pale and emaciated is the face, the heart is moist, and the body is languid —
O friend, the disease within the heart reveals completely a <s>kṣetriya</s> (hereditary/field-born) disease!' //

In [verses] beginning with these etc. /
Even when [the subsidiary status] is superimposed, there is no contradiction — as in [the verse] beginning with '<s>pāṇḍukṣāmam</s>' (pale and emaciated). /
Or as in [the verse] beginning with '<s>kopāt komala-lola-bāhu-latikā-pāśena</s>' (in anger, with the noose of a tender, swaying creeper-arm). /
This — [<s>Locana</s>:] deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>) is obstructed by eagerness (<s>autsukya</s>); judgment (<s>mati</s>) by recollection (<s>smṛti</s>); apprehension (<s>śaṅkā</s>) by despondency (<s>dainya</s>); and fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>) by anxiety (<s>cintā</s>). /
And this was stated by us at the very beginning of the Second <s>Uddyota</s>. /
'Second' — the purport is: even when the <s>vibhāvas</s> of <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) that have become opposed [to love] are ascertained, the firmness of attachment (<s>anurāga</s>) is declared [to prevail] through its being incapable of severance. /

children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Therefore indeed' — precisely because of the faultiness of the primacy of two contradictory [elements] in one [and the same context] at one [and the same time].
'In the <s>atirātra</s>' etc. —

children.text: atirātre atirātrayāge ṣoḍaśinaṃ somapātraviśeṣam gṛhṇanti yathā---- ehi gaccha patottiṣṭha vada maunaṃ samācara /
children.translated_text: In the <s>atirātra</s> sacrifice, they take the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s>, a particular <s>soma</s>-vessel — as in: 'Come, go, fall, rise, speak, practice silence —
thus do the wealthy play with supplicants who are seized by the grip of hope.' //

Here, the disease appropriate to <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic <s>rasa</s>) is established through the device of <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia); [the expressions] 'from anger,' 'having bound,' and 'is killed' — of the <s>anubhāvas</s> of <s>raudra</s> (the furious <s>rasa</s>) that are forcibly superimposed through <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), the subsidiary status [arises] precisely from the non-completion of that [<s>rūpaka</s>]. /
And this was stated previously, in the passage 'not [to be] excessively pursued to completion.' /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Antarā</s>' means 'in between.' /
'Break in the flow' — the meaning is: a break in the continuity of contemplation. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'That which has become opposed' — the meaning is: that which has become antagonistic to <s>anurāga</s> (love). /
'Of <s>anurāga</s>' — the meaning is: of the love directed toward <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>. /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] '<s>Bhrami</s>' (dizziness) — this [verse] and the one beginning with '<s>pāṇḍivatī</s>' etc. are also cited in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. /
<s>Bhrami</s> is a certain internal modification that manifests as if the directions are spinning. /
<s>Pralaya</s> (dissolution) is the loss of activity; <s>mūrcchā</s> (swooning) is the cessation of the functions of the external and internal sense-organs. /
<s>Tamas</s> (darkness) means blindness. /
'The cloud itself is the serpent' — born from it [the cloud-serpent]. /
'Poison' — water itself [is] the venom. /
Here, the <s>anubhāvas</s> — dizziness etc. — of the disease appropriate to <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic <s>rasa</s>), since they are also possible in <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation), [attain] natural subsidiary status. /
'<s>Pāṇḍukṣāmam</s>' (pale and emaciated) — '<s>hṛdayam</s>' (heart) means the chest. /
'<s>Sarasam</s>' (moist) — containing the juice of food; or alternatively, containing the juice of sandalwood paste etc. /
'<s>Alasam</s>' (languid) — incapable of external activity. /
'<s>Kṣetriya</s>' — a disease that is to be treated in another body [i.e., hereditary], incurable — this is the extent [of the meaning]. /
'<s>Roga</s>' (disease) means illness. /
Some [say] '<s>kṣetriya roga</s>' means consumption (<s>kṣayaroga</s>). /
'Reveals' — the statement [of the symptoms] with singular endings is with the intent that each [symptom] — face, etc. — has an individual syntactic connection [with the verb]. /
Here, the disease appropriate to <s>karuṇa</s> attains subsidiary status in <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) through superimposition — she says in the <s>Locana</s>: 'here' etc. /
'Through the device of <s>śleṣa</s>' — the meaning is: through the display of <s>anubhāvas</s> common to both [disease and love-sickness]. /
'Is established' — the meaning is: displayed through superimposition as having subsidiary status. /
'Having bound' etc. — the meaning is: of binding etc. /
'From the non-completion of that' — the meaning is: from the non-completion of the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). /
'Subsidiary status' — the meaning is: subsidiary status to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] 'The attainment of subsidiary status' — if this attainment of subsidiary status is yet another [type], [it occurs] when, by virtue of being the governing [<s>rasa</s>], with respect to a single primary sentence-meaning, two mutually contradictory <s>rasas</s> or <s>bhāvas</s> attain subsidiary status — even in that [case], there is no fault. /
As stated in 'cast aside, clinging to the hand' etc. /
How is there non-contradiction there? — if [asked:] because both of them are established through their orientation toward something else. /
Even when oriented toward something else, how is the contradiction of the two mutually opposing [rasas] removed? — if [asked:] it is stated — /
In a [Vedic] injunction, the combination of contradictories — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'another' — the meaning is: this is the fourth type. /
For previously, the contradictory [<s>rasa</s>] was said [to attain] subsidiary status in another <s>rasa</s> relevant to the topic; but now, the subsidiary status of both contradictory [<s>rasas</s>] in another matter — this is the remainder. /
'Cast aside' etc. — this was explained in the passage 'with respect to a primary sentence-meaning elsewhere.' /
But [objection:] even when oriented toward something else, the inherent nature [of the rasas] does not cease; and the contradiction is caused precisely by their inherent nature — with this intent he says: 'even when oriented toward something else' etc. /
'Of the two contradictory [rasas]' — this qualifier is with the intent of [expressing] the reason, [namely:] 'because of their respective natures.' /
'It is stated' — this is the purport: the contradiction or non-contradiction of <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions) is not based on inherent nature alone — since they fall within a particular aggregate of conditions — because even between hot and cold, there is an absence of contradiction [in certain conditions]. /
'In a [Vedic] injunction' — 'do this very thing, do not do [it]' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'and another attainment of subsidiary status' — this is the syntactic connection. /
'In that [case] too' — the meaning is: even in such an attainment of subsidiary status. /
The elaboration of 'another' — in the <s>Locana</s>: 'the fourth' etc. /
She shows the distinction from what was previously stated — 'previously' etc. /
'Of the contradictory [rasa]' — the meaning is: the contradictory <s>rasa</s> as subsidiary. /
'In another <s>rasa</s>' — 'in a particular <s>rasa</s>' — 'in another matter' — 'in the topic at hand' carries over. /
'Even when oriented toward something else' — the meaning is: even when [attaining] subsidiary status to another. /
'Says' — the meaning is: asks. /
'Qualifier' — the meaning is: [it is] the qualifier of 'of the two that are being connected [syntactically].' /
'This is the purport' — this is the essential meaning of the passage beginning with 'in a [Vedic] injunction' etc. /
Asking 'what?' — he says: 'of the particular aggregate of conditions' etc. /
This is the meaning: the contradiction or non-contradiction of things is not caused by inherent nature alone, but rather arises also through the entry of a particular aggregate of conditions. /
Here, that contradiction — namely, the non-co-occurrence on the same locus and the obstruction of the production [of one by the other] — the contradiction of pot-ness etc. with cloth-ness etc., and of cold touch etc. with hot touch etc. — the contradiction in the form of non-co-occurrence — is caused by inherent nature. /
Likewise, the non-contradiction of those [qualities] — with substance-ness etc. and with qualities such as color etc. — in the form of co-occurrence — should also be understood. /
The contradiction of cold touch, fragrance of non-perfume, etc. with hot touch, fragrance of non-perfume, etc. in [their] being produced in a substance originated by their [respective] locus — is caused by the entry of a particular aggregate of conditions; likewise, the non-contradiction of hot and cold touch should be understood as caused by the entry of the particular aggregate of conditions [for producing] soft rice etc. /
In the context of injunction, taking the aggregate of conditions for engagement, and in the context of prohibition, taking the aggregate of conditions for cessation — through the entry of those [conditions], contradiction and non-contradiction should be understood. /
'Of hot and cold' — the meaning is: of hot and cold touches. /
'Because of the absence of contradiction' — the remainder is: 'through the entry of a particular aggregate of conditions.' /
She gives an example of 'in a [Vedic] injunction' etc. — 'do this very [thing]' etc. /
By 'this,' a single action is intended. /
'At one [and the same time]' is the remainder. /
'Thus, just as' — the meaning is: thus, just as the faultiness [of simultaneous contradictory injunctions] in a [Vedic] injunction [is resolved through alternatives]. /
The purport is: because performing and not-performing cannot be carried out by one [person] at one [and the same] time. /
He states a corroborating [example] — 'therefore indeed' etc. /
Faultiness — or alternatively, in restatement. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] just as. /
By the word 'injunction' (<s>vidhi</s>), here, primacy at one [and the same time] is meant. /
And therefore, 'in the <s>atirātra</s> [rite] they take the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> [cup]' — this contradictory injunction terminates in an option — [say] the experts in sentence-meaning. /
'Restatement' — the meaning is: in the [context of] subsidiary status to another [<s>rasa</s>]. /

children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] As stated — '<s>raudrasya caiva yat karma sa jñeyaḥ karuṇo rasaḥ</s>' (that which is the action of the <s>raudra</s> [furious sentiment] should be known as <s>karuṇa rasa</s> [the pathetic sentiment]). /
To this he says — 'excess of delight' etc. /

children.translated_text: Here is an example — 'O <s>kurabaka</s> tree, you are being separated from the pleasure of the playful striking of [her] breasts; O <s>bakula</s> tree, to be remembered by you is the service of [her] mouth-nectar;
