children.translated_text: O <s>aśoka</s> tree, deprived of the contact of [her] feet, you will attain a state of sorrow' — thus, upon [her] departure from [her] own city, the women of [his] enemies said. //

etc. /
For here, when injunction and prohibition are incorporated by virtue of being subordinate [to the main statement], there is no contradiction — so here too the same will apply. /
For in this verse, the matter of jealousy-based <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic love-in-separation) and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos) is not being enjoined [as primary]; /
since the surpassing power of the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s> is the sentence-meaning, and because those two [sentiments] are established as subsidiary to it. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] On their being subsidiary to sport — for here there is no assertion of contradictory meanings — by the maxim of the two assassins stationed near the king: even of contradictory [elements], those that have been made subordinate by being directed toward another purpose — whatever contradiction there might be [is resolved]. /
Merely on account of their contradictoriness — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] by the maxim of the <s>aruṇa</s>-vessel — 'they should grasp' — thus the grasping of the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> cup was enjoined. /
And again, by 'one does not grasp the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> at the <s>atirātra</s> [ritual],' that was prohibited — and although there is an injunction regarding the contradictory [pair of] grasping and non-grasping, nevertheless that injunction culminates in the option: one may or may not grasp the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> — this is the meaning. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'come!' — /
O supplicant, you come — arrive! /
'Thus' — /
the meaning is: in the manner stated. /
'By hopes' — /
the meaning is: seized by planets in the form of hopes — by those. /
'By supplicants' — the syntactic connection is: by beggars the wealthy ones are made to sport. /
Here, showing that by the manner of 'come!' they sport, 'go!' they sport, etc. — even of things having the nature of presence and absence, such as going and coming — because of their being subsidiary through syntactic connection as modes of the principal sport — there is no fault — [<s>Abhinavagupta</s>] says in the <s>Locana</s>: 'on their being subsidiary to sport' etc. /
'Here' — /
the meaning is: in the verse beginning with 'come!' /
'Of contradictory meanings' — /
the meaning is: of meanings that are mutually contradictory in pairs — going and coming, falling and rising, speech and silence — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — in the sense of reason. /
'Of the king' — /
the meaning is: two persons, assassins stationed near the king — established in dependence on the king — who are engaged in mutual enmity and intent on killing each other — the maxim of those two — this is the meaning. /
'Other' — /
the meaning is: made subordinate by being directed toward another [purpose] — made dependent by that — this is the meaning. /
By this sequence, 'come, go' etc. — by the sequence of the heard [words], whatever self-awareness is cognized — even when that [self-awareness] is present, /
'of those that do not find rest' — /
the meaning is: of those that do not attain rest of cognition in themselves. /
The purport is: because of their syntactic connection as subsidiary to sport. /
'Of each other's nature' — /
whatever is the nature, the essence, of each other — in the contemplation of that, what need be said — that contemplation simply does not arise — this is the meaning. /
He states a distinction — 'merely' etc. /
'<s>Aruṇa</s>' — /
the meaning is: by the maxim of the <s>aruṇa</s>-vessel. /
The syntactic connection of this is with 'is conceivable.' /
In the injunctive sentence '<s>aruṇayā</s>' etc., because of the restriction that <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations) are connected with the principal verbal action, the mutually unconnected [elements] — redness, tawny-eyedness, etc. — which are meanings of words in the instrumental case — are first connected as instruments to the principal verbal action of <s>soma</s>-purchasing; afterwards, mutual connection [among them follows] — and one cannot say that the operation of injunction and subsidiary-statement (<s>anuvāda</s>) does not exist with respect to <s>rasas</s>, since [<s>rasas</s>] are accepted as sentence-meanings. /
Of the sentence-meaning, i.e., the expressed meaning, the injunction and subsidiary-statement — [<s>Locana</s>:] whatever subsequent mutual connection of these [elements] at the sentence level is conceivable — let that be set aside. /
Objection: injunction applies to that which is the primary expressed meaning; /
but subsidiary-statement (<s>anuvāda</s>) applies to what is expressed non-primarily. /
And the expressibility of <s>rasa</s> has been rejected by you yourself — anticipating this objection, he resolves it — 'nor' etc. /
The injunction and subsidiary-statement are based merely on the distinction of primary and non-primary; and those [distinctions] exist in the domain of suggestion too — this is the purport. /
And it has been stated that <s>rasa</s> itself is primarily the sentence-meaning of poetry. /
Therefore, where that meaning is non-primary, there the status of being merely re-stated (<s>anūdyamānatva</s>) is appropriate even for <s>rasa</s>. /
Or, since <s>rasa</s> has the status of being merely re-stated by virtue of being implicitly included through the re-stated <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. — he says: 'of the sentence-meaning' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>aruṇā</s> (ruddy), <s>piṅgākṣī</s> (tawny-eyed)' etc. — /
this is clear in the <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> technical terminology etc. /
'At the sentence level' — /
the meaning is: to be established through the sentence. /
'Of these' etc. — /
the meaning is: the subsequent connection, like 'whoever comes, he goes' etc. — this is the meaning. /
The syntactic connection is: 'that, merely on account of contradictoriness, let it be set aside.' /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'of injunction and prohibition' — /
the meaning is: of going and coming etc. /
'By virtue of being re-stated' — /
the remainder is: in the enjoining of sport. /
'Just so' etc. — he explains what was already stated — 'the verse' etc. /
'Being enjoined' — /
the meaning is: primacy. /
'Nor' etc. — he introduces the text of the <s>Locana</s> up to 'since accepted' — 'objection' etc. /
'That which is expressed' — /
the meaning is: that expressed meaning. /
'Therein the injunction' — the purport is: the injunction and subsidiary-statement of that. /
He states the purport of the resolution beginning with 'of those' — 'primary' etc. /
— up to 'is appropriate.' /
'Injunction and subsidiary-statement' — the remainder is: 'of meaning.' /
'In the domain of suggestion too' — even when suggestedness is the case. /
'Where the status of being re-stated of <s>rasa</s> [applies]' — to this he says: 'primarily' etc. /
'That meaning' — the suggested meaning. /
'Or' — indicating an alternative view. /
'Of those <s>rasas</s> that are implicitly included, who would obstruct [them]?' /
Or, by those who do not accept that <s>rasas</s> etc. are directly the meaning of poetry — even by them, the dependency of those [<s>rasas</s>] upon that [poetry] must necessarily be accepted. /
Even so, there is no contradiction in this verse; /
because from the enjoined portion — [which is] the ancillary of the re-stated [elements], the cause consisting of the subject-matter of both <s>rasas</s> — a particular cognition of emotion arises, and therefore there is no contradiction whatsoever. /
The production of a particular effect from a cause that has the cooperation of two contradictory [elements] is observed; for it is the simultaneous production of contradictory results by a single cause that constitutes contradiction — not the cooperation of two contradictory [elements]. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Or, even if the incorporation of two contradictory <s>rasas</s> by virtue of being re-stated does not obtain, it will obtain by virtue of cooperation — thus, in every case, the well-reasoned subordinate-and-principal relationship of the two non-contradictory [<s>rasas</s>] [is established] — there is no difficulty here — he shows this: 'indeed' etc. /
'Of that as cause' — /
the meaning of poetry — the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. — are the cause of <s>rasas</s> etc.; the state of being those — their being such (<s>tattā</s>). /
The re-stated hand-gestures etc. — the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. that are components of <s>rasa</s> — whatever dual subject-matter consisting of <s>karuṇa</s> and <s>vipralambha</s> has those as its cause — that cooperating with the enjoined [portion] — namely, the burning of sins produced by the fire born of the arrow of <s>Śambhu</s> (Lord <s>Śiva</s>) — from that, the cognition of a particular emotion — in the domain of the <s>preyas</s> (charming) figure of speech — characterized by the surpassing power of the Lord — cognition — this is the connection. /
The production of a particular effect — namely, the making of soft cooked rice — from a cause, namely rice-grain etc., that has the cooperation of two contradictory [elements] — namely, the cold and hot that belong to water and fire — is observed. /
For everywhere, the cause-and-effect relationship — as in seed-and-sprout etc. — is precisely like this, and not otherwise. /
Objection: then contradiction would be ineffectual everywhere — anticipating this, he says: 'of contradictory results' etc. /
And thus they say: 'There is no production of the contradictory [from the same cause].' /
Objection: but if in poetry whose subject is to be enacted, such a sentence occurs — then [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'connected' etc. /
The meaning is: implicitly included, i.e., attracted, by the re-stated <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. /
He states that [implication] with that intent — /
'Of that as cause' — he explains this — 'of poetry' etc. /
'The re-stated ancillary' etc. — he explains by construing with the verse 'thrown, grasping with hands' etc. — 'the re-stated' etc. /
'Hand-gestures etc. are <s>vibhāvas</s> etc.' — here the sequential correspondence is not intended; /
since hand-gestures are <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) — or the reading is '<s>anubhāvādayaḥ</s>' (consequents etc.). /
'Of that as cause' — /
the meaning is: those are the causes of which — that. /
'Of <s>rasa</s>-kind' — /
the meaning is: having the nature of <s>rasa</s>, or having the nature of <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion). /
The elaboration of 'of the enjoined portion' — '<s>Śāmbhava</s>' etc. /
'Of the enjoined portion' — explained through proximity to the qualified [term] as 'of the enjoined portion' — he shows this by saying 'from that.' /
'Cognition of a particular emotion' — he explains this — 'emotion' etc. /
The elaboration of 'particular emotion' — 'in the domain of the <s>preyas</s> figure' etc. /
What is that? — to this he says — 'the Lord' etc. /
'Everywhere' etc. — /
the purport is: the cause-and-effect relationship, having the cooperation of contradictory [elements] such as fire-water etc., pertains to the seed etc. [producing] the sprout etc. /
'There is no production' — /
it seems that the reading should be '<s>notpādanam</s>' (no production) [rather than '<s>nopādānam</s>']. /
If in this kind of context the subject-matter involves enactment, how should the acting be performed? — [the answer is:] whatever procedure applies in the domain of the re-stated expressed meaning of such a kind, that same will apply here too. /
Thus, by resorting to the method of injunction and subsidiary-statement, the contradiction in this verse has been resolved. /
Furthermore: in the description of the surpassing power of a hero whose rise is to be celebrated, the <s>karuṇa rasa</s> (pathetic sentiment) concerning his adversaries does not produce distress in the discerning [audience] — [<s>Locana</s>:] if the complete acting [of the verse] is performed, then how can the acting of contradictory subject-matter be performed simultaneously? — with this intention, he raises the objection — 'thus' etc. /
He resolves this — 'the re-stated' etc. /
Whatever procedure applies to a context where the re-stated expressed meaning of such a contradictory nature is the subject — such as 'come, go, fall, rise' etc. — that same [procedure applies] here too. /
What has been said amounts to this: in 'thrown, grasping with hands' etc., the incidental subject-matter should first be presented primarily through the sequence of presenting the appearance of one frightened and agitated etc. /
Although here the <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) too is merely ancillary, nevertheless, compared to <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation), its greater proximity to being the principal topic [is evident] — since it is useful with respect to the power of <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord). /
But <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) [is more] remote, having arrived through the force of the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) and <s>upamā</s> (simile) in '<s>kāmīva</s>' (like a lover). /
And thus, with tears in the eyes — through the acting sequence of overwhelmingly presenting the <s>karuṇa</s> as the primary [sentiment], and suggesting the <s>vipralambha</s> only slightly through its similarity with <s>karuṇa</s> — /
in '<s>kāmīva</s>' (like a lover) — although the acting appropriate to amorous indignation (<s>praṇayakopa</s>) is performed — nevertheless, the <s>vipralambha</s> that is cognized even from that, in the immediately following [passage] 'let him burn sins' etc. — being surrendered to the acting performed with grandeur — that power of the Lord — culminates in subsidiary status — thus there is no contradiction whatsoever. /
He concludes this resolution of contradiction — 'thus' etc. /
He states the resolution of contradiction in another context by another method — 'furthermore' etc. /
'Of the discerning' — of the assembled audience possessed of discrimination. /
'Does not produce distress' — /
the meaning is: no melting of the heart arises in such a context, because of the absence of repose in the savoring of <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos). /
Rather, that <s>karuṇa rasa</s> — [which is really] the anger that attains the status of a <s>vyabhicāribhāva</s> (transitory emotion) of the <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic sentiment) — being in the form of its result, /
culminating through the medium of manifesting its own cause — culminates precisely in the intensification of the savoring of <s>vīra</s> (the heroic). /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She explains for the instruction of actors — 'what has been said' etc. /
'Should be presented' — should be enacted. /
'Through the force of <s>utprekṣā</s> and <s>upamā</s>' — the meaning is: through the force of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) or <s>upamā</s> (simile). /
'Having performed' — the syntactic connection is with 'acting.' /
She raises an objection — 'in <s>kāmīva</s>' etc. /
She resolves it — 'nevertheless' etc. /
'Performed' — /
the meaning is: the subject of performance. /
The remainder is: 'it would be.' /
She introduces the passage beginning with 'furthermore' — 'in another context too' etc. /
'In another context' — in another topic, in [the verse beginning with] '<s>kuravaka</s>' etc. /
'By another method' — the meaning is: by the fifth method. /
'Says' — the meaning is: says incidentally. /
'In such a context' — /
the meaning is: in examples such as [the verse beginning with] '<s>kuravaka</s>' etc. /
'Distress' — she states the reason: rather, delight and its intensification is what one attains; therefore, since [the <s>karuṇa</s>] has the quality of blunted power, there is no fault in that which would obstruct it. /
Therefore, it is proper to say that what opposes <s>rasa</s> that has become the sentence-meaning is '<s>rasa-virodhī</s>' (an opponent of <s>rasa</s>) — but not of something that is merely a component.

children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The elaboration — '<s>cittadruti</s>' (melting of the heart) etc. /
'<s>Kuravaka</s>' — /
'<s>Mukhāsavasevanam</s>' (the serving of mouth-nectar) is also a reading. /

children.text: sa pādāghātādaśokastilakakuravakau vīkṣaṇālaṅganābhyām strīṇāṃ sparśātpriyaṅgurvikasati bakulaśśīdhugaṇḍūṣasekāt //
children.translated_text: 'He [the <s>aśoka</s> tree] blossoms from the striking of [women's] feet; the <s>tilaka</s> and <s>kuravaka</s> [bloom] from their glance and embrace; the <s>priyaṅgu</s> [blooms] from women's touch; the <s>bakula</s> [blooms] from the sprinkling of mouth-rinsed liquor.' //

'Or of a <s>bhāva</s> (emotion)' — /
In that <s>rasa</s>, either of the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) that is the principal [element], or of a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) — as, for example, of <s>autsukya</s> (eagerness) in <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation). /

children.translated_text: And thus here, by the principle of 'distinguished distinction' (<s>viśiṣṭa-vaiśiṣṭya-nyāya</s>), the <s>karuṇa</s> [sentiment] enhanced by <s>vipralambha</s> [produces] the excess of the power of <s>Tripuraripu</s> (Śiva) — 'This is that very hand — the one that excels at loosening the girdle (<s>raśanā</s>), that presses against full breasts,
that touches the navel, thigh, and hip, that unties the undergarment (<s>nīvī</s>)!' //

This statement should be considered here. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>, '<s>karuṇa rasa</s>' — /
The remainder is: 'being composed.' /
'Excess of delight' — /
The meaning is: in the savoring of <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic sentiment). /
'Of that' — /
The meaning is: of <s>karuṇa</s>. /
'Having blunted power etc.' — /
The meaning is: because of the blunting of power through its becoming subordinate to another — this has its connection with 'is not a fault.' /
'That brings about the conflict of that' — this is a qualifier of 'of that.' /
The meaning is: that which brings about the conflict with the excess of savoring <s>vīra rasa</s>. /
In the reading '<s>akuṇṭhaśaktikatvāt</s>' (because of having unblunted power) — 'of that' means 'of the savoring of <s>vīra</s>.' /
'That which brings about the conflict of that' — ending in the ablative, the remainder is: from <s>karuṇa</s>. /
He concludes — 'therefore' etc. /
'Of what has become the sentence-meaning' — /
The meaning is: of the principal, the one under discussion. /
'To call it a conflict of <s>rasa</s>' — /
The meaning is: to designate [it] by the word 'conflicting' in [passages like] '<s>virodhirase</s>' etc. /
And thus the purport is: the inclusion of what is related to a <s>rasa</s> that conflicts with the <s>rasa</s> etc. that constitutes the sentence-meaning is a fault. /
'But not' etc. — /
The meaning is: it is not proper to call that which conflicts with some <s>rasa</s> or <s>bhāva</s> that is subordinate a 'conflict of <s>rasa</s>.' /
And thus the purport is: the inclusion of what is related to a <s>rasa</s> that conflicts with some subordinate [element] is not a fault. /
As in [the example beginning with] '<s>yathākṣipta</s>' — the inclusion of what is related to <s>karuṇa</s>, which conflicts with <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
Regarding 'or of a <s>bhāva</s>' — the word '<s>bhāva</s>' is intended to denote both the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent) and the <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) — he says in the <s>Locana</s>: 'in that' etc. /
'In that <s>rasa</s>' — in the <s>rasa</s> under discussion. /
The elaboration of 'of what has become the sentence-meaning' — 'of what is principal' etc. /
Alternatively, the combination of even something that is a <s>karuṇa rasa</s> topic and has become the sentence-meaning with a <s>śṛṅgāra</s> element of such a kind, resting on a particular mode of expression, arises precisely for the maturation of <s>rasa</s>. /
Because objects that are sweet by nature, when they have attained a state worthy of lamentation, being remembered through graces belonging to their former condition, generate an even greater immersion in grief. /
As — [<s>Locana</s>:] Now, in the very verse cited earlier beginning with '<s>kṣipta</s>' etc., he resolves the conflict by another method — 'alternatively' etc. /
And here is the purport: previously, the absence of conflict between <s>vipralambha</s> (separation) and <s>karuṇa</s> was stated through the one going to a subordinate position elsewhere. /
But now, that <s>vipralambha</s> has assumed the very subordination to <s>karuṇa</s> — how then is it established [that there is] no conflict? — For it was stated that the <s>karuṇa rasa</s> arises from the <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) that is the fall of a loved one etc. /
And 'being loved' is grounded in attractiveness. /
Therefore, through the figurative expression '<s>kāmī vā ardrāparādhaḥ</s>' (the lover, or the one soft in his offenses), this is stated. /
When observing the activities of the fire of <s>Śambhu</s>'s (Śiva's) arrow, the past tale of amorous quarrel, now being remembered in its destroyed state, attains the status of a <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) of grief. /
To this he says — 'through a particular mode' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] To prevent wandering to an alternative meaning of the passage beginning with 'alternatively' — through the absence of vulgarity, by leading [the elements] to the form of <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, etc. — she introduces the text of the passage — 'now' etc. /
In place of 'or alternatively' etc., 'alternatively' etc. up to 'absence of fault' is also a reading. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>, 'alternatively' etc. /
'Of what has become the sentence-meaning' — /
The meaning is: of what is expressed (<s>vācya</s>). /
The word '<s>api</s>' (even) indicates the apparent conflict according to the previously stated method in [the matter of] maturation of <s>rasa</s>. /
'Of some' — /
The meaning is: of some [element] having the form of a <s>vibhāva</s> etc. /
'That is a topic of <s>karuṇa rasa</s>' — that is a subordinate part of <s>karuṇa</s>. /
'Of such a kind' — equal to it in being expressed. /
Or: with a <s>śṛṅgāra</s> element that is conflicting, i.e., a component of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
He gives an example of what was stated — 'this' etc. /
This verse is also cited in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. /
Connecting what was said in the context of '<s>kṣipta</s>' etc. to the present, he says — 'therein' etc. /
'He used to behave' — /
The meaning of that is: he used to perform hand-grasping etc. /
Since the meaning intended by the <s>Vṛtti</s> text is unclear, he states the purport in the <s>Locana</s> — 'and here is the purport' etc. /
'Elsewhere' — in [the context of] the excess of the power of <s>Tripuraripu</s> (Śiva, the destroyer of the three cities). /
'But now' — the connection of this is with 'thus it is established.' /
'How then is it a conflict?' — /
The meaning is: [<s>vipralambha</s>] is not a conflict of <s>karuṇa</s>. /
'From the <s>vibhāva</s> etc. — it was stated' — /
The remainder is: by the sage [<s>Bharata</s>]. /
'Grounded in attractiveness' — this is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. /
'Through the figurative expression' — /
This is stated from the standpoint that this is the figure of speech (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy). /
'This is stated' — /
The meaning is: the meaning about to be stated is conveyed. /
'Of <s>Śambhu</s>' — /
The meaning is: by observing the activities of the fire of <s>Śambhu</s>'s arrow. /
'<s>Avalokane</s>' (in observing) is also a reading, and its connection is with 'being remembered.' /
'The former' — /
The meaning is: the former, i.e., previously experienced tale of an amorous quarrel — the meaning is an event such as the intolerance of being grasped by the hand etc. /
'Being remembered' — /
The remainder is: by the women of <s>Tripura</s>. /
'In its destroyed state' —

children.text: tadatra tripurayuvatīnāṃ śāmbhavaḥ śarāgnirārdrāparādhaḥ kāmī yathā vyavaharati sama tathā vyavahṛtavānityanenāpi prakāreṇāstyeva nirvirodhatvam /
children.translated_text: Therein, the fire of <s>Śambhu</s>'s arrow upon the women of <s>Tripura</s> — the lover, [acting] as if he had committed a tender offense — just as he used to behave toward them, so he behaved — by this method too, the absence of conflict certainly exists. /

children.text: tasmādyathā yathā nirūpyate tatā tathātra doṣābhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the more [the matter] is examined, the more the absence of fault here [is evident]. /

Having thus examined what is useful for the portion of the <s>kārikā</s> [dealing with] the utterances that have attained the state of being subordinate to this extent — 'the expression (<s>ukti</s>) is a pretext' — he concludes: 'thus' etc. /
By the word '<s>tāvat</s>' (thus far), he indicates that there is still more to be said. // 20 //

The absence of conflict in all of these and similar [verses] should be understood. /
Thus, the division of the domain of inclusion and non-inclusion of <s>rasas</s> etc. that conflict with [other] <s>rasas</s> etc. has been shown. /
Now, in order to set forth the proper sequence for installing them in a single extended composition, it is said — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The meaning is: devoid of vulgar expression. /

Here, upon seeing the arm of <s>Bhūriśravas</s> that has fallen on the battlefield, this is the lamentation of his beloved women. /
'<s>Raśanā</s>' means the girdle; '<s>rasanotkarṣī</s>' means one that pulls the girdle upward during occasions of lovemaking. /
With the intention that by this method of resolving conflict, much more illustrative material is substantiated, he says — 'and thus' etc. /

Regarding 'now, of those' — he glosses the word 'of those' — 'of the <s>rasa</s>s' etc. /
'Sequence' etc. /
Even though the composition of extended works (<s>prabandha</s>s) with multiple <s>rasa</s>s is well-established,

Even though the composition of extended works with multiple <s>rasa</s>s is well-established,

children.text:
prabandheṣu mahākāvyādiṣu nāṭakādiṣu vā viprakīrṇatayāṅgāṅgibhāvena bahavo rasā upanibadhyanta ityatra prasiddhau satyāmapi yaḥ prabandhānāṃ chāyātiśayayogamicchati tena teṣāṃ rasānāmanyatamaḥ kaścidvivakṣito raso 'ṅgitvena viniveśayitavya ityayaṃ yuktataro mārgaḥ /
nanu rasāntareṣu bahuṣu prāptaparipoṣeṣu satsu kathamekasyāṅgitā na virudhyata ityāśaṅkyedamucyate--
children.translated_text:
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] In extended compositions — in <s>mahākāvya</s>s (epic poems) and the like, or in <s>nāṭaka</s>s (dramas) and the like — many <s>rasa</s>s are composed in a scattered manner (<s>viprakīrṇa</s>) and in the relationship of principal and subordinate — given that this is well-established, whoever desires the excellence of outstanding beauty for [their] extended compositions should install some particular intended <s>rasa</s>, one among those <s>rasa</s>s, as the principal (<s>aṅgī</s>) — this is the more proper path. /
Now, given that many other <s>rasa</s>s have attained full maturation, how is the principal status of one not contradicted? — anticipating this, it is stated —
The inclusion of other <s>rasa</s>s, which pertains to the <s>rasa</s> under discussion —
does not destroy the principal status of that [<s>rasa</s>] which shines forth as the permanent [<s>sthāyin</s>]. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.22 //
The inclusion of other <s>rasa</s>s, which pertains to the <s>rasa</s> under discussion —
does not destroy the principal status of that [<s>rasa</s>] which shines forth as the permanent [<s>sthāyin</s>]. // 22 //

children.translated_text: The meaning is: with their termination in the separate heroes — the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero), <s>pratināyaka</s> (antagonist), <s>patākā</s>-hero, and <s>prakarī</s>-hero etc. /
'In the relationship of principal and subordinate' — the meaning is: with their termination in a single hero. /
'More proper' — /

children.text: yadyapi ramavakārādau paryāyabandhādau ca naikasyāṅgitvaṃ tathāpi nāyuktatā tasyāpyevaṃvidho yaḥ prabandhaḥ tadyathā nāṭakaṃ mahākāvyaṃ vā tadutkṛṣṭataramiti taraśabdasyārthaḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: Even though in works like the <s>Ramavakāra</s> and in compositions with alternating arrangement, the principal status does not belong to a single [<s>rasa</s>], still that is not improper; but a composition of such a kind — namely a <s>nāṭaka</s> or a <s>mahākāvya</s> — that is more excellent — such is the meaning of the word '<s>tara</s>' (comparative suffix). // 21 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] In extended compositions, the <s>rasa</s> that, being introduced first, is permanent (<s>sthāyin</s>) by virtue of being pursued again and again — the inclusion within it of other <s>rasa</s>s occurring in the interstices, which pervades the entire composition — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'Even though well-established' — /
The meaning is: even though it has been set forth by the sage <s>Bharata</s> and others. /
'Of those' — of the extended compositions. /
'In <s>mahākāvya</s>s and the like' — the word 'and the like' [refers to] the type. /
He mentions the non-performable varieties; the second [use of 'and the like'] refers to the performable [varieties]. /
'In a scattered manner' — /

children.text:
nanviti /

'yuktatara' ityatra tarabarthaṃ darśayati---yadyapityādi /
tathāpi ca tasyāpi nāyuktatā iti sambandhaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Even of that' — /
the meaning is: 'even of <s>samavakāra</s> and such [dramatic forms].' /
'Of such a kind' — /
the meaning is: 'having many <s>rasas</s>, and having a single <s>rasa</s> as principal.' // 21 //

'But' (<s>nanu</s>) — if [the subsidiary <s>rasas</s>] have attained full nourishment on their own, how can they have subsidiary status? And if they have not attained full nourishment, how can they have the status of <s>rasa</s>? — thus, <s>rasa</s>-status and subsidiary status are mutually contradictory; and if their subsidiary status is not [possible], how has the principal status of one [<s>rasa</s>] been stated? — this is the purport. /
'Of another <s>rasa</s>' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] of [the <s>rasa</s>] that is the topic, pervading the entire plot (<s>itivṛtta</s>), and through precisely that extensively pervading nature, suited for principal status — the connection of the word '<s>teṣām</s>' (of those) is with '<s>krama</s>' (sequence) — this is the meaning. /
She elaborates 'even though well established' — by '<s>Bharata</s>' etc. /
She explains the <s>vṛtti</s> text — by 'great' etc. /
She shows the meaning of the comparative suffix '<s>tara</s>' in '<s>yuktatara</s>' (more appropriate) — by 'even though' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: 'nevertheless, even that [approach] is not inappropriate.' /

children.text:
'nanvi'tyādiśaṅkāgranthasya bhāvamāha---svayamityādi /
labdhaparipīṣatve iti /
rasāntarāṇāmiti śeṣaḥ /
nanvaṅgatvaṃ māstvityatrāha--teṣāṃ cetyādi /
vṛttau sa nāṅgitāmupahanti /
etadevopapādayitumucyate--
children.translated_text:
She states the purport of the objection-passage 'but' etc. — 'on their own' etc. /
'When [they have] attained full nourishment' — '<s>rasāntarāṇām</s>' (of other <s>rasas</s>) is the remainder. /
As for [the possible retort] 'let there not be subsidiary status' — to this he says: 'of those, and' etc. /
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] That [supplementation] does not destroy the principal status. /
Precisely to demonstrate this, it is stated —

children.text: kāryam ekaṃ yathā vyāpi prabandhasya vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Just as a single pervading purpose (<s>kārya</s>) is established for the extended composition (<s>prabandha</s>),

children.text: tathā rasasyāpi vidhau virodho naiva vidyate // DhvK_3.23 //

children.text: locanam rasasya rasāntarairitivṛttavaśāyātatvena parimitakathāśakalavyāpibhiryaḥ samāveśaḥ samupabṛṃhaṇaṃ sa tasya sthāyitvenetivṛttavyāpitayā bhāsamānasya nāṅgitāmupahanti, aṅgitāṃ poṣayatyevetyarthaḥ /

etaduktaṃ bhavati---aṅgabhūtānyapi rasāntarāṇi svavibhāvādisāmagnyā svāvasthāyāṃ yadyapi labdhaparipoṣāṇi camatkāragocaratāṃ pratipadyante, tathāpi sa camatkārastāvatyeva na parituṣya viśrāmyati kiṃ tu camatkārāntaramanudhāvati /
children.translated_text: What is said amounts to this: even the subsidiary <s>rasas</s>, through the aggregate of their own <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., when they have attained full nourishment in their own state and have reached the domain of aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) — nevertheless, that wonder does not rest content with just so much, but rather pursues yet another [level of] wonder.
For indeed, in every instance of the principal-subsidiary relation, this is precisely the conclusion.

children.text: yathāha tatrabhavān--- guṇaḥ kṛtātmasaṃskāraḥ pradhānaṃ pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: As the revered [<s>Bharata</s>] says: 'A subordinate [element], having refined itself,
then functions for the benefit of the principal — for indeed, it abides thus in extensive service [to the principal].'

[<s>Locana</s>:] The inclusion, i.e., the supplementation, of a <s>rasa</s> by other <s>rasas</s> — which pervade only limited portions of the narrative by virtue of being governed by the plot — that [supplementation] does not destroy the principal status of the [main <s>rasa</s>] that appears as pervading the entire plot through its <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) status; rather, it nourishes that principal status — this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: 'Of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s>' — /

children.text: yayohi parasparonmūlanātmakatayaivodbhavastatra ko 'ṅgāṅgibhāvaḥ ālambananimagnarūpatayā ca ratiruttiṣṭhati tataḥ palāyamānarūpatayā jugupseti samānāśrayatvena tayoranyonyasaṃskāronmūlanatvam /
children.translated_text: For those whose very arising is of the nature of mutual uprooting — there, what principal-subsidiary relation [could exist]? And since <s>rati</s> (love) arises in the form of being immersed in its object (<s>ālambana</s>), and <s>jugupsā</s> (disgust) [arises] in the form of fleeing from it — because of their sharing the same locus, each uproots the other's disposition. /
<s>Bhaya</s> (fear) and <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) too should likewise be stated as mutually contradictory. /

children.text: śāntasyāpi tattvajñānasamutthitasamastasaṃsāraviṣayanirvedaprāṇatvena sarvato nirīhasvabhāvasya viṣayāsaktijīvitābhyāṃ ratikrodhābhyāṃ virodha eva // 23 //
children.translated_text: And <s>śānta</s> (tranquil <s>rasa</s>) too — since its vital essence is the world-weariness (<s>nirveda</s>) arising from the knowledge of truth toward all objects of worldly existence, [and] since its inherent nature is complete desirelessness — it is indeed in contradiction with <s>rati</s> (love) and <s>krodha</s> (anger), which have their life in attachment to objects and [attachment to] life. // 23 //

'To demonstrate' — the purport is: through the exposition of an appropriate analogy. /
And this is justified precisely by reasoning: for a single governing, pervading purpose (<s>kārya</s>), being served by other incidental purposes, must necessarily be accepted. /
The principal-subsidiary relation of the mental states of the hero that follow in the wake of that [purpose arises] precisely from the force of that [relation among purposes]. /
'Falling into the stream' — the purport is: what is novel here? /
'<s>Tathā</s>' (so too) — [means] by pervasion. /
Or alternatively, the word '<s>eva</s>' is out of [its normal] sequence; [the meaning is:] in exactly that manner, in the form of the principal-subsidiary relation of purposes, the [same relation] of <s>rasas</s> too descends by the very same force — this is the meaning. /
And thus the <s>vṛtti</s> will say: '<s>tathaiva</s>' (in exactly the same way). /
'<s>Kārya</s>' (purpose) — [this refers to] the seed characterized as 'that which, though cast forth in a small measure, spreads in many directions.' /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In some texts, after '<s>bahuṣu</s>' the reading '<s>na</s>' is absent; and in place of 'how is the principal status of one [<s>rasa</s>] not [possible]?' the reading 'the principal status of one' is seen. /
She explains the <s>kārikā</s> — 'of the topic' etc. /
The elaboration of '<s>asya</s>' (of this) — '<s>tasya</s>' (of that) etc. /
She shows the resolution obtained by this <s>kārikā</s> for the objection 'but' etc. — 'what is said' etc. /
'<s>Guṇa</s>' (subordinate) — the subordinate [element]. /
'A subordinate [element], having been refined by another, then — having thus refined itself — functions for the extensive benefit of the principal, the <s>aṅgin</s>' — for indeed [it does]. /
This verse is also cited in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. /
'Through exposition' — the meaning is: through demonstration. /
'This very' — the meaning is: what is about to be stated by '<s>kārya</s>' etc. /
'Following in the wake of that' — the meaning is: attached to the respective purposes. /
'Of the mental states of the hero' — by the word '<s>nāyaka</s>' (hero), the hero, the sub-hero, and all [such characters] are intended here. /
'By the very force of that' — the meaning is: by the very force of the principal-subsidiary relation of the purposes. /
She explains the word '<s>tathā</s>' in the <s>kārikā</s> — 'by pervasion' etc. /
She also explains otherwise — 'or alternatively' etc. /
'Out of [normal] sequence' — the meaning is: the word '<s>eva</s>' connects syntactically with '<s>tathā</s>.' /
Of the body of the extended composition consisting of <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) etc. — just as a single following purpose, being pervasive, is conceived, and it is not confused by other incidental purposes, and even when supplemented by them, its primacy is not diminished — in exactly the same way, even when a single <s>rasa</s> is being established, there is no contradiction whatsoever. /
On the contrary, for those of awakened discrimination who maintain contemplative attention — in the hearts of such sensitive readers — in such a subject-matter, an excess of delight arises. /
Now, [the question of] those <s>rasas</s> that are mutually non-contradictory — such as <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), or <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>hāsya</s> (comic) — [<s>Locana</s>:] [the seed, which is] 'from the germ or the first turning-point [onward], the cause of non-severance when there is a severance of purposes, up to the concluding composition — that is the <s>bindu</s> (drop/point)' — by the <s>arthaprakṛti</s> (content-element) of the <s>bindu</s> form, [it] pervades up to the denouement — thus he says: 'following' etc. /
By this, the two content-elements — <s>bīja</s> (seed) and <s>bindu</s> (point) — are encompassed. /
'By other purposes' — 'the <s>patākā</s> (banner), from the germ or [first] turning-point, withdraws' — the incidental purpose that resides in the content-element characterized as <s>patākā</s>, and those purposes that are of even lesser extent, characterized as <s>prakarī</s> (minor episode) — 'by those' — thus the placement of the five content-elements in the form of sentence-and-paragraph unity has been stated. /
'Of such a kind' — as in [the play] <s>Tāpasavatsarāja</s>. /
Thus, by this verse, two things have been established: the exposition of an analogy for the principal-subsidiary relation, and the fact that the principal-subsidiary relation of <s>rasas</s> falls into being [determined] by the force of the plot. /
The <s>vṛtti</s> text too should be understood with the intent of both [of these points]. /
The non-contradiction of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> with <s>vīra</s> [is present] when, through warfare, strategic prowess, etc., the prize of winning a gem-like maiden [is at stake] etc. /
As for the subsidiary status of <s>hāsya</s> (comic) — that is quite evident. /
Even though <s>hāsya</s> by its own nature does not [serve as] a human goal, by producing greater delight [in the audience], it [functions] precisely as subsidiary to <s>śṛṅgāra</s> — such is its nature. /
Even of <s>raudra</s> (furious), with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> there is somehow no contradiction. /
As stated: '<s>śṛṅgāra</s> is forcefully enjoyed by those [furious ones].' /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'That' — the meaning is: the principal-subsidiary relation. /
Showing the meaning intended by the word '<s>kārya</s>' through etymological derivation, she elaborates — 'that which, though cast forth in a small measure' etc. /
The connection of '<s>bīja</s>' (seed) is with 'pervades.' /
'By this' — the meaning is: by the word '<s>kārya</s>.' /
She elaborates what is intended by 'by other purposes' — 'from the germ' etc. /
'Of even lesser extent than that' — than the content-element characterized as <s>patākā</s>. /
'By those' — up to this, [it is] the elaboration of 'by other purposes.' /
She concludes — 'thus' etc. /
'Has been stated' — the meaning is: indicated by '<s>kārya</s>' and '<s>kāryāntaraiḥ</s>.' /
She illustrates [the meaning of] 'of such a kind [of subject-matter]' — 'as in <s>Tāpasa</s> [vatsarāja]' etc. /
She states the essential meaning — 'thus' etc. /
'By this' — the meaning is: by '<s>kāryam</s>' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: by this verse, two things are established — the exposition of an analogy for the principal-subsidiary relation, and the fact that the principal-subsidiary relation of <s>rasas</s> falls into being [determined] by the force of the plot. /
She demonstrates the non-contradiction of <s>rasas</s> — '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' etc. /
'Non-contradiction' — the meaning is: the absence of contradiction when [they share] a single locus. /
'Its subsidiary status' — subsidiary status to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
'By producing greater delight' — /
Of <s>raudra</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, of <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous), of <s>vīra</s> and <s>raudra</s>, of <s>raudra</s> and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>adbhuta</s> — among these, let there be the principal-subsidiary relation. /
But how would [such a relation be possible] for those whose mutual nature is that of the suppressed and the suppressor? /
For example: <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s> (the disgusting), <s>vīra</s> and <s>bhayānaka</s> (the fearful), <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) and <s>raudra</s>, or <s>śānta</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> — anticipating this [objection], this is stated — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'By them' — the meaning is: by <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Dānavas</s>, and arrogant humans — beginning with the <s>raudra</s> [<s>rasa</s>]. /
Only the naivety pertaining to the <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) should be avoided there. /
The combination of <s>vīra</s> and <s>adbhuta</s> [arises] through the wonder generated by an inconceivable sweeping-away of the earth etc. /
As the sage says: 'And the action that belongs to the heroic [<s>rasa</s>] — that is the wondrous [<s>rasa</s>].' /
The combination of <s>vīra</s> and <s>raudra</s> [occurs] in a <s>dhīroddhata</s> (impetuous-bold) [hero] like <s>Bhīmasena</s> etc. — because of the non-contradiction of anger and enthusiasm. /
The [combination] of <s>raudra</s> and <s>karuṇa</s> too was stated by the sage himself: 'And the action that belongs to the furious [<s>rasa</s>] — that should be known as the pathetic <s>rasa</s>.' /
'Of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>adbhuta</s>' — as in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, in the scene of the magician's display. /

children.translated_text: 'Mutually' — /
the mutual disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — the uprooting of that [disposition], meaning the destruction thereof — this is the meaning. /
'In just this way' — /
the meaning is: because of sharing a single locus. // 23 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] There is also the reading '<s>samadhikarasotpādanena</s>.' /
The meaning is: by the production of excess in the tasting of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>-<s>rasa</s>. /
'Such-ness' (<s>tathātva</s>) — the status of being a human goal. /
'By that' — by <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
'As stated' — 'by the sage' is the remainder. /
She states a distinction — 'only' etc. /
'Inconceivable' etc. — for the wonder of the <s>vīra</s> arises from the attainment of an inconceivable thing. /
'As stated' — 'non-contradiction' is the remainder. /
Here, the non-contradiction should be understood as [arising from] having a single <s>ālambana</s> (object). /
Of <s>raudra</s> and <s>karuṇa</s>, since [their combination] is possible only with different loci. /
'Of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>adbhuta</s> too' — 'non-contradiction' is the remainder. /
She elaborates the stated mutual suppression — 'for of those' etc. /
'Of those' — the meaning is: of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, <s>bībhatsa</s>, and such [pairs]. /
'There, of those two' — /
She shows the reason for the stated [suppression] — '<s>ālambana</s>' etc. /
'Arises' — comes into being. /
'From that' — the meaning is: from the <s>ālambana</s>. /
'<s>Jugupsā</s>' (disgust) — 'arises' carries over. /
'<s>Iti</s>' — in the causal sense. /
'Because of sharing the same locus' — the meaning is: because of having a single <s>ālambana</s> and a single substratum. /
'Of those' — the meaning is: of <s>rati</s> and <s>jugupsā</s>. /
Whether a [subsidiary] <s>rasa</s> is non-contradictory or contradictory with the principal <s>rasa</s> —

children.text: paripoṣaṃ na netavyas tathā syād avirodhitā // DhvK_3.24 //

children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Disregarding the particular <s>rasa</s> that is the principal, he states three modes of avoiding maturation — by the passage from 'therein' to 'third.'

children.translated_text: But when one should say 'it should be made subordinate,' what possibility is there of excess, that he should say 'excess should not be done'? — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'equality of excellence' etc.
'On one side, the beloved weeps; on the other, the blast of battle-trumpets;

children.text: snehena raṇarasena ca bhaṭasya dolāyitaṃ hṛdayam //
children.translated_text: by affection and by the passion for battle, the warrior's heart is swung to and fro.' //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] When the principal [<s>rasa</s>] is another <s>rasa</s> such as <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc., suggested by the composition, a non-antagonistic or antagonistic <s>rasa</s> should not be brought to full maturation. /
Therein, the first [mode of] avoiding maturation is this: the non-antagonistic <s>rasa</s> should not be made excessively superior with respect to the principal <s>rasa</s>. /
Because even when there is equality of excellence between them, conflict does not arise. /
As for example — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'Non-antagonistic or antagonistic' — /
The intention of the word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) is this: when the excellence of another <s>rasa</s> with respect to the principal <s>rasa</s> is being composed, then even a <s>rasa</s> that is not antagonistic to it, when composed [with excess], invites criticism. /
But when, through proper technique, the subsidiary status of the [other] <s>rasa</s> with respect to the principal <s>rasa</s> is logically established, then even an antagonistic <s>rasa</s>, when composed through the device of differentiating domains etc. (as will be stated), does not produce a fault — thus antagonism and non-antagonism are inconsequential. /
Only the manner of placement is to be attended to. /
'<s>Aṅginī</s>' — the locative is in the sense of disregard.

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'This' — /
The meaning is: what will be stated. /
'With respect to' — this connects with 'excellence.' /
'Even though not antagonistic to it' — the meaning is: even though not antagonistic to the principal <s>rasa</s>. /
'As a subsidiary' — the meaning is: through bringing it to subsidiary status. /
'Then' — the meaning is: in that case. /
'<s>Aṅginī</s>' — this is the citation of the text-word. /
'The locative' — the meaning is: the locative in '<s>aṅgini rasāntare</s>' (regarding another <s>rasa</s> as the principal). /
'In the sense of disregard' — the meaning is: the locative is taught by the <s>sūtra</s> 'the sixth case-ending is also [used] in the sense of disregard.' /
The elaboration of the word '<s>rasāntara</s>' — 'a particular <s>rasa</s>.' /
The elaboration of 'disregarding' — 'setting aside.' /
'Should be stated' — the meaning is: when [in fact] one should say 'the non-antagonistic <s>rasa</s> should be made subordinate with respect to the principal <s>rasa</s>.' /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'of them' — the meaning is: of the principal <s>rasa</s> and of another <s>rasa</s> that is not antagonistic to it. /
'On one side' — in one place. /
'On the other' — in another place. /
'Swung to and fro' — agitated by doubt. /
'From the neck' — having cut from the neck. /
The necklace — having removed it from the neck. /
'By the cord of the girdle itself, the lord of serpents' — this is a <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). /
'At twilight' — the heroine-status of twilight (<s>sandhyā</s>) is to be understood. /
In her, the jealousy — because of that, <s>Paśupati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) who attends to the twilight, the Supreme Lord, is made to smile — she by whom [he is so made]. /
'Delighted' — pleased; the verse-meaning is interpolated.

children.translated_text: This is the domain of that view — [Locana:] and the beginning of the second view through 'but in an alternative view' etc. is extremely ill-fitted — enough with much conversation with the predecessors!
'Of those' (<s>yeṣām</s>) —

children.text: bhāvādhyāyasamāptāvasti ślokaḥ--- bahūnāṃ samavetānāṃ rūpaṃ yasya bhavedbahu /
children.translated_text: At the conclusion of the chapter on <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions), there is a verse: 'That whose form is predominant among many assembled [emotions] —

children.text: sa mantavyo rasasthāyī śeṣāḥ sañcāriṇo matāḥ //
children.translated_text: that should be regarded as the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) of <s>rasa</s>; the rest are considered <s>sañcārins</s> (transitory emotions).' //

— in this context: /
The second [method] is: not introducing in abundance <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) that conflict with the principal <s>rasa</s> (<s>aṅgirasa</s>), or, when they are introduced, quickly resuming the <s>vyabhicārin</s> of the principal <s>rasa</s>. /
[Locana:] '<s>Iti</s>' is the <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit rendering). /
'The beloved weeps' — from this, the intensification of <s>rati</s> (love) [is suggested]. /
'<s>Rasaratūrya</s>' and 'of the warrior' — from these, the intensification of <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) [is suggested]. /
'Wavering' (<s>dolāyita</s>) — by this, the equality of those two [rasas], without either being lesser or greater, is stated. /
And some say that this applies only to independent verses (<s>muktaka</s>) and not to extended compositions (<s>prabandha</s>) — but that is wrong; because in plot-based narratives (<s>ādhikārika itivṛtta</s>), the equal prominence of the fruit of the three aims of life (<s>trivarga</s>) is possible. /
For example — in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, with the intention that success depends on the minister, the attainment of sovereignty over the earth is the plot-based fruit, and the attainment of the jewel-maiden is the incidental fruit; but from the hero's perspective, the reverse. Thus, when the intelligence of the minister and the intelligence of the hero — [are unified] by the political maxim that the intellects of lord and minister are one — when unified, it culminates precisely in equal prominence. /
As stated: 'Through the poet's efforts, of the capable leaders' — enough with much digression! /
Having thus established the first mode, he states the second — '<s>aṅgī</s>' etc. /
'Not introducing' — /
'In what has become subordinate' — [Bālapriyā:] the meaning is: through the statement of the <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) in the form of weeping performed by the beloved. /
'Intensification of <s>rati</s>' — /
The connection with 'is stated' is by inversion. /
'Is stated' [means] 'is suggested.' /
'Of those two' — /
The meaning is: of the intensification of <s>rati</s> and the intensification of <s>utsāha</s>. /
'Equality is stated' — /
Here the contextual <s>rasa</s> is <s>vīra</s> (heroic), understood from the force of the word 'of the warrior'; [and] <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, which does not conflict with it, is described with equal prominence. In [verses like] 'from the throat' etc., however, the contextual <s>rasa</s> is <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation), and <s>hāsya</s> (the comic), which does not conflict with it, is shown with equal prominence. /
'This' — /
The meaning is: the equality of the intensification of the two. /
'Only to independent verses' — the meaning is: only in <s>muktaka</s> (independent verses). /
'Of the <s>trivarga</s>' — /
The meaning is: of the fruit that has the form of the three aims of life — its equal prominence — of that. /
'Equal prominence precisely' — the remainder is: of <s>vīra</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
She supplements from 'not introducing' — 'in what has become subordinate' etc. /
'That' — the meaning is: the subordinate <s>rasa</s>. /
The third [method] is: repeatedly reviewing [the subordinate rasa] in its subordinate capacity — of the <s>rasa</s> that, even while being brought to fullness, has become subordinate. /
Other modes too should be conceived in this direction. /
But of the conflicting <s>rasa</s>, some diminishment relative to the principal <s>rasa</s> must be effected. /
As, for example, of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> when <s>śānta</s> (tranquility) is the principal, or of <s>śānta</s> when <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is the principal. /
If [objected:] how can a <s>rasa</s> devoid of fullness have the status of <s>rasa</s>? — the answer is: it has been stated 'relative to the principal <s>rasa</s>.' /
For the principal — [Locana:] the remainder is: '<s>rasa</s>.' /
Now, [if objected:] thus it would not be satisfied — anticipating this objection, he states an alternative view: 'when introduced' etc. /
Therefore, the use of '<s>vā</s>' (or) indicates the firmness of the latter alternative, not a disjunction. /
And thus this is a single [composite] method. /
Otherwise [if taken as a disjunction], there would be two [methods]. /
Of the principal <s>rasa</s>, whichever is its <s>vyabhicārin</s> — its resumption, its reconnection. /
As in the verse 'from anger, the tender swaying creeper-arm' — in the <s>rati</s> (love) that has become the principal, the anger that is introduced as subordinate — therein, having been bound firmly — the resumption of jealousy, eagerness, and joy, which are appropriate <s>vyabhicārins</s> of <s>rati</s>, [follows] quickly through 'she weeps,' 'she laughs,' etc. /
He states the third mode — 'in its subordinate capacity' etc. /
And here, in the <s>Tāpasa-Vatsarāja</s>, the <s>sambhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment in union) of <s>Vatsarāja</s> regarding <s>Padmāvatī</s> should be cited as an example. /
'Others too' — /
The intensification of the <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> [of the conflicting rasa] too should not be done — or the introduction of those conflicting with the principal <s>rasa</s> should not be done at all; and even what has been done should be nourished by [re-framing it through] the <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> of the principal <s>rasa</s> until it becomes identical in form with those. /
Even the <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> of conflicting <s>rasas</s> that have been brought to fullness should be made to awaken to [their] subordinate status — etc. /
One can conceive [these methods] for oneself. /
Having thus stated the mode common to both conflicting and non-conflicting [rasas], he states yet another distinction — specific to conflicting [rasas] — by virtue of being included in the method of avoiding common faults — 'of the conflicting' — [Bālapriyā:] 'in <s>rati</s> as subordinate' — /
The connection of this is with 'introduced.' /
The meaning is: displayed through the medium of <s>anubhāvas</s>. /
'Therein' — /
The meaning is: in the anger — as its <s>vyabhicārin</s>. /
'Should be cited as an example' — /
The purport is: that [sambhoga-śṛṅgāra] is subordinate there. /
'Others too' etc. — she elaborates what was stated: '<s>vibhāvas</s>' etc. /
'Of the <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s>' — the qualifier of this is: 'of those conflicting with the principal <s>rasa</s>.' /
'Introduction should not be done at all' — here the carryover of the two genitive-case [words] applies. /
'Even what has been done' — 'introduction' carries over. /
'Of the principal' — /
Of the principal <s>rasa</s>, whichever are the <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> — by making them identical in form with those — this is the meaning. /
'To be nourished' — to be fostered. /
'To be made to awaken to subordinate status' — to be led to subordinate status. /
'The mode common to both conflicting and non-conflicting' — /
The remainder is: 'which is possible.' /
'Of the conflicting' — /
The meaning is: a particular avoidance-method specific to conflicting [rasas] and not common [to both], which is related to being included in the method of avoiding common faults — that is what is meant. /
'Is possible' — /
Here she supplements: 'of the principal' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>: 'and this' etc. — /
In compositions with multiple <s>rasas</s>, one <s>rasa</s>'s relative pre-eminence — this is impossible to reject — this is the syntactic connection. /
By what is it impossible to reject? — to this it is said: 'of <s>rasas</s>' etc. /
He elaborates this view — '<s>upakārya</s>' (the beneficiary) etc. /
'Otherwise' — /
To the extent that there is no repose in one's own aesthetic relish (<s>camatkāra</s>) — to that extent the fullness should not be produced; but the fullness that naturally occurs — who can obstruct it? /
And this relative pre-eminence of one <s>rasa</s> in multi-<s>rasa</s> compositions — even by those who do not accept the principal-subordinate relationship of <s>rasas</s> — is impossible to reject. And by this method, the introduction of both non-conflicting and conflicting <s>rasas</s> in compositions through the principal-subordinate relationship would be without contradiction. /
And this entire [argument] — of those whose view is that '<s>rasa</s> becomes the <s>vyabhicārin</s> of another <s>rasa</s>' — [Locana:] '<s>iti</s>' means: 'is possible.' /
'Is possible' — the remainder is: 'by virtue of non-contradiction with the principal.' /
'And this' etc. — /
'The beneficiary-benefactor relationship of <s>rasas</s> does not exist, because of [each rasa's] repose in its own aesthetic relish; otherwise, because of the impossibility of <s>rasa</s>-status — and in its absence, how can there be principal-subordinate relationship?' — this too is the view of some. /
Even by them, the pre-eminence of some <s>rasa</s> — [being] greater pervasion of the composition — and the lesser pervasion of the composition by others — must be accepted. Because of the very impossibility of the composition's coherence otherwise — and because, if the <s>rasa</s> that pervades more of the composition has no connection with the other <s>rasas</s>, there would be no coherence of the narrative either — this very beneficiary-benefactor relationship [results]. /
Nor is there any contradiction with aesthetic relish (<s>camatkāra</s>-repose) — as was stated immediately [before]. He says this: 'even by those who do not accept' etc. /
By mere words alone, that one does not accept [this]; /
[but] one is compelled to accept it unwillingly — this is the purport. /
But another explains — the passage 'and this relative' etc. is intended with respect to the second view: where there is no beneficiary-benefactor relationship of <s>rasas</s>, even there, greater narrative-pervasion alone constitutes principal-status — this is the meaning. /
But that is wrong; for thus, the conclusion marked by the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) would apply to only one side — [Bālapriyā:] the meaning is: '[this applies to] that view.' /
'In its absence' — the meaning is: in the absence of <s>rasa</s>-status. /
'How can there be principal-subordinate relationship?' — the principal-subordinate relationship is of <s>rasas</s> — how [can it apply]? — this is the meaning. /
'Even by them' — the connection of this is with 'must be accepted.' /
The passage 'relative pre-eminence of one <s>rasa</s>' is elaborated by this — 'pre-eminence' etc. /
'Pre-eminence' is elaborated: 'greater' etc. /
'Impossible to reject' — the elaboration of this is: 'must be accepted.' /
Here she states the reason — '<s>itivṛtta</s>' (narrative) etc. /
'Of the narrative-coherence' — of the story-coherence. /
'Thus, if accepted, the beneficiary-benefactor relationship too would be accepted' — he says this: 'greater' etc. /
'Connection' — the meaning is: relationship. /
'Of that' — the meaning is: of that. /
'Would not exist' — 'connection' carries over. /
Nor is there any contradiction with <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic relish) — 'the <s>camatkāra</s>-repose' — the syntactic connection is: '[there is] no contradiction of <s>camatkāra</s>-repose whatsoever.' /
'He says' — the meaning is: he says with that purport. /
'By mere words' — by verbal assertion alone — this is the meaning. /
'Must be compelled to accept' — the remainder is: 'by reasoning.' /
'The second view' — the view that will be stated by 'but in an alternative view' etc. — this is the meaning. /
'Of <s>rasas</s>' etc. — /
The meaning is: rather, of those with <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotions). /
'Even there' — the meaning is: even in that view. /
'Greater' etc. — /
And thus, the [idea that] greater narrative-pervasion constitutes principal-status and lesser narrative-pervasion constitutes subordinate-status — this is the purport. /
'By the word <s>sarva</s>' — by using the word '<s>sarva</s>' (all). /
'Conclusion' — 'it is stated by that view' — is the conclusion — this is the meaning. /
'Of one side' — of the one side [being] 'a <s>rasa</s> becomes the <s>vyabhicārin</s> of another <s>rasa</s>' — pertaining to that one view — this is the meaning.

children.translated_text:
Thus. /
According to the method stated therein, the mental modification (<s>cittavṛtti</s>) that pervades the principal narrative (<s>itivṛtta</s>) necessarily shines forth as permanent (<s>sthāyin</s>), while that which terminates in an incidental narrative appears as transitory (<s>vyabhicārin</s>) — thus at the time of aesthetic savoring, there is no contradiction whatsoever between the permanent and transitory status of <s>bhāvas</s> — so some have explained. /
And thus <s>Bhāguri</s> too, having raised the objection 'do <s>rasas</s> also possess the status of being permanent and transitory?,' answered affirmatively: 'indeed they do.' /
But others [say]: even of a <s>rasa</s> that has been listed as permanent (<s>sthāyin</s>), there exists transitory status in another <s>rasa</s> — as anger [is transitory] in <s>vīra</s> (the heroic); and of what has been listed as transitory (<s>vyabhicārin</s>), there is permanent status in another <s>rasa</s> — as world-weariness (<s>nirveda</s>), which manifests knowledge of truth, [is permanent] in <s>śānta</s> (the quiescent); or alternatively, of a <s>vyabhicārin</s> as such, permanence obtains in relation to another <s>vyabhicārin</s> — as of madness (<s>unmāda</s>) in the fourth act of the <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> — to convey this much meaning, this verse [was composed]: 'among the many <s>bhāvas</s> that are modifications of consciousness (<s>cittavṛtti</s>), that whose form is most abundantly perceived is the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion), and that is the <s>rasa</s>, worthy of aesthetic experience (<s>rasīkaraṇa</s>); the rest are transitory (<s>sañcārin</s>)' — thus they explain, and the principal-subordinate relationship (<s>aṅgāṅgitā</s>) of <s>rasas</s> is not thereby stated through their being permanent and transitory <s>bhāvas</s>. /
Therefore, others [read] '<s>rasa-sthāyī</s>' with the genitive, locative, or accusative case in [constructions with] '<s>āśrita</s>' etc. — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'there is also the reading <s>iti ca pāṭhaḥ</s>.' /
That [reading] is poorly connected — this is its deficiency. /
'Of many' — /
the remainder is: of many <s>bhāvas</s> that are assembled and established in oneself. /
The meaning is: of particular modifications of consciousness. /
'Among [them]' — of whichever <s>bhāva</s>, the form is abundant, i.e., greatly pervading the composition. /
'<s>Rasa-sthāyī</s>' — /
the analysis is: '<s>rasaḥ sthāyī</s>' (the <s>rasa</s> is permanent). /
'<s>Kharpare śarī</s>' — this is a case of <s>visarga</s>-elision. /
The construction is: that permanent [<s>bhāva</s>] should be regarded as <s>rasa</s>. /
'The rest' — /
the word '<s>rasāḥ</s>' (rasas) carries over by way of implication. /
Showing the stated meaning, he says — 'therein' etc. /
'According to the method stated therein' — by the method that was stated in that verse. /
'At the time of aesthetic savoring' — /
there is also the reading 'even in aesthetic savoring.' /
'Of the permanent and transitory status of <s>bhāvas</s>' — /
the remainder is: 'of <s>rasas</s>.' /
'And thus' etc. — /
the syntactic connection is: '<s>Bhāguri</s> too answered affirmatively by accepting.' /
Intending to show the justification for that alternative view, he introduces the passage beginning with 'alternative view' — 'but others' etc. /
Herein, up to '<s>vīra</s>' is one sentence; up to '<s>śānta</s>' the second; and up to 'fourth act' the third — this should be understood. /
'Of madness' — /
the remainder is: in relation to deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>) etc. /
The elaboration of 'assembled' is: 'of <s>bhāvas</s> that are modifications of consciousness.' /
The construction is: that should be regarded as the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) and as <s>rasa</s>. /
The explanation of '<s>sthāyī</s>' is: '<s>sthāyibhāva</s>.' /
Of '<s>rasa</s>' — [the explanation is:] 'worthy of aesthetic experience.' /
'The rest' — /
the meaning is: the other <s>bhāvas</s>. /
'Not' etc. — /
rather, the purport is: only of <s>sthāyins</s> (permanent emotions). /
'Proper' — /
there is also the reading 'stated.' /
'With the genitive' etc. — /
the purport is: the analysis is '<s>rasasya</s>' (of <s>rasa</s>), '<s>rase</s>' (in <s>rasa</s>), '<s>rasaṃ</s>' (the <s>rasa</s>) — the permanent [emotion]. /
According to that view, it is stated. /
But in the alternative view: '<s>sthāyins</s> (permanent emotions) of <s>rasas</s>' — <s>bhāvas</s> called <s>rasa</s> by courtesy — the subsidiary status of those is entirely without contradiction. /
Thus, having taught the means of non-contradiction for the incorporation of both non-contradictory and contradictory [<s>rasas</s>] with the principal <s>rasa</s> that pervades the composition, the common [means of non-contradiction] — now, in order to teach that [means] with respect to the contradictory [<s>rasa</s>] alone, this is stated —

children.text: viruddhaikāśrayo yas tu virodhī sthāyino bhavet /
children.translated_text: That which, sharing a single locus, would be an opponent of the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion),

children.text: sa vibhinnāśrayaḥ kāryas tasya poṣe 'py adoṣatā // DhvK_3.25 //
children.translated_text: should be given a separate locus; and even in its nourishment, there is no fault. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.25 //
That which, sharing a single locus, would be an opponent of the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion),
should be given a separate locus; and even in its nourishment, there is no fault. // 25 //

children.text:
/ aikādhikaraṇyavirodhī nairantaryavirodhī ceti dvividho virodhī /
tatra prabandhasthena sthāyināṅginā rasenaucityāpekṣayā viruddhaikāśrayo yo virodhī yathā vīreṇa bhayānakaḥ sa vibhinnāśrayaḥ kāryaḥ /
tasya vīrasya ya āśrayaḥ kathānāyakastadvipakṣaviṣaye sanniveśayitavyaḥ /
tathā sati ca tasya virodhino 'pi yaḥ paripoṣaḥ sa nirdeṣaḥ vipakṣaviṣaye hi bhayātiśayavarṇane locanam gamigāmyādīnāmiti samāsaṃ paṭhanti /
children.translated_text: And when this is done, even the nourishment of that opponent is without fault, for in the description of the excess of fear in the domain of the adversary — [<s>Locana</s>:] they read the compound as '<s>gamigāmyādīnām</s>' (of goers, things to be gone to, etc.).
He says: 'even in the alternative view' etc.
'By the word <s>rasa</s>' — etc.
The meaning is: as stated in the earlier <s>kārikā</s> '<s>rasāntarasamāveśaḥ prastutasya rasasya yaḥ</s>' (the incorporation of another <s>rasa</s> into the <s>rasa</s> under discussion). // 24 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] That which opposes [<s>rasa</s>] through sharing a single locus (<s>aikādhikaraṇya</s>) and that which opposes through contiguity (<s>nairantarya</s>) — the opponent is twofold. /
Therein, that opponent which shares a single locus with the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) that serves as the principal <s>rasa</s> pervading the composition, in terms of propriety — as <s>bhayānaka</s> (the terrible) is [opposed] to <s>vīra</s> (the heroic) — should be given a separate locus. /
That [locus] which is the substratum of the hero of the narrative should be placed in the domain of his adversary.

children.text: tasya virodhino 'pi tathākṛtasya tathānibaddhasya bālapriyā āśritādiṣu gamyādīnāmiti /
children.translated_text: Of that opponent too, when so composed, when so arranged — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>āśritādiṣu gamyādīnām</s>' etc.
The syntactic connection is with 'by the accusative.'
The <s>vārttika</s> 'the listing of <s>gamya</s> etc.' pertaining to the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>dvitīyāśrita</s>' etc. is recalled by this. // 24 //

Now, concluding the common method, he introduces the uncommon [method] — 'thus' etc. /
'That' — the means of non-contradiction. /
'Contradictory' — /
the qualifier contains the reason. /
That which, being contradictory — since the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) cannot conceivably share a single locus with another <s>sthāyin</s> — would be an opponent — as fear [is opposed] to enthusiasm (<s>utsāha</s>) — should be given a separate locus, [that is,] should be directed to the adversary of the hero etc.

children.translated_text:
'The common method' — /
the meaning is: the method of non-contradiction common to both the non-contradictory and the contradictory [opponent]. /
'Concluding' — by this, the <s>vṛtti</s>-meaning up to 'he teaches' is shown. /
'The uncommon' — pertaining to the contradictory [opponent] alone. /
By this, the <s>vṛtti</s>-meaning of 'with respect to the contradictory [<s>rasa</s>] alone' is shown. /
'Contradictory' — the meaning is: of the word '<s>viruddhaikāśraya</s>' (sharing a single locus with the contradictory). /
She elaborates the word '<s>viruddha</s>' — '<s>sthāyī</s>' etc. /
'Whose single locus cannot be conceived' — whose single substratum-status [cannot be conceived]. /
That <s>sthāyin</s> of such a kind. /
'Of that' — /
explaining the referent of that word, he says: 'of that opponent too' etc. /
'So composed' — made with a separate locus. /
The elaboration of the same — 'so arranged.' /
The splendor of the hero's valor, prowess, etc. is all the more brilliantly illuminated. /
And this has been vividly demonstrated in my own [work], the <s>Arjunacarita</s>, in the episode of <s>Arjuna</s>'s descent to the netherworld. /
Thus, it has been shown how the opponent sharing a single locus attains subordinate status to the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) as the <s>rasa</s> pervading the composition, without contradiction. /
But for the second [type of opponent], in order to teach that, it is stated —
When sharing a single locus, [it is] without fault; when contiguous, [it is] contradictory —
<s>rasa</s> should be suggested, by the wise poet, with the intervention of another <s>rasa</s>. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.26 //
When sharing a single locus, [it is] without fault; when contiguous, [it is] contradictory —
<s>rasa</s> should be suggested, by the wise poet, with the intervention of another <s>rasa</s>. // 26 //

children.text:
yaḥ punarekādhikaraṇatve nirvirodho nairantarye tu virodhī sa rasāntakhyavadhānena locanam paripuṣṭatāyāḥ pratyuta nirdeṣatā nāyakotkarṣādhānāt /
aparipoṣaṇantu doṣa eveti yāvat /
apiśabdo bhinnakramaḥ /

children.translated_text: precisely because of the same explanation in the <s>vṛtti</s> as well.

children.text: aikādhikaraṇyamekāśrayeṇa sanbandhamātram, tena virodhī yathā---bhayanotsāhaḥ, ekāśrayatve 'pi sambhavati kaścinni rantaratvena nirvyavadhānatvena virodhī, yathā ratyā nirvedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sharing a single locus (<s>aikādhikaraṇya</s>) means merely the relation of having a single substratum — the opponent of that kind is, for example, <s>bhayānaka</s> (the terrible) with <s>vīra</s> (the heroic); even when sharing a single locus, there is a certain [opponent] that is contradictory through contiguity (<s>nairantarya</s>), i.e., through being without interval — as <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness) is [contradictory] with <s>rati</s> (love).
'Has been demonstrated' —

children.text: 'samutthite dhanurdhvanau bhayāvahe kirīṭino mahānuplavo 'bhavatpure purandaradviṣām' ityādinā // 25 //
children.translated_text: by [the verse] '<s>samutthite dhanurdhvanau bhayāvahe kirīṭinaḥ</s>' (when the terrifying sound of the bow of the crowned one [<s>Arjuna</s>] arose), '<s>mahānuplavo 'bhavat pure purandaradviṣām</s>' (a great calamity befell the city of the enemies of <s>Indra</s>) — etc. // 25 //

That which, again, is non-contradictory when sharing a single locus but contradictory through contiguity — that [should be suggested] with the interposition of another <s>rasa</s> — [<s>Locana</s>:] rather, when nourished, there is faultlessness — because it enhances the hero's excellence. /
But non-nourishment is indeed a fault — this much [is meant]. /
The word '<s>api</s>' (even) is in a different sequence.

dvitīyasyeti /
nairantaryavirodhinaḥ /
taditi /
nirvirodhitvam /

gamyamarthamāha--aparipoṣaṇantvityādi /
apiśabda iti /

evaṃ kārikāvyākhyānena 'tatre'tyādivṛttigranthasya vivaraṇādaikādhikaraṇyavirodhītyādipūrvabhāgamātraṃ bhayenotsāha iti /
