children.translated_text: '<s>śraveṇa tasya tu dhvaner viluptalabandhanaṃ aśeṣadaityayoṣitāṃ ślathībabhūva jīvitam</s>' (but by hearing that sound, the life of all the <s>Daitya</s> women, whose bonds of shame were severed, became slack) — [this is] the latter half.
The syntactic connection is: at the sound of the bow of the crowned one (<s>kirīṭin</s>), <s>Arjuna</s>.
'Of the enemies of <s>Purandara</s>' — of the <s>Asuras</s> (demons).
The [passage] beginning with '<s>śraveṇa</s>' is merely a partial elaboration of the calamity (<s>upplava</s>) itself. // 25 //

'Of the second' — of the opponent through contiguity. /
'That' — the non-contradictoriness. /
'When sharing a single locus' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] she explains '<s>poṣe adoṣatā</s>' (faultlessness in nourishment) — 'rather' etc. /
She states the implied meaning — 'but non-nourishment' etc. /
'The word <s>api</s>' — the meaning is: the word '<s>api</s>' in '<s>poṣe 'py adoṣatā</s>' (even in nourishment, faultlessness). /
'Because of the explanation' — the meaning is: because of the explanation '<s>tasya virodhino 'pi</s>' (of that opponent too). /
Thus, through the explanation of the <s>kārikā</s>, the elaboration of the <s>vṛtti</s> text beginning with '<s>tatra</s>' — only the first portion up to '<s>bhayenotsāhaḥ</s>' (fear with enthusiasm). /
She explains '<s>nairantaryavirodhī</s>' (the opponent through contiguity) — 'when sharing a single locus' etc. /
'When sharing a single locus' — even when possible — a certain [opponent] that is contradictory through contiguity — this is the syntactic connection. /
The elaboration of 'through contiguity' — 'through being without interval.' /
'When arose' —

children.text:
vṛttau 'aikādhikaraṇyavirodhina' ityasya 'aṅgabhāvagamane nirvirodhitva'mityanena sambandhaḥ /
kārikāyām /
'ekāśrayatve nairantarye'ityubhayatra saptamī nimitta ityāśayena vyācaṣṭe---ekāśrayatvenetyādi /
nirdeṣa ityasya vyākhyānam---na virodhīti /
prabandhe niveśāyitavyaḥ /
yathā śāntaśṛṅgārau nāgānande niveśitau /
locanam nimittena yo nirdeṣaḥ na virodhī kiṃ tu nirantaratvena nimittena virodhameti sa tathāvidhaviruddharasadvayāvaruddhena rasāntareṇa madhye niveśitena yuktaḥ kārya iti kārikārthaḥ /
prabandha iti bāhulyāpekṣaṃ, muktake 'pi kadācidevaṃ bhavedapi /
yadvakṣyati---'ekavākyasthayorapi' iti /
yatheti /
tatra hi--'rāgasyāspadamityavaimi na hi me dhvaṃsīti na pratyayaḥ' ityādinopakṣepātprabhṛti parārthaśarīravitaraṇātmakanirvahaṇaparyantaḥ śānto rasastasya viruddho malayavatīviṣayaḥ śṛṅgārastadubhayāviruddhamadbhutamantarīkutya kramaprasarasambhāvanābhiprāyeṇa kavinā nibaddhaḥ 'aho gītamaho vāditram' iti /
etadarthameva 'vyaktirvyañjanadhātunā' ityādi nīrasaprāyamapyatra nibaddhamadbhutarasaparipoṣakatayātyantarasarasatāvahamiti 'nirdeṣadarśanāḥ kanyakāḥ puruṣārthahetukamidaṃ nimittanaimittikaprasaṅgene'ti /
anantaraṃ ca nimittanaimittikaprasaṅgāgato yaḥ śekharakavṛttāntoditahāsyarasopakṛtaḥ śṛṅgārastasya viruddho yo vairāgyaśamapoṣako nāgīyakalebarāsthijālāvalokanādivṛttāntaḥ sa bālapriyā virodhavānityasya vivaraṇam---virodhametīti /
uttarārdhaṃ vyācaṣṭe---sa ityādi /
prabandha itīti /
prabandhe niveśāyitavya ityatra prabandhagrahaṇamityarthaḥ /
yathā śāntaśṛṅgārau nāgānande niveśitāvityetadvivṛṇoti---tatretyādi /
ityādinā ya upakṣepasta smādityarthaḥ /
pareti /
parārthaṃ yaccharīravitaraṇaṃ tadātmakaṃ yannirvahaṇaṃ tatparyanta ityarthaḥ /
śānto rasa iti nibaddha ityasyāpakarṣaḥ /
tasyetyādi /
śṛṅgāraḥ ityadbhumantarīkṛtya nibaddha ityanvayaḥ /
krameti /
krameṇa yaḥ prasaraḥ ratirūpaśṛṅgārasya nāyake prasaraṇaṃ tasya sambhāvanārūpo ya abhaprāyastenetyarthaḥ /
ityādinibaddhamiti sambandhaḥ /
iti ceti /
nirdeṣadarśanāḥ kanyakā ityuktyā vaktari ratyanāvirbhāvaprakāśanāditi bhāvaḥ /
cittavṛttīti /
cittavṛttīnāṃ rāgādīnāṃ ye prasarāsteṣu, yadvā cittavṛttīnāṃ prasaro yeṣu viṣayeṣu teṣu yatprasaṃkhyānaṃ doṣadarśanaṃ, tadeva dhanaṃ yeṣāṃ te /
tadvacanamāha--puruṣārthetyādi /
sāṃkhyakārikāyāḥ pūrvārdhamidam /
"prakṛtervibhutvayogānnaṭavadyvavatiṣṭhate liṅam" ityuttarārtham /
nimittaṃ dharmādinaimittikaṃ dharmādikāraṇaṃ sthūladehādi tayoḥ prasaṅgena sambandhena /
'idaṃ liṅgaṃ' sakṣmaśarīram /
'naṭavadvyavatiṣṭhate' yathā naṭo vividhaṃ rūpaṅgṛhītvā vyavaharati tathā devādiśarīraṃ gṛhītvā vyavaharati /
kimartham, tatrāha--'puruṣārthe'ti /
puruṣārthaphalakamityarthaḥ /
tattadbhogādṛṣṭabalāttattadbhogārthameva tathā vyavaharatīti yāvat /
kuto 'syaiṃvavidho mahimetyatrāha---'prakṛte'rityādi /

children.translated_text: Thus is the explanation thereof. /

children.text: śāntaśca tṛṣṇākṣayasuravasya yaḥ paripoṣastallakṣaṇo rasaḥ pratīyata eva /
children.translated_text: And the <s>śānta</s> [sentiment] — the <s>rasa</s> whose characteristic is the maturation of the bliss of the extinction of craving (<s>tṛṣṇākṣaya</s>) — is indeed perceived. /

children.text: tathā coktam--- yacca kāmasukhaṃ loke yacca divyaṃ mahatsukham /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said — 'Whatever happiness of desire exists in the world, and whatever great celestial happiness there is —
these do not amount to a sixteenth part of the happiness of the extinction of craving.' //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In the <s>Vṛtti</s>, the connection of '<s>aikādhikaraṇyavirodhina</s>' (conflicting through co-location) is with 'absence of conflict when going to subsidiary status.' /
In the <s>kārikā</s>: /
With the intent that the locative in both [clauses] '<s>ekāśrayatve</s>' (when there is a single locus) and '<s>nairantarye</s>' (when there is contiguity) is in the sense of cause (<s>nimitta</s>), he glosses — 'by virtue of being on a single locus' etc. /
The commentary on '<s>nirdeśa</s>' (indication) — 'is not contradictory' etc. /
Should be installed in the extended composition (<s>prabandha</s>). /
As <s>śānta</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> were installed in the <s>Nāgānanda</s>. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The indication that is [made] by cause — that [indication] is not contradictory; rather, through contiguity as the cause, [what] arrives at contradiction — that should be made proper by means of another <s>rasa</s> installed in between, one that is contained within the pair of conflicting <s>rasas</s> — this is the meaning of the <s>kārikā</s>. /
The word '<s>prabandha</s>' (extended composition) is with reference to prevalence; in a <s>muktaka</s> (stand-alone verse) too, this could sometimes occur. /
As he will state — 'even of the two situated in a single sentence.' /
'As' — /
For there, in the <s>Nāgānanda</s> — from the <s>upakṣepa</s> (introduction) beginning with '<s>rāgasyāspadamityavaimi na hi me dhvaṃsīti na pratyayaḥ</s>' (I know that [this body] is the abode of passion; I have no conviction that it will not perish) up to the <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion) that consists of giving away one's body for another's sake — <s>śānta rasa</s> (the quiescent sentiment) [extends]; the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> directed toward <s>Malayavatī</s>, which conflicts with it — with <s>adbhuta</s> (the marvelous), which does not conflict with either, placed as intermediary — was composed by the poet with the intention of allowing a gradual unfolding: '<s>aho gītam aho vāditram</s>' (ah, the song! ah, the music!). /
For this very purpose, [the passage] '<s>vyaktir vyañjana-dhātunā</s>' (manifestation [arises] through the medium of suggestion) etc. — though mostly devoid of <s>rasa</s> — was composed here, and as [an element] that promotes the maturation of <s>adbhuta rasa</s>, it brings about extreme savorousness: '<s>nirdeśadarśanāḥ kanyakāḥ</s>' (the maidens are [those who] look at the indication), '<s>puruṣārtha-hetukam idaṃ nimitta-naimittikaprasaṅgena</s>' (this [subtle body] serves the purpose of <s>puruṣārtha</s>, through the connection of cause and effect)' etc. /
And then, the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> that has arrived through the connection of cause and effect, supported by the <s>hāsya rasa</s> (comic sentiment) arising from the episode of <s>Śekhara</s> — [and] the episode of viewing the bones and skeleton of the <s>Nāgīya</s> (serpent) body, which nourishes <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) and <s>śama</s> (tranquility) and which conflicts with that [<s>śṛṅgāra</s>] — that — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The elaboration of 'arrives at contradiction' — 'arrives at contradiction' etc. /
She glosses the second half — 'that' etc. /
'The word <s>prabandha</s>' etc. — /
The meaning is: the use of the word '<s>prabandha</s>' in '<s>prabandhe niveśāyitavyaḥ</s>' (should be installed in the extended composition). /
She elaborates on 'as <s>śānta</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> were installed in the <s>Nāgānanda</s>' — 'there' etc. /
The meaning is: from the <s>upakṣepa</s> (introduction) [consisting of] the passage beginning with [those words]. /
'For another's sake' — /
The meaning is: the <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion) which consists of the giving away of one's body for another's sake — up to that point. /
'<s>Śānta rasa</s>' — the syntactic connection is with 'was composed.' /
'Of that' etc. — /
The syntactic connection is: '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>,' with <s>adbhuta</s> placed as intermediary, 'was composed.' /
'Gradual unfolding' — /
The meaning is: the gradual unfolding that is the spreading forth of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> in the form of love in the hero — the intention that has the form of anticipation of that. /
The syntactic connection is: '[was composed] beginning with [those words] etc.' /
'And' — /
'The maidens who look at the indication' — by this statement, [the fact that] the non-manifestation of love in the speaker [is conveyed] — this is the purport. /
'Mental activities' — /
Of the mental activities such as passion etc. — in their outflowings; or, of the mental activities — the outflowing — in those objects toward which [they flow] — [those objects] in which the discernment that is the seeing of faults is itself the wealth — those [who are such]. /
He states that utterance — '<s>puruṣārtha</s>' etc. /
This is the first half of a <s>Sāṃkhya-kārikā</s>. /
'<s>prakṛter vibhutva-yogān naṭavad vyavatiṣṭhate liṅgam</s>' (by the association with the pervasiveness of <s>Prakṛti</s>, the subtle body abides like an actor) — this is the second half. /
'Cause' (<s>nimitta</s>) — <s>dharma</s> (merit) etc.; 'effect' (<s>naimittikaṃ</s>) — the gross body etc. caused by <s>dharma</s> etc.; through their connection. /
'This <s>liṅga</s>' — the subtle body. /
'Abides like an actor' — just as an actor, having assumed various forms, acts, so too [the subtle body], having assumed bodies of gods etc., acts. /
For what purpose? — to this he says: '<s>puruṣārtha</s>' etc. /
The meaning is: having the fruit of <s>puruṣārtha</s> (the goals of human life). /
For the sake of the enjoyment of this and that — by the force of unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) — for the sake of this and that enjoyment alone it so acts — this much [is the meaning]. /
How does it have such greatness? — to this he says: 'of <s>Prakṛti</s>' etc. /

locanam mitrāvasoḥ praviṣṭasya malayavatīnirgamanakāriṇaḥ 'saṃsarpadbhiḥ samantāt' ityādi /
kāvyopanibaddhakrodhavyabhicāryupakṛtavīrarasāntarito niveśitaḥ /
nanu nāstyeva śānto rasaḥ tasya tu sthāyyeva nopadiṣṭo muninetyāśaṅkyāha--śāntaśceti /
tṛṣṇānāṃ viṣayābhilāṣāṇāṃ yaḥ kṣayaḥ sarvato nivṛttirūpo nirvedaḥ tadeva sukhaṃ tasya sthāyibhūtasya yaḥ paripoṣo rasyamānatākṛtastadeva lakṣaṇaṃ yasya sa śānto rasaḥ /
pratīyata eveti /
svānubhavenāpi nivṛttabhojanādyaśeṣaviṣayecchāprasaratvakāle sambhāvyata eva /
anye tu sarvacittavṛttipraśama evāsya sthāyīti manyante /
tṛṣṇāsadbhāvasya prasajyaprataṣedharūpatve cetovṛttitvābhāvena bhāvatvāyogāt /
paryudāse tvasmatpakṣa evāyam /
bālapriyā kāmāditattatpuruṣārthalābhaḥ krameṇaiva bhavatītyaṃśe upaṣṭambhakamidaṃ vacanamiti bodhyam /
niveśita ithi /
nāgānandanāṭakamavalokayatāṃ sahṛdayānāṃ spaṣṭo 'yaṃ viṣayaḥ /
nivṛttirūpo nirveda iti /
nivṛttirūpaḥ pradhvaṃsahetuḥ /
nirveda iti /
tattvajñānajanito viṣayeṣu heyatvabuddhirityarthaḥ /
yadvā---sarvato nivṛttirūpa iti /
sarvasmādviṣayānmanonivṛttirūpa ityarthaḥ /
nivṛttirnāma kāciccittavṛttiḥ /
tasya sthāyibhūtasyeti /
sukhasyetyantasya vivaraṇam /
rasyamānatākṛto yaḥ paripoṣa iti sambandhaḥ /
nivṛtteti /
nivṛttaḥ bhojanādyaśeṣaviṣayāyā icchāyāḥ prasaro yataḥ puruṣāttasya bhāvastatvaṃ tasya kāle prasarakāle iti vā pāṭhaḥ /
sambhāvyate jñāyate /
śamaḥ sthāyīti kecit /
tanmatamāha--anya iti /
sarveti /
sarvāsāṃ cittavṛttīnāṃ ratyādirūpāṇāṃ praśamaḥ prakarṣeṇa śama ityarthaḥ /
tṛṣṇākṣayaśabdārtho 'pyayameveti bhāvaḥ /
asyeti /
śāntasyetyarthaḥ /
sarvacittavṛttipraśama ityanena sarvāsāṃ cittavṛttīnāmabhāvasya vivakṣaṇedoṣaṃ darśayannāha--tṛṣṇetyādi /
tṛṣṇānāṃ sarvāsāṃ cittavṛttīnāṃ sadbhāvasya prasarasya yaḥ prasajyapratiṣedho 'tyantābhāvastadrūpatve /
sarvacittavṛttipraśamapadārthasyeti śeṣaḥ /
cetovṛttitvābhāveneti /
abhāvarūpatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
bhāvatvāyogāditi /
bhāvāntarbhāvāsambhavādityarthaḥ /
paryudāsa iti /

children.translated_text: The remainder is: 'is intended.' /
The meaning is: when the meaning is intended by the method of <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion-type negation). /

children.text: yathā adharmādipadasya dharmavarodhipāpādikamarthaḥ, tathā tṛṣṇākṣayapadasya sarvañcittavṛttipraśamapadasya vā sarvacittavṛttivirodhī locanam anye tu--- svaṃ svaṃ nimittamāsādya śāntādbhāvaḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: Just as the meaning of the word '<s>adharma</s>' (non-dharma) is sin etc. that opposes <s>dharma</s>, so the meaning of the word '<s>tṛṣṇākṣaya</s>' (extinction of craving), or of the expression '<s>sarvacittavṛttipraśama</s>' (quiescence of all mental activities), is [a particular mental state] that opposes all mental activities — [<s>Locana</s>:] But others — '<s>svam svam nimittam āsādya śāntād bhāvaḥ pravartate</s>' — each <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), having encountered its own particular cause, proceeds forth from the quiescent [state];
'<s>punar nimittāpāye tu śānta eva pralīyate</s>' — and again, upon the disappearance of [its] cause, it dissolves back into the quiescent [state] alone. //

[<s>Locana</s>:] Upon the entry of <s>Mitrāvasu</s>, [it is the passage] beginning with '<s>saṃsarpadbhiḥ samantāt</s>' (creeping all around) etc. that causes the exit of <s>Malayavatī</s>. /
[<s>Śṛṅgāra</s>] was installed as intermediated by the <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic sentiment) associated with the <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) of anger, which is connected with the poetry of the composition. /
Now, anticipating the objection that <s>śānta rasa</s> does not exist at all, and that its <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) has not been taught by the sage [<s>Bharata</s>], he says — 'and <s>śānta</s>' etc. /
The extinction of cravings — that is, the complete cessation in the form of turning away from desires for objects — that is <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness); that itself is the happiness; the maturation of it in the form of being savored — that very [maturation] being the characteristic of which — that is the <s>śānta rasa</s>. /
'Is indeed perceived' — /
Even from one's own experience, during the time when the outflow of desire for all objects without exception — food and so forth — has ceased, [it] is indeed envisaged. /
But others hold that the complete quiescence of all mental activities is its <s>sthāyin</s>. /
[The objection:] Since the absence of the existence of cravings, having the form of a <s>prasajya-pratiṣedha</s> (implicative negation), would lack the nature of a mental activity and thus could not qualify as a <s>bhāva</s> (emotion) — /
But in the <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion-type negation) interpretation, this is precisely our own position. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] It should be understood that this statement supports the view that the attainment of each successive <s>puruṣārtha</s> (goal of human life) — <s>kāma</s> (desire) etc. — occurs only gradually. /
'Was installed' — /
This subject matter is clear to sensitive readers who examine the <s>Nāgānanda</s> play. /
'Cessation in the form of turning away' — /
The meaning is: [<s>nirveda</s>] whose form is [that of] being the cause of destruction. /
'<s>Nirveda</s>' — /
The meaning is: the cognition of worthlessness toward objects, born of true knowledge. /
Or: 'complete cessation in the form of turning away' — /
the meaning is: the turning away of the mind from all objects. /
Cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>) is a certain mental activity. /
'Of it in its permanent state' — this is the elaboration of 'of happiness' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: 'the maturation that consists in being savored.' /
'Ceased' — /
'<s>Nivṛttaḥ</s>' — of the person from whom the outflow of desire for all objects — food and the like — has ceased — the state of being such — at the time of that state — or there is also the reading '<s>prasarakāle</s>' (at the time of outflow). /
'Is envisaged' — is known. /
'Quiescence is the <s>sthāyin</s>' — so hold some. /
He states their view — 'others' etc. /
'Of all' — /
the meaning is: the quiescence — that is, the intense calming — of all mental activities in the form of love (<s>rati</s>) etc. /
The purport is that the meaning of the word '<s>tṛṣṇākṣaya</s>' (extinction of craving) is also precisely this. /
'Of this' — /
the meaning is: of <s>śānta</s>. /
Showing the fault in the intention of denoting the absence of all mental activities by '<s>sarvacittavṛttipraśama</s>' (complete quiescence of all mental activities), he says — '<s>tṛṣṇā</s>' etc. /
The absolute absence — in the form of a <s>prasajya-pratiṣedha</s> (implicative negation) — of the existence, i.e., the outflow, of all mental activities, i.e., all cravings — if [the quiescence of all mental activities] were to have such a form — /
The remainder is: of the meaning of the expression '<s>sarvacittavṛttipraśama</s>.' /
'By the absence of the nature of a mental activity' — /
the purport is: because [it] has the nature of an absence. /
'Could not qualify as a <s>bhāva</s>' — /
the meaning is: because of the impossibility of being included among the <s>bhāva</s>s. /
'<s>Paryudāsa</s>' — /

iti bharatavākyaṃ dṛṣṭavantaḥ sarvarasasāmānyasvābhāvaṃ śāntamācakṣaṇā anupajātaviśeṣāntaracittavṛttirūpaṃ śāntasya sthāyibhāvaṃ manyante /
etacca nātīvāsmatpakṣāddūram /
prāgabhāvapradhvaṃsābhāvakṛtastu viśeṣaḥ /
yuktaśca pradhvaṃsa eva tṛṣṇānām /
yathoktam---'vītarāgajanmādarśanāt' iti /
pratīyata eveti /
munināpyaṅgīkriyata eva 'kvacicchamaḥ' ityādi /
vadatā /
na ca tadīyā paryantāvasthā varṇanīyā yena sarvaceṣṭoparamādanubhāvābhāvenāpratīyamānatā syāt /
'śṛṅgārāderapi phalabhūmāvavarṇanīyataiva pūrvabhūmau tu 'tasya praśāntavāhitā saṃskārāt /
tacchidreṣu pratyayāntarāṇa saṃskārebhyaḥ' bālapriyā cittavṛttiviśeṣo yadi vivakṣitastadeti yāvat /
asmatpakṣa evāyamiti /
nirvedarūpacittavṛttiviśeṣe eva paryavasānāditi bhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: '<s>Svam svam</s>' (each one's own) — /
This verse is found in the concluding portion of the sixth chapter [of the <s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s>]. /

children.text: asmātpūrvo 'yaṃ ślokaḥ--- bhāvā vikārā ratyādyāḥ śāntastu prakṛtarmataḥ /
children.translated_text: The verse preceding this one is — '<s>bhāvā vikārā ratyādyāḥ śāntas tu prakṛtir mataḥ</s>' — the <s>bhāva</s>s such as <s>rati</s> (love) etc. are modifications; but <s>śānta</s> is considered the natural state (<s>prakṛti</s>). /
A modification born from the natural state dissolves back into that very [natural state]. //

Thus, those who have observed this statement of <s>Bharata</s> and who describe <s>śānta</s> as the common nature of all <s>rasas</s> hold that the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) of <s>śānta</s> is in the form of a mental state in which no other particular mental activity has arisen. /
And this is not very far from our own position. /
The distinction, however, is based on prior-absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) versus destruction-absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>). /
And the destruction [of cravings] alone is the proper [reading], since it is the extinction of cravings [that is meant]. /
As stated — '<s>vītarāga-janmā darśanāt</s>' (born from one who is free from passion, as is observed). /
'Is indeed perceived' — /
Even the sage [<s>Bharata</s>] accepts it, as shown by [his] saying '<s>kvacic chamaḥ</s>' (sometimes tranquility) etc. /
Speaking [thus]. /
Nor is it the case that the final stage of that [<s>śānta rasa</s>] should be depicted, such that through the absence of all activity and hence the absence of <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), there would be non-perceptibility. /
'Even for <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc., in the stage of fruition, there is indeed non-depictability; but in the prior stage, its calm flow [is established] from <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impressions). /
In the gaps of those [impressions], other cognitions [arise] from [other] <s>saṃskāra</s>s' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] if a particular type of mental activity is intended — then that much [is the import]. /
'This is precisely our own position' — /
the purport is: because it culminates in a particular mental activity in the form of <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness). /

children.translated_text: And the common form is being useful for the acquisition of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>.

children.text: nanvevaṃ dayāvīro dharmavīro dānavīro vā nāsau kaścit, śāntasyaivedaṃ nāmāntarakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: But thus, compassion-hero, <s>dharma</s>-hero, or generosity-hero — he is not any [of these]; this is merely a renaming of <s>śānta</s> [as <s>vīra</s>].

children.text: tathā hi muniḥ-- dānavīraṃ dharmavīraṃ yuddhavīraṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: For thus the sage [<s>Bharata</s>] said: '<s>Dānavīra</s> (generosity-hero), <s>dharmavīra</s> (dharma-hero), <s>yuddhavīra</s> (battle-hero),
and <s>rasavīra</s> (passion-hero) too — <s>Brahmā</s> declared [<s>vīra</s>] to be of three kinds with [this] fourfold classification.' //

'Thus' — /
'One's own' — one's own, belonging to oneself. /
'Occasion' — in the form of women etc. /
'From the tranquil' — from the unmodified inner faculty (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) which is [one's] nature (<s>prakṛti</s>). /
'Emotion' — <s>rati</s> (love) etc. /
'Follows' — /
A mental state (<s>cittavṛtti</s>) in which no particular [modification] has arisen, which does not depend on the particular external objects such as women etc., which is internal and directed toward the self — of that nature, this is the meaning. /
'This' — the meaning is: the stated view. /
'Not too far' etc. — the meaning is: close to our position. /
'Prior non-existence' — /
The meaning is: this position terminates in the prior non-existence of all mental states, whereas our position [terminates] in the absolute destruction of all mental states — this is the distinction. /
'And it is proper' etc. — the meaning is: only the position of the destruction of craving is proper. /
'As stated' — the meaning is: it has been stated that there is the destruction of all cravings. /
The remainder is: by the author of the <s>Nyāyasūtras</s>. /
'Free from passion' — /
This <s>sūtra</s> is located in the third chapter, first section. /
'Of one free from passion' — of one devoid of <s>rāga</s> (passion) etc. /
'Because birth is not seen' — since birth does not occur, therefore — this is the meaning. /
But only for one possessing passion is there birth — this is the purport. /
This serves to establish the eternality of the self. /
He explains 'is indeed apprehended' also in another way — 'by the sage' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: 'by the sage who speaks.' /
Here 'the state of tranquility' means directed toward <s>nirveda</s> (disillusionment) through <s>yoga</s> — this is the purport. /
For the cessation of activity etc. are the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) of <s>śānta</s> to be stated, and they are not suitable for dramatic representation. /
Therefore, some say that <s>śānta</s> is not apprehensible through its <s>anubhāvas</s>; to refute that view, he says: 'nor' etc. /
'Of that' — the meaning is: related to <s>śānta</s>. /
'The final state' — the state of desirelessness. /
'Not being apprehensible' — the remainder is: of <s>śānta</s>. /
'In the stage of fruition' — the meaning is: in the state of erotic enjoyment. /
'In the prior stage' etc. — /
The connection is: but in the prior stage, the actions of <s>Janaka</s> and others characterized by <s>śānta</s> are indeed observed. /
The variegated [<s>Locana</s>:] — from the two <s>sūtras</s> here — activities like <s>yama</s> (restraint), <s>niyama</s> (observance), etc. that are wondrous in form, or activities characterized by bearing the yoke of kingship etc. — even of <s>Janaka</s> and others who are characterized by <s>śānta</s>, these are indeed observed — thus, because of the existence of <s>anubhāvas</s>, and because of the existence of numerous <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) conceivable within [the practice of] <s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, etc. — [<s>śānta rasa</s>] is indeed apprehended. /
If one objects: 'it is not apprehended, and its <s>vibhāvas</s> do not exist' — no; it is indeed apprehended. /
And its <s>vibhāvas</s> must indeed exist — the ripening of previous meritorious deeds, the grace of the Supreme Lord, the study of esoteric scriptures of the self (<s>adhyātmarahasyaśāstra</s>), the cultivation of those free from passion, etc. — by these <s>vibhāvas</s>. Thus the existence of <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s>, as well as the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion), has been demonstrated. /
If one objects: 'there is no accord of the heart there, so the status of being relished is not established' — who says thus that it does not exist? For it has been said that it is indeed apprehended. /
If one objects: 'it is apprehended, but it is not a matter of praise for everyone' — then <s>śṛṅgāra</s> too [does not please] those who are free from passion — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The various states — those are called stages (<s>bhūmis</s>). /
'<s>Praśānta</s>' etc. — /
'From the <s>saṃskāra</s> (impression) of its tranquil flow, [and] in its intervals, other cognitions [arise] from the <s>saṃskāras</s>' — these are <s>Yoga Sūtras</s>. /
Of the first [<s>sūtra</s>], this is <s>Bhoja's</s> commentary: 'Of that mind, from the <s>saṃskāra</s> of cessation as described, there arises tranquil flow — the mind, having abandoned distractions, undergoes a transformation of uniform flow — this is the meaning.' /
This <s>sūtra</s> is in the third section, and '<s>tacchidra</s>' etc. is in the fourth. /
Of this too, <s>Bhoja's</s> commentary is: 'In that <s>samādhi</s>, in the intervals of one who is established [therein], the other cognitions that are of the nature of arising [from samādhi] — those knowledges arise from the <s>saṃskāras</s> born of the experience of arising, which are of the form "I" and "mine," even though they are diminishing.' /
'Wondrous in form' — the meaning is: causing wonder. /
'Kingdom' etc. — the remainder is: activities. /
Here the distinction is: during the time of <s>samādhi</s>, activities like <s>yama</s> etc.; during the time of arising, activities like bearing the yoke of kingship. /
'Of <s>Janaka</s> etc.' — King <s>Janaka</s> is well known as a great <s>yogin</s>. /
'Thus' — in the sense of reason. /
'<s>Yama</s>' — the meaning is: because of the existence of numerous <s>vyabhicārins</s> such as <s>mati</s> (deliberation), <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), <s>smṛti</s> (memory), etc. that are conceivable in the midst of, i.e. within, the <s>yoga</s>-limbs such as <s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, etc. /
'Is indeed apprehended' — the remainder is: <s>śānta rasa</s>. /
He raises a doubt — 'but' etc. /
'But it is apprehended' — the remainder is: <s>śānta</s>. /
'Why?' — to this he says: 'its [vibhāvas] do not exist' etc. /
He resolves — 'no' etc. /
'What then are the <s>vibhāvas</s>?' — to this he says: 'of that' etc. /
'Of that' — and its <s>vibhāvas</s> must indeed exist — this is the syntactic connection. /
He enumerates them — 'previous' etc. /
The ripening of previous meritorious deeds (<s>kuśala</s>), and the grace of the Supreme Lord, and the cultivation of esoteric self-knowledge scriptures such as <s>Vedānta</s> etc. and of those free from passion — by these and other [<s>vibhāvas</s>], this is the meaning. /
He concludes — 'thus' etc. /
'By this much alone' — by the method just described alone. /
He raises a doubt — 'but' etc. /
'There' — in <s>śānta</s>. /
'Of the heart' — the remainder is: of the cognizers. /
He resolves — 'who' etc. /
'That' — the accord of the heart; 'stated' — /
The remainder is: by the <s>vṛtti</s>-author. /
He introduces the passage beginning with 'if indeed' — 'but' etc. /
'Is apprehended' — the remainder is: <s>śānta</s>. /
He states the distinguishing [point] — 'of everyone' etc. /
He answers the objection — 'then' etc. /
'That [<s>śṛṅgāra</s>] too' — even that <s>śṛṅgāra</s> too — 'he says thus.' /
The meaning is: he says with that intention. /
'But' etc. — /
That [<s>śānta</s>], being predominantly <s>dharma</s>-oriented, if it is perhaps [merely] <s>vīra rasa</s> — if one supposes thus — even granted that it is not within the experience of all people, it is not [therefore] possible to deny that it is a great mental state within the reach of universal, exalted beings. /
Nor is it proper to subsume it within <s>vīra</s> (heroic), since [<s>vīra</s>] has been established as consisting of self-assertion (<s>abhimāna</s>), /
whereas this [<s>śānta</s>] is established as having the sole form of the pacification of ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>). /
Even though such a distinction exists between the two — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'praiseworthy' — thus [if one says] that too falls from the status of <s>rasa</s> — he responds 'if indeed' etc. /
But one who supposes that 'that which is predominantly <s>dharma</s>-oriented is simply <s>vīra</s>' says — 'nor' etc. /
'Of that' — of <s>vīra</s>. /
'As consisting of self-assertion' — /
For <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) means 'I am such and such' — this is the sense. /
'And of this' — and of <s>śānta</s>. /
'And of the two' — /
The meaning of the word 'and' is: even though they are extremely opposed through having desire and being desireless. /
But between <s>vīra</s> and <s>raudra</s>, there is no extreme opposition.

tathāhīti /

ādhikārikatvena tu śānto raso na nibaddhavyaiti candrikākāraḥ /
children.translated_text: The author of the <s>Candrikā</s> says: but <s>śānta rasa</s> should not be composed as the principal (<s>ādhikārika</s>) [<s>rasa</s>].
That has not been considered by us here, because it is a different topic.
And since its fruit is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), being established in the highest <s>puruṣārtha</s> (human goal), this [<s>śānta rasa</s>] is the most pre-eminent among all <s>rasas</s>.

children.text: sa cāyamasmadupādhyāyabhaṭṭatautena kāvyakautuke, asmābhiśca tadvivaraṇe bahutarakṛtanirṇayapūrvapakṣasiddhānta ityalaṃ bahunā // 26 //
children.translated_text: And this [topic] has been elaborated with extensive refutation of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) and establishment of the <s>siddhānta</s> (conclusion) by our teacher <s>Bhaṭṭa Tauta</s> in the <s>Kāvyakautuka</s>, and by us in the commentary on that — enough of this much. // 26 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Is indeed <s>vīra</s>' — this is the connection. /
'That is <s>śānta</s> which is predominantly <s>dharma</s>-oriented' — [the objector says it is] <s>dharmavīra</s>. /
'Thus' etc. — the meaning is: he says in order to refute those who make this supposition. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'nor' etc. /
'In <s>vīra</s>' — in <s>dharmavīra</s>. /
'Of that' — of <s>śānta</s> —

children.text:
bālapriyā āgamapurassaramiti /

sā jugupsā /

tasyāḥ jugupsāyāḥ /
śāntasya sarvarasāpekṣayotkarṣa ityāha--mokṣetyādi /

children.translated_text: 'And that' (<s>sa ca</s>) —
The meaning is: 'and <s>śānta</s>.'
'Much' (<s>bahu</s>) etc. —

children.text: vahutaraṃ yathā tathā kṛtanirṇayau kṛtavicārau pūrvapakṣasiddhāntau yasya saḥ // 26 //
children.translated_text: [He] whose objection (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) and conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) have been determined with much greater [elaboration] — [that is the meaning]. // 26 //

[Bālapriyā:] 'Preceded by scripture' (<s>āgamapurassaram</s>) — /
The purport is: because [the verse says] '<s>Brahmā</s> declared.' /
By the word '<s>eva</s>' in 'the threefold [classification] alone,' the exclusion of <s>dayā-vīra</s> (heroism of compassion) [from separate status] is [indicated]. /
'He says' — /
The meaning is: he says with the stated intention. /
The reading '<s>ādigrahaṇena</s>' (by the inclusion of '<s>ādi</s>') before '<s>viṣaya</s>' etc. and after '<s>dayāvīrādīnāṃ ca</s>' is seen in all examined manuscripts, and its syntactic connection with '<s>viṣaya</s>' etc. does not work; therefore here it should be supplemented as 'the inclusion of <s>dharma-vīra</s> (heroism of righteousness) and <s>dāna-vīra</s> (heroism of generosity).' /
Or alternatively, it should be understood that the text should be read in that way. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'of the particular modifications of consciousness' — /
The remainder is: 'that are being savored.' /
<s>Dayā-vīra</s> (heroism of compassion) by name is the enthusiasm (<s>utsāha</s>) in the form of effort for the benefit of others. /
'<s>Sarvākāram</s>' (in every form) is an adverbial qualifier of the verb. /
The meaning is: in every manner. /
'By the absence of ego' — the instrumental is in the sense of cause; and '<s>rahitatve</s>' (in the state of being devoid) is also a reading. /
The remainder is: 'of the hero.' /
'Otherwise' — when accompanied by ego. /
Some [hold] that because the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) of <s>śānta</s> (the quiescent) has the nature of disgust toward sense-objects (<s>viṣaya-jugupsā</s>), <s>śānta</s> is subsumed under <s>bībhatsa</s> (the disgusting). /
That view is refuted incidentally in the <s>Locana</s> — '<s>viṣaya</s>' etc. /
'Because of having the nature of disgust toward sense-objects' — /
The remainder is: 'of <s>śānta</s>.' /
'Of this' — or alternatively, [it means] the inferiority [of śānta]. /
'Is suspected' — /
The remainder is: 'by some.' /
In reality it is not so — he says: 'but that' etc. /
'That' — that disgust. /
'Of this' — of this <s>śānta</s>. /
'Of that' — of that disgust. /
He states the superiority of <s>śānta</s> relative to all other <s>rasas</s> — '<s>mokṣa</s>' etc.
To confirm precisely this, this is stated —
Even of two [<s>rasas</s>] separated by another <s>rasa</s>, [or] situated in a single sentence —

children.text: nivartate hi rasayoḥ samāveśe virodhitā // DhvK_3.27 //
children.translated_text: the contradiction of <s>rasas</s> ceases when they are incorporated [together]. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.27 //
Even of two separated by another <s>rasa</s>, situated in a single sentence —
the contradiction of <s>rasas</s> ceases when they are incorporated [together]. // 27 //
[Vṛtti:] That the contradiction of two [rasas] separated by another <s>rasa</s> and situated in a single composition ceases — in this there is no doubt.
Since even of two <s>rasas</s> situated in a single sentence, the contradiction ceases by the stated method.
As for example — 'Their arm-intervals embraced by celestial women, whose middles of arms are fragrant with the pollen of fresh <s>Pārijāta</s> garlands — [those very arms] smeared with much dust,
tightly embraced by she-jackals — [those very warriors] fanned by celestial women with sandalwood-water sprinklings, fragrant garments of wish-granting creepers —
fanned by the quivering bloody wings of the flesh-eaters [vultures] — [those very warriors' own] —
fanned by celestial women with sandalwood-water sprinklings, fragrant garments of wish-granting creepers —
seated upon the couches of aerial chariots, at that time, filled with curiosity,
being pointed out by the fingers of women — the heroes did not see their own fallen bodies.' //

children.text:
locanam sthirīkartumiti /
śiṣyabuddhāvityarthaḥ /
apiśabdena prabandhaviṣayatayā siddho 'yamartha iti darśayati---bhūreṇviti /
viśeṣaṇairatīva dūrāpetatvamasambhāvanāspadamuktam /
svadehānityanena dehatvābhimānādeva tādātmyasambhāvanāniṣpatterekāśrayatvamasti, bālapriyā apiśabdeneti /
'ekavākyasthayorapī'tyapiśabdenetyarthaḥ /
vṛttau---'bhūreṇvi'tyādi /
idaṃ kāvyaprakāśe 'pyudāhṛtam /
vīrāḥ patitān svadehānapaśyannita sambandhaḥ /
yathākramaṃ kutūhalahetugarbhamekaṃ dehānāmaparaṃ vīrāṇāṃ viśeṣaṇam /
'dīgdhān' vyāptān 'vāsite'ti /
surabhīkṛtetyarthaḥ /
'bāhumadhyaṃ' bakṣaḥ /
'kravyabhujāṃ' māṃsāśinām /
candanavārīṇāṃ seko yatra tādṛśaiḥ /
'kalpalatādukūlaiḥ' kalpalatodbhūtapaṭṭavastraiḥ, yadvā--kalpalatā eva dukūlāni taiḥ /
'lalanāḥ' svarveśyāḥ /
locane---viśeṣaṇairiti /
bhūreṇvityādidehaviśeṣaṇairityarthaḥ /
asambhāvanāspadam svīyatvasambhāvanāyā abhāvasya nimittam /
dūrāpetatvaṃ dūraviprakṛṣṭatvamatyantavailakṣaṇyamiti yāvat /
uktaṃ vyañjitam /
nanu śṛṅgārabītbhasayorekasminnekālambanakayoreva virodhaḥ, ekasminnekadaikasya ratijugupsayoranudayāt ; prakṛte ca bhūremudigdhatvādaviśiṣṭavīradehālambanako bībhatso divyatvaviśiṣṭavīradehālambanakaśca śṛṅgāra iti tayoḥ kathamekālambanakatmarūpaikāśrayatvamiti śaṅkāṃ pariharannāha--svetyādi /
dehatvābhimānāditi /
vīrāṇāṃ patitadeheṣu svadehatvabuddherityarthaḥ /
ityādau /
atra hi śṛṅgārabībhatsayostadaṅgayorvā vīrarasavyavadhānena samāveśo na virodhī /
children.translated_text:
[Locana:] 'To confirm' — the meaning is: in the understanding of the student. /
By the word '<s>api</s>' (even), he shows that this matter is already established as pertaining to extended compositions — '<s>bhūreṇu</s>' etc. /
By the qualifying descriptions, the extreme remoteness — being the ground of inconceivability — is stated. /
'Their own bodies' — by this, because the conception of identity arises precisely from the attachment to body-ness, there is single-substratum-ness. /
[Bālapriyā:] 'by the word <s>api</s>' — /
The meaning is: by the word '<s>api</s>' in 'even of two situated in a single sentence.' /
In the <s>vṛtti</s> — '<s>bhūreṇu</s>' etc. — /
This is also cited in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. /
The syntactic connection is: 'the heroes did not see their own fallen bodies.' /
The qualifiers in sequence are: one of the bodies, and the other of the heroes — both containing the reason for curiosity. /
'Smeared' — pervaded. '<s>Vāsita</s>' — /
made fragrant — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Bāhumadhyam</s>' (middle of arms) — the chest. /
'<s>Kravyabhujām</s>' (of flesh-eaters) — of carnivores. /
'<s>Candanavārī</s>' — with whose sprinkling of sandalwood-waters — by such [garments]. /
'<s>Kalpalatādukūlaiḥ</s>' — with silken garments produced from wish-granting creepers; or alternatively, the wish-granting creepers themselves are the garments — by those. /
'<s>Lalanāḥ</s>' (women) — celestial courtesans. /
In the <s>Locana</s> — 'by the qualifying descriptions' — by the qualifying descriptions of the bodies beginning with '<s>bhūreṇu</s>' etc. — this is the meaning. /
'The ground of inconceivability' — the cause of the absence of the conception of being one's own. /
'Remoteness' — extreme distance — utter dissimilarity, in sum. /
'Stated' — suggested. /
Now, [objection:] the contradiction of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s> is only when they share a single locus and a single object — since <s>rati</s> (love) and <s>jugupsā</s> (disgust) cannot arise simultaneously in one [person] regarding one [object]; and in the present case, <s>bībhatsa</s> has as its object the body distinguished as smeared with dust etc. while <s>śṛṅgāra</s> has as its object the body distinguished by divinity — so how can there be single-locus-ness between those two? — resolving this doubt, he says: 'their own' etc. /
'From attachment to body-ness' — from the <s>vīras</s>' (heroes') conception that 'these are our bodies' — this is the meaning. /
Thus — for here, the incorporation of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s>, or of those as constituents [of <s>vīra</s>], with the interposition of <s>vīra-rasa</s>, is not contradictory.
One should determine contradiction and non-contradiction in this manner everywhere;

children.text: viśeṣatas tu śṛṅgāre sukumāratamā hy asau // DhvK_3.28 //
children.translated_text: but especially in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, for it is the most delicate [of all rasas]. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.28 //
One should determine contradiction and non-contradiction in this manner everywhere;
but especially in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, for it is the most delicate [of all rasas]. // 28 //

children.text:
yathoktalakṣaṇānusāreṇa virodhāvirodhau sarveṣu raseṣu prabandhe 'nyatra ca nirūpayetsahṛdayaḥ; viśeṣatastu śṛṅgāre /
sa hi ratapāripoṣātmakatvādrateśca locanam anyathā vibhinnaviṣayatvātko virodhaḥ /
nanu vīra evātra raso na śṛṅgāro na bībhatsaḥ, kintu ratijugupase hi vīraṃ prati vyabhicārībhūte /
bhavatvevam, tathāpi prakṛtodāharaṇatā tāvadupapannā /

children.translated_text: He says this — 'or of those as constituents' (<s>tadaṅgayoḥ vā</s>).
The meaning is: of the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotions) of those two [rasas] as constituents [of <s>vīra</s>].
'With <s>vīra-rasa</s>' —

children.text: 'vīrāḥ svadehān' ityādinā tadīyotsāhādyavagatyā kartṛkarmaṇoḥ samastavākyārthānuyāyitayā pratītiriti madhyapāṭhābhāve 'pi sutarāṃ vīrasya vyavadhāyakateti bhāvaḥ // 27 //
children.translated_text: 'The heroes [saw] their own bodies' — by this, through the apprehension of their enthusiasm etc., as agent and object — because of the accompaniment of the entire sentence-meaning in its totality — the cognition [arises]; thus, even in the absence of an intervening textual passage, <s>vīra</s> all the more serves as the interposing [<s>rasa</s>] — this is the purport. // 27 //

[Vṛtti:] Following the characteristics as stated, the sensitive reader should determine contradiction and non-contradiction in all <s>rasas</s>, in extended compositions and elsewhere; but especially in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
For it, because of having the nature of the fullness of <s>rati</s> (love), and because <s>rati</s> — [Locana:] otherwise, because of the difference of their objects, what contradiction is there? /
Now, [if objected:] <s>vīra</s> (the heroic) alone is the <s>rasa</s> here, not <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, not <s>bībhatsa</s>; rather, <s>rati</s> and <s>jugupsā</s> have become <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) with respect to <s>vīra</s>. /
Let it be so; even then, the relevance of the present example is established.

children.text:
anyatra ceti muktakādau /
sahi śṛṅgāraḥ sukumāratama iti sambandhaḥ /
sukumārastāvadrasajātīyaḥ bālapriyā etatpradarśanārthaṃ svapadopādānamiti bhāvaḥ /
tādātmyeti /
pratipatturdvayordehayoraikyabuddhiniṣpatteratyarthaḥ /
tathā ca svarlalanāgatasya śṛṅgārasya bībhatsasya ca dehadvayaikyābhimānī vīra eka eva viṣaya iti bhāvaḥ /
'tadaṅgayorve'ti granthamavatārayati--nanvityādi /
vīra eveti /
sāhasena raṇamadhyanipātanādyanubhāvenākṣepalabhyagarvādisañcāriṇā ca vīrarasa eva pratīyata ityarthaḥ /
tatsthāyibhāvāviti /
śṛṅgārabībhatsayoḥ sthāyibāvau ratijugupse ityarthaḥ /
ityādineti /
vīrapadena dehapātādyanubhāvena cetyarthaḥ /
utsāhādītyādipadena garvādeḥ parigrahaḥ /
avagatyetyanantaraṃ vīro rasa iti śeṣaḥ /
vīravyavadhānaṃ vivṛṇoti--kartṛkarmaṇorityādi /
kartṛkarmaṇoḥ vīrasya kartuḥ patitadeharūpakarmaṇaśca /
samastetyādi /
atra vākyaṃ padasamudāyaḥ bhūroṇvityādivākyārthānvayitayā karmaṇaḥ na vetyādivākyārthānvayitayā kartuśca pratītirityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: '<s>Iti</s>' — in the sense of reason.
'The purport is' (<s>bhāva</s>) —

children.text: ayamarthaḥ--'bhūreṇvi'tyādiviśeṣaṇārthabodhe bībhatsastadviśeṣyārthabodhe vīro, na vetyādiviśeṣaṇārthabodhe śṛṅgārastadviśeṣyārthabodhe vīraścāsvādyata iti rītyā vīrasya madhye madhye āsvādaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: when the meaning of the qualifiers beginning with '<s>bhūreṇu</s>' is cognized, <s>bībhatsa</s> [is savored]; when the meaning of the qualified [noun] of that [qualifier] is cognized, <s>vīra</s> [is savored]; when the meaning of the qualifiers beginning with '<s>na va</s>' etc. is cognized, <s>śṛṅgāra</s> [is savored]; and when the meaning of the qualified [noun] of that is cognized, <s>vīra</s> is savored — in this manner, the savoring of <s>vīra</s> [occurs] in between.

children.text: śrutakrameṇa bodhe tvādau bībhatso, yojana yā bodhe tvādau śṛṅgāra iti // 27 //
children.translated_text: But in the cognition [that follows] the heard sequence, <s>bībhatsa</s> [comes] first; in the cognition [that follows] syntactic construal, <s>śṛṅgāra</s> [comes] first. // 27 //

[Vṛtti:] 'And elsewhere' — in independent verses (<s>muktaka</s>) etc. /
'For it' — the syntactic connection is: '<s>śṛṅgāra</s> is the most delicate.' /
Delicate, first of all, is [the nature of] the <s>rasa</s>-class — [Bālapriyā:] the purport is: [the Locana] introduces its own word [for explanation]. /
'Identity' (<s>tādātmya</s>) — /
The meaning is: the conception of identity between the two bodies — this is what arises from the thought [of the heroes]. /
And thus, the single substratum of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s> of the celestial women is the hero alone, through the identity-conception involving the two bodies — this is the purport. /
She introduces the passage '<s>tadaṅgayoḥ vā</s>' — 'now' etc. /
'<s>Vīra</s> alone' — the meaning is: through the <s>anubhāvas</s> such as daringly plunging into the midst of battle through reckless valor, and through <s>sañcārins</s> such as pride obtained through defiance — only <s>vīra-rasa</s> is apprehended. /
'<s>Sthāyibhāvas</s>' — the meaning is: <s>rati</s> and <s>jugupsā</s>, the permanent emotions of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s>. /
'And by this' — and by the word '<s>vīra</s>' and by the <s>anubhāvas</s> such as the falling of the body. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), pride and the like are included. /
After 'by apprehension' — the remainder is: '<s>vīra</s> is the <s>rasa</s>.' /
She elaborates the interposition by <s>vīra</s> — 'of the agent and object' etc. /
Of the agent and object — of the hero as agent and the fallen body as object. /
'Entire' etc. — /
Here, the sentence (<s>vākya</s>) means the aggregate of words; by the accompaniment of the sentence-meaning beginning with '<s>bhūreṇu</s>' etc. in its totality with the object, and [the sentence-meaning] beginning with '<s>na va</s>' etc. in its totality with the agent — the cognition [arises] — this is the meaning.

children.text:
'prabandhe 'nyatra ce'tyatrānyatrapadaṃ vyāpaṣṭe--muktakādāviti /
'sukumāratamo hi svalpenāpi nimittena bhaṅgasambhavātsukumāratamaḥ sarvebhyo rasebhyo manāgapi virodhisamāveśaṃ na sahate /
children.translated_text:
She explains the word 'elsewhere' in 'in extended compositions and elsewhere' — 'in independent verses etc.' /
'The most delicate' — for because of the possibility of disruption even by a slight cause, [<s>śṛṅgāra</s>] is the most delicate — it does not tolerate even the slightest incorporation of what is opposed [to it].
The good poet should be extremely attentive precisely in that <s>rasa</s>;

children.text: bhavet tasmin pramādo hi jhaṭity evopalakṣyate // DhvK_3.29 //
children.translated_text: for negligence in it is noticed instantly. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.29 //
The good poet should be extremely attentive precisely in that <s>rasa</s>;
for negligence in it is noticed instantly. // 29 //

children.text:
tatraiva ca rase sarvebhyo 'pi rasemyaḥ saukumāryātiśayayogini kaviravadhānavān prayatnavānsyāt /
tatra hi pramādyatastasya sahṛdayamadhye kṣipramevāvajñānaviṣayatā bhavati /
śṛṅgāraraso hi saṃsāriṇāṃ niyamenānubhavaviṣayatvātsarvarasebhyaḥ kamanīyatayā pradhānabhūtaḥ /
evaṃ ca sati--
children.translated_text:
[Vṛtti:] And precisely in that <s>rasa</s> which possesses the excess of delicacy above all other <s>rasas</s>, the poet should be attentive, should be diligent. /
For when he is negligent in that, swiftly indeed does he become an object of contempt among the sensitive. /
For <s>śṛṅgāra-rasa</s>, because it is invariably the object of experience for those in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), is the foremost among all <s>rasas</s> in loveliness. /
And this being so —
In order to make the students receptive, or for the beauty of the poem alone —
the touch of a <s>rasa</s> opposed to it, upon its constituent elements, is not faulty. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.30 //
In order to make the students receptive, or for the beauty of the poem alone —
the touch of a <s>rasa</s> opposed to it, upon its constituent elements, is not faulty. // 30 //

children.text: locanam tato 'pi karuṇastato 'pi śṛṅgāra iti tamapratyayaḥ // 28-29 //
children.translated_text: [Locana:] More than that is <s>karuṇa</s>; more than that is <s>śṛṅgāra</s> — thus [the meaning of] the superlative suffix (<s>tama</s>). // 28-29 //

children.text: śṛṅgārasya viruddhā ye śāntādayasteṣvapi tadaṅgānāṃ śṛṅgārāṅgānāṃ sambandhī sparśo na duṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, those that are opposed — <s>śānta</s> etc. — even in those, the touch [i.e., contact] that relates to the constituent elements of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is not faulty.

children.text: tayā bhaṅgyā rasāntaragatā api vibhāvānubhāvādyā varṇanīyā yayā śṛṅgārāṅgabhāvamupāgaman /
children.translated_text: Those <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, etc. that belong to another <s>rasa</s> should be described in such a manner that they attain the status of being constituents of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>.

children.text: yathā mamaiva stotre--- tvāṃ candracūḍaṃ sahasā spṛśantī prāṇaiśvaraṃ gāḍhaviyogataptā /
children.translated_text: As in my own <s>stotra</s> (hymn) — 'She who, scorched by the intense separation from her Lord — the moon-crested one — touching <s>Candracūḍa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) suddenly —
like a figurine in the form of a moonstone, even though her consciousness dissolves, dissolves further for me.' //

'And this being so' — /
Since it [<s>śṛṅgāra</s>] is in harmony with all [audiences] — this is the meaning. /
'Of it' (<s>tad</s>) —

children.text: bālapriyā sa' iti kārikāpāṭhābhiprāyeṇa vyācaṣṭe---sa hītyādi /
children.translated_text: [Bālapriyā:] With the intention of the <s>kārikā</s> reading '<s>sa</s>' (he/that), she explains — 'for it' etc.
'Of the <s>rasa</s>-class' (<s>rasajātīya</s>) —
The meaning is: possessing the genus of <s>rasa</s>-hood. // 28-29 //

children.translated_text: was brought down [as drama and poetry] by the sages for the benefit of the audience alone.

children.text: kiṃ ca śṛṅgārasya sakalajanamanoharābhirāmatvāttadaṅgasamāveśaḥ kāvyeśobhātiśayaṃ puṣyatītyanenāpi prakāreṇa virodhini rase śṛṅgārāṅgasamāveśo na virodhī /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, since <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is delightful and captivating to the minds of all people, the incorporation of its components enhances the surpassing beauty of poetry — by this method too, the incorporation of the components of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> in a <s>rasa</s> that opposes [it] is not contradictory.

children.text: tataśca satyaṃ manoramā rāmāḥ satyaṃ ramyā vibhūtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And therefore — 'True, the pleasures are delightful; true, the splendors are charming;
but life is as unsteady as the sidelong glance of a woman intoxicated [with youth]!' //

She explains 'if so' — 'since' etc. /
The meaning is: because <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is the object of all experience. /
Intending to explain the meaning of 'should be made subordinate' etc., she first explains the latter half beginning with 'that which is opposed to it' — 'that' etc. /
She states the purport — 'by that' etc. /
'Of another <s>rasa</s>' — /
the meaning is: <s>śānta</s> etc. /
'By which they attained the status of being ancillary to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>' — /
the meaning is: by which turn of expression, by which description, they come to acquire the status of being <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
Here he states the example — 'you' etc. /
'Scorched by intense separation' — scorched intensely, or by intense non-contact with you, experiencing the heat of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). /
That consciousness of mine, which wanders among other objects — the inner organ or its modification — touching you, making you somewhat its object, dissolves, attaining the relation of having your form as its nature — wherein, in that knowledge, the contact of a <s>rasa</s> opposed to <s>śṛṅgāra</s> — that which belongs to the components of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> — not only is it not faulty when the characteristic of non-contradiction is present, but even when done for the purpose of making the audience receptive, or for the beauty of poetry alone, it is not faulty — for the audience, having been made receptive through the components of <s>śṛṅgāra-rasa</s>, easily receive the instructions of moral discipline. /
For the assembly of drama etc. has the form of instruction in good conduct — [<s>Locana</s>:] here, even the <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> of <s>śānta</s> are presented through the turn of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
The syntactic connection is: the beauty of poetry that serves to make the audience receptive — for that purpose alone, it is not faulty. /
By the word '<s>vā</s>' (or), an alternative view is stated. /
She explains that very [alternative] — 'not merely' etc. /
This is the explanation of the word '<s>vā</s>.' /
'The characteristic of non-contradiction' — the previously stated [methods of] nourishment, avoidance, etc. /
The beauty of poetry that serves to make the audience receptive — for that purpose too, or the incorporation of the contradictory — not merely through the previously stated methods; but the beauty of poetry does not exist without making the audience receptive; the [distinction of] with-interval and without-interval is also not obtained — as explained by others. /
'Easily' — /
the meaning is: preceded by delight. /
Objection: poetry has the nature of play — where then is the discourse of instruction that is the domain of the <s>Vedas</s> etc.? — anticipating this, he says: 'good conduct' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the meditator, meditation, and the object of meditation shine forth [as one] — that is shown by this. /
The word '<s>api</s>' (even) indicates apparent contradiction. /
'Dissolves' — dissolution means the non-manifestation of the inner organ or its modification. /
By this, knowledge directed solely toward the object of meditation is shown. /
Or — 'having dissolved, it dissolves' — having become liquefied, it becomes utterly melted — this is the meaning. /
The melting of the heart of devotees is well known; but in the interpretation [as referring to] a doll, touched by the moonbeam, having become somewhat moist, again becomes moist through the dissolution of all its parts — this is the meaning. /
Here, through the cognition that [the speaker is] a heroine scorched by separation etc., the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> are attained — she says: 'through the turn of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, the presentation.' /
She explains the first half — 'to make the audience receptive' etc. /
She shows that the word '<s>eva</s>' is connected with the negative — 'not at all' etc. /
'An alternative view' — /
the meaning is: another [view], different from the views stated in the earlier <s>kārikās</s> beginning with 'non-contradictory or contradictory.' /
The purport is: not indicating two alternatives within this [verse] itself. /
'This explanation' — /
the meaning is: the explanation [given by] 'not merely' etc. /
'The characteristic of non-contradiction' — she explains this word — 'nourishment' etc. /
'To make the audience receptive' etc. up to 'for that purpose too, or' — [and] 'the incorporation of the contradictory' — [these form] the elaboration of the <s>vṛtti</s> passage 'should be made subordinate' up to 'done.' /
The elaboration of 'done' is 'the incorporation of the contradictory.' /
She states the result — 'not merely through the previously stated methods' etc. /
The remainder is: the incorporation of the contradictory is not faulty. /
Rather, the purport is: even when so done, it is not faulty. /
She justifies what was said — 'the beauty of poetry that serves to make the audience receptive' — 'but' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: 'does not exist.' /
The meaning is: does not exist [separately]. /
'The [distinction of] with-interval' — /
the meaning is: the interval or non-interval by another <s>rasa</s> — not even by that. /
'Is obtained' carries over. /
The meaning is: the beauty of poetry is not [obtained separately]. /
'As' etc. — /
the syntactic connection is: 'is not as explained by others.' /
And the alternative explanation is: 'to make the audience receptive, or for the beauty of poetry' — this should be understood as indicating two alternatives. /
She explains the <s>vṛtti</s> passage 'should be made subordinate' etc. — 'in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>' etc.

'rāmāḥ' ramaṇyaḥ kāmā iti ca pāṭhaḥ 'vibhūtayaḥ' aiśvaryāṇi /

mattā yauvanādimadayuktāyā aṅganā praśastāṅgā nārī tasyāḥ apāṅgabhaṅgaḥ kaṭākṣa- sa iva lolamasthiram /
'hī'ti prasiddhau /
rāmādīnāṃ manoramatve 'pi satyeva jāvite janaiḥ svopabhoghāyopādeyāstāḥ jīvitaṃ cāsthiramiti kiḍkṛtaṃ tāsāmupādeyatvamato ramyatve 'pi tāssarvā niṣphalā eveti bhāvaḥ /
uktamarthaṃ locane vivṛṇoti--atretyādi /

children.translated_text:
In [verses] such as these, there is no fault of <s>rasa</s>-contradiction. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'By the sages' — the meaning is: by <s>Bharata</s> and others. /
And this — from <s>śāstras</s> (treatises) and <s>itihāsas</s> (epics) comparable to a lord and a friend, preceded by affection, in the manner of a wife — the capacity of drama and poetry to produce learning has been established by us previously — therefore, from fear of repetition, it is not written here. /
Objection: but if the presentation of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. through the turn of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is itself sufficient to make the audience receptive — then is there no further method? /
No; there is another method — he says: 'furthermore' etc. /
'Surpassing beauty' — /
the meaning is: a particular <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornamental figure) such as <s>upamā</s> (simile) etc. — it nourishes, it makes beautiful. /
As stated: 'the properties (<s>dharma</s>) that produce the beauty of poetry are <s>guṇas</s> (qualities); the causes of their surpassing [beauty] are <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures).' /
'Intoxicated woman' — /
for here, when the impermanence of everything is being described as a <s>vibhāva</s> of <s>śānta</s>, no <s>vibhāva</s> is composed in the turn of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>; rather, 'true' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] she explains 'easily' — 'preceded by delight' etc. /
And this — with respect to <s>śāstras</s> and <s>itihāsas</s> comparable to a lord and friend — in relation to them. /
The capacity of drama and poetry to produce learning, being in the manner of a wife — preceded by affection — has been established by us previously — this is the syntactic connection. /
The meaning of '<s>iti</s>' is: 'therefore.' /
She introduces the passage beginning with 'furthermore' — 'objection' etc. /
'The turn of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>' — /
the meaning is: the status of <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, etc. of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
She resolves — 'no' etc. /
'That' — /
the meaning is: another method. /
'Surpassing beauty' — she explains with the intent of showing the meaning appropriate to the present context — '<s>alaṅkāra</s>' etc. /
'<s>Satyam</s>' etc. — /
'<s>Satyam</s>' indicates partial concession. /
'<s>Rāmāḥ</s>' — there is also the reading '<s>kāmāḥ</s>' (pleasures), meaning delightful. '<s>Vibhūtayaḥ</s>' — riches, splendors. /
'<s>Mattā</s>' — /
a woman intoxicated with the pride of youth etc. (<s>mattā</s>) — '<s>aṅganā</s>' — a woman of beautiful limbs — of hers, the sidelong glance (<s>apāṅgabhaṅga</s>) — the sidelong look — like that, unsteady, unstable. /
'<s>Hi</s>' — in [the sense of] common knowledge. /
Even though the delightfulness of pleasures etc. is indeed true, since life, by which people enjoy them, is unstable — what is the use of their being enjoyable? — therefore, even though charming, all those are fruitless — this is the purport. /
She explains the stated meaning in the <s>Locana</s> — 'here' etc. /
'Of the impermanence of everything' — /
there is also the reading 'of complete impermanence.' /
The meaning is: when the instability of all life [is being described]. /
The syntactic connection is: 'is not composed.' /
'Of any <s>vibhāva</s>' — of any <s>vibhāva</s> of <s>śānta</s> etc. /
'In the turn of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>' — by means of composition as a <s>vibhāva</s> of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
'<s>Satyam</s>' —
Having thus understood the domain of non-contradiction and contradiction of <s>rasas</s> etc.,

Having thus understood the domain of non-contradiction and contradiction of <s>rasas</s> etc.,

children.text: viṣayaṃ sukaviḥ kāvyaṃ kurvanmuhyati na kvacit // 31 //
children.translated_text: a good poet, while composing poetry, is never confused anywhere. // 31 //

children.text:
itthamanenānantaroktena prakāreṇa rasādīnāṃ rasabhāvatadābhāsānāṃ parasparaṃ virodhasyāvirodhasya ca viṣayaṃ vijñāya sukaviḥ kāvyaviṣaye pratibhātiśayayuktaḥ kāvyaṃ kurvatra kvacinmuhmati /
evaṃ rasādiṣu virodhāvirodhanirūpaṇasyopayogitvaṃ pratipādya vyañjakavācyavācakanirūpaṇasyāpi tadviṣayasya tatpratipādyate--
children.translated_text:
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Thus, having understood in this manner just described the domain of contradiction and non-contradiction of <s>rasas</s> etc. — <s>rasas</s>, <s>bhāvas</s>, and their semblances (<s>ābhāsas</s>) — mutually, a good poet — one endowed with a surplus of creative genius (<s>pratibhā</s>) — while composing in the domain of poetry, is never confused anywhere. /
Having thus taught the usefulness of determining contradiction and non-contradiction among <s>rasas</s> etc., the determination of the suggestor (<s>vyañjaka</s>), the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>), and the expressor (<s>vācaka</s>) in that domain is also taught —

children.text: vācyānāṃ vācakānāṃ ca yad aucityena yojanam /
children.translated_text: The conjunction with propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) of expressed meanings (<s>vācyas</s>) and expressors (<s>vācakas</s>) —
in the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc., this is the principal task of the great poet. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.32 //
The conjunction with propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) of expressed meanings and expressors —
in the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc., this is the principal task of the great poet. // 32 //

children.text: locanam parahṛdayānupraveśenoktam; na khalvalīkavairāgyakautukaruciṃ prakaṭayāmaḥ, api tu yasya kṛte sarvamabhyarthyate tadevedaṃ calamiti; tatra mattāṅganāpāṅgabhaṅgasya śṛṅgāraṃ prati sambhāvyamānavibhāvānubhāvatvenāṅgasya lolatāyāmupamānatoktati priyatamākaṭākṣo hi sarvasyābhilaṣaṇīya iti ca tatprītyā pravṛttimān guḍajihvikayā prasaktānuprasaktavastutattvasaṃvedanena vairāgye paryavasyati vineyaḥ // 3.0 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] This is stated through entering into the heart of the other [i.e., the poet]; we certainly do not display a fondness for false renunciation, but rather: that for whose sake everything is sought — that very thing is fleeting — [thus]. Therein, the sidelong glance of the intoxicated woman, since its unsteadiness is stated as a simile for the most cherished thing [life], with respect to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, the <s>vibhāva</s> and <s>anubhāva</s> status being conceivable — because the sidelong glance of the beloved is indeed desirable to everyone — and thus, through the delight in that, one who has become engaged, through the guile of sweetened-bait, through the cognition of the truth of things in connected succession, culminates in <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) — the audience [becomes receptive]. // 3.0 //
Concluding this very [topic], he states the fruit of the stated section — 'having understood thus' etc. // 31 //

children.text: tathā ca yayā kayāpi vidhayā śṛṅgārāṅgayojanaṃ kāvyaśobhākaramiti bhāvaḥ // 3.0 //
children.translated_text: And thus, by whatever method the conjunction of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>-components [with other rasas] produces the beauty of poetry — this is the purport. // 3.0 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] In the domain of <s>rasas</s> etc. — the suggestors (<s>vyañjakas</s>) are the expressed meanings (<s>vācyas</s>), the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc., and the expressors (<s>vācakas</s>), the <s>sup</s>-endings (<s>tiṅ</s>-endings) etc. — their determination — 'of that' etc. /
'Of that domain' — /
of the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
'That' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the meaning is: by this. /
'Of the other' — /
the meaning is: through the acceptance of the meaning intended by the other [person]. /
'False' — /
the meaning is: a false, i.e., untrue, fondness for the curiosity of renunciation — this is the meaning. /
'Of which' — /
the meaning is: of life. /
Therein, regarding life. /
The syntactic connection is: therein, the unsteadiness stated as a simile — this. /
The meaning is: the unsteadiness determined as the counterpart of the simile. /
'Conceivable' — /
the meaning is: conceivable as the <s>vibhāva</s> of the hero and as the <s>anubhāva</s> of the heroine, by reason of [their] being ancillary to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
She states the fruit of that statement — 'beloved' etc. /
'Through the delight in that' — through the delight in the sidelong glance's being a simile — this is the meaning.
She introduces the <s>kārikā</s> beginning with 'having understood' — 'concluding this very [topic]' etc. // 3.1 //

The elaboration of 'in the domain of <s>rasas</s> etc.' is: 'in the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc.' /
She explains the passage beginning with 'of suggestor-expressed-meaning' — of the expressed meanings (<s>vācyas</s>) that are the suggestors of <s>rasa</s> etc. — the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. — and of the expressors (<s>vācakas</s>) — the particular <s>sup</s> (nominal) and <s>tiṅ</s> (verbal) endings etc. — in the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc. — the conjunction with propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) — this is the principal task of the great poet. /
For this indeed is the principal activity of the great poet: making <s>rasas</s> etc. primarily the intended meaning of poetry, and composing words and meanings in accordance with their manifestation. /
And this — the composition of poetry with the intent of <s>rasa</s> etc. — is well established even in <s>Bharata</s> etc. — intending to teach this, he says —
The employment of meanings and words in accordance with <s>rasa</s> etc. —

'Making it the purpose of poetry' — /
Otherwise, what distinction would the meaning of poetry have from the meanings of ordinary and scientific sentences? /
And this has been determined in the first <s>Uddyota</s> — in the passage 'the soul of poetry is that very meaning' — in the intervening [discussion]. // 3.2 //

[Vṛtti:] For <s>vṛtti</s> (literary style) is called 'mode of conduct' (<s>vyavahāra</s>). /
Therein, that mode of conduct which is in accordance with <s>rasa</s>, possessing propriety (<s>aucitya</s>), and based on the expressed meaning — those are the <s>vṛttis</s> such as <s>Kaiśikī</s> etc. /
And those based on the expressive function [of words] are <s>Upanāgarikā</s> etc. /
For <s>vṛttis</s>, arranged with the purpose of [conveying] <s>rasa</s> etc., bring forth the lustre (<s>chāyā</s>) of both drama and poetry. /
For <s>rasa</s> etc. are the life-force (<s>jīvabhūta</s>) of both of them. /
But <s>itivṛtta</s> (narrative/plot) etc. is merely the body. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Usefulness' is the principal [sense] — /
What was stated in '<s>ālokārthī</s>' (one who seeks illumination) — that very [point] has been recapitulated [here]. /
'Of the great poet' — the determination of the result is stated as [already] established. /
The meaning is: thus indeed is great poetry, and not otherwise. /
'Of the particular <s>itivṛttas</s>' — /
For <s>itivṛtta</s> (narrative) is what is expressed in a composition (<s>prabandha</s>); its particulars have been stated before — 'charming with the propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>bhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>sañcārins</s>,
