children.translated_text: He raises the doubt: 'when the suggestedness is equal, whence the difference?' — 'even there' etc.
'Quite clearly' —
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] The illumination at the level of word and sentence belongs to the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (non-intended expressible);
and of the other — the <s>dhvani</s> whose suggested [meaning] is in the form of reverberation (<s>anuraṇanarūpavyaṅgya</s>). //

Here some say — 'The attribute-substance (<s>guṇa-guṇi</s>) relationship of <s>rasas</s> etc. with <s>itivṛtta</s> (narrative) etc. is appropriate, but not the soul-body (<s>jīva-śarīra</s>) relationship. /
For the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) appears as pervaded by <s>rasa</s> etc., not as separate from <s>rasa</s> etc.' — thus. /
To this we reply — if the expressed meaning were indeed pervaded by <s>rasa</s> etc., just as the body is pervaded by whiteness, /
then, just as when the body appears, whiteness necessarily appears to everyone, so too <s>rasas</s> etc. would appear to both the sensitive reader (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) and the insensitive one (<s>asahṛdaya</s>) together with the expressed meaning. /
But this is not the case; and this has already been established in the first <s>Uddyota</s>. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] By 'locana' etc., the mode of conduct (<s>vyavahāra</s>) characterized by verbal function (<s>śabdavṛtti</s>), whose life is the service of <s>rasa</s>, has been stated. /
'Body' — /
'For the <s>itivṛtta</s> (narrative) is the body of drama' — thus the sage (<s>Muni</s>, i.e., <s>Bharata</s>). /
And it was previously stated that drama is indeed <s>rasa</s>. /
'Attribute-substance relationship' — /
Due to appearing in a thoroughly intermixed manner, the property-property-bearer (<s>dharma-dharmi</s>) relationship is appropriate. /
'But not' — /
The purport is: because the sequence is not apprehended. /
'In the first' — /
This was established by the passage beginning with 'it is not known merely by knowledge of the science of words and meanings.' /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In the <s>kārikā</s>, the syntactic connection is: that mode of conduct (<s>vyavahāra</s>) of words and meanings which is in accordance with <s>rasa</s> etc. and possesses propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) — these are the <s>vṛttis</s> (styles), and these are established as twofold. /
In the <s>Locana</s> — 'whose life is the service of <s>rasa</s>' — /
The meaning is: that whose life (<s>jīvita</s>) is indeed the service of <s>rasa</s> (<s>rasopayoga</s>). /
The rest is all clear. /
The explanation of 'attribute-substance relationship' is: 'property-property-bearer relationship.' /
He shows the reason here — 'thoroughly' etc. /
The completion is: of <s>rasa</s> etc. and the expressed meaning, like attribute and substance. /
Here <s>rasa</s> etc. occupies the position of attribute, and the expressed meaning in the form of <s>itivṛtta</s> (narrative) etc. occupies the position of substance. /
Regarding 'not as separate,' he states the reason — 'because the sequence is not apprehended.' /
The completion is: of the cognition of the expressed meaning and the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s> — the restatement of 'if' etc. /
Here he gives an example — 'just as' etc. /
'The body pervaded by whiteness' — this is the attribute-substance relationship in its identity-form. /
'If that be so' — /
The meaning is: if the expressed meaning were pervaded by <s>rasa</s> etc. /
Its connection is with 'would appear.' /
He states, preceded by showing the example — 'just as' etc. /
'Necessarily appears' — /
The purport is: because the perception of a substance necessarily has as its object the form belonging to it. /
'So' — /
The connection is with 'necessarily.' /
'Would appear' — /
The meaning is: if the expressed meaning were pervaded by <s>rasa</s> etc., then it would necessarily be cognized together with <s>rasa</s> etc. by all. /
He resolves the undesired consequence here — 'but this is not the case.' /
'There might be the view' — this is indicative of an objection. /
The construction is: just as the quality of genuineness (<s>jātyatva</s>). /
The quality of genuineness might be the view [that it is] present in excellent gems; just as the genuineness of gems is apprehended only by a special perceiver, so too the <s>rasa</s>-nature of expressed meanings [might be perceived only by the discerning]. /
This is not so; because just as when a gem appears with its genuineness, one observes only the non-difference of that [genuineness] from the gem's own nature, similarly for <s>rasas</s> etc. one would observe only their non-difference from the expressed meaning in the form of <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, etc. /
But this is not the case. [<s>Locana</s>:] 'But surely, if the property-form of something [always manifests] upon its manifestation, it necessarily appears to everyone' — this is non-conclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). /
For the property of a ruby — the distinctive quality called genuineness (<s>jātyatva</s>) — does not necessarily appear to everyone even when it [the ruby] appears — thus one raises the objection: 'there might be the view.' /
He resolves this — 'this is not so.' /
What has been said amounts to this — the qualification 'when there is the nature of being thoroughly emerged' has been made by us with respect to 'being a property of that.' /
And the emerged nature (<s>unmagna-rūpatā</s>) does not belong to genuineness as it does to form (<s>rūpa</s>), because of its thoroughly latent nature. /
But <s>rasas</s> etc. do indeed have emerged nature — thus some have understood this passage. /
Our teachers, however, say — by 'to this we reply' the following is stated — /
If <s>rasas</s> etc. are [like] a species-particular (<s>jāti-viśeṣa</s>). /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] As in <s>Mālatī</s>: 'like a <s>candramaṇi</s> (moonstone) of genuine quality on a mountain.' /
'By a special perceiver' — by a special knower, as agent. /
She introduces the passage beginning with 'there might be the view' in the <s>Locana</s> — 'but surely' etc. /
'That which' etc. /
'Which' — [refers to] whiteness etc. /
'Of which' — of the body etc. /
'That' — whiteness etc. /
The connection is: 'upon the manifestation of that' — upon the manifestation of the body etc. — 'this' — the meaning is: the invariable rule (<s>niyama</s>). /
Wherever there is the property-nature of something, there the scope of the perceptual experience of that subject [necessarily includes it] — this is the universal concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>), in sum. /
'Non-conclusive' — /
The meaning is: inconclusive, i.e., subject to deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). /
Where is the deviation? To this he says — 'of a ruby' etc. /
'Upon its manifestation' — upon the appearance of the ruby. /
'Does not appear' — /
And thus with respect to the property of a ruby — genuineness — there is deviation; this is the purport. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s> — 'just as' etc. /
'With genuineness' — in the mode of genuineness. /
'Appearing' — being the object of direct perception by a special perceiver. /
'Non-difference from the gem's own nature' — non-difference from the gem. /
'Of that' — of genuineness. /
'Is observed' — is known. /
'<s>Vibhāva</s>' etc. — /
The meaning is: non-difference from the expressed meaning which is in the form of <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, etc. /
'But this is not the case' — /
The meaning is: it is not observed thus. /
To 'why?' he says — 'for not' etc. /
The connection is: 'for there is no apprehension.' /
He states the purport of the passage 'because' etc. up to 'but this is not the case' in the <s>Locana</s> — 'what has been said amounts to this' etc. /
'The nature of being thoroughly emerged' — /
The meaning is: being cognized as different from its substratum. /
'If that be so' — /
'thus' is the completion. /
'Being a property of that' etc. — /
The meaning is: 'being a property of that' is the qualification. /
'Has been made' — /
The meaning is: has been intended. /
The meaning is: in the [statement] 'wherever there is the property-nature of that,' 'when there is the nature of being thoroughly emerged' is also included. /
And thus, genuineness serves as the counter-example — he says 'emerged' etc. /
The emerged nature does not belong to genuineness as it does to form (<s>rūpa</s>) such as whiteness etc. — this is the meaning. /
'Because of its thoroughly latent nature' — because of its non-emerged nature. /
The meaning is: because of not being cognized as different from its substratum. /
'This passage' — /
The meaning is: the passage from 'because' etc. to 'but this is not the case.' /
For surely no one apprehends that <s>rasas</s> are just <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions). /
And precisely for this reason, the cognition of <s>rasas</s> etc. being invariably accompanied by the cognition of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., due to the establishment of their cognitions in a cause-effect relationship, sequence is inevitable. /
But that [sequence] is not made manifest due to its subtlety — thus it was stated: 'being of imperceptible sequence, the suggested <s>rasas</s> etc.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The properties of expressed meanings — if that be so, there are two alternatives: they are either like form (<s>rūpa</s>) etc. or like genuineness (<s>jātyatva</s>) residing in gems. /
The first alternative does not hold, because they do not thus appear to everyone. /
Nor does the second, because like genuineness, they do not manifest as non-different. /
And this reason applies to the first alternative as well. /
Therefore he says — with 'there might be the view' etc. up to 'but this is not the case.' /
He corroborates this very point — 'for not' etc. /
And 'precisely for this reason' — /
Since the cognition of <s>rasas</s> etc. does not occur as a property of the expressed meaning, and since the cognition of the expressed meaning is in every way not useless for the cognition thereof, precisely for that reason, sequence is inevitable, because there can be no mutual benefit between simultaneous [cognitions]. /
But that [sequence], due to the practice of sensitive appreciation, is not perceived by <s>sahṛdayas</s>; otherwise it would indeed be perceived — this was stated earlier. /
Even for one whose position is that <s>rasa</s> is a special form of cognition itself, since <s>rasas</s> etc. are [merely] designated [as such], it is the same. /
Objection: let <s>rasas</s> etc. be different from the expressed meaning — even then, the sequence is not perceived, as you yourself have stated. /
And there is no evidence for positing [such sequence]. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She says from 'our teachers say' etc. /
'Not appearing thus' — thoroughly, by means of [the passage] up to 'but this is not the case,' [the passage] from 'would appear' has been elucidated. /
'Not manifesting' — /
The meaning is: not appearing. /
'In the first alternative too' — /
The meaning is: in the alternative 'like form etc.' too. /
The purport is: because form etc. also manifests as non-different. /
'Up to' — 'thus' is the completion. /
'He says' — the connection is with the preceding. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>, intending that 'precisely for this reason' is one reason and 'due to establishment' is another, she explains — 'since not' etc. /
'In the cognition thereof' — in the cognition of <s>rasa</s>. /
'In every way' — /
The connection is with 'not.' /
'Not useless' — rather, useful indeed. /
'Sequence is inevitable' — the elaboration of this is: 'one must necessarily proceed by sequence.' /
'Why?' — to this he says: 'between simultaneous' etc. /
'Mutual benefit being impossible' — the meaning is: the impossibility of the relationship of benefactor and benefited. /
'Even for one whose position' — /
The connection is with 'position stated earlier.' /
'Even [in that] view' — 'view' is the completion. /
'Because of being designated' — because like <s>Rāhu's</s> head [which is merely a designation], /
he introduces the passage — 'objection' etc. /
'Has been stated' — /
By that statement, 'there is sequence' has been indicated; this is the purport. /
'Positing [sequence]' — the meaning is: positing of sequence. /
'The arising of <s>rasa</s>-cognition' — its connection is with 'from observation' through 'arising.' /
'Arising' — this is the qualification of 'arising.' /
She states the upshot — 'therefore' etc. /
'Simultaneously' — all at once. /
'Verbal expression' etc. — /
The activity of verbal expression means the communication of the expressed meaning. /
Objection: the word itself, delimited by context etc., equally produces the cognition of both the expressed and the suggested — so what is the point of positing sequence? /
Surely the suggestive capacity of words is not based on the prior apprehension of the expressed meaning. /
For indeed, from musical (<s>gīta</s>) words too, <s>rasa</s> is manifested. /
And those [musical words] have no prior apprehension of the expressed meaning. /
To this too we say — it is indeed accepted by us that the suggestive capacity of words operates through delimitation by context etc. /
But that suggestive capacity of theirs is sometimes based on the particular nature of the word-form, and sometimes based on the denotative power (<s>vācaka-śakti</s>). /
Among those [words] whose [suggestive capacity] is based on denotative power — if it were accomplished merely through the cognition of their own form without the cognition of the expressed meaning, then it would not be based on denotative power. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] But in wordless melodic song (<s>svarālāpa-gīta</s>) devoid of lexical words, from the observation that mere sound is the operative factor, /
then by that single universal [power] alone, both the expressed and the intended suggested <s>rasa</s> etc. would appear simultaneously — and so the two operations of expression and suggestion would serve no purpose — thus he says: 'objection.' /
Even where musical words do have a meaning, there too the cognition of that [meaning] is useless, because from the observation that <s>rasa</s> arises through following the melodic mode (<s>grāma-rāga</s>) while the tracking of expressed meaning is set aside. /
And this [arising without expressed meaning] is not seen to occur everywhere — thus he says: 'and not.' /
'Of those' — of the musical words etc. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), sounds of instruments, laments, etc. are indicated. /
'Accepted' — /
The purport is: for we have stated 'where meaning or word [is the suggestor].' /
'Then not' — /
And so, just as from song itself there would be the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> without apprehension of meaning from poetic words too — but this is not so — therefore the denotative power must also be considered relevant; and that [denotative power] is established only in the expressed meaning — therefore the cognition of the expressed meaning comes first. /
Thus he says — 'but.' /
'That' — the denotative power. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Thus he says' — /
The meaning is: by 'objection' etc. up to '[prior] apprehension,' he presents the objection stated [above]. /
She introduces the passage beginning with 'and not' — 'even where' etc. /
'Useless' — the reason for this he states: 'melodic' etc. /
'<s>Apa</s>' — /
<s>Apahaṣṭita</s> means disregarded; the tracking of expressed meaning (<s>vācyānusāra</s>) — the following of expressed-meaning cognition — [being disregarded] by that arising of <s>rasa</s>; its condition is its nature; by that [nature]. /
'That' — /
The meaning is: the cognition of the expressed meaning. /
'Of musical words' — in 'etc.' the meaning of the '<s>ādi</s>' word is stated: '<s>ādi</s>' etc. /
<s>Vilapita</s> (lamentation) means <s>vilāpa</s> (wailing); '<s>vilāpa</s> is meaningless speech' — thus <s>Amara</s> [lexicon]. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>, 'that suggestive capacity' — /
The meaning is: suggestive capacity assisted by context etc. /
'Of those' — of words. /
'Particular nature of the word-form' — /
The meaning is: particular nature of the word's own form. /
'Denotative' — /
Denotative power means <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation); that itself is the basis, the cause, of which — that. /
The purport is: because manifestation is preceded by the cognition of the denoted meaning. /
'Of those [whose]' — /
The connection is with 'that suggestive capacity.' /
'That' — the meaning is: suggestive capacity. /
'Then not' — /
And so, in the absence of the suggestive capacity being based on denotative power — /
Just as from song — the meaning is: equal to song — /
There would be the apprehension of <s>rasa</s> without the apprehension of meaning from poetic words too; but this is not so — /
'Thus' — expressing the reason. /
Established only in the expressed meaning — having only the expressed meaning as its object. /
'Previously' etc. — /
Based on that [denotative power] — by that rule itself — the posteriority to expressed-meaning cognition of the cognition of the suggested meaning has been obtained. /
But if that sequence is not perceived due to its subtlety, then what can be done? /
And when without the cognition of the expressed meaning, merely through words delimited by context etc., the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. could be accomplished — then for those [listeners] whose context has not been determined, and who are themselves uninstructed in the denotation-denotatum relationship, [<s>Locana</s>:] 'Denotation-denotatum relationship' — /
That itself, the denotative power, is stated. /
What has been said amounts to this — let the expressed meaning not be the suggestor of <s>rasa</s> etc.; let the cognition thereof arise from words alone — even so, since [the word's] own denotative power must necessarily be relied upon as an auxiliary in producing that [<s>rasa</s>-cognition], the priority of the cognition of the expressed meaning follows. /
Objection: just as with musical words, the denotative power is useless here too; as for the fact that <s>rasa</s>-cognition does not arise in some cases despite hearing poetry — in those cases the appropriate auxiliary [factor] such as context-comprehension is absent — thus objecting, he says: 'and if.' /
For what is meant by 'context-comprehension'? Is it the assistance of other sentences? Or the denotatum of other sentences? /
Even when both are known, without the cognition of the meaning of the sentence in question, <s>rasa</s> does not arise. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The meaning is: it must be accepted that the cognition of the expressed meaning comes first. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>, 'but' — in the sense of 'if.' /
'Based on that' — /
The meaning is: that of which it is the basis. /
The connection is with 'suggestive capacity.' /
'That' — /
The meaning is: 'then.' /
'But that sequence' — /
The meaning is: the sequence in the form of posteriority to the cognition of the expressed meaning. /
The connection is with: of the cognition of the suggested meaning. /
Regarding 'based on that,' the word 'that' is explained in the <s>Locana</s>: 'denotative power.' /
'That itself' — /
'That very' — /
The reading is 'sa eva' (that very one). /
The meaning is: the denotation-denotatum relationship itself. /
She states the purport — 'what has been said amounts to this' etc. /
'Suggestor of <s>rasa</s> etc.' — /
The meaning is: generator of the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
'Cognition thereof' — /
The meaning is: the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
'By that' — /
The meaning is: by the word. /
'In producing that' — /
The meaning is: in [the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc.] that is to be produced. /
'Thus' — expressing the reason. /
Objection — etc. /
'Just as with musical words' — /
The meaning is: just as with musical words. /
'Here too' — in the case of poetic words too. /
Surely, in this way, wherever the word is heard but the meaning is not apprehended, there <s>rasa</s>-cognition would arise — to this he says: 'as for the fact that' etc. /
'As for the fact that' — meaning 'as for the case where.' /
'Thus objecting, he says' — the meaning is: through an objection, a resolution is presented by the passage 'objection' etc. up to '[prior] apprehension.' /
The meaning of the word '<s>mātra</s>' (mere) in the <s>Vṛtti</s> passage 'accomplishable through mere words' is elucidated: 'without the cognition of the expressed meaning.' /
'Context having been determined for them' — /
'That' then — 'then.' /
'Determined' — known, the context — by whom; for them. /
'Expressed meaning' etc. — /
The meaning is: for those who themselves do not know the particular expressed meaning of each denotative word. /
'That' — the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
She elucidates in the <s>Locana</s>: 'context-comprehension' etc. /
'Context-comprehension' — the thing to be comprehended, i.e., the meaning of the word 'context.' /
'Sentence' — /
Another sentence is an auxiliary — that which has this quality is its nature, or: another sentence, as auxiliary — this is the meaning. /
The hearing of mere poetry alone would produce that [<s>rasa</s>-cognition]. /
And in the case of simultaneity, the cognition of the expressed meaning would be useless; or if [it is] useful, then there is no simultaneity. /
Even for those whose suggestive capacity arises from the cognition of the particular word-form, as with musical words etc., for them too [there is sequence] between the cognition of the form and the cognition of the suggested meaning, invariably. [<s>Locana</s>:] 'By oneself' — /
The purport is: [those] whose context has been explained by someone else alone. /
And one cannot, by concealing the expressed-meaning cognition which possesses positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), take resort to the existence and non-existence of an unseen [factor] — for that would nourish nothing more than jealousy — this is the intention. /
Objection: let the expressed-meaning cognition be useful — what purpose does relying on sequence serve, since mere simultaneity itself constitutes usefulness in the form of dependence on a single causal complex? — thus objecting, he says: 'between simultaneous' etc. /
'For in this way, usefulness' — the meaning is: [calling it] usefulness for something that provides no benefit would be merely a matter of naming, devoid of substance — this is the purport. /
For you too have accepted that the benefactor precedes — he says: 'of those [whose]' etc. /
By that very example, we shall establish the priority of the expressed-meaning cognition as well — this is the purport. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Of the sentence in question' — is the completion. /
'But' — in the sense of an alternative question. /
'Of other sentences' etc. — /
The meaning is: the denotatum of other sentences. /
'Both' — /
The meaning is: the other sentences and their denotatum — both. /
The cognition of the meaning of the sentence in question — /
The meaning is: without the apprehension of the meaning of each word constituting the sentence in question. /
She corroborates the denotation-denotatum relationship not being understood — 'mere context' etc. /
By the word '<s>mātra</s>' (mere), the exclusion of the expressed meaning is indicated. /
'By whom' — /
The meaning is: of certain perceivers. /
'Explained' — /
The meaning is: made known. /
Objection: by the sentence, [if] an unseen special [factor] too serves as an auxiliary for <s>rasa</s>-cognition — since in its absence alone, at the time when expressed-meaning cognition is absent, <s>rasa</s> etc. do not arise — he resolves the objection: 'and not' etc. /
The connection is: 'and would not nourish.' /
'Positive and negative concomitance' — /
The meaning is: possessing positive and negative concomitance — when expressed-meaning cognition is present, <s>rasa</s> etc. cognition is present; when it is absent, that too is absent. /
'As resort' — in the sense of 'as cause.' /
The completion is: of the presence and absence of <s>rasa</s>-cognition. /
Objection — etc. /
'Usefulness' — the completion is: toward the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
'By relying on sequence' — /
The meaning is: by relying on the sequence — the temporal priority — between the cognition of the expressed meaning and the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
Then, what is the usefulness? — to this he says: 'mere' etc. /
What kind is it? — objecting thus, he says: 'one' etc. /
The meaning is: the simultaneity (<s>sahabhāva</s>) with <s>rasa</s> etc. that has the form of dependence on a single causal complex — of the cognition of the expressed meaning — this is the purport. /
'Usefulness' — the meaning of the word 'usefulness.' /
'Objecting' — /
The meaning is: tentatively suspecting. /
She states the purport of the passage 'between simultaneous' etc.: 'for in this way' etc. /
'For something that provides no benefit' — the connection of 'usefulness' is with '[mere] naming.' /
'Mere' — she elucidates the meaning of the word 'mere': 'substance' etc. /
'Substance' — the substance, i.e., the content, which is the nature of benefaction. /
'Priority' — /
The meaning is: existing at a prior time. /
She states the purport of the passage beginning with 'sequence' [up to] the end: 'by your example' etc. /
'By your example' — by the example of song etc. She introduces the passage — 'objection' etc. /
'Of the word' — its connection is with 'is done' [i.e., 'the action is performed']. /
Sequence. /
But that sequence — the temporal priority-posteriority of the word's activities — is not perceived when the result is unachievable by any other means, when [the activities] are swiftly operative without waiting for the time of expressed-meaning cognition, when [the result] is non-contradictory to the expressed meaning, and when [the result is] unlike any other expressible meaning, namely <s>rasa</s> etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'If the sequence indeed [exists], why is it not perceived?' — thus objecting, he says: 'but that.' /
He states the nature of the sequence by 'the action [temporal priority-posteriority]' — 'is done' etc. /
The two activities — the cognition of the expressed and the suggested, or alternatively, the operation of denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>) and the operation called suggestion (<s>dhvanana</s>) — their temporal priority is not perceived. /
'Where?' — he says: 'in the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc.' /
'Of what kind?' — unlike any other expressible particular — unlike the particular expressed meanings — [the answer is] in every way inexpressible, i.e., different from the expressible. By this statement of inexpressibility, 'the sequence must exist' has been indicated. /
Also, 'non-contradictory to the expressed meaning' — but when contradictory, it is indeed perceived — this is the meaning. /
'Why is it not perceived?' — he states another reason embedded in a reason, expressed in the locative of cause: 'in those that are swiftly operative' — /
The arrangements (<s>ghaṭanās</s>) that were previously described as possessing the qualities of sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>) etc. during the examination of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) — those arrangements are such that their result is the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc.; and they are 'unachievable by other means' — for the arrangement of <s>ojas</s> (vigor) does not produce the cognition of <s>karuṇa</s> (compassion) etc. [but only <s>vīra</s> (heroic) etc.]. /
What has been said amounts to this — because in poetry possessing <s>guṇas</s>, the arrangement is employed with an unmixed subject-matter, therefore the sequence is not perceived. /
Objection: let the arrangements stand thus — why is the sequence not perceived? To this he says: 'swiftly operative' — without waiting for the time of expressed-meaning cognition, those [arrangements] swiftly bring about <s>rasa</s> etc. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The meaning is: they produce the relishing (<s>āsvāda</s>) of that. /
What has been said amounts to this — because <s>rasas</s> etc. are suggested by arrangement, even when the apprehension of meaning is not employed, already from the mere hearing of the appropriate arrangement, because the relishing of <s>rasa</s> has been initiated, therefore, even though accompanied by fully manifest relishing produced at a time posterior to the expressed-meaning cognition, it does not appear as arising afterwards. /
For indeed in a well-practiced domain, the sequence of the cognition of invariable concomitance is not perceived in just this way. /
For this practice is precisely this: that even without deliberate attention, due to the potency of the latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>), by constantly standing ready to manifest, — thus, because the <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) 'where there is smoke, there is fire' is established in the heart, mere knowledge of the property of the subject (<s>pakṣa-dharma</s>) becomes useful, and occupies the place of the inferential cognition (<s>parāmarśa</s>); since upon the sudden arising of smoke-cognition, aided by the recollection of the concomitance with it, due to the absence of the entry of any intervening cognition following upon the pursuit of something of a different kind, in the swiftly operative fire-cognition — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The meaning is: the arrangement. /
'Of <s>rasas</s> etc.' — the elaboration is: 'the relishing of that' etc. /
She elucidates the answer obtained through the passage beginning with 'but that' to the question 'the sequence — why is it not perceived' — 'what has been said amounts to this' etc. /
'Because they are suggested by arrangement' — the meaning is: because they are suggested by arrangement, even without the employment of meaning-cognition. /
'Already' — even before the cognition of the expressed meaning. /
'Appropriate' — the meaning is: practiced. /
'Initiated' — slightly manifested. /
'By that' — its syntactic connection is with 'does not appear.' /
'Expressed-meaning cognition' — the fully manifest relishing that arises due to its arising at a time posterior to expressed-meaning cognition — even though endowed with that; 'endowed with fully manifest relishing' is also a reading. /
'As arising afterwards' — as arising at a time posterior to expressed-meaning cognition — /
'Does not appear' — /
The completion is: to <s>sahṛdayas</s> (sensitive readers). /
'Practice' etc. — /
In the <s>Nyāya-bhāṣya</s>: 'Practice is the repetition of cognitions concerning the same object.' /
'Deliberate attention' etc. — /
In the <s>Nyāya-bhāṣya</s>: 'Deliberate attention is the fixing of the mind with the desire to remember.' /
Fixing means concentration. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.) in 'deliberate attention etc.,' the grasping of 'signs' (<s>liṅga</s>) etc. mentioned in the <s>Nyāya-sūtra</s> — 'based on deliberate attention, practice, and sign' — is indicated. /
The connection of 'without' is with 'standing ready to manifest.' /
'Due to its potency' — due to the firmness in the form of immediately-awakening equanimity — this is the meaning. /
'Standing ready to manifest' — in the sense of being the provider of the awakening in the form of recollection — this is the meaning. /
The usage is like '<s>kūlaṃ pipatiṣatī</s>' (the bank that wishes to fall). /
What was stated generally by 'practice' etc., she shows specifically — 'thus' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: 'of this concomitance — thus.' /
'Established in the heart' — the meaning is: existing within the inner faculty in the form of a latent impression. /
'Subject-property' — the meaning is: the mere knowledge that the <s>liṅga</s> (probans) such as smoke etc. resides in the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>) such as the mountain etc. /
By 'mere,' the exclusion of the <s>parāmarśa</s> (inferential cognition) — the cognition of the subject as possessing the probans qualified by concomitance with the probandum — is indicated. /
'Useful' — the completion is: in the inference of fire etc. /
'Thus' — expressing the reason. /
'Inferential cognition' — becomes the equivalent of the inferential cognition; this view is clear. /
The connection of 'suddenly' is with 'recollection of the concomitance.' /
'The concomitance with that' — the meaning is: aided by the recollection of the concomitance of fire etc. with smoke etc. /
'That' etc. — /
From those two — the smoke-cognition and the concomitance-recollection — that which is different in kind: the intervening cognition in the form of examination through pursuit and following of deliberate attention etc. — somewhere, however, it is indeed perceived — /
as in the cases of suggested meanings in the form of reverberation (<s>anuraṇana</s>). /
In that case too, how? — if asked, we say: /
In <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) whose suggested meaning is reverberation based on the power of meaning (<s>arthaśakti</s>), the expressed meaning and the meaning implied by its capacity — being utterly unlike any other expressible meaning — the two cognitions thereof, whose cause-effect relationship cannot be denied, clearly display temporal sequence. /
As in the verses cited in the first <s>Uddyota</s> to establish the suggested meaning. /
And in such a domain, because of the utter dissimilarity between the expressed and the suggested, it cannot be said that the cognition of one is the cognition of the other. /
But in <s>dhvani</s> whose suggested meaning is reverberation based on the power of words (<s>śabdaśakti</s>) — '<s>gāvo vaḥ pāvanānāṃ</s>...' (May the cows of the purifiers produce in you supreme and immeasurable delight) — [<s>Locana</s>:] the sequence is not perceived; and similarly here too. /
But if the <s>rasa</s> were contradictory to the expressed meaning and the appropriate arrangement were not present, then the sequence would indeed be perceived. /
The <s>Candrikā</s>-author, however, following the principle 'reciting without having studied,' explained with deliberate avoidance [of the true meaning] — the result of that word, or the result [consisting of] the cognition of the expressed and suggested — its accomplishment is unachievable by other means, i.e., producible only by verbal operation. /
But we do not perceive any truth of meaning in this explanation — so enough of this extended dispute with [our] predecessors. /
But where there is no suggestedness through arrangement, there [the sequence] is indeed perceived — he says: 'but somewhere, however.' /

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Thus previously' — the purport is: the arrangement of phonemes (<s>varṇasaṅghaṭanā</s>) etc. has not been stated as its suggestor. /
'In the <s>gāthās</s>' — /
'<s>Bālapriyā</s>' — his entrance into it — the meaning is: from the separation [i.e.,] absence of that. /
'Of the quickly-arising' — in that which arises instantaneously. /
'In the cognition of fire' — when fire is inferred from a mountain etc. /
'Sequence' — /
the remainder is: of the cognition of smoke accompanied by the recollection of invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>). /
He concludes — 'likewise' etc. /
The similarity should be understood through the instantaneity caused by repeated practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>). /
He states the meaning to be understood from the passage 'non-contradiction with the expressed' etc. [spoken by] the young woman — 'if' etc. /
He explains the commentary on the passage beginning with 'not other' etc. — 'of that' etc. /
'The reality of the meaning' — /
The meaning is: the coherence (<s>saṅgatatva</s>) of the meaning. /
He establishes that the sequential order is quite clear — 'of the non-intended' etc. /
'Thus previously it was stated' — the connection is: the arrangement of phonemes etc. has not been stated as the suggestor of this. /
In [the passage beginning with] 'thus' etc., where two meanings are cognized verbally, the cognition of the two meanings as having the relation of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison), when the word denoting simile (<s>upamāvācaka</s>) is absent, is suggested by the force of meaning — therein also, the cognitions of the expressed and the suggested figure of speech are easily discernible. /
'Sequential order' — /
Even in <s>dhvani</s> that consists of suggestion (<s>anuraṇanarūpavyaṅgya</s>) based on the power of the word at the level of word-illumination (<s>padaprakāśa</s>), the connection of the qualifying word with both meanings, [achieved] without a connecting word (<s>yojakaṃ pada</s>), though non-verbal, is established by force of meaning — here too, the sequential order of the cognitions of merely the expressed and the figure suggested by its force is well-established, just as before. /
'<s>Locana</s>' — in the [<s>Prākrit</s> verses] beginning with '<s>bhama dhammia</s>' etc. /
And those have been explained in that very [passage]. /
'Verbal' — /
The meaning is: even in the verbal [cognition]. /
The word denoting simile is '<s>yathā</s>' (just as) etc. /
'By the force of meaning' — /
This means: by the force of the sentence-meaning. /
Having thus examined the word-illumination and sentence-illumination based on verbal power (<s>śabdaśaktimūla</s>), he examines the word-illumination — 'word-illumination' etc. /
'Of the qualifying word' — /
of [the word] '<s>jaḍa</s>' (dull/inert). /
'The connecting [word]' — /
'<s>kūpa</s>' (well) and '<s>aham</s>' (I) — the combining through co-referentiality (<s>samānādhikaraṇatā</s>) with both. /
The expressed, and that which is suggested by its force — of those two, which are merely figures of speech — /
the cognitions of those two — their sequential order (<s>paurvāparya</s>) is the sequence. /
'Well-established' — the meaning is: well-discerned (<s>sulakṣita</s>). /
By the word '<s>mātra</s>' (merely), he shows that the cognition of <s>rasa</s> even there is of imperceptible sequence (<s>alakṣyakrama</s>). /
'<s>Bālapriyā</s>' — by which the indistinctness of the sequential order would occur — this is the purport. /
'Even in the verbal' — /
The meaning is: even in that which is produced by words, i.e., by <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation). /
By the word '<s>api</s>' (even/also), the position that what is not the primary meaning is also suggested is indicated. /
Regarding 'absence of the word denoting simile' — he elaborates on the word denoting simile (<s>upamāvācakapadaṃ</s>) — '<s>upamā</s>' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'suggested' — /
The meaning is: produced. /
'Of the expressed' — /
The meaning is: of the cognitions of the expressed and of the suggested figure of speech — of those two — this is the meaning. /
The second meaning too is expressed; mere simile is suggested — this is according to that opinion; the same should be understood in the case to be stated immediately after. /
She introduces into the <s>Locana</s> by first paraphrasing the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'thus' etc. /
'Word-illumination' — /
The connection is: based on verbal power (<s>śabdaśaktimūla</s>). /
She comments keeping in mind the stated example beginning with '<s>prātuṃ dhanaiḥ</s>' — 'of [the word] <s>jaḍa</s>' etc. /
She explains the meaning of the word '<s>yojana</s>' (connection) — '<s>kūpa</s>' etc. /
'And of both' — /
The meaning is: of both the word-meanings '<s>kūpa</s>' and '<s>aham</s>.' /
'Combining' means mixing together. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'even non-verbal' — /
The meaning is: even that which is not conveyed by a connecting word. /
'By force of meaning' — by suggestion (<s>vyañjanā</s>). /
'Established' — having become the object of cognition. /
She comments on [the passage] beginning with 'expressed' etc. — 'the expressed' etc. /
Here the expressed figure is <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), since '<s>jaḍatva</s>' (inertness) applies to both. /
And the suggested [figure] is simile (<s>upamā</s>). /
The expressed, and the figure suggested by its force — those very two are the 'mere' [figures] — and the meaning of the <s>vṛtti</s> should be understood thus. /
To dispel the apprehension of imperceptibility, she comments in accordance with that — 'well-discerned' etc. /
'By the word <s>mātra</s>' — /
The meaning is: by the word '<s>mātra</s>' in 'merely figure of speech' (<s>alaṅkāramātra</s>). /
And even in the meaning-based (<s>ārthī</s>) cognition, in the domain described, since it is produced by the capacity of the word that is capable of connection with both meanings, it is conceived as based on verbal power (<s>śabdaśaktimūlā</s>). /
But for the <s>dhvani</s> of the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (non-intended expressible) type, the illumination of another meaning is necessarily preceded by the cognition of aversion to one's own primary domain — hence the sequence is invariable (<s>niyamabhāvī</s>). /
Therein, since it is of the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> type, the examination of the sequential cognition of the suggested together with the expressed was not undertaken. /
Therefore, just as of denotation and denoted meaning — [<s>Locana</s>:] Objection: thus the being meaning-based (<s>ārthya</s>) and the being based on verbal power are contradictory — anticipating this, he says — 'even in the meaning-based' etc. /
The purport is: there is no contradiction here. /
And this has been determined at length previously, so it is not repeated. /
'Its own domain' — /
The primary domain of the word '<s>andha</s>' (blind) etc. is 'one whose eyes are impaired' etc.; the aversion toward that — the meaning is: disregard. /
'The examination was not undertaken' — /
The remainder is: through the method of determining the nomenclature. /
The purport is: because it is inappropriate here to doubt simultaneous [cognition]. /
Thus, <s>rasas</s> etc. are the life-force of both the <s>vṛttis</s> (styles) such as <s>Kaiśikī</s> etc. — which are in the form of <s>itivṛtta</s> (narrative) components — and of <s>Upanāgarikā</s> etc.; since both types of literary style (<s>vṛttivyavahāra</s>) have <s>rasa</s> etc. as their governing domain — what was undertaken [namely] that in connection with it, to establish the extra-expressed nature of <s>rasas</s> etc., the sequence [of cognitions] was examined — this he concludes — 'therefore' etc. /
'Of denotation' — '<s>Bālapriyā</s>' — the cognition of <s>rasa</s> — /
The meaning is: the cognition of <s>rasa</s> or <s>bhāva</s>. /
'Even there' — /
The meaning is: even in the stated domain based on verbal power. /
In '<s>prātum</s>' etc., <s>nirveda</s> (dispassion) is the suggested [meaning]. /
'Not here' etc. — /
The meaning is: there is no contradiction since the qualifier 'capable of connection with both meanings' etc. is present. /
Having thus taught the sequence of suggested and suggestor in the <s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s> (intended-other-primary-expressible) type, in order to show that there is sequence of suggested and suggestor everywhere, he says — in the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'non-intended' etc. /
He explains 'aversion to its own domain' with reference to the previously stated example beginning with '<s>niḥśvāsāndha</s>' — 'of the word <s>andha</s> etc.' etc. /
'Domain' — the expressed meaning. /
'Disregard' — /
The meaning is: abandonment, because the expressed meaning is sublated (<s>bādhita</s>). /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'of another meaning' — /
The meaning is: of the suggested. /
'Sequence' — /
The remainder is: of the cognitions of expressed and suggested. /
'Since it is of the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> type' — /
The meaning is: because the expressed is non-intended in the domain of <s>avivakṣitavācya-dhvani</s>. /
'Of the sequence' — /
The meaning is: the examination of what is the sequence-cognition — i.e., the examination of the sequence of the cognitions of expressed meaning and suggested meaning. /
'Was not undertaken' — here she supplies in the <s>Locana</s> — 'the nomenclature' etc. /
She states the purport — 'simultaneous' etc. /
'Here' — /
The meaning is: in the <s>avivakṣitavācya-dhvani</s>. /
Objection: the life-status of <s>rasa</s> etc. for the <s>vṛttis</s> was introduced, and the sequence of expressed-and-suggested cognitions was concluded with 'therefore' etc. /
Since this is disconnected, she introduces that passage — 'thus <s>rasas</s> etc.' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: 'and of the <s>vṛttis</s> [called] <s>Upanāgarikā</s> etc.' /
She states the reason for the life-status of <s>rasas</s> etc. for both types — with 'of all' etc. /
The construal is: what was undertaken — that was examined in connection with it. /
'This' — /
The meaning is: the examination of sequence that arose incidentally (<s>prasaṅgāgata</s>). /
The cognitions of expressed and suggested are sequential because of the cause-effect relation, just like the cognitions of denotation and denoted — thus the sequence of expressed-and-suggested cognitions is invariable because of the cause-and-caused relation. /
But that [sequence], by the reasoning stated, is sometimes perceptible and sometimes not perceptible. /
Thus, having determined the varieties of <s>dhvani</s> through the suggestor, someone might say — what is this suggestive capacity, namely the illumination of suggested meaning? For the suggestive capacity and the suggestedness are not inherent in meaning; the suggestedness depends on the establishment of the suggestor, and the establishment of the suggestor depends on the suggested — hence there is indeterminacy due to mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>). /
Objection: [<s>Locana</s>:] previously the cognition of the verbal form — the suggested is distinct from the expressed — then [comes the cognition] of the denoted. /
As you yourself stated — 'By words whose referents have not been ascertained, meaning is not illuminated' — etc. /
Therefore, even in [the passage] 'because its form is not ascertained, what does it say? — this is asked,' the sequence may not be perceptible, because the convention (<s>samaya</s>), like invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>), has been practiced. /
At the beginning of the <s>Uddyota</s>, what was stated — that through suggestion the nature of <s>dhvani</s> is being taught — now concluding that, having established the suggestive capacity in the first <s>Uddyota</s>, in order to impress upon the minds of students in a single connected section, he states the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) — 'thus indeed' etc. /
'Someone' — /
a <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> etc. /
'What is this' — /
This is the purport of the objection to be stated. /
'<s>Bālapriyā</s>' — she comments to remove the apprehension of deficiency in the example of the inference stated in the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'of denotation' etc. /
'As [you] state' — /
The meaning is: because [you] state. /
'Referent' etc. — /
'Referent-ness' means being the object of auditory and other cognitions. /
'Not ascertained' — the meaning is: unknown. /
'Is not illuminated' — rather, only by [words] that are known — this is the meaning. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.) indicating the passages referred to, she also shows a half-verse — 'therefore' etc. /
'Therefore' — /
The meaning is: since only what has been ascertained has the capacity to convey meaning, therefore — this is the meaning. /
'Because its form is not ascertained' — /
The meaning is: because the form of the word is uncertain when the listener has not heard properly. /
'What does it say? — this is asked' — /
The meaning is: [the listener] asks 'what are you saying?' /
The purport is: out of the desire to know both the word and its meaning. /
Incidentally she says — 'here too' etc. /
'Here too' — even of the cognitions of denotation and denoted meaning. /
'Like invariable concomitance' — just as of invariable concomitance itself. /
'Of the convention' — of the designation-convention (<s>saṅketa</s>) for particular words for particular meanings. /
'May not be perceptible' — sometimes may be imperceptible. /
The passage from 'thus indeed' to 'determined' is not [directly] useful; he introduces [the passage] beginning with 'someone,' showing its purpose, since the determination of suggestive capacity is repeated — with 'at the beginning of the <s>Uddyota</s>' etc. /
'In a single connected section' — in a single <s>prakaraṇa</s>. /
'What is this' — here the word '<s>kim</s>' expresses censure or question; since the reason is not stated therein, she says — 'of the [objection] to be stated' etc. /
The meaning is: 'indeterminacy due to mutual dependence' is what is to be stated. /
'Of the objector' — of the disputant. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'illumination of suggested meaning' — /
The meaning is: the capacity favorable to the cognition of suggested meaning. /
After this, 'if' is the remainder. /
She negates — 'not indeed' etc. /
The remainder is: of the word. /
The establishment of the word has already been demonstrated; and the establishment of the suggestor depends on that — so what occasion is there for objection? /
This is indeed true; the existence of a meaning beyond the expressed was established by previously stated reasoning — but why is that meaning designated specifically as 'suggested' (<s>vyaṅgya</s>)? /
And where there is primacy — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'previously' — /
In the first <s>Uddyota</s>, in the refutation of the non-existence position. /
And therefore, the establishment of that does not depend on the establishment of the suggestor — so that mutual dependence might be suspected — rather, because it has been established by other means — this is the purport. /
Therefore he says — 'of that establishment' etc. /
'But that' — /
Let that second meaning exist; if its name is 'suggested' (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), why is it not called 'expressed' (<s>vācya</s>)? Or why is not even what is considered 'expressed' called 'suggested'? For by virtue of being apprehended, it has the nature of being a word-meaning — that itself is expressiveness (<s>vācakatva</s>). /
'<s>Abhidhā</s>' (denotation) — '<s>Bālapriyā</s>' — the suggestive capacity and the suggestedness of meaning — 'not indeed' — do not exist inherently. /
'Indeed' — /
In the sense of common knowledge. /
The remainder is: therefore. /
The meaning is: therefore, by elimination. /
'Suggestedness depends on the establishment of the suggestor' — and 'the establishment of the suggestor depends on the suggested' — /
'Thus' — /
The meaning is: for this reason. /
'Indeterminacy' — non-establishment. /
Alternatively — 'not indeed' connects with the preceding. /
To indicate that suggestive capacity belongs to the word alone, it is said 'and suggestedness belongs to meaning.' /
And thus, since suggestedness belongs to meaning, therefore suggestive capacity belongs to the word alone — and that is the illumination of suggested meaning — 'not indeed' — this is the connection. /
Here she states the reason — 'the establishment of suggestive capacity' etc. /
If there is no reading of '<s>vyaṅgyatvam</s>' after 'depending on the establishment of suggestive capacity,' then the construction is thus — suggestive capacity, the illumination of suggested meaning, is not indeed [self-existent]. /
Why? — here she says '<s>vyaṅgyatvam</s>' etc. /
'Objection' etc. — this is the passage of the <s>siddhāntin</s>'s (proponent's) resolution. /
Anticipating forgetfulness, she explains the word 'previously' found there in the <s>Locana</s> — 'in the first' etc. /
She states the implication — 'and therefore' etc. /
The word 'and' is for emphasis; she states the reason referred to by 'therefore' — 'by other means' etc. /
'Therefore he says' — /
The meaning is: therefore he says. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'depending on the establishment of that' — /
The meaning is: depending on the establishment of the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). /
Having paraphrased the <s>siddhāntin</s>'s statement with 'true' etc., the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> states the refutation with 'but that' etc. — she explains that passage — with 'let that exist' etc. /
'But that meaning' — the commentary on this is: 'let that second meaning exist.' /
She explains the exclusive particle (<s>evakāra</s>) in 'specifically as suggested' in two ways — with 'of that' etc. /
'Is not called' — /
And therefore a restrictive ground for the application of the word 'suggested' must be stated, and thus [the argument] would culminate in mutual dependence itself — this is the purport. /
With 'and where' etc., she introduces the passage that states another objection in the form of the non-establishment of the meaning qualified by suggestedness — with 'by virtue of being apprehended' etc. /
'By virtue of being apprehended' — by virtue of being apprehended through words. /
'The nature of being a word-meaning' — /
And thus: being apprehendable through words is expressedness (<s>vācyatva</s>) — this is the meaning. /
'That itself' — /
The meaning is: that which is the correlate of the apprehendability in meaning — that itself. /
I.e., the capacity to make [meaning] apprehended. /
Let it be so; then what? Therefore she says — '<s>abhidhā</s> indeed' etc. /
'<s>Abhidhā</s>' — denotation included within expressiveness. /
[That expressive function] whose extent is up to which [meaning] — there, only as expressed should it be designated, since the sentence has that as its purport. /
And therefore, the function of the sentence that illuminates it is expressiveness alone. /
What need is there to postulate another function for it? Therefore, the meaning that is the object of purport (<s>tātparya</s>) is primarily expressed. /
But the intervening cognition of another expressed meaning in such a domain is merely a means toward that [final] cognition, just as the cognition of word-meanings [is a means] toward the cognition of sentence-meaning. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Indeed, expressiveness is appropriate only in that which is the ultimate aim; and that ultimate aim lies in that primary meaning — thus, what has been determined as the supreme form of <s>dhvani</s> — in that very [domain], it would be appropriate to apply the function of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation). /
Therefore he says — 'and where' etc. /
'That which illuminates it' — /
