children.translated_text: For sometimes the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) has primacy, and the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) attains subordinate status — [<s>Locana</s>:] having thus, in the present context, refuted the principle of word-meaning and sentence-meaning (<s>padārtha-vākyārtha-nyāya</s>) that serves to establish the power of <s>tātparya</s> (purport), and intending to establish the favored <s>prakāśa-śakti</s> (illuminating power), he applies the appropriate principle of the lamp and the pot (<s>pradīpa-ghaṭa-nyāya</s>) to the present context — saying 'therefore' etc.

children.text: yato 'sau padārthavākyāthanyāyo neha yuktastasmāt prakṛtaṃ nyāyaṃ vyākaramapūrvakaṃ dārṣṭāntike yojayati--yathaiva hīti /
children.translated_text: Since the principle of word-meaning and sentence-meaning is not appropriate here, therefore he applies a grammatical principle preceded by the new [analogy] to the <s>dārṣṭāntika</s> (the thing to be illustrated) in the present context — 'just as indeed' etc.

children.text: nanu pūrvamuktam--- yathā padārthadvāreṇa vākyārthaḥ sa pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Objection: it was stated previously — 'just as the sentence-meaning is apprehended through the medium of word-meanings,
so the apprehension of the [suggested] thing is preceded by the sentence-meaning.' //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'She is the <s>Bālapriyā</s>' — this is the meaning. /
In that very [context], the meaning of that [expression] has become the culmination. /
Objection: but denotative power (<s>vācakatva</s>) is with respect to the meaning that has become the culmination; from that, what [follows]? To this he says — 'that-culmination' etc. /
'That-culmination' (<s>tatparyantatā</s>) — the state of being the culmination with respect to that denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>), i.e., the state of being the object of purport (<s>tātparya</s>) — this much [is meant]. /
'In that' — /
the meaning is: 'in that which has become the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), which is not desired by you.' /
Revealing that what was stated constitutes a refutation, he states the conclusion — 'thus' etc. /
'Thus' — in the sense of a reason. /
'Foremost' (<s>mūrdhābhiṣikta</s>) — the principal [meaning] characterized by <s>rasa</s> etc. /
'Form' (<s>rūpa</s>) — essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>). /
'In that very [domain]' — /
The word '<s>eva</s>' connects with [the phrase] 'through the operation of denotation' (<s>abhidhāvyāpāreṇa</s>). /
'It would be fitting' — /
Hence the suggestive power (<s>vyañjakatva</s>) would be merely nominal — this is the purport. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>: 'where' etc. /
'Where' — in poetry etc. /
'Predominant establishment' — /
The meaning is: the establishment of the meaning as the object of purport (<s>tātparya</s>). /
'There' — in poetry etc. /
'That' — the meaning established with predominance. /
In the <s>Locana</s>: 'that' etc. /
'Necessarily' — /
The purport is: otherwise the beauty of poetry would not be established. /
'By this, through a general statement' — /
The meaning is: through a statement common to three positions — [namely] that the cognition of word-meanings is merely a means to the cognition of sentence-meaning, just as the cognition of sentence-meaning [is a means to the cognition of the suggested meaning] — by such a statement common to [all] three positions. /
He presents those three positions in order — 'in the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> view, for' etc. /
'For the sake of the sentence-meaning' etc. /
The activity of those words is solely for the sake of the sentence-meaning through the medium of producing the sentence; given that [activity], the conveying of their own meanings is an indispensable concomitant (<s>nāntarīyaka</s>), arrived at by the force of invariable concomitance. /
Just as [logs are used] for the purpose of cooking — here it is said: where a word, while denoting its own meaning, causes the apprehension of another meaning, there [we must consider] whether its denoting of its own meaning and its being the cause of the apprehension of that other meaning are without distinction or with distinction. /
Firstly, there is no absence of distinction; because those two operations, having different objects and different forms, are indeed cognized [as distinct]. /
For the operation characterized as denotative capacity (<s>vācakatva</s>) has the word's own meaning as its object, while that characterized as conveyance (<s>gamakatva</s>) has the other meaning as its object. /
[In the] <s>Locana</s>: the sentence-meaning is that very meaning which is elicited through purport (<s>tātparya</s>) from the word-meanings apprehended through words; and that alone is the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>). /
In the <s>Prābhākara</s> view also, the long, extended operation is directed toward the sentence-meaning as the occasioned [result] (<s>nimittin</s>), while the status of word-meanings as occasions (<s>nimitta</s>) is ultimately real. /
But for the Grammarians (<s>Vaiyākaraṇas</s>), that [status of word-meanings as occasions] is not ultimately real — this is the distinction. /
And this has been determined by us at length in the first <s>Uddyota</s> itself, so it is not labored over again; only the textual construction (<s>granthayojanā</s>) is done. /
That threefold position should be construed as the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view). /
'Here' — in the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>. /
'It is said' — is the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion). /
The distinction in essential nature is between denotative capacity (<s>vācakatva</s>) and conveyance (<s>gamakatva</s>); the distinction in object is: in the own meaning and in the other meaning, respectively. /
Objection: 'therefore that meaning is apprehended' — how then is it called 'another meaning'? /
'If not, then that [word] is not anything of his' — what is the object-meaning? [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the burning of logs that have been employed for [the benefit of] a child. /
Therefore the denotative operation (<s>abhidhāvyāpāra</s>) of words extends only up to the sentence-meaning, just as the operation of logs extends up to cooking — this is the meaning. /
'Thus' — /
The meaning is: by the method just stated. /
'Apprehended through words' — here /
the meaning is: apprehended through words occurring in sentences. /
'That alone' — /
By the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone), word-meanings are excluded, since they are merely means to the cognition of [sentence-meaning] and thus not the object of purport (<s>tātparya</s>). /
'Operation' — /
The remainder is: of words that constitute the sentence. /
'Of the occasioned' — /
The meaning is: of the form of the effect (<s>kārya</s>) that is occasioned. /
Even though the status of word-meanings as occasions (<s>nimitta</s>) is established by the very statement that the sentence-meaning is occasioned, in order to show the distinction from the Grammarian view, he says — 'of word-meanings, however' etc. /
The statement of the occasion-occasioned relationship (<s>nimittanimitibhāva</s>) between word-meanings and sentence-meaning is from the standpoint of origination, but the cognition arises first of the sentence-meaning according to the <s>Prābhākara</s> view, due to the doctrine of denotation-as-connected-with-action (<s>kāryānvitābhidhāna</s>) — this should be understood. /
'That is not ultimately real' — /
The meaning is: not ultimately real because it is of the nature of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). /
He states the purpose of briefly presenting the three positions — 'that is this' etc. /
'Should be construed' — /
The purport is: otherwise the fault of groundlessness would arise. /
'It is said' — he supplies: '<s>siddhānta</s>' (established conclusion). /
He clarifies the two distinctions — in essential nature and in object — stated by the <s>Vṛtti</s>-text beginning with 'where' — 'denotative capacity' etc. /
'In object' — /
'Distinction' is carried over [from the previous clause]. /
The purport is: denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>) is in the own meaning because it depends on convention (<s>samaya</s>); the operation of conveyance is in the other meaning because it does not depend on that [convention]. /
He introduces the text beginning with 'nor is it its own or other's' — 'objection' etc. /
'Therefore' — /
The meaning is: from that word, because the cognition of the denoted meaning arises — therefore, from that word. /
'That' — [the meaning] intended as suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). /
Objection: it is not apprehended from that word but rather through the force of what is related to it — to this he says: 'if not' etc. /
'He' — that word. /
Nor can the ordinary usage of 'own' and 'other' with respect to the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) and suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) be denied, since one is cognized as being directly related and the other as being related to what is related. /
For the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) is directly related to the word, while the other [meaning] is implied by the capacity of the denotation (<s>abhidheya</s>) — [it is] related to what is related. /
And if its relationship to [the word] were direct, then there would be no usage of 'other meaning' at all. /
Therefore the distinction in object between those two operations is very well established. /
The distinction in form is also well established. /
For the denotative capacity is not the same as the conveyance capacity. /
Because even a non-denotative [entity] such as a musical sound (<s>gīta</s>) etc. is seen to cause the apprehension of meaning characterized by <s>rasa</s> etc. /
And because it is well known that even a non-verbal [entity] such as a gesture etc. illuminates particular meanings. /
Thus — 'by one whose face is lowered due to the conjunction of bashfulness' — [from the] <s>Locana</s> — having raised the doubt, he says 'nor' etc. /
'Would not be' — /
The word '<s>eva</s>' is displaced in sequence; the meaning is: would not be at all. /
Insofar as there is no direct relationship, the usage of 'other meaning' is indeed appropriate — thus the distinction in object has been stated. /
Objection: even though the objects differ, just as in the case of the word '<s>akṣa</s>' (which has multiple meanings like 'eye,' 'die,' 'axle'), there is only one operation characterized as denotation for a polysemous word — anticipating this objection, he establishes the distinction in form — 'the distinction in form also' etc. /
He demonstrates [this] through well-known [examples] — 'for not' etc. /
He states the reason for one who disputes [this] — 'of even a non-denotative' etc. /
If denotative capacity were identical with conveyance, then a non-denotative [entity] would also lack conveyance; and [conversely,] where there is conveyance, there would necessarily be denotative capacity as well. /
But neither of these two [holds true] in the case of a musical sound, nor in the case of non-verbal [entities] such as downward-facing posture, trembling of the bosom, onset of tears, etc. — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] of that other meaning — /
'not anyone' — /
the meaning is: there is no one who is both a conveyor and a denoter. /
From that, what [follows]? To this he says — 'thus' etc. /
'Object-meaning' — meaning that has the nature of an object. /
Alternatively — the meaning of the word 'object' (<s>viṣaya</s>). /
'What' — /
the meaning is: another meaning would not be the object of the word. /
'Having raised the doubt, he says' — /
the meaning is: he says by [the passage beginning with] 'nor' and ending with 'would not be.' /
'The word <s>eva</s>' — /
the meaning is: the word '<s>eva</s>' in 'usage indeed' (<s>vyavahāra eva</s>). /
He elaborates the purport — 'insofar as' etc. /
'Insofar as' — by which reason. /
Objection: since the intended conclusion is already achieved by establishing the difference in objects, what is the purpose of establishing the difference in form? — To this, he introduces that text — 'objection' etc. /
'Of <s>akṣa</s>-word etc.' — by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), words like '<s>hari</s>' etc. are included. /
'Of a polysemous [word]' — /
the meaning is: of one having multiple meanings such as sense-organ etc. /
'One only' — /
the purport is: even when recurrence [of the denotative function] is required [for each meaning], in each case the operation is denotation alone. /
Having stated the well-known [fact] as a reason for the distinction in essential form, he shows the seed for stating yet another reason — 'for one who disputes' etc. /
'One who disputes' — one who says 'denotative capacity itself is conveyance, nothing else is experienced.' /
He explains the purport — by [the passage beginning with] 'if that very' etc. /
'Would not be' — here the reason is stated: 'where there is conveyance' etc. /
The construction is: where there is conveyance, denotative capacity also would certainly not not be — i.e., it would indeed be. /
'Because' — is the remainder. /
'Nor' — /
In the cited verse, a specific gesture has been shown by the skilled poet as a cause of meaning-illumination. /
Therefore, because of the difference in objects and the difference in form, the word's denoting its own meaning and its being the cause of apprehending another meaning — the distinction between these two is perfectly clear. /
'And if there is distinction' — then now, the apprehension of another meaning, which is implied by the capacity of the denotation, is not to be designated as expressed (<s>vācya</s>). /
But its being within the scope of verbal operation is indeed accepted by us; however, that is as suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) only, not as expressed (<s>vācya</s>). /
The well-known fitness for being related to another denotation — [from the] <s>Locana</s>: because [we see] that even a non-denotative [entity] causes apprehension, and because even a non-verbal conveyor is well known as non-denotative — this is the purport. /
He concludes this — 'therefore distinct' etc. /
'Not then' — /
For expressedness (<s>vācyatva</s>) is being the object of the denotative operation, not being the object of [just] any operation; for if that were so, it would be the fallacy of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>) — this is what he says: 'verbal operation' etc. /
Objection: let there be no denotative capacity in [the case of] song etc.; but here, in the case of another meaning, it is indeed denotative capacity of the word that is being asserted — what then restricts that denotative capacity? Anticipating this objection, he says — 'well-known' etc. /
'By another word' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] this is both — denotative capacity and conveyance — /
In the case of a musical sound and onset of tears etc., it does not exist — this is the syntactic connection; rather, only conveyance exists — this is the purport. /
By 'downward-facing posture' etc., the meanings taught by the verse 'due to the conjunction of bashfulness' are indicated. /
'Whence?' — to this he says: 'of that' etc. /
'Of that' — of that musical sound etc. /
'This is the purport' — /
the meaning is: the purport of the <s>Vṛtti</s>-text from 'of even a non-denotative' to 'is well established.' /
'This' — /
the meaning is: the refutation of the position of non-distinction, through the demonstration of the distinction between denotative capacity and suggestive capacity. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>: 'and if there is distinction' etc. /
'Of apprehension' — is carried over [from the previous clause]. /
'Of that which is to be apprehended' — the syntactic connection is: that other meaning which is related to the operation of apprehension. /
There is also the reading 'of what is to be apprehended' (<s>avagamanīyasya</s>). /
He states the reason for its being related to apprehension — 'of the denoted' etc. /
He elaborates what was said — 'expressedness is not to be predicated [of it]': expressedness is being the object of the denotative operation. /
The meaning is: being directly its object. /
'Of [any] operation merely' — /
the meaning is: of operation in general. /
'If that were so' — if it were the object of operation in general. /
'Proving what is already established' — /
of that meaning — /
because it would [merely] prove the status of being the object of the suggestive operation, which is already established in our view — the fallacy called 'proving what is already established' — this is the meaning. /
He introduces the text beginning with 'well-known' as [an objection and] its resolution — 'objection' etc. /
'Let there be no denotative capacity' — /
the purport is: because the expressed [meaning] is absent [in such cases]. /
'But here, of the word' — this is the syntactic connection. /
'Here' — in poetry. /
'But' — the word indicates a distinction. /
'Of the word' — of the denotative [word]. /
'In the other meaning' — [the meaning] intended as suggested. /
'Also' — in the sense of inclusion. /
'What indeed' etc. — /
the purport is: the fact that it is another meaning does not restrict that [denotative capacity]. /
Demonstrating the syntactic connection [and] explaining that the statement of the <s>Locana</s> alone is fitting, he explains the meaning of the word '<s>eva</s>' — 'by another word' etc. /
'By another word' — in [expressions like] 'a hamlet on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc., by the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc. /
'Of that other meaning' — of coolness, purificatory power, etc. /
And there, the apprehension of that other meaning being objectified by another word that denotes its own meaning — there the statement of illumination alone is fitting. /
Nor does the principle of word-meaning and sentence-meaning apply to the expressed and suggested [meanings]. /
Because even when the cognition of word-meaning is absent — [from the] <s>Locana</s>: that objectification — there the statement of illumination alone is fitting, not the statement of denotative capacity of the word, nor is the statement of expressedness of the meaning fitting there; for denotative capacity means the capacity to convey without intermediary by force of convention, just as that very word [conveys] its own meaning — thus he says: 'denoting its own meaning.' /
Expressedness means being conveyed without intermediary by force of convention, just as that very meaning [is conveyed] with respect to another word — he says: 'well-known.' /
That fitness for being related to another denotation that is well-known as having the status of expressed, through the well-known denotative capacity — or the fitness [to be so related] in the case of what is characterized by that — [of the meaning] so characterized. /
Nor does the word have such denotative capacity with respect to that meaning here, nor does that meaning have the aforementioned expressedness with respect to that word. /
If it does not exist, then how was the objectification of that [meaning] stated? Anticipating this doubt, he says — 'of cognition' etc. /
And yet that meaning is cognized, but not through the operation of expressed-expressor relationship — therefore that operation is indeed of a different kind — this much [is meant]. /
Objection: even so, let there be no denotative capacity, yet the power of purport (<s>tātparyaśakti</s>) will [suffice] — anticipating this objection, he says — 'nor' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] in that meaning — /
the statement of illumination — the statement of conveyance — /
Of the word — of the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc. — the statement of denotative capacity is not fitting — as the reason for this, he introduces the phrase 'denoting its own meaning,' preceded by the definition of denotative capacity — 'denotative capacity indeed' etc. /
'Of that very word' — of that very word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc. /
'In its own meaning' — in 'river-flow' etc. /
'Thus he says' — he says with that intention. /
The statement of expressedness is not fitting — as the reason for this, he introduces the text beginning with 'well-known,' preceded by the statement of the definition of expressedness — 'expressedness indeed' etc. /
'Of the meaning' — of coolness, purificatory power, etc. /
'Another word' — the word for coolness, purificatory power, etc. /
He comments in accordance with the topic at hand — 'well-known' etc. /
'As having the status of expressed' — is supplied. /
'By another denotation' — by another word, by the word for coolness, purificatory power, etc. /
'There, or' — /
the meaning is: 'or' [in the sense of] 'that which is defined by that expressedness.' /
'Fitness' means suitability. /
'Of what is characterized by that' — is a qualifier of 'of another meaning'; 'by fitness' — the third case-ending is in the sense of characterization — this is the purport. /
He concludes — 'nor such' etc. /
'The meaning' — the meaning of coolness, purificatory power, etc. /
'Of the word' — of the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc. /
'By fitness' — since the third case-ending is explained as characterization — because the connection with 'of cognition' has been removed by that explanation — he introduces the word 'if' — 'if' etc. /
'If it does not exist' — by this, what was said in 'nor such' etc. is recapitulated. /
'Of that' — of the meaning of coolness, purificatory power, etc. /
'Objectification' — /
the remainder is: by the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc. /
'And yet' — is the explanation of the meaning of the word '<s>ca</s>' (and) occurring in the <s>Vṛtti</s>. /
'That meaning' — the meaning of coolness, purificatory power, etc. /
'Through the operation' — after this, the remainder is: 'but through another operation.' /
And thus he states the conclusion — 'thus' etc. /
He introduces [the text] in accordance with the relevant context — 'objection' etc. /
'The power of purport will [suffice]' — /
[a position] maintained by certain scholars. /
Even by those who do not accept its unreality, the principle of pot-and-its-material-cause must be accepted for sentence-meaning and word-meaning. /
For just as when a pot is produced, the material causes [of the pot] are not perceived separately, so too when a sentence — or its meaning — is cognized, the words and their meanings are not perceived separately at that time; if they were perceived separately, the cognition of sentence-meaning itself would become remote. /
But this principle does not apply to the expressed and suggested [meanings]; for when the suggested [meaning] is being cognized, the cognition of the expressed [meaning] does not become remote. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'By certain' — by the Grammarians. 'Even by those' — /
by <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> and others. /
He explains that very principle — 'for just as' etc. /
'Of the material causes' — /
the inherent causes (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>), the pot-sherds, are indicated by this expression. /
According to the Buddhist and <s>Sāṅkhya</s> views, although at the time of production the material [causes] do not exist — in one [system] due to momentariness, in the other due to being concealed — yet to this extent, that they are not perceived separately, the illustration holds. /
'Would become remote' — /
the purport is: because of the absence of identity of meaning [between the two cognitions]. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'of another meaning' — is the remainder. /
The power of the sentence favorable to the cognition of another meaning — that is the power of purport (<s>tātparyaśakti</s>), not [a power that is] not intended by you — this is the purport. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>: 'nor' etc. /
Just as the sentence-meaning is apprehended through the power of purport when the word-meaning is cognized, so too, when the sentence-meaning is cognized, another meaning [is apprehended] — this is not proper — this is the meaning. /
'Another meaning apprehensible through the power of purport' — since it is apprehensible by the collection of words, like the sentence-meaning — this is the inference intended by the objector here. /
'Nor' — here the reason is stated: 'because' etc. /
By this, the reason of dissimilarity of the illustration is shown. /
'Even when absent' — /
the purport is: because only the sentence-meaning in the form of <s>sphoṭa</s> is real. /
In the <s>Locana</s>: 'by <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> and others' — /
by the word 'others' (<s>prabhṛti</s>), the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> etc. are included. /
'Inherent' (<s>samavāyin</s>) — /
the inherent cause is that in which the thing being produced inheres. /
'Pot-sherds' — fragments. /
'By this expression' — by the expression 'material cause' (<s>upādāna-kāraṇa</s>). /
'Indicated' — shown. /
Objection: the general statement 'even by those' does not apply, since in the Buddhist and <s>Sāṅkhya</s> views, at the time of being taken up, the material [causes] do not exist — he raises this doubt: 'Buddhist' etc. /
'Do not exist' — here the reason is stated: 'in one' etc. /
'In one' — in the Buddhist view. /
'Momentary' — /
'Of the material [causes]' is carried over. /
For their doctrine is: whatever exists is momentary. /
'In the other' — in the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> view. /
'Due to being concealed' — due to the concealment of the material [causes]. /
He resolves [the difficulty] — 'yet' etc. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>: 'sentence' etc. /
Although the immediate topic is word-meaning and sentence-meaning, the mention of words and sentences is for the sake of the illustration. /
'Of words and their meanings' — /
'are not perceived separately' is carried over. /
When the sentence is cognized, therefore of the words; when the sentence-meaning is cognized, therefore of the word-meanings — there is no separate perception — this is the meaning. /
He shows the fault [that would arise] from separate perception — 'of those' etc. /
'Of those' — of words and their meanings. /
'At that time' — at the time of that cognition. /
'Separately' — as distinct from the sentence and sentence-meaning. /
'Would become remote' — /
the meaning is: the cognition of word-meaning would become remote. /
Here the reason to be understood is shown by the <s>Locana</s>: 'because of the absence of identity of meaning' — because the cognitions of word-meaning and sentence-meaning are inseparable, since the former illuminates the latter. /
Therefore the principle of the pot and the lamp applies to them: just as when a pot is cognized through the medium of a lamp, the light of the lamp does not cease, so too when the suggested meaning is cognized, the appearance of the expressed meaning [does not cease]. /
But what was stated in the first <s>Uddyota</s> — 'just as through the medium of word-meanings' etc. — that was with the intention of [showing merely] similarity in being a means. /
Objection: thus, the sentence would be connected with two meanings simultaneously; in that case, its very sentencehood would be disrupted, since that [sentencehood] is defined by unity of meaning (<s>ekārthya</s>). This is not a fault; because of the establishment [of those two meanings] in the relation of subordinate and principal. /

children.translated_text: He states the reason for the absence of that similarity — '<s>guṇavṛtti</s>' (secondary expressive function) etc.
The meaning is: both the <s>gauṇī</s> (figurative/secondary) and the <s>lākṣaṇikī</s> (indicatory/metonymic) forms [of expression].

children.text: nanu vyañjaktvena kathaṃ śūnyā guṇāvṛttirbhavati, yataḥ pūrvamevoktam-- mukhyāṃ vṛttiṃ parityajya guṇavṛttyārthadarśanam /
children.translated_text: Objection: how can the <s>guṇavṛtti</s> (secondary expressive function) be devoid of suggestive capacity, since it was stated previously — 'The apprehension of meaning through the secondary expressive function, abandoning the primary expressive function —

children.text: yaduddiśya phalaṃ tatra śabdo naiva skhaladgatiḥ //
children.translated_text: the word does not falter in its course toward the result for which [the secondary function] is employed.' //

[Bālapriyā:] Anticipating the doubt — 'how then is this very principle laboriously refuted here?' — he says 'but that which' etc. /
'That' — /
The meaning is: not with complete similarity. /
'Thus' — /
The meaning is: in the manner of simultaneous manifestation of both, like the lamp and the pot. /
'Of that' — of sentence-hood (vākyatā). /
'Having the definition of aikārthya (unity of meaning)' — for it has been stated: 'a sentence is one because of unity of meaning.' /
'Once' — [Bālapriyā:] the meaning is: because of the absence of unity of purpose. /
And 'the becoming-distant is not desired' — therefore the separate apprehension of those two is not to be accepted — this is the purport. /
He states the particular [point] relevant to the present context — 'but this is not' etc. /
To [the question] 'why?' he replies — 'for it does not' etc. /
'For it does not become distant' — this is the syntactic connection. /
Here he states the reason — 'in the expressed meaning' etc. /
The meaning is: because of the separate cognition of the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) together with the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>). /
He introduces the passage in the <s>Locana</s> beginning with 'therefore' etc. — 'thus' etc. /
The principle relevant to the context is the principle of the pot and the lamp (<s>ghaṭa-pradīpa-nyāya</s>). /
'Preceded by grammar' — preceded by exposition. /
Having excluded the word 'merely' in the [passage about] similarity being merely instrumental, he shows — 'but not' etc. /
'Having the definition of <s>aikārthya</s>' — /
<s>Aikārthya</s> is the state of that which has one meaning. /
He states the authority for this being a definition — 'because of unity of meaning' etc. /
Anticipating the objection that unity of meaning is not a definition since even a sentence having multiple meanings (as in the <s>śleṣa</s> ornament) is still a sentence, he resolves [this] by showing the intention — 'once' etc. /
Where a particular [meaning] serves a particular purpose, sometimes the expressed meaning has primacy and the other has subordinate status. /
There, when the suggested meaning has primacy, it has already been stated that it is <s>dhvani</s>; when the expressed meaning has primacy, another variety will be indicated. /
Therefore this is established: even when poetry has the suggested meaning as primary, the suggested meaning does not have the status of non-knowability, but rather has precisely the status of being suggested (<s>vyaṅgyatva</s>). /
Moreover, when there is no intention of giving primacy to the suggested meaning, the expressed-meaning-status should not be accepted by you [the opponent], because the word is not directed toward that. /
Thus at least this much exists: the suggested is some domain of words. /
Even where it has primacy, why should its essential nature be denied? /
[<s>Locana</s>:] For the heard word — wherever it produces recollection of convention — if that [meaning] has been conveyed by this very [hearing], then, because of the absence of activity after cessation, and because of the impossibility of many convention-recollections simultaneously, what occasion is there for differentiation of meaning? /
'Again, whether heard or remembered — it is not that [previous one]' — this is the purport. /
'Of those two' — of the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) and the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). /
'There' — /
The meaning is: when from among both varieties, the first variety [obtains]. /
'Another variety' — /
Designated as <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (suggested meaning in subordinate status). /
'Suggestedness itself' — the meaning is: the status of being illuminable (<s>prakāśyatva</s>) itself. /
Now, if the meaning which the word is directed toward is the word-meaning, then when the suggested has primacy, expressed-meaning-status alone would be proper; and if so, when it lacks primacy, would suggested-meaning-status be appropriate? — if so, our position is established. He states this — 'moreover' etc. /
Anticipating the objection 'let it not have suggested-meaning-status when it has primacy,' he says — 'even where' etc. /
'Being-other-than-the-meaning,' 'being related to the related,' 'being of unutilized convention' — [these are explained] in the <s>Bālapriyā</s> itself. /
'Recollection of convention' — recollection of conventional assignment (<s>saṅketa</s>). /
'Produces' — generates, by virtue of being an awakener (<s>udbodhaka</s>). /
'That' — that meaning. /
'By this very' — by this very word heard once. /
'If conveyed' — if made known through the assistance of context etc. /
'Then' — in that case, 'what occasion is there for differentiation of meaning?' — this is the connection. /
Anticipating the objection that if convention-recollection is the cause of meaning-cognition, then there could be many such [recollections], he eliminates the first alternative of the disjunction 'successively or simultaneously' — 'because of the absence of activity after cessation' etc. /
He eliminates the second — 'of conventions' etc. /
Now, in the domain of <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), multiplicity of meaning is observed — therefore he says — 'again' etc. /
'Whether heard or remembered' — in both cases, 'word' is to be supplied. /
Or alternatively: 'heard' — connected; 'word' is to be supplied. 'Remembered' — 'meaning' is to be supplied. /
'It is not that' — /
The meaning is: the previous word or meaning is not [the same]. /
And thus, in the case of <s>śleṣa</s>, since cognition occurs through repetition, the sentence and its meaning are different [each time], and their unity is merely figurative — this is the purport. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'this is not a defect' — /
The meaning is: it is not a defect in the form of sentence-division. /
'In the secondary' — /
And thus, in a sentence, the suggested meaning subordinate to the expressed, or the expressed meaning subordinate to the suggested — only one unified meaning is conveyed — this is the purport. /
She introduces the passage in the <s>Locana</s> beginning with 'moreover' etc. — 'objection' etc. /
'Proper' — this much is the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view). /
The <s>siddhāntin</s> (proponent), having asked 'if it is appropriate when it lacks primacy, then is suggested-meaning-status fitting?', restates the opponent's reply — 'suggested-meaning-status, if so' etc. /
By this, the passage in the <s>vṛtti</s> beginning with 'at least this much exists' etc. is elaborated. /
He states the purport — 'being-other-than-the-meaning' etc. /
'Being-other-than-the-meaning' — being of a meaning different from the primary meaning. /
'Being related to the related' — /
Thus, first, the suggestive power (<s>vyañjakatva</s>) is indeed something other than the denotative power (<s>vācakatva</s>); and further, <s>vyañjakatva</s> differs from <s>vācakatva</s> in that <s>vācakatva</s> resides in words alone, while the other [<s>vyañjakatva</s>] resides in both words and meanings, since the suggestive power of both words and meanings has been established. /
But <s>guṇavṛtti</s> (secondary expressive function), whether through figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) or indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), also resides in both [words and meanings]. /
However, <s>vyañjakatva</s> differs from that too, both in essential nature and in domain. /
The difference in essential nature is this: that [characteristic] which non-primarily — [<s>Locana</s>:] is the basis of suggested-meaning-status, and that exists even when [the suggested] has primacy — therefore its essential nature is not to be rejected — this is the purport. /
He concludes this — 'thus' etc. /
The meaning is: both in terms of difference of domain and difference of essential nature. /
'At least' — he intimates something further to be stated. /
He states that very thing — 'and furthermore' etc. /
By this he shows that there is also a difference in causation, arising from difference in the aggregate [of causal conditions]. /
And this — when elaborated in connection with the definition of <s>dhvani</s>, the word 'vā' in 'where meaning or word,' and the reduplication in 'vyaṅktaḥ' — has been shown by us in the first <s>Uddyota</s> itself, and therefore is not expanded upon again here. /
Thus, having demonstrated the difference of the illuminating power (<s>prakāśakatva</s>) from the primary denotative power (<s>vācakatva</s>) through difference of domain, difference of essential nature, and difference of causation, and [anticipating] the doubt — since there is no difference in respect of residing in both [words and meanings], what then is the difference between <s>vyañjakatva</s> and <s>gauṇatva</s> (figurative/secondary function)? — intending to demonstrate [the difference] from the non-primary [function] as well, he says — 'guṇavṛtti' etc. /
'Residing in both also' — residing in words and meanings. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the word's related [entity] is the expressed or indicated meaning — being related to that — this is the meaning. /
By this, cognizability through words is shown. /
He states the reason for being-other-than-the-meaning — 'being of unutilized convention' etc. /
The meaning is: having as its domain a cognition that does not depend on the apprehension of convention (<s>saṅketa</s>). /
'Thus' — the meaning is: this triad. /
Now, let this be so; what relevance does it have to the present context? — to this he says — 'and that' etc. /
'Even when it has primacy' — /
'Of the suggested' is to be supplied. /
'He intimates something further to be stated' — /
Because the word 'tāvat' has the sense of 'firstly' — this is the purport. /
'That very thing' — /
The meaning is: that very thing further to be stated. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, by [the word] 'from this [further consideration],' the reason in the form of difference of basis, which will be stated [beginning with] 'where,' is referred to — anticipating this, she explains — 'by this' etc. /
'From difference of aggregate' — /
The meaning is: from difference of the group of auxiliary factors (<s>sahakāri</s>). /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, by the word 'basis,' causation is meant — she says — 'there is also a difference of causation.' /
The meaning is: from difference of the group of auxiliary factors. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, by the word 'basis,' causation is meant — she says — 'there is also a difference of causation.' /
Although, since the basis-status of meaning for <s>vyañjakatva</s> depends on words themselves, and thus the word is the primary basis of <s>vyañjakatva</s> just as it is of <s>vācakatva</s>, there is unity of causation — nevertheless, from the difference of auxiliary factors, there is also a difference in the word as the causal entity — this is the meaning. /
The elaboration of 'of words and meanings' etc. is — 'and this' etc. /
Having first restated the <s>vṛtti</s>, she introduces the passage beginning with 'guṇavṛtti however' — by 'thus' etc. /
The connection is: having thus demonstrated the non-difference from the primary denotative power, intending to demonstrate [the difference] from the non-primary [function] as well, he says. /
What now is that demonstration? — to this, the passage beginning with 'since there is no difference in respect of residing in both' up to 'one would doubt' is stated. /
'Then' — /
The meaning is: if there is a difference between <s>vācakatva</s> and <s>vyañjakatva</s>, then. /
'What' — the meaning is: there is none. /
One might be confused that 'of both — in the form of figurative usage and indication — residing in both' means [this]; she explains — 'of words' etc. /
Through figurative usage and indication, the function (<s>vṛtti</s>) is the <s>guṇavṛtti</s>, which is well-known. /
But <s>vyañjakatva</s> is indeed the primary function of words. /
For the cognition of the triad of suggested meanings arising from meanings [etc.] — not even the slightest non-primary-ness is observed in it. /
And this is another difference in essential nature: what <s>guṇavṛtti</s> is — in its primary mode — is called <s>vācakatva</s> (denotative power) itself. /
But <s>vyañjakatva</s> is entirely distinct from <s>vācakatva</s>. /
And this has been demonstrated. /
And this is yet another difference in essential nature: when in <s>guṇavṛtti</s>, a meaning indicates another meaning, /
then it transforms into the form of the indicated meaning, having abandoned its own form. /
As in 'a settlement on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc. /
But in the path of <s>vyañjakatva</s>, when a meaning illuminates another meaning, it is perceived as illuminating that other while itself manifesting its own form — like a lamp. /
As in '<s>Pārvatī</s> counted the līlā-lotus petals' etc. /
And if, wherever a meaning with unobscured self-cognition indicates another meaning, the usage of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) is applied there, then in that case it would follow that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> alone is the primary function of words. /
Since the expressed meanings of most sentences manifest meanings that are objects of purport (<s>tātparya</s>) beyond the expressed meaning. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The essential natures of figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) and indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) have been distinguished and determined in the first <s>Uddyota</s> itself, so they are not written about again. /
'Primarily itself' — the meaning is: with unfailing course. /
'The triad of suggested meanings' — /
consisting of <s>vastu</s> (subject matter), <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament), and <s>rasa</s>. /
'<s>Vācakatva</s> itself' — the meaning is: therein too, the utilization of convention exists in just the same way. /
'Has been demonstrated' — /
just now. /
'Transforms' — /
The meaning is: not manifesting in its own form. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] And the <s>guṇavṛtti</s> — that it also resides in both [words and meanings] — this is the construction in the <s>vṛtti</s> — this is the purport. /
She reminds [us] of what was said before — 'of figurative usage and indication' etc. /
'Primarily itself' — she explains this 'primarily' in accordance with the present context — 'with unfailing course' etc. /
She elaborates on '<s>vācakatva</s> itself is <s>guṇavṛtti</s>' — 'therein also' etc. /
'Therein also' — even in <s>guṇavṛtti</s> also. /
'In just the same way' — just as in <s>vācakatva</s>, in just the same way. /
'Utilization of convention' — the utilization of apprehension of conventional assignment. /
'Exists indeed' — this is the meaning. /

'Through the medium of that relation' — the meaning is: through the cause in the form of the relation of proximity to its own meaning. /
'Another domain' — such as bank etc. /
'Extends to' — makes [it] its own domain. /
'Word' is to be connected — the meaning is: the <s>Gaṅgā</s>-word etc. /
In the <s>Locana</s> — 'reasoning' — /
The meaning is: the reasoning stated in 'accordance with reason.' /
She completes — 'a lamp etc.' /
Now, <s>vyañjakatva</s> is the making-known [function]; and that is primarily of the sense-organ etc.; so what is the purpose of citing the lamp etc.? — to this she says — 'but of the sense-organ etc.' /
By the word 'ādi,' inference (<s>liṅga</s>) etc. are included. /
Since in the production of cognition it is an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), there is no <s>vyañjakatva</s> — this is the connection. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'in such a domain' — /
The meaning is: in a domain where cognition is preceded by the cognition of the expressed and the expressor. /
'Of <s>vācakatva</s> itself' — the meaning is: residing in <s>vācakatva</s> itself as basis. /
'How is it distinguished' — the meaning is: it is not distinguished. /
Here she states the reason — 'of that' etc. /
But <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> <s>dhvani</s> — how is it distinguished from <s>guṇavṛtti</s>? /
Since in its twofold division, the form of the twofold division of <s>guṇavṛtti</s> is indeed observed. /
This too is not a defect. Since <s>avivakṣitavācya dhvani</s>, though it takes the path of <s>guṇavṛtti</s> as its basis, is not of the form of <s>guṇavṛtti</s> itself. /
For <s>guṇavṛtti</s> is seen to be devoid of <s>vyañjakatva</s> as well. /
And <s>vyañjakatva</s> is the cause of the stated charm — [<s>Locana</s>:] he thus shows the acceptance and the rejection of the objection — 'avivakṣita' etc. /
The word 'tu' indicates a distinction from the preceding. /
'Of that' — of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> — in its twofold division, the twofold aspect consisting of figurative and indicatory nature is observed, becomes manifest — this is the meaning. /
He resolves this — 'this too is not [a defect]' etc. /
Of <s>guṇavṛtti</s> — whose path — the twofold division — is the basis, i.e., the ground that enters first as a cause — this is the meaning. /
And this has been determined previously. /

vyaṅgyaprakāśanaṃ hi vyañjakatvam /

prādhānyeneti /

prakāśakatvalakṣaṇamiti /
arthabodhanasāmarthyarūpamityarthaḥ /

kḷptakalpyamānayoḥ kḷptaṃ balavaditi nyāyo 'nena darśitaḥ /

padārthānāmityarthaḥ /

satyametat; kiṃ tu vakrabhiprāyuprakāśanena yadvyañjakatvaṃ tatsarveṣāmeva laukikānāṃ vākyānāmaviśiṣṭam /

children.translated_text: '<s>āpta</s>' (trustworthy) — /
But in the printed book, the reading is thus: '<s>āptavādāvisaṃvādād atra ced anumānataḥ</s>' (if here, from the non-discrepancy of trustworthy testimony, through inference). /

And the remainder of this is: '<s>nirṇayas tāvatā siddhyed buddhy-utpattir na tat-kṛtā</s>' /
(the ascertainment would be accomplished by that much; the arising of cognition is not caused by that) /

'<s>anyad eva hi satyatvam āptavādatva-hetukam</s>' //
(for the truth [of a statement] caused by its being a trustworthy utterance is indeed something different) //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Thus' — /
For a figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) is not devoid of purpose, and the operation of suggestion (<s>vyañjanāvyāpāra</s>) is directed toward the purposive aspect — anticipating that this was indeed conceded by you yourselves — he says that the intended suggestive capacity, which has the form of being the resting-place [of cognition], does not exist therein — 'and suggestive capacity' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In the <s>Locana</s> — 'he shows' — /
The remainder is: the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector). /
The elaboration of '<s>guṇavṛtti</s>' etc. is — '<s>gauṇī</s>' etc. /
To prevent straying to another meaning, she explains '<s>lakṣyate</s>' — 'will be manifested' (<s>nirbhāsyate</s>). /
The remainder is: in the manner stated in the passage beginning with 'not indeed.' /
'In the earlier stage' — /
The meaning is: in the stage prior to suggestion (<s>vyañjanā</s>). /
'Previously itself' — /
The meaning is: in the context of the commentary on the <s>gāthās</s> beginning with '<s>bhrama dhārmike</s>' in the passage beginning with 'not indeed.' /
'Absence of that form' — /
The meaning is: absence of the form of <s>guṇavṛtti</s> (secondary expressive function). /
Objection: since the passage '<s>guṇavṛtti</s> is seen to be devoid of suggestive capacity' already establishes the absence of <s>guṇavṛtti</s>-form in the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (non-intended expressible), what is the purpose of the passage beginning with 'and suggestive capacity'? — Therefore she introduces that passage — 'objection' etc. /
Objection: let the previous statement apply to something else — to this she says — 'not indeed' etc. /
'Thus' etc. — /
The meaning is: let other statements be set aside; this was indeed asserted by you yourselves. /
The elaboration of 'intended' is — 'having the form of being the resting-place.' /
'Therein' — /
The meaning is: in mere <s>guṇavṛtti</s>. /
'Does not exist' — /
Suggestive capacity here does not mean merely being the instrument of suggestion, but rather being the instrument of suggestion that constitutes a resting-place [for cognition]. /
The meaning is: that does not occur without suggestion that is a cause of beauty (<s>cārutvahetuvyaṅgya</s>). /
The elaboration of what was said — 'is seen to be devoid of suggestive capacity' — is in the <s>vṛtti</s>: 'but <s>guṇavṛtti</s>' etc. /
But <s>guṇavṛtti</s> occurs by relying solely on a property of the expressed meaning, and by relying on mere suggestion. /
It is in the form of identity-based figurative usage (<s>abhedopacāra</s>); the syntactic connection of 'just as' etc. in the sentence beginning with 'which also' etc., and the continuation of 'of the expressed' etc. and 'of the suggested' etc., should be understood. /
Therein, she explains 'by relying on a property of the expressed meaning' in accordance with the topic at hand in the <s>Locana</s> — 'the property that pertains to the expressed domain' etc. /
Does not subsist without the suggested. /
But <s>guṇavṛtti</s> occurs in the form of identity-based figurative usage, relying solely on a property of the expressed meaning and on mere suggestion — for example: 'because of sharpness, this boy is fire (<s>agni</s>),' 'because of its delightfulness, her face is the very moon (<s>candra</s>)' — in such cases. /
And as in '<s>priye jane nāsti punaruktam</s>' ('regarding a beloved person, there is no repetition') — in such cases. /
Even that <s>guṇavṛtti</s> which is in the form of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) can occur by relying merely on the connection with the indicated meaning (<s>upalakṣaṇīyārtha</s>), without the cognition of beautiful suggested meaning — as in the domain of '<s>mañcāḥ krośanti</s>' ('the platforms are crying out'). /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Property of the expressed' — /
The meaning is: for the purpose of strengthening that which relies on the property, i.e., the operation of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation), whose domain is the expressed. /
The purport is: because in <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) based on what is heard, it culminates in the establishment of the meaning other than the expressed meaning. /
Therein, she gives the example of the <s>gauṇa</s> (figurative) — 'just as' etc. /
She begins to illustrate the second type also as devoid of suggestive capacity — 'which also' etc. /
The beautiful form is the resting-place; in its absence, that operation of suggestive capacity does not open up at all, since [cognition] rests back in the expressed meaning alone — like a common person who glimpsed divine splendor for a moment and then lost it. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The remainder is: of the expressive [word]. /
The elaboration of the purport — 'for the purpose of strengthening that.' /
The meaning is: for the purpose of strengthening the expressed meaning. /
How is <s>guṇavṛtti</s> for the purpose of strengthening that? — To this she gives an illustrative example — 'of what is heard' etc. /
Just as in '<s>pīno devadatto divā na bhuṅkte</s>' ('Fat <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day') — what is heard, namely fatness etc., necessitates the postulation of eating at night etc. as its explanation. /
And the postulated other meaning culminates in the establishment of fatness etc. — similarly, in the domain of <s>guṇavṛtti</s>, the other meaning that is indicated culminates in establishing the expressed meaning of the other word — this is the meaning. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'by relying on mere suggestion' — by the word '<s>mātra</s>' (mere), the primary suggested [meaning] that causes beauty is excluded. /
'<s>Priye jane</s>' — /
The word '<s>priya</s>' (beloved), like '<s>tīkṣṇatvāt</s>' (because of sharpness) etc., states the cause in the form of a <s>guṇa</s>-based property; by the word '<s>punaruktam</s>' (repetition), the meaning of unacceptability — /
this was stated previously in the examples. /
In these examples, the excess of qualities like sharpness etc. is the suggested [meaning], but that does not produce beauty — this is the purport. /
'Indicated' — /
The meaning is: by relying merely on the connection with the indicated meaning — i.e., the boys on the platform etc. — the relation of container and contained etc. — and by that alone, without the primary meaning of the word '<s>mañca</s>' (platform). /
The statement of what is excluded by the word '<s>mātra</s>' is 'beautiful form' etc. /
'Platforms' — /
Here, the plurality of the boys on the platforms is the suggested, and that too does not produce beauty. /
She explains 'beautiful form' in the <s>Locana</s> — 'resting-place' etc. /
Objection: even without the cognition of beautiful suggested meaning, let the operation of <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion) exist — to this she says — 'in its absence' etc. /
'In its absence' — in the absence of beautiful suggested meaning. /
'That' — that which is based on <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication). /
'Opens up' — manifests. /
Why? — to this she says — 'resting back' etc. /
'For a moment' — /
one who saw for just a moment and then lost the divine splendor — such a common, poor person — like that. /
Just as such a person reverts to his ordinary condition, so too the operation of <s>vyañjanā</s>; but where that cognition of beautiful suggested meaning is its cause, even there [the operation functions] only through the entrance of suggestive capacity, just like expressiveness (<s>vācakatva</s>). /
In a sentence whose meaning is impossible — for example, in '<s>suvarṇapuṣpāṃ pṛthivīm</s>' ('the earth with golden flowers') — there, the cognition of beautiful suggested meaning alone is the motivating [factor] — [<s>Locana</s>:] Objection: where cognition rests in the suggested meaning, what is to be done? — anticipating this, he says — 'but where' etc. /
There is another operation of suggestion, quite manifest — this is the meaning. /
He states the example already accepted [by the opponent] — 'like expressiveness' etc. /
For in the case of expressiveness, the operation of suggestion was indeed accepted by you yourself, by not rejecting the first variety of <s>dhvani</s> — this is the purport. /
Moreover, when another real entity is possible as the primary [referent], that very other real entity is superimposed as primary — the [superposition] operates merely due to the difference of domain — this is the life of figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>). But since golden flowers are fundamentally impossible, what superimposition-usage can there be of their gathering? For '<s>suvarṇapuṣpāṃ pṛthivīm</s>' would be a superimposition — therefore, here the operation of suggestion alone is primary, not the usage of superimposition; the latter merely arises without obstructing the operation of suggestion. /
Therefore she says — 'impossible' etc. /
'Motivating' — /
For the suggested [meaning] alone has the form of purpose and is the resting-place of cognition; when superimposed, if [the meaning] is impossible, rest of cognition is not even to be suspected. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The meaning is: since cognition rests in the expressed meaning alone, therefore. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'but where' etc. /
'That' — /
The meaning is: <s>guṇavṛtti</s>. /
'Through the entrance of suggestive capacity alone' — /
The remainder is: occurs. /
She introduces this passage — 'objection' etc. /
'Another' — /
The meaning is: distinct from that which conveys beautiful suggested meaning. /
'First' — /
The meaning is: <s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s> (intended-other-primary-expressible). /
'By not rejecting' — by accepting. /
She introduces the passage beginning with 'impossible' etc. by way of its purport — 'moreover' etc. /
'And' in 'and impossible' — the conjunctive particle is explained by 'moreover.' /
'Another real entity' etc. — /
The meaning is: superimposition occurs only when both the substratum (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) and the superimposed (<s>āropya</s>) exist. /
Just as fire [is superimposed] on a boy etc. /
Objection: when both exist, whence the usage of superimposition? — to this she says — 'merely by being a different domain' etc. /
The meaning is: merely by virtue of being a different domain. /
The purport is: because in reality there is no identity between the two. /
'Thus' etc. — /
The meaning is: the superimposition of one onto the other, when both the superimposed and the substratum exist inherently — this is the essential life of figurative usage. /
Let this be so; then what? — therefore she says — 'of golden flowers' etc. /
'Fundamentally' — absolutely. /
'Of their gathering' — of the gathering of golden flowers. /
'There' — in the domain of the example '<s>suvarṇapuṣpām</s>' etc. /
'What' — /
The meaning is: devoid of life. /
Objection: then how is the usage '<s>suvarṇapuṣpāṃ pṛthivīm</s>' justified? — to this she says — '<s>suvarṇa</s>' etc. /
The connection is: 'that would be a superimposition.' /
Without that [superimposition], the great poet's usage cannot be sustained — this is the purport. /
She states the implication — 'therefore' etc. /
'The usage of superimposition' — /
The meaning is: the usage of <s>guṇavṛtti</s> based on superimposition. /
'Therefore she says' — /
The meaning is: says with the stated intention. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, the meaning of 'motivating' is: motivating the usage. /
She states the purport of the passage beginning with 'beautiful form' — 'the suggested' etc. /
'Having the form of purpose' — a qualifier that contains the reason. /
Objection: even in the domain of an impossible referent, when <s>guṇavṛtti</s> exists, the usage of <s>dhvani</s> alone is appropriate by force of reasoning. /
Therefore, in <s>avivakṣitavācya-dhvani</s>, in both sub-varieties, <s>guṇavṛtti</s> is undifferentiated by the specific feature of suggestive capacity — it is not identical with it, [not having] the capacity to delight the hearts of the sensitive (<s>sahṛdaya</s>), being merely a cause of cognition in another domain — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'even when [it] exists' — /
The purport is: when it is relied upon for just a moment for the fulfillment of the suggestive operation. /
'Therefore' — /
'Undifferentiated by the specific feature of suggestive capacity' — the meaning is: that whose differentiation, i.e., distinction, through suggestive capacity, is absent — suggestive capacity is not its distinguishing mark. /
Alternatively: 'undifferentiated by the specific feature of suggestive capacity' means — subordinated in its own nature by the specific operation characterized as suggestive capacity, pervaded throughout. /
'Identical with it' — /
That which has a single form together with that [suggestive capacity] — it is not of such a nature. /
The suggestive capacity in <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> is distinct from the <s>guṇavṛtti</s> because the latter is a cause of beautiful cognition separately — just like the suggestive capacity pertaining to <s>vivakṣitavācya</s>; for <s>guṇavṛtti</s> does not have the nature of being a cause of beautiful cognition — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Let the resting-place of cognition be only the superimposed [meaning] conjoined with mere suggestion; why resort to beautiful suggested meaning? — to this she says — 'superimposed' etc. /
'Is impossible' — this contains the reason. /
'Relied upon for just a moment' — by this, it is shown that the meaning which is the domain of <s>guṇavṛtti</s> is the object of an intermediate <s>tātparya</s> (purport). /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'in such a domain' — /
The meaning is: a sentence whose referent is impossible. /
He concludes — 'therefore' etc. /
She explains 'undifferentiated by the specific feature of suggestive capacity' in accordance with the topic — 'by suggestive capacity' etc. /
'By that' — the third case-ending is instrumental. /
She states the established implication — 'suggestive capacity' etc. /
'Of that' — of that <s>guṇavṛtti</s>. /
'Distinction' — a subordinate property. /
Having thus commented with the intent of concluding the demonstrated distinction between suggestive capacity and <s>guṇavṛtti</s>, she also comments on this passage with the intent of concluding the demonstrated primacy of suggestive capacity and subordinacy of the other — 'alternatively' etc. /
'Alternatively' — moreover. /
'Undifferentiated' — not distinguished — is not [characteristic]. /
The meaning is: [<s>guṇavṛtti</s>] does not come to be distinguished [independently]. /
Since what culminates in that suggested [meaning] — how then can the suggested have primacy? — to this she says — 'and that' etc. /
'And' is for emphasis. /
Culminating in intention alone — culminating only in the suggested meaning of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
'The intended thing' — /
The meaning is: the expressed meaning. /
And therefore, the expressed meaning does not have the primacy characterized as being intended in poetic sentences — this is the purport. /
She introduces the passage beginning with 'but that which' etc. to ward off the apprehension of purposelessness — 'objection' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>: if that which is the suggested [meaning] in the form of a particular intention, being illuminated by purport, is illuminated through word and meaning, then it becomes the intended — this is the connection. /
'Intended' — primary. /
'That very' — that which is in the form of a particular intention. /
'Of unlimited scope' — this contains the reason. /
'Rather, shown in such a way' — this is the connection. /
'In such a way' — in the manner stated. /
'And if not in the form of intention' — /
'Intended' is to be connected. /
'No over-pervasion' etc. — /
In the domain of subordinated suggested meaning, the suggested that is in the form of a particular intention — that which is suggested in the form of a particular intention, illuminated through word and meaning, becomes the intended, being illuminated by purport. /
Rather, that alone — being non-pervasive since it is the motivating cause of the <s>dhvani</s>-usage, which has unlimited scope — /
that which is thus shown, in the form of the three varieties, illuminated by purport, whether in the form of intention or not in the form of intention — all of it is the motivating cause of the <s>dhvani</s>-usage — therefore, in the specific suggestive capacity as stated, the definition of <s>dhvani</s> has neither over-pervasion nor under-pervasion. /
Therefore, according to the view of those who know the truth of sentences (<s>vākyatattvavid</s>), the verbal operation characterized as suggestive capacity is not contradictory [to other principles], but rather is seen to be concordant. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Having thus shown that the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> have no disagreement here, he shows that the Grammarians (<s>Vaiyākaraṇas</s>) also have none — 'thoroughly ascertained' etc. /
'Thoroughly ascertained' — established by proof from all sides; 'free from corruption' — devoid of the imprint of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), by virtue of having shed the manifold of differentiation; called '<s>Śabda</s>' (Word) — having the nature of illumination and self-awareness (<s>prakāśaparāmarśasvabhāva</s>); '<s>Brahman</s>' — 'great' by virtue of being all-pervasive, 'nourished' by being replete with the powers of all particulars, and 'nourishing' by virtue of having the power to create the universe and being the Lord — by whom [this is known] — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Somewhere [a reading occurs]; taking that — there is no over-pervasion therein, because the suggested meaning of <s>rasa</s> etc. does not have the form of intention [in that case] — and in that domain there is no under-pervasion either — this is the meaning. /
He concludes — 'therefore' etc. /
'Is not contradictory' — this is the connection. /
By mentioning the term '<s>vākyatattvavid</s>' (one who knows the truth of sentences), he paraphrases what has been said in the <s>vṛtti</s>; while commenting on the concluding passage, by stating the meaning of the word '<s>vipaścit</s>' (wise one) qualified by the qualifiers beginning with 'thoroughly ascertained' etc., he states the purport of the passage to follow — with 'thus' etc. /
'That' — /
The meaning is: disagreement. /
She explains the passage beginning with 'thoroughly ascertained' etc. in detail, following the statements of <s>Bhartṛhari</s> such as '<s>anādinidhanaṃ brahma</s>' ('the beginningless and endless <s>Brahman</s>') etc. — 'from all sides' etc. /
'From all sides' — toward opponents on many fronts; by the word '<s>apabhraṃśa</s>' (corruption), which indicates a specific fault, the imprint of <s>avidyā</s>, which is the cause of all faults, is indicated — with this intention she comments — 'having shed' etc. /
'By virtue of having shed the manifold of differentiation' — by being free from contact with the manifold of differentiation. /
The third case-ending is in the sense of specification (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). /
The reason for having shed the manifold of differentiation is '<s>avidyā</s>' etc. /
The elaboration of the word '<s>śabda</s>' is: 'called <s>śabda</s> and <s>artha</s> (word and meaning).' /
That which has as its designation '<s>śabda</s>' and '<s>artha</s>' — that. /
The meaning is: having the nature of name and form. /
Alternatively: that in which <s>śabda</s> (word) and <s>artha</s> (meaning) have their manifestation (<s>ākhyā</s>) — that is the abode of the manifestation of word and meaning. /
She states its unconditioned form — 'illumination' etc. /
The meaning is: having the nature of self-luminous consciousness. /
Intending the derivation of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' from the root '<s>bṛh</s>' (to expand/grow), she explains — 'by being all-pervasive, great' etc. /
Having thus commented in terms of the unconditioned (<s>nirupādhi</s>) reference, she also comments in terms of the conditioned (<s>sopādhi</s>) reference — 'of the particulars' etc. /
The meaning is: fullness through the powers of all particular, individual [entities]; and by that — /
She connects with 'great' — /
Intending the derivation of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' from the root '<s>bṛh</s>' — /
And also intending another derivation — 'nourishing' etc. /
Having explained '<s>Brahman</s>' in terms of the root '<s>bṛh</s>' (to expand), she also explains it in terms of '<s>bṛṃh</s>' (to nourish) — 'the power of creating the universe' etc. /
And the Lordship — by virtue of being the controller of everything. /
The meaning is: [<s>Brahman</s>] is both the efficient and material cause. /
The <s>dhvani</s>-usage is dependent on the view of the wise who have this [understanding] — this is the connection. /
'Of those' — of words. /
'As' — the domain that has been shown, characterized by intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>). /
'Which is that' — /
The meaning is: the domain characterized by intention. /
'As a limiting condition' — /
The continuation is: is cognized. /
With the intention that the word '<s>upādhi</s>' here is a synonym for 'distinguishing factor,' she comments in the <s>Locana</s> — 'by the speaker's intention' etc. /
'Appears as a qualifier' — /
By this: in the cognition 'this meaning has been intended by the speaker,' the intention appears as a qualifier of the meaning. /
To strengthen what was said with 'therefore,' she reminds of what was stated before: the operation of words toward the suggested [meaning] is only as an indicator (<s>liṅga</s>). /
But when that [suggested meaning] is made its object, [it is cognized] as what is to be conveyed. /
When that which is in the form of intention and that which is not in the form of intention are both cognized, the operation [of words] is either through expressiveness (<s>vācakatva</s>) alone or through some other relation. /
First, through expressiveness — as was stated previously. /
Through another relation — this is suggestive capacity alone. /
And suggestive capacity is not merely of the form of being an indicator — since it is seen otherwise in lamps etc. [i.e., suggestion operates differently from inference]. /
Therefore, the object to be conveyed (<s>pratipādya</s>) is not related to words as something to be inferred (<s>liṅgitva</s>), like the expressed meaning. /
For that which is related to them as something to be inferred, as the domain has been shown, is not cognized as expressed, but rather as a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>). /
And if the object to be conveyed were [merely] something to be inferred, then the absence of the disputes that worldly people actually engage in regarding it would follow. /
And this too has been stated. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Appears as a qualifier.' /
'Of the object to be conveyed' — /
I.e., of the suggested meaning. /
'As something to be inferred' — /
The meaning is: as something to be inferred. /
'By worldly people themselves' — /
Regarding intention, the world does not disagree; but regarding the meaning, [the world] is indeed given to disagreement. /
Objection: when the suggested meaning has been cognized, the ascertainment of its truth is made through inference alone — [which is] another means of valid cognition — hence it is ultimately inference after all. /
Not so; for even of the expressed meaning, the ascertainment of truth is through inference alone. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'of the object to be conveyed' etc. /
She explains 'of the object to be conveyed' in accordance with the topic in the <s>Locana</s> — 'i.e., of the suggested' etc. /
Objection: how can the ascertainment of non-inferability follow from understanding that [something] is the object of dispute, since dispute is possible even regarding what is to be inferred? — to this she says — 'regarding intention' etc. /
'Regarding intention' — regarding what is intended (<s>vivakṣā</s>). /
'Regarding the meaning' — regarding the meaning that is the object of intention. /
'Is indeed given to disagreement' — /
The meaning is: is indeed given to disagreement regarding truth etc. /
The formal argument: the disputed meaning is not to be inferred, because it is the object of dispute — unlike the speaker's intention, which [can be ascertained] by elimination. /
She introduces the passage beginning with 'just as' etc. — 'objection' etc. /
'Cognized' — /
The meaning is: apprehended from the word after the cognition of the expressed meaning. /
'Of this' — of this cognized suggested meaning. /
'From inference alone' — after this, 'from another means of valid cognition' is also a reading in some manuscripts. /
'Is made' — /
The remainder is: by the cognizers. /
The purport is: the word has validity regarding its own meaning only when accompanied by another corroborating means of valid cognition. /
'Thus' — in the sense of reason. /
'Again' etc. — /
The purport is: even if the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) does not have inferability with respect to the word, it does have inferability with respect to the corroborating other means of valid cognition. /
First comes the apprehension of the meaning from the word; afterwards comes the operation of the corroborating inference regarding it — for the nature of the meaning is the domain of the word, while the truth pertaining to it is the domain of inference — hence inference does not infer what has already been apprehended through words — she resolves this — 'not so' etc. /
And just as, in the domain of the expressed, when the cognition of correctness is sometimes produced through conformity with another means of valid cognition, [the expressed meaning's] being an object of another means of valid cognition does not diminish its being an object of verbal operation — so too for the suggested. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] As they say — '<s>āptavādāvisaṃvādasāmānyādatra cedanumānatā</s>' ('Here, inferability would follow from the general [principle of] non-discordance with authoritative speech'). /
And this much does not make the cognition of the expressed inferential — rather, [the inference pertains to] the additional [fact of] truth belonging to it; the same will apply to the suggested. /
This he states — with 'just as' etc. /
And this is stated by way of concession — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] By the word '<s>api</s>' (even/also) in 'of the expressed too,' the suggested is included. /
'As they say' — /
The remainder is: the author of the <s>Ślokavārttika</s>, in the <s>Vākyādhikaraṇa</s> (section on sentences). /

'<s>vākyārthaś cānya eveti jñātaḥ pūrvataran tataḥ</s>' /
(and that the sentence-meaning is indeed different — this was known earlier, from that) /

'<s>tatra ced āptavādena satyatvam anumīyate</s>' //
(if in that case the truth is inferred through trustworthy testimony) //
