children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She shows the absurdity in not undertaking [the definition] — 'of all' etc.
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>, she concludes — 'thus indeed' etc.
The verse beginning with '<s>vimati</s>' (subject of dispute) is contained within the <s>Vṛtti</s>. /
'Whose true nature is unknown' — this type of poetry, designated as <s>dhvani</s>, has been revealed — this is it. //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'How can there be the inferentiality of the cognition of sentence-meaning here?' — /
'From the non-discrepancy of trustworthy testimony' — is the statement of the reason. /
'Here' — /
the meaning is: in the cognition of sentence-meaning. /
'Inferentiality' (<s>anumānatā</s>) — the state of being an inference (<s>anumiti</s>). /
After '<s>ced</s>' (if), '<s>na</s>' (not) is the remainder. /
Here he states the reason — 'the ascertainment by that much' etc. /
The purport is: from these statements, it is obtained that the truth of the sentence-meaning is to be ascertained only through inference of the form of trustworthy-utterance-hood (<s>āptoktatvarūpānumāna</s>). /
The reading '<s>āptavādāvisaṃvādas sāmānyād anumānataḥ</s>' is seen in many texts. /
Its meaning is thus: the non-discrepancy (<s>avisaṃvāda</s>), i.e., truth (<s>satyatva</s>), of trustworthy testimony (<s>āptavāda</s>) — that is, trustworthy utterance — regarding its own object — i.e., the state of having a true object — /
that is inferable from generality (<s>sāmānya</s>), i.e., knowable through inference from [the mark of] being a trustworthy utterance etc. /
Objection: then let the cognition of the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) also be accepted as merely inferential — to this he says: 'nor' etc. /
Then what — is there no inferential cognition here at all? There is — he says: 'but' etc. /
'Of truth' — /
'the cognition is inferential' is carried over. /
'That will apply to the suggested also' — /
the meaning is: the inferential truth will apply to the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgyārtha</s>) as well. /
The purport is: the suggested meaning is conveyed by the word; its truth, however, is knowable through inference. /
'And this' — /
the meaning is: the inferential truth of the suggested [meaning], as stated by the text beginning with 'just as.' /
'Conceding' — /
the meaning is: treating as existent the purposefulness that in reality does not exist. /
He establishes the purposelessness — 'for not' etc. /
And in the domain of poetry, since the determination of truth or falsehood of the cognitions of suggested meaning is purposeless, the examination of the operation of other means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) there results only in ridicule. /
Therefore it cannot be said that everywhere the cognition of the suggested is merely the cognition of the inferable (<s>liṅgipratīti</s>). /
But the suggestive capacity (<s>vyañjakatva</s>) of words that pertains to the suggested of the inferable type — that is not productive of the usage of '<s>dhvani</s>.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'This has no purpose for us' — they say. /
'In the domain of poetry' — /
'Purposelessness' — /
For the validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) of those sentences [i.e., poetic sentences] is not sought through the medium of conveying true meaning, for the sake of prompting action, like sentences such as the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> injunction etc., because [poetic sentences] culminate in delight (<s>prīti</s>) alone. /
And because delight itself — in the form of extraordinary aesthetic rapture (<s>alaukikacamatkāra</s>) — serves as a component of literary cultivation (<s>vyutpatti</s>). /
And this was stated at length previously. /
'Only for ridicule' — /
This person who is not a <s>sahṛdaya</s> (connoisseur), being harsh-hearted through the approach of mere dry logic, is not capable of grasping the [aesthetic] experience — this is the ridicule. /
Objection: if so, then let it not be the case that wherever there is suggestive capacity there is inferentiality; [but] wherever there is inferentiality, there is suggestive capacity — how can this be denied? Anticipating this, he says: 'but the inferable' etc. /
That suggestive capacity is not the defining mark of <s>dhvani</s>, because it does not operate in the domain beyond the speaker's intention — this is the purport. /
Objection: if the suggestive capacity whose object is the speaker's intention, which shares the same fate as inference alone, is not productive of the usage of <s>dhvani</s>, then for what purpose — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] of those poetry-formed [sentences] — /
'Like <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> injunction etc.' — /
is an illustration by way of dissimilarity. /
'For the sake of prompting action' — for the sake of producing the capacity to prompt activity. /
'Is sought' — is investigated. /
'Delight alone' — /
by the word '<s>mātra</s>' (alone/merely), the prompting of action is excluded. /
[Objection:] whence [comes] the culmination in delight alone? To this he says: 'of delight' etc. /
'Was stated' — /
the purport is: on the occasion of determining the essential nature of <s>rasa</s>. /
He states the nature of the ridicule — 'this person' etc. /
'Dry' — /
the meaning is: harsh-hearted, i.e., lacking in aesthetic sensibility (<s>arasika</s>), through the approach of one dry [method alone], namely logical reasoning (<s>tarka</s>), i.e., inference. /
'The experience' — /
the meaning is: the essential nature of the experience born of poetry. /
'Let it not be' — /
the purport is: because there is deviation [from the pervasion] in cases such as lamplight etc. /
'Thus' — /
the meaning is: this [stated above]. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>, it was stated that 'that suggestive capacity is not productive of the usage of <s>dhvani</s>,' but the reason for the non-productivity was not stated — therefore, showing the intended reason, he says: 'that' etc. /
'That suggestive capacity' — /
the meaning is: the suggestive capacity of the word that pertains to the inferable suggested meaning of the form of the speaker's intention (<s>vaktrabhiprāya</s>). /
'Is not the defining mark of <s>dhvani</s>' — is not the defining characteristic of the domain of <s>dhvani</s>-usage. /
Here he states the reason for the non-pervasion (<s>avyāpti</s>) — 'the intention' etc. /
'Intention' (<s>abhiprāya</s>) means the desire to express (<s>vivakṣā</s>); the object that is beyond that — the suggested meaning in the form of <s>rasa</s>, figures of speech (<s>alaṅkāra</s>), etc. — because [that suggestive capacity] does not operate in that [domain] — the meaning is: because of the absence of operation. /
Where the suggested meaning beyond the speaker's intention — in the domain of <s>dhvani</s>-usage — because of the absence therein of the suggestive capacity pertaining to the inferable suggested meaning of the form of the speaker's intention — hence the non-pervasion — this much [is meant]. /
Anticipating the doubt of contradiction with his own previous statement, he introduces [the text] — 'objection' etc. /
'Sharing the same fate as inference alone' — /
the meaning is: having the same mode, i.e., equal procedure, with inference. /
But rather, the operation of words characterized as suggestive capacity should be accepted even by one who holds the doctrine of the innate word-meaning relation (<s>autpattikaśabdārthasambandha</s>) — [the passage] was presented for this purpose of demonstration. /
That suggestive capacity — sometimes in the form of an inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>), sometimes in another form — is not to be rejected by adherents of any view, [whether they regard] words as denotative or non-denotative — this is the effort made by us. /
Thus indeed, the suggestive capacity is invariably distinct from the types of word-function such as secondary expressive function (<s>guṇavṛtti</s>), denotative capacity (<s>vācakatva</s>), etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Anticipating that 'this was already introduced previously,' he says: 'but rather' etc. /
He determines this very [point] in summary — 'for that indeed' etc. /
For since the suggestive capacity is observed as being supported — sometimes by inference, in the case of the speaker's intention etc.; sometimes by direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), in the case of lamplight etc.; sometimes by the status of being a cause (<s>kāraṇatva</s>), in the case of musical sound etc.; sometimes by denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>), in the <s>vivakṣitānyapara</s> (intended-other-primary) type; and sometimes by the secondary expressive function (<s>guṇavṛtti</s>), in the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (non-intended expressible) type — for this very reason, its form is established as distinct from all of those — thus he says: 'thus indeed' etc. /
Objection: what is the purpose of restricting the form of what is well-known — [namely] the operation of denotation, the secondary expressive function, etc.? /
By the intervention of another set of auxiliary conditions, that very [function takes on] a distinctive [form] — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'previously introduced' — /
the meaning is: presented by the text beginning with 'of such a kind.' /
'This very' — /
the meaning is: what was just stated. /
Explaining the meaning of the text 'thus indeed' etc. together with the text 'for that indeed' etc., she says: 'since' etc. /
The elaboration of 'sometimes' is: 'in the case of the speaker's intention etc.' /
The same should be understood for the subsequent [instances] as well. /
'Sometimes in another form' — the <s>Vṛtti</s>-text is elaborated as: 'by direct perception' etc. /
The elaboration of 'thus indeed' etc. is: 'from those very [sources], from all of them' etc. /
Since the suggestive capacity of the word pertaining to the domain of the speaker's intention etc. [operates] through inference, [i.e.,] through the inferential cognition; /
the suggestive capacity pertaining to lamplight etc. and having a pot etc. as its object [operates] through direct perception, [i.e.,] through the visual cognition of the pot etc.; /
the suggestive capacity pertaining to musical sound etc. and having [<s>rasa</s>] as its object [operates] through the status of being a cause, [i.e.,] through producing <s>rasa</s>; /
the suggestive capacity pertaining to the <s>vivakṣitānyapara</s> type [operates] through denotation; /
and the suggestive capacity pertaining to the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> type [operates while being] supported by the secondary expressive function — [all these] are observed — 'from those very [sources]' is the meaning. /
The purport is: these [functions] merely support the suggestive capacity; they do not have the same form as it. /
'From all of them' — /
the meaning is: from the forms of inference etc. /
'Distinct' etc. — /
By this, the following argument is demonstrated: the suggestive capacity, which is the subject of dispute, is distinct from the types such as inference etc., because it appears as persisting even when those [other types] are absent — whatever appears as persisting when [certain things] are absent is different from those [things], like a thread from flowers. /
'Thus he says' — /
the meaning is: he states that distinctness. /
'Objection' etc. — /
The syntactic connection is: what is the purpose of restricting the form of the well-known [functions such as] the operation of denotation, secondary expressive function, etc.? /
'Through the postulation of suggestive capacity as something additional' — /
is the remainder. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' after '<s>guṇavṛtti</s> etc.,' <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) is included. /
Then how should it be stated? To this he says: 'of that very' etc. /
'Of that very' — of the operation of denotation etc. itself. /
'Another set of auxiliary conditions' — /
the meaning is: of the form of the knowledge of the listener's creative faculty (<s>pratipattṛpratibhā</s>), the speaker's excellence (<s>vaktṛvaiśiṣṭya</s>), etc. /
Even if it [suggestive capacity] falls within that [scope of denotation etc.], when its [distinctness] is forcefully asserted, the illumination of <s>dhvani</s> as a particular [type], for the sake of removing misunderstanding or for the literary cultivation of connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) — what is being done [in that regard] is not to be disregarded at all. /
For the rejection of useful particular definitions cannot be accomplished by a definition that captures merely the general [category]. /
For if that were so, once the definition of mere existence (<s>sattā</s>) were given, the fault of redundancy would arise for all definitions of all existent things. /
Thus indeed — 'the subject of dispute that was always of unknown true nature to the wise' — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Anticipating 'let its form be called that very suggestive capacity,' he says: 'even if it falls within that [scope]' etc. /
The purport is: we do not prohibit the assignment of terminology etc. /
'Misunderstanding' (<s>vipratipatti</s>) — the notion that such a particular [type] does not exist; 'cultivation' (<s>vyutpatti</s>) — the removal of doubt and ignorance. /
'For not' — /
[He means:] the definitions of useful particulars — [the definitions] pertaining to them. /
By the word 'useful' (<s>upayogin</s>), useless [categories] like 'crow's teeth' etc. are excluded. /
'For if so' — /
In the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system, among the categories (<s>padārtha</s>) such as substance (<s>dravya</s>) etc., immediately after [their enumeration], at the beginning, by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>sad anityam</s>' (existent [and] non-eternal) etc., the definition of the three — substance, quality, and action — in the form of possessing existence (<s>sattāvattva</s>) etc. was stated; keeping that in mind, it was stated in the <s>Vṛtti</s>: 'in mere existence' etc. /
She elaborates that — 'the three categories' etc. /
'Mixed with three categories' (<s>tripadārthasaṅkarī</s>) — /
The correct reading is '<s>tripadārthasaṅkīrṇā</s>' (pervading the three categories). /
The meaning is: pervading the three categories of substance etc. /
She explains the intended [meaning] from 'of all' etc. to 'the fault [would arise]' — with 'the <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>' etc. /
Another type of poetry is seen — [that which has] subordinated suggested meaning (<s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>),

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Thus, having established the entire intrinsic form of <s>dhvani</s> together with its divisions and subdivisions, and its form through the divisions of suggestors (<s>vyañjaka</s>) — all this having been taught, the section on the suggestor-thesis (<s>vyañjakavāda</s>) was composed in order to implant in the student's mind, in one continuous exposition, the vital relationship between the suggested and the suggestor — thus, whatever was to be said regarding <s>dhvani</s> has been said. /
Now, however, in order to establish its very soul-nature through the avenue that even this suggested meaning in its subordinated form (<s>guṇībhūta</s>) sanctifies the poet's speech — he says 'another type.' [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She explains the purpose of the statement in the <s>Locana</s> — 'the reason for its being a subject of disagreement.' /

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Now, in order to introduce the subsequent textual composition whose purpose is the exposition of <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion), preceded by a statement of the purport, she summarizes the meaning of the textual composition from the beginning up to this point — 'thus' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: thus, whatever was to be said regarding <s>dhvani</s>, that has been said. /
In the first <s>Uddyota</s>, the general definition of <s>dhvani</s> together with its introduction was stated; in the second, the divisions such as <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (non-intended expressed meaning) etc. and their sub-divisions were demonstrated. /
Thus he says — 'its intrinsic form together with divisions and subdivisions.' /
By 'and that which,' the content of the third <s>Uddyota</s> is stated. /
By 'all this having been taught,' he indicates that the exposition of the nature of <s>dhvani</s> has been fully accomplished by just that much. /
By 'vital' (<s>prāṇabhūta</s>), the absolute necessity of the examination of the suggested-suggestor relationship is demonstrated. /
By 'in one continuous exposition' etc., the suspicion of repetition is dispelled. /
By 'regarding <s>dhvani</s>,' the existence of another subject to be established is suggested. /
Objection: since <s>dhvani</s> has been accepted as the soul of poetry, and since only the exposition of the nature of <s>dhvani</s> which is the soul of poetry has been completed, for what purpose is the exposition of <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> undertaken, given that it is not the soul of poetry? — with this intent she introduces — 'now' etc. /
'This suggested meaning' — the suggested meaning of the type [just] described. /
'Even in subordinated form' — the purport is: not only in its predominant form. /
'Sanctifies' — the meaning is: produces a superabundance of lustre (<s>chāyā</s>). /
'Through this avenue' — the meaning is: through the avenue of the <s>kaimutya</s> (a fortiori) principle. /
'Of that very [<s>dhvani</s>]' — the meaning is: of <s>dhvani</s> alone. /
For it was stated previously — 'And such is this suggestedness' etc. up to 'just as kingship.' /
Since the connection of the suggested with the beauty-preeminence of the expressed meaning has been shown in the <s>kārikā</s> as a cause, not merely the connection with the suggested [matters] — the suggested meaning which has been presented as resembling the charm of a woman, when it is predominant, is called <s>dhvani</s>.

children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Objection: how can the extremely predominant <s>rasa</s> etc. become subordinate, and if they become subordinate, how would there not be lack of charm? Anticipating this doubt, [she shows that] on the contrary, beauty results — she demonstrates this through a well-known illustration: 'and therein' etc.
In the domain of the figure <s>rasavat</s> (possessing <s>rasa</s>) etc.

children.text: evaṃ vastuno rasādeśca guṇībhāvaṃ pradarśyālaṅkārātmano 'pi tṛtīyasya vyaṅgyaprakārasya taṃ darśayati---vyaṅgyālaṅkārasyeti /
children.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the subordination of <s>vastu</s> (content) and <s>rasa</s> etc., she demonstrates that [subordination] of the third type of suggested meaning as well — that of the suggested figure of speech (<s>vyaṅgyālaṅkāra</s>) — 'of the suggested figure of speech' etc.
Of simile (<s>upamā</s>) etc. // 3.4 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Thus' — /
the meaning is: the connection with the suggested constitutes the embellishment (<s>upaskāra</s>) of the expressed. /
'Was established' — /
in the passage 'the suggested is indeed something else' (<s>pratīyamānaṃ punar anyad eva</s>). /
'Was stated' — /
In the intervening [passage] at 'where the meaning or the word,' the suggested [meaning] and the triad of <s>vastu</s> (thing/content) etc. [were discussed]; therein, the varieties of the suggested in the form of <s>vastu</s> that were stated — he shows their subordinate status (<s>guṇabhāva</s>) in sequence — 'therein' etc. /
'In beauty' (<s>lāvaṇya</s>) — /
This is the utterance of a certain young man, pregnant with longing and wonder. /
Here, by the word '<s>sindhu</s>' (ocean/river), fullness is suggested; by the word '<s>utpala</s>' (lotus), playful side-glances are suggested; by the word '<s>śaśin</s>' (moon), the face is suggested; by the word '<s>dviradakumbhataṭī</s>' (surface of an elephant's frontal globe), the pair of breasts is suggested; by the word '<s>kadalikāṇḍa</s>' (plantain stem), the pair of thighs is suggested; by the word '<s>mṛṇāladaṇḍa</s>' (lotus stalk), the pair of arms is suggested. /
And therein, since their primary meanings are entirely impossible [in the context], by the principle stated with the word '<s>andha</s>' (blind), the expressed meaning is eclipsed (<s>tiraskṛtavācyatva</s>). /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The expressed meaning here is not what is intended [as primary], but rather it becomes the locus of a particular excellence produced by its connection with the suggested — thus she says: 'embellishment of the expressed.' /
When the subordinate status of the suggested is to be stated, in order to dispel the doubt of incongruity in the <s>Vṛtti</s>'s demonstration of the subordinate status of <s>vastu</s> etc., she says: 'and the suggested is the triad of <s>vastu</s> etc.' /
'Was stated' is the remainder. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>: 'in beauty' — /
'Here' — in this region. /
'Quite another' — an unprecedented one. /
'Who is this ocean of beauty (<s>lāvaṇyasindhu</s>)?' — a river of beauty. /
'Where' — in whom. /
'With the moon' — with the full moon. /
'They merge' — they become commingled. /
'Rises up' — becomes elevated. /
'<s>Dvirada</s>' — elephant. /
'Where' etc. — /
'they exist' is the remainder. /
'<s>Kadalikāṇḍa</s>' — plantain stem. /
Intending to demonstrate in sequence everything stated in the <s>Vṛtti</s> beginning with 'of the suggested that is merely <s>vastu</s> (content),' he first prepares the ground in the <s>Locana</s> — 'longing' etc. /
The sequence is: first wonder, then longing; not wishing to specify that [order], he says 'pregnant with longing and wonder.' /
'Of a certain' — /
The non-specification of the particular [person] is because it is not relevant. /
'By the word <s>sindhu</s>' — /
The syntactic construction is: by the word '<s>sindhu</s>,' fullness is suggested, and so on. /
'Fullness' — /
the meaning is: qualified by completeness. /
'Lotuses' — in accordance with the plural ending, she says: 'playful side-glances' (<s>kaṭākṣacchaṭā</s>). /
'Is suggested' — the connection here is by way of transposition. /
'Therein' — /
the meaning is: when the stated <s>vastu-dhvani</s> (content-suggestion) is present. /
'Of these' — of the words '<s>sindhu</s>,' '<s>utpala</s>,' etc. /
The connection is with 'the eclipsing of the expressed meaning.' /
Here he states the reason — 'of the own meaning' etc. /
'Of the own meaning' — of river, blue lotus, etc. /
Even from words whose expressed meaning is not eclipsed, when the suggested [meaning] is apprehended, sometimes by the predominance of the expressed — [<s>Locana</s>:] and that apprehended particular meaning, in the expressed portion that is embraced by the utterance 'quite another indeed, who is this [beauty]?' — produces a luster of charm, because the expressed [meaning] itself, through the emergence of its own essence, makes the submerged class of suggested meanings appear as beautiful. /
And the beauty [arises] because — through the form of the aggregate obtained from the repose in that most felicitous single locus, which is the heroine's form, of the class of entities such as <s>kuvalaya</s> (day-lotus) etc. that are the essence of the entire world and whose conjunction is most improbable — with the precedence of the attainment of being a <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) for wonder, and through the emergence of the expressed form that is so variegated, being embellished by the suggested meaning — [it serves] as a <s>vibhāva</s> for longing etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Blind' — /
the meaning is: by the principle stated in the explanation of the word '<s>andha</s>' in the passage '<s>niḥśvāsāndha ivādarśaḥ</s>' (like a mirror blinded by breath). /
'Even though apprehended' — by the word '<s>api</s>' (even), she shows that the attainment of subordinate status, contrary to the naturally obtained principal status, is contradictory. /
'That particular meaning' — the class of suggested meanings that have been explained. /
'Quite another indeed' etc. — /
the meaning is: [the suggested meanings are] embraced in a general way by the two utterances 'quite another indeed' and 'who is this.' /
'In the expressed portion' — in the sentence-meaning constituted by the expressed meanings of the words '<s>sindhu</s>,' '<s>utpala</s>,' etc. — [the meanings] river, blue lotus, etc. /
'Luster of charm' — the beauty that is the cause of the perception of poetic charm. /
'Produces' — creates. /
By this, the subordinate status of the suggested is demonstrated. /
Here she validates [this] by the experience of the connoisseur (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) itself — 'of the expressed itself' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: because of the expressed itself appearing as beautiful. /
Here she shows the qualifying phrase pregnant with the reason — 'of its own essence' etc. /
'Of its own' — of the expressed; whose essence is its own nature — its emergence, i.e., standing forth prominently — characterized by that. /
Thus, the submerged (<s>nimajjita</s>) class of suggested meanings previously mentioned — of that characterized by it. /
The submergence of the class of suggested meanings is the low position [attained] through being [merely] beheld through the face of the expressed. /
But how can such an expressed [meaning] be beautiful? To this she says: 'and the beauty' etc. /
'Of this' — of this expressed [meaning]. /
In the verse, she first explains the beauty of the expressed through [its serving as] a <s>vibhāva</s> of wonder predominantly — 'of the improbable' etc. /
'Whose conjunction is being treated as most improbable' — those whose conjunction is coming to be regarded as impossible. /
And those entities such as <s>kuvalaya</s> (day-lotus) etc. that are the essence of the entire world — of the class of those. /
'That most felicitous single locus' — the form of the heroine; therein, the repose, i.e., the state of being situated in close embrace — the aggregate-form, i.e., the compactness, obtained thereby — by reason of the state of that. /
'The precedence of the attainment of the status of being a <s>vibhāva</s> for wonder' — 'with precedence' is also a reading. /
She states the reason for the attainment of being a <s>vibhāva</s> for longing etc. — 'by the suggested' etc. /
'Embellished by the suggested meaning' — embellished by the class of suggested meanings such as side-glances, face, etc. that were stated. /
'So variegated' — having attained variety, i.e., distinction, through the embellishment by the suggested meaning. /
Objection: if the status of being a <s>vibhāva</s> for longing etc. belongs only to [the expressed] as embellished by the suggested meaning and not by its own nature, then the primacy of the suggested would follow, since it alone is the productive factor in the attainment of <s>vibhāva</s>-status — to this she says: 'through the emergence of the expressed form.' /
The meaning is: by reason of the emergence of the expressed meaning's own nature — [the nature of] <s>kuvalaya</s>, moon, etc. /
With respect to poetic charm, when subordination obtains, there is the category of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (suggestion-as-subordinate), as exemplified: '<s>anurāgavatī sandhyā</s>' (the twilight is full of color/passion) — and such examples. /
The subordination of that very [suggestion] is by its being illuminated through [the poet's] own speech, as exemplified: '<s>saṅketakālamanasam</s>' (absent-minded at the time of the tryst) — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'For this very reason' — although the expressed has primacy [here], nevertheless in <s>rasa-dhvani</s>, even that [expressed meaning] becomes subordinate — thus all [cases] should be considered under the category of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>. /
For this very reason, the statement that '<s>dhvani</s> alone is the soul [of poetry]' has been proclaimed many times. /
Others, however — the connoisseurs [say] — this is an utterance concerning a river made beautiful by the flowing beauty of young women who have descended for water-sport; and there too, the same method of construal as stated [above] applies. /
Or [it may concern] a young woman who has descended for bathing in the vicinity of a river. /
In all cases, since [the utterance] operates primarily through the medium of wonder, the suggested [meaning] is subordinate. /
'Was exemplified' — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The purport is: for the perception of the suggested [meanings] such as side-glances, face, etc. in the form of the expressed <s>kuvalaya</s>, moon, etc. is indeed the cause for generating longing etc. /
'For this very reason' — /
the meaning is: precisely because of the subordination of the suggested in the manner described. /
'This much' — the meaning is: the meaning extending up to the attainment of the status of being a <s>vibhāva</s> for longing etc. preceded by the attainment of the status of being a <s>vibhāva</s> for wonder. /
But immediately after, its subordination alone [obtains] — thus she says: 'nevertheless' etc. /
'In <s>rasa-dhvani</s>' — in the <s>dhvani</s> of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc. /
'Even of that' — even of the expressed. /
Not only here [is this the case] — she says: 'thus of all' etc. /
Here she states the corroboration — 'for this very reason' etc. /
The purport is: if in the subcategory of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, the expressed meaning alone had primacy, then the proclamation everywhere that '<s>dhvani</s> is the soul of poetry' would be incongruous. /
Showing that [the verse about] this [utterance] should, by following propriety and the mode of an independent verse rather than one found in a continuous composition, be construed as describing a particular described [object] — she states an alternative interpretation: 'others, however' etc. /
'A river made beautiful by the flowing beauty' — by this, '<s>lāvaṇyasindhu</s>' (ocean of beauty) is elaborated: the analysis is either 'a river consisting of beauty' or 'a river made beautiful by beauty'; [and thus] the word '<s>sindhu</s>' is not an eclipsed-expressed suggestor, but [has its primary meaning] — this is the purport. /
But for the words '<s>utpala</s>' etc., the same suggestive sequence as stated before [applies] — thus she says: 'and there too' etc. /
In this interpretation, the attribution of the felicity of being brought together in a single locus [the heroine's form] for <s>kuvalaya</s> etc. does not apply harmoniously — subtly indicating this lack of congruence, she states another interpretation: 'or' etc. /
'In the vicinity of a river' — /
Because the river is pervaded by the unsurpassable flood of beauty belonging to the young woman, the river is 'consisting of beauty' — from this meaning, in this interpretation too the word '<s>sindhu</s>' has its primary meaning; and the previously stated fault does not arise, because it is the young woman alone who is being described — this is the purport. /
In all three interpretations, the status of being the subcategory of <s>vivakṣitaguṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (intended-subordinate-suggestion) is unobstructed — thus she says: 'in all cases' etc. /
'Was determined' — /
the meaning is: just as the subordination of the suggested hero's-narrative was shown here, so it has been demonstrated. /
Objection: since the words '<s>sandhyā</s>' etc. have non-eclipsed expressed meanings and convey meanings such as the heroine etc., while the word '<s>anurāga</s>' (passion/color), well-known as denoting love, is to be explained through <s>jahatsvārthalakṣaṇā</s> (indication abandoning its own meaning) for the primary meaning of redness — how then can there be non-eclipsed expressedness? Wishing to resolve this doubt, [she explains that] rather, that word, through <s>yogarūḍhi</s> (conventional restriction of an etymological compound), denotes redness itself, not the meaning of the form of love — etc. /
The subordination of the suggested in the form of <s>rasa</s> etc. was shown in the figure <s>rasavat</s> (possessing <s>rasa</s>); and therein, their subordination is relative to the governing sentence, like a servant who has followed [his master] when the master sets out on a journey. /
Regarding the subordination of the suggested figure of speech, the domain is <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) etc. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] And this was determined in the first <s>Uddyota</s> itself. And the word '<s>anurāga</s>' is used with respect to longing through the indication characterized by being colored by that — like the word '<s>lāvaṇya</s>' (beauty/saltiness) — with this intention, the non-eclipsed expressedness was stated. /
'Of that very' — /
of <s>vastu</s> (content) alone. /
'<s>Rasa</s> etc.' — /
by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), <s>bhāvas</s> etc. [are included]; by the word '<s>rasavat</s>,' the figures such as <s>preyas</s> (the charming) etc. are indicated.

children.translated_text: Objection: even when <s>rasa</s> etc. is primary, could not its subordination occur by the force of the poet's intention? — To this she says — 'in subordination' etc.
'A well-known example' —
The meaning is: an example well-known for its beauty.

children.text: na hi rājño vivāhapravṛttamṛtyānuyāyitvamasundaraṃ bhāti, pratyuta bhṛtyotkarṣaviśeṣo 'pi rājotkarṣātiśayāyaiva kalpiṣyata iti cārutvameva puṣṇātīti bhāvaḥ // 3.4 //
children.translated_text: For the death-following nature of a king engaged in marriage does not appear ugly; rather, even the special excellence of the servant is conceived only for the purpose of the king's surpassing excellence — thus, it nourishes beauty alone — this is the purport. // 3.4 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] Having thus demonstrated the subordinate status (<s>guṇabhāva</s>) of all three types, in order to show that this [category] pervades many instances, he says — 'likewise' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] But she shows that through conventional indication (<s>nirūḍhalakṣaṇā</s>), the non-obscured expressibility is well-established — 'of the word <s>anurāga</s>' etc. /
'In desire, in love' — /
'That' — /
The meaning is: by the indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) whose cause is the capacity to color objects — i.e., the thing denoted by that word, the coloring of objects by it. /
'Like the word <s>lāvaṇya</s>' — /
The meaning is: just as the word '<s>lāvaṇya</s>' (charm/salt) in the sense of a particular type of beauty. /
It should be understood that the meaning in the form of love is suggested alone. /
'By the word <s>rasavat</s>' — /
The meaning is: by the word '<s>rasavat</s>' in the context where the <s>rasavat alaṅkāra</s> was demonstrated. /
And in the <s>vṛtti</s> there is also the reading: 'the domain of <s>rasavad-alaṅkāra</s> was previously demonstrated.' /
With the intention that the fruit of demonstrating the subordinate status of <s>rasa</s> etc. preceded by showing examples is the removal of the doubt of its impossibility, she raises the doubt — 'but exceedingly' etc. /
Since even the expressed has relative primacy, therefore 'exceedingly' is said. /
'How' — /
The purport is: the co-existence of primacy and subordination in a single [entity] is indeed contradictory.

'Bringing pleasure' — by this, this very type should be applied to those; thus —
Poetic compositions whose words are lucid and profound, bringing pleasure,

tena gaṅgāsnānaharicaraṇārādhanādyupāyaśatalabdhāyā lakṣmyāścandrodayapānagoṣṭhyupabhogalakṣaṇaṃ mukhyeṃ phalamiti trailokyasārabhūtatā bālapriyā ityatra tatprakārasya cārutvehetutvaṃ darśitamityāśayenāha--cārutvaheturityādi /
tatra tathāvidhe kāvyabandhe /
sahṛdayatvapratiṣṭālābhaścaitatprakārayojanakauśalaśālitānibandhana eveti tadarthibhistadviṣaye mahāprayatna ādheya iti darśayituṃ sumedhasetyuktamityāha--yastvetamityādi /

children.translated_text: [The lemma:] '<s>alīka</s>' (false) etc.

children.text: ayaṃ na sahṛdayaḥ kintvalīkasahṛdayabhāvanayā asatyasya sahṛdayatvastha bhāvanayā rasāsvādavaivaśyaṃ manasaḥ prakaṭayituṃ mukulitalocana āste, paśyatāsya vipralambhakabhāvamiti sahṛdayagoṣṭhīṣuparihāsapātraṃ syādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: This person is not a [true] connoisseur (<s>sahṛdaya</s>); rather, through the pretense of false connoisseurship — the assumption of unreal connoisseurship — sitting with half-closed eyes to display the involuntariness of the mind in tasting <s>rasa</s> — 'look at this one's deceptive behavior' — thus he would be an object of ridicule in gatherings of connoisseurs — this is the meaning.
<s>Lakṣmī</s> is the daughter, <s>Hari</s> the son-in-law, his wife is <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
and <s>Amṛta</s> and <s>Mṛgāṅka</s> (Moon) are the two sons — oh, what a family the great Ocean has! //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] And those poetic compositions which, though unlimited in their forms, manifest as delightful through such meaning, bringing pleasure to the discerning — in all of them, this type called <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggested meaning) should be applied. /
For example: — /
'<s>lacchī duhidā jāmāuo harī taṃsa dhariṇiā gaṅgā</s>' — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Clear — by virtue of possessing the quality of lucidity (<s>prasāda</s>); and profound — by virtue of suggesting meaning; whose words are such — [describing] those poetic compositions. /
'Bringing pleasure' — this is the cause of beauty. /
Therein, this very type — this is the purport. /
'The wise person' — /
The purport is: one who is unable to apply this type therein would be an object of ridicule, with eyes half-closed in the pretense of being a false connoisseur — this is the purport. /
<s>Lakṣmī</s> (Prosperity) — the ground of all people's desire — is the daughter. /
The son-in-law is <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), who is constantly engaged in bestowing all enjoyments and liberation. /
And the wife is <s>Gaṅgā</s>, for whom the means toward all desirable things is unhinderd. /
And the two sons are <s>Amṛta</s> (nectar) and <s>Mṛgāṅka</s> (the Moon); '<s>Amṛta</s>' here means wine (<s>vāruṇī</s>). /
Therefore, of <s>Lakṣmī</s> obtained through hundreds of means such as bathing in <s>Gaṅgā</s>, worship at the feet of <s>Hari</s>, etc., the primary fruit is enjoyment in the form of drinking parties at moonrise — hence the Ocean alone is the essence of the three worlds — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] with the intention that the beauty-causing nature of that type has been shown here, she says — 'the cause of beauty' etc. /
'Therein' — in such a poetic composition. /
The attainment of the reputation of being a connoisseur (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) depends on the skill of applying this type — therefore, those who desire it should make great effort in that domain — intending to show this, she says 'the wise person' — 'one who' etc.

children.translated_text: 'By that' —
The meaning is: by the stated collection of meanings.
'Experiences subordination through bathing in <s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc. — up to this point, this is the meaning:

children.text: yasyāṃ snānādyadārādhanāditaśca yā labhyate sā gaṅgāsya gṛhiṇyeva, sa harirasya jāmātaiva, sā lakṣmīrasyātmajaiva, labdhāyā āmiamiaṅkā a suā aho kuḍumbaṃ mahoahiṇo //
children.translated_text: She from whose bathing, worship etc. is obtained — that <s>Gaṅgā</s> is verily his wife; that <s>Hari</s> is verily his son-in-law; that <s>Lakṣmī</s> is verily his daughter; and the obtained <s>Amṛta</s> and <s>Mṛgāṅka</s> are his sons — oh, what a family the great Ocean has! //

Thus is the <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit rendering). /
Showing the suggested meaning-content of the words contained therein, she states the construction — '<s>Lakṣmī</s>' etc. /
'All' etc. /
'The entirety' etc. /
'Of whom' etc. — these are statements of the suggested meaning of each respective word. /
'<s>Amṛta</s>' — /
The meaning is: the referent of the word '<s>amṛta</s>.' /
'Wine (<s>vāruṇī</s>)' — /
Not nectar (<s>pīyūṣa</s>), because unlike moonrise, it is not common to all people — this is the purport.
This group of expressed figures of speech (<s>vācyālaṅkāra</s>), when accompanied by a suggested element,

children.text: prāyeṇaiva parāṃ chāyāṃ bibhral lakṣye nirīkṣyate // DhvK_3.36 //
children.translated_text: is almost always seen in examples bearing a surpassing lustre. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.36 //
This group of expressed figures of speech, when accompanied by a suggested element,
is almost always seen in examples bearing a surpassing lustre. // 36 //

children.text: vācyālaṅkāravargo 'yaṃ vyaṅgyāṃśasyālaṅkārasya vastumātrasya vā yathoyogamanugame sati cchāyātiśayaṃ vibhrallakṣaṇakārairekadeśena darśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] This group of expressed figures of speech — when accompanied, as appropriate, by the suggested element of another figure or of mere subject-matter — bearing a surpassing lustre, has been demonstrated in part by the writers on <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (poetic science).

children.text: sa tu tathārūpaḥ prāyeṇa sarva eva parīkṣyamāṇo lakṣye nirīkṣyate /
children.translated_text: But that [group], being of such a form, is almost always observed in examples when carefully examined.

For thus — other figures besides <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) and <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) etc. are also mostly seen to be in contact with another suggested figure or another subject-matter.

children.text: locanam pratīyamānā satī aho kuṭumbaṃ mahodadherityahośabdācca guṇībhāvamanubhavati // 3.5 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] Being cognized, 'oh, what a family the great Ocean has!' — and from the exclamatory word '<s>aho</s>' it also experiences subordination. // 3.5 //

children.text:
evaṃ niralaṅkāreṣūttānatāyāṃ tucchatayaiva bhāsamānamamunāntaḥsāreṇa kāvyaṃ pavitrīkṛtamityuktvālaṅkārasyāpyanenaiva ramyataratvamiti darśayati--vācyeti /
aṃśatvaṃ guṇamātratvam /

children.translated_text: 'In part' —
By this, the <s>ekadeśavivartirūpaka</s> (partial-transformation metaphor) is demonstrated.

children.text: bālapriyā lakṣmyāssampadrūpāyā upabhogābhāve cālabdhakalpatvāccandrodayakāle vāruṇyupabhogo hi mukhyaṃ phalaṃ, sa candrassā vāruṇī cāsya putrabhāvameva bhajata iti mahodadhireva trailokyasāra itīyānartho 'tra dhvananavyāpārādavagamyate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Since <s>Lakṣmī</s>, being in the form of wealth, without enjoyment would be as if unattained — and the primary fruit is the enjoyment of wine at the time of moonrise — that Moon and that wine assume the very status of being his sons — therefore the great Ocean alone is the essence of the three worlds — this meaning here is apprehended through the operation of suggestion (<s>dhvananvyāpāra</s>).

children.text: sa cāvagatassannaho kuṭumbamiti śabdaspṛṣṭatayā guṇībhāvamavalambate yataḥ, tadvyaṅgyārthajātopaskṛta eva vācyārtho vismayavibhāvatāṃ prāpnoti camatkārātiśayañca vidhatta iti // 3.4//
children.translated_text: And that [meaning], having been apprehended, assumes subordinate status through being touched by the word '<s>aho kuṭumbam</s>' ('oh, what a family!'); because the expressed meaning, embellished by that collection of suggested meanings, attains the status of an excitant of wonder (<s>vismayavibhāva</s>) and produces surpassing aesthetic delight (<s>camatkāra</s>). // 3.4 //

Having thus stated that in [compositions] without [expressed] figures, what appears as mere shallowness in its obviousness is purified by this inner substance [of suggestion] as poetry — he shows that even figures of speech attain greater beauty through this alone — 'expressed' etc. /
'Being a component' (<s>aṃśatva</s>) means being merely a subordinate element (<s>guṇamātratva</s>).

children.translated_text: The meaning is: marked by that propriety which resides in the heart of the poet.

children.text: karoti cettadā nāstyevāsau prakāra iti sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If he does [otherwise], then that type simply does not exist' — this is the connection.
Would not bring excellence.

children.text: bhāmahenāpyatiśayoktilakṣaṇe yaduktam--- locanam dūrvākāṇḍaviḍambakaśca nibiḍo yatpāṇḍimā gaṇḍayoḥ kṛṇṇe yūni sayauvanāsu vanitāsveṣaiva veṣasthitiḥ //
children.translated_text: What was also stated by <s>Bhāmaha</s> in the definition of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'The pallor of whose cheeks closely rivals the shoot of <s>dūrvā</s> grass — in the dark-complexioned youth, among women in the bloom of youth, this very condition of appearance [prevails].' //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Having stated the purport of the previous <s>kārikā</s>, she introduces the next <s>kārikā</s> — 'thus' etc. /
'In those without figures' — /
The purport is: in the stated example beginning with '<s>Lakṣmī</s>' etc., no figure is clearly apprehended. /
'In the obviousness' — /
The meaning is: in the cognition at first glance. /
'Appearing as poetry' — this is the connection. /
'Appearing' is also a reading. /
'By this' — by the subordinated suggested meaning. /
'Having inner substance' — /
Inner substantiality even in subordination is the natural state of possessing excellence, according to the maxim of the gold-dust during children's play. /
'Of figures' — the singular is generic. /
'By this alone' — /
The meaning is: by the subordinated suggested meaning alone. /
'Greater beauty' — /
Since beauty already exists by virtue of being a figure, the comparative suffix (<s>tarap</s>) [is used]. /
For this very reason, 'surpassing lustre' was said — and [the expression] 'surpassing lustre' [was used]. /
Regarding 'accompaniment by the suggested element' — she says that the component-status (<s>aṃśatva</s>) of the suggested with respect to the expressed is subordination itself — 'component-status means merely being a subordinate element.' /
'By this is demonstrated' — /
By the maxim that grasping a part of a name is grasping the whole name, the word '<s>ekadeśa</s>' (part) refers to the <s>ekadeśavivartirūpaka</s> (partial-transformation metaphor) — this is the purport. /
For, first of all, the pregnancy with <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) can be accomplished in all figures. /
And that has indeed been accomplished by great poets; it nourishes some supreme beauty of poetry. How indeed [can it fail, since] <s>atiśayayogitā</s> (association with excellence), when produced with propriety regarding its own domain, [produces excellence] in poetry — [<s>Locana</s>:] The meaning of this is: in <s>ekadeśavivartirūpaka</s> — '<s>rājasaṃsairavījyanta śaradaiva saronṛpāḥ</s>' ('The kings of the lakes were fanned by autumn itself as their royal attendant') — therein, what is cognized as the <s>cāmara</s>-bearing nature of the swans — that, in the expressed meaning '<s>nṛpāḥ</s>' (kings), having attained subordinate status, was demonstrated only to that extent by the writers on <s>alaṅkāra</s> — and through that very door, this type [of subordinated suggestion] is indicated — this is the meaning. /
But others explained '<s>ekadeśena</s>' (in part) as merely 'through the variety of a portion of the expressed' — thus leaving [the matter] unexplicated. /
The suggested meaning, [these compositions] that touch another figure or another subject-matter — those that embrace [them] for their own embellishment — they are 'such.' /
'By great poets' — /
By <s>Kālidāsa</s> etc. /
Regarding the statement that it nourishes the beauty of poetry — she states the reason — 'how indeed' etc. /
'Indeed' — in the sense of reason. /
'<s>Atiśayayogitā</s>' — how could it not bring excellence? — the meaning is: there is no such type of poetry that fails to attain excellence [when this is present]. /
Is it not so in every case? — she says — 'in its own domain' etc. /
'In its own domain' — in the domain of one's own hyperbole. /
'Propriety' — characterized by plausibility. /
'By that, present in the heart' —

children.text: atra hi bhagavato manmathavapuṣaḥ saubhāgyaviṣayaḥ sambhāvyata evāyamatiśaya iti tatkāvye lokottaraiva śobhollasati /
children.translated_text: For here, regarding the body of the blessed <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), this excellence in the domain of beauty is quite conceivable — thus in such poetry, a transcendent beauty shines forth.
But through impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>), beauty would dissolve entirely.
For example — 'Space was created small, without even considering, by <s>Vedhas</s> (the Creator);
such was to be the swelling of your breasts, of this very nature.' //

children.translated_text: Even granting this, what follows from it in the present context? — to this she says: 'and not' etc.
'How can it have the status of being suggested?' —

children.text: vyaṅgyaṃ hi vācyāta pṛthaktayā tatpratītyuttaraṃ śabdātpratīyate samānyantvanyathā gaurityādiśabdena saiṣā sarvaiva vakroktiranayārtho vibhāvyate /
children.translated_text: For the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) is cognized from words as separate from the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>), subsequent to the cognition of it; but the universal is not [cognized] otherwise [i.e., not separately] — as with the word '<s>gaḥ</s>' (cow) etc.: 'This very <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression) is all [of alaṅkāra]; through it, meaning is manifested.',
'The poet must make effort in this; what <s>alaṅkāra</s> exists without it?' //

Thus. /
Objection: it was stated that <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) exists latently within all <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures) in the form of the suggested — how [is that consistent]? Since <s>Bhāmaha</s> declared <s>atiśayokti</s> to be the common form of all <s>alaṅkāras</s>. /
And the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) does not shine forth as distinct from and subsequent to the particular cognition arising from words — so how can it have the status of being suggested? — thus objecting, he says: 'by <s>Bhāmaha</s>' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She gives the example endowed with propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) — 'that which' etc. /
This verse has been explained. /
'Of the blessed' — this is the reason for 'of the body of <s>Manmatha</s>' and for 'it is quite conceivable.' /
'Is quite conceivable' — /
The meaning is: 'it could be so' — being conceivable by perceivers. /
The word '<s>eva</s>' (indeed) excludes inconceivability. /
'This excellence in the domain of beauty' — /
The meaning is: the excellence of qualities such as beauty, which is understood through the description of the particular state of the women. /
'In such poetry' — in poetry of that kind. /
Intending to clarify this very point by way of a counter-example, he says — 'through impropriety' etc. /
'Would dissolve' — /
The purport is: because the splendor of beauty belongs to poetry [only when propriety is maintained]. /
'Small' — /
'Was created small' — /
The purport is: because there is insufficient space for the breasts. /
'This' — /
The meaning is: that which is being seen. /
'Of this nature' — /
The meaning is: impossible to describe. /
Here, through the statement that even space — which by nature is unlimited expanse — was made small, a greatness of the breasts even exceeding that is suggested — thus <s>atiśayokti</s> is the suggested meaning; however, since such greatness of breasts is inconceivable, this [verse] possesses impropriety and therefore is incapable of producing poetic excellence — this is the purport. /
She introduces the passage beginning with 'by <s>Bhāmaha</s> too' [by asking] what is its purpose in the present context — 'objection' etc. /
'What was stated' — /
The purport is: by the passage stating that the embedding of <s>atiśayokti</s> within all <s>alaṅkāras</s> is possible. /
'How' — /
The meaning is: it is inappropriate. /
'Why?' — to this she says: 'since' etc. /
'<s>Bhāmaha</s>' — the teacher named <s>Bhāmaha</s>, preeminent among the definers of <s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
'Declared' — /
The meaning is: he stated by the passage 'This very <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression) is all [of alaṅkāra].' /
'All <s>vakrokti</s>' — every <s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
'This very one' — that which has been called <s>atiśayokti</s> is that itself — thus the particularity of each <s>alaṅkāra</s> and <s>atiśayokti's</s> being their common form — this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: For example, in '<s>prabhāmahatyā śikhayeva dīpaḥ</s>' (like a lamp with the flame of radiant glory) and similar cases, the semblance of <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination figure) is clearly observed.
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Desired in illustration' —
Example — 'This <s>Bhāsvān</s> (the Sun), of diminished radiance, wishes to go toward setting;
rise is for the sake of fall' — thus awakening people of fortune. //

Thus. /
Regarding that, <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is the <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure of speech) that presides over [all other figures]; through the power of the poet's creative intuition, there is a conjunction of excellence of beauty in that [figure], while for the other— [this is explained in] the <s>Locana</s>. What <s>Bhāmaha</s> also stated — the meaning to be understood there is precisely this, though the connection is remote. /
What was that statement? — 'This very one' (<s>saiṣā</s>). /
That <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) which has been identified is itself all <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression) — every variety of <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure of speech). /
This is because of the statement: 'The oblique expression of word and meaning is regarded as the ornamentation of speech.' /
For the obliqueness of the word and the obliqueness of the meaning — that is, the state of abiding in a form that transcends the ordinary — this itself is the ornamental nature of the <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure), and transcendence of the ordinary is itself <s>atiśaya</s> (excellence); therefore <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is the universal characteristic of all <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures). /
Thus — through this <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), meaning, even though it has been rendered stale by the enjoyment of all people, is made to appear with novelty. /
Likewise, a pleasure-garden and such things are elevated to the status of <s>vibhāva</s> (aesthetic stimulus). /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: Because the universal and the particular appear simultaneously without differentiation — in response to the cognition of the particular <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure), the appearance of their separateness is pervasive; and when the pervasive [universal] is negated, it also negates the <s>vyaṅgyatva</s> (suggestive quality) that is its own pervaded [particular]; therefore the assertion of its <s>vyaṅgyatva</s> (suggestive quality) is unjustified because it contradicts <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s statement — this is the meaning. /
Because of the intervening distance [between the passages], he shows the connection — 'by <s>Bhāmaha</s> also' and so forth. /
That which was stated means: that which was stated by <s>Bhāmaha</s>. /
He glosses the verse — 'that which' and so forth. /
'Identified' means: identified by the passage beginning with 'Whatever speech is occasioned by a cause' — this is the meaning. /
'Oblique' means: distinguished by the obliqueness of its own nature, which will be described. /
Since <s>ukti</s> (expression) means the meaning being expressed, he glosses it with that intention — 'that which' and so forth. /
'Identified' means: identified by the passage beginning with 'Whatever speech is occasioned by a cause' — this is the meaning. /
'Oblique' means: distinguished by the obliqueness of its own nature, which will be described. /
Since <s>ukti</s> (expression) means the meaning being expressed, he glosses it with that intention — 'variety of <s>alaṅkāra</s>' (figure). /
This means: a particular <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) — this is the meaning. /
To establish that the word <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression) has the sense of <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure), he corroborates it with <s>Bhāmaha</s>'s own statement — 'oblique' and so on. /
'Ornamentation' — there is also the reading '<s>alaṅkriyā</s>' (act of adorning). /
With the intention that the word 'oblique' here, its literal meaning being impossible, is used figuratively by virtue of similarity to mean 'possessing an alternative form that transgresses the well-known path,' he says — 'of the ordinary' and so forth. /
'In a form transcending the ordinary' means: in a form distinguished from the ordinary — one that departs from what is well-known in common parlance, treatises, epics, and the like. /
And that form is characterized by the attainment of suitability for the suggestion of the intended <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). /
'This very one' means: it is precisely this form, transcending the ordinary, which has the nature of suitability for the suggestion of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) — this is the meaning. /
'The ornamental nature of the <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure)' means: the figurative status of <s>upamā</s> (simile) and other [figures]. /
And thus the word <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression) has the sense of <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) — this is the import. /
Even so, how does it have the nature of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole)? To this he says — 'transcendence of the ordinary is itself <s>atiśaya</s> (excellence).' /
He states the conclusion — 'therefore.' /
He elaborates the portion beginning with 'through this' — 'thus' and so forth. /
'Thus' means: what is about to be stated serves as proof for what has been said — this is the meaning. /
'Of all' — 'rendered stale' means: brought to a state of being unsavored. /
The explanation of the meaning of the word 'vi-' is 'with novelty.' /
This means: with a quality of ever-new distinctiveness — this is the meaning. /
'Is made to appear' means: is brought into being. /
As they say: 'It is the nature of things that they are not savored as they truly are directly, but become so when they enter the domain of good poets' speech.' /
And he shows that something else is also intended by the pair of meanings conveyed by 'is made to appear' — 'likewise' and so forth. /
'A pleasure-garden and such' — but this is merely <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament) [not the essential life of poetry]; therefore, by virtue of being fit for incorporation into the body of all <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures), through figurative identification (<s>abhedopacāra</s>), that alone has the form of all <s>alaṅkāras</s> — this very meaning is to be understood. /
And that [<s>atiśayokti</s>'s] intermixture with other <s>alaṅkāras</s> — [this is explained in] the <s>Locana</s>: and it is especially made to appear, is rendered full of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) — thus much was stated by him; regarding what that meaning is there, he says: through figurative identification (<s>abhedopacāra</s>), that alone has the form of all <s>alaṅkāras</s>. /
He states the ground for the figurative usage — 'of all <s>alaṅkāras</s>' and so forth. /
He states the purpose of the figurative usage — through [the passage] beginning with '<s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole)' up to 'merely <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament).' /
The cancellation of the primary meaning is also shown right here, through [the passage] beginning with 'through the power of the poet's creative intuition.' /
This is the import: If <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) has the nature of a universal present in all <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures), then since that [universality] culminates in complete identity, no <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) distinct from it would be perceived, and consequently the poet's creative intuition would not need to be taken into account with respect to it. /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'meaning' is to be supplied from context. /
'Is especially made to appear' — the elaboration of this is: 'of <s>rasa</s>' and so forth. /
'Thus' and so forth is a summary statement of the meaning. /
'So much' indicates non-discrepancy. /
'There' means: in that statement — this is the meaning. /
'That' means: what is intended by the word 'this' in the phrase 'this very one' — this is the meaning. /
For in figurative usage, three things must necessarily be stated: the ground, the purpose, and the cancellation of the primary meaning. /
Regarding that, [the passage] beginning with 'of all <s>alaṅkāras</s>' presents the ground, which has the character of a relation to the referent — he says 'figurative usage' and so forth. /
'He states the ground' — and thus the similarity to the primary meaning, in the form of fitness for incorporation into the body of all <s>alaṅkāras</s>, is the ground — this is the import. /
[The passage] beginning with '<s>atiśayokti</s>' presents the purpose — he says 'figurative usage' and so forth. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s> (gloss): 'presides over this <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure)' — meaning: connects with whatever <s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
'Of that' means: of that which is connected with <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — this is the meaning. /
'Of the other' means: of that which is not connected with <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — this is the meaning. /
And thus, the illumination of excellence of beauty through the connection of <s>upamā</s> (simile) and other [figures] with <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is the purpose — this is the import. /
In the <s>Locana</s> — 'right here' means: in the very passage that presents the purpose — this is the meaning. /
When the question arises, how does one understand the cancellation of the primary meaning through this? — revealing the intention, he says 'this is the import' and so forth. /
Just as <s>gotva</s> (cowness) and the like have the nature of a universal by virtue of recurring in particulars such as hornless cows and polled cattle, so too <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), by virtue of recurring in particulars such as <s>upamā</s> (simile) and the rest, has a universal nature; therefore 'all <s>vakrokti</s> is this very one' — this designation of identity is either primary, or else — with the intention of not insisting on the universal-particular relationship — through this mode of speech, the intended meaning is either that <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) alone is the soul of poetry (thereby refuting the opposing thesis), or that <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is the life-force of poetry. Having considered this alternative, he refutes the first — 'if indeed' and so forth. /
'Culminating in complete identity' — and thus, just as hornless cows and polled cattle are of the nature of <s>gotva</s> (cowness), so all <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures) would be of the very nature of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — this is the import. /
But let there be identity! — to this he says: 'therefore none distinct from it' and so forth. /
'Distinct from it' means: distinct from <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). /
'There' means: in the conjunction of excellence. /
'Would not need to be taken into account' — just as hornless cows and the like inherently possess the form of <s>gotva</s> (cowness) without dependence on anything else, so too <s>upamā</s> (simile) and the like would inherently possess conjunction with excellence, and the varying degrees of excellence due to varying degrees of poetic intuition that are actually observed — sometimes as <s>vācya</s> (explicitly stated) and sometimes as <s>vyaṅgya</s> (suggested) — /
even <s>vyaṅgyatva</s> (suggestive quality) — [this is explained in] the <s>Locana</s> — would not be perceptible, nor would mere <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament) be perceptible as anything [distinct]. /
Now, if [<s>atiśayokti</s>] is intended as the life-force of poetry in this way, even so, when employed without <s>aucitya</s> (propriety), it would [still] be so [i.e., the life-force]. /
If one objects: 'It is [only] when possessed of <s>aucitya</s> (propriety) that it is the life-force' — the foundation of <s>aucitya</s> (propriety) is nothing other than <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), and the like; therefore that alone — the inner controller, the primary life-force — must be acknowledged, not that [<s>atiśayokti</s>]. /
By this, those certain ones who say: 'In poetry, which is a beautiful combination of word and meaning united with <s>aucitya</s> (propriety), what need is there of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) as something essential?' — they, considering their own statement to be witness to the acknowledgment of the existence of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion), are refuted. /
Therefore the <s>vyaṅgyatva</s> (suggestive quality) of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is well-established. /
What was stated [earlier] about its incorporation into other <s>alaṅkāras</s> — that very thing he divides threefold — 'of that' and so forth. /
'As <s>vācya</s> (explicitly stated)' — that [<s>atiśayokti</s>] also becomes explicitly stated. /
As in: 'Indeed, what other [woman] is this here?' /
Here, even in <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), there is <s>atiśaya</s> (excellence). /
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'would be contradicted' — this is the import. /
He states another objection — 'merely <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament)' and so forth. /
Moreover, some mere <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament) is seen that is not embraced by <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole); that too would be impossible — this is the meaning. /
Having raised the second [alternative], he refutes it — 'now' and so forth. /
'That' means: <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). /
'Intended as the life-force of poetry in this way' — stated as 'this very one is all <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression)' in order to demonstrate that it is the life-force of poetry; 'even so' indicates acceptance for the sake of argument. /
Is mere <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) intended as the life-force, or something qualified by some particular quality? Not the first alternative — he says 'even without <s>aucitya</s> (propriety).' /
'That' is supplied from context. /
As in [the verse beginning with] 'little was created' and so forth. /
Likewise it would be the life-force of poetry. /
He concedes the second — 'when possessed of <s>aucitya</s> (propriety).' /
As in [the verse beginning with] 'when I rest' and so forth. /
Then our position is established — he says 'the foundation of <s>aucitya</s> (propriety)' and so forth. /
<s>Rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and the like alone are what motivate <s>aucitya</s> (propriety) — this was stated earlier. /
The reason for primacy — 'the inner controller.' /
'Not that' means: not that <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) possessed of <s>aucitya</s> (propriety). /
In passing, he says — 'by this' and so forth. /
'By this [they are] refuted' — this is the connection. /
'Their own statement itself' means: the very statement '<s>aucitya</s>-united' — this is the meaning. /
'The existence of <s>dhvani</s>' — since <s>aucitya</s> (propriety) is grounded in <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and the like, [their statement] would serve as evidence for the acknowledgment of the existence of <s>rasa</s>-<s>dhvani</s> (suggestion of aesthetic sentiment) and the like — this is the meaning. /
He concludes — 'therefore' and so forth. /
'This is merely figurative identification (<s>abhedopacāra</s>)' — the designation 'this very one is all <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression)' is merely figurative identification, like 'the face is the moon' — this is the meaning. /
He states the result of establishing the figurative nature — 'and therefore' and so forth. /
Showing the relevance of the passage beginning with 'of that' to the present topic, he says — 'what was stated' and so forth. /
'Was stated' means: was stated earlier as the ground for the figurative usage — this is the meaning. /
'Incorporation into other <s>alaṅkāras</s>' means: intermixture with other <s>alaṅkāras</s> — this is the meaning. /
He glosses the connection of 'of that' with 'as <s>vācya</s> (explicitly stated)' as well — 'that also' and so forth. /
'That' means: <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). /
He shows the example here as the one already given beginning with '<s>lāvaṇya</s> (gracefulness)' — 'as in' and so forth. /
Here, showing the explicitly stated <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure), he states the absence of <s>vyaṅgyatva</s> (suggestive quality) of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — 'here' and so forth. /
The <s>vācyatva</s> (explicit statement) of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) is quite evident from the identification of the eyes and the like with lotuses and such; but <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is sometimes predominant and sometimes subordinate. /
In the first case, it is the path of explicitly stated <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure). /
In the second, it is subsumed under <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion). /
In the third, it has the nature of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion). /
And this pattern applies to other <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures) as well, but for those, it does not apply to all cases. /
But for <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), it can apply to all <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures) — this is the distinctive point. /
And in those <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures) where the apprehension of their essential nature occurs through the medium of similarity — as in <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>upamā</s> (simile), <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal pairing), <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration), and the like — in those, the similarity itself, [apprehended] through the medium of the properties being suggested, becomes the bearer of extraordinary beauty; therefore all of these, possessing conjunction with excellence of beauty, belong to <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion) alone — [this is explained in] the <s>Locana</s> — and are merely touched by language. /
He states the division of scope for this threefold classification — 'regarding that' and so forth. /
Among those varieties, the first variety — in that [case]. /
But if <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is indeed of such a nature, then why was 'first, to begin with' indicated in sequence with reference to [something else]? — anticipating this doubt, he says 'and this' and so forth. /
That which was analyzed in [the case of] <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — the pattern of entering into other <s>alaṅkāras</s> as well. /
But even so, with what intention was 'first' said? — anticipating this doubt, he says 'of those' and so forth. /
Thus, having said that there is a touch of <s>vyaṅgya</s> (suggestion) in <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures), [the question arises:] what appears there as <s>vyaṅgyatva</s> (suggestive quality)? /
He explains the division — 'and in those' and so forth. /
The essential nature of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and the like was stated earlier. /
As for <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration): 'through the action itself, of that meaning' — <s>Bālapriyā</s>: even though <s>vyaṅgyatā</s> (suggestive quality) had begun to be established, because it is touched by the word 'another,' <s>vācyatva</s> (explicit statement) has supervened — thus both have <s>vācyatva</s> (explicit statement) — this is the meaning. /
According to the modern view, however, in 'another indeed here' there is <s>bhedātiśayokti</s> (hyperbole of distinction), while in 'where the lotuses' and so forth there is <s>rūpakātiśayokti</s> (hyperbolic metaphor). /
According to the view of King <s>Bhoja</s>, however, this is <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) — and other differences of opinion should be understood. /
'Of this' — because the demonstration of the threefold classification without the division of scope would yield meager results — this is the import. /
The first variety is that in which both [<s>atiśayokti</s> and the other <s>alaṅkāra</s>] have the nature of being explicitly stated. /
The pattern described in [the case of] <s>atiśayokti</s> has been extended to other <s>alaṅkāras</s> by the passage beginning with 'and this'; then for what purpose? — to introduce [the next point], he says 'but if' and so forth. /
'If indeed' — the word 'if' is used for what is not in doubt. /
This would be applicable only to <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), since its fitness for incorporation into the body of all <s>alaṅkāras</s> has been stated — this is the import. /
'Analyzed' — 'that which' and so forth. /
For sequence is possible only when there are indeed many sequential items, not otherwise — this is the import. /
'Analyzed' — 'variety' is to be supplied. /
'With what intention was "first" said' — 'firstness' should be understood as 'primacy'; the question is: what is the basis of primacy? — this is the meaning. /
He says 'of those' and so forth — meaning: he says [the passage] from 'of those' up to 'distinctive point.' /
'Having said that there is a touch of <s>vyaṅgya</s> (suggestion)' — meaning: having said [this] through the passage beginning with 'this group of explicitly stated <s>alaṅkāras</s>.' /
'What' means: another <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) or another thing — this is the meaning. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s> (gloss): 'apprehension of their essential nature' means: attainment of the status of <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) — this is the meaning. /
'<s>Rūpaka</s>' (metaphor) and so forth — in <s>rūpaka</s> and the like, the similarity is suggested, whereas <s>upamā</s> (simile) is of that very nature itself — this should be understood. /
In the <s>Locana</s> — 'through the action' — this is a characterization presented as an illustration of the general [principle]. /
The domains [are as follows]: /
In <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection-figure), <s>paryāyokti</s> (circumlocution), and the like, since the essential nature is established through the necessary concomitance of the suggested component, the status of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion) is beyond dispute. /
And regarding the <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatā</s> (subordinated suggestive quality) of <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures), for some there is a fixed rule regarding which particular <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) is contained within them — /
as in the case of <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) containing the <s>preyas</s> (endearment) figure. /
For some there is a fixed rule regarding containment of <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) in general — /
as in the case of <s>sandeha</s> (doubt) and the like containing <s>upamā</s> (simile). /
For some <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures), mutual containment is also possible — /
as with <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) and <s>upamā</s> (simile). /
Regarding that, <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) is well-known as containing <s>upamā</s> (simile). /
And <s>upamā</s> (simile) also sometimes follows in the shadow of <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) — /
as in <s>mālopamā</s> (garland-simile). /
