[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'The figure <s>preyas</s> (the charming)' — /
because that [utterance] culminates in flattery (<s>cāṭu</s>). /
And that [<s>vyājastuti</s>, ironic praise] has been exemplified by us in the second <s>Uddyota</s>. /
'Containing simile' (<s>upamāgarbhatva</s>) — by the word '<s>upamā</s>' (simile), all its particular varieties such as <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) etc. [are meant]; alternatively, '<s>aupamya</s>' (similitude) is common to all [figures], so by that, everything is implied. /
'Quite clearly' — /
'By her, he is both purified and adorned' — since this [statement], standing in the position of the lamp (<s>dīpa</s>), illuminates [both subjects simultaneously], the figure <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) has entered here suggestively (<s>pratīyamānatayā</s>); [also,] the statement of a common property (<s>sādhāraṇadharmābhidhāna</s>) — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] and <s>haraṇa</s> (lit. 'carrying away,' a figure) as defined by <s>Bhāmaha</s>. /
'Sets out' (<s>yiyāsati</s>) — begins to go. /
Just as here the suggestedness of simile [is shown], so it is clear in the <s>Kuvalayānanda</s> etc. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>: 'these are the domain of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> alone' — /
the purport is: because the apprehended property serves as an ancillary to the accomplishment of the expressed meaning. /
'The determination of its status etc.' — /
the meaning is: the determination as <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) etc. /
'The <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-ness' — /
the purport is: because it serves to embellish the expressed meaning. /
In the <s>Locana</s>, she states the reason for its containing the figure <s>preyas</s> — 'flattery' etc. /
'And that' — /
the meaning is: and <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise). /
Since in [the statement about] some [figures'] containing mere figures of speech, the word 'mere figure of speech' (<s>alaṅkāramātra</s>) denotes the generic [category of] figures, the further statement of 'containing simile' — denoting a specific [figure] — would seem contradictory; to this she says: 'by the word <s>upamā</s>' etc. /
'Particular varieties' — particular varieties of simile. /
The purport is: because of the statement 'simile with its distinctions concealed is held to be <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor)' etc. /
'<s>Rūpaka</s> etc.' — /
'are intended' is the remainder. /
The word '<s>upamā</s>' here does not denote the figure of simile but rather similitude (<s>aupamya</s>) — thus she says: 'alternatively' etc. /
'Common to all' — /
the meaning is: common to all — simile, <s>rūpaka</s>, etc. /
How is the shade of <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) apprehended in a garland-simile (<s>mālopamā</s>)? To this she provides justification — 'by her' etc. /
'By illuminating from the lamp-position' — /
by this, the etymology of the word '<s>dīpaka</s>' is shown: either 'like a lamp' (<s>dīpa iva</s>) or 'it illuminates' (<s>dīpayati</s>). /
This is clear in the <s>Kuvalayānanda</s>. /
'The figure <s>dīpaka</s> has entered here suggestively' — this is the syntactic connection. /
'Suggestively' means: as something suggested (<s>vyaṅgyatayā</s>). /
'Here' — in the domain of garland-simile, in [the verse beginning with] '<s>prabhāmahatyā</s>' (by the splendor of her) etc. /
Thus, when there is contact with the suggested element, the figures such as <s>rūpaka</s> etc., possessing a surplus of charm, are all avenues of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinate suggestion). /
And <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-ness is the common [feature] of all those of that kind — both stated and unstated. /
In its definition, all of these — [<s>Locana</s>:] for this, in the case of simile, is [achieved] through the clear mode of denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>) itself. /
'Of that kind' — /
the meaning is: possessing a surplus of charm. /
'Well-defined' (<s>sulakṣitā</s>) — for the form of these [figures] that is devoid of that [<s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-quality] is not to be sought after in poetry. /
For simile is [exemplified by]: 'as a cow, so is a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox).' /
<s>Rūpaka</s> is: '<s>khalevālī yūpa</s>' (the winnowing basket is the sacrificial post). /
<s>Śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) is: '<s>dvirvacane acī</s>' — inherent in the grammatical rule. /
<s>Yathāsaṅkhya</s> (serial correspondence) is: '<s>tudīśālature</s>.' /
<s>Dīpaka</s> (illumination) is: '<s>gām aśvam</s>' (a cow, a horse). /
<s>Sasandeha</s> (doubt) is: '<s>sthāṇur vā syāt</s>' (it might be a post). /
<s>Apahṇuti</s> (concealment/denial) is: '<s>nedaṃ rajatam</s>' (this is not silver). /
<s>Paryāyokta</s> (circumlocution) is: '<s>pauno divā nātti</s>' (the son of Pūru does not eat during the day). /
<s>Tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction) is: '<s>sthā dhvori cca</s>' (standing and running both). /
<s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) — all are indicatory (<s>jñāpaka</s>), just as in the domain of the technical term '<s>pada</s>' (word), the end-statement [provides indication] — '<s>anyatra saṃjñāvidhau pratyayagrahaṇe tadantavidhir na</s>' (in rules other than those prescribing technical terms, the mention of a suffix does not constitute a rule about what ends in that suffix). /
And <s>ākṣepa</s> (reproach/objection) — in both [domains], in optional rules, with the intention of stating a specific alternative, [the rule] first negates even the desired prescription — through that negation — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] here, showing the reason, she says: 'the common property' etc. /
'This in simile' — /
the meaning is: in garland-simile. /
'Through the mode of denotation' — through the operation of denotation (<s>abhidhāvyāpāra</s>). /
By the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone), suggestion (<s>vyañjana</s>) is excluded. /
The meaning is this: here, in simile, the required property — such as purity etc. — is clearly expressed by [the passage] 'by her' etc., not [expressed] as an object standing in the lamp-position with the intention of <s>dīpaka</s>. /
'By the splendor' — by [her] flame; like a lamp, by her. /
'He is both purified' etc. — the cognition of the triple sentence-meaning arises first; after that, the subsumption of purity and adornment under the triple simile-standard comprising lamp, <s>Himavat</s> etc. and the single comparand is apprehended — thus <s>dīpaka</s> has entered here suggestively. /
But in the domain of garland-simile with a separately adopted property beyond [what is needed for] it, the property is clearly expressed as connected with both [terms] — hence <s>dīpaka</s> does not enter suggestively; therefore she said 'garland-simile.' /
Regarding 'of that kind' — the word '<s>jāti</s>' (kind) here is an expression for the qualifying condition (<s>upādhi</s>) in the form of possessing a surplus of charm — thus she says: 'possessing a surplus of charm.' /
Objection: <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> is itself a distinct type, and simile etc. are separate figures — how then, when the definition of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> is formulated, is the defined-ness of those [figures] established? Revealing this intention, she says: 'for what indeed' etc. /
'Of these' — /
the meaning is: of simile etc. /
'Devoid of that' — devoid of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-ness. /
'Not to be sought after' — /
the purport is: because it is useless for the status of being a [poetic] figure. /
To support what was stated, she says: 'for simile indeed' etc. /
'In the <s>sūtra</s> on reduplication, <s>acī</s>' — /
in this <s>sūtra</s>, the word '<s>dvirvacana</s>' (reduplication) has two referents. /
'<s>Tudī</s>' — /
for in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tudīśāla</s>' etc., the connection is through serial correspondence. /
'<s>Gām aśvam</s>' — here, it should be understood through a single action. /
'<s>Sthā dhvori</s>' — /
by this <s>sūtra</s>, one [rule] is prescribed for two [cases]. /
'All are indicatory' — /
the purport is: the respective metalinguistic rules (<s>paribhāṣā</s>) etc. are apprehended by the respective words occurring in the <s>sūtra</s>. /
'<s>Na</s>' (not) — /
'indicates' is the remainder. /
'Well-defined' — they become [well-defined] in both [cases]. /
But through the statement of each one's specific form — without the general definition — words cannot be truly known, as through a serial enumeration — because of [their] infinity. /
For the modifications of speech are infinite, and the figures of speech are of precisely those types. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] by the principle of 'having been made equivalent' (<s>samīkṛta</s>). /
<s>Atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is: '<s>samudraḥ kuṇḍikā</s>' (the ocean is a water-pot); '<s>vindhyo vardhitavān arkavartmā agṛhṇāt</s>' (the <s>Vindhya</s> grew, the sun's path seized [it]). /
Likewise others. /
Nor is such [language used] for poetic purposes [alone]; <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-ness itself is identified as the essential core (<s>marman</s>) of figurativeness — it defines them well. /
By which, having made [them] fully complete, they become identified, i.e., comprehended; otherwise, there would necessarily be under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>). /
Thus he says: 'of each one' etc. /
Nor can the generic nature of <s>atiśayokti</s>, <s>vakrokti</s> (crooked speech), simile, etc. be established when they are devoid of charm; and charm depends on this — this very <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-ness is the general definition. /
And the charm of the suggested is of the nature of fitness for the manifestation of <s>rasa</s>; and <s>rasa</s>'s being of the nature of bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) through repose in its own essence — so there is no infinite regress at all — this is the purport. /
'For infinite indeed' — /
this was explained in the first <s>Uddyota</s> itself, in the intervening [passage at] 'because of the infinity of speech-modifications.' /
Objection: in all [cases of] figures, no other figure shines as suggested; then how [can it be claimed that] through <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'in optional rules' etc. — /
this is clear to the grammarians. /
'The ocean is a water-pot' — /
the purport is: since the ocean is referred to as a water-pot, taking the water-pot as the object [of comparison] in order to demonstrate the abundance of water, [this is] hyperbole in the form of non-difference where there is [actually] difference. /
In [the passage] '<s>Vindhya</s>' etc., that [hyperbole] is in the form of connection where there is no connection. /
Concluding, she says: 'likewise others' etc. /
'Likewise' etc. — /
the meaning is: the stated illustrations and such. /
'Thus' — in the sense of a reason. /
The elaboration of 'in its definition, all of these become well-defined' is: '<s>guṇībhūta</s>' etc. /
'By which' — /
the meaning is: through <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-ness. /
'Otherwise' — /
the meaning is: without the stated general definition, through the statement of each particular definition alone. /
In some texts, however, the passage from 'for simile indeed' etc. to 'become comprehended' is not seen. /
Objection: if <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-ness alone is the general definition of all figures, and if through that definition their defined-ness is established — then this is improper, since <s>atiśayokti</s> etc. have the nature of the generic [category of] figures, and are already fulfilled by that definition alone — to this she says: 'nor' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: the generic nature of <s>atiśayokti</s> etc., which are devoid of charm, is not established. /
From that, what [follows]? To this she says: 'charm' etc. /
'Depends on this' — /
the meaning is: depends on <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-ness. /
Objection: the charm of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> that produces the charm of figures must be stated; but that [charm] too is produced by another, and that by yet another — hence the fault of infinite regress arises; to this she says: 'of the suggested' etc. /
What was stated — 'in its definition, all of these become well-defined' — objecting to that, and intending to resolve it, she introduces the subsequent text: 'objection' etc. /
'In all' — /
in <s>dīpaka</s> etc. [another figure] shines [as suggested] only sometimes; but in <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection/reproach) etc., [the domain] of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> exists through yet another mode, characterized as the subsumption of the suggested meaning. /
That — this second [type] too, which is of the nature of an outflow of <s>dhvani</s>, which is the domain of the great poet, which is supremely delightful — should be noted by the connoisseurs. /
In no way whatsoever is there [poetry] that captivates the hearts of connoisseurs without that — [<s>Locana</s>:] the comprehension of all through what was defined. /
Not so; either mere <s>vastu</s> (content) or <s>rasa</s>, when suggested, will become subordinate — that very [point] is what he says: 'and of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>' etc. /
'Through another mode' — characterized by <s>vastu</s> or <s>rasa</s>. /
Or, if the introductory passage is thus: objection — if the figures are defined through <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, then the definition should be stated; why has it not been stated? Anticipating this, she says: '<s>guṇībhūta</s>' etc. /
'Domain-ness' — the meaning is: to-be-defined-ness. /
By what is there to-be-defined-ness? The mode that is distinct from <s>dhvani</s> — the subsumption of meaning through suggestedness, by name — that itself is the definition; by that — this is the meaning. /
Once the suggested [meaning] is defined and its subordination determined, what else of this need be defined? — this is the purport. /
Thus, having carried to completion [the thesis that] 'the soul of poetry is <s>dhvani</s>,' he concludes — with 'that this' etc., up to 'beauty.' /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Not' — this is the purport. /
'Then how' etc. — /
the purport is: it is not a [valid] definition because of non-pervasion. /
Regarding '<s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-ness' — by the word 'suggested' (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), not merely a figure of speech is intended; but also <s>vastu</s>, <s>rasa</s>, etc. — hence this is not non-pervasive — thus she says: 'not so' etc. /
'Either mere <s>vastu</s>' etc. — /
the purport is: in a domain of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> where no figure shines [as suggested]. /
'Characterized as the subsumption of suggested meaning' — this is elaborated in substance by 'when suggested, will become subordinate.' /
'Through suggestedness, the subsumption of meaning' — the subordinate status (<s>guṇabhāva</s>) relative to the expressed; that is the definition, i.e., the uncommon property or essential nature, of this other mode — by that — this is its meaning. /
'Through another mode' — the third case-ending is in the sense of characterization — thus she says: 'characterized by' etc. /
And thus: of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, being any one of <s>vastu</s>, <s>rasa</s>, or <s>alaṅkāra</s>, when subordinate — this is the meaning. /
The connection is with 'its domain-ness exists.' /
'Among the figures' — the connection is through transposition. /
Considering the laboriousness of the above-stated textual construal, she states [the passage] through another mode — 'or' etc. /
'Defined' — /
'would be' is the remainder. /
'Of that' — of that <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>. /
Since she said 'by the definition,' the meaning of 'domain-ness' is established as 'to-be-defined-ness' — thus she says: 'to-be-defined-ness, that is.' /
'By what is there to-be-defined-ness?' — this is the introductory question for 'through another mode.' /
'Distinct from <s>dhvani</s>' — /
the distinction is: previously, 'other mode' was relative to [other] figures; now it is relative to <s>dhvani</s>. /
'Subsumption of meaning' — establishment in subordinate status relative to the expressed. /
'Definition' — uncommon property. /
Objection: this definition was not stated previously; how then is there reference to it as if established? To this she says: 'the suggested' etc. /
The definition of the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) has already been stated in the first <s>Uddyota</s>. /
The subordination has been determined by [the passage] 'where [there is] connection with the suggested' etc. — this is the purport. /
She states the purport of the conclusion beginning with 'that this,' by showing the specific meaning to be concluded — /
'Having carried to completion' — having brought to full resolution. /
'The mode where there is no beauty through contact with the suggested meaning' — /
this then is the supreme secret of poetry — thus should it be contemplated by the wise. /
The principal ornament of the words of great poets, even those bearing [other] embellishments,
is this lustre (<s>chāyā</s>) of the suggested meaning — an adornment like modesty (<s>lajjā</s>) in women. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.37 //
The principal ornament of the words of great poets, even those bearing embellishments,
is this lustre of the suggested meaning — an adornment like modesty in women. // 37 //
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] By this [suggested meaning], even a well-known meaning acquires some ineffable charm.

children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] In order to show that what was previously stated — 'being the secret doctrine (<s>upaniṣad</s>) of all excellent poets' poetry' — is not to be regarded as mere flattery in the form of <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogy) — 'this is it.' // 3.6 //

children.translated_text: Because even in ascetics (<s>yatins</s>) who are free from passion, when the loincloth is displaced, one observes the blemish of shame.
For indeed, of someone — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Since [the passage] 'this is it' etc. is not included within the summation, she introduces that passage — 'that which' etc.
'Mere flattery' — mere enticement of the mind.
'In the form of <s>arthavāda</s>' — in the form of eulogy. // 3.6 //

'The principal ornament' — /
'Even those bearing embellishments' — the meaning is: even those devoid of word-ornaments (<s>śabdālaṅkāra</s>). /
The lustre (<s>chāyā</s>), i.e., beauty, produced by the suggested meaning — and that is similar to modesty (<s>lajjā</s>), because the beauty whose essence is concealment is its life-breath. /
Even for heroines bearing ornaments (<s>alaṅkāra</s>), modesty is the principal adornment. /
That by which the suggested lustre — having the form of the beauty of the heart born from the inner sprouting of love — [shines forth]: for modesty is nothing but the blossoming of love in the form of the desire to conceal the erotic transformation that has sprouted within.

children.translated_text: The verse '<s>kuraṅgī</s>' (deer-like one) etc. is cited in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>.
For here the desire to conceal the erotic transformation is clearly understood.

children.translated_text: By another mode as well — for example: 'Those certain special playful gestures (<s>līlā-viśeṣas</s>) of the doe-eyed one, arising from intimacy, in carrying out the commands of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love),

children.translated_text: they remain unimpaired — to be contemplated constantly, in solitude, with the mind alone.' //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She shows that the syntactic connection of 'principal' in the <s>kārikā</s> is with 'ornament' — 'principal ornament.' /
'Bearing embellishments' — /
By the word 'embellishments' (<s>alaṅkṛti</s>), both poetic <s>alaṅkāras</s> and [literal] ornaments like bracelets etc. should be understood. /
The elaboration of 'the lustre of the suggested meaning' is: 'produced by the suggested' etc. /
'The suggested' — having the nature of thing (<s>vastu</s>), <s>alaṅkāra</s>, <s>rasa</s>, etc. /
The explanation of 'like modesty' is: 'similar to modesty.' /
She states the reason for the similarity to modesty — 'concealment' etc. /
'Concealment itself is the essence' — the beauty whose nature is such, i.e., whose very life-breath is beauty; the condition of that is its state; therefore — this is the meaning. /
The quality of having concealment-essence-beauty as the life-breath of the suggested has been stated by way of the illustration of a woman's pitcher-like breasts. /
Regarding modesty, she will explain immediately after. /
She shows the application to the analogue of both 'even those bearing embellishments' and 'principal ornament' — '<s>alaṅkāra</s>' etc. /
She also applies 'the lustre of the suggested meaning' to the analogue — 'the suggested' etc. /
Here, in the analogue, the meaning of the word '<s>chāyā</s>' is not 'beauty,' but rather some indescribable condition of the heart that becomes possible at the onset of youth in women — she says: 'inner' etc. /
'Born from the inner sprouting of love' — that beauty of the heart born from it; that itself being the form of her, i.e., she whose nature is the mental transformation caused by the sprouting of love — in sum. /
The syntactic connection is: by which [she becomes] 'of suggested [lustre].' /
She corroborates what was stated — 'modesty' etc. /
She states the reason for the impossibility of that [lustre] without [modesty], by way of negative concomitance — 'free from passion' etc.

children.translated_text:
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Of the poet' — the verse is '<s>kuraṅgīvāṅgāni</s>' etc. /
Thus the lustre, i.e., beauty, of the suggested meaning — the coaxing of the beloved's desire, jealous anger (<s>māna</s>), etc. — by which [it shines]. /
For the wave of <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> (erotic sentiment), restrained by modesty, out of its fullness gives birth to those amorous gestures (<s>vilāsas</s>) in the form of a series of transformations of the eyes and body — thus this is the blossoming of modesty whose essence is the beauty of concealment — this is the purport. /
'Intimacy' — /
<s>Manmatha</s> is the teacher whose commands are honored by the three worlds, and precisely therefore the destroyer of timidity and modesty — by [the beloved] who, when this inviolable command is given, in the course of its necessary execution, through the abandonment of timidity and modesty, [performs gestures] brought forth during the time of intimate union (<s>sambhoga</s>); 'of the doe-eyed one' — gestures purified by the glances appropriate to the experience of unsophisticated love-making, those other special gestures (<s>vilāsas</s>) being transformations of limbs and eyes; and precisely therefore 'unimpaired' — ever-fresh, blossoming moment by moment in ever-new forms; 'with the mind alone' — unoccupied with anything else, preceded by dwelling in solitude, with the withdrawal of all senses, to be contemplated — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She explains that word — 'of the suggested' etc. /
'By which reason' — the syntactic connection is: 'beauty.' /
'How can modesty be its cause?' — to this she says: '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' etc. /
'This' — this is the connection. /
The purport is: the series of eye-transformations etc. that has arisen constitutes the form of the lustre of the suggested. /
She explains the verse — 'by the teacher <s>Manmatha</s>' etc. /
'A king [is respected], but the teacher's command is truly inviolable' — because of statements like 'when the guru is angry, no one [can help]' etc. — therefore the characterization as teacher. /
'Three worlds' — /
As stated in <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> — 'even in the lowest creatures' etc. /
'Precisely therefore' — precisely because of having commands honored by the three worlds. /
'Given' — for the purpose of indicating that it must be accepted. /
'Command' — /
The meaning is: the command that all young women, abandoning modesty and timidity, should become devoted to love-making. /
The connection is: 'through abandonment, it is to be done.' /
'Unsophisticated' — /
'Unsophisticated' means unaffected; the enjoyment, i.e., relishing, of love-making — on that occasion, in sum. /
The meaning is: purified by appropriate glances. /
'The enjoyment of love-making' — is also a reading. /
'Special gestures' — the meaning of the word 'special' in this context. /
'Other' — /
The meaning is: extraordinary. /
'Precisely therefore' — precisely because of their extraordinary nature. /
The result of dwelling in solitude is stated — 'with the withdrawal of all senses.' /
She gives two meanings of the potential suffix — 'capable, worthy.' /
Here, by the word '<s>ke 'pi</s>' (certain, some), in expressing the expressed meaning unclearly, the suggested thing — effortless and infinite — is conveyed; what lustre has not been produced [by this]!
The transition to another meaning through <s>kāku</s> (intonation/irony) which is also observed —

children.text: sā vyaṅgyasya guṇī-bhāve prakāram imam āśritā // DhvK_3.38 //
children.translated_text: that, when the suggested becomes subordinate, has resorted to this type [of <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>]. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.38 //
The transition to another meaning through <s>kāku</s> which is also observed —
that, when the suggested becomes subordinate, has resorted to this type. // 38 //

children.text: yā caiṣā kākvā kvacidarthāntarapratītirdṛśyate sā vyaṅgyasyārthasya guṇībhāve sati guṇībhūtavyaṅgyalakṣaṇaṃ kāvyaprabhedamāśrayate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] And this cognition of another meaning through <s>kāku</s> (intonation) that is sometimes observed — when the suggested meaning becomes subordinate, it takes resort to the variety of poetry characterized as <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion).
For example — 'Content, [<s>Locana</s>:] capable, worthy, appropriate.',
'For some [gestures] are incapable of being described by any other means.' // 37 //

And that [thing] should be understood as including unspeakability, being knowable only through experience, producing supreme delight, etc.
'What lustre' etc. —

children.translated_text: The meaning is: the suggested meaning that has been described enhances the expressed meaning and produces the beauty of excellent poetry. // 3.7 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She gives another example of <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> — 'transition to another meaning' etc. /
The word '<s>kāku</s>' is derived from the root '<s>kaka</s>' meaning 'unsteadiness/fickleness.' /
For indeed, that word, being read in a sequence of expectant and non-expectant [meanings] etc., desires something beyond the primary meaning — thus its fickleness is spoken of. /
Alternatively, '<s>ku</s>' in the sense of 'slightly' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The elaboration of 'worthy' is: 'appropriate.' /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>, 'expressing the expressed meaning unclearly' — /
The purport is: because the word '<s>kim</s>' denotes an object delimited by an unascertained particular property.

kākumudāharaṇe darśayati--svasthā ityādi /
iti ceti /
caturṣu sthaleṣu cetyarthaḥ /
sākāṅkṣetyādi /
sākāṅkṣā dīptā gadgadena tārāpraśamanoddīpanābhyāṃ citritā viśeṣavatī cetyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: Or, for example —

children.text: āma asaio orama paivvae ṇa tueṃ maliṇiaṃ sīlam /
children.translated_text: '<s>āma asaio orama paivvae ṇa tueṃ maliṇiaṃ sīlam</s>' /

children.text: kiṃ uṇa jaṇassa jāa vva cāndilaṃ taṃ ṇa kāmemo //
children.translated_text: '<s>kiṃ uṇa jaṇassa jāa vva cāndilaṃ taṃ ṇa kāmemo</s>' //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Intending to comment on the <s>kārikā</s> and <s>vṛtti</s>, she first states the derivation of the word <s>kāku</s> (vocal intonation) — 'of <s>ka</s>' etc. /
'Of this root' — connected with this root. /
Objection: <s>laulya</s> (eagerness) means desire — how does it apply here? — to this she says — 'for therein' etc. /
'Therein' — in the domain of <s>kāku</s>. /
'With expectancy' (<s>sākāṅkṣā</s>) — /
As stated in the <s>Kāvyānuśāsana</s>: 'And that <s>kāku</s> is of two kinds — with expectancy (<s>sākāṅkṣā</s>) and without expectancy (<s>nirākāṅkṣā</s>), since sentences are [likewise] with and without expectancy. /
When from a sentence, through the force of convention, the meaning that is understood is not exactly as it appears, but rather is something less or more, determinable by the force of [other] means of knowledge — that sentence has expectancy; the opposite is without expectancy. For the expectancy, [which properly belongs] to the speaker, is figuratively attributed to the sentence. /
And that is ascertained by the force of context. /
And its having a specific domain is also determined from that alone. /
The domain is also threefold: another meaning, a specification within that very [expressed] domain, or the absence of that meaning' — etc. /
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' in '<s>nirākāṅkṣā</s> etc.,' figures such as <s>dīpta</s> (blazing) etc. are included. /
'Sequence' means type. /
'That [is] a word' — /
Since <s>kāku</s>, being of the nature of a specific type of sound-modulation (<s>dhvaniviśeṣa</s>), is a property of the word — therefore '<s>śabda</s>' (word) is said. /
'The primary' — /
The meaning is: a meaning exceeding the primary meaning that is understood by the force of convention. /
'Desires' — /
The meaning is: desires in the sense of wishing to communicate. /
'Is expressed' — /
The remainder is: by figurative attribution (<s>upacāra</s>). /
She states it in another way — 'or if' etc. /
'The heart' — /
The meaning is: for the cognition of that thing which resides in the heart, having the form of injunction, prohibition, etc. /
'The <s>Dhārtarāṣṭras</s> prosper while I am alive.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The substitute '<s>ka</s>' [for a consonant]. /
Thereby, <s>kāku</s> is the partial ground for the cognition of what resides in the heart; the apprehension of another meaning through it — that particular type of poetry resorts to this variety of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggested meaning). The reason here is: the suggested [meaning] therein necessarily has subordinate status. /
By the expression 'apprehension of another meaning,' poetry itself is referred to here. /
But one should not say that the cognition itself has the character of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>; rather, through the medium of the cognition, the poetry is so characterized. /
Others, however, say: 'Where the suggested has subordinate status, this is the type [of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>]; otherwise, even there it is <s>dhvani</s> itself.' /
But that is wrong; because in all uses of <s>kāku</s>, the suggested meaning, even when disclosed, has subordinate status by virtue of being touched by the word — for <s>kāku</s> is indeed a certain property of the word itself; what is touched by it — as in '<s>gopyaivaṃ gaditaḥ saleśam</s>' ('thus spoken by the cowherd-girl with a trace [of reproach]'), like '<s>hasannetrārpitākūtam</s>' ('with intent cast through laughing eyes') — is favored by the word itself. /
For this very reason, in [the verse] '<s>bhama dhammia</s>' etc., when <s>kāku</s> is applied, the status of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> alone [obtains], as it has been explicitly stated, and the world holds this view. /
'Well' (<s>svasthā</s>) — /
'They prosper,' 'while I am alive,' 'the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭras</s>' — and thus in [all] four cases, [the <s>kāku</s> is] variegated with expectancy, blazing, faltering, high-pitched, calming, and kindling [qualities] — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] the meaning is: some device. /
'Ground' — this is a statement of the meaning of the word '<s>ka</s>' (prefix). /
She comments on the <s>kārikā</s> — 'by that' etc. /
'By that' — by that <s>kāku</s>. /
'Apprehension of another meaning' — by this, a particular type of poetry that makes known another meaning is intended — she will state this; with that intention she explains 'that' — 'that particular type of poetry' etc. /
'Subordinate status' — the seventh case-ending is in the sense of cause; the meaning is: because of the subordinate status — she says — 'therein' etc. /
'But not' etc. — /
If 'apprehension of another meaning' is taken in its literal sense as 'the cognition of another meaning,' then one would have to attribute the character of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> to the cognition itself — and that is not intended — this is the purport. /
Explaining the stated meaning in its intended sense, she says — 'through the medium of cognition' etc. /
The meaning is: through the medium of the cognition of another meaning's subordination, the <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> nature of the poetry that is its cause is demonstrated. /
But others — in the domain of <s>kāku</s>, where the suggested has primacy, that is <s>dhvani</s>; where it has subordinate status, that is <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> — 'this is shown by the [phrase] "subordination of the suggested"' — they explain thus; having presented their view, she refutes it — 'others' etc. /
She establishes the 'touched-by-word' nature — 'for <s>kāku</s> indeed' etc. /
'Property' — /
As stated: <s>kāku</s> is a property of recitation that carries [the speaker's] intention. /
And <s>Amara</s> [says]: '<s>kāku</s> is a modification [of voice], feminine, [arising] from grief, fear, etc., in sound.' /
'Touched by it' — /
The meaning is: made the object [of cognition] through the verbal property in the form of <s>kāku</s>. /
'Favored by the word itself' — the connection of this is: because of the non-difference of property and property-bearer — this is the purport. /
She gives an example of the word-disclosed nature and word-favored nature — '<s>gopī</s>' etc. /
'For this very reason' — /
The meaning is: because of the subordinate status of the meaning suggested by <s>kāku</s>. /
'<s>Kāku</s>' etc. — /
The meaning is: when the prohibition of wandering is suggested by <s>kāku</s>, it is precisely <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>. /
She states the reason here — 'explicitly stated' etc. /
'Then' — in the application of <s>kāku</s>. /
She illustrates the <s>kāku</s> examples — '<s>svasthā</s>' etc. /
'And' — and in the four cases — this is the meaning. /
'With expectancy' etc. — /
The meaning is: having expectancy, blazing, variegated by faltering voice, high pitch, calming and kindling [of emotion] — i.e., having specific features.

children.text:
śabdaśaktireva hi svābhidheyasāmarthyākṣiptakākusahāyā satyarthaviśeṣapratipattiheturna kākumātram. viṣayāntare svecchākṛtātkākumātrāttathāvidhārthapratipattyasambhavāt /
sa cārthaḥ kākuviśeṣasahāyaśabdavyāpāropārūḍho 'pyarthasāmarthyalabhya iti vyaṅgyarūpa eva /
vācakatvānugamenaiva tu yadā locanam kākurasambhāvyo 'yamartho 'tyarthamanucitaścetyamuṃ vyaṅgyamarthaṃ spṛśantī tenaivopakṛtā satīkrodhānubhāvarūpatāṃ vyaṅgyopaskṛtasya vācyasyaivādhatte /
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] But when, through conformity with expressiveness alone — [<s>Locana</s>:] <s>kāku</s>, touching this suggested meaning [that] 'this meaning is inconceivable and utterly inappropriate' — being enhanced by that very [quality] — assumes the form of an <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) of anger, [thus] it belongs to the expressed meaning alone that is embellished by the suggested.
'Yes' (<s>āma</s>) —

children.text: āma asatyaḥ uparama pativrate na tyā malinitaṃ śīlam /
children.translated_text: 'Yes, [we are] unchaste; desist, O faithful wife; your virtue has not been stained by you.' /

children.text: kiṃ punarjanasya jāyeva nāpitaṃ taṃ na kāmayāmahe //
children.translated_text: 'But what more — like the wife of [any common] man, we do not desire that barber!' //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] For it is verbal power (<s>śabdaśakti</s>) alone — aided by <s>kāku</s> suggested by the force of its own denoted meaning — that is the cause of the cognition of the specific true meaning, not <s>kāku</s> alone. Because the cognition of such a specific meaning is impossible from mere <s>kāku</s> produced at one's whim in another domain. /
And that meaning, though mounted upon the verbal operation aided by the specific <s>kāku</s>, is obtainable by the force of the meaning — hence it is of the nature of the suggested alone.

children.text:
iti cchāyā /
āma asatyo bhavāmaḥ ityabhyupagamakākuḥ sākāṅkṣopahāsā /
uparameti nirākāṅkṣatayā sūcanagarbhā /
pativrate iti dīptasmitayoginī /
na tvayā malinitaṃ śīlamiti sagadgadākāṅkṣā /
kiṃ punarjanasya jāyeva manmathāndhīkṛtā, candilaṃ nāpitamiti pāmaraprakṛtiṃ na kāmayāmahe iti nirākāṅkṣagadgadopahāsagarbhā /
eṣā hi kayācinnāpi tānuraktayā kulavadhvā dṛṣṭāvinayāyā upahāsyamānāyāḥ pratyupahāsāveśagarbhoktiḥ kākupradhānaiveti /
guṇībhāvaṃ darśayituṃ śabdaspṛṣṭatāṃ tāvatsādhayati--śabdaśaktirevetyādinā /
bālapriyā dīptatārāvalaṅkārāntargatau praśamanoddīpane tvaṅgāntargate iti vivekaḥ /
ayamartha iti /
mayi jīvati dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ svasthā bhavantīti vācyārtha ityarthaḥ /
spṛśantīti /
viṣayīkurvāṇā satītyarthaḥ /
tenaiva uktena vyaṅgyenaiva /
upakṛtā satīti hetukathanam /
vyaṅgyeti /
asambhāvyatvādirūpoktavyaṅgyenopaskṛtasyetyarthaḥ /
ādhatta sampādayati /
tathāca vyaṅgyaṃ guṇībhūtamiti bhāvaḥ /
āmeti /
vayamasatyaḥ svairiṇyo bhavāmaḥ /
āmetyabhyupagame /
uparama tvaṃ madupahāsādvirama /
śīlaṃ sadvṛttam /
kiṃ punaḥ kintu /
janasya jāyeveti /
tvamivetyarthaḥ /
tvaṃ yathā kāmayase tatheti yāvat /
locane--sākāṅkṣeti /
sākāṅkṣā upahāsavyañjikā cetyarthaḥ /
pativrata iti na malinitamityatra ca kākvā tattadabhāvo vyaṅgya ityabhiprāyeṇāha--pativrata ityādi /
candilamityasya chāyā--nāpitamiti /
tena gamyamāha--pāmareti /
guṇībhāvamiti /
vyaṅgyasyeti śeṣaḥ /
anugama ityasya tadviśiṣṭavācyapratītistadā guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatayā tathāvidhārthadyotinaḥ kāvyasya vyapadeśaḥ /
vyaṅgyaviśiṣṭavācyābhidhāyino hi guṇībhūtvayaṅgyatvam /
children.translated_text:
Thus is the <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit rendering). /
'Yes, we are unchaste' — this is the <s>kāku</s> of concession (<s>abhyupagama</s>); it has expectancy and is laden with mockery. /
'Desist' — being without expectancy, it is pregnant with innuendo. /
'O faithful wife' — it partakes of the blazing (<s>dīpta</s>) and satirical (<s>smita</s>) [types]. /
'Your virtue has not been stained' — [has] expectancy with a faltering [voice]. /
'But what more — like the wife of [any common] man, blinded by <s>Manmatha</s> (god of love) — that barber, of base nature — we do not desire' — this is without expectancy, laden with mockery and faltering voice. /
For this is the speech of some virtuous housewife (<s>kulavadhū</s>) who is actually attracted [to someone], counter-mocking another woman who taunts her for being seen in an improper situation — [a speech] that is pregnant with counter-mockery and essentially governed by <s>kāku</s>. /
To demonstrate the subordinate status [of the suggested], she first establishes its 'touched-by-word' nature — with 'verbal power alone' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Blazing (<s>dīpta</s>) and high-pitched (<s>tāra</s>) belong to other figures, while calming (<s>praśamana</s>) and kindling (<s>uddīpana</s>) belong to other ancillary [types] — this is the distinction. /
'This meaning' — /
The meaning is: the expressed meaning is 'while I am alive, the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭras</s> prosper.' /
'Touching' — /
The meaning is: making [it] the object, being [thus]. /
'By that very' — by the stated suggested [meaning] alone. /
'Being enhanced' — this states the reason. /
'Suggested' — /
The meaning is: embellished by the stated suggested [meaning] in the form of inconceivability etc. /
'Assumes' — produces. /
And thus the suggested is subordinated — this is the purport. /
'Yes' (<s>āma</s>) — /
'We are unchaste, libertine women.' /
'<s>Āma</s>' — in the sense of concession. /
'Desist' — you, stop your mockery of me. /
'Virtue' (<s>śīla</s>) — good conduct. /
'But what more' — rather. /
'Like the wife of [common] people' — /
The meaning is: like you. /
Just as you desire — this much. /
In the <s>Locana</s> — 'with expectancy' — /
The meaning is: having expectancy and being indicative of mockery. /
'O faithful wife' and 'has not been stained' — she says with the intention that through <s>kāku</s>, the absence of those [qualities] is suggested — 'O faithful wife' etc. /
The <s>chāyā</s> of '<s>candilam</s>' is 'the barber' (<s>nāpitam</s>). /
By that she indicates the intended meaning — 'of base nature' etc. /
'Subordinate status' — /
The remainder is: of the suggested. /
The meaning of 'conformity' is: when the cognition of the expressed qualified by the suggested [occurs], then, as <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, such is the designation of the poetry that illuminates such meaning. /
For <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> is [the type] that denotes the expressed qualified by the suggested.

children.text: prabhedasyāsya viṣayo yaś ca yuktyā pratīyate /
children.translated_text: The domain of this sub-type, and what is understood through reasoning,

children.text: vidhātavyā sahṛdayair na tatra dhvani-yojanā // DhvK_3.38 //
children.translated_text: connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdayas</s>) should not apply the designation of <s>dhvani</s> there. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.38 //
The domain of this sub-type, and what is understood through reasoning,
connoisseurs should not apply the designation of <s>dhvani</s> there. // 38 //

children.text:
saṅkīrṇo hi kaściddhvanerguṇībhūtavyaṅgyasya ca lakṣye dṛśyate mārgaḥ /
locanam nanvevaṃ vyaṅgyatvaṃ kathamityāśaṅkyāha---sa ceti /
adhunā guṇībhāvaṃ darśayati---vācakatveti /
vācakatve 'nugamo guṇatvaṃ vyaṅgyavyañjakabhāvasya vyaṅgyaviśiṣṭavācyapratītyā tatraiva kāvyasya prakāśakatvaṃ kalpyate; tena na tathā vyapadeśa iti kākuyojanāyāṃ sarvatra guṇībhūtavyaṅgyataiva /
children.translated_text: [<s>Locana</s>:] The conformity with expressiveness constitutes the subordinate status of the relationship of suggested and suggestor; through the cognition of the expressed qualified by the suggested, the illuminating capacity of the poetry is conceived as [residing] in that [expressed meaning] alone; therefore, there is no [separate] designation [as <s>dhvani</s>] — thus in the application of <s>kāku</s>, everywhere there is only <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> status.

children.text: ata eva 'mathnāmi kauravaśataṃ samare na kopāt' ityādau viparītalakṣaṇaṃ ya āhuste na samyakyarāmamṛśuḥ /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, those who say that in '<s>mathnāmi kauravaśataṃ samare na kopāt</s>' ('I shall churn the hundred <s>Kauravas</s> in battle — not out of anger') etc. there is <s>viparītalakṣaṇā</s> (contrary indication) — they have not examined [the matter] correctly.

children.text: yato 'troccāraṇakāla eva 'na kopāt' iti dīptatāragadgadasākāṅkṣakākubalānniṣedhasya niṣidhyamānatayaiva yudhiṣṭhirābhimatasandhimārgākṣamārūpatvābhiprāyeṇa pratipattiriti mukhyārthabādhādyanusaraṇavidhnābhāvātko lakṣaṇāyā avakāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because at the very time of utterance, 'not out of anger' — through the force of <s>kāku</s> [that is] blazing, high-pitched, faltering, and with expectancy — the cognition of the negation is as that which is itself being negated, with the intention of [expressing] the impossibility of the path of peace desired by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> — therefore, since there is no obstacle to the normal flow of the primary meaning being sublated, what scope is there for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication)?

children.text: 'darśe yajeta' ityatra tu tathāvidhakākvādyupāyāntarābhāvadbhavatu viparītalakṣaṇā ityalamavāntareṇa bahunā // 3.8 //
children.translated_text: But in '<s>darśe yajeta</s>' ('one should sacrifice at the new moon'), since there is no other means such as <s>kāku</s> etc. of that kind, let there be <s>viparītalakṣaṇā</s> (contrary indication) — but enough of this digression. // 3.8 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] For a certain mixed path is seen in examples between <s>dhvani</s> and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Anticipating the doubt — 'but then how [can there be] suggestedness?' — he says — 'and that' etc. /
Now he demonstrates the subordination — 'expressiveness' etc.

children.text:
adhunā saṃkīrṇa viṣayaṃ vibhajate---prabhedasyeti /
yuktyeti /
cārutvapratītirevātra yuktiḥ /
bālapriyā vivaraṇam--guṇatvamiti /
kasyetyataḥ pūrayati--vyaṅgyetyādi /
'tadviśiṣṭe'tyādivṛttigranthavivaraṇam--vyaṅgyaviśiṣṭetyādi /
tatraiva vyaṅgyaviśiṣṭavācya eva /
prakāśakatvaṃ bodhakatvam /
vṛttau 'yadā tade'tyanayoryatastata ityarthau bodhyau /
mathnāmītyādi /
pratijñātakauravaśatavadhasya kruddhasya bhīmasenasya vacanamidamata eva na mathnāmītyādau viparītalakṣaṇeti kecittadāha--viparītetyādi /
iti niṣedhasya niṣiddhyamānatayaiva pratipattiriti sambandhaḥ /
kākukalpanāyāṃ hetuḥ--yudhiṣṭiretyādi /
yudhiṣṭhirābhimato yassandhimārgastasya yadakṣamārūpatvamakṣamyatvaṃ tadabhiprāyo bhīmagatastenetyarthaḥ /
itītyādi /
ayaṃ bhāvaḥ--na mathnāmītyādirūpasya mathanādiniṣedhasyādau pratītiḥ paścāttu mathnāmyevetyādirūpasya tanniṣedhaniṣedhasya pratītiritina, kintūccāraṇakāla eva kākubalānmathanādiniṣedhasya niṣeṣapratiyogitvenaiva na mathnāmi netyākārikā pratītirato mathanādiniṣedhasya vācyasya niṣedho vyaṅgya eveti /

children.translated_text: Incidentally, she responds to the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> — '<s>darśa</s>' etc.

children.text: na dṛśyate candro 'treti vyutpattyā darśaśabdo 'māvāsyāyāṃ prayujyate /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>darśa</s>' is used for the new moon (<s>amāvāsyā</s>), by the etymology: 'the moon is not seen here.'
And thus, here the <s>viparītalakṣaṇā</s> (contrary indication) is from the root '<s>dṛś</s>' (to see) in the sense of 'absence of seeing' — this is the purport.
This is clear in the commentary on the <s>Śrautasūtra</s>. // 3.8 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Now she differentiates the mixed domain — 'of this sub-type' etc. /
'Through reasoning' — /
The cognition of beauty is itself the reasoning here. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The elaboration — 'subordinate status' etc. /
She supplies [the answer to] 'of what?' — 'of the suggested' etc. /
The elaboration of the <s>vṛtti</s> passage beginning with 'qualified by that' — 'qualified by the suggested' etc. /
'In that alone' — in the expressed qualified by the suggested alone. /
'Illuminating capacity' means the capacity to communicate. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'when that' — the meanings of 'since' and 'therefore' should be understood for these two [words]. /
'I shall churn' etc. — /
This is the speech of <s>Bhīmasena</s>, who is enraged and has vowed to slay a hundred <s>Kauravas</s>; for this very reason, some say that in 'I shall not churn' etc. there is <s>viparītalakṣaṇā</s> — she presents that — '<s>viparīta</s>' etc. /
The connection is: the cognition of the negation is as that which is itself being negated — 'thus.' /
The reason for postulating <s>kāku</s> — '<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>' etc. /
The meaning is: the impossibility, i.e., the intolerability, of the path of peace desired by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> — [this] intention residing in <s>Bhīma</s> — by that. /
'Thus' etc. — /
This is the purport: it is not that the negation of churning etc. is first cognized and then the negation of that negation, [producing] 'I shall indeed churn' — rather, at the very time of utterance, through the force of <s>kāku</s>, the negation of churning etc. is cognized as the counterpart of its own negation — i.e., 'I shall not not churn' — the cognition is not piecemeal; therefore the negation of the expressed, which is the negation [of action], is suggested alone.

children.text: pramukha evānyatarāvadhāraṇaniyamāsambhavo yatra yuktiparāmarśaṃ tatra yasya yuktisahāyatā tatra tena vyapadeśaḥ kartavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Where, at the very outset, the determination of one or the other [as predominant] is not possible, there, through recourse to reasoning, the designation should be made in accordance with whichever [category] reasoning supports.
One need not always be a partisan of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: yathā--- patyuḥ śiraścandrakalāmanena spṛśeti sakhyā parihāsapūrvam /
children.translated_text: For example — 'By this [lac-dye], touch the crescent-moon on the husband's head' — said by her friend in jest.

children.text: sā rañjayitvā caraṇau kṛtāśīrmākhyena tāṃ nirvacanaṃ jaghāna //

children.translated_text: The meaning is: <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation).
Intending both that the word '<s>uccaiḥ</s>' denotes something situated in an elevated position and that it qualifies the flowers, she explains — '<s>uccaiḥ</s>' means 'the high ones' etc.

children.text: yathā ca--- prāyacchatoccaiḥ kusumāni māninī vipakṣagotraṃ dayitena lambhitā /
children.translated_text: And as in — 'The jealous woman (<s>māninī</s>) offered high flowers, having been addressed by her beloved with the name of her rival's family;

children.text: na kiñcidūce caraṇena kevalaṃ lileśa bāṣpākulalocanā bhuvam //
children.translated_text: she said nothing, and merely traced the ground with her foot, her eyes agitated with tears.' //

[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Of the husband' — /
'By this' — for the moon, reddened with lac-dye, would not gain superiority [over the wife's feet] without propitiating [the husband] through unceasing falling at his feet — and thus there is also the instruction that one should not instantly become submissive to the husband at his every wish. /
The crescent-moon that is borne on the head — even that she humiliates — thus the defeat of the co-wife in the eyes of the world is stated. /
'Silently' — /
Although by this [word], modesty, concealed joy, jealousy, timidity, pride in one's fortune, etc. are suggested, nevertheless, the word-meaning of 'silently' — expressing a quality appropriate to a young woman, with the characteristic of not being explicitly stated — merely performs the function of embellishing [the expressed meaning]. /
The expressed meaning, thus embellished, attains the status of being an ancillary to <s>śṛṅgāra</s> — and so /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Without' — the meaning is: without that domain. /
Since the logical entity denoted by 'reasoning' — as accepted by logicians — is not possible here, she explains that word — 'beauty' etc. /
'Here' — in this domain of inquiry into the truth of poetic meaning. /
If the aesthetic delight (<s>camatkāra</s>) of the mind comes from the expressed meaning alone embellished by the suggested, then it is <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion); but when it comes from the suggested meaning itself which has subordinated the expressed, then it is <s>dhvani</s> — thus the determination of one or the other is accomplished through the force of the effect in the form of the cognition of beauty — this is the meaning. /
She shows the two suggested meanings conveyed by [the text] up to 'touch' — 'lac-dye' etc. /
'Gaining superiority' — /
The purport is: because the moon is extremely white and the lac-dye is red [i.e., the lac reddening represents supremacy over the moon]. /
Having stated the suggested meaning [that is] the qualification-component of being reddened with lac-dye, she states the suggested meaning [arising] from the instruction to touch the head with the foot — 'without ceasing' etc. /
'Instantly' — /
The meaning is: by the force of compulsion arising from the unsurpassable natural passion. /
She states the suggested meaning supported by the qualification of the feminine gender marker and the designation of the head — 'that which is borne on the head' etc. /
'Is stated' — the meaning is: is suggested. /
She demonstrates the suggested meaning shown by the <s>Vṛtti</s> passage beginning with 'silently,' and its subordination — 'by this' etc. /
'By this' — by 'she silently struck.' /
'That' — the meaning is: the class of suggested meanings such as modesty etc. /
'Appropriate to a young woman' — /
By this, the capacity of the expressed meaning to produce aesthetic delight is shown. /
'But the expressed meaning, thus embellished' — /
The meaning is: the expressed meaning 'she silently struck,' embellished by the stated suggested meaning. /
'<s>Śṛṅgāra</s>' —

children.translated_text: 'Here, however' — in 'of the husband' etc.
'Of the expressed meaning too' —
The word '<s>api</s>' (too) is in inverted order [i.e., applies to something earlier in the sentence].
The qualifier of the word '<s>dhvani</s>' is not stated [explicitly]. // 39 //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Here, through the negation-mode expressions 'silently struck' and 'said nothing,' since the suggested meaning has been somewhat objectified through statement, only its subordination (<s>guṇībhāva</s>) is fitting. /
When the suggested meaning is apprehended through purport without oblique expression (<s>vakrokti</s>), then it has predominance. /
As in '<s>evaṃ vādini devarṣau</s>' (while the divine sage was speaking thus) and similar [passages]. /
Here, however, there is the oblique mode of expression — therefore the expressed meaning too has predominance. /
Consequently, the designation of reverberation-type suggested <s>dhvani</s> should not be applied here. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'She offered' — /
'<s>Uccaiḥ</s>' — /
The meaning is: the high flowers — [those growing on high branches] — [were] requested by the beloved herself, since she could not pluck them on her own. /
Our teachers, however, [explain it as]: the most delightful flowers, [offered] in a loud voice saying 'in such-and-such [container], take them, take them!' — by one who is offering with excessive devotion. /
Precisely therefore 'addressed' [was used]. /
'Said nothing' — /
In occasions of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> of this sort — 'he remembers only her' — thus the display of jealous anger (<s>māna</s>) is itself not appropriate here — therefore a surpassing accumulation of wrath is suggested; the expressed meaning of the denial of speech is merely an embellishment [of this]. /
This he will state — 'there is the oblique mode of expression.' /
'Of that' — of the suggested.

children.translated_text: The purport is: otherwise it would be contradictory.
'Qualifier' —
The meaning is: the qualifier 'reverberation' (<s>anuraṇana</s>) etc.
The purport is: that qualifier indicates that the nature of <s>dhvani</s> in the form of the imperceptibly-sequenced suggested meaning exists here too. // 3.9 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She states that suggested meaning through its qualifier — 'by the beloved herself' etc. /
The meaning of the word '<s>uccaiḥ</s>' as denoting 'in a loud voice' and as qualifying the act of giving is her preferred [interpretation] — she says: 'our [teachers]' etc. /
'In such-and-such' — /
The meaning is: a receptacle such as the palm of the hand etc. /
The connection is with 'flowers.' /
The explanation of '<s>uccaiḥ</s>' — 'in a loud voice.' /
She states that the reason for giving in a loud voice is the indication of excessive devotion — 'devotion' etc. /
She adduces another word to strengthen the coherence of the stated meaning — 'precisely therefore' etc. /
'Precisely therefore' — precisely because of the giving of flowers in a loud voice. /
Showing the purpose of 'she said nothing,' she states the suggested meaning — 'in occasions of this sort' etc. /
'Display of jealous anger' — the purport is: through <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) such as the rolling of eyes etc. /
'That' — /
The meaning is: the suggested meaning being subordinated to the expressed meaning, it acquires the character of being expressed. /
'In inverted order' —
This type, though [classified as] subordinated suggestion (<s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>), assumes the form of <s>dhvani</s>
when reconsidered from the perspective of the purport of <s>rasa</s> etc. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.40 //

children.translated_text: 'Me' —
The meaning is: even me, who am standing right before [you].
The connection with 'you consider' is also with 'not.'

children.text: kaṭhoraṃ strīcetastadalamupacārairvirama he kriyātkalyāmaṃ vo hariranunayaṣvevamuditaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'A woman's heart is hard — enough of these attentions! Desist, O you! May <s>Hari</s>, thus addressed in [the affairs of] love, bestow auspiciousness upon you!' //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Even the variety of poetry classified as <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>, when reconsidered from the perspective of the purport of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc., becomes <s>dhvani</s> itself. /
As in the two verses just cited above. /
And as in — '<s>Rādhā</s> is hard to propitiate, O fortunate one! Though you wipe away with the garment of <s>Ajādhana</s> (the One for whom <s>Ajā</s> is wealth = <s>Śiva</s>), your Lord of Life, even by that, this tear has fallen.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'This very' — /
The meaning is: that very thing which was formulated — the <s>dhvani</s>-nature of <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> in the domain of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
'Of equal lustre' — /
In 'of the husband' etc. and 'she offered' etc., since the subordination to the expressed meaning in the form of the denial of speech — which is the expressed meaning — is understood for the <s>bhāva-dhvani</s> in both, they have equal lustre. /
'Hard to propitiate' — /
O fortunate one! This tear that has fallen — by you who wipe it away even with the garment of your Lord of Life, <s>Ajādhana</s> — [still] <s>Rādhā</s> is hard to propitiate — a woman's heart is hard — enough of these attentions! O you, desist! Thus addressed in [the affairs of] love, may <s>Hari</s> bestow auspiciousness upon you — this is the syntactic connection. /
In the <s>Locana</s>, intending to explain the verse, she prepares the ground — 'without cause' etc. /
She formulates the class of suggested meanings belonging to the words of the verse — 'O fortunate one' etc. /
'Who' — 'you' is the completion. /
'You cannot' — /
The meaning is: thus is the intention residing in <s>Rādhā</s>. /
'Is suggested' — is the completion. /
The same should be understood in what follows too. /
She states another suggested meaning — 'that very thing, and' etc. /
'This' is to be connected. /
She clarifies 'thus cherished' — 'that which' etc. /
By the present-tense suffix in 'wiping,' indicating the non-cessation of the wiping, she states the suggested meaning — 'by this, on the contrary' etc. /
She states the suggested meaning of the stem-component — 'and this much' etc.

children.translated_text: As in this very verse, the word '<s>Rāvaṇa</s>' has the suggestive power belonging to another subdivision [of <s>dhvani</s>]. /

children.text: yatra tu vākye rasāditātparye nāsti guṇībhūtavyaṅgyaiḥ padairudbhāsite 'pi tatra guṇībhūtavyaṅgyataiva samudāyadharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: But where the sentence does not have <s>rasa</s> etc. as its purport, even when individual words exhibiting <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion) shine forth, there the <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-status alone is the property of the whole. /
For example — 'They serve even kings, they consume even poison, /

children.text: ramante ca saha strībhiḥ kuśalāḥ khalu mānavāḥ //
children.translated_text: and they sport with women — skilled indeed are men!' //

[Locana:] 'That you, having forgotten me, consider her alone as the angry one' — /
otherwise, how could you do this? /
'Has fallen' — /
The meaning is: now even the occasion for weeping has passed. /
But if it is said: 'with even this much regard, why do you not relinquish your anger?' — then what can be done? The heart of a woman is hard by nature. /
For 'woman' — this is merely a particular thing, devoid of the conjunction of love etc.; and this is its nature. 'Within herself' — thus women, though tender-hearted, [are obstinate] — there is nothing [harder] than diamond that their heart [resembles], since even upon witnessing such an episode, it does not split into a thousand pieces. /
'By courtesies' — /
by those prompted by gallantry. /
'In attempts at reconciliation' — by the plural, the indication is that time and again this is the settled behavior of this man of many beloveds — thus his surpassing good fortune is stated. /
Thus this cluster of suggested meanings adorns the expressed meaning. /
But that adorned expressed meaning — it has the status of a component of jealous <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation marked by jealousy) — thus. /
But he who explained the component-status with respect to <s>rasa</s> of the suggested meaning alone in all three verses — /
he sold the deity and performed the festival of pilgrimage in its honor. /
For thus, the subordinate status of the suggested that is the subject [of this discussion] would be completely uprooted. /
For the subordination of the suggested meaning — which is other than <s>rasa</s> etc. — operates precisely through its being a component of <s>rasa</s>. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] By 'has fallen,' using the past tense, she states the suggested meaning — 'has passed' etc. /
Intending to elaborate on 'hard' etc., she says — 'but if' etc. /
'Why do you not relinquish' — after this, 'thus' is to be supplied. /
'If it is said thus' — this is the connection. /
'Then, in that case.' /
'Woman' — she states that suggested meaning — 'devoid of love' etc. /
'For this is "woman"' — this is the connection. /
'This' — /
the meaning is: hard-heartedness. /
Having thus stated the suggested meaning directed toward the addressee, she states the suggested meaning pertaining to <s>Rādhā</s> — 'within herself' etc. /
'Within herself, and this' — /
the meaning is: the suggested meaning pertaining to <s>Rādhā</s> that is about to be stated. /
'Thus' — /
the meaning is: 'thus much' — this is the meaning. /
'Not anything' — /
the meaning is: not ultimately [so]. /
She states the component-status of the stated class of suggested meanings with respect to both the expressed meaning and its <s>rasa</s> — 'thus' etc. /
She restates the alternative interpretation — 'but he who' etc. /
'Of the suggested meaning alone' — /
by the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone), the expressed meaning embellished by the suggested is excluded. /
'He explained' — /
the intention of this interpreter is: since subordination with respect to that whose primary and principal [status is established] is improper, and since <s>rasa</s> alone has that primacy, this interpretation is not the better one — she shows this by way of a mocking expression — 'he sold the deity' etc. /
Just as someone, out of poverty, having sold the deity, procured money and undertook to perform the festival of pilgrimage in its honor — so too one who set out to establish <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion) has resorted to a certain method that contradicts it — thus the great mastery of this one! — this is the mockery. /
'This too' — [the objection] 'how would it be uprooted?' — to this she says — 'for the suggested' etc. /
The suggested meaning other than <s>rasas</s> etc., consisting of <s>vastu</s> (subject matter) and <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament), /
its component-status — /
The meaning is: it is precisely the fitness to be a component of <s>rasa</s> [that constitutes subordination]; therefore, in that [subordination], primacy indeed accrues — it is not subordination. /
Thus being established, in the verse beginning with '<s>nyakkāro hy ayam eva</s>' ('this indeed is the humiliation'), the words — though they convey the expressed meaning qualified by the suggested — with respect to the <s>raudra rasa</s> (furious aesthetic sentiment) that has become the sentence-meaning, suggestive power is stated. /
One should not create the confusion that those words have <s>dhvani</s> in the form of expressed meaning transferred to another meaning (<s>arthāntarasaṃkramitavācya</s>), because they have the status of <s>vivakṣitavācya</s> (intended expressed meaning). /
For in those [words], the expressed meaning's being qualified by the suggested is perceived, not its transformation into the form of the suggested. /
Therefore, the sentence there is <s>dhvani</s>, but the individual words are <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion). /
And not only are the words that are <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> alone the suggestors of the <s>dhvani</s> whose latent sequence is imperceptible (<s>alakṣyakrama-vyaṅgya</s>), but even those having expressed meaning transferred to another meaning, which are forms of <s>dhvani</s> subdivision, [can be suggestors]. /

children.translated_text: 'With infinite' — /
the meaning is: with infinite, i.e., unlimited, time — the creation which is '<s>tanvī</s>' (slender), i.e., the slender creation — even of the one who makes that — this is the meaning. /

children.text: lāvaṇyadraviṇavyayo na gaṇitaḥ kleśo mahān svīkṛtaḥ svacchandasya sukhaṃ janasya vasataḥ cintānalo dīpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The expenditure of the wealth of <s>lāvaṇya</s> (charm) was not reckoned, great toil was undertaken; of the person living according to his own will, the fire of anxiety was kindled. /

children.text: eṣāpi svayameva tulparamaṇābhāvādvarākī hatā ko 'rthaścetasi vedhasā vinihitastanvyāstanuṃ tanvatā //
children.translated_text: This one too, being pitiable due to the absence of a fitting lover, is herself unfortunate — what purpose was fixed in the mind by <s>Vedhas</s> (the Creator) while fashioning the slender body of this slender maiden? //

[<s>Locana</s>:] Primacy — nothing else — enough of disputation with predecessors. /
'Thus being established' — /
the meaning is: when, by the method just stated, the division between <s>dhvani</s> and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> has been settled. /
He explains the '<s>api</s>' (also/even) word occurring in the <s>kārikā</s> — 'and not only' etc. /
And this verse has already been explained, so it is not written again. /
'But where' etc. — /
Even though here there is the cognition of <s>śānta rasa</s> (the tranquil aesthetic sentiment) in the form of world-weariness (<s>viṣayanirvedātmaka</s>), nevertheless this aesthetic delight (<s>camatkāra</s>) is established in the expressed meaning alone. /
The suggested, however, is the quality of producing effects contrary to what is expected etc. — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] therefore the subordinate status should be stated only with respect to the expressed meaning — this is the purport. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>: 'of the words' etc. /
The suggested meanings have been stated previously. /
'In the <s>raudra rasa</s> (furious sentiment) that has become the sentence-meaning' — /
the meaning is: in the <s>raudra rasa</s>. /
She says incidentally — 'one should not' etc. /
'Not only' — she introduces the passage in the <s>Locana</s> beginning with 'the <s>kārikā</s>' — '<s>kārikā</s>' etc. /
The '<s>api</s>' word — the '<s>api</s>' in '<s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> also.' /
'To explain' — /
the purport is: the '<s>api</s>' word includes what is not [otherwise] mentioned. /
Now, in [the verse beginning with] '<s>rājānam</s>' (kings) etc., how can there be absence of <s>rasa</s> etc. as purport? /
Since the worldly activity of king-service etc., being characterized as equivalent to consuming poison, through engendering weariness toward all worldly activity, has the capacity to suggest <s>śānta rasa</s> (tranquil sentiment) — she restates the objection and resolves it — 'even though' etc. /
'This' — /
the meaning is: experienced by connoisseurs. /
'Established in the expressed meaning' — /
the meaning is: since they even serve kings etc., the expressed meaning — that men are skilled — conveys [this], i.e., it is prompted by the expressed meaning. /
In the [passage beginning with] 'etc.' /
Great effort must be made regarding the discrimination of primacy and non-primacy of the expressed and suggested, by which the domains of <s>dhvani</s>, <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, and the <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech) become clearly known without confusion. /
Otherwise, confusion arises even in the domain of well-known <s>alaṅkāras</s>. /
As in — [<s>Locana</s>:] belonging to that very [expressed meaning]; and that is touched — merely suggested — by the two '<s>api</s>' words connected on both sides, by the '<s>ca</s>' word connected with three positions, by the '<s>khalu</s>' word connected on both sides, and by the word '<s>mānava</s>' (man) — and therefore it is subordinated. /
And she shows that this discrimination is not without use — 'of the expressed and suggested' etc. /
'And of the <s>alaṅkāras</s>' — /
where there is no suggested meaning at all, there the pure [<s>alaṅkāras</s>] have primacy. /
'Otherwise' — /
the meaning is: if one were not assiduous [in discrimination]. /
The type of suggested meaning that I had previously conjectured — that itself is undoubtedly a locus of confusion — this is the intent of the '<s>eva</s>' word. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] By the '<s>eva</s>' word, the exclusion is of being established in <s>śānta rasa</s>. /
Now, even so, here the quality of inconceivability, producing-effects-contrary-to-expectation, etc. is suggested. /
And from that alone comes the aesthetic delight — therefore she says — 'the suggested, however' etc. /
'Contrary' — /
the meaning is: producing effects contrary to the intended result. /
'Belonging to that very [expressed meaning]' — /
the meaning is: belonging to the expressed meaning alone. /
'It follows' — is subordinate. /
She establishes that very [point] by showing the reason — 'and that' etc. /
And that is touched — merely suggested — the connection is thus. /
'Connected on both sides by the two <s>api</s> words' — /
the meaning is: '<s>rājānam api sevante</s>' (they serve even kings), '<s>api</s>'; '<s>viṣamam api upabhuñjate</s>' (they consume even poison), '<s>api</s>' — connected by action and object. /
Now, '<s>rāja</s>' (king) — a subject [that is] foremost among things difficult to approach. /
The action of service — even by those with composed minds, difficult to perform because of the ease of downfall at every moment. /
Likewise in other cases too, this should be understood. /
'Connected with three positions by the <s>ca</s> word' — /
Since one indicator-word serves for many according to the principle 'the last [indicator serves for all],' '<s>ramante ca</s>' (and they sport) — the '<s>ca</s>' word, being a connective, is connected with the three actions — this is the meaning. /
'Connected on both sides by the <s>khalu</s> word' — /
the meaning is: the '<s>khalu</s>' word should be connected with both '<s>kuśalā</s>' (skilled) and '<s>mānavāḥ</s>' (men). /
'And by the word <s>mānava</s>' — this is the construction. /
'Touched' — /
the meaning is: slightly illuminated. /
'Thus' — for this reason. /
Regarding 'and of the <s>alaṅkāras</s>' — where there is no suggested meaning at all, there the pure ones have primacy — she says: 'where' etc. /
'Of those' — /
the meaning is: of the <s>alaṅkāras</s>. /
The '<s>eva</s>' in 'in the domain of well-known <s>alaṅkāras</s> alone' — by the '<s>eva</s>' word, she says — 'how much more so in the domain of the suggested' — showing this meaning — 'the type of suggested meaning' etc. /
'Conjectured' — having imagined, shown. /
'Locus of confusion' — domain of confusion. /
She shows the suggested meanings of the words in the cited verse — '<s>draviṇa</s>' etc. /
'By the word <s>draviṇa</s>' — /
the meaning is: through the superimposition of the status of wealth upon <s>lāvaṇya</s> (charm/beauty). /
'Stated' — /
the meaning is: suggested with reference to <s>lāvaṇya</s>. /
Not having said '<s>vidita</s>' (known) but having said '<s>gaṇita</s>' (calculated), she states the suggested meaning — 'with long [time]' etc. /
'There' — /
the meaning is: in such an expenditure. /
