yasmādanena vācyena guṇībhūtātmanā nissāmānyaguṇāvalopādhmātasya nijamāhimotkarṣajanitasamatsarajanajvarasya viśeṣajñamātmano na kañcidevāparaṃ paśyataḥ paridevitametaditi prakāśyate /
tathā cāyaṃ dharmakīrteḥ śloka iti prasiddhiḥ /
sambhāvyate ca tasyaiva /
yasmāt-- anadhyavasitāvagāhanamanalpadhīśaktinā- pyadṛṣṭaparamārthatattvamadhikābhiyogairapi /
locanam dhikte kārṣṇyamiti sā paraṃ prastutaparatayeti nātrāsambhava ityāśaṅkyāha--na ceti /
nissāmānyeti nijamahimeti viśeṣajñamiti paridevitamityetaiścaturbhirvākyakhaṇḍaiḥ krameṇa pādacatuṣṭayasya tātparyaṃ vyākhyātam /
nanvatrāpi kiṃ pramāṇamityāśaṅkyāha--tathā ceti /
nanu kimiyatetyāśaṅkya tadāśayena nirvivādatadīyaślokārpitenāsyāśayaṃ saṃvādayati--sambhāvyata iti /
avagāhanamadhyavasitamapi na yatra āstāṃ tasya sampādanam /
bālapriyā locane--krameṇeti /
nissāmānyaguṇetyanena lāvaṇyetyādyapādatātparyārtha uktaḥ, evaṃvadato hyalokasāmānyaguṇagaṇapūrṇatvādaho /
ahamiti mahīyānavalepaḥ parisphuṭaṃ gamyata iti bhāvaḥ /
atrāpīti /
aprastutapraśaṃsāpakṣe 'pītyarthaḥ /
vṛttau--'tathāce'tyādi /
cakāro hetau /
yato 'yaṃ dharmakīrteḥ śloka iti prasiddhiratastathāpūrvoktārthaka ityarthaḥ /
viniścayavṛttyante sthito 'yaṃ śloka iti prasiddhiratastathāpūrvoktārthaka ityarthaḥ /
viniścayavṛttyante sthito 'yaṃ śloka iti śrūyate /
locane--kimityādi /
iyateti /
dharmakīrteḥ śloka ityetāvatetyarthaḥ /
tadāśayena dharmakīrterāśayena /
nirvivādeti /
prakṛtodāharaṇe hi vivādo vyājastutyaprastutapraśaṃsāviṣayo na vakṣyamāṇatadīyaśloka iti bhāvaḥ /
asyeti /
lāvaṇyetyādiprakṛtaślokasyetyarthaḥ /
saṃvādayatīti /
ayaṃ bhāvaḥ--yo yasyāśayo 'nyatra suspaṣṭapratipattikassa eva sambhavan anyatrāparisphuṭapratītike viṣaye 'pyadhyavasātumucita ityato vākyaśeṣanyāyānusāreṇātrāprastutapraśaṃsāvadhāraṇasiddhiriti /
vṛttau--'sambhāvyate ca tasyaive'ti /
śloko 'yaṃ dharmakīrtisambandhitvenaivānumīyate cetyarthaḥ /
atra hetumāha--'yasmāda'tyādi /
'anadhyavasite'ti /
anadhyavasitaṃ sudhībhirna sampipādayiṣitamavagāhanamavabodhaḥ, payaḥpakṣe yadā dānāyāntaḥ praveśo yasya tat /
analpā dhīśaktirbuddhisāmarthyaṃ yasya tenāpyanyena kenacit kartrā /
adhikairabhiyogaiḥ prayatnairapi /

children.translated_text: [The verse continues:] 'wherein the ultimate truths have not been seen' /
the meaning is: wherein the excellent truths of meaning, unprecedented, are contained. /
But in the alternative reading [about milk/ocean], this is elaborated in the <s>Locana</s> — 'not having obtained' etc. /

children.text: mataṃ mama jagatyalabdhasadṛśapratigrāhakaṃ prayāsyati payonidheḥ paya iva svadehe jārām //
children.translated_text: 'My doctrine, having not obtained in the world a recipient equal [to itself], will undergo decay in its own body, like the milk of the ocean.' //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] In this [verse], someone has explained it as '<s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) is the figure' — that is not apt; because if this expressed content were to culminate merely in the form of that figure, there would be no coherent fit. /
For this [utterance] is not, to begin with, the imaginative elaboration of some passionate person (<s>rāgin</s>). /
Because for him, an utterance of such a kind as 'she too, by herself, wretched one, is destroyed due to the absence of an equal lover' is impossible. /
Nor [is it the utterance] of one free from passion (<s>nīrāga</s>) — [<s>Locana</s>:] by the word '<s>draviṇa</s>' (wealth), it is stated that [it amounts to] nearly everything one possesses, and that it serves for multiple purposes. /
'Reckoned' (<s>gaṇita</s>) — /
for that expenditure which is accomplished over a long time, and not instantaneously like lightning — there, reckoning must necessarily be involved. /
But not even a trace of discernment arose in the Creator (<s>vidhi</s>), who engages in creation over infinite time — this [implies] the supreme thoughtlessness of the Supreme [Being]. /
For this very reason he says: 'great is the toil.' /
'Of the self-willed one' — /
the meaning is: of the unrestrained one. /
'She too' — /
that what is created by oneself is itself destroyed — this great disparity is expressed by the word '<s>api</s>' (also/even) and by the particle '<s>va</s>.' /
'What purpose' — /
the meaning is: neither for oneself, nor for the world, nor for the created [being]. /
'Of him' — /
for a passionate man, the words 'wretched one, destroyed' (<s>varākī hatā</s>) — a speech tinged with pitifulness and tainted with inauspiciousness — [are inappropriate]. /
'Due to the absence of an equal lover' — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'did not arise' — /
the purport is: because of not reckoning that. /
'Of this Creator' — /
'Thoughtlessness' (<s>aprekṣāvattva</s>) — acting without deliberation. /
'Was stated' is carried over. /
Indicating the suggestive sign for the intention of [denying] the instantaneousness of creation, she says: 'for this very reason' etc. /
She says that of the three [things] stated in the three quarters [of the verse], no single purpose appropriate to any one [of them] is discernible upon examination — 'neither for oneself' etc. /
'Purpose' is carried over. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>: '<s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) is the figure' — /
the purport is: because through the medium of censure, praise of the heroine is apprehended. /
'There is no coherent fit' — /
the meaning is: good congruence does not obtain. /
Here she states the reason — 'because' etc. /
'This' — /
the meaning is: as stated in the verse. /
'Imaginative elaboration' (<s>vikalpa</s>) — subject of varied imagination. /
'Not' — here the reason is stated: 'of him' etc. /
How is the impossibility of such an utterance for a passionate person [established]? She justifies this in the <s>Locana</s>: 'for a passionate man indeed' etc. /
'Wretched one' — a speech embraced by pitifulness; 'destroyed' — tainted by inauspiciousness; such speech is indeed inappropriate for a passionate man — this is the syntactic connection. /
The purport is: for a passionate man, having his mental activity immersed in her, esteeming her alone, relishing the nectar of the beauty of her form — how could he consider her pitiableness or inauspiciousness? /
'Due to the absence of an equal lover' — /
the speech of a passionate man is carried over. /
'For oneself' — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] for oneself — utterly inappropriate. /
Even for oneself, if there were the impossibility of [finding] a counterpart of her form, and [yet] passionate attachment — it would amount to being nearly animalistic. /
Objection: even for a passionate man, [consider] one who has adopted a vow for a limited period due to some cause, or one like <s>Rāvaṇa</s> regarding <s>Sītā</s> etc., or one like <s>Duṣyanta</s> regarding <s>Śakuntalā</s> etc. whose specific birth was not ascertained — would not this utterance, pregnant with pride in one's own good fortune and pregnant with praise of her, be possible? /
Or, for one free from passion — by reason of being colored by the residual impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) of passion from beginningless time, even while standing neutral, actually perceiving her thus — this utterance is not to be deemed impossible. /
For one free from passion does not perceive things in a distorted manner. /
For the sound of a <s>vīṇā</s> does not appear to him as resembling the cawing of a crow. /
Therefore, following the subject at hand, this utterance is possible for both [types of persons]. /
Even in <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant), the irrelevant meaning that is stated must be one that is [actually] possible; for in [the case of a subject like] brilliance/fire, <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> of this kind is not possible — oh — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'truly' — or alternatively, the meaning is: relating to one's own self. /
'Utterly inappropriate' — /
let there be the conceivability of the absence of an equal lover with respect to other people; but the conceivability of that with respect to oneself too is not proper — hence that speech is utterly inappropriate — this is the meaning. /
Whence this impropriety? To this she says: 'even for oneself' etc. /
'Impossibility of [finding] a counterpart of her form' — /
the meaning is: when there is the absence of conceiving a beauty proportionate to hers. /
Or the meaning is: when there is the absence of conceiving the possibility of being an equal lover. /
'When there is passionate attachment' — when there is passion toward her. /
Showing how, if this verse were contained within a larger composition, the meaning would be constructed to accord with the context, she introduces the text 'nor' etc. — 'objection' etc. /
'Even for a passionate man, this utterance is it not possible?' — this is the syntactic connection; the meaning is: it is indeed possible. /
Objection: but the impossibility [of such an utterance for him] was already stated! To this she says: 'due to some cause' etc. /
'Pregnant with pride in one's own good fortune' — /
but 'due to the absence of an equal lover' [is understood] with respect to people other than oneself — this is the purport. /
Having justified [its being] the utterance of a passionate person, she justifies [its being] the utterance of one free from passion — 'free from passion' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: this utterance of one free from passion is not not to be deemed possible — i.e., it is indeed possible. /
Here she states the reason — 'from beginningless time' etc. /
'Actually perceiving her thus' — perceiving her as endowed with unsurpassable beauty and other qualities. /
And from such perception, due to the force of the residual impression of former passion, such an utterance is indeed possible — this is the meaning. /
She justifies the statement 'actually perceiving thus' — 'for not indeed' etc. /
She concludes — 'therefore' etc. /
'Of both' — of the passionate and of the one free from passion. /
To corroborate what was stated, she says: 'in <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> also' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: the irrelevant meaning that is stated must be one that is possible. /
She establishes what was stated through a counter-example — 'for not' etc. /
'In brilliance/fire' — in a subject that is the relevant fire/brilliance. /
She states the distinction — 'that' etc. /
'That' — that <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>. /
'Having [the relevant as] its purpose' — having the purport directed toward the relevant meaning. /
'Thus' — in the sense of a reason. /
'Here' — /
the meaning is: in [the verse beginning with] 'in beauty' etc. /
'There is no impossibility' — /
'of the expressed content' is the remainder. /
But rather, there is possibility in the manner stated — this is the purport. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>: '<s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>' — /
the meaning is: <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> based on resemblance. /
'With the subordinated self' (<s>guṇībhūtātman</s>) — /
the meaning is: serving as a means. /
Here, since the expressed meaning embellished by the suggested [meaning] alone has primacy, it should be understood as the figure <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>. /
Because its sole function is the removal of such inappropriate construals. /
Nor is this verse heard [as being] in any composition, such that the context-appropriate meaning could be constructed for it. /
Therefore this is <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>. /
For through this expressed [meaning], which has a subordinated nature, the lamentation of one who — through the observation of extraordinary qualities free from any commonality, [and whose] unique exalted greatness generates the fever of jealousy in people — perceiving himself as the expert [alone] and seeing no other equal — is revealed. /
And thus, there is the well-known tradition that this is a verse of <s>Dharmakīrti</s>. /
And it is plausible as his alone. /
Because — 'a comprehension not undertaken [by anyone], even by one of no small intellectual power,' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] '[Your intellect] has the blackness' — that [<s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>], since it is supremely directed toward the relevant [meaning] — 'hence there is no impossibility here' — anticipating this objection, he says: 'nor' etc. /
By '<s>nissāmānya</s>' (without commonality), '<s>nijamahima</s>' (unique exalted greatness), '<s>viśeṣajña</s>' (the discerning expert), and '<s>paridevita</s>' (lamentation) — by these four sentence-segments, the purport of the four quarters [of the verse] is explained in sequence. /
Objection: what is the authority here? Anticipating this, he says: 'and thus' etc. /
Objection: what does this amount to? Anticipating this, by his [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>'s] intention, using an undisputed verse that belongs to him, he corroborates the intention of this [verse] — 'it is plausible' etc. /
'A comprehension not undertaken' — comprehension, i.e., understanding, not undertaken, i.e., not wished to be accomplished by the wise; in the alternative reading [about milk/ocean], when for the sake of giving, the entry within [the ocean] is [what is meant]; of that. /
'By one of no small intellectual power' — by anyone else, another agent, even of no small intellectual power, i.e., of considerable mental capacity. /
'Even with extraordinary efforts' — even with excessive exertions. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In the <s>Locana</s>: 'in sequence' — /
by '<s>nissāmānyaguṇa</s>' (extraordinary qualities), the purport of the first quarter beginning with '<s>lāvaṇya</s>' (beauty) is stated; for when one speaks thus, the self-aggrandizing pride [arising from the thought] 'I am great' because of being full of a constellation of qualities not common to [ordinary] people — is clearly apprehended — this is the purport. /
'Here too' — /
the meaning is: in the interpretation as <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> as well. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>: 'and thus' etc. /
The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) is in the sense of a reason. /
Since this is well known as a verse of <s>Dharmakīrti</s>, therefore it has the previously stated meaning — this is the meaning. /
It is heard that this verse stands at the end of the <s>Viniścayavṛtti</s>. /
In the <s>Locana</s>: 'what' etc. /
'This much' — /
the meaning is: by this much alone, that it is a verse of <s>Dharmakīrti</s>. /
'By his intention' — by the intention of <s>Dharmakīrti</s>. /
'Undisputed' — /
the purport is: in the present illustration, the dispute concerns whether it is <s>vyājastuti</s> or <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>, not about the verse of his that is to be cited. /
'Of this' — /
the meaning is: of the verse under discussion beginning with '<s>lāvaṇya</s>' (beauty). /
'He corroborates' — /
the purport is this: the intention that is of someone and that is clearly understood elsewhere — that very [intention], being possible, is fit to be inferred even in another domain of unclear understanding — hence, following the principle of sentence-completion (<s>vākyaśeṣanyāya</s>), the determination as <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> here too is established. /
In the <s>Vṛtti</s>: 'and it is plausible as his alone' — /
the meaning is: this verse is inferred as being connected to <s>Dharmakīrti</s> alone. /
Here she states the reason — 'because' etc. /
'Not undertaken' — /
a comprehension, i.e., understanding, not wished to be accomplished by the wise — the entry within [the ocean] that is not undertaken — of that. /
'Of no small intellectual power' — of one whose intellectual capacity is not small — even by such another agent. /
'Even with extraordinary efforts' — even with excessive exertions. /

evaṃvidha iti /

children.translated_text: He states that the verse beginning with '<s>anadhyavasita</s>' also finds repose in <s>vīrarasa</s> (the heroic sentiment) — 'of the other' and so forth.

children.text: aprastutapraśaṃsāyāṃ ca yadvācyaṃ tasya kadācidvivakṣitatvaṃ, kadācidavivākṣitatvaṃ, kadācidvivakṣitāvivakṣitatvamiti trayī bandhacchāyā /
children.translated_text: In <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (indirect praise), the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) is sometimes intended (<s>vivakṣita</s>), sometimes unintended (<s>avivakṣita</s>), and sometimes both intended and unintended (<s>vivakṣitāvivakṣita</s>) — thus there is a threefold range of compositional possibilities.

children.text: tatra vivakṣitatvaṃ yathā-- parārthe yaḥ pīḍāmanubhavati bhaṅge 'pi madhuro yadīyaḥ sarveṣāmiha khalu vikāro 'pyabhimataḥ /
children.translated_text: Of these, an example of the intended (<s>vivakṣita</s>) type: 'He who endures suffering for the sake of others, who is sweet even when broken, whose transformation is indeed desired by all here —

children.text: na samprāpto vṛrddhi yadi sa bhṛśamakṣetrapatitaḥ kimikṣordeṣo 'sau na punaraguṇāyā marubhuvaḥ //
children.translated_text: if he has not attained growth, he has surely fallen on barren ground. Is the fault that of the sugarcane (<s>ikṣu</s>)? No, rather it is of the unmeritorious desert (<s>marubhūmi</s>).'

<s>Locana</s>: By this verse too, precisely this kind of intent has been made manifest. 'Supreme' — the essential truth of meaning (<s>arthatattva</s>) that is superior even to the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem and the like; 'not obtained' — even though sought with effort, not attained; 'of matching worth' — whose counterpart is of such nature; 'each recipient' — each individual receiver, i.e., each aquatic creature, being comparable to <s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>, and <s>Dhanvantari</s> — in such a place, that which has not obtained a worthy recipient. 'Of this kind' means: the subject matter is lamentation. And in this much of the meaning, there is a pair of <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech), namely <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (indirect praise) and <s>upamā</s> (simile). What follows, however, is repose in <s>adbhuta</s> (the marvelous), through being an abode of wonder in oneself. <s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'Of the other' — this work (<s>grantha</s>) that demonstrates my view, a view of such nature. 'Not obtained' — a worthy recipient equal to oneself, one who would enlighten others and himself understand — whose such counterpart does not exist. 'Will undergo old age in its own body' — will become worn out. By 'not figuratively apprehended' (<s>anadhyavasita</s>), through an a fortiori argument (<s>kaimutya</s>), he states the meaning obtained — in the <s>Locana</s>: 'Let alone' and so forth. 'Of that' means: of the immersion, is the meaning. The gloss on 'supreme' is: 'the essential truth of meaning that is superior even to the <s>Kaustubha</s> and the like.' 'Unseen' — because the supreme essential truth of meaning found therein is superior and unseen elsewhere — this is the purport. With the intention that by prohibiting its attainment, the search for means to it is established, he says: 'with effort' and so forth. 'Of matching worth' — 'thing' is to be supplied. 'Of such nature, each recipient' — 'each' (<s>prati</s>) is an indeclinable compound (<s>avyayībhāva</s>) in the sense of distributive repetition (<s>vīpsā</s>). 'An <s>avyayībhāva</s> compound' takes neuter gender according to the rule. The gloss on 'each' is: 'each individual.' The word 'receiver' (<s>grāha</s>) here is not in its primary meaning, but is used in a transferred sense through connection with the quality of being an aquatic creature — hence he says: 'aquatic creature' and so forth. The meaning is: a thing comparable to aquatic creatures like <s>Airāvaṇa</s> (crocodile) and others is not found elsewhere. 'In this much of the meaning' means: in the expressed meaning (<s>vācyārtha</s>) of the two stated verses. '<s>Aprastuta</s>' and so forth — in the verse beginning with '<s>lāvaṇya</s>' there is <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (indirect praise), and in the verse beginning with '<s>anadhyavasita</s>' there is <s>upamā</s> (simile) — thus there is a pair of figures consisting of these, is the meaning. 'What follows, however' means: after the cognition of the beautiful expressed meaning adorned by the stated <s>alaṅkāras</s>. 'In oneself' — the speaker <s>Dharmakīrti</s> is the referent of the word 'self' here. 'Wonder' means: by being the object of wonder. In the verse beginning with '<s>lāvaṇya</s>,' by demonstrating his own fullness of worldly virtues, and in the verse beginning with '<s>anadhyavasita</s>,' by demonstrating his being the promulgator of such a doctrine — through conveying his own supreme superiority over all, wonder directed at oneself is generated in the listener of those verses — this is the purport. Alternatively: 'by being an abode of wonder' means: by being the locus of wonder. Because the condition described in those verses — of oneself, of one's own doctrine — such a pitiable state, inconceivable even in a dream, has come to pass, there is self-directed wonder. 'Repose in <s>adbhuta</s> (the marvelous)' means: through the connoisseurs' (<s>sahṛdayas</s>') savoring of that wonder — this is the purport.

children.translated_text: the possibility of the expressed meaning (<s>vācyārtha</s>) — this is the meaning.
And this should be understood in the manner previously stated.
In the <s>vṛtti</s> (auto-commentary): 'In <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (indirect praise).'

children.text: nirāloke loke kathamidamaho cakṣuradhunā samaṃ jātaṃ sarvairna samamathavānyairavayavaiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'In a world devoid of light, how is it that this eye has now come into being, equal to all [other eyes]? Or rather, not equal to the other limbs.'

'Or, as in my own verse: "These that are seen — are they not of beautiful form? Their fruitfulness belongs to the one into whose perception they come even for a moment." <s>Locana</s>: And [the verse also touches] <s>vīrarasa</s> (the heroic sentiment) through arousing enthusiasm (<s>utsāha</s>) in the audience, by being an object of great reverence and by being attainable only through effort — [the implication being] that such an exceedingly valuable work, benefiting only a few worthy persons, has been produced — thus, by displaying one's own skilful authorship, through a touch of <s>dharmavīra</s> (heroism in righteousness), there is repose in <s>vīrarasa</s>. This should be understood thus; otherwise, what would be accomplished by mere lamentation? And if what were conveyed about oneself were merely thoughtlessness, what would follow from that? Since neither self-benefit nor benefit to others would result — enough of this elaboration. Now, objection: let <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (indirect praise) apply when the literal meaning is incongruous, but here there is indeed congruity — anticipating this, to show that it applies even when there is congruity, he begins: '<s>aprastuta</s>' and so forth. 'Indeed' — meaning: by whom this world is adorned. The fruitfulness of those who have come even for a moment into the perception of whose eye — this is it. <s>Bālapriyā</s>: Two reasons for generating enthusiasm in the audience — 'great reverence' and so forth. 'Of the doctrine' is to be supplied. 'Enthusiasm' means: enthusiasm regarding the acceptance of the doctrine. 'Of such nature' and so forth — 'doctrine' is to be supplied. 'Skilful authorship' means: the authorship of good deeds in the form of creating an excellent doctrine. 'Otherwise' means: in the absence of repose in <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). 'By mere lamentation' — the word 'mere' excludes the previously stated locus of repose. Now, objection: thoughtlessness of oneself has been shown by this, since lamentation about one's own condition everywhere conveys just that — so there is no absence of purpose. To this he responds: 'thoughtlessness' and so forth. The connection of the passage beginning 'Now, in <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>' — since it is incidental, he introduces it thus: 'Now' and so forth. 'Of the meaning as it stands' means: of the expressed meaning as literally heard. 'Incongruity' — impossibility. 'But here' means: in the verse beginning with '<s>lāvaṇya</s>.' 'Congruity' means:

children.translated_text: In the phrase 'you speak as if with detachment,' the word 'as if' (<s>iva</s>) functions to convey the cognition: 'it is understood that you are speaking out of detachment' — this is the meaning.
'How is my detachment known?' — to this he says: 'by the tone of voice' (<s>kākū</s>) and so forth.
<s>Kākū</s> (vocal inflection) means the modification of voice that indicates grief.

children.text: vāmenātra vaṭastamadhvagajanaḥ sarvātmanā sevata na cchāyāpi paropakārakariṇī mārgasthitasyāpi me //
children.translated_text: 'O traveler, worship this banyan (<s>vaṭa</s>) tree with all your heart by an inauspicious path! Not even the shade of me, who stands on the road doing service to others, [is sought].'

For in these two verses, the sugarcane (<s>ikṣu</s>) and the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) are intended in their literal form and yet are not the main subject (<s>prastuta</s>). Since the purport of both verses is to describe the condition of someone possessed of great qualities who has fallen into an unworthy domain and has not attained his due share — [the sugarcane and the eye] are the main subject by implication. An example of the unintended (<s>avivakṣita</s>) type: 'Who are you, sir? I'll tell you — know me as a wretched <s>śākhoṭaka</s> tree, struck by fate. You speak as if with detachment! Well noted — why then is this being told?' <s>Locana</s>: 'Eye' is the syntactic connection. 'Light' also means 'discernment' (<s>viveka</s>). 'Not equal' — for the hand is useful for touching, giving, and receiving, among other things. 'Limbs' means: those that are mostly utterly insignificant. 'Not attained' — one whose superior (<s>para</s>) share, consisting of the gain of wealth or the spreading of fame, has not been reached. 'I'll tell you' and so forth is the reply. By this word he means: this is unspeakable, for when heard it produces <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness); nevertheless, if you insist, then I'll tell you — out of detachment. <s>Bālapriyā</s>: The locus of description of the ostensibly irrelevant meaning — this is the meaning. 'Intended' (<s>vivakṣitatva</s>) — 'of that' is to be connected. 'For the sake of others' — 'suffering' means the pressing of sugarcane, while for a worthy person it means distress. Similarly, 'breaking' means the snapping of stalks, and also calamity caused by lack of wealth. 'Sweetness' means a particular flavor, and also gentleness. 'Transformation' means sugar and the like [from sugarcane], and also emotional states [in a person]. For worthy persons are not to be avoided even in states of anger and the like. 'Barren ground' (<s>akṣetra</s>) means an arid, infertile place, and also a place devoid of discernment and the like. 'Is the fault' and so forth — the fault lies with the desert itself, is the purport. 'These' — 'of them' is the back-reference to 'who,' and 'this' refers back to 'whose.' 'Indeed of beautiful form' — he glosses this in the <s>Locana</s>: 'by whom' and so forth. 'Discernment too' — the word 'too' (<s>api</s>) includes the meaning of physical light; he shows the intended reason for the absence of equality: 'the hand indeed' and so forth. 'This' is illustrative; the feet and the like are also useful for walking and so forth. He states the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgyārtha</s>): 'utterly insignificant' and so forth. By the word 'share' (<s>bhāga</s>), gain of wealth or gain of widespread fame should be understood, since both are expressible by the word 'share' as something deserved — hence he says: 'gain of wealth' and so forth. 'By this' means: by the word 'I'll tell you.' 'He says' means 'he suggests.' He states the reason for unspeakability: 'when heard' and so forth. 'When being heard' — not merely after hearing — the use of the present participle (<s>śatṛ</s> suffix) indicates that hearing itself is a cause of intense <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness).

children.text: na hi vṛkṣaviśeṣeṇa sahoktipratyuktī sambhavata ityavivakṣitābhidheyenaivānena ślokena samṛddhāsatpuruṣasamīpavartino nirdhanasya kasyacinmanasvinaḥ paridevitaṃ tātparyeṇa vākyarthīkṛtamiti pratīyate /

children.translated_text: An example of the type that is both intended and unintended (<s>vivakṣitāvivakṣita</s>):
[Prakrit verse:] 'To the <s>badarī</s> (jujube) trees that have strayed onto the wrong path, devoid of fruit, flowers, and leaves —

children.text: verīeṃ vaiṃ dento pāmara ho ohasijjihasi //
children.translated_text: giving sustenance to enemies, O wretch, you will be laughed at by people.'

Since a dialogue of address and reply with a particular species of tree is not possible, by this verse — in which the denoted meaning is unintended (<s>avivakṣitābhidheya</s>) — the lamentation of some self-respecting but destitute person dwelling near a prosperous but unworthy man is made the purport, rendered into a unified sentence-meaning (<s>vākyārtha</s>), and thus suggested.

children.translated_text: <s>Locana</s>: 'Well noted' is the reply. 'Why?' is a question about the reason for the detachment. 'This is being told' and so forth — the reply begins with a recollection accompanied by <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness), conveying that it must somehow be narrated. 'By an inauspicious one' means: by an improper one; it implies one not distinguished by noble family and the like. 'Banyan' (<s>vaṭa</s>) means: one devoid of fruit-giving and the like, offering only shade, with a rigid trunk — this is the meaning. 'Not even the shade' — for the <s>śākhoṭaka</s> tree is a particular kind of tree whose tendrils and young shoots have been licked by cremation-ground flames. He states the reason for the unintended interpretation here: 'For it is not [possible]' and so forth. 'Prosperous' qualifies 'unworthy person.' <s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'This is being told' — regarding the intention behind the promise to narrate, he says: 'with <s>nirveda</s>' and so forth. Because the object of recollection produces world-weariness, <s>nirveda</s> accompanies the recollection — hence the recollection is said to be 'accompanied by <s>nirveda</s>.' 'Must be narrated' means: the deliberation of finding appropriate words. 'Reply' — this connects with 'this is being told' and so forth. 'By an inauspicious one' — he applies this to the intended meaning: 'by an improper one' and so forth. He states the meaning understood through the semantic force of the word 'banyan' (<s>vaṭa</s>): 'shade' and so forth. 'Devoid' qualifies 'giving' (i.e., a giver devoid of [real generosity]). 'Here' means: in the example beginning with 'who are you?' In the <s>vṛtti</s>: 'on the wrong path.' O wretch, you who give sustenance to such <s>badarī</s> (jujube) trees will be laughed at by people — this is the construal. <s>Badarī</s> is a particular species of tree. '<s>Prācīnāṃ prāntato vṛtti</s>' — thus says <s>Amara</s> [the lexicographer]. After 'is possible,' in some readings 'and not impossible' is also [found]. Here, the expressed meaning is neither entirely possible nor entirely impossible. Therefore, the predominance and subordination of the expressed and suggested meanings must be carefully determined.
When the suggested meaning is thus established through [the states of] primacy and subordination,

children.translated_text: Having thus determined <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) incidentally, he concludes what is the actual topic to be determined — 'therefore' etc.

children.text: aprastutapraśaṃsāyāmapi lāvaṇyetyatra śloke yasmādyvāmoho loksya dṛṣṭastato hetorityarthaḥ // 40 //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: since even in <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>, in this verse beginning with '<s>lāvaṇya</s>' (charm), the infatuation of the world is seen — therefore, for that reason. // 40 //

[<s>Locana</s>:] In this reading, with '<s>samṛddha</s>' (enriched) — by mere enrichment — it should be explained as a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound, not with <s>guṇa</s> etc. /
'Not absolutely' — /
The purport is: it cannot be said that the restriction to being expressed absolutely does not exist, since the suggested [meaning] also has existence. /
Thus: 'of one born in a low family' — means: not born in a such [good] family. /
'Of one who is ugly' — means: devoid of <s>lāvaṇya</s> (charm).

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Having thus determined the nature of the suggested, in order to determine 'what is the status of that which is entirely devoid of it' — he says with 'primacy' etc. /
With a pair of <s>kārikās</s>. /
'Word-<s>citra</s>' — /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] In the text there is the reading 'having the picturesqueness of <s>yamaka</s> (rhyming), <s>cakrabandha</s> (wheel-composition), etc.' /
She explains the passage beginning with '<s>vācyārtha</s>' etc. in terms of its purport in the <s>Locana</s> — 'the restriction to being expressed does not exist.' /
The meaning is: there is no restriction that the expressed meaning does not occur. /
'It cannot be said that it does not exist' — /
The meaning is: it cannot be said that the expressed meaning does not occur at all. /
'From existence' — from being. /

Of 'fruit' etc. — the meaning is: devoid of son, brother, etc. /
She states the suggested meaning of '<s>vṛtti</s>' (livelihood) as 'protection' — with the intention [of showing this], she says — 'even of such a nature' etc. /
'Even of such a nature' — even one who is lowborn and devoid of qualities like charm etc. /
'Is protected' —

children.translated_text: The meaning is: of that which is not the topic at hand.
Objection: let it be the poet's domain; why then [discuss it]? — to this she says — 'and of the poet' etc.
As stated: 'This is indeed the nature of things — that they are not directly [appealing] in themselves;
they become pleasing [only] when they have entered the domain of the speech of good poets.' //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Showing the connection between the preceding and following passages, she introduces the following passage — 'thus' etc. /
'Devoid of that' — /
The meaning is: devoid of suggested meaning. /
'What is the status' — /
The meaning is: what is the usage. /
The construal is: with a pair of <s>kārikās</s>. /
[The threefold division of poetry:] With the mere demonstration of division being accomplished — 'word-<s>citra</s>' and 'meaning-<s>citra</s>' — under the same heading: when the suggested meaning has primacy, [that is] the type of poetry called <s>dhvani</s>; when it has subordinate status, [that is] <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>. /
That which is other than these — devoid of purport directed toward <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc., and lacking the power to illuminate a specific suggested meaning — poetry composed by relying merely on the variety of the expressed and the expressor, resembling a painting — when it appears thus, that is <s>citra</s>. /
That is not primary poetry. /
For it is merely an imitation of poetry. /
Therein, some is word-<s>citra</s> — such as difficult <s>yamaka</s> (rhyming) etc. /
Meaning-<s>citra</s> is that which is other than word-<s>citra</s>, devoid of contact with suggested meaning, primarily established as sentence-meaning, and lacking purport toward <s>rasa</s> etc. — [such as] <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) etc. /
Now, what is this <s>citra</s>? — It is where there is no contact with cognized meaning. /
For the cognized meaning has been previously shown as threefold. /
Therein, where there is no suggestion of subject-matter (<s>vastu</s>) or another figure — that indeed is to be conceived as the domain of <s>citra</s>. /
But where <s>rasa</s> etc. are not outside [the domain] — that type of poetry simply cannot exist. /
Because the absence of contact with subject-matter is untenable for poetry. /
And all worldly subject-matter necessarily attains the status of some <s>rasa</s> or <s>bhāva</s> — at least as a <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant). /
For <s>rasas</s> etc. are specific modifications of the mind, and there is no thing that does not produce a specific modification of the mind — or in the absence of producing one — [<s>Locana</s>:] the purport is: it is well-established that meaning-<s>citra</s> should be considered as equivalent to that [word-<s>citra</s>]. /
'Resembling a painting' — /
The meaning is: devoid of the life-force of <s>rasa</s> etc., and being in the form of a mere replica of the primary [poetry]. /
'Now what is this' — the intention [of raising this] in the form of a censure is what is about to be stated. /
The answer to that here is — 'where not' etc. /
The objector shows his own intention — 'the cognized' etc. /
'Absence of contact with subject-matter' — /
The meaning is: meaninglessness like '<s>ka-ca-ṭa-ta-pa</s>' syllables, or incoherent meaning like 'ten pomegranates' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She states the intention behind the naming — '<s>yamaka</s>' etc. /
'<s>Bandha</s>' etc. is a separate word. /
'It is well-established' — /
The meaning is: since <s>yamaka</s> etc. has the form of a specific arrangement of syllables, its picturesque nature has been determined by the writers on <s>alaṅkāra</s>. /
She states what is the basis for resembling a painting — '<s>rasa</s> etc.' /
'Primary' etc. — /
The meaning is: and being in the form of an imitation of <s>dhvani</s>, possessing beauty created by <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures). /
She shows the reason for the censure in 'what is this' — 'what is about to be stated.' /
She explains 'absence of contact with subject-matter' in two ways — '<s>ka-ca-ṭa-ta-pa</s> syllables' etc. /
'Let it not be' — /
The purport is: because only <s>dhvani</s> and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> are appropriate as the poet's domain. /
She explains the purport — 'of poetry' etc. /
'Is not designated' — /
The purport is: because of the statement 'that is not primary poetry; for it is merely an imitation of poetry.' /
'That' — /
The meaning is: the domain of <s>citra</s>. /
Its status as the poet's domain would not exist — and yet some [type] characterized as <s>citra</s> is being examined as the poet's domain. /
Here it is said: truly there is no such type of poetry where there is no cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. at all. /
Rather, when the poet, devoid of the intention regarding <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc., composes a word-figure or a meaning-figure, then, relative to that intention, the absence of <s>rasa</s> etc. in the meaning is conceived. /
For the meaning of words in poetry is only what has been mounted upon intention. /
And by the force of the expressive capacity of the expressed, even in the absence of the poet's intention, in such a domain, the cognition of <s>rasa</s> etc. that occurs is extremely feeble — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'Let it not be the poet's domain' — anticipating this doubt, he says — 'and it is the poet's domain' etc. /
Even though it is not designated as having the form of poetry, still it must be stated as having been made the poet's domain — because nothing else, comparable to the story of <s>Vāsuki</s>, can be designated here. If it is indeed the poet's domain, then surely it must generate pleasure — and that [pleasure] necessarily culminates in <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transient feelings) — this is the purport. /
'But' — /
The intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>) [must be] with purport directed toward that, not subordinately in any way — /
thus the method of deliberation that was stated regarding the composition of figures — the meaning is: when [the poet] does not follow that. /
'Devoid of <s>rasa</s> etc.' — /
There is no cognition of <s>rasa</s> at all therein — like a meat-dish prepared by a cook ignorant of cooking. /
Objection: due to the beauty of the subject-matter, surely there is sometimes such a tasting, even in a [work] produced by one unskilled — like in a <s>śikhariṇī</s> [verse] — anticipating this doubt, she says — 'of the expressed' etc. /
'By this too' — /
Previously the complete absence of it was stated; now — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'of another' — /
The meaning is: of [something] other than what has been made the poet's domain. /
'Comparable to the story of <s>Vāsuki</s>' —

children.translated_text: The remainder is: of the tasting of <s>rasa</s>.

children.translated_text: By 'it becomes' — by conceiving the <s>nīrasatva</s> (flavorlessness) in another manner, the domain of <s>citra</s> is established.
This has been stated: 'When there is an absence of intention directed toward <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc.,
that which is composed with [only] figures as its foundation — that is considered the domain of <s>citra</s>.' //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Thus' — /
Objection: let it have the capacity to generate pleasure; even so, how [can one claim] the absence of absence-of-<s>rasa</s> etc.? — to this she says — 'and that' etc. /
The purport is: because the specific pleasure born of poetry is necessarily dependent solely on the tasting of <s>rasa</s>. /
She explains the purport of the passage beginning with 'but' — 'intention' etc. /
'When it does not follow' — /
The purport is: by following that [deliberation], in the composition of figures, figures have the nature of being ancillary to <s>rasa</s>. /
She states the purport with an example — 'not at all' etc. /
'Therein' — /
The meaning is: in the domain of figure-composition without following the method of deliberation stated [earlier]. /
'Cognition of <s>rasa</s>' — /
By the word '<s>rasa</s>' (flavor), both <s>rasa</s> such as <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc. and <s>rasa</s> such as sweetness etc. [in food] are intended. /
'Such a tasting' — /
The meaning is: tasting of <s>rasa</s>. /
'Like in a <s>śikhariṇī</s>' — /
<s>Śikhariṇī</s> is a specific preparation mixed with curds etc. /
She states the meaning of the word '<s>api</s>' (too) in 'by this too' — 'previously' etc. /
'Absence of that' — absence of <s>rasa</s>. /
'Feebleness' —
'But when the intention toward <s>rasa</s> etc. is one that bears purport —

children.text: tadā nāstyeva tatkāvyaṃ dhvaneryatra na gocaraḥ //
children.translated_text: then there simply is no such poetry where <s>dhvani</s> is not the domain.' //

children.translated_text: The meaning is: <s>citra-kāvya</s> (picture-poetry) has been composed [by poets].
Objection — 'The words that abandon the capacity for transformation —
In the boundless ocean of poetry, the poet is the sole creator (<s>Prajāpati</s>);
as it pleases him, so does this world revolve.' //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] And this <s>citra</s> (picture-poetry) has been conceived by us from observing the poetic practice of poets of unbridled speech, without regard for the purport of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
But for contemporary [poets], when the proper principles of poetic conduct are being established, there is simply no variety of poetry other than <s>dhvani</s>. /
For in the case of poets who possess maturity, the very activity [of composing] does not shine without the purport of <s>rasa</s> etc. /
And when the purport is <s>rasa</s> etc., there simply does not exist that thing which, when brought into ancillary relation with the intended <s>rasa</s>, does not become favorable. /
For even inanimate entities (<s>bhāvas</s>), when appropriately employed as <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) of the suitable <s>rasa</s> or through composition involving sentient happenings — there are simply none that do not attain ancillary status to <s>rasa</s>. /
And thus this is declared — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'But weakness' — this is the meaning of the word '<s>api</s>' (even/also). /
And when a <s>Śikhariṇī</s> [metre] is composed by an ignorant person — 'oh, a <s>Khikhariṇī</s>!' — there is no aesthetic delight from knowing it [as a metre]; rather, [connoisseurs] say 'this is like yogurt, jaggery, and pepper mixed incongruously.' /
'Stated' — /
The meaning is: by me myself. /
The meaning is: the composition of <s>alaṅkāras</s> pertaining to word and meaning. /
Objection: since 'that is called <s>citra</s>' has been taught, what [is the point] of this instruction? /
For it has been stated that this is not of the nature of true poetry. /
If [one says] it is taught as something to be rejected — then one would also have to say 'when a pot is made, one does not become a poet' — thus anticipating [this objection], he establishes that since poets have indeed composed it, it is taught as something to be rejected — by 'and this' etc. /
'Of those possessing maturity' — /
Those who possess maturity characterized by the propriety of <s>rasa</s> in the domain of word and meaning. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] By 'thus say [the critics],' the weakness of <s>rasa</s>-relishing has been shown. /
She prevents the error that 'stated' indicates it was stated by someone else — 'by me myself.' /
The meaning is: by me, the author of the <s>Vṛtti</s>, myself. /
'Not of the nature of poetry' etc. — /
The syntactic connection is: for it has been stated that that is not of the nature of poetry. /
'That' means <s>citra</s>. /
She raises a doubt in between — 'as something to be rejected' etc. /
'As something to be rejected' — as something to be abandoned. /
'That' — <s>citra</s>. /
She replies — 'pot' etc. /
'That has been composed' —

if that same [poet] becomes dispassionate, all of that becomes devoid of <s>rasa</s>.' //
'Even inanimate entities as if sentient, and sentient beings as if inanimate —
the good poet employs them as he wishes in poetry, with complete freedom.' //

children.translated_text: And this has been determined on the occasion of ascertaining the nature of <s>rasa</s>.
'The world' —
The meaning is: because of immersion in that <s>rasa</s>.
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Those skilled in the arrangement of words call it maturity of words (<s>śabdapāka</s>).' //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] Therefore, there simply does not exist that thing which, with its entire being, does not assume ancillary status to the <s>rasa</s> intended by a poet whose purport is <s>rasa</s>, by his will. /
Or, when thus composed, does not nourish the surpassing beauty — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'The words that abandon the capacity for transformation' — /
By this too, resort to <s>rasa</s>-propriety alone is what should be stated; otherwise it would be without reason. /
'Boundless' — /
The meaning is: without beginning or end. /
He states the transformation according to pleasure — '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' etc. /
'<s>Śṛṅgāra</s>' — [means] one whose nature is the experience of relishing the <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> stated in connection with <s>śṛṅgāra</s>; not one who is [merely] addicted to women — this should be understood. /
Precisely for this reason, the sage <s>Bharata</s> — in passages like 'the <s>bhāva</s> residing within the poet' and 'brings forth the meanings of poetry' etc. — uses the very word 'poet' /
in the most elevated sense.

Since by this [verse] a different definition of maturity has been stated — she says: 'the words that' etc. /
'Not addicted to women' — /
The completion is: this is the meaning of the word '<s>śṛṅgāri</s>' (one disposed to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>). /
'Addiction' means attachment.

children.text:
iti ślokaḥ, kāvyārthānityādivākyaṃ ca nāṭyaśāstre saptamādhyāye vartete /
vāgaṅgamukharāgātmanā abhinayena satvalakṣaṇena cābhinayena karaṇena /
kaveḥ varṇanānipuṇasya yo 'ntargato 'nādipraktanasaṃskārapratibhānamayo deśakālādibhedābhāvātsarvasādhāraṇībhāvenāsvādayogyaścittavṛttilakṣaṇo bhāvastam /
bhāvayannāsvadayogyīkurvan /
kāvyārthānita /
koḥ kavatervā kavanīyaṃ kāvyaṃ tatra ca padārthavākyārthau raseṣvevaṃ paryavasyata ityasādhāraṇyātprādhānyacca kāvyasyārthā rasāḥ arthyante pradhānyenetyarthā, iti cābhinavabhāratyāṃ vivṛtam /
kathaṃ jagato rasamayatvamityata āha--tadrasetyādi /
rasopalakṣaṇamiti /
puṇṇāti /
sarvametacca māhakavīnāṃ kāvyeṣu dṛśyate /
asmābhirapi sveṣu kāvyaprabandheṣu yathāyathaṃ darśitameva /
sthite caivaṃ sarva eva kāvyaprakāro na dhvanidharmatāmatipatati rasādyapekṣāyāṃ kaverguṇībhūtavyaṅgyalakṣaṇo 'pi prakārastadaṅgatāmavalambata ityuktaṃ prāk /
yadā tu cāṭuṣu devatāstutiṣu vā rasādīnāmaṅgatayā vyavasthānaṃ hṛdayavatīṣu ca saprajñakagāthāsu kāsucidyvaṅgyaviśiṣṭavācye prādhānyaṃ tadapi guṇībhūtavyaṅgyasya dhvaniniṣpandabhūtatvemevetyuktaṃ prāk /
tadevamidārnīntanakavikāvyanayopadeśe kriyamāṇe prāthamikānāmabhyāsārthināṃ yadi paraṃ citreṇa vyavahāraḥ, prāptapariṇatīnāṃ tu locanam śṛṅgārapadaṃ rasopalakṣaṇam /
sa eveti /
yāvadrasiko na bhavati tadā paridṛśyamāno 'pyayaṃ bhāvavargo yadyapi sukhaduḥkhamohamādhyasthyamātraṃ laukikaṃ vitarati, tathāpi kavivarṇanopārohaṃ vinā lokātikrāntarasāsvādabhūvaṃ nādhiśeta ityarthaḥ /
cārutvātiśayaṃ yanna puṣṇāti tannāstyeveti saṃbandhaḥ /
sveṣviti /
viṣamabāṇalīlādiṣṭu /

children.translated_text: 'In those full of heart' —
'<s>Hiaalaliā</s>' — in those [songs] well known in the assembly of <s>Prākṛta</s> poets.
'<s>Laṅghiagaaṇā phalahīlaāo hontutti vaḍḍhaantīa</s>' —
'<s>Hāli assa āsisaṃ pālivesavatuā viṇiṭhṭhaviā</s>' //

This verse, and the statement 'the meanings of poetry' etc., are found in the seventh chapter of the <s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s>. /
Through acting whose nature is voice, limbs, facial expression, and <s>rāga</s>, and through acting characterized by <s>sattva</s> — as the instrument. /
'Of the poet' — of one skilled in description; the <s>bhāva</s> that resides within — having the nature of the manifestation of beginningless latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), which, due to the absence of distinctions of place, time, etc., is universally shared and fit for relishing, characterized by a mental state — that [<s>bhāva</s>]. /
'Bringing forth' — making fit for relishing. /
'The meanings of poetry' — /
'<s>Kāvya</s>' derives from '<s>ku</s>' or '<s>kavater</s>'; what is to be composed is <s>kāvya</s>; therein, both word-meaning and sentence-meaning culminate in <s>rasas</s> — thus, due to their extraordinary nature and primacy, the meanings of <s>kāvya</s> are <s>rasas</s> — 'meanings' means those sought with primacy — and this has been explained in the <s>Abhinavabhāratī</s>. /
'How can the world be full of <s>rasa</s>?' — to this he says: 'because of immersion in that <s>rasa</s>' etc. /
'Indicative of <s>rasa</s> in general' — the meaning is [that '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' is used] as an indicator of <s>rasa</s> in general. /
'Full' — /
All this is seen in the poetry of great poets. /
By us too, in our own poetic compositions, it has been duly demonstrated. /
And this being established, every variety of poetry does not transgress the domain of <s>dhvani</s> — when <s>rasa</s> etc. is intended by the poet, even the variety characterized as <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> depends on it — this was stated earlier. /
But when in <s>cāṭu</s> (flattering verses) or praises of deities, <s>rasas</s> etc. are established as ancillaries, and in certain <s>gāthās</s> (songs) full of heart and wit, the expressed meaning qualified by the suggested has primacy — even that is nothing but the vibration of <s>dhvani</s> in its <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> form — this was stated earlier. /
Thus, when the instruction on the poetic conduct of contemporary poets is being given, for beginners seeking practice, if there is activity only with <s>citra</s> [poetry], [that is fine]; but for those who have attained maturity — [<s>Locana</s>:] The word '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' is indicative of <s>rasa</s> in general. /
'If he himself [becomes dispassionate]' — /
As long as one is not aesthetically sensitive, then even though this class of <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions) is observed, although it produces only ordinary [feelings] of pleasure, pain, delusion, and indifference, nevertheless, without the elevation of the poet's description, it does not attain the state of relishing <s>rasa</s> that transcends the worldly — this is the meaning. /
'Does not nourish surpassing beauty' — the connection is: that which does not [nourish beauty] simply does not exist. /
'In our own' — /
In [compositions like] <s>Viṣamabāṇalīlā</s> etc.

children.text:
bālapriyā rasasāmānyopalakṣakamityarthaḥ /
vītarāgaścedityādikaṃ vivṛṇoti--yāvadrasiko na bhavatītyādi /
sukheti /
madhye tiṣṭhatīti madhyasthaḥ tasya bhāvo mādhyasthyaṃ sukhaduḥkhamohānāṃ yanmādhyasthyaṃ tadekānubhavaṃ tanmātramityarthaḥ /
mātrapadena rasāsvādavyavacchedaḥ /
vitaratīti /
bhāvavargasya triguṇātmakatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
hṛdayavatīṣvityasya vivaraṇam--
hiaalaliā ityādi /
trivargeti /
trivargasya dharmāditrayasya ya upāyaḥ, sa evopeyo jñātavyastatra kuśalāsvityartha- /
children.translated_text: The means of the triad (<s>trivarga</s>) — the three goals of <s>dharma</s> etc. — is itself what is to be sought — this is to be understood in those [songs] skilled in that — this is the meaning.
'<s>Laṅghia</s>' —
'The cotton plants have risen beyond the sky' — thus, of one who augments [with blessings].
The neighbor's young wife has fulfilled the ploughman's blessing. //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The meaning is: indicative of <s>rasa</s> in general. /
She explains 'if he becomes dispassionate' etc. — 'as long as he is not aesthetically sensitive' etc. /
'Pleasure' — /
'Standing in the middle' means 'neutral'; its state is neutrality (<s>mādhyasthya</s>); indifference toward pleasure, pain, and delusion — experiencing only that much and nothing more — this is the meaning. /
By the word '<s>mātra</s>' (only), the exclusion of <s>rasa</s>-relishing is indicated. /
'Produces' — /
The purport is: because the class of <s>bhāvas</s> is constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>. /
The elaboration of 'in those full of heart' — '<s>hiaalaliā</s>' etc. /
'The triad' —

children.text:
iticchāyā /
he hālika! kārpāsalatāḥ tvadupajīvanabhūtāḥ kārpāsastambāḥ /
laṅghitagaganāḥ atyuccāḥ /
bhavantu iti hālikasyāśiṣaṃ vardhayantyā punaḥ punaḥ kurvatyā kayācit /
prātīti /
prātiveśinī vadhūrityarthaḥ /
nirvāpitā nirvṛtiṃ prāpitā /
kārpāsalatānāṃ paripoṣe tatsthale niśśaṅkaṃ hālikena saha ramaṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti baddhathā nirvṛtirityanena taccauryasambhogābhilāṣo vadhvā vyajyate, tacca guṇībhūtam; tadetadyvācaṣṭe--atretyādi /
children.translated_text: By the nourishment of the cotton plants, she will be able to sport fearlessly with the ploughman at that place — thus, with this [hope-]bound contentment, the young wife's desire for secret love-making is suggested; and that [suggested meaning] is subordinated (<s>guṇībhūta</s>). She explains this — 'here' etc.
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] '<s>Dhvani</s> alone is poetry' — this is established.

children.text: tadayamatra saṃgrahaḥ--- yasmin raso vā bhāvo vā tātparyeṇa prakāśate /
children.translated_text: Here then is the summary — 'That [poetry] in which <s>rasa</s> or <s>bhāva</s> shines forth with purport,
or where <s>vastu</s> (thing/subject-matter) or <s>alaṅkāra</s> alone is expressed through indirection —'

This is the <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit rendering): /
'O ploughman! The cotton plants — the cotton stalks that are the basis of your livelihood — /
have risen beyond the sky — [may they become] very tall. /
May they be [so]' — thus, of some [woman] who augments the ploughman's blessing, making it again and again. /
'Neighbor' — /
The meaning is: a neighbor's young wife. /
'Has been delighted' — has been brought to contentment.

children.text:
kāvyādhvani dhvanirvyaṅgyaprādhānyaikanibandhanaḥ /
locanam atra godāvarīkacchalatāgahane bhareṇa jambūphaleṣu pacyamāneṣu /
hālikavadhūḥ paridhatte jambūphalarasaraktaṃ nivasanamiti tvaritayauryasaṃbhogasaṃbhāvyamānajambūphalarasaraktatvaparabhāganihnavanaṃ guṇībhūtavyaṅgyamityalaṃ bahunā /
dhvanireva kāvyamiti /
ātmātminorabheda eva vastuto vyutpattaye tu vibhāgaḥ bālapriyā prātiveśyiko nirvṛtiṃ prāpita iti ca locane pāṭhaḥ /
so 'pi sādhuḥ /
tadanusāreṇa gāthā chāyā ca paṭhanīyā /
atra pakṣe saṅketasthānārthinaṃ svānuraktaṃ prātiveśyikaṃ tatsambhogābhilāṣiṇī kācidyadṛcchayā dṛṣṭaṃ hālikaṃ pratyevamāśīrvādena saṅketasthānaṃ jñāpitavatīti tatsammogābhilāṣo vyaṅgyo bodhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In this alternative reading, a certain [woman] desiring union with her enamored neighbor who seeks a meeting-place, having seen a ploughman by chance, through this blessing has indicated the meeting-place to him — thus the desire for union is the suggested meaning to be understood.
'<s>Golākaccha</s>' —
'In the grove on the bank of the <s>Godā[varī]</s>, when the <s>jambū</s> fruits are abundantly ripening,
the ploughman's wife puts on a garment stained with <s>jambū</s> juice.' //

[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] 'In the highway of poetry, <s>dhvani</s> is that whose sole basis is the predominance of the suggested.' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Here, in the dense bower of creepers on the bank of the <s>Godāvarī</s>, when the <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple) fruits are ripening abundantly — /
The ploughman's wife puts on a garment stained with <s>jambū</s> fruit juice — thus the concealment of the redness that could be attributed to the staining by <s>jambū</s> juice on the cloth, connoting hasty secret love-making, is the <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> — enough of excessive [explanation]. /
'<s>Dhvani</s> alone is poetry' — /
Between the soul and its possessor there is actually no difference; but the distinction is made for the sake of instruction. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'The neighbor has been delighted' is also a reading in the <s>Locana</s>. /
That too is correct. /
According to that, the <s>gāthā</s> and its <s>chāyā</s> should be read [accordingly].

children.text:
iti cchāyā /
bhareṇetyasyātiśayenetyarthaḥ /
locane 'gode'tyādeḥ godāvarītyādivivaramaṃ bodhyam /
guṇībhūtaṃ vyaṅgyaṃ darśayati---tvaritetyādi /
tvaritaḥ patitajambūphale nikuñcadeśe sicayāstaraṇe tvarayā kṛto yaścauryasambhogastena sambhāvyamānaḥ samutpādyamāstaddhetukatayā tarkyamāṇo vā yo jambūphalarasaraktatvena parabhāgaḥ sicyasya tattadbhāge varṇāntaraprāptiḥ tasya nihnavanaṃ gopanecchetyarthaḥ /
guṇībhūtavyaṅgyamiti /
sarvāvayavāvacchedena jambūphalarasaraktasya sicayasya paridhānena tannihnavanaṃ gamyate, tattu vācyārthe guṇībhūtamityarthaḥ /
nanu dhvanikāvyayorātmaśarīrasthānīyayorbhedādvṛttau ' dhvanireva kāvyam' iti sāmānādhikaraṇyena nirdeśo 'nupapanna ityata āha--ātmātminorityādi /

children.translated_text: '<s>Ātmin</s>' means the body.
'For instruction' — for the instruction of students.
'Distinction' —

children.text: dhvaniḥ kāvyasyātmā sarvatra tatra viṣayī jñeyaḥ sahṛdayairjanaiḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Vṛtti</s>:] '<s>Dhvani</s> is the soul of poetry; everywhere, in that [domain], it should be recognized as the master by people of sensitive heart.' //

This is the <s>chāyā</s>. /
The meaning of 'abundantly' is: 'exceedingly.' /
In the <s>Locana</s>, for '<s>gode</s>' etc., the elaboration '<s>Godāvarī</s>' etc. should be understood. /
She shows the <s>guṇībhūta</s> suggested meaning — 'hasty' etc. /
'Hasty' — where the <s>jambū</s> fruits have fallen, in that grove-area, in the hastily-done spreading of the garment for the hurried secret love-making; 'connoted' — being produced [as inference] or being surmised as the cause thereof; the redness through <s>jambū</s>-fruit juice representing the advantage of concealment — the acquisition of a different color on that part of the garment; 'concealment' — the meaning is: the desire to hide. /
'<s>Guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>' — /
Through putting on a garment reddened by <s>jambū</s>-fruit juice in its entirety, that concealment is understood; but it is subordinated to the expressed meaning — this is the meaning. /
Objection: since <s>dhvani</s> and <s>kāvya</s>, being in the position of soul and body, are different, the co-referential predication in the <s>Vṛtti</s> '<s>dhvani</s> alone is poetry' is unjustified — to this she says: 'of the soul and its possessor' etc.
Together with its own subdivisions — along with <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s> —

children.text: saṅkara-saṃsṛṣṭibhyāṃ punar apy uddyotate bahudhā // DhvK_3.43 //
children.translated_text: through <s>saṅkara</s> (mixture) and <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination), it shines forth again in manifold ways. // <s>DhvK</s> 3.43 //
Together with its own subdivisions — along with <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s> —
through mixture and combination, it shines forth again in manifold ways. // 43 //

children.text:
tasya ca dhvaneḥ svaprabhedairguṇībhūtavyaṅgyena vācyālaṅkāraiśca saṅkarasaṃsṛṣṭivyavasthāyāṃ kriyamāṇāyāṃ bahuprabhedatā lakṣye dṛśyate /
tathāhi svaprabhedasaṅkīrṇaḥ svaprabhedasaṃsṛṣṭo guṇībhūtavyaṅgyasaṅkīrṇo guṇībhūtavyaṅgyasaṃsṛṣṭo vācyālaṅkārāntarasaṅkīrṇo vācyālaṅkārāntarasaṃsṛṣṭaḥ saṃsṛṣṭālaṅkārasaṅkīrṇaḥ saṃsṛṣṭālaṅkārasaṃsṛṣṭaśceti bahudhā dhvaniḥ prakāśate /
locanam kṛta ityarthaḥ /
vāgrahaṇāttadābhāsādeḥ pūrvoktasya grahaṇam /
saṃvṛtyeti /
gopyamānatayālabdhasaundarya tyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'From poetry, <s>dhvani</s>' — /
in the path of poetry. /
'The subject' — /

children.text: sa trividhasya dhvaneḥ kāvyamārgo viṣaya ita yāvat // 41//
children.translated_text: This much [is meant]: the path of poetry is the domain of the threefold <s>dhvani</s>. // 41 //

[Vṛtti:] And when the determination of admixture (<s>saṅkara</s>) and combination (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>) of that <s>dhvani</s> with its own subdivisions, with <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, and with expressed <s>alaṅkāras</s> is being made, a great multiplicity of subdivisions is seen in the target [of analysis]. /
For indeed, <s>dhvani</s> manifests in many ways: mixed with its own subdivisions, combined with its own subdivisions, mixed with <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, combined with <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, mixed with other expressed <s>alaṅkāras</s>, combined with other expressed <s>alaṅkāras</s>, mixed with combined <s>alaṅkāras</s>, and combined with combined <s>alaṅkāras</s>. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Made' — this is the meaning. /
By the word '<s>vā</s>' (or), the previously stated [categories] such as their semblances (<s>ābhāsas</s>) etc. are included. /
'By concealment' (<s>saṃvṛttyā</s>) — /
The meaning is: beauty that is attained through being kept hidden. /

children.text:
evaṃ ślokadvyena saṃgrahārthamabhidhāya bahuprakāratvapradarśikāṃ paṭhati--saguṇīta /
sahaguṇībhūtavyaṅgyena sahālaṅkārairye vartante sve dhvaneḥ prabhedāstaiḥ saṃkīrṇatayā saṃsṛṣṭyā vānantaprakāro dhvanirita tātparyam /
bahuprakāratāṃ darśayati--tathāhīti /
svebhedairguṇībhūtavyaṅgyenālaṅkāraiḥ prakāśyata iti trayo bhedāḥ /
tatrāpi pratyekaṃ saṃkareṇa saṃsṛṣṭyā ceta ṣaṭ /
saṃkarasyāpi trayaḥ prakārāḥ anugrāhyanugrāhakabhāvena saṃdehāspadatvenaikapadānupraveśeneti dvādaśa bhedāḥ /
pūrvaṃ ca ye pañcatriṃśadbhedā uktāste guṇībhūtavyaṅgyasyāpi bālapriyā śabdārthamayaṃ kāvyaṃ śarīramiti vibhāga ityarthaḥ /
vāgrahaṇāditi /
bhāvo veti vākārādityarthaḥ /
saṃvṛttyābhihitāvatyasya vivaraṇam--gopyamānatayā labdhasondarya iti /

children.translated_text: With the intention that by stating the domain-status of <s>dhvani</s>, the domain-status of the path of poetry is obtained, she says — 'of the threefold' etc. /
In [the passage beginning with] '<s>yasmin</s>' (in which) etc. /
In which <s>dhvani</s> of poetry — /

children.text: prakāśate sarvatra tatra vyaṅgyaprādhānyaikanibandhano dhvaniḥ viṣayī san sahṛdayairjanairjeya ityanvayaḥ // 41//
children.translated_text: The syntactic construction is: everywhere there, <s>dhvani</s> — whose sole basis is the primacy of the suggested — being the subject [of inquiry], should be known by connoisseur-minded people. // 41 //

Having thus stated in summary through a pair of verses, he recites [the verse] demonstrating the multiplicity of types — 'with <s>guṇībhūta</s>' etc. /
The purport is: <s>dhvani</s> is of infinite types through being mixed or combined with <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, with <s>alaṅkāras</s>, and with its own subdivisions that coexist with them. /
He shows the multiplicity — 'for indeed' etc. /
Three divisions [arise]: it shines forth with its own subdivisions, with <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, and with <s>alaṅkāras</s>. /
And in each of those, through admixture (<s>saṅkara</s>) and combination (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>) — six. /
And admixture also has three types — through the relation of supporter and supported, through being a locus of doubt, and through entry into a single seat — [thus] twelve divisions. /
And the thirty-five divisions that were stated previously — those also apply to <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Poetry consisting of word and meaning is the body' — the meaning is: thus is the division. /
'By the word <s>vā</s>' — /
The meaning is: from the letter '<s>vā</s>' in '<s>bhāvo vā</s>' (or <s>bhāva</s>). /
The elaboration of what was stated as 'by concealment' — 'beauty attained through being kept hidden.' /

children.text:
kārikāṃ vyācaṣṭe---sahetyādi /
udyātata ityatra dhvaniriti śeṣa iti bhāvaḥ /
saguṇībhūtavyaṅgyaissālaṅkāraissvaprabhedaiḥ saha saṅkarasaṃsṛṣṭyoruktyā pratyekaṃ taistribhissaha te labhyete ityāśayena vibhāgān darśayati--svaprabhedairityādi /
prakāśyata iti sammiśnyata iti ca pāṭhaḥ /
dvādaśeti /
svaprabhedādibhistribhiḥ saha saṅkarakṛtā nava, saṃsṛṣṭikṛtāstraya iti dvādaśetyarthaḥ /
pūrvaṃ ca ye pañcatriṃśadbhedā uktā iti /
dvitīyodyotāvasāna 'evaṃ dhvaneḥ prabhedān pratipādye'ti vṛttigranthavyākhyānāvasare ye pañcatriśadbhedāḥ tatra svaprabhedasaṅkīrṇatvaṃ kadācidanugrāhyānugrāhakabhāvena /
yathā--'evaṃvādini devarṣau' ityādau /
atra hyarthaśaktyudbhavānuraṇanarūpavyaṅgyadhvaniprabhedenālakṣyakramavyaṅgyadhvaniprabhedo 'nugṛhyamāṇaḥ pratīyate /
evaṃ kadācitprabhedadvayasampātasandehena /

children.translated_text: As in — /

children.text: khaṇapāhuṇiā deara esā jāāeṃ kiṃpi de bhaṇidā /
children.translated_text: '<s>khaṇapāhuṇiā deara esā jāāeṃ kiṃpi de bhaṇidā</s> /
<s>ruai paḍoharavalahīdharammi aṇuṇijjau varāri</s>' //

She explains the <s>kārikā</s> — 'with' etc. /
The purport is: in '<s>udyātata</s>' (it rises/shines forth), '<s>dhvani</s>' is to be supplied. /
'With <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, with <s>alaṅkāras</s>, with its own subdivisions' — by stating the admixture and combination of each of the three, those are obtained — with this intention she shows the divisions — 'with its own subdivisions' etc. /
There is also the reading 'shines forth' and 'is mixed.' /
'Twelve' — /
The meaning is: nine produced by admixture with the three [categories] beginning with its own subdivisions, and three produced by combination — [thus] twelve. /
'And the thirty-five divisions that were stated previously' — /
At the end of the second <s>Uddyota</s>, in the occasion of explaining the <s>vṛtti</s> passage 'having thus demonstrated the divisions of <s>dhvani</s>' — the thirty-five divisions [stated] there — with its own subdivisions being mixed — sometimes through the relation of supporter and supported. /
As in '<s>evaṃ vādini devarṣau</s>' (while the divine sage was speaking thus) etc. /
For here, the subdivision of <s>dhvani</s> [based on] the suggested whose form is reverberation born from the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktyudbhavānuraṇanarūpavyaṅgya</s>) is perceived as being supported by the subdivision of <s>dhvani</s> whose suggested meaning has an imperceptible sequence. /
Likewise, sometimes through doubt arising from the convergence of two subdivisions. /

children.translated_text: 'She' — /
the meaning is: she who became a momentary guest — she is the heroine. /

children.text: (kṣaṇaprādhuṇikā devara eṣā jāyayā kimapi te bhaṇitā /
children.translated_text: ('A momentary guest, O brother-in-law! This one has been told something by your wife. /
She weeps in the empty attic room — let the wretched one be consoled!' //

[<s>Locana</s>:] are to be considered. /
'Its own subdivisions' — as many as [there are], 'figure' [means] one — thus seventy-one. /
Therein, when multiplied by the three types of admixture and by combination — two hundred and eighty-four. /
When those are multiplied by the thirty-five primary divisions — seven thousand four hundred and twenty result. /
Due to the infinity of <s>alaṅkāras</s>, [the number is] uncountable. /
Therein, desiring to give examples for a few divisions for the sake of proficiency, since among the own subdivisions those stated as 'other word-meanings' (<s>anyapadārtha</s>) in the <s>kārikā</s> have primacy, he gives precisely four examples based on those — 'therein' etc. /
'Being supported' — /
For through the perceived bashfulness, /
the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> of desire is here supported as a <s>vyabhicāribhāva</s> (transitory emotion). /
'A momentary guest' — O brother-in-law! This one has been told something by your wife and is weeping. /
In the empty attic room, let the wretched one be consoled. /
She [the heroine] was indeed enamored of [her] brother-in-law; his wife, having learned the affair, said something [harsh] — thus this speech [is] of that woman whose affair has been discovered. — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'herself discovered' — this is the meaning. /
'Those' — /
the meaning is: the thirty-five divisions. /
'Its own subdivisions' — /
the meaning is: the sub-divisions of <s>dhvani</s>. /
'As many as' — /
the meaning is: thirty-five. /
'Figure' — /
the meaning is: as delimited by figure-hood. /
'Therein' etc. — /
the meaning is: seventy-one multiplied by four. /
'Two hundred and eighty-four' — after this, the reading 'when those are multiplied by the thirty-five primary divisions, seven thousand four hundred and twenty result' is seen in many manuscripts; its meaning does not appear coherent and should be determined by the learned. /
'Uncountable' — /
therefore, [the figure-hood delimited as] one alone should be taken — this is the purport. /
'As other word-meanings' — /
the meaning is: as the other word-meanings in the two <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compounds beginning with '<s>saguṇībhūta</s>' etc. /
Here she elaborates what was stated in the <s>vṛtti</s> beginning with 'for here, the power of meaning' — 'through bashfulness' etc. /
'As a <s>vyabhicāribhāva</s>' — /
the meaning is: by reason of bashfulness being a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
'Guest' — /
this festive occasion should be understood as pertaining to the brother-in-law. /
The expressed meaning of 'guest' [literally: one who has come] is 'having arrived.' /
The statement of its deeper significance — 'having been brought by invitation.' /
By this, the necessity of reconciliation is suggested. /
'Brother-in-law' etc. — showing the implied tone (<s>chāyā</s>). /
'Something' — the meaning is: something inappropriate. /
Since she weeps, therefore 'wretched one' — pitiable. /
The connection is: 'let her be consoled by you.' /
She explains this <s>gāthā</s> (verse) with an introduction — 'she' etc. /

children.translated_text: For here there is the combination of [<s>dhvani</s> whose] expressed meaning is transferred to another meaning and [<s>dhvani</s> whose] expressed meaning is completely obscured. /

children.text: guṇībhūtavyaṅgya saṅkīrṇatvaṃ yathā--'nyakkāro hyayameva me yadarayaḥ' ityādau /
children.translated_text: Admixture with <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> [occurs] as in '<s>nyakkāro hy ayam eva me yad arayaḥ</s>' (this indeed is the humiliation to me, that the enemies...) etc. /

children.text: yathā vā-- kartā dyūtacchalānāṃ jatumayaśaraṇoddīpanaḥ so 'bhimānī kṛṣṇākeśottarīyavyapanayanapaṭuḥ pāṇḍavā yasya dāsāḥ /
children.translated_text: As, for example — 'The contriver of stratagems through gambling, the one who ignited the house of lac, that proud one, the one skilled at stripping <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s hair-cloth, he whose servants are the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, /

children.text: rājā duḥśāsanādergururanujaśatasyāṅgarājasya mitraṃ kkāste duryodhano 'sau kathayata na ruṣā draṣṭumabhyāgatau svaḥ //
children.translated_text: the king, the elder of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> and others, the master of a hundred younger brothers, the friend of the king of <s>Aṅga</s> — that <s>Duryodhana</s> sits [there]! Tell [him] — are you not come in anger to see [him]?' //

— thus is the <s>chāyā</s> [Sanskrit shadow-rendering].) /
Here, the word '<s>anunīyatām</s>' (let her be consoled) is conceivable both as having its expressed meaning transferred to another meaning (<s>arthāntarasaṅkramitavācya</s>) and as having its expressed meaning intended-with-another-primary (<s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s>). /
And there is no evidence for determining one or the other alternative. /
Through the entry of a single suggestor, however, the suggested-meaning-status of the imperceptibly-sequenced suggested [meaning], in relation to the other subdivision — [<s>Locana</s>:] of her who has seen, of that other woman, the beloved of that brother-in-law who is [also her] paramour. /
Therein, your wife has come to know this affair — thus, wishing to provoke a quarrel between both [parties], she speaks thus. /
Therein, the transference of the expressed meaning into another meaning [takes the form]: 'let her be gratified by intimate union, which alone is befitting' — such is the form of the transference of the expressed meaning. /
Alternatively, since you are enamored of this very one — out of the purport of jealousy and anger — the 'consoling' [literally expressed] is intended-with-another-primary, [the other primary meaning being] the jealous anger [that is suggested]. /
This [expression] — 'she is the fitting, blameless object of love, even now' — this is the intended consolation; 'but we have now become blameworthy' — with this as the primary [suggested] meaning, in both ways [of interpretation], through the revelation of one's own intention, there is no evidence for determining one alternative — thus it was stated [by the author]. /
For it is the nature of the <s>vivakṣita</s> (intended meaning) that it is another-primary while remaining in its own form. — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Brother-in-law' — /
the meaning is: her brother-in-law, the brother of [her] husband — she is enamored of him. /
'Discovered' — /
the meaning is: she whose affair — the mutual love etc. between her and the brother-in-law — is known. /
'The affair of that' — /
the meaning is: the affair of what was said by his wife etc. /
'Of the beloved' — the syntactic connection is: 'this is the speech of the beloved.' /
'Having been told something by the wife' — this merely shows the reason for weeping; there is no further purpose to stating that — she says: 'therein' etc. /
'In that speech.' /
'Therein' — the connection is: 'thus she speaks.' /
'She' is to be supplied. /
'Wishing to provoke a quarrel between both' — /
the meaning is: wishing to produce a quarrel between that brother-in-law and his wife. /
She elaborates the doubt-based admixture stated in the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'therein' etc. /
'In such speech.' /
'In the form of such another meaning' — the connection [is made]. /
'Of the expressed meaning' — of the expressed meaning of '<s>anunayati</s>' (he/she consoles). /
'Transference' — /
the sense of '<s>vivakṣitam</s>' (intended) is drawn over [from the next interpretation]. /
The expressed meaning of '<s>anunayati</s>' is: an activity producing satisfaction, such as sweet speech etc. — that, in its form as intimate union, is to be indicated [as] intended — this is the meaning. /
And here the suggested meaning — 'your attachment to her has been discovered by me' etc. — should also be understood. /
'Of this very one' — /
there is also the reading: 'O brother-in-law, of that very one.' /
The meaning is: of this very one who weeps. /
'Thus' — in the sense of a reason. /
'Jealousy' — /
the meaning is: from the purport of jealousy and anger residing in the speaking woman. /
'Consoling' — /
the meaning is: the expressed meaning of '<s>anunayati</s>' (consoling). /
'Another-primary' — /
the meaning is: having the suggested [meaning of] jealous anger as primary. /
She justifies what was stated — 'she' etc. /
The connection is: 'this too is intended as having this as primary.' /
'In both ways' — /
the meaning is: in the alternative of the transference of the expressed meaning of '<s>anunayati</s>' to another meaning, and in the alternative of being intended [as] another-primary. /
'One's own intention' — /
the meaning is: the desire of the speaking woman. /
'Stated' — /
'by the author of the <s>vṛtti</s>' is to be supplied. /
She says incidentally — 'for of the <s>vivakṣita</s>' etc. /
[This] occurs abundantly. /
As in '<s>snigdhaśyāmala</s>' (glossy-dark) etc. /
And the combination with its own subdivisions [occurs] as in the previous example itself. /
