children.translated_text: 'Sensory cognition' — worldly visual knowledge pertaining to various respective objects; 'practice' thereof means repetition; the meaning is: 'illuminated' (<s>ullasite</s>) by that, i.e., made manifest.
She connects the stated meaning with the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'that will be stated' etc.

children.text: te dve apyavalambya viśvamaniśa nirvarṇayanto vayaṃ śrāntā naiva ca labdhamabdhiśayana tvadbhaktitulyaṃ sukham //
children.translated_text: 'Relying on those two [visions], examining the universe ceaselessly, we are exhausted — and not at all have we obtained happiness equal to devotion to You, O You who recline on the ocean.' //

[<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Saṃkrānti</s>' (transference) is the attainment by that [expressed meaning] of this other form. /
Alternatively, this is the utterance of a woman attached to her brother-in-law (<s>devara</s>), directed to that very brother-in-law upon observing his amorous affair with another woman — because of the vocative address '<s>devara</s>' (O brother-in-law). /
But in the earlier interpretation, the address '<s>devara</s>' was explained with reference to her [the co-wife who recently arrived]. /
'Abundantly' — /
everywhere in poetry, the purport of <s>rasa</s> etc. exists; therein, the manifestation of both <s>rasa-dhvani</s> and <s>bhāva-dhvani</s> by a single suggestor [is possible] — as in '<s>snigdhaśyāmala</s>' (smooth and dark), the <s>vipralambhaśṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation) and its transitory emotion (<s>vyabhicārin</s>) of the nature of the agitation of grief are relishable. /
Having thus explained the threefold <s>saṃkara</s> (mixture), he illustrates <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (blending) — 'of the sub-type itself' etc. /
'For here' — /
in the word '<s>lipta</s>' (smeared) etc., the expressed meaning is eclipsed (<s>tiraskṛta</s>); but in '<s>Rāma</s>' etc., it is transferred (<s>saṃkrānta</s>) — this is the meaning. /
Having thus illustrated the four varieties for each sub-type, he illustrates for <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinate suggestion) — '<s>guṇībhūta</s>' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Of the expressed meaning standing in its own form.' /
'Of that expressed meaning.' /
'Attainment of this other form' — attainment of another intended form. /
'Of [a woman] attached to her brother-in-law' — /
the meaning is: of one attached to he who is her brother-in-law. /
The connection of '<s>saha</s>' (together with) is with '<s>sambhoga</s>' (amorous enjoyment). /
She states the indicator for the stated meaning — '<s>devara</s>' etc. /
'With reference to her' — /
the meaning is: with reference to the one who had recently arrived. /
The meaning is: the brother-in-law-hood determined by her [is to be understood]. /
This verse is cited in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> as well. /
She justifies the statement 'it occurs abundantly' — 'everywhere' etc. /
The syntactic connection is: because of relishability, manifestation [occurs]. /
'In the word <s>lipta</s> (smeared) etc.' — /
In '<s>snigdhaśyāmalakāntiliptaviyat</s>' (the sky smeared with smooth dark radiance), since the expressed meaning of '<s>lepa</s>' (smearing) — the contact of a liquid substance with all parts — is sublated (<s>bādha</s>), the root '<s>lip</s>' (to smear), indicating contact through indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), reveals its intensification. /
Similarly, in '<s>payodās suhṛdo yeṣām</s>' (those whose friends are the rain-clouds), since the expressed meaning is sublated, the word '<s>suhṛt</s>' (friend) indicates [the meaning] 'benefactor' through indication, and reveals its intensification — this is the meaning. /
'In <s>Rāma</s> etc.' — /
the meaning is: in the word '<s>Rāma</s>' etc. /
'Expressed' is carried over. /
'Transferred' — /
how transference works was stated in the second <s>Uddyota</s>. /
By the phrase '<s>Rāma</s> etc.,' the words '<s>nyakkāra</s>' (humiliation) etc. referring to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> etc. are included. /
The verse beginning with '<s>karte</s>' (the maker) is found in the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>. /
For here, the imperceptible-sequence suggested meaning (<s>alakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s>), which has become the sentence-meaning, is intermixed with words that denote expressed meanings qualified by suggested [meanings]. /
And for this very reason, even when there is mingling — with <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> being at the level of word-meaning and <s>dhvani</s> being at the level of sentence-meaning — there is no contradiction, just as with other sub-types. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'For here' — in both illustrations. /
'Of the imperceptible-sequence suggested' — /
of the <s>raudra</s> (furious) [<s>rasa</s>]; by the phrase 'qualified by the suggested,' the subordination of the suggested [to the expressed] is indicated. /
'By words' — the instrumental is in the sense of characterization (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). /
Therefore, the meaning characterized by those [words] — the expressed meaning that stands in subordination to the suggested — by that, the mingling [occurs]. /
And that [mingling is] through the relation of supporter and supported (<s>anugrāhya-anugrāhaka</s>), through the conjunction of doubt (<s>sandeha</s>), and through the entry of a single suggestor — [each type] should be applied to the two illustrations as appropriate. /
Thus — by all the word-meanings [in] '<s>me yad araya</s>' (what, my enemies) etc. and [in] '<s>karte</s>' (the maker) etc., it is the <s>raudra</s> (furious <s>rasa</s>) alone that is supported, in the form of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. /
And in '<s>karte</s>' etc., word by word, subsidiary-sentence by subsidiary-sentence, and compound by compound, it is possible to conjecture suggested [meanings] — hence it was not written [explicitly]. /
'The <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> are his slaves' — this is an imitation of <s>Duryodhana</s>'s speech. /
Therein, <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>-ness can also be construed, because the expressed meaning itself inflames anger (<s>krodha</s>). /
'And by servants who have accomplished their purpose, the master must necessarily be seen' — thus the nature of reverberation based on the capacity of meaning (<s>arthaśaktyanuraṇanarūpatā</s>) is also [possible]. /
In either case, since there is no evidence for adopting just one interpretation, charm [results]. /
The entry of a single suggestor, moreover, [occurs] because by those very words, both the subordinated suggested [meaning] and the primary <s>rasa</s> are manifested through the medium of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] To prevent the misunderstanding that '<s>atra</s>' (here) in the <s>Vṛtti</s> refers only to the illustration '<s>karte</s>,' she elaborates: 'in both illustrations.' /
'Of the <s>raudra</s>' — /
the purport is: the apprehension of anger (<s>krodha</s>) belonging to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in '<s>nyakkāra</s>' etc. and to <s>Bhīmasena</s> in '<s>karte</s>' etc. /
'By [the phrase] qualified by the suggested' — /
the meaning is: by the statement of qualification by the suggested. /
'Subordination' — /
'relative to the expressed meaning' is the remainder. /
'Is indicated' — is shown. /
Since the literal meaning of 'intermixed by words' is sublated, she explains: 'by words — the instrumental is in the sense of characterization.' /
The meaning of 'instrumental' is: it conveys characterization. /
She shows that very meaning — 'characterized by those' etc. /
She says what it is intermixed with — 'the meaning' etc. /
'The meaning' — the expressed meaning. /
'By that' — /
the meaning is: by the expressed meaning that is <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>. /
'And that' — /
the meaning is: the mingling. /
The connection of these three [instrumentals ending in] third case is with this. /
And 'by the word-meanings of <s>karte</s>' etc. — /
'by word-meanings' is carried over. /
Objection: in '<s>nyakkāra</s>' etc., the suggested meanings were explained previously. But in '<s>karte</s>' etc., are they not present? To this she says: 'in <s>karte</s> etc.' — /
'His utterance' — /
the meaning is: the utterance of <s>Duryodhana</s>: 'the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> are my servants.' /
Having shown, by the statement 'the <s>raudra</s> alone is supported,' the mixture through the supporter-supported relation, she shows it through the conjunction of doubt — 'therein' etc. /
The degradation of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> etc. should be understood [as the suggested content]. /
'In the meaning' etc. — /
the meaning is: the suggested [meaning] based on the capacity of meaning that was stated — that nature too — this is the meaning. /
'Can be construed' is carried over. /
'In either case' etc. — /
and thus there is a doubt-mixture of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> and <s>dhvani</s> — this is the purport. /
'By those' — /
the meaning is: by [the words] '<s>me yad araya</s>' (what, my enemies) etc. /
The connection is: and because of the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> through the medium of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. /
'For this very reason' — having explained this — 'for this very reason' etc.: just as the sub-types of <s>dhvani</s> among themselves are intermixed, and are not contradicted by having the word-meaning level and the sentence-meaning level [respectively] — /
Moreover, when a single suggestor is the locus, the principal-subordinate relationship is contradicted, but not with respect to the difference in suggested [meanings] — hence from that too, there is no contradiction here. /
And this usage of <s>saṃkara</s> (mixture) and <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (blending) should be considered as non-contradictory in the domain of suggested-suggestor relationship, just as the expressed-expressor relationship of many [meanings] in a single [locus]. /
But where some words have <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (non-intended expressed) [meaning], or have expressed meanings in the form of reverberation-type suggestion — there, between <s>dhvani</s> and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, there is <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (blending). /
As in — '<s>teṣāṃ gopavadhūvilāsasuhṛdām</s>' (of those who were the friends of the playful dalliances of the cowherd women) etc. /
For here, the words '<s>vilāsasuhṛdām</s>' (friends of dalliances) and '<s>rādhārahaḥsākṣiṇām</s>' (witnesses to <s>Rādhā</s>'s secrets) are of the <s>dhvani</s> type, while the words '<s>te</s>' (those) and '<s>jāne</s>' (I know) are of the <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> type. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] 'For this very reason' — /
the meaning is: since this is seen in the present example, therefore. /
Objection: suggested [meaning] being subordinate and principal — this is indeed contradictory; [hence] even though it is seen, since it has been stated [as such], it should not be credited — anticipating this, he shows that at least due to the difference in suggestors, there is no contradiction — 'for this very reason' etc. /
'Of its own' — /
she cites as illustrations those very sub-type-varieties that were previously illustrated as mixed. /
He explains that very [point] — 'just as indeed' etc. /
The supplementation 'so too here' should be supplied here. /
Or the reading is 'for thus' (<s>tathā hi</s>). /
Objection: through the difference in suggestors, let the first two varieties be resolved; but regarding the entry of a single suggestor, what is to be said? Anticipating this, he gives the definitive resolution — 'moreover' etc. 'From that too' — /
since the suggested [meaning] that is subordinate is one and the suggested that is principal is another — what contradiction is there? /
Objection: this usage of <s>saṃkara</s> etc. is heard in the domain of expressed figures, not in the domain of suggested — anticipating this, he says: 'and this' etc. /
'Should be considered' — /
should be so ascertained through contemplation, i.e., through [aesthetic] experience, because experience alone is the authority in both domains — this is the purport. /
Having thus illustrated three varieties of mixture in <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, he illustrates blending (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>) — 'but where the words' etc. /
'Some' — by this — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] she introduces the text up to 'no contradiction' — 'objection' etc. /
'Even though seen' — /
'in the example' is the remainder. /
'Of its own' — /
the connection is: she cites as illustrations. /
'Like other sub-type-varieties' — by this she shows the illustration — this is the meaning. /
'Of the first two varieties' — /
the meaning is: of the two mixtures through the supporter-supported relation and through the conjunction of doubt. /
'What is to be said' — /
what is to be done. /
Or the reading is '<s>ca</s>.' /
The purport is: because of the absence of difference in suggestors. /
She states the purport — 'since another' etc. /
'Should be considered' — she explains this in accordance with the topic — 'through contemplation' etc. /
'Through experience' — through the experience of the connoisseur (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). /
'By this' — /
by the statement 'some [words have] <s>avivakṣitavācya</s>, some have expressed meanings in the form of reverberation-type suggestion.' /
'Friend' etc. — /
the mingling of expressed figures, being in the domain of <s>mukhyārtha</s> (primary meaning), with reference to imperceptible-sequence suggestion, in poetry that has <s>rasa</s> and figures of speech — is everywhere well established. /
The mingling of other sub-types also sometimes occurs indeed. /
As in my own [verse] — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] she removes the occasion for mixture. /
By the word '<s>suhṛt</s>' (friend) and '<s>sākṣin</s>' (witness), the <s>dhvani</s> is of the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (non-intended expressed) type, since the expressed meanings of friendship and being a witness are sublated with respect to inanimate latticework-bowers, the word '<s>suhṛt</s>' indicates [the meaning of] 'benefactor' and the word '<s>sākṣin</s>' indicates 'one who is near.' /
The intensification contained in benefaction etc. is the suggested [meaning] — and of these two words, the <s>dhvani</s> — this is the meaning. /
The connection is: manifested by the word. /
'Subordination' — /
'relative to the expressed' is the remainder. /
Regarding 'mingling of expressed figures' — she shows the purpose of the qualifying word 'expressed' (<s>vācya</s>) in 'figure' — 'regarding suggestedness' etc. /
'The stated eightfold classification' — /
the meaning is: the eightfold classification produced by mixture and blending. /
'Of such a kind' — /
the meaning is: possessing <s>rasa</s> and figures. /
She demonstrates the well-established-ness — '<s>vivakṣā</s>' etc. /
'The supportership of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>' — /
the meaning is: the supporter-supported relationship together with <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. /
The purport is: because the observation of various actions belonging to another hero inflames the passion (<s>rati</s>) [of the audience]. /
'In the verse' — /
'previously cited' is the remainder. /
'In the absence of context etc.' — the locative is in the sense of a cause. /
Having thus shown the illustration of the threefold mixture of expressed figures, and intending to show the illustration of the domain of blending thereof, she says — 'although' etc. /
'With which intention' — /
the meaning is: with the intention of the absence of supportership. /
'Here' — /
the meaning is: for here, the blending of <s>rasa</s> with <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) alone [obtains]. /
Stating [something] for the purpose of the forthcoming discussion, she says — 'in the production' etc. /
She elaborates the words '<s>vyāpāravatī</s>' (endowed with activity) etc. — by 'therein' etc. /
'That <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (vision) which is endowed with activity to make one relish <s>rasas</s>, which is novel — certain — of poets, and that learned discernment whose flash is directed toward established meanings' — /
[<s>Locana</s>:] '<s>Vyāpāravatī</s>' — /
for it was said that <s>rasa</s> has production as its life-force. /
Therein, the description (<s>varṇanā</s>) consisting of the arrangement of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., and the activity (<s>kriyā</s>) from that point up to the [final] synthesis — that is the operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>); constantly engaged with that [is the vision]. /
'<s>Rasān</s>' (the <s>rasas</s>) — /
the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotional states) whose essence is relishability — 'to make relishable,' i.e., to make fit for attaining relishability. /
'A certain' (<s>kācit</s>) — [the vision that is] dawning by abandoning the condition of understanding that falls within ordinary worldly affairs. /
For this very reason, those poets — because of [their engagement in] the practice of description. /
'Novel' (<s>navā</s>) — /
stringing the worlds [of experience] with ever-new, ever-new varieties moment by moment. /
'Vision' (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) — /
of the nature of creative intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>); therein, '<s>dṛṣṭi</s>' being visual cognition, and '<s>ṣāḍava</s>' etc. [i.e., sweet things] — 'to make one relish <s>rasas</s>' [i.e., flavors] — the figure of apparent contradiction (<s>virodhālaṅkāra</s>) [arises] because [visual cognition cannot produce taste]; for this very reason [it is called] 'novel.' /
And the <s>dhvani</s> supported by that [figure] — for visual cognition [being attributed the capacity to produce taste] is not [an instance of] non-intended [expressed meaning], because of the impossibility of complete [sublation]. /
Nor is it primarily directed toward the suggested; rather, it is transferred to another meaning — the one characterized as creative intuition (<s>pratibhāna</s>), which is evoked by sensory cognitions of various kinds. /
And in the transference, the contradiction serves as a supporter. /
This he will state — by [the passage] 'through the figure of contradiction' etc. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] '<s>Vibhāvas</s> etc.' — /
the meaning is: meanings such as <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, etc. /
'Synthesis' — /
the meaning is: the synthesis of the respective words. /
'Activity' — /
the meaning is: mental activity consisting of the respective contemplations. /
For the constant conjunction, [she says] 'continuously' — thus she says: 'with that' etc. /
The conjunction should be understood as the cause-effect relationship. /
The elaboration of the literal meaning of '<s>rasān</s>' — 'whose essence is relishability' etc. /
She states what is intended by the word '<s>rasa</s>' in the present context — '<s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotional states).' /
'Cognition that falls within ordinary worldly affairs' — /
the meaning is: cognition pertaining to various ordinary worldly objects. /
'For this very reason' — /
the meaning is: precisely because of the dawning of the vision [of creative intuition]. /
She states the purpose of the word 'poet' — 'because of the practice of description.' /
'Stringing' — illuminating. /
Keeping in mind the transference to be stated, she says: 'of the nature of <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuition).' /
Here, '<s>dṛṣṭi</s>' is visual cognition. /
'To make one relish <s>rasas</s>' — to make one taste sweet substances like <s>ṣāḍava</s> (a confection) etc. having flavors like sweetness, etc.; alternatively — to make one taste the sweet and other flavors inherent in <s>ṣāḍava</s> etc. — 'endowed with activity' — since the meaning is contradictory, the figure of apparent contradiction (<s>virodhābhāsālaṅkāra</s>) [arises] — thus she says: 'therein, <s>dṛṣṭi</s>' etc. /
She indicates the suggestive sign of contradiction — 'for this very reason' etc. /
The purport is: 'novel' indicates the contradiction. /
'<s>Dhvani</s>' — the <s>dhvani</s> whose expressed meaning '<s>dṛṣṭi</s>' (vision) has been transferred to another meaning. /
'Not non-intended to the extreme' — /
the meaning is: not eclipsed to the utmost degree. /
'Because of the impossibility of impossibility' — /
the purport is: because even the visual cognition belonging to the poet, concerning moonrise-gardens etc., is useful for the production of <s>rasa</s>. /
'Nor primarily directed toward the other' — /
the meaning is: not intended as directed primarily toward the suggested. /
'But rather, transferred to another meaning — the one characterized as creative intuition.' /
The meaning is: the word '<s>dṛṣṭi</s>' here indicates cognition, having the form of <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuition). /
The indistinctness etc. of <s>pratibhāna</s> is the suggested [meaning] here. /

children.translated_text: 'Determines' means demonstrates.

children.text: sphuṭitānītyasya truṭitānītyarthaṃ manasivṛtya tatra hetuṃ gamyaṃ darśayati--antarityādi /
children.translated_text: Keeping in mind the meaning of '<s>sphuṭitāni</s>' (blossomed/burst) as '<s>truṭitāni</s>' (broken), she shows the implicit reason therein — 'within' etc.
She says that by '<s>sphuṭitāni</s>' another meaning too is discerned — 'likewise' etc.

children.text: yatra strīṇāṃ harati surataglānimaṅgānukūlaḥ siprāvātaḥ priyatama iva prārthanācāṭukāraḥ //
children.translated_text:
'Where the <s>Siprā</s>-breeze, friendly to the limbs, removes the languor of lovemaking from women — /
like a most beloved one, with the sweet coaxing of entreaty.' //

[<s>Locana</s>:] 'And that which is such a vision' — that whose opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>) is in the domain of meaning, the domain to be ascertained, [and which is] firmly established and steady. /
'Likewise' — whose opening is in well-established, worldly meaning, but not in unprecedented meaning as poets [discover] — that [is the vision of the wise]. /
'Of the wise ones' — this is the wisdom of the wise (<s>vaipaścitī</s>). /
'Relying on those two' — /
By the expression '<s>vaipaścitī</s>' meaning 'of the wise,' [the phrase] 'I am not a poet, not a scholar' — the modesty of the self is suggested. /
The meaning is: this pair of visions, though not my own — like furnishings brought from elsewhere into a poor man's house, as mere instruments — has been adopted by me. /
'Relying on those two' — /
For with a single vision, proper examination cannot be accomplished. /
'The universe' — the entirety. /
'Ceaselessly' — /
Again and again, without stopping. /
'Examining' — by description; that is, describing what has been ascertained: 'this is thus' — examining through reflection, inference, etc. — analyzing [it]; 'what here might be the essence' — sifting grain by grain. /
And what is examined — that is properly examined by a vision that operates in the middle [between extremes] and that has its opening firmly established in particular meanings, a steady [vision]. /
'We' — /
The meaning is: those who are addicted to gathering false views and truth-views. /
'Exhausted' — /
The purport is: not only was the essence not obtained, but rather weariness was gained. /
The word '<s>ca</s>' is in the sense of '<s>tu</s>' (but). /
'Recline on the ocean' (<s>abdhiśayana</s>) — /
The meaning is: through <s>yoganidrā</s> (yogic sleep), You are therefore the knower of the essential nature, established in Your own nature. /
One who is exhausted naturally reveres one who is resting. /
'Devotion to You' — /
You alone are the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), the essence of the universe; devotion to that — arising from the sequence of worship preceded by faith etc. — is immersion in that — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She states the meaning of 'domain of meaning' — 'to be ascertained' etc. /
She also explains it in another way — 'likewise' etc. /
Having stated the suggested meaning of 'relying on those two,' she states its expressed meaning — 'though not one's own' etc. /
'Into a house' — /
The remainder is: non-existent ornaments etc. /
She states the purpose of saying 'both' — 'not indeed with one' etc. /
She states two meanings of 'ceaselessly' — 'again and again' etc. /
She explains 'examining' in two ways through the reliance on the poet's vision — 'examining by description' etc. /
'Likewise' etc. — and so on. /
'By description — examining' means observing. /
She explains the examination through reliance on the wise person's vision — 'this is thus' etc. /
She elaborates on the very act of examining — 'what here might be the essence' etc. /
The fruit of relying on both visions — 'not indeed with one' etc. /
She further clarifies what was previously stated — 'and what' etc. /
She states the purport of 'we' — 'false' etc. /
False vision is the poet's vision; truth-vision is the wise person's vision; those who are addicted to gathering both — the meaning is: those whose purport is [in both]. /
The meaning of '<s>tu</s>' for '<s>ca</s>' — /
The meaning is: it communicates a specific nuance. /
She states the implicit meaning of 'recline on the ocean' — 'through <s>yoganidrā</s>' etc. /
'Therefore' — /
The meaning is: because of the very absence of happiness equal to devotion to You. /
'Of the essence' — /
The meaning is: the knower of one's own essential nature, which is the essence of the universe. /
She also shows another suggested meaning — 'of the inner' etc. /
'Immersion in that' — /
The meaning is: the excess of love directed toward that. /
Alternatively: the meaning is: the inner faculty (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) having its activity shaped by the form of that [Supreme Self]. /
The nature of devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) being of the form of supreme bliss is demonstrated in texts like the <s>Bhaktir asāyana</s> etc. /
She states the introduction to this verse — 'thus' etc. /
'Thus this utterance' — this is the connection. /
She states the ultimate purport of this verse — 'of all' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s>, by '<s>saṅkīrṇatva</s>' (mixed nature), she shows that the mixing (<s>saṅkara</s>) through the relationship of that-which-is-enhanced and that-which-enhances (<s>anugrāhya-anugrāhaka</s>), and mixing through the entry of a single word [into two domains], are intended — 'therein' etc. /
'Therein' — in the stated verse itself. /
'Entry of a single word' — /
The remainder is: of <s>dhvani</s> whose expressed [meaning] has crossed over to another meaning, together with the figure of contradiction (<s>virodhālaṅkāra</s>). /
She also shows doubt-mixing (<s>sandehasaṅkara</s>) here — 'relying on vision' etc. /
'Or the figure of contradiction' — /
In 'relying on those two, examining' — therein, by the word '<s>te</s>' (those), when the referent of the word '<s>dṛṣṭi</s>' (vision/sight) is reflected upon — 'seeing by relying on sight' — through the cognition of a contradictory meaning, [it becomes] the figure of contradiction — this is the meaning. /
Accepting the meaning to be stated, the contradiction is resolved here. /
'Blind' etc. — /
As in '<s>niḥśvāsāndha</s>' etc., by a word like '<s>andha</s>' (blind) etc., the word '<s>dṛṣṭi</s>' (vision), whose expressed meaning is utterly obscured, when reflecting upon the meaning in the form of <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuition) — [it becomes] <s>dhvani</s> whose expressed meaning is utterly obscured — this is the meaning. /
'In the earlier [instance] too' — /
The meaning is: even in 'the vision that is active in tasting <s>rasas</s>.' /
'Thus' — /
The meaning is: doubt-mixing. /
'New' etc. — /
The connection is: by reliance through the word '<s>nava</s>' (new). /
The meaning is: by the illumination through the word '<s>nava</s>.' /
'As verbal-power-reverberation' — the third case-ending is in the qualifier. /
'Illustrates' — /
The meaning is: demonstrates. /
'Of the complete sentence' — /
The meaning is: of the full sentence. /
Some [portions] contain expressed figures, and some are endowed with <s>dhvani</s>-varieties. /
For example: 'Prolonging the bold, intoxicatingly sweet cry of the <s>sārasa</s> (crane) birds — /
at dawns, tinged with the friendly astringency of the fragrance of blossoming lotuses —' /
[<s>Locana</s>:] Or by <s>dhvani</s> — or alternately — by both simultaneously, resting in [different] words — thus there are three varieties. /
Encapsulating this, he states with emphasis — 'by reference to words alone' etc. /
Where not even the suspicion of the enhanced-enhancer relationship enters — to illustrate that third variety, he begins — 'for where' etc. /
Because where some [words] contain figures and some are endowed with <s>dhvani</s> — as in 'prolonging' etc. /
The connection with the preceding passage should be made by repeating: 'the mixture with expressed figures is by reference to words of such a nature alone.' /
'For here' — /
The word '<s>hi</s>' here should be connected after the word '<s>maitrī</s>' (friendliness) — this is the textual coherence. /
'Prolonging' — /
For by the <s>Siprā</s>-breeze that cry is carried even far away; and those [cranes], joyful from the touch of the gentle wind, cry for a long time; and that cry, mixed with the sweet sound born of the <s>Siprā</s>-waves agitated by the wind, becomes long — thus the prolongation is [threefold]. /
'Bold' (<s>paṭu</s>) — /
And that gentle breeze, whose born sound does not overpower the crane's cry but rather, being its companion, enhances it. /
And its enhancing is not useless, because intoxicated by it, [the cry becomes] melodious, sweet, worth listening to. /
'At dawns' — /
The dawn is the appropriate occasion for such service [of the breeze]. /
The plural indicates that this delight [occurs] always and constantly there. /
'Blossoming' — with the abundance of honey contained within. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Absence of that' — /
The meaning is: absence of that mixing. /
'Alternately' — /
The remainder is: to be understood as resting in [different] words. /
'The third [variety] indeed' — /
The meaning is: what was stated as 'by both simultaneously, resting in [different] words' — that very [third variety]. /
She connects the sentence beginning with 'for where' — 'because' etc. /
'Because' — this states the meaning of the word '<s>hi</s>.' /
'By repetition' — /
The repetition of the words 'mixture with expressed figures is by reference to words alone' — and therein, the meaning of 'by reference to words' is 'by reference to words of such a nature' — this is the purport. /
This is specification, and the remainder 'therein' should be understood. /
She explains the threefold prolongation of the cry caused by the <s>Siprā</s>-breeze as stated in 'prolonging' — spatial, temporal, and through mixing with its own kind — with 'by the <s>Siprā</s>-breeze' etc., ending with 'prolongation.' /
'Bold' — 'capable' — [taken as] a qualifier of the action 'prolonging' — with this intention she comments — 'and that' etc. /
'Gentle' — mild. /
'Enhances, nourishes' — because it is sweet, therefore it is not useless — this is the connection. /
'Of such service' — /
The meaning is: service in the form of removing the languor after love-making etc. /
'There' — /
The meaning is: in <s>Ujjayinī</s>.

children.translated_text: She introduces the passage beginning with 'combined' etc. — 'thus, with this much' etc. /
'Of those, among themselves too' — /

children.text: dantakṣatāni karajaiśca vipāṭitāni prodbhinnasāndrapulake bhavataḥ śarīre /
children.translated_text: The bite-marks and the scratches torn by nails — on your body covered with thick goose-bumps —
bestowed by the lioness with a passionate heart, have been gazed upon with longing even by the sages. //

[Locana:] 'Thus' — those lotuses that are bloomed, blossomed, and charming to the eyes — the friendship (<s>maitrī</s>) that exists with their fragrance — [meaning] the acquisition of mutual affinity through unbroken contact — by that, it is tinged with the astringent (<s>kaṣāya</s>); and 'colored astringent by the nectar' — meaning made of an astringent hue [reddish-yellow] by the pollen-nectar. /
'Of women' — /
of all such [beings] who are the essence of the three worlds — he who thus acts: he dispels the languor (<s>glāni</s>) produced by love-making, the physical weariness; and furthermore, he dispels the languor pertaining to that [love-making] by rekindling the desire for amorous union. /
And not even by overwhelming mastery — for it is agreeable to the body, pleasant to touch, and residing within the heart. /
'In the beloved' — for the purpose of entreaty regarding that [beloved], he causes flatteries to be uttered. /
The beloved too, his desire for union awakened by the touch of that wind, /
utters flatteries for the purpose of entreaty — thus, being made to act in this way by that [wind], that wind is the very totality of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) whose life-breath is mutual love. /
And this is fitting for that [wind], since it is the breeze familiar with [the river] <s>Siprā</s> — thus urbane, not uncultivated. — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She states the deeper meaning — 'charming to the eyes' etc. /
Since the primary meaning of the word '<s>maitrī</s>' (friendship) is obstructed here, she shows what is intended by that word — 'unbroken contact' etc. /
'Unbroken contact' (<s>abhyāsaṅgāviyoga</s>) — the non-separation of contact, non-interruption — that is, unbroken contact — this much [is meant]. /
By that, the acquisition of mutual affinity, of mutual beneficence — this is the meaning. Here, unbroken contact is the indicated meaning (<s>lakṣyārtha</s>), while the acquisition of mutual affinity is the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) — this is the distinction. /
'Tinged' — connected. /
She states an alternative meaning — 'by the nectar' etc. /
Mixed with the yellowish [hue] — [meaning] reddish, of astringent color. /
'Of all' — this states the meaning of the plural. /
'Of such' — qualified by womanhood. /
'Of the three worlds' etc. — stating the implied meaning. /
She explains '<s>surata-glāni</s>' (love-making weariness) in two ways — as 'the weariness produced by love-making' and 'the weariness pertaining to love-making' — 'produced by love-making' etc. /
'Weariness' (<s>tānti</s>) — /
The meaning is: physical exhaustion. /
'Languor' (<s>glāni</s>) — /
The meaning is: listlessness. /
'And not' — /
'Dispels' is carried over. /
'Agreeable to the body' — she says that the meaning is also 'agreeable to the heart' — 'residing within the heart.' /
The meaning is: gentle, tender. /
Intending the word-division 'in the beloved' [as locative], she also construes it as a qualifier of the wind — 'the beloved' etc. /
The elaboration of the locative 'in the beloved' is — 'regarding that [domain].' /
'For the purpose of entreaty' — /
The meaning is: producing the desire for union in women. /
'One who makes flattery' — from the causative form, the agent-suffix — she says: 'flatteries' — here indeed the word '<s>maitrī</s>' is a <s>dhvani</s> of the <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (non-intended expressed meaning) type. /
In the other words, other <s>alaṅkāras</s> [are present]. /
The <s>dhvani</s> mixed with combined <s>alaṅkāras</s> — as in — [<s>Locana</s>:] the meaning is: mostly rustic/unrefined. /
The beloved too, at the end of love-making, agreeable to the body through massage etc., one who utters flatteries for the purpose of entreaty — in precisely this manner dispels the weariness of love-making. /
The cooing — and words of non-acceptance etc. — the sweet sounds, he prolongs. /
And at the occasion of uttering flatteries — the face that is bloomed, blossomed, bearing the beauty of a lotus — the friendship with its fragrance, the intimacy with its innate sweetness — by that, it becomes tinged with the astringent. /
Agreeable to the limbs — in the practices of the sixty-four arts. /
Thus, where the sounds, forms, fragrances, and touches are pleasing, and where even the wind is thus urbane — that place must certainly be visited by you — this is the utterance of the lover to the cloud regarding [the city of] <s>Ujjayinī</s> in the <s>Meghadūta</s>. /
She applies the definition to the example — 'the word <s>maitrī</s>' etc. /
The word '<s>hi</s>' (indeed) should be read after [the previous word] — this has already been stated. /
'Other <s>alaṅkāras</s>' — /
The meaning is: <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), <s>svabhāvokti</s> (description of nature), <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), and <s>upamā</s> (simile), in that order. /
Thus, with this much — together with its own subdivisions, with <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, and with <s>alaṅkāras</s> — /
by admixture and combination — /
thus, having explained up to this point and examined the examples, she illuminates the meaning of the pair of words 'again' in the <s>kārikā</s> portion, precisely through examples — 'combined' etc. /
The meaning of the word 'again' is: not only are the combination and admixture of <s>dhvani</s> with its own subdivisions etc. intended, but also [those] of the latter among themselves — the own subdivisions — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'he makes [her] utter' — /
She explains this very [point] — 'the beloved too' etc. /
'By that' — /
The meaning is: by the wind. /
'Mutual' etc. — /
The purport is: because it kindles the desire for union in women and in the beloved. /
'Familiar with <s>Siprā</s>' — from this, the heroine-status of <s>Siprā</s> [personified] is understood. /
'Thus' — in the sense of reason. /
She applies the qualifiers to the beloved as well in the analogue — 'the beloved too' etc. /
'By massage etc., agreeable to the body' — this is the construction. /
'One who utters flatteries' — /
The meaning is: one who makes flattering speeches. /
'Words of non-acceptance' — /
The meaning is: words such as 'I won't' etc. /
The elaboration of '<s>madakala</s>' (intoxicated-sweet) is — 'sweet sounds.' /
'At the occasion of flattery-making' etc. — /
The meaning is: at the occasion of hearing the flattering speeches of the beloved. /
'Blossomed' — /
The purport is: due to the smile born of hearing the flatteries. /
The word '<s>kamala</s>' (lotus), through contextual indication (<s>sādhyavasānalakṣaṇā</s>), is intended to mean 'face' — she says: 'lotus' etc. /
'Face' — /
'Of women' is to be supplied. /
She also explains 'agreeable to the body' in another way — 'in the limbs' etc. /
Showing the essential meaning of the verse, she concludes the elaboration — 'thus' etc. /
'That place' — /
The meaning is: the region of <s>Ujjayinī</s>. /
'<s>Utprekṣā</s>' etc. — /
'Skillfully prolonging' — therein there is implied <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy); '<s>pratyūṣa</s>' — description of natural state (<s>svabhāvokti</s>); 'agreeable to the body, gentle' — through superimposition of this upon the wind, <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor); or alternatively, the meaning of '<s>rūpaka</s>' here is <s>rūpakātiśayokti</s> (hyperbolic metaphor). /
Since the word '<s>kamala</s>' (lotus) evokes cognition of the face, <s>upamā</s> (simile) should be understood there. /
'Like the beloved' — and <s>upamā</s> [is also present] — this is the meaning. /

children.translated_text: That <s>rasa</s> — either <s>dharma-vīra</s> or <s>śānta</s> — and the combination of <s>dhvani</s> with combined <s>alaṅkāras</s> [is exemplified] as follows —
'<s>ahiṇaapaoarasaesu pahiasāmāiesu diahesu</s> /
<s>sohai pasāraagiāṇaṃ ṇacciaṃ moravandāṇam</s>' //

[Vṛtti:] Here, the illumination is of <s>dhvani</s> of the imperceptibly-sequenced suggested meaning, which is mixed with the <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) figure that is combined with <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression). /
Because the <s>dayā-vīra</s> (heroism of compassion) has, in ultimate analysis, become the sentence-meaning. /
[<s>Locana</s>:] The admixture and combination of <s>dhvanis</s> that are mixed or combined with their own subdivisions or with <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> is difficult to discern — therefore a perfectly clear example is not [easily] available — with this intention, the admixture and combination with a figure, [specifically] of a figure combined or mixed with [another] figure, within <s>dhvani</s>, are to be demonstrated. /
Of that fourfold division, he gives an example of the first division — 'bite-marks' etc. /
Someone utters a flattery to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has given away his own body to a lioness intent on devouring her own cubs. /
'Thick goose-bumps have arisen' — where, by the flood of bliss born from the attainment of benefit for another. /
'Whose heart is passionate about blood' — one whose desire is for blood; and 'whose heart is enamored' — /
the contradiction is between 'sages whose amorous passion has been awakened' [being aroused by compassionate acts]. /
'With longing' — [meaning:] 'we too shall someday ascend to this path of compassion; then we shall truly become sages' — with such daydreaming. /
And <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) arises because of the cognition of the heroine's episode. /
'Of <s>dayā-vīra</s>' — /
Because of being motivated by compassion, the <s>dharma</s> here — <s>dharma-vīra</s> (heroism of righteousness) itself is denoted by the word <s>dayā-vīra</s>. /
And <s>vīra</s> (heroic) is the <s>rasa</s> here, since <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm/perseverance) alone is the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) — this is the purport. /
Or, by the word <s>dayā-vīra</s>, he designates the <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) [rasa]. /
That [rasa] is here — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'the combination and admixture are intended' continues [from above]. /
'This meaning' — the connection is with the preceding. /
Now, what is the basis in the <s>vṛtti</s> for demonstrating only the division of being mixed with combined <s>alaṅkāras</s> etc.? — to this she says: 'of the own subdivisions' etc. /
'With <s>dhvani</s>' — /
The meaning is: together with <s>dhvani</s>. /
'Because it is difficult to discern' — /
The meaning is: for the reason of being difficult to discern. /
'Clear' — /
The meaning is: perfectly clear. /
'To be demonstrated' — capable of being demonstrated. /
'The first division' — /
The meaning is: the division in the form of being mixed with combined <s>alaṅkāras</s>. /
'Born from the attainment of benefit for another' — /
The meaning is: born from the [successful] rescue of others. /
And born from the <s>nāyikā</s>'s union — [this is also implied]. /
By 'your body,' the body of the lover is understood; and by 'the lioness's wife' (<s>mṛgarājavadhū</s>), the wife of a person named <s>Mṛga</s> or belonging to that clan is understood. /
In 'gazed upon with longing even by sages' — the contradiction is stated as: 'even by those dispassionate toward sense-objects, whose passion has been awakened' — she says 'sages and' etc. /
She states the relevant meaning — 'with longing' etc. /
'With daydreaming' — this is the construction. /
Since by the <s>Muni</s> [author] <s>dayā-vīra</s> was not directly mentioned [in the text], she says — '<s>dayā</s>' etc. /
The connection is: because of being motivated by compassion here, <s>dharma-vīra</s> alone is denoted by the word <s>dayā-vīra</s>. /
She states an alternative — 'by the word <s>dayā-vīra</s>' etc. /
She elaborates the <s>vṛtti</s> passage beginning with 'combined with <s>samāsokti</s>' etc. — 'that, here' etc. /

children.translated_text: <s>Locana</s>: <s>Rasa</s> is supported by blended figures of speech (<s>saṃsṛṣṭālaṅkāra</s>). This meaning is accomplished through the power of <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression)—just as a certain person, at the moment of union with a beloved sought through hundreds of desires, experiences <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation), so too you, through the gift of your own body for the benefit of others, display an excess of <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) kindled by the abundance of <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent indicators) and <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinant causes). Regarding 'on the two days': likewise, when they have assumed the appearance of night toward the travelers—because they cause delusion in the darkened ones; or alternatively, <s>śyāmāyita</s> means the darkening of the travelers due to the power of grief, from which comes <s>śyāmikā</s> (discoloration). The dance of the flocks of peacocks with outstretched necks is resplendent. When the travelers serve as the audience (<s>sāmājika</s>) who relish dramatic performance (<s>abhinayaprayoga</s>), the dance of the flocks of peacocks with extended songs—that is, songs following excellent melodic progressions—and likewise with necks extended for the neck-gesture (<s>grīvārecaka</s>), is resplendent. 'Acting like dark women toward the travelers'—the <s>kyac</s> suffix is used in the sense of behavior. Through this suffix, an implicit simile (<s>luptopamā</s>) is indicated. In 'the travelers being spectators,' the <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound being transparent constitutes <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). By these two [figures], the blending (<s>saṃsarga</s>) of <s>dhvani</s> [with figures] is intended—this is the author's purport. Since in this very example the other pair of sub-types can also be illustrated, no separate example was given. Thus: when <s>vyāghra</s> (tiger) and such belong to the <s>ākṛtigaṇa</s>, 'the travelers being spectators' involves both <s>upamā</s> (simile) and <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). <s>Bālapriyā</s>: Regarding '<s>rasa</s> is supported by blended figure of speech': the meaning is 'by <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) as a figure blended with <s>samāsokti</s>.' Keeping in mind that the supportive role of <s>virodha</s> is clear from the cognition of the enrichment of <s>dayāvīra</s> (the heroic sentiment of compassion) through the phrase 'gazed upon even by sages in whom longing has arisen,' he explains the role of <s>samāsokti</s> with 'through the power of <s>samāsokti</s>' and so on. The word 'iti' means 'in this sense.' Regarding '<s>anubhāva</s>' and so on: the <s>anubhāva</s> is the manifestation of intense <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation); the <s>ālambanavibhāva</s> (foundational determinant) is the lioness; the <s>uddīpanavibhāva</s> (excitant determinant) should be understood as the tooth-marks and such. 'The second' means: that which has the nature of being blended with blended figures of speech. Regarding '<s>Abhinava</s>' and so on: this is a description of the rainy season (<s>varṣā</s>). Here, first he explains the denoted meaning with '<s>abhinava</s>' and so on. '<s>Pathika</s>' means those separated from their beloveds (<s>virahin</s>). In '<s>śyāmāyiteṣu</s>,' intending that the <s>kyac</s> suffix is used in the sense of behavior from the word <s>śyāmā</s> meaning 'night,' he explains with 'because they cause delusion' and so on. Intending that <s>śyāmāyita</s> means <s>śyāmikā</s>, he says 'or alternatively' and so on. <s>Śyāmikā</s> is a change of complexion. By showing an alternative shade of meaning, he reveals the suggested sense here, with 'who relish dramatic performance' and so on. The explanation of 'with extended songs' is given as 'excellent' and so on. Here, in the alternative reading, 'with outstretched necks' should also be construed—thus he says 'likewise' and so on. He elaborates on the blending of <s>dhvani</s> with blended figures with 'toward the travelers' and so on. Regarding '<s>rūpaka</s>': the sense is that the quality of being spectators is superimposed upon the travelers. Regarding '<s>dhvani</s>': the meaning is 'of the suggested sense expressed through the phrase beginning with dramatic performance and so on.' <s>Saṃsarga</s> means blending (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>). Regarding 'the other pair of sub-types': here indeed, through <s>upamā</s> and <s>rūpaka</s>, the <s>dhvani</s> that has the form of suggested meaning arising from the power of words (<s>śabdaśaktyudbhava</s>) and taking the form of resonance (<s>anuraṇana</s>) is in a state of blending.

children.text: uktasvarūpadhvaninirūpaṇanipuṇā hi satkavayaḥ sahṛdayāśca niyatameva locanam sandehāspadatvena saṅkīrṇābhyāmabhinayaprayoge, abhinavaprayoge ca rasikeṣviti prasāritagītānāmiti yaḥ śabdaśaktyudbhavasta saṃsargamātramanugrāhyatvābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: For good poets and connoisseurs who are skilled in the investigation of <s>dhvani</s> whose nature has been described, by setting their vision on the right path, certainly attain the highest degree of excellence in the composition and comprehension of poetry.

children.text: 'pahiasāmāiesu' ityatra tu pade saṅkīrṇābhyāṃ tābhyāmupamārūpakābhyāṃ śabdaśaktimūlasya dhvaneḥ saṅkīrṇatvamekavyañjakānupraveśāditi saṅkīrṇālaṅkārasaṃsṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the word '<s>pahiasāmāiesu</s>' (Prakrit for 'among the traveler-spectators'), through these two blended figures—<s>upamā</s> and <s>rūpaka</s>—the <s>dhvani</s> whose suggested content takes the form of resonance (<s>anuraṇana</s>) rooted in the power of words (<s>śabdaśakti</s>) is in a state of blending.
One should understand that there is also a pair of sub-types: blended with blended figures (<s>saṅkīrṇālaṅkārasaṅkīrṇa</s>). (43)
He concludes this with 'thus' (<s>evam</s>).
This is clear. (44)

children.text:
atha 'sahṛdayamanaḥprītaye' iti yatsūcitaṃ tadidānīṃ na śabdamātramapi tu nirvyūḍhamityāśayenāha--ityukteta /
yaḥ prayatnato vivecyaḥ asmābhiścoktalakṣaṇo dhvaniretadeva kāvyatattvaṃ yathoditena prapañcanirūpaṇādinā vyākartumaśaknuvadbhiralaṅkāraiḥ rītayaḥ bālapriyā saṅkīrṇālaṅkārasaṃsṛṣṭatvasaṅkīrṇālaṅkārasaṅkīrṇatvarūpabhedadvayamityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: The syntactical connection is: 'through the two blended [figures], <s>upamā</s> and <s>rūpaka</s>.'

children.text: 'ahiṇaa' ityasya abhinaya abhinava ityubhayathāpi cchāyeti darśayan dhvaniṃ darśayati--abhinayetyādi /
children.translated_text: Showing that '<s>ahiṇaa</s>' (Prakrit) can mean both <s>abhinaya</s> (dramatic gesture) and <s>abhinava</s> (new/fresh), and that this constitutes a shade of meaning, he demonstrates the <s>dhvani</s> in the <s>Locana</s> with the passage beginning '<s>abhinaya</s>' and so on.
Because there is no capacity for being supported [by the figure].
The continuation is: 'of that [dhvani], through <s>upamā</s> and <s>rūpaka</s>.' (43)

Now, what was indicated by the phrase 'for the delight of the hearts of connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>)' is now shown to be not merely a verbal [promise] but fully demonstrated—thus he concludes with 'this <s>dhvani</s> whose characteristics have been stated' and so on.
Regarding 'this' (<s>etad</s>):
The meaning is: the statement of the many varieties. (44)

children.text:

children.translated_text: Regarding 'of the connoisseurs' (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) and so on: the meaning is 'as was stated: we shall describe its true nature for the delight of the hearts of connoisseurs.' Regarding 'in composition and in understanding': as the author of the treatise previously declared:
This essence of poetry (<s>kāvyatattva</s>), as has been described, which had flashed forth but indistinctly (<s>asphuṭasphurita</s>),
was [the reason why] literary styles (<s>rīti</s>) were introduced by those who were unable to articulate it fully. (DhvK 3.46)

children.text:
etaddhvanipravartanena nirṇītaṃ kāvyatattvamasphuṭasphuritaṃ sadaśaknuvadbhiḥ pratipādayituṃ vaidarbhī gauḍī pāñcālī ceti rītayaḥ pravartitāḥ /
rītilakṣaṇavidhāyināṃ hi kāvyatattvametadasphuṭatayā manāksphuritamāsāditi lakṣyate tadatra sphuṭatayā sampradarśitenānyena rītilakṣaṇenana kiñcit /
children.translated_text: This essence of poetry, established through the exposition of <s>dhvani</s>, having flashed forth but indistinctly, the earlier masters who were unable to articulate it introduced the constructs known as <s>rītis</s> (literary styles).
Some [styles] are based on the essence of words (<s>śabdatattva</s>), others are endowed with the essence of meaning (<s>arthatattva</s>);
the compositional modes (<s>vṛtti</s>) also become illuminated when this characteristic of poetry is understood. (DhvK 3.47)
Some [styles] are based on the essence of words (<s>śabdatattva</s>), others are endowed with the essence of meaning (<s>arthatattva</s>);
the compositional modes (<s>vṛtti</s>) also become illuminated when this characteristic of poetry is understood. (47)

children.text:
asmin vyaṅgyavyañjakabhāvavivecanamaye kāvyalakṣaṇe jñāte sati yāḥ kāścitprasiddhā upanāgārakādyāḥ śabdatattvāśrayā vṛttayo yāścārthatattvasambanddhāḥ kaiśikyādayastāḥ samyagrītipadavīmavataranti /

prakarṣapadavīmiti /
nirmāṇe bodhe ceti bhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: Regarding 'by those who were unable to articulate': the reason is—'having been made to flash forth indistinctly' (<s>asphuṭaṃ kṛtvā sphuritam</s>).
'It is characterized thus' (<s>lakṣyata</s>).
For <s>rīti</s> (literary style) ultimately resolves into the <s>guṇas</s> (poetic qualities) alone.

children.text: yadāha--viśeṣo guṇātmā guṇāśca rasaparyavasāyina eveti hyuktaṃ prāgguṇanirūpaṇe 'śṛṅgāra eva madhuraḥ' ityatreti // 45//
children.translated_text: As was stated: 'The distinguishing feature is constituted by the <s>guṇas</s>, and the <s>guṇas</s> culminate in <s>rasa</s> alone'—for this was said earlier in the discussion of the <s>guṇas</s>.

When this characteristic of poetry, consisting of the discernment of the relation between the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) and the suggestive (<s>vyañjaka</s>), is understood, then the well-known <s>rītis</s> such as <s>Vaidarbhī</s> and others, as well as the <s>vṛttis</s> (compositional modes) such as <s>Vaidālī</s> and so forth—the nature of all these also becomes clearly illuminated.

children.text:
prakāśanta iti /
anubhavasiddhatāṃ kāvyajīvitatve prayāntītyarthaḥ /
rītipadavīmiti /
bālapriyā ityuktetyādikamekaṃ vākyamasphuṭetyādivākyāntaraṃ tatraitadityanena dhvaneḥ parāmarśaśceti bodhyam /

children.translated_text: He supplies [the words] 'in composition and in understanding' to complete the phrase 'attain the highest degree of excellence.'

children.text: 'asphuṭasphuritaṃ sadi'ti vṛtyā tatpadaṃ hetugarbhamiti darśitaṃ, tadeva spaṣṭayati--vyākartumityādi /
children.translated_text: It was shown through the <s>vṛtti</s> (auto-commentary) that the expression '<s>asphuṭasphuritam</s> being so' contains the reason within the word itself; he makes this explicit with 'having been made to flash forth indistinctly' and so on.
To the question 'how is what was said in the <s>vṛtti</s> as it is characterized justified?'—he provides the justification with '<s>rīti</s> indeed' and so on.
Here the syntactical connection is: 'thus it was indeed stated.' (45)

Regarding 'become illuminated': the meaning is that they attain the status of being established through direct experience (<s>anubhavasiddhatā</s>) as the life-force of poetry. Wishing to express poetry that follows the well-established path of <s>rīti</s> and is pure in tradition (<s>sampradāyaśuddha</s>), he says 'some based on words' and so on.

children.translated_text: In some manuscripts there is also the reading '<s>bhāva</s>.'

children.text: tatpakṣe anākhyeyāṃśabhāvitvamiti śloke tasyoktameva dhvanilakṣaṇaṃ sādhīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In that reading, 'the nature of having an indescribable aspect' — in the verse, the stated definition of <s>dhvani</s> alone is the better [definition].
This has been stated: 'The fact of being illuminated by an indescribable aspect — by virtue of [having] an inexpressible meaning — this is of <s>dhvani</s>

children.text: na lakṣaṇaṃ, lakṣaṇaṃ tu sādhīyo 'sya yathoditam //
children.translated_text: not the definition; rather, the definition that has been stated [previously] is the better one.' //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Keeping in mind the purport that will be stated in the <s>vṛtti</s>, namely 'being established through experience,' she explains — 'through experience' etc. /
Just as the genuineness (<s>jātyatva</s>) of particular gems, the beauty that shines forth as indescribable in poetry — where the designation <s>dhvani</s> applies — whatever definition of <s>dhvani</s> is stated by someone — [the objection that] it is unfounded does not merit consideration. /
For the specific feature residing in the inherent nature of words is: when there is absence of awkwardness, the usage of what is not previously used [i.e., originality]. /
But the specific feature residing in the expressive [words] is: lucidity (<s>prasāda</s>) and suggestive capacity (<s>vyañjakatva</s>). /
And the specific feature of meanings is: manifestation with clarity, subordination to the suggested, and being qualified by a suggested component. /
And those specific features can be explained, and have been explained in many ways. /
But the supposition of a specific feature that is indescribable and beyond these is rooted only in the absence of discriminative faculty. /
Since the indescribability — [<s>Locana</s>:] just like that [i.e., like <s>rīti</s>], because it culminates in <s>rasa</s>. /
There is also the reading '<s>pratītipadavīm</s>' (the path of cognition). /
For the <s>anuprāsa-vṛtti</s> (alliterative style) called <s>nāgarikā</s> (urbane) rests in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc., [being like] a refined comparison. /
'Harsh' (<s>paruṣā</s>) — in blazing [<s>rasas</s>] like <s>raudra</s> etc. /
'Gentle' (<s>komalā</s>) — /
In <s>hāsya</s> (comic) etc. /
Likewise — regarding what was stated by the sage (<s>Muni</s>, i.e., <s>Bharata</s>): '<s>vṛttis</s> (styles) are the matrices of poetry' — therein, the specific mode of behavior appropriate to <s>rasa</s> is the <s>vṛtti</s>. /
As he states: '<s>Kaiśikī</s> has delicate costume and arises from <s>śṛṅgāra-rasa</s>' — etc. /
To this extent, in the passages beginning with 'others have declared its non-existence' among the alternatives of non-existence — '<s>vṛttis</s> and <s>rītis</s> have come within the range of hearing; what then is this <s>dhvani</s> beyond them?' /
Therein, some kind of acceptance was made, and some kind of refutation was given, through the statement '<s>asphuṭasphurita</s>' (indistinct flash). /
Now, what was said in 'it is established that words [cannot reach] the domain beyond' — that was refuted even in the first <s>Uddyota</s>, with the intention that in the narration of the complete exposition, indescribability is simply inconceivable. /
'Absence of awkwardness' — /
The meaning is: absence of harshness to the ear etc. /
'Usage of what is not previously used' means non-repetition. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Just like that' — just like <s>rīti</s> (literary style). /
It should be said that this is the explanation of 'they shine forth, entering the path of <s>rīti</s>' — but that is impossible, because the two have different meanings. /
Moreover, in 'entering the path of <s>rīti</s>,' even the causal status of knowledge of the definition of poetry is difficult to establish — therefore, the reading here must be otherwise — she says: '<s>pratītipadavīm</s>' (the path of cognition). /
She shows the <s>rasa</s>-culminating nature of <s>vṛtti</s> specifically — '<s>nāgarikā</s>' etc. /
In the <s>vṛtti</s> — 'where' etc. /
The construal is: where, like the genuineness of particular gems, the beauty of certain words and meanings, knowable [only] to a particular type of apprehender, shines forth as truly indescribable. /
'Unfounded' — /
The meaning is: because of being unfounded — this is the reason. /
Intending that beauty is indeed a specific feature that should be articulated, she establishes the statement 'it does not merit consideration' — 'since' etc. /
'Residing in the inherent nature' — the connection of this is with 'specific feature.' /
In the <s>Locana</s>, having paraphrased the <s>vṛtti</s>, she says — 'to this extent' etc. /
'<s>Dhvani</s>' — /
The word 'stated' (<s>yadūce</s>) applies here by attraction. /
'Refutes' — /
The meaning is: having paraphrased with 'where' etc., refutes with the passage 'that is unfounded' etc. /
The connection is: refutes with [this] intention. /
She explains 'absence of awkwardness' — 'of what is heard' etc. /
[The claim of] the absence of discriminative faculty — this portion [namely, the claim] that it is beyond all words — is not possible for anyone. /
For ultimately, its expression is possible through the word '<s>anākhyeya</s>' (indescribable) itself. /
When there is absence of being the domain of conceptual cognition (<s>savikalpaka</s>) that touches universals — but what is sometimes called 'indescribability,' namely the nature of being manifest — that too is not possible for specific poetic [instances], just as for specific gems. /
Because the forms of those have been analyzed by the writers on <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (poetic definition). /
And because the valuation of specific gems is seen to be based merely on the supposition of universals. /
But even for both of these [gems and poetry], there indeed exists knowability by a specific type of apprehender. /
For indeed only specialists are knowers of the true nature of gems, and only connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdayas</s>) are appreciators of the <s>rasas</s> of poetry — who disagrees here? /
But the indescribability that is the domain of all definitions, well-known among the Buddhists — we shall examine that in another work, in the examination of that doctrine. /
But here, the illumination of even a fragment heard from another work would cause displeasure to the connoisseurs, and therefore it is not undertaken. /
Or, just as for the Buddhists the definition of direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) etc. [is indescribable], so too our definition of <s>dhvani</s> will be [equally valid]. /
Therefore, since another definition does not work, and since it is not [merely] a matter of words and meanings — [<s>Locana</s>:] 'so much' — pertaining to words and pertaining to meanings. /
'Absence of discriminative faculty' — where that faculty declines — its nature is lack of discrimination. /
'The conceptual cognition that touches universals — the word arising from that' — she shows that even in the illustration, indescribability does not exist — 'and of particular gems' etc. /
Objection: that is not cognized by everyone — anticipating this, she responds by way of concession — 'of both' etc. /
'Of gems and of poetry.' /
Objection: 'words do not even touch the meaning,' and in [the statement] 'the cognizer of the indescribable' etc. — how then is the indescribability of things stated? — to this she says — 'but what' etc. /
For thus, <s>dhvani</s> would be exactly like the state of all entities, and 'the nature of <s>dhvani</s> is indescribable' would be an over-pervasive definition — this is the purport. /
'In another work' — in the <s>Viniścayaṭīkā</s>, the commentary on <s>Dharmottara</s>'s [work] — that was composed by this very author — therein that was explained. /
[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] She comments — 'of discrimination' etc. /
She explains 'universal' etc. — 'universal' etc. /
'Touching universals' — /
The meaning is: apprehending universals such as genus (<s>jāti</s>) etc. /
'Conceptual cognition' — /
The meaning is: determinate cognition (<s>savikalpakajñāna</s>). /
'The word arising from that' — /
The meaning is: the word that has the form of usage and is caused by that. /
'Shows that it does not exist' — /
The purport is: because the valuation of particular gems is seen to be based on the mere supposition of the universal of genuineness etc. /
'That' — /
The meaning is: genuineness and beauty. /
She shows the fault of the definition in the form of indescribability, as indicated by the statement 'we shall examine that in another work' — 'for thus' etc. /
'Of all entities' — /
The meaning is: of all referents. /
The connection is: the definition would be over-pervasive. /
'By me alone' is the meaning — /
By this, the nature of the [verse] beginning with '<s>anākhyeya</s>' as a <s>parikara-śloka</s> (ancillary verse) is shown. /
'Of the indescribable component' — /
The meaning is: of that which is the indescribable aspect, the essential-nature aspect.
Thus ends the Third <s>Uddyota</s> in the <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> composed by the revered teacher <s>Rājānaka Ānandavardhana</s>. //

children.text:
locanam uktamiti /
saṃgrahārthaṃ mayaivetyarthaḥ /
anākhyeyāṃśasyābhāso vidyate yasmin kāvye tasya bhāvastanna lakṣaṇaṃ dhvaneriti sambandhaḥ /
atra hetuḥ--nirvācyārthatayeti /
nirvibhajya vaktuṃ śakyatvādityarthaḥ /
anyastu 'nirvācyārthatayā' ityatra niso nañarthatvaṃ parikalpyānākhyeyāṃśabhāsitve 'yaṃ heturiti vyācaṣṭe, tattu kliṣṭam /
children.translated_text: But another [commentator], taking '<s>nis</s>' in '<s>nirvācyārthatayā</s>' as having a negative meaning, explains that this is the reason for having an indescribable aspect — but that is forced.
And the reason [in that interpretation] is not different from what is to be proved — therefore the explanation stated [by us] alone [is correct] — may there be auspiciousness.
Having reflected upon the varieties of <s>dhvani</s> that were brought to fame in the <s>Kāvyāloka</s> [i.e., Dhvanyāloka],
now this <s>Locana</s> (Eye) will render the people fulfilled, [just as the eye renders people capable of seeing].

[<s>Locana</s>:] 'Has been stated' — /
The meaning is: 'by me alone,' for the purpose of summary. /
The connection is: the nature of that poetry in which there is a manifestation of an indescribable aspect — that is not the definition of <s>dhvani</s>. /
The reason here: 'by virtue of having an inexpressible meaning' — /
The meaning is: because it is capable of being stated by dividing [it into parts].
[I bow to] the <s>Madhyamā</s> (the Middle [goddess/speech]) who bestows clarity upon the threaded [i.e., systematically presented] categories,
who is dear to <s>Trilocana</s> (Three-eyed <s>Śiva</s>) — I salute <s>Parameśvarī</s> (the Supreme Goddess) in her <s>Madhyamā</s> form. //

Thus ends the Third <s>Uddyota</s> in the <s>Sahṛdayāloka-Locana</s>, the elucidation of <s>Dhvani</s>, composed by the most eminent among the great <s>Māheśvara</s> teachers, <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. //

children.translated_text: For <s>Madhyamā</s> [speech] gives clarity to <s>Vaikharī</s> [speech, i.e., articulate speech].
'<s>Madhyamā</s>' —
The meaning is: having the form of <s>Madhyamā</s>.

children.text: śubhamastu sarvaṃ śivam iti śrīrāmaśārakaracitāyāṃ locanaṭippaṇyāṃ tṛtīya uddyotaḥ //
children.translated_text: May all be auspicious, may all be blessed — thus ends the Third <s>Uddyota</s> in the <s>Locanaṭippaṇī</s> (Gloss on the Locana) composed by <s>Rāmaśāraka</s>. //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] [Five <s>ṛ</s>-signs] — should be read. /
'That' — /
The meaning is: being of an indescribable nature. /
'<s>Nirvācyārthatayā</s>' — or the reading '<s>nirvācyāṃśatayā</s>.' /
The explanation of '<s>nir</s>' is: 'by dividing.' /
She states another defect — 'and the reason' etc. /
'Not different from what is to be proved' — /
The meaning is: non-distinct from the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved). /
'<s>Kāvyāloka</s>' [i.e., Dhvanyāloka] — /
'Brought to fame' — /
The meaning is: elaborated. /
'Reflecting upon' — this contains the reason. /
'<s>Locana</s>' etc. — /
The purport is: just as the eye renders people fulfilled, so does this commentary. /
'Of the threaded' — /
of the categories that have been properly indicated by <s>sūtras</s> (aphorisms), having the form of the varieties of <s>dhvani</s> etc. — the poetic modes — their attainment of clarity — /
that which bestows the attainment of clarity.
Fourth <s>Uddyota</s>

children.text: caturtha uddyotaḥ evaṃ dhvaniṃ saprapañcaṃ vipratipattinirāsārthaṃ vyutpādya tadvyutpādane locanam caturtha uddyotaḥ kṛtyapañcakanirvāhayoge 'pi parameśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Fourth <s>Uddyota</s>. Having thus taught <s>dhvani</s> with its full elaboration for the purpose of removing misconceptions, in that teaching — [<s>Locana</s>:] Fourth <s>Uddyota</s>. Even when the accomplishment of the fivefold duties is conjoined [with Him] — <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) —
who is not dependent on any other instrument through that [power] — I salute that <s>Śāṅkarī</s> (Śakti of Śiva). // //

children.translated_text: Since it is known in a very clear form, therefore a clear exposition [appears] different from an unclear exposition — hence 'another purpose' is stated.

children.text: athavā pūrvoktayoḥ prayojanayorantaraṃ viśeṣo 'bhidhīyate; kena viśeṣeṇa satkāvyakaraṇamasya prayojanaṃ, kena ca satkāvyabodha iti viśeṣo nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the distinction (<s>antara</s>) between the two previously stated purposes is being expressed: by what specific distinction is the composition of good poetry its purpose, and by what [distinction] is the knowledge of good poetry [its purpose] — this distinction is being determined.

children.text: bālapriyā atha caturthodyotaṭippaṇī prārabhyate arthodyotaṃ caturthe ca locanasya yathāmati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Now the gloss on the Fourth <s>Uddyota</s> is begun: 'In the fourth [<s>Uddyota</s>], I shall illuminate the meaning of the <s>Locana</s> according to my understanding —
I shall comment upon [it] to some extent — may the wise be gracious to me herein.' // //

To fashion the connection with the next <s>Uddyota</s>, the author of the <s>vṛtti</s> says — 'thus' etc. /
'Another purpose' — /
Although the purpose was already stated previously through '<s>sahṛdayamanaḥprītaye</s>' ('for the delight of the hearts of connoisseurs'), and by the end of the Third <s>Uddyota</s> it was somewhat clarified as 'either to compose good poetry or to know it' — still, the effort now is to make it even more clear.

children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>kṛtya</s>' (actions): The fivefold <s>kṛtya</s> (divine actions) consists of creation and so forth. As stated: 'His fivefold action is declared to be creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment, and the bestowing of grace—of Him who is eternally manifest.' By which cause, namely that which has the form of <s>Māyā</s>, He requires no other instrument—this is the syntactic connection. The meaning is: relying upon <s>Māyā</s> alone, He accomplishes creation and the rest. Regarding 'the connection with another <s>uddyota</s> (illumination)': the meaning is the connection of the fourth <s>uddyota</s> with the third <s>uddyota</s>. Anticipating the objection that since the very same purpose already stated is going to be discussed again, speaking of 'another purpose' is unjustified, he resolves this with 'although' and so forth. To the objection that even though the purpose in the form of aesthetic delight has been stated, what is to be discussed is something different from that, he says 'in the third' and so forth. 'That very'—the meaning is: that very purpose. 'To make clearer'—'that very' is carried forward syntactically. 'Is known'—the remainder is 'what is to be discussed.' To the question 'what follows from that?' he says 'therefore' and so forth. 'From what has been unclearly established'—the remainder is 'from the purpose.' The meaning is: through the statement 'those who are properly engaged, whether in composing or understanding good poetry, should carefully discriminate <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion),' the fact that discriminating <s>dhvani</s> serves the purpose of both composing and knowing good poetry is obtained by implication—therefore that purpose has been unclearly established. 'Clear establishment'—the meaning is: clearly stated. He explains in another way with 'or rather' and so forth. An elaboration of what was already said—'by what distinguishing feature' and so forth. 'Of this'—the meaning is: of the elucidation of <s>dhvani</s>. Another purpose is stated—
The path that has been shown for <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) together with <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggested meaning),
By this, the quality of <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuition) of poets attains infinity. // <s>DhvK</s> 4.1 //
The path that has been shown for <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) together with <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggested meaning),
By this, the quality of <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuition) of poets attains infinity. // 1 //

For by being adorned with even any one of these modes,

For by being adorned with even any one of these modes,
speech attains novelty even while dealing with previously treated subjects. // 2 //

children.text: locanam tatra satkāvyakaraṇe kathamasya vyāpāra iti pūrvaṃ vaktavyaṃ niṣpāditasya jñeyatvāditi taducyate--

children.translated_text: 'The path of <s>dhvani</s>' and so forth. // 1 //

<s>Locana</s>: In this regard, the question of how this functions in the composition of good poetry should be addressed first, since what has been accomplished is to be known—therefore that is stated—

nanu dhvanibhedāt pratibhānāmānantyamiti vyadhikaraṇametadityabhiprāyeṇāśaṅkate--kathamitīti /
atrottaram--ato hīti /
āsatāntāvad bahavaḥ prakārāḥ, ekenāpyevaṃ bhavatītyapiśabdārthaḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati--varṇanīyavastuniṣṭhaḥ prajñāviśeṣaḥ pratibhānaṃ, tatra varṇanīyasya pārimityādādyakavinaiva spṛṣṭatvāt sarvasya tadviṣayaṃ pratibhānaṃ tajjātīyameva syāt /
tataśca kāvyamapi tajjātīyameveti bhraṣṭa idānīṃ kaviprayogaḥ, uktavaicitryeṇa tu ta evārthā niravadhayo bhavantīti tadviṣayāṇāṃ pratibhānāmānantyamupapannamiti /
nanu pratibhānantyasya kiṃ phalamiti nirṇetuṃ vāṇī navatvamāyātītyuktaṃ, tena vāṇīnāṃ kāvyavākyānāṃ tāvannavatvamāyāti /
tacca pratibhānantye satyupadyate, taccārthānantye, tacca dhvaniprabhedāditi /
bālapriyā kathamasya vyāpāra itīti /
dhvanipratipādanaṃ kathamupayogītyetadityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Thus this'—this is the syntactic connection. // 1 //

With the idea that infinity of <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuitions) resulting from the varieties of <s>dhvani</s> is a predication across different substrata, he raises the objection—'how' and so forth. The answer to this is 'for by this' and so forth. 'Let the many modes remain as they are; even by a single one this can happen'—such is the meaning of the word '<s>api</s>' (even). What is being said is this: <s>pratibhāna</s> (creative intuition) is a special capacity of insight directed toward the subject to be described. Now, since the totality of describable subjects has already been touched upon by the first poet himself, all <s>pratibhāna</s> regarding those subjects would be of the same kind. Consequently, poetry too would be of the same kind, and thus the enterprise of poets today would be futile. But through the variety already described, those very same subjects become unlimited, and therefore the infinity of <s>pratibhānas</s> directed toward them is established. Now, to determine what the fruit of this infinity of <s>pratibhāna</s> is, it is said 'speech attains novelty.' Thus, speech—that is, poetic utterances—attains novelty. And that arises when there is infinity of <s>pratibhāna</s>, and that in turn arises from the infinity of meanings, and that from the varieties of <s>dhvani</s>. <s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'How does this function'—the meaning is: how is the elucidation of <s>dhvani</s> useful?

children.translated_text: The word '<s>iti</s>' indicates conclusion.

children.text: ato dhvaneruktaprabhedamadhyādanyatamenāpi prakāreṇa vibhūṣitā satī vāṇī purātanakavinibaddhārthasaṃsparśavatyapi navatvamāyāti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, speech, when adorned by even any one mode among the aforementioned varieties of <s>dhvani</s>, attains novelty even while being connected with subjects treated by ancient poets.

children.text: tathāhyavivakṣitavācyasya dhvaneḥ prakāradvayasamāśrayaṇena navatvaṃ pūrvārthānugame 'pi yathā--- smitaṃ kiñcinmugdhaṃ taralamadhuro dṛṣṭivibhavaḥ parispando vācāmabhinavavilāsorbhisarasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, by resorting to the two modes of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (unintended expressed meaning) type of <s>dhvani</s>, novelty is achieved even when following previously treated subjects, as in: 'A slightly innocent smile, the splendor of a glance tremulous and sweet, the movement of speech rippling with waves of fresh <s>vilāsa</s> (playful grace),

children.text: gatānāmārambhaḥ kisalayitalīlāparimalaḥ spṛśantyāstāruṇyaṃ kimiva hi na ramyaṃ mṛgadṛśaḥ //
children.translated_text: the beginning of her gaits fragrant with tender-shoot-like sportiveness—of the doe-eyed maiden entering <s>tāruṇya</s> (youth), what indeed is not lovely?'

Regarding 'across different substrata'—the meaning is: incongruent. He shows the meaning of the word '<s>api</s>' in 'even by any one' with 'let them remain' and so forth. 'What is being said is this'—the meaning is that the purport to be stated through the latter half of the first <s>kārikā</s> (verse) and through the second <s>kārikā</s> is being demonstrated. He states that very purport with 'the subject to be described' and so forth, up to 'from the varieties of <s>dhvani</s>.' 'Directed toward the subject to be described' means pertaining to each particular describable object. 'A special capacity of insight'—the meaning is: having the nature of a flash of inspiration. The remainder is 'of the poet.' 'Of the same kind'—the meaning is: of the same kind as the <s>pratibhāna</s> of the first poet. 'Of the same kind indeed'—the meaning is: of the same kind as the poetry of the first poet. The word '<s>iti</s>' has a causal sense. 'Futile'—the continuation is 'would be.' 'Through the variety already described'—the meaning is: through the variety of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggested meaning). The elaboration of 'of speech' is 'of poetic utterances.'
