apaunaruktyābhimāno na bhavatīti /
vācyānāṃ ca kāvye pratibhāsamānānāṃ yadrūpaṃ tattu grāhyaviśeṣābhedenaiva pratīyate /
children.translated_text: And as for the form in which the expressed contents (<s>vācya</s>) appear in poetry — that is apprehended only through the non-difference of the particular object of cognition (<s>grāhyaviśeṣa</s>).
Therefore, one who advocates variety in expression (<s>uktivaicitrya</s>), even while not wishing it, must necessarily accept variety in the expressed content (<s>vācyavaicitrya</s>) as well.
Here then is the summary — if for even a single [poet] other than <s>Vālmīki</s>,
creative intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) regarding poetic meanings is admitted, then that infinitude [of meaning] is inexhaustible.

By such reasoning, only the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) is apprehended. 'Why?' — The purport is: how can those who hold the present thesis accept the repetitiveness of meaning when it is not being experienced [as such]? He makes this very point explicit — with 'if not' etc. 'For expression (<s>ukti</s>)' etc. — if the distinction in expression consists merely in synonymy (<s>paryāya</s>), then when the same meaning is composed using other synonyms without deficiency, one does not hold the conviction that there is no repetition. [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Even in the case of direct perception' — the meaning is: even when poets have direct perception of the true nature of things. 'Is apprehended' — the word 'by the poet's speech' is to be supplied. In the <s>Vṛtti</s>: 'of what is to be conveyed' — the meaning is: the commonality, i.e., the generic nature, of things to be experienced and of experiences. 'Of that' — the meaning is: of the commonality of what is to be conveyed and the conveyance. 'When it is not the domain' — 'of the ancients' is to be connected. 'Of those' — the meaning is: of the moderns. And the connection is: 'it is merely conceit.' After 'here it is said' (<s>tatrocyate</s>), the reading is: 'but what was said, namely that poetic activity relies only on the generic' etc. In some manuscripts, however, before this passage there is also the reading: 'if poetic activity relies only on the generic, then the variety of poetry of the demonstrated kind arising from differences in states etc. — should it then be considered merely repetitive? If not so, then why is there not infinitude of poetic meaning?' That passage from the <s>Locana</s> extends from 'then what about this?' to 'if not.' She elucidates the purport of the passage beginning with 'for expression' etc. — beginning with 'merely in synonymy' etc. 'Merely in synonymy' means: merely in designation by another word. 'Then' — that is to say. 'Without deficiency' — without incompleteness. 'The conviction of non-repetition does not arise.'

children.text:
kiñca, uktivaicitryaṃ yatkāvyanavatve nibandhanamucyate tadasmatpakṣānuguṇameva /
yato yāvānayaṃ kāvyārthānantyabhedahetuḥ prakāraḥ prāgdarśitaḥ sa sarva eva punaruktivaicitryāddviguṇatāmāpadyate /
yaścāyamupamāśleṣādiralaṅkāravargaḥ locanam tasmādviśiṣṭavācyapratapādakanaivokterviśeṣa iti bhāvaḥ /
grāhyaviśeṣeti /
grāhyaḥ pratyakṣādipramāṇairyo viśeṣaḥ tasya yo abhedaḥ /
tenāyamarthaḥ--padānāntāvatsāmānye vā tadvati vāpohe vā yatra kutrāpi vastuni samayaḥ, kimanena vādāntareṇa? vākyāttadviśeṣaḥ pratīyata iti kasyātra vādino vimatiḥ /
anvitābhidhānatadviparyayasaṃsargabhedādivākyārthapakṣeṣu sarvatra viśeṣasyāpratyākhyeyatvāt /
uktivaicitryañca na paryāyamātrakṛtamityuktam /
anyattu yattatpratyutāsmākaṃ pakṣasādhakamityāha---kitrceti /
punariti /
bhūya ityartha-. upamā hi nibha, pratim cchala, pratibimba, praticchāya, tulya, sadṛśābhāsādibhirvicitrābhiruktibhirvicitrībhavatyeva /
vastuta etāsāmuktīnāmarthavaicitryasya vidyamānatvāt /
niyamena bhānayogāddhi nibhaśabdaḥ, bālapriyā kintu paunaruktyabuddhireva bhavatītyarthaḥ /
viśiṣṭavācyeti /
vācyaviśeṣetyarthaḥ /
pratyakṣādipramāṇaiḥ grāhya iti sambandhaḥ /
tenāyamartha iti /
uktagranthena vakṣyamāṇo 'rthassidhyatītyarthaḥ /
mīmāṃsakādīnāṃ mate sāmānye vastuni, naiyāyikamate tadvati, bauddhamate apohe samayaḥ /
vādāntareṇavādaviśeṣeṇa /
tadviśeṣaḥ vastuviśeṣaḥ /
kasyātra vimatiḥ na kasyāpi /
atra hetumāha---anvitetyādi /
anvitābhidhānādīnāṃ ye vākyārthatvapakṣāsteṣu sarveṣvapītyarthaḥ /
viśeṣasyāpratyākhyeyatvāditi /
pratītāviti śeṣaḥ /
vastuviśeṣapratīteḥ pratyākhyātumaśakyatvādityarthaḥ /
punaruktivaicitryādityatratyapunaśśabdasya vyākhyānam---bhūya iti /
'yaścāyam' ityādigranthasya bhāvārthavivaraṇam--upametyādi /
upamā hi vicitrībhavatyeveti sambandhaḥ /
nanu nibhapratimādiśabdānāṃ samānārthakatvāt kathaṃ ta citryamityata āha---vastuta ityādi /
upasaṃharati---evamiti /
taditi /
ralaṅkāravargaḥ prasiddha sa bhaṇitivaicitryādupanibadhyamānaḥ svayamevānavadhirdhatte punaḥ śataśākhatām /
children.translated_text: The well-known group of <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech), when composed with variety of expression (<s>bhaṇitivaicitrya</s>), itself becomes boundless, further branching into hundreds of sub-varieties.

children.text: bhaṇitiśca svabhāṣābhedena vyavasthitā satī pratiniyatabhāṣāgocarārthavaicitryanibandhanaṃ punaraparaṃ kāvyārthānāmānantyamāpādayati /
children.translated_text: And expression (<s>bhaṇiti</s>), being established according to the distinctions of one's own language, produces yet another infinitude of poetic meanings, grounded in the variety of content within the domain of each particular language.

children.text: yathā mamaiva--- mahamaha itti bhaṇantau vajjadi kālo jaṇassa /
children.translated_text: As for example my own [verse] — 'Saying "it is great, it is great!" (<s>mahaṃ maha itti bhaṇantau</s>), the life of a person passes by;

children.text: toi ṇa deu jaṇaddaṇa goarī bhodi maṇaso // //
children.translated_text: yet, O <s>Govarī</s> (lit. one of the cow-herder clan), the mind does not grant [us even] a single moment of respite from the torment of birth.'

Moreover, the variety of expression (<s>uktivaicitrya</s>) that is cited as the basis for the novelty of poetry — that itself supports our position. For whatever variety of causes for the infinitude of poetic meaning was previously demonstrated, all of that is doubled through the variety of expression. And this group of <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech) such as <s>upamā</s> (simile), <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), and so on — [<s>Locana</s>:] Therefore, the distinction of expression (<s>ukti</s>) consists precisely in conveying a distinguished expressed content (<s>vācya</s>) — this is the purport. Regarding '<s>grāhyaviśeṣa</s>' (particular object of cognition) — <s>grāhya</s> means that which is cognizable by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and other <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge); the non-difference of its particularity. Hence the meaning is this: whether the convention pertains to the universal, or to the universal-possessor, or to exclusion (<s>apoha</s>) — in whichever entity — what is the point of this doctrinal alternative? That the particular is cognized from the sentence — which theorist disputes this? Because in all the theories of sentence-meaning — whether <s>anvitābhidhāna</s>, its opposite [<s>abhihitānvaya</s>], or those based on varieties of syntactic connection — the particular cannot be rejected. And it has been said that variety of expression is not produced merely by synonymy. But the other point — that it actually supports our position — he states with 'moreover' etc. 'Again' (<s>punar</s>) — the meaning is 'further.' For <s>upamā</s> (simile) indeed becomes varied through varied expressions such as <s>nibha</s> (resembling), <s>pratima</s> (likeness), <s>cchala</s> (semblance), <s>pratibimba</s> (reflection), <s>praticchāya</s> (shadow-image), <s>tulya</s> (equal), <s>sadṛśa</s> (similar), <s>ābhāsa</s> (appearance), and so on. In reality, this is because variety of meaning exists in these expressions. Because the word <s>nibha</s> necessarily involves the relation of shining — [<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] Rather, the meaning is: the notion of repetition alone arises. '<s>Viśiṣṭavācya</s>' — the meaning is: a particular expressed content. 'Cognizable by perception and other <s>pramāṇas</s>' — this is the connection with <s>grāhya</s>. 'Hence this meaning' — the meaning is: by the stated passage, the meaning about to be stated is established. In the view of the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> etc. the convention is in the universal; in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, in the universal-possessor; in the <s>Bauddha</s> view, in exclusion (<s>apoha</s>). 'By a doctrinal alternative' — by a particular doctrine. 'That particular' — the particular of the thing. 'Who disputes this?' — no one. He states the reason — beginning with '<s>anvita</s>' etc. The meaning is: in all the theories of sentence-meaning including <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> etc. 'Because the particular cannot be rejected' — the word 'in cognition' is to be supplied. The meaning is: because the cognition of the particular of a thing cannot be denied. The explanation of the word <s>punar</s> ('again') in 'through the variety of expression again' — is 'further.' The elucidation of the purport of the passage beginning with 'and this group' — begins with '<s>upamā</s>' etc. The connection is: <s>upamā</s> indeed becomes varied. Now, since words like <s>nibha</s>, <s>pratima</s>, etc. are synonymous, how can there be variety? To this he responds — beginning with 'in reality' etc. He concludes — with 'thus' etc. 'That' —

children.text:
itthaṃ yathā yathā nirūpyate tathā tathā na labhyate 'ntaḥ kāvyārthānām /
idaṃ tūcyate--- avasthādivibhinnānāṃ vācyānāṃ vinibandhanam /
yatpradarśitaṃ prāk locanam tadanukāratayā tu pratimaśabda ityevaṃ sarvatra vācyaṃ kevalaṃ bālopayogi kāvyaṭīkāpariśīlanadaurātmyādeṣu paryāyatvabhrama iti bhāvaḥ /
evamarthānantyamalaṅkārānantyañca bhaṇitivaicitryādbhavati /
anyathāpi ca tattato bhavatīti darśayayi---bhaṇitiśceti /
pratiniyatāyā bhāṣāyā gocaro vācyoyo 'rthastatkṛtaṃ yadvaicitryaṃ tannibandhanaṃ nimittaṃ yasya, alaṅkārāṇāṃ kāvyārthānāñcānantyasya /

children.translated_text: The variety of expression, which is the object [of that cause], is made into the agent — this is the syntactic connection.
The cause is shown under the guise of a qualifier of the object.

children.text: mama mama iti bhaṇato vrajati kālo heturdarśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The cause is shown [in the verse]: 'Of one who recites "mama mama" (mine, mine), time passes by.'

children.text: tathāpi na devo janārdano gocaro bhavati manasaḥ // //
children.translated_text: Even so, Lord <s>Janārdana</s> does not come within the range of the mind.

Thus, the more one examines, the more one cannot find the end of poetic meanings. But this is stated: 'The composition of expressed meanings differentiated by conditions and so forth' — what was shown earlier in the <s>Locana</s> is that through resemblance to that, the word <s>pratimā</s> (image) [is used]; thus everywhere the expressed meaning is merely beneficial for beginners — the idea being that confusion regarding synonymy arises from the vice of excessive familiarity with poetic commentaries. In this way, the infinity of meanings and the infinity of <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech) arise from variety of expression (<s>bhaṇiti-vaicitrya</s>). And it is shown that this arises in yet another way as well — with 'bhaṇitiś ca' (and the mode of expression). The expressed meaning which is the domain of a particular language, and the variety produced by that — this is the basis, the cause, of the infinity of <s>alaṅkāras</s> and poetic meanings.

children.text: madhumathana iti yo anavarataṃ bhaṇati, tasya kathanna devo manogocaro bhavatīti vīrodhālaṅkāracchāyā /
children.translated_text: One who continuously recites '<s>Madhumathana</s>' (Churner of <s>Madhu</s>) — how could the Lord not be within the range of the mind? This is a semblance of <s>virodha-alaṅkāra</s> (the figure of contradiction),
evoked by the expression 'mahamaha' in the <s>Saundhava</s> (Saindhavī) <s>Prākṛta</s> dialect. // 7 //

children.text:
avasthādivibhinnānāṃ vācyānāṃ vinibandhanam /
bālapriyā arthādyānantyamityarthaḥ /
tata iti /
bhaṇitivaicitryādityarthaḥ /
yastetyanyapadārthavivararaṇam--alaṅkārāṇāmityādi /
viśeṣaṇacchaleneti /
pratiniyatetyādiviśeṣaṇavyājenetyarthaḥ /
'mahe'tyādeḥ chāyāmāha--mametyādi /
mama mama iti bhaṇataḥ mamāyaṃ mamedamityādi bhaṇataḥ /
atra mameti prakṛtārthaḥ /
madhumathana iti pratīyamāno viruddhārthaḥ /
tathāpīti virodhadyotakam /
samunmiṣiteti /
mahamaha ityasya mama mama iti madhumathana iti ca chāyā bhavatīti bhāvaḥ // 7 // // //
children.translated_text: The <s>chāyā</s> (Sanskrit shadow-rendering) of 'mahamaha' is both 'mama mama' and '<s>Madhumathana</s>' — this is the purport. // 7 //

<s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'The composition of expressed meanings differentiated by conditions and so forth' — the meaning is: the infinity of meanings and so forth. 'From that' means: from variety of expression. The explanation of the other term in 'yastetyanyapadārtha' is: 'of <s>alaṅkāras</s>' and so forth. 'Under the guise of a qualifier' means: under the pretext of the qualifier beginning with 'pratiniyata' (particular) and so forth. He states the <s>chāyā</s> (shadow-meaning) of the verse beginning with 'mahe' — 'mama' and so forth. 'Of one who recites mama mama' means: of one who says 'this is mine, this is mine' and so on. Here 'mama' is the literal meaning; '<s>Madhumathana</s>' is the suggested contradictory meaning. 'Even so' (<s>tathāpi</s>) indicates the contradiction. 'Samunmiṣita' (evoked) means:

children.text:
ita ūrdhvaṅkārikāvṛtyorbhedasya durgrahatayā tadubhayaṃ pṛthakpradarśayan vivṛṇoti--avasthetyādi /
bhūmnaiva dṛśyate lakṣye
children.translated_text: From here onward, since the distinction between the <s>kārikā</s> and the <s>vṛtti</s> (prose commentary) is difficult to grasp, he elucidates both separately, showing [each distinctly] — beginning with 'avastha' and so forth. 'It is seen abundantly in the object of study'
'that cannot be set aside;'
'. . . . . . . . . . . but that shines forth due to being grounded in <s>rasa</s>.' // <s>DhvK</s> 4.8 //
'... that cannot be set aside;'
'But that shines forth due to being grounded in <s>rasa</s>.' // 8 //
This is stated here in brief, for the instruction of good poets —
'If connected with <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and so forth, and following propriety (<s>aucitya</s>),'
'the course of subject-matter, differentiated by place, time, and so forth, is pursued [by the poet].' // <s>DhvK</s> 4.9 //
'If connected with <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and so forth, and following propriety (<s>aucitya</s>),'
'the course of subject-matter, differentiated by place, time, and so forth, is pursued [by the poet].' // 9 //
Then what count can there be of other poets of limited powers?
'Even by thousands of thousands of <s>Vācaspatis</s> (masters of speech), with effort,'

children.text: nibaddhā sā kṣayaṃ naiti prakṛtir jagatām iva // DhvK_4.10 //
children.translated_text: 'that [poetic creation], once composed, does not reach exhaustion — like the <s>prakṛti</s> (primal nature) of the worlds.' // <s>DhvK</s> 4.10 //
'that, once composed, does not reach exhaustion — like the <s>prakṛti</s> of the worlds.' // 10 //
'Even by thousands of thousands of <s>Vācaspatis</s>, with effort,'

children.text: yathāhi jagatprakṛtiratītakalpaparamparāvirbhūtavicitravastuprapañcā satī locanam bhūmnaiva dṛśyate lakṣye tattu bhāti rasāśrayāt // //
children.translated_text: For just as the <s>prakṛti</s> (primal nature) of the world, having manifested the variegated expanse of things through the succession of past <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic cycles), <s>Locana</s>: 'is seen abundantly in the object of study — but that shines forth due to being grounded in <s>rasa</s>.'
The other text is the intermediate gloss (<s>madhyopaskāra</s>). // 8 //
Thus the <s>kārikā</s>.
Here, however, the meaning of the [first] three quarters is restated, and the meaning of the fourth quarter is stated as something new.
'Tad' (that) and so forth [refers to the beginning of the verse].
Up to 'śaktīnām' (of powers) is the intermediate gloss (<s>madhyopaskāra</s>) of the two <s>kārikās</s>.
He explains the fourth quarter of the second <s>kārikā</s> with 'yathā hi' (for just as). // [9], 10 //

children.text: 'yatpradarśitaṃ prāgi'ti 'na tacchakyamapohitum' iti ca grantha ityarthaḥ // 8 // // //
children.translated_text: The texts 'what was shown earlier' and 'that cannot be set aside' constitute the [intermediate] text — this is the meaning. // 8 //
<s>Bālapriyā</s>: 'The other text' means:

children.text:
caturthetyādi /
'tattu bhāta rasāśrayā'dityasyārtho 'tra vidhīyamāna ityarthaḥ /
karikayoriti /
'rasabhāve'tyādeḥ 'vācaspatī'tyādeśca kārakayorityartha- /
upaskāra iti /
yadyanvīyate anyaiḥ kavibhiḥ tattarhi ityarthaḥ /
anyeṣāṃ vālmīkivyatiriktānām /
kavīnāṃ gaṇanā kā /
te agaṇyā bhaveyuriti tadarthaḥ /
turyaṃ pādamiti /
prakṛtirjagatāmiveti pādamityarthaḥ /
vyācaṣṭa iti /
kṣayaṃ naitītyanena saha vivṛṇotītyarthaḥ /
yathāhītīti /
'yathāhī'tyādinā 'abhidhātum' ityantagranthenetyarthaḥ. 'tadvadi'tyādikaṃ tu vācaspatītyādipādatrayārthavivaraṇam /
vṛttau 'jagatprakṛtiri'ti /

children.translated_text: The <s>prakṛti</s> (primal nature) which is the cause of the world — this is the meaning.
'Atīta' (past) means:

children.text: atītānāṃ kalpanāṃ paramparāyāmāvirbhūntaḥ āvirbhāvitaḥ vicitrāṇāṃ vastūnāṃ prapañco yayā sā 'parī'ti /
children.translated_text: That in which there has been the manifestation, through the succession of past <s>kalpas</s>, of the expanse of variegated things — thus 'parī' means:
One whose creative power for producing further objects is exhausted, destroyed — this is the meaning. // [9], 10 //

'Caturtha' (the fourth) and so forth. The meaning of 'but that shines forth due to being grounded in <s>rasa</s>' is here being expounded — this is the meaning. 'Of the two <s>kārikās</s>' means: of the <s>kārikā</s> beginning with '<s>rasabhāva</s>' and the <s>kārikā</s> beginning with '<s>vācaspati</s>'. 'Gloss' (<s>upaskāra</s>) means: 'if it is pursued' by other poets, then — this is the meaning. 'Of others' means: of those other than <s>Vālmīki</s>. What count can there be of poets? They would be innumerable — that is the meaning. 'The fourth quarter' means: the quarter '<s>prakṛtir jagatām iva</s>' (like the <s>prakṛti</s> of the worlds). 'He explains' means: he elucidates together with 'it does not reach exhaustion.' 'Yathā hi' means: by the passage beginning with 'yathā hi' and ending with 'abhidhātum' (to state). The passage beginning with 'tadvad' and so forth is the explanation of the meaning of the three quarters beginning with '<s>vācaspati</s>'. In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'jagat-prakṛti' means:

children.text:
punaridānīṃ parikṣīṇā parapadārthānirmāṇaśaktiriti na śakyate 'bhidhātum /
tadvadeveyaṃ kāvyasthitiranantābhiḥ kavimatibhirupabhuktāpi nedānīṃ parihīyate, pratyuta navanavābhirvyutpattibhiḥ parivardhate /
itthaṃ sthite 'pi--
children.translated_text: Yet again, it cannot now be said that its creative power for producing further objects is exhausted. Just so, this state of poetry (<s>kāvya-sthiti</s>), though enjoyed by countless poetic minds, is not now diminished; rather, it grows ever more through ever-new cultivated insights (<s>vyutpatti</s>). Even though this is so —

children.text: saṃvādās tu bhavanty eva bāhulyena sumedhasām /
children.translated_text: 'Correspondences (<s>saṃvādas</s>) do indeed occur abundantly among the wise-minded;'

children.text: sthitaṃ hy etat saṃvādinya eva medhāvināṃ buddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For this is established: the intellects of the wise are indeed concordant.'
'But —'

children.text: naika-rūpatayā sarve te mantavyā vipaścitā // DhvK_4.11 //
children.translated_text: 'all those [correspondences] should not be considered by the discerning person as being of a single form.' // <s>DhvK</s> 4.11 //
'Correspondences (<s>saṃvādas</s>) do indeed occur abundantly among the wise-minded;'

children.text: sthitaṃ hyetat saṃvādinya eva medhāvināṃ buddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For this is established: the intellects of the wise are indeed concordant.'

children.text: kintu-- naikarūpatayā sarve te mantavyā vipaścitā // 11 //
children.translated_text: 'But — all those should not be considered by the discerning person as being of a single form.' // 11 //

children.text: kathamiti cet--- saṃvādo hyanyasādṛśyaṃ tatpunaḥ pratibimbavat /
children.translated_text: If one asks how — 'For correspondence (<s>saṃvāda</s>) is similarity with another; and that again is like a reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>),'
'like the form of a painting (<s>ālekhya</s>), and like one with a similar body (<s>tulya-dehin</s>) among embodied beings.' // 12 //

children.text: saṃvādo hi kāvyārthasyocyate yadanyena kāvyavastunā sādṛśyam /
children.translated_text: Correspondence (<s>saṃvāda</s>) of poetic meaning is said to be the similarity of one poetic subject-matter with another.

That, again, is established in three ways among embodied beings: like a reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>), like the form of a painting (<s>ālekhyākāra</s>), and like one with a similar body (<s>tulya-dehin</s>).

children.text: kiñciddhi kāvyavastu vastvantarasya śarīriṇaḥ pratibimbakalpam, locanam saṃvādā iti kāri kāyā ardhaṃ, naikarūpatayeti dvitīyam // 11 //
children.translated_text: For some poetic subject-matter is like the reflection of another embodied person. <s>Locana</s>: The first half of the <s>kārikā</s> is '<s>saṃvādāḥ</s>' and so on; the second [half] is '<s>naika-rūpatayā</s>.' // 11 //
With the intention 'Is this a royal decree?' he raises a doubt — 'katham iti cet' (if one asks how). In response to this —

children.text: saṃvādo hy anya-sādṛśyaṃ tat punaḥ pratibimbavat /
children.translated_text: 'For correspondence (<s>saṃvāda</s>) is similarity with another; and that again is like a reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>),'

children.translated_text: Here, understanding that '<s>saṃvādāḥ</s> of the wise-minded' means 'correspondences of the intellects of the wise and of their poems,' [the commentator] has stated in the <s>vṛtti</s> 'this is established' and so forth, as well as 'correspondence of poetic meaning is said to be' — this should be understood. // 11 //

Thus by this <s>kārikā</s>. This has been explained in the <s>vṛtti</s> by breaking it into parts. It is shown that the word 'ca' (and) in '<s>śarīriṇām</s>' (of embodied beings) should be understood with each clause.

children.translated_text: 'Explained in the <s>vṛtti</s> by breaking into parts' — the implied completion is: 'in certain manuscripts.' Hence it will be stated: 'In certain manuscripts the <s>kārikās</s> are seen unbroken.' The explanation by breaking into parts should be understood as: '<s>saṃvādo hy anya-sādṛśyam</s>' — 'correspondence of poetic meaning is said to be similarity with another poetic subject-matter; that again is like a reflection; that again, among embodied beings, is like a reflection' — and so forth. 'With each clause' and so forth: the meaning is that '<s>śarīriṇām</s>' has a syntactic connection with all three [similes] — <s>pratibimba</s> and so forth. Another [type of correspondence] is like a painting; yet another is similar to one with a similar body.
'Among those, the first has no independent nature; the second has an insubstantial nature;'

'Among those, the first has no independent nature; the second has an insubstantial nature;'

children.translated_text: The next one — similarity with another that is like a painting — though possessing another body, should be abandoned because of its insubstantial nature.

children.translated_text: But the third — poetic subject-matter that is concordant [with another] while possessing a distinct and beautiful body — should not be abandoned by the poet.

children.translated_text: For it cannot be said that an embodied being who is similar to another embodied being is just one and the same.
<s>Locana</s>: The meaning is 'of the principal [type].' // 12 //
Among those, the first — poetic subject-matter that is like a reflection — should be avoided by the wise poet, because it has no independent nature, being devoid of a real body.
'Among those, the first has no independent nature; the second has an insubstantial nature;'
'but the third has a well-established nature — the poet should not abandon similarity with another.'

children.text: anukāre hyanukāryabuddhireva citrapustādāviva na tu sindūrādibuddhiḥ sphurati, sāpi ca na cārugatvāyeti bhāvaḥ //13//
children.translated_text: For in an imitation, only the cognition of the thing imitated arises — as in a painted figure and so forth — and not the cognition of the pigments like vermilion and so on; and even that [cognition of the imitated thing] does not lead to aesthetic charm — this is the purport. // 13 //

Thus the <s>kārikā</s>. '<s>Ananyātma</s>' (having no independent nature): that whose nature or essential character is not different from the earlier composed poem — [meaning] that the form in which it appears has already been touched upon by a previous poet; just as the form in which a reflection appears is really just the original object itself. As for what it itself is like, he says — 'devoid of a real body': for nothing novel has been imagined by that [poet]; a reflection too is exactly like this. Having thus explained the first type, he explains the second — 'the next one' and so forth.

children.translated_text: and as 'should be abandoned.' // 12 //

<s>Bālapriyā</s>: In the <s>vṛtti</s>, 'of poetic meaning' is to be supplied. He explains the similarity with another that pertains to poetic meaning — 'that by another' and so forth. In the three [similes] beginning with '<s>pratibimbavat</s>' (like a reflection), the suffix <s>vati</s> follows a word ending in the sixth case (genitive). In [the case of] a reflection, similarity with another is similarity with the embodied original (<s>bimba</s>); likewise in the cases of the painting-form and the similar-bodied one, similarity with the embodied being should be understood. The passage beginning with 'kiñcid dhi' states the upshot. There, the explanation of the word '<s>śarīriṇaḥ</s>' is given in the <s>Locana</s> beginning with 'pūrvam eva' and so forth. The explanation of the meaning conveyed by '<s>na anya-sāmyaṃ tyajet kaviḥ</s>' (the poet should not abandon similarity with another) is given in the <s>vṛtti</s> as 'should be avoided by the wise one'

children.translated_text:
[<s>Vṛtti</s>:] When the essential self — the core of the true nature — comes into being, even though another of the same kind previously existed, the thing shines forth even more. /
For a thing graced by the lustre of what was charming in the past nourishes supreme beauty, like [a new] body. /
It does not, however, appear as mere repetition. /
Like the moonlit face of a slender woman. /
Thus, for the time being, the boundaries of sentence-meanings that constitute aggregates and possess mutual correspondence have been demarcated. /
And to establish that for poetic subject-matters that are in the form of word-meanings and resemble other subject-matters, there is simply no fault — it is stated:
Just as the arrangement of phonemes etc. is employed, where an old arrangement of subject-matter is [also reused] —

anena sādasya heturdarśitaḥ /
pūrvopaskāreṇa saha paṭhatīti /

yeṣāṃ sukavīnāṃ prāktanapuṇyābhyāsaparipākavaśena pravṛttisteṣāṃ paroparacatārthaparigrahaniḥspṛhāṇāṃ svavyāpāro na kvacidupayujyate /
saivabhagavatī sarasvatī svayamabhimatamarthamāvirbhāvayati /

ityakliṣṭarasāśrayocitaguṇālaṅkāraśobhābhṛto yasmādvastu samīhitaṃ sukṛtibhiḥ sarvaṃ samāsādyate /

kārikāyāṃ suveriti jātāvekavacanamityabhiprāyeṇa vyācaṣṭe--sukavināmiti /
etadeva spaṣṭayati--prāktanetyādi /
na teṣāmityantena /
āvirbhāvayatīti /

children.translated_text: The meaning is: creates only the new. // 17 // // //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Let them be extended' — /
'Measured' means weighed; 'having manifold meanings [as sweet] as nectar' — having manifold meanings equal to nectar; as many meanings as there are, so many [are the expressions] — this is the purport. /
As in <s>Māgha</s>: 'speech having as many words as meanings.' /
'Speeches' — in the form of poetry. /
By poets, 'let them be extended' — let them be composed in full detail. /
'Unprecedented' —

children.translated_text: 'With aspiration' — with thought.
'Without effort' — devoid of effort regarding poetry.
'Would be' —
'How could it not be? It would indeed be' — this is the meaning. // 17 //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] 'Thus' — /
The meaning is: by the method of exposition through <s>kārikā</s> and <s>Vṛtti</s>. /
The poetry that bears beauty consisting of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures) that are effortless (<s>akliṣṭa</s>) and appropriate as the support of <s>rasa</s>. /
A garden too — the effortless, timely lustre produced by watering etc. — supported by that and produced by it — the attainment of qualities such as delicacy, lustre, fragrance, etc. of ornaments —

children.text:
ityakliṣṭetyādiślokasthasyetipadasya vivaraṇam---kāriketyādi /

asya dhvanirdarśita ityanena sambandhaḥ /
akliṣṭeti śobhāyāḥ rasāśrayociteti guṇālaṅkārayośca viśeṣaṇamiti darśayan vyācaṣṭe--akliṣṭetyādi /
tata iti /

children.translated_text: For through the timely watering, the attainment of qualities such as delicacy etc. in the garden — which has the form of the aggregate of creepers, trees, etc. — comes about through the abundance of sprouts, leaves, flowers, etc.
The word '<s>alam</s>' here means 'sufficiently' — with this intention, she explains: 'the making of sufficiency.'
The meaning is: the bringing about of completeness.

children.text: kāvyākhye 'khilasaukhyadhāmni vibudhodyāne dhvanirdarśitaḥ so 'yaṃ kalparūpamānamahimā bhogyo 'stu bhavyātmanām //
children.translated_text: 'In the divine garden called poetry — the abode of all happiness — this <s>dhvani</s> has been shown; may this greatness, which has the stature of the wish-fulfilling tree, be enjoyed by those of noble soul.' //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] The elaboration of the word 'thus' in the verse beginning with 'effortless' — '<s>kārikā</s>' etc. /
The meaning is: by the method of the examination through the <s>kārikā</s> and the <s>Vṛtti</s>. /
The connection is with 'this <s>dhvani</s> has been shown.' /
Showing that 'effortless' qualifies beauty, while 'support of <s>rasa</s>' and 'appropriate' qualify <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s>, she explains —

children.text:
satkāvyatattvanayavartmaciraprasupta- kalpaṃ manassu paripakvadhiyāṃ yadāsīt /
locanam etacca sarvaṃ pūrvameva vitatyoktamiti ślokārthamātraṃ vyākhyātam /

ye kaṣṭopadeśenāpi vinā tathāvi dhaphalabhājaḥ tairityarthaḥ /
akhilasaukhyadhāmnīti /
akhilaṃ duḥkhaleśenāpyananuviddhaṃ yatsaukhyaṃ tasya dhāmni ekāyatana ityarthaḥ /
sarvathā priyaṃ sarvathā ca hitaṃ durlabhaṃ jagatīti bhāvaḥ /
vibudhodyānaṃ nandanam /
sukṛtīnāṃ kṛtajyotiṣṭomādīnāmeva samīhitāsādanimittam /
vibudhāśca kāvyatatvavidaḥ /
darśita iti /
sthita eva san prakāśitaḥ, aprakāśitasya hi kathaṃ bhogyatvam /
children.translated_text: means: while already existing, it has been made manifest; for how can something unmanifest be an object of enjoyment?

children.text: kalpataruṇā upamānaṃ yasya tādṛṅmahimā yasyeti bahuvrīhigarbho bahuvrīhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having the <s>kalpataru</s> (wish-fulfilling tree) as its standard of comparison' — this is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound embedded within another <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, meaning 'one whose glory is such that the <s>kalpataru</s> is its analogue.'
For in poetry, the attainment of all desires depends solely on that [<s>dhvani</s>].
And this has been stated at length.

[Locana]: All this has already been stated at length previously, so only the verse-meaning is explained. '<s>Sukṛtibhiḥ</s>' (by the fortunate ones) — those who, even without arduous instruction, are recipients of such fruits — by them, is the meaning. '<s>Akhilasaukhyadhāmni</s>' (in the abode of complete bliss) — '<s>akhila</s>' means that bliss which is not pervaded even by a trace of suffering; '<s>dhāmni</s>' means 'in its sole abode' — that is the meaning. The purport is: that which is in every way pleasing and in every way beneficial is rare in this world. '<s>Vibudhodyāna</s>' (garden of the gods) means <s>Nandana</s> (the divine pleasure-garden). It is the cause of fulfilling the desires only of the meritorious — those who have performed the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and other rites. And '<s>vibudhāḥ</s>' (the wise ones) also means those who know the true nature of poetry. 'Shown' (<s>darśita</s>) —

udyānasyeva kāvyasyāpi vibudhapadārthasambandho 'rthādvivakṣita ityāśayenāha---vibudhāścetyādi /
kāvyatatvavidaśceti yojanā /
cakāreṇa devā ityarthasya samuccayaḥ /

atra kalpatarusāmyasya mahimni śabdena bodhane 'pi mahimāśraye dhvanau tasya paryavasānaṃ bodhyam /
kāvyaṃ nandanodyānena tulyaṃ dhvaniḥ kalpatarutulyaśceti bhāvaḥ /
ata eva dhvaneḥ kalpatarusāmyaprayojakaṃ darśayannāha---sarvetyādi /
samīhitaṃ prītyādi /

satkāvye'ti /
satkāvyatvasya dhvanisvarūpasya 'nayavartma, nyāyyamārgaḥ sādhakaṃ yuktijātamityarthaḥ /
'cire'ti /

children.translated_text: means: from a long time, like something dormant — clearly unmanifest, is the meaning.
'<s>Paripakvadhiyām</s>' — of those earlier authors whose understanding had matured, who knew the highest [truths].
'<s>Tat</s>' — [refers to]

children.text: dhvanisvarūpaṃ tatsā tadyvākarotsahṛdayodayalābhaheto- rānandavardhana iti prathitābhidhānaḥ //
children.translated_text: the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> — that [nature] was elucidated by the one whose celebrated name is <s>Ānandavardhana</s>, for the sake of attaining the elevation of <s>sahṛdayas</s> (connoisseurs).

[Bālapriyā]: '<s>Tathāvidhaphalabhājaḥ</s>' — those who partake of such fruits, i.e., those whose nature it is to partake of such things as poetic cultivation and the like, those who are worthy of them — that is the meaning. 'By them' — meaning by princes and others. The word '<s>khila</s>' here means 'suffering.' '<s>Akhila</s>' is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound meaning 'that in which there is no <s>khila</s> (suffering)' — with this intention he glosses it as 'suffering' etc. He states the purport with 'in every way' etc. With '<s>kṛtajyotiṣṭoma</s>' etc., the meaning of the word '<s>sukṛti</s>' on the side of the garden [metaphor] is explained. Since the connection of the word '<s>vibudha</s>' with poetry, just as with the garden, is implicitly intended — with this understanding he says '<s>vibudhāś ca</s>' etc. The construction is '<s>kāvyatatvavidaś ca</s>' (and those who know the true nature of poetry). By the particle '<s>ca</s>', the meaning 'gods' is included as well. 'Shown' (<s>darśita</s>) — demonstrating that this establishes the capacity for enjoyment, he says 'of the unmanifest' etc. With the intention that the word '<s>upamāna</s>' means 'that which is compared,' he gives the analysis '<s>kalpataruṇā</s>' etc. If, however, the word '<s>upamāna</s>' has the sense of 'instrument of comparison,' then the analysis would be '<s>kalpataruḥ upamānam</s>' (the <s>kalpataru</s> is the standard of comparison). '<s>Bahuvrīhi</s>' — here, although the similarity with the <s>kalpataru</s> is expressed verbally as pertaining to 'glory,' one should understand that it ultimately rests in <s>dhvani</s>, which is the locus of that glory. The purport is: poetry is equal to the <s>Nandana</s> garden, and <s>dhvani</s> is equal to the <s>kalpataru</s>. For this very reason, showing what makes <s>dhvani</s> comparable to the <s>kalpataru</s>, he says 'all' etc. '<s>Samīhita</s>' means delight and the like. '<s>Tadekāyattā</s>' means 'occasioned solely by <s>dhvani</s>.' '<s>Satkāvye</s>' — '<s>satkāvyatvasya</s>': the '<s>nayavartma</s>' (path of method) of the true nature of good poetry, i.e., of the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s>, means the proper path, the set of reasonings that establish it — that is the meaning. '<s>Cire</s>' —

children.text: iti śrīrājānakānandavardhanācāryaviracite dhvanyāloke caturtha uddyotaḥ samāpto 'yaṃ granthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the Fourth <s>Uddyota</s> (Illumination) in the <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> composed by the revered master <s>Rājānaka Ānandavardhana</s>. This work is complete.

children.translated_text: 'For the attainment' — the connection is: 'must be made to engage for the attainment [of the treatise's purpose].'

children.text: locanam tadeva nāmaśravaṇaṃ keṣāñcannivṛttiṃ karoti, tanmātsaryavijṛmbhitaṃ nātra gaṇanīyam, niśreyasaprayojanādeva hi śrutātko 'pi rāgāndho yadi nivartate kimetāvatā prayojanamaprayojanamapyavaśyaṃ vaktavyameva syāt /
children.translated_text: [Locana]: Indeed, that very hearing of the name causes some people to turn away — but that outburst of jealousy is not to be reckoned here. For even from that which has the highest good as its purpose, if some person blinded by passion turns away, does the purpose thereby become purposeless? What is purposeless need not be stated at all.
Therefore, the name is well established as an ancillary to the engagement of those who seek [knowledge].
[The verse]: She who bestows the outward expression of the variety of meanings that have been made clear [in the mind],

[Locana]: '<s>Tad vyākarot sahṛdayodayalābhahetoḥ</s>' — this is the conclusion recapitulating the subject-matter (<s>abhidheya</s>), the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>), and their connection (<s>sambandha</s>). Here, people generally act under the force of their estimation of worldly reputation. And that estimation arises from hearing the name [of the author], through the recollection of other well-known qualities associated with that person — their conduct, poetic skill, learning, and so forth. For example: 'This was composed by <s>Bhartṛhari</s> — one whose magnanimity is of such greatness, in whose treatise such essential content is seen, this is his collection of verses — therefore this should be studied with care.' Thus people are seen to engage. And people must indeed be made to engage, for the attainment of the purposes set forth in that treatise. Because inducing engagement in the audience who is to be benefited is an ancillary purpose, authors include their own names — with this intention he says '<s>Ānandavardhana</s>.' By the word '<s>prathita</s>' (celebrated), this alone is made known. [Bālapriyā]: The set of reasonings — that is the meaning. '<s>Vyākarot</s>' — he made clear, he elucidated. '<s>Sahṛdaye</s>' — the '<s>udaya</s>' (rise) of <s>sahṛdayas</s> means their <s>abhyudaya</s> (elevation), i.e., the delight caused by the comprehension of the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s>; for the sake of attaining that — for the purpose that consists in attaining that, is the meaning. '<s>Tena brūmaḥ sahṛdayamanaḥprītaye tatsvarūpam</s>' (Therefore we speak of its essential nature for the delight of the connoisseur's heart) — this conclusion accords with the opening. Considering the verse-meaning to be clear, he explains in the Locana the point that needs to be stated — '<s>satkāvye</s>' etc. '<s>Iti sambandha-abhidheya-prayojana-upasaṃhāraḥ</s>' — the connection (<s>sambandha</s>) is the relation of expounded and expounder between the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s> and this treatise. The subject-matter (<s>abhidheya</s>) is the essential nature of <s>dhvani</s>. The purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) is the delight caused by knowledge of <s>dhvani</s>'s essential nature. By '<s>tad vyākarot sahṛdayodayalābhahetoḥ</s>', the subject-matter and purpose are explicitly stated, while the connection is understood by implication. Then he introduces the fourth quarter-verse beginning with '<s>Ānanda</s>' — with 'here' etc. '<s>Sambhāvanāpratyaya</s>' — means 'an apprehension of esteem.' '<s>Nāma</s>' — the hearing of the author's name; by virtue of that, is the meaning. '<s>Prasiddha</s>' — 'well-known, other' — other than the name. Or: '<s>prasiddham anyam</s>' means 'well-known and distinctive,' that is the meaning. Such conduct associated with that person, the author — good conduct, and so forth — through the recollection of that, is the meaning. 'And that estimation arises' — this is the connection. He illustrates what has been said with an example — 'For example' etc. '<s>Bhartṛhariṇā idaṃ kṛtam</s>' etc. — this is a description of the form of popular cognition. '<s>Yasya</s>' — of <s>Bhartṛhari</s>. '<s>Ayam</s>' — this utterance is directed at the work. '<s>Iti</s>' — means 'with this cognition.'
I pay homage to that fourth power [of speech, <s>Vaikharī</s>], which reveals meanings as if directly perceptible.

That which shines forth illuminating all worthy objects, whose excellence is to be inferred from the arrangement of the true meanings of the <s>Kāvyāloka</s> — which blossoms through the discernment of <s>Ānandavardhana</s> —
that is the <s>Vilocana</s> (Eye/Commentary) of <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, which has been set to work [upon this text].

ānandavardhanasya yo vivekaḥ vivicyatattadarthāvabodhaḥ tena vikāsī prakāśamāno yaḥ kāvyalokastasya yānyarthatatvāni sārārthāḥ teṣāṃ ghaṭanātsaṃyojanāddhetoḥ /
anumeyassāra utkarṣo yasya tat, kiñca yat pronmiṣat sahṛdayeṣu prakāśamānamatha ca prakarṣeṇa unmiṣat sat sakalānāṃ sarveṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ kāvyādīnāṃ sadviṣayān sārārthān sakalān sadviṣayānvā atha ca sakalānāṃ sarveṣāṃ kāvyādīnāṃ sadbiṣayān sārārthān sakalān sadviṣayān vā atha ca sakalān sadviṣayān vidyamānān padārthān prakāśayatīti tathā bhavati tat tathāvidham /
abhinavaguptasya tannāmnaḥ svasya, atha ca abhinavaṃ navīnāṃ guptamanyeṣāmaviditaṃ ca locanamālocanaṃ jñānaṃ netraṃ ca vyāpāryata ātmanā vyāpāritam /
ṇijantātkarmaṇi laṅ /

children.translated_text: Here, the similarity of [this] knowledge to an eye is implied.
'<s>Śrī Siddhi</s>' — [the verse begins]:

children.text: śrīmataḥ siddhicelasya tannāmnaḥ guroḥ caraṇābjaparāgaiḥ pūto yo locanam śrīsiddhicelacaraṇābjaparāgapūtabhaṭṭendurājamatisaṃskṛtabuddhileśaḥ /
children.translated_text: One whose intellect has been purified by the pollen of the lotus-feet of the glorious <s>Siddhicela</s>, his teacher of that name — [Locana]: Purified by the pollen of the lotus-feet of the venerable <s>Siddhicela</s>, the intellectual capacity refined by the understanding of <s>Bhaṭṭendurāja</s> —
The master of sentences, authorities, words, and <s>Vedas</s>, whose delight was in the service of composition — he composed the commentary on the substance of <s>Dhvani</s>.

[Bālapriyā]: '<s>Tat</s>' — means 'therefore.' '<s>Etad eva prathitam</s>' — means 'this alone has been made known,' i.e., what was stated has been made manifest, that is the meaning. '<s>Tad eva nāmaśravaṇam</s>' — the very hearing of the name that induces engagement in many people — that very hearing of the name, is the meaning. '<s>Karoti</s>' — produces. '<s>Niḥśreyasa</s>' — means 'from that whose purpose is the highest good.' '<s>Śrutāt</s>' — means 'from the reality taught by scripture, i.e., from knowledge.' '<s>Etāvat</s>' — means 'merely by the turning away of one blinded by passion.' '<s>Prayojanam</s>' — means 'the purpose in reality.' '<s>Aprayojana</s>' — means 'different from purpose.' '<s>Vaktavyam eva syāt kim</s>' — this is the connection: 'need it be stated?' The purport is: it need not be stated. '<s>Prathitaṃ nāma pravṛttyaṅgam</s>' — this is the connection. The author, having made obeisance to <s>Parā</s> [speech] at the end of the first <s>Uddyota</s>, to <s>Paśyantī</s> at the end of the second, and to <s>Madhyamā</s> at the end of the third, now performs obeisance to <s>Vaikharī</s> at the end of the fourth <s>Uddyota</s> — with '<s>sphuṭī</s>' etc. '<s>Sphuṭīkṛtāni</s>' — the varieties of meaning that have been made clear, i.e., made distinct in the mind by the speaker — their '<s>bahiḥprasara</s>' (outward flow), i.e., manifestation among listeners — she who bestows that. '<s>Pratyakṣa</s>' — she who shows meanings as if directly perceptible — who displays even imperceptible meanings as though they were directly perceived, is what is meant. The '<s>turyā śakti</s>' (fourth power) is the power in the form of <s>Vaikharī</s> [the fully articulated level of speech]. 'I pay homage' — that is the meaning. '<s>Ānanda</s>' etc. — the '<s>viveka</s>' (discernment) of <s>Ānandavardhana</s>, i.e., the understanding that discriminates each particular meaning; '<s>vikāsī</s>' means 'blossoming, becoming manifest through that'; the '<s>Kāvyāloka</s>' [that so blossoms] — from the arrangement, i.e., the synthesis, of its true meanings, its essential contents — [the commentary] whose excellence is to be inferred from that. Moreover, '<s>yat pronmiṣat</s>' — that which shines forth among connoisseurs, and moreover, shining forth with special intensity; '<s>sakalānāṃ</s>' — of all literary works and the like; illuminating their worthy objects, their essential meanings — or illuminating all existing worthy objects — it becomes such. '<s>Abhinavagupta</s>' — of himself bearing that name; and also: '<s>abhinava</s>' means 'novel' and '<s>gupta</s>' means 'hidden from others,' i.e., unknown to others; '<s>locana</s>' means contemplation, knowledge, and also 'eye' — which has been employed by himself. The causative passive past tense is from the <s>ṇij</s>-ending [conjugation], in the <s>karmaṇi</s> (passive) voice.

children.text: sajjanān kavirasau na yācate hlādanāya śaśamṛtkimarthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: This poet does not beseech good people for their delight — is the moon ever asked for its nectar?

children.text: naiva nindati khalānmuhurmuhuḥ dhikkṛto 'pi na hi śītalo 'nalaḥ // //
children.translated_text: Nor does he ever revile the malicious — for fire is never cold, even when cursed.
In truth, in a heart filled with <s>Śiva</s>, everything clearly shines forth as pervaded by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: nāśivaṃ kvacana kasyacidvacaḥ tena vaśśivamayī daśā bhavet //
children.translated_text: No one's speech is ever inauspicious anywhere — therefore may your state be one pervaded by <s>Śiva</s> (auspiciousness).

children.text: iti mahāmāheśvarābhinavaguptaviracite kāvyālokalocane caturtha udyotaḥ samāptaścāvaṃ granthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the Fourth <s>Uddyota</s> in the <s>Kāvyālokalocana</s> (Eye on the Light of Literature) composed by the great <s>Māheśvara</s> (Shaiva master) <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. And thus this work is complete.

children.text:
bālapriyā bhaṭṭendurājaḥ tasya matyā jñānena saṃskṛto buddhileśo yasya saḥ /
vākyeti /
vākyaṃ mīmāṃsāśāstraṃ, pramāṇaṃ nyāyaśāstraṃ, padaṃ vyākaraṇaśāstraṃ, tadvedināṃ gururityarthaḥ /
prabandhasevāyāṃ raso yasya saḥ /
abhinavagupta iti śeṣaḥ /
dhvanivastuvṛrtti dhvanigranthavivṛtim /
vyaracayat kṛtavān /
sajjanāniti /
asau kavirityātmānaṃ nirdiśyoktiḥ /
hlādanāya svagranthādaraṇeva svaprīṇanāya sajjanānna yācate /
kuto na yācata ityāśaṅkāṃ dṛṣṭāntapradarśanena parihariti---śaśabhṛtkimarthita iti /
hlādanāyetyanuṣaṅgaḥ /
kimirthitaḥ janairarthitaḥ /
kiṃ naivetyarthaḥ /
candra iva sajjanaḥ svayameva parānāhlādayatīti candrasyeva parāhlādanaṃ sajjanasya svabhāva ityarthaḥ /
naiveti /
muhurmuhuḥ dhikkṛto 'pi khalaiḥ punaḥ punaradhikṣipto 'pi /
asau kavirityanuṣaṅgaḥ /
khalānnaiva nindati kuta ityata āha---na hītyādi /
analaḥ agniḥ, śītalaḥ anuṣṇaḥ /
na hi yathā agniḥ sarvadā uṣṇasvabhāva eva tathā khalajanaḥ paradūṣaṇasvabhāva eva, svabhāvaścāparihārya ityarthaḥ /
ata ityubhayatra pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ /
atha paramamāheśvaro granthakāro granthānte paramaśivānusandhānātmakaṃ paramamaṅgalamanutiṣṭhannāha---vastuta ityādi /
janasya hṛdi hṛdaye vastutaḥ śivamaye sati śivamaye hṛdīti vā yojanā, sarvataḥ sarvaṃ vastu sphuṭaṃ śivamayaṃ virājate bhāti /
nāśivamityādi /
kvacana kvacidapi kasyacidvacaḥ aśivaṃ na bhavati, kintu sarvatra śivameva bhavatītyarthaḥ /
anena vastutaḥ śivamaye svasya hṛdaye sarvaṃ śivamayaṃ bhāti /
atassarvatrāpi viṣaye svavacaḥ śivamevetyarthaḥ pradarśitaḥ /
teneti /
svavacanenetyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Or' — this is a statement addressed to the listeners.

children.text: śivamayī maṅgalamayī daśā bhavet bhavatviti sarvaṃ śivam /
children.translated_text: May there be a state pervaded by <s>Śiva</s>, i.e., pervaded by auspiciousness — let there be — all is <s>Śiva</s> (auspicious).
May the divine <s>Vāṇī</s> (Goddess of Speech) be victorious, together with the good poets and sages!
And may the <s>Kāvyāloka</s> (Dhvanyāloka) together with the <s>Locana</s> be delightful to those who have hearts! // //

[<s>Bālapriyā</s>:] <s>Bhaṭṭendurāja</s> — one whose trace of intellect has been refined by his knowledge, i.e., learning. /
'Of sentences' (<s>vākya</s>) — /
'<s>Vākya</s>' means the science of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>; '<s>pramāṇa</s>' means the science of <s>Nyāya</s>; '<s>pada</s>' means the science of Grammar (<s>Vyākaraṇa</s>) — the meaning is: the teacher of those who know these. /
'One whose relish (<s>rasa</s>) is in the practice of literary composition (<s>prabandhasevā</s>).' /
The remainder is: <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. /
'<s>Dhvanivastuvṛtti</s>' — the elaboration of the <s>Dhvani</s>-treatise. /
'Composed' — made. /
'Of the good people' — /
This is a statement referring to himself as 'that poet.' /
'For the delight' — by the high regard for his own treatise, i.e., for his own satisfaction, he does not beseech the good people. /
Anticipating the doubt 'why does he not beseech?' she resolves it by showing an illustration — '<s>śaśabhṛt</s> (Moon), is he besought?' etc. /
'For the delight' is to be connected. /
'Is he besought' — is he entreated by people? /
The meaning is: certainly not. /
Just as the moon delights others of its own accord, so too the good person — the meaning is: delighting others is the nature of the good person, just as it is of the moon. /
'Not at all' — /
Even though reviled again and again, even though repeatedly disparaged by the wicked. /
The continuation is: 'that poet.' /
Why does he not reproach the wicked? — to this she says — 'not indeed' etc. /
'Fire' (<s>anala</s>) — flame; 'cool' (<s>śītala</s>) — not hot. /
Not indeed — just as fire is always of a hot nature, so the wicked person is always of a nature to disparage others — and one's nature cannot be avoided — this is the meaning. /
'Therefore' — connects with the preceding in both cases. /
Now the author, a supreme <s>Māheśvara</s> (devotee of Śiva), at the end of the treatise, performing the supreme auspicious act that consists of contemplation of <s>Paramaśiva</s>, says — 'in reality' etc. /
'Of a person, in the heart' — when the heart is in reality of the nature of <s>Śiva</s> — or the construction is: 'in the heart that is of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>' — from all sides, everything manifestly shines forth as pervaded by <s>Śiva</s>. /
'Nothing inauspicious' etc. — /
Nowhere, for no one, does any speech become inauspicious; rather, everywhere it is auspicious alone — this is the meaning. /
By this: in the heart, which is in reality of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, everything shines as of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>. /
Therefore, in all domains, one's own speech is auspicious alone — this meaning is demonstrated. /
'By that' — /
The meaning is: by one's own speech.
One who from the beginning has been an ocean of all learning, a royal sage, [bearing the title] <s>Mahāgo-Śrī-bhṛd</s>,
who obtained the titles '<s>Sahṛdayatilaka</s>' (Ornament of Connoisseurs) and others from [the king]. // //
Honored by the daughter of the <s>Aṅgala-Śrī-Cakravartin</s> — his wisdom [was established],
who commented on the <s>Śākuntalā</s> etc., and who was the teacher beginning with <s>Go-Śrī-Śa</s>. // //
The crest-jewel of those who know the <s>śāstras</s> and literature, bearing the secondary name <s>Parīkṣit</s>,
the friend and fellow-student <s>Go-Śrī-Śa</s>, whose support extends in all directions. // //
I, <s>Rāma</s> by name, born of the <s>Śāraka</s> [family], composed this <s>ṭippaṇī</s> (gloss)
in the <s>Kaliyuga</s> year [marked by] arrows (5), fires (3), and the sky (0) [i.e., year 1530?] — may this be dear to the young [students]! // //

children.text: prauḍhaṃ kva locanaṃ kvāhaṃ mandadhīrbahudhātra tat /
children.translated_text: How profound is the <s>Locana</s>, and how dull-witted am I — in many places therein
there may be errors in the <s>ṭippaṇī</s> — let it be corrected by the wise! //

children.text: iti śrīsahṛdayatilaka paṇḍitarāja birudadvayaśālinā rāmanāmnā śārakeṇa viracitāyāṃ kāvyālokalocanaṭippaṇyāṃ bālapriyākhyāyāṃ caturtha udyotaḥ samāpto 'yaṃ granthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the Fourth <s>Uddyota</s> — and this work is complete — in the <s>ṭippaṇī</s> (gloss) on the <s>Kāvyāloka-Locana</s>, called <s>Bālapriyā</s> (Beloved of the Young), composed by <s>Rāma</s> of the <s>Śāraka</s> [family], adorned with the two titles <s>Sahṛdayatilaka</s> (Ornament of Connoisseurs) and <s>Paṇḍitarāja</s> (King of Scholars). //
